Volume One

In the name of God, Most Gracious, Most Merciful. Abū al-Ḥusayn Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Faḍl al-Qaṭṭān informed us in Baghdad. He said:

It was read aloud to Abū Muḥammad ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar ibn Durustawayh, while I was present and listening. He said:

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to us:

The Year 135

In this year, Abū Muslim returned from Samarqand and arrived in Marw in Jumādā II.

In this year he dispatched delegations to Abū al-ʿAbbās. When Shawwāl came, he encamped at the Gate of Kushmayhan and gave the troops their stipends, intending to raid al-Ṭirāz and its surrounding districts. Ziyād ibn Ṣāliḥ al-Khuzāʿī rebelled against him and wrote to Sibāʿ ibn al-Nuʿmān and Muḥammad ibn Zurʿah, urging them to rebel against him as well. They refused and informed Abū Muslim of this. Abū Muslim then set out from his camp, heading for Ziyād, and killed Ziyād in this year.

Yaḥyā ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās, the brother of Abū al-ʿAbbās ʿAbd Allāh, died.

…ibn Muḥammad in Fārs, where he was governor.

Al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Ḥarashī led the summer campaign.

Sulaymān ibn [ʿAlī ibn] ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās led the pilgrimage for the people.

In it, Ziyād ibn ʿUbayd Allāh al-Ḥārithī was removed from authority over Mecca alone, and al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Maʿbad ibn al-ʿAbbās was appointed.

The Year 136

In the year 136 AH, Abū Jaʿfar al-Manṣūr led the people on the pilgrimage, and al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Maʿbad was in charge of Mecca.

Salamah related to us. Aḥmad, from Isḥāq ibn ʿĪsā, from Abū Maʿshar:

Abū al-ʿAbbās died on the thirteenth night of Dhū al-Ḥijjah. His caliphate lasted four years and ten months, and Abū Jaʿfar ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad was installed as caliph.

Ibrāhīm ibn al-Mundhir related to us. He said: Zayd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd ibn Aslam related to us that his grandfather, Zayd ibn Aslam, died in the year Abū Jaʿfar was installed as caliph, during the first ten days of Dhū al-Ḥijjah, in the year 136 AH. Abū al-ʿAbbās’s caliphate lasted five years.

[I heard Ibrāhīm ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Bukayr say: Rabīʿah died…

“In the year one hundred and thirty-six.”

Allegiance was pledged to Abū Jaʿfar ʿAbd Allāh ibn [Muḥammad ibn] ʿAlī ibn ʿAbbās in Mecca, in Muḥarram, on the Day of ʿĀshūrāʾ, in the year one hundred and thirty-six. After him, allegiance was pledged to ʿĪsā ibn Mūsā ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn al-ʿAbbās. Abū Jaʿfar ʿĪsā ibn Mūsā ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-ʿAbbās took charge of receiving the oath of allegiance and sending out letters to all the prominent men.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAlī raided the summer frontier.

Al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Maʿbad was in charge of Mecca.

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAmr Abū Zurʿa al-Dimashqī related to me. He said: Sulaymān ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd informed us, saying: I heard Bishr ibn Muslim say: I heard my grandfather Mujāhid ibn Sulaymān say that Asad ibn Widāʿa was killed in the year one hundred and thirty-six. He said:

I heard ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm say: Asad ibn Widāʿa was judge of the army district at Ḥimṣ.

Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us, saying: Muʿāwiya ibn Ṣāliḥ al-Ḥaḍramī al-Ḥimṣī related to us from Asad ibn Widāʿa—and Asad had long been held in good regard. He said: I heard Sulaymān ibn Salama al-Khabāʾirī al-Ḥimṣī say: Asad ibn Widāʿa was a Ṭāʾī of the Nabḥān clan.

“Abū al-ʿAlāʾ said: I asked Yazīd ibn ʿAbd Rabbih, ‘Did Baqiyya relate to you from …’”

…from Ibn Abī Maryam, who said: ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz wrote to the governor of Ḥimṣ: “Look to the people who have devoted themselves to jurisprudence and confined themselves to the mosque, turning away from the pursuit of worldly things. Give each of them one hundred dinars from the treasury of the Muslims, to help them in what they are doing, as soon as this letter of mine reaches you; the best good is that which is hastened. Peace be upon you.”

I heard ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm say: Yūnus ibn Maysara was killed here.

He said: ʿAbd al-Aʿlā ibn Mushir was killed on the day ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAlī entered.

Volume One137

In the year one hundred and thirty-seven

Salama related to us, saying: Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal said, from Saḥq1, from Abū Maʿshar:

Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAlī led the pilgrimage in the year one hundred and thirty-seven.

He said: Ibn Bukayr said: Abū al-Shaḥmāʾ Sahl ibn Ḥassān al-Kalbī died in the year one hundred and thirty-seven.

Some people have said that ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās was appointed heir apparent after Abū Jaʿfar. The Commander of the Faithful, Abū Jaʿfar, arrived at al-Ḥīra, and Abū Muslim arrived to meet Abū Jaʿfar at al-Ḥīra. Abū Jaʿfar entered Kūfa, led the people in prayer, addressed them, and informed them that he was setting out. Then he departed and went as far as al-Anbār, where he settled and gathered his forces around him. He had …

ʿĪsā had written to ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAlī concerning the pledge of allegiance to Abū Jaʿfar. The letter reached him while he was at Raʾs al-Durūb, heading toward the Byzantine lands with the people of Khurāsān, al-Jazīra, and Syria. He turned back with the people and proceeded until he settled in the city of Ḥarrān. He summoned the Khurāsānī troops, incorporated them into the “Eighties,” assigned them the special allotments, and had allegiance pledged to himself. He departed from Ḥarrān, intending for Iraq. Then he attacked the people of Khurāsān and killed them. Abū Muslim and ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAlī marched against one another at Bāb al-Ghādir, in the land of Naṣībīn, and fought fiercely. ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAlī was routed, and with him ʿAbd al-Ṣamad ibn ʿAlī. The two fled to Hishām’s Raṣāfa. He seized ʿAbd al-Ṣamad ibn ʿAlī and sent him to Abū Jaʿfar, who granted him security and pardoned him. ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAlī arrived in Baṣra to visit Sulaymān ibn ʿAlī, who treated him generously, and he went into hiding with him. Abū Jaʿfar sent Yaqṭīn ibn Mūsā to Abū Muslim, ordering him to take an inventory of what was in ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAlī’s camp. Abū Muslim was angered by this and resolved upon defiance and attack. Abū Jaʿfar set out for al-Madāʾin, and Abū Muslim set out, taking the road to Khurāsān, which he intended to reach in defiance of Abū Jaʿfar.

“Abū Muslim was killed on Wednesday, when seven nights of Shaʿbān had passed, in this year.”

Al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Maʿbad was in charge of Mecca; he died at the end of the pilgrimage. Ismāʿīl added his post to Ziyād ibn ʿUbayd Allāh’s, and Abū Jaʿfar confirmed him in it.

In this year, a Kharijite rebel rose in Naysābūr and marched to al-Rayy, gaining control of it and of Qūmis. Abū Jaʿfar dispatched Jumhūr ibn Marrār al-ʿIjlī, who killed him and killed nearly fifty thousand, taking their children captive.

In this year, Ḥarmala al-Shaybānī rose in the region of al-Jazīra.

Volume One138

[In the year one hundred and thirty-eight]

In the year one hundred and thirty-eight, al-Faḍl ibn Ṣāliḥ ibn ʿAlī led the people on the pilgrimage.

Salama related to us, saying: Aḥmad said: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd said: Yūnus died in the year one hundred and thirty-eight or thirty-nine.

In this year, Jumhūr ibn Marrār al-ʿIjlī was deposed. Muḥammad ibn al-Ashʿath marched against him and killed him.

In this year, the Byzantine tyrant raided Malāṭiya, demolished it, and spared those of its combatants and dependents who were there.

Khuzayma ibn Khāzim marched against Ḥarmala al-Shaybānī and killed him.

Ziyād ibn ʿUbayd Allāh al-Ḥārithī was in charge of Mecca and Medina.

In this year, Abū Jaʿfar demolished part of the Sacred Mosque and enlarged it.

Volume One139

[In the year one hundred and thirty-nine]

In the year one hundred and thirty-nine, al-ʿAbbās ibn Muḥammad led the people on the pilgrimage.

Ḥaywa related to us, saying: Baqiyya ibn al-Walīd related to us, saying: “Ismāʿīl ibn Umayya died in the year one hundred and thirty-nine,” one day before he entered Mecca.

He said: Ibn Bukayr said: Khālid ibn Yazīd al-Jumaḥī died in the year one hundred and thirty-nine. His teknonym was Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥīm. He had stayed with ʿAṭāʾ for a year, then remained in Alexandria until he died.

Ibn Bukayr said: Al-Layth used to say: “A trustworthy man related to me from Saʿīd ibn Abī Hilāl, and the account grew long for him until he became impatient. Shuʿba said: ‘It is all from Saʿīd ibn Abī Hilāl.’ I doubted three or four things in it, so I went to Khālid ibn Yazīd and heard all of it from him.”

Salama related to us: “Aḥmad said: Yaḥyā said: ‘I arrived in Mecca in the year one hundred and forty-four, and Ismāʿīl ibn Umayya and ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān had died. Ḥajjāj ibn Arṭāʾa arrived among us that year, and I saw al-Awzāʿī and Thawr in the year one hundred and fifty.’”

Yaḥyā said: Dāwūd ibn Abī Hind died in the year one hundred and thirty-nine.

Yazīd ibn Hārūn said: Dāwūd ibn Abī Hind died in the year one hundred and thirty-nine. He and Saʿīd ibn Abī ʿArūba passed by us before that, and I heard from them both.

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAmr related to me, saying: ʿAmr ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAẓīm ibn ʿAmr ibn Muhājir related to me—and I asked him about the date of ʿAmr ibn Muhājir’s death. He said:

My uncle Muḥammad ibn Muhājir related to me that ʿAmr ibn Muhājir died in the year one hundred and thirty-nine.

Abū Yūsuf said: I asked ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm about ʿAmr ibn Muhājir. He said: Suwayd saw him and related from him.

Abū Hāshim Ziyād ibn Ayyūb related to me, saying: I heard Saʿīd ibn ʿĀmir say: Yūnus ibn ʿUbayd died in the year one hundred and thirty-nine.

Aḥmad ibn al-Khalīl related to us, saying: Mūsā ibn Hilāl al-ʿAbdī related to us: Yūnus ibn ʿUbayd died in the year one hundred and thirty-nine.

Volume One140

[In the year one hundred and forty]

In the year one hundred and forty, Abū Jaʿfar ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās led the people on the pilgrimage.

Salama related to us: Aḥmad said: Yazīd ibn Hārūn said: Abū al-ʿAlāʾ al-Qaṣṣāb died in the year one hundred and forty.

He said: I heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad ibn Dhakwān mention, on the authority of Yazīd ibn ʿAbd Rabbih, who said: ʿAmr ibn Qays said: “Al-Ḥajjāj said to me, ‘When were you born, Abū Thawr?’ I replied, ‘In the Year of Unity, in the year forty.’ He said, ‘That is when I was born, too.’”

He said: Al-Ḥajjāj died in the year ninety-five, and ʿAmr ibn Qays died in the year one hundred and forty.

He said: I heard Abū Ayyūb Sulaymān ibn Salama al-Khabāʾirī al-Ḥimṣī say:

ʿAmr ibn Qays al-Sakūnī, Abū Thawr, died in the year one hundred and forty, and Jibrīl ibn Yaḥyā al-Bajalī performed the funeral prayer over him.

Al-ʿAbbās ibn al-Walīd ibn Ṣubḥ related to us, saying: Abū Mushir related to us, saying: I heard Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz say: ʿUrwa ibn Ruwaym died in the year one hundred and forty. He died at Dhū Khashab, and was carried to Medina and buried there.

He said: ʿAlī said: Dāwūd ibn Abī Hind died in the year one hundred and forty on the road to Mecca.

Abū Jaʿfar set out on pilgrimage, entering the state of consecration at al-Ḥīra, and conducting the pilgrimage for the people. Ziyād ibn ʿUbayd Allāh al-Ḥārithī was in charge of Medina and Mecca. After the pilgrimage, Abū Jaʿfar went on to Medina, then proceeded from there to Jerusalem. Al-Layth ibn Saʿd came to visit him.

“I heard Ibn Bukayr say: He said: Al-Layth said: Abū Jaʿfar said to me, ‘Will you govern Egypt for me?’ I replied, ‘No, Commander of the Faithful. I am unequal to that; I am a man from among the clients.’

“He said, ‘You are not unequal to it with me; rather, your intention is inadequate for working for me in that position.’” “Do you want a strength greater than mine and my authority? But since you refuse, point me to a man to whom I can entrust the affairs of Egypt.” I said: “ʿUthmān ibn al-Ḥakam al-Judhāmī, a righteous man with a clan behind him.” When he heard of this, he swore by God, Mighty and Glorious, never to speak to al-Layth ibn Saʿd.

Abū Muslim had appointed him as his deputy when he set out for Iraq. He was killed at Marw on the night of Friday, in Rabīʿ I of the year one hundred and forty.

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Sulaymān took office after Abū Dāwūd was killed.

Ibn Fuḍayl related to us from Yazīd, who said: I heard from Sufyān in the year forty.

Volume One141

In the year one hundred and forty-one

“Ṣāliḥ ibn ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās led the people on the pilgrimage.”

Ibn Bukayr said: ʿUqayl ibn Khālid died in Egypt in the year one hundred and forty-one or forty-two.

Aḥmad related to us: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd said: ʿĀṣim al-Aḥwal died in the year one hundred and forty-one or forty-two, and Khālid in the year one hundred and forty-one.

Muḥammad ibn Fuḍayl related to me from Yazīd ibn Hārūn, who said: Sufyān related to us from Khālid al-Ḥadhdhāʾ, while Khālid was still alive. Yazīd said: I heard from Sufyān in the year one hundred and forty.

Abū Hāshim Ziyād ibn Ayyūb related to me, saying: I heard Saʿīd ibn ʿĀmir say:

Asmāʾ ibn ʿUbayd died in the year one hundred and forty-one.

In this year, Ziyād ibn ʿUbayd Allāh was removed from the governorship of Medina and Mecca. Muḥammad ibn Khālid ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Qasrī was appointed over Medina and arrived there in Rajab. Al-Haytham ibn Muʿāwiya was put in charge of Mecca and al-Ṭāʾif.

Volume One142

[In the year one hundred and forty-two]

In the year one hundred and forty-two, Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās led the people on the pilgrimage, and al-Haytham ibn Muʿāwiya was in charge of Mecca.

Salama related to us, saying: Aḥmad related to us: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd said: Ḥumayd died in the year one hundred and forty-two, or in the latter part of forty-three, shortly before al-Taymī.

Muḥammad ibn Abī Ismāʿīl died in the year one hundred and forty-two.

Asad ibn ʿAbd Allāh Abū Mālik al-Khuzāʿī was appointed over Khurāsān. At that time, the officials of Khurāsān were appointed by al-Mahdī. Al-Mahdī was heir apparent and was residing at al-Rayy.

In this year, the people of Ṭabaristān rebelled and killed the Muslims there. Khāzim ibn Khuzayma and Rawḥ ibn Ḥātim marched against them, accompanied by Abū al-Khaṣīb. They besieged Ṭabaristān, and their stay there grew long. Abū al-Khaṣīb said, “Beat my back, and shave my head and beard.” They did so, and he went to the Iṣbahbad, who granted him security, treated him generously, and entrusted him with guarding the gate. One night, he opened the gate to the Muslims. They entered the city, killed those within it, and took the dependents captive. The Iṣbahbad sucked a ring of his that contained poison, and died, bound for the Fire.

“In this year, Sulaymān ibn ʿAlī died” in Baṣra, on the night of Saturday, with seven nights of Jumādā II remaining. He was nearing sixty. ʿAbd al-Ṣamad ibn ʿAlī performed the funeral prayer over him.

In this year, Abū Jaʿfar fasted in Baṣra and led the people in the festival prayer.

Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥasan rose in Medina on Wednesday, with three nights of Jumādā II remaining, in the year one hundred and forty-five. He remained there until ʿĪsā ibn Mūsā ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās arrived against him with an army …

whom Abū Jaʿfar had sent from Kūfa. Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥasan was killed on Monday, on the fifteenth of Ramaḍān, in the year one hundred and forty-five. Rayyāḥ ibn ʿUthmān ibn Ḥayyān was then in charge of Medina and had imprisoned him. When Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh was killed, Muḥammad’s supporters entered the prison where Rayyāḥ was and killed him.

Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥasan rose in Baṣra on the night the month of Ramaḍān began, and was killed with five nights of Dhū al-Qaʿda remaining, in the year one hundred and forty-five.

Al-Sarī ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib was then in charge of Mecca.

In this year, a battle took place between the people of Medina and the people of Khurāsān on Friday, with seven nights of Dhū al-Ḥijja remaining. The people of Khurāsān were routed, and Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥasan gained control of Baṣra, including its treasury and all that it contained. He divided it among his supporters, giving each man two hundred dirhams, then assigned stipends to the people. He gained control of Wāsiṭ, al-Ahwāz, and its districts.

In this year, Yaʿqūb ibn al-Faḍl al-Hāshimī rose and gained control of all Fārs. He called people to support Ibrāhīm. Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAlī fortified himself in the city of Dārābjird, where he was governor.

The Banū Labīd al-Yashkurī rose, gained control of Kaskar, and called for support of Ibrāhīm.

Then Ibrāhīm set out for Kūfa, took the route through Kaskar, and appointed as his deputy over …

In Basra, Numayla ibn Murra al-Saʿdī was [appointed]. Abū Jaʿfar’s troops, whom he had sent against Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh, came to him, and he sent them against Ibrāhīm. They met at a village in the Sawād called Bākhumrā and fought fiercely. ʿĪsā ibn Mūsā was routed; afterward, Ibrāhīm’s men were routed. Ibrāhīm stood firm with about four hundred men, and they were all killed. Many men were killed alongside Ibrāhīm.

In this year the Turks came out at al-Abwāb and inflicted losses on the Muslims.

In this year Abū Jaʿfar moved to Baghdad. When news reached him of Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh’s revolt, he returned to Kūfa.

In this year ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Rabīʿ al-Ḥārithī was appointed over Medina.

Volume One143

In the year 143 AH

ʿĪsā ibn Mūsā ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās led the pilgrimage.

Salama related to us; Aḥmad said: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd—that is, he died—in the year 143 AH, and al-Taymī died in 143 AH.

Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn Manṣūr related to me: Mūsā ibn Hilāl related to us, saying:

Kahmas died in the year 143 AH.

In this year Abū Jaʿfar was sent to Basra. He ordered everyone who possessed ten thousand dirhams or more to send a man to fight the Daylam, because they had inflicted losses on the Muslims.

Al-Haytham ibn Muʿāwiya was dismissed from Mecca and al-Ṭāʾif, and al-Sarī ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith ibn al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib was appointed in his place.

Volume One144

In the year 144 AH

Abū Jaʿfar al-Manṣūr led the pilgrimage.

“Abū Nuʿaym said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shubrumah and ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd died in the year 144 AH.

Aḥmad ibn al-Khalīl related to me: Mūsā ibn Hilāl al-ʿAbdī related to us, saying:

ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd died in the year 144 AH, on the road to Mecca.”

In this year Muḥammad ibn Khālid ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Qasrī was dismissed from Medina, and Riyāḥ ibn ʿUthmān al-Murrī was appointed in his place. [He ordered the seizure of] Muḥammad ibn Khālid, his secretary, and his officials, and the recovery of the funds in their possession.

Abū Jaʿfar led the pilgrimage. On his way, he seized ʿAbd [Allāh] ibn al-Ḥasan and his companions over what he suspected them of concerning the affair of Ibrāhīm and Muḥammad, the two sons of ʿAbd Allāh. He seized them at al-Rabadha.

Volume One145

In the year 145 AH

Al-Sarī ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib led the pilgrimage.

“Abū Nuʿaym said: Hishām ibn ʿUrwa and ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Abī Sulaymān died in the year 145 AH.”

Salama related to us, and Aḥmad said: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd related to us, saying: Hishām ibn ʿUrwa died after the defeat—the defeat of Ibrāhīm—as though it were in the following year. The defeat took place in the year 145 AH.

Ismāʿīl died in the year 145 AH, and I think ʿAbd al-Malik died in that year.

In this year Muḥammad and Ibrāhīm, the sons of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥasan, were killed.

I heard Abū Ayyūb Sulaymān ibn Salama al-Khabāʾirī al-Ḥimṣī say: Asad ibn Wadāʿa, a Ṭāʾī of Banū Nabhan, was killed in the year 145 AH.

Abū al-ʿAlāʾ [said]: I heard ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm say: Asad ibn Wadāʿa was the judge of the army district at Ḥimṣ.

He said: Yūnus—that is, ibn Maysara—was killed here, and ʿAbd al-Aʿlā ibn Mushir was killed on the day ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAlī entered.

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAmr al-Dimashqī related to me: Sulaymān ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd informed me, saying: I heard Bishr ibn Muslim say: I heard my grandfather Mujāhid ibn Sulaymān say that Asad ibn Wadāʿa was killed in the year 136 AH.

I asked ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm about ʿAmr ibn Muhājir. He said: Suwayd had seen him and transmitted from him.

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAmr related to me, saying: ʿAmr ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAẓīm ibn ʿAmr ibn Muhājir also related to me. I asked him about the date of ʿAmr ibn Muhājir’s death. He said: ʿUmar ibn Muḥammad ibn Muhājir related to me, saying: ʿAmr ibn Muhājir died in the year 139 AH.

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAmr related to me, saying: I asked Ibn Yazīd ibn Abī Maryam about his father’s death. He said: After the year 145 AH.

Volume One146

In the year 146 AH

ʿAbd al-Wahhāb ibn Ibrāhīm led the pilgrimage.

He said: Abū Nuʿaym said: Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid, Hishām ibn Ḥassān, and ʿAwf died in the year 146 AH.

Aḥmad said: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd said: ʿAwf died in the year 146 AH, and Ashʿath died a little earlier, in the year 6 [AH].

“In this year Abū Jaʿfar completed the construction of the City of Peace, moved into it, and transferred the treasuries, public funds, and administrative bureaus there.”

Jaʿfar ibn Ḥanẓala al-Bahrānī led the summer expedition.

In this year Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān was appointed over Basra. He sought everyone who had been with Ibrāhīm and killed them, demolished their houses, and cut down their palm trees.

In this year al-Sarī ibn ʿAbd Allāh was dismissed from Mecca, and ʿAbd al-Ṣamad ibn ʿAlī was appointed.

In this year ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Rabīʿ al-Ḥārithī was dismissed from Medina, and Jaʿfar ibn Sulaymān was appointed. ʿAbd al-Wahhāb ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad led the pilgrimage.

Al-Sarī ibn ʿAbd Allāh died in Mecca in Muḥarram of the year 147 AH.

“I heard Ibn Bukayr say: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd died in the year 146 AH.”

Volume One147

In the year 147 AH

Abū Jaʿfar led the pilgrimage.

Aḥmad said: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd said: Hishām ibn Ḥassān died in the year 147 AH.

I heard Makkī ibn Ibrāhīm say: Mālik ibn Anas was flogged in the year 147 AH. Sulaymān ibn Jaʿfar ibn Sulaymān ibn ʿAlī flogged him. He said: He was struck seventy lashes.

He said: I heard Abū Ayyūb Sulaymān ibn Salama al-Khabāʾirī al-Ḥimṣī say:

Al-Zubaydī died in the year 147 AH.

“He said: I asked ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm about al-Waḍīn ibn ʿAṭāʾ’s death. He said: In the year 147 AH or thereabouts.” He said: I asked him about ʿUthmān ibn Abī ʿĀtika. He said: He was the teacher of the people of Damascus and the judge of the army district, and he died in the year forty-something and one hundred.

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAmr al-Dimashqī related to me, saying: Yazīd ibn ʿAbd Rabbih related to me, saying: Al-Zubaydī died in the year 147 AH.

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAmr related to me, saying: Muḥammad ibn al-ʿAlāʾ—a shaykh from among the people of the mosque—related to me, saying: I saw ʿUthmān ibn Abī al-ʿĀtika preaching to the people. He died while al-Faḍl ibn Ṣāliḥ was in charge over us. He governed us in the year 149 AH, for nine years.

In this year the Turks came out and took many Muslims and protected people captive. They entered Tiflis, defeated Jibrīl ibn Yaḥyā al-Bajalī, and killed Ḥarb ibn ʿAbd Allāh.

“In this year ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAlī died in the City of Peace, having passed the age of fifty.”

In this year Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān was dismissed from Basra, and Muḥammad ibn Abī al-ʿAbbās was appointed over it.

In this year Ismāʿīl ibn Muslim al-Makkī died, and Muḥammad ibn Abī al-ʿAbbās led the funeral prayer for him.

Abū Jaʿfar led the pilgrimage. ʿAbd al-Ṣamad ibn ʿAlī was over Mecca, and Jaʿfar ibn Sulaymān was over Medina.

The people pledged allegiance to al-Mahdī, Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn (Abī) Jaʿfar, Commander of the Faithful, as their successor after his father Abū Jaʿfar. This took place in Mecca on Thursday, thirteen nights having passed of Rabīʿ I, in the year 147 AH.

Volume One148

In the year 148 AH

Abū Jaʿfar ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī led the pilgrimage.

“Abū Yūsuf related to us. Abū Nuʿaym said: Al-Aʿmash, Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā, Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, and Zakariyyā ibn Abī Zāʾida died in the year 148 AH.”

Ḥaywa ibn Shurayḥ related to me, saying: Ḍamra said: Al-Shaibānī died in the year 148 AH.

He said: Ibn Bukayr said: ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Yaʿqūb ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Anṣārī—whose kunya was Abū Umayya—was born in the year 91 or 92, and died in the year 148 AH.

Aḥmad said: Yaḥyā said: Al-Aʿmash died in the year 148 AH.

Aḥmad said: Yazīd ibn Hārūn said: They claimed that al-ʿAwwām died in the year 148 AH.

It is said that al-Aʿmash was born in the year al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib was killed.

Ibn Numayr related to us, saying: Yaḥyā related to us, saying: I heard al-Aʿmash say: “I was born shortly before the killing of al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī.”

I heard al-Makkī ibn Ibrāhīm say: Hishām ibn Ḥassān died on the first day of Ṣafar in the year 148 AH. He said: Saʿīd ibn Abī ʿArūba was still alive then. Then I arrived in the year 150 AH, and he had died.

Abū Yūsuf said: It reached me from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Dāwūd that ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, al-Aʿmash, and Hishām ibn ʿUrwa were born in the same year.

Aḥmad ibn al-Khalīl related to me, saying: Aḥmad ibn Sulaymān related to us, saying: I heard Wakīʿ say: Al-Aʿmash died in the year 148 AH. He said: We wrote down reports from Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna a year before al-Aʿmash died; when we wrote them from him, he was forty years old.

Volume One149

In the year 149 AH

Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm led the pilgrimage.

“He said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAmr al-Dimashqī related to me, saying: Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān Abū al-Jamāhir related to us, saying: I saw al-Waḍīn ibn ʿAṭāʾ, and I used to pass by him. He died in the year 149 AH.”

In this year al-ʿAbbās ibn Muḥammad led a campaign against the Byzantines.

In this year al-Manṣūr set out for al-Ḥadītha, in the land of al-Mawṣil.

“In this year the construction of the City of Peace’s wall and moat, and all its works, was completed.”

ʿAbd al-Ṣamad ibn ʿAlī was dismissed from Mecca, and Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm was appointed over it. He entered Mecca in Shawwāl of the year 149 AH, with Abū ʿAbd al-Ṣamad as his chief of police.

Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm conducted the pilgrimage for the people.

Jaʿfar ibn Sulaymān was over Medina.

Volume One150

In the year 150 AH

ʿAbd al-Ṣamad ibn ʿAlī led the pilgrimage.

“Abū Nuʿaym said: Abū Ḥanīfa died in the year 150 AH. He was born in the year 80 AH, and was seventy years old when he died.”

Aḥmad said: I heard Yaḥyā say: Ibn Jurayj died in the year 150 AH, and ʿUthmān ibn al-Aswad died before that. Ḥanẓala was alive in the year 151 AH, and Sayf ibn Abī Sulaymān al-Makkī was alive in the year 150 AH; Ibn Abī Najīḥ died before the plague.

Salama related to us, saying: Aḥmad said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān related to us, saying: ʿAlī ibn Jurayj died in the year 146 AH, and Ibn Jurayj did not read aloud to the people.

He said: I arrived in the year 147 AH and heard people receive reports from him. In the evenings he would dictate twenty reports by way of intercession. I too heard the Manāsik from him in the year 149 AH.

He said: Ibn Jurayj and Ibn ʿAwn died in the year 150 AH.

In this year the people of Herat, the people of Bādhghīs, and others among the people of Khurāsān revolted. They numbered about three hundred thousand fighters. They gained control over most of Khurāsān and over Marw al-Rūdh, where they carried out a great slaughter. A number of commanders fought them, including Jibrīl ibn Yaḥyā, Muʿādh ibn Muslim, Ḥammād ibn Yaḥyā, and Abū al-Najm al-Sijistānī, but they were all defeated. Abū Jaʿfar sent Khāzim ibn Khuzayma against them. He defeated them and inflicted great slaughter among them. The number of those killed among them reached about seventy thousand. The non-Arab leader took refuge on a mountain with those of his companions who remained. Khāzim ibn Khuzayma brought forward the captives and killed them, then besieged the non-Arab leader. Abū ʿAwn sent reinforcements to Khāzim on Abū Jaʿfar’s behalf. Khāzim said to him, “Stay where you are until we need you.” The non-Arab leader surrendered on Abū ʿAwn’s terms, and Abū ʿAwn ruled that all those with him be released, while the non-Arab leader and his family were to be bound in iron. They numbered thirty thousand.

“In this year Jaʿfar ibn Abī Jaʿfar died in the City of Peace. Abū Jaʿfar led the funeral prayer for him, and he was buried in the Quraysh cemetery.”

In this year Jaʿfar ibn Sulaymān was dismissed from Medina, and al-Ḥasan ibn Zayd ibn al-Ḥasan ibn al-Ḥasan was appointed over it.

ʿAbd al-Ṣamad ibn ʿAlī led the pilgrimage.

Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm was over Mecca, with Abū ʿAbd al-Ṣamad as his chief of police.

In this year ʿAbda ibn Farqad al-Saʿdī, then al-Taymī, was appointed over Marw.

Volume One151

In the year 151 AH

Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm led the pilgrimage.

[Abū Yūsuf related to us: Abū Nuʿaym said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAwn died in the year 151].

Aḥmad said: Yaḥyā related to us, saying: Ibn ʿAwn died in the year 151, at its beginning. He was older than al-Tamīmī.

He said: I heard Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb say: Ibn ʿAwn died in the year 151.

He said: I heard Makkī ibn Ibrāhīm say: I sat with Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq, who used to dye his hair black. He mentioned reports concerning the divine attributes, and I recoiled from them, so I did not return to him.

[ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAmr related to us, saying: I heard Aḥmad ibn Khālid al-Wahbī say: Ibn Isḥāq died in the year 151].

[He said: I heard Sulaymān say: I remember Ibn ʿAwn’s death. I did not used to write down from Ḥammād reports of Ibn ʿAwn. I used to say, “He is a man whose death I witnessed.” He said: Then I wrote them down later].

In that year al-Mahdī arrived from al-Rayy, in Shawwāl.

In that year ʿAbd al-Wahhāb ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad led the summer campaign.

In that year Abū Jaʿfar renewed the oath of allegiance to himself, his son al-Mahdī, and—after al-Mahdī—to ʿĪsā ibn Mūsā, requiring it of his family in his presence at his assembly. This was on a Friday, when he granted them permission generally.2

[In that year Jaʿfar al-Ṣaghīr ibn Abī Jaʿfar died in Ṣafar at Madīnat al-Salām].

In that year Ḥumayd ibn Qaḥṭaba was appointed over Khurāsān. He arrived at his post on Saturday, two nights into Shaʿbān, and remained there until he died in the year 159.

Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm led the people on the pilgrimage.

Al-Ḥasan ibn Zayd was over Mecca and Medina.

In the year 152,

Abū Jaʿfar led the people on the pilgrimage.

Ḥaywa ibn Shurayḥ and Saʿīd ibn Asad related to us. They said: Ḍamra related to us, saying:

Ibrāhīm ibn Abī ʿAbla died in the year 152 or 153. Saʿīd said:

“In the year 152,” without expressing doubt.

Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd al-Ṣamad said: Hishām ibn (Abī) ʿAbd Allāh died in the year 152.

Yaḥyā said: “Fifty-odd.”

Zayd ibn al-Ḥubāb said: I visited Hishām al-Dastawāʾī in the year 153, and he died a few days afterward.

Saʿīd ibn Asad related to me, saying: Ḍamra related to us, saying: Ibrāhīm ibn [Abī] ʿAbla al-Qurashī died in the year 152.

I heard Zayd ibn al-Mubārak say: Maʿmar died in the year 152, in the month of Ramaḍān.

In that year Ṣāliḥ ibn ʿAlī, governor of Ḥimṣ and Qinnasrīn, died, and his son al-Faḍl ibn Ṣāliḥ succeeded him in his post.

[In that year Maʿn ibn Zāʾida al-Shaybānī was killed in Khurāsān].

In that year Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm led the summer campaign, but did not reach the enemy.3

In that year Abū Jaʿfar set out unexpectedly on pilgrimage and came to Kūfa. Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān—the governor of Kūfa—knew nothing of his arrival. This was in the month of Ramaḍān. Neither Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān nor ʿĪsā ibn Mūsā nor anyone else who was there knew of it.

Abū Jaʿfar led the people on the pilgrimage. Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm was over Mecca, and al-Ḥasan ibn Zayd was over Medina. Abū Jaʿfar distributed money, so that each person received one dirham.

In the year 153,

al-Mahdī Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib led the people on the pilgrimage.

He said: Ibn Bukayr said: Yūnus ibn Yazīd al-Aylī died in the year 150-odd.

After returning from the pilgrimage, Abū Jaʿfar went to al-Baṣra, where he built a palace and alighted at the Greater Bridge. He equipped an army at sea to fight the Sind.

In that year Abū Jaʿfar summoned the judges from Kūfa, al-Baṣra, and Madīnat al-Salām, concerning the grievance ʿĪsā ibn Mūsā had brought against him at Kaskar.

In that year Maʿyūf ibn Yaḥyā al-Jaḥḍarī led the summer campaign but did not reach the enemy.4

[In that year Mūsā ibn Sulaymān ibn ʿAlī died at Madīnat al-Salām].

In that year Khāzim ibn Khuzayma died, and Abū Jaʿfar performed the funeral prayer over him.

Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm was appointed over Mecca, and al-Ḥasan ibn Zayd over Medina.

In this year al-Mahdī made the pilgrimage to the Well of Ibn al-Murtafiʿ. He called out to the people of Mecca to come to him and stayed there for three days. The people of Mecca came to him, and he gave them a portion of an allotment.

A rock was shaken in this year, at the end of Dhū al-Ḥijja.

In the year 154,

Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-ʿAbbās led the people on the pilgrimage; he was governor of Kūfa.

Al-Ḥasan ibn Zayd was over Medina.

[Ṣafwān ibn Ṣāliḥ related to me, saying: I heard al-Walīd and more than one of our companions say: Ibn Jābir died in the year 154].

Abū Nuʿaym said: ʿAlī ibn Ṣāliḥ ibn Ḥayy died in the year 154, and [so did] Maʿmar in the year 154, aged fifty-eight.

[I heard ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm say: Ibn Jābir died in the year 154 …

and fifty.

I asked Hishām ibn ʿAmmār about Ibn Jābir’s age. He said: “He was an old man”].

Hishām related to us, saying: al-Walīd ibn Muslim related to us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd ibn Jābir, who said: Makḥūl and I would enter the mosque after the people had prayed. Makḥūl would give the call to prayer, pronounce the commencement, step forward, and lead them in prayer. I would come with Sulaymān ibn Mūsā after they had prayed; he would give the call to prayer and pronounce the commencement, then I would step forward and lead them in prayer with a ʿiqāl. He was older than Sulaymān.

[ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm related to me, saying: al-Walīd ibn Muslim related to us, from Ibn Jābir, who said: In the days of al-Walīd ibn ʿAbd al-Malik, I used to ride behind my father. Sulaymān ibn Yasār came to us, and he invited my father to the bathhouse and prepared a meal for him.

Ibn Jābir said: I was in charge of the allotments in the days of Hishām.

Ibn Jābir said: I led Sulaymān ibn Mūsā in prayer, and I was older than he].

It is also said that Jaʿfar ibn Burqān died in the year 154.

In that year Abū Jaʿfar set out for Jerusalem.

The House of Ziyād at ʿArafa collapsed on the eve of ʿArafa, with pilgrims inside, at the time the imam prayed.

In the year 155,

ʿAbd al-Ṣamad ibn ʿAlī led the people on the pilgrimage.

Ḥaywa ibn Shurayḥ related to me, saying: Ḍamra related to us, saying: ʿUthmān ibn ʿAṭāʾ died in the year 155.

Abū Nuʿaym said: Misʿar ibn Kidām ibn Ẓuhayr died in the year 155.

He said: I asked ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm about the death of Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh …

al-Shuʿaythī. He said: “He was from an earlier generation, lived on, and al-Awzāʿī narrated from him.”

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAmr related to me, saying: I asked Abū Sufyān ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Sinān al-Naṣrī about the death of Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Shaʿthī. He said: “I saw him and sat with him. He died a little after the year 154”.

In that year Yazīd ibn Ḥātim set out for Ifrīqiya and conquered it.

In that year Abū Jaʿfar dispatched his son al-Mahdī to build al-Rāfiqa.

That year Yazīd ibn Asad al-Sulamī led the summer campaign.

In that year al-Ḥasan ibn Zayd was dismissed from Medina, and ʿAbd al-Ṣamad ibn ʿAlī was appointed in his place.

Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-ʿAbbās was over Mecca.

Mecca was shaken by an earthquake that year, at night, at the end of Dhū al-Qaʿda.

In the year 156,

al-ʿAbbās ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-ʿAbbās led the people on the pilgrimage.

Ḥaywa ibn Shurayḥ related to me, saying: Ḍamra related to us, saying: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamla died in the year 156.

Abū Nuʿaym said: ʿUmar ibn Dharr died in the year 156.

Aḥmad said: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad related to us, saying: Ibn Abī ʿArūba died in the year 156.

He said: I heard ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Muʿādh say: Sawwār died in the year 156.

In that year Abū Jaʿfar married ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Qutham ibn al-ʿAbbās to Lubāba daughter of ʿAlī.

At that time Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm was amīr of Mecca and was at Madīnat al-Salām; his son Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad was his deputy.

ʿAbd al-Ṣamad ibn ʿAlī was over Medina.

In the year 157,

Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad led the people on the pilgrimage.

Al-ʿAbbās ibn al-Walīd ibn Mazyad al-ʿAdawī, from among the people of Beirut, related to me, saying: Al-Awzāʿī was born in the year Ṭuwāna was conquered, and he died in the year 157.

He said: Ibn Bukayr said: Qubāth ibn Razīn al-Lakhmī died in the year 157 or 158. Then I was informed that my book had been shown to Ibn Bukayr, and he said: “In the year 156 or 157.”

Saʿīd ibn Asad related to me, saying: Ḍamra related to us, saying: I heard al-Awzāʿī say: “I had reached puberty, or was close to reaching it, during the governorship of ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz.” Al-Awzāʿī died in the year 157.

He also said: Al-Awzāʿī was born in the year 88.

Al-ʿAbbās ibn al-Walīd ibn Mazyad related to me, saying: My father informed me: Al-Awzāʿī died on Sunday, when two nights remained of Ṣafar, in the year 157.

I heard ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm say: Al-Awzāʿī died in the year 157.

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAmr related to me, saying: Abū Mis-har related to us, saying: …

Hiql ibn Ziyād said: Al-Awzāʿī answered seventy thousand questions or thereabouts.

[In that year Abū Jaʿfar moved the markets from al-Madīna and Madīnat al-Sharqiyya to Bāb al-Karkh, Bāb al-Shaʿīr, and al-Miḥwal—the market known as al-Karkh—and ordered them built with his own funds, under the supervision of his client al-Rabīʿ.

In that year he widened the city’s roads and suburbs, setting their width at forty cubits, and ordered the houses that projected beyond that measure to be demolished].

[In that year Abū Jaʿfar built his palace known as al-Khuld.

In that year he constructed the bridge by Bāb al-Shaʿīr].

At that time Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm was amīr of Mecca.

Khalaf ibn ʿAbd Rabbih was in charge of his police.

ʿAbd al-Ṣamad ibn ʿAlī was over Medina.

In the year 158,

Ibrāhīm ibn Yaḥyā ibn Muḥammad led the people on the pilgrimage.

Salama related to us: Aḥmad said, from Isḥāq, from ʿĪsā, from Abū Maʿshar, who said: Abū Jaʿfar performed the pilgrimage in the year 158. He died one day before the Day of Tarwiya. His caliphate lasted twenty-two years less three days, and the people pledged allegiance to Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-ʿAbbās.

Ibn Bukayr said: [Ḥaywa ibn Shurayḥ al-Kindī, known by the kunyā Abū Zurʿa, died in the year 158].

I heard Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Tujībī say: Ḥaywa ibn Shurayḥ used to pass by us riding a bareback horse, leading another horse, as he went to water them.

He said: He had long, abundant hair and a thin beard. He said: I saw him and remember him clearly. He died in the year 158, when I was ten years old.

Ibn Bukayr said: I saw Ḥaywa ibn Shurayḥ on a horse; he was white-bearded and ruddy-complexioned. I heard nothing from him.

[I heard Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb say: I began seeking hadith in the year 158. I used to attend Shuʿba’s gatherings. When Shuʿba died, I sat with Ḥammād ibn Zayd and stayed with him until he died.

He said: I sat with him for nineteen years]. I sat with him in the year 160, and he died in the year 179.

I heard Abū Ayyūb Sulaymān ibn Salama al-Khabāʾirī al-Ḥimṣī say: Ṣafwān ibn ʿAmr died in the year 158.

[Ibrāhīm ibn al-Mundhir related to me, saying: Ibn Abī Fudayk related to me, saying: He died …

Ibn Abī Dhiʾb in the year 158].

[Ibrāhīm said: Ibn Abī Dhiʾb was born in the year 80, the year of the devastating flood].

Ibrāhīm said: Muḥammad ibn Fulayḥ said: My father was born in the year 73, and Mālik was three years older than my father. Mālik was born in the year 90. On this reckoning, Ibn Abī Dhiʾb was ten years older than Mālik.

In that year Abū Jaʿfar took up residence in his palace, in which he did not abide. He performed the pilgrimage that year and died at Biʾr Maymūn at dawn on Saturday, six nights into Dhū al-Ḥijja.

It is said that he died aged sixty-five.

At that time Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-ʿAbbās was amīr of Mecca.

At that time Yaḥyā ibn Maymūn al-Ḥadhdhāʾ was in charge of his police.

At that time ʿAbd al-Ṣamad was over Medina.

In the year 159,

Yazīd ibn Manṣūr, al-Mahdī’s maternal uncle, led the people on the pilgrimage.

Abū Nuʿaym said: Mālik ibn Mighwal died in the year 159, [and Ibn Abī Dhiʾb died in the year 159].

“In it, al-Mahdī built the mosque at al-Ruṣāfa.”

In it, Muḥammad b. ʿAbd Allāh al-Kathīrī was dismissed from the governorship of Medina, and ʿUbayd Allāh b. Muḥammad b. Ṣafwān al-Jumaḥī was appointed over it.

In it, al-Mahdī resolved to have the oath of allegiance given to his son Mūsā and to depose ʿĪsā b. Mūsā.

The emir of Mecca at that time was Muḥammad b. Ibrāhīm b. Muḥammad b. ʿAlī.

The people departed from the pilgrimage that year.

Muḥammad b. Ibrāhīm was dismissed, and al-Kathīrī was appointed over it.

In the year 160 AH

Al-Mahdī Muḥammad b. b. ʿAbd Allāh led the people on the pilgrimage.5

Abū al-Walīd Hishām b. ʿAbd al-Malik reported to us: He said, “Shuʿba died in the year 160 AH, at the beginning of the year.”

Abū al-Walīd said: “I heard Shuʿba say, ‘This ḥadīth distracts you from the remembrance of God, Mighty and Exalted, and from prayer. Will you then desist?’”

Abū Nuʿaym said: “Isrāʾīl b. Yūnus died in the year 160 AH.”

Ibn Bukayr said: “Ḥarmala b. ʿImrān b. Murrān al-Tujībī was born in the year 80 AH and died in Ṣafar of the year 160 AH. He was kunya-named Abū Ḥafṣ.”

Sulaymān b. Ḥarb said: “Al-Ḥasan b. Abī Jaʿfar died in the year 160 AH.”

On the day of al-Rūs.

“Al-Masʿūdī died in the year 160 AH.”

Aḥmad said: Yaḥyā said, “Shuʿba died at the age of seventy-five.”

Yaḥyā said: “Shuʿba was ten years older than Sufyān. Sufyān and Mālik b. Anas were close in age, and Ibn ʿUyayna was ten years younger than al-Thawrī.”

I heard Ibn Bukayr say: “Ḥarmala died in Ṣafar of the year 160 AH. I saw him and sat in his lap countless times.” I said, “Did he dye his hair?” He said:

“Yes.” I said, “To whom did he belong?” He said: “He was a client of Tujīb, kunya-named Abū Ḥafṣ.”

Ibn Bukayr said: “Ibn Shimāsa died after the year 100 AH, and Ḥarmala was born in the year 80 AH.”

I said to Ibn Bukayr, “Did he hear from Ibn Shimāsa?” He said, “I have no doubt.” I said to Ibn Bukayr, “Are you certain that Ḥarmala dyed his hair?” He said, “Yes.”

Abū al-Walīd said: “Shuʿba died in the year 162 AH.”

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. ʿAmr al-Dimashqī reported to us: He said, “Yazīd b. ʿAbd Rabbih told me, ‘I heard Ḥarmala’s descendants say, “Ḥarmala b. ʿImrān b. Qurrān.”’ They said:

“Qurrān was martyred during the conquest of the Maghrib in the year 60 AH.”

In the year 161 AH

Mūsā b. al-Mahdī, who was heir apparent, led the people on the pilgrimage.

Abū Nuʿaym said: “Al-Thawrī died in the year 161 AH.”

Saʿīd b. Asad told me: Ḍamra reported to us: “Rajāʾ b. Abī Salama died in either the year 161 or 162 AH.” Ḥammād b. Salama heard from Rajāʾ b. Abī Salama and said, “Rajāʾ is Abū al-Miqdām”; Ibn ʿAwn also transmitted from him.

Aḥmad said: “Abū al-Muhājir al-Raqqī died in the year 161 AH.”

Aḥmad b. al-Khalīl said: Yaḥyā b. Ayyūb told me: “I heard Wakīʿ say, ‘Sufyān was born in the year 77 AH, so it seems he lived for sixty-four years.’”

In it, al-Mahdī completed the maqsūra of the City of the Messenger.

In it, al-Muqannaʿ appeared in Khurāsān.

In it, al-Mahdī ordered an enlargement of the Sacred Mosque, the Mosque of the Messenger ﷺ, and the Congregational Mosque at Baṣra; they were enlarged and raised.

Jaʿfar b. Sulaymān was over Mecca and Medina.

In the year 162 AH

Ibrāhīm b. Jaʿfar b. Abī Jaʿfar ʿAbd Allāh al-Manṣūr led the people on the pilgrimage.

Ibn Bukayr said: “Saʿīd b. Miqlāṣ—Miqlāṣ was kunya-named Abū Ayyūb—al-Khuzāʿī was born in the year 100 AH and died in either the year 161 or 162 AH. He was kunya-named Abū Yaḥyā.”

Ibrāhīm b. Nashīṭ died in either the year 161 or 162 AH.

ʿAlī b. al-Madīnī said: “Hammām b. Yaḥyā al-ʿAwḏī died in the year 162 AH.”

Yazīd b. Ibrāhīm al-Tustarī said: Abū ʿAmr al-Ḍarīr reported to us from Abū ʿAwāna, who said: “I visited Hammām,” and he related an account.

Abū Yūsuf said: “The Qurʾān-reciter used to say, ‘Saʿīd b. Abī Ayyūb, the client of Abū Hurayra, reported to us.’ I heard ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz b. ʿImrān, who was the grandson of Saʿīd b. Abī Ayyūb, object to this, saying, ‘He was only a client of Khuzāʿa.’ He showed me books and documents belonging to his forefathers, in all of which they traced their lineage to Khuzāʿa.”

In it, Thumāma b. al-Walīd al-ʿAbsī led the summer expedition; then he was dismissed, and al-Ḥasan b. Qaḥṭaba took his place. He campaigned in Byzantine lands, burning and laying waste, and captured a fortress.

Jaʿfar b. Sulaymān was over Mecca; Jaʿfar was in Medina, and his deputy over Mecca was Saʿīd b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Jumaḥī.

Al-Faḍl told me: “I heard Abū ʿAbd Allāh say, ‘Sharīk was born in the year 95 AH, and Abū Bakr b. ʿAyyāsh was born in the year 96 AH,’ while Sufyān was born in the year 97 AH.”

In the year 163 AH

ʿAlī b. al-Mahdī conducted the pilgrimage for the people.

Al-Mahdī came to Bayt al-Maqdis and prayed there.

Ibn Bukayr said: “Mūsā b. ʿAlī b. Rabāḥ b. Quṣayr al-Lakhmī was born in the Maghrib in the year 89 AH and died in Alexandria in the year 163 AH. He was kunya-named Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān.”

Ibn Bukayr said: “ʿAbd al-Aʿlā b. Saʿīd al-Jayshānī was born in the year 100 AH and died in the year 163 AH.”

Ibn Bukayr said: “I saw Ḥumayd, the companion of Ibn Lahīʿa. He was killed in the year 163 AH.”

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. ʿAmr al-Dimashqī told me: Sulaymān al-Bahrānī told me: “I heard Yaḥyā b. Ṣāliḥ say, ‘Shuʿayb, Ḥurayz, and Abū Mahdī died in the year 163 AH.’” Yaḥyā b. Ayyūb al-Miṣrī died in the year 163 AH; his kunya was Abū al-ʿAbbās.

One of the family of Abū Maryam told me: Yaḥyā b. Ayyūb said, “I went out to a funeral in Mecca with Ibn Jurayj on a day of intense heat. Ibn Jurayj said:

‘The ḥadīth has enslaved you, Abū al-ʿAbbās.’”

Jaʿfar b. Sulaymān was over Mecca and Medina.

Muʿādh b. Muslim was dismissed from Khurāsān, and al-Musayyab b. Zuhayr was appointed in his place. He arrived— Al-Musayyab arrived at his post in Jumādā I of the year 163 AH.

In the year 164 AH

Ṣāliḥ al-Faqīr b. ʿAbd Allāh b. Muḥammad al-Manṣūr led the people on the pilgrimage.

Abū ʿUtba al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī b. Muslim al-Sakūnī al-Ḥimṣī told me in the cloth market: “I raided Jabala in the year 164 AH, and Arṭāʾa—I mean Ibn al-Mundhir—had died a year before that.”

Al-Aḥmūsī ʿUmar died in the year 164 AH.

Al-ʿAbbās b. al-Walīd b. Ṣubḥ told me: “Yaḥyā b. Ṣāliḥ reported to us: ʿUfayr b. Maʿdān reported to us: ‘ʿUmar b. Mūsā came to us in Ḥimṣ, and we gathered around him in the mosque. He kept saying, “Your righteous shaykh reported to us; your righteous shaykh reported to us.” When he had repeated this many times, I said to him, “Who is our righteous shaykh? Name him for us so that we may know him.” He replied, “Khālid b. Maʿdān.” I said, “In what year did you meet him?” He said, “I met him in the year 108 AH.” I said, “And where did you meet him?” He said, “I met him on the campaign to Armenia.”

“‘I said to him, “Fear God, Mighty and Exalted, shaykh; do not lie. Khālid b. Maʿdān died in the year 104 AH, yet you claim that you met him four years after his death. And I will add one more thing: he did not campaign in Armenia.”’” He used to campaign against the Byzantines!!

Jaʿfar b. Sulaymān was over Mecca and Medina, and that year his deputy over Mecca was ʿUthmān b. Khālid al-Taymī.

Jaʿfar b. Sulaymān was dismissed.

In the year 165 AH

Ṣāliḥ al-Faqīr b. ʿAbd Allāh b. Muḥammad led the people on the pilgrimage.

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. ʿAmr told me: “Ibrāhīm b. ʿAbd Allāh b. al-ʿAlāʾ told me: ‘My father, ʿAbd Allāh b. al-ʿAlāʾ b. Zabr, was born in the year 75 AH and died in [the year] 165 AH.’” Saʿīd b. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz led the funeral prayer for him.

“I asked ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Ibrāhīm about ʿAbd Allāh b. al-ʿAlāʾ, and he said, ‘He was trustworthy.’” Abū Mushir transmitted from him. He said: “I heard Ibn ʿĀmir say, ‘Ibn Thawbān was among the class of notables.’ I said to him, ‘Ibn al-Mubārak did not transmit from him.’ He replied, ‘Ibn al-Mubārak only transmitted from leading figures among our shaykhs, and ʿAbd Allāh b. al-ʿAlāʾ was one of the notables of the town.’”

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. ʿAmr told me: Muʿāwiya b. Abī ʿUbayd Allāh told me: Abū Mushir reported to us: “We were with Saʿīd b. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz and Ibn Zabr when news of Ibn Thawbān’s death was brought to us, and Saʿīd b. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz said, ‘Indeed, we belong to God, and to Him we return.’”

The emir over Mecca at that time was ʿUbayd Allāh b. Qutham.

[In it,] Hārūn married Umm Jaʿfar Zubayda.

In it, Hārūn sent his son on a campaign to Byzantine lands. Hārūn was heir apparent, and he penetrated deep into Byzantine territory until he reached the gulf on which Constantinople stands. The ruler of the Byzantines at that time was a woman, Alyūn, and Hārūn made a truce with her after the Muslims had endured great hardship and intense fear.

In the year 166 AH

Muḥammad b. Ibrāhīm b. Muḥammad b. ʿAlī led the people on the pilgrimage.

I heard Yaḥyā b. ʿAbd Allāh b. Bukayr say: “Abū Shurayḥ ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Shurayḥ al-Maʿāfirī died in the year 166 or 167 AH.”

In it, al-Mahdī secured the oath of allegiance for Hārūn as heir apparent after Mūsā.

In it, al-Mahdī released ʿAbd al-Ṣamad b. ʿAlī.

In it, al-Mahdī moved to ʿĪsābādh and settled there.

In it, al-Mahdī performed the ʿumra of the month of Ramaḍān.

Aḥmad b. Ismāʿīl was emir of Mecca.

In it, al-Faḍl b. Sulaymān was appointed over Khurāsān. He arrived to take up his post with five days remaining in Rabīʿ I. Al-Musayyab b. Zuhayr was dismissed, and al-Faḍl remained in office until the year 170 AH.

In the year 167 AH

Ibrāhīm b. Yaḥyā b. Muḥammad, governor of Mosul, led the people on the pilgrimage. He had been governor over Medina.

I heard Sulaymān b. Ḥarb say: “Abū Hilāl al-Rāsibī died in the year 167—”

—AH, and Ibn al-Mubārak attended his death during his second arrival in Baṣra.

Ṣafwān b. Ṣāliḥ told me: “I heard al-Walīd and others say, ‘Saʿīd b. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz al-Tanūkhī died in the year 167 AH.’”

Abū Nuʿaym said: “Qays b. al-Rabīʿ, Ḥasan b. Ṣāliḥ, and Jaʿfar al-Aḥmar died in the year 167 AH.”

I heard Abū Umayya al-Fāriḍ say, in Sulaymān b. Ḥarb’s gathering in Mecca: “Ḥammād b. Salama died in the year 167 AH.”

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. ʿAmr told me: Abū Mushir reported to us: “I sat with Saʿīd b. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz al-Tanūkhī for twelve years. He died in the year 167 AH.”

I heard Abū al-Nuʿmān say: “Abū Hilāl Muḥammad b. Sulaym was a client of Banū Salima, but he used to reside among Banū Rāsib.”

In it, ʿĪsā b. Mūsā died in Kūfa. Rawḥ b. Ḥātim, its governor, had people witness his death, and Rawḥ led the funeral prayer for him. On the day he died, he was sixty-five years old.

I heard Abū ʿAlī al-Shāfiʿī say: “Muḥammad b. Dāwūd b. ʿĪsā said to us, ‘Tonight I have reached the age of seventy, and none of my forefathers reached it.’”

In it, Ibrāhīm b. Yaḥyā died in Medina, where he was governor. A son of ʿAbd al-Ṣamad b. ʿAlī led the funeral prayer for him. He had arrived in Medina while passing through, and happened to be there, so he led the prayer for him his death having occurred at the time of his departure from the pilgrimage season.

In it, al-Mahdī set out for Ṭabaristān.

In this year, the part of the Sacred Mosque facing the valley was demolished. Al-Mahdī ordered the purchase of the houses beyond the valley, and made a road for the people. He incorporated into the Sacred Mosque the road and the valley, which had served as a road and a channel for floodwater. Yaqṭīn b. Mūsā and Ibrāhīm b. Ṣāliḥ undertook its demolition and rebuilding by al-Mahdī’s order. I heard the owners of those houses say: “For every cubit, we were compensated with a cubit elsewhere, and we were paid one hundred dinars for every cubit.”

In this year, al-Mahdī ordered an enlargement of the Mosque of the Messenger on the side facing the valley. Aḥmad b. Ismāʿīl was governor of Mecca.

Ibrāhīm b. Yaḥyā died after returning from Mecca.

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. ʿAmr reported to us: Abū Mushir reported to us: Saʿīd b. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz said, “Al-Zuhrī led us in prayer while he was staying at al-Rāhib, on a Ḥīrī carpet.”

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. ʿAmr reported to us: Abū Mushir reported to us: Saʿīd reported to us, saying:

“We were confused about the brisk walking, so we asked ʿAṭāʾ b. Abī Rabāḥ. He said, ‘There is nothing incumbent upon you.’”

Abū Mushir said to us: “Saʿīd b. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz heard nothing from ʿAṭāʾ apart from this question.”

In the year 168 AH

ʿAlī b. Muḥammad b. al-Mahdī led the people on the pilgrimage.

I heard Yaḥyā b. ʿAbd Allāh b. Bukayr al-Makhzūmī say: “Ghawth b. Sulaymān b. Ziyād al-Ḥaḍramī died in the year 168 AH.”

Ibn Bukayr said: “Nāfiʿ b. Yazīd al-Qaysī, the client of Umm al-ʿAynāʾ, died. He was a client—”

…for Qays, in the year 168.

[I heard Sulaymān ibn Salamah al-Ḥimṣī al-Khabāʾirī say: “Ḥurayz died in the year 168.”]

In that year, Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz died.

I heard Abū Saʿīd ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm say: “Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz died in the year 167.”

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAmr related to us: Abū Mushir related to us: “I sat with Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Abī Yaḥyā al-Tanūkhī for twelve years. He died in the year 167.”

In that year, the Bedouin Arabs of the Basra desert rebelled, abandoning prayer, waylaying travelers, and violating sacred prohibitions.

In that year, Egypt revolted because of Mūsā ibn Muṣʿab’s harsh treatment of its people; he imposed the land tax on pack animals and livestock.

In that year, al-Mahdī set out for Mā Sabadhān.

Aḥmad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAlī was governor of Mecca.

His chief of police was Muḥammad ibn Jubayr ibn Wahb al-Jumaḥī.

Isḥāq ibn ʿĪsā was governor of Medina.

In the year 169,

Sulaymān ibn ʿAbd Allāh Abū Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad led the people on the pilgrimage.

Salamah related to us: Aḥmad reported from Isḥāq ibn ʿĪsā, from Abū Maʿshar, who said: “Al-Mahdī, Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās, died at Mā Sabadhān on Thursday night, eight nights remaining in Muḥarram. His caliphate lasted ten years and forty-five days and nights. His son Hārūn was with him and led the funeral prayer over him. He took the oath of allegiance from those present for his brother Mūsā, and then for himself after him. He departed in the year 169.” Then Mūsā ibn Muḥammad was installed as caliph in the year 169.

In that year, Ḥasan and Ḥusayn were killed at Fakhkh.

I asked Hishām ibn ʿAmmār about the death of Saʿīd ibn Bashīr. He said: “In the year 169.”

Hishām related to us: “I heard a session of Saʿīd ibn Bashīr’s with our companions, but I did not write it down.” Hishām said: “I saw Bukayr ibn Maʿrūf and heard a great deal from him, but I did not write down anything from him. He used to dye his hair yellow. He said: ‘He wrote to Ibn Lahīʿah and to Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā’—meaning Abū Mushir—‘and to a third person he mentioned, [sending] one hundred and two ḥadīths.’ He said:

“‘After that, I made two further visits.’”

Abū Yūsuf said: “Hishām meant to mislead me.” I said to Hishām: “But al-Layth and Ibn Lahīʿah had died?” He said: “Yes.”

He—that is, al-Mahdī—came to the people of Mecca on Saturday, seven nights remaining in Ṣafar, in the year 169.

The people of Mecca pledged allegiance to Mūsā and Hārūn after Mūsā.

The governor of Mecca at that time was [Aḥmad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAlī.

Then Aḥmad was dismissed and ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Qutham was appointed. He entered Mecca in the year 169, in Jumādā II of that year.

Al-Awqaṣ, the judge of Mecca, died. I heard the shaykhs of Mecca say:

“No one governed Mecca like al-Awqaṣ and Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb.”

Al-Awqaṣ died in Jumādā I, and Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sufyānī, of Banū Makhzūm, succeeded him.

Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī ibn Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib rose in Medina on Saturday morning, the sixteenth of Dhū al-Qaʿdah. The ʿAbbāsids went out against him with Sulaymān ibn Abī Jaʿfar until they met him at Fakhkh. They left ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Qutham in charge of Mecca. They killed Ḥusayn, along with a number of his family, at Fakhkh in the valley of Mecca on Saturday, the Day of Tarwiyah. Twenty-one days passed between his uprising and his killing. Also killed with him that day was Jubayr ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sulaymān ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jubayr al-Nawfalī. Among those killed was al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad: Mūsā ibn ʿĪsā ordered his execution, and he was killed in captivity. Yaḥyā and Idrīs, the sons of ʿAbd Allāh, got away. Idrīs made it to the Maghrib and remained there until he died, leaving a son called Idrīs. As for Yaḥyā, he came to Fārs and passed through Fasā, where he settled during the governorship of ʿAmmār ibn ʿAlī over Fasā.

I heard Ḥammād ibn Ḥafṣ say: “The reason Yaḥyā left Fasā and fled to the mountains was that a retainer of ʿAdawiyyah ibn ʿAlī came to him and said, ‘The amīr’s brother, ʿAdawiyyah, is summoning you.’ He treated his words dismissively and said, ‘Who is ʿAdawiyyah?’ The messenger rebuked him, and it seems he took [that] very seriously. This was the reason he left Fasā and fled to the mountains. He reached the mountains of Daylam—and his story is a long one. A non-Arab protected him and gave him shelter, until Hārūn sent Abū al-Bakhtarī the judge to him. The non-Arab refused [to hand him over] until Hārūn gave him the strongest possible guarantee of safety, and then he brought Yaḥyā to Hārūn.”

Shihāb ibn ʿAbbād al-Qaysī related to me: Sufyān related to us, from Mujālid, from al-Shaʿbī, who said: “ʿAlī said, ‘Who will charge these people’—meaning the people of Kūfah? Someone said:

“‘He charged with the most futile arrow.’”6

Shihāb said: “Sufyān related this to us fifty-one years after al-Ḥusayn was killed at Fakhkh.” Shihāb related this to me in the year 221.

Sulaymān ibn Abī Jaʿfar had been appointed governor of Mecca and set out for his post. A number of his family members went with him, among them al-ʿAbbās ibn Muḥammad, ʿĪsā ibn Mūsā, Ismāʿīl ibn ʿĪsā, and Muḥammad and Jaʿfar, the sons of Sulaymān. A number of retainers went with them as well. When news of the young Ḥusayn’s affair reached them, they gathered and chose Sulaymān ibn Abī Jaʿfar to lead them, until they met him. What transpired was what transpired, both for him and for them.

In this year, the tyrant of the Byzantines marched out and demolished the city of al-Ḥadath.

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Qutham was governor of Mecca.

His chief of police was ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Saʿīd ibn Ḥassān al-Makhzūmī.

“is summoning you.” He made light of his words and said, “Who is ʿAdawiyyah?” The messenger rebuked him, and it seems he took [that] very seriously. This was the reason he left Fasā and fled to the mountains. He reached the mountains of Daylam—and his story is a long one. A non-Arab protected him and gave him shelter, until Hārūn sent Abū al-Bakhtarī the judge to him. The non-Arab refused [to hand him over] until Hārūn gave him the strongest possible guarantee of safety, and then he brought Yaḥyā to Hārūn.

Shihāb ibn ʿAbbād al-Qaysī related to me: Sufyān related to us, from Mujālid, from al-Shaʿbī, who said: “ʿAlī said, ‘Who will charge these people’—meaning the people of Kūfah? Someone said:

“‘He charged with the most futile arrow.’”7

Shihāb said: “Sufyān related this to us fifty-one years after al-Ḥusayn was killed at Fakhkh.” Shihāb related this to me in the year 221. Sulaymān ibn Abī Jaʿfar had been appointed governor of Mecca and set out for his post. A number of his family members went with him, among them al-ʿAbbās ibn Muḥammad, ʿĪsā ibn Mūsā, Ismāʿīl ibn ʿĪsā, and Muḥammad and Jaʿfar, the sons of Sulaymān. A number of retainers went with them as well. When news of the young Ḥusayn’s affair reached them, they gathered and chose Sulaymān ibn Abī Jaʿfar to lead them, until they met him. What transpired was what transpired, both for him and for them.

In this year, the tyrant of the Byzantines marched out and demolished the city of al-Ḥadath.

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Qutham was governor of Mecca.

His chief of police was ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Saʿīd ibn Ḥassān al-Makhzūmī.

Al-ʿUmarī was governor of Medina.

In the year 170,

Hārūn led the people on the pilgrimage.

Salamah related to us: Aḥmad reported from Isḥāq ibn ʿĪsā, from Abū Maʿshar: “Mūsā ibn Muḥammad died in the year 170, and Hārūn succeeded him.”

Aḥmad said: “I have been told that Mūsā’s caliphate lasted one year and four months. Hārūn was installed as caliph in Rabīʿ II of the year 170.”

The historians said that his caliphate lasted one year, one month, and some days.

Ibn Bukayr said: “ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAyyāsh ibn ʿAbbās al-Qitbānī died in the year 170.”

Hārūn was installed as caliph; Isḥāq ibn Sulaymān was appointed, and al-ʿUmarī was dismissed.

In that year, al-Maʾmūn was born on Friday night, on the fifteenth of Rabīʿ I, the night Mūsā died.

In that year, Muḥammad ibn Hārūn was born on Friday, when sixteen nights of Shawwāl had passed.

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Qutham governed Mecca.

ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar al-Rukānī was his chief of police.

Then ʿUbayd Allāh was dismissed, and Mūsā ibn ʿĪsā was appointed over Mecca and Yemen.

Hārūn returned, following Mūsā ibn ʿĪsā.

In that year, Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad al-Khuzāʿī arrived in Khurāsān as governor, succeeding al-Faḍl ibn Sulaymān. He arrived on Thursday, when one night of Dhū al-Qaʿdah had passed, in the year 170.

In the year 171,

ʿAbd al-Ṣamad ibn ʿAlī led the people on the pilgrimage.

He sent those of the family of Abū Ṭālib who were in the city of Madīnat al-Salām to Medina, to reside there.

In that year, Mūsā ibn ʿĪsā was dismissed in Ṣafar. ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Qutham was appointed governor of Mecca; he had been at al-Ṭāʾif.

In that year, al-Khayzurān, Hārūn’s mother, performed the lesser pilgrimage in Ramaḍān and remained in the vicinity until she performed the pilgrimage.

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Qutham governed Mecca.

Isḥāq ibn Sulaymān governed Medina.

In the year 172,

Sulaymān ibn Abī Jaʿfar led the people on the pilgrimage. It has also been said that it was rather Yaʿqūb ibn Abī Jaʿfar who performed the pilgrimage.

In that year, Isḥāq ibn Sulaymān was dismissed from Medina, and ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Ṣāliḥ was appointed.

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Qutham governed Mecca.

In that year, Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad al-Khuzāʿī, governor of Khurāsān, arrived from Marw at Balkh on campaign in Dhū al-Qaʿdah of the year 172. His son al-ʿAbbās ibn Jaʿfar set out for Kābul and entered it. His deputy in Marw was Shuʿayb ibn Ḥāzim.

I asked Ibn Bukayr about ʿUqbah ibn Nāfiʿ, Nājiyah ibn Bakr, and ʿUthmān ibn al-Ḥakam. He said: “There is no fault in them; they are people of piety. ʿUthmān is Judhāmī and the best of them, then ʿUqbah, “then Nājiyah.” I said: “Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr al-Nāfiʿī?” He said: “He is Egyptian; there is no fault in him.”

He said: “I asked him, ‘Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allāh?’ He said: ‘Excellent! He is Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Saʿd. I have not mentioned anyone like him today. He was the best and most knowledgeable of them, and was of the same generation as Ibn Wahb. He died in the year 173.’”

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Qutham was dismissed, and Sulaymān ibn Jaʿfar was appointed.

In the year 173,

Hārūn ibn Muḥammad al-Rashīd led the people on the pilgrimage. It was the year in which he distributed a dirham apiece to everyone, young and old.

Sulaymān ibn Jaʿfar governed Mecca, and ʿAbd al-Karīm ibn Shuʿayb al-Ḥajabī was his chief of police. According to what some of the shaykhs of Mecca told me, Ibn Shuʿayb lived on the outskirts of Mecca. He had a Bedouin manner and regularly attended the mosque. Sulaymān ibn Jaʿfar saw him and admired his bearing. He wanted him to take office and serve as his chief of police, but Ibn Shuʿayb refused. Sulaymān said: “We will pay you fifteen dinars each month, and you may choose: if you find the work to your liking, you may stay; otherwise, you may resign.” Ibn Shuʿayb accepted, and Sulaymān appointed him chief of police.

There was an official in charge of Mecca’s market. Sulaymān referred legal disputes to the market official and marriage arrangements to Ibn Shuʿayb. Ibn Shuʿayb would perform several marriages in a day. It was also the practice among the people of Mecca that an elder would arrange the marriage of his daughter or sister in the ruler’s presence. He said: “After some days, Sulaymān came to him and asked, ‘Ibn Shuʿayb, how do you find your position?’ He said, ‘Good and pleasant. I am paid fifteen dinars, and all we do is arrange marriages.’”

He said: “When half a year or so had passed, those women whose marriages he had arranged began coming to him and saying, ‘Either resolve the problem of maintenance and clothing, or divorce me.’ This was the practice of the people of Mecca: they all agreed that a man unable to provide for his family must either resolve the problem of maintenance or divorce his wife. He used to rule among them accordingly. When the pilgrimage season ended, he asked to be released from his post. Sulaymān said to him:

“‘What made you decide that?’ He said, ‘For six months I arrange marriages, and for six months I break them up. I have no need for this.’”

When they brought him a suspicious or dissolute person—they claimed—he would say: “Woe to you!

“What business have you with these people? You should keep an eye on the Iraqis; search out their faults and look into their affairs.” He later became judge of Mecca. I said to this shaykh: “So this is how he became judge, while he was urging people to search out others’ faults!” He said: “I’ll explain. A pilgrim from Iraq had arrived. One of the pilgrims, a man who traded during the pilgrimage season and came for both trade and pilgrimage, had rented a place. Ibn Shuʿayb heard a suspicious report about him, raised an accusation against him, and nearly exposed him. Something unpleasant happened between them. When the pilgrim was about to depart, a woman from his neighborhood came to him and spent the night at his lodging.”

Abū Yūsuf said: “They claimed she was his sister. As he was about to leave, he got her drunk and stripped her, then left her in the house and locked her inside with a padlock. He took the padlock to Ibn Shuʿayb and said: ‘I left behind in the house where I was staying some provisions and supplies that we had left over, as well as a great deal of clothing that we had put away and left there. You may seek God’s reward by distributing them to needy neighbors and others.’” He said: “Ibn Shuʿayb went and opened the padlock. There was a naked woman left behind in the house. This was why he used to say: ‘Search out the misdeeds of those debauched people who come here and corrupt our household servants and enslaved women,’ and the like.”

In the year 174,

Hārūn led the people on the pilgrimage.

Muḥammad ibn Rumḥ al-Tujībī said: “Bakr ibn Muḍar died in Dhū al-Ḥijjah, on the Day of ʿArafah, in the year 174.”

He said: “I saw al-Layth ibn Saʿd sitting by his grave while he was being buried, and tears streamed down his beard.”

Muḥammad said: “ʿAbd Allāh ibn Lahīʿah ibn ʿAṭiyyah al-Ḥaḍramī died in the year 174…”

“…and ninety.”

Ibn Bukayr said: “ʿAbd Allāh ibn Lahīʿah al-Ḥaḍramī was born in the year 96 and died when six nights remained in Jumādā II, in the year 174. Dāwūd ibn Mazīd ibn Ḥātim performed the funeral prayer over him. Ibn Lahīʿah’s teknonym was Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān.”

Ibn Bukayr said: “Bakr ibn Muḍar ibn Muḥammad ibn Ḥakīm ibn Salmān was born in the year 103 and died in the year 174.” Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Muḥammad al-Bazzāz al-Ḥarrānī related this to me.

He said: “I performed the pilgrimage in the year 173, and I was already grown.”

[He said: “I heard Muḥammad ibn al-Muthannā say: ‘Sallām ibn Abī Muṭīʿ, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī al-Zinād, ʿAmr ibn Thābit, and Dāwūd al-ʿAṭṭār died in the year 174.’”]

I heard Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad al-Shāfiʿī say: “I heard Dāwūd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān say: ‘I was born in the blessed year, the year of ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz’s caliphate.’”

[Aḥmad ibn al-Khalīl related to us: Yaḥyā ibn Ayyūb related to me: “Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Jumaḥī died in the year 174. He held office for seventeen years.”] He had been their judge when he was appointed.

Sulaymān ibn Jaʿfar was governor of Mecca. He was dismissed, and Mūsā ibn ʿĪsā was appointed in his place. The judge Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sufyānī used to lead the people in prayer, until Mūsā ibn ʿĪsā ibn Mūsā sent his son, al-Athram Ibrāhīm ibn Mūsā ibn ʿĪsā, as governor of Mecca. He entered the city in Ramaḍān.

An epidemic broke out in Mecca. The Commander of the Faithful, Hārūn, set out on pilgrimage. When news of the epidemic reached him, he slowed his journey until he entered Mecca on the Day of Tarwiyah. He performed the circumambulation and the saʿy, then went straight to Minā and did not leave Mecca.

In the year 175,

Hārūn led the pilgrimage.

Muḥammad ibn Rumḥ al-Tujībī said: “Al-Layth ibn Saʿd died in the year 175, on the middle day of Shaʿbān.”

[Ibn Bukayr said: “Al-Layth ibn Saʿd al-Fahmī was born in the year 94 and died on the middle day of Shaʿbān [a Friday], in the year 175. Mūsā ibn ʿĪsā al-Hāshimī performed the funeral prayer over him, and he was buried after the Friday prayer. His teknonym was Abū al-Ḥārith.”]

[Ibn Bukayr said: “Al-Layth ibn Saʿd performed the pilgrimage in the year 113 and heard from Ibn Shihāb in Mecca. In that year, he heard from Ibn Abī Mulaykah, ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ, Abū al-Zubayr, Nāfiʿ, ʿImrān ibn Abī Anas, and a number of shaykhs.”]

Ibn Bukayr said: “Ḥubaysh ibn Saʿīd related to me from al-Layth ibn Saʿd, who said:

“‘I went to Abū al-Zubayr, and he brought out books for us. I asked, “Did you hear this from Jābir?” He said, “And from others.” I asked, “Did you hear this from Jābir?” and he brought this sheet out to me.’”

Ibn Bukayr said: “Al-Layth said: ‘I went to Nāfiʿ, and he asked me [where I was from]. I said, “I am a man from Egypt.” He said, “From which [people]?” I said, “From Qays.”’

Ibn Rifāʿah said: ‘Or a man from his people.’ Al-Layth said: ‘A man recited to…’”

Nāfiʿ: “Like the one about whom you published a story concerning his father.” He said: “He means the one who drinks from a silver vessel.”

[Ibn Bukayr said: Someone who heard al-Layth told me that he used to say: “I wrote down much knowledge from Ibn Shihāb, and I considered riding the post to him at al-Ruṣāfah. But I feared that doing so might not be for God, Mighty and Exalted, so I gave it up.”]

Ibn Bukayr said: Shuʿayb ibn al-Layth told me, from his father al-Layth, who said: He used to say to us: “One of my family told me: ‘You were born in the year 92,’ but the year I am certain of is 94.”

I asked Muḥammad ibn Ḥumayd: “When did Tamīm ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān die?” He said: “In the year 75.”

[Ibn Bukayr said: I often heard al-Layth ibn Saʿd say: “I am older than Ibn Lahīʿah—so praise be to God, who has granted us the use of our reason.”

Ibn Bukayr said: Shuʿayb ibn al-Layth told me, from his father, who said: “When I took my leave of Abū Jaʿfar at Bayt al-Maqdis, he said: ‘I was impressed by the soundness of your judgment, and praise be to God, who has placed someone like you among my subjects.’

Shuʿayb said: He used to say: ‘Do not tell anyone this while I am alive.’”]

In the year 176

Sulaymān ibn Abī Jaʿfar led the people on the pilgrimage.

[Abū ʿAwānah died in the year 176.]

In that year al-Faḍl ibn Yaḥyā was appointed governor of al-Jibāl, and he corresponded with Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-ʿAlawī. The non-Arab of al-Jibāl had accepted him under a guarantee of safe conduct, on the condition that he would neither betray him nor surrender him, and he kept his word. Hārūn sent Abū al-Bakhtarī to the non-Arab, who said: “You claim that he is the son of your Prophet. Is he truthful?” He replied: “Yes.” The man said: “Then I could not betray him.”

Hārūn was displeased with Abū al-Bakhtarī and said: “Commander of the Faithful, would it have been permissible for me to say anything other than what I said?” Then Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbd Allāh inclined toward making peace and requested a guarantee of safe conduct for himself and for a number of people whose names were not specified. He named the number, but it was not disclosed.

In the year 177

Hārūn led the people on the pilgrimage.

ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn Ziyād died in the year 77.

Al-Faḍl related to us, from Aḥmad, who said: “Sharīk died in the year 77 AH, and he was born in the year 95.”

Aḥmad said: “I think Sallām ibn Abī Muṭīʿ died in the year 77.”

He said: “I heard him say: ‘Sharīk was two years older than Sufyān. Sharīk was born in the year 95, and Sufyān in the year 96.’”

Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm was dismissed from Mecca and Medina. ʿAlī ibn ʿĪsā ibn Mūsā was appointed over Medina, and ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Qutham was appointed over Mecca.

ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Ṣāliḥ was dismissed from command of the summer expedition.

Hārūn, Commander of the Faithful, led the people on the pilgrimage. ʿAlī ibn ʿĪsā was in charge of Medina, and ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Qutham was in charge of Mecca.

Al-Ghuṭrīf was dismissed from Khurāsān.

The deputy of Dāwūd ibn Yazīd departed, and Ḥamzah ibn Mālik arrived on Saturday, the sixth of Muḥarram in the year 177 AH, as deputy for al-Faḍl ibn Yaḥyā ibn Barmak over Khurāsān and Sijistān.

In that year the people of Dahlak revolted against the Muslims. A battle took place between them at Dahlak, on the day of ʿĀqil, Wednesday, thirteen days into Ṣafar in the year 177 AH. They killed the governor and most of the Muslims there, except those who fled, and they destroyed the mosques.

In the year 178 AH

Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm led the people on the pilgrimage.

Jaʿfar ibn Sulaymān al-Ḍubaʿī died in that year. He was reliable, precise, and excellent in receiving and transmitting traditions, except that his home was near those of Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, the sons of ʿAlī ibn al-Muqaddamī.

In that year ʿAlī ibn ʿĪsā was dismissed from Medina, and ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Qutham from Mecca.

Muḥammad was appointed over Mecca and took up residence there.

He sent his son al-ʿAbbās to govern Medina. Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm led the people on the pilgrimage; at that time he was governor of Mecca, Medina, and Yemen, and ʿAbbād al-Sahmī was chief of his police.

In the year 179 AH

Hārūn led the people on the pilgrimage.

[Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb said: “I kept the company of Ḥammād ibn Zayd for nineteen years. I began keeping his company in the year 160 AH, and he died in the year 179 AH.

Sulaymān said: “I began seeking traditions in the year 158 AH. I used to go to Shuʿbah, who died in the year 160 AH, and I devoted myself to Ḥammād after Shuʿbah’s death.

Sulaymān said: “When Ṣafar begins, I will have completed seventy-seven years of age. That will be in Dhū al-Ḥijjah of the year 216 AH.”]

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb said: “I did not see Abū al-Rabīʿ with Ḥammād ibn Zayd.”

Sulaymān said: “The wicked man spoke truly”—meaning Abū al-Rabīʿ—“when he said, ‘I did not see Sulaymān with Ḥammād.’”

Ibn Bukayr said: Mālik ibn Anas died in the year 179 AH.

[In that year Ḥammād ibn Zayd died.] Mālik died at the age of eighty-four.

[Khālid al-Wāsiṭī died in that year.] So did Abū al-Aḥwaṣ Sallām ibn Sulaym.

Ibrāhīm ibn al-Mundhir related to us: Muḥammad ibn Fulayḥ told me: “My father was born in the year 93, and Mālik was three years older than him.”

In the year 180 AH

ʿĪsā ibn Mūsā led the people on the pilgrimage.

ʿAbd al-Wārith ibn Saʿīd died in the year 180 AH. He was known by the kunya Abū ʿUbaydah and was a client of Balʿanbar.

He said: “I asked Hishām ibn ʿAmmār about the death of Ṣadaqah ibn Khālid, and he said: ‘He died in the year 180 AH.’”

I heard ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm say: “Ṣadaqah was born in the year 118.”

ʿAlī said: “Sulaymān ibn Jaʿfar died in the year 180 AH.”

Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal said: “ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAmr died in the year 180 AH.”

In the year 181 AH

Hārūn led the people on the pilgrimage.

[I heard al-Ḥasan ibn al-Rabīʿ say: “I witnessed the death of Ibn al-Mubārak. He died in the year 181 AH, in Ramaḍān, ten days into the month. He died at dawn, and we buried him at Hīt.”]

Al-Ḥasan said: “I asked Ibn al-Mubārak—before he died—and he said: ‘I am sixty-three years old.’”

I heard Bishr ibn Abī al-Azhar say: Ibn al-Mubārak said: “ʿAbd Allāh ibn Idrīs asked me about my age and said: ‘How old are you?’ I replied: ‘The non-Arabs can hardly remember that, but I recall that I wore black as a boy, when Abū Muslim came out.’ He said to me: ‘So you were put to the test by wearing black!’ I said: ‘I was younger than that; Abū Muslim made everyone wear black, young and old alike.’”

Abū ʿUmar Ḥafṣ ibn Maysarah al-Ṣanʿānī—of Ṣanʿāʾ in Syria—died in the year 181 AH.

In that year Muṣʿab ibn Māhān, the companion of al-Thawrī, died.

In that year Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAyyāsh died.

Muḥammad ibn Fuḍayl related to us: I heard my father say: “Ibn al-Mubārak came and visited Abū al-Malīḥ al-Raqqī to bid him farewell. Then fourteen days passed between them”—that is, between the deaths of Ibn al-Mubārak and Abū al-Malīḥ.

[I heard al-Ḥajjāj ibn Muḥammad al-Khawlānī say: “Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAyyāsh died in the year 181 AH, on Tuesday, six days into Jumādā.”]

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿImrān was dismissed from Mecca, and ʿUbayd Allāh ibn— Qutham was appointed in his place. Ibn Qutham died while governor of Mecca, in Dhū al-Ḥijjah of the year 181 AH.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muṣʿab was in charge of Medina.

In the year 182 AH

Mūsā ibn ʿĪsā led the people on the pilgrimage.

Ibn Bukayr said: al-Faḍl ibn Faḍālah ibn ʿUbayd al-Ḥimyarī—known by the kunya Abū Muʿāwiyah—was born in the year 107 and died in Shawwāl of the year 181 or 182 AH. It seems that he settled on 181.

Ibn Bukayr said: Abū al-Samḥ ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Samḥ ibn Usāmah al-Tujībī was born in the year 125 and died in the year 182 AH.

Ibn Bukayr said: al-Layth ibn ʿĀṣim—known by the kunya Abū al-Ḥārith al-Khawlānī—was born in the year 130 and died in the year 182 AH.

Abū Bishr Bakr ibn Khalaf and Ḥasan said: Yazīd ibn Zurayʿ died in the year 182 AH.

[Abū Yūsuf Yaʿqūb, the judge, died in that year.]

ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn died in that year, and Muḥammad ibn Hārūn, Commander of the Faithful, led the funeral prayer over him.

[The poet Marwān ibn Abī Ḥafṣah died in that year.]

Hārūn had appointed ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAlī over Mecca, and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muṣʿab over Medina.

In the year 183 AH

Al-ʿAbbās ibn Mūsā led the people on the pilgrimage.

Yaʿqūb related to us: I heard Ḥasan say: “Hushaym ibn Bashīr Abū Muʿāwiyah al-Sulamī died in the year 183 AH. He was born in the year 104.”

Yaʿqūb said: I heard Hishām ibn ʿAmmār and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm say:

“Yaḥyā ibn Ḥamzah died in the year 183 AH.”

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: I heard Abū Mushir say: “Yaḥyā ibn Ḥamzah was born in the year 103 and died in the year 183.”

[I heard Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmmār al-Mawṣilī say: “ʿAfīf died in the year 183.”]

ʿAlī ibn al-Madīnī said: “Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd died in the year 183 AH, aged seventy-three.”

Ḥammād al-Barbarī was appointed in Dhū al-Qaʿdah and dismissed in Muḥarram.

[In that year Bakkār ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muṣʿab was appointed over Medina. His father, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muṣʿab, departed for Madīnat al-Salām and took up residence at the Gate.]

In the year 184 AH
