Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad al-Mahdī led the people on the pilgrimage.

Abū Bishr said: Bishr ibn al-Mufaḍḍal died in the year 184 AH.

Ḥammād al-Barbarī was dismissed from Mecca at the beginning of this year, in Muḥarram, and al-ʿUthmānī was appointed over it in Rabīʿ.

In that year Hārūn arrived in Madīnat al-Salām. He had traveled from al-Raqqah by boat along the Euphrates.

In that year he exacted the outstanding sums owed by his officials after a number of years of his caliphate had passed. He required some to pay a tenth, others a fifth, and waived what was due from others. The person in charge of this and overseeing it was Muḥammad ibn Jamīl, Abū Ṣāliḥ the scribe.

Al-ʿUthmānī was in charge of Mecca.

Bakkār ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muṣʿab was in charge of Medina.

In this year or the year 185, Wakīʿ ibn al-Jarrāḥ related in Mecca, from Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid al-Bāhī, that when the Messenger of God ﷺ died, he was not buried until his belly had swollen and his little finger had curled; and he mentioned other things besides this. The report was brought to al-ʿUthmānī, who sent for Wakīʿ and imprisoned him. He resolved to kill and crucify him, and ordered a crossbeam to be erected outside the Sanctuary. The news reached Wakīʿ while he was in prison.

Al-Ḥārith ibn al-Ṣiddīq said: When news of this reached me—and good news had already reached him—I went in to see Wakīʿ. He said: “At that time there was estrangement between him and Sufyān,” and he said: “It seems we have no choice but to turn to this man and need him”—meaning Sufyān. He said: “I told him:

‘Abū Sufyān, put this out of your mind. Even if he does not get you, he has already spoken.’ He sent for him and sought his help. Sufyān went in to al-ʿUthmānī and interceded for him, but al-ʿUthmānī refused. Sufyān said to him: ‘I am giving you sincere counsel. This man is a scholar and has a clan. If you proceed against him, the least that could happen is that his clan and children will gather at the gate of the Commander of the Faithful, and he will summon you to answer them.’ Sufyān’s words had an effect on him, and he ordered Wakīʿ released from prison.”

Al-Ḥārith ibn al-Ṣiddīq said: “I went back to Wakīʿ and told him. Then the assistants came and took him out of prison. He mounted a donkey, we loaded his belongings, and he departed. Al-Ḥārith said: The next day I went in to see al-ʿUthmānī and said: ‘Praise be to God, who has spared you from being tried by this man. May God, Mighty and Exalted, preserve you.’ He said: ‘Ḥārith, I have never regretted my intention as much as I regret what occurred to me that night: the account of Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh. I moved my father and the martyrs after forty years and found them moist, seeping; nothing about them had changed.’”

I heard Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr say: “We were in Medina when the people of Mecca wrote to the people of Medina about what had happened with Wakīʿ, Ibn ʿUyaynah, and al-ʿUthmānī. They said: ‘When he arrives in Medina, do not rely on the governor; stone him until you kill him.’ They resolved to do so. We heard what they intended, so we sent a dispatch to Wakīʿ telling him not to come to Medina, but to travel by way of al-Rabadhah. He had already passed the fork in the road toward Medina. When the dispatch reached him, he turned back to al-Rabadhah and went on to Kūfah.”

In the year 185 AH

Manṣūr ibn Muḥammad led the people on the pilgrimage.

Ibn Bukayr said: Ḍimām ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Mālik al-Maʿāfirī—whose teknonym was Abū Ismāʿīl—was born in the year 97 and died in the year 185.

Abū Isḥāq al-Fazārī died in the year 185.

Muḥammad ibn Fuḍayl said: Abū Isḥāq al-Fazārī died in the year 188.

I heard Zayd ibn al-Mubārak say: I saw Ibn ʿUyaynah in the year 185. He came to Abū al-Dardāʾ, then turned back to greet him.

Abū Yūsuf related to us: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAmr al-Dimashqī related to me, saying:

Ibn Sulaymān ibn ʿUtbah related to me, saying: Sulaymān died in the year 185, and I heard Abū Mushir affirm his reliability.

I heard ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm say: I heard Abū Mushir say: Khālid ibn Yazīd ibn Abī Mālik was born in the year 105 and died in the year 185.

“I heard Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmmār al-Mawṣilī say: al-Muʿāfā died in the year 185”. ʿAbd al-Wahhāb was born in the year 108.

In this year, Ḥāḍir and his companion were killed before Hārūn with the khayzarāniyya, because of their views on Rāfiḍism. Ibrāhīm ibn ʿUthmān ibn Nahīk was in charge of killing Ḥāḍir, and Harthamah ibn Aʿyan was in charge of killing his companion.

“In this year, ʿAbd al-Ṣamad ibn ʿAlī died at the age of seventy-nine. Hārūn, Commander of the Faithful, led the funeral prayer for him”.

In this year, Hārūn set out for al-Raqqah by way of Mosul.

In this year, a thunderbolt struck the Sacred Mosque in the month of Ramaḍān. It burned a canopy and killed two men.

“In this year, Yazīd ibn Mazīd died at Bardhaʿa”.

Manṣūr ibn al-Mahdī conducted the pilgrimage.

Al-ʿUthmānī was in charge of Mecca, and Bakkār ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muṣʿab was in charge of Medina.

The Year 186

Hārūn conducted the pilgrimage.

In this year, he wrote the two documents.

Abū Bishr said: al-Muʿtamir ibn Sulaymān died in the year 186. He was born in the year 106.

I heard Abū Mūsā say: Khālid ibn al-Ḥārith died in the year 186, and Muʿtamir died in the year 187, on the day Rummān was killed. Rummān was crucified in the morning, and we went to Muʿtamir’s funeral in the evening. Muʿtamir was older than Ibn ʿUyaynah, and likewise, Hushaym was three years older than Ibn ʿUyaynah.

Hushaym said: Yaʿlā ibn ʿAṭāʾ left us in the year 120. At that time, Ibn ʿUyaynah was thirteen years old, and Hushaym was sixteen.

In the year 187

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās ibn Muḥammad conducted the pilgrimage.

In this year, Rabāḥ ibn Zayd died at the age of eighty-one, as Aḥmad related from Ibrāhīm ibn Khālid al-Ṣanʿānī, the muezzin of the people of Ṣanʿāʾ.

In this year, al-Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ, Abū ʿAlī, died in Muḥarram, on the eleventh day of the month, as Ibn Abī ʿUmar related.

I heard ʿIyāḍ in the year 187.

Zayd said: Rabāḥ stopped transmitting ḥadīth more than ten years before his death.

Zayd said: I went with Ibrāhīm al-Rāzī al-Ṣaghīr to Rabāḥ. We entered to see him, and Ibrāhīm tried in every way to get him to relate something, but he refused. Ibrāhīm said to him:

“Ibn al-Mubārak related to us from you that Wahb ibn Munabbih said: ‘Knowledge has an excess, just as wealth has an excess.’”

He said: “If Ibn al-Mubārak related something to you, he related only the truth; and if he related something to you, then it is as he related it.” He said nothing more to us than this.

Zayd said: Ibn Thawr said: “Rabāḥ went too far both when he transmitted and when he stopped transmitting.”

He said: “He used to write for them on slips of paper and read them aloud to them. Then he stopped, and no one could hope to get anything from him.”

I heard Abū Mūsā say: Bishr ibn al-Mufaḍḍal died in the year 187, two and a half months after Muʿtamir.

The Year 188

Hārūn conducted the pilgrimage.

In this year, Rishdīn ibn Saʿd, Abū al-Ḥajjāj al-Mihrī, died.

I heard Abū al-Ṭāhir say: He died in the year 188 or 189.

I heard Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmmār al-Mawṣilī say: ʿUmar ibn Ayyūb died in the year 188.

The Year 189

Al-ʿAbbās ibn Mūsā ibn ʿĪsā conducted the pilgrimage.

Muḥammad ibn Fuḍayl said: ʿUmar ibn ʿUbayd, Yaʿlā’s brother, died in the year 189.

I heard ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm and Hishām ibn ʿAmmār say: Shuʿayb died in the year 189.

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: In Rajab.

I heard Abū Mūsā say: ʿAbd al-Aʿlā died in the year 189, on the day Wakīʿ came to us at ʿAbbādān for the second time.

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAmr al-Ḥarrānī related to me, saying: I heard Abū Mushir say: Ṣadaqah was sound in what he took and sound in what he gave.

The Year 190

“Naṣr ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Kūfī related to me, saying: We wrote down material from Ḥakkām—I think it was in the year 190—and he died in Mecca before he could perform the pilgrimage”.

The Year 191

Al-Faḍl ibn al-ʿAbbās ibn Muḥammad conducted the pilgrimage.

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Qāsim al-Miṣrī died in the year 191. He died on the night before Thursday, on the ninth of Ṣafar.

Makhlad ibn Ḥusayn died in the year 191.

Muḥammad said: Muʿtamir al-Raqqī died in Shaʿbān of the year 191.

The Year 192

Al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar ibn Abī Jaʿfar conducted the pilgrimage.

Ibn Idrīs was born in the year 115 and died in the year 192.

The Year 193

Dāwūd ibn ʿĪsā ibn Mūsā conducted the pilgrimage.

Ibn Bukayr said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Kulayb ibn Kaysān al-Murādī, whose teknonym was Abū ʿAbd Allāh, died in the year 193.

Ibn ʿUlayyah, Ismāʿīl ibn Ibrāhīm, the client of Banū Asad, died in the year 193 and was born in the year 110.

I heard Ḥammād ibn Ismāʿīl ibn ʿUlayyah say: Sufyān ibn Wakīʿ came to us in the year 193, one or two days after my father’s death, having traveled westward.

Hārūn, Commander of the Faithful, died in Rabīʿ II of the year 193. “Muḥammad ibn Hārūn was appointed caliph in the year 193”.

Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh died in the year 193.

“I heard Saʿīd ibn Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Umawī say: I heard Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh—who had come to offer my father condolences for his brother Muḥammad ibn Saʿīd, who was older than him—ask my father: ‘When was he born?’ He said: ‘At the time of al-Jarrāḥ’s death.’ Abū Bakr said: ‘That was when I reached puberty’”.

Al-Ḥasan ibn al-Rabīʿ said: Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh was born in the year 95.

“Muḥammad ibn Fuḍayl related to me, saying: We were in Mecca in the year 193 when Rāshid al-Ḥannāq came to us. He said: ‘We buried Ismāʿīl ibn ʿUlayyah on Thursday, with five or six days remaining of Dhū al-Qaʿdah.’ He said: ‘We traveled for nine days’”.

Abū Bishr Bakr ibn Khalaf said: Ibn ʿUlayyah and Ghundar died in the same year, and al-Ḥaqq died in the same month.

Muḥammad said: I went to Marwān in the year 193, but he did not relate anything to me. Then I came in the year 194, and he had died.

He said: I wrote material from Yaḥyā ibn Sulaymān in the year 193. Then I arrived in the year 194, and he had died.

He said: I performed the pilgrimage in this year and passed through Kūfah while Ḥafṣ ibn Ghiyāth was still alive. Then we returned to Kūfah, and he had died.

“Mujāhid ibn Mūsā related to me, saying: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam related to us, saying: I asked Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh about his name, and he said: ‘It is my name’”.

The Year 194

ʿAlī ibn Hārūn ibn Muḥammad conducted the pilgrimage.

Muḥammad said: We wrote material from al-Walīd in Mecca in the year 194. Then he set out, and someone who had accompanied him told me that he died on his return journey at Dhū al-Marwah.

I heard ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm say: Suwayd ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz was born in the year 108.

I heard Hishām ibn ʿAmmār and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān say: Suwayd died in the year 194.

“I heard Saʿīd ibn Yaḥyā al-Umawī say: My father died in the year 194”.

The Year 195

Dāwūd ibn ʿĪsā ibn Mūsā conducted the pilgrimage.

“Muḥammad ibn Fuḍayl related to us, saying: Abū Muʿāwiyah al-Ḍarīr, Muḥammad ibn Khāzim, died in the year 195, at the end of Ṣafar [or] at the beginning of Rabīʿ I. Abū Muʿāwiyah was born in the year 113”.

I heard ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm say: al-Walīd ibn Muslim’s grandson, his daughter’s son, said:

“He was born in the year 119.”

I heard Hishām ibn ʿAmmār say: al-Walīd died in the year 195.

I heard ʿAbd al-Raḥmān say: al-Walīd died in Muḥarram, at Dhū al-Marwah, in the year 195.

The Year 196

Al-ʿAbbās ibn Mūsā ibn ʿĪsā conducted the pilgrimage.

Muḥammad ibn Fuḍayl said: Abū Sufyān Wakīʿ ibn al-Jarrāḥ al-Ruʾāsī died in the year 196. He was born in the year 119.

The Year 197

Al-ʿAbbās ibn Mūsā ibn ʿĪsā conducted the pilgrimage.

“ Ibn Wahb, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Wahb ibn Muslim al-Miṣrī, was born in Dhū al-Qaʿdah of the year 125 and died in Shaʿbān, with five days remaining in the month, in the year 197”.

“Baqiyyah ibn al-Walīd, Abū Yaḥmad al-Maythamī, died in the year 197”.

Ibn Bukayr said: Ibn Wahb told me: I was born in Dhū al-Qaʿdah of the year 125.

“Muḥammad ibn al-Muṣaffā related to us, saying: Baqiyyah ibn al-Walīd died in the year 197”.

ʿUmar ibn ʿUthmān ibn Saʿīd told me: Baqiyyah was born in the year 110.

Abū Ayyūb Sulaymān ibn Salamah al-Khabāʾirī told me: Baqiyyah, Abū Yaḥmad, was the son of al-Walīd ibn Ṣāʾil al-Kilāʿī al-Maythamī.

“Yazīd ibn ʿAbd Rabbih said: I heard Baqiyyah say: ‘I was born in the year 110’”.

The Year 198

Al-ʿAbbās ibn Mūsā ibn ʿĪsā ibn Muḥammad also conducted the pilgrimage.

“Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmar said: Abū Muḥammad Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah ibn Abī ʿImrān al-Hilālī—who was their client—died in the year 198, on the last day of Jumādā II”.

Al-Ḥumaydī said: Sufyān related to us, saying: Qāsim related to me in the year 120 and I was thirteen years old at the time.

Al-Juʿfī related to us, saying: Sufyān said: I was born in the year 107, and my father took me on the pilgrimage in the year 114.

He said: Ibn Shihāb came to us in the year 123. He said: I heard him say: “The Commander of the Faithful, Hishām ibn ʿAbd al-Malik, sent us with this boy to set him straight. Then we waited for him until the following year, when news of his death reached us”. His son performed the pilgrimage—a son of Hishām ibn ʿAbd al-Malik.

Al-Juʿfī said: I heard Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah say in the year 172:

“Abū Isḥāq related to us seventy years ago, saying: Ṣilah ibn Zufar related to us seventy years ago, saying: I was sitting with ʿAbd Allāh when a man came to him.”

Muḥammad ibn Fuḍayl said: Maʿn ibn ʿĪsā died on a Tuesday in Shawwāl of the year 198.

He said: Ibn Numayr died in the year 198.

“In this year, Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī died”. And [he] died— ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, who was sixty-three years old. He was born in the year 135.

Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmar told me: Sufyān said: “Hishām ibn Ḥujayr would sometimes joke with me, saying, ‘Abū ʿAbd Allāh, there were the days you memorized things as a boy, and we do not accept a boy’s testimony; and there were the days you memorized things as a man, so we accept it from you.’”

[I heard Abū Mūsā say: “Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd died in the year 198, and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān died four months after him.”]

Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah died in this year.

Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmar related to us: Sufyān said: “Al-Zuhrī came to us in Mecca in the year 123 and stayed until the new moon of al-Muḥarram. Then he set out and performed the lesser pilgrimage from al-Jiʿrānah. He said, ‘Let no one follow me.’ I was then sixteen years and three months old. I was born in the middle of Shaʿbān in the year 107. Al-Zuhrī died in the year 124.”

Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmar related to us: Sufyān said: “Al-Zuhrī said, ‘This man sent us with his son, so we are setting his crookedness right’”—meaning Hishām ibn ʿAbd al-Malik.

Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmar related to us: Sufyān said: “Misʿar said to me: ‘So-and-so says, “Misʿar relates to so-and-so, but not to us.” Not everyone is easy for me to speak to; perhaps I said, “I feel more inclined to speak to him.”’”

I said to him: “Our neighbor Khālid has asked me to speak to you, so that he may come to you and you relate to him.”

He said: “Tell him to come.” I said to him: “And should I come with him?” He said: “As for you, you”

“have come to us.”

[ʿAlī ibn al-Madīnī said: “Sufyān performed the pilgrimage seventy-two times. ʿAṭāʾ died in the year 115. Sufyān performed the pilgrimage a year after his death, when he was nine years old, and continued to perform it until he died. He stayed in Mecca from the year 122 until the year 126, then went out to Kūfah.”]

Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Qaṭṭān died in the year 198. He was born in the year 120.

[ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī died in the year 198, aged sixty-three. He was known by the teknonym Abū Saʿīd. He was born in the year 135.]

ʿAlī said: “Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd died at the age of seventy-eight. He died early in the year 198, and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān died four months after him. Ibn ʿUyaynah died seven days after ʿAbd al-Raḥmān. Abū al-Walīd was three years older than ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, and Ghundar was older than Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd.”

Volume One199

The year 199

Ḥusayn ibn Ḥasan al-Ṭālibī led the people on the pilgrimage and stripped the Kaʿbah.

Ibn Bukayr said: “Shuʿayb ibn al-Layth ibn Saʿd died with one day remaining in Ramaḍān of the year 199. His teknonym was Abū ʿAbd al-Malik.”

Dāwūd ibn ʿĪsā was governor of Mecca. His son Muḥammad ibn Dāwūd was appointed to lead the pilgrimage in the year 199. On the seventh of Dhū al-Ḥijjah, he preached to the people in Mecca and instructed them in the rites of pilgrimage. Then on the Day of Tarwiyah he set out for Minā, and by evening he had performed the pilgrimage, praying with the people at Minā the noon, afternoon, sunset, and night prayers, but not the dawn prayer. He set out in the latter part of the night, until he encountered him at the edge of the Sacred Precinct. Then they headed along the road to Iraq, fleeing.

Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan entered Mecca on the Day of ʿArafah, at the time of the afternoon prayer, and preached to the people in Mecca that day. He kept the people waiting at ʿArafah until the afternoon prayer was nearly missed. Then the people prayed at ʿArafah without an imam. They set out to the place of standing and were moved on without an imam, until Ḥusayn ibn Ḥasan arrived at ʿArafah late in the night and stood there. That same night he came to Muzdalifah and prayed with the people there, standing with them at Quzaḥ. Then he combined the prayers and moved on with them until he had stoned the Jamarah, and he departed on the Day of Sacrifice. He continued in office over Mecca and removed the covering of the House on the first night of al-Muḥarram in the year 200. He covered it with yellow cloth, and placed white cloth over that. He continued to serve as governor of Mecca.

[They pledged allegiance to Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib as caliph on Friday, three days into Rabīʿ al-Ākhir of the year 200. He continued to be greeted as caliph until Tuesday, five days into Jumādā al-Ūlā of the year 200.

I heard Abū Bishr Bakr ibn Khalaf say: “Abū Shuʿayb the Blind took me by the hand and brought me in to Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, and I pledged allegiance to him. He ordered a piece of brocade for me from what he had removed from the Kaʿbah.” He said: “I left it with Abū Shuʿayb, and he threw some of that covering over the animals—his own animals and those of his companions.”]

Volume One200

The year 200

Abū Isḥāq ibn Hārūn led the people on the pilgrimage.

Abū Yūsuf said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm told me: I heard— Abū Ḍamrah say: “I was born in the year 104.” ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: “He died in the year 200.” He said: “He asked me, ‘Where are you from?’ I said, ‘From Damascus.’ He said:

‘I know it, by God. I entered it in the days of Hishām.’” ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: “Someone said to Abū Ḍamrah, ‘Did you read the tradition of Jaʿfar to him as I read it?’ He said, ‘What concern is it of yours or mine? A neighbor of ours read it to him.’ Then he said: ‘Ṣāliḥ ibn Kaysān al-Naṣrī related to us: I heard Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb say: “A liar lies only because of his own lowliness.”’”

I heard ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm say: “Ibn Shuʿayb and ʿUmar died in the year 200, and their births were close together. Ibn Shuʿayb was born in the year 116, and ʿUmar was born in the year 118.”

I heard Mūsā ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Masrūq al-Kindī say: “Al-ʿAnqazī died in the year 200.”

On Tuesday, five days into Jumādā al-Ūlā of the year 200, Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad set out on the fifth of Jumādā al-Ūlā in the year 200. He set out that day, together with those who were with him, as the day advanced; and Waraqāʾ entered Mecca after noon. Isḥāq ibn Mūsā ibn ʿĪsā arrived at the afternoon prayer time—he was governor of Ṣanʿāʾ. When he heard that Ibrāhīm ibn Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad al-Ṭālibī was approaching, intending for Ṣanʿāʾ, he left the city and arrived in Mecca. Al-Jalūdī entered with him at the end of Jumādā al-Ūlā, and continued in office over it. An army from Ṣanʿāʾ arrived at Nakhlah. Al-Jalūdī went out to meet them on the seventh of Dhū al-Ḥijjah, defeated them, and scattered their forces.

Abū Isḥāq ibn Hārūn, the Commander of the Faithful’s appointee to lead the pilgrimage in the year 200, entered and granted Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad safe conduct after the afternoon prayer … Al-Jalūdī and the judge Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān went out to meet him and brought him to Mecca on the tenth of Dhū al-Ḥijjah. They dressed him in black, and he ascended the pulpit, renounced his claim, and pledged allegiance to ʿAbd Allāh. Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī and Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān, who had been governor of Medina and Mecca, arrived in Medina. Rajāʾ took them to Baghdad. After that, on the second of al-Muḥarram, al-Jalūdī took Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar to ʿAbd Allāh al-Maʾmūn. Al-Jalūdī left his son as governor of Mecca. There was a dispute between him and the people of Mecca, who pelted him with stones until they forced him into Dār al-ʿAjalah.

He seized some of them and flogged them, cut off the hands of two men, and flogged ʿUthmān ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakr al-Makhzūmī.

Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn ʿĪsā ibn Māhān had been appointed over Ṣanʿāʾ. His son al-Aḥwal set out for it, while he remained in Mecca until the appointment to it came to him.

Ibn al-Jalūdī set out for Iraq.

Ḥamdawayh ibn ʿAlī continued in office over Mecca.

Volume One201

The year 201

Isḥāq ibn Mūsā ibn ʿĪsā al-Hāshimī led the people on the pilgrimage.

He said: I heard Mūsā ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Masrūq al-Kindī say: “Abū Usāmah died in the year 201.”

Isḥāq ibn Mūsā had brought with him the pledge of allegiance to ʿAlī ibn Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad al-Ṭālibī as heir apparent, but Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī prevented him from making it public. Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī continued as governor of Mecca until he left for Ṣanʿāʾ in Ṣafar of the year 201. Yazīd ibn Muḥammad ibn Ḥanẓalah was appointed governor of Mecca. Yazīd remained its governor until Ibrāhīm ibn ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān al-Ḥajabī rose against him in Rabīʿ al-Awwal, on Sunday, twelve days into Rabīʿ al-Awwal of the year 201, with a crowd that Ibrāhīm ibn ʿUbayd Allāh had gathered. They fought in the Sacred Mosque, and Ibrāhīm ibn ʿUbayd Allāh’s followers were killed—al-Naqqār, the freedman of Jaʿfar ibn Sulaymān, …

One of the shaykhs of Mecca told me: “The Banū Makhzūm feared that Ibrāhīm’s followers and the rabble would enter their houses, so they appealed to al-ʿĀʾidhī, who was obeyed among the people of Mecca. They said to him, ‘Ride out, for when people see you they will leave us alone.’ He mounted a mule and went to the mosque to restrain the people. The rabble turned on him and spoke abusively to him. Fearing for his life, he shouted to those with him, ‘Charge the sons of such-and-such!’ He made a charge, and the rabble and the people scattered. They caught up with Ibrāhīm at Bāb Shaybah and struck him with swords until he was carried to his house in Quʿayqiʿān. Yazīd ibn Muḥammad ibn Ḥanẓalah came to him at his house and brought him out in the worst of … to the market, until he put him in prison. Ibrāhīm died that same day.”

Yazīd ibn Muḥammad continued in office over Mecca until Jumādā. Ibrāhīm ibn Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad al-Ṭālibī came from Ṣanʿāʾ, heading for Mecca. They gathered forces against him and dispersed the people to fight Ibrāhīm. When they learned of his arrival, Yazīd continued to hold Mecca [and] they dug a trench around its upper, lower, and outlying parts. The judge went into hiding— Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, Suhayl, a freedman of al-ʿAbbās, and many of those who were with them, and they left Mecca. Yazīd ibn Muḥammad ibn Ḥanẓalah remained in that encampment at Mecca until Ibrāhīm ibn Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar came into view above Mecca.

I heard Abū Bishr Bakr ibn Khalaf say: “I heard Yazīd ibn Muḥammad ibn Ḥanẓalah on the pulpit in Mecca urging the people to seek martyrdom and to march with him. He said: ‘Indeed, the people have united behind al-Maʾmūn, and the people of the greatest frontier—the people of Khurāsān—have pledged allegiance to him. God Almighty said in His Book:

“Go forth, whether lightly or heavily equipped” (Qurʾān 9:41).’”

Ibrāhīm ibn Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar came to Mecca from its upper side on the first night of Shaʿbān, accompanied by al-ʿUmarī, ʿUmar ibn Ibrāhīm, and his son. Al-ʿUmarī went forward to Yazīd ibn Muḥammad ibn Ḥanẓalah and spoke to them, asking him to withdraw from them. He refused and ordered those with him to fight them. The fighting broke out, Yazīd’s followers fled from him, and Yazīd was killed. Ziyād, the freedman of Ibrāhīm ibn ʿUbayd Allāh, cut off his head and took it to Ibrāhīm ibn ʿUbayd Allāh’s followers. Ibrāhīm ibn Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar entered Mecca on a rainy day and took control of it. He pardoned everyone among the people who had risen against him. He continued as governor of Mecca until al-Jalūdī arrived on the seventh of Dhū al-Ḥijjah as governor of Mecca, bringing with him Ibrāhīm ibn Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar’s appointment to lead the pilgrimage.

Volume One202

The year 202

Ibrāhīm ibn Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad al-Ṭālibī led the people on the pilgrimage. In the year 202, al-Jalūdī came with his appointment.

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṭālibī became governor of Medina and Mecca in Rabīʿ al-Awwal of the year 204.

Volume One203

The year 203

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sulaymān ibn ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar led the people on the pilgrimage.

I heard Mūsā ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Masrūq say: “Ḥusayn al-Juʿfī died in the year 202 or at the beginning of the year 203. Zayd ibn Ḥubāb al-ʿUklī, Muḥammad ibn Bishr, Abū Dāwūd al-Ḥafarī, Abū Aḥmad al-Zubayrī, and Yaḥyā ibn Ādam died in the year 203.”

I heard Mūsā ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān say: “Abū Dāwūd al-Ḥafarī, Muḥammad ibn Bishr, al-Aḥdab, and Yaḥyā died in the year 203.”

Volume One204

The year 204

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṭālibī led the people on the pilgrimage.

Abū Dāwūd al-Ṭayālisī died in the year 204, aged seventy-two.

Ashhab ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz al-Qaysī al-Miṣrī died in the year 204. He was born in the year 140.

Volume One205

The year 205

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn al-Ḥasan again led the people on the pilgrimage.

Volume One206

The year 206

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn al-Ḥasan again led the people on the pilgrimage.

Yazīd ibn Hārūn died, and [Ḥajjāj ibn Muḥammad [died] in the year 206]. Yazīd ibn Hārūn was born in the year 118.

[Muḥammad said: “Yazīd died at the beginning of the year 206, and was born in the year 117 118.”]

Muḥammad ibn Fuḍayl said: “And Muʾammal ibn Ismāʿīl …” Muʾammal died in the year 206.

Abū al-Ḥasan said: “He died in Ramaḍān of the year 206.”

Volume One207

The year 207

Abū ʿĪsā ibn Hārūn led the people on the pilgrimage.

I heard ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm say: “Al-Walīd ibn Yazīd is reliable. He died in the year 207.”

[ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAmr related to us: “I attended the funeral of Zayd ibn ʿUbayd at Bāb al-Ṣaghīr in the year 207.”]

Volume One208

The year 208

Ṣāliḥ ibn Hārūn, son of the Commander of the Faithful, led the people on the pilgrimage.

Muḥammad ibn Fuḍayl said: “Wahb ibn Jarīr died in the year 208. He led the pilgrimage for us, and I heard from him; then he departed and died on the road.”

He said: “Jaʿfar ibn ʿAwn had arrived in this year, then departed and died.”

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn al-Ḥasan was governor of Mecca and Medina. His dismissal arrived during this pilgrimage season with Ṣāliḥ ibn Hārūn, who appointed Ṣāliḥ al-ʿAbbās ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh to Mecca in Dhū al-Qaʿda of the year 208. ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Hajhāj arrived with a letter appointing ʿAmr ibn ʿUmar ibn Saʿd al-Sahmī governor of Mecca. ʿAmr ibn ʿUmar governed it during Ṣafar, Rabīʿ al-Awwal, and Rabīʿ al-Ākhir. Ṣāliḥ ibn al-ʿAbbās entered Mecca on the last day of Rabīʿ al-Ākhir, and ʿAmr ibn ʿUmar was appointed judge of Mecca.

Volume One209

The year 209

Ṣāliḥ ibn al-ʿAbbās ibn Muḥammad led the people on pilgrimage.

Muḥammad ibn Fuḍayl said: “Yaʿlā ibn ʿUbayd died in the year 209.” Qutham ibn Jaʿfar ibn Sulaymān governed Medina; then he was dismissed, and Jaʿfar ibn al-Qāsim ibn Jaʿfar ibn Sulaymān al-ʿAbbāsī governed after him.

Volume One210

The year 210

Ṣāliḥ ibn al-ʿAbbās led the people on pilgrimage.

In this year Marwān ibn Muḥammad al-Ṭāṭarī died. He was born in the year 147.

Volume One211

The year 211

In this year ʿAbd al-Razzāq ibn Hammām, Abū Bakr, died. He was born in the year 126.

Abū Yūsuf said: “In this year Ṣāliḥ ibn al-ʿAbbās led us on pilgrimage.”

Yūsuf ibn Yaʿqūb al-Shāfiʿī was appointed judge in Dhū al-Ḥijja of the year 210; the appointment to the judgeship came to him from the Commander of the Faithful.

Volume One212

The year 212

ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUbayd Allāh ibn al-ʿAbbās ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās led the people on pilgrimage.

In this year Muḥammad ibn Yūsuf al-Fāryābī, a client of Banū Tamīm, died at the beginning of the year.

A reliable man among our companions told me: “Al-Fāryābī said: ‘I was born in the year 120.’”

In this year Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yazīd al-Muqriʾ died at the end of the year.

In this year Abū al-Mughīra died.

Volume One213

The year 213

ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUbayd Allāh also led the people on pilgrimage.

In this year Abū ʿĀṣim al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Makhlad al-Shaybānī died.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUbayd Allāh led the people on pilgrimage, and Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb was appointed judge over Mecca. In this year Bishr ibn Shuʿayb died.

“In this year ʿAbd al-Wahhāb ibn Saʿīd ibn ʿAṭiyya, the Damascene mufti, died”.

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Ḥasanī was appointed, with al-Nawfalī alongside him, at the beginning of Dhū al-Ḥijja in the year 213. He was dismissed in the year 214.

Volume One214

The year 214

Isḥāq ibn al-ʿAbbās ibn Muḥammad led the people on pilgrimage.

“ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā, Abū Muḥammad, died in this year”, “as did Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Muthannā ibn Anas al-Anṣārī. [I heard al-Anṣārī] say in the year 212: ‘I have reached nearly ninety-four years of age’”.

In this year Aḥmad ibn Khālid al-Wahbī died.

In this year ʿAmr ibn Abī Salama al-Tinnīsī died.

Sawwār ibn ʿUmāra al-Ramlī died in this year, or in the year 215.

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Ḥasanī was dismissed from Mecca.

Sulaymān ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-ʿAbbāsī governed Mecca and Medina, while his son Muḥammad was in charge of Mecca. They alternated in office: at times the father was in charge of Mecca and the son of Medina.

Al-Maʾmūn campaigned against the Byzantines and took Qurrat. His son al-ʿAbbās entered by way of the Darb al-Ḥadath.

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn al-Jahm governed, and Bakūr and Majah, the Abyssinian kings, arrived with him in the year 215.

Volume One215

The year 215

ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUbayd Allāh ibn al-ʿAbbās ibn Muḥammad led the people on pilgrimage.

“In this year ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Shaqīq died. ʿAlī said: ‘I was born before the killing of Abū Muslim’”. In this year Muḥammad ibn al-Mubārak al-Ṣūrī died.

I heard ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAmr say: “Abū Mushir performed the funeral prayer over Muḥammad ibn al-Mubārak at Bāb al-Jābiya. When he had finished, he praised him.”

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: “He was born in the year 153”.

Al-Walīd ibn ʿUtba told me, from Marwān, who said: “There is no one among us like him.”

I heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad ibn Dhakwān say: Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn said: “Muḥammad ibn al-Mubārak is the leading shaykh of the city after Abū Mushir.”

“ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad said: ‘He would not transmit from ʿAmr ibn Wāqid until Marwān ibn Muḥammad al-Ṭāṭarī died’”.

“He said: ‘Marwān used to say: “ʿAmr ibn Wāqid is a liar.”

“I asked ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm about ʿAmr ibn Wāqid. He said: ‘Our shaykhs did not transmit from him.’ It seemed he had no doubt that the man was lying’”.

Al-Maʾmūn campaigned in this year.

Volume One216

The year 216

Abū Yūsuf said: “I arrived in Mecca at the beginning of Ramaḍān, and I heard the Musnad of al-Ḥumaydī; he began it in Shawwāl.

“ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUbayd Allāh ibn al-ʿAbbās ibn Muḥammad led the people on pilgrimage.

“I set out and stayed in Mecca until the new moon of al-Muḥarram. I departed after the new moon of al-Muḥarram” for Egypt, and we passed through al-Suwaydāʾ once. That was at the beginning of the year 217.

News reached us that Muḥammad ibn Kathīr al-Miṣṣīṣī had died before he arrived in Egypt, at a day’s journey from Egypt.

Volume One217

The year 217

I heard from Abū Ṣāliḥ, Saʿīd ibn Abī Maryam, Abū al-Aswad al-Naḍr ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār, and others.

At the end of the year I set out for Syria.

In this year, in Damascus, I heard Abū Mushir say: “Ibn Lahīʿa wrote to us, reporting from Bukayr ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Umm ʿAlqama, from ʿĀʾisha, about a pregnant woman who sees blood. She said:

‘She does not pray.’

“Al-Maʾmūn had arrived in Egypt in al-Muḥarram. He stayed there for a month or part of a month, attacked al-Bayḍāʾ and took its people captive, then left it heading toward Tarsus. He campaigned in Byzantine territory and laid siege to Luʾluʾa but did not take it. ʿUjayf took it afterward.

“I wrote down traditions from Abū Tawba and others. I attended the pilgrimage in this year, and the pilgrimage was led by by Sulaymān ibn ʿAbd Allāh, who was governor of Medina and Mecca.

Volume One218

The year 218

Al-Maʾmūn campaigned against the Byzantines. When he was at al-Badhindūn, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Hārūn died in Rajab of the year 218. His caliphate had lasted twenty-one years, less a few days.

Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān announced his death in Mecca on Wednesday, thirteen days into Ramaḍān, and pledged allegiance to Abū Isḥāq ibn Hārūn. He was carried to Adhana and buried there on Wednesday, the twenty-third of Ramaḍān.

Ṣāliḥ ibn al-ʿAbbās led us on pilgrimage. He had arrived as governor over Mecca and Medina.

“Abū Nuʿaym al-Faḍl ibn Dukayn died in the year 218, and he was born in the year 130”.

In this year Abū Mushir died. He was born in the year 140.

“I witnessed Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, the judge, al-Makhzūmī, come to Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb—he had written to Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb that he should suspend [himself] from the judgeship—to greet him, bid him farewell, and depart for Baghdad. Sulaymān asked him: ‘What is taking you away?’”

He said: “I am going to offer the Commander of the Faithful condolences for the judge, and congratulations on what is to come.”

Sulaymān said, laughing: “You are only going so that Ibn Abī Duʾād might arrange for you to be appointed judge of Mecca, but he will not do so. Ibn al-Ḥurr has already set out; he will appoint him as judge and make him one of his protégés, so he will be remembered for it. You will not be his protégé; you are too distinguished for that.” He left, and it was as Sulaymān had said”.

Volume One219

The year 219

Ṣāliḥ ibn al-ʿAbbās led the people on pilgrimage, and Ṭāhir ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṭāhir arrived with the key to the Kaʿba; I was with him.

In this year Zamzam was demolished, then decorated with gold and mosaics, and the dome was built. In this year Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī died.

“In this year ʿAlī ibn ʿAyyāsh al-Ḥimṣī died”. He was born in the year 143.

Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm arrived with Ṭāhir and Ibn Faraj al-Rakhkhajī. They had with them a key made of solid gold. A dispute arose between them and the keepers of the Kaʿba, until they reached an agreement that the House would be locked with two keys: the old one and the one they had brought. The keepers went to the caliph and made a request of him, saying: “This is the key of God’s Messenger ﷺ.”

He ordered that the key he had sent be removed and the first key restored to them. He gave them the key and bestowed gifts upon them.

Zamzam was demolished, then decorated with gold and mosaics, and the dome was built. It was completed on the remaining five days of Dhū al-Qaʿda in the year 220.

Abū Yūsuf said: “In this year, 219, I set out and heard from Ādam, Abū al-Yamān, al-Wuḥāẓī, and shaykhs in Palestine, Damascus, and Ḥimṣ.

“I was present when Ṭāhir ibn ʿAbd Allāh came to Sulaymān with his scribes, among them Ibn Shuʿayb, his father’s client. He said to Sulaymān: ‘Take your books and come to us to transmit traditions.’ Sulaymān was troubled by this. Ibn Khāqān was staying in Mecca, so Sulaymān said: ‘Do you know where Ibn Khāqān is staying?’ I said: ‘Yes.’ He said: ‘Go tell him that Sulaymān is waiting for him in the mosque.’ They sent for him. When he met Sulaymān, he said: ‘I see you are troubled.’ Sulaymān replied: ‘Yes. This man told me, “Take your books and come to us to transmit traditions,” but I will not do that.’ Ibn Khāqān said to him:

“‘Do not be troubled; this is an easy matter. Stay here until I return to you.’ He went in to see Ṭāhir and then came out, saying: ‘God has spared you.’ Sulaymān asked: ‘Has he changed his mind?’ Ibn Khāqān said: ‘I told him, “I think you should visit the judge in his session, for the emir will be pleased by that, and your standing with him will be raised by your visiting the scholars.” So he went to him in the evening with his scribe, carrying a written third, and the scribe began asking him questions while he transmitted traditions to him.’”

Volume One220

The year 220

Ṣāliḥ ibn al-ʿAbbās led the people on pilgrimage, and ʿUjayf arrived.

“In this year Ādam ibn Abī Iyās died”.

In this year ʿAbd Allāh ibn Maslama ibn Qaʿnab died at the end of the year, before the new moon of al-Muḥarram, or after al-Muḥarram had ended, in Ṣafar of the year 221. Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, Ibn al-Ḥurr, was appointed judge. He arrived in Mecca, and his letter of appointment read:

“The Commander of the Faithful has decided to appoint Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn as judge.” Ṣāliḥ said to him:

“He has only said ‘appoint.’ If you agree that I appoint you and you become judge, then so be it; otherwise, submit to me a letter explaining that.” He said to him—he was among his own people and of their number—“Rather, I agree to be your judge.”

The judgeship remained with him on this basis.

Volume One221

The year 221

Muḥammad ibn Dāwūd ibn ʿĪsā led the people on pilgrimage.

In this year Abū al-Yamān al-Ḥakam ibn Nāfiʿ died. He was born in the year 138.

Ṣāliḥ was dismissed, and Muḥammad ibn Dāwūd ibn ʿĪsā was appointed.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad al-ʿUmarī arrived to take charge of security in Mecca on behalf of Muḥammad ibn Dāwūd, two days before Dhū al-Ḥijja in the year 221. He took over the office from Ṣāliḥ. Muḥammad ibn Dāwūd ibn ʿĪsā arrived seven days into Dhū al-Ḥijja of the year 221, having been appointed over the people. The Arabs attended the reading of his appointment letter. In it was the instruction that he take gold from gold, silver from silver, grain from grain, hoofed livestock from sheep, and padded feet from camels. When the pilgrimage season ended, he distributed his officials among the districts under his administration. He appointed a man from Banū Jumah over a district in his jurisdiction, among Suksuk and ʿĀmir.

He counted their livestock and said: “Bring one dinar for each obligatory due.” They refused him and said:

“You are a disobedient Khārijite, seeking to seize our property. Your master’s appointment letter only says that you are to take one sheep for each obligatory due, the maximum price and value of which is seven or eight dirhams.” He contended with them, and they contended with him; he fought them, and they fought him, until there were dead on both sides. The Jumahī was killed. Ibn Dāwūd summoned the Jumahī’s brother and appointed him over the district, authorizing him to levy forced service and enlist the Bedouins and others. He set out and plundered the two tribes, and his army’s wrongdoing grew severe.

Abū Yūsuf said: “I heard one of the fools who went out with him say: ‘We deflowered more than ten thousand virgins.’”

Volume One222

The year 222

Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā led us on pilgrimage.

“In this year Abū Ṣāliḥ Yaḥyā ibn Ṣāliḥ al-Wuḥāẓī died. He was born in the year 147”.

Volume One223

The year 223

Muḥammad ibn Dāwūd led us on pilgrimage. He departed from Mecca on the eighth and entered it for an ʿumra. He shortened the prayers on his way there and, in Mecca, would leave his residence—the governor’s palace—and lead the people in two-rakʿa prayers. This caused the people hardship and distress. Every man of learning objected to this conduct of his. He then began the pilgrimage and led us on pilgrimage in this manner.

Volume One224

The year 224

Muḥammad ibn Dāwūd ibn ʿĪsā led us on pilgrimage.

“In this year Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān, Abū al-Jamāhir, died. He was born in the year 121—” and forty-one and one hundred [AH].

In it, Saʿīd ibn al-Ḥakam ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Maryam died. He was born in the year one hundred and forty-four.

“In it, Ḥaywah ibn Shurayḥ died,” as did Yazīd ibn ʿAbd Rabbih.

The Year 225

Muḥammad ibn Dāwūd ibn ʿĪsā led us on the pilgrimage.

In it, Aṣbagh ibn Nūḥ ibn Saʿīd died.

The Year 226

I do not know who led the people on the pilgrimage, for I was in Egypt.

The Year 227

The Commander of the Faithful, Jaʿfar ibn Abī Isḥāq, led the people on the pilgrimage.

In it, Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Uways died.

In it, Abū Isḥāq died, in the month of Rabīʿ al-Awwal.

In it, al-Mubarraqa rebelled in Palestine.

Rajāʾ al-Ḥaḍārī fought the people of Kafr Baṭnā.

The caliphate of Abū Isḥāq lasted nine years, two months, and eight days.

Hārūn ibn Abī Isḥāq was installed as caliph.

The Year 228

Muḥammad ibn Dāwūd ibn ʿĪsā led the people on the pilgrimage.

“ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAmr told me: Abū al-Naḍr al-Farādīsī told me: ‘I was born in the year one hundred and forty-one.’” He died after al-Mubarraqa was captured; al-Mubarraqa’s capture took place after the death of the Commander of the Faithful, Abū Isḥāq.

The Year 229

Muḥammad ibn Dāwūd ibn ʿĪsā led the people on the pilgrimage.

The Year 230

Muḥammad ibn Dāwūd ibn ʿĪsā led us on the pilgrimage.

Abū Yūsuf said: I arrived from Egypt for the pilgrimage season. Ibn Dāwūd went out to meet Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm and entered consecration for an ʿumrah. He returned to Mecca—to his home and residence—intending to pray. He would leave his house for the mosque and pray two rakʿahs.

The Year 231

Muḥammad ibn Dāwūd ibn ʿĪsā led us on the pilgrimage.

In it, Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bukayr died on the fifteenth of Ṣafar. Ibn Dāwūd went out and entered consecration from outside [Mecca], then returned to his home, intending to pray in the Sacred Mosque.

The Year 232

Muḥammad ibn Dāwūd ibn ʿĪsā led us on the pilgrimage.

Hārūn died with six days of Dhū al-Ḥijjah remaining. His caliphate lasted five years and nine months, less six days. Jaʿfar ibn Abī Isḥāq was installed as caliph with six nights of Dhū al-Ḥijjah remaining, in the year two hundred and thirty-two. News of Hārūn’s illness had arrived before the pilgrimage season, and Zamzam water and perfume from the Kaʿbah had been sent to him. Then news of his death arrived on Thursday, on the sixteenth of Muḥarram, in the year two hundred and thirty-three.

The Year 233

Muḥammad ibn Dāwūd ibn ʿĪsā led us on the pilgrimage. He announced to us Hārūn’s death, which had occurred on the sixteenth of Muḥarram, in the year two hundred and thirty-three. He announced it from the pulpit, on the basis of a letter from his deputy to him, and allegiance was pledged to Jaʿfar. Then the dispatch pouch conveying news of Hārūn’s death reached him.

“In it, Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm al-Baghdādī died.”

“In it, Sulaymān ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Dimashqī died. Mālik ibn Ṭawq performed the funeral prayer over him. He was born in the year one hundred and fifty-three.”

The Year 234

Muḥammad ibn Dāwūd ibn ʿĪsā led us on the pilgrimage.

In it, Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Numayr died on the first of Shaʿbān, as did Abū Khaythamah and al-Qadīmīnī; Ibn Abī ʿAbdah al-ʿAnbarī died at the beginning of the year, while returning from a journey, one night before reaching Baṣrah; and Ibn ʿAbdah al-Hamdānī and Ibn Nufayl died. “Also, ʿAlī ibn Baḥr al-Barrī and Yaḥyā ibn Ayyūb al-Baghdādī.” And Abū Zayd ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī al-Ghamr al-Miṣrī.

In this year, Ītākh performed the pilgrimage, then returned, and his trace has endured to this day.

The Year 235

Muḥammad ibn Dāwūd ibn ʿĪsā led us on the pilgrimage.

“In it, ʿAlī ibn al-Madīnī and Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shaybah died.”

In it, the followers of Jaʿfar the tailor brandished their swords against the pilgrims in the Sacred Mosque, until people were trampled and some killed others. This was on Friday, the fifth day of al-Thamān.

In it, Ibn Ḥanẓalah was dismissed. He arrived with a letter dismissing him, sent by Abū al-ʿAbbās Muḥammad ibn Dāwūd. He resumed the judgeship in the year two hundred and thirty-six.

The Year 236

“In it, Ibrāhīm ibn al-Mundhir died in Muḥarram, returning from the pilgrimage; he died in Medina.”

Muḥammad ibn Dāwūd invoked blessings for Muḥammad, Ibrāhīm, and Abū ʿAbd Allāh, whom he appointed heir to the caliphate in Ṣafar, on Friday, the tenth of Ṣafar. The Shiʿi arrived by way of Baṣrah, and allegiance was pledged to them.

Abū Jaʿfar al-ʿAllāf died in Jumādā al-Ākhirah, on Thursday, the first day of the month.

Muḥammad ibn Fuḍayl died on the night of Friday, six days into Shaʿbān.

News of Muḥammad ibn Ḥātim ibn Maymūn’s death was brought to us by the porters who had arrived from Baṣrah, in Jumādā al-Ūlā.

In it, Shaybān al-Aylī died; the pilgrims announced his death.

Abū Yūsuf said: I performed the pilgrimage in this year. Al-Muntaṣir led us on the pilgrimage, and I returned to Baṣrah. Ibn Dāwūd was dismissed from Mecca, and ʿĪsā ibn ʿAlī was appointed over it. He left Baṣrah in Ramaḍān, in the year two hundred and thirty-seven, while I was in Fārs. He led the people on the pilgrimage, and Ibn Dāwūd performed the pilgrimage with him. Then he returned and died on the way.

ʿAbd al-Aʿlā died while I was in Baṣrah.

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Muʿādh, Ibn Ḥassān, ʿAbbās al-Nursī, and Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm died.

The Year 238

ʿĪsā ibn ʿAlī led the people on the pilgrimage, then returned and died while I was in Fārs.

“Ṣafwān ibn Ṣāliḥ al-Thaqafī al-Dimashqī died in the year two hundred and thirty-seven.” He was born in the year one hundred and sixty-eight or one hundred and sixty-nine.

The year two hundred and thirty-nine and the year two hundred and forty

Muḥammad ibn Dāwūd ibn ʿĪsā led the people on the pilgrimage. Abū Yūsuf said: I was in Sīrjān.

In the year two hundred and forty, while I was in Balkh, the son of Muḥammad ibn Dāwūd ibn ʿĪsā led the people on the pilgrimage.

In it, Abū Bishr Bakr ibn Khalaf died.

“Al-Walīd ibn ʿUtbah died in the year two hundred and forty. He was born in the year one hundred and seventy-six.”

“In it, Abū Rajāʾ Qutaybah ibn Saʿīd died, in Shaʿbān or Ramaḍān.”

In it, ʿAlī ibn Abī ʿAlī died.

The Year 241

Abū Yūsuf said: In the year two hundred and forty-one, Muḥammad ibn Dāwūd ibn ʿĪsā led us on the pilgrimage.

“Abū Tawbah died.”

Abū Qudāmah died in the month of Rabīʿ al-Awwal.

“Abū ʿAbd Allāh Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal died in the month of Rabīʿ al-Ākhir, on Friday.”

A messenger traveled from al-Karkh to Nīshāpūr in eight days to announce his death.

I returned from the year two hundred and forty-one to Palestine, and reached ʿAsqalān in twenty nights.

In the year two hundred and forty-two, I heard Hishām ibn ʿAmmār say: “I heard a session of ḥadīth from Saʿīd ibn Bashīr with our companions, but I did not write it down.” Hishām said: “I saw Bukayr ibn Maʿrūf and heard much from him, but I did not write down anything from him. He used to dye his hair red.” He said: “He wrote to Ibn Lahīʿah and to Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā—that is, Abū Mushir—and to a third man he mentioned, [requesting] one hundred and two ḥadīths.” I went to Egypt twice after that. I said:

“Has al-Layth ibn Saʿd and Ibn Lahīʿah died?” He said: “Yes.” He said: “I ate at al-Shāfiʿī’s and spoke with him, and he spoke with me, in Egypt.” Hishām ibn ʿAmmār was born in the year one hundred and fifty-three.

Abū Ṣāliḥ ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṣāliḥ told us: Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd told me, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: I heard Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, when ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf died, say: “O my mountain!”

Al-Makkī ibn Ibrāhīm told us: al-Jaʿd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān told me, from ʿĀʾishah daughter of Saʿd, that Saʿd ibn Mālik was informed of Saʿīd ibn Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Nufayl’s death—he had died at al-ʿAqīq—and Saʿd went out to him and washed him.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān told us: ʿAbd Allāh informed us: Sayf ibn Abī Sulaymān informed us: I heard Mujāhid say: “ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakr al-Ṣiddīq died. Ibn ʿUmar went out with him, and when he reached the mound above Mecca, he said: ‘Send the women back.’”

Al-Rabīʿ ibn Yaḥyā al-Murʾī told me: Shuʿbah told us: … [text continues]

ʿUyaynah, from Abū Bakrah, that he was present at the funeral of ʿUthmān ibn Abī al-ʿĀṣ.

Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr told us: Ismāʿīl ibn Ibrāhīm told us: ʿUyaynah informed us, from his father, who said: “I attended the funeral of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Samurah. Ziyād came out walking in front of his bier. When we had gone partway along the road, Abū Bakrah met us.”

Abū Bishr Bakr ibn Khalaf told me: al-Muʿtamir told us, from Qurrah ibn Khālid, from Abū al-Ḍaḥḥāk, who said: “I saw Muṣʿab ibn al-Zubayr walking without a cloak at the funeral of al-Aḥnaf ibn Qays.”

Abū Yūsuf said: They claimed he did it because of the heat.

ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn ʿImrān told me: Ibn Wahb informed us: Makhramah informed me, from his father, from Nāfiʿ, that he prayed with Abū Hurayrah over ʿĀʾishah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ—when they had prayed the dawn prayer.

ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn ʿImrān told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Usāmah informed us that Nāfiʿ, the freedman of Ibn ʿUmar, told him: “The funeral bier of Umm Kulthūm, ʿUmar’s wife, and that of her son, who was called Zayd, were placed [for the funeral prayer]. The imam on that day was Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ. Among the people were Ibn ʿAbbās, Abū Hurayrah, Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, and Abū Qatādah.”

Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr told us: Ismāʿīl ibn Ibrāhīm told us: Yūnus ibn ʿUbayd informed us, from ʿAmmār ibn Abī ʿAmmār, the freedman of Banū Hāshim, who said: “I was among those who went back and forth between Umm Kulthūm and her son Zayd. The governor of Medina performed the funeral prayer over them, and al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn were there.”

Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bukayr told us: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Lahīʿah told me:

Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb told me that ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Zayyāt told him that al-Walīd ibn ʿUtbah performed the funeral prayer over Abū Hurayrah.

ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn ʿImrān told me: Ibn Wahb said: ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith informed me, from [Ibn] Abī Ḥabīb, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Zayyāt.

ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Jurayj informed us: I said to Nāfiʿ: “Did Ibn ʿUmar ever pray in the middle of the graves in the morning?” He said:

“We prayed over ʿĀʾishah and Umm Salamah in the middle of al-Baqīʿ. Abū Hurayrah was the imam on the day we prayed over ʿĀʾishah, and ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar was present.”

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Maslamah told us, from Mālik, from Abū al-Naḍr, the freedman of ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from ʿĀʾishah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ—that she ordered that Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ be brought past her in the mosque, when he died, so that she might pray for him.

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī told us: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Muḥammad told us, from ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn Ḥamzah, from ʿAbbād ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr, from ʿĀʾishah, that she ordered that Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ be brought past her in the mosque so that she might perform the funeral prayer over him.

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā told us, [from Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid, from Mūsā] ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yazīd, that ʿAlī performed the funeral prayer over Abū Qatādah, [saying seven takbīrs over him, for he had been present at Badr].

Al-Ḥajjāj told us: Abū ʿAwānah told us, from Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid, from al-Shaʿbī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Mughaffal, that ʿAlī performed the funeral prayer over Sahl ibn Ḥunayf, saying six takbīrs over him.

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī told us: Sufyān told us: I heard al-Aʿmash say: I heard Abū Wāʾil Shaqīq ibn Salamah say: “When the day of Ṣiffīn came and the two arbiters had judged, I heard Sahl ibn Ḥunayf say:”

Qabīṣah told us: Sufyān told us, from Sālim ibn Abī Ḥafṣah, from Abū Ḥāzim, who said: “I myself saw al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī when al-Ḥasan died. He was saying this with his finger: ‘Let him go forward. Were it not a Sunnah, I would not have let him go forward.’” Saʿīd told us, from Sufyān, from Sālim ibn Abī Ḥafṣah, from Abū Ḥāzim al-Ashjaʿī, that Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī said to Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ: “Let him go forward”—meaning ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn—“for were it not a Sunnah, I would not have let him go forward.”

ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān told us, from Abū Ḥamzah al-Sukkarī, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from Muḥārib ibn Dithār, who said: “One of the Mothers of the Believers died—I think she was Maymūnah—and she instructed that Saʿīd ibn Zayd perform the funeral prayer over her.”

Abū ʿĀmir Qabīṣah and Abū Nuʿaym told us: Sufyān told us, from Abū Isḥāq, who said: “We went out with the funeral of al-Ḥārith al-Aʿwar, and so-and-so said—I did not retain [the wording] from Abū Nuʿaym.” Qabīṣah said: “[Then] ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yazīd al-Khaṭmī said: ‘Strip away…’”

“Remove the cloth”—Abū Nuʿaym said: “Uncover it, for he is only a man.”

Ismāʿīl ibn Ibrāhīm related to us. He said: Shuʿbah informed us, from Abū Isḥāq, who said:

Al-Ḥārith requested that ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yazīd al-Anṣārī perform the prayer over him. He said: “Remove the cloth from the grave.”

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā related to us. He said: Sufyān informed us, from Abū Isḥāq, who said:

Abū Maysarah requested that Shurayḥ perform the prayer over him.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān related to us. He said: ʿAbd Allāh related to us. He said: Shuʿbah said: We were at the funeral of Abū Maʿshar, and there was a crush around it. I said to Manṣūr—

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb and ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān related to us. They said: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, from Ayyūb, who said: We went out for the funeral of Zurārah ibn Awfā on an intensely hot day. Muḥammad remained standing “until he was placed in the burial niche.” This is the wording of Ibn ʿUthmān. Sulaymān’s wording is: He said, “We went out for the funeral of Zurārah ibn Awfā, and we reached the grave before the niche had been made.” He said: Muḥammad stood until he was placed in the burial niche. Ayyūb said: A report from Ibn ʿUmar reached Muḥammad, and I think he understood it incorrectly.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān related to us. He said: ʿAbd Allāh informed us. He said: Maʿmar informed us, from ʿAlī ibn Yazīd: When Zayd ibn Thābit was buried, Ibn ʿAbbās threw earth over him.

Abū Bishr related to me. He said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī related to me, from Ḥammād ibn Salamah, from Thābit, who said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Mughaffal requested that Abū Barzah perform the prayer over him.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān related to us. He said: ʿAbd Allāh informed us. He said: Sufyān said: Tamīm ibn Salamah requested that Manṣūr perform the prayer over him, but the governor arrived and performed the prayer over him.

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us. He said: Khālid ibn al-Ḥārith related to us. He said: Awf related to us, from Khuzāʿī, a descendant of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Mughaffal, who said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Mughaffal requested: “Let my companions take charge of me, and let Ibn Ziyād not perform the prayer over me.”

He said: Abū Barzah, ʿĀʾidh ibn ʿAmr, and a number of the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ—took charge of him.

Ibn Bukayr and Abū Zayd related to me. They said: Yaʿqūb ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān related to us, from his father, who said: I saw ʿAlī ibn Ḥusayn carrying the bier of ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtbah ibn Masʿūd.

Ibn Bukayr related to us. He said: Yaʿqūb ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān related to us, from Ḥamzah ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtbah ibn Masʿūd, who said: ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz used to say: “If ʿUbayd Allāh were alive, I would defer to his judgment in every matter.”

Ibn Numayr related to us. He said: Ibn Idrīs related to us, from his father and Ashʿath, from Abū Isḥāq, who said: I testified concerning Zirr ibn ʿAbd al-Salūlī, and Shurayḥ accepted my testimony alone.

Abū Bishr related to me. He said: Abū Qutaybah related to me, from Shuʿbah, from Nuʿaym ibn Abī— Hind, who said: I saw Abū Wāʾil at the funeral of Khaythamah, riding a donkey, with his hand on his head, saying: “Alas, my eyes!”

Bundār related to us. He said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and Ibn Abī ʿAdī related to us. They said: Shuʿbah related to us, from Ibn Ḥuṣayn, who said: ʿUbaydah al-Salmānī requested that al-Aswad ibn Yazīd perform the prayer over him. He said: It was near sunset, and he feared that al-Mukhtār would perform the prayer over him, so he hurried and performed the prayer over him.

Abū Mūsā related to us. He said: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar related to us, from Shuʿbah, from Yazīd ibn Abī Ziyād, who said: I saw Abū Juḥayfah when they passed by him with the funeral bier of Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī. He said: “One has found rest, and others have found rest from him.”

Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmmār related to me. He said: “Ibn Idrīs related to us, from Shuʿbah, from Nuʿaym ibn Abī Hind, who said: I saw Abū Wāʾil on a donkey at the funeral of Khaythamah, saying: ‘Alas, what grief!’—or words to that effect.”

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us. He said: Khālid ibn al-Ḥārith related to us. He said: Awf related to us, from Khuzāʿī, a descendant of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Mughaffal, who said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Mughaffal requested, saying:

“Let my companions take charge of me, and let Ibn Ziyād not perform the prayer over me.” He said: Abū Barzah, ʿĀʾidh ibn ʿAmr, and a number of the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ—took charge of him.

Muḥammad ibn al-Muthannā related to us. He said: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar related to us. He said: Shuʿbah related to us, from Yazīd ibn Abī Ziyād, who said: Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī died, and they passed by Abū Juḥayfah with his bier. He said: “One has found rest, and others have found rest from him.”

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā related to us. He said: Al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Ṣāliḥ informed us, from al-Ḥakam, from Ḥanash, who said: Sahl ibn Ḥunayf died, and he was brought to al-Raḥbah. ʿAlī performed the prayer over him, saying six takbīrs. Some of the people seemed to object to that, so we asked him about it. He said:

“He fought at Badr.” When we reached the cemetery, Qaraẓah ibn Kaʿb caught up with us among some of his people—or among some of the Anṣār—and they said: “Commander of the Faithful, we did not attend the prayer over him.”

He said: “Pray over him.” So they prayed over him, with Qaraẓah ibn Kaʿb as their imam. ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān related to us. He said: ʿAbd Allāh related to us. He said: Sufyān related to us, from Aslam al-Minqarī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abzā, from his father, who said: When the people fell into the affair of ʿUthmān, I met Ubayy ibn Kaʿb.

Ibn ʿUthmān related to us. ʿAbd Allāh related to us. Abū ʿAwānah related to us, from Sulaymān al-Shaybānī, who said: Usayr ibn ʿAmr related to us. He said: When so many people had been killed, I heard that Abū Masʿūd had set out, so I caught up with him at al-Silāḥayn. I said to him: “You had two companions— “—to whom I was inclined: Ḥudhayfah and Abū Mūsā.” He said: “He means that they had died.”

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us. He said: Sufyān related to us. He said: ʿAmr ibn Dīnār related to us, from Abū Jaʿfar, who told him, saying: Ḥarملah, the client of Usāmah, told me, saying:

Usāmah ibn Zayd sent me to ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib. Then he said to me: “He will ask you about me and say, ‘What kept him from coming to me?’ Convey my greetings to him, and tell him: ‘By God, if you were in the jaws of a lion, I would want to be with you. But this is a matter I do not approve of.’”

I went to ʿAlī and told him.

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us. He said: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, from Ayyūb, from Nāfiʿ, who said: Ibn ʿUmar arrived three days after the death of ʿĀṣim ibn ʿUmar. He went to his grave and performed the prayer over him.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rajāʾ related to us. He said: Zāʾid informed us, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAlqamah ibn Yazīd, who said: ʿAlī performed the prayer over Marthad ibn al-Mukaffif al-Nakhaʿī. Qaraẓah ibn Kaʿb and his companions came after the burial, and ʿAlī ordered them to perform the prayer over him.

Ibn ʿUthmān related to us. He said: ʿAbd Allāh informed us. He said: Sharīk informed us, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Jumalī, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, from Khaythamah: Abū Mūsā performed the prayer over al-Ḥārith ibn Qays al-Juʿfī after the prayer had already been performed over him; he caught up with them at the cemetery.

ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn Bakkār related to me. He said: Muḥammad ibn Shuʿayb informed us. He said:

Saʿīd ibn Bashīr informed me that Qatādah related to them: Bashīr ibn Kaʿb came to the grave of ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān after he had been buried, said the takbīr, and performed the prayer over him as one does over the dead.

Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr related to us. He said: Mahdī ibn Saḥnūn related to us, from Shuʿayb ibn al-Ḥabḥāb, who said: Ibrāhīm was in hiding from al-Ḥajjāj. He died and was buried at night. I attended the funeral prayer over him. Then, in the morning, I went to al-Shaʿbī and sat with him. He said: “Last night a man died who has left no one like himself behind.”

Abū al-Yamān related to us. He said: Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz related to us, from Ibn ʿAbd Rabbih, who said: Al-Ṣanābiḥī came to Damascus, and death came upon him. He said to Yazīd ibn Numrān:

“If I remain in this house for three days, find me an undisturbed grave.”

Ibn ʿUthmān related to us. He said: ʿAbd Allāh informed us. He said: Ibn Jurayj informed us. He said:

I heard Ibn Abī Mulaykah.

And ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz related to us, from Ibn Wahb, from Ibn Jurayj, with a similar report. He said:

I saw Ibn ʿAbbās when he had finished preparing the grave of ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Sāʾib. When the people stood around it, Ibn ʿAbbās got up and stood beside it.

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us. Al-Aswad ibn Shaybān related to us. He said: Al-Ḥasan was at the funeral of al-Naḍr ibn Anas. Al-Ashʿath ibn Sulaym al-ʿIjlī said: “Abū Saʿīd, I am pleased not to hear a sound at the funeral.” He replied: “There are people devoted to what is good.”

He said: That day, Mūsā ibn Anas also performed the prayer at the grave of al-Naḍr ibn Anas.

Nūḥ ibn al-Haytham al-ʿAsqalānī related to me. He said: Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd related to us, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: I saw Saʿd between the two poles of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān’s bier, carrying it on his shoulder.

Ibn ʿUthmān related to us. He said: My father informed me, from Shuʿbah, who said: I heard Saʿd ibn Ibrāhīm relate, from his father, who said: I saw Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ at the funeral of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf.

Al-Ḥumaydī related to us. He said: Sufyān related to us. Ismāʿīl related to us, from Abū Isḥāq, who said: I saw Abū Juḥayfah holding one of the poles of Abū Maysarah’s bier.

Ādam related to us. He said: Shuʿbah related to us. He said: Abū Bishr related to us that he heard Yūsuf ibn Māhak say: I saw Ibn ʿUmar at the funeral of Rāfiʿ ibn Khadīj.

Ibn Bukayr and Ibn Abī al-Ghamr related to us. They said: Yaʿqūb ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān related to us, from his father, who said: I saw ʿAlī ibn Ḥusayn carrying the bier of ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtbah ibn Masʿūd.

Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz al-Ramlī related to us. He said: ʿAbd al-Ghanī ibn [ʿAbd Allāh ibn] Nuʿaym al-Urdunnī related to us. He said: The funeral procession of Sulaymān ibn ʿAbd al-Malik came out before us, with Rajāʾ ibn Ḥaywah holding the front of the bier.

Hishām ibn ʿAmmār related to us. Maʿn related to us. He said: Hārūn, the client of Quraysh, related to us. He said: I saw al-Muṭṭalib between the two poles of Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh’s bier; he was outside with us.

Hishām said: Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh.

Abū Bishr related to us. Al-Muʿtamir related to us, from Qurrah ibn Khālid, from Abū al-Ḍaḥḥāk, who said:

I saw Muṣʿab ibn al-Zubayr walking in the funeral procession of al-Aḥnaf without a cloak. At that time, al-Aḥnaf was the foremost man among the people.

ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn ʿImrān related to me. He said: Ibn Wahb related to us. He said: Ibn Abī al-Zinād informed me, from his father, who said: I was sitting with ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar ibn Abī Ṭālib in al-Baqīʿ, when a funeral procession came into view before us.

Ibn al-Aṣbahānī related to us. He said: Sharīk related to us, from ʿĀṣim, from Abū Wāʾil, who said: Abū Maysarah requested: “When I die, walk quickly with me.”

Ibn ʿUthmān related to us. ʿAbd Allāh related to us. He said: Ibn Jurayj informed us, and ʿAṭāʾ informed me, saying: We attended the funeral of Maymūnah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ—with Ibn ʿAbbās, at Sarif.

Aḥmad ibn Yūnus related to us. He said: Abū Shihāb related to us, from Ibn ʿAwn, from ʿĀmir, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā, who said: We were with ʿUqbah ibn ʿAmr, Abū Masʿūd, at the bridge of al-Ṣāliḥīn when we caught up with a funeral procession.

Saʿīd related to us. He said: Ismāʿīl ibn Ibrāhīm related to us. He said: Ayyūb informed us, from Ibn Abī Mulaykah, who said: I visited Asmāʾ bint Abī Bakr after ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr had been killed. He said: A letter came from ʿAbd al-Malik ordering that his body be handed over to his family. I brought it to Asmāʾ. She washed him, shrouded him, applied camphor to him, then buried him. Ayyūb said: I think he said: She lived only three days after that, then died.

Ibn ʿUthmān related to us. He said: ʿAbd Allāh informed us. He said: Dāwūd ibn Qays informed us. He said:

My mother told me: Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ died at al-ʿAqīq. Dāwūd said: It is about ten miles away. She said: I saw him carried on the shoulders of men until they brought him there. He was brought into the mosque from the direction of Marwān’s Gate, and placed beside the houses of the Prophet ﷺ—in the courtyard of the Ḥijr. The imam performed the prayer over him, and then I performed it over him following the imam’s prayer.

Al-Ḥasan ibn al-Rabīʿ related to us. He said: Mahdī ibn Maymūn related to us. He said: I saw al-Ḥasan in the cemetery perform the prayer over Abū Naḍrah.

Ādam related to us. He said: Shuʿbah related to us, from Misʿar ibn Kidām, from Thābit ibn ʿUbayd, who said: I performed the prayer with Zayd ibn Thābit over his mother, and he said four takbīrs over her.

ʿAmr ibn Marzūq related to us. He said: Shuʿbah informed us, from Saʿīd ibn Ibrāhīm, from Ṭalḥah ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAwf, who said: I prayed behind Ibn ʿAbbās at a funeral when I was a young boy.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yūsuf related to us. He said: Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz related to us—I think from Sulaymān—that Ḥabīb ibn Maslamah performed the prayer over Shuraḥbīl ibn al-Simṭ.

Ibn ʿUthmān related to us. He said: ʿAbd Allāh related to us. He said: Sufyān said: Tamīm ibn Salamah requested that Manṣūr perform the prayer over him, but the governor arrived and performed the prayer over him.

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā related to us. Sufyān related to us, from Abū Isḥāq, who said: Abū Maysarah requested that Shurayḥ perform the prayer over him.

Ibn ʿUthmān related to us. He said: ʿAbd Allāh related to us. Al-Muʿtamir related to us: Al-Ḥasan visited Abū Naḍrah while he was ill. Abū Naḍrah said: “Pray over me.”

Abū ʿUmar al-Namirī and Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us. They said: Shuʿbah related to us. He said:

Abū Bakr ibn Ḥafṣ informed me. He said: I saw Ibn ʿUmar at the funeral of Rāfiʿ ibn Khadīj, and I heard Ibn ʿUmar say: “If you do not perform the prayer over him before the sun turns red, then do not perform the prayer over him until it has set.”

Ibn Qaʿnab and Ibn Bukayr related to us, from Mālik, from Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥarmalah, the client of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Sufyān ibn Ḥuwayṭib: Zaynab bint Abī Salamah died while Ṭāriq was governor of Medina. Ibn Abī Ḥarmalah said: I heard Ibn ʿUmar say to her family—

Abū Nuʿaym and Qabīṣah related to us. They said: Sufyān related to us, from Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid, from Ḥakīm ibn Jābir: Al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī performed ablution for al-Ashʿath when he was dying.

“Abū Nuʿaym ibn Dukayn related to us. He said: Ḥanash ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Laqīṭ al-Nakhaʿī related to us while we were in their mosque. He said: I saw Suwayd ibn Ghaflah going to a woman [of his] among Banū Asad, when he was one hundred and twenty-seven years old.”

Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd related to us. He said: Sharīk related to us, from ʿUthmān ibn Abī Zurʿah, from Abū Laylā al-Kindī, from Suwayd ibn Ghaflah, who said: I took the hand of the collector of the Prophet— I brought him a fine she-camel, and he said, “What sky would shelter me, and what earth would bear me, if I took the best of a man’s property?” So I brought him a she-camel from among the camels, and he accepted it.

Saʿīd related to us: Hushaym related to us: Hilāl ibn Khabbāb informed us, from Maysara Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Suwayd ibn Ghafala, who said: “The Prophet’s collector of alms came to us, and I went to him and sat with him. I heard him say, ‘My instructions are that we take nothing from a nursing animal, that we do not separate what is gathered together, and that we do not bring together what is scattered apart.’ A man brought him a large-humped she-camel and said, ‘Take it,’ but he refused.”

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us: Sufyān related to us: ʿĀṣim ibn Kulayb al-Jurmī related to us: “I saw Suwayd ibn Ghafala passing by us on foot on his way to Friday prayer. He was one hundred and sixteen years old, and he married a virgin when he was one hundred and sixteen years old.”

Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr related to us: Hushaym related to us: Mughīra related to us, from Abū Wāʾil, who said: “The Prophet’s collector of alms came to us. He used to take one she-camel from every fifty. I brought him a ram of mine and said, ‘Take the alms due on this.’ He said:

‘There is no alms due on this.’”

[Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shayba related to me: Abū Muʿāwiya related to us, from al-Aʿmash, who said: Shaqīq said to me, “Sulaymān, if only you had seen me when we were fleeing from Khālid ibn al-Walīd on the day of Bazākha. I fell from the camel, and my neck was almost snapped. Had I died that day, I would have been in the Fire. And I heard Shaqīq say, ‘That day I was eleven years old.’”]

“I was in the Fire. I heard Shaqīq say, ‘That day I was eleven years old.’”] In another copy: “twenty-one years old”.

Ibn Numayr related to me: Abū Muʿāwiya related to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Shaqīq, who said:

“Abū Bakr’s letter came to us while we were at al-Qādisiyya. At the bottom of it, he had written: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Arqam.”

Abū Saʿīd al-Ashajj related to me: Aḥmad ibn Bashīr related to us, from Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, who said: “I heard ʿAmr ibn Maymūn say, ‘In the Jāhiliyya, I worshipped al-Lāt.’”

[Abū Saʿīd related to us: ʿAmr ibn Qays ibn Yasīr related to us, from his father, from his grandfather Yasīr ibn ʿAmr, who had lived in the Jāhiliyya. He said, “The fool entered the state of consecration.”]

ʿUthmān ibn Abī Shayba related to us: Abū Muʿāwiya related to us, from al-Shaybānī, from Yasīr ibn ʿAmr, who said: “In the time of your Prophet, I was eleven years old.”

Ibn Abī Shayba related to us: Abū Bakr related to us, from Abū Isḥāq, who said: “ʿAmr ibn Maymūn lived in the Jāhiliyya.”

Abū Yaʿqūb Yūsuf ibn Muḥammad al-Ṣaffār related to me: Abū Usāma related to us, from Hishām ibn Ḥassān, from Ibn Sīrīn, who said: ʿUbayda said, “I became Muslim and prayed two years before the Prophet ﷺ died.”

Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī related to me: al-Naḍr ibn Shumayl related to us: Ibn ʿAwn informed us, from Ibn Sīrīn, who said: “ʿUbayda was the headman of his people. A young man said to him, ‘Abū Muslim …’”

Abū Nuʿaym related to us: ʿĪsā ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī related to us: “I heard Abū ʿAmr al-Shaybānī say, ‘I remember hearing of the Messenger of God ﷺ while I was tending my family’s camels at Kāẓima.’”

Abū Bishr Bakr ibn Khalaf related to me: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd related to us, from Hishām ibn Ḥassān, from Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn, from ʿUbayda, who said: “I became Muslim two years before the Prophet ﷺ died, but I did not see him.”

Ismāʿīl ibn al-Khalīl related to me: Ḥafṣ related to us, from Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid, who said: “ʿAmr ibn Maymūn stopped before Abū ʿAmr al-Shaybānī. We saw him smile. Then he came to us, and we said to him, ‘What did he say to you?’ He said, ‘I worshipped al-Lāt in the Jāhiliyya.’”

Abū Bakr related to us: Sufyān related to us: [Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid said: “I heard Abū ʿAmr al-Shaybānī—who lived to be one hundred and twenty—say:

‘My youth reached its full strength on the day of al-Qādisiyya, when I was forty years old.’”]

Abū al-Nuʿmān related to us: Thābit related to us: ʿĀṣim related to us, who said— “I asked Abū ʿUthmān, ‘Did you see the Prophet ﷺ?’ He said, ‘No.’ I asked, ‘Did you see Abū Bakr?’ He said, ‘No, but I followed ʿUmar when he rose.’ He said, ‘I gave alms to the Prophet ﷺ three times.’”

ʿUthmān ibn al-Haytham related to us: ʿImrān ibn Ḥudayr related to us, from Abū ʿUthmān, who was ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mall.

Abū Bishr Bakr related to me: Marḥūm related to us: “I heard Thābit say: Abū Rāfiʿ said, ‘The tastiest food I ate in the Jāhiliyya was sahʾ salʿ.’” [The reading “sahʾ salʿ” is obscure.]

Al-Ḥajjāj related to us: Ḥammād related to us, from ʿAlī ibn Zayd, from al-Ḥasan:

Al-Aḥnaf ibn Qays said: “While I was circumambulating the House in the time of ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān, a man from Banū Layth took my hand and said, ‘Shall I give you glad tidings?’ I said, ‘Yes.’ He said, ‘Do you remember that the Messenger of God ﷺ sent me to your people, Banū Saʿd? I began presenting Islam to them and calling them to it. You said to me, “He calls to Paradise and commands what is good,” twice. That reached the Prophet ﷺ and he said, “O God, forgive al-Aḥnaf.”’ Al-Aḥnaf used to say, ‘I have no deed on which I place greater hope.’”

Muḥammad ibn Abī Zakīr related to us: Ibn Wahb informed us: my father, Wahb, related to me: “I was told that Muʿāwiya ibn Abī Sufyān said to al-Aḥnaf ibn Qays, ‘By what means did you become a chief among your people, when you are neither the oldest nor the most noble among them?’ He replied, ‘I do not meddle in what I have been spared, and I do not neglect what I have been entrusted with.’”

“among your people, when you are neither the oldest nor the most noble among them?” He said, “I do not meddle in what I have been spared—or, he said, I avoid what I have been spared, and I do not neglect what I have been entrusted with.”

[Al-Ḥajjāj related to us: Ḥammād related to us, from Ḥumayd, from Abū ʿUthmān, who said:

“I have reached nearly one hundred and thirty years of age, and there is nothing about me that I do not find changed except my hopes: I find them as they were.”]

[Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us: Sufyān related to us: Hilāl al-Wazzān related to us: our old master ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUkaim—who had lived in the Jāhiliyya—was summoned by al-Ḥajjāj ibn Yūsuf. He rose, performed ablution, then prayed two rakʿas, then said, “O God, You know that I have never committed adultery, never stolen, never consumed an orphan’s property, and never slandered a chaste woman. If I am truthful, ward off his evil from me.”]

Abū Bakr related to us: Sufyān related to us: Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid related to us: “I heard Abū ʿAmr al-Shaybānī—who lived to be one hundred and twenty—say, ‘My youth reached its full strength on the day of al-Qādisiyya, when I was forty years old.’”

Ibn Numayr related to us: [Ibn Idrīs related to us, from Muḥammad ibn [Abī] Ayyūb, from Hilāl ibn Abī Ḥumayd, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUkaim, who said: “I will not help anyone against ʿUthmān again.” He was asked, “Abū Maʿbad, did you help in his death?” He said, “I count …”]

“mentioning his evil deeds as assistance in his death.”]

Salama related from Aḥmad: Hushaym was asked, “And Zirr ibn Ḥubaysh?” He said, “One hundred and twenty-two years”. He was asked, “And Suwayd ibn Ghafala?” He said, “One hundred and twenty-eight”. He was asked, “Who reported that?” He said, “Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid.”

Salama related from Aḥmad, who said: Ḥajjāj related to us: Abū Isrāʾīl said, “I was born after al-Jamājim, and al-Jamājim was in the year 83.” He said, “I was seventy-eight years old.”

ʿAlī related to us, from Abū Dāwūd, from [Shuʿba, from Abū Isḥāq, from Ḥāmid, who said: “I heard Saʿd say, ‘ʿAlī, the Devil of al-Rudhayma, was killed.’”] Abū Yūsuf was asked about this Ḥāmid. He said, “I do not know him.”

Salama related to me, from Aḥmad, who said: Abū Dāwūd related to us: Shuʿba informed us, from Abū Isḥāq, who said: Ḥudhayfa said, “Ṣila’s heart is made of gold.”

Salama related to us, from Aḥmad, who said: Abū Dāwūd related to us: Shuʿba informed us, from Yaʿlā, who said: “He used to relate to me from his father, leaving out the intermediary; he did not narrate it from anyone else. I said—” to him, “From whom did your father narrate?” He would say, “You do not accept reports from my father, though he lived into ʿUthmān’s time and lived through such-and-such!”

Salama related to us: Aḥmad related to us: Muʾammal related to us: “I heard Shuʿba say, ‘I asked Yūnus, “Did al-Ḥasan hear anything from Abū Hurayra?” He said, “No.”’ I heard Qatāda say, ‘Al-Ḥasan did not hear hadith directly from any of the Badr veterans.’”

Salama related to me, from Aḥmad, and Umayya ibn Khālid related to us: “I heard Shuʿba say: Khālid al-Ḥadhdhāʾ said, ‘Everything Muḥammad says, “I was informed on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbās,” he actually heard only from ʿIkrima. He met him during the days of al-Mukhtār in al-Kūfa.’”

Aḥmad said: Thābit ibn al-Walīd ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jumayʿ related to us: my father related to me: Abū al-Ṭufayl said to me, “I lived through eight years of the Messenger’s life ﷺ and I was born in the year of Uḥud.”

Salama related to us: Aḥmad related to us: Ḥammād ibn Usāma related to us:

Hishām informed us, from his father, who said: “Abū Bakr ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Hishām and I were turned back from the road in the time of the Battle of the Camel because we were deemed too young.”

[Abū Bakr ibn [Abī] Shayba related to us: ʿAbd al-Raḥīm ibn Sulaymān related to us, from ʿĀṣim al-Aḥwal, who said: Ṣubayḥ asked Abū ʿUthmān al-Nahdī—and I was listening—“Did you live to see the Prophet ﷺ?” He said to him, “Yes. I became Muslim in the time of the Messenger of God ﷺ and paid him alms three times, but I did not meet him. I went on campaigns during the time of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb. I was present at al-Qādisiyya, Jalūlāʾ, Tustar, Nahāwand, al-Yarmūk, Ādharbayjān, Mihrān, and Rustum. We used to eat clarified butter and leave the meat-fat. I asked him about al-ṭurūf. He said, ‘We did not ask about it’—meaning the food”

“of the polytheists.”]

Abū Bakr related to us: Ghundar related to us, from [Shuʿba, from Qays ibn Muslim, from Ṭāriq ibn Shihāb, who said: “I saw the Messenger of God ﷺ and I went on thirty-three or forty-three campaigns—from major expeditions to raiding parties—during the caliphates of Abū Bakr and ʿUmar.”]

Abū Saʿīd ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm related to me: al-Walīd related to us: al-Awzāʿī related to us: Ḥassān ibn ʿAṭiyya related to me, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Sābiṭ, from ʿAmr ibn Maymūn al-Awdī, who said: “Muʿādh ibn Jabal came to us in Yemen as the Messenger of the Messenger of God ﷺ to us. At dawn I heard a takbīr from a man with a hoarse voice. I offered him my greeting, and I did not leave him until I buried him, dead, in Syria. Then I looked for the most learned person after him, went to Ibn Masʿūd, and stayed with him until he died.”

[Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā related to me: Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā ibn al-Ṭabbāʿ related to us:
