Thābit ibn al-Walīd ibn Jumayʿ—at Hushaym’s door—related to me, from his father, from Abū al-Ṭufayl, who said: “I was born in the year of Uḥud. I lived through eight years of the life of the Messenger of God ﷺ.”]

Muḥammad ibn Ḥumayd related to us: Ibrāhīm ibn al-Mukhtār related to us, from ʿAnbasa, from ʿĀṣim, who said: “I asked Abū Wāʾil, ‘Whom did you live to see?’ He said, ‘While I was tending my family’s sheep, a mounted party came and scattered my sheep. One of them stopped and said, “Gather this man’s sheep for him, just as you scattered them.” Then they set off. I followed one of them and asked, “Who is that?”’”

“He said, ‘The Prophet ﷺ.’”

Muḥammad ibn Ḥumayd related to us: Salama and ʿAlī related to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ḥassān ibn Thābit, from his father, who said: “Ḥassān ibn Thābit lived one hundred and four years, and his father Thābit lived one hundred and four years. Mundhir lived one hundred and four years, and Ḥarām, his great-grandfather, lived one hundred and four years. Whenever ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ḥassān related this report to us, he would stretch his neck up toward us and bend his legs beneath him in the same way. He died at the age of forty-eight.”

ʿAlī related to us, from ʿUthmān ibn Nufayl: [Abū Mushir related to us: Saʿīd related to us, from Yūnus ibn Maysara, who said: “I asked Yazīd ibn al-Aswad al-Jurashī, ‘Abū al-Aswad, how old did he live to be?’ He said, ‘I lived to see al-ʿUzzā worshipped in the village of my people.’”]

[ʿUqba ibn Mukarram related to us: Yaʿqūb ibn Isḥāq related to us: Mahdī ibn ʿImrān al-Ḥanafī related to us: “I heard Abū al-Ṭufayl say, ‘On the day of Badr I was a boy. I had tied my waist-wrapper tightly around me, and I was carrying meat from the mountain down to the plain.’”]

[Aḥmad ibn al-Khalīl related to us: Yaḥyā ibn Abī Bukayr related to us: Nuʿaym ibn Maysara related to us, from one of them, from Suwayd ibn Ghafala, who said: “I am a contemporary of the Messenger—”

“of God ﷺ. I was born in the Year of the Elephant.”]

Aḥmad ibn Yūnus related to me: ʿĪsā ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān related to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAmr ibn Ḥurayth, who said: “I was in my mother’s womb on the day of Badr.”

Ḥarmala related to us: Ibn Wahb related to us: Ibn Lahīʿa related to us:

Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb related to me: “Qabīṣa ibn Dhuʾayb was born in the Year of the Elephant.”

Ibn Bukayr related to us: Yaʿqūb related to us: my father informed me that Ḥakīm ibn Ḥizām lived to be one hundred and twenty years old: sixty in Islam and sixty as a polytheist.

[Ibrāhīm ibn al-Mundhir related to me: Zayd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd ibn Aslam related to me: my father ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd related to me, from his father: “Aslam died at the age of one hundred and fourteen.”]

Ibrāhīm ibn al-ʿAlāʾ ibn al-Ḍaḥḥāk al-Zubaydī related to me: Ismāʿīl related to us, from ʿAyyāsh: ʿUmar ibn Muḥammad related to us, from Shuraḥbīl, who—as he claimed—was one hundred and sixty years old.

Muḥammad ibn Abī Usāma al-Ḥalabī related to us: [Mubashshir related to us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-ʿAlāʾ ibn al-Lajlāj, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: “I have not filled my belly with food since I became Muslim with the Messenger of God ﷺ.”] “I eat what suffices me and drink what suffices me.” He said: “He lived for one hundred and twenty years: fifty in the Jāhiliyya,” and seventy in Islam.

Abū Saʿīd ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm related to me: al-Walīd told us: Saʿīd—meaning Ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz—told us that Abū Idrīs al-Khawlānī was born during the days of the expedition of Ḥunayn and God’s defeat of Hawāzin.

Salamah related to us, from Aḥmad, who said: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd said: Muṭarrif was twenty years older than al-Ḥasan, and his brother was ten years older than al-Ḥasan. Muṭarrif died after the Plague of al-Jārif.

Aḥmad said: Yaḥyā said: Ibn Masʿūd and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd Allāh died when [the latter] was six years old, or thereabouts, and they used to consider Abū ʿUbaydah superior. Abū Yūsuf said: I fear this is a mistake.

Aḥmad said: Yaḥyā said: Ibrāhīm was not with Ibn al-Ashʿath.

Abū Bishr related to us: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān related to us: Shuʿbah related to us, from Yazīd ibn Abī Ziyād, who said: I asked Abū Wāʾil, “Which of you is older, you or Masrūq?” He said: “I am older than Masrūq.”

Abū Bishr related to us: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad related to us: Hammām related to us:

Qatādah related to us, from Abū al-ʿĀliyah, who said: “I learned the Qurʾān ten years after the death of your Prophet ﷺ.”

Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Samurah related to us: al-Muḥāribī related to us, saying: Ashʿath ibn Sawwār claimed that Shurayḥ died at the age of one hundred and twenty, and that Abū Rajāʾ al-ʿUṭāridī died at the age of one hundred and twenty-seven.

[Biographies of Men]

The ʿAbādilah among the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ and among those who saw him

(ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Quḥāfah, Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq)

Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq ﵁. Abū Bakr’s name was ʿAtīq ibn Abī Quḥāfah. Abū Quḥāfah’s name was ʿUthmān ibn ʿĀmir ibn ʿAmr ibn Kaʿb ibn Saʿd ibn Taym ibn Murrah ibn Kaʿb ibn Luʾayy ibn Ghālib ibn Fihr. al-Ḥajjāj ibn Abī Manīʿ related this to us, from his grandfather, from al-Zuhrī. ʿAtīq was his epithet; his name was ʿAbd Allāh. Abū Nuʿaym al-Faḍl ibn Dukayn related this to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Shurayk related to us: Ibn Abī Mulaykah related to me, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr, who said: “I was named after my grandfather Abū Bakr and given his kunya.”

Ibn Bukayr related to us: Ibn Lahīʿah related to us: ʿUmārah ibn Ghaziyyah related to me, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Qāsim, from his father, who asked ʿĀʾishah about Abū Bakr’s name.

She said: “ʿAbd Allāh.” I said: “But people say it was ʿAtīq.” She said: “Abū Quḥāfah had three sons, and he named one ʿAtīq, Muʿtaq, and ʿUtayq.” ʿAmr ibn Khālid related to us: Ibn Lahīʿah related to us, from Abū al-Aswad, from ʿUrwah, who said: “Abū Bakr’s name was ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān ibn ʿĀmir ibn ʿAmr ibn Kaʿb ibn Taym ibn Murrah.” Saʿīd ibn Sulaymān related to us: Isḥāq ibn Yaḥyā ibn Ṭalḥah related to us: Muʿāwiyah ibn Isḥāq related to us, from his father, who said:

ʿĀʾishah said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said, “Abū Bakr is one whom God has freed from the Fire.” From that day onward, people called him ʿAtīq.

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā related to us, from Isrāʾīl, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Barāʾ, who said: Abū Bakr bought a saddle from ʿĀzib for thirteen dirhams. Abū Bakr said to ʿĀzib, “Tell al-Barāʾ to carry it to my mount.” ʿĀzib said to him, “Not until you tell us what you and the Messenger of God ﷺ did when you left and the polytheists were pursuing you.” He said: “We set out from Mecca in the night, and we traveled through the night and the day until it was midday. When the sun stood at its zenith, I looked about to see whether there was any shade where we could take shelter. Then I saw a rock, and when I reached it, there was some shade beside it, so I leveled it. Then I spread out a fur for the Messenger of God ﷺ and said, ‘Lie down, Messenger of God.’ So he lay down. Then I went to look around me and see whether I could spot any pursuer. There I saw a shepherd driving his sheep toward the rock, wanting what I wanted”—meaning the shade. “I said, ‘Whose are you, young man?’ He said, ‘A Qurashī man’s,’ and named him, so I recognized him. I said, ‘Is there any milk among his sheep?’ He said, ‘Yes.’ I said, ‘Will you milk some for me?’ He said, ‘Yes.’ I told him to seize a ewe from his flock and told him to brush the dirt from its udder. Then I told him to shake his hands. He did so, striking one hand against the other. He milked me a little milk, and I had brought a water-skin for the Messenger of God ﷺ with a cloth over its mouth. I poured [the milk] into it until it had cooled from below. Then I went to the Messenger of God ﷺ and found that he had awakened. I said, ‘Drink, Messenger of God.’ The Messenger of God ﷺ drank until I was satisfied. Then I said, ‘The time to depart has come, Messenger of God.’ He said:

“Indeed.” So we set out, while the people were pursuing us, but none of them caught up with us except Surāqah ibn Mālik ibn Juʿshum, riding a horse. I said, ‘The pursuer has caught up with us, Messenger of God.’ He said, ‘Do not grieve; God is with us.’ When Surāqah drew near, and there were only a spear’s length or two between us and him, I said, ‘The pursuer has caught up with us, Messenger of God,’ and I wept. He said, ‘What makes you weep?’ I said, ‘By God, I am not weeping for myself; I am weeping for you.’ The Messenger of God ﷺ prayed against him, and his horse sank into the ground up to its belly. Surāqah leapt off it and said, ‘Muḥammad, I know this is your doing. Pray to God to deliver me from what I am in. By God, I will mislead those pursuing us behind me. Here is my quiver; take from it whatever you need. You will pass by my camels and sheep at such-and-such a place, so take whatever you need from them.’ The Messenger of God ﷺ said, ‘We have no need of your camels.’ The Messenger of God ﷺ prayed for him, and he went off, returning to his companions. The Messenger of God went on…” may ﷺ and I went with him until we reached Medina at night.

Abū al-Yamān related to us: ʿAṭṭāf ibn Khālid related to us, from Ṭalḥah ibn ʿAbd Allāh [ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān] ibn Abī Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, from his father, who said: I heard my father mention that he had heard Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq say: “I asked, ‘Messenger of God, is action according to what has already been decreed, or according to something to be begun anew?’ He said, ‘Rather, it is according to something already decreed.’

“I asked, ‘Then why act, Messenger of God?’ He said, ‘Everyone is made ready for that for which he was created.’”

And Abū al-ʿAbbās ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās,

son of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib. ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib’s name was Shaybah ibn Hāshim, and Hāshim’s name was ʿAmr ibn ʿAbd Manāf. ʿAbd Manāf’s name was al-Mughīrah ibn Quṣayy ibn Kilāb ibn Murrah ibn Kaʿb ibn Luʾayy ibn Ghālib ibn Fihr.

Al-Rabīʿ ibn Yaḥyā related to us, saying: Shuʿbah related to us: Abū Bishr Jaʿfar ibn Abī Waḥshiyyah related to us, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: “The Messenger of God ﷺ died when I had learned the Qurʾān’s muḥkam, and I was then ten years old.” He had been circumcised. Saʿīd was asked, “What is the muḥkam of the Qurʾān?” He said: the mufaṣṣal.

And Abū Muḥammad ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar,

son of Abū Ṭālib ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib ibn Hāshim ibn ʿAbd Manāf ibn Quṣayy ibn Kilāb ibn Murrah ibn Kaʿb ibn Luʾayy ibn Ghālib ibn Fihr.

Abū Nuʿaym al-Faḍl ibn Dukayn related to us: Misʿar related to us, from a man of Fahm, who said: I heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar say: “I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say, ‘The best meat—or the tastiest meat—is the meat of the back.’” He said: “We were with the Prophet ﷺ and they used to toss him meat.”

And ʿAbd Allāh ibn Mālik ibn Buḥaynah,

who was of Azd Shanuʾah and was an ally of Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib ibn ʿAbd Manāf.

Abū al-Yamān al-Ḥakam ibn Nāfiʿ related this to us, saying: Shuʿayb informed us, from al-Zuhrī.

Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us: al-Layth related to me, saying: Jaʿfar ibn Rabīʿah related to me, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Hurmuz al-Aʿraj, from Ibn Buḥaynah, who said: “When the Messenger of God ﷺ prostrated, he held his arms away from his sides until I could see the whiteness of his armpits.”

And Abū Bakr ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr,

son of al-ʿAwwām ibn Khuwaylid ibn Asad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā ibn Quṣayy ibn Kilāb ibn Murrah ibn Kaʿb ibn Luʾayy ibn Ghālib ibn Fihr. They were the in-laws of the Messenger of God ﷺ and were among the confederates of the Ḥilf al-Fuḍūl.

Zayd ibn Bishr and Abū al-Ṭāhir Aḥmad ibn ʿAmr ibn al-Sarḥ related to me. They said:

Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Aswad related to me, from ʿĀmir ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr, from his father, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Announce the marriage.”

And ʿAbd Allāh ibn Zamʿah ibn al-Aswad,

son of al-Muṭṭalib ibn Asad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā ibn Quṣayy ibn Kilāb ibn Murrah ibn Kaʿb ibn Luʾayy ibn Ghālib ibn Fihr.

ʿAyyāsh ibn al-Walīd related to me: ʿAbd al-Aʿlā related to us: Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq related to us, from al-Zuhrī, who said: ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Abī Bakr ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Hishām related to me, from his father, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Zamʿah, who said: “When the Messenger of God was overcome by illness, I was with him among a group of Muslims. Bilāl called him to prayer, and he said, ‘Tell someone to lead the people in prayer.’ I went out, and there was ʿUmar among the people; Abū Bakr was away. I said, ‘Stand up, ʿUmar, and lead the people in prayer.’ When ʿUmar said the opening takbīr, the Messenger of God ﷺ heard his voice. ʿUmar had a loud voice. The Messenger of God ﷺ said, ‘Where is Abū Bakr? God and the Muslims will not accept that.’”

He said: “So he sent for Abū Bakr, and Abū Bakr came after ʿUmar had performed that prayer [and led the people in prayer].” ʿAbd Allāh ibn Zamʿah said: ʿUmar said to me, “Woe to you! What have you done to me, Ibn Zamʿah? By God, when you told me to do it, I thought only that the Messenger of God ﷺ had ordered you to do so. Had it not been for that, I would not have led the people in prayer.” He said: “I replied, ‘By God, the Messenger of God ﷺ did not order me to do so. But when I did not see Abū Bakr present, I considered you the most entitled of those present to lead the people in prayer.’”

And ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Arqam al-Zuhrī.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Maslamah related to us, from Mālik, from Hishām ibn ʿUrwah, from his father: ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Arqam used to lead his companions in prayer. One day, I was present at the prayer, and he went to relieve himself. Then he returned and said: “I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say:

‘If one of you feels the need to relieve himself, let him do that before prayer.’”

And ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAdī,

son of al-Ḥamrāʾ al-Zuhrī.

Abū al-Yamān related to us, saying: Shuʿayb related to me, from al-Zuhrī, who said: Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān informed me that ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAdī ibn al-Ḥamrāʾ al-Zuhrī told him that he heard the Messenger of God ﷺ while he stood in the market of Mecca, say: “You are surely the best land of God and the dearest land of God to me. Were I not being driven out of you from you, I would not have left.”

And Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd,

son of al-Ḥārith ibn Shamakḥ ibn Makhzūm ibn Ṣāhilah ibn Kāhil ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Saʿd ibn Jadhīmah ibn Kaʿb ibn Saʿd, one of Banū Hudhayl, an ally of Banū Zuhrah and their sister’s son.

Al-Ḥajjāj related to us: Ḥammād related to us, from ʿĀṣim, from Zirr, from ʿAbd Allāh, who said: “The Messenger of God ﷺ and Abū Bakr came to me after fleeing from the polytheists, while I was tending sheep for Ibn Abī Muʿayṭ.”

Abū Yūsuf said: He was among those who migrated to Abyssinia and had been present at Badr.

And ʿAbd Allāh ibn Hishām al-Qurashī,

then one of Banū Taym.

Abū al-Aswad al-Naḍr ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār and Ibn Bukayr related to us, from Ibn Lahīʿah, from Zuhrah ibn Maʿbad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Hishām al-Qurashī, then al-Taymī, from his grandfather ʿAbd Allāh ibn Hishām—when he was a child, the Messenger of God ﷺ had stroked his head and prayed for him—who said: “We were with the Messenger of God ﷺ and he was holding…” the hand of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb. ʿUmar said to him: “By God, Messenger of God, you are dearer to me than everything except myself.” The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “No, by Him in whose hand is my soul—not until I am dearer to you than yourself.” ʿUmar said: “Then now, by God, you are dearer to me than myself.” The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Now, ʿUmar.”

And ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Asad ibn Hilāl,

son of ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn Makhzūm. ʿAbd Allāh’s kunya was Abū Salamah. Ḥajjāj related this to us, from his grandfather, from al-Zuhrī.

Abū Ṣāliḥ al-Ḥarrānī and Ibn Bukayr related to us. They said: Yaʿqūb ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān related to us, saying: ʿAmr ibn Abī ʿAmr, the client of al-Muṭṭalib, related to me, from al-Muṭṭalib ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥanṭab, from Umm Salamah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ who said: “One day Abū Salamah came to me and said, ‘I heard words from the Messenger of God that are dearer to me than red camels.’ He said, ‘I heard him say: “Whenever a believing servant suffers a calamity and says what God has commanded him to say, then says, ‘O God, reward me for my calamity and replace it for me with something better,’ God will reward him for his calamity and replace it for him with something better.”’”

And ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAyyāsh,

son of Abū Rabīʿah al-Makhzūmī.

It is said that he saw the Prophet ﷺ. He was born in Abyssinia during the migration.

Abū Ṣāliḥ related to me: al-Layth related to me: Khālid ibn Yazīd related to me, from Saʿīd ibn Abī Hilāl, from Abū al-Naḍr, from Ziyād, the client of Ibn ʿAyyāsh, from Ibn ʿAyyāsh: The Messenger of God ﷺ sat at the grave of Saʿd ibn Muʿādh. Then he uttered the words of return to God and said, “If anyone were to be spared the trial of the grave, its pain, or its constriction, it would have been Saʿd ibn Muʿādh. Yet he was indeed constricted once, and then relief was granted him.”

And ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Sāʾib al-Makhzūmī,

then al-ʿĀʾidhī.

Abū ʿĀṣim al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Makhlad related to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Yaḥyā ibn ʿUbayd, from his father, that ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Sāʾib said: I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say, “Our Lord, grant us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire”—that is, between the Yemeni Corner and the Black Stone, while he was circumambulating.

And ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Rabīʿah al-Makhzūmī

Ismāʿīl ibn al-Khalīl and Hishām ibn ʿAmmār related to me; they said: Ḥātim ibn Ismāʿīl related to us, from Ismāʿīl ibn Ibrāhīm al-Makhzūmī, from his father, from his grandfather ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Rabīʿah: The Messenger of God ﷺ borrowed from him a sum of some ten thousand. When the Messenger of God ﷺ returned from Ḥunayn, he came to him and said:

He said to me, “Call for me Ibn Abī Rabīʿah.” He said to him, “Take back what you lent me. May God bless your wealth and your children. The repayment for a loan is praise and fulfillment.” Hishām said: “Reward and fulfillment.” The Messenger of God ﷺ said, “Whoever cheats us is not one of us.”

And ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Umayyah ibn al-Mughīrah,

son of ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar ibn Makhzūm.

ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn ʿImrān related to us: Asad ibn Mūsā related to us—I suppose it is said that perhaps he was from Fāris—: Ibn Abī al-Zinād related to us, from his father, from ʿUrwah He said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Umayyah informed me that he saw the Messenger of God ﷺ praying in a single garment, with its two ends crossed over one another.

And Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar al-Khaṭṭāb,

son of Nufayl ibn ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā ibn Riyāḥ ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Razāḥ ibn ʿAdī ibn Kaʿb ibn Luʾayy ibn Ghālib ibn Fihr. Al-Ḥajjāj related this to us, from his grandfather, from al-Zuhrī.

Abū al-Yamān related to us: Shuʿayb informed us.

And al-Ḥajjāj ibn Abī Manīʿ related to us: My grandfather related to me. Both of them related it from al-Zuhrī, who said: Sālim ibn ʿAbd Allāh informed me that ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar said: I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: “Three men from among those who came before you set out, until nightfall brought them to a cave and they entered it. Then a rock rolled down from the mountain and blocked the cave against them. They said, ‘By God, nothing will save you from this rock except that you call upon God by virtue of your righteous deeds.’ One of them said, ‘O God, I had two elderly parents, and I would not give evening milk to my family or property before them. One evening I was delayed until dawn, and I did not return to them until they had fallen asleep. I milked their evening drink and brought it to them, but found them asleep. I felt scruple about waking them, and disliked giving evening milk to my family or property before them …’”

So I stood with the cup in my hands, waiting for them to wake, until dawn broke. They awoke and drank their evening milk. “O God, if I did that seeking Your countenance, then relieve us of the predicament we are in”—al-Ḥajjāj said: “of the pressure of this rock”—and it moved enough to open a gap, though they could not get out of it. The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “The other said, ‘O God, I had a cousin who was the person I loved most. I sought to have her yield herself to me, but she refused me until a year’s hardship befell her”—al-Ḥajjāj said: “she was afflicted by years of hardship”—“then she came to me. I gave her one hundred and twenty dinars on condition that she let me have her. She agreed. But when I was able to take her, she said:

‘It is not lawful for you to break the seal except by its right.’

I felt scruple about lying with her, so I turned away from her, though she was the person I loved most, and left the gold I had given her.

‘O God, if I did that seeking Your countenance, then relieve us of the predicament we are in’”—al-Ḥajjāj said: “of the pressure of this rock”—“and the rock shifted, though they still could not get out of it. The Messenger of God ﷺ said: ‘The third said, “O God, I hired laborers and paid them their wages, except for one man among them. He left what was owed to him and went away, so I invested his wage until it grew abundant …”’” the wealth, and I made a profit. After some time he came to me and said, ‘Abū ʿAbd Allāh, give me my wages.’ I said to him, ‘Everything you see is from your wage: camels, cattle, sheep, and slaves.’ He said, ‘Abū ʿAbd Allāh, do not mock me.’ I said to him, ‘I am not mocking you.’ He took all of it and drove it away, leaving nothing behind. ‘O God, if I did that seeking Your countenance, then relieve us of the predicament we are in’”—al-Ḥajjāj said: “of the pressure of this rock”—“and it shifted, and they came out of the cave walking.”

And ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĀmir ibn Rabīʿah,

an ally of Banū ʿAdī ibn Kaʿb, and he was from Yemen.

Saʿīd ibn Abī Maryam related to me: Yaḥyā ibn Ayyūb informed me:

Muḥammad ibn ʿAjlān related to me, from Ziyād, the client of ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĀmir ibn Rabīʿah, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĀmir ibn Rabīʿah, that he heard him say: The Messenger of God ﷺ came in to see my mother when I was a boy. I turned and went out, and my mother called me: “ʿAbd Allāh, come here, take this.” The Messenger of God ﷺ said to her, “What are you giving him?” She said:

“I am giving him dates.” He said, “Had you not done so, a lie would have been recorded against you.”

And ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ,

son of Wāʾil ibn Hāshim ibn Saʿd ibn Fahm.

Abū Saʿīd ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm related to us: Muḥammad ibn Shuʿayb related to us, from ʿAmr ibn Yazīd al-Baṣrī, from ʿAmr ibn Muhājir, from ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, from Yaḥyā ibn al-Qāsim, from his father, from his grandfather ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said, “No community has ever perished except through associating partners with God, and its association of partners began only with denying divine decree.”

And ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥudhāfah al-Sahmī

Abū al-Aswad and Ibn Bukayr related to us, from Ibn Lahīʿah, from Abū al-Naḍr, from Sulaymān ibn Yasār and Qabīṣah ibn Dhuʾayb, who both related from Umm al-Faḍl, the wife of al-ʿAbbās. She said: We were with the Messenger of God ﷺ at Minā during the Days of Tashrīq, when she heard someone calling out, “These days are days of eating, drinking, and remembrance of God.” She said:

“So she sent a messenger to ask, ‘Who is the man, and who commanded him?’ The messenger came to me and told me that it was a man called Ibn Ḥudhāfah, who said, ‘The Messenger of God ﷺ commanded me to do this.’”

And ʿAbd Allāh ibn Thaʿlabah ibn Ṣuʿayr al-ʿUdhrī,

an ally of Banū Zuhrah. It is said that he saw the Prophet ﷺ during the days of the Conquest, and that he wiped his face.

Abū al-Yamān related to us: Shuʿayb informed me, from al-Zuhrī, who said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Thaʿlabah ibn Ṣuʿayr related to me, and the Messenger of God ﷺ had wiped his face at the time of the Conquest.

Abū al-Nuʿmān related to us: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, from al-Nuʿmān ibn Rāshid, from al-Zuhrī, from Ibn Ṣaghīr, from his father, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said concerning the alms of breaking the fast, “Pay one ṣāʿ of wheat or grain for every male or female, young or poor, free or enslaved person. As for the rich person, God will purify him by it; as for the poor person, He will return to him more than he gave.”

And ʿAbd Allāh ibn Saʿd ibn Abī Sarḥ

Abū al-Aswad related to us: Ibn Lahīʿah informed us, from ʿAyyāsh ibn ʿAbbās al-Qitbānī, from al-Haytham ibn Shafiyy, Abū al-Ḥuṣayn, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Saʿd ibn Abī Sarḥ, who said: While the Messenger of God ﷺ and ten of his Companions were with him—Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, ʿUthmān, al-Zubayr, and others—on a mountain when it moved beneath them. The Messenger of God ﷺ said, “Be still, Ḥirāʾ, for upon you are only a prophet, a man of truth, or a martyr.” Abū Sarḥ ibn Ḥabīb ibn Judhaymah ibn Naṣr ibn Mālik ibn Ḥassal ibn ʿĀmir ibn Luʾayy. It is said that he died at ʿAsqalān after the killing of ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān.

Ḥarmalah related to me: Ibn Wahb informed us, from Ibn Lahīʿah, from Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb, who said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Saʿd remained at ʿAsqalān after the killing of ʿUthmān. He disliked being with Muʿāwiyah and said, “I would not join a man whom I knew to have desired the killing of ʿUthmān.” He remained there until he died.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Umm Maktūm

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, from ʿĀṣim from Abū Razīn: Ibn [Umm] Maktūm asked the Prophet ﷺ

and he was a man from Banū ʿĀmir ibn Luʾayy.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yūsuf related to us: Yaḥyā ibn Ḥamzah related to us: ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī related to me, from Ibn Muḥayrīz, from ʿAbd Allāh al-Saʿdī of Banū Mālik ibn Ḥassl, who used to relate that he came to the Messenger of God ﷺ.

Abū Yūsuf said: I do not know of anyone from Quraysh called ʿAbd Allāh, who heard from the Prophet and related from him, other than these men.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṭahfah al-Ghifārī

Ādam related to us, from Ibn Abī Dhiʾb, from al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from a son of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṭahfah al-Ghifārī, who said: My father related to me: The Messenger of God ﷺ saw me lying on my face and said, “This is a way of lying down that God dislikes.”

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Mughaffal

Abū Nuʿaym related to us: Abū Jaʿfar al-Rāzī related to us, from al-Rabīʿ, from Abū al-ʿĀliyah and others, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughaffal, who said: “I am indeed one of the group whom God mentioned: ‘Nor upon those who, when they came to you for you to provide mounts for them, you said, “I can find nothing on which to mount you”’ (Qurʾān 9:92). ʿAbd Allāh ibn Mughaffal said: I used to take some branches from the tree beneath which the Messenger of God ﷺ received the pledge, and use them to shade him.”

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sarjis, a Muzanī

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, from ʿĀṣim, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sarjis, who said: I came to the Prophet ﷺ and went around behind him. He realized what I wanted, so he drew his cloak away from his back. There was the seal, on the raised part of his shoulder, like a clenched fist, surrounded by moles resembling warts.

He was a Muzanī.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Shikhkhīr

Abū Muṭarrif, ʿĀmirī.

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ḥammād related to us; he said: Kahmas related to us, from Abū al-ʿAlāʾ Yazīd ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Shikhkhīr, from his father, ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Shikhkhīr, that he prayed with the Prophet ﷺ—and the Messenger of God spat, then rubbed it away with his sandals. He is ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Shikhkhīr, Abū Muṭarrif, and he is ʿĀmirī.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jarād

ʿĀmirī.

ʿAmr ibn Ḥabbāb al-Baṣrī related to us: Yaʿlā ibn al-Ashdaq related to us: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jarād related to us that he went out in a campaign of the Messenger of God ﷺ—and the Messenger of God ﷺ—said: “The one who enjoins what is right is like the one who does it.” Jarād was ʿĀmirī Khafājī, and Khafāja are from Banū ʿUqayl.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Hilāl al-Thaqafī

Abū Nuʿaym related to us; he said: Sufyān related to us, from Ibrāhīm ibn Maysara, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Hilāl al-Thaqafī, who said: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ—and said, “I nearly got killed over a young she-goat—or a sheep—from the alms.” The Messenger of God ﷺ—said, “Were it not that they are given…”

“the poor among the Emigrants, I would not have taken it.”

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Busr

Māzinī.

Abū al-Yamān related to us; he said: Ḥurayz ibn ʿUthmān al-Raḥabī related to us; he said:

I asked ʿAbd Allāh ibn Busr, a Companion of the Prophet of God ﷺ—and a Māzinī: “Was the Prophet ﷺ—an old man?” He said: “There were a few white hairs in his goatee.”

Abū al-Yamān related to us; he said: Ṣafwān related to us, from Sawāda and ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥajjāj, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Jundī, who said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Busr, the Companion of the Prophet ﷺ—said to me, “O son of al-Jundī.” I said to him, “At your service, Abū Ṣafwān.”

He said: “By God, some people will be transformed while they are drinking wine and playing musical instruments, until they become apes and swine.”

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rabīʿah al-Sulamī

Abū ʿUmar al-Namirī related to us; Shuʿbah related to us; he said: al-Ḥakam informed me; he said:

I heard Ibn Abī Laylā say, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rabīʿah: The Messenger of God ﷺ—was on a journey or in transit when he heard a man saying, “God is greatest, God is greatest. I bear witness that there is no god but God. I bear witness that Muḥammad is the Messenger of God.” He repeated what the man had said.

The Messenger of God ﷺ—said, “This is a shepherd, or a man away from his family.” When they descended into the valley, there he was: a shepherd, and there was a dead sheep. The Messenger of God ﷺ—said, “Do you think this is of little consequence to its owners?” They said, “Yes, by God, Messenger of God.” He said, “By God, this world is of less consequence to God than this sheep is to its owners.” Abū Yūsuf said: He is said to have seen the Prophet and to have been his Companion; he was Sulamī.

Abū Yūsuf said: “I know of no one from Muḍar or Rabīʿah, among those who saw the Prophet ﷺ—and narrated from him, whose name was ʿAbd Allāh apart from these men.”

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rawāḥah

Abū Nuʿaym related to us: Zamʿah ibn Ṣāliḥ, from Salamah ibn Wahrān, from ʿIkrimah, who said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rawāḥah said: “The Messenger of God ﷺ—forbade us to recite the Qurʾān while in a state of major ritual impurity.”

Abū Yūsuf said: “The permissibility is transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās. Rawāḥah ibn Mālik ibn Imriʾ al-Qays ibn al-Ḥārith ibn al-Khazraj, then from Banū Imriʾ al-Qays…” ibn Thaʿlabah ibn Kaʿb ibn al-Khazraj ibn al-Ḥārith ibn al-Khazraj, leader of Banū al-Ḥārith ibn al-Khazraj; he fought at Badr and was killed on the day of Muʾtah with Jaʿfar ibn Abī Ṭālib.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Zayd

[ibn Thaʿlabah] al-Anṣārī [ibn ʿAbd Rabbih][ibn Zayd] ibn al-Ḥārith ibn al-Khazraj, one of those who pledged at al-ʿAqabah and a veteran of Badr).

Abū al-Yamān al-Ḥakam ibn Nāfiʿ related to us; he said: Shuʿayb related to me, from al-Zuhrī, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, who related to him that ʿAbd Allāh ibn Zayd al-Anṣārī, one of Banū al-Ḥārith ibn al-Khazraj, was shown the call to prayer in a dream. He informed the Messenger of God ﷺ—of what he had seen of the call to prayer in his dream. The Messenger of God ﷺ—had already commanded the call to prayer, and so the Messenger of God ﷺ—said, “Rise, Bilāl, and give the call to prayer.”

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Zayd ibn ʿĀṣim

Al-Muʿallā ibn Asad related to us: Wuhayb related to us, from ʿAmr ibn Yaḥyā, from— ʿAbbād ibn Tamīm, that ʿAbd Allāh ibn Zayd was asked at the time of al-Ḥarrah, “There is Ḥanẓalah—or the son of Ḥanẓalah—over there, pledging allegiance to the people.” He said, “To what?” They said, “To death.”

He said, “To what?” They said, “To death.” He said, “I will not pledge allegiance to anyone to this effect after the Messenger of God ﷺ.”

He is Zayd ibn ʿĀṣim al-Māzinī.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAtīk al-Anṣārī

Aṣbagh ibn Faraj related to us; he said: ʿĪsā ibn Yūnus reported to us, from Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq, from Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm al-Taymī, from Muḥammad, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAtīk al-Anṣārī, from his father, who said: I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ—say: “Whoever leaves his home as a fighter in the path of God—” Then the Messenger of God ﷺ—made a gesture with three of his fingers and joined them together. “And where are those who fight in the path of God? If he falls from his mount and dies, his reward is assured with God; or if a creature stings him and he dies, his reward is assured with God; or if he dies a natural death, his reward is assured with God. Whoever is killed by a sudden blow has earned the abode [of Paradise].”

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yazīd

Ibn Numayr related to us; he said: Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh related to us, from Ibn Ḥuṣayn, from Abū Burdah, who said: I was sitting with Ibn Ziyād, and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yazīd was with him. The heads of the Khārijites were being brought in. Whenever they passed by with a head, I would say, “To the Fire!” He said: He said to me, “Do not do that, nephew, for I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ—say: ‘The punishment of this community will be in its worldly life.’”

ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAdī al-Anṣārī

Salamah ibn Shabīb and ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh related to us; the two said: ʿAbd al-Razzāq related to us; Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yazīd al-Laythī, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAdī ibn al-Khiyār, that ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAdī al-Anṣārī related to him: While the Messenger of God ﷺ—was sitting among the people, a man came to him asking permission to speak privately with him. He gave him permission, and the man spoke privately with him about killing a man among the hypocrites—he was seeking permission to do so. The Prophet ﷺ—raised his voice as he spoke and said, “Does he not testify that there is no god but God?” The man said, “Indeed, but his testimony does him no good.” He said, “Does he not pray?” The man said, “Indeed, but his prayer does him no good.” He said, “Those are the people whose killing I have been forbidden.”

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Ḥabībah al-Anṣārī

Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Uways related to us: Mujammiʿ ibn Yaʿqūb related to us, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, from one of the elders of his family, who said that he asked ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Ḥabībah al-Anṣārī, “What did you experience of the Messenger of God ﷺ?” He said:

One day the Messenger of God ﷺ—came to our mosque while I was a young boy. I came and sat beside him, on his right. Abū Bakr was on his left. A drink was brought, and he drank; then he passed it to me on his right. Then he stood and prayed, and I saw him praying in his sandals.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥārithah

Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Uways related to us: Muḥammad ibn Ṭalḥah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ṭalḥah ibn ʿUbayd Allāh al-Qurashī, then al-Taymī, related to us; he said: Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥārithah ibn al-Nuʿmān related to me, from his father, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥārithah, who said: When Ṣafwān ibn Umayyah ibn Khalaf al-Jumaḥī arrived, the Messenger of God ﷺ—said to him, “[With] whom are you staying, Abū Wahb?” He said, “I am staying with al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib.” He said, “You are staying with the man among Quraysh who loves Quraysh most.”

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥanẓalah ibn Abī ʿĀmir

Abū al-Naḍr Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm al-Qurashī al-Dimashqī related to us; he said:

Saʿīd ibn Yaḥyā al-Lakhmī related to us; Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq informed us, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā ibn Ḥibbān, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar, who said: I asked him, “Do you know whether Ibn ʿUmar performed ablution for every prayer, whether he was in a state of purity or not? What was the reason for that?” He said: Asmāʾ bint Zayd ibn al-Khaṭṭāb related this to me: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥanẓalah ibn Abī ʿĀmir related to us that the Messenger of God ﷺ—commanded ablution for every prayer, whether one was in a state of purity or not. When this became difficult for them, he commanded the use of the tooth-stick for every prayer.

He said: Ibn ʿUmar thought that he had the strength to do that.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd ibn Hilāl

ʿĪsā ibn Muḥammad related to me; he said: Zayd ibn al-Ḥubāb informed us, from Busr ibn ʿImrān al-ʿAttābī, who said: My patron, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Hilāl, related to me: My father took me to the Messenger of God ﷺ—and said, “Messenger of God, pray to God for him and bless him.” He said: I shall never forget the Messenger of God’s hand resting on my crown until I felt its coolness; he prayed for me and blessed me.

He said: He used to fast by day and keep vigil by night. His head and beard were white, and his hair was so abundant that he could scarcely part it.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām

Muʿādh ibn ʿAwd Allāh al-Baṣrī related to us: ʿAwf al-Aʿrābī related to us, from Zurārah ibn Awfā, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām, who said: When the Messenger of God ﷺ—arrived in Medina, the people rushed out ahead of him. They said, “The Messenger of God ﷺ—has arrived.” I went with the people to see his face. When I saw it, I knew that his face was not the face of a liar. The first thing I heard him say was: “O people, offer food, spread greetings of peace, maintain ties of kinship, and pray while people are sleeping; you will enter Paradise in peace.” The section on the Anṣār ends.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Awfā, Aslamī

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā related to us; he said: Sulaymān ibn Zayd, Abū Ādam, informed me, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Awfā, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ—said: “Mercy does not descend upon a people among whom there is one who severs ties of kinship.”

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Ḥadrad

And ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aqram al-Khuzāʿī.

Al-Ḥasan ibn al-Rabīʿ related to us; Ibn Idrīs informed us, from Ibn Isḥāq, who said:

Yaʿqūb ibn ʿUtbah related to me, from al-Zuhrī, from Ibn Ḥadrad, an Aslamī, from his father, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Ḥadrad, who said: I was among the cavalry of Khālid ibn al-Walīd on the day of Hawāzin.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Maslamah related to us; Dāwūd ibn Qays informed us, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aqram al-Khuzāʿī, from his father: He was with his father at al-Qāʿ in Namirah. A mounted party passed by them and halted beside the road. My father said to me, “Stay with your young camels while I go over to these riders and ask them.” He said: He went over, and I went with him, until the prayer was called. There was the Messenger of God ﷺ—among them. I would watch the Messenger of God’s two armpits, where the skin was pale, whenever he prostrated.

Abū Yūsuf said: “He said ‘Namirah’; the correct reading is ‘Thumrah.’ He erred in it—” just as Ibn al-Mubārak also erred in it.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥawālah

“Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us: Muʿāwiyah ibn Ṣāliḥ related to us that Ḍamrah ibn Ḥabīb related to him, from Ibn Zughab al-Iyādī, who said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥawālah al-Azdī, a Companion of the Prophet ﷺ—stayed with me. We had heard that he had been allotted two hundred, but he had insisted on only one hundred. I said to him, ‘Is it true what we heard, that he allotted you two hundred, but you insisted on only one hundred?’ By God, although he was staying with me, nothing prevented him from saying, ‘May you be bereft of your mother! Is one hundred each year not enough for Ibn Ḥawālah?’ Then he began to relate to us from the Messenger of God ﷺ. He said:

“‘The Messenger of God ﷺ—sent us out on foot around Medina to gain spoils, but we returned without gaining anything. When the Messenger of God ﷺ—saw the hardship we were in, he said: “O God, do not leave them to me, lest I prove too weak to care for them; do not leave them to the people, lest they become insignificant in their eyes or the people take the spoils for themselves at their expense; and do not leave them to themselves, lest they prove incapable of it. Rather, provide for them Yourself.” Then he said:

“‘“Syria will surely be conquered for you; the treasures of Persia and Byzantium will surely be divided among you; and each one of you will surely have such-and-such wealth, until one of you will be given one hundred dinars and be dissatisfied with it.” Then he placed his hand on my head and said: “Ibn Ḥawālah, when you see the caliphate settle in the Holy Land, earthquakes, tribulations, and events will have come…”’”

“The bones are nearer to people than this hand of mine is to your head.”

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥabashī

Abū Muḥammad ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā related to us: Ibn Jurayj informed us, from ʿUthmān ibn Abī Sulaymān, from Saʿīd ibn Muḥammad ibn Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥabashī, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ—said, “Whoever cuts down a lote tree, God will turn his head upside down into the Fire.”

Abū Mūsā ʿAbd Allāh ibn Qays al-Ashʿarī

Abū Nuʿaym related to us: Ṭalḥah ibn Yaḥyā informed us, from Abū Burdah, who said: Abū Mūsā came to ʿUmar and said, “May the Ashʿarī enter? May ʿAbd Allāh ibn Qays enter? May Abū Mūsā enter?” Then he left. ʿUmar sent someone after him, and Abū Mūsā said, “I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ—say: ‘Let each of you ask permission three times; if permission is granted, he may enter, and if not, let him return.’” He said, “If you do not bring me someone to testify to this, I shall punish you and do such-and-such to you.” So Abū Mūsā brought Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, who said, “O ʿUmar, have you sent for someone to punish the Companions of Muḥammad? I heard the Prophet ﷺ—say that.”

ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Jazʾ al-Zubaydī

Saʿīd ibn Abī Maryam related to us: Ibn Lahīʿah informed us, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Milīl, that his father told him that he heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Jazʾ al-Zubaydī recount: The Jews brought to the Messenger of God ﷺ—a Jewish man and woman who had committed adultery after having been married. The Messenger of God ﷺ—ordered that they be stoned. ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith said: “I was among those who stoned them.”

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Unays

Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Uways related to us: ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Qudāmah related to me, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Kaʿb ibn Mālik, from his uncle Miʿqal, from his father, from his mother, from her father, who said: The Banū Salimah said, “Who will pray with the Messenger of God ﷺ—and ask him about this night that we are seeking?” ʿAbd Allāh ibn Unays said, “I will.” I went to the Prophet ﷺ—on the evening of the twenty-second of Ramaḍān. I prayed the sunset prayer with him on the night of the twenty-third of Ramaḍān. Then I returned with him to his house. A little food was brought to the Messenger of God ﷺ—which looked small but was abundant and good. He said: I began to hold back so that the Messenger of God ﷺ—would have enough to eat. The Prophet ﷺ—said, “Eat, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Unays, for I can see what you are doing, and God will place a blessing in it.” He said: I replied:

“O Messenger of God, my companions from the Banū Salimah said, ‘Who will pray with the Messenger of God and ask him about this night that we are seeking, so that he may tell us about it, O Messenger of God?’” He said, “Seek it, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Unays, on this night.” When I had left, he said, “Seek it, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Unays, during the last ten nights.” ʿAbd Allāh said: It occurred to me that he had said what he did only because he feared people would rely on that night. He said: Whenever the twenty-third of Ramaḍān came, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Unays would come down from his land at Naqm and spend the night in the Mosque of the Messenger of God ﷺ—then return to his family.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muʿāwiyah al-Ghāḍirī

Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm related to us: ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith related to me:

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sālim related to me, from al-Zubaydī, who said: Yaḥyā ibn Jābir related to me:

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Jubayr told him that his father told him that ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muʿāwiyah al-Ghāḍirī told them that the Messenger of God ﷺ—said: “There are three things: whoever does them has tasted the sweetness of faith. Whoever worships God alone, for there is no god but God; gives the alms-tax on his property willingly, his heart content, making a contribution each year; and does not give” a decrepit or mangy one, nor a small and inferior one, nor a defective one, nor a ewe that has borne a lamb, nor one that is lying down—but rather something from the middle quality of your property. For God has not asked you for its best, nor commanded you to give its worst. And a servant purifies himself.” A man said, “What is a person’s purifying himself, O Messenger of God?” He said, “That he knows that God, mighty and exalted, is with him wherever he may be.”

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Qays

Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī, also.

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb and Ḥajjāj related to us, both saying: Ḥammād ibn Salamah related to us, from ʿAlī ibn Zayd, from ʿUmārah al-Qurashī, from Abū Burdah ibn Abī Mūsā, from his father, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ—said, “Our Lord will appear to us smiling on the Day of Resurrection.”

ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās

From ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb.

Abū ʿĀṣim al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Makhlad related to us: Jaʿfar ibn ʿUmārah ibn Thawbān related to us: I saw Muḥammad ibn ʿAbbād kiss the Stone and prostrate upon it. I asked, “What is this?” He said, “I saw ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās kiss it and prostrate upon it, and say: ‘I saw ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb kiss it and prostrate upon it, and say: I saw the Messenger of God ﷺ—do the same.’”

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Kaʿb al-Ḥimyarī

From ʿUmar ibn Abī Salamah, from Umm Salamah.

Aṣbagh ibn al-Faraj related to us: Ibn Wahb informed me: ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith informed me, from ʿAbd Rabbih ibn Saʿīd, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Kaʿb al-Ḥimyarī, from ʿUmar ibn Abī Salamah, that he asked the Prophet ﷺ—“May a fasting person kiss?” The Messenger of God ﷺ—said, “Ask this woman”—meaning Umm Salamah.

She told him that the Messenger of God ﷺ—did that. He said, “O Messenger of God, God has forgiven you your earlier and later sins.” The Prophet ﷺ—said, “By God, I am indeed the most God-fearing of you, the most fearful of Him, and the most knowledgeable of you about His limits.”

ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān ﵁

Son of Abū al-ʿĀṣ ibn Umayyah ibn ʿAbd Shams ibn ʿAbd Manāf ibn Quṣayy ibn Kilāb ibn Murrah ibn Kaʿb ibn Luʾayy ibn Ghālib ibn Fihr.

He said: He was given the teknonym Abū ʿAbd Allāh, then the teknonym Abū ʿAmr.

Abū ʿĀṣim al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Makhlad related to us, from ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn Jaʿfar, from his father, from Maḥmūd ibn Labīd, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān, who said: I heard the Messenger of God may ﷺ—[saying,] “Whoever builds a mosque for God, We will build for him its like in Paradise.”

ʿUthmān ibn Ṭalḥah ibn Abī Ṭalḥah

Abū Ṭalḥah’s name was ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā ibn ʿUthmān ibn ʿAbd al-Dār ibn Quṣayy ibn Kilāb ibn Murrah [ibn Kaʿb] ibn Luʾayy ibn Ghālib ibn Fihr.

Al-Ḥajjāj and Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us, both saying: Ḥammād related to us: Hishām ibn ʿUrwah informed us, from his father, from ʿUthmān ibn Ṭalḥah, that the Messenger of God ﷺ—entered the House and prayed two cycles between the two columns, facing them.

ʿUthmān ibn Maẓʿūn

Son of Ḥabīb ibn Ḥudhāfah ibn Jumah ibn ʿAmr ibn Huṣayṣ ibn Kaʿb ibn Luʾayy ibn Ghālib. He was present at Badr.

Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Uways related to us: ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Qudāmah ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad ibn Ḥāṭib al-Jumaḥī related to me, from his father and also from ʿUmar ibn Ḥusayn, from ʿĀʾishah daughter of Qudāmah ibn Maẓʿūn, from her father, from his brother ʿUthmān ibn Maẓʿūn, who said: “O Messenger of God, I am a man whom this celibacy in the military expeditions is causing hardship. Will you permit me to be castrated, so that I may castrate myself?”

He said, “No. Rather, you must fast, Ibn Maẓʿūn, [with fasting], for it is a protection.”

ʿUthmān ibn Abī al-ʿĀṣ al-Thaqafī

ʿAmr ibn Ḥafṣ ibn Ghiyāth related to us: My father related to us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Isḥāq, from Yazīd ibn al-Ḥakam, from ʿUthmān ibn Abī al-ʿĀṣ, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ—said, “He has indeed sheltered himself behind a substantial shield against the Fire: [the deaths] of three of his children before him in Islam.” The cemetery was mentioned in his presence, and he said, “Whoever is stingy or … is not one of us.”8

ʿUthmān ibn Ḥunayf al-Anṣārī

Saʿīd ibn Abī Maryam related to us: Ibn Lahīʿah related to us: al-Ḥārith ibn Yazīd al-Ḥaḍramī related to me, that al-Barāʾ ibn ʿUthmān al-Anṣārī told him, from Hāniʾ ibn Muʿāwiyah al-Ṣadafī, who said: I performed the pilgrimage in the time of ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān and sat in a gathering in the Mosque of the Prophet ﷺ. There was a man addressing them. He said:

“One day we were with the Messenger of God ﷺ—when a man came forward and prayed toward this column. He hurried away before completing his prayer, then left. The Messenger of God ﷺ—said, ‘If this man were to die, he would die with nothing of the religion.’ A man may indeed shorten his prayer and complete it.” I asked who the man was, and I was told: “ʿUthmān ibn Ḥunayf al-Anṣārī.”

Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib

Son of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib ibn Hāshim ibn ʿAbd Manāf ibn Quṣayy ibn Kilāb ibn Murrah ibn Kaʿb ibn Luʾayy ibn Ghālib ibn Fihr.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān related to me: ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mubārak informed us, from Yūnus, from al-Zuhrī, who said: ʿAlī ibn Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī informed us that Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī told him that ʿAlī said. And Saʿīd ibn ʿUfayr related to me: Ibn Wahb related to me, from Yūnus, who said: Ibn Shihāb said: ʿAlī ibn Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī informed me, from his father, that ʿAlī said:

“I had an old she-camel from my share of the spoils on the day of Badr, and that day the Messenger of God ﷺ—gave me an old she-camel from the fifth. When I intended to marry Fāṭimah, daughter of the Messenger of God ﷺ—I made an arrangement with a goldsmith from the Banū Qaynuqāʿ that he would travel and bring back some aromatic rushes which I intended to sell to the goldsmiths, so that I could use the money toward my wedding feast. While I was gathering for my two she-camels some camel saddles, sacks, and ropes, and my two she-camels were kneeling beside the room of a man from the Anṣār, I returned after gathering what I had gathered. I found that both their humps had been cut off, their flanks slit open, and pieces of their livers taken. I could not hold back my tears when I saw that sight. I said, ‘Who did this?’ They said:

‘Ḥamzah ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib. He is in that house, drinking with a group of the Anṣār. A singing girl is with him and his companions.’ She sang:

‘Come now, Ḥamzah, to the old, lean she-camels’

Ḥamzah rose, took his sword, cut off their humps, slit open their flanks, and took their livers. ʿAlī said: I set out to go to the Messenger of God ﷺ”

ﷺ—while Zayd ibn Ḥārithah was with him. The Messenger of God ﷺ—recognized from my face what had happened to me. The Messenger of God ﷺ—said, “What is wrong?” I said:

“O Messenger of God, by God, I have never seen anything like today. Ḥamzah attacked my two she-camels, cut off their humps, and slit open their flanks. Here he is in a house with a group of drinkers.” The Messenger of God ﷺ—called for his cloak and put it on. Then he set out on foot, and Zayd ibn Ḥārithah and I followed him until we came to the house where Ḥamzah was. He asked permission to enter, and they gave him permission. There they were, drinking. The Messenger of God ﷺ—began to rebuke Ḥamzah for what he had done. Ḥamzah was drunk, and his eyes were red. He looked at the Messenger of God ﷺ then raised his gaze and looked at his knees, then raised his gaze and looked at his navel, then raised his gaze and looked at his face. Then Ḥamzah said, “Are you anything but slaves of my father?” The Messenger of God ﷺ—realized that he was drunk, so he backed away on his heels, turned around, and left, and we left with him.

ʿAlī ibn Shaybān al-Ḥanafī

Then one of the Banū Suḥaym.

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb, Abū al-Nuʿmān, and al-Ḥasan ibn al-Rabīʿ related to us. They said: Mulāzim ibn ʿAmr related to us: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Badr informed us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAlī ibn Shaybān, from his father ʿAlī ibn Shaybān, who was one of the delegation that came to the Messenger of God with the Banū Suḥaym. He said: We prayed a prayer with the Prophet of God ﷺ. He glanced out of the corners of his eyes and saw a man who did not straighten his back in bowing and prostration. When he said the salutation, he said, “O people, there is no prayer for a man who does not straighten his back in bowing and prostration.” I prayed with the Prophet of God ﷺ—on another day. When he had said the salutation, there was a man behind the row who had prayed alone. The Messenger of God ﷺ—stood until he had finished his prayer. When he said the salutation, he said, “Repeat your prayer. There is no prayer for one who stands alone behind the row.”

Abū Muḥammad Ṭalḥah ibn ʿUbayd Allāh

Son of ʿUthmān ibn ʿAmr ibn Kaʿb ibn Saʿd ibn Taym ibn Murrah ibn Kaʿb ibn Luʾayy ibn Ghālib ibn Fihr ibn Mālik.

Abū ʿĀṣim al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Makhlad related to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn al-Munkadir related to me, from Muʿādh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿUthmān, from his father, who said: We were with Ṭalḥah ibn ʿUbayd Allāh, and they were in a state of consecration for pilgrimage. A bird’s meat was offered to him while Ṭalḥah was asleep. Some of us ate, while others abstained scrupulously. When he woke, he was told about it. He said, “Those who ate it were guided to the right choice,” and added, “We ate with the Messenger of God ﷺ.”

Ṭalḥah ibn Mālik

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us: Muḥammad ibn Abī Razīn related to us:

My mother related to me: Whenever a man of the Arabs died, Umm al-Ḥarīr would be deeply distressed. She was asked, “Umm al-Ḥarīr, we see that when a man of the Arabs dies, you are deeply distressed. Why?” She said, “I heard my patron say: The Messenger of God ﷺ—said—”

And he said: “Among the signs of the Hour’s approach is the destruction of the Arabs.”

Volume One

Ṭalḥa al-Naṣrī

Ādam ibn Abī Iyās related to us: Sulaymān ibn Ḥayyān related to us: Dāwūd ibn Abī Hind related to us, from Abū Ḥarb ibn Abī al-Aswad al-Daylī, from Ṭalḥa al-Naṣrī, who said:

“I came to Medina as a migrant. When a man came to Medina, he would have a host with whom he stayed; if he had no host, he stayed on the Ṣuffa. I came there without a host, so I stayed on the Ṣuffa. The Messenger of God ﷺ would pair two men together and allot them a mudd of dates. One day, while the Messenger of God ﷺ was at prayer, a man called out to him, saying, ‘Messenger of God, the dates have scorched our bellies, and our hide garments have worn through.’ The Messenger of God ﷺ praised God and extolled Him, and mentioned what he had suffered at the hands of his people. Then he said: ‘I remember that my companion and I spent a dozen or more nights with no food but the barīr—the barīr is the fruit of the arāk tree—until we came to our brothers among the Anṣār, who shared their food with us. Most of their food was dates. By God, besides whom there is no god, if I could provide you with bread and meat, I would feed you with it. A time will come upon you—or upon those of you who live to see it—when you will wear things like the coverings of the Kaʿba, and bowls will be brought to you morning and evening.’ They said, ‘Messenger of God, will we then be better off, or are we better off today?’ He said, ‘You are better off today. Today you are brothers; then, some of you will strike off the necks of others.’”

Volume One

Al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwām

Ibn Khuwaylid ibn Asad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā ibn Quṣayy ibn Kilāb ibn Murra ibn Kaʿb ibn Luʾayy ibn Ghālib ibn Fihr ibn Mālik ibn al-Naḍr ibn Kināna.

ʿAbd al-Salām ibn Muḥammad ibn Saʿīd al-Ḥaḍramī al-Ḥimṣī related to us: Baqiyya ibn al-Walīd informed us: Numayr ibn Yazīd al-Qutbī related to me, saying: I heard Quḥāfa ibn Rabīʿa ibn Quḥāfa relate from his father, that he heard al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwām, the intimate companion of the Messenger of God ﷺ say:

“The Messenger of God ﷺ saw a bone beside a piece of dung, picked it up, and said, ‘This is food for the jinn.’ Al-Zubayr said: ‘It is not permissible for anyone who has heard this hadith to cleanse himself with a bone or a piece of dung after the Messenger of God ﷺ said this.’”

ʿAbd al-Salām said: “I found it in three places: in one, the Prophet ﷺ sees a bone beside a piece of dung.”

Volume One

Al-Zubayr al-Kilābī

“Ṣafwān ibn Ṣāliḥ related to me: al-Walīd ibn Muslim related to us: Sayyid al-Kilābī related to us that he heard al-ʿAlāʾ ibn al-Zubayr al-Kilābī relate from his father, who said: ‘I saw the Persians defeat the Byzantines; then I saw the Byzantines defeat the Persians; then I saw the Muslims defeat the Persians and the Byzantines. All of this took place in fifteen years.’”

Volume One

Chapter on Saʿd

[Saʿd ibn Tamīm al-Sakūnī]

Sulaymān ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān related to me: al-Walīd ibn Muslim related to us, saying: ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-ʿAlāʾ and another related to us that they heard Bilāl ibn Saʿd relate from his father, who said:

“It was asked, ‘Messenger of God, what is due to the caliph after you?’ He said: ‘The same as what is due to me, so long as he is just in judgment, moderate in giving, and kind to his kin. Whoever does not do this is not of me, and I am not of him.’”

Volume One

Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ

He is Mālik ibn Wuhayb ibn ʿAbd Manāf ibn Zuhra ibn Kilāb ibn Murra ibn Kaʿb ibn Luʾayy ibn Ghālib ibn Fihr ibn Mālik ibn al-Naḍr.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yūsuf related to us, saying: I heard Mālik ibn Anas relate from Abū al-Naḍr, from ʿĀmir ibn Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, from his father, who said:

“I never heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say of anyone walking on earth that he was among the people of Paradise except ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām. He said: ‘This verse was revealed about him: “And a witness from the Children of Israel has testified to its like” [46:10],’” the verse.

Volume One

Saʿd ibn Sahl al-Sāʿidī

Abū Saʿīd ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm related to us: Ibn Abī Fudayk related to us, from Ibn Abī Ḥumayd, from Abū Ḥāzim, from ʿAbbās ibn Sahl ibn Saʿd, who said:

“I heard my father say: My grandfather related to me that the Prophet ﷺ said: ‘If I pray the dawn prayer and then sit in a gathering remembering God until the sun rises, that is dearer to me than a charge upon swift horses in God’s path until the sun rises.’”

Volume One

Saʿd ibn Mālik, Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī

Aḥmad ibn Ṣāliḥ related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb related to us: ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith informed me that Ibn Shihāb related to him that Abū Salama ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān related to him, from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, from the Messenger of God ﷺ who said: “Water is only from water.” Ibn Shihāb said: “Abū Salama used to act accordingly.”

Abū Yūsuf said: “In our view, this has been abrogated.”

Volume One

Saʿd ibn ʿĀʾidh

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Saʿd ibn ʿAmmār ibn Saʿd ibn ʿĀʾidh al-Qaraẓ related to us, saying: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAmmār related to me, and ʿAmmār— And ʿUmar, the two sons of Ḥafṣ ibn ʿUmar ibn Saʿd, from ʿAmmār ibn Saʿd, from his father Saʿd al-Qaraẓ, who said that he heard him say:

“This call to prayer is the call of Bilāl, which the Messenger of God ﷺ commanded him to make, and this is its form: ‘God is greatest, God is greatest; God is greatest, God is greatest. I testify that there is no god but God; I testify that there is no god but God. I testify that Muḥammad is the Messenger of God; I testify that Muḥammad is the Messenger of God.’ Then he repeats the words, saying: ‘I testify that there is no god but God; I testify that there is no god but God. I testify that Muḥammad is the Messenger of God; I testify that Muḥammad is the Messenger of God. Come to prayer, come to prayer; come to salvation, come to salvation. God is greatest, God is greatest; there is no god but God.’”

The call to commence the prayer is said once, each phrase once, and “The prayer is about to begin” is said once.

Volume One

Saʿd ibn al-Rabīʿ ibn ʿAmr

One of the Banū al-Ḥārith ibn al-Khazraj. He was a chief who took part in Badr and was killed on the day of Uḥud. ʿĪsā ibn Muḥammad related to us, saying: al-Ḥasan ibn Aʿyan al-Ḥarrānī informed us, saying:

ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd related to us: Saʿd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Ayyūb al-Anṣārī related to us, from his grandmother Umm Saʿd, daughter of Saʿd ibn al-Rabīʿ, who said:

“The Messenger of God ﷺ wiped my face. She used to say: ‘I heard my father say: I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: “Al-ʿAqīq is a blessed valley.”’”

Volume One

Saʿd ibn Muʿādh ibn Nuʿmān

Ibn Imriʾ al-Qays ibn Zayd ibn ʿAbd al-Ashhal ibn Jusham ibn al-Ḥārith ibn al-Khazraj ibn ʿAmr ibn Mālik ibn al-Aws; he fought at Badr. ʿAmr related this to us, from Ibn Lahīʿa, from Abū al-Aswad, from ʿUrwa.

Volume One

A man of the Anṣār called Saʿd ibn Zayd

ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb al-Ḥajabī related to us, saying: Ibrāhīm ibn Jaʿfar al-Anṣārī, a descendant of Muḥammad ibn Maslama, related to us, saying: A man of our people named Sulaymān ibn Muḥammad ibn Maḥmūd ibn Maslama related to me, from Saʿd ibn Zayd ibn Saʿd al-Ashhalī:

“A sword from Najrān was presented to the Prophet ﷺ—it was presented to the Prophet ﷺ. When it was brought to him, he gave it to Muḥammad ibn Maslama and said: ‘Fight with this in God’s path. When people’s necks are at odds, strike it against the stone. Then enter your house and remain as one cast aside, until a mistaken hand kills you or a decree of death comes upon you.’”

Volume One

Abū Muḥammad ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf

Ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Zuhra ibn Kilāb ibn Kaʿb ibn Luʾayy.

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā Abū Muḥammad related to us, saying: Ṭalḥa ibn Jubayr informed us, from al-Muṭṭalib ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Muṣʿab ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, who said:

“When the Messenger of God ﷺ conquered Mecca, he set out for al-Ṭāʾif and besieged them for nineteen nights, or eighteen, but did not conquer it. Then he advanced far at dawn or in the evening, then dismounted, then rested at midday. He said: ‘People, I have gone ahead of you, and I urge you to treat my family well, for your meeting place is the Pond. By Him in whose hand is my soul, you shall surely establish prayer and pay alms, or I shall surely send to you a man of mine, or one like myself, who will strike down your fighters and take your children captive.’ He said: The people thought he meant Abū Bakr and ʿUmar; then he took ʿAlī by the hand ﵃ all—and said, ‘This is the one.’”

“‘Treat my family well. Your meeting place is the Pond. By Him in whose hand is my soul, you shall surely establish prayer and pay alms, or I shall surely send to you a man of mine, or one like myself, who will strike down your fighters and take your children captive.’ He said: The people thought he meant Abū Bakr and ʿUmar; then he took ʿAlī by the hand ﵃ all—and said, ‘This is the one.’”

Volume One

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Samura

Ibn Ḥabīb ibn Shams ibn ʿAbd Manāf ibn Quṣayy ibn Kilāb ibn Murra ibn Kaʿb ibn Luʾayy.

Mahdī ibn Jaʿfar al-Ramlī related to us, saying: Ḍamra related to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shawdhab, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Qāsim, from Kathīr, the client of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Samura [from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Samura], who said:

“When the Messenger of God ﷺ equipped the army of hardship, ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān came with a thousand dinars, carrying them in his garment, and poured them into the lap of the Prophet ﷺ. I saw the Messenger of God ﷺ turning those dinars over in his hand and saying: ‘Nothing that Ibn ʿAffān does after this day will harm him.’”

Volume One

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Azhar al-Zuhrī

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā related to us, saying: Usāma ibn Zayd informed us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Azhar, who said:

“I saw the Prophet ﷺ in the year of the conquest, when I was a young boy. He was asking about the home of Khālid ibn al-Walīd. A man who had been drinking was brought to him,”

“and he ordered them to strike him with whatever they had in their hands. Some struck him with a whip, and some with a stick. The Prophet ﷺ threw dust over him.”

Saʿīd ibn Abī Maryam related to us, from Nāfiʿ ibn Yazīd, who said: Jaʿfar ibn Rabīʿa related to me, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Sāʾib, that ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Azhar related to him, from his father ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Azhar, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said:

“The likeness of a believer when he is afflicted by a fever or high temperature is like that of iron put into a fire: its dross goes away and its purity remains.”

Volume One

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ḥasana

An ally of Banū Zuhra.

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā related to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Zayd ibn Wahb, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ḥasana, who said:

“I set out with ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ. The Messenger of God ﷺ came out carrying a small hide shield, or something like one. He sat down and screened himself with it, then urinated while seated. My companion and I said, ‘Look at the Messenger of God ﷺ—how he urinates like a woman, seated.’ He came to us and said, ‘Do you not know what befell the man among the Children of Israel? If any of them got urine on him, he would cut it away with scissors. He forbade them to do that, and so he was punished in his grave.’”

Volume One

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakr al-Ṣiddīq

He was connected by alliance to Ḥilf al-Fuḍūl and al-Muṭayyibīn, and they were related to them by marriage; the Messenger of God ﷺ was among them.

Abū Saʿīd al-Juʿfī related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb related to me, saying:

ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith related to me that Bukayr related to him, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakr, or from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakr, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said:

“Alms are not lawful for a wealthy person, nor for a strong, able-bodied person.”

Volume One

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿUthmān al-Taymī

Abū ʿĀṣim al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Makhlad related to us, from Ibn Abī Dhiʾb, from Saʿīd ibn Khālid, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿUthmān—a man of Banū Taym—who said:

“The frog was mentioned in the presence of the Messenger of God ﷺ and he forbade killing it.”

Volume One

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Muʿādh al-Taymī

Abū Yūsuf related to us: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Mubārak related to me: ʿAbd al-Wārith related to us: Ḥumayd al-Aʿraj related to us, from Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm al-Taymī, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Muʿādh al-Taymī—who was one of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ—who said:

“The Messenger of God ﷺ addressed us while we were at Minā. Our ears were opened so that we could hear what he said even while we were in our lodgings,”

“so that we could hear what he said while we were in our lodgings. He began teaching us our rites until he reached the stone heaps. He said, ‘With pebbles the size of date pits,’ and placed the tips of his two index fingers one over the other.

“He ordered the Emigrants to lodge in the front part of the mosque, and ordered the Anṣār to lodge behind the mosque; then the people lodged afterward.”

Volume One

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ṣafwān al-Jumaḥī

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Abū al-Walīd Hishām ibn ʿAbd al-Malik related to us: Jarīr related to us, from Manṣūr, from Mujāhid, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ṣafwān, who said:

“When the day of the conquest came, I put on my clothes and went out. I happened upon the Prophet ﷺ as he had come out of the House. I asked ʿUmar, ‘What did the Messenger of God ﷺ do?’

“He said, ‘He prayed two units.’”

Volume One

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yaʿmur al-Daylī

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shayba related to me: Abū Shabāba related to us: Shuʿba related to us, from Bukayr ibn ʿAṭāʾ, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yaʿmur al-Daylī, that the Prophet ﷺ forbade the gourd vessel and the pitch-coated vessel.

Volume One

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Muzanī

Abū Yūsuf related to us; Abū al-Walīd Hishām ibn ʿAbd al-Malik related to us; Abū Maʿshar related to us; Yaḥyā ibn Shibl related to me, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from his father, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ—was asked about the people of the Heights. He replied: “They are people who were killed in the path of God while disobeying their parents. Their disobedience to their parents kept them from Paradise, while their being killed in the path of God kept them from the Fire.”

Volume One

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿUmayra al-Muzanī

Abū Yūsuf related to us; Ḥaywa ibn Shurayḥ related to us; Baqiyya ibn al-Walīd related to us, from Buḥayr ibn Saʿd, from Khālid ibn Maʿdān, from Jubayr ibn Nufayr, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayra:

The Messenger of God ﷺ—said: “There is no Muslim soul that its Lord takes whose desire is to return to you, even if it were to have the world and all that is in it, except the martyr.” The Messenger of God ﷺ—also said: “To be killed in the path of God is dearer to me than having the people of mud-brick houses and the people of tents.”

Volume One

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Khanbash al-Taymī

Abū Yūsuf related to us; ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh related to us; Jaʿfar ibn Sulaymān al-Ḍubaʿī related to us; Abū al-Tayyāḥ related to us. He said: A man said to ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Khanbash:

“Tell us what the Prophet ﷺ—did when the devils sought him.”

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān replied: “The devils descended upon the Messenger of God ﷺ—from the mountains and valleys. With them was a devil carrying a flame of fire, intending to burn the Messenger of God with it. When the Messenger of God ﷺ—saw them, he was frightened. Gabriel came to him and said, ‘Muḥammad, say [this].’ He asked, ‘What should I say?’ He said, ‘Say: “I seek refuge in the perfect words of God, which neither the righteous nor the wicked can overstep, from the evil of what He created, brought forth, and formed; from the evil of what descends from heaven and of what ascends into it; from the evil of what enters the earth and of what emerges from it; from the evil of the trials of night and day, and from the evil of those who come by night—except one who comes bringing good, O Most Merciful.”’” He said: “The devils’ fire was extinguished, and God routed them.”

Volume One

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿUqayl al-Thaqafī

Abū Yūsuf related to us; Aḥmad ibn Yūnus related to us; Zuhayr related to us; Abū Khālid Zayd al-Asadī related to us; ʿAwn ibn Abī Juḥayfa al-Suwāʾī related to us; ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAlqama al-Thaqafī related to us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿUqayl, who said: I set out with a delegation to the Prophet ﷺ. We came to the Prophet ﷺ—and made our camels kneel at the door. No man whom we had entered upon was more hateful to us than he was. He said: One of them spoke up:

“Messenger of God, why did you not ask your Lord for a kingdom like Solomon’s?” The Messenger of God ﷺ—laughed, then said: “Perhaps your companion has something better with God than Solomon’s kingdom. God sent no prophet without granting him a supplication. Some of them made it a [supplication for] faith, and, God willing, it was granted to them; others invoked it against their people when they disobeyed them, and they were destroyed by it. God has given me a supplication, and I have kept it with my Lord as intercession for my community on the Day of Resurrection.”

Volume One

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Khabbāb al-Sulamī

Abū Yūsuf related to us; al-Ḥajjāj ibn Nuṣayr related to us; Sakan ibn al-Mughīra al-Qurashī related to us, from al-Walīd ibn Ziyād, from Farqad Abū Ṭalḥa, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Khabbāb al-Sulamī, who said: I was beside the Messenger of God ﷺ—as he was preaching. He urged people to equip the Army of Hardship, but no one responded. ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān stood and said:

“Messenger of God, one hundred camels, with their saddle-cloths and packsaddles, as support for this army.” He said:

Then he urged them again, but no one responded. ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān stood and said: “Messenger of God, two hundred camels, with their saddle-cloths and packsaddles, as support for this army.” ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Khabbāb said:

“It is as though I can see the Messenger of God’s hand as he moved it and gestured with it, saying: ‘Nothing that ʿUthmān does after today will harm him.’”

Volume One

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Maʿqil al-Sulamī

Abū Yūsuf related to us; Muslim ibn Ibrāhīm related to us; al-Ḥasan ibn Abī Jaʿfar related to us; Abū Muḥammad related to us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Maʿqil al-Sulamī, the companion of al-Dathaniyya. He said: I asked, “Messenger of God, what do you say about the hyena?” He replied, “I do not eat it, nor do I forbid it.”

I said, “Since you do not forbid it, I shall eat it.” He said: I asked, “Prophet of God, what do you say about the desert monitor lizard?”

He replied, “I do not eat it, nor do I forbid it.” He said: I said, “Since you do not forbid it, I shall eat it.”

He said: I asked, “Prophet of God, what do you say about the hare?” He replied, “I do not eat it, nor do I declare it forbidden.” He said: I said, “Since you do not declare it forbidden, I shall eat it.” He said:

I asked, “Prophet of God, what do you say about the wolf?” He replied, “Would anyone eat that?” I said:

“Prophet of God, what do you say about the fox?” He replied, “Would anyone eat that?!”

Volume One

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn [Ḥabīb] al-Khaṭmī

Abū Yūsuf related to us; Hishām ibn ʿAmmār related to us; Ḥātim ibn Sulaymān related to us; Mūsā ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān related to us that he heard Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb al-Quraẓī ask his father about maysir [gambling]. He said: I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ—say: “Whoever plays maysir, then gets up to pray, is like someone who performs ablution with pus and the flesh of swine, then gets up to pray and says, ‘Will God accept his prayer?!’”

Volume One

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abzā

Abū Yūsuf related to us; Saʿīd ibn Asad related to us; Ḍamra related to us, from Ibn Shawdhab, from ʿAbd Allāh, from Hushaym, who said: I sat with ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abzā, and he said, “Shall I show you the prayer of the Messenger of God ﷺ?” We said, “Yes.” He stood and faced the qibla, then recited; then he bowed until every bone settled into its place. Then he rose until every bone settled into its place; then he prostrated until every bone settled into its place. Then he rose and did the same in the second rakʿa. Then he said, “This is how the Messenger of God ﷺ—prayed.”

Volume One

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Shibl al-Anṣārī

Abū Yūsuf related to us; Abū al-Yamān related to us; Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAyyāsh related to us, from Ḍamḍam ibn Zurʿa, from Shurayḥ ibn ʿUbayd, from Abū Rāshid al-Ḥabranī, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Shibl: The Prophet ﷺ—forbade eating the desert monitor lizard.

Volume One

Abū al-Aʿwar Saʿīd ibn Zayd

Son of ʿAmr ibn Nufayl ibn ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā ibn Riyāḥ ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Qurṭ ibn Razāḥ ibn ʿAdī ibn Kaʿb ibn Luʾayy ibn Ghālib ibn Fihr ibn Mālik ibn al-Naḍr ibn Kināna.

Abū Yūsuf related to us; Abū Nuʿaym related to us; Isrāʾīl related to us, from Ibrāhīm ibn al-Muhājir, who related to me from someone who heard ʿAmr ibn Ḥurayth report from Saʿīd ibn Zayd, who said: I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ—say: “People of the Arabs, praise God, who has removed stumbling from you.” Abū Yūsuf related to us; Abū al-Yamān related to us; Shuʿayb ibn Abī Ḥamza related to me, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Ḥusayn, who related to me from Nawfal ibn Musāḥiq, from Saʿīd ibn Zayd, from the Prophet ﷺ—that he said: “Among the worst forms of usury is assailing a Muslim’s honor without right. For kinship is a bond from the All-Merciful; whoever severs it, God will forbid Paradise to him.”

Volume One

Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ

Son of Umayya ibn ʿAbd Shams.

“Abū Yūsuf related to us; Abū Saʿīd al-Juʿfī related to us; ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ajlaḥ related to us; Hishām ibn ʿUrwa related to us, from his father: Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ said that the Messenger of God ﷺ—said: ‘Among the best of you in Islam are the best of you in …’” the Age of Ignorance.”

Volume One

Saʿīd ibn ʿĀmir ibn Ḥudhaym al-Jumaḥī

Abū Yūsuf related to us; ʿUthmān ibn Abī Shayba related to us; Jarīr related to us, from Yazīd ibn Abī Ziyād, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Sābiṭ, from Saʿīd ibn ʿĀmir ibn Ḥudhaym, who said: I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ—say: “People will be gathered for the reckoning. The poor among the Muslims will come, moving lightly as pigeons move. They will be told, ‘Stop for the reckoning,’ and they will say:

‘By God, we have no account to give, and we left nothing behind.’ He said: Then your Lord, mighty and glorious, will say, ‘My servants.’ Paradise will then be opened to them, and they will enter it seventy years before the people.”

Volume One

Saʿīd ibn Saʿd ibn ʿUbāda

Al-Anṣārī, then al-Sāʿidī.

Abū Yūsuf related to us; Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shayba related to us; Ibn Numayr related to us; Ibn Isḥāq related to us, from Yaʿqūb ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ashajj, from Abū Umāma ibn Sahl ibn Ḥunayf, from Saʿīd ibn Saʿd ibn ʿUbāda, who said: Among the houses where we lived was a man who was deformed weak. We were suddenly upon him while he was committing an indecent act with one of the household’s slave women. Saʿd ibn ʿUbāda brought his case before the Messenger of God ﷺ—and he said, “Flog him with one hundred lashes.”

They said, “Prophet of God, he is too weak for that. If we struck him one hundred times, he would die.”

He said, “Take a palm-stalk cluster with one hundred twigs and strike him with it once.”

Volume One

Saʿīd ibn Ḥurayth al-Makhzūmī

Abū Yūsuf related to us; Abū Nuʿaym al-Faḍl ibn Dukayn related to us; Ismāʿīl ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Muhājir related to us. He said: I heard ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr say: I heard ʿAmr ibn Ḥurayth say: I had an older brother called Saʿīd ibn Ḥurayth, who had been a Companion of the Prophet ﷺ. He said, “What an excellent brother he was!” He said:

“I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ—say: ‘Whoever among you sells a house or a piece of property [which] is likely not to be blessed for him, unless he invests it in something like it.’”

Volume One

ʿĀmir ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Jarrāḥ

Son of Hilāl ibn Aḥyab ibn Ḍabba ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Fihr; Abū ʿUbayda ibn al-Jarrāḥ.

Abū Yūsuf related to us; ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAmr al-Ḥarrānī related to us; Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān related to us, from Ibn Ghunaym al-Baʿlabakkī, from Hishām ibn al-Ghāz, from Makhūl, from Abū Thaʿlaba al-Khushanī, from Abū ʿUbayda ibn al-Jarrāḥ, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ may ﷺ—said: “This affair will remain upright, standing for justice, until a man from the Umayyads breaches it.”

Volume One

ʿĀmir ibn Wāthila, Abū al-Ṭufayl al-Bakrī

Abū Yūsuf related to us; ʿAmr ibn Sahl related to us; Mahdī ibn ʿImrān related to me, from Abū al-Ṭufayl, who said: I saw the Messenger of God ﷺ—and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd with a group of his Companions enter a house in Mecca. There was a velvet covering laid down, with a one-eyed boy beneath it. They lifted it. The Messenger of God ﷺ—said, “Do you testify that I am the Messenger of God?” The boy said, “I am the Messenger of God.” The Messenger of God ﷺ—said, “Seek refuge in God from the evil of this one.”

Volume One

Abū al-Faḍl al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib

“Abū Yūsuf related to us; ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā related to us, from Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid, from Yazīd ibn Abī Ziyād, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Nawfal, from al-ʿAbbās, who said: I said, ‘Messenger of God, when Quraysh meet one another, they meet with cheerful faces; but when they meet us, they meet us with faces we do not recognize.’ At that, the Messenger of God ﷺ—became very angry. Then he said: ‘By Him in whose hand is Muḥammad’s soul, faith does not enter a man’s heart until he judges in favor of God and His Messenger.’”

Volume One

ʿAbbās ibn Mirdās al-Sulamī

Abū Yūsuf related to us; Abū al-Walīd Hishām ibn ʿAbd al-Malik related to us; ʿAbd al-Qāhir ibn al-Sarī al-Sulamī related to us; Ibn Kināna ibn ʿAbbās ibn Mirdās al-Sulamī related to me, from his father, from his grandfather ʿAbbās ibn Mirdās: The Messenger of God ﷺ may ﷺ—supplicated for his community on the evening of ʿArafa, asking for forgiveness and mercy, and he supplicated at length. God answered him: “I have done so, except for the wrong some of them do to others.
