As for their sins between Me and them, I have forgiven them.” He said, “My Lord, You are able to reward this wronged person with something better than what he was wronged of, and to forgive this wrongdoer.” But He did not answer him that evening. When morning came at al-Muzdalifa, he repeated the supplication, and God answered him: “I have forgiven them.” Then the Messenger of God ﷺ—smiled. One of his Companions said to him, “Messenger of God, you smiled at a time when you would not usually smile.” He replied, “I smiled at God’s enemy, Iblīs: when he learned that God had answered my prayer for my community, he bent down, crying out woe and destruction, and threw dust upon his head.”

Volume One

Qays ibn Makhrama

Abū Yūsuf related to us; Ḥāmid ibn Yaḥyā related to us; Ṣadaqa related to us, from Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq, who related to me from al-Muṭṭalib ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Qays ibn Makhrama, from his father, from his grandfather Qays ibn Makhrama, who said: “I and the Messenger of God ﷺ—were born in the Year of the Elephant, so we were of the same age.”

Volume One

Qays ibn ʿĀṣim al-Tamīmī

Then one of the Banū Munqir.

Abū Yūsuf related to us; Qabīṣa related to us; Sufyān related to us, from al-Agharr, from Khalīfa ibn Ḥuṣayn, from his father: His grandfather Qays ibn ʿĀṣim came to the Prophet ﷺ—and accepted Islam. He instructed him to bathe with water and lotus leaves.

Qays al-Tamīmī

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Abū al-Walīd related to us: Qays ibn al-Rabīʿ related to me, from Jābir, from al-Mughīra ibn Shibl, from Qays al-Tamīmī, who said: Jarīr sent me as an envoy to the Messenger of God ﷺ. I came to him, and he passed by five women and greeted them.

Qays ibn al-Nuʿmān al-ʿAbdī

Then al-Rabʿī.

Abū Yūsuf related to us: ʿUthmān ibn al-Haytham, the muezzin, related to me: ʿAwf ibn Abī Jamīla related to us, from Abū al-Qamūṣ Zayd ibn ʿAlī, from one of the delegation who came to the Prophet of God ﷺ—as part of the delegation of ʿAbd al-Qays—unless it was Qays ibn al-Nuʿmān, for I have forgotten his name—who said: Among the gifts we presented to him was a tender branch and a waterskin of taʿḍūḍ dates. We placed them before him. I think he took one date from it, then put it back in its place and said, “Send it to Muḥammad’s family.” One of us said, “Messenger of God, our land is a land of hardship and disease, and only drinks agree with us. Which vessels are lawful for us, and which are forbidden to us?” He said, “Do not drink from the dried gourd, the hollowed-out log, or the pitch-coated vessel. Drink from a vessel whose mouth is tied over. If its contents grow strong break it with water; if you cannot manage it, pour it away.” We said, “Messenger of God, how would you know what the dried gourd, the hollowed-out log, and the pitch-coated vessel are?” He said, “I do not know! Which of Hajar’s fortresses is the more renowned?” He said, “I replied, ‘Al-Mushaqqar’.” He said: By God, I entered it, took its key, and stood at the spring of al-Zarāra, on the rock from which the water emerges. Then he earnestly prayed for ʿAbd al-Qays. He turned him away from the spring of the qibla, raised his hands, and said, “O God, forgive ʿAbd al-Qays! O God, forgive ʿAbd al-Qays!” He kept his hands raised and turned around until he faced the qibla, saying, “O God, forgive ʿAbd al-Qays, for they embraced Islam willingly, neither humiliated nor deprived of their due. Some people did not embrace Islam until they were humiliated and deprived of their due. The best people of the East are ʿAbd al-Qays; the best people of the East are ʿAbd al-Qays.”

Qays ibn Abī Ṣaʿṣaʿa

Abū Ṣaʿṣaʿa’s name was ʿAmr ibn Zayd ibn ʿAwf ibn Mabdhūl, of Banū Māzin ibn al-Najjār, and then of Banū ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf ibn Mabdhūl ibn ʿAmr ibn Ghanm ibn Māzin. He was one of the men of al-ʿAqaba and a veteran of Badr. ʿAmr related this to us, from Ibn Lahīʿa, from Abū al-Aswad, from ʿUrwa.

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bukayr related to us: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Lahīʿa related to me: Ḥibbān ibn Wāsiʿ al-Anṣārī related to me, from his father, from Qays ibn Abī…

Ṣaʿṣaʿa, who said: “Messenger of God, in how many days should I recite the Qurʾān?” He replied, “In fifteen.” He said, “I find that I am able to do more than that.” He replied, “Every week.” He said:

“I find that I am able to do more than that.” He said: He continued reciting it in this way for some time, until he grew old—or he would bind something over his eyes—and he used to recite it every fifteen days. He said, “If only I had accepted the first instruction from the Messenger of God ﷺ.”

Qays ibn Saʿd ibn ʿUbāda

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Abū al-Aswad al-Naḍr ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār related to us: Ibn Lahīʿa informed us, from Ibn Hubayra, who said: I heard a shaykh tell Abū Tamīm that he had heard Qays ibn Saʿd ibn ʿUbāda—when he was in Egypt—say: The Messenger of God ﷺ—said, “Whoever knowingly attributes a lie to me, let him take his place in Hell”—or, “a house [there].” “Indeed, whoever drinks wine will come thirsty on the Day of Resurrection. Every intoxicant is forbidden. Beware of al-ghabrāʾ.”

Zayd ibn Ḥāritha

son of Sharāḥīl ibn Kaʿb ibn ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā ibn Yazīd ibn Imruʾ al-Qays, al-Kalbī, the client of the Messenger of God ﷺ. He took part in Badr.

Abū Yūsuf related to us: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yūsuf related to us: Ibn Lahīʿa related to us: ʿUqayl informed me, from Ibn Shihāb, from ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr, from Usāma ibn Zayd ibn Ḥāritha, from his father: Gabriel came down to the Prophet ﷺ—at the beginning of his revelation and taught him ablution. The Prophet performed ablution, and when he had finished, he took water in his hand and sprinkled it on his private parts.

Zayd ibn Sahl

son of al-Aswad ibn Ḥarām ibn ʿAmr ibn Zayd Manāt ibn ʿAdī ibn ʿAmr ibn Mālik ibn al-Najjār. He was known by the teknonym Abū Ṭalḥa al-Anṣārī, and was one of the men of al-ʿAqaba and a veteran of Badr.

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us: al-Layth related to me, from Yaḥyā ibn Sulaym ibn Zayd, the client of the Messenger of God ﷺ—that he heard Ismāʿīl ibn Bashīr, the client of Banū Maghāla, say: I heard Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh and Abū Ṭalḥa ibn Sahl al-Anṣārī say: The Messenger of God ﷺ—said, “There is no one who abandons a Muslim in a situation where his honor is being diminished and his sanctity violated, except that God will abandon him in a situation in which he would wish for God’s help. And there is no one who helps a Muslim in a situation where his honor is being diminished and his sanctity violated, except that God will help him in a situation in which he would wish for God’s help.”

Zayd ibn Thābit al-Anṣārī

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Abū Thumāma related to us that Muḥammad ibn ʿAjlān related to him, from Abū al-Zinād, from Khārija ibn Zayd ibn Thābit, from his father: The Messenger of God ﷺ—said, “War is stratagem.”

Zayd ibn Khārīja al-Anṣārī

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Abū Saʿīd ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm related to us: Marwān ibn Muʿāwiya al-Fazārī related to us: ʿUthmān—meaning Ibn Ḥakīm—related to us, from Khālid ibn Salama, from Mūsā ibn Ṭalḥa, from Zayd ibn Khārija, a kinsman of Banū al-Ḥārith ibn al-Khazraj, who said: I asked the Messenger of God ﷺ “How should we invoke blessings upon you?”

He said, “Invoke blessings upon me; say: ‘O God, bless Muḥammad and the family of Muḥammad, as You blessed Abraham. Truly, You are Praiseworthy, Glorious.’”

Zayd ibn Saʿna

Abū Yūsuf related to me: Muḥammad ibn Abī al-Sarī related to me: al-Walīd ibn Muslim related to us: Muḥammad ibn Ḥamza ibn Yūsuf ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām related to me, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām said: When God intended to guide Zayd ibn Saʿna, Zayd said: “I recognized every sign of prophethood in Muḥammad ﷺ—when I looked at him, except for two things that I had not yet tested in him: his forbearance precedes his anger, and the greater the provocation, the greater his forbearance. I would therefore approach him gently, so that I might associate with him and learn how his forbearance stood up to anger. One day he came out from the apartments with ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib. A man came to him on his mount, looking like a Bedouin, and said, ‘Messenger of God, the people of the village of such-and-such have embraced Islam and entered the faith. I had told them that if they embraced Islam, sustenance would come to them in abundance. But they have been struck by a year of hardship, distress, and drought, and I fear, Messenger of God, that they will leave Islam out of greed, just as they entered it out of greed. If you think it appropriate, send something to help them.’ Zayd ibn Saʿna said: I came closer to him and said…”

“Muḥammad, will you sell me a known quantity of dates, due at a known time, from the orchard of such-and-such people?” He said, “No, Jew, but I will sell you a known quantity of dates, due at such-and-such a time, without specifying that it come from the orchard of such-and-such people.” I said, “Agreed.” He made the sale with me. I opened my money belt and gave him eighty dinars for a known quantity of dates, due at such-and-such a time. He gave the money to the man and said, “Hurry to help them, and relieve their need with it.” Zayd ibn Saʿna said:

Two or three days before the due date, the Messenger of God ﷺ—went out to attend the funeral of a man from the Anṣār. Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, and ʿUthmān were with him, along with a group of his Companions. When he had performed the funeral prayer and approached a wall to sit beside it, I came to him. I looked at him with a stern face, then seized the front of his shirt and cloak and said:

“Pay me what you owe me, Muḥammad! By God, I have always known you, Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, to delay repayment; I learned that from dealing with you.” I looked at ʿUmar. His eyes were rolling in his face like a revolving sphere. Then he glared at me and said, “Jew, would you do this to the Messenger of God? By Him who sent him with the truth, were I not afraid of missing him, I would strike off your head with my sword.” The Messenger of God ﷺ—looked at ʿUmar calmly and patiently, with a smile, then said:

“ʿUmar, he and I needed something other than this from you: you should have told me to repay him well, and told him to make his demand well. Go with him, ʿUmar, pay him what he is owed, and give him twenty ṣāʿs of dates in addition, to make up for the alarm you caused him.” Zayd ibn Saʿna said: ʿUmar took me with him, paid me what I was owed, and gave me twenty ṣāʿs extra. I said, “What is this extra amount?” He said, “The Messenger of God ﷺ—ordered me to give you extra to make up for the alarm I caused you.” I said, “Do you know who I am?”

He said, “No. Who are you?” I said, “I am Zayd ibn Saʿna.” He said, “The learned man?” I said, “The learned man.”

I said to him what I had said. He said, “What made you do to the Messenger of God ﷺ—what you did?” I said, “I recognized every sign of prophethood in the face of the Messenger of God ﷺ—when I looked at him, except for two things that I had not yet tested in him: his forbearance precedes his anger, and the greater the provocation, the greater his forbearance. I have now tested them. So I call you to witness, ʿUmar, that I am satisfied with God as Lord, Islam as religion, and Muḥammad as prophet. I also call you to witness that half my wealth—since I am among the wealthiest people—is charity for the community of Muḥammad.” ʿUmar said, “Or for some of them, since you cannot provide for them all.” ʿUmar and Zayd returned to the Messenger of God ﷺ. Zayd said, “I bear witness that there is no god but God and that Muḥammad is the Messenger of God.” He believed in him, affirmed him, pledged allegiance to him, and took part with him in many campaigns. Then he died in the expedition to Tabūk, advancing and not retreating—may God have mercy on Zayd.

Al-Walīd said: Muḥammad ibn Ḥamza ibn Yūsuf ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām related all of this to me, from his father, from his grandfather, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām.

Zayd ibn Arqam, Abū ʿAmr

Abū Yūsuf related to me: ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā related to me: Isrāʾīl informed us, from ʿUthmān, from Iyās ibn Abī Ramla al-Shāmī, who said: I heard Muʿāwiya ask Zayd ibn Arqam, “Were you present with the Messenger of God ﷺ—on two festivals that fell on the same day?” He said, “Yes.” [He] said, “What did he do?” He said, “He performed the festival prayer, then granted an exemption from the Friday prayer, saying, ‘Whoever wishes to pray may do so.’”

Usāma ibn Zayd ibn Ḥāritha

Abū Yūsuf related to us: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yūsuf related to us: al-Walīd ibn Muslim related to us: Muḥammad ibn al-Muhājir related to us, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk al-Maʿāfirī, from Sulaymān ibn Mūsā, from Kurayb, the client of Ibn ʿAbbās, who related to me from Usāma ibn Zayd: The Messenger of God ﷺ—said to his Companions, “Is there anyone eager to strive for Paradise? Paradise has no equal in rank or merit. By the Lord of the Kaʿba, it is a shimmering light, a swaying fragrant plant, a lofty palace, a flowing river, abundant ripe fruit, and a beautiful, lovely wife amid joy and bliss. In an eternal dwelling, amid joy, bliss, and radiance; in a lofty, splendid, sound abode.” They said, “We are eager to strive for it, Messenger of God.” [He said,] “Say, ‘If God Most High wills.’” Then he mentioned the jihād and urged them to it.

Usāma ibn ʿUmayr al-Hudhalī

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Muslim ibn Ibrāhīm related to us: Shuʿba related to us, from Qatāda, from Abū al-Malīḥ, from his father, that the Prophet ﷺ—said, “God does not accept a prayer without purification, nor charity from misappropriated spoils.”

Usāma ibn Sharīk al-ʿĀmirī

Abū Yūsuf related to us: ʿUthmān ibn Abī Shayba related to me: Jarīr related to us, from al-Shaybānī, from Ziyād ibn ʿAlāqa, from Usāma ibn Sharīk, who said: I went out with the Messenger of God ﷺ—to perform the pilgrimage. People would come to him, some saying, “Messenger of God…”

“I hastened before making the circumambulation,” or, “I delayed something,” or, “I did something ahead of its proper time.” He would say:

“There is no blame, no blame—except for a man who violates a Muslim’s honor unjustly. That is blame and ruin.”

Muʿāwiya ibn Abī Sufyān

son of Ṣakhr ibn Ḥarb ibn Umayya ibn ʿAbd Shams. Muʿāwiya’s teknonym was Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān.

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Junāda ibn Muḥammad al-Muzanī al-Dimashqī related to us: ʿĪsā ibn Yūnus ibn Abī Isḥāq al-Subayʿī related to us, from al-Awzāʿī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Saʿd, from al-Ṣanābiḥī, from Muʿāwiya ibn Abī Sufyān, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ—forbade obscure and difficult questions.

Muʿāwiya ibn al-Ḥakam al-Sulamī

from Qays ʿAylān.

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Yaḥyā ibn Ṣāliḥ al-Wuḥāẓī related to me: Fulayḥ ibn Sulaymān related to us, from Hilāl ibn ʿAlī, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār, from Muʿāwiya ibn al-Ḥakam al-Sulamī, who said: When I came to the Messenger of God ﷺ—and learned the teachings of Islam, one of the things I learned was this: I was told, “When you sneeze, praise God; and when someone sneezes and praises God, say, ‘May God have mercy on you.’”

Muʿāwiya ibn Ḥayda al-Qushayrī

one of Banū ʿĀmir ibn Ṣaʿṣaʿa, of Hawāzin.

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Makkī ibn Ibrāhīm related to us. Bahz said that he mentioned it, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: When food was brought to the Messenger of God ﷺ—he would ask whether it was a gift or charity. If they said it was a gift, he would reach out his hand; if they said it was charity, he would say to his Companions:

“Eat.”

Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaḥsh

of Banū Asad Khuzayma, an ally of Banū Umayya ibn ʿAbd Shams.

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Ibn Abī Maryam related to me: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn Abī Kathīr informed us: al-ʿAlāʾ ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān informed me: Abū Kathīr, the client of Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaḥsh, informed me, from his patron Muḥammad, who said: I was with the Messenger of God ﷺ—and he passed by Maʿmar, who was sitting by his house in the market with his thighs uncovered. The Messenger of God ﷺ—said, “Maʿmar, cover your thighs, for the thighs are nakedness.”

Muḥammad ibn Ḥāṭib al-Jumaḥī

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Muḥammad ibn Muʿāwiya related to us: Sharīk related to us, from Simāk ibn Ḥarb, from Muḥammad ibn Ḥāṭib, who said: I came close to a cooking pot of ours, and my hand was burned by it. My mother took me to al-Baṭḥāʾ and said, “Messenger of God, this son of mine has burned his hand.” He began to speak words whose meaning I do not know, but he blew gently. I asked about it during ʿUthmān’s caliphate, and they said, “The Messenger of God used to…”

And Muḥammad ibn Maslamah

Son of [Salamah] ibn Khālid ibn ʿAdī ibn Mujdiʿah ibn al-Ḥārith; he was a participant at Badr. Abū Yūsuf related to us, saying: ʿAmr related this to me, from Ibn Lahīʿah, from Abū al-Aswad, from ʿUrwah.

Abū Yūsuf related to us; ʿAmr ibn ʿAwn related to us; Abū Shihāb ʿAbd Rabbih ibn Nāfiʿ related to us, from al-Ḥajjāj, from Ibn Abī Mulaykah, from Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān ibn Abī Ḥathmah, from his uncle Sahl ibn Abī Ḥathmah, who said: I saw Muḥammad ibn Maslamah following a woman with his gaze on a rooftop terrace. She was called Buthaynah daughter of al-Ḍaḥḥāk, the sister of Abū Jubayrah. She said:

“Do you do this when you are a Companion of the Messenger of God ﷺ?” He replied: “Yes. The Messenger of God ﷺ—said: ‘If God places in a man’s heart the intention to propose to a woman, there is no harm in his looking at her.’”

And Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām

Abū Yūsuf related to us; ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Shaqīq related to us; ʿAbd Allāh related to us; Mālik ibn Mighwal informed us, saying: I heard Sayyār Abū al-Ḥakam relate from Shahr ibn Ḥawshab, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām, who said: When the Messenger of God ﷺ—arrived in Medina, or, he said, “when the Messenger of God ﷺ—arrived among us,” he said: “God Most High has praised you favorably for your purification. Will you tell me about it?” They said:

“Messenger of God, we find written in the Torah that one should cleanse oneself with water.” Mālik said:

“He means His words: ‘Men who love to purify themselves’” [Qur’an 9:108].

Yaʿlā ibn Umayyah al-Tamīmī

Then, one of the Banū Ḥanẓalah; an ally of the Banū ʿAbd Shams.

Abū Yūsuf related to us; Abū ʿĀṣim al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Makhlad related to us; Muḥammad ibn Ḥuyayy related to me, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaʿlā, from Yaʿlā, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ—said: “The sea is Hell.” Then Yaʿlā recited: “a Fire whose enclosing walls will surround them” (Qur’an 18:29). Yaʿlā said:

“By God, I shall never enter it, and by God, not a drop of it shall ever touch me.”

Yaʿlā ibn Murrah al-Thaqafī

Abū Yūsuf related to us; Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us; Muʿāwiyah ibn Ṣāliḥ related to me, from Rāshid ibn Saʿd, from Yaʿlā ibn Murrah, who said: We went out with the Messenger of God ﷺ—and were invited to a meal. There was al-Ḥusayn playing in the road, so the Prophet ﷺ—hastened ahead of the people, then stretched out his hand. Al-Ḥusayn kept darting away, once this way and once that way, while he was making him laugh, until he caught him. He placed one hand beneath his chin and the other between his head and neck; then he released him and kissed him. Then the Prophet ﷺ—said:

“Ḥusayn is of me, and I am of Ḥusayn. May God love whoever loves [Ḥusayn]. Al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn are two grandsons among the grandsons.”

Ṣafwān ibn Umayyah

Son of Khalaf ibn Wahb ibn Ḥudhāfah ibn Jumāḥ ibn ʿAmr ibn Huṣayṣ ibn Kaʿb ibn Luʾayy ibn Ghālib ibn Fihr.

Abū Yūsuf related to us; Aṣbagh ibn Faraj related to us; Ibn Wahb informed me, from Yūnus, who said: Ibn Shihāb said: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab related to me that Ṣafwān said: “By God, the Messenger of God ﷺ—gave me what he gave me while he was the person I hated most. He kept giving to me until he became the person I loved most.”

And Ṣafwān ibn al-Muʿaṭṭal al-Sulamī

Abū Yūsuf related to us; Abū Muḥammad Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm related to me; ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar informed us, from Muḥammad ibn Yūsuf al-Aʿraj [from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Faḍl], from Abū Bakr ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Hishām, from Ṣafwān ibn al-Muʿaṭṭal, who said:

I saw the Messenger of God ﷺ—on a journey. He prayed the late evening prayer, then slept. When it was midnight, he awoke and recited these ten verses from the end of Sūrat Āl ʿImrān. Then he took a tooth-stick and cleaned his teeth with it, performed ablution, and stood to pray two cycles. I do not know whether his standing, bowing, or prostration was longest. Then he slept, then awoke and recited the verses, cleaned his teeth with the tooth-stick, performed ablution, and stood to pray as he had done the first time. He continued sleeping, praying two cycles, and doing in each pair of cycles as he had done in the first two, until he had prayed eleven cycles.

Maʿqil ibn Yasār

[Abū Yūsuf related to us; Abū al-Walīd related to me; Abū ʿAzzah al-Dabbāgh related to us; Abū al-Rabāb, the client of Maʿqil ibn Yasār, related to us, from Maʿqil ibn Yasār, who said: We were with the Messenger of God ﷺ—and came upon a place where there was garlic. Some people ate some of it. Then they came to the prayer place, and the Prophet ﷺ—smelled its odor and said: “Whoever has eaten of this plant, let him not approach our prayer place.”]

And Maʿqil ibn Sinān al-Ashjaʿī

Abū Yūsuf related to us; Abū Saʿīd ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm related to us; Ibn Abī Fudayk related to us; Mūsā al-Zamʿī related to me, from Abū al-Ḥuwayrith, that Nāfiʿ ibn Jubayr informed him, saying: Maʿqil ibn Sinān came to me, and has just now left my presence. He informed me that the Messenger of God ﷺ—said: “Ghifār, Aslam, Juhaynah, and Muzaynah are the protégés of God and His Messenger.”

Qurrah ibn al-Aghar al-Muzanī

Abū Yūsuf related to us; Muḥammad ibn Abī al-Sarī related to us; Bakr ibn Bishr al-ʿUqaylī related to me; ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn Abī Sawwār related to me; Iyās ibn Muʿāwiyah ibn Qurrah al-Muzanī related to me, from his father, from his grandfather Qurrah al-Muzanī, who said: We were with the Messenger of God ﷺ—and modesty was mentioned in his presence. They said: “Messenger of God, is modesty part of religion?” The Messenger of God ﷺ—said: “Modesty, chastity, reticence in speech—not reticence of the heart—and intellect are part of faith. They increase one’s share in the Hereafter and diminish one’s share in this world; what they increase in the Hereafter is greater than what they diminish in this world. Avarice, obscenity, and foul speech are part of hypocrisy. They diminish one’s share in the Hereafter and increase one’s share in this world; what they diminish in the Hereafter is greater than what they increase in this world.” Iyās said: I related this to ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, and he instructed me to dictate it to him. I dictated it, and then he wrote it in his own hand. He then led us in the noon and afternoon prayers, and it remained in his palm; he did not put it down.

And Qurrah ibn Daʿmūṣ al-Numayrī

One of the Banū ʿĀmir ibn Ṣaʿṣaʿah of Hawāzin.

Abū Yūsuf related to us; Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us; Jarīr ibn Ḥāzim related to us, saying: I saw a man in Ayyūb’s place, wearing a woolen robe. When he saw the people conversing, he [said]: “My master Qurrah ibn Daʿmūṣ related to me, saying: I came to Medina and went to the Prophet ﷺ—while his Companions were with him. I wanted to draw near to him, but I could not, so I said: ‘Messenger of God, will you ask forgiveness for the Numayrī boy?’ He replied: ‘May God forgive you.’” He said:

“The Messenger of God ﷺ—sent al-Ḍaḥḥāk as a collector. He came back with choice camels, and the Prophet ﷺ—said to him: ‘Did you go to Hilāl ibn ʿĀmir, Numayr ibn ʿĀmir, and ʿĀmir ibn Rabīʿah and take the choicest of their property?’ He said: ‘Messenger of God, I heard you speak of the campaign, so I brought you camels for you to ride and for your Companions to load.’ He said: ‘By God, what you left behind is dearer to me than what you brought. Go and return them to their owners, and collect their alms from the lesser portions of their property.’”

Khālid ibn al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah

His teknonym was Abū Sulaymān; the Sword of God.

Abū Yūsuf related to us; Junādah ibn Muḥammad al-Muzanī related to us; Baqiyyah related to us, from Thawr ibn Yazīd, from Ṣāliḥ ibn Yaḥyā ibn al-Miqdām, from his father, from his grandfather, from Khālid ibn al-Walīd, who said: On the day of Khaybar, the Messenger of God ﷺ—forbade eating the meat of horses, mules, domesticated donkeys, and every beast of prey with fangs.

And Khālid ibn Zayd

Abū Ayyūb al-Anṣārī, son of Kulayb ibn Thaʿlabah. He was one of the Banū al-Najjār ibn Mālik ibn ʿAmr ibn al-Khazraj, then of the Banū Ghanm ibn Mālik, then of the Banū Thaʿlabah ibn ʿAbd ʿAwf ibn Ghanm.

Abū Yūsuf related to us; Abū ʿUtbah al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Muslim al-Sakūnī al-Ḥimṣī related to me; Muʿāwiyah ibn Yaḥyā related to me, from Naṣr ibn ʿAlqamah, from his brother, from Abū Ayyūb al-Anṣārī, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ—said: “Whoever meets [the enemy] for God’s sake and remains steadfast until he is killed or overcome will not be put to trial in his grave.”9

Khālid ibn ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā

Son of Salāmah, one of the Banū Ḥabtar al-Kaʿbī.

Abū Yūsuf said: Sulaymān ibn ʿUthmān ibn al-Walīd related to us; my uncle Abū Miṣraf related to me, from Saʿīd ibn al-Walīd ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd ibn Khālid ibn ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā; my father related to me, from his father, from Khālid ibn ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā ibn Salāmah, that he slaughtered a sheep for the Prophet ﷺ. Khālid had a large family; he would slaughter a sheep and his family would not get so much as a little piece. The Prophet ﷺ—ate from it, then said: “Show me your bucket, Abū Khinnās.” He put what remained of the sheep into it, then said: “O God, bless Abū Khinnās.” It broke free and got ahead of them. He said: “Share it among yourselves.” His family ate from it and had some left over.

Muʿādh ibn Jabal

Son of ʿAmr ibn [Aws ibn] ʿĀʾidh ibn ʿAdī ibn Kaʿb ibn [ʿAmr ibn] Udayy ibn Saʿd ibn ʿAlī ibn Asad ibn Sāradah ibn Tazīd ibn Jushm.

One of the participants at al-ʿAqabah; a participant at Badr.

Abū Yūsuf related to us; Ḥaywah ibn Shurayḥ and Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī related to us, both saying:

Baqiyyah related to us, from Ṣafwān ibn ʿAmr, who said: I heard Shuraḥbīl ibn Maʿshar al-ʿAbsī relate from Muʿādh ibn Jabal, from the Messenger of God ﷺ—who said: “Any servant who takes a stand in this world for ostentation and to gain a reputation will have God make him heard.” Ḥaywah added: “before all creatures on the Day of Resurrection.” Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān added: “And whoever shows off before a Muslim, God will expose him on the Day of Resurrection.”

And Muʿādh ibn al-Ḥārith

Son of Rifāʿah ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Sawād ibn Mālik ibn Ghanm. ʿAfrāʾ was his mother; he was a participant at Badr.

Abū Yūsuf related to us; Abū ʿUmar related to us; Shuʿbah related to us, from Saʿd ibn Ibrāhīm, who said: I heard Naṣr ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān relate from Muʿādh ibn ʿAfrāʾ that he was circumambulating the House. He circumambulated after the afternoon prayer without praying. A man of Quraysh said to Muʿādh: “What prevents you from praying?” He replied: “I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ—forbid prayer after two prayers: after the dawn prayer until the sun rises, and after the afternoon prayer until the sun sets.” Abū Yūsuf related to us; Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us with a similar report.

Ubayy ibn Kaʿb

Son of Qays ibn ʿUbayd ibn Zayd ibn Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmr ibn Mālik ibn al-Najjār, who are the Banū Ḥudaylah. His teknonym was Abū al-Mundhir; he was a participant at Badr.

[Abū Yūsuf related to us; Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm ibn al-ʿAlāʾ related to us; ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith related to me; ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sālim related to me, from al-Zubaydī; al-Zuhrī informed me; Isḥāq, the client of al-Mughīrah ibn Nawfal, informed me [that al-Mughīrah ibn Nawfal] informed him, from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb al-Anṣārī, that the Messenger of God ﷺ—said: “The Hour will not come until the Euphrates uncovers a mound of gold. People will fight over it, and nine tenths of them will be killed.”]

And Ubayy ibn ʿUmārah al-Anṣārī

His name is also given as ʿUmārah, with the ʿayn vowelled with kasrah.

Abū Yūsuf related to us; Saʿīd ibn ʿUfayr related to us; Yaḥyā ibn Ayyūb related to us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Razīn, from Muḥammad ibn Yazīd ibn Abī Ziyād, from Ayyūb ibn Qaṭan, from ʿUbādah, from Ubayy ibn ʿUmārah, that the Messenger of God ﷺ—prayed in his house. He said: I asked, “Messenger of God, may I wipe over the leather socks?” He replied: “Yes.” I asked, “For one day?” He replied: “And for two days.” I asked, “And for two days?” Then I asked, “And three, Messenger of God?” He replied:

“Yes, as you wish.”

ʿUbādah ibn al-Ṣāmit

Son of Qays ibn Aṣram, of the Banū Ghanm ibn ʿAwf ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf ibn al-Khazraj, who are the Qawāqilah. Abū Yūsuf related to us; al-Ḥasan ibn Rabīʿ related this to us, from Ibn Idrīs, from Ibn Isḥāq.

[Abū Yūsuf related to us;] Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Uways related to us; my father related to me, from al-Walīd ibn Dāwūd al-Anṣārī, from the family of ʿUbādah ibn al-Ṣāmit, from his uncle ʿUbādah ibn al-Walīd, who related to him from his father, from his grandfather, that the Messenger of God ﷺ—said: “Quraysh, the Anṣār, Aslam, Ghifār, Juhaynah, Muzaynah, and Ashjaʿ are protégés apart from the people; there is no— They have no protector apart from God.

ʿUbāda al-Zuraqī

Abū Yūsuf said: Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us; Abū Ḍamra Anas ibn ʿIyāḍ al-Laythī related to us; ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ḥarmala related to me, from Yaʿlā ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Hurmuz: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUbāda al-Zuraqī informed him that he used to hunt sparrows at the well of Ihāb—which belonged to them. ʿUbāda saw me after I had caught a sparrow, took it from me, released it, and said: “The Messenger of God ﷺ declared what lies between its two lava fields inviolable, just as Abraham declared Mecca inviolable.” ʿUbāda was one of the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ.

Rifāʿa ibn Rāfiʿ

Son of Mālik ibn al-ʿAjlān ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿĀmir ibn Zurayq. ʿAmr mentioned this, from Ibn Lahīʿa, from Abū al-Aswad, from ʿUrwa.

Abū Yūsuf related to us: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Maslama and Ibn Bukayr related to us, from Mālik, from Nuʿaym ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mujmir, from ʿAlī ibn Yaḥyā al-Zuraqī, from his father, from Rifāʿa ibn Rāfiʿ al-Zuraqī, who said: “We used to pray behind the Messenger of God ﷺ. When he raised his head from bowing, he said, ‘God hears whoever praises Him.’ A man behind the Messenger of God may ﷺ and to You belongs praise.” Ibn Bukayr said: “Our Lord, to You belongs praise, abundant, good, and blessed praise therein.” When the Messenger of God ﷺ had finished, he said:

“Who spoke just now?” A man said: “I did, Messenger of God.” The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “I saw thirty-odd angels hastening to see which of them would write it down first”.

Rifāʿa ibn ʿArāba al-Juhanī

Juhayna belongs to Quḍāʿa.

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Ādam ibn Abī Iyās related to us; Shaybān related to us; Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr related to us; Hilāl ibn Abī Maymūna al-Madanī related to me, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār, from Rifāʿa ibn ʿArāba al-Juhanī, who said: “We set out with the Messenger of God ﷺ and when we were at al-Kadīd—or he said, at Qudayd—he praised God and extolled Him. Then he said: ‘I testify before God that no man who sincerely bears witness in his heart that there is no god but God and that I am the Messenger of God, and then acts rightly, will fail to enter Paradise. My Lord has promised me that He will admit seventy thousand of my community to Paradise without reckoning or punishment. I hope they will not enter it until you, and those of your wives and offspring who are righteous, have taken up dwellings in Paradise’”.

Kaʿb ibn Mālik

Son of Abī [Kaʿb ibn] al-Qayn ibn Kaʿb ibn Sawād ibn Ghanm ibn Thaʿlaba.

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Abū ʿĀṣim related to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who related to me:

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Kaʿb informed him, from his father and his uncle ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Kaʿb…

…from Kaʿb ibn Mālik: The Messenger of God ﷺ would return from a journey only by day. When he arrived, he would begin at the mosque, pray two rakʿas there, and then sit.

Kaʿb ibn ʿUjra al-Anṣārī

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Saʿīd ibn Abī Maryam related to us; Muḥammad ibn Hilāl related to us; Saʿīd ibn Isḥāq ibn Kaʿb ibn ʿUjra related to me, from his father, from Kaʿb ibn ʿUjra, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Come to the pulpit.” We came, and when he climbed one step, he said, “Amen.” Then, when he climbed the second step, he said, “Amen.” Then, when he climbed the third step, he said, “Amen.” When he had finished, he descended from the pulpit. He said: We asked him:

“Messenger of God, today we heard something from you that we had not heard before.” He said: “Gabriel appeared to me and said: ‘Far removed is the one who reaches Ramaḍān and is not forgiven.’ I said, ‘Amen.’ When I climbed the second step, he said: ‘Far removed is the one in whose presence you are mentioned and who does not invoke blessings upon you.’ I said, ‘Amen.’ When I climbed the third step, he said: ‘Far removed is the one whose parents, or one of them, reach old age while he is alive, and they do not admit him to Paradise.’”

Kaʿb ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAbbād

He was surnamed Abū al-Yusr, and was one of the men of al-ʿAqaba and a veteran of Badr.

Makkī ibn Ibrāhīm related to us: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Saʿīd ibn Abī Hind related to us, from Ṣayfī, the client of Aflaḥ, the client of Abū Ayyūb, from Abū al-Yusr: The Messenger of God ﷺ used to supplicate with these words from among nine: “O God, I seek refuge in You from senility; I seek refuge in You from falling, from grief, drowning, burning, and senility; I seek refuge in You from Satan’s assaulting me at death; and I seek refuge in You from dying on…”

…Your path while turning away, and I seek refuge in You from dying by a venomous bite.

Qatāda ibn al-Nuʿmān

Son of Zayd ibn ʿĀmir ibn Sawād ibn Kaʿb ibn al-Khazraj al-Ẓafarī. Ẓafar is Kaʿb ibn al-Khazraj. Abū Yūsuf related to us: ʿAmr related to us, from Ibn Lahīʿa, from [Abū] al-Aswad, from ʿUrwa, with this information.

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Muḥammad ibn Jahḍam related to me; Ismāʿīl ibn Jaʿfar related to us, from Mālik ibn Anas, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Ṣaʿṣaʿa, from his father, from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, who said: My brother Qatāda ibn al-Nuʿmān informed me: “A man stood in prayer in the time of the Prophet ﷺ in the pre-dawn hours. He began reciting the whole sūra ‘Say: He is God, One,’ repeating it without adding anything to it. When morning came, a man said:

‘Messenger of God, a man stood in prayer last night in the pre-dawn hours and began reciting the whole sūra “Say: He is God, One” (112:1), repeating it without adding anything to it, as though the man considered it too little.’ The Messenger of God ﷺ said: ‘By Him in whose hand is my soul, it is indeed equivalent to one-third of the Qurʾān’”.

Salmān al-Fārisī, Abū ʿAbd Allāh

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Abū al-Walīd Hishām ibn ʿAbd al-Malik related to us; Abū ʿAwāna related to us, from al-Mughīra, from Ziyād ibn Kulayb, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqama, from Qarthʿ, from Salmān who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Do you know what Friday is?” I said:

“God and His Messenger know best.” Then he said: “Do you know what Friday is?” I said, on the third or fourth time: “It is the day on which your father—or your forefather—was gathered.” He said: “I shall tell you about Friday: no Muslim purifies himself, then walks to the mosque, then listens in silence until the imam has finished his prayer, without it being an expiation for him for the sins between then and the previous Friday, provided he avoids the deadly sins”.

Salmān ibn ʿĀmir al-Ḍabbī

“Abū Yūsuf related to us: Aḥmad ibn Abī al-Ḥajjāj al-Dārimī, Abū Jaʿfar, related to us, from Abū ʿĀṣim al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Makhlad, who informed us, from Abū Naʿāma ʿAmr ibn ʿĪsā al-ʿAdawī, from ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Bashīr, from Salmān ibn ʿĀmir: He came to the Prophet ﷺ among a group of women from Banū Ḍabba, and said: ‘My father used to provide hospitality to guests, maintain ties of kinship, honor his pact, and do such-and-such. Will that benefit him?’ He said: ‘Did your father die an unbeliever?’ He said: ‘Yes.’

“He said: ‘It will not benefit him.’ When the man turned to leave, he said: ‘Bring the old man to me.’ He said: ‘That will be for his offspring: they will never be humiliated, never be poor, and never be disgraced’”.

Thābit ibn Ṣāmit al-Anṣārī

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Uways related to us; Ibrāhīm ibn…

Ismāʿīl, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Thābit ibn Ṣāmit, from his father, from his grandfather: The Messenger of God ﷺ stood praying in the mosque of Banū ʿAbd al-Ashhal, wearing a cloak wrapped around him. He held his hands over it to protect himself from the cold of the pebbles.

Thābit ibn al-Ḍaḥḥāk al-Anṣārī

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Muslim ibn Ibrāhīm related to us; Abān related to us; Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr related to us, from Abū Qilāba, from Thābit ibn al-Ḍaḥḥāk al-Anṣārī: The Prophet of God ﷺ said: “Whoever falsely swears by a religion other than Islam is as he has said. A man is not bound by a vow concerning what he does not own. Whoever kills himself with something in this world will be punished with it on the Day of Resurrection”.

Thābit ibn Qays ibn Shammās al-Anṣārī

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Aḥmad ibn ʿAmr ibn al-Sarḥ and Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā related to me; they both said: Ibn Wahb informed us; Dāwūd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Makkī related to me, from ʿAmr ibn Yaḥyā al-Māzinī, from Yūsuf ibn Muḥammad ibn Thābit ibn Qays ibn Shammās, from his father, from his grandfather, from the Messenger of God ﷺ: He came to him and said:

“Remove the affliction, Lord of mankind, from Thābit ibn Qays ibn Shammās”. Then he took some earth from Baṭḥān, put it in a cup containing water, and poured it over him.

Thābit ibn Wadīʿa al-Anṣārī

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Abū al-Walīd Hishām ibn ʿAbd al-Malik and Muslim ibn Ibrāhīm related to us; they both said: Shuʿba related to us, from al-Ḥakam, from Zayd ibn Wahb, from al-Barāʾ, from Thābit ibn Wadīʿa: The Prophet ﷺ was asked about the ḍabb. He said: “A people transformed [into it]—and God knows best.” Muslim said: The Prophet ﷺ was brought a ḍabb, and he said: “A people transformed [into it]—and God knows best”.

ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ

Son of Wāʾil ibn Saʿd ibn ʿAmr ibn Huṣayṣ ibn Kaʿb ibn Luʾayy ibn Ghālib.

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Abū Nuʿaym ibn Dukayn related to me; Mūsā ibn ʿAlī ibn Rabāḥ related to us and said: I heard my father relate from Abū Qays, the client of ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ, that he heard ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ say: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “The distinction between our fast and the fast of the People of the Book is the pre-dawn meal.”

ʿAmr ibn Ḥurayth al-Makhzūmī

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Abū Nuʿaym related to us; Misʿar related to us, from al-Walīd ibn Sarīʿ, from ʿAmr ibn Ḥurayth: I heard that he heard the Prophet ﷺ recite at dawn: “By the night when it darkens” (81:17).

ʿAmr ibn Qays

Son of Zāʾida ibn Umm Maktūm al-Fihrī. Abū Yūsuf related to us this information: Ibrāhīm, from Ibn Fulayḥ, from Mūsā.

ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf

An ally of Banū ʿĀmir ibn Luʾayy, and a veteran of Badr.

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Abū al-Yamān related to us; Shuʿayb related to me, from al-Zuhrī; ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr related to me that al-Miswar ibn Makhrama informed him that ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf al-Anṣārī—an ally of Banū ʿĀmir ibn Luʾayy, who had taken part in Badr with the Messenger of God ﷺ—informed him that the Messenger of God ﷺ sent Abū ʿUbayda ibn al-Jarrāḥ to Bahrain to collect its tribute. The Messenger of God ﷺ had made peace with the people of Bahrain and appointed al-ʿAlāʾ ibn al-Ḥaḍramī over them. Abū ʿUbayda arrived with money from Bahrain. The Anṣār heard of Abū ʿUbayda’s arrival, so they came to pray the dawn prayer with the Messenger of God ﷺ. When the Messenger of God ﷺ had prayed the dawn prayer and turned away, they approached him. The Messenger of God ﷺ smiled when he saw them, then said: “I suppose you have heard that Abū ʿUbayda has arrived with something.” They said:

“Yes, Messenger of God.” The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Then rejoice, and hope for what will please you. By God, it is not poverty that I fear for you. What I fear for you is that the world will be spread out before you as it was spread out before those who came before you, and that you will compete for it as they competed for it, and it will destroy you as…”

…it destroyed them.

ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf al-Muzanī

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Uways related to us; Kathīr ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf ibn Yazīd ibn Milḥa al-Muzanī related to me, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: “Whoever revives one of my practices that has been abandoned after my time will receive a reward like the reward of those among the people who act upon it, without that diminishing their rewards in any way. Whoever introduces an innovation that God and His Messenger do not approve of will bear a sin like the sin of those among the people who act upon it, without that diminishing their sins in any way”.

ʿAmr ibn Umayya al-Ḍamrī

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Abū Saʿīd Yaḥyā ibn Sulaymān al-Juʿfī related to me; Ibn Wahb related to me; Yaḥyā ibn Ayyūb informed me, from Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd, from Jaʿfar ibn ʿAmr ibn Umayya al-Ḍamrī, from his father: al-Ṣaʿb ibn Jaththāma gave the Prophet ﷺ a hindquarter of a donkey when he was at al-Juḥfa, and he and the people ate from it.

ʿAmr ibn Mālik al-Ruʾāsī

Then one of Banū ʿĀmir ibn Ṣaʿṣaʿa.

Abū Yūsuf related to us: ʿUthmān ibn Abī Shayba related to us; Wakīʿ ibn al-Jarrāḥ related to us, from his father, from a shaykh called Ṭāriq, from ʿAmr ibn Mālik al-Ruʾāsī, who said: “I came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: ‘Messenger of God, be pleased with me.’ He turned away from me three times. I said: ‘Messenger of God, by God, the Lord is indeed sought to be pleased, and He is pleased; so be pleased with me.’ He was then pleased with me.”

ʿAmr ibn Arāka al-Thaqafī

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Ibn Bukayr related to us; ʿAbd Allāh ibn Lahīʿa related to me, from al-Walīd ibn Abī al-Walīd, from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from al-Ḥasan: ʿAmr ibn Arāka al-Thaqafī, a Companion of the Prophet ﷺ was sitting with Ziyād ibn Abī Sufyān on his couch when a witness was brought before him. The witness stammered during his testimony, and Ziyād said to him: “By God, I shall cut out your tongue.”

ʿAmr ibn Arāka said to him: “I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ forbid mutilation and command charity”.

ʿAmr ibn Ghaylān al-Thaqafī

Abū Yūsuf related to us: al-Ḥakam ibn Mūsā related to us; Ṣadaqa ibn Khālid related to us, from Yazīd ibn Abī Maryam, from Abū ʿUbayd Allāh, from ʿAmr ibn Ghaylān al-Thaqafī, who said:

The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “O God, whoever believes in me, affirms me, and knows that what I have brought is the truth from You: increase his wealth and children, and prolong his life.”

ʿAmr ibn Sufyān al-Thaqafī

Abū Yūsuf related to us; Abū Saʿīd ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm related to us; al-Walīd ibn Muslim related to us; Muḥammad—meaning Ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Shuʿaythī—related to me, from al-Ḥārith ibn Badal al-Baṣrī, from a man of his people who witnessed that on the day of Ḥunayn, and from ʿAmr ibn Sufyān al-Thaqafī, who said: “The Muslims were routed on the day of Ḥunayn, and no one remained with the Messenger of God ﷺ except ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib and Abū Sufyān ibn al-Ḥārith. He said: The Messenger of God ﷺ took a handful of pebbles and threw them in their faces. He said: We fled, and it seemed to us that every stone or tree was a horseman pursuing us.” Al-Thaqafī said:

I turned away from my horse and kept going until I entered al-Ṭāʾif.

ʿAmr ibn ʿAbsah al-Sulamī

Abū Yūsuf related to us; ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yūsuf related to us; Yaḥyā ibn Ḥamzah related to us, from Abū Ḥamzah al-ʿAnsī of the people of Ḥimṣ, who related to him from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jubayr al-Ḥaḍramī, Rāshid ibn Saʿd al-Maqrīʾ, and Shabīb al-Kilāʿī, from Jubayr ibn Nufayr, from ʿAmr ibn ʿAbsah, who said: “On the day of the horses, I presented ʿUyaynah ibn Badr to the Messenger of God ﷺ. The Messenger of God ﷺ said to ʿUyaynah: ‘I know horses better than you do.’ ʿUyaynah said: ‘If you know horses better than I do, then I know men better than you do.’ He said: ‘How so?’ He replied: ‘The best men are men who wear the striped cloak when they lay their swords across their shoulders and set their spears against the backs of their horses: the men of Najd.’ The Messenger of God ﷺ said: ‘You have lied. Rather, they are the people of Yemen; faith is Yemeni, extending to Lakhm, Judhām, and ʿĀmilah. Those of Ḥimyar who are eaten are better than those who eat them, and Ḥaḍramawt is better than Banū al-Ḥārith.’ He named the aqyāl and the anfāl. The Messenger of God ﷺ said:

‘There is no soothsayer, diviner, or king except God.’10

“He said: Al-Samṭ sent word to ʿAmr ibn ʿAbsah, saying: ‘Did you hear the Messenger of God ﷺ say, “Ḥaḍramawt is better than Banū al-Ḥārith”?’ He said: ‘Yes.’ Al-Samṭ said: ‘I believe in God and His Messenger.’ The Messenger of God ﷺ cursed the four kings: Jamdāʾ, Makhūsāʾ, Abḍaʿah, and Mishrakhāʾ, and their sister al-ʿAmradah. He said: She used to bring believers before her and punish them. The Messenger of God ﷺ said: ‘God commanded me to curse Quraysh twice, and I cursed them twice. Then He commanded me to pray for them twice, and I prayed for them twice. The tribes with the greatest numbers in Paradise are Madhḥij, Aslam, Ghifār, and Muzaynah, and their mixed branches from Juhaynah are better in God’s sight on the Day of Resurrection than Banū Asad, Tamīm, Hawāzin, and Ghaṭafān. I do not care if both clans perish.’ He commanded me to curse two tribes: Tamīm ibn Murrah seven times— “So I cursed them seven times; and Bakr ibn Wāʾil five times, so I cursed them five times. Banū ʿUṣayyah disobeyed God and His Messenger. Indeed, ʿUṣayyah and Qays Juʿdah are two tribes, none of whom will ever enter Paradise: Maʿāṭis and Malāmis, while the finest of the tribes are Najrān and Banū Taghlib.”

Yaḥyā said: “Thawr ibn Yazīd related this report to me. He said: ‘Maʿādis and Malādis.’ He claimed that they were two tribes who lost their way, seeking lightning in a year of drought. They became lost in the recesses of the earth, where they could not be reached. This was in the Jāhiliyyah.”

ʿAmr al-ʿAjlānī

Abū Yūsuf related to us; Abū Saʿīd ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm related to us; Ibn Abī Fudayk related to us; ʿAbd Allāh ibn Nāfiʿ, the client of Ibn ʿUmar, related to me, from his father, that ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-ʿAjlānī related to Ibn ʿUmar, from his father, that the Messenger of God ﷺ forbade facing either of the two qiblahs while relieving oneself or urinating.

ʿAmr ibn Shās al-Aslamī

Abū Yūsuf related to us; Aḥmad ibn ʿUmar Abū Jaʿfar related to me; ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mighrāʾ related to us, from Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq, from Abān ibn Ṣāliḥ, from al-Faḍl ibn Miʿqal ibn Sinān, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bayān or Nayyār, from his maternal uncle ʿAmr ibn Shās—who was one of the people of al-Ḥudaybiyyah—who said: “I went out with ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib among the cavalry he had sent to Yemen, and he treated me rather harshly, so I became displeased with him. When I came to Medina, I voiced my complaint against him in the mosque’s gathering places. Then one morning I came forward— “while the Prophet ﷺ was seated in the mosque. When he saw me, he fixed his eyes on me—that is, he glanced at me—until I had taken my place in the gathering. When I sat down, he said:

‘O ʿAmr ibn Shās.’ I replied: ‘At your service; may my father and mother be your ransom, O Messenger of God.’ He said: ‘By God, you have hurt me.’ I replied: ‘We belong to God and to Him we return. I seek refuge in God from hurting the Messenger of God.’ He said: ‘Indeed, whoever hurts ʿAlī has hurt me.’”

ʿAmr ibn Taghlib

Abū Yūsuf related to us; Abū al-Nuʿmān related to us; Jarīr ibn Ḥāzim related to us, from al-Ḥasan, from ʿAmr ibn Taghlib, who said: “Wealth came to the Messenger of God ﷺ. He gave some people and withheld from others. He heard that they had taken offense, and said: ‘I give to one man and leave another; the one I leave is dearer to me than the one I give to. I give to some people because of the anxiety and distress in their hearts, and I rely on others because of the contentment and goodness God has placed in their hearts. Among them is ʿAmr ibn Taghlib.’ ʿAmr said: ‘I would not want to have red camels in exchange for the words of the Messenger of God ﷺ.’”

ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥamiq al-Khuzāʿī

Abū Yūsuf related to us; Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us; Abū Shurayḥ ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Shurayḥ al-Maʿāfirī related to me that he heard ʿUmayrah ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Maʿāfirī say: “My father related to me that he heard ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥamiq say: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: ‘There will be a tribulation in which the safest people—or, he said, the best people—will be the western army.’ Ibn al-Ḥamiq said: ‘For that reason—’”

“I came to you in Egypt.”

ʿAmr ibn Akhṭab

Abū Zayd al-Anṣārī.

“Abū Yūsuf related to us; ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Shaqīq related to us; al-Ḥusayn ibn Wāqid informed us, from Abū Nahīk al-Azdī, who said: ‘I heard Ibn Akhṭab say: I looked at the seal between the shoulders of the Messenger of God ﷺ and touched it with my hand.’ Al-Ḥusayn said: ‘I heard it from ʿAlbāʾ ibn Aḥmar, who had heard it from ʿAmr ibn Akhṭab.’”

ʿAmr ibn Ḥazm al-Anṣārī

Abū Yūsuf related to us; Ismāʿīl ibn Yūnus related to us; Qays Abū ʿImārah, the client of Sawdah daughter of Saʿīd, the client of Banū Sāʿidah among the Anṣār, related to me, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Bakr ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr ibn Ḥazm al-Anṣārī, from his father, from his grandfather, who heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: “Whoever visits a sick person remains in mercy until, when he sits beside him, he is immersed in it. Then, when he rises from beside him, he continues wading through it until he returns from where he set out. And whoever consoles his believing brother for a calamity—”

“God will clothe him in robes of honor on the Day of Resurrection.”

ʿAmr ibn Yathribī al-Ḍamrī

Abū Yūsuf related to us; Muḥammad ibn Bashshār related to us; Abū ʿĀmir related to us; ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Ḥasan related to us; ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Saʿīd related to me, who said: “I heard ʿUmārah ibn Ḥārithah al-Ḍamrī relate from ʿAmr ibn Yathribī al-Ḍamrī, who said: I attended the Prophet’s sermon at Minā. Among the things he said in his sermon was [that] he said: ‘Nothing of a man’s wealth is lawful to another except what he gives willingly.’ When he heard him say this, he said: ‘Messenger of God, what do you think if I come across my cousin’s sheep and take one sheep from them and slaughter it—is there anything against me for that?’ He said: ‘If you come upon a ewe carrying a knife and a fire striker in the wasteland of al-Jumaysh, do not touch it.’”

ʿAmr ibn Maʿdīkarib

“Abū Yūsuf related to us; Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Uways related to us; my father related to me, from ʿAmr ibn Shamir, from Ibn Abī Ṭawq, from Shuraḥbīl ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ”, who heard ʿAmr ibn Maʿdīkarib say: “Today we say what the Messenger of God ﷺ taught us—”

“God bless him and grant him peace.” He said: “I asked him: ‘Abū Thawr, how did the Messenger of God ﷺ teach you?’ He said: ‘He taught us: “At Your service, at Your service; You have no partner, at Your service. Truly, praise, blessing, and dominion belong to You; You have no partner.”’”

ʿAmr ibn Murrah al-Juhanī

Abū Yūsuf related to us; Abū al-Yamān related to us; Shuʿayb reported to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Ḥasan; ʿĪsā ibn Ṭalḥah related to me, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah al-Juhanī, who said: “A man from Quḍāʿah came to the Messenger of God ﷺ and said to him: ‘I testify that there is no god but God and that you are the Messenger of God; I have performed the prayers, fasted the month, kept vigil during Ramaḍān, and paid the alms-tax.’

“The Prophet ﷺ said to him: ‘Whoever dies upon this will be among the most truthful and the martyrs.’”

Salamah ibn al-Muḥabbiq al-Hudhalī

Abū Yūsuf related to us; Abū ʿĀṣim related to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from ʿAbd al-Karīm ibn Abī al-Mukhāriq, from Muʿādh ibn Muʿāwiyah, from Sinān ibn Salamah, from Salamah ibn al-Muḥabbiq: “The Messenger of God ﷺ sent two sacrificial camels with a man and said to me: ‘Mark them, then slaughter them; dip their sandals in their blood and strike their sides with them, so that it will be known that they are sacrificial camels.’”

Salamah ibn Qays al-Ashjaʿī

Abū Yūsuf related to us; Abū Nuʿaym related to us; Sufyān related to us, from Manṣūr, from Hilāl ibn Yasāf, from Salamah ibn Qays, who said: “The Messenger of God ﷺ said to me: ‘When you sniff water into your nose, draw it in deeply, and when you use stones to clean yourself, use an odd number.’”

Salamah ibn Nuʿaym al-Ashjaʿī

Abū Yūsuf related to us; Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shaybah related to us; Hāshim ibn al-Qāsim related to us; Shaybān related to us, from Manṣūr, from Sālim ibn Abī al-Jaʿd, from Salamah ibn Nuʿaym al-Ashjaʿī—who was one of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ—who said: “The Messenger of God ﷺ said: ‘Whoever meets God without associating anything with Him will enter Paradise.’ Ḥāmid added to the report: ‘Even if he committed adultery and theft.’”

Salamah ibn Salāmah ibn Waqsh

One of the Banū Aws ibn Ḥārithah, from Banū Zaʿūrāʾ ibn ʿAbd al-Ashhal; he had pledged allegiance at al-ʿAqabah and fought at Badr. Abū Yūsuf related this to us from ʿAmr, from Ibn Lahīʿah, from Abū al-Aswad, from ʿUrwah.

Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us; al-Layth related to me; Zayd ibn Jubayrah ibn Maḥmūd ibn Abī Jubayrah al-Anṣārī—of Banū ʿAbd al-Ashhal—related to me, from his father Jubayrah ibn Maḥmūd, from Salamah ibn Salāmah ibn Waqsh, a Companion of the Messenger of God ﷺ who was the last of the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ to die—it cannot have been Anas ibn Mālik— “for he lived longer than him—that the two of them went to a wedding feast. Salamah was in a state of ablution, and he ate, then performed ablution. I said to him: ‘Were you not in a state of ablution?’ He said: ‘Yes, but the Messenger of God ﷺ and I went to an invitation to which we had been invited. The Messenger of God ﷺ was in a state of ablution; he ate, then performed ablution.’ I said to him: ‘Were you not in a state of ablution?’ He said: ‘Yes, but things arise, and this is one of the things that arose.’”

Salamah ibn Ṣakhr al-Anṣārī

Then one of the Banū Bayāḍah.

Abū Yūsuf related to us; Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shaybah related to us; Ibn Numayr related to us; Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq related to us, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAṭāʾ, from Sulaymān ibn Yasār, from Salamah ibn Ṣakhr al-Bayāḍī, who said: “I was a man who had intercourse with women often; I did not think any man had as much intercourse as I did. When Ramaḍān began, I made my wife forbidden to me by the formula of ẓihār until Ramaḍān ended. One night, while she was speaking to me, some of her body was uncovered to me. I sprang upon her and had intercourse with her. In the morning I went to my people and told them what had happened. I said to them: ‘Ask the Messenger of God ﷺ for me.’ They said: ‘We would not do that, lest a Book from God be revealed concerning us, or a pronouncement from the Messenger of God ﷺ be made among us, and its shame remain upon us. Rather, we will leave you to bear the consequence of your deed. Go yourself and tell the Messenger of God ﷺ your situation.’ I went out until I came to him and told him what had happened. The Messenger of God ﷺ said: ‘Was it you who did that?’ I said: ‘It was I, and here I am, Messenger of God, patiently accepting God’s judgment upon me.’ He said: ‘Then free a slave.’ I said: ‘By Him who sent you with the truth, I own nothing but myself.’ He said: ‘Then fast two consecutive months.’ I said:”

“Messenger of God, was it anything other than fasting that brought me into the affliction I have suffered?” He said: “Then give alms: feed sixty needy people.” I said: “By Him who sent you with the truth, we spent this very night without any supper.” He said: “Go to the collector of the alms of Zurayq and tell him to hand it over to you; then feed sixty needy people and make use of what remains.”

Salamah ibn al-Akwaʿ

Abū Yūsuf related to us; Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥārith al-Qurashī—the muezzin of the mosque in Egypt—related to us; Yaḥyā ibn Rāshid, a man from Baṣrah, related to us, from Yazīd, the client of Salamah ibn al-Akwaʿ, that Salamah ibn al-Akwaʿ said: “I saw the Messenger of God ﷺ perform ablution. He wiped his head once, then prayed and gave the salutation once.”

Salamah ibn Nufayl al-Sakūnī

Abū Yūsuf related to us; ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yūsuf related to us; ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sālim al-Ḥimṣī related to us; Ibrāhīm ibn Sulaymān ibn al-Afṭas related to me, from al-Walīd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Jarashī, from Jubayr ibn Nufayr, who said: “Salamah ibn Nufayl al-Sakūnī informed me: I drew close to the Messenger of God ﷺ until my knees almost touched his thigh. I said: ‘Messenger of God, horses have been abandoned and weapons laid aside, and some people claim there will be no fighting.’

“He said: ‘They have lied. Fighting has now come. A group of my community will always stand firm upon the truth, prevailing over the people. God will cause the hearts of a people who fight them to deviate, as they seek to overcome them.’ He said—while turning his back toward Yemen: ‘I feel the breath of the Merciful coming from over there, and it has been revealed to me that I am held back—’” without delay, and they follow me in droves. Goodness is bound to the forelocks of horses until the Day of Resurrection, and their people are aided in them. Ibn Durustawayh: buhiya means “when horses are left idle and are not used.”

Salamah ibn Umayyah al-Tamīmī

An ally of Banū ʿAbd Shams.

Abū Yūsuf related to me: Ibn Numayr related to us; my father related to me; Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq related to us, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ṣafwān ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṣafwān, from his two paternal uncles, Salamah ibn Umayyah and Yaʿlā ibn Umayyah, who said: We went out with the Prophet ﷺ on the expedition to Tabūk, and we had a companion with us. He and another man fought while we were on the road. The man bit his hand, and our companion pulled his hand out of his mouth, knocking out his incisor. He came to the Prophet ﷺ seeking compensation for his incisor. The Prophet ﷺ said: “Does one of you go to his brother, bite him with a stallion’s bite, then come seeking compensation? There is no compensation for him.” The Messenger of God ﷺ dismissed the claim.

Sahl ibn Ḥunayf

Son of Wāhib ibn ʿUqaym ibn Thaʿlabah ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Mujdiʿah ibn ʿAmr.

They claim that he is the one called Mujdiʿ ibn ʿĪsā ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf, a participant at Badr.

ʿAmr related this to us, from Ibn Lahīʿah, from Abū al-Aswad, from ʿUrwah.

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us; Abū Surayḥ told me that he heard Sahl ibn Abī Umāmah ibn Sahl ibn Ḥunayf relating from his father, from his grandfather, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Do not make things hard on yourselves. Those before you perished only because they made things hard on themselves. You will find their remnants in monasteries and hermitages.” The Messenger of God ﷺ also said: “Whoever sincerely asks God in his heart for martyrdom, God will bring him to the ranks of the martyrs, even if he dies in his bed.”

Sahl ibn Abī Umāmah ibn Sahl ibn Ḥunayf related from his father, from his grandfather, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Do not be severe with yourselves, for those who came before you perished because of their severity toward themselves. You will find their remnants in monasteries and hermitages.” The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Whoever sincerely asks God in his heart for martyrdom will be brought to the ranks of the martyrs, even if he dies in his bed.”

And Sahl ibn Saʿd

Abū al-ʿAbbās al-Anṣārī, then al-Sāʿidī.

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Ibrāhīm ibn al-Mundhir related to me; Muḥammad ibn Fulayḥ related to us, from Mūsā ibn ʿUqbah, from al-Zuhrī, from Sahl ibn Saʿd, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said on the day of Uḥud: “O God, forgive my people, for they do not know.”

And Sahl ibn al-Ḥanẓaliyyah al-Anṣārī

Abū Yūsuf related to us: al-ʿAbbās ibn al-Walīd ibn Mazīd related to us; my father related to us; Ibn Jābir related to us; Rabīʿah ibn Yazīd told me: Abū Kabshah al-Salūlī arrived in Damascus during ʿAbd al-Malik’s governorship. ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĀmir said to him: “What brought you here? Perhaps you have come to ask the Commander of the Faithful for something?” He said: “Would I ask anyone for anything after what Sahl ibn al-Ḥanẓaliyyah told me?” ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĀmir said: “And what did he tell you?” He said: “I heard him say:

ʿUyaynah ibn Badr and al-Aqraʿ ibn Ḥābis came to the Messenger of God ﷺ and asked him for something. He summoned Muʿāwiyah and ordered him to do something—I do not know what it was. Muʿāwiyah went off and returned with two documents. He handed one to ʿUyaynah ibn Badr—who was the more forbearing of the two men—and ʿUyaynah tied it to his turban. He handed the other to al-Aqraʿ ibn Ḥābis, who said to Muʿāwiyah:

“What is in it?” He said: “What he ordered.” Al-Aqraʿ said: “How badly I would represent my people if I came to them carrying a document whose contents I did not know, like the document of al-Mutalammis!” The Messenger of God ﷺ was facing a man and speaking with him. When he heard al-Aqraʿ’s words, he took the document, opened it, and found in it what he had ordered. He threw it away, then stood and followed al-Aqraʿ until he passed by the mosque door, where he saw a camel kneeling. He said: “Where is the owner of this camel?” They searched for him but did not find him. He said: “Fear God in your treatment of these beasts. Ride them while they are sound, and eat them while they are sound”. Then I followed him until he entered his house. He said, as if displeased just moments earlier: “Whoever asks people for something despite having sufficient means is only amassing coals from Hell.” I said: “Messenger of God, what are sufficient means?” He said: “That you know your family has enough to give them their morning meal or their evening meal”. He said: “After this, would I ask anyone for anything?”

And Sahl ibn Muʿādh ibn Anas al-Juhanī

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Muqriʾ related to us; Saʿīd ibn Abī Ayyūb related to us, from Abū Marḥūm ʿAbd al-Raḥīm ibn Maymūn, from Sahl ibn Muʿādh al-Juhanī, from his father, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Whoever gives up wearing fine clothing, though able to afford it, out of humility before God, God will summon him on the Day of Resurrection before all creation and let him choose whichever robes of faith he wishes to wear.”

ʿUtbah ibn Ghazwān

Son of Jābir ibn Wahb ibn Nushayb ibn Mālik ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Māzin ibn Manṣūr ibn ʿIkrimah, an ally of Banū Nawfal ibn ʿAbd Manāf. Nawfal’s mother was Wāqidah bint ʿAmr al-Māzinīyah. Māzin was the son of Manṣūr ibn ʿIkrimah.

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Abū Nuʿaym al-Faḍl ibn Dukayn related to us; Qurrah ibn Khālid al-Sadūsī related to us; Ḥumayd ibn Hilāl told me: Khālid ibn ʿUmayr said: ʿUtbah ibn Ghazwān addressed us, saying: “People, I remember being the seventh of seven with the Messenger of God ﷺ. We had no food but the leaves of the samur tree, until the corners of our mouths were sore. I found a cloak, tore it in half, and gave half of it to Saʿd ibn Mālik. There is not one of those seven men who does not govern one of the garrison towns.”

And ʿUtbah ibn ʿAbd al-Sulamī

Abū Yūsuf related to us: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yaḥyā ibn Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Makhzūmī related to us; and ʿUtbah ibn ʿAbd al-Sulamī.

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Ḥaywah ibn Shurayḥ and al-Walīd ibn ʿUtbah related to me. They said:

Baqiyyah ibn al-Walīd related to us, from Buḥayr ibn Saʿīd, from Khālid ibn Maʿdān, from ʿUtbah ibn ʿAbd, who said that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “If a man were to fall upon his face from the day he was born until he died an old man, seeking God’s good pleasure, he would consider it insignificant on the Day of Resurrection”.

ʿUtbah ibn al-Nudr al-Sulamī

Abū Yūsuf related to us: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yaḥyā ibn Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Makhzūmī related to us: Yazīd ibn Yaḥyā related to us, from Abū Wahb, from Makḥūl, from Khālid ibn Maʿdān, from ʿUtbah ibn al-Nudr al-Sulamī, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “When your military campaigns become infrequent and the maʿāfir [garments] are deemed lawful, then your best form of jihad is ribāṭ [guarding the frontier].”

Faḍālah al-Laythī

Abū Yūsuf related to us: ʿAmr ibn ʿAwn related to us; Khālid informed us, from Dāwūd, from Abū Ḥarb, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Faḍālah, from his father, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ taught me. Among what he taught me, he said: “Be diligent in observing the five prayers.”

I said: “These are times when I have other things to attend to. Give me one comprehensive instruction which, if I carry it out, will suffice for me.” He said: “Be diligent in observing the two ʿaṣr prayers”—that was not a term in our dialect. I said: “What are the two ʿaṣr prayers?” He said: “A prayer before sunrise and a prayer before sunset”.

And Faḍālah ibn ʿUbayd al-Anṣārī

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us; al-Layth ibn Saʿd told me, from Ḥumayd ibn Hāniʾ, from Abū ʿAlī al-Janabī, ʿAmr ibn Mālik. Faḍālah ibn ʿUbayd al-Anṣārī, a Companion of the Messenger of God ﷺ told me, from the Messenger of God ﷺ that he said during the Farewell Pilgrimage: “Shall I tell you who the believer is? The one whom people trust with their property and their lives”.

Mālik ibn al-Ḥuwayrith al-Laythī

Abū Yūsuf related to us: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn Ḥumayd ibn al-Aswad told me; Unays ibn Sawwār al-Jurmī related to us; my father related to us, from Mālik ibn al-Ḥuwayrith, a Companion of the Prophet ﷺ. He mentioned that the Prophet ﷺ said: “When God, Mighty and Majestic, intends to create a servant, and the man has intercourse with the woman, his fluid reaches every vein and limb of hers. When the seventh day comes, God gathers it, then brings together every vein belonging to him apart from Adam’s; He fashions you in whatever form He wills” (82:8).

Mālik ibn ʿAmr al-Qushayrī

Abū Yūsuf related to us; he said: al-Ḥajjāj related to us; he said: Ḥammād related to us, from ʿAlī ibn Zayd, from Zurārah ibn Awfā, from Mālik ibn ʿAmr al-Qushayrī, who said: I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: “Whoever frees a Muslim slave, that slave will be his ransom from the Fire: a bone of his will be freed for each bone of the slave’s. Whoever reaches old age with either of his parents alive, yet is not forgiven, may God cast him far away. Whoever takes an orphan of two Muslim parents into his household for food and drink until God makes the orphan self-sufficient, Paradise is assured for him”.

Mālik ibn Rabīʿah al-Salūlī

Of Qays ʿAylān.

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Muslim ibn Ibrāhīm related to us; Aws ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Salūlī told me: My paternal uncle, Yazīd ibn Abī Maryam al-Salūlī, told me, from his father, Mālik ibn Rabīʿah, who heard the Prophet ﷺ say: “O God, forgive those who shave their heads.” A man said: “Messenger of God, and those who shorten their hair?” The Prophet ﷺ said this on the third or fourth occasion: “And those who shorten their hair.” Mālik said: “I saw myself with my head shaved, and I would not trade that for red camels or a great fortune”.

Mālik ibn ʿUmayr al-Ḥanafī

Abū Yūsuf related to us: al-Ḥasan ibn al-Rabīʿ related to us; Ibn al-Mubārak related to us, from Ismāʿīl ibn Sumayʿ al-Ḥanafī, from Mālik ibn ʿUmayr—who had lived into the Jāhiliyyah—who said: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: “I met the enemy, and my father was among them. I heard him say something vile to you, and I could not restrain myself until I stabbed him with my spear”—or, “until I killed him.” The Prophet ﷺ fell silent. Then another man came to him and said: “I met my father, but left him, preferring that someone else should meet him.” He remained silent toward him.

Mālik ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Awsī

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Abū Ṣāliḥ and Ibn Bukayr related to us. They said: al-Layth related to us; ʿUqayl told me, from Ibn Shihāb, who informed me: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtbah related to me, from Shibl ibn Khulayḍ al-Muzanī, from Mālik ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Awsī, from the Messenger of God ﷺ that he said: “If a slave woman commits fornication, flog her. Then if she commits fornication again, flog her. Then if she commits fornication again, flog her. Then if she commits fornication again, sell her, even for a rope.” (A ḍafīr is a rope).

And Mālik ibn Rabīʿah

Son of al-Badan ibn ʿĀmir ibn ʿAwf ibn Ḥārithah ibn ʿAmr ibn al-Khazraj ibn Sāʿidah; a participant at Badr, kunya Abū Usayd al-Sāʿidī.

Abū Yūsuf related to us: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Maslamah and Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān al-Tanūkhī related to us. They said: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Muḥammad related to us, from Abū al-Yamān [from] Shaddād ibn Abī ʿAmr ibn Ḥammās, from his father, from Ḥamzah ibn Abī Usayd al-Anṣārī, from his father, who heard the Prophet ﷺ as he was leaving the mosque. Men and women mingled on the road, so the Messenger of God ﷺ said to the women:

“Move back; you must not walk through the middle of the road. Keep to the edges of the road.”

The woman would press herself against the wall, so closely that her garment would catch on something on the wall because of how tightly she pressed herself against it.

And Mālik ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Khuzāʿī

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Abū Saʿīd ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm related to us; al-Fazārī related to us; Manṣūr ibn Ḥayyān al-Asadī related to us; Sulaymān ibn Bishr al-Khuzāʿī informed me, from his maternal uncle Mālik ibn ʿAbd Allāh, who said: I went on a military campaign with the Messenger of God ﷺ and I never prayed behind an imam whose performance of an obligatory prayer was briefer than his.

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Ibn al-Ḥimmānī related to us; ʿAbd al-Wāḥid related to us, from Manṣūr, from Sulaymān ibn Bishr, from his maternal uncle, from ʿAbd Allāh, in a similar version.

ʿUqbah ibn Mālik al-Laythī

Abū Yūsuf related to us: ʿAmr ibn ʿĀṣim related to us; Sulaymān ibn al-Mughīrah related to us; Ḥumayd ibn Hilāl related to us, from Naṣr ibn ʿĀṣim al-Laythī, from ʿUqbah ibn Mālik al-Laythī, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “God, Mighty and Majestic, has denied me [the right of intercession] for anyone who kills a believer”—he said it three times.

And ʿUqbah ibn al-Ḥārith

Son of ʿĀmir ibn Nawfal ibn ʿAbd Manāf.

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us; Wuhayb ibn Khālid related to us, from Ayyūb.

The final entries on the Companions

Abū Yūsuf related to us: al-Muʿallā ibn Asad related to us, from Wuhayb, from al-Nuʿmān ibn Rāshid, who is weak, “and Isḥāq ibn Rāshid, whose ḥadīth is sound”.

“Abū Yūsuf related to us; he said: I heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muʿādh say: I saw in my father’s book, in his handwriting: Ḥātim ibn Abī Ṣaghīrah; Abū Ṣaghīrah was his maternal uncle, and he was Ḥātim ibn Muslim”. ʿAlī said: The name of Abū al-ʿĀliyah’s father was Muslim.

Abū Yūsuf related to us; he said: I heard Abū Mūsā say: al-Ḥasan’s mother was called Khayrah. Abū Mūsā said: ʿĀmir ibn Ṣāliḥ ibn Rustum said to me: “Whose son is al-Ḥasan?”

I said: “The son of Abū al-Ḥasan.” He said: “Al-Ḥasan ibn Yasār.” He said: “Whose son is Dāwūd?”

I said: “The son of Abū Hind.” He said: “Dāwūd ibn Dīnār.” He said: “Ayyūb al-Sakhtiyānī?”

I said: “Ayyūb ibn Abī Tamīmah.” He said: “Ayyūb ibn Kaysān.” He said: “Abān?” I said:

“Ibn Abī ʿAyyāsh.” He said: “Abān ibn Fayrūz.”

Abū Mūsā said: I saw in Khālid ibn al-Ḥārith’s book: “Sulaymān ibn Ṭarkhān al-Taymī related to us”.

(The merit of the Radiant City)

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Abū Bakr ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr ibn ʿĪsā al-Ḥumaydī and Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr related to us. They said: Sufyān related to us; Ibn Jurayj informed us, from Abū al-Zubayr, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Abū Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Soon people will spur their camels in pursuit of knowledge, but they will find no scholar— More knowledgeable than a scholar of Medina. Abū Yūsuf related to us: Some Medinese related to me, from Maʿn, from Zuhayr al-Tamīmī, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUmar, from Saʿīd ibn Abī Hind, from Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī, from the Prophet ﷺ—who said: “The seeker of knowledge will come from the East and the West, but no scholar more knowledgeable than the scholar of the people of Medina will be found”—or he said, “the scholar of Medina.” Abū Yūsuf related to us: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Maslama and Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bukayr related to us, from Mālik.

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Abū Nuʿaym and Qabīṣa related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us.

Al-Ḥumaydī related to us: Sufyān related to us. All of them, from Muḥammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jābir: An Arab nomad pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God for Islam. Medina’s fever struck the nomad, and he came to the Prophet and said, “Messenger of God, release me from my pledge.” The Messenger of God refused. Then he came to him and said, “Release me from my pledge.” He refused. Then he came to him and said, “Release me,” but he refused. The nomad left, and the Prophet said: “Medina is like a bellows: it expels its dross and purifies its good.” This is the wording of Mālik’s report, and it has one of the finest chains of transmission. Ibn Maslama and Ibn Bukayr are reliable and accomplished; Mālik, al-Thawrī, and Ibn ʿUyayna are the authorities to whom trustworthiness in knowledge, precision, and retention ultimately leads. Ibn al-Munkadir is the pinnacle of precision, retention, and asceticism. There is not one of them who is not an authoritative proof.

Abū Yūsuf Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to us: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Maslama and Ibn Bukayr related to us, from Mālik.

Al-Ḥumaydī related to us: Sufyān related to us.

Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us: al-Layth related to me.

Al-Ḥajjāj related to us: Ḥammād ibn Salama related to us. All of them, from Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd, who heard Abū al-Ḥubāb Saʿīd ibn Yasār say: I heard Abū Hurayra say: The Messenger of God ﷺ—said: “I was commanded concerning a town that consumes the towns. They call it Yathrib, but it is Medina. It expels people as a bellows expels the dross from iron.” In Abū Ṣāliḥ’s report it says, “It expels the worst of people,” and in Ḥammād’s report, “It expels the dross.” Every one of the named transmitters in this report is individually an authoritative proof. Yaḥyā is a leader in knowledge, and Saʿīd ibn Yasār is a reliable Medinese. The Companions of the Prophet ﷺ—whether young or old, of high or low rank, are authoritative proofs.

Abū al-Walīd Hishām ibn ʿAbd al-Malik and Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us, saying: Shuʿba related to us, from ʿAdī ibn Thābit al-Anṣārī, who said: I heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yazīd al-Khaṭmī relate, from Zayd ibn Thābit, who said: When the Messenger of God ﷺ—set out for Uḥud, some of those who had gone out with him turned back. He said: The Companions of the Messenger of God were divided into two groups. One group said, “We will kill them,” and the other said, “We will not kill them.” Then this was revealed: “Why are you divided into two parties concerning the hypocrites, when God has cast them back because of what they earned?” The Prophet said: “It is Ṭayyiba; it expels the dross just as fire expels the dross from silver.”

Muḥammad ibn Maslama al-Makkī related to us: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Muḥammad related to us, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUmar, from Ḥafṣ ibn ʿĀṣim, from Abū Hurayra: The Prophet ﷺ—said: “Faith will surely withdraw to Medina, just as a serpent withdraws to its burrow.” This is a sound report with a good chain of transmission.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Maslama and Saʿīd ibn Abī Maryam related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Muḥammad informed us, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUmar ibn Ḥafṣ ibn ʿĀṣim ibn Ḥabīb ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Ḥafṣ ibn ʿĀṣim, from Abū Hurayra: The Prophet ﷺ—said: “Faith will surely withdraw to Medina, just as a serpent withdraws to its burrow.” This is a sound report with a good chain of transmission.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Maslama and Saʿīd ibn Abī Maryam related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Muḥammad informed us, from al-ʿAlāʾ, from his father, from Abū Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ—said: “A time will come upon people when a man will call his cousin and his kinsman, ‘Come to prosperity!’ Yet Medina is better for them, if only they knew. By Him in whose hand is my soul, no one leaves it out of aversion to it without God replacing him there with someone better. Indeed, Medina is like a bellows: it removes the dross. The Hour will not come until Medina expels its worst people, as a bellows expels the dross from iron.” This is a good chain of transmission. Among the people of Medina, ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz is a trusted leader. Al-ʿAlāʾ ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yaʿqūb, a client of the Ḥuraqīs, is reliable, as is his father. Whoever belongs to the people of knowledge and is sincere with himself knows that everyone whom Mālik included and identified by name in his Muwaṭṭaʾ is reliable and may serve as an authoritative proof.

The chain by which his name is reported is reliable; it establishes him as an authoritative proof.

Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Uways related to us: Kathīr ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf al-Muzanī related to me, from his father, from his grandfather: The Messenger of God ﷺ—said: “Religion will surely withdraw to the Ḥijāz, just as a serpent withdraws to its burrow. Religion will surely find refuge in the Ḥijāz as the mountain goats find refuge on the mountaintop. Religion began as something strange and will return as something strange, so blessed are the strangers who, after me, set right what people have corrupted of my Sunna.” Many have criticized Kathīr, though they would have been better served by keeping silent about him. Those who spoke against him were ignorant of him and the circumstances surrounding him. I heard Ibn Uways say: Mālik asked me about his report, and Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Anṣārī transmitted from him. I have no doubt that I heard Ibrāhīm ibn al-Mundhir—if I did not hear it from him, then a reliable person related it to me from him—say: Kathīr used to claim that the Prophet ﷺ—had granted his grandfather a piece of land. He would dispute with those in that region over it, and was much given to litigation. He went to Ibn ʿImrān to litigate, and Ibn ʿImrān said to him:

“Kathīr, you are an idle man, much given to disputes over what you do not know, and you claim what is not yours. You have no firm evidence for what you seek. Do not come near me, and let me not see you unless you see that I have finished dealing with people of falsehood. When you see that, then come.” One day, while Ibn ʿImrān was there, Kathīr ibn ʿAbd Allāh came to him. He said, “Did I not tell you not to come near me unless you saw that I had finished dealing with people of falsehood?” Kathīr replied, “You are right, may God set the judge aright. I have come only because the people of falsehood have come to you. So-and-so and so-and-so have come to you, and they are people of falsehood, so I came along with them.” Ibn ʿImrān then dealt with him accordingly. Abū Yūsuf said: He ordered that Kathīr be tied to a pillar until he rose from the court. Abū Yūsuf said: These men used to keep close company with Ibn ʿImrān.

They were devoted to Ibn ʿImrān.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad, nephew of Juwayriya, related to us: Juwayriya related to us, from Mālik.
