Abū Bakr and Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl related to us, from Ibn Wahb, from Mālik, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtba ibn Masʿūd, who informed him: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās informed him, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf: A man came to ʿUmar while he was at Minā and told him that a man had said, “By God, if ʿUmar were to die, I would pledge allegiance to so-and-so.” When this reached ʿUmar, he said, “This evening I shall stand before the people and warn them against those who would usurp the community’s authority.” ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: I said, “Commander of the Faithful, do not do that today. The pilgrimage season has brought together the rabble and the mob, and they are the ones who will crowd around you. I fear that if you make a speech to them today, they will carry it off without understanding it or putting it in its proper place. Wait until you reach Medina. It is the abode of the Emigration and the Sunna, and you will be among the people’s scholars and notables. Then you can say what you have to say from a position of strength, and they will understand your words and put them in their proper place.” ʿUmar said, “By God, if I reach Medina safely, I shall address the people there at the first gathering I attend.”

The First Generation of the Successors of Medina

(The Jurists among the Successors of Medina)

Abū Ṣāliḥ ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṣāliḥ related to us: al-Layth ibn al-Hādī related to me, from al-Mundhir ibn ʿAlī ibn Abī al-Ḥakam: His nephew proposed marriage to his cousin, and they disputed over some matter— “Then the young man said, ‘She is divorced if I marry her before I eat the male palm’s unopened spadix’—the ghaḍīḍ is the male palm’s spadix—‘then they regretted what had happened.’” Al-Mundhir said, “I will bring you a clear ruling on that.” He said: I went to Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib and said to him, “A man from my family proposed marriage to his cousin. A dispute arose between them over some matter, and he said, ‘She is divorced if I marry her before I eat the ghaḍīḍ.’” Ibn al-Musayyib said, “He is liable for nothing; he divorced someone he does not possess.” Then I asked ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr about it, and he said, “He is liable for nothing; he divorced someone he does not possess.” Then I asked Abū Salama ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, and he said, “He is liable for nothing by divorcing someone he does not possess.” Then I asked Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Hishām about it, and he said, “He is liable for nothing; he divorced someone he does not possess.” Then I asked ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUtba ibn Masʿūd about it, and he said, “He is liable for nothing; he divorced someone he does not possess.” Then I asked ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, and he said, “Have you asked anyone?” I said, “Yes,” and named them.

He said: Then I returned to the people and told them what I had asked about.

Abū Muḥammad ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad al-Miṣrī related to me: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī al-Zinād informed us, saying: Abū al-Zinād said: Among the jurists and scholars of Medina whom I encountered, whose judgment was approved and whose opinions were followed, were Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib, ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr, al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad, Abū Bakr ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, Khārija ibn Zayd, ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtba, and Sulaymān ibn Yasār, along with elders besides them, their peers among the people of jurisprudence and merit.

“ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan al-ʿAsqalānī related to us: Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mubārak related to us, saying: The jurists of Medina whose opinions people followed were seven.” He named those whom Abū al-Zinād had named, except that he did not mention Abū Bakr ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, and included among them Sālim ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar.

Ḥarmala ibn Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥarmala al-Tujībī related to me: Ibn Wahb informed us, from Ibn Lahīʿa, who informed me: Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb said that Qabīṣa ibn Dhuʾayb was born in the Year of the Elephant. Ibn Lahīʿa said: When Ibn Shihāb mentioned Qabīṣa ibn Dhuʾayb, he would say, “He was one of the scholars of this community.”

Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān related to me, from Saʿīd ibn Abī Ayyūb, who related to me, from Jaʿfar ibn Rabīʿa, from Rabīʿa ibn Yazīd, from Ismāʿīl ibn ʿUbayd Allāh, who said: I entered upon Umm al-Dardāʾ, and Qabīṣa ibn Dhuʾayb was with them. I said to him, “Abū Saʿīd …”

“Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥīm related to me, saying: I heard ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh say:

‘Among the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ—there were only three who had companions who memorized what they transmitted from them and upheld their teachings in jurisprudence: Zayd, ʿAbd Allāh, and Ibn ʿAbbās. The ten people most knowledgeable about Zayd ibn Thābit and his teachings were Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib, Abū Salama ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtba ibn Masʿūd, ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr, Abū Bakr ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, Khārija ibn Zayd, Sulaymān ibn Yasār, Abān ibn ʿUthmān, Qabīṣa ibn Dhuʾayb, and another man whom he named. The most knowledgeable of their teachings and reports was Ibn Shihāb, then Mālik ibn Anas, then, after Mālik, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī.’”

Ibn Numayr and Abū Saʿīd al-Ashajj related to me, saying: Ḥafṣ ibn Ghiyāth related to us: al-Aʿmash related to us: Abū al-Zinād said: The jurists of Medina were counted as four: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib, ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Marwān, ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr, and Qabīṣa ibn Dhuʾayb.

“Saʿīd ibn Asad related to me: Ḍamra related to us, from Rajāʾ ibn Abī Salama, from ʿUbāda ibn Nusayy, who said: Ibn ʿUmar was asked, ‘You, the elders of Quraysh, are on the verge of passing away. Whom shall we ask after you?’ He replied, ‘Marwān has a son who is a jurist, so ask him.’”

Jarīr said, from Mughīra, from al-Shaʿbī: Qabīṣa ibn Dhuʾayb was among the people most knowledgeable about Zayd ibn Thābit’s judicial rulings.

“Ibrāhīm ibn al-Mundhir related to us: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn ʿĀmir—a man from ʿĀmila, from Taymāʾ—related to us. A shaykh who used to sit with Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib related to me, saying: One day Ibn Ziml al-ʿUdhrī passed by him while we were with him. Saʿīd tossed a pebble at him, and he came over. Saʿīd said to him:

‘I heard that you praised this man’—and he pointed toward Syria, meaning ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Marwān. He said, ‘Yes, Abū Muḥammad, I praised him. Would you like to hear the poem?’ He said, ‘Yes, sit down.’ He recited it to him until he reached this verse:

‘Quraysh did not reproach you for any traitin Yathrib, when you were a young man there.’

Saʿīd said to him, ‘You speak truly. But when he went to Syria, he changed.’”

Abū Yūsuf said: Those whom we have named are reliable and precise, and their reports establish the standing of authoritative proofs.

They are the jurists among the Successors of Medina, and before them came a generation who transmitted knowledge and were distinguished by retention and precision. However, they did not possess the same degree of jurisprudence as those men. As for transmission, retention, and precision, they had as much as one could wish for, and they transmitted reports from the Messenger of God ﷺ. Among them were:

Mujammiʿ ibn Yazīd ibn Jāriya al-Anṣārī

[According to the wording of the source,] he had seen him.

Maḥmūd ibn al-Rabīʿ al-Anṣārī

ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān related to me: ʿAbd Allāh informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī, who related to him: Maḥmūd ibn al-Rabīʿ informed me—and he claimed that he remembered the Messenger of God ﷺ—and remembered a mouthful of water that the Prophet had spat out from a bucket in their house.

“Sulaymān ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān related to me: al-Walīd related to us: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Namir related to us, saying: Al-Zuhrī said: Maḥmūd ibn al-Rabīʿ informed me—and he claimed that he remembered the Messenger of God ﷺ. He said: The Messenger of God ﷺ—died when I was five years old.”

Ibn ʿUthmān said, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mubārak, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī: Maḥmūd ibn al-Rabīʿ informed me, saying: I heard ʿItbān ibn Mālik al-Anṣārī, one of the Banū Sālim, and he mentioned his report. Maḥmūd said: I related his report to a group that included Abū Ayyūb, the Companion of the Messenger of God ﷺ.

Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us: al-Layth related to me: Yūnus and ʿUqayl related to me, saying: Ibn Shihāb said: I asked al-Ḥuṣayn ibn Muḥammad al-Anṣārī—one of the Banū Sālim and among their notables—about the report of Maḥmūd ibn al-Rabīʿ, and he confirmed it.

Al-Ḥumaydī related to us: Sufyān related to us: al-Zuhrī related to us, saying: I heard Maḥmūd ibn al-Rabīʿ relate, from ʿUbāda ibn al-Ṣāmit, that the Messenger of God ﷺ—said: “There is no prayer for one who does not recite the Opening of the Book in it.”

Maḥmūd ibn Labīd

He is reliable.

Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Abī Salama related to us, from Ibn Shihāb, from Maḥmūd ibn Labīd, from Shaddād ibn Aws, who said: “O tidings of death for the Arabs! O tidings of death for the Arabs! O tidings of death for the Arabs!” He said—and I do not know whether he said this, though I think he did—one word: “The thing I fear most for you is ostentation and the hidden desire.”

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Azhar

Ibn ʿAbd ʿAwf al-Zuhrī, cousin of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf. They say he died a few months before the Battle of al-Ḥarra. Azhar died during the time of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, and he had— He exceeded one hundred.

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā related to us: Usāma ibn Zayd informed us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Azhar, who said: “I saw the Prophet ﷺ in the year of the Conquest, when I was a young boy.” ʿUqayl related from Ibn Shihāb that ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Azhar al-Zuhrī informed him, from his father: “The Messenger of God ﷺ was brought a man who had been drinking while he was at Ḥunayn.”

Saʿīd ibn Abī Maryam related to us, from Nāfiʿ ibn Yazīd, who said: Jaʿfar ibn Rabīʿa related to me, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Sāʾib, that ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Azhar related to him, from his father, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Azhar: “The Messenger of God ﷺ said: ‘The likeness of a believing servant when he is afflicted by illness or fever is that of a piece of iron placed in the fire: its dross departs, and what is good in it remains.’” Aḥmad ibn al-Khalīl related to me: Isḥāq related to us: al-Faḍl ibn Mūsā related to us: al-Juʿayd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: “Al-Sāʾib ibn Yazīd died at the age of ninety-four. He was sturdy and of moderate build. He said: ‘I know that I enjoyed my hearing and sight only through the Prophet’s prayer for me ﷺ. My maternal aunt took me to the Prophet ﷺ and said, “My sister’s son is ill; will you pray to God for him?” He said: “So he prayed for me.”’”

Among them:

Al-Miswar ibn Makhrama al-Zuhrī

Al-Zuhrī related from him, and he has a report from the Prophet ﷺ.

Abū al-Yamān related to us: Shuʿba informed me, from al-Zuhrī, who informed me that ʿAlī ibn Ḥusayn had informed him that al-Miswar ibn Makhrama related to him, saying: “The Messenger of God ﷺ stood, and I heard him when he recited the tashahhud. Then he said: ‘To proceed.’”

Al-Sāʾib ibn Yazīd al-Kindī

Abū al-Yamān related to us: Shuʿba informed me, from al-Zuhrī, who informed me that al-Sāʾib ibn Yazīd said: “The Messenger of God ﷺ said: ‘There is no contagion, no Ṣafar, and no hāmah.’” Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr related to us: Sufyān related to us, saying: I heard al-Zuhrī say:

“I heard al-Sāʾib ibn Yazīd say: ‘I can remember the Prophet’s return from the expedition to Tabūk. I went out with the boys to the mountain pass of al-Wadāʿ to meet the Prophet ﷺ.’”

ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĀmir ibn Rabīʿa

An ally of the Banū ʿAdī.

Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us: al-Layth related to me, from Yūnus, from Ibn Shihāb, who informed me that ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĀmir ibn Rabīʿa had informed him that his father, ʿĀmir, related to him: “He saw the Messenger of God ﷺ performing a voluntary night prayer on the back of his mount, wherever it turned.”

Among them:

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Thaʿlaba ibn Ṣuʿayr

Al-ʿUdh rī, an ally of the Banū Zuhra.

Zayd ibn Bishr al-Ḥaḍramī related to me: Ibn Wahb informed me: Mālik ibn Anas related to me, from Ibn Shihāb al-Zuhrī, that he used to sit with ʿAbd Allāh ibn Thaʿlaba ibn Ṣuʿayr and learn genealogies and other things from him. One day he asked him about a matter of jurisprudence, and he said:

“If you want that, then you should go to this shaykh, Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab.” Ibn Shihāb said:

“So I sat with him for seven years, thinking that no one else possessed knowledge.” He said: “Ibn Shihāb’s legal opinions—and his approach11—were such that he would refer to the opinion of Sālim ibn ʿAbd Allāh from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab.”

Abū al-Ṭufayl ʿĀmir ibn Wāthila al-Bakrī

Abū al-Yamān related to us: Shuʿba informed me, from al-Zuhrī: ʿĀmir ibn Wāthila al-Laythī related to me, saying: “A man from Taymāʾ, who was one of the People of the Book, came to ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Marwān and said, ‘Commander of the Faithful, Ibn Hurmaz has wronged me and transgressed against me.’ ʿAbd al-Malik gave him no reply. Then he returned to complain to him about Ibn Hurmaz, but ʿAbd al-Malik gave him no reply. The man said—and he was angry—‘Commander of the Faithful, we find in the Torah that God sent down to Moses son of ʿImrān that the ruler bears no responsibility for a scholar’s injustice and oppression so long as he has not been informed of that scholar’s injustice and jawhar.12 But once he is informed and approves it, he shares in his injustice and oppression.’ When he said that, ʿAbd al-Malik removed Ibn Hurmaz from his post.”

—The section on those who had seen the Prophet has ended— Among the Successors of Medina

ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib

Ibn Qaʿnab and Ibn Bukayr related to us. They said: Mālik related to us, from Ibn Shihāb, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Part of a person’s good Islam is leaving what does not concern him.”

Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī

Ibn Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib.

Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm al-Zubaydī related to me: ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith related to us: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sālim related to us, from al-Zubaydī, who informed me, from al-Zuhrī, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Abī Rāfiʿ, from Abū Hurayra, who said: “He used to relate from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: ‘On the Day of Resurrection, a group of my Companions will come to me and approach the Pool. I will say, “My Lord, my Companions!” It will be said, “You do not know what they introduced after you; they turned back on their heels.”’”

Muʿāwiya ibn ʿAbd Allāh

Ibn Jaʿfar ibn Abī Ṭālib.

Aṣbagh ibn al-Faraj related to us: Ibn Wahb informed me: Yūnus informed me, from Ibn Shihāb, who said: “I heard Muʿāwiya ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar speak to al-Walīd ibn ʿAbd al-Malik at supper, while we were between Mecca and Medina. He said to him, ‘Commander of the Faithful, Abān ibn ʿUthmān married the daughter of ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān to spite the daughter of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar, after she refused to sell him her inheritance from him while he was ill, when he had suffered paralysis. Then he did not stop at that—’”

“—until he divorced Umm Kulthūm, so she became free to marry during his illness. This al-Sāʾib ibn Yazīd, the son of al-Nimr’s sister, is alive and can testify to ʿUthmān’s ruling concerning Tumāḍir bint al-Aṣbagh: she inherited from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf after she became free to marry. He can also testify to ʿUthmān’s ruling concerning Umm Ḥakīm bint Qāriẓ: she inherited from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Mukammal after she became free to marry. So summon him and ask him about his testimony.”

When Muʿāwiya had finished speaking, al-Walīd said: “I do not think ʿUthmān ruled in that way.”

Muʿāwiya said: “If al-Sāʾib does not testify to that, then I will refute it, both in his presence and in his absence.”

Kathīr ibn ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib

Al-Ḥumaydī related to us: Sufyān related to us, saying: “I heard al-Zuhrī say: ‘Kathīr ibn ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib informed me, from his father, who said: “I was with the Prophet ﷺ on the day of Ḥunayn, and the Messenger of God ﷺ was on his mule.”’”

Abū Rushd Tammām ibn ʿAbbās

Al-Ḥajjāj related to us: Ḥammād related to us, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr, from al-Zuhrī, from Tammām ibn al-ʿAbbās, from his mother, who said: “The last thing I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ recite in the Maghrib prayer was ‘By the Mount and a Book inscribed.’” Yazīd ibn Hārūn said, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr: “And Ibn Wahb said, from Usāma, from Ibn Shihāb.” Both of them said: “The Surah of Those Sent Forth.” This is more likely.

Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh

Ibn ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib.

Abū al-ʿAbbās Ḥaywa ibn Shurayḥ related to me: Baqiyya ibn al-Walīd informed us, from al-Zubaydī, from al-Zuhrī, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās, who said: “Ibn ʿAbbās used to relate:”

“God, Mighty and Majestic, sent an angel to His Prophet ﷺ, accompanied by Gabriel ﵇. The angel said to the Messenger of God ﷺ, ‘God, Mighty and Majestic, gives you the choice between being a servant who is a prophet and being an angel who is a prophet.’ The Prophet of God ﷺ turned toward Gabriel ﵇ as though seeking his counsel. Gabriel gestured to the Messenger of God ﷺ with his hand: ‘Be humble.’ The Messenger of God ﷺ said, ‘Rather, I will be a servant who is a prophet.’ He said: ‘After that saying, he never ate reclining until he met his Lord.’”

ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Marwān ibn al-Ḥakam and ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith

Ibn Nawfal ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib.

[Abū al-Yamān] and ʿAlī ibn ʿAyyāsh related to us. They said: Shuʿayb informed us, from al-Zuhrī, who related to me, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Nawfal, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Khabbāb ibn al-Aratt, from his father—who had fought at Badr with the Messenger of God ﷺ—that he kept watch on the Messenger of God ﷺ during a night when the Messenger of God ﷺ prayed through the whole night. When it was dawn and the Messenger of God ﷺ had finished his prayer, Khabbāb came to him and said: “Messenger of God, may my father be your ransom! I saw you pray tonight in a way I have never seen you pray before.” The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Yes. It was a prayer of hope and fear. I asked my Lord not to destroy us by what He destroyed”

“the nations before us with, and He granted me that. I asked my Lord not to bring an enemy against us from outside our own people, and He granted me that. I asked my Lord not to divide us into factions, but He denied me that.”

Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Nawfal

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Maslama ibn Qaʿnab, Ibn Bukayr, and ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Abī Salama related to us, from Mālik, from Ibn Shihāb, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, who related to him that he heard Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ and al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Qays, in the year of Muʿāwiya ibn Abī Sufyān’s pilgrimage, discussing combining the ʿumra with the ḥajj.

Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: “Only someone ignorant of God’s command would do that.” Saʿd said:

“What a terrible thing you have said, nephew!” Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: “But ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb used to forbid it.” Saʿd said: “The Messenger of God ﷺ did it, and we did it with him.”

ʿAbd al-Malik ibn al-Mughīra ibn Nawfal

Ibn al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib.

Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us: al-Layth related to me: Yūnus related to me, from Ibn Shihāb, who said:

“ʿAbd al-Malik ibn al-Mughīra ibn Nawfal informed me that he heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar being asked for a legal opinion about making a woman lawful for her husband again. ʿAbd Allāh said: ‘That is fornication.’”

Muḥammad ibn Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim

Ibn ʿAdī ibn Nawfal ibn ʿAbd Manāf.

Abū al-Walīd related to us: Shuʿba related to us: Sufyān ibn Ḥusayn and Muḥammad ibn Abī Dhiʾb informed us that they heard al-Zuhrī, from Muḥammad ibn Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim, from his father: “He heard the Prophet—”

“ ﷺ—say: ‘The one who severs kinship ties will not enter Paradise.’”

Nāfiʿ ibn Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim

Al-Aṣbagh related to us: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yūnus informed me, from Ibn Shihāb, who informed me that Nāfiʿ ibn Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim related to him, from ʿUthmān ibn Abī al-ʿĀṣ al-Thaqafī: “He complained to the Messenger of God ﷺ of pain in his body that had afflicted him since he became Muslim. The Messenger of God ﷺ said to him: ‘Put your hand on the place that hurts and say “In the name of God” three times. Then say seven times: “I seek refuge in God and in His power from the evil of what I feel and fear.”’”

ʿAmr ibn Muḥammad ibn Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim

Abū al-Yamān related to us: Shuʿayb informed us, from al-Zuhrī, who informed me that ʿAmr ibn Muḥammad ibn Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim said that Muḥammad ibn Jubayr [said]: Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim informed me that while he was traveling with the Messenger of God ﷺ, accompanied by a group returning from Ḥunayn, the Bedouins clung to him, asking him questions, until they forced him against a tree and snatched his cloak. The Messenger of God ﷺ stopped and said: “Give me back my cloak. If I had as many of these thorn trees as there are here, I would divide them among you. Then you would find me neither miserly, nor a liar, nor a coward.”

ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr

“ʿĪsā ibn Hilāl al-Sulayḥī related to me: Abū Ḥaywa, Shurayḥ ibn Yazīd, related to us: Shuʿayb ibn Abī Ḥamza related to us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUrwa, who said: ‘I was a boy with two locks of hair. He said: I stood to pray two rakʿas after the afternoon prayer. He said: ʿUmar ibn—’”

“—al-Khaṭṭāb saw me, and he had the whip with him. When I saw him, I ran away from him. He hurried after me until he caught hold of my two locks of hair. He said: He forbade me. I said: ‘Commander of the Faithful, I will not do it again.’”

ʿAbbād ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr

Muḥammad ibn al-Muthannā related to us: Yaʿlā ibn ʿUbayd related to us: Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq related to us, from Muḥammad ibn Shihāb, from Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbbād, from ʿAbbād, who said: “I was told that when ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb entered Bayt al-Maqdis, he said: ‘At Your service, O God, at Your service.’”

Abū ʿUbayda ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Zamʿa

Ibn al-Aswad ibn al-Muṭṭalib ibn Asad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā.

Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shayba related to us: Wakīʿ related to us, from Zamʿa ibn Ṣāliḥ, from al-Zuhrī, from Wahb ibn ʿAbd ibn Zamʿa, from Umm Salama, who said: “Abū Bakr went on a trading journey to Buṣrā before the Prophet’s death ﷺ. With him were Nuʿaymān and Suwayṭ ibn Ḥarmala, both of whom had fought at Badr. Nuʿaymān was in charge of the provisions. Suwayṭ, who was a man given to joking, said to him: ‘Feed me.’ He replied: ‘Wait until Abū Bakr comes.’

“Suwayṭ said: ‘I will certainly anger you!’ They passed by some people, and Suwayṭ said to them: ‘Will you buy a slave of mine?’ They said: ‘Yes.’ He said: ‘He is a slave, but he can speak and will tell you, “I am a free man.” If you are going to let him go when he says that, then do not spoil my slave for me.’”

“They said: ‘We will buy him from you.’ He said: ‘So they bought him for ten she-camels.’ They came and put a turban or a rope around his neck. Nuʿaymān said: ‘This man is making fun of you. I am a free man; I am not a slave.’ They said: ‘We have been told about your trick.’ He said: ‘So they took him away.’

“He said: Abū Bakr came, and they told him what had happened. He followed them, returned the she-camels to them, and took Nuʿaymān back. When they arrived before the Prophet ﷺ, they told him, and the Prophet ﷺ and his Companions around him laughed at it for a year.”

ʿĪsā ibn Ṭalḥa ibn ʿUbayd Allāh

Ibn Qaʿnab and Ibn Bukayr related to us, from Mālik, from Ibn Shihāb al-Zuhrī, from ʿĪsā ibn Ṭalḥa ibn ʿUbayd Allāh, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ, who said: “The Messenger of God ﷺ stood at Minā during the Farewell Pilgrimage, while people asked him questions. A man came and said: ‘Messenger of God, I did not realize; I shaved my head before sacrificing.’ The Messenger of God ﷺ said: ‘Sacrifice, and there is no blame.’ Another man came and said: ‘Messenger of God, I did not realize; I slaughtered before throwing the pebbles.’ He said: ‘Throw the pebbles, and there is no blame.’ He said: The Messenger of God ﷺ was asked about nothing done earlier or later without saying: ‘Do it, and there is no blame.’”

Muʿādh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿUthmān al-Taymī

Abū al-Yamān related to us: Shuʿayb informed me—ḥāʾ.

Al-Ḥajjāj related to us: my grandfather related to us. Both related it from al-Zuhrī, who informed me that Muʿādh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Taymī said that his father, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿUthmān, said: “I accompanied ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb to Mecca. A party from Thaqīf presented him with two leather flasks of nabīdh—the sāṭīḥa is larger than an idāwa and smaller than a mazāda.” ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿUthmān said: “ʿUmar ibn—” al-Khaṭṭāb [drank] one of them—Ḥajjāj said: immediately. Then milk was brought to him, and he refrained from drinking the other until what was in it had fermented. ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb went to drink from it, found that it had fermented, and said: “Dilute it with water.”

And Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf

Abū al-Yamān related to us: Shuʿayb informed me. Ḥ

And al-Ḥajjāj related to us: My grandfather related to me, from al-Zuhrī, who informed me that Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf lost consciousness during his illness, in a spell in which they thought his soul had departed. They covered him with a garment, and his wife, Umm Kulthūm bt. ʿUqba, went out to the mosque, seeking help through what she had been commanded to seek help through: patience and prayer. They remained for an hour while he was unconscious. Then he came to, and the first thing he said was “God is greatest.” The people of the household and those nearby said “God is greatest.” Then he asked, “Did I lose consciousness just now?” They said, “Yes.” He said:

“You are right. During my spell of unconsciousness, two men took me away. I felt harshness, severity, and coarseness from them. They said, ‘Come along; we will take you before the Mighty, the Trustworthy.’ They took me along until they met a man, who said, ‘Where are you taking this man?’ They said, ‘We are taking him before the Mighty, the Trustworthy.’ He said, ‘Go back, for he is among those for whom felicity and forgiveness were decreed while they were still in their mothers’ wombs, and his sons will enjoy his company for as long as God wills.’ He lived for a month after that, then died.”

And Ḥumayd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf

Abū al-Yamān related to us: Shuʿayb informed me.

And al-Ḥajjāj related to us: My grandfather informed me, from al-Zuhrī, from Ḥumayd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, that he heard Muʿāwiya ibn Abī Sufyān, while he was in Medina, say in his sermon:

“I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: ‘This day—and this day is ʿĀshūrāʾ—”

“God has not made its fast obligatory for you, and I am fasting. Whoever wishes to fast may fast, and whoever wishes to break the fast may do so.”

And Zurāra ibn Muṣʿab ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf

Aḥmad ibn Asad al-Bajalī related to us: Ibn al-Mubārak related to us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from Zurāra ibn Muṣʿab, from al-Miswar ibn Makhrama, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, who said:

“One night I kept watch with ʿUmar. A lamp appeared to us, so we went to it. There was a closed door and voices and commotion. He said to me, ‘This is the house of Rabīʿa ibn Umayya ibn Khalaf, and they are drinking now. What do you think?’ I said, ‘I think we have done what we were forbidden to do: spying.’”

He said: “So he turned back, and I turned back with him.”

And Ṭalḥa ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAwf

Abū ʿĀṣim, Ādam, ʿĀṣim ibn ʿAlī, and Aḥmad ibn Yūnus related to us. They said:

Ibn Abī Dhiʾb related to us, from al-Zuhrī, from Ṭalḥa ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAwf, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Azhar, from Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “A Qurashī has the strength of a man from outside Quraysh, like mine.” Al-Zuhrī was asked, “What did he mean by that?” He said, “Soundness of judgment.”

And ʿĀmir ibn Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ

Ibn Quʿnab and Ibn Bukayr related to us, from Mālik, from Ibn Shihāb, from ʿĀmir ibn Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, from his father, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ came to visit me in the year of the Farewell Pilgrimage. He said: I was suffering from an illness that had become severe, and I said to him, “Messenger of God, you see how much pain I am in. I have wealth, and no one will inherit from me except a daughter. May I give away two-thirds of my wealth?” He said:

“ ‘No.’ I said, ‘Then half?’ He said: ‘[No]’. I said, ‘Then a third?’ He said:

“ ‘A third is much—or a great deal. It is better for you to leave your heirs wealthy than to leave them dependent, begging from people. Whatever you spend seeking God’s countenance, you will be rewarded for it, even what you put into your wife’s mouth.’ He said: I asked, ‘Messenger of God, will I be left behind after my companions?’ He said: ‘You will not be left behind and then do a righteous deed without thereby increasing in rank and elevation. Perhaps you will be left behind so that some people benefit through you and others are harmed through you. O God, bring my Companions’ emigration to completion, and do not turn them back on their heels. But wretched is Saʿd ibn Khawla.’ The Messenger of God ﷺ grieved for him because he died in Mecca.”

And Ismāʿīl ibn Muḥammad

ibn Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ.

Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us: al-Layth related to me: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Khālid related to me, who said: Ibn Shihāb said, “Ismāʿīl ibn Muḥammad ibn Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ related to me, from Ḥamza ibn al-Mughīra, that he heard al-Mughīra ibn Shuʿba report that he traveled with the Messenger of God ﷺ on the expedition to Tabūk.”

And among them: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Miswar ibn Makhrama al-Zuhrī

ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn ʿImrān related to me: Ibn Wahb related to us: Usāma ibn Zayd related to me:

Ibn Shihāb related to him that ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Miswar ibn Makhrama said: I set out with my father, Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd Yaghūth al-Zuhrī in the year of Adhruḥ. The sickness struck Syria, and we stayed at al-Sarḥ for fifty nights.

Then Ramadan came upon us. Al-Miswar and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Aswad fasted, while Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ broke the fast and refused to fast. I said to Saʿd, “Abū Isḥāq, you were a Companion of the Messenger of God ﷺ and witnessed Badr, while al-Miswar and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān are fasting and you are breaking the fast?” Saʿd said, “I have better understanding than they do.”

And among them: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muslim ibn ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh

ibn Shihāb ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Zuhra.

Al-Muʿallā ibn Asad related to us: Wuhayb related to us, from al-Nuʿmān ibn Rāshid, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muslim, the brother of al-Zuhrī, from Ḥamza ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmayr, who said: We went to Syria to ask questions. When we arrived in Medina, Ibn ʿUmar said to us, “You went to Syria to ask questions? I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: ‘A person will continue to ask people until he meets God with no morsel of flesh on his face.’”

And among them: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Mukammal al-Zuhrī

Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us: al-Layth related to me: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Khālid related to me, from Ibn Shihāb, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Mukammal, that he asked Ibn ʿAbbās, “May a man recite something from the Qurʾān while he is not in a state of purity?” ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās said, “A verse or two.”

And ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd al-Qārī

an ally of Banū Zuhra.

Al-Aṣbagh ibn Faraj related to me: [Ibn] Wahb informed me: Yūnus informed me, from Ibn Shihāb, who related to me that ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd al-Qārī said: One day the Messenger of God ﷺ stood on the pulpit to preach. He praised God, extolled Him, and bore witness [to His oneness]; then he said:

“To proceed: I intend to send some of you to the kings of the non-Arabs.”

And among them: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Qārī and Abū ʿUbayda

ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir, an ally of Banū Zuhra.

Muḥammad ibn al-Minhal related to me: Yazīd ibn Zurayʿ related to us: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Isḥāq related to us, from Abū ʿUbayda ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir, who said: I asked Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh about wiping over the leather socks. He said, “My nephew, that is the Sunna.” I asked him about wiping over the turban. He said, “I do not touch the hair with water.”

And among them: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥārith

ibn Hishām al-Makhzūmī.

Al-Ḥajjāj ibn Abī Manīʿ related to us: My grandfather related to us, from al-Zuhrī, who informed me that Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Hishām said: ʿĀʾisha, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ said: The wives of the Prophet ﷺ sent Fāṭima, daughter of the Messenger of God ﷺ to the Messenger of God ﷺ. She asked permission to enter while the Messenger of God was with ʿĀʾisha under her mantle, and he gave her permission, so she entered.

And among them: ʿIkrima ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān

ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Hishām.

ʿAmr ibn al-Rabīʿ related to us: Yaḥyā ibn Ayyūb informed me, from Yūnus, from Ibn Shihāb, who informed me that ʿIkrima ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Hishām said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said, “Do not let this wolf’s tail deceive you until you see it spread out across the horizon”—and he pointed with his finger, meaning the dawn on the horizon.

And among them: ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Abī Bakr

ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Hishām al-Makhzūmī.

Al-Aṣbagh related to us: Ibn Wahb informed me: Yūnus informed me, from Ibn Shihāb, who informed me that ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Abī Bakr ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān related to him, from Umayya ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Khālid ibn Usayd, that he asked Ibn ʿUmar: “What do you think of shortening the prayer while traveling? We do not find it in the Book; we find mention only of the prayer at home.” Umayya said that ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar said:

“My nephew, God sent Muḥammad ﷺ when we knew nothing. We do only what we saw the Messenger of God ﷺ do. Shortening the prayer while traveling is a Sunna established by the Messenger of God ﷺ.”

And among them: al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Rabīʿa al-Makhzūmī

Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us: al-Layth related to me: ʿUqayl related to me—concerning a man who gives his wife to her family or places her affairs in her own hands or in the hands of her family—who said: Ibn Shihāb informed me, from al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Rabīʿa, that Muʿāwiya ruled that any man who did that, whereupon she divorced herself with three pronouncements of divorce, was thereby free of him.

And among them: Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd Allāh

ibn Abī Rabīʿa al-Makhzūmī.

Al-Ḥajjāj ibn Abī Manīʿ related to us: My grandfather related to us, from al-Zuhrī, who informed me that Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Rabīʿa said: Al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās informed him that ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās had informed him: While he was traveling with ʿUmar on the road to Mecca during his caliphate, with the Emigrants and the Helpers with him, ʿUmar began chanting a verse. A man from Iraq—he was the only Iraqi with them—said to him, “Someone other than you should say it, Commander of the Faithful.” ʿUmar felt embarrassed by that, so he spurred his mount until he had fallen behind the caravan.

And among them: Khālid ibn al-Muhājir ibn Khālid Sayf Allāh al-Makhzūmī

Abū Ṣāliḥ and Ibn Bukayr related to us. They said: Al-Layth related to us: Yūnus related to me, from Ibn Shihāb, who informed him that Khālid ibn al-Muhājir ibn Khālid Sayf Allāh informed him: While he was sitting with Ibn ʿAbbās, a man came to him and asked him for a legal opinion about temporary marriage. Ibn ʿAbbās instructed him to do it. Ibn Abī ʿAmra al-Anṣārī said to him, “Wait, Ibn ʿAbbās.” Ibn ʿAbbās said:

“By God, it is no new matter; it was practiced in the time of the leader of the God-fearing.” Ibn Abī ʿAmra said, “Ibn ʿAbbās, it was only a concession in the early days of Islam for one compelled to it, like [eating] blood, carrion, and pork. Then God established the religion firmly and prohibited it.”

And among them: al-Muṭṭalib ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥanṭab al-Makhzūmī

Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us: al-Layth related to me: Yūnus related to me, from Ibn Shihāb, who informed me that al-Muṭṭalib ibn ʿAbd Allāh said: It reached him that the Messenger of God ﷺ passed through the cemetery at al-Baqīʿ al-Gharqad, riding a white mule. His mule shied, and some Muslim men rushed toward it to take hold of its bridle. The Messenger of God ﷺ said to them, “Leave it. It was startled only by the punishment of Saʿd ibn Zurāra, who is being punished in his grave. He was a hypocrite.”

And Muḥammad ibn ʿAbbād ibn Jaʿfar al-Makhzūmī

Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us: al-Layth related to me: ʿUqayl related to me, from Ibn Shihāb, who informed me that Muḥammad ibn ʿAbbād ibn Jaʿfar al-Makhzūmī heard one of their scholars say: The first thing God revealed to His Prophet ﷺ was “Recite in the name of your Lord who created” (96:1) through “Taught the human being what he did not know” (96:5). They said: This was the beginning of it, revealed to the Messenger of God ﷺ on the day of Ḥirāʾ. Its ending was revealed afterward, at whatever time God willed.

And among them: Sālim ibn ʿAbd Allāh

and ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar

and ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb

and Ḥamza ibn ʿAbd Allāh and Ḥafṣ ibn ʿĀṣim ibn ʿUmar

and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Wāqid ibn ʿAbd Allāh

and Wāqid ibn ʿAbd Allāh

and Abū Bakr ibn ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar

and ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd ibn al-Khaṭṭāb

and Abū Bakr ibn Sulaymān ibn Abī Ḥathma

and ʿUthmān ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Surāqa

and Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥāṭib, an ally of Banū ʿAdī

and:

The Successors

from Banū Jumāḥ:

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥayrīz

and Ṣafwān ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṣafwān ibn Umayya.

And from Banū Fihr:

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shuraḥbīl ibn Ḥasana

and Muḥammad ibn Suwayd

And from Banū Sahm:

ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb

and Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ

And from Banū ʿĀmir ibn Luʾayy:

Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Māʿiz al-ʿĀmirī

And among the Anṣārī Successors from whom al-Zuhrī transmitted,

among them:

Abū Umāma ibn Sahl ibn Ḥunayf ibn Wāhib ibn Thaʿlaba ibn al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf ibn Mujdiʿa ibn al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf ibn Mālik ibn al-Aws ibn Ḥāritha.

Abū al-Walīd al-Ṭayālisī—Hishām ibn ʿAbd al-Malik—related to me: Sulaymān ibn Kathīr related to us: al-Zuhrī related to us, from Abū Umāma ibn Sahl ibn Ḥunayf, from his father, that the Prophet ﷺ prohibited two kinds of dates: al-Jaʿrūr and the kind called al-Ḥubayq. Some people would select the worst of their fruit and give it as alms. Then the verse was revealed: “Do not select the bad of it to spend” (2:267).

And among them: Khārija ibn Zayd

ibn Thābit al-Anṣārī, then al-Khazrajī.

Abū Thawāba Faḍāla ibn al-Mufaḍḍal related to us: My father, al-Mufaḍḍal ibn Faḍāla ibn ʿUbayd al-Qitbānī, related to me that Muḥammad ibn ʿAjlān related to him, from Abū al-Zinād, from Khārija ibn Zayd ibn Thābit, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “War is deception.”

And among them: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Khārija ibn Zayd

Ibrāhīm ibn al-Mundhir related to me: Ibn Wahb related to me: Yūnus informed me, from Ibn Shihāb, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Khārija ibn Zayd, from ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr: I went to ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb and said to him, “Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, we sit with these rulers of ours, and they say things that we know to be other than the truth, yet we affirm them; and they adjudicate through injustice, and we support them and make it seem good to them. What do you think of that?” He said, “Nephew, in the time of the Messenger of God ﷺ—we used to count this as hypocrisy. I do not know how it is regarded among you.”

And among them:

Saʿīd ibn Sulaymān ibn Zayd ibn Thābit

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm related to us; ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yaḥyā related to us, from Nāfiʿ ibn Yazīd, from ʿUqayl, from al-Zuhrī, from Ibn Sulaymān ibn Zayd ibn Thābit, from his father, from his grandfather.

Abū al-Ṭāhir related to me, from his maternal uncle’s book. He said: ʿUqayl related to me; Saʿīd ibn Sulaymān related to me, saying: “His father, Sulaymān ibn Zayd, informed me, from his grandfather Zayd ibn Thābit, who said: ‘I used to write down the Revelation for the Messenger of God ﷺ. When it was sent down to him, he would be seized by a severe [trembling?], and sweat would pour from him like pearls. Then it would pass from him. I would enter to see him with a piece of saddle cloth or a shard, and write as he dictated to me. I would not leave until my leg was nearly broken by the weight of the Qurʾān, and I would say, “I will never walk on my leg again.” When he had finished, he would say, “Read it,” and I would read it to him. If anything had been omitted from it, he would correct it. Then I would take it out to the people.’”13

And among them:

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Kaʿb ibn Mālik

son of Abī [Kaʿb ibn] al-Qayn ibn Kaʿb ibn Sawād ibn Ghanm ibn Thaʿlaba ibn ʿUbayd ibn ʿAdī ibn Ghanm ibn Kaʿb ibn Salima.

Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us; al-Layth related to me; ʿUqayl related to me, and Ibn ʿUthmān related to us: ʿAbd Allāh informed us; Yūnus informed us. Al-Juʿfī related to us, saying: Ibn Wahb related to me; Yūnus informed me. Both transmit from Ibn Shihāb, who informed me that ʿAbd Allāh ibn Kaʿb ibn Mālik al-Anṣārī told him that ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās had informed him that ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib came out from the presence of the Messenger of God ﷺ—during the illness in which he died. The people said, “Abū Ḥasan, how is the Messenger of God ﷺ—this morning?” He replied, “By God’s praise, he is this morning recovering.” ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib took him by the hand and said to him, “Do you not see that, by God, in three days you will be a slave to the staff? By God, I think the Messenger of God ﷺ—will die of this illness. I recognize the faces of the Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib at the time of death. Go to the Messenger of God ﷺ—and ask him who will hold this authority. If it is to be ours, we will know; and if it is to belong to someone else, we will speak to him so that he may advise them concerning us.” ʿAlī said, “By God, if we ask the Messenger of God ﷺ—for it and he denies it to us, the people will never give it to us. By God, I will not ask the Messenger of God ﷺ—for it.”

And among them:

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Kaʿb

Abū ʿĀṣim related to us, from Ibn Jurayj. Ibn Shihāb related to me that ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Kaʿb ibn Mālik informed him, from his father and his uncle ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Kaʿb ibn Mālik, that the Messenger of God ﷺ—never returned from a journey except during the day. When he arrived, he would begin at the mosque, pray two cycles of prayer there, and then sit.

And among them:

Bashīr ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Kaʿb ibn Mālik

Ḥajjāj related to us; my grandfather related to me, from al-Zuhrī, who said: Bashīr ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Kaʿb ibn Mālik used to relate that Kaʿb ibn Mālik used to relate:

“The Messenger of God ﷺ—said: ‘By Him in whose hand is my soul, it is as though they are being pelted with arrows by the verses of poetry they recite to them.’”

And among them:

Abū Bakr ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr ibn Ḥazm

Abū Saʿīd ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm related to us; Ibn Abī Fudayk related to us, from Mūsā ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿUmar ibn Saʿīd, from Ibn Shihāb, from Abū Bakr. Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr ibn Ḥazm related to us, from his father, from ʿUmar, who said: “I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ—say: ‘The Hour will not come until a valley among the valleys of the Ḥijāz flows with fire, whose light will illuminate the necks of the camels at Buṣrā.’”

And among them:

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Bakr ibn Muḥammad

ibn ʿAmr ibn Ḥazm.

Abū al-Yamān related to us; Shuʿayb related to me. And al-Ḥajjāj related to us; my grandfather related to us. Both transmit from al-Zuhrī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Bakr, that ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr informed him that ʿĀʾisha, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ—informed him, saying: “A woman came to me with her two daughters, asking me for something. I had nothing with me except one date, so I gave it to her. She took it and divided it between her two daughters without eating any of it herself. Then she got up and left with her daughters. The Messenger of God ﷺ—came in to me, and I told him her story. The Messenger of God ﷺ—said: ‘Whoever is tested with daughters and treats them well, they will be a shield for him from the Fire.’”

And among them:

ʿUmāra ibn Khuzayma ibn Thābit

Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us; al-Layth related to us; Yūnus related to me, from Ibn Shihāb, who informed me that ʿUmāra ibn Khuzayma ibn Thābit—Khuzayma ibn Thābit being the one whose testimony the Messenger of God ﷺ—made equivalent to the testimony of two men—said: “His uncle, who was one of the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ—informed him that Khuzayma ibn Thābit had seen in a dream that he was prostrating upon the forehead of the Messenger of God ﷺ. Khuzayma came to the Messenger of God ﷺ—and told him about it. He said: ‘The Messenger of God ﷺ—lay down for him and then said, “Make your dream come true.” So he prostrated upon his forehead.’”

And:

Namla ibn Abī Namla al-Anṣārī

Abū al-Yamān related to us; Shuʿayb informed me.

Ḥajjāj related to us, from his grandfather, from al-Zuhrī. Namla ibn Abī Namla al-Anṣārī related to me that his father, Abū Namla al-Anṣārī, told him: “While I was sitting with the Messenger of God ﷺ—a Jewish man came to him and said, ‘Muḥammad, does this dead body speak?’ The Messenger of God ﷺ—said to him, ‘I do not know.’ The Jew said, ‘I testify that it does speak.’ The Messenger of God ﷺ—said to him:

‘As for what the People of the Book tell you, neither affirm it nor deny it. Say, “We believe in God, His Books, and His Messengers.” If it is true, you will not have denied it; and if it is false, you will not have believed it.’”

And among them:

Ayyūb ibn Bashīr ibn Nuʿmān ibn Akkāl

one of the Banū Muʿāwiya ibn Mālik ibn ʿAwf ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf ibn Mālik.

Abū al-Yamān related to us; Shuʿayb informed me, from al-Zuhrī, who informed me that Ayyūb ibn Bashīr al-Anṣārī related to him, from one of the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ—that when the Messenger of God ﷺ—went out on that expedition, he mounted the pulpit. When he had completed his testimony of faith, the first thing he said was to ask forgiveness for the martyrs who had been killed on the day of Uḥud.

And among them:

ʿAbbād ibn Tamīm

ibn Zayd ibn ʿĀṣim ibn Kaʿb ibn ʿAmr al-Māzinī, then al-Najjārī.

ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Shaqīq related to us; ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mubārak informed us; Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥafṣa informed us, from al-Zuhrī, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, from ʿAbbād ibn Tamīm, from his paternal uncle, that the Messenger of God ﷺ—said: “There is no need to perform ablution except when you detect an odor or hear a sound.”

And:

Muḥammad ibn al-Nuʿmān ibn Bashīr ibn Saʿd

Abū al-Yamān related to us; Shuʿayb informed me, from al-Zuhrī, who related to me that Ḥumayd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and Muḥammad ibn al-Nuʿmān ibn Bashīr had heard al-Nuʿmān ibn Bashīr say: “My father, Bashīr ibn Saʿd, gave me a young male servant. Then he walked with me until he brought me to the Prophet ﷺ—and said, ‘Messenger of God, I have given this son of mine a young male servant. If you think it right to approve it, I shall approve it.’ The Messenger of God ﷺ—said:

‘Have you given each of your sons a gift?’ Bashīr replied, ‘No.’ The Messenger of God ﷺ—said:

“Then take it back.”

And:

Thābit ibn Qays al-Zuraqī

Abū Ṣāliḥ and Ibn Bukayr related to us, from al-Layth, from Yūnus, from Ibn Shihāb, from Thābit ibn Qays, one of the Banū Zurayq, that Abū Hurayra said: “A wind caught the people on the road to Mecca while ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb was out, and it grew strong. ʿUmar said to those around him:

‘What is the wind?’ They gave him no reply. The question ʿUmar had asked reached me, so I urged my mount on until I caught up with him. I said, ‘Commander of the Faithful, I was told that you asked about the wind. I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ—say: “The wind is from God’s mercy. It brings mercy and it brings punishment. So do not curse it; ask God for its good, and seek refuge in Him from its evil.”’”

And among them:

Al-Ḥuṣayn ibn Muḥammad al-Anṣārī

then al-Sālimī, of the Banū ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf.

Maḥmūd ibn al-Rabīʿ related it.

And among them:

Faḍāla ibn Muḥammad al-Anṣārī

Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us; al-Layth related to me; ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Khālid related to me, from Ibn Shihāb, from Faḍāla ibn Muḥammad al-Anṣārī, who said that a trustworthy person from his people informed him that Kaʿb ibn ʿAjra al-Anṣārī was afflicted by an injury to his head and shaved his hair before the sacrificial animal had reached its place of sacrifice. The Messenger of God ﷺ—ordered him to fast for three days.

And among them:

Ḥafṣ ibn ʿUmar ibn Saʿd al-Qaraẓ

Ḥaywa ibn Shurayḥ related to me; Baqiyya related to us, from al-Zubaydī, from al-Zuhrī, from Ḥafṣ ibn Saʿd ibn Qaraẓ, that his father and paternal uncles informed him, from their father Saʿd ibn Qaraẓ, that the Sunnah for the two feasts of Sacrifice and Fast-Breaking is for the imam to say “God is most great” seven times in the first cycle before the recitation, and five times in the second cycle before the recitation.

And:

Ḥarām ibn Saʿd ibn Muḥayyiṣa

Ādam related to us; Ibn Abī Dhiʾb related to us; al-Zuhrī related to us, from Ḥarām ibn Muḥayyiṣa, from his father, who said: “I asked the Messenger of God ﷺ—about the earnings of a cupper. He forbade me to take them. I complained to him of my need, and he said, ‘Use it to feed your water-bearing camel.’”

And:

ʿUmar ibn Thābit al-Anṣārī

Abū al-Yamān related to us; Shuʿayb informed me, from al-Zuhrī, who informed me that ʿUmar ibn Thābit al-Anṣārī told him that one of the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ—had informed him that the Messenger of God ﷺ—said to the people, while warning them of the trial of the Antichrist:

“Know that none of you will see his Lord until he dies, and that ‘unbeliever’ is written between the Antichrist’s eyes, which will be read by everyone who detests his deeds.”

And among them:

Yazīd ibn Wadīʿa ibn Ḥudhāfa al-Anṣārī

Abū al-Yamān related to us; Shuʿayb informed me, from al-Zuhrī, who related to me that Yazīd ibn Wadīʿa ibn Ḥudhāfa al-Anṣārī said that Abū Hurayra said: “I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ—say: ‘The Anṣār are chaste and steadfast. In this matter, the people follow Quraysh: their believers follow its believers, and their wicked follow its wicked.’”

And among them:

Ismāʿīl ibn Muḥammad ibn Thābit

ibn Qays ibn Shammās al-Anṣārī.

Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Uways related to us; my father related to me, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, that Ismāʿīl ibn Muḥammad ibn Thābit al-Anṣārī informed him that Thābit ibn Qays al-Anṣārī said: “Messenger of God, I fear that I am ruined.” He asked, “Why?” He said, “God has forbidden a man to be praised for what he has not done, yet I find that I love praise. Ostentation is forbidden, yet I find that I love fine appearance. We are forbidden to raise our voices above yours, yet I am a man with a loud voice.” The Messenger of God ﷺ—said: “Thābit, would you not be content to live as one praised, or to be killed as a martyr and enter Paradise?”

And ʿUqba ibn Suwayd:

Abū al-Yamān related to us; Shuʿayb informed me; and Ḥajjāj related to us, from his grandfather, from al-Zuhrī, who informed me that ʿUqba ibn Suwayd al-Anṣārī heard his father—who was one of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ—say: “We returned with the Messenger of God ﷺ—from the expedition to Ḥunayn. When Uḥud came into view, the Messenger of God ﷺ—said: ‘A mountain that loves us and that we love.’”

And among them:

ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Khālid al-Anṣārī

Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us; al-Layth related to me; ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Khālid related to me, from Ibn Shihāb, from ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Khālid al-Anṣārī: “The alms due on cattle are like the alms due on camels, except that no ages of cattle are specified.”

Muḥammad said: “The people of the Ḥijāz act upon it today.”

And among them:

Muḥarrar ibn Abī Hurayra

ʿĪsā ibn Muḥammad related to us; Isḥāq ibn ʿĪsā related to me, from Ibn Lahiʿa, from Jaʿfar ibn Rabīʿa, from al-Zuhrī, from Muḥarrar ibn Abī Hurayra, from ʿUmar, who said: “The Messenger of God ﷺ—forbade withdrawing from a free woman without her permission.”

And:

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-Sāʾib ibn Abī Lubāba

Abū Lubāba was Rifāʿa ibn al-Mundhir al-Rawāsī.

Al-Rabīʿ ibn Rūḥ related to me; Muḥammad ibn Ḥarb related to us; al-Zubaydī related to us, from al-Zuhrī, from Ḥusayn ibn [Abī] al-Sāʾib ibn Abī Lubāba, that his grandfather told him that when God accepted Abū Lubāba’s repentance for having stayed behind from the Messenger of God ﷺ—and for past matters that had angered the Messenger of God ﷺ—Ḥusayn claimed that Abū Lubāba said, when God accepted his repentance: “Messenger of God, I shall leave the home of my people where I committed the sin and move away to live near you. And I shall divest myself of my property as alms for God and His Messenger.” The Messenger of God ﷺ—said, as Ḥusayn related: “One third will suffice you.”

And among them:

Muḥammad ibn ʿUbāda ibn al-Ṣāmit

Yūsuf related to me; Isḥāq ibn Sulaymān related to us, saying: “I heard Muʿāwiya ibn Yaḥyā, from al-Zuhrī, from Muḥammad ibn ibn ʿUbāda ibn al-Ṣāmit, from his father, that the Messenger of God ﷺ—said: ‘The Night of Decree is in Ramaḍān. Whoever spends it in prayer out of faith and seeking reward will have his past sins forgiven. It is an odd-numbered night: the third, fifth, seventh, or ninth. Among its signs is that it is a bright, clear, still night, neither hot nor cold, as though the moon is present in it. No star is permitted to be cast in that night until morning. Among its signs—that is, its distinguishing mark—is that the sun rises the following morning level, without rays, as though it were the full moon. God has forbidden Satan to come out with it.’”14

And among them:

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd ibn Jāriya

Abū al-Yamān related to us; Shuʿayb informed me, from al-Zuhrī, who said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd ibn Jāriya said: “The Messenger of God ﷺ—used to pray the dawn prayer in the darkness before daybreak.”

And among them:

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Thaʿlaba al-Anṣārī

He transmits this report from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd ibn Jāriya.

Among them:

Ḥamzah ibn Abī Usayd

Muḥammad ibn Wahb ibn ʿUmar ibn Abī Karīmah told us: Muḥammad ibn Salamah told us, from Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq, from al-Zuhrī, from Ḥamzah ibn Abī Usayd, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ went out to the funeral of a man from the Anṣār in al-Baqīʿ. There was a wolf lying across the path, its forelegs outstretched. The Messenger of God ﷺ said, “This is Uways, seeking an allotment from me, so allot him his due.” They said, “Do you think this is right, Messenger of God?” He said, “One sheep from every grazing herd each year.” They said, “That is a lot.” He gestured to the wolf, saying, “Snatch from them stealthily.” Then the wolf went away.

And:

Usayd ibn Rāfiʿ ibn Khadīj

“Ḥarmalah told us: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Wahb related to us, from Ibn Lahīʿah, from Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb, from Ibn Shihāb, from Usayd ibn Rāfiʿ, from his father, who said: The Prophet ﷺ forbade leasing land in exchange for a portion of what it produced.”

Among them:

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Qatādah

ʿĪsā ibn Muḥammad told us: ʿAmr ibn al-Rabīʿ ibn Ṭāriq informed us, from Rushdayn ibn Saʿd, from ʿUqayl, from Ibn Shihāb, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Qatādah, from his father: He used to offer a sheep as a sacrifice on behalf of his household.

Among them:

Saʿd ibn Isḥāq ibn Kaʿb ibn ʿUjrah

Among them:

Khallād

Al-Zuhrī said: Khallād informed me that his father heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: “When one of you defecates, let him clean himself three times.”

Among them:

Yaḥyā ibn ʿUmārah ibn Abī Ḥasan al-Anṣārī

ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Uwaysī related to me: Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd related to us, from Ibn Shihāb, from Yaḥyā ibn ʿUmārah ibn Abī Ḥasan al-Māzinī, that it had reached him that some men among the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ asked the Messenger of God ﷺ about the whisperings with which Satan whispers within them. They said, “Messenger of God, we find things within ourselves such that it would be dearer to one of us to fall from the Pleiades than to speak of them.” The Prophet ﷺ said, “Have you found that to be pure faith? Satan seeks to get at a servant through what is lesser than that; when he is protected from it, he is raised to what lies beyond.”

And:

ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Thaʿlabah

Al-Ḥumaydī told us: Sufyān told us: al-Zuhrī told us: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Thaʿlabah told me that he heard ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd ibn Jāriyah say: “I heard—”

“My paternal uncle, Mujammaʿ ibn Jāriyah, say: ‘I heard the Prophet ﷺ’” and he mentioned the Antichrist, saying, “By Him in whose hand is my soul, the son of Mary will surely kill him at the gate of Ludd.”

Among them:

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā ibn Ḥibbān al-Anṣārī

Abū Ṣāliḥ and Ibn Bukayr told us, from al-Layth, from ʿUqayl, from Ibn Shihāb, who informed me that Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā ibn Ḥibbān said: A man said, “Messenger of God, I wish to devote all my prayer to you.” He said, “Then God will suffice you in the affairs of this world and the next.”

And:

Abū Sufyān ibn Jabr ibn ʿAtīk

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā related to me: Ibn Abī Maryam related to us: Ibn Lahīʿah informed us, from Jaʿfar ibn Rabīʿah, from Ibn Shihāb, who informed me that Abū Sufyān ibn Jabr ibn ʿAtīk said: Ḥafṣah bint Mubashshir al-Anṣārīyah became thirsty and could not fast because of her thirst. Abū Sufyān said: I asked ʿIkrimah, the client of Ibn ʿAbbās, and he said, “She should feed thirty poor people, one mudd each, grinding it, baking it, and preparing a relish with it.” He said: I went to Sālim ibn ʿAbd Allāh and asked him. He said:

“How badly ʿIkrimah has spoken! Rather, she should feed thirty poor people, one mudd each, without grinding it, baking it, or preparing a relish with it.”

Among them:

Naṣr al-Anṣārī

Al-Zuhrī said: Naṣr al-Anṣārī informed me that he heard Kaʿb al-Aḥbār say:

“He informed me that Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī said: ‘I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: When one of you has finished his prayer in the mosque and then returns home, let him pray then, and let him assign a share of his prayer to his home.’”

And:

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Thawr

Al-Zuhrī transmitted from him, from Ibn ʿAbbās: “I asked ʿUmar about … twice.”

Among the Successors of Medina from Muḍar, from whom al-Zuhrī transmitted

Among them:

Sinān ibn Abī Sinān al-Duʾalī

Abū al-Yamān told us: Shuʿayb informed me, from al-Zuhrī, who told me: Sinān ibn Abī Sinān al-Duʾalī and Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān told me that Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Anṣārī informed them: He went on a military expedition with the Messenger of God ﷺ on a campaign before Najd. When the Messenger of God ﷺ turned back, Jābir turned back with him. One day, the midday rest overtook them in a valley thick with thorn trees. The Messenger of God ﷺ dismounted, and the people dispersed among the thorn trees to take shade. The Messenger of God ﷺ rested beneath a tree and hung his sword on it. Jābir said:

“We slept for a while, and then the Messenger of God ﷺ called us. We answered him, and there was a Bedouin sitting beside him. The Messenger of God ﷺ said, ‘This man drew my sword while I was asleep. I awoke and found it unsheathed in his hand. He said, “Who will protect you from me?” I replied, “God.”’”

“He asked a second time, ‘Who will protect you from me?’ I replied, ‘God.’ Then he sheathed the sword and sat down. The Messenger of God ﷺ did not punish him, although he had done that.”

Among them:

al-Haytham ibn Abī Sinān al-Duʾalī

“Abū Ṣāliḥ and Ibn Bukayr told us; they said: al-Layth related to us: Yūnus related to me, from Ibn Shihāb, who informed me that al-Haytham ibn Abī Sinān heard Abū Hurayrah—while he was delivering a sermon—say in his sermon, as he mentioned the Messenger of God ﷺ: ‘Your brother does not speak falsehood’—meaning ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rawāḥah. He said:

The Messenger of God is among us, reciting His Book,when the clear light of dawn breaks forth and shines.Guidance came to us after blindness, and our heartsare certain that what he said will come to pass.A man whose side shuns his bed,when the beds weigh heavily upon the unbelievers.”

Among them:

ʿIkrimah ibn Muḥammad al-Duʾalī

Abū al-Yamān told us: Shuʿayb informed me.

And Ḥajjāj related to us, from his grandfather, from al-Zuhrī, who informed me that ʿIkrimah ibn Muḥammad al-Duʾalī said:

“His sister sent him to Abū Hurayrah to ask him about one who says, ‘There is no god but God,’ ten times.

Abū Hurayrah said to him: ‘Whenever one of you says it ten times, it is equivalent to freeing a person. So do not—’”

“Be unable to amass many people to free.”

And:

al-Sāʾib ibn Mālik al-Duʾalī

Ḥajjāj told us: My grandfather told us, from al-Zuhrī, who told me that al-Sāʾib ibn Mālik al-Duʾalī said: During ʿUmar’s caliphate, Ibn Abī ʿUrwah used to seek khulʿ from some of the women he married. Because of this, people began speaking about him in a way he disliked. When he learned of it, he took ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Arqam with him into his house and said to his wife, while Ibn al-Arqam could hear:

“I adjure you by God: do you hate me?” His wife said, “Do not adjure me.” He said, “No, I adjure you by God.” She said, “By God, yes.” Ibn Abī ʿUrwah said to ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Arqam, “Listen.”

Then Ibn Abī ʿUrwah went to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb and said, “Commander of the Faithful, you are saying that I wrong women and seek khulʿ from them. Ask ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Arqam what he heard from my wife.” ʿUmar sent for Ibn Abī ʿUrwah’s wife, and she came to him with her paternal aunt.

He said, “Are you the one whose husband tells me that you hate him?” She said, “Commander of the Faithful, I am the first to repent and return to God’s command. Commander of the Faithful, he adjured me, and I felt constrained to tell the truth. Would I lie, Commander of the Faithful?” He said, “Yes, lie to us. If one of you does not love one of us, do not tell him so. For few households are built on love; rather, people live together through Islam, kinship, and kindness.”

Among them:

al-Naḥḥām al-Kinānī

Abū al-Yamān told us: Shuʿayb reported to us.

And Ḥajjāj related to us, from his grandfather, from al-Zuhrī, who informed me that a man from Banū Mālik ibn Kinānah, one who followed jurisprudence and was called al-Naḥḥām, heard Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī addressing them:

“I tell you about these prayers of yours: when you avoid the major sins, we pray the noon prayer, then we commit offenses against ourselves. When we pray the night prayer—we mean the late-night prayer—it atones for what is between them; then we commit offenses against ourselves. When we pray the dawn prayer, it atones for what is between them, if you avoid the major sins.”15

And:

ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yazīd al-Laythī

He settled in Palestine.

Al-Muʿallā ibn Asad told us: Wuhayb related to us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yazīd al-Laythī, from Abū Ayyūb al-Anṣārī, from the Prophet ﷺ who said: “The witr prayer is due. Whoever wishes to pray witr as five units, let him do so; whoever wishes to pray it as three, let him do so; whoever wishes to pray it as one, let him do so. Whoever is unable should indicate it with a gesture.”

ʿAlqamah ibn Waqqāṣ al-Laythī

Muḥammad ibn Abī al-Sarī related to me: ʿAbd al-Razzāq related to us: Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī, who said: I was with al-Walīd ibn ʿAbd al-Malik, and he said, “The one who bore the greater part of it was ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib.” I said, “No. Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr, ʿAlqamah ibn Waqqāṣ, and ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh told me that they heard ʿĀʾishah say: ‘The one who bore the greater part of it was ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy ibn Salūl.’”

ʿĀmir ibn Akīmah al-Laythī

And:

Ibn Qaʿnab and Ibn Bukayr told us, from Mālik, from Ibn Shihāb, from Ibn Akīmah al-Laythī— “—from Abū Hurayrah: The Messenger of God ﷺ finished a prayer in which he had recited aloud and said, ‘Did any of you recite along with me just now?’ A man said, ‘Yes, Messenger of God.’ He said, ‘I wondered why I was being contended with over the Qurʾān.’ [The people then stopped reciting during the prayers in which the Messenger of God ﷺ recited aloud,] when they heard this from the Messenger of God ﷺ.”

And:

The nephew of Abū Ruhm al-Ghifārī

“Abū al-Yamān told us: Shuʿayb informed me.

And Ḥajjāj related to us, from his grandfather, from al-Zuhrī, who told me that the nephew of Abū Ruhm al-Ghifārī heard Abū Ruhm—who was among the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ who pledged allegiance to him beneath the tree—say: ‘I went on the Tabūk campaign with the Messenger of God ﷺ.’” When he turned back, he traveled at night—Ḥajjāj said, “journeyed at night”—by way of al-Akhṣar. I traveled close to him. Drowsiness overcame us, and I kept waking up to find my mount drawing near his mount. Its closeness alarmed me, for fear that I might strike his foot in the stirrup, so I would draw my mount back. At some point in the night my eyes overcame me, and my mount pressed against the mount of the Messenger of God ﷺ while his foot was in the stirrup, and I struck his foot. I did not wake until I heard him say, “Easy!” I said, “Messenger of God, ask forgiveness for me.” He said, “Go on.” The Messenger of God ﷺ began asking me about those of Banū Ghifār who had stayed behind, and I told him. As he questioned me, he said, “What became of those fair men?”—Ḥajjāj said, “the tall, ruddy, slender men.” I told him that they had stayed behind. He said, “What became of the dark—”

“—curly-haired, tightly curled men”—Ḥajjāj said, “the short men”—“who own livestock at Shabakat Sharḫ?”

Ḥajjāj said, “At Shabakat Shāriḥ.” I mentioned the men among Banū Ghifār, but did not name them until I remembered that they were a group from Aslam. I said, “Messenger of God, those are a group from Aslam, and they have stayed behind, Messenger of God.” He said, “What prevents any of those who stay behind from loading an energetic man onto one of his camels to serve in the path of God? For the dearest of my people to me to stay behind are the Emigrants from Quraysh, the Anṣār, Ghifār, and Aslam.”

Among them:

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mālik ibn Juʿshum al-Mudlijī

Ḥajjāj ibn Abī Manīʿ told us: My grandfather told me, from al-Zuhrī, who informed us that ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mālik ibn Juʿshum said: His father informed him that he heard Surāqah ibn Mālik ibn Juʿshum say: “The messengers of the unbelievers of Quraysh came to us, offering the blood-money for each of the Messenger of God ﷺ and Abū Bakr to whoever killed or captured them.”

Al-Ḥasan ibn al-Rabīʿ told us: Ibn Idrīs told us: Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq told us, from Ibn Shihāb, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mālik ibn Juʿshum, from his father, that his brother Surāqah ibn Juʿshum said: “I drew near the Messenger of God ﷺ while he was on a she-camel. I looked at his shins; they were like date-palm spathes.”

Among them:

Jaʿfar ibn ʿAmr ibn Umayyah al-Ḍamrī

Abū Nuʿaym told us: Ibrāhīm ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Mujammaʿ related to us: al-Zuhrī told me, from [Jaʿfar ibn ʿAmr] ibn Umayyah al-Ḍamrī, from his father: He saw the Messenger of God ﷺ eat meat from a shoulder, then pray without performing ablution.

Among them:

Yazīd ibn al-Aṣamm al-Hilālī

He was from Hawāzin, from Banū ʿĀmir ibn Ṣaʿṣaʿah.

Al-Ḥumaydī told us: Sufyān related to us: ʿAmr ibn Dīnār told us: I said to Ibn Shihāb, “Abū al-Shaʿthāʾ informed me, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that the Prophet ﷺ married while in a state of consecration.” Ibn Shihāb said, “Yazīd ibn al-Aṣamm informed me that the Prophet ﷺ married Maymūnah while not in a state of consecration, and she was his maternal aunt.” I said to Ibn Shihāb, “Do you prefer the word of a Bedouin who urinates on his heels to that of Ibn ʿAbbās, when she is also Ibn ʿAbbās’s maternal aunt?!”

And:

ʿArāk ibn Mālik al-Ghifārī

Ibn Qaʿnab and Ibn Bukayr told us, from Mālik, from Ibn Shihāb, from ʿArāk ibn Mālik and Sulaymān ibn Yasār: A man from Banū Saʿd ibn Layth raced a horse, and it stepped on the finger of a man from Juhaynah. The man was frightened by it and died. ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said to the one who claimed blood-money from them, “They must swear fifty oaths that he did not die from it.” They refused and felt scruples— Of the oaths, he said to the others, “You swear.” But they refused, so ʿUmar imposed half the blood-money upon the Saʿdīs.

And among them:

ʿUmar ibn Muḥriz al-Ashjaʿī

He was of Qays ʿAylān, of Ghatafān.

Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us: al-Layth related to me: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Khālid related to me, from Ibn Shihāb, that ʿUmar ibn Muḥriz al-Ashjaʿī related to him that he had heard from someone who narrated that Gabriel said: “There is no group of human beings living in ten houses whose homes I have not searched, and I have found no one among them more generous in spending wealth than the Messenger of God ﷺ.”

And among them:

Mālik ibn Aws ibn al-Ḥadathān al-Naṣrī

He was of Hawāzin, then of Qays ʿAylān.

Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Uways related to us: my father related to us: Ibn Shihāb al-Zuhrī, Muḥammad ibn Muslim ibn ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Shihāb, informed us that Mālik ibn Aws ibn al-Ḥadathān informed him, saying: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said: Abū Bakr said: The Messenger of God ﷺ—said, “We are not inherited from; what we leave is charity.”

And among them:

Muslim ibn Yazīd

He was one of the Banū Saʿd ibn Bakr ibn Qays.

Abū Ṣāliḥ and Ibn Bukayr related to us, both saying: al-Layth related to us: Yūnus related to me, from Ibn Shihāb, that he said: Muslim ibn Yazīd, one of the Banū Saʿd ibn Bakr ibn Qays, related to me:

Abū Shurayḥ ibn ʿAmr al-Khuzāʿī informed him—he was one of the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ—that the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ killed a man from Hudhayl. They had been pursuing him over a blood-feud from the pre-Islamic period, and he was in the Sacred Precinct, making his way to the Messenger of God ﷺ to pledge allegiance to him upon Islam. They killed him. When the Messenger of God ﷺ learned of his killing, he became exceedingly angry. The Banū Bakr went to Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, and the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ seeking their intercession with the Messenger of God ﷺ. In the evening, the Messenger of God ﷺ stood among the people, praised God as He deserves, and then said: “To proceed: God made Mecca sacred; the people did not make it sacred. He permitted it to me for one hour of the day, and thereafter it is sacred, as God made it sacred the first time. The most defiant of people toward God are three: a man who kills there; a man who kills someone other than his killer; and a man who pursues a blood-feud from the pre-Islamic period. By God, I shall pay blood-money for this man whom you killed.”

And:

ʿAbbād ibn Ziyād ibn al-Mughīra ibn Shuʿba

Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us: al-Layth related to me: Yūnus related to me, from Ibn Shihāb: ʿAbbād ibn Ziyād related to me, from ʿUrwa and Ḥamza, the two sons of al-Mughīra ibn Shuʿba, that they heard al-Mughīra ibn Shuʿba relate: He travelled with the Messenger of God ﷺ on the expedition to Tabūk. When dawn was near, the Messenger of God ﷺ turned aside. He said: I turned aside with him. He dismounted to relieve himself, and I had a water-skin with water in it. When the Messenger of God ﷺ came back to me, he told me I poured water from the water-skin over his hands three times. Then the Messenger of God ﷺ washed his face. He then went to bare his forearms, but the sleeves of the Messenger of God’s coat were too tight. So the Messenger of God ﷺ put his hands inside the neck opening and brought them out from beneath the coat. He washed them up to the elbows, then wiped his head and performed ablution over his leather socks. Then the Messenger of God ﷺ came back, and al-Mughīra came with him. They found that the people had begun the prayer and had put ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf forward to lead them. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān had led them in one rakʿa of the dawn prayer before the Messenger of God ﷺ arrived. The Messenger of God ﷺ came and stood in line with the people behind ʿAbd al-Raḥmān for the second rakʿa. When ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said the salutation, the Messenger of God ﷺ stood to complete his prayer. The people were alarmed by this and repeated the glorification of God many times. When the Messenger of God ﷺ had completed his prayer, he said to the people, “You did well,” or “You acted rightly.”

And:

Sālim ibn Abī ʿĀṣim al-Thaqafī

Ibrāhīm ibn al-Mundhir related to me: Maʿn related to me: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yaḥyā ibn Sulaymān related to me, from Ibn Shihāb, from Sālim ibn Abī ʿĀṣim al-Thaqafī, who said: I heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd say, “It is said: Whoever disowns a child who is his will have a bond fastened between its two ends on the Day of Resurrection.”

ʿAmr ibn al-Sharīd

And:

Ibn Qaʿnab, Ibn Bukayr, and Abū al-Walīd related to us, from Mālik, from Ibn Shihāb, from ʿAmr ibn al-Sharīd: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās was asked about a man who had two wives, one of whom breast-fed a boy and the other a girl. He was asked, “May the boy marry the girl?”

He said, “No: the milk is one and the same.” Then he took [something].

And:

ʿAmr ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yaʿlā ibn Umayya

Saʿīd ibn Abī Maryam related to us: Yaḥyā ibn Ayyūb informed us: ʿUqayl ibn Khālid related to me, from Ibn Shihāb, who informed him that Yaʿlā said: I spoke to the Messenger of God ﷺ about my father Abū Umayya on the day of the Conquest. I said, “Messenger of God, will you accept my father’s pledge of allegiance to emigrate?”

The Messenger of God ﷺ said, “Rather, I shall accept his pledge to strive in God’s cause, for emigration has come to an end.”

And among them:

ʿAmr ibn Abī Sufyān

Ibn Usayd ibn Jāriya al-Thaqafī.

Abū al-Yamān related to us: Shuʿayb informed me, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿAmr ibn [Abī] Sufyān ibn Usayd ibn Jāriya, from Abū Hurayra, from the Messenger of God ﷺ that he said: “Every prophet has a supplication. I intend, God willing, to keep my supplication in reserve as intercession for my community.”

And:

Yaʿqūb ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīra ibn al-Akhnas

Ḥarmala ibn Yaḥyā related to us: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yaḥyā ibn Ayyūb and Ibn Lahīʿa informed me, from ʿUqayl, from Ibn Shihāb, from Yaʿqūb ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīra ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Akhnas, from Ibn ʿUmar: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Iblīs entered Iraq and took care of his need there. Then he entered Syria, but they drove him away until he entered Busāq. Then he entered Egypt, where he laid eggs, hatched them, and spread out his ʿabqarī.”

And among them:

ʿUthmān ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Suwayd

And among them:

Muḥammad ibn Abī Sufyān al-Thaqafī

Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us: Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd related to me, from Ṣāliḥ ibn Kaysān, from Ibn Shihāb, from Muḥammad ibn Abī Sufyān ibn al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Jāriya al-Thaqafī, from Yūsuf ibn al-Ḥakam, from Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ. Another narrator said: from Muḥammad ibn Saʿd, from Saʿd, who said: I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say, “Whoever desires the humiliation of Quraysh, God will humiliate him.”

And:

Dāwūd ibn Abī ʿĀṣim al-Thaqafī

Saʿīd ibn Kathīr ibn ʿUfayr related to me: Ibn Wahb related to me: Yūnus informed me, from Ibn Shihāb, who said: Ibn al-Musayyab used to say, “It is a single divorce, and he may take her back.” Abū Bakr ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Hishām used to say the same as Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib says. Dāwūd ibn Abī ʿĀṣim ibn ʿUrwa ibn Masʿūd al-Thaqafī informed me of that from him. I did not hear it from Abū Bakr, nor did I ask him about it.

And:

ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAwf al-Qārī

“Abū Ṣāliḥ and Ibn Bukayr related to us, from al-Layth, from ʿUqayl, from Ibn Shihāb: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAwf al-Qārī, ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz’s administrator of the register of Palestine, informed me” that he had heard that God commanded the earth to obey Moses concerning Qārūn. When Moses met him, he said to the earth, “Obey!” It swallowed him up to his knees. Then he said, “Obey!”

It swallowed him up to his hips, while he called upon Moses for help. Then Moses said, “Obey!” and the earth swallowed him into its depths. God then revealed to Moses: “How hard your heart is—or, how callous your heart is—O Moses! By My might and majesty, had he called upon Me for help, I would have helped him.” Moses said, “My Lord, I did it in anger for Your sake.”

And among them:

ʿAwf ibn al-Ḥārith ibn al-Ṭufayl al-Azdī

Abū al-Yamān related to us: Shuʿayb informed me.

And Ḥajjāj related to us, from his grandfather, from al-Zuhrī: ʿAwf ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Ṭufayl related to me—he was the maternal half-brother of ʿĀʾisha, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ—that ʿĀʾisha related: ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr said, regarding a sale or a gift that ʿĀʾisha had given him, “By God, ʿĀʾisha must stop, or I shall place her under restraint.” She said, “Did he really say that?” They said, “Yes.”

ʿĀʾisha said, “I vow to God that I shall never speak to Ibn al-Zubayr again.” Ibn al-Zubayr then sought someone to intercede with her after her estrangement from him had lasted a long time. She said, “By God, I shall never allow anyone to intercede for him, nor shall I break the vow I have made.” When this went on for a long time, Ibn al-Zubayr spoke to al-Miswar ibn Makhrama and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd Yaghūth, both of whom were of the Banū Zuhra. He said to them, “I adjure you by God to bring me in to ʿĀʾisha, for it is not lawful for her to vow to sever relations with me.” Al-Miswar and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān came with him, wrapped in their cloaks, and sought permission to enter ʿĀʾisha’s presence. They said, “Peace be upon you, and God’s mercy and blessings. May we come in?”

ʿĀʾisha said, “Come in.” They asked, “All of us?” She said, “Yes, come in, all of you,” not knowing that Ibn al-Zubayr was with them. When they entered, Ibn al-Zubayr drew aside the curtain and embraced ʿĀʾisha. He began pleading with her and weeping, while al-Miswar and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān kept urging her to speak to him and accept his apology. They said, “The Messenger of God ﷺ forbade what you know of estrangement; it is not lawful for a Muslim to shun his brother for more than three days.” When they pressed ʿĀʾisha repeatedly with reminders and appeals, she began reminding them of her vow and weeping, saying, “I have made a vow, and a vow is a grave matter.” They persisted until she spoke to Ibn al-Zubayr. Then she freed forty slaves to expiate that vow. After freeing the forty slaves, she would still recall that vow, then weep until her tears soaked her veil.

And among them:

Al-Muʿallā ibn Ruʾba al-Tamīmī

Al-Aṣbagh related to me: Ibn Wahb informed me: Yūnus informed me, from Ibn Shihāb: al-Muʿallā ibn Ruʾba related to me, from Hāshim ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr, who informed me that ʿUmar ibn Ibn al-Khaṭṭāb16 suffered a calamity and came to the Messenger of God ﷺ and complained to him asking him to grant him one wasq of dates. The Messenger of God ﷺ said to him:

“If you wish, I shall order that you be given one wasq; or, if you wish, I shall teach you words that are better for you than it.”

He said, “Teach them to me, and order that I be given a wasq, for I need it.” He said, “I shall do so.” And he said:

“Say: O God, protect me through Islam when I am sitting, and protect me through Islam when I am lying down. Do not let an enemy or an envious person prevail against me. I seek refuge in You from the evil of what You hold by its forelock, and I ask You for all the good that is in Your hand.”

And:

Saʿīd ibn Marjāna

ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn ʿAbd Allāh related to me: Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd related to us, from Ibn Shihāb, from someone who related to him, from Saʿīd ibn Marjāna, who said: I sat with ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar, and he recited this verse: “To God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Whether you disclose what is within yourselves …” (2:284) to the end of the verse. He wept until I heard his sobbing. I got up and went to Ibn ʿAbbās, and told him what Ibn ʿUmar had recited.
