He said, “May God forgive Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān. When it was revealed, the Muslims experienced what ʿAbd Allāh experienced. Then God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed, ‘God does not burden any soul beyond its capacity’ (2:286) to the end of the verse. The whisperings were something the Muslims could not bear, and thereafter the matter was settled by God’s decree: the soul shall have what it has earned and bear what it has acquired, in word and deed.”

And among the Successors of Medina from Yemen:

Qabīṣa ibn Dhuʾayb

Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us: al-Layth related to me: Yūnus related to me, from Ibn Shihāb: Qabīṣa informed me ibn Dhuʾayb that he heard Abū Hurayra say: The Messenger of God ﷺ forbade a woman from being married together with her maternal aunt, or a woman together with her paternal aunt. We consider a woman’s father’s maternal aunt, her mother’s paternal aunt, and those whom I have mentioned to be in the same category. If this is through suckling, we consider it to be in the same category.

And among them:

ʿUthmān ibn Isḥāq ibn Kharasha

Al-Zuhrī transmitted from him, from Qabīṣa, the report about the grandmother.

Ḥanẓala ibn ʿAlī al-Aslamī

Abū Ṣāliḥ, Ibn Bukayr, and Muḥammad ibn Khallād related to us, from al-Layth: Ibn Shihāb related to me that Ḥanẓala ibn ʿAlī al-Aslamī informed him that he heard Abū Hurayra say: The Messenger of God ﷺ said, “By Him in whose hand is Muḥammad’s soul, the son of Mary will surely set out through the mountain pass of al-Rawḥāʾ, as a pilgrim or one performing the lesser pilgrimage, or he will combine the two.

And among them:

Abū ʿUthmān ibn Sunna

He was a Damascene.

And among them:

Ibn Abī Anas

Ḥajjāj related to us: my grandfather related to us, from al-Zuhrī: Ibn Abī Anas, a client of the Taymīs, related to me that his father related to him that he heard Abū Hurayra say: The Messenger of God ﷺ said, “When Ramadan comes, the gates of mercy are opened, the gates of Hell are closed, and the devils are chained.”

And:

Ibn Abī Ḥadred al-Aslamī

Al-Ḥasan ibn al-Rabīʿ related to us: Ibn Idrīs related to us, from Ibn Isḥāq: Yaʿqūb ibn ʿUtba related to me, from al-Zuhrī, from Ibn Abī Ḥadred al-Aslamī, from his father, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Ḥadred, who said: That day I was among Khālid’s cavalry. One of them said—and he was then about my age, his hands bound to his neck with a worn-out rope, and a group of women gathered not far away—“Young man!” I said, “Yes.” He said, “Will you take this rope and lead me—” to these women, so I may fulfill their need, and then you may return me afterward and do with me as you wish?” I said, “What you ask is a small thing.” He said: So I took hold of his worn rope and led him to them. He said:

“Be safe, Ḥubaysh, while life yet lasts:

“Have you considered: if I sought you out and found youat Ḥilya, or came upon you at al-Khawāniq,

“Was it not right that a lover should be grantedwhat he has striven for, journeying through the night and the rain?

“I am not to blame: when we turned aside together, I said,‘Reward me with affection before one of the calamities strikes.

“‘Reward me with affection before separation carries us far apart,and the commander departs with the beloved who is leaving.’”

She said, “And may you live for ten years, and a year, and eight more in succession.” Then I led him away, and his neck was struck [he was beheaded].

Among them:

Thaʿlaba ibn Mālik al-Quraẓī

Abū al-Yamān related to us: Shuʿayb informed us; and Ḥajjāj related to us, from Qurra, from al-Zuhrī, who said: Thaʿlaba ibn Mālik al-Quraẓī informed me—he had met ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb—and said: “We would converse when ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb sat on the pulpit, until the muezzin finished his call and ʿUmar began to speak. When ʿUmar spoke, our conversation stopped and we fell silent. None of us spoke until the imam had finished his sermon.”

Among them:

Ḍamra ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Unays al-Juhanī

Aḥmad ibn ʿAbda related to me: Fuḍayl ibn Sulaymān related to us, from Bukayr ibn Mismār, from al-Zuhrī, who said: “I asked Ḍamra ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Unays, ‘What did the Prophet ﷺ say to your father about the Night of Decree?’ He said: ‘My father was a man of the desert. He said:

“‘I said, “Messenger of God, tell me of a night on which I may stay there.” He said, “Stay there on the night of the twenty-third.”’ He said: ‘When he had turned away, the Messenger of God ﷺ said, “Seek it during the last ten nights.”’”

Among them:

ʿIyāḍ ibn Ṣayrī al-Kalbī

Al-Ḥajjāj ibn Abī Manīʿ related to us: My grandfather related to us, from al-Zuhrī, who said: ʿIyāḍ ibn Ṣayrī al-Kalbī informed me—he was a cousin and in-law of Usāma, whom Usāma had married to one of his daughters—that he heard Usāma ibn Zayd relate that a man who had come from one of the rural districts fell ill when he drew near Medina. This alarmed the people. When the Messenger of God ﷺ heard of it, he said:

“I hope that its mountain passes will not emerge upon us”—that is, the mountain passes of Medina.

Among them:

ʿIyāḍ ibn Khalīfa

Saʿīd ibn Abī Maryam related to us: Muḥammad ibn Sālim informed us: ʿAmr ibn Dīnār related to me: Ibn Shihāb informed me, from ʿIyāḍ ibn Khalīfa, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, who said that he heard him at Ṣiffīn say: “Reason is in the heart, compassion is in the liver, tenderness is in the spleen, and the soul is in the lung.”

And:

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Khalīfa

Al-Ḥumaydī related to us: Sufyān related to us: ʿAmr ibn Dīnār related to us, from Ibn Shihāb, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Khalīfa, who said: “I saw al-Hurmuzān at ʿArafāt with ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, raising his hands as he proclaimed the talbiya or the takbīr.”

Among them:

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Unays al-Sulamī

The account of the conversion to Islam of al-ʿAbbās ibn Mirdās al-Sulamī.

Among them:

ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Musayyab

Regarding the matter of al-akhlāf.

Among them:

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Saʿd, the cripple Abū al-Aswad related to me: Ibn Wahb informed us: Qurra ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān related to me, from Ibn Shihāb and Ṣafwān ibn Sulaym, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Saʿd, who related to him from Abū Hurayra, who said: “I prostrated with the Messenger of God ﷺ during ‘When the sky is split asunder’ (84:1) and ‘Recite in the name of your Lord’ (96:1)—two prostrations.”

And:

ʿUbayd ibn al-Sabbāq

Abū al-Yamān related to us: Shuʿayb informed me, from al-Zuhrī, who said: Ibn Sabbāq informed me that Zayd ibn Thābit al-Anṣārī—one of those who used to write down the revelation for the Messenger of God ﷺ—said: “Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq ﵁ sent for me after the people of al-Yamāma had been killed. ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb ﵁ was with him. Abū Bakr said, ‘ʿUmar came to me and said, “The killing of the Qurʾān reciters at al-Yamāma has become severe, and I fear that killing will become severe among the reciters in other places, so that much of the Qurʾān will be lost unless you gather it together. I think you should order that the Qurʾān be gathered.”’ Abū Bakr said, ‘I said to ʿUmar, “How can I do something that the Messenger of God ﷺ did not do?”’”

And:

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ḥāṭib ibn Abī Baltaʿa

Aṣbagh related to us, from Ibn Wahb, from Yūnus, from Ibn Shihāb, from ʿUrwa, from— ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ḥāṭib ibn Abī Baltaʿa. Ḥāṭib was a man from Yemen who was an ally of al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwām.

Among them:

Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān

He transmitted from ʿUmar and ʿUthmān.

Among them:

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAdī ibn al-Khiyār al-Nawfalī

And:

Saʿd ibn Ibrāhīm

Al-Faḍl ibn Ziyād related to me. He said: “I heard Abū ʿAbd Allāh”—that is, Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal—and he was asked, “Why did Mālik not transmit from Saʿd ibn Ibrāhīm?” He replied, “He had an incident with Saʿd.” Then he said, “Saʿd does not care if Mālik does not transmit from him.”

Among them:

Saʿīd ibn ʿUbayd ibn al-Sabbāq

Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us: al-Layth related to me: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Khālid related to me, from Ibn Shihāb, from Ibn ʿUbayd ibn al-Sabbāq, from his father ʿUbayd, who said: “Juwayriya, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ used to relate that the Messenger of God ﷺ came to her one day and said, ‘Is there any food?’ She said: ‘I replied, “Messenger of God, by God, we have no food except a bone from a sheep that I gave to our freedwoman from the alms.”’ He said, ‘It has reached its proper place.’”

Among them:

[Abū] Khuzāma ibn Yaʿmar al-Saʿdī

Saʿd Hudhaym was of Quḍāʿa.

Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us: al-Layth related to me: Yūnus related to me, from Ibn Shihāb, who said: Abū Khuzāma, one of the Banū al-Ḥārith ibn Saʿd, related to me that his father informed him that he asked the Messenger of God ﷺ: “Messenger of God, what do you think of incantations that we use, medicines that we take, and precautions that we observe? Do any of these ward off anything from God’s decree?” The Messenger of God ﷺ said, “They are part of God’s decree.”

And:

Ṭāriq ibn Maḥāsin

Ibn ʿUthmān related to us: ʿAbd Allāh informed us: Yūnus informed us, from al-Zuhrī, from Ṭāriq—he is ibn Maḥāsin—who said: “Abū Hurayra said: ‘A man stung by a scorpion was brought to the Messenger of God ﷺ. He said to him, “Had he said, ‘I seek refuge in the perfect words of God from the evil of what He has created,’ it would not have stung him—or harmed him.”’”

Among them:

Ṭāriq ibn Saʿd

Abū al-ʿAbbās al-Aʿraj related to me: ʿAbbād ibn Mūsā related to us: Ṭalḥa ibn Yaḥyā related to us: Yūnus ibn Yazīd related to us, from Ibn Shihāb, from Ṭāriq ibn Saʿd, from Abū Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said, “In Paradise there is a tree whose shade a rider would travel through for a hundred years.”

Among them:

Khālid ibn Rabāḥ

Abū Saʿīd ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and Sulaymān ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān related to me. They said:

Al-Walīd ibn Muslim related to us: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Numayr related to us, from al-Zuhrī, who said: Khālid ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rabāḥ al-Sulamī informed me that he prayed one rakʿa with Muʿāwiya on the day Muʿāwiya was stabbed at Īliyāʾ. Muʿāwiya was stabbed when he had completed it; he did no more than raise his head from prostration. Muʿāwiya said to the people, “Complete your prayer.” Each man stood and completed his prayer. He appointed no one to lead them, nor did the people appoint him.

Among them:

Farāfiṣa al-Ḥanafī

And among the clients from the people of Medina:

Those from whom al-Zuhrī transmitted.

Among them:

ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār

And ʿAṭāʾ, the client of Banū Sabāʿ.

And:

Nāfiʿ, the client of Abū Qatāda

And:

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Hunayda

The client of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb.

Aṣbagh ibn Faraj related to me, from Ibn Wahb, from Yūnus, from Ibn Shihāb, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Hunayda, from Ibn ʿUmar, from the Prophet ﷺ: “When God intends to create a soul…”

Among them:

Abū ʿUbayda Saʿd

The client of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Azhar.

Ibn Qaʿnab and Ibn Bukayr related to us, from Mālik, from Ibn Shihāb, from Abū ʿUbayda, the client of Ibn Azhar, who said: “I attended the Festival prayer with ʿUmar, and I attended the Festival prayer with ʿUthmān, and I attended the Festival prayer with ʿAlī while ʿUthmān was under siege.”

Among them:

Abū ʿAbd Allāh Salmān al-Agharr

The client of Juhayna.

Ibn Qaʿnab and Ibn Bukayr related to us, from Mālik, from Ibn Shihāb, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Agharr, from Abū Hurayra, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Our Lord descends each night to the lowest heaven when the last third of the night remains and says, ‘Who will call upon Me, that I may answer him? Who will ask Me, that I may give him? Who will seek My forgiveness, that I may forgive him?’”

And:

Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, the client of Ghifār

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us: Sufyān related to us: al-Zuhrī related to us, who said: “I heard Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from Abū Dharr, say: The Messenger of God ﷺ said, ‘When one of you stands to pray, mercy faces him, so let him not brush aside the pebbles.’” Sufyān said:

“Saʿd ibn Ibrāhīm asked al-Zuhrī, ‘Who is Abū al-Aḥwaṣ?’ Al-Zuhrī said, ‘Have you not seen the old man who prays in the garden?’ Al-Zuhrī began describing him, but Saʿd did not know him.”

Among them:

Abū Ṣāliḥ al-Sammān

The client of ʿAmr ibn al-Rabīʿ ibn Ṭāriq.

Yaḥyā ibn Ayyūb related to us, from Yūnus, from Ibn Shihāb: Abū Ṣāliḥ al-Sammān related to me, from Abū Hurayra, from the Messenger of God ﷺ who said: “One who is killed in the path of God is a martyr; one who dies of an abdominal illness is a martyr; one who dies by drowning is a martyr; and a woman who dies in childbirth is a martyr.”

Among them:

Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥunayn

The client of the family of al-ʿAbbās.

Ibn Abī Uways related to me: My brother related to me, from Sulaymān ibn Bilāl, from Usāma ibn Zayd, from Ibn Shihāb, from Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥunayn, that ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās and al-Miswar ibn Makhrama disagreed over whether a person in consecration could wash his head with water without being in a state of major ritual impurity. He said:

“He sent me to Abū Ayyūb, who was at one of the watering places of Mecca, to ask him about it. I came to him and found Abū Ayyūb bathing between the two ʿarnayn, while someone screened him with a cloth. I asked him, and he lowered the cloth with his hand until his head became visible to me. Then he moved both hands over his head and hair, passing his hands forward and back through his hair. Then he said, ‘This is how I saw the Messenger of God ﷺ bathe while in consecration.’” Ibrāhīm said: “I returned to them and told them.”

Among them:

Nabhān, the client of Umm Salama

Saʿīd ibn Abī Maryam related to me: Nāfiʿ ibn Yazīd informed us: ʿUqayl ibn Khālid related to me: Ibn Shihāb informed us, from Nabhān, the client of Umm Salama, from Umm Salama, who said: “The Messenger of God ﷺ came in while Maymūna and I were sitting, and sat down. The blind Ibn Umm Maktūm asked permission to enter. He said, ‘Veil yourselves from him.’ We said, ‘Messenger of God, is he not blind, unable to see?’ He said, ‘Can you two not see him?’”

Among them:

Yazīd ibn Hurmuz

The son of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Hurmuz al-Aʿraj.

And:

Isḥāq, the client of al-Mughīra ibn Nawfal

Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm related to us: ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith related to me: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sālim related to me, from al-Zubaydī, who said: al-Zuhrī informed me: Isḥāq, the client of al-Mughīra ibn Nawfal, informed me that al-Mughīra ibn Nawfal related to him, from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb al-Anṣārī, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “The Hour will not come until the Euphrates uncovers a mound of gold. People will fight over it, and nine-tenths of them will be killed.”

And:

Suhaym, client of Zuhrah

Abū al-Yamān related to us: Shuʿayb informed me. And Ḥajjāj related to us, from Qurrah, from al-Zuhrī, who said: Suhaym, client of the Banū Zuhrah, also informed me; he had heard Abū Hurayrah say:

The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “An army will raid this House, and they will be swallowed up by the earth at al-Bayḍāʾ.”

Among them is:

Kurayb, client of Ibn ʿAbbās

Sulaymān ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān related to us: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Bishr related to us, from Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq; Ibn Shihāb informed me, from Kurayb, from Ibn ʿAbbās: A man used to say to the Prophet ﷺ “You have entered the state of consecration for the pilgrimage alone.” He said, “It is only an ʿumrah.”

Among them is:

Abū Ḥasan, client of Ibn ʿAbbās

Abū Ṣāliḥ and Ibn Bukayr related to us, saying: al-Layth related to us; ʿUqayl related to me, from Ibn Shihāb. Abū Ḥasan, client of ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith—one of the earliest clients of Quraysh, and among their people of knowledge and rectitude—informed me that he heard a woman asking ʿAbd Allāh ibn Nawfal for a legal opinion about a boy of illicit birth whom she had to emancipate as a slave in fulfillment of an obligation. ʿAbd Allāh ibn Nawfal said to her:

“I do not think that emancipating a boy of illicit birth would discharge the obligation of emancipation incumbent upon you.” ʿAbd Allāh ibn Nawfal said: “I heard ʿUmar say, ‘Being made to ride in a pair of sandals in the path of God is dearer to me than emancipating a boy of illicit birth.’”

And:

Kathīr ibn Aflaḥ, client of Abū Ayyūb

Zayd ibn al-Mubārak related to us: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from Kathīr ibn Aflaḥ, client of Abū Ayyūb al-Anṣārī—and ʿAbd al-Razzāq said, from his father—who said: Ibn Sallām used to go to the Quraysh leaders before the people of Egypt arrived and say to them:

“Do not kill this man.” They would say, “By God, we do not intend to kill him.” Aflaḥ said: He would come out leaning on my arms, saying, “By God, they will surely kill him.” When Ibn Sallām was near death, he said, “Leave this man for forty nights; by God, if you leave him, he will surely die within that time.” But they refused. Some days later, he came back and said, “Leave him for fifteen nights; by God, if you leave him, he will surely die within that time.”

Among them is:

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Abī Rāfiʿ

Ādam related to us: Shuʿbah related to us: Sufyān ibn Ḥusayn said: I heard al-Zuhrī relate from Ibn Abī Rāfiʿ, from his father.

Al-Muʿallā related to us, from Yazīd ibn Zurayʿ, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Abī Rāfiʿ, from ʿAlī: He used to instruct people, and considered it good, to recite behind the imam in the noon and afternoon prayers: the Opening of the Book and a sūrah in each of the first two rakʿahs, and the Opening of the Book in the last two rakʿahs.

Among them is:

Ṣāliḥ ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Farwah

ʿAlī ibn ʿUbayd Allāh and ʿĪsā ibn Muḥammad related to us, saying: Yaʿqūb ibn Azhar ibn Saʿd related to us: Ibn Shihāb’s brother’s son related to me, from his paternal uncle. Ṣāliḥ ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Farwah informed me, from ʿĀmir ibn Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, who informed us that he heard Abān ibn ʿUthmān say: ʿUthmān said: I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say, “Tell me: if there were a river at the threshold of one of your homes, and he bathed in it five times every day, what dirt would remain on him?” They said, “None.” He said, “The prayers remove sins just as water removes dirt.”

Among them is:

Muzāḥim, client of ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz

Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Numayr related to us: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar al-ʿUmarī related to us: Yūnus ibn Yazīd related to us, from al-Zuhrī, from Muzāḥim, who said: I went out with ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz on one of his journeys. He said: He ordered a sheep to be slaughtered. A dog came and stood beside us. ʿUmar said, “Muzāḥim, throw him some of it, for he is the deprived one.”

Among them is:

Ḥarmalah, client of Usāmah

Sulaymān ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, Abū Saʿīd and Ṣafwān related to us. They said:

Al-Walīd ibn Muslim related to us: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Namir related to us, from al-Zuhrī. Ḥarmalah, client of Usāmah ibn Zayd, related to me that while he was sitting with ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar, al-Ḥajjāj ibn Ayman ibn Umm Ayman entered. He was a man from the Anṣār, and Ayman was a brother of Usāmah ibn Zayd and older than Usāmah. Ḥarmalah said: Al-Ḥajjāj performed a prayer without completing its bowing or prostration. When he had finished, Ibn ʿUmar called to him: “Nephew, do you think you have prayed? You have not prayed; repeat your prayer.” When al-Ḥajjāj turned away, ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar said to me, “Who is this?” I said, “Al-Ḥajjāj ibn Ayman ibn Umm Ayman.” Ibn ʿUmar said, “If the Messenger of God ﷺ had seen him, he would have loved him”—and he mentioned in this connection what Umm Ayman had borne, for she had been the Messenger of God’s nurse.

Among them is:

Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān,

client of the Banū ʿĀmir.

Ibn Qaʿnab and Ibn Bukayr related to us, from Mālik, from Ibn Shihāb, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Thawbān, from Muḥammad ibn Iyās ibn al-Bukayr, who said: A man divorced his wife three times before consummating the marriage, then decided that he wanted to marry her. He came to seek a legal opinion, and I went with him to ask on his behalf. He asked ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās and Abū Hurayrah, and they said, “We do not consider it to be a single divorce.” Ibn ʿAbbās said to him, “You have let go of what was yours to have of her.”

Among them is:

Ḥabīb, client of ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr

Abū Ṣāliḥ, Ibn Rumḥ, Aḥmad ibn Yūnus, and Ibn Bukayr related to us, from al-Layth ibn Saʿd. Ibn Shihāb related to me, from Ḥabīb, client of ʿUrwah, from Nadbah, client of Maymūnah, from Maymūnah, wife of the Prophet ﷺ: The Messenger of God ﷺ used to be intimate with one of his wives while she was menstruating, provided she wore a waist-wrapper reaching halfway down her thighs or to her knees, secured around herself.

And:

Jarīr ibn Abī ʿAṭāʾ,

client of the Banū Zuhrah.

Abū al-Yamān related to us: Shuʿayb informed me, from al-Zuhrī. Ibn Abī ʿAṭāʾ, a client of the Banū Zuhrah, informed me that he accompanied ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar on pilgrimage. When the Day of ʿArafah came, Ibn Abī ʿAṭāʾ awoke fasting, while ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar awoke not fasting. ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar said to him, “What do you think is keeping you from lunch?” He said, “I am fasting.” ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar fell silent. Ibn Abī ʿAṭāʾ then said, “What do you think, Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, about fasting on this day?” ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar replied, “As for me, I do not fast it.” Ibn Abī ʿAṭāʾ said to him:

“Then should I break my fast?” ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar said to him, “Do you want to say that Ibn ʿUmar ordered me to break my fast?” Ibn Abī ʿAṭāʾ said: So I broke my fast, and he neither forbade me nor censured me for it.

Among them is:

Busr ibn Saʿīd,

client of the Ḥaḍramīs.

Hārūn ibn ʿAbd Allāh related to me: Ibn Abī Fudayk related to us: Mūsā ibn Yaʿqūb ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Wahb ibn Zamʿah related to me, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Isḥāq, from Ibn Shihāb, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Surāqah, from Busr ibn Saʿīd, from Zayd ibn Khālid al-Juhanī, who informed him that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Whoever equips a warrior has a reward like his, and whoever looks after his family in his absence has a reward like his.” Ibn Shihāb said: Then Busr ibn Saʿīd informed him of it.

Among them are:

Abū Ḥamzah Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb al-Quraẓī,

and:

ʿĀṣim ibn ʿUmar ibn Qatādah al-Ẓafarī These are the names of the Successors of the third generation,

those from whom Mālik ibn Anas narrated.

Among them is:

Isḥāq ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Ṭalḥah al-Anṣārī

Ibn Qaʿnab and Ibn Bukayr related to us, from Mālik, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Ṭalḥah, from Anas ibn Mālik: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “O God, bless their ṣāʿ and their mudd”—meaning the people of Medina.

And:

Suhayl ibn Abī Ṣāliḥ Dhakwān al-Sammān,

client of Ghaṭafān.

Ibn Qaʿnab and Ibn Bukayr related to us, from Mālik, from Suhayl ibn Abī Ṣāliḥ, from his father, from Abū Hurayrah, who said: When people saw the first fruit, they would bring it to the Messenger of God ﷺ. When the Messenger of God ﷺ took it, he would say:

“O God, bless our fruits, bless our city, and bless our ṣāʿ and our mudd. O God, Abraham is Your servant, Your intimate friend, and Your prophet, and I am Your servant and Your prophet. He supplicated You for Mecca, and I supplicate You for Medina for the like of what he supplicated You for Mecca, and the like of it as well.” Then he would call the youngest child he saw and give him that fruit.

And:

Muḥammad ibn Muslim ibn ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Shihāb al-Zuhrī,

descendant of al-Ḥārith ibn Zuhrah.

Ibn ʿUfayr related to me, from ʿAṭṭāf, from ʿAbd al-Aʿlā [from Ibn Shihāb], who said: [ʿAbd al-Malik said to me], “By God, you had a father who was active in the civil strife and harmed us in it.” I said, “Commander of the Faithful …” He said, as the righteous servant had said:

“There shall be no reproach upon you today.” 12:92

Nāfiʿ, client of Ibn ʿUmar ﵁

ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn ʿImrān related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb related to us, saying: Usāmah ibn Zayd informed me, from Abū Bakr ibn Ḥafṣ ibn Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, from Sālim ibn ʿAbd Allāh, who said: “Ask Nāfiʿ, for he is the most knowledgeable of us about the hadith of Ibn ʿUmar.”

And:

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Dīnār, client of Ibn ʿUmar

Abū Ṣāliḥ and Ibn Bukayr related to us, saying: al-Layth ibn Saʿd related to us. Rabīʿah ibn Abī ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Dīnār related to me—he was one of the upright Muslims, truthful and devout—who said: The sun set while we were with ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar, and we continued on our way. When we saw that evening had come, we said to him, “The prayer.” He remained silent until the twilight had disappeared and the stars had come into view. He turned aside and performed the two prayers together. Then he said, “I saw the Messenger of God ﷺ when the journey pressed on him, perform these two prayers,” meaning that he combined them after nightfall.

[Mālik’s criterion in the Muwaṭṭaʾ]

Abū Yūsuf said: I have made a thorough investigation and listed the names one by one, because the general point is that Mālik ibn Anas did not include in the Muwaṭṭaʾ any chain of transmission or mention any narrator from whom he transmitted unless that person was trustworthy, with the exception of ʿAbd al-Karīm ibn Umayyah, who was weak and held an evil opinion. I have written, in the fourth volume, what has reached us concerning their merits and qualities.

Muḥammad related to me, saying: I heard ʿAlī:

Among Ibn ʿAbbās’s companions, those who transmitted from Abū Hurayrah

are ʿAṭāʾ, Ṭāwūs, Mujāhid, and ʿIkrimah. The ten jurists transmitted from Abū Hurayrah:

Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, Sulaymān ibn Yasār, Abū Bakr ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, Qabīṣah ibn Dhuʾayb, ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh, ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr, Sulaymān, and al-Qāsim. ʿAlī said: Khārijah and Abān ibn ʿUthmān were among the jurists, but I do not recall anything from them from Abū Hurayrah or from Ibn ʿUmar.

He said: I asked ʿAlī, “Did Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm al-Taymī meet any of the Prophet’s companions ﷺ?” He said, “Anas ibn Mālik, and he saw Ibn ʿUmar.”

I said to him, “Jābir?” He said, “No. He has good hadith, sound transmission, and is trustworthy when a trustworthy person transmits from him. I have seen light in his hadith. As for the transmission of the people of Kūfah from his son, from him, it is worthless. His son is weak and munkar in hadith.”

Abū Ṭuwālah ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān,

descendant of Maʿmar al-Anṣārī. He heard from Anas ibn Mālik.

Ṣāliḥ ibn Muḥammad ibn Zāʾidah,

Abū Wāqid al-Laythī. Al-Darāwardī and Wahīb ibn Khālid transmitted from him. “Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb had heard some of his hadith from Wahīb, and Wahīb was enough for him; but Sulaymān did not know who he was, so he would not transmit from him in Baṣrah. When Sulaymān was appointed judge over Mecca and met the Medinans, they praised him, told him about his standing, and said, ‘This man was among our best and most ascetic; he was a man of military campaigns and striving in God’s cause.’ So he transmitted from him in Mecca.”

Al-Faḍl ibn Ziyād related to me: He said, “I asked Abū ʿAbd Allāh—or he was asked—about Muṣʿab ibn Muḥammad, and he said, ‘I know nothing but good of him.’”17

ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith was one of the hadith scholars.

Isḥāq ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Ṭalḥa was a thoroughbred authority in hadith. He was asked about ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn Jaʿfar and said, “Yaḥyā said: ‘Sufyān used to regard ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn Jaʿfar as weak.’ But ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd’s hadith is quite close [to acceptability]; there is nothing wrong with him.”

Aḥmad said: “Hishām ibn ʿAmr al-Fazārī, from whom Ḥammād narrated, is one of the trustworthy.”

“I heard Abū ʿAbd Allāh mention ʿAbbād ibn al-ʿAwwām and say: ‘He resembled the hadith scholars.’”

I heard Abū ʿAbd Allāh say: “ʿAbbād heard that Ismāʿīl had declared him mistaken in a hadith, so he said, ‘Tell him: take the pen from behind your ear.’”

I heard Abū ʿAbd Allāh say: “One day I was present with Hushaym, and he mentioned ʿAbbād. He said:

‘Pray to God, Mighty and Majestic, for our brother ʿAbbād, for he is ill.’”

One day I was present when ʿAbbād said of a hadith he had mentioned, “Hushaym made a mistake.” Abū ʿAbd Allāh said, “Consider this: Hushaym prays for him, while ʿAbbād declares him mistaken.”

He said: “I asked Abū ʿAbd Allāh about Yazīd ibn ʿAbd al-Malik al-Nawfalī. He said: ‘A shaykh from the people of Medina; there is nothing wrong with him.’”

I heard al-Ḥumaydī say: “I came to Medina and began by visiting ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Muḥammad al-Darāwardī. A group of people from Medina came, reproaching me and saying, ‘You left our shaykh and began with him, going to visit him.’ He said: ‘They reproached me for what I had done. I had only gone to al-Darāwardī’” “to greet him and write down something from him; my reliance, God willing, would be on Ibn Abī Ḥāzim. Word reached al-Darāwardī that the people had gathered around me. When I returned to him, he said, ‘Qurashī, I heard what happened. I had resolved to bring out my books and notebooks for you, so you could copy them and I could read them to you.’ He brought out his notebooks, and they proved to be sound books with well-grounded hadiths. Hadiths used to be brought to him and read aloud to him. If there was a flaw in any hadith attributed to him, it came from what I have told you: people used to read from his books. He would also discuss hadiths that he did not have with him, and they would dismiss them, saying, ‘This was not in his books.’ He would discuss a report attributed to the Prophet and say, ‘This is disconnected in the original of his book.’”

Al-Faḍl related to me: He said, “I heard Abū ʿAbd Allāh mention Sulaymān ibn Bilāl and say:

‘He was trustworthy. He was the secretary of Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd, and he had been in charge of the market of Medina.’”

I heard Abū ʿAbd Allāh say: “Al-Darāwardī’s book had become more reliable than his memory. He was known for seeking knowledge and hadith.”

I heard Abū ʿAbd Allāh mention a report from Hishām, from his father, from ʿĀʾisha: “He used to seek for the Prophet ﷺ water made sweet from the houses of al-Suqyā.” He said, “Only al-Darāwardī narrated it, and it was not in the original of his book.”

Abū Ṭālib related to us from Abū ʿAbd Allāh, who was asked about ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn [Abī] Ḥāzim and ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz al-Darāwardī. He said: “Al-Darāwardī was known for hadith and the pursuit of knowledge. When he narrated from his own book, it was sound; when he narrated from other people’s books, he would make mistakes. He used to read from their books to people and would make mistakes. Sometimes he reversed a hadith of ʿAbd Allāh al-ʿUmarī, narrating it from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUmar.” He was asked, “Perhaps ʿUbayd Allāh narrated it?” He said: “ʿUbayd Allāh was more firmly grounded than that. When he read from his own book, it was sound. Ibn Abī Ḥāzim was not known for pursuing hadith beyond his father’s books. He was a jurist; it is said that there was no one in Medina more learned in jurisprudence than he after Mālik. It is said that Sulaymān ibn Bilāl bequeathed to him, and Sulaymān’s books came into his possession, though he had not heard them. He narrated from people whom he was not known to have heard from, and he was scarcely known for pursuing hadith beyond his father’s books, for they say he heard those books.”

Al-Darāwardī was from a village in al-Ahwāz. Yaʿqūb al-Mājishūn was from Isfahan. When some of them greeted one another, he would say, “Shūnī, shūnī,” and so he was called al-Mājishūn. He said: “ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Salama is Yaʿqūb ibn Abī Salama, and this ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Salama is his brother. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz is the son of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Salama. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz used to speak sharply about Mālik. He said, ‘What was Mālik doing? He was a jurist, and when he was asked about hadith, he would say, “We only give legal opinions!!”’”

He said: “I asked Abū ʿAbd Allāh, ‘What is the quality of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd ibn Aslam’s hadith?’ He said, ‘His brother is more firmly grounded’”—meaning ʿAbd Allāh ibn Zayd ibn Aslam.

Abū Ṭālib said, reporting from Abū ʿAbd Allāh: “I asked him about Usāma ibn Zayd ibn Aslam.” He said: “Usāma ibn Zayd, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd, and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Zayd are the three sons of Zayd ibn Aslam. Usāma and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān are comparable to one another and are weak, while ʿAbd Allāh is trustworthy.”

Aḥmad ibn Budayl related to me: He said, Isḥāq ibn Sulaymān related to us: He said, Mūsā ibn ʿUbayd related to us: He said, Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Qarrāẓ related to me: “I was among the earliest Persian captives taken in the time of ʿUmar.”

Abū Ṣāliḥ and Ibn Bukayr related to us: They said, al-Layth related to us: He said, ʿUqayl related to me, from Ibn Shihāb, who said: ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtba informed me, from Shibl ibn Khālid al-Muzanī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Mālik al-Awsī, from the Messenger of God ﷺ that he said: “If a slave girl commits fornication, flog her. Then if she commits fornication again, flog her. Then if she commits fornication again, flog her. Then if she commits fornication again, sell her, even for a rope. A ḍafīr is a rope.”

Ḥaywa and Ibn al-Muṣaffā related to us: They said, Baqiyya related to us, from al-Zubaydī, from— Al-Zuhrī, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Shibl—Ḥaywa said, “ibn Khālid,” while Ibn al-Muṣaffā said, “ibn Khulayḍ al-Muzanī”—who informed him that ʿAbd Allāh ibn Mālik al-Awsī informed him that the Prophet ﷺ said: “If a slave girl commits fornication, flog her. Then if she commits fornication again, flog her. Then, if she commits fornication, sell her, even for a rope made of hair”—on the third or fourth occasion.

ʿUbayd Allāh also reported from Zayd ibn Khālid al-Juhanī something similar.

Ibn Qaʿnab and Ibn Bukayr related to us, from Mālik, from Ibn Shihāb, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Abū Hurayra and Zayd ibn Khālid al-Juhanī, that the Messenger of God ﷺ was asked about a slave woman who had committed fornication but was not married. He said: “If she commits fornication, flog her. Then if she commits fornication again, flog her. Then if she commits fornication again, flog her. Then sell her, even for a rope.” Ibn Shihāb said: “I do not know whether this is after the third or the fourth time. A ḍafīr is a rope.”

Al-Ḥumaydī related to us: He said, Sufyān related to us: He said, al-Zuhrī related to us: ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtba related to me, from Abū Hurayra and Zayd ibn Khālid al-Juhanī, who were asked. They said: “We were with the Messenger of God ﷺ when he was asked about a slave woman who commits fornication,” and he related a similar report.

He said, “On the third or fourth occasion.” Maʿmar says: “From Zayd and Abū Hurayra.” Ibn ʿUyayna says: “Shibl ibn Maʿbad,” which is an error.

Ādam related to us: He said, Ibn Abī Dhiʾb related to us: He said, al-Zuhrī related to us, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Abū Hurayra and Zayd ibn Khālid al-Juhanī, who said: “A Bedouin came and said, ‘Messenger of God, judge between us by the Book of God, Mighty and Majestic.’ His opponent stood up and said:

‘He speaks the truth, Messenger of God. Judge between us by the Book of God, Mighty and Majestic.’

The Bedouin said: ‘My son was a hired laborer for this man and committed fornication with his wife. They told me that stoning was due for my son, so I ransomed him from it for a hundred sheep and a slave girl. Then I asked the people of knowledge, and they told me that my son was liable only to a hundred lashes and banishment for a year.’ The Messenger of God ﷺ said: ‘I shall judge between you by the Book of God, Mighty and Majestic. As for the sheep and the slave girl, they are to be returned to you. Your son is liable to a hundred lashes and banishment for a year. As for you, Unays’”—to a man among the people—“‘go tomorrow to this man’s wife and stone her.’ Unays went the next day and stoned her.”

Ibn Qaʿnab and Ibn Bukayr related to us, from Mālik, from Ibn Shihāb, from ʿUbayd Allāh, from Abū Hurayra and Zayd ibn Khālid al-Juhanī, who informed him that two men brought a dispute before the Messenger of God ﷺ. One of them said, “Messenger of God, judge between us by the Book of God, Mighty and Majestic.” The other—who was more learned in jurisprudence than the two—said, “Yes, Messenger of God, judge between us by the Book of God, and permit me to speak.” He said, “Speak.” The man said, “My son was a hired laborer for this man.” A hired laborer is an ʿasīf. He then related a similar account.

Abū Ṣāliḥ, Ibn Bukayr, Ibn Rumḥ, and Muḥammad ibn Khallād related to us: They said, al-Layth related to us: He said, Ibn Shihāb related to me, from ʿUbayd Allāh, from Abū Hurayra and Zayd ibn Khālid, who said: “A man from among the Bedouins came to the Messenger of God ﷺ” and related a similar account. Abū Ṣāliḥ likewise transmitted it from al-Layth, from Yūnus, from Ibn Shihāb, from ʿUbayd Allāh and Abū Hurayra and Ibn Khālid, who were asked.

Al-Ḥumaydī said: Sufyān was asked, “But Mālik and Maʿmar both say that there is uncertainty in it.”

He said: “But I say it; I have firmly retained it from al-Zuhrī in both hadiths.”

Abū al-Yamān transmitted it from Shuʿayb, and Ḥajjāj transmitted it from his grandfather, from al-Zuhrī, and said:

“From Abū Hurayra alone.” Abū Ghassān transmitted it from ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn al-Mājishūn and said, “From Zayd ibn Khālid,” without mentioning Abū Hurayra. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Khālid likewise transmitted it from Abū Hurayra alone.

Abū Ṣāliḥ, Ibn Bukayr, and Ibn Rumḥ related to us: They said, al-Layth related to us: He said, Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb related to me, from ʿAmmār ibn Abī Farwa, that Muḥammad ibn Muslim related to him, that ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr related to him, that ʿAmra bint ʿAbd al-Raḥmān related to him, that ʿĀʾisha related to her that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “If a slave woman commits fornication, flog her; and if she commits fornication again, flog her; and if she commits fornication again, flog her; then sell her, even for a rope. A ḍafīr is a rope.”

Abū al-Yamān related to us: He said, Shuʿayb informed me.

And Ḥajjāj related to us, from his grandfather, from al-Zuhrī, from Abū Bakr ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Hishām, that Ḥazn ibn Jābir informed him. Ḥajjāj said:

“Jazīʾ ibn Jābir al-Khathʿamī heard Kaʿb al-Aḥbār say: ‘When God, Mighty and Majestic, spoke to Moses ﵇ in all the tongues before his own, Moses ﵇ kept saying, “My Lord, I do not understand this,” until, the second time, He spoke to him in his own tongue, in a voice like his.’ He said:

‘My Lord, is there anything among Your creation that resembles Your speech?’ He said, ‘No; the closest in resemblance to My speech is the loudest of what is heard among thunderclaps.’”

Aṣbagh ibn Faraj related to us, from Ibn Wahb, from Yūnus, who said, “Jazʾ ibn Jābir informed him.” Aḥmad ibn Shabīb related to us, from his father, from Yūnus, who said, “Jazʾ ibn Jābir informed him.” Zayd ibn al-Mubārak related to us, from Ibn Thawr, from Maʿmar, who said, “Jazʾ ibn Jābir informed him.” Abū Bakr said: “The correct form is Jazz ibn Jābir. This is what the people of Palestine say, and they know better than others because he was a man from Palestine.”

Saʿīd ibn Asad related to me: He said, Ḍamra related to us, from Rajāʾ ibn Abī Salama, that Jazz ibn Jābir was a judge in Palestine. He left behind only half a dirham, and he was one of those who wept much. Ibn Muḥayrīz used to say, “You should follow Jazz ibn Jābir,” meaning because of his piety and merit.

“Wuhayb ibn al-Ward and ʿAbd al-Jabbār ibn al-Ward are Meccans, both trustworthy.”

The people of Mecca say: “Wuhayb was one of the abdāl, trustworthy, firmly grounded, and careful about his sustenance; he avoided eating the food and fruit from Mecca’s private estates.” I heard Ibn Numayr say: “I was told that ʿAbbād ibn Kathīr said to Wuhayb ibn al-Ward, ‘I have hadiths about meritorious acts, but the hadith scholars do not write them down from me or listen to them from me. Take them from me and narrate them to them, so that they may learn them and you may earn a reward.’”

He replied, “You have done what you have done to yourself, and now you want to disgrace me!”

Saʿīd related to us, from Sufyān, from Muṣʿab ibn Muḥammad ibn Shuraḥbīl, one of the Banū ʿAbd al-Dār: “His hadith is good.”

“Isḥāq ibn Rāshid is a Jazīrī; his hadith is good.”

Maʿmar ibn Rāshid was a Basran who settled in Yemen; the two were not related.

Saʿīd related to us: He said, Sufyān related to us, from ʿUmar ibn Ḥabīb, a trustworthy Meccan.

“ʿUmar ibn Ḥabīb al-Baṣrī, the judge, is weak; his hadith is not to be written down.”

“Ismāʿīl ibn Kathīr, Abū Hāshim, is a trustworthy Meccan”. Ibn Jurayj, Yaḥyā ibn Sulaym, and Sufyān al-Thawrī narrated from him; he is trustworthy.

Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, the client of the family of Ṭalḥa, is a trustworthy Meccan.

Ibn ʿUyayna narrated from Ziyād ibn Saʿd, who is trustworthy, originally from Khurāsān and settled in Mecca.

Shibl ibn ʿAbbād is a trustworthy Meccan.

Al-Ḥajjāj and Ibn Abī Uways related to us, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Qudāma al-Jumaḥī, a trustworthy Medinan.

Al-Makkī related to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Saʿīd ibn Abī Hind, a trustworthy Medinan. Mālik ibn Anas, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar, ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mubārak, and Ibn Abī Fudayk narrated from him.

Mūsā ibn Ismāʿīl related to us: He said, Mūsā ibn Abī al-Furāt related to us, a Meccan; there is nothing wrong with him.

Muḥammad ibn Muslim al-Ṭāʾifī—although Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna is more firmly grounded than he—is also “trustworthy; there is nothing wrong with him.”

Abū ʿĀṣim related to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ṣiddīq ibn Mūsā, who is ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr; he is a Medinan.

Saʿīd ibn Mīnāʾ is a Meccan, and Ayyūb al-Sakhtiyānī narrated from him.

Abū Bakr ibn Kaysān. Kaysān said: “I performed tamattuʿ while I was a slave, so I asked Ibn ʿUmar and Makhrama ibn Bukayr.” Mālik used to speak well of him.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Nawfal ibn al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib al-Hāshimī is trustworthy.

ʿAbd Allāh, from whom ʿAmr ibn Murra narrates, is firmly grounded and was a teacher.

ʿAbd Allāh, from whom Khalaf ibn Khalīfa narrated, is weak.

Abū Nuʿaym related to us: He said, Muḥammad ibn Shurayk, Abū ʿUthmān, a Meccan, related to us: “There is nothing wrong with him.”

Abū Zayd Saʿīd ibn al-Rabīʿ related to us: He said, Shuʿba related to us, from Muslim ibn Nayyāq, who said: “I heard Ibn ʿAmr, who saw a man trailing his waist-wrapper, say: ‘I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: “Whoever trails his waist-wrapper, seeking nothing but vanity, God, Mighty and Majestic, will not look at him on the Day of Resurrection.”’” Shuʿba did not hear from al-Ḥasan ibn Muslim; al-Ḥasan had died before his father, Muslim ibn Nayyāq.

Abū Nuʿaym related to us: He said, ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn Ayman related to us: “I saw Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥanafiyya wearing a turban.” ʿAbd al-Wāḥid was a Meccan.

Muslim ibn Ibrāhīm related to us: He said, Hammām ibn Yaḥyā related to us, from al-Qāsim ibn ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn Ayman, who said:

[And] Abū Bishr related to me: He said, ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Ibrāhīm al-Jiddī, from the people of Jidda, related to us: He said, Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad al-Ṭāʾifī related to us: He said, al-Qāsim ibn ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn Ayman related to me: He said, ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUrwa related to us, from ʿUrwa, from— ʿĀʾisha said: “I boasted of my father’s wealth in the pre-Islamic period; it amounted to a thousand thousand uqiyyas.” The Prophet ﷺ—said: “Be quiet, ʿĀʾisha, for I was to you as Abū Zarʿ was to Umm Zarʿ.”

Abū ʿĀṣim related to us, from Yazīd ibn [Abī] ʿUbayd, from Salama ibn al-Akwaʿ, that he used to forbid his sons to play at arbaʿ ʿashara [“fourteen”].

Abū Ṣāliḥ informed us; Bakr ibn Muḍar related to me, from ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith, from Bukayr ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ashajj, from Yazīd, the client of Salama ibn al-Akwaʿ, from Salama ibn al-Akwaʿ, who said: When this verse was revealed, “And those who are able to fast may redeem it by feeding a poor person” (Qurʾān 2:184), whoever among us wished to break the fast and offer redemption did so, until the verse that followed it was revealed and abrogated it.

Ibn Abī ʿUmar related to us; Sufyān related to us; I said to Ṣadaqa ibn Yasār: “They claim that you are one of the Khārijites.” He smiled and said: “I am not one of them, though I used to be one of them.”

Ṣadaqa was a trustworthy Meccan.

ʿAmr ibn ʿAṭāʾ ibn Warāz was a Meccan, mild in disposition.

Rabīʿa ibn Abī ʿAbd al-Raḥmān—and Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān’s name was Farrūkh.

Aḥmad ibn al-Khalīl related to me; al-Haytham ibn Jamīl related to us; ʿAṭṭāf ibn Khālid related to us, from his mother, from the wife of Abū Bakr ibn ʿAmr ibn Ḥazm, who said:

Abū Bakr did not lie down on his bed at night for forty years.

Ibrāhīm ibn al-Mundhir related to us; Ibn Nāfiʿ related to me; Miktal ibn Abī Sahl related to me, from Abū Bakr ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Hishām, from Zayd ibn Thābit, who said: “When you see the people of Medina following a practice, know that it is the Sunna.”

Ismāʿīl related to us; Ibn ʿAwn informed us, from Ibrāhīm, who said: ʿAlqama rode to ʿUmar, and they said to him: “Preserve something for us from him.” When he returned, he said: “Among what I preserved was that he performed ablution twice for each part.” ʿAlī said: “Abū Farwa was a Nahdī, affiliated with the Juhayna.”

Muḥammad ibn [Abī] Zukayr al-Ṣadafī related to me; Ibn Wahb informed us, from Mālik, who said: I heard him relate that the man said: “The noblest of people will be raised from Medina: Muḥammad and his party, and the martyrs of Badr and Uḥud.”

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us; Sufyān related to us; Misʿar related to us. I said to Jundub ibn Abī Thābit: “Which of them adhere more closely to the Sunna, the people of the Ḥijāz or the people of Iraq?” He said: “Rather, the people of the Ḥijāz.”

[Muḥammad ibn Abī al-Sarī related to us; ʿAbd al-Razzāq related to us; he said: He informed us—]

al-Thawrī, from Abū Farwa, from Abū ʿAmr al-Shaybānī, from Ibn Masʿūd: A man from Banū Shamkh of Fazāra married a woman, then saw her mother and was attracted to her. He asked Ibn Masʿūd for a legal opinion about this, and Ibn Masʿūd instructed him to separate from his wife and marry her mother. He married her, and she bore him children. Then Ibn Masʿūd came to Medina and asked about the matter; he was told that she was not lawful to him. When he returned to Kūfa, he said to the man: “She is forbidden to you; she is not permissible for you. Separate from her.”

Abū Bishr related to us; Rawḥ related to us; Shuʿba related to us, saying: Abū Farwa informed me, from Abū ʿAmr al-Shaybānī, who said: A man from Banū Fazāra married a woman, but she died before he had consummated the marriage. ʿAbd Allāh gave him a dispensation to marry her mother, and gave him a dispensation regarding currency exchange. When ʿAbd Allāh came to Medina and returned, he took me by the hand, went to the members of the household whom he had instructed, and forbade them; then he went to the money changers and forbade them.

Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr related to us; Ḥudayj ibn Muʿāwiya related to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Saʿīd ibn Iyās, from a man who married a woman from Banū Shamkh. Later, he saw her mother and was attracted to her. He went to Ibn Masʿūd and said: “I married a woman but have not consummated the marriage; then I became attracted to her mother. May I divorce the woman and marry her mother?” He said: “Yes.” The man divorced her and married her mother. ʿAbd Allāh then came to Medina and asked the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ. They said: “That is not proper.” Then he returned and went to Banū Shamkh, saying: “Where is the man who married the mother of the woman who had been his wife?” They said: “Here.” He said: “Let him separate from her.” They said: “But she has borne him many children.” He said: “Let him separate from her, for she is forbidden by God, Mighty and Majestic.”

Ḥammād related to us; al-Ḥajjāj informed us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū ʿAmr al-Shaybānī, that a man asked Ibn Masʿūd about a man who had divorced his wife before consummating the marriage: “May he marry her mother?” He said: “Yes.” The man married her, and she bore him children. He came to ʿUmar and asked him. He said: “Separate the two of them.” The man said: “But she has borne children.” ʿUmar said: “Even if she has borne ten, separate the two of them.”

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā related to us, from Shaybān, from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrāhīm, who said:

ʿAbd Allāh used to sell the discarded contents of the public treasury until he met his companions, who forbade him to do so. He said: “I see no harm in it, but I will not do it.”

Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr related to us; Hushaym related to us, from Mujālid, from al-Shaʿbī, that ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd sold the public treasury’s discarded debased coins and worn coins for dirhams at less than their weight. This was reported to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, who forbade him to do so and said: “Heat them until the copper or iron in them is gone and the silver is pure; then sell the silver by its weight.”

[Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us; Sufyān related to us; Ṣāliḥ ibn Ṣāliḥ ibn Ḥayy al-Hamdānī related to us. He was better than his two sons, ʿAlī and al-Ḥasan, and ʿAlī was the better of the two—meaning, of the other one. He said: A man came to al-Shaʿbī while I was with him and said: “Abū ʿAmr, some people among us say that when a man emancipates his slave woman and then marries her, he is like one who rides his sacrificial camel.”

Al-Shaʿbī said: Abū Burda ibn Abī Mūsā related to me, from his father, that the Messenger of God ﷺ—said: “There are three who will be given their reward twice: a man from the People of the Book who believed before the Prophet ﷺ—was sent, for he has two rewards; and a man—] who had a slave woman, taught her and taught her well, disciplined her and disciplined her well, then emancipated her and married her—he has two rewards; and a slave who obeys God and fulfills his master’s due—he has two rewards. Take this without charge, for a man would travel to Medina for less than this.”

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā related to us, from Isrāʾīl, from Abū Isḥāq, from Saʿd ibn Iyās, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd: A man from Banū Shamkh ibn Fazāra asked him about a man who married a woman, then saw her mother and was attracted to her. He divorced his wife and asked: “May he marry her mother?” He said: “There is no harm.” The man married her. ʿAbd Allāh was in charge of the public treasury and used to sell its discarded contents, giving a great deal and taking little, until he came to Medina and asked the Companions of Muḥammad ﷺ. They said: “This woman is not lawful for that man, and silver is valid only when exchanged weight for weight.” When ʿAbd Allāh returned, he went to the man but did not find him; he found his people and said: “The opinion I gave your companion is not lawful.” They said: “But she has borne him many children.” He said: “Even so.” He went to the money changers and said: “Company of money changers, what I used to trade with you in [is not lawful]; silver may only be exchanged for silver weight for weight.”

[ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm related to us, from Abū Qaṭan, from Abū Khalda, from Abū al-ʿĀliya, who said: We used to hear reports from the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ—in Medina and Baṣra, but we were not satisfied until we went to them and heard from them.]

They were not satisfied until they went to them and heard from them.

Muḥammad ibn Abī Zukayr related to me; Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: I heard Mālik say: “By God, Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab and the other people of Medina were not troubled by what anyone said. Had ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz acquired this knowledge in Medina, many people would have cast doubt on it.”

[Abū al-Ṭāhir Aḥmad ibn ʿAmr ibn al-Sarḥ related to us; Anas ibn ʿIyāḍ related to us, from Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Dīnār, that ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz wrote to Abū Bakr ibn ʿAmr ibn Ḥazm: “Look for whatever there is of the Messenger of God’s reports, or of the Sunna, or of ʿAmra’s reports, and write it down, for I fear that knowledge will disappear and the scholars will be gone.”

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us; Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, from Yazīd ibn Ḥāzim, from Sulaymān ibn Yasār, who said: Abū Usayd said—and his eyesight had gone blind by the time ʿUthmān was killed: “Praise be to God, who allowed me to enjoy my sight throughout the lifetime of the Messenger of God ﷺ—so that I could look upon him with both eyes. Then, when God took His Prophet and intended to test His servants, He took my sight from me.”

[Al-Ḥajjāj related to us; Ḥammād related to us; Ayyūb informed us, from Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn, from ʿUbayda, who said: ʿAlī said: “My judgment and ʿUmar’s judgment had agreed that mothers of children [umm walads] were not to be sold.” He said: “Then later I came to think that she could be sold to pay her master’s debt and emancipated from her child’s share.” I said: “Your judgment and ʿUmar’s judgment in agreement are dearer to me than your judgment in—] disagreement.”]

Abū Nuʿaym related to us; al-Haytham ibn al-Mufaḍḍal related to us, saying: I told Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī: “The people of Kūfa claim that ʿUbayda al-Salmānī said to ʿAlī, ‘Your judgment together with ʿUmar’s, when you agreed, is dearer to me than your judgment when you held it alone.’” A man from Banū Hāshim said: “Did that really happen?” Muḥammad said: “Yes, it did.”

Muḥammad ibn Abī Zukayr related to me; Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Mālik related to us, saying:

ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, Mujāhid, and others among the people of Mecca said: “Our affairs remained alike, with us matching one another, until ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ went to Medina. When he returned to us, his superiority over us became clear.”

ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn ʿImrān and Zayd ibn Ḥuraysh related to me; they said: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: I heard Mālik say that ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz used to write to the provincial centers, teaching them the Sunan and jurisprudence. He would write to the people of Medina to ask them about what had gone before, and they would act according to what they had. He would write to Abū Bakr ibn Ḥazm, asking him to collect the Sunan for him and write them to him. ʿUmar died while Ibn Ḥazm had written books but had not yet sent them to him.

ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz and Zayd related to me; they said: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Mālik related to me that ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz used to say: “The scholars of [the people of] Medina visit me, and the knowledge of Ibn al-Musayyab reaches me.”

ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz and Zayd related to me; they said: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Mālik related to me: Abū Bakr ibn Ḥazm was in charge of the judiciary of Medina and governed Medina. Someone said to him: “I do not know what to do about disagreement.” Abū Bakr said— “Abū Bakr said: ‘Nephew, if you find the people of Medina united on a matter, do not doubt that it is the truth.’”

Salama related to us, from Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, who said: Shuʿayb ibn Ḥarb related to us, saying:

Mālik ibn Anas said: “Our earlier generations did not learn from your earlier generations. ʿAlqama, al-Aswad, and Masrūq were indeed there, but none of us learned from them. In the same way, our later generations will not learn from your later generations.”

He said: Then he mentioned Sufyān and said: “He parted from me on the understanding that he would not drink nabīdh.”

Muḥammad ibn Abī Zukayr related to me; Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Mālik related to me that a man said to Rabīʿa: “But al-Nakhaʿī said such-and-such.” Rabīʿa said: “If al-Nakhaʿī were here, we would have someone take him by the hand and make him stand up.”

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā related to us; Jaʿfar ibn Ziyād informed us, from Manṣūr, from Masrūq, who said: “Knowledge came down to three: a scholar in Medina, a scholar in Syria, and a scholar in Iraq. The scholar of Medina was ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, the scholar of Kūfa was ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, and the scholar of Syria was Abū al-Dardāʾ. When they met, the scholar of Syria and the scholar of Iraq would ask the scholar of Medina, while he did not ask them.”

Abū Saʿīd Yaḥyā ibn Sulaymān related to us; Ibn Idrīs related to me, saying:

Abū Isḥāq al-Shaybānī related to us, from ʿĀmir al-Shaʿbī, who said: “The knowledge of the Messenger of God ﷺ—came down to six men: ʿUmar, ʿAlī, ʿAbd Allāh, Zayd ibn Thābit, Abū al-Dardāʾ, and Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī.”

Abū Saʿīd related to us; Ziyād al-Bakkāʾī and Jarīr al-Ḍabbī related to us, from Manṣūr, from al-Shaʿbī, from Masrūq, who said: “I mixed with the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ—and found that their knowledge came down to these six, except that he [mentioned] my father and did not mention Abū Mūsā.” He said: “Then I mixed with these six and found that their knowledge came down to ʿUmar, ʿAlī, and ʿAbd Allāh.”

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us; Sufyān related to us, saying: Umayy al-Ṣayrafī related to me: Abū al-ʿUbaydayn said to ʿAbd Allāh: “Do not disagree among yourselves, Companions of Muḥammad, lest we disagree after you.” He said: “May God have mercy on you, Abū al-ʿUbaydayn. The Companions of Muḥammad are only those who were buried with him in the burd.”18

Qabīṣa related to us; Sufyān related to us, from Manṣūr, from Mālik ibn al-Ḥārith—or one of his companions—from Masrūq, who said: “The core of the Companions of the Prophet’s knowledge ﷺ—came down to six: ʿUmar, ʿAlī, Zayd ibn Thābit, Ubayy, Abū al-Dardāʾ, and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd. Then the knowledge of these six came down to two: ʿAlī and ʿAbd Allāh.”

Al-ʿAbbās ibn Muḥammad al-Dūrī related to us; Yaḥyā ibn Abī Bukayr related to us, saying:

Shuʿba related to us, from [ʿUmāra ibn Abī Ḥafṣa, from Abū Mijlaz, from Qays ibn ʿAbbād, who said: “I came to Medina seeking knowledge and distinction. I saw a man wearing two green garments, with his hand resting on a man’s shoulder, and the latter had braided locks. I asked: ‘Who is this?’ They said: ‘This is ʿAlī, and ʿUmar has his hand resting on ʿAlī’s shoulder.’]

The Virtues of Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq ﵁

Naṣr ibn ʿAlī al-Jahḍamī related to us; ʿAbd Allāh ibn Dāwūd related to us. He said:

Salama ibn Nubayṭ informed us, from Nuʿaym ibn Abī Hind, from Nubayṭ ibn Sharīṭ, from Sālim ibn ʿUbayd, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ lost consciousness during his illness and said: “Has the time for prayer come?” They said: “Yes.” He said: “Tell Bilāl to give the call to prayer, and tell Abū Bakr to lead the people in prayer—or, to pray for the people.” Then he lost consciousness and came to, and said: “Has the time for prayer come?” They said: “Yes.” He said: “Tell Bilāl to give the call to prayer, and tell Abū Bakr to lead the people in prayer.” Then he lost consciousness and came to, and said: “Has the time for prayer come?” They said: “Yes.” He said: “Tell Bilāl to give the call to prayer, and tell Abū Bakr to lead the people in prayer.” ʿĀʾisha said: “My father is a tenderhearted man; if he stands in that place, he will weep and be unable.” Then the Prophet lost consciousness and came to, and said: “Tell Bilāl to give the call to prayer, and tell Abū Bakr to lead the people in prayer, for you are the women of Joseph.” He said: Bilāl was ordered to give the call to prayer, and Abū Bakr was ordered to lead the people in prayer. Then the Messenger of God ﷺ—felt some relief and said: “Find someone for me to lean on.” Burayra and another man came, and he leaned on them. When Abū Bakr saw him, he moved to step back, but the Prophet gestured— He signaled to him with his hand to remain in his place. Then he came and sat beside Abū Bakr until Abū Bakr had finished the prayer.

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Muʿādh related to us, saying: al-Muʿtamir related to us, from his father; Nuʿaym ibn Abī Hind related to us, from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿĀʾishah, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ—fainted. When he recovered, he said, “Has the call to prayer been given?” She said: We—or I—said, “No.” He said, “Tell Bilāl to call the people to prayer, and let Abū Bakr lead the people in prayer.” She said:

I said, “O Prophet of God, Abū Bakr is a tender-hearted man, and he cannot stand in your place.”

She said: He looked at me when I had finished speaking. Then he fainted. When he recovered, he said, “Has the call to prayer been given?” She said: I said, “No.” He said, “Tell Bilāl to call the people to prayer, and let Abū Bakr lead the people in prayer.” Then the Messenger of God ﷺ—recovered. She said: Ḥafṣah gestured to me and said, “O Prophet of God, Abū Bakr is a gentle man; he cannot recite without weeping.” She said: He looked at her when she had finished speaking. Then the Messenger of God ﷺ—fainted. When he recovered, he said, “Has the call to prayer been given?” She said: I said, “No.” He said, “Tell Bilāl to call the people to prayer, and let Abū Bakr lead the people in prayer, for you are the companions of Joseph.” Then the Messenger of God ﷺ—fainted. She said:

Bilāl called the prayer, and Abū Bakr led the people in prayer. Then the Messenger of God ﷺ—recovered, and Nawbah and Burayrah came and carried him. ʿĀʾishah said: It was as though I could see the toes of the Messenger of God ﷺ—tracing lines on the ground, or scraping the ground. She said: When Abū Bakr sensed the Prophet’s arrival, he wanted to step back, but the Prophet gestured to him to remain. She said: The Prophet ﷺ—was brought and placed beside Abū Bakr—or, she said, in the row.

Nuʿaym ibn Ḥammād and Muḥammad ibn Abī Zukayr related to us, from Ibn Wahb, who said: Ḥaywah ibn Shurayḥ informed us, from Abū Ṣakhr, from Ibn Qusayṭ, from ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr, from ʿĀʾishah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ—who said: No night has ever passed before my eyes like the night when the Messenger of God ﷺ—kept saying, “ʿĀʾishah, has dawn appeared?” And I would say, “No, Messenger of God,” until Bilāl called the dawn prayer. Then Bilāl came, and the Messenger of God ﷺ—said, “Tell your father to lead the people in prayer.” Bilāl used to greet Abū Bakr and ʿUmar just as he used to greet the Prophet ﷺ.

Muḥammad ibn Fuḍayl related to us, saying: Sinān related to us, saying: Shuʿbah related to us, from Saʿd ibn Ibrāhīm, from ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr, from ʿĀʾishah, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ—said during the illness in which he died, “Tell Abū Bakr to lead the people in prayer.”

ʿĀʾishah said, “O Messenger of God, Abū Bakr is a tender-hearted man; whenever he stands in your place, emotion overcomes him.” He said, “Tell him to lead the people in prayer.” She repeated to him what she had said, and the Prophet ﷺ—repeated to her what he had said. When it was the fourth time, she repeated it to him.

The Messenger of God ﷺ—said, “You are the companions of Joseph. Tell Abū Bakr to lead the people in prayer.”

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā related to us, from Shaybān, from al-Aʿmash, from Ismāʿīl ibn Rajāʾ al-Zubaydī, from Aws ibn Ḍamʿaj, from Abū Masʿūd al-Anṣārī, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ—said, “The one who should lead the people is the one most versed in the Book of God. If they are equal in recitation, then the one most knowledgeable of the Sunnah.”

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, saying: “We memorized it from al-Aʿmash, but did not find it here in Mecca.” He said: I heard Ismāʿīl ibn Rajāʾ narrating from Aws ibn Ḍamʿaj al-Ḥaḍramī, from Abū Masʿūd al-Anṣārī, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ—said, “The one who should lead the people is the one most versed in the Book of God. If they are equal in recitation, then the one most knowledgeable of the Sunnah.”

ʿUmar ibn Ḥafṣ ibn Ghiyāth related to us, saying: My father related to us, saying: al-Aʿmash related to us, saying: Ismāʿīl ibn Rajāʾ related to us, saying: Aws ibn Ḍamʿaj related to us, from Abū Masʿūd al-Anṣārī, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ—said, “The one who should lead the people is the one most versed in the Book of God. If they are equal, then the one most knowledgeable of the Sunnah.”

Muḥammad ibn Fuḍayl related to us, saying: Yazīd ibn Hārūn related to us, saying: Shuʿbah informed us, from Ismāʿīl ibn Rajāʾ, from Aws ibn Ḍamʿaj, from Abū Masʿūd, who said:

The Messenger of God ﷺ—said, “The one who should lead the people is the one most versed in the Book of God and the earliest in recitation. If they are equal in recitation, then the one most knowledgeable of the Sunnah.”

Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr related to us, saying: al-Ḥusayn ibn Yazīd al-Qurashī related to us, saying:

I heard Ismāʿīl ibn Rajāʾ narrating from Aws ibn Ḍamʿaj, from Abū Masʿūd, ʿUqbah ibn ʿAmr al-Anṣārī, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ—said, “The one who should lead the people is the one most versed in the Book of God. If they are equal in recitation, then the one most knowledgeable of the Sunnah.”

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā related to us, saying: Sulaym, the client of al-Shaʿbī, related to us, from al-Shaʿbī, who said: The Prophet ﷺ—was asked, “Appoint a successor over us.” He said, “I appoint no successor over you; rather, let Abū Bakr lead you in prayer.”

Aḥmad ibn Yūnus related to us, saying: Zāʾidah related to us, saying: Mūsā ibn Abī ʿĀʾishah related to us, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from ʿĀʾishah, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ—became gravely ill and said, “Have the people prayed?” We said, “No, they are waiting for you, Messenger of God.”

He said, “Put some water for me in the washing basin.” She said: We did so, and he washed. Then he tried to rise, but fainted. When he recovered, he said, “Have the people prayed?” I mentioned this to him three times, she said.

The people were gathered in the mosque, waiting for the Messenger of God ﷺ—to lead the late evening prayer. He sent word to Abū Bakr to lead the people in prayer.

Aḥmad ibn Yūnus related to us, saying: Abū Maʿshar related to us, from Muḥammad ibn Qays, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ—was ill for thirteen days. Whenever he felt some relief, he prayed; and whenever he lay down, Abū Bakr prayed.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rajāʾ related to us, saying: Zāʾidah informed us, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr, from Abū Burdah ibn Abī Mūsā, from his father, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ—fell ill and said, “Tell Abū Bakr to lead the people in prayer.” ʿĀʾishah said, “O Messenger of God, Abū Bakr is a gentle man.” He said, “Tell Abū Bakr to lead the people in prayer.” ʿĀʾishah said, “O Messenger of God, Abū Bakr is a gentle man.” He said, “Tell Abū Bakr to lead the people in prayer, for you are the companions of Joseph.” Abū Bakr then led the prayer during the lifetime of the Messenger of God ﷺ.

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā related to us, from Isrāʾīl, from Abū Isḥāq, from Arqam ibn Shuraḥbīl, who said: I travelled with Ibn ʿAbbās from Medina to Syria and asked him: “The Messenger of God ﷺ?” He said: When the Messenger of God ﷺ—[fell ill] with the illness in which he died, we were in ʿĀʾishah’s house. He said, “Let Abū Bakr lead the people in prayer.” ʿĀʾishah said, “O Messenger of God, Abū Bakr is a man who is overcome by emotion.”

He said, “Send for ʿUmar.” ʿUmar said, “I would not step forward while Abū Bakr is alive.” Abū Bakr came and led the people in prayer.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rajāʾ related to us, saying: Qays informed us, from Ibn Abī al-Sifr, from Ibn Shuraḥbīl, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: I entered upon the Messenger of God ﵌—while his wives were with him. They screened themselves from me, except Maymūnah, who had room to do so. He said:

“No one who witnessed the fierce [unclear] shall remain in the house, except that my hand did not reach al-ʿAbbās.”19 Then he said, “Tell Abū Bakr to lead the people in prayer.” ʿĀʾishah said to Ḥafṣah, “Tell him: ‘Abū Bakr is a man who weeps when he stands in that place.’” He said, “Tell Abū Bakr to lead the people in prayer.” Abū Bakr led the people in prayer.

Muslim ibn Ibrāhīm related to us, saying: Shuʿbah related to us, from Sulaymān al-Aʿmash, from Ibrāhīm, from al-Aswad, from ʿĀʾishah: The Prophet ﷺ—prayed behind Abū Bakr.

Ibn Numayr related to us, saying: Wakīʿ related to us, saying: al-Aʿmash related to us, from Ibrāhīm, from al-Aswad, from ʿĀʾishah, who said: When the Messenger of God ﷺ—fell ill with the illness in which he died, Bilāl came to announce the prayer to him. He said, “Tell Abū Bakr to lead the people in prayer.”

Muḥammad ibn Fuḍayl related to us, saying: Shabābah related to us, saying: Shuʿbah related to us, from Nuʿaym ibn Abī Hind, from Abū Wāʾil, from Masrūq, from ʿĀʾishah, who said: During the illness in which he died, the Messenger of God ﷺ—prayed sitting behind Abū Bakr.

Muḥammad ibn Fuḍayl related to us, saying: Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī related to us, from Zāʾidah, from ʿĀṣim, from Shaqīq, from Masrūq, from ʿĀʾishah, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ—fell ill, and his illness became severe. He said, “Tell Abū Bakr to lead the people in prayer.”

Al-Ḥajjāj ibn Abī Manīʿ related to us, saying: My grandfather related to us, from al-Zuhrī, who said: Ḥamzah ibn ʿAbd Allāh related to me that ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar said: When the Messenger of God ﷺ—fell ill with the illness from which he died, he said, “Let Abū Bakr lead the people in prayer.”

ʿAbbās ibn al-Walīd related to me, saying: ʿAbd al-Aʿlā related to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq related to us, from al-Zuhrī, who said: ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Abī Bakr ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Hishām related to me, from his father, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Zamʿah, who said: When the Messenger of God ﷺ—was gravely ill, I was with him among a group of Muslims. Bilāl called him to prayer, and he said, “Tell someone to lead the people in prayer.” I went out and found ʿUmar among the people, while Abū Bakr was away. I said, “Stand up, ʿUmar, and lead the people in prayer.” When ʿUmar said the opening takbīr, the Messenger of God ﷺ—heard him. ʿUmar had a loud voice. The Messenger of God ﷺ—said, “Where is Abū Bakr? God and the Muslims reject—” that.” He said: He sent for Abū Bakr, who came after ʿUmar had prayed.

Abū Saʿīd ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm related to us, saying: Ibn Abī Fudayk related to us, saying: Mūsā al-Zamʿī related to me, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Isḥāq ibn al-Ḥārith, that Ibn Shihāb related to him, that ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh related to him, that ʿAbd Allāh ibn Zamʿah related to him: He visited the Messenger of God ﷺ—during the illness in which he died. ʿAbd Allāh said:

The Messenger of God ﷺ—said to me, “Tell the people to pray.” I went out and met people whom I did not address. When I met ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, I looked no further. I said to him, “Lead the people in prayer.” He went out to lead the people in prayer. When the Prophet ﷺ—heard ʿUmar’s voice, Ibn Zamʿah said, the Prophet ﷺ—came out and put his head out from his room. Then he said, “No, no. Let Ibn Abī Quḥāfah lead them in prayer,” saying this angrily.

Abū ʿUmar Ḥafṣ ibn ʿUmar related to us, saying: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, saying: Hishām related to us, from Muḥammad, who said: After the Prophet ﷺ—Abū Bakr was the most devoted worshipper of this community.

Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shaybah related to me, saying: Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī al-Juʿfī related to me, from Zāʾidah, from ʿĀṣim, from Zirr, from ʿAbd Allāh, who said: When the Prophet ﷺ—died, the Anṣār said, “Let there be a leader from among us and a leader from among you.” ʿUmar came to them and said:

“Assembly of the Anṣār, do you not know that the Messenger of God ﷺ—ordered Abū Bakr to lead the people in prayer? Which of you would be content to step ahead of Abū Bakr?” The Anṣār said:

“We seek refuge in God from stepping ahead of Abū Bakr.”

ʿĪsā ibn Muḥammad related to me, saying: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam informed me, saying: Ḥumayd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Ruʾāsī related to me, from Salamah ibn Nubayṭ al-Ashjaʿī, from Nuʿaym, from Nubayṭ, from Sālim ibn ʿUbayd, who was a man from among the people of the Ṣuffah, who said: The Prophet ﷺ—fainted during his illness. When he recovered, he said, “Has the time for prayer come?” They said, “Yes.” He said, “Tell Bilāl to call the prayer, and tell Abū Bakr to lead the people in prayer.” Then he fainted and recovered, and said the same thing. ʿĀʾishah said, “Abū Bakr is a tender-hearted man.” He said, “You are the companions of Joseph. Tell Bilāl to call the prayer and tell Abū Bakr to lead the people in prayer.”

Abū al-Nuʿmān and Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us, saying: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us,

from Abū Ḥāzim, from Sahl ibn Saʿd al-Sāʿidī, who said: There was fighting between Banū ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf, and news of it reached the Prophet ﷺ. He prayed the noon prayer, then went to them to make peace between them. He said, “Bilāl, if the time for prayer comes and I have not come to you, tell Abū Bakr to lead the people in prayer.” When the time for the afternoon prayer came, Bilāl gave the call and the iqāmah, then told Abū Bakr to step forward.

A chapter concerning ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb ﵁

ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Uwaysī related to me, saying: Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd related to us, from Ṣāliḥ ibn Kaysān, from Ibn Shihāb, from Ḥamzah ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar, that he heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar say: The Messenger of God ﷺ—said, “While I was sleeping, a cup of milk was brought to me, and I drank from it until I could see its refreshment coming out through my fingernails.” He said: Then I gave what remained to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb. Those around him said:

“What interpretation did you give that, Messenger of God?” He said, “Knowledge.”

Abū Ṣāliḥ and Ibn Bukayr related to us, saying: al-Layth related to us, saying: ʿUqayl related to me, from Ibn Shihāb, who said: Ḥamzah ibn ʿAbd Allāh informed me that ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar said:

I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ—say: Then he mentioned a similar report.

Saʿīd ibn ʿUqbah related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb related to us, from Yūnus, who said: Ibn Shihāb said: Ḥamzah ibn ʿAbd Allāh informed me that ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar said: I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ—say: Then he mentioned a similar report.

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us, saying: Maʿn ibn ʿĪsā al-Qazzāz related to us, saying: al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Iyās related to us, from al-Qāsim ibn Yazīd ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Qusayṭ, from his father, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from his brother al-Faḍl, who said: I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ—say, “ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb is with me wherever I love, and I am with him wherever he loves; and after me, the truth is with ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb wherever he may be.”

Muslim ibn Ibrāhīm related to us, saying: Shuʿbah related to us, from Qays ibn Muslim, from Ṭāriq ibn Shihāb, who said: We used to say, “ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb speaks through the tongue of an angel.”

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us, saying: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, from Ayyūb, who said:

“If a disagreement is reported from the Prophet ﷺ—and in that disagreement you find Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, hold fast to their position, for it is the truth and the Sunnah.”

Sulaymān related to us, saying: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd related to us, from Muḥammad ibn al-ʿAjlān, from Saʿd ibn Ibrāhīm, from Abū Salama, from ʿĀʾisha, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said, “There used to be men among the communities of the past who were inspired. If there is one in this community, it is ʿUmar.”

Qabīṣa related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, from Ṣāliḥ—meaning Ibn Ḥayy—who said:

Al-Shaʿbī said: “Whoever wishes to rely on the soundest judgment in legal decisions should rely on ʿUmar’s judgments, for he used to consult others.”

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us; Sufyān related to us, saying: Mujālid ibn Saʿīd related to us, from al-Shaʿbī, who said: I heard Qabīṣa ibn Jābir say: “I accompanied ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, and I never saw a man more proficient in reciting the Book of God, more learned in God’s religion, or more capable of understanding it than he was. I also accompanied Ṭalḥa ibn ʿUbayd Allāh, and I never saw a man more generous with substantial wealth without being asked for it.” Sufyān said: “He was called ‘the Overflowing One.’”

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us; Sufyān related to us, saying: ʿAmr ibn Dīnār related to us:

A client of Ṭalḥa ibn ʿUbayd Allāh told me: “Ṭalḥa’s daily income was one thousand wāfī dirhams.”

Abū Bakr related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, saying: Ṭalḥa ibn Yaḥyā told me: My grandmother, Suʿdā bint ʿAwf al-Murriyya, told me: “One day I came to Ṭalḥa ibn ʿUbayd Allāh while he was distressed. I said to him, ‘Why do I see you so troubled? Has something concerning your family upset you, so that we might make amends with you?’ He said, ‘I have no complaint against you; indeed, you are an excellent wife for a Muslim man. It is only that a great deal of money has accumulated in the treasury, and it weighs on me.’ I said, ‘What prevents you from using it? Send for your people and distribute it among them.’ She said: So he sent for his people and distributed it among them.”

Suʿdā said: “I asked the treasurer, ‘How much was it?’ He said, ‘Four hundred thousand.’”

Then he returned to the report of Qabīṣa ibn Jābir: “I accompanied Muʿāwiya ibn Abī Sufyān, and I never saw a man more weighty in forbearance, slower to anger, or more far-reaching in deliberation than he. I accompanied ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ, and I never saw a man clearer—or, he said, more articulate—in judgment, or more forbearing as a companion than he. I accompanied Ziyād, and I never saw a man more bountiful as a companion, more generous in company, or whose inner nature more closely resembled his outward conduct than he. I accompanied al-Mughīra ibn Shuʿba. If a city had eight gates and one could leave it only by trickery, he would leave through all eight of them.”

“Abū Bakr said: I heard Sufyān ask about this report of ʿAbd al-Malik:

‘Did you hear it from ʿAbd al-Malik?’ He said, ‘I did not hear all of it.’ Then I heard Sufyān relate from ʿAbd al-Malik, from Qabīṣa ibn Jābir, who said: ‘I accompanied Ṭalḥa ibn ʿUbayd Allāh, and I never saw a man more generous with substantial wealth without being asked for it.’ He mentioned that he had heard it from ʿAbd al-Malik, and I thought that he had not heard all of it.”

Ibrāhīm ibn al-Mundhir related to us; Sufyān told me, from Ḥamza, from Kathīr, from al-Muṭṭalib ibn ʿAbd Allāh, who said: Al-Mughīra ibn Shuʿba said:

“I was the first to offer a bribe in Islam. I used to come and sit by the door, waiting to be admitted to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb. I said to his chamberlain, Yarfaʾ, ‘Take this turban; I have a sister to match it, so you can wear them as a pair.’ He would let me in, so that I could sit behind the door. Anyone who saw me would say, ‘He enters upon ʿUmar at an hour when no one else enters upon him.’”

Abū Jaʿfar Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā al-Awdī related to me, saying: Abū Nuʿaym related to us, saying: Yūnus related to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Mughīra ibn Shuʿba, who said: A man said:

“May God set the commander aright: your doorkeeper knows certain men and gives them preferential access.” He said, “May God excuse him! By God, familiarity is useful even with a vicious dog and a charging camel.” He said, “Let alone a freeborn man of noble lineage! By God, we used to curry favor to gain access to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb.”

Zayd ibn Numayr al-Ṣanʿānī—who was one of the finest men—related to us, saying: Wakiʿ related to us— Wakīʿ said: Abū al-ʿUmays related to us, from al-Qāsim ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Ibn Masʿūd:

“When he came to the land of Abyssinia, he was seized over something and held by it, so he gave two dinars until he was released.”

Wakīʿ related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, from ʿUthmān, from Mujāhid, who said:

“Make your wealth a shield for your religion.”

Zayd related to us; ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān related to us, from Muḥammad ibn Saʿīd, from his father, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: “The bribe for which its giver incurs sin is not one given to protect his property and his life. The bribe for which one incurs sin is one given so that one may obtain what is not rightfully his.”

Al-Ḥajjāj related to us; Ḥammād related to us, saying: Zayd ibn Aslam related to us, from his father, who said: “When ʿUmar sent me to one of his sons, he would say, ‘Do not let him know I sent you, for I fear Satan may prompt him to tell a lie.’”

One day a woman came to ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar and said:
