“Abū ʿĪsā does not provide for me or clothe me.” He said, “Woe to you! Who is Abū ʿĪsā?”

She said, “Your son ʿAbd al-Raḥmān.” He said, “Does ʿĪsā have a father?” So he sent me to him and said:

“Do not tell him.” He said, “So I went to him, and he had a cock and a hen from India. I said, ‘Answer your father, the Commander of the Faithful.’ He said, ‘What does he want of me?’ I said, ‘He forbade me to tell you; I do not know.’ He said, ‘Then I will give you the cock and the hen if you tell me.’” He said: So I made him promise that he would not tell ʿUmar, and I told him. He gave me the cock and the hen. When I came to ʿUmar, he said, “Did you tell him?” By God, I could not bring myself to say no, so I said, “Yes.” He said:

“Did he bribe you?” I said, “Yes.” He said, “What did he bribe you with?” I said, “A cock and a hen.” He took hold of my hand with his left hand and began striking me with the whip, while I kept jumping about. He said, “You are certainly a tough one.” Then he said, “Is he to be called Abū ʿĪsā? Does ʿĪsā have a father?”

Aḥmad ibn Yūnus related to us, saying: Zuhayr related to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq related to us, saying: Makḥūl told me, from Ghuḍayf ibn al-Ḥārith, from Abū Dharr, who said:

“I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: ‘God Most High placed the truth upon ʿUmar’s tongue, and he speaks by it.’”

Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yūnus, a Kufan, related to us; Mindal related to us, from Muḥammad ibn al-ʿAjlān, from Saʿd ibn Ibrāhīm, from Abū Salama, from ʿĀʾisha, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “God Most High placed the truth upon ʿUmar’s tongue, and he speaks by it.”

Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yūnus, a Kufan, related to us; Mindal related to us, from Muḥammad ibn al-ʿAjlān, from Saʿd ibn Ibrāhīm, from Abū Salama, from ʿĀʾisha, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “There used to be inspired men among the communities of the past. If there is one among them in my community, it is ʿUmar.”

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā related to us, from Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid, from al-Shaʿbī, that ʿAlī said: “We did not consider it unlikely that the Sakīna spoke upon ʿUmar’s tongue.”

ʿUbayd Allāh related to us; Abū Isrāʾīl, a Kufan, related to us, from al-Walīd ibn al-ʿAyzār, from ʿAmr ibn Maymūn, from ʿAlī, who said: “While we, the Companions of the Messenger of God, were gathered together, we did not deny that the Sakīna spoke upon ʿUmar’s tongue.”

Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān related to us, saying: Ḥaywa related to us, from Bakr ibn ʿAmr al-Maʿāfirī, from Mishraḥ ibn Hāʿān al-Maʿāfirī, from ʿUqba ibn ʿĀmir al-Juhanī, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “If there were to be a prophet after me, it would be ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb.”

Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd Allāh related to us; Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh related to us, from ʿĀṣim, from Zirr, who said: ʿAbd Allāh used to preach and say: “I think there is an angel between ʿUmar’s eyes who guides him aright and sets him straight. I also think that Satan fears ʿUmar, lest he commit some act and ʿUmar turn him back from it.”

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā related to us, from Shaybān, from al-Aʿmash, from Shaqīq, who said: ʿAbd Allāh said: “By God, if ʿUmar’s knowledge were placed on one pan of a balance, and the knowledge of the people of the earth placed on the other pan ʿUmar’s knowledge would outweigh it, from the time he went away”—meaning, on the day he went away with nine-tenths of all knowledge.

Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us, saying: Mūsā ibn ʿAlī told me, from his father, that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb addressed the people at al-Jābiya and said: “Whoever wishes to ask about the Qurʾān, let him go to Ubayy ibn Kaʿb; whoever wishes to ask about the shares of inheritance, let him go to Zayd ibn Thābit; whoever wishes to ask about jurisprudence, let him go to Muʿādh ibn Jabal; and whoever wishes to ask about wealth, let him come to me, for God has made me its treasurer and distributor. I shall begin with the wives of the Messenger of God ﷺ and give to them; then with the earliest Emigrants. My companions and I were driven from Mecca, from our homes and our property; then with the Helpers, who had settled in the abode and in faith before them.” Then he said: “Whoever was quicker to emigrate will receive his stipend sooner, and whoever was slower to emigrate will receive his stipend later. No man should come to me unless his riding animal is kneeling.”

ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān related to us; ʿAbd Allāh related to us, saying: Saʿīd ibn Yazīd informed us:

“I heard al-Ḥārith ibn Yazīd al-Ḥaḍramī relate, from ʿAlī ibn Rabāḥ, from Nāshira ibn Sumayy al-Yazanī, who said: I heard ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb say, on the day of al-Jābiya, while addressing the people: ‘God has made me the treasurer of this wealth and its distributor.’ Then he said, ‘Rather, God distributes it, and I shall begin with the family of the Prophet ﷺ then with the most distinguished among them.’ He assigned ten thousand to each of the Prophet’s wives, except Juwayriya, Ṣafiyya, and Maymūna. ʿĀʾisha said, ‘The Messenger of God ﷺ used to treat us equally, and ʿUmar treated them equally.’ Then he said, ‘I shall begin with my companions, the earliest Emigrants, for we were driven from our homes unjustly and through aggression; then with the most distinguished among them.’ He assigned five thousand to those among them who had fought at Badr, and four thousand to those of the Helpers who had fought at Badr. He assigned three thousand to those who had witnessed al-Ḥudaybiya. He said, ‘Whoever is quicker to emigrate will receive his stipend sooner, and whoever is slower—’”

“‘—to emigrate will receive his stipend later. No man should come to me unless his riding animal is kneeling. I ask you to excuse me concerning Khālid ibn al-Walīd. I ordered him to reserve this wealth for the weaker among the Emigrants, but he gave it to men of strength, distinction, and eloquence. So I removed him and appointed Abū ʿUbayda ibn al-Jarrāḥ in his place.’”

Abū ʿUmar ibn Ḥafṣ ibn al-Mughīra stood up and said: “By God, you have not excused yourself, ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb! You have removed a young man whom the Messenger of God ﷺ appointed; you have sheathed a sword that the Messenger of God ﷺ unsheathed; you have lowered a banner that the Messenger of God ﷺ raised; you have severed kinship and envied your cousin.” ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said: “You are a close relative, young in years, and you grow angry on behalf of your cousin.”

Saʿīd ibn Kathīr ibn ʿUfayr al-Miṣrī related to me, saying: Ibn Lahīʿa told me that Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb related to him, that his father, Abū al-Khayr, related to him: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Marwān said to Kurayb ibn Abraha: “Were you present with ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb at al-Jābiya?” He said:

“No.” He said: “Then who can tell us about it?” Kurayb said: “If you send for Sufyān ibn Wahb al-Khawlānī, he will tell you about it.” So he sent for him and said, “Tell me about ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb’s sermon on the day of al-Jābiya.” Sufyān said:

“When the spoils had been gathered, the commanders of the military divisions sent to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, asking him to come in person. He came, praised God, and extolled Him. Then he said, ‘To proceed: We shall distribute this wealth justly among those upon whom God has bestowed it, except for these two clans of Lakhm and Judhām; they have no share in it.’ Abū Ḥadīda al-Ajdhāmī stood up before him and said, ‘We adjure you by God, ʿUmar, to act justly.’ ʿUmar said, ‘I seek justice. Am I to treat people who spent on mounts, girded themselves for travel, and journeyed through the lands as I would people who stayed in their own country? If the migration had been to Ṣanʿāʾ or ʿAdan, not one person from Lakhm or Judhām would have migrated to it.’”

Abū Ḥadīda stood up and said: “God settled us in His lands wherever He willed, and brought migration to our own lands. We accepted it and supported it. Does that deprive us of our right, ʿUmar?” He said: “You have your share along with the Muslims.”

Then he distributed the wealth, and each man received half a dinar. If a man had his wife with him, he gave him a dinar. Then he summoned Ibn Qāṭūrā, the landowner, and said: “Tell me what provisions a man needs for a month and for a day.”

The mudd-measure and the qisṭ-measure were brought to him. He said: “These two mudd-measures are enough for him for a month, along with one qisṭ of oil and one qisṭ of vinegar.” ʿUmar ordered two mudd-measures of wheat to be ground, then kneaded, then baked. He seasoned them with two qisṭ-measures of oil, then seated thirty men to eat them; they were enough to satisfy them. Then ʿUmar took the two mudd-measures in his right hand and the qisṭ-measure in his left, and said: “O God, I do not permit anyone after me to reduce these amounts. O God, whoever reduces them, reduce his lifespan.”

ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz grew angry and said, “You are an old man who has become senile.” Sufyān said: “God has excused me on account of my age.” Then ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said, “Is there any drink?” He said, “We have honey, and we have a drink that we make from grapes.” ʿUmar called for it, and it was brought to him. It was like ṭilāʾ—the ṭilāʾ used on camels. ʿUmar dipped his finger into it, then said, “I see no harm in this.”

ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān related to us; ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mubārak related to us, saying: ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mawhab informed us, saying: I heard Abū Hurayra say: “I came to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb from Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī with eight hundred thousand dirhams. He said to me, ‘How much have you brought?’”

I said, “I have brought eight hundred thousand dirhams.” He said, “Didn’t I tell you that you are a foolish man from Tihāma? You have brought only eighty thousand dirhams. How could it be eight hundred thousand dirhams?” So I counted out one hundred thousand at a time until I had counted eight hundred thousand.

He said, “Is it wholesome, woe to you?” I said, “Yes.” ʿUmar spent the night sleepless. When the call to the dawn prayer was made, his wife said to him, “Commander of the Faithful, did you not sleep at all last night?” He said, “How can ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb sleep, when the people have received last night something like which they have received nothing since Islam began? What assurance has ʿUmar, if he were to die while that wealth was with him and he had not placed it where it was due?”

After he prayed the dawn prayer, a group of the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ gathered around him. He said to them: “Last night the people received something like which they have received nothing since Islam began. I have formed an opinion, so advise me. I thought I would measure out the people’s shares with a measuring vessel.” They said, “Do not do that, Commander of the Faithful. People are entering Islam, and the wealth is increasing. Instead, give it to them according to a register; as the number of people and the wealth increase, you can assign their shares accordingly.”

He said, “Then advise me: with whom should I begin?” They said, “With yourself, Commander of the Faithful, for you are responsible for this.” Some of them said, “The Commander of the Faithful knows best.” He said:

“No. I shall begin with the Messenger of God ﷺ then with those nearest to him, one after another.” He arranged the register accordingly. ʿUbayd Allāh said: “He began with Hāshim and al-Muṭṭalib, giving them all the same amount. Then he gave to Banū ʿAbd Shams, then to Banū Nawfal ibn ʿAbd Manāf. He began with Banū ʿAbd Shams because their ancestor was Hāshim’s maternal brother.”

ʿUbayd Allāh said: “The first to distinguish between Banū Hāshim and al-Muṭṭalib in the summons was ʿAbd al-Malik. ʿAbd Allāh ibn Qays ibn Makhrama, a brother of Banū al-Muṭṭalib, came to him. ʿAbd al-Malik said to him, ‘Are you content, Abū ʿAbd Allāh, to be summoned by the name of someone other than your father and answer?’ He said, ‘Who summons me by someone other than my father?’ He said, ‘Are not Banū Hāshim summoned, while Banū al-Muṭṭalib are not, and you answer?’ He said, ‘It was something the Messenger of God ﷺ did. What can I do about that?’ He said, ‘Ask me to distribute you among separate clan representatives, and I will do it.’”

When he gave permission to the people, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Qays stood and said, “Commander of the Faithful, we have come to morning without a clan representative. The Banū Hāshim are summoned, and we respond. So appoint a clan representative for us.” He wrote to him that they should be assigned to a clan representative, and that this should be entrusted to ʿAbd Allāh ibn Qays: he would oversee it and appoint whomever he wished.

Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad al-Shāfiʿī related to us: My grandfather Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī related to me, from Zayd ibn ʿAlī, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ—said, “Hāshim and al-Muṭṭalib are like these two,” and he brought his fingers together and interlaced them. “May God curse whoever divides between them. They raised us when we were small, and we made them great.”20

Qabīṣah ibn ʿUqbah related to us: I heard Sufyān say, “Whoever gives ʿAlī precedence over Abū Bakr and ʿUmar has disparaged the Emigrants and the Helpers, and I fear that, despite this, no deed will benefit him.”

ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn ʿImrān related to us: Asad ibn Mūsā told us; Yūsuf ibn ʿAmr told us: Mālik ibn Anas was asked about ʿAlī and ʿUthmān. He said, “I never met anyone whose example I followed who did not give Abū Bakr and ʿUmar precedence, and refrain from speaking about ʿAlī and ʿUthmān.”

Ibrāhīm ibn al-Mundhir related to us: Maʿn ibn ʿĪsā told us, from Khārijah ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sulaymān, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar: The Messenger of God ﷺ—said, “Indeed, God has placed the truth upon ʿUmar’s heart and upon his tongue. Whenever a matter arose among the people and they offered their opinions about it, ʿUmar expressed his view, and then the Qurʾān came with what ʿUmar had said.”

Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us: Muʿāwiyah ibn Ṣāliḥ related to me, from Rabīʿah ibn Yazīd, from— Abū Uways al-Khawlānī, from Yazīd ibn ʿUmayrah al-Zubaydī, that when death approached Muʿādh ibn Jabal, he was asked, “Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, give us your final counsel.” He said, “Sit me up.” He said, “Knowledge and faith are in their place; whoever seeks them will find them. Knowledge and faith are in their place; whoever seeks them will find them. So seek knowledge from four men: ʿUwaymir Abū al-Dardāʾ, Salmān al-Fārisī, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām, who was a Jew and then became Muslim. I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ—say that he is the tenth of ten in Paradise.”

[Reports concerning Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib]

Muḥammad ibn Abī Zukayr related to me: Ibn Wahb informed us: I heard Mālik, who was asked whether Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib had met ʿUmar. He said, “No, but he was born in ʿUmar’s time. When he grew up, he devoted himself to asking about ʿUmar’s circumstances and affairs until it was as though he had seen him.” Mālik said, “It reached me that ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar used to send to Ibn al-Musayyib to ask him about some of ʿUmar’s circumstances and affairs.”

Abū Nuʿaym related to us: Misʿar related to us, from Saʿd ibn Ibrāhīm [from his father], from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib, who said, “No one remains more knowledgeable than I am about the judgments of the Messenger of God ﷺ—and of Abū Bakr and ʿUmar.”

ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Uwaysī related to me: Mālik ibn Anas told us that it had reached him that Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib said, “I would travel in pursuit of a single ḥadīth…”

…for a single ḥadīth, traveling through nights and days. Mālik said, “Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib used to visit Abū Hurayrah at al-Shajarah.”

Muḥammad ibn Abī Zukayr related to me: Ibn Wahb said, “Mālik informed me that al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad used to ask about a matter, then say to the person he asked, ‘Whom did you ask?’ The man would say, ‘I asked ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr, and I asked so-and-so, and I asked so-and-so.’ Al-Qāsim would ask him, ‘Did you ask Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib?’ He would say, ‘Yes.’ Al-Qāsim would ask, ‘What did he say?’ The man would say, ‘He said such-and-such.’ Al-Qāsim would say to him, ‘Then follow his view: he is our master and the most learned among us.’” Mālik then mentioned al-Qāsim’s virtue, saying, “Al-Qāsim was one of the jurists of this community.”

Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr related to us: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Muḥammad told us: Mūsā ibn Abī Maʿbad informed me: I asked al-Qāsim and Sālim about something, and they said to me, “Go to Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib and ask him, then come back to us and tell us.” I went to Saʿīd, then returned to al-Qāsim and Sālim and told them. They said, “That is our view.”

ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn ʿImrān related to us: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Wahb told us: Usāmah ibn Zayd informed me that Nāfiʿ related to him that Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib was asked about a legal question and answered it. Ibn ʿUmar was informed of his answer, and was amazed at Ibn al-Musayyib’s legal opinion. Then Ibn ʿUmar said, “Have I not told you about this man”—meaning Ibn al-Musayyib—“who, by God, is one of the authorities on legal opinions?”

ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn ʿImrān and Zayd ibn Bishr related to me: They said, “Ibn Wahb informed us: Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān al-Murādī related to me, from a shaykh of the people of Medina called Abū…”

Isḥāq, who said: “In that time, I would see a man enter the mosque to ask about a matter of jurisprudence.” Zayd said, “The people would pass him from one gathering to another until he was sent”—Zayd said, “until he was passed”—“to Ibn al-Musayyib’s gathering.”

Muḥammad ibn Abī Zukayr related to us: Ibn Wahb informed us: Mālik related to me that Saʿīd used to keep the company of Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ and Abū Hurayrah. Ibn Wahb said, “I heard Mālik say, ‘It reached me that Saʿīd used to be called the transmitter of Ibn ʿUmar.’”

Muḥammad ibn Abī Zakariyyā related to me: Ibn Wahb informed us: Mālik related to me: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib was a man who fasted. A man came in to him while he was eating bread and chard, and he said to him, “Come and eat.” The man then asked him about something. Mālik said, “I thought it concerned judicial matters.” Saʿīd said to him, “I see that you are a fool. Go to the judge appointed to deal with this. Do you think I would occupy myself with this?” Or he said, “with you.”

Zayd ibn Bishr and ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz related to me: They said, “Ibn Wahb informed us: Ibn Abī al-Zinād related to me that when Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib was ill, he would say, ‘Sit me up, for I consider it grave to relate a ḥadīth of the Messenger of God ﷺ—while I am lying down,’” in connection with a ḥadīth he mentioned.

Zayd ibn Bishr related to us: Ibn Wahb informed me: I heard al-Layth say, “Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd related to me.”

[And] Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us: Al-Layth related to me, from Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd, that Ibn—

…al-Musayyib was called the transmitter of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb because he was the most knowledgeable of people about ʿUmar’s legal rulings and judgments.

Ibn Bukayr related to me: Al-Layth related to me, from Jaʿfar ibn Rabīʿah, who said: I asked ʿIrāk ibn Mālik, “Who is the most learned jurist among the people of Medina?” He said, “As for the one most knowledgeable about the judgments of the Messenger of God ﷺ—and the judgments of Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, and ʿUthmān, the most learned in jurisprudence, and the most knowledgeable about what had passed in the affairs of the people, that is Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib. As for the one with the most ḥadīth, that is ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr. He would never fail to take pride in some distinction of ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh.” He said, “Then ʿIrāk would say to you, ‘In my view, Ibn Shihāb is the most learned of them all, for he gathered their knowledge together with his own.’”

ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan al-ʿAsqalānī related to us: Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mubārak told us: “The jurists of the people of Medina whose opinions they followed were seven: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib, Sulaymān ibn Yasār, Sālim ibn ʿAbd Allāh, al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad, ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr, ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUtbah, and Khārijah ibn Zayd ibn Thābit. When a legal question came to them, they would all meet and consider it. The judge would not issue a ruling until the question had been referred to them; they would consider it and then give their decision.”

Ibn Bukayr related to us: Al-Layth said: Ibn Shihāb said, “No one has endured the pursuit of knowledge as I have, and no one has disseminated it as I have. As for ʿUrwah, he was a well whose water the buckets do not muddy. As for Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib, he made himself available to the people, and his renown spread everywhere.”

Ibn Bukayr related to me: I heard al-Layth say, “The sons of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ—used to sit with Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib. None of them would ask him…”

…about anything unless they asked him about something, whereupon he would relate it to them.

Ibn Bukayr related to me: I heard Mālik say, “Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib was asked about a legal question, and he was told, ‘Al-Ḥasan said such-and-such about it.’ He said, ‘The weavers of the people of Iraq crowded around him and corrupted him.’”

Ibn Bukayr related to me: I heard al-Layth say, “ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn came in to Ṭāriq, and Ṭāriq said, ‘I shall send for Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib: either he pledges allegiance, or I strike off his head.’ He left and passed by Abū Bakr ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, and told him. The two of them went to Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib and said to him, ‘Will you pledge allegiance?’ He said, ‘I will not play with my religion as you two have played with yours.’ They said to him, ‘Then go out to the desert; perhaps he will forget about you.’ He said, ‘No.’ They said, ‘Then stay in your house.’ He said, ‘I hear the caller summoning people to prosperity, so how can I not answer him?’ They said, ‘Then move from your place, for it faces his; when he comes out, he will see you.’ He said, ‘Should I move to another place? This is a place where we have sat for such-and-such a long time.’ When Ṭāriq went out, ʿAmr ibn ʿUthmān followed him and said to him, ‘May God reward you well for what you did, especially for our shaykh Saʿīd.’ He said, ‘By God, I did not think of him.’ And he said, ‘He escaped me only because I forgot.’”

Zayd ibn Bishr, Abū al-Ṭāhir, and Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā related to us: They said, “Ibn Wahb informed us: Mālik related to me, from Ibn Shihāb, that he used to sit with ʿAbd Allāh ibn Thaʿlabah ibn Ṣuʿayr and learn genealogy and other things from him. One day he asked him about a matter of jurisprudence, and he said, ‘If you want to learn about that, you should go to this shaykh, Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib.’”

Ibn Shihāb said, “I sat with him for seven years, and I did not think that anyone possessed knowledge besides him.”

He also said, “Ibn Shihāb’s legal opinions, and the direction he took in what he adopted, followed the views of Sālim ibn ʿAbd Allāh and Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib.”

Zayd ibn Bishr al-Ḥaḍramī related to us: Ḍammām related to us, from one of the people of Medina, who said:

“When the pledge of allegiance to Sulaymān ibn ʿAbd al-Malik took place alongside the pledge to al-Walīd, Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib disliked pledging allegiance twice. The governor of Medina wrote to ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Marwān informing him that Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib disliked pledging allegiance to both of them. ʿAbd al-Malik wrote to the governor of Medina: ‘Why did you need to report this about Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib? We did not fear anything from him. But since this has become known and spread among the people, summon him to do what those who entered into this pledge have done. If he refuses, flog him a hundred lashes, shave his head and beard, dress him in garments of hair, and make him stand before the people in the Muslims’ market, so that no one else dares oppose us.’

“When those of Quraysh learned of this, they asked the governor not to act hastily against him, so that they might frighten him with death; perhaps he would comply. They sent a client of his who was in the guard, and said, ‘Go, frighten him with death and tell him that he is to be killed. Perhaps that will frighten him into joining what the people have joined.’ His client came to him while he was at his mosque, praying, and the client wept. Saʿīd said to him, ‘Woe to you, what makes you weep?’ He said, ‘I weep for what is intended for you. A letter has come about you: if you do not pledge allegiance, you will be killed. I have come so that you may purify yourself, put on clean clothes, and settle your affairs.’ He said, ‘Woe to you! You found me praying at my mosque. Do you think I was praying without being pure, or that my clothes were unclean? As for what you said about settling my affairs, I would be more misguided than the one who sent you if I had spent a night without settling them. Do as you wish: I would not pledge allegiance twice in Islam, after a ḥadīth I heard from the Messenger of God ﷺ—in which he said, “If there are two pledges of allegiance, then annul the later of them.”’”

He went with him. When he came to the governor, they summoned him, but he refused to comply. The governor ordered him to wear garments of hair and ordered that he be stripped. He was flogged a hundred lashes, his head and beard were shaved, and he was made to stand before the people. He said, “Had I known that this was all there was to it, I would not have taken off my clothes willingly, nor agreed to it.”

Ḍammām said, “It reached me that when Hishām ibn Ismāʿīl addressed the people on Friday, Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib would turn his face toward him for as long as he was speaking of God. But when Hishām raised his voice to praise ʿAbd al-Malik and say what he would about him, Saʿīd would turn his face away. When Hishām noticed this, he ordered a guard to strike Saʿīd in the face whenever he turned away from him. The guard did so. Saʿīd said to Hishām”—and gestured to him with his hand, saying—“It is three.” No more than three months passed before Hishām was dismissed.

Muḥammad ibn Abī Zukayr related to us: Ibn Wahb informed us: Mālik related to me that Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib was flogged a hundred lashes and made to wear garments of hair. Mālik said, “ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz said, ‘I do not envy a man who has not suffered harm in this affair.’” Ibn Wahb said, “Mālik also related to me: It reached me that when Ibn al-Musayyib sat down, his family sent him food they had prepared for him. When it was brought to him, Saʿīd said, ‘I will not taste it. Look for the four loaves that I used to eat with oil at home, and send them to me.’” Mālik said, “There was a man imprisoned with him whose family sent him various kinds of food. Saʿīd said to him, ‘Tell me, do you intend to stay here? Keep this away from you.’”

Al-Ḥajjāj related to us: Ḥammād told us, from ʿAlī ibn Zayd, who said: I asked Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib, “Your people claim that what kept you from the pilgrimage was that you had vowed to God that, when you saw the Kaʿbah, you would pray against the Banū Marwān.” He said, “I did not do that. Whenever I pray to God, I pray against them. I have performed the ḥajj and the ʿumrah more than twenty times.”

Muḥammad ibn Abī Zukayr related to us: Ibn Wahb informed us: I heard Mālik relate that a young official sent Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib five thousand dirhams— The messenger said to him, “This has been sent to you—may God set you right—so that you may spend it and use it for your needs.” Saʿīd was earnestly occupied in disputing with a servant of his over half a dirham that he claimed the servant owed him, while the servant said, “You are owed nothing by me.” Saʿīd said to the messenger, “Go back to your work.” The messenger offered it to him again, but Saʿīd said, “Get away from me,” and refused to take it from him. [And] a man entrusted him with taking possession of an estate. Ibn al-Musayyib said to him, “This half-dirham is dearer to me than that.”

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us: Sallām ibn Miskīn related to us, from ʿImrān ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Khuzāʿī, who said: “Al-Walīd ibn ʿAbd al-Malik came to Medina and stayed there. He sent a messenger to Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib, summoning him. The messenger came to him and said, ‘The Commander of the Faithful summons you, so answer him.’ He said to him, ‘Tell him: I have no need of you, and your need will not be fulfilled by me.’ The messenger went back and said, ‘Go and tell him: I only wish to speak to him about a need.’ The messenger came and said, ‘He only wants you for a need.’ He said, ‘I have no need of him, and his need will not be fulfilled by me.’ The messenger said, ‘The Commander of the Faithful sends for you, and you say this? If he had given me instructions concerning you, I would have carried your head to him.’”

Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us: Al-Layth ibn Saʿd related to me: I said to Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd, “Ibn Shihāb said, ‘I found ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr to be a sea whose water the buckets do not muddy, while Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib made himself available to the people.’” Yaḥyā said, “As for the one most knowledgeable about the Sunnahs and the judgments of ʿUmar, that is Ibn al-Musayyib; as for the one with the most ḥadīth, that is ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr.”

Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us: Al-Layth related to me, from Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd, who said, “When ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar was asked about something that puzzled him, he would say, ‘Ask Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib, for he kept the company of the righteous.’”

Muḥammad ibn Abī Zukayr related to us: Ibn Wahb informed us: Mālik related to me: A man came to Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib while he was ill and asked him about a ḥadīth while he was lying down. Saʿīd sat up and related it to him. The man said, “I wish you had not troubled yourself.”

He replied, “I disliked relating a ḥadīth to you from the Messenger of God ﷺ—while I was lying down.” Saʿīd did not care who among the people disagreed with him, because of his knowledge.

Saʿīd ibn Asad related to us: Ḍamrah related to us, from Rajāʾ ibn Jamīl al-Aylī, who said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd al-Qārī said to Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib, when he came to Medina for the pledges of allegiance to al-Walīd and Sulaymān after their father: “I will advise you on three things.”

He said, “What are they?” [He said,] “Your place should be changed, for you stand where Hishām ibn Ismāʿīl can see you.” He said, “I would not leave a place where I have stood for forty years.” He said, “Or you could go out to perform the ʿumrah.” He said, “I would not spend my money and weary my body on something without an intention.” He said, “Then what is the third?” He replied, “Pledge allegiance.” He said, “What do you think? If God has blinded your heart as He has blinded your eyes, what can I do?” He was blind.

Rajāʾ said, “Hishām summoned him to pledge allegiance, but he refused. Hishām wrote about him to ʿAbd al-Malik. ʿAbd al-Malik wrote to him:

‘What business has Mālik with Saʿīd? We had nothing against him that we disliked. But since you have done this, flog him thirty lashes, dress him in garments of hair, and make him stand before the people, so that the people do not follow his example.’

“Hishām summoned him, but he refused, saying, ‘I will not pledge allegiance to two men.’ Hishām flogged him thirty lashes, dressed him in garments of hair, and made him stand before the people. Rajāʾ said, ‘Some of the people of Aylah related to me, those who were…’”21

At the police station in Medina, he said: “We knew he would not put on the clothes willingly.” He said: “So we told him, ‘Abū Muḥammad, they are going to kill you; cover your nakedness with them.’” He said: “So he put them on. When he had been struck thirty times, he realized that we had tricked him. He said, ‘O sincere advisers—welcome!’ three times. ‘Had I not thought they were going to kill me, I would not have put them on.’”

Abū Zayd ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī al-Ghamr related to us. He said: Ibn al-Qāsim informed us, from Mālik, who said: Nāfiʿ ibn Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim visited Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib while he was ill and had not eaten for three days. He spoke to him. Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib said to him: “How can a person eat when he is in such a state?” He replied:

“One who belongs to this world must eat for as long as he is in it.” He said: “He did not do so until he had sipped a little broth. Then he said to him, ‘Ask for well-being, for I think Satan was vexed by your place in the mosque.’” Ibn al-Musayyib said: “O God, keep me safe, and keep others safe from me.”

Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā related to us. He said: Ashhab, Mālik’s associate, informed me. He said: Mālik said: “Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib was knowledgeable about sales.” He was asked: “And Sulaymān ibn Yasār?” He said: “I have not heard.” Sulaymān, as far as is known, had knowledge and had heard reports.

Mālik said: “Ibn al-Musayyib and al-Qāsim died without leaving a book. Abū Qilāba died, and I was told that he left behind a mule-load of books.”

Saʿīd ibn Asad related to me. He said: Ḍamra related to us, from Ibn Shawdhab, from ʿAbd Allāh, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Qāsim, who said: “I sat with Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib while he was alone in the mosque. He said to me, ‘People have been forbidden to sit with me.’ I said, ‘I am a stranger here.’ He said, ‘I am telling you only so that you do not incur harm by being caught up in this.’”

Al-Rabīʿ ibn Rūḥ al-Ḥimṣī related to us; he said: Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAyyāsh related to us, from ʿUmar ibn Muḥammad, who said: When the allegiance to al-Walīd and Sulaymān was sought, Hishām ibn Ismāʿīl was governor of Medina. He [summoned] Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib, who was with his kinsmen of Banū Makhzūm, to pledge allegiance to the two of them. Saʿīd refused, so Hishām had him flogged and dressed him in garments of hair. Saʿīd said: “Where are you taking me?” They said: “We are going to kill you.” He said: “Then I am truly Saʿīd, as my mother named me.” When they let him go, he said: “By God, had I known that you had dressed me in these clothes only so you could strike me, I would not have put them on. But I thought you were going to kill me, so I agreed in order to cover my nakedness.” ʿUmar said:

“Saʿīd did not take an allowance from the house of Marwān until he passed away. One of his family would take it and put it aside; when he died, they divided it among themselves.”

Abū Saʿīd Aḥmad ibn Dāwūd al-Ḥaddād related to me. Khālid ibn ʿAbd Allāh related to us, from Dāwūd ibn Abī Hind, that Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib erased his name from the register during the civil strife.

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm related to us. Sahl ibn Hāshim related to us, from al-Awzāʿī— He said: Al-Zuhrī and Makkḥūl were asked: “Who was the most learned of those you met?” They replied: “Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib.”

Abū Bakr ibn ʿAbd al-Malik related to me. He said: ʿAbd al-Razzāq related to us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, who said: “I met four oceans of knowledge among Quraysh: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib, ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr, Abū Salama, and ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh.” Maʿmar said: “We used to think we had gathered a great deal from al-Zuhrī, until al-Walīd was killed and al-Zuhrī’s notebooks were brought out on pack animals.”

ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd ibn Kathīr ibn Dīnār related to us. Baqiyya related to us, saying: al-Ḥasan ibn ʿUmar al-Fazārī related to us, from Maymūn ibn Mihrān, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib, that he spent forty years without ever meeting people leaving the mosque while he was entering it. He said:

“He would enter before dawn.”

Ibrāhīm ibn al-Mundhir related to me. Maʿn related to us, from Muḥammad ibn Hilāl, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib, who said: “For forty years I have not met those leaving.”

Ibrāhīm related to us. He said: ʿUmar ibn ʿUthmān al-Taymī related to us. He said: Aflah ibn Ḥumayd related to us. He said: “I saw Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib with a small lock of hair, somewhat marked by the lashes.”

The excellence of Abū Bakr and ʿUmar

Qabīṣa related to us. He said: Sufyān related to us, from Khālid and ʿĀṣim, from Abū Qilāba, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “The most merciful of my community is Abū Bakr; the firmest of them is ʿUmar; the most modest of them is ʿUthmān; the best reciter among them is Ubayy; the most knowledgeable among them concerning inheritance shares is Zayd ibn Thābit; and the most knowledgeable among them concerning what is lawful and unlawful is Muʿādh ibn Jabal. Every community has a trusted one, and the trusted one of this community is Abū ʿUbayda ibn al-Jarrāḥ.”

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā and Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us. They said: Abū Hilāl related to us, from a man whom I think was Najīḥ, from Anas ibn Mālik, who said: “May God have mercy on Abū Bakr and ʿUmar; their practice is a sunna.”

[Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us. Ḥammād related to us, saying: Ayyūb said: “When a disagreement is reported to you concerning the Prophet ﷺ and you find Abū Bakr and ʿUmar on one side of that disagreement, hold fast to their position: it is the truth, and it is the sunna.”]

Abū ʿĀṣim al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Makhlad and Qabīṣa related to us, from Sufyān, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr, from a client of Ribʿī, from Ribʿī, from Ḥudhayfa, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Follow the two who come after me: Abū Bakr and ʿUmar; follow the guidance of ʿAmmār; and hold fast to the covenant of Ibn Masʿūd.”

ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn ʿAbd Allāh related to me. He said: Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd related to us, from Sufyān, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr, from Hilāl, the client of Ribʿī, from Ribʿī, from Ḥudhayfa ibn al-Yamān, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Follow the two who come after me”—meaning Abū Bakr and ʿUmar.

[Abū al-Nuʿmān related to us. He said: Ḥammād related to us, from Khālid, who said: “We hold that the abrogating guidance in the words of the Messenger of God ﷺ is what Abū Bakr and ʿUmar followed.”]

[The Jurists among the Companions]

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us. Sufyān related to us, saying: Muṭarrif related to us, from al-Shaʿbī, from Masrūq, who said: “The judicial authority among the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ rested with six: ʿUmar, ʿAlī, Ibn Masʿūd, Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, Zayd ibn Thābit, and Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī. Half of them belonged to the people of Kūfa: ʿAlī, Ibn Masʿūd, and Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī.”

Ibn Numayr related to us. Ibn Idrīs related to us, from al-Shaybānī, from al-Shaʿbī, who counted six of the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ from whom knowledge was taken.

I said: “Where is Muʿādh?” He replied: “He had died before then.”

Abū Nuʿaym and Qabīṣa related to us. They said: Sufyān related to us, from Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: ʿUmar said: “ʿAlī is the best judge among us, and Ubayy is the best reciter among us; yet we leave aside some of what Ubayy says.” Qabīṣa added: “Ubayy would say, ‘I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say it,’ and [ʿUmar would say,] ‘I leave it aside for a reason: God says, “Whatever verse We abrogate or cause to be forgotten, We bring one better than it or the like of it” (2:106).’”

Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bukayr related to us. He said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Lahīʿa related to us. He said:

Al-Ḥārith ibn Yazīd related to me. He said: I heard ʿAlī ibn Rabāḥ say: Nāshira ibn Samiyy al-Yazanī related to me, saying: “I used to follow Muʿādh ibn Jabal, learning the Qurʾān from him and receiving knowledge from him. When I was in Medina and prayed in the Prophet’s mosque ﷺ I recited the Qurʾān. A man passed by me, tapped my shoulder, and said to me: ‘That is not how you recite.’”

When I had finished, I went to Muʿādh and told him what the man had said. Muʿādh ibn Jabal said:

“Would we recognize him?” I said: “Yes,” and pointed him out. Muʿādh went over to him and said: “I have been told that you corrected this man’s recitation.” He said: “Yes”—and it was Ubayy ibn Kaʿb—“Yes, Muʿādh. God’s Prophet ﷺ sent you to Yemen, and after you left, Qurʾān was revealed and Qurʾān was abrogated. Bring me your companions so that they may recite the Qurʾān to me.” Muʿādh said: “Nāshira, Ubayy ibn Kaʿb is the most knowledgeable of people about the opening and closing of a verse; Abū al-Dardāʾ is the most capable of people in expressing a wise saying; and ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb is the most knowledgeable of people about an obligatory duty and its apportionment.”

Abū Ghassān related to us. He said: Isḥāq ibn Saʿīd related to us. He said: My father informed me, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAyyāsh ibn Abī Rabīʿa: “His daughter was married to Wāqid ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar. ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAyyāsh entered to visit his daughter, and I said to him, ‘Abū al-Ḥārith, will you tell me about ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib?’ He said, ‘By God, nephew, I am certainly biased against him.’ I said, ‘What does that bias of yours consist of?’ He said, ‘He was a man fond of joking, and whenever he wished to make a cutting remark—and he had a cutting wit—he did so.’ I said, ‘And what was that cutting wit of his?’ He said, ‘Reciting the Qurʾān, knowledge of judicial decisions, and an unbreakable resolve in battle.’”

Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān al-Dimashqī al-Tanūkhī related to us. Ibn Abī al-Rijāl related to us, from Isḥāq ibn Yaḥyā ibn Ṭalḥa, who said: My uncle Ṭalḥa informed me. He said: I asked Ibn ʿAyyāsh: “Abū ʿAbbās, tell me about our predecessors, so that it is as though I had seen them.” He said:

“You ask me about Abū Bakr. By God, nephew, he was devout, pure, noble; all goodness was in him…”

“…in him. He was a man from whom you could draw out a flash of temper”—meaning irritability. “You ask me about ʿUmar. By God, as I knew him, he was strong and pure; snares had been laid for him at every watchpost, and he was wary of them. He was a man whose conduct in the marketplace was harsh. You ask me about ʿUthmān. By God, as I knew him, he fasted much and kept vigil in prayer. He was a man who loved his people. You ask me about ʿAlī. By God, as I knew him, he was forbearing and learned. I never saw him say anything without saying it well. He was a man who did not rely on his own standing; and I never saw him set his sights on anything, saying, ‘I shall take it,’ without being turned away from it.” He said: “Did you consider him deprived?” He replied: “That is what you say.”

Abū Ghassān related to us. He said: ʿUmar ibn Ziyād related to us, from al-Aswad ibn Qays:

I said to him: “What does ‘fond of joking’ mean?” He said: “He had a playful manner.”

Ibrāhīm ibn al-Mundhir related to us. He said: Muḥammad ibn Ṭalḥa ibn Isḥāq ibn Yaḥyā ibn Ṭalḥa related to me, from Mūsā ibn Ṭalḥa, who said: “ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwām, Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, and Ṭalḥa ibn ʿUbayd Allāh were of the same age”—that is, they were born in the same year.

Aḥmad ibn al-Khalīl related to me. He said: Abū Aḥmad al-Zubayrī related to us. He said: Sharīk related to us, from Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid, who said: I heard al-Shaʿbī swear by God that ʿAlī had entered and had not recited the Qurʾān.

[Zayd ibn Thābit]

Abū al-Walīd Hishām ibn ʿAbd al-Malik related to us. He said: Jarīr related to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Thābit ibn ʿUbayd, from Zayd ibn Thābit, who said: The Prophet ﷺ said:

“Letters come to me that I do not want anyone to read. Can you write Syriac well?” I said: “No.” He said:

“Then learn it.” So I learned it in seventeen days.

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us. He said: Shuʿba related to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Masrūq, who said: “I came to Medina and asked about the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ. I found that Zayd was among those firmly grounded in knowledge.”

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rajāʾ related to us. He said: Isrāʾīl informed us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Masrūq, who said: “I came to Medina and asked about those firmly grounded in knowledge. I found Zayd ibn Thābit among them.”

Ibn Numayr related to us. He said: Abū Muʿāwiya related to us. He said: Al-Aʿmash related to us, from Ibrāhīm, from Masrūq, who said: “I met Zayd ibn Thābit and found him to be among those firmly grounded in knowledge.”

[ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā and Abū Nuʿaym related to us. They said: Razīn related to us, from al-Shaʿbī, who said: “Zayd ibn Thābit was about to mount, and he had put his foot in the stirrup when Ibn ʿAbbās took hold of the stirrup and said, ‘Stand aside, cousin of the Messenger of God ﷺ.’”

He replied: “No; this is how we treat scholars and elders.”]

Abū al-Nuʿmān related to us. He said: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, from Ayyūb, who said: Ibn ʿAbbās said: “And Zayd is being buried! Does anyone who wishes to know how knowledge goes away—well that is how knowledge goes away.” He said: “And he said, ‘Today a great body of knowledge has been lost through you.’”

ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān related to us. He said: ʿAbd Allāh informed us. He said: Maʿmar informed us, from ʿAlī ibn Zayd, that when Zayd ibn Thābit was buried, Ibn ʿAbbās scattered earth over him.

Then he said: “This is how knowledge is buried.” I told ʿAlī ibn Ḥusayn about it, and he said: “By God, a great body of knowledge was buried with Ibn ʿAbbās.”

Abū al-Yamān related to us. He said: Shuʿayb informed me.

And Ṭalḥa related to us. He said: My grandfather related to me. Both of them related from al-Zuhrī, who said: Ibn al-Sabbāq informed me that Zayd ibn Thābit al-Anṣārī said: “Abū Bakr said to me, ‘You are a young, intelligent man, and we do not mistrust you. You used to write for the Messenger of God ﷺ and you followed the Qurʾān; so collect it.’”

Mūsā ibn Ismāʿīl related to us. He said: Ḥammād ibn Salama related to us, from ʿAmmār ibn Abī ʿAmmār, who said: “When Zayd ibn Thābit died, I sat with Ibn ʿAbbās in the shade of a palace. He said: ‘This is how knowledge goes away. A great body of knowledge was buried today.’”

Abū al-Nuʿmān related to us. He said: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, from Ayyūb, who said: Ibn ʿAbbās said: “And Zayd is being buried! Does anyone who wishes to know how knowledge goes away—well, this is how knowledge goes away.” He said: “And he said, ‘Today a great body of knowledge will be buried with you.’”

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā related to us, from Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid, from Abū Isḥāq, from Masrūq, who said: “I came to Medina and asked about the Companions of Muḥammad. They told me that Zayd ibn Thābit was among those firmly grounded in knowledge.”

Abū Hāshim Ziyād ibn Ayyūb related to us. He said:

Saʿīd ibn ʿĀmir related to us. He said: Ḥumayd ibn al-Aswad related to us, from Mālik ibn Anas, who said: “After ʿUmar, the leader of the people among us was Zayd ibn Thābit; and after Zayd, the leader of the people among us was ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar.”

Abū Bakr ibn ʿAbd al-Malik related to us. He said: Kathīr ibn Hishām related to us. He said: Jaʿfar ibn Burqān related to us. He said: I heard al-Zuhrī say: “Had Zayd ibn Thābit not written down the laws of inheritance, I would have thought they would disappear from among the people.”

Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmar related to us. He said: Sufyān related to us, from Ibn Judʿān, from someone who heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: “When news of Zayd ibn Thābit’s death arrived, he said: ‘This is how knowledge goes away.’” Ibn Judʿān said: “I mentioned that to Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib. He said, ‘I too say what he said’—meaning Ibn ʿAbbās—‘This is how knowledge goes away.’” Ibn Judʿān said: “And I say, as Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib said: ‘This is how knowledge goes away.’”

[Abū Hurayra]

[Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us. He said: Abū Hilāl related to us, from al-Ḥasan, who said:

Abū Hurayra said: “If I told you everything in this pouch of mine, you would pelt me with dung.” Al-Ḥasan said: “By God, he spoke truly. If he had told them that the House of God would be demolished or burned, people would not have believed him.

Abū Hilāl related to us, from Qatāda, who said: Ḥudhayfa said: “If I were on a riverbank with my hand outstretched to scoop up water, and I told you everything I know, my hand would not reach my mouth before I was killed.”]

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad al-Zuraqī related to us. He said: I heard ʿAmr ibn Yaḥyā al-Saʿīdī, from his grandfather Saʿīd ibn ʿAmr, from ʿĀʾisha, who said to Abū Hurayra: “You report things from the Messenger of God ﷺ that I never heard from him.” He said to her: “Indeed—”

The mirror and the kohl-vessel used to distract you from those traditions.

[Those among the Companions who memorized the Qurʾān]

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā related to us, from Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid, from al-Shaʿbī, who said:

Six men from the Anṣār memorized the Qurʾān during the lifetime of the Messenger of God ﷺ: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, Zayd ibn Thābit, Muʿādh ibn Jabal, Abū al-Dardāʾ, Saʿd ibn ʿUbayd, and Abū Zayd. Mujammiʿ ibn Jāriya had learned it except for two or three sūrahs. He said: None of the caliphs among Muḥammad’s Companions ﷺ—memorized it except ʿUthmān.

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us; Ḥammād related to us, from Ayyūb and Hishām, from Muḥammad, who said: Four men memorized the Qurʾān during the lifetime of the Messenger of God ﷺ—and there is no disagreement about them: Muʿādh ibn Jabal, Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, Zayd, and Abū Zayd. They differed about two of three men. Some said: ʿUthmān and Abū al-Dardāʾ; others said: ʿUthmān and Tamīm al-Dārī.

[Abū ʿUbayda ibn al-Jarrāḥ]

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us; Ḥammād ibn Salama related to us, from Thābit, from Anas said: The people of Yemen came to the Prophet ﷺ—and said, “Send a man with us to teach us the Qurʾān.” He took Abū ʿUbayda by the hand and sent him with them, saying, “This is the trusted man of this community.”

ʿAlī and Ḥajjāj related to us; they said: Shuʿba related to us, from Khālid al-Ḥadhdhāʾ, from Abū Qilāba, from Anas ibn Mālik, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ—said, “Every community has a trusted man, and the trusted man of this community is Abū ʿUbayda ibn al-Jarrāḥ.”

Ḥajjāj related to us; Ḥammād related to us, from Ziyād al-Aʿlam, from al-Ḥasan: The Prophet ﷺ—said, “There is no one among my Companions from whom, if I wished, I could find fault with some trait of character, except Abū ʿUbayda ibn al-Jarrāḥ.”

Abū Ṣāliḥ al-Ḥarrānī, ʿAbd al-Ghaffār ibn Dāwūd, related to us; he said: ʿAbd al-Razzāq ibn ʿUmar related to us, from al-Zuhrī, from Sālim, from his father, who said: ʿUmar said, “I never sought an office that I would have liked to hold more than I did on one occasion. A group came to the Prophet ﷺ—complaining about their governor, and he said, ‘I shall certainly send you a man who is truly trustworthy.’ I hoped that the Prophet’s prayer might reach me, but he appointed Abū ʿUbayda and passed me over.”

Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us; ʿAbd al-Razzāq related to us, from al-Zuhrī, from Anas ibn Mālik, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ—said, “Every community has a trusted man, and this is our trusted man,” and he took Abū ʿUbayda ibn al-Jarrāḥ by the hand.

ʿUbayd Allāh related to us, from Isrāʾīl, from Abū Isḥāq, from Ṣila, from Ibn Masʿūd:

Al-ʿĀqib and al-Sayyid came to the Messenger of God ﷺ—and he intended to invoke a mutual imprecation against them. One of them said to his companion, “Do not invoke a mutual imprecation against him. By God, if he is a prophet and we invoke it against him, neither we nor our descendants after us will prosper.” They said, “We will give you what you asked for; send a trustworthy man with us. We will take no one with us except a trustworthy man.” The Messenger of God ﷺ—said, “I shall certainly send with you a man who is truly trustworthy.” His Companions craned their necks to see who it would be. He said, “Stand up, Abū ʿUbayda ibn al-Jarrāḥ.” When he had turned away, he said, “This is the trusted man of this community.”

[ʿĀʾisha]

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us; Sufyān related to us, from Sulaymān, from Muslim, from Masrūq, who said—swearing an oath—“I saw the leading Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ—asking ʿĀʾisha about the laws of inheritance.”

ʿAmr ibn Ḥafṣ related to us; he said: My father related to us; al-Aʿmash related to us; Muslim related to us, from Masrūq, who was asked, “Was ʿĀʾisha proficient in the laws of inheritance?” He replied, “I saw the leading Companions of Muḥammad ﷺ—asking her about the laws of inheritance.”

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us; Ḥammād related to us, from Hishām ibn ʿUrwa, that his father mentioned ʿĀʾisha and said: “She was the most learned of people in ḥadīth, the most learned of people in the Qurʾān, and the most learned of people in poetry.” He said: “Four years before she died, I said, ‘If ʿĀʾisha were to die, I would regret nothing that I had failed to ask her.’”

[ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb]

ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān related to us; ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mubārak informed us; Muḥammad ibn ʿAjlān informed us, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar: He was asked about a matter and said, “I do not know it.” Then he said, “How well Ibn ʿUmar spoke! He was asked about something he did not know and said, ‘I do not know.’”

Ibn ʿUthmān related to us; ʿAbd Allāh related to us; Ḥaywa ibn Shurayḥ informed me; ʿUqba ibn Muslim informed me that Ibn ʿUmar was asked about something and said, “I do not know.” Then he added, “Do you want to make our backs bridges for you into Hell, so that you can say, ‘Ibn ʿUmar gave us this legal opinion’?”

Ibn ʿUthmān related to us; ʿAbd Allāh related to us; al-Muʿtamir ibn Sulaymān informed us, from Abū Makhzūm al-Nahshalī, from Sayyār Abū al-Ḥakam, who said: Ibn ʿUmar said, “You ask us for legal opinions as though we ourselves will not be questioned about the opinions we give you.”

Ibn Numayr related to us; Ibn Idrīs related to us, from Ḥuṣayn, from Sālim ibn Abī al-Jaʿd, from Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh, who said: “We encountered no one, and saw no one, without the world having turned him aside; no one was so turned aside except ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar.”

ʿAmr ibn ʿĀṣim related to us; Sulaymān ibn al-Mughīra related to us; ʿAlī ibn Zayd related to us, From Yūsuf ibn Mihrān, who said: We were with ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jābir al-Anṣārī in the Ḥijr when ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar passed by him, circumambulating the House. Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh said, “Whoever would be pleased to look upon one of the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ—who came before him and after him and did not alter or change [his ways]—or words to that effect—let him look at this man,” meaning Ibn ʿUmar. Jābir said, “There is not one of them but that he has…” He gestured toward ʿAbd Allāh with his hand, looking intently—that is, he had reached out.22

Muḥammad ibn Abī Zakīr related to us; Ibn Wahb informed us; Mālik informed me that a man related to him that ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar used to follow the conduct, practices, and way of life of the Messenger of God ﷺ—and took great care over them. His concern for this had taken a toll on his intellect.

Muḥammad informed me; Ibn Wahb informed us; he said: Mālik related to me, from Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd, who said: I said to Sālim, “Did you hear your father say such and such?” He replied, “Perhaps I heard him say it about a matter more than a hundred times.” I said to Mālik, “A hundred times!” He said, “Yes, and a thousand times, given the many years. Ibn ʿUmar lived for sixty years after the Prophet ﷺ—giving legal opinions to people during the pilgrimage season and at other times. He was one of the leaders of religion.”

Qabīṣa related to us; Sufyān related to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ṭāwūs, who said: “I have seen no man more scrupulous than Ibn ʿUmar.”

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us; Ḥammād “ibn Zayd” related to us, from Wāṣil, the client of Abū ʿUyayna, from Ḥafṣ, from ʿĀmir al-ʿAtakī, who said: I asked Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab about knowledge in the turban? He replied, “Ibn ʿUmar disliked it. If I were to testify of anyone on earth that he is among the people of Paradise, I would testify that ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar is.”

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us; Ḥammād related to us, from Ayyūb, from Nāfiʿ: Muʿāwiya sent Ibn ʿUmar one hundred thousand dirhams. When Muʿāwiya called for the pledge of allegiance to Yazīd ibn Muʿāwiya, [Ibn ʿUmar] said, “Do you think this is what he wanted? If so, my religion would be cheap to me.”

Saʿīd ibn Asad informed me; he said: Ḍamra related to us, from Ibn Shūdhāb, who said:

Muʿāwiya said to ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar, “I have heard that Ibn ʿUmar wants this office, though he has three traits that are unsuitable in a caliph: he is a jealous man, he is a man of little eloquence, and he is miserly.” Ibn Jaʿfar went and told Ibn ʿUmar. Ibn ʿUmar said, “As for his claim that I am a jealous man, I used to close my door upon my family; what need do people have to know what is beyond that? As for his claim that I am a man of little eloquence, I was the most learned of people in the Book of God, Mighty and Majestic, and no speech is more eloquent than it. As for his claim that I am a miserly man, I used to divide it among the people. If I did that, what need would people have for what Ibn al-Khaṭṭāb left me as an inheritance?” Ibn Jaʿfar told Muʿāwiya what he had said. Muʿāwiya replied, “I adjure you: let no one hear this from you.”

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Maslama related to us; he said: ʿAbd Allāh al-ʿUmarī related to us, from Nāfiʿ, who said:

A man came to Ibn ʿUmar to ask him about something. He said, “I have no knowledge of it.” After the man had turned away, Ibn ʿUmar looked around and said, “How well Ibn ʿUmar spoke! He was asked about something he did not know and said, ‘I do not know.’”

Abū al-Walīd Khalaf ibn al-Walīd related to us; he said: Ibn al-Mubārak related to us, from Ḥaywa ibn Shurayḥ, who said: I heard ʿUqba ibn Muslim—or ʿUqba ibn Muslim related to me—that Ibn ʿUmar was asked about something and said, “I do not know.” Then he said, “Do you want to make our backs bridges for you into the Fire of Hell, so that you can say, ‘Ibn ʿUmar gave us this legal opinion’?”

Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr related to us; he said: Sufyān related to us, from ʿĀṣim ibn Muḥammad, from his father, who said: “I never heard Ibn ʿUmar mention the Prophet ﷺ—without weeping.”

Abū Bakr related to us; Sufyān related to us; he said: Mālik ibn Mighwal related to us, from Abū Isḥāq al-Hamadhānī, who said: We were with Ibn Abī Laylā in his house, where people used to gather around him. Abū Salama ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān came to him and said, “Was ʿUmar superior among you, or his son?” They replied, “No, ʿUmar.” Abū Salama said, “ʿUmar lived in a time when he had peers, whereas Ibn ʿUmar lived in a time when he had no peer.”

[Reports about ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās and reports about his father, al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib]

Al-Ḥajjāj related to us; he said: Ḥammād related to us; he said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān ibn Khuthaym related to us, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: I was in the house of Maymūna bint al-Ḥārith. She set out water for ablution for the Prophet ﷺ—and the Prophet said, “Who set this out?” Maymūna replied, “ʿAbd Allāh did.” He said:

“O God, teach him interpretation and grant him understanding of religion.”

Aḥmad ibn Yūnus and Abū Ghassān related to us; they said: Zuhayr related to us; he said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān ibn Khuthaym related to us, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said that he heard him say: The Messenger of God ﷺ—placed his hand above my shoulder, or on my shoulder—or “my shoulder,” said Aḥmad; Saʿīd was uncertain—and said, “O God, grant him understanding of religion and teach him interpretation.”

Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd Allāh related to us; he said: Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh related to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Ziyād ibn Ḥuṣayn, from Abū al-ʿĀliya, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: “I recited the firmly established [sūrahs] during the lifetime of the Messenger of God ﷺ” meaning the Mufaṣṣal. He said: At that time he was twelve years old.

Abū Bakr related to us; Sufyān related to us; he said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Yazīd related to us; Ibn Abī Mulayka related to me; he said: We entered upon Ibn ʿAbbās, and he said, “Ask me about Sūrat al-Baqara and Sūrat Yūsuf, for I recited the Qurʾān when I was young.”

Saʿīd ibn Abī Maryam related to me; Nāfiʿ ibn ʿUmar al-Jumaḥī informed us; he said:

Ibn Abī Mulayka related to me; he said: I entered upon Ibn ʿAbbās, and he said, “I have awoken in good spirits, so ask me about matters from Sūrat al-Baqara and Sūrat Yūsuf.” He singled these two out from among the sūrahs. He said: We assigned one man to ask the questions, but he knew nothing.

Ibn Numayr related to me; he said: Muḥammad ibn Bishr related to us; Ismāʿīl related to us, from Shuʿayb ibn Yasār, from ʿIkrima, who said: The Prophet ﷺ—called Ibn ʿAbbās, seated him on his lap, passed his hand over his head, and prayed for him to be granted knowledge.

Qabīṣa related to us; he said: Sufyān related to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Abū Wāʾil, who said: Ibn ʿAbbās recited Sūrat al-Nūr and then explained it. A man said, “If this Dailamī had heard it, he would have become Muslim.”

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us; he said: Ḥammād related to us, from al-Zubayr ibn al-Khirrīt, who said: ʿIkrima said, “Ibn ʿAbbās knew the Qurʾān better than ʿAlī, while ʿAlī knew the ambiguous matters better than Ibn ʿAbbās.”

Abū Nuʿaym related to us; Sufyān related to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sayf, who said: ʿĀʾisha was asked, “Who has been appointed to lead the pilgrimage this year?” They said, “Ibn ʿAbbās.”

She said, “He is the most learned of people about the pilgrimage.”

ʿUmar ibn Ḥafṣ ibn Ghiyāth related to us; he said: My father related to us; al-Aʿmash related to us; he said: Muslim related to us, from Masrūq, who said: ʿAbd Allāh said, “If Ibn ʿAbbās had lived to our age, no man among us would have matched him.”

Ismāʿīl ibn al-Khalīl related to me; ʿAlī ibn Mushir informed us; al-Aʿmash informed us, from Muslim, from Masrūq, from ʿAbd Allāh, who said: “If Ibn ʿAbbās had lived to our age, no man among us would have matched him.” Al-Aʿmash said: I heard them relate that ʿAbd Allāh said:

“How excellent an interpreter of the Qurʾān Ibn ʿAbbās is!”

Ibn Numayr related to me; he said: Ḥafṣ related to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Abū al-Ḍuḥā, from Masrūq, who said: ʿAbd Allāh said, “How excellent an interpreter of the Qurʾān Ibn ʿAbbās is!”

Muḥammad ibn Abī al-Sarī related to us; he said: ʿAbd al-Razzāq related to us; he said: al-Thawrī related to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Abū al-Ḍuḥā, from Masrūq, from ʿAbd Allāh, who said: “If Ibn ʿAbbās had lived to our age, no man among us would have matched him. How excellent an interpreter of the Qurʾān Ibn ʿAbbās is!”

Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shayba related to us; he said: Abū Usāma related to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Mujāhid, who said: “Ibn ʿAbbās was called ‘the Sea’ because of the abundance of his knowledge.”

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us; he said: ʿAmr ibn Dīnār related to us; he said: I said to Jābir ibn Zayd, “They claim that the Messenger of God ﷺ—forbade the meat of domestic donkeys.” He said, “Where is that Sea”—meaning Ibn ʿAbbās—“?” Then he recited:

“Say: ‘I find in what has been revealed to me nothing forbidden…’”

6:145, the verse.

Qabīṣa related to us; he said: Sufyān related to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ṭāwūs, who said:

“I have seen no man more scrupulous than Ibn ʿUmar, nor have I seen a man more learned than Ibn ʿAbbās.”

Ibn Numayr related to us; he said: My father related to us; al-Aʿmash related to us, from Ibrāhīm, from Masrūq, who said: Ibn ʿAbbās sent for ʿAlqama and the companions of ʿAbd Allāh. He began asking questions, and the man answering would sometimes be wrong and sometimes right. We felt it would be discourteous to correct him while we were eating his food.

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā related to us, from Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid, from Yazīd ibn [Abī] Ziyād, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Nawfal ibn ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā, from al-ʿAbbās, who said: “I said: ‘Messenger of God, when Quraysh meet one another, they greet one another with cheerful faces; but when they meet us, they meet us with faces we do not recognize.’ At that, the Messenger of God ﷺ became very angry. Then he said: ‘By Him in whose hand is Muḥammad’s soul, faith does not enter a man’s heart until he loves you for God’s sake, mighty and majestic is He, and for the sake of His Messenger ﷺ.’”

Ziyād ibn Ayyūb related to us; he said: Yaḥyā related to us; he said: Hishām ibn Yūsuf al-Ṣanʿānī related to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sulaymān al-Nawfalī, judge of Ṣanʿāʾ, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās, from his father, from his grandfather Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Love God, mighty and majestic is He, for the blessings with which He sustains you; love me for love of God, mighty and majestic is He; and love my family for love of me.”

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā related to us, from Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid, from Yazīd ibn Abī Ziyād, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Nawfal, from al-ʿAbbās, who said: “I said: ‘Messenger of God, Quraysh sat together and discussed their lineages, and they made your likeness that of a date palm in a hollow of the earth.’ The Messenger of God ﷺ said: ‘When God, mighty and majestic is He, created creation, He placed me among the best of them. Then, when He divided them, He placed me among the better of the two groups. Then, when He formed the tribes, He placed me among the best tribe. Then, when He formed the houses, He placed me among the best of their houses. Thus, I am the best of them in person and the best of them in house.’”

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā, Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb, and Ḥajjāj ibn Minhāl related to us; they said:

Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “God, mighty and majestic is He, chose the Arabs, and from among them He chose Kināna”—or he said, “al-Naḍr ibn Kināna”; Ḥammād was uncertain—“then He chose Quraysh from among them, then He chose Banū Hāshim from among them.”

Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd related to me; he said: Qays related to us, from al-Aʿmash, from ʿAbāya ibn Rabīʿ al-Asadī, from Ibn ʿAbbās: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “God, mighty and majestic is He, created creation in two groups and placed me in the better of the two groups. That is what God, mighty and majestic is He, says: ‘And the companions of the right’ (56:27), and ‘the companions of the left’ (56:41). I am among the companions of the right, and I am the best of the companions of the right. Then He divided the two groups into thirds and placed me in the best of the three. That is what He says: ‘Then the companions of the right’ (56:8) and ‘the foremost, the foremost’ (56:10). I am the best of the foremost. Then He made the thirds into tribes and placed me in the best tribe among them. That is what He says: ‘We made you peoples and tribes so that you may know one another. Indeed, the most noble of you in God’s sight is the most God-fearing of you. Indeed, God is All-Knowing, All-Aware’ (49:13). I am the most God-fearing of Adam’s offspring and the most noble of them in the sight of God, mighty and majestic is He. Then He made the tribes into houses and placed me in the best house among them. That is what He says: ‘God only desires to remove impurity from you, People of the House, and to purify you completely’ (33:33). I and my family are purified of sins.”

Abū Nuʿaym related to us; he said: Sufyān related to us, from Yazīd ibn Abī Ziyād, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Nawfal, from al-Muṭṭalib ibn Abī Wadāʿa, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ heard some of what people were saying. He ascended the pulpit, praised God, and extolled Him. He said: “Who am I?” They said: “You are the Messenger of God.” He said: “I am Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib.” He said: “God, mighty and majestic is He, created creation and placed me among the best of His creation. Then He made them two groups and placed me in the better tribe among them. He made them into houses and placed me in the best house among you. I am the best of you in house and the best of you in person.”

ʿAlī ibn al-Mundhir related to me; he said: Ibn Fuḍayl related to us; he said: Yazīd ibn Ibn Abī Ziyād related to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith, who said: Al-Muṭṭalib ibn Rabīʿa ibn al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib told me: Al-ʿAbbās came to the Prophet of God ﷺ while he was with him. He said: “What has angered you?” He replied: “Messenger of God, what is it between us and Quraysh? When they meet one another, they greet one another with cheerful faces, but when they meet us, they do otherwise.” The Messenger of God ﷺ became angry until his face reddened and sweat gathered between his eyes—for when he became angry, it would gather there. When he had calmed down, he said: “By Him in whose hand is Muḥammad’s soul, faith does not enter a man’s heart until he loves you for God’s sake, mighty and majestic is He, and for the sake of His Messenger ﷺ.”

Then he said: “O people, whoever harms al-ʿAbbās has harmed me. A man’s paternal uncle is the twin of his father.”

Khālid al-Ṭaḥḥān and Jarīr al-Rāzī related it in the same way. ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā related to us; he said: Isrāʾīl informed us, from ʿAbd al-Aʿlā, who heard Saʿīd ibn Jubayr say: Ibn ʿAbbās informed me that a man reviled a father he had had in the pre-Islamic period, so al-ʿAbbās slapped him. The man’s people came and said: “By God, we will slap him as he slapped him,” and they put on their weapons. This reached the Messenger of God ﷺ who ascended the pulpit and said: “O people, which person do you know to be most honored in the sight of God mighty and majestic is He?” They said: “You.” He said: “Al-ʿAbbās is of me, and I am of him. Do not revile our dead and thereby harm our living.” The narrator said: The people came and said: “Messenger of God, we seek refuge in God from your anger. Ask forgiveness for us.”

ʿUbayd Allāh related to us; he said: Abū Isrāʾīl related to us, from al-Ḥakam, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ appointed ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb to collect alms. He went to al-ʿAbbās to request his alms, and al-ʿAbbās spoke harshly to him. ʿUmar went to ʿAlī and told him about it, asking him to mention it to the Prophet ﷺ. ʿAlī went to him and informed him. The Messenger of God ﷺ said to ʿUmar: “May your hands be covered with dust! Did you not know that a man’s paternal uncle is the twin of his father? Al-ʿAbbās advanced us the alms for this year in the previous year.”

ʿUbayd Allāh related to us; he said: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Siyāh related to us, from Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit: The Prophet ﷺ sent ʿUmar to collect alms, but al-ʿAbbās withheld it from him.

ʿUmar said: “Messenger of God, al-ʿAbbās has withheld the alms.” He replied: “Ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, did you not know that a man’s paternal uncle is the twin of his father?” He said: “You have spoken truly.”

ʿĪsā ibn Muḥammad related to us; he said: Wahb ibn Jarīr related to us; he said: My father related to us; he said: I heard al-Aʿmash relate, from ʿAmr ibn Murra, from Abū al-Bakhtarī, from ʿAlī: ʿUmar consulted the people and said: “What do you say about this surplus money we have?”

They said: “Commander of the Faithful, you have kept us busy—or we have kept you busy—from your family, your estate, and your trade; so it is yours.” He said: “Mine! What do you say?” I replied: “They have advised you.” He said: “Speak.” I said: “Commander of the Faithful, why do you turn your certainty into suspicion and your forbearance into ignorance?”

He said: “You will have to take back what you said, or I will punish you.” I said: “Yes, indeed, by God I will take it back. Do you remember when the Messenger of God ﷺ sent you as a collector and you went to al-ʿAbbās, and he withheld his alms from you? There was a dispute between you, and you came to me and said: ‘Come with me to the Prophet ﷺ so that I can tell him what al-ʿAbbās did.’ We went to him and found him heavy-hearted. We went back, then came to him the next day and found him in good spirits. I told him what al-ʿAbbās had done. He said: ‘Did you not know, ʿUmar, that a man’s paternal uncle is the twin of his father?’ He said: ‘We had been in need, so we borrowed the alms for two years from al-ʿAbbās.’ We mentioned to him how heavy-hearted he had seemed that day and how cheerful he had seemed the next.

“He said: ‘The first day you came to me, two dinars of the alms were still with me. That is why I seemed heavy-hearted to you. Then you came to me today, after I had sent them off, and that is why I seemed cheerful to you.’ ʿUmar said: ‘You have spoken truly, by God. By God, I shall thank you for both the first and the last.’ I said: ‘Commander of the Faithful, why are you quick to punish and slow to give thanks?’”

Sufyān ibn Uways related to us; he said: My father related to me, from Abū al-Zinād, from al-Aʿraj, from Abū Hurayra: The Messenger of God ﷺ ordered alms to be collected. It was said: “Ibn Jamīl, Khālid ibn al-Walīd, and al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib have withheld it.” The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Ibn Jamīl has cause for resentment only because he was poor and God, mighty and majestic is He, and His Messenger made him rich. As for Khālid, you are wronging Khālid: Khālid has dedicated his coats of mail and his slaves in the path of God. As for al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, the uncle of the Messenger of God ﷺ it is due from him, and an equal amount besides it.” Yaḥyā related to us; he said: Ibn Abī al-Zinād related to us, from his father, from al-Aʿraj, from Abū Hurayra, who said: The Prophet ﷺ ordered alms to be collected. One of those who made insinuations said: “Ibn Jamīl, Khālid ibn al-Walīd, and al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib have refused to give alms…”

“…They have refused to give alms. The Prophet ﷺ delivered a sermon and refrained from reproaching two of them, al-ʿAbbās and Khālid, while he accepted alms on behalf of Ibn Jamīl. Then the Messenger of God ﷺ said: ‘Ibn Jamīl has cause for resentment only because he was poor and God, mighty and majestic is He, and His Messenger enriched him from His bounty. As for Khālid ibn al-Walīd, you are wronging Khālid: Khālid has dedicated his coats of mail and his slaves in the path of God, mighty and majestic is He. As for al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, the uncle of the Messenger of God ﷺ it is due from him, and an equal amount besides it.’”

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī, Ibrāhīm ibn al-Mundhir, and Nuʿaym ibn Ḥammād related to us; they said:

Muḥammad ibn Ṭalḥa informed us; he said: Abū Suhayl ibn Mālik told us that he heard Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab relate, from Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, who said: While the Messenger of God ﷺ was preparing an expedition in the horse market of Medina, al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib appeared. The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “This is al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, the one who, on behalf of your Prophet, is the most open-handed of Quraysh and the most devoted in maintaining kinship ties.” In Ibrāhīm’s version of the report, he said: I heard Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ say: “We were with the Messenger of God ﷺ in the horse market, when al-ʿAbbās appeared. He said: ‘The most devoted in maintaining its ties.’” Nuʿaym said: I asked Muḥammad: “‘And its brother’?” He said: “‘And its brother’ and ‘the most devoted in maintaining its ties’ mean the same; sometimes I say ‘and its brother.’”

Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Uways related to us; he said: Muḥammad ibn Ṭalḥa ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ṭalḥa ibn ʿUbayd Allāh al-Qurashī, then al-Taymī, told me: Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥāritha ibn al-Nuʿmān told me, from his father, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥāritha, who said: When Ṣafwān ibn Umayya ibn Khalaf al-Jumaḥī arrived, the Messenger of God ﷺ said to him:

“Whose house are you staying at, Abū Wahb?” He said: “I am staying with al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib.” He said: “You are staying with the man of Quraysh who loves Quraysh most intensely.”

ʿAmr ibn ʿĀṣim related to us; he said: Sulaymān ibn al-Mughīra related to us, from Ḥumayd ibn Hilāl, who said: Ibn al-Ḥaḍramī sent the Messenger of God ﷺ eighty thousand from Bahrain. No greater sum of money had ever come to him, either before or after. He said:

He said: It was spread out on a mat, and the call to prayer was made. The Messenger of God ﷺ came and stood over the money. The people of the mosque came. That day there was no counting or weighing; it was only a matter of taking. Al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib came, wearing a short cloak, and tried to stand up but could not. He raised his head to the Messenger of God ﷺ and said: “Messenger of God, help me up.” The Messenger of God ﷺ smiled until his laughing teeth—or his canine tooth—showed. He said to him:

“Put some of the money back, then stand with what you can manage.” He did so. As he left, al-ʿAbbās kept saying: “As for one of the two things God, mighty and majestic is He, promised us, He has fulfilled it for us. We do not know what He will do about the other: ‘O Prophet, say to those captives who are in your hands: If God knows any good in your hearts…’ (8:70),” through the end of the verse. He said: “This is the good that He has given me in return for what He took from me; I do not know what God, mighty and majestic is He, will do in the Hereafter.” The Messenger of God ﷺ continued to stand over that money until not a dirham remained, and he did not send a single dirham to his family.23 Then he went to the prayer and prayed.

Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Anṣārī related to us; he said: My father related to me, from his uncle Thumāma, from Anas, who said: When there was a drought, ʿUmar would go out to pray for rain and take al-ʿAbbās with him. He would say: “O God, we have suffered drought. We used to seek access to You through our Prophet ﷺ; now we seek access to You through the uncle of our Prophet, so give us rain.” He said: They would then be given rain.

Isḥāq ibn Ḥātim related to us; he said: ʿAbd al-Wahhāb related to us, from Thawr ibn Yazīd, from Makḥūl, from Kurayb, the client of Ibn ʿAbbās, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Prophet ﷺ said to al-ʿAbbās: “Come to me tomorrow morning, Monday, you and your sons.”

He said: He came in the morning, and we came with him. He wrapped us in a cloak of his, then said: “O God, forgive al-ʿAbbās and his sons with a manifest and inward forgiveness that leaves no sin. O God, provide for him through his sons.”

Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿīd related to us; he said: Ismāʿīl ibn Qays ibn Saʿd ibn Zayd ibn Thābit al-Anṣārī related to us; he said: Abū Ḥāzim related to me, from Sahl, who said: We were with the Messenger of God ﷺ when al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib stood up and screened him. He said:

The Prophet ﷺ saw him and said: “O God, shield al-ʿAbbās and his sons from the Fire.”

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā related to us; he said: Jarīr ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd related to us, from Mughīra, from Abū Razīn, who said: Al-ʿAbbās was asked: “Are you older, or the Prophet ﷺ?” He said: “He is older than I am, but I was born before him.”

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rajāʾ related to us, from Isrāʾīl, from Abū Isḥāq, from Ḥāritha, from ʿAlī, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said on the day of…

Badr: “See whom you can capture from Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, for they were only brought out against their will.”

Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Uways related to us; he said: My father related to me, from Ḥumayd ibn Qays al-Makkī, client of Banū Asad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ and others among the companions of Ibn ʿAbbās, from Ibn ʿAbbās: The Prophet ﷺ said: “O Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, I have asked God, mighty and majestic is He, for three things on your behalf: that He make firm the one who stands among you, guide the one among you who has gone astray, and teach the one among you who is ignorant. I have also asked God, mighty and majestic is He, to make you generous, compassionate, and valiant. Even if a man were to walk between the Corner and the Station, pray and fast, then meet God, mighty and majestic is He, while hating the People of the House of Muḥammad ﷺ he would enter the Fire.”24

Al-Ḥasan ibn al-Rabīʿ related to us; he said: Ibn Idrīs related to us, from Ibn Isḥāq.
