ʿAmmār ibn al-Ḥasan related to me; he said: Salama related to us, from Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq, from al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Maʿbad, who said that one of his family told him, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ that he said on the day of Badr: “Whoever among you encounters al-ʿAbbās, let him hold back, for he was brought out under compulsion.” Abū Ḥudhayfa ibn ʿUtba ibn Rabīʿa said: “Are our fathers, sons, and brothers to be killed while we spare al-ʿAbbās? By God, if I encounter him, I will strike him with the sword”—ʿAmmār said: “I will cleave him with the letter ḥāʾ,” while al-Ḥasan said it with the letter jīm—“.” This reached the Messenger of God ﷺ who said to ʿUmar: “Abū Ḥafṣ, would the face of the Messenger of God’s uncle be struck with a sword?” ʿUmar said: “That was the first day he called me Abū Ḥafṣ.”

ʿAmmār ibn al-Ḥasan related to me; he said: Salama related to us; he said: Muḥammad told me, from al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Maʿbad, from one of his family, from Ibn ʿAbbās.

Muḥammad ibn Wahb related to me; he said: Muḥammad ibn Salama related to us, from Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq, who said: Al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Maʿbad ibn ʿAbbās told me, from one of his family, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: When evening came on the day of Badr, and the prisoners were being held—ʿAmmār said: “held in bonds”—the Messenger of God ﷺ stayed awake throughout the first night. His companions said to him: “Messenger of God, why are you not sleeping?” He said:

“I hear al-ʿAbbās’s groaning in his bonds.” They went to al-ʿAbbās and released him, and the Messenger of God ﷺ slept.

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā related to us; he said: Isrāʾīl informed us, from Ibrāhīm ibn al-Muhājir, from Mujāhid, from Anas: When the prisoners were captured on the day of Badr, al-ʿAbbās was captured by a man from the Anṣār. They had threatened to kill him. The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “I did not sleep last night because of al-ʿAbbās, for the Anṣār claim that they will kill him.” ʿUmar said: “Shall I go to them, Messenger of God?” He went to the Anṣār and said:

“Release al-ʿAbbās.” They said: “If the Messenger of God is pleased with that, then take him.”

Al-Ḥasan ibn al-Rabīʿ related to us; he said: Ibn Idrīs related to us, from Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said to al-ʿAbbās: “ʿAbbās, ransom yourself, your nephew ʿAqīl ibn Abī Ṭālib, Nawfal ibn al-Ḥārith, and your ally ʿUtba ibn Jaḥdam, the brother of Banū al-Ḥārith ibn Fihr, for you are a man of wealth.” He said:

“Messenger of God, I had indeed become Muslim, but the people compelled me.” He said: “God…”

“I know better about your being a Muslim. If it is as you say, God will reward you for it, so ransom yourself.”

Al-Ḥasan related to us; he said: Ibn Idrīs related to us; he said: Ibn Isḥāq said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Najīḥ related to me, from ʿAṭāʾ, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās, who said: “God—Mighty and Glorious—is the One who prescribed for them that one man should fight ten.” He mentioned the account up to: “For what you took, there will be a tremendous punishment” (Qurʾān 8:68). And He said: “O Prophet, say to those captives who are in your hands: ‘If God knows any good in your hearts, He will give you something better than what was taken from you’” (Qurʾān 8:70).

He said:

Al-ʿAbbās used to say: “By God, this verse was revealed concerning me, when I told the Messenger of God ﷺ—about my Islam, after he questioned me, and I asked him to set against my account the twenty uqiyyas that he had taken from me. He refused to set them against my account. In return for those twenty uqiyyas, God—Mighty and Glorious—gave me twenty slaves, every one of whom traded with capital he had in his possession, in addition to what I hope for of God’s forgiveness—Mighty and Glorious is He.”

ʿAmmār related to me; he said: Salama related to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, from al-Kalbī, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: “Al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib used to say: ‘By God, this was revealed concerning me, when I told the Messenger of God ﷺ—about my Islam and asked him to settle accounts with me.’” He mentioned the account.

Zayd ibn al-Mubārak related to us; he said: Muḥammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Maʿmar, who said:

I heard Thābit al-Bunānī, from Anas, say: “When the Messenger of God ﷺ—conquered Khaybar, al-Ḥajjāj ibn ʿIlāṭ said: ‘Messenger of God, I have property in Mecca, and I have family there. I wish to go to them, and I shall be free to say anything against you or say whatever I please.’”

“He had family there, and I want to go to them; so I am free to take liberties with you and say whatever I please.”

The Messenger of God ﷺ—gave him permission to say whatever he wished. When he arrived, he said to his wife: “Keep this from me, and gather whatever property of mine you have with you, for I want to buy from Muḥammad and his companions’ spoils. They have been overpowered, and their property has been seized.”

This news spread through Mecca. It weighed heavily on the Muslims and reached them; the polytheists openly displayed their joy and delight. The news reached al-ʿAbbās, and he was stricken and distressed, unable to stand. Maʿmar said:

ʿUthmān al-Jazarī informed me, from Miqsam, who said: Al-ʿAbbās took one of his sons, named Qutham, lay back, and placed him on his chest, saying:

“Qutham is like the man of the lofty nose—

So hasten with blessings, despite whoever is disgraced.”

Maʿmar said, in the account from Anas: Al-ʿAbbās sent one of his servants to al-Ḥajjāj, saying:

“Woe to you! What have you brought, and what are you saying? What God has promised is better than what you have brought.”

Al-Ḥajjāj said: “Boy, give Abū al-Faḍl my greetings, and tell him to leave me one of the rooms in his house so that I may come to him, for the news is what will please him.”

When the servant reached the door of the house, he said: “Rejoice, Abū al-Faḍl!” Al-ʿAbbās leapt up in delight and kissed him between the eyes. The servant told him what al-Ḥajjāj had said, and al-ʿAbbās set him free.

Then al-Ḥajjāj came and told him that the Messenger of God ﷺ—had conquered Khaybar and taken their property as spoils, and that God’s allotted shares had been distributed from it. The Messenger of God ﷺ—had chosen Ṣafiyya daughter of Ḥuyayy for himself and offered her the choice of freeing her so that she might become his wife, or sending her back to her family. She chose to be freed and become his wife. “But I came to collect property of mine that was here and take it away. I asked the Messenger of God ﷺ—for permission to speak, and he gave me permission to say whatever I wished. So keep this from me, Abū al-Faḍl, for three days, then say whatever you wish.” He said:

His wife gathered his belongings for him, and then he continued on his way. Three days later, al-ʿAbbās went to al-Ḥajjāj’s wife and asked: “What has your husband done?”

“He has gone,” she replied. “May God Most High not grieve you, Abū al-Faḍl. What reached you distressed us greatly.”

“Indeed, may God—Mighty and Glorious—not grieve me. By God’s praise, it was nothing but what I love: God—Mighty and Glorious—has granted victory to His Messenger, God’s allotted shares have been distributed at Khaybar, and the Messenger of God ﷺ—has chosen Ṣafiyya for himself. If you have need of your husband, go join him.”

“By God, I think you are telling the truth,” she said.

“By God, I am telling the truth, and matters are as I tell you.”

Then he went to the gatherings of Quraysh. They said: “By your Lord, the outcome will not be good for you, Abū al-Faḍl.”

“Nothing but good has come to me, praise be to God. Al-Ḥajjāj told me such-and-such, and asked me to keep it secret for three days because of his own need.” Thus God—Mighty and Glorious—dispelled the Muslims’ gloom and distress at the hands of the polytheists. The Muslims came out of their quarters and gathered at al-ʿAbbās’s place after he had told them the news.

Al-Ḥajjāj related to us; he said: Ḥammād related to us, from ʿAlī ibn Zayd, from al-Ḥasan:

“There was some money left in the public treasury. Al-ʿAbbās said to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb and the people: ‘What do you think? If the paternal uncle of Moses were among you, would you honor him and acknowledge his right?’ They said: ‘Yes.’

“He said: ‘Then I, the paternal uncle of your Prophet, have a greater right to be honored.’ ʿUmar spoke to the people, and they gave it to him.”

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rajāʾ related to us; he said: Qays ibn al-Rabīʿ informed us, from Ibn Abī al-Sifr, from Ibn Shuraḥbīl—who is Arqam—from Ibn ʿAbbās, from al-ʿAbbās, who said: “I went in to see the Prophet ﷺ—while his wives were with him. They veiled themselves from me, except Maymūna, who had—”

That was enough for her. He said: “Let no one remain in the house who witnessed the forceful dosing—for my oath did not include al-ʿAbbās.”

Abū al-Yamān related to us; he said: Shuʿayb ibn Abī Ḥamza informed me, from al-Zuhrī.

Al-Ḥajjāj related to us; he said: My grandfather related to us, from al-Zuhrī.

ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Shaqīq related to us; he said: ʿAbd Allāh informed us; he said:

Maʿmar and Yūnus informed us, from al-Zuhrī.

Abū Ṣāliḥ and Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bukayr related to us; they said: al-Layth related to us; he said:

ʿUqayl related to me, from Ibn Shihāb, who said: Abū Bakr ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Hishām informed me that the Messenger of God ﷺ—fell ill with the illness from which he died while he was in the house of Maymūna, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ. His pain grew so severe that he became overwhelmed by it. Some of his wives gathered around him, among them Umm Salama, his paternal uncle al-ʿAbbās, and Asmāʾ daughter of ʿUmays. They consulted about administering medicine to the Messenger of God ﷺ—while he was overwhelmed. They administered it to him while he was in that state. When he recovered, he said:

“Who did this to me? This is the doing of women who came from over there”—and he pointed toward the land of Abyssinia. The Messenger of God ﷺ—said: “No one is to remain in the house without being given the medicine”—as punishment for them—“except the paternal uncle of the Messenger of God ﷺ.”

Abū Bakr said:

Maymūna was given the medicine that day while she was fasting, because of the oath of the Messenger of God ﷺ.

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us; he said: Ḥammād ibn Salama related to us, from ʿAlī ibn Zayd, from al-Ḥasan, from al-Aḥnaf ibn Qays, who heard ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb say: “Quraysh are the leaders of the people; not one of them enters through a door without a group of people entering with him. When ʿUmar was stabbed, he ordered Ṣuhayb to lead the people in prayer and provide them with food for three days, until they had agreed upon a man. When the dining tables were set out, the people refrained from eating. Al-ʿAbbās said: ‘People, the Messenger of God ﷺ—has died, and we ate and drank after him. Abū Bakr died, and we ate. The people must eat.’”

Then he reached out his hand and ate, and the people ate. Thus I understood what ʿUmar had said.

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā related to us; he said: Mūsā ibn ʿUbayda related to us, from Yaʿqūb ibn Zayd, that ʿUmar went out on a Friday and al-ʿAbbās’s drainpipe spilled water on him. He ordered it removed. Al-ʿAbbās said: “You have removed my drainpipe. No one put it where it was except the Messenger of God ﷺ—with his own hand.”

ʿUmar said: “By God, no one will put it back except you, with your own hand; and you shall have no ladder except ʿUmar.”

Al-ʿAbbās placed his feet on ʿUmar’s shoulders, then put it back where it had been.

Muḥammad ibn Wahb related to me; he said: Muḥammad ibn Salama related to me, from Ibn Isḥāq, who said: Ḥusayn ibn ʿAbd Allāh [ibn ʿUbayd Allāh] ibn ʿAbbās related to me, from ʿIkrima, the client of Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: Abū Rāfiʿ, the client of the Messenger of God ﷺ—said: “I was a boy belonging to al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib. Islam had entered our household, so al-ʿAbbās and Umm al-Faḍl became Muslims, and I became Muslim. Al-ʿAbbās held his people in awe and disliked opposing them, so he concealed his Islam.”

Al-Ḥasan ibn al-Rabīʿ related to us; he said: Ibn Idrīs related to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, who said: Ḥusayn ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās related to me, from ʿIkrima, who said: Abū Rāfiʿ said—and he mentioned the same report, word for word.

Yaḥyā ibn Yaḥyā related to us; he said: ʿAbd al-Jabbār ibn Ward al-Makkī related to us; he said:

I heard ʿAṭāʾ say: “Never have I seen a gathering more distinguished than Ibn ʿAbbās’s: one with more learning and a greater serving dish than his. The people learned in the Qurʾān ask him, and the poets are with him asking him, and the grammarians are with him asking him; each departs through a broad valley.”

Yūsuf ibn Kāmil al-ʿAṭṭār related to us; he said: Ḥammād related to us; he said: ʿAlī ibn Zayd related to us, from Yūsuf ibn Mihrān, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: “Al-ʿAbbās had a house beside the mosque in Medina. ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said to him: ‘Sell it to me, or give it to me, so that I may incorporate it into the mosque.’ He refused. ʿUmar said: ‘Let us appoint as arbitrator between us a Companion of the Prophet ﷺ.’ They appointed Ubayy ibn Kaʿb between them, and he ruled in favor of al-ʿAbbās over ʿUmar.

“ʿUmar said: ‘No one among the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ—has a greater claim upon me than you.’

“Ubayy ibn Kaʿb said: ‘Or is anyone a more sincere adviser to you than I?’ Then he said: ‘Commander of the Faithful, have you not heard the account of David? God—Mighty and Glorious—commanded him to build the Holy House. He included in it the house of a woman without her permission. When he reached the men’s dwellings, God—Mighty and Glorious—prevented him from building it. David said: “My Lord, if You prevent me from building it, then make it possible through my successor.”’

“Al-ʿAbbās said: ‘Did you not rule in my favor concerning it, so that it became mine?’

“‘Yes,’ he replied.

“Then I call you to witness that I have dedicated it to God—Mighty and Glorious is He.”

Muḥammad ibn Wahb related to us; he said: Muḥammad ibn Salama related to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, who said: al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Maʿbad related to me, from one of his relatives, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ—that he said to his Companions:

“I know that men from Banū Hāshim and others have been brought out unwillingly; they have no desire to fight us. If any of you meets a man from Banū Hāshim, let him not kill him. If any of you meets Abū al-Bakhtarī ibn Hishām ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Asad, let him not kill him. If any of you meets al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, let him not kill him, for he was brought out only under compulsion.”

Abū Ḥudhayfa ibn ʿUtba ibn Rabīʿa said: “Are our fathers, sons, brothers, and clansmen to be killed while al-ʿAbbās is spared? By God, if I meet him, I will plunge the sword into him.”

This reached the Messenger of God ﷺ—and he said to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb: “Abū Ḥafṣ—” ʿUmar said: “That was the first day the Messenger of God ﷺ—called me Abū Ḥafṣ—‘Is the face of the Messenger of God’s paternal uncle to be struck with a sword?’”

ʿUmar said: “Prophet of God, let me strike off his head with the sword, for by God he has become a hypocrite.”

Abū Ḥudhayfa used to say: “I do not feel safe from that statement I made that day, and I shall always fear its consequences unless God expiates it for me through martyrdom.” He was killed as a martyr on the day of Yamāma.

ʿAbd al-Wahhāb ibn al-Ḍaḥḥāk related to me; he said: Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAyyāsh related to us; he said: Ṣafwān ibn ʿAmr related to us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Jubayr ibn Nufayr, from Kathīr ibn Murra al-Ḥaḍramī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr, from the Prophet ﷺ—who said:

“God—Mighty and Glorious—took me as an intimate friend, just as He took Abraham as an intimate friend. My station and Abraham’s station in Paradise on the Day of Resurrection will face one another, and al-ʿAbbās is between us, a believer between two intimate friends.”

Al-Ḥumaydī related to us; he said: Anas ibn ʿIyāḍ related to us, from ʿUbayd Allāh, from— Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar: Al-ʿAbbās asked the Prophet ﷺ—for permission to spend the nights of Minā in Mecca because of his water-providing duties, and he gave him permission.

Qabīṣa related to us; he said: Sufyān related to us, from Mūsā ibn Abī ʿĀʾisha, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Razīn, from ʿAlī, who said: “I said to al-ʿAbbās: ‘Ask the Messenger of God ﷺ—to appoint us over the alms.’ He replied: ‘I would not appoint you over the refuse of people’s sins.’

“I said to al-ʿAbbās: ‘Ask the Messenger of God ﷺ—for the custodianship of the Kaʿba.’ He replied: ‘I will give you something better than that: providing water, with which you quench people’s thirst. Do not think little of it.’”

Ibn Abī Uways related to us; he said: My father related to me; he said: Muḥammad ibn Muslim informed me that ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith related to him, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ—said: “Alms are not fitting for the family of Muḥammad; they are only the people’s impurities.”

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Mubārak related to us; he said: Sufyān ibn Ḥabīb related to us; he said:

Shuʿba related to us, from ʿAmr ibn Murra, from Dhakwān Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Ṣuhayb, the client of al-ʿAbbās, who said: “I saw ʿAlī kissing al-ʿAbbās’s hand and saying: ‘Uncle, be pleased with me.’”

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rajāʾ related to us, from Isrāʾīl, from Simāk, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Prophet ﷺ—said, when he had finished at Badr: “Go after the caravan; nothing stands between you and it.”

Al-ʿAbbās called out to him: “That is not right for you.”

He said: “Why?”

He replied: “Because God—Mighty and Glorious—has promised you one of the two groups, and—”

“God—Mighty and Glorious—has granted you what He promised.”

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā related to us; he said: Hushaym related to us, from Abū Bishr, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: “I had mastered the definitive passages during the lifetime of the Messenger of God ﷺ.”

I asked: “What are the definitive passages?”

He replied: “The detailed passages.”

The Messenger of God ﷺ—died when I was ten years old.

Al-Rabīʿ ibn Yaḥyā related to us; he said: Shuʿba related to us, from Abū Bishr, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: “The Messenger of God ﷺ—died when I had read the definitive passages of the Qurʾān, and I was ten years old—and I had been circumcised.”

Saʿīd was asked: “What are the definitive passages of the Qurʾān?”

He replied: “The detailed passages.”

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Muʿādh related to us; he said: My father related to us; he said: Shuʿba related to us, from Abū Isḥāq al-Sabīʿī [from] Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās: “The Messenger of God ﷺ—died when I was fifteen years old.”

Aḥmad ibn Manīʿ related to us; he said: Hushaym related to us; he said: Abū Bishr informed us, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: “ʿUmar used to admit the people of Badr, and he admitted me along with them. Some of them said: ‘Will you admit this youth when we have sons just like him?’”

He said: “There is something in him that you know.” Then one day he admitted them and admitted me with them. He asked them about this sūra: “When God’s help and victory come, and you see the people entering God’s religion in throngs” (Qurʾān 110:1–2). They replied: “God—Mighty and Glorious—commanded His Prophet ﷺ—when God—Mighty and Glorious—had given him victory—”

“—to seek forgiveness and accept his repentance.”

He said to me: “What do you say, Ibn ʿAbbās?”

I replied: “That is not so. Rather, He informed His Prophet ﷺ—that his appointed time was near. ‘When God’s help and victory come’ (Qurʾān 110:1)—that is, the conquest of Mecca—‘and you see the people entering God’s religion in throngs’ (Qurʾān 110:2): that is, at that point, the sign of your death. ‘Then glorify your Lord with praise and ask His forgiveness; indeed, He is ever accepting of repentance’ (Qurʾān 110:3).”

He said to them: “How can you blame me for it after you have seen what you see?”

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us; he said: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, from Ayyūb, from ʿIkrima, that ʿAlī was brought a group of heretics or apostates. He ordered them to be burned, and they were burned. This reached Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: “Had it been me, I would have killed them, in accordance with the statement of the Messenger of God ﷺ—and I would not have burned them, because of the Messenger of God’s prohibition. The Messenger of God ﷺ—said: ‘Whoever changes his religion, kill him.’ And he said: ‘Do not punish with the punishment of God—Mighty and Glorious is He.’”

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us, and Jarīr informed us, from Ayyūb, with a similar report. He added: Ibn ʿAbbās’s words reached ʿAlī, who said: “Alas for Ibn Umm al-Faḍl! He is indeed a diver into hidden matters.”

ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Shaqīq related to us; he said: ʿAbd Allāh informed us; he said: Maʿmar informed us, from ʿAlī ibn Badīma al-Jazarī, who related to him, from Yazīd ibn al-Aṣamm, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: A man came to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, and ʿUmar began asking him about the people.

He said: “Commander of the Faithful, among them are such-and-such people who have recited the Qurʾān.”

Ibn ʿAbbās said: “By God, I would not like them to rush into the Qurʾān in this way today.”

ʿUmar rebuked me— Then he said, “Enough!” I went home, dejected and sad. I said, “I had attained such a standing with this man that I thought I had fallen from his favor.”

He said: I returned home and lay down on my bed until the women of my household came to visit me, though I was not ill. It was only what ʿUmar had said to me that had affected me. While I was in that state, a man came to me and said, “Answer the Commander of the Faithful.” I went out, and there he was, standing nearby and waiting for me. He took my hand, then drew me aside and said, “What did you object to in what the man said?”

I said, “Commander of the Faithful, if I did wrong, I ask God Almighty and Majestic to forgive me and I repent to Him; so let me settle wherever you wish.” He said, “You must tell me what you objected to in what the man said.”

I said, “Commander of the Faithful, whenever they hasten in this way, they will incline away from the right course; whenever they incline away, they will disagree; and whenever they disagree, they will fail.” He said, “May your father be blessed! By God, I had been keeping this from people until you came and said it.”

Al-Ḥumaydī related to us: Sufyān related to us: Sālim related to me, from Mundhir, who said: When Ibn ʿAbbās died, Ibn al-Ḥanafiyyah said, “Today the learned man of this community has died.”

Ḥassān, Ibn Qaʿnab, and Ibn Bukayr related to us, from Mālik, from Ibn Shihāb, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtbah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ—led us in prayer. Ibn Bukayr’s version of the report says, “with no wall in front of him.” I went to a donkey of mine, as I was nearing puberty—in another version, “I was nearing the age of puberty”—and passed in front of part of the rows. Then I dismounted, let the female donkey graze, and entered the row.

No one reproached me for that.

Al-Ḥumaydī related to us: Sufyān related to us: I memorized it from al-Zuhrī, who related it to us from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtbah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: “Al-Faḍl and I came on a female donkey.” Ibn al-Mubārak said, from Maʿmar: “Al-Faḍl and I came riding one behind the other.”

Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr related to us: Hushaym related to us: Abū Ḥamzah ʿImrān ibn Abī ʿAṭāʾ al-Qaṣṣāb informed us. He said: I witnessed Ibn ʿAbbās’s death at al-Ṭāʾif. Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥanafiyyah took charge of him and pronounced four takbīrs over him.

Abū Nuʿaym said: Ibn ʿAbbās died in the year sixty-eight.

Hudayyah ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb al-Marwazī al-Kittānī related to us: al-Faḍl ibn Mūsā related to us: Muḥammad ibn ʿAṭāʾ related to us, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ—seated me close beside him, stroked my head, placed his hand on my chest, and said:

“O God, grant him understanding of religion and teach him interpretation.”

Mūsā ibn Ismāʿīl related to us: Wuhayb related to us, from Khālid, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ—embraced me and said:

“O God, teach him wisdom.”

Abū Bishr related to us: ʿAbd al-Wahhāb related to us, from Khālid, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, with a similar report. Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shaybah and Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥīm related to us, saying: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bukayr related to us, from Ḥātim ibn Abī Ṣaghīrah, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, that Kurayb informed him, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ—who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ—prayed that God Almighty and Majestic increase my understanding and knowledge.

Sufyān ibn Wakīʿ related to us, from Ibn ʿUyaynah, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from Kurayb, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ—prayed that God increase my knowledge and understanding.

Aḥmad ibn Manīʿ related to me: Abū Aḥmad al-Zubayrī related to us: Sufyān related to us, from Layth, from Abū al-Jahḍam, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ—prayed for me twice, and I saw Gabriel twice.

Al-Ḥasan ibn al-Rabīʿ informed us: Ibn Idrīs related to us, from ʿĀṣim ibn Kulayb, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: ʿUmar used to summon me along with the elder Companions of Muḥammad, and some of them felt resentment about that. He used to tell me not to speak until they had spoken. He summoned me while they were with him and said, “You know what the Messenger of God ﷺ—said about the Night of Decree: ‘Seek it during the last ten nights, on an odd-numbered night.’ Which of those ten nights do you think it is?” They mentioned every odd-numbered night among the ten. Then he said to me, “Why are you not speaking, Ibn ʿAbbās?” I said:

“If you wish, I will speak.” He said, “I summoned you only so that you would speak.” I said, “I would be speaking from my own opinion.”

He said, “I am asking you for your opinion.” I said: “I heard God Almighty and Majestic mention the number seven more often in the Qurʾān.” He said: “Then he counted the heavens and the earth, the circuits around the Kaʿbah, and all sorts of things that I know, until he said, ‘and He made what is between the earth seven.’”25

Yūsuf ibn Kāmil related to us: ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn Ziyād related to us: ʿĀṣim ibn Kulayb related to us: My father related to me, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: When ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb summoned the elder Companions of Muḥammad ﷺ—he summoned me with them and said, “Do not speak until they have spoken.” One day—or, he said, one night—he summoned me and said: “The Messenger of God ﷺ—said about the Night of Decree what you know: ‘Seek it during the last ten nights, on an odd-numbered night.’ Which odd-numbered night do you think it is?” Some of them said, “The ninth, the seventh, the fifth, or the third.” Then he said to me, “Ibn ʿAbbās, why are you not speaking?” I said, “If you wish, I will speak.” He said, “I summoned you only so that you would speak.” I said:

“Shall I speak about it from my own opinion?” He said, “I am asking you for your opinion.” I said: “I heard God Almighty and Majestic mention the number seven more often.” Then I said, “The heavens are seven, and the earths are seven,” until I recited: “Then We split the earth open, and caused grain to grow in it, and grapes and green fodder, and olive trees and date palms, and densely planted gardens, and fruits and herbage” (80:26–31). Every densely planted place is a garden, and every garden is densely planted; al-abb is what the earth grows that people do not eat. ʿUmar said, “Were you unable to say something like what this boy said, whose hair has not yet filled out?” Then he said, “I had forbidden you to speak; but when I summon you with them, speak.”

Yaḥyā ibn26 related to us: ʿAbd al-Jabbār ibn al-Ward al-Makkī related to us: I heard ʿAṭāʾ say: I have never seen an assembly more honorable than Ibn ʿAbbās’s, greater in learning and more generous in its hospitality. The people of the Qurʾān would be with him, asking him questions; the people of poetry would be with him, asking him questions; and the people of grammar would be with him, asking him questions. Each would leave with ample room to pursue his own field.

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us: Ḥammād related to us, from Ayyūb, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: I spent the night in the house of my aunt Maymūnah. The Messenger of God ﷺ—got up to pray during the night. I came and stood to his left, but he moved me to his right. He prayed, then slept until I heard him breathe heavily. Then he went out to pray. Ayyūb said:

I was told that he prayed for him that night: “O God, [grant him] wisdom”—or he said, “O God, increase him in knowledge.”

Al-Ḥajjāj related to us: Ḥammād related to us: ʿAmmār ibn Abī ʿAmmār related to us, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: I was with my father in the presence of the Prophet ﷺ—and a man was speaking privately with the Prophet. He seemed to be turning away from my father. We left him, and my father said, “Did you see how your cousin seemed to turn away from me?” I said to him, “Father, there was a man speaking privately with him.” He said, “Was anyone with him?” I said, “Yes.” So we returned. My father said, “Messenger of God, I said such-and-such to ʿAbd Allāh, and he replied to me such-and-such. Was anyone with you?” He said, “Did you see him, ʿAbd Allāh?” I said, “Yes.” He said, “That was Gabriel; he was the one who kept me from you.”

Al-Ḥumaydī and Ibn Abī ʿUmar related to me, saying: Sufyān related to us: ʿĀṣim ibn Kulayb related to us: My father informed me that he heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: When ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb had performed a prayer, he would sit with the people, and anyone who had a need would speak to him. If no one had a need, he would get up, go inside, and perform several prayers, during which he would not sit with the people. Ibn ʿAbbās said: I came to the door and said, “Yarfaʾ, has some illness befallen the Commander of the Faithful?” He said, “The Commander of the Faithful has no illness.” So I sat down. ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān came and sat down. Yarfaʾ came out and said, “Get up, Ibn ʿAffān; get up, Ibn ʿAbbās.” We entered to see ʿUmar, and before him were piles of wealth, with a kirfah on each pile.27 ʿUmar said, “I looked among the people of Medina and found that the two of you have among the largest clans there. Take this wealth and divide it; whatever remains, return it.” He said: As for As for ʿUthmān, he scooped up [the money]. As for me, I crawled on my knees and said, “Even if there is a shortfall, you would make us repay it.” ʿUmar said, “A familiar trait—I know it from Akhshan”—Sufyān said, “meaning a stone from a mountain”—“Was this not with God while Muḥammad and his Companions were eating qadd?” I said:

“Indeed, by God, this was with God, mighty and majestic, while Muḥammad was alive. Had it been opened to him, he would have done with it something other than what you are doing.” ʿUmar grew angry and said, “Then what would he have done?” I said:

“Then he would have eaten and fed us.” ʿUmar sobbed until his ribs shifted, then said:

“I wish I had come out of it even, with neither liability nor claim.”

Mūsā ibn Masʿūd related to me: ʿIkrima ibn ʿAmmār related to us, from Simāk Abū Zumayl al-Duʾalī—who had been partial to Najda—who said: Ibn ʿAbbās said: When the Khārijites broke away, they adopted a position, and they were six thousand. They agreed to rise against ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, with the Prophet’s Companions alongside him. He said: A man would keep coming and saying, “Commander of the Faithful, the people are going out against you”—meaning ʿAlī. He would say, “Leave them. I will not fight them until they fight me, and they will do so.”

One day, before the noon prayer, I came to him and said, “Commander of the Faithful, let us wait until it is cooler for the prayer, so that perhaps I may go in among these people and speak with them.” He said, “I fear they may harm you.” I said, “No indeed,” for I was a man of good character who harmed no one. He gave me permission, so I put on one of the finest Yemeni robes, combed my hair, and went in among them at midday. I entered among people more assiduous in worship than any I had ever seen: their foreheads were sore from prostration, their hands were like camel knees, and they wore freshly washed tunics, with their sleeves rolled up. Their faces were worn from staying awake. I greeted them.

They said, “Welcome, Ibn ʿAbbās. What brings you here?” I said, “I have come to you from the Emigrants and the Helpers, and from the son-in-law of the Messenger of God ﷺ. The Qurʾān was sent down upon them, and they know its interpretation best.” A group among them said, “Do not argue with Quraysh, for God has said, ‘Rather, they are a contentious people’ (43:58).” Two or three said, “If only you would speak with them”. I said to them, “Tell me what you object to in the son-in-law of the Messenger of God ﷺ and in the Emigrants and Helpers, upon whom the Qurʾān was sent down, when not one of them is among you and they know its interpretation better than you.” They said, “Three things.” I asked, “What are they?” They said, “The first is that he appointed men to arbitrate in God’s matter, mighty and majestic, when God, mighty and majestic, has said, ‘Judgment belongs to none but God’ (6:57). What place can men and their judgment have after God, mighty and majestic, has spoken?” I said:

“That is one. What is the next?” They said, “The second is that he fought but took no captives and seized no booty. If they were believers, then fighting them and taking them captive was not lawful for us. And what is the third?” They said, “He erased his own designation as Commander of the Faithful. If he is not Commander of the Faithful, then he is surely commander of the unbelievers.” I said:

“Do you have anything besides this?” They said, “This is enough for us.” I said to them, “As for your claim that he appointed men to arbitrate in God’s matter, mighty and majestic, I will recite to you from the Book of God, mighty and majestic, something that refutes your claim. Will you then reconsider?” They said, “Yes.” I said, “God, mighty and majestic, has referred a judgment to men over a quarter of a dirham—the price of a hare—and recited this verse: ‘Do not kill game while you are in a state of consecration’ (5:95), through to the end of the verse; and concerning a woman and her husband: ‘If you fear a breach between the two, appoint an arbiter from his family and an arbiter from her family’ (4:35), through to the end of the verse. I adjure you by God: do you consider men’s judgment to reconcile people and spare their blood better, or their judgment concerning a hare and a woman’s intimacy?” from among you. So which of the two do you consider better?” They said, “Rather, this one.”

He asked, “Have I answered this objection?” They said, “Yes.” I said, “As for your claim that he fought but took no captives and seized no booty: would you then take your mother ʿĀʾisha captive? By God, if you say, ‘She is not our mother,’ you have left Islam; and by God, if you say, ‘We would take her captive and deem lawful with her what we deem lawful with other women,’ you have left Islam. You are caught between two errors. God, mighty and majestic, has said, ‘The Prophet has greater claim on the believers than they have on themselves, and his wives are their mothers’ (33:6). If you say, ‘She is not our mother,’ you have left Islam. Have I answered this objection?” They said, “Yes.”

“As for your claim that he erased his own designation as Commander of the Faithful, I will bring you an example you will accept: the day of al-Ḥudaybiya. The idolaters’ scribes were Abū Sufyān ibn Ḥarb and Suhayl ibn ʿAmr. He said, ‘ʿAlī, write: “This is what Muḥammad, the Messenger of God ﷺ has agreed to.”’ The idolaters said, ‘By God, if we knew that you were the Messenger of God ﷺ we would not have fought you.’ The Messenger of God ﷺ said, ‘O God, You know that I am Your Messenger. Erase it, ʿAlī, and write: “This is what Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh has agreed to.”’ By God, the Messenger of God ﷺ is better than ʿAlī, yet he erased his own designation.” He said: Two thousand of them turned back, and the rest went out and were killed.

Aḥmad ibn Yūnus related to us: al-Muʿāfā ibn ʿImrān al-Mawṣilī related to us:

Idrīs ibn Sinān—or Ilyās, the son of Wahb’s daughter—related to us: Wahb ibn Munabbih related to me that Ibn ʿAbbās performed seven circuits around the House in the morning. Wahb said: Ṭāwūs and I were with him, along with his freedman ʿIkrima. His eyesight had grown weak, and he leaned on a staff. When he finished his circumambulation, he turned toward al-Ḥaṭīm and prayed two units. Then he rose, and we rose with him. He handed his staff to his freedman ʿIkrima and leaned on me and on Ṭāwūs. Then he set off with us toward the western side of the Kaʿba, between the gate of Banū Sahm and the gate of Banū Jumāḥ. We stopped beside a group of people whom Ibn ʿAbbās had heard were discussing predestination and other matters over which people disagree. When he stood before them, he greeted them. They returned his greeting, welcomed him, and made room for him, but he did not wish to sit with them. Then he said:

“O company who debate matters that do not concern them and bring them no benefit, do you not know that God, mighty and majestic, has servants whom fear of Him has made silent, though they are neither inarticulate nor mute? They are eloquent speakers, noble, intelligent, and learned in God, mighty and majestic, and His signs. But when they recall the majesty of God, mighty and majestic, their tongues fall silent, their hearts are overcome, and their minds are bewildered, out of reverence for God, mighty and majestic, and in exaltation and veneration of Him. When they recover from this, they hasten to God, mighty and majestic, with pure deeds. They count themselves among the wrongdoers and sinners, though they are indeed pure and righteous; or among those who fall short and are remiss, though they are indeed intelligent and strong. They are not satisfied with little for God, mighty and majestic, nor do they regard much as great enough for Him, and they do not flaunt their deeds before Him. Whenever you meet them, you will find them troubled, apprehensive, alarmed, fearful, anxious, and deeply concerned. Where are you in relation to them, O company of innovators? Know that those most knowledgeable about predestination are the ones most silent about it, and that those most ignorant about predestination are the ones most vocal about it.”

Wahb said: Then he turned away from them and left them. Ibn ʿAbbās learned that they had dispersed from that gathering and did not return to it until Ibn ʿAbbās died.

ʿAbd al-Aʿlā ibn Ḥammād ibn Naṣr al-Nursī related to us: Hārūn ibn ʿAbd al-Wāḥid Abū al-Ḥakam related to us, from Mūsā ibn Abī Darm, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: Ibn ʿAbbās was told of a gathering in the Sacred Mosque, near the gate of Banū Sahm, where some men of Quraysh would sit and argue, raising their voices.

Ibn ʿAbbās said, “Let us go to them.” We went until we stood beside them. Ibn ʿAbbās said, “Tell them what the young man said to Job when he was in his affliction.” The young man said, “Job, was the majesty of God, mighty and majestic, and the remembrance of death not enough to weary your tongue, break your heart, and cut short your argument? Job, did you not know that God, mighty and majestic, has servants whom fear of God, mighty and majestic, has made silent, though they are neither inarticulate nor mute? They are eloquent speakers, intelligent, free-spoken, and learned in God, mighty and majestic, and His signs. But when they recall the majesty of God, mighty and majestic, their hearts are torn, their tongues grow weary, and their minds and wits are bewildered. When they recover from this, they hasten to God, mighty and majestic, with pure deeds. They do not regard much as too great for God, mighty and majestic, nor are they satisfied with little for Him. They count themselves among the wrongdoers and sinners, though they are indeed pure and righteous; and among those who neglect their duties and fall short, though they are indeed intelligent, strong, lean, and tireless. The ignorant see them and say, ‘They must be ill to lie down.’ A grave matter has affected these people.”

Marwān said: A man wrote to me that, following Wahb’s speech, Ibn ʿAbbās said, “It is enough to make you a wrongdoer that you are always arguing, enough to make you a sinner that you are always disputing, and enough to make you a liar that you are always speaking about something other than God, mighty and majestic.”

Abū ʿĀṣim al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Makhlad and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ḥammād al-Shuʿaythī related to us, from Kahmas ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Burayda, who said: A man reviled Ibn ʿAbbās.

He said, “You revile me on account of three things. When I come upon a verse from the Book of God, mighty and majestic, I wish that all people knew of it what I know. When I hear of a judge among the Muslim judges who rules justly, I rejoice, though I may never have a case brought before him. And when I hear of rain falling on land in the lands of the Muslims, I rejoice, though I have no grazing livestock there.”

Among them were some men of Quraysh arguing, their voices rising. Ibn ʿAbbās said, “Come with me to them.” We went until we stood before them. Ibn ʿAbbās said, “Tell them what the young man said to Job while he was in his affliction.” The young man said, “O Job, was there not in the majesty of God—mighty and exalted is He—and in the remembrance of death enough to weary your tongue, break your heart, and cut off your argument? O Job, did you not know that God—mighty and exalted is He—has servants whom fear of God—mighty and exalted is He—has made silent, though they are neither incapacitated nor mute? They are eloquent speakers, articulate, intelligent, fluent, and learned in God—mighty and exalted is He—and His signs. Yet when they remember the majesty of God—mighty and exalted is He—their hearts are torn, their tongues falter, and their minds and understanding are bewildered. When they recover from that, they hasten to God—mighty and exalted is He—with pure deeds. They do not consider much to be too much for God—mighty and exalted is He, nor are they content with little for Him. They count themselves among the wrongdoers and sinners, though they are surely pure and righteous; and among those who have neglected their duties and fallen short, though they are surely discerning and strong: emaciated, ever striving. The ignorant person sees them and says, ‘They have lain down from illness’; some grave affair has overtaken these people.” Marwān said: A man wrote to me that, following Wahb’s words, Ibn ʿAbbās said, “It is enough to make you a wrongdoer that you are always disputing, and enough to make you a sinner that you are always wrangling; and enough to make you a liar that you are always speaking about something other than God—mighty and exalted is He.”

Abū ʿĀṣim al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Makhlad and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ḥammād al-Shuʿaythī related to us, from Kahmas ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Buraydah, who said: A man reviled Ibn ʿAbbās.

He said, “You revile me on account of three qualities: When I come upon a verse from the Book of God—mighty and exalted is He—I wish that all people knew of it what I know. When I hear of a judge among the judges of the Muslims who rules justly, I rejoice, though I may never have a case brought before him. And when I hear that rain has fallen on land belonging to the Muslims, I rejoice, though I have no grazing livestock there.”

Abū al-Nuʿmān related to us: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, from al-Zubayr ibn Khurayt, from ʿIkrimah, who said: “Ibn ʿAbbās was the more knowledgeable of the two in the Qurʾān, while ʿAlī was the more knowledgeable of the two in the ambiguous passages.”

Yaḥyā ibn Yaḥyā related to us: al-Muʿtamir ibn Sulaymān related to us: I heard my father relate, from Ṭāwūs, who said: “We were with Ibn ʿAbbās”—Saʿīd ibn Jubayr was writing—“when someone said to Ibn ʿAbbās, ‘They are writing.’ He said, ‘Are they writing?!’ Then he stood up. He was good-natured; were it not for his good nature, he would have expressed his disapproval more forcefully than by standing up.”

[Abū al-Nuʿmān and Yaḥyā ibn Yaḥyā related to us, from Ḥammād ibn Zayd, from al-Zubayr ibn Khurayt, from ʿIkrimah, who said: “Ibn ʿAbbās would put a fetter on my leg while I was learning the Qurʾān and jurisprudence.” Abū al-Nuʿmān said: “While I was learning the Qurʾān and the Sunna.”]

Yūsuf ibn ʿAdī related to me: ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUmar related to us, from Zayd ibn Abī Unaysah, from al-Minḥāl ibn ʿAmr, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās. Saʿīd said: “A man came and said, ‘I find things in the Qurʾān that seem to differ to me, and this has troubled my heart.’ Ibn ʿAbbās said, ‘Is it disbelief?’ He replied, ‘It is not disbelief, but apparent difference.’ He said, ‘Then bring forward what has troubled you.’ The man said to him:

“‘I hear God—mighty and majestic—say, “On that day there will be no ties of kinship between them, nor will they ask one another” (23:101); yet in another verse He says, “And they will turn to one another, questioning each other” (37:27); and in another verse—’”

“‘“And they will not conceal anything from God” (4:42); and in another verse He says, “By God, our Lord, we were not polytheists” (6:23)—so in this verse they concealed the truth. And in His words, “Or [consider] the heaven: He built it, raised its height and fashioned it; darkened its night and brought forth its brightness; and after that He spread out the earth” (79:27–30), He mentioned the creation of heaven before the earth. Then, in another verse, He says, “Do you indeed disbelieve in Him who created the earth in two days, and set up equals to Him? That is the Lord of the worlds” (41:9). And He says, “And He determined its provisions therein in four days, equally for those who ask,” (41:10) up to the end of the verse, “willingly” (41:11). Thus, in this verse He mentioned the creation of the earth before heaven. And His words, “God is ever Forgiving, Merciful” (4:96); “God is ever Mighty, Wise” (4:158); and “God is ever Hearing, Seeing” (4:134)—does this mean that He was so, and then ceased to be so?’”

Ibn ʿAbbās said: “Bring forward what has troubled your mind about this.” The questioner said, “If you explain this to me, that will suffice.” Ibn ʿAbbās said: “His words, ‘On that day there will be no ties of kinship between them, nor will they ask one another’ (23:101): this is at the first blast, when it is blown into the Trumpet and ‘all who are in the heavens and all who are on earth will fall dead, except those whom God wills’ (39:68). At that time there will be no ties of kinship between them, nor will they ask one another. Then, when the second blast comes, they will rise, and they will turn to one another, questioning each other.

“As for His words—mighty and majestic—‘By God, our Lord, we were not polytheists’ (6:23), and His words—mighty and majestic—‘They will not conceal anything from God’ (4:42), God—mighty and majestic—will forgive the sins of those who are sincere in their faith on the Day of Resurrection—”

“—their sins; no sin is too great for Him to forgive, but He does not forgive polytheism. When the polytheists saw this, they said, ‘Our Lord forgives sins but does not forgive polytheism. Come, then, let us say that we were only sinners, not polytheists.’ So God—mighty and majestic—said, ‘If you conceal polytheism, then let their mouths be sealed.’ Their mouths will be sealed, their hands will speak, and their feet will testify to what they used to do.” “At that, the polytheists will realize that nothing can be concealed from God—mighty and majestic. This is the point of His words—mighty and majestic—‘On that day those who disbelieved and disobeyed the Messenger will wish that the earth were leveled over them, and they will not conceal anything from God’ (4:42).

“As for His words, ‘He built the heaven, raised its height and fashioned it; darkened its night and brought forth its brightness; and after that He spread out the earth’ (79:27–30): He created the earth in two days before heaven. Then He turned to heaven and fashioned them in two further days. Then He descended to the earth and spread it out. Spreading it out means that He brought forth from it water and pasture, cut rivers through it, made roads, and created mountains, sands, mounds, and what lies between them, in two further days. This is the meaning of His words, ‘And after that He spread out the earth’ (79:30), and His words, ‘Do you indeed disbelieve in Him who created the earth in two days, and set up equals to Him? That is the Lord of the worlds. He placed firm mountains upon it, blessed it, and determined its provisions therein in four days, equally for those who ask’ (41:9–10). Thus, He made the earth and everything in it in four days, and made the heavens in two days.

“As for His words, ‘God is ever Forgiving, Merciful’ (4:96); ‘God is ever Mighty, Wise’ (4:158); and ‘God is ever Hearing, Seeing’ (4:134), God—mighty and majestic—made Himself so; He named Himself so, and no one else made Him so. That is the meaning of ‘God is ever’ (4:17): He has always been so.”

Ibn ʿAbbās said to the man: “Remember what I have told you, and know that whatever seems to differ to you in the Qurʾān is like the examples I have told you. God—mighty and majestic—has left nothing without giving it the intended meaning, but people do not know. So let the Qurʾān not seem to differ to you, for all of it is from God—mighty and majestic.”

Yūsuf ibn Mihrān related to me, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: “Caesar wrote to Muʿāwiyah ibn Abī Sufyān: ‘Peace be upon you. To proceed: Tell me the word dearest to God—mighty and majestic—then the second, third, fourth, and fifth dearest words; the most honored of His male servants and the most honored of His female servants; four things that contain a spirit but did not move in a womb; a grave that travels with its occupant; a place the sun shone upon only once; the Milky Way—what is its place in the sky?—and the rainbow, and how it first came to be.’ When he read the letter, he said, ‘God, curse him! How should I know what this is?’”

He said: “Then he sent for me to ask me about it. I said: ‘As for the word dearest to God—mighty and majestic—it is “There is no god but God”; no deed is accepted except through it. The second is the greeting, “Glory be to God,” and the creatures’ prayer. The third is “Praise be to God,” the word of thanksgiving. The fourth is “God is greatest,” the opening words of prayer, and [the words of] bowing and prostration. The fifth is “There is no might nor power except through God.” Write this to him, for they will understand.

“‘When a servant says “There is no god but God,” God—mighty and majestic—says, “My servant has made his faith sincere.” When he says “Glory be to God,” He says, “My servant has declared Me holy.” When he says “Praise be to God,” He says, “My servant has thanked Me.” When he says “God is greatest,” He says, “My servant has spoken the truth: I am the greatest.” When he says “There is no might nor power except through God,” He says, “My servant has surrendered himself to Me.”

“‘As for the most honored of His male servants, it is Adam, whom He created with His own hand and taught all the names. As for the most honored of His female servants, it is Mary, daughter of ʿImrān, who guarded her chastity. As for the four that contain a spirit but did not move in a womb, they are Adam and Eve; Moses’ staff, when he cast it down and it became a manifest serpent; and the ram that was sacrificed in place of Ishmael. As for the place the sun shone upon only once, it is the sea when it parted for the Children of Israel. As for the grave that travels with its occupant, it is the belly of the fish in which Jonah was.’” As for the Milky Way, it is a gate among the gates of— “—heaven. As for the rainbow, it is a safeguard against drowning, granted after the people of Noah.” When Caesar read his letter, he said: “By God, I did not know these things, and you could have learned them only from a man of the Prophet’s household.”

ʿAbd al-Wahhāb ibn al-Ḍaḥḥāk related to us: ʿĪsā ibn Yūnus related to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Shaqīq ibn Salamah, who said: “When al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib was killed, ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr rose up and called upon Ibn ʿAbbās to pledge allegiance to him. Ibn ʿAbbās refused. Yazīd ibn Muʿāwiyah thought that Ibn ʿAbbās’s refusal meant he was holding fast to his pledge of allegiance to Yazīd, so he wrote to him:

“‘To proceed: I have heard that the heretic Ibn al-Zubayr called you to pledge allegiance to him and enter his obedience, so that you might support him in falsehood and share in his sins; and that you held fast to your pledge to us, out of loyalty to us and obedience to God—mighty and majestic—because He has made you aware of our rightful claim. May God reward you, as a kinsman, with the best reward He grants to those who maintain their kinship ties and fulfill their covenants. Whatever else I may forget, I shall not forget your kindness and the promptness of your support, to which you are entitled by your kinship with the Messenger. So look for whoever comes to you from the regions, among those whom Ibn al-Zubayr has bewitched with his tongue and ornate speech, and inform them of your view. They will listen to you more and obey you more readily than they will the vile, criminal renegade.’

“Ibn ʿAbbās wrote back to him:

“‘To proceed: Your letter has reached me. You mention Ibn al-Zubayr’s calling me to pledge allegiance to him and enter his obedience. If that is indeed so, then, by God, I do not hope by it to earn your kindness or praise. God—mighty and majestic—knows what I intend by it. You claim that you have not forgotten my kindness and the promptness of your support. O man, keep your kindness and the promptness of your support, for I am withholding my affection from you. By my life, you give us only a little of the right we are owed from you, while you withhold a great deal of it. You have asked me to urge people to support you and turn them away from Ibn al-Zubayr. No: I will do so neither gladly nor willingly. You ask for my support and urge me to love you, yet you have killed al-Ḥusayn ﵁—and the young men of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, the beacons of guidance and stars of distinction. Your cavalry left them—’”

“‘—at your command, on one stretch of ground, wrapped in blood and stripped bare in the open, neither provided for nor laid on pillows. The winds blew dust over them, and the lame hyenas came upon them, until God—mighty and majestic—made a people available to them who had no part in their bloodshed; they shrouded and buried them. By God, you deceived me and them, and took the seat you now occupy. Whatever else I may forget, I shall not forget your driving al-Ḥusayn ﵁—from the sanctuary of the Messenger of God ﷺ—to the sanctuary of God—mighty and majestic—and your sending men against him to kill him in the Sanctuary. You persisted in this and continued in it until you drove him from Mecca to Iraq. He set out afraid and watchful, while your cavalry pressed upon him, out of enmity toward God—mighty and majestic—His Messenger, and his household, from whom God has removed defilement and whom He has purified completely. Those men are unlike your coarse, barefoot forefathers, with the livers of donkeys.

“‘He asked you for a truce and requested that you let him return, but you seized the opportunity presented by his few supporters and the annihilation of his household. You joined forces against him as though you had killed a household of Turks. Nothing astonishes me more than your seeking my affection when you have killed my two sons, while your sword drips with my blood and you are taking your revenge upon me. God willing, my blood will not go unavenged by you, nor will you get my revenge before I do. Even if you precede me in this world, prophets were killed before that, and God—mighty and majestic—will seek justice for their blood. God—mighty and majestic—is sufficient as a helper for the oppressed and an avenger against the wrongdoers. So let it not delight you if you prevail over us today: we shall prevail over you one day.

“‘You mentioned my loyalty and what you have made me aware of concerning your rightful claim. If that is indeed so, then by God I pledged allegiance to you and to those before you. You know that my father and my father’s son [i.e., my brother] have a greater right to this authority than you do. Yet you, Quraysh, outnumbered us until you deprived us of our right and took authority for yourselves without us. Destruction be upon whoever dares to do wrong and leads the foolish astray against us, just as Thamūd, the people of Lot, and the people of Midian were destroyed.

“‘Indeed, among the most astonishing of astonishing things—and what could be more astonishing?—is your bringing the daughters of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib and the young children of his descendants to you in Syria like captives brought in, to show people that you—’”

“‘—have conquered us and that you are doing us a favor, when it is through us that God—mighty and majestic—has favored you. By God, if you should wake secure from a wound dealt by my hand, I hope that God—mighty and majestic—will make the wound dealt by my tongue, my breaking of your case, and my undoing of it severe. By God, after you killed the descendant of the Messenger of God ﷺ—I do not despair that He will seize you with a painful seizure and take you from this world disgraced and cast down. Live on, you wretch, as long as you can. By God, your sins before God have multiplied many times over, and you have committed a grave offense. Peace be upon whoever follows the guidance.’”

Aḥmad ibn Saʿīd related to me: Wahb ibn Jarīr related to us: my father related to us: I heard Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq relate, from ʿUthmān ibn Abī Sulaymān ibn Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim, from Nāfiʿ ibn Jubayr, who said: “I heard Ibn al-Zubayr address the people in Mecca, saying, ‘Here is a man whose heart God—mighty and majestic—has blinded just as He blinded his sight; he gives people legal opinions permitting temporary marriage. By God, if a man who has done it is brought to me, I shall stone the two of them.’ Ibn ʿAbbās thrust out his chest toward him and said, ‘You are talking nonsense. It was only Ibn Ṣafwān who ordered you to do this, when al-Juʿayd’s aunt was brought in, her belly reaching her mouth and her nose.’28 Ibn al-Zubayr fell silent. Nāfiʿ said: I related this report to ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, and he said, ‘By your life, Ibn ʿAbbās truly was an Arab.’”

Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr related to us: Sufyān related to us, from ʿAbd al-Karīm al-Jazarī, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, who said: “I used to hear reports from Ibn ʿAbbās. Had he given me permission, I would have kissed his head.”

Abū al-Nuʿmān related to us: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, from Mujālid, from al-Shaʿbī, that al-ʿAbbās said to his son ʿAbd Allāh: “I see that this man”—meaning ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb—“has honored you, brought you close in the sitting place, and included you among people who are not your peers. So bear three things in mind—”

“—with regard to me: let him never discover you telling a lie; never disclose a secret to him; and never backbite anyone in his presence.”

[Abū Nuʿaym ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Hānīʾ al-Nakhaʿī related to us: ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Muʾammal related to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Mulayka, who said: Ibn ʿAbbās was asked, “Who is the most honored of people to you?” He replied, “The companion who pushes through the people to sit with me. If I could keep flies from landing on his face, I would.”]

Abū Nuʿaym related to us: he said: Ṣāliḥ ibn Rustum related to us, from Ibn Abī Mulayka, who said: “I accompanied Ibn ʿAbbās from Mecca to Medina—or from Medina to Mecca—and he would pray two cycles. When he stopped, he would rise for half the night and recite the Qurʾān in measured fashion, letter by letter. He did much glorifying of God and weeping during this, and he would recite: ‘The agony of death has come in truth: that is what you used to shun’ (50:19).”

ʿAlī ibn ʿUthmān ibn Nufayl related to us: Abū Mushir related to us: one of al-Awzāʿī’s companions, Walīd ibn Yazīd, related to me that he heard al-Awzāʿī say: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said to ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-ʿAbbās: “By God, you are the most handsome-faced of our young men, the soundest in judgment, and the most learned in the Book of God—mighty and majestic.”

[A narrator related to us, from Abū al-Mughīra ʿAbd al-Quddūs, from Ibn ʿAyyāsh, from someone who related to him, from Kaʿb, who said: “Black banners of the Banū al-ʿAbbās will appear until they reach Syria, and God—mighty and majestic—will, by their hands, destroy every tyrant and enemy of theirs.”]

Al-Ḥajjāj related to us; he said: Ḥammād related to us, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, who said: I heard ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-ʿAlāʾ al-Ḥaḍramī say: “Maʿn related to me that he heard the Prophet ﷺ—say: ‘At the end of this community there will be people who have a reward like that of its first members. They will enjoin what is right, forbid what is wrong, and fight the people of civil strife.’” [Muḥammad ibn Khālid ibn al-ʿAbbās related to me: al-Walīd related to us: Abū ʿAbd Allāh related to me, from al-Walīd ibn Hishām al-Muʿayṭī, from Abān ibn al-Walīd ibn ʿUqba ibn Abī Muʿayṭ, who said: “ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās came to Muʿāwiyah while I was present. He gave him a gift and gave him a generous one. Then he said, ‘Abū al-ʿAbbās, will you have a dynasty?’ He replied, ‘Excuse me, Commander of the Faithful.’ He said, ‘You must tell me.’ He replied, ‘Yes.’ He asked, ‘Who will be your supporters?’

“‘The people of Khurāsān. The Banū Umayya and the Banū Hāshim will have clashes.’”

Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz al-Ramlī related to us: al-Walīd ibn Muslim related to us, from ʿAlī ibn Ḥawshab, from Makḥūl, who said: “If you see a Hāshimī banner, do not oppose it, for its dynasty will be long.”

Ibrāhīm ibn Ayyūb al-Dimashqī related to me: al-Walīd related to us: Abū ʿAmr Ṣadaqa ibn ʿAmr al-Jumaḥī related to me, from a man of Dhū Yaman, from Dhū ʿIṣyān, that when Ibn Dāwūd ibn ʿAlī arrived in Mecca, he said to him: “Abū ʿAmr, by God, moving a mountain from its place is easier than removing a kingdom appointed for the Banū al-ʿAbbās.”

[Ibrāhīm ibn Ayyūb related to me; he said: al-Walīd related to us; he said: ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Ḥumayd ibn Abī Ghaniya related to us, from al-Minḥāl ibn ʿAmr, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, who said: “We heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās while we were saying, ‘Twelve rulers, then no ruler; and twelve rulers, then the Hour.’ Ibn ʿAbbās said, ‘How foolish you are! From among us, the People of the House, after that will come—’”

“‘—al-Manṣūr, al-Saffāḥ, and al-Mahdī; he will hand it over to Jesus son of Mary.’”

Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shayba and ʿAlī ibn al-Mundhir related to us; they said: Ibn Fuḍayl related to us, from Abū Ḥayyān, from Yazīd ibn Ḥayyān, who said: “Ḥuṣayn ibn ʿUqba and I went to Zayd ibn Arqam. Zayd said: ‘The Messenger of God ﷺ—stood up, praised and extolled God, and admonished us. Then he said: “To proceed, people: I await the messenger of my Lord, and I shall answer him. I am leaving among you the two weighty things. One of them is the Book of God—mighty and majestic—in which there is light and guidance. Hold fast to the Book of God—mighty and majestic.” He urged us concerning it, then said:

“‘“And my household: I remind you of God—mighty and majestic—concerning my household.”’ He said this three times. Yazīd and Ḥuṣayn asked him, ‘Who are the members of his household? Are his wives not among his household?’ He replied, ‘His wives are among his household, but his household are those for whom charity was forbidden after his death.’ Ḥuṣayn said:

“‘“Who are they, Yazīd?” He said, “They are the family of al-ʿAbbās, the family of ʿAlī, the family of Jaʿfar, and the family of ʿAqīl.”’

“Yaḥyā related to us: Jarīr related to us, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿUbayd Allāh, from Abū al-Ḍuḥā, from Zayd ibn Arqam, who said: The Prophet ﷺ—said: ‘I am leaving among you that which, if you hold fast to it, you will never go astray: the Book of God—mighty and majestic—and my descendants, the members of my household. The two will never part until they come to me at the Pond.’

“Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā related to me: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Sharīk related to us—”

He said: My father related to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit, from Abū al-Ṭufayl, from Zayd ibn Arqam, from the Prophet of God ﷺ—who said: “I have left among you the Two Weighty Things: the Book of God, Mighty and Glorious, a rope extended from heaven to earth, and my kindred, the people of my household. So consider how you will succeed me with regard to them both, for they will never part until they come to me at the Pool.”

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā related to us: Isrāʾīl informed us, from ʿUthmān ibn al-Mughīra, from ʿAlī ibn Rabīʿa, who said: I met Zayd ibn Arqam as he was about to enter upon al-Mukhtār. I said to him: “A report has reached me from you.” He asked: “What is it?” I said: “Did you hear the Prophet ﷺ—say: ‘I am leaving among you the Two Weighty Things: the Book of God, Mighty and Glorious, and my kindred’?”

He said: “Yes.”

ʿUbayd Allāh related to us: Fuḍayl ibn Marzūq informed us, from ʿAṭiyya, from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ—said: “I am leaving among you the Two Weighty Things, one of which is greater than the other: the Book of God, Mighty and Glorious, a rope extended from heaven to earth, one end in the hand of God, Mighty and Glorious, and one end in your hands. So hold fast to it. And behold, my kindred.” Fuḍayl said: I asked ʿAṭiyya about his kindred. He said: “The people of his household.”

ʿUbayd Allāh related to us: Sharīk informed us, from al-Rukayn, from Qāsim ibn Ḥassān, from Zayd ibn Thābit, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ—said: “I am leaving among you my successor: the Book of God, Mighty and Glorious, and my kindred, the people of my household. They will never part until they come to me at the Pool.”

ʿUbayd Allāh related to us: Abū Isrāʾīl related to us, from ʿAṭiyya, from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ—said: “I am leaving among you the Two Weighty Things, one of which is greater than the other: the Book of God, Mighty and Glorious, a rope joined from heaven to—” earth, and my kindred, the people of my household. They will never part until they come to me at the Pool.”

ʿUbayd Allāh related to us: Mūsā ibn ʿUbayda related to us, from Iyās ibn Salama ibn al-Akwaʿ, from his father, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ—said: “The stars are a safeguard for the people of heaven, and the people of my household are a safeguard for my community.”

Al-ʿAbbās ibn al-Walīd ibn Ṣāliḥ related to me: Isḥāq ibn Saʿīd, Abū Salama, related to us: Khulayḍ ibn Daʿlaj related to me, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ—said: “The bow is a safeguard for the earth against being inundated, and loyalty to Quraysh is a safeguard for the people of the earth against discord. When a tribe opposes them, they become a faction of Iblīs.”

Muslim ibn Ibrāhīm related to us: al-Ḥasan ibn Abī Jaʿfar related to us:

ʿAlī ibn Zayd related to us, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, from Abū Dharr, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ—said: “The likeness of the people of my household is the likeness of Noah’s Ark: whoever boards it is saved, and whoever stays behind from it is drowned. Whoever fights us at the end of time has only fought alongside the Antichrist.”

ʿUbayd Allāh related to us, from Isrāʾīl, from Abū Isḥāq, from a man who related to him, from Ḥanash, who said: I saw Abū Dharr holding the ring of the Kaʿba’s door and saying: “People, I am Abū Dharr. Whoever knows me—behold, I am Abū Dharr al-Ghifārī. I tell you only what I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ—say. I heard him say: ‘People, I have left among you the Two Weighty Things: the Book of God, Mighty and Glorious, and my kindred, the people of my household. One of them is superior to the other: the Book of God, Mighty and Glorious. They will never part until they come to me at the Pool. Their likeness is that of Noah’s Ark: whoever boards it is saved, and whoever leaves it is drowned.’”

ʿUbayd Allāh related to us, from Isrāʾīl, from Sālim, from Saʿīd, concerning His words, “Say: I ask of you no reward except affection for near kin” (42:23)— “—that you should maintain the kinship between me and you.”

ʿUbayd Allāh related to us: Isrāʾīl related to us, from Jābir, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from Abū Masʿūd, who said: “If I were to perform a prayer without invoking blessings upon the family of Muḥammad, I would consider that my prayer was not complete.”

Ibrāhīm ibn al-Mundhir related to us: Muḥammad ibn Ṣadaqa related to me: “Ibn Abī al-Zinād, from Hishām ibn ʿUrwa, said: I asked my father about ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās and his learning. He said: ‘I have never seen anyone like Ibn ʿAbbās.’”

Al-Ḥajjāj related to us: Ḥammād related to us, from Yaʿlā ibn ʿAṭāʾ, from Bujayr, Abū ʿAbd Allāh, who said: When Ibn ʿAbbās’s bier was carried, a great bird came and mingled with his shrouds.

Saʿīd ibn Abī Maryam related to me: Nāfiʿ ibn ʿUmar al-Jumaḥī informed us: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yāmīn related to me that a bird entered the clothes of ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās while he lay on his bier, being carried. It was not moved away until he was buried. He said: I do not know whether ʿAbd Allāh or Yāmīn saw it.

Abū Nuʿaym related to us: Bassām al-Ṣayrafī related to us: “ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yāmīn said: My father told me that when Ibn ʿAbbās’s funeral passed through al-Jīra—it is a valley—a white bird called a ghurnūq came and entered the bier. It was not seen after—”

“—that.”

Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Muthannā ibn Anas al-Anṣārī related to us: Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr related to me, from Abū Salama, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: “I found most of the Messenger of God’s knowledge among this group of the Anṣār. I would come to one of their doors and sit there. Had I wished to be admitted, I would have been admitted because of my kinship with the Messenger of God ﷺ—but I sought in doing so to put him at ease.”

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us: Sufyān related to us: Sālim related to us, from Mundhir, who said: When Ibn ʿAbbās died, Ibn al-Ḥanafiyya said: “Today the learned and devout man of this community has died.”

Saʿīd related to us: Sufyān related to us, from ʿAbd al-Karīm al-Jazarī, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, who said: “I used to hear ḥadīth from Ibn ʿAbbās. If he would permit me, I would kiss his head.”

Al-Ḥumaydī related to us: Sufyān related to us. Ibn Abjar said: “The people of Mecca did not become learned in religion until Ibn ʿAbbās came to them.”

“Sufyān related to us: Ibn Abī Najīḥ related to us: I heard Mujāhid say:

‘I have never seen anyone at all like Ibn ʿAbbās—unless someone should say: “The Messenger of God—God bless—”’”

“—bless him and grant him peace—: ‘He died on the day he died, and he was indeed the learned man of this community.’”

Abū Bakr related to us: Sufyān related to us: Ibrāhīm ibn Maysara related to us:

I heard Ṭāwūs say: “Ibn ʿAbbās told me: ‘Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī consulted me about setting out. I said: “Were it not that this would bring reproach upon me or you, I would have seized you by the head.”’ What he said in reply to me was: ‘If I am killed in such-and-such a place, that is dearer to me than for you to support me—meaning, in Mecca.’” Ibn ʿAbbās said: “That is what made me resign myself to it.” Then Ṭāwūs said: “I have never seen anyone who showed greater reverence for the things God has forbidden than Ibn ʿAbbās. If I wished to weep, I would weep.”

Salama related to us: Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal related to us: ʿAbd al-Razzāq related to us: Maʿmar said: “Most of Ibn ʿAbbās’s knowledge came from three people: ʿUmar, ʿAlī, and Ubayy ibn Kaʿb.”

ʿAbd al-Razzāq related to us: I heard Maʿmar say: “Ibn ʿAbbās used to say to a brother of his from among the Anṣār: ‘Come with us to the Companions of Muḥammad ﷺ—perhaps they may need us.’ When he prayed, his young servants would sit behind him. If he came to a verse about which he had heard nothing, he would repeat it and they would write it down. When he left, he would ask about it.”

Nūḥ ibn al-Haytham al-ʿAsqalānī related to us: al-Walīd related to us, from Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, from Dāwūd ibn ʿAlī, that they said: “Messenger of God, Umm al-Faḍl is pregnant.” The Messenger of God ﷺ—said: “Perhaps God, Mighty and Glorious, will brighten our faces with a boy.” Then ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās was born.

Quṭba ibn al-ʿAlāʾ ibn al-Minhāl al-Ghanawī related to us: Sufyān related to us, from— Sālim, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, who said on the day Ibn ʿAbbās died: “Today the learned and devout man of Quraysh has died.”

Aḥmad ibn Manīʿ related to us: Ibn ʿUlayya related to us: Ayyūb related to us: I was informed, from Ṭāwūs, who said: “I have never seen anyone who showed greater reverence for the sacred things of God, Mighty and Glorious, than Ibn ʿAbbās. If I wished to weep when I remembered him, I would weep.”

Aḥmad ibn Manīʿ related to us: Yazīd ibn Hārūn related to us: Jarīr ibn Ḥāzim informed us, from Yaʿlā ibn Ḥakīm, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: “When the Messenger of God ﷺ—was taken in death, I said to a man from the Anṣār: ‘Come, let us ask the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ—while they are still numerous.’ He said: ‘How astonishing you are, Ibn ʿAbbās! Do you think people need you, when among the people are the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ—who are here?’ He left it at that, while I set about asking the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ—about ḥadīth. If a ḥadīth about a man reached me, I would go to his door while he was taking his midday rest and use my cloak as a pillow at his door. The winds would blow dust over me. He would come out, see me, and say: ‘Cousin of the Messenger of God, what brought you here? Why did you not send for me, so that I could come to you?’ I would reply: ‘I am more entitled to come to you,’ and ask him about the ḥadīth.

“That Anṣārī man lived until he saw people gathered around me, asking me questions. He said: ‘This young man was wiser than I.’”

Samura

Salama related to me: Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal related to us: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad related to us:

Abū Hilāl related to us: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṣubayḥ related to us, from Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn, who said: “As far as I know, Samura was a man of great trustworthiness, truthful in his reports, and devoted to Islam and its people.”

ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr

Saʿīd ibn Abī Maryam related to us: Nāfiʿ related to us, from Ibn Kumayl, who said: I sat with ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz. He asked: “Did Ibn al-Zubayr pray the dawn prayer while it was still dark?” I said: “Yes.” He asked: “What did he intend by that?” I said: “The practice of your father, ʿUmar.”

He said: “Ibn al-Zubayr did not treat prayer carelessly. We have seen no man whose standing in prayer was longer, whose bowing was longer, whose prostration was longer, whose sitting was more complete, whose glances about were fewer, and whose prayer was more perfect than Ibn al-Zubayr. We have seen no one with a more forceful sermon or a shrewder opponent; yet when he was given authority, people found in him what they had not known before.”

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUmayr al-Laythī

Abū Nuʿaym related to us: ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn Ayman related to us: I saw ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUmayr al-Laythī preaching from the time he prayed the dawn prayer until the sun rose, and from the time he prayed the afternoon prayer until the sun set. His hair fell in a mass to his nape, or something like that, and I saw that his beard was yellow.

Al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad

Al-Ḥumaydī related to us: Sufyān related to us: ʿAmr ibn Dīnār related to us:

“I have never seen anyone more knowledgeable about the matters over which people differed than al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad. Your al-Zuhrī was merely one of his young pupils”—meaning Ibn Shihāb.

Al-Ḥumaydī related to us: Sufyān related to us: I heard ʿAmr ibn Dīnār say:

“I set out for Medina, making straight for al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad.”

Ibn Abī ʿUmar related to us: Sufyān related to us: ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn— Ayman related to us: “Al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad used to stay with us, and we would provide for him for three days. Once three days had passed, he would accept nothing from us.”

Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib

“My father sent me to Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī. I saw that his eyes were lined with kohl, and I returned and said to my father: ‘You sent me to a man such-and-such’”—I had spoken ill of him. He said: “My son, he is the best of people.”

Abū Nuʿaym related to us: ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn Ayman related to us: I came to Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥanafiyya, whose eyes were lined with kohl and whose beard was dyed red. I saw that he wore a close-fitting cap on his head and a black turban.

Al-Ḥumaydī and Ibn Abī ʿUmar related to us: Sufyān related to us, from ʿAmr, who said: Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī said to me: “Shall I give you a thousand dinars and you invest them?” I said: “I have no need of them.”

ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn

Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmar related to us: Sufyān related to us: Al-Zuhrī said: “I have seen no Hāshimite superior to ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn.” Al-Zuhrī also said: “How numerous were the gatherings of ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn! I have seen no one more learned in jurisprudence than him, but he related few ḥadīths.”

Ibrāhīm ibn al-Mundhir related to us: Sufyān related to us, from Ibn Shihāb, who said: “I have seen no Qurashī superior to ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn.”

Zayd ibn Bishr related to us: Ibn Wahb informed me: Ibn Zayd related to us: “My father used to say: ‘I have never seen anyone like ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn among them.’”

Muḥammad ibn [Abī] Zukayr related to me: Ibn Wahb informed us:

Mālik related to me: Nāfiʿ ibn Jubayr said to ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn: “You sit with people of low standing.” ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn replied: “I sit with those whose company benefits my religion.” Nāfiʿ felt resentment about this, while ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn was a man of religious merit.

Mālik said: “ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtba ibn Masʿūd was one of the people’s learned men. When he entered into prayer, if someone sat beside him, he would not turn toward him until he had finished his prayer, which was as long as people saw it to be. Mālik said: ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, too, was a man of merit. He would come and sit with him, while ʿUbayd Allāh prolonged his prayer and paid him no attention. ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, who was himself a man of such standing, said to him: ‘Anyone who seeks this matter must exert himself for it.’”

Mālik said: “Ibn Shihāb kept company with ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtba ibn Masʿūd to such an extent that he would draw water for him.”

Al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, from Ayyūb, who said:

“I saw al-Qāsim wearing a khazz cap and a patterned, colored sābarī cloak dyed with a little saffron. He would leave a hundred thousand [dirhams], and something of them troubled his conscience.”

Sulaymān related to us: Wuhayb related to us: I heard Ayyūb mention al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad and say: “I saw him wearing a khazz cap. I have never seen a man superior to him. He left a hundred thousand, and it was lawful for him.”

Muḥammad ibn [Abī] Zukayr related to us: Ibn Wahb informed us, from Mālik, who said: He mentioned the merit of al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad and said: “Al-Qāsim was one of the jurists of this community.”
