Abū Bakr related to us: Sufyān related to us: ʿAmr related to us, who said: Ayyūb al-Sakhtiyānī— He informed him, saying: Jābir ibn Zayd was mentioned in the presence of Ibn Sīrīn, and Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn said:

“Jābir ibn Zayd was a Muslim when it came to the dirham.”

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us: Sufyān related to us: ʿAmr related to us, who said: “I never knew Jābir ibn Zayd to hold the opinion of the Ibāḍiyya, nor did I hear it from him. I read to him the epistle of al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad, and he said: ‘I have never loved anything he disliked, nor disliked anything he loved.’”

Abū Bakr related to us: Sufyān related to us: ʿAmr related to us, who said: A man came to Abū al-Shaʿthāʾ, greeted him, praised him, and prayed for him. When he had turned away, I said: “Do you know this man, Abū al-Shaʿthāʾ?” He said: “No, except that I think he is one of these Ṣufriyya of yours.”

Through the same chain: ʿAmr related to us, who said: “I have not seen anyone more knowledgeable in giving legal opinions than Jābir ibn Zayd.”

ʿAmr said: “Whenever I saw him, I would say, ‘He does not know how to do anything.’ He did not have that sort of bearing.”

Through the same chain: ʿAmr ibn Dīnār related to us, who said: Jābir ibn Zayd said to me: “O ʿAmr, al-Ḥakam ibn Ayyūb appointed some men to the judiciary, and I was among them. O ʿAmr, if anything had come of that, I would have mounted my riding beast and then fled across the land.”

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, from Yaḥyā ibn ʿAtīq, who said:

Jābir was mentioned in the presence of Muḥammad, and he said: “May God have mercy on Jābir. He was a Muslim when it came to the dirham.”

He said: Ḥammād related to us, from Hishām, from Muḥammad, who said: “It used to be said: ‘A Muslim is truly a Muslim when it comes to the dirham.’”

Abū al-Nuʿmān related to us: Ḥammād related to us, from Ayyūb, who mentioned him—meaning Jābir ibn Zayd—and said: “By God, he was intelligent, intelligent, intelligent—a man with resolve for God.” (4a)

Abū al-Nuʿmān and Sulaymān related something similar to us. They both said: Ḥammād related to us, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, who said: Jābir ibn Zayd was asked, “Abū al-Shaʿthāʾ, they are writing down what you say?” He said: “We belong to God! They are writing down an opinion of mine that I may retract tomorrow.”

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us: Ḥammād related to us, from Ḥabīb, from Thābit al-Bunānī, who said: I said to Jābir ibn Zayd: “What do you long for?” He said: “A glance from al-Ḥasan.”

He said: “So I went to him, and he came to him and greeted him.”

Abū Bakr related to us: Sufyān related to us, who said: We heard ʿAmr relate: Abū al-Shaʿthāʾ said to me: “O ʿAmr, I have a she-camel on which I stand at ʿArafa. Her name is Jazza. I would not want a camel in her place, one on which I could stand at ʿArafa, even if I were offered two hundred dinars for her.” ʿAmr said:

I said to him: “Abū al-Shaʿthāʾ, if I were with you, I would sell her to you.”

Abū ʿUmar Ḥafṣ ibn ʿUmar related to us: Ziyād ibn al-Rabīʿ al-Yaḥmadī related to us: Ṣāliḥ—meaning al-Dahhān—related to us, who said: “I never heard Jābir—meaning Ibn Zayd—say, ‘The Messenger of God ﷺ said,’ while children here say, ‘The Messenger of God ﷺ said,’ twenty times in an hour. I know of no more than fifteen or sixteen traditions, or thereabouts, that Jābir narrated from the Messenger of God ﷺ.”

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us: Sufyān related to us: ʿAmr ibn Dīnār informed me: Abū Maʿbad informed me, and he was among the most truthful of Ibn ʿAbbās’s freedmen.

“He said: Sufyān related to us: ʿAmmār al-Duhnī related to us, from Muslim al-Baṭīn, who said:

‘I saw Abū Yaḥyā al-Aʿraj—who was learned in the traditions of Ibn ʿAbbās—meet with Saʿīd ibn Jubayr in a mosque in Kūfa, and the two discussed the traditions of Ibn ʿAbbās.’”

Sufyān said: ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib mentioned to me that he had witnessed a gathering—then ʿAṭāʾ sighed and wept—in which so-and-so, so-and-so, and Miqsam were present. He mentioned some people, and among them was Saʿīd ibn Jubayr.

ʿAlī said: Abū Maʿbad’s name was Nāfidh, and Abū Yaḥyā’s name was Miṣdaʿ; he was the freedman of Muʿādh ibn ʿAfrāʾ.

Aḥmad ibn al-Khalīl related to us: al-Khalīl ibn Zakariyyā related to us: Saʿīd ibn Abī ʿArūba related to us (4b).

Qatāda related to me, who said: “There were four of the Successors who were the most learned. ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ was the most learned of them in the rites of pilgrimage; ʿIkrima, the freedman of Ibn ʿAbbās, was the most learned of them in the Prophet’s campaigns ﷺ; Saʿīd ibn Jubayr was the most learned of them in Qurʾānic exegesis; and al-Ḥasan ibn Abī al-Ḥasan was the most learned of them in what is lawful and unlawful.”

Aḥmad ibn al-Khalīl related to us: Masʿūd ibn Khalaf related to us: al-Ḥajjāj related to us, who said: I asked Shuʿba about al-Ḥakam and Ḥammād. He said: “Al-Ḥakam had more traditions of the two,”

“while Ḥammād was the better of the two in judgment.”

Abū Yūsuf said: “In the view of Abū Bisṭām, al-Ḥakam is superior to Ḥammād in all respects.”

He said: Ḥajjāj said: Shuʿba saw me at the home of al-Ḥasan ibn Dīnār, so I kept trying to hide from him. When I came to him, he said to me: “You should know that I saw you.” Then he said to me:

“Even so, he has kept company with the shaykhs.”

Ḥajjāj said: Shuʿba urged me to study with al-Mubārak ibn Faḍāla and Abū ʿAwāna, and he said to me: “Keep close to Abū ʿAwāna.”

Aḥmad ibn al-Khalīl related to us: Hārūn ibn Maʿrūf related to us: Ḍamra ibn Rabīʿa related to us, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿAṭāʾ, who said: “Makḥūl could not say ‘qul’ [‘say’]; he would say ‘kul’ [‘eat’].”

He said: “Whatever Makḥūl said in Syria was accepted from him. ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ was black, intensely black, and had no hair on his head except a few hairs at the front of his head, so when he would call out—”

“Whenever he spoke, whatever he said in the Ḥijāz [except] was accepted from him.”

Ḍamra said: I heard someone say: “ʿAṭāʾ’s mother was Baraka, and his father, Abū Rabāḥ, was black.”

Ḍamra said: “Yazīd Abū Ḥabīb was black.”

Aḥmad ibn al-Khalīl related to me: Isḥāq related to us: Saʿīd ibn ʿĀmir related to us: Hammām ibn Yaḥyā informed us, who said: Shuʿba came to Qatāda, and Qatāda related a tradition. Shuʿba asked: “From whom did you hear this?” Qatāda said: “By God, we used to be too intimidated to ask them, ‘From whom did you hear it?’” He mentioned al-Ḥasan and Saʿīd. Qatāda did not leave before Shuʿba related a tradition, whereupon Qatāda asked him:

“From whom did you hear this?” Shuʿba replied: “I ask you and you do not answer me, then you ask me!” (5a)

Aḥmad related to me: Isḥāq related to us: al-Faḍl ibn Mūsā related to us, who said:

I heard al-Aʿmash say: Ibrāhīm was asked about Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib. He said: “That is a man who rose in status through his pledge of allegiance.” He was asked about Shurayḥ, and he said: “That is a man who loves rulers. But I did see something about him that pleased me: he said to one of his sons, ‘Boy, get up and call the adhān,’ and the boy called the adhān for him.”

[ʿAmr ibn Dīnār]

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us: Sufyān related to us, who said: I heard ʿAmr say: “When ʿAṭāʾ died—”

“When ʿAṭāʾ died, Ibn Hishām said to me: ‘Would you sit with the people, give them legal opinions, and have a stipend assigned to you?’

“I said: ‘That is not what I need,’ and I refused him.”

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us: Sufyān related to us, who said: I heard ʿAmr and al-Zuhrī recite poetry in their gatherings in the Sacred Mosque. I saw ʿAmr ibn Dīnār stay up talking until nearly a quarter of the night had passed, and I saw Ayyūb al-Sakhtiyānī stay up talking with him until nearly a quarter of the night had passed. When they left, Ayyūb would enter the circumambulation area. Sometimes I would enter with him, and he would say: “If I were not here, would you circumambulate?” I would reply: “You would not find me here.” Then he would say to me: “Go.”

“He said: ʿAmr ibn Dīnār would relate a tradition according to its meaning, whereas Ibrāhīm ibn Maysara would relate it only as he had heard it.” And I saw ʿAmr dye his hair with henna.

He said: I heard a man from Mecca say to ʿAmr: “When Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna goes to the House, he writes down what you say.” ʿAmr lay back on his bed in the mosque and wept. He said: “I adjure by God every Muslim who writes anything down from me!” ʿAmr said to me: “Boy, when I was your age, I would forget nothing I heard.”

Abū Bakr related to us: Sufyān related to us, who said: It was mentioned to me that ʿAmr said: “They are writing down my sins.”

Abū Bakr related to us: Sufyān related to us: ʿAmr related to us, who said: “I came to Muḥammad ibn—”

“ʿAlī, Abū Jaʿfar, and he said to his two brothers, Zayd and ʿUmar: ‘Go to your uncle and bring him down.’”

Sufyān said: “I saw ʿAmr dye his hair with henna.”

ʿAmr said: “I brought together al-Jaʿd and al-Hayṣam, the two sons of Bishr, and they discussed something in my presence.”

(5b) Muḥammad related to me, who said: Sufyān said: ʿAmr ibn Dīnār said to me:

“I never sat in Ibn ʿAbbās’s presence; I was never with him except standing.”

He said: ʿAlī said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: Shuʿba said: “You have not seen anyone more reliable than ʿAmr ibn Dīnār.” He thought I meant the elder authorities, so he said: “Nor al-Ḥakam, nor Qatāda.”

Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmar related to us, who said: Sufyān said: “ʿAmr ibn Dīnār went to Medina but did not hear anything there.”

ʿAmr ibn Qays said: “Sufyān, what did ʿAmr do in Medina? Chewing ʿajwa dates distracted him.”

Sufyān said: I asked ʿAmr ibn Dīnār: “Did you see al-Aswad ibn Yazīd?” He said: “Yes.”

I asked: “Did you memorize anything from him?” He said: “No.”

Ibn Abī ʿUmar related to me, who said: Sufyān said: Ibn Abī Najīḥ said: “We had no one more learned than ʿAmr ibn Dīnār.”

He said: ʿAlī related, from Bishr ibn al-Sarī, from Ibrāhīm ibn Nāfiʿ, who said: Ḥasan ibn Muslim died before Ṭāwūs.

He said: ʿAlī said: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam related to us, from Ibn al-Mubārak, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujāhid, whom he heard recite, “and the purified ones” [al-mukhlaṣīn].

Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr and al-Ḥumaydī related to us, both saying: Sufyān related to us: Ibn Jurayj related to us, who said: I heard Mujāhid recite, “Divorce them at the beginning of their waiting period.”

Abū Yūsuf related to us, who said: Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna said: “I never heard Ibn Jurayj say, ‘I heard Mujāhid,’ about anything except this.”

Al-Faḍl ibn Ziyād related to me, who said: I heard Abū ʿAbd Allāh being asked: “Who is the most reliable person regarding ʿAṭāʾ?” He said: “ʿAmr and Ibn Jurayj.” He was asked: “Which of the two came first?” He said: “ʿAmr ibn Dīnār.” Shuʿba said: “I have seen no one like ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, nor al-Ḥakam, nor Qatāda.” He was asked: “Who is the most reliable person regarding ʿAmr ibn Dīnār?”

He said: “No one is more reliable than Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah.” He was asked, “What about Ḥammād ibn Zayd?” He said:

“No. How many traditions did Ḥammād ibn Zayd narrate? Perhaps they would reach one hundred and fifty.”

[Abū al-Zubayr Muḥammad ibn Muslim ibn Tadrus and others]

Aḥmad ibn Manīʿ related to us; Hushaym related to us; Ibn Abī Laylā and al-Ḥajjāj reported to us, from ʿAṭāʾ, who said: “Whenever we left Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh, we would review his traditions. Abū al-Zubayr was the one among us with the best memory for traditions.”

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us; Sufyān related to us (6a); Sulaymān ibn Abī Muslim al-Aḥwal, Ibn Abī Najīḥ’s maternal uncle, related to us; he was trustworthy.

Al-Ḥumaydī related to us; Sufyān related to us; ʿAmr related to us. Muslim al-Muṣabbiḥ also informed us. ʿAmr said: “Muslim was a righteous man who would pray the morning prayer in the Sacred Mosque,” and he spoke well of him.

Al-Ḥumaydī related to us; Sufyān related to us; al-Walīd ibn Kathīr related to us, from Ibn Tadrus, the client of Ḥakīm ibn Ḥizām.

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī said: “Tadrus ibn Mūsā, and Abū al-Zubayr Muḥammad ibn Muslim ibn Tadrus.”

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā related to me; Sufyān related to us, from Dāwūd ibn— Shābūr, from Mujāhid, who said: “We boast to people of four: our jurist, Ibn ʿAbbās; our caller to prayer, Abū Maḥdhūrah; our reciter, ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Sāʾib; and our preacher, ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr.”

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā related to me; Sufyān related to us and said: “I heard Ayyūb whenever he mentioned Abū al-Zubayr say, ‘Abū al-Zubayr, Abū al-Zubayr, Abū al-Zubayr.’” He said: “Our jurist is enough for him.”

Muḥammad said: “My father considered him trustworthy.”

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā related to me; Sufyān related to us and said: “I heard Abū al-Zubayr say:

“ʿAṭāʾ would bring me to Jābir because I had the best memory for traditions among them.”

Muḥammad related to me and said: Sufyān said: “Whenever Abū al-Zubayr disputed with ʿAmr ibn Dīnār about a tradition of Jābir, he would add something to it.”

Salamah related to us, from Aḥmad; Hushaym related to us; Ḥajjāj and Ibn Abī Laylā related to us, from ʿAṭāʾ, who said: “We would be with Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh, and he would relate traditions to us. When we left him, we would review his traditions.” He said: “Abū al-Zubayr had the best memory for traditions among us.”

[ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr]

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us; Sufyān related to us; ʿAmr informed us, saying: “I saw ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr preaching in the mosque.”

Sufyān said: “ʿAmr informed us, saying: ‘Our love for ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr and our admiration for him led us to follow him until we missed a rakʿah of the sunset prayer.’”

Ibn Numayr related to us; Ibn Idrīs and Ḥafṣ ibn Ghiyāth related to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Abū Rāshid, who said: “Some people from Baṣra came to ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr. He said, ‘What brings you here?’ They said, ‘Your brothers sent us to ask you about ʿAlī and ʿUthmān.’”

Ibn Numayr said: “Abū Rāshid’s name was Saʿd; he was ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr’s client.”

[Hishām ibn Ḥujayr]

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā related to me; Sufyān related to us and said: “I heard Ibn Shubrumah say:

“There is no one in Mecca better than Hishām ibn Ḥujayr.”

[Ṭalq ibn Ḥabīb]

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us; Sufyān related to us; Misʿar related to us, from Saʿd ibn Ibrāhīm, who said: “Whenever Ṭalq ibn Ḥabīb met us, we would scarcely part before saying: ‘O God,46 establish for the Muslims a rightly guided course of action, in which Your friend is honored, Your enemy humbled, obedience to You is practiced, and what incurs Your anger is avoided.’”

Al-Ḥumaydī related to us; Sufyān related to us; Misʿar related to us, from Saʿd, who said: “Whenever Ṭalq ibn Ḥabīb met us, he would say: ‘God’s blessings are too numerous to count, and His claims are too great for servants to fulfill. So end your evenings repentant and begin your mornings repentant.’”

Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmar related to us; Sufyān related to us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, who said:

“We saw no one in our town more devoted to guarding his prayer than Ṭalq ibn Ḥabīb.”

[Ibn Jurayj]

Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmar related to us; Sufyān related to us and said: “I heard Ibn Jurayj say:

“No one compiled knowledge as I did.”

“He also said: ‘I kept the company of ʿAmr ibn Dīnār for seven years after I had finished studying with ʿAṭāʾ.’”

I heard Yūsuf ibn Muḥammad say: “Ibn Abī Najīḥ was more learned in jurisprudence than Ibn Jurayj, though his jurisprudential knowledge did not match the extent of his compilations. He was Mecca’s jurisconsult after ʿAṭāʾ and Ibn Abī Najīḥ.”

“He said: I heard Yūsuf—or someone else among the Meccans—say: ‘Ibn Jurayj went out—’”

—to their encampment on the outskirts of Mecca and compiled his books on sheets of rough paper, then copied them onto clean sheets. Whenever a traditionist arrived, he would bring him his book and say, “Have me dictate what is in these chapters.”

Salamah related to us, from Aḥmad; ʿAbd al-Razzāq related to us and said: “My father said: ‘47 to Ibn Isḥāq, for I saw him in a good position with Ibn Abī Najīḥ.’” He said: “So I went to him and found that he had forgotten. He said, ‘Bring me the rough copy.’ I heard that al-Mubārak came to him, and he brought out his book for him.”

He [ʿAbd al-Razzāq] also said: ʿAbd al-Razzāq related to us, from Ibn Jurayj: “When I say to you, ‘I said,’ I mean ʿAṭāʾ.”

Sandal said: “If ʿAṭāʾ, Ibn Jāriyah, had been Ibn Jurayj’s son, he would not have been carried for him.”

Sandal was ʿUmar ibn Qays, the brother of Ḥumayd ibn Qays.

ʿAbd al-Razzāq said, from Ibn Jurayj: “Whenever I corrected ʿAṭāʾ, he would put his hand on his head and then say, ‘Yes’”—drawing out the word.

He said: “I heard Zayd ibn al-Mubārak say: ‘Ibn Jurayj came as a guest, seeking an opportunity to approach Maʿn ibn Zāʾidah al-Shaybānī. Maʿn had promised him, when he passed by him, to pay his debt. He got nothing until people collected a dinar or two for him; then he departed with it.’”

[ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bābāh]

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Saʿd related to us; ʿUmar related to us; ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Najīḥ related to me, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bābāh, the client of the family of Ḥujayr ibn Abī Ihāb.

[Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq]

“‘I heard Ibn Shihāb say: “Knowledge will remain in Medina as long as the client of Makhramah is there.”’”

Sufyān said: “No one criticized him with regard to traditions. The people of Medina only took issue with him over his belief in predestination.”

He said: “I heard one of the descendants of Juwayriyah ibn Asmāʾ, who used to keep close company with ʿAlī, say: ‘I heard ʿAlī say: “Sixty of Ibn Isḥāq’s traditions were presented to me. I found fault with only four of them; I thought that some were his and some were not his.”’”

“He said: ʿAlī said: ‘I found only two objectionable traditions from Ibn Isḥāq: Nāfiʿ—’”

—from Ibn ʿUmar, from the Prophet ﷺ—concerning when one of you becomes drowsy on Friday; and al-Zuhrī, from ʿUrwah, from Zayd ibn Khālid: “When one of you touches his private parts.” He did not transmit these two from anyone, whereas with the rest he would say, “So-and-so mentioned it”; but in this one he says, “He related to us.”

Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmar related to us; Sufyān related to us and said: Al-Hudhalī said:

“Knowledge will remain in Medina as long as this man remains”—meaning Ibn Isḥāq.

[Khallād ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān]

Al-Faḍl ibn Ziyād related to us; Aḥmad related to us; ʿAbd al-Razzāq related to us and said (7b): “Dāwūd ibn ʿAlī sought Khallād—meaning Ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Jundah, who was one of the abnāʾ—in order to appoint him over Yemen, and his mind left him for several days.”

Salamah related to us, from Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, who said: ʿAbd al-Razzāq said: “Wahb ibn Munabbih, al-Mughīrah ibn Ḥakīm, and Khallād ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān were among the abnāʾ.”

ʿAbd al-Razzāq said: Maʿmar said: “I saw no one in Ṣanʿāʾ who did not garble traditions, except Khallād ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān.”

[Al-Mughīrah ibn Ḥakīm]

[Wahb ibn Munabbih]

“‘He performed the pilgrimage in his year—the year one hundred—and Wahb performed the pilgrimage. When they had prayed the night prayer, a group came to them, including ʿAṭāʾ and al-Ḥasan, intending to discuss predestination with him. He turned to a serious subject and kept at it until dawn, so they left without asking him anything.’

“He said: Aḥmad related to us; Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Ṣamad ibn Maʿqil related to us and said: ‘I heard my mother say: “I heard women say that Umm Wahb said, ‘I saw in a dream:

“‘“Your child is a son of ṭīb”—and ṭīb means “gold” in the Ḥimyaritic language.’”

“Aḥmad said: She said, ‘I saw as though I had given birth to a son made of gold.’”

Abū Yūsuf related to us and said: Aḥmad related to us; Ghawth ibn Jābir ibn Ghaylān ibn Munabbih related to us and said: “They were four brothers. The eldest was Wahb, then Maʿqil Abū ʿAqīl, Hammām, and Ghaylān, who was the youngest and Ghawth’s grandfather. He was Wahb ibn Munabbih ibn Kāmil ibn Sayj, who was al-Aswār.”

Ghawth said: “Wahb died in the year one hundred and fourteen.”

Ghawth said: “Hammām, the last of them, died shortly before Abū Jaʿfar died.”

Wahb died, then Maʿqil, then Ghaylān, then Hammām.

[ʿUrwah ibn Muḥammad al-Saʿdī]

ʿAlī said: “ʿUrwah ibn Muḥammad governed Yemen for twenty years. When he left, he took with him a sword and a codex.”

[Baṣra]

Abū ʿUthmān Saʿīd ibn Yaḥyā al-Umawī related to me; my paternal uncle Muḥammad ibn Saʿīd related to us; al-Mujālid related to us, from al-Shaʿbī, who said: “I used to sit with al-Aḥnaf and boast to his companions, who were from Baṣra, about the people of Kūfah (8a). He said to us: ‘You are our dependents; we rescued you from your slaves.’” I recalled a line spoken by Aʿshā Hamdān:

“Are you proud that you killed slaves,

or that once you routed the clan of Righal?

“Then we drove you to them by force,

and we put your affairs in order after your failure.

“So when you boast against us, remember

what we did to you on the Day of the Camel:

“between an old man dyeing his moustache,

and a bright young man trailing his robe.

“He came to us roaring in his ample garment,

so we slaughtered him as a lamb is slaughtered.

“We showed clemency, but you forgot our clemency

and denied God’s great blessing.

Al-Aḥnaf said: “Girl, bring that yellow sheet.”

Abū ʿUthmān related to me; my father related to us; Mujālid related to us, from ʿĀmir, who said: “I used to sit with al-Aḥnaf ibn Qays and boast to the people of Baṣra about the people of Kūfah. One day my words went too far with him, though I did not realize it. He said, ‘Girl, bring that book.’

“She brought it, and he said, ‘Read it aloud’—though none of the people there knew what it contained. He said:

“She read it, and there it was:

“‘In the name of God, Most Gracious, Most Merciful. From al-Mukhtār ibn Abī ʿUbayd to al-Aḥnaf ibn Qays and those of Rabīʿah and Muḍar who are with him: Peace be upon you. I praise God to you—there is no god but He. To proceed: Woe to the mother of Rabīʿah and Muḍar! Al-Aḥnaf is leading his people to Saqar, from which they will be unable to emerge. I have no power to alter for you what has been inscribed in destiny. I have been told that you deny me and harm my messengers. Prophets before me were denied and harmed; I am no better than many of them. Peace.’

“When she had read it, he said: ‘Tell me, is this from someone of Baṣra or someone of Kūfah?’ I said: ‘May God forgive you, Abū Baḥr! We were only joking and laughing.’ He said:

“‘You will tell me who it is from.’ I said, ‘May God forgive you.’ He said, ‘You will tell me.’ I said, ‘It is from the people of Kūfah’ (8b).”

He said: “How can you boast over the people of Basra when this man is one of your own?”

[Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us: Sufyān related to us, from Mujālid, from al-Shaʿbī, who said:

I boasted over the people of Basra and bested them by citing the people of Kufa. Al-Aḥnaf was silent and did not speak. When he saw that I had bested them, he sent a servant of his, who brought a letter. He said, “Here, read this.” I read it, and there it was: from al-Mukhtār to him, stating that he was a prophet. Al-Aḥnaf said, “How could someone like this be among us?”

Al-Ḥumaydī related to us: Sufyān related to us: Shuʿba ibn al-Ḥajjāj related to us. He said: Al-Ḥasan was asked, “Which are better, the people of Kufa or the people of Basra?” Al-Ḥasan replied, “He used to begin with the people of Kufa.”

Al-Makkī ibn Ibrāhīm related to me, from ʿAbd Rabbih ibn Rāshid, who said: I was in the mosque at Mecca when I saw a circle of people. I approached them, and Ibn ʿUmar was among them. He asked me, “Where are you from?” I said, “From the people of Basra.” He said, “The people of Basra are better than the people of Kufa.”

Abū Hāshim Ziyād ibn Ayyūb related to us: Saʿīd ibn ʿĀmir related to us: Yūnus ibn ʿUbayd said, “I count it among God’s blessings upon me that I was not raised in Kufa.” Saʿīd was asked, “Did you hear this from Yūnus?” He said, “No, but a man told me it on his authority.”

[Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī]

Al-Ḥajjāj ibn al-Minhāl related to us: Ḥammād related to us: ʿAlī ibn Zayd informed us, saying:

I met ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr, Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, Yaḥyā ibn Jaʿda, al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad, Sālim and others, yet I saw no one like al-Ḥasan. Had al-Ḥasan met the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ when he was a man, they would have needed his judgment.

ʿAmr ibn ʿĀṣim al-Kilābī related to us: Sulaymān ibn al-Mughīra related to us, from Thābit, who said:

Muṭarrif said, “I would not like to say ‘Amen’ to anyone’s supplication until I had heard what he says, except al-Ḥasan ibn Abī al-Ḥasan.”

ʿAmr related to us—he said: Sulaymān ibn al-Mughīra related to us: Thābit related to us, saying: Ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Abī al-Ḥasan said to his father, al-Ḥasan, “Father, our house is leaking; shall we plaster it?” He replied, “Put some ash there,” then turned away from the matter.

ʿAmr ibn ʿAwn related to us: Hushaym related to us, from Manṣūr, who said: Ibn Sīrīn would laugh until his eyes filled with tears, while al-Ḥasan would speak to us and weep.

ʿAmr ibn al-Rabīʿ ibn Ṭāriq related to us: al-Sarī informed us that al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Abī Hilāl al-Bāhilī once said to al-Ḥasan, “Abū Saʿīd, you told me a report, but I forgot it. Repeat it to me.” Al-Ḥasan replied, “Were it not for forgetfulness, there would be many jurists.”

Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz al-Ramlī and Saʿīd related to us, saying: Ḍamra related to us, from Ibn Shūdhub, who said: Ibn Sīrīn said to his companions, “Welcome, O al-mudarfishūn!”

Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz and Saʿīd ibn Asad related to us, saying: Ḍamra related to us, from Jābir ibn Abī Salama, who said: Yūnus ibn ʿUbayd described al-Ḥasan and Ibn Sīrīn. He said:

“As for al-Ḥasan, I have seen no man whose words so closely matched his deeds. As for Ibn Sīrīn, whenever two matters concerning his religion presented themselves to him, he chose the more reliable of the two.”

Abū al-Nuʿmān related to us: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, from Ayyūb, who said: “Two kinds of people have lied about al-Ḥasan: people whose view is predestination, who attribute it to al-Ḥasan so as to make it currency among the people; and people with hatred for al-Ḥasan in their hearts, who say, ‘Does he not say such-and-such? Does he not say such-and-such?’”

Abū al-Nuʿmān related to us: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, from Ayyūb, who said: “I was told to Ibn al-Ashʿath, ‘If you would like them to be killed around you as they were killed around ʿĀʾisha’s camel, bring out al-Ḥasan.’ He sent for him and compelled him [to come].”

Abū al-Nuʿmān related to us: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, from Ayyūb, who said: “I disputed with al-Ḥasan about predestination more than once, until I threatened him with the authorities. He said, ‘I will not speak about it again after today.’”

Ayyūb said: “I know no one who can find fault with al-Ḥasan except on this matter. I met Al-Ḥasan, by God, and he does not say it.”

Abū al-Nuʿmān related to us: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, from Ayyūb, from al-Ḥasan, who said:

“Had God willed, He would have entrusted this matter to His servants—to the people—and said, ‘Whoever strives for Me, I will reward him.’ But instead, there is a command concerning one matter and a prohibition concerning another. Then He said, ‘Strive for Me in what I have commanded you.’”

Abū al-Nuʿmān related to us: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, from Ayyūb, who said: I heard al-Ḥasan say, “Are you not amazed at Saʿīd ibn Jubayr? He came to me at al-Bayḍāʾ during the plague [while consulting me about fighting these people].”

Then Qatāda said: Al-Ḥasan related to us that he had not met any of the men of Badr face-to-face to hear a report from them, nor Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, nor Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ.

[ʿUthmān ibn Abī Shayba related to me: Ibn Idrīs related to us, from Shuʿba, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṣubayḥ, from Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn, who said: “There were three who would accept as truthful anyone who related something to them: Anas, Abū al-ʿĀliya, and al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī.”]

[ʿUthmān related to us: Jarīr related to us, from a man, from ʿĀṣim al-Aḥwal, from Ibn Sīrīn, who said: “Do not relate anything to me from al-Ḥasan or Abū al-ʿĀliya, for the two of them do not mind from whom they take a report.”]

Muslim ibn Ibrāhīm related to us: Ḥammād ibn Salama related to us: ʿAlī ibn Zayd informed us, saying: I related a report to al-Ḥasan while I had it concealed at my house. He asked me to repeat it six times. When it later became known, he began relating that report. I said, “Abū Saʿīd, who told you this?” He said, “Leave me be.” When I pressed him further, he said, “You told it to me.”

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us: Abū Hilāl related to us, saying: Naṣr Abū Khuzayma and I went in to see al-Ḥasan on a Friday, and he had not attended the Friday prayer. I said, “Abū Saʿīd, did you not attend the congregational prayer?” He said, “I intended to, but God’s decree prevented me.”

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to me: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to me, from Ibn ʿAwn, from al-Ḥasan, who said: “ʿUmar met ʿAlqama ibn ʿUlātha in the middle of the night. ʿUmar resembled Khālid ibn al-Walīd. ʿAlqama said to him, ‘Khālid, this man is dear to you. These people have refused anything but stinginess. I have come intending to ask him about two matters concerning us here [unclear]; my kinsman—I intended to ask him to assign him a stipend. But if they have treated you this way, I will not ask him for anything.’ ʿUmar said to him, ‘Easy now, easy! What is it you have?’ He said, ‘Yes: there are people who have a claim upon us, so we give them their due, and our reward is with God.’”

When morning came, people went in to see ʿUmar, and ʿAlqama and Khālid ibn al-Walīd went in to him. ʿUmar turned to Khālid and said, “Well? What has ʿAlqama been saying to you since last night?” He said, “He did not say anything to me.”

He said: “Well? What has ʿAlqama been saying to you since last night?” He said, “By God, he did not say anything to me.” He said, “And you swear to it too!”] He said: Al-Ḥasan was asked, “What was ʿAlqama saying?” He replied, “By God, he was afraid.”

Sulaymān related to us: Ḥammād ibn Salama related to us, from Ḥumayd, from Abū Naḍra, with a similar version of this report. He said: ʿAlqama kept saying to Khālid, “Stop, Khālid, stop, Khālid.”

ʿUmar said, “Indeed, he has said a word that I would prefer to be present in every Muslim over red camels.”

He said, “They are a people who have a claim upon us, so we give them their due, and our reward is with God.”

Sulaymān related to us: Ḥammād ibn Salama related to us, from Ḥumayd, who said: I went with al-Ḥasan to Abū Naḍra, and he related this report to us. I had not heard al-Ḥasan before that.

He said: Then, after that, I heard al-Ḥasan relate it. Al-Ḥasan’s telling of it was better than Abū Naḍra’s.

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us: Ḥammād related to us, from Ibn ʿAwn, who said: I mentioned some men to Ibn Sīrīn. One day he said to me, “Abū ʿAwn, have you heard that so-and-so came to us?”

I said, “Abū Bakr, what did you think of him?” He said, “I saw a man who thinks he knows what we do not know.”

Sulaymān said: al-Khalīl ibn Aḥmad said, “People are of three kinds: two who know and one who does not know. A learned man who knows that he is learned—that one knows. A learned man who does not know that he is learned—that one knows. And a man who does not know, yet thinks he knows—that one does not know.” Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us: Ḥammād related to us, from Ibn ʿAwn, who said: “Had we known that they were attributing it to al-Ḥasan, we would have said something about them that would hang around their necks, and they would never be able to undo it.”

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, from Khālid al-Ḥadhdhāʾ, who said: A man from the people of Kufa used to come to Basra, but would not visit al-Ḥasan because of the question of predestination. One day he met him on the road and asked him, “Abū Saʿīd, ‘They will continue to differ, except those upon whom your Lord has mercy.’” He replied, “Yes. Those who are recipients of His mercy do not differ.”

The man said, “Then what of His saying, ‘For that He created them’?” He replied, “These people were created for Paradise, and those people for the Fire.”

The man said, “I will not ask about al-Ḥasan again after today.” (10b) Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us: Ḥammād related to us, from Khālid al-Ḥadhdhāʾ, who said: I was away for a while. When I returned, they told me that al-Ḥasan had spoken about predestination. I went to him and said, “Abū Saʿīd, was Adam created for Paradise or for the earth?” He said, “Abū Manāzil, this was not the sort of question you used to ask me.”

I said, “I wanted to know.” He replied, “No, rather, for the earth.” I said, “What do you think: if he had held fast and not eaten from the tree?” He said, “He could not have held fast and refrained from eating from the tree, for he was created for the earth. Consider the saying of God, Mighty and Majestic: ‘You cannot lead astray anyone concerning it, except one who is to enter the blazing Fire.’” He said: “The devils could mislead by their error only those whom God had decreed to enter the blazing Fire.”

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb and al-Ḥajjāj ibn al-Minhāl related to us, saying: Abū al-Ashhab related to us, from al-Ḥasan, concerning His saying, Mighty and Majestic: “‘A barrier was placed between them and what they desired.’” (34:54)

He said: “Faith.”

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us: Ḥammād related to us, from Ḥabīb ibn al-Shahīd and Manṣūr ibn Zādhān, who said: We asked al-Ḥasan about everything from “Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds” (1:2) to “Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of humankind” (114:1), and he interpreted it in affirmation.

(20b) … … the encampment, and so-and-so was with him discussing the matter of fighting and so-and-so was with him.

Abū al-Nuʿmān said: “This was when Ibn al-Ashʿath sent for him and compelled him [to come].”

Al-Ḥajjāj related to us: Ḥammād related to us, from Ḥumayd, who said: Al-Ḥasan came to Mecca, and the jurists of Mecca asked me to speak to him. One day he sat with them, and I spoke to him. He said, “Yes.”

They gathered, and he was seated on a couch. That day he delivered a sermon. By God, I never saw him before or after that day speak as he did then. They asked him about a long scroll, from here to there. That day, he made only one mistake: something about forty, “mashāh”, between two men; he said “mashāh” there. A man said to him, “Abū Saʿīd, who created Satan?” He said:

“Glory be to God! Is there any creator other than God? He created Satan, and He created good and evil.”

The man said, “What is the matter with them—may God fight them! How can they lie about this shaykh?”

Al-Ḥajjāj ibn al-Minhāl and Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us, saying: Abū al-Ashhab related to us, from al-Ḥasan, concerning this verse: “‘A barrier was placed between them and what they desired.’” (34:54) He said, “A barrier was placed between them and faith.”

Al-Ḥajjāj related to us: Ḥammād related to us, from Ḥumayd, who said: I read the whole Qurʾān to al-Ḥasan at the home of Abū Khalīfa. He interpreted all of it for me in affirmation. I asked him about His saying, “Thus do We let it enter the hearts of the sinners” (26:200). He said, “God put associating partners with Him into their hearts.” I asked him about His saying, “And they have deeds besides that, which they are to perform” (23:63).

He said, “Deeds they will perform, though they have not yet performed them.” He said: I asked him about God’s saying, “You cannot lead astray anyone concerning it, except one who is to enter the blazing Fire” (37:162–163). …

Abū al-Nuʿmān related to us: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, from Khālid al-Ḥadhdhāʾ, who said: A man asked al-Ḥasan, saying, “‘They will continue to differ, except those upon whom your Lord has mercy’ (11:118–119).” He replied:

“Those who are recipients of His mercy [do not] differ. ‘For that He created them’ (11:119).” He said, “He created these people for His Paradise, and He created those people for His Fire.”

Abū al-Nuʿmān related to us: Ḥammād related to us, from Khālid, who said: I said to al-Ḥasan, “Abū Saʿīd, tell me: was Adam created for heaven or for earth?” He said, “He was created for the earth.”

(21a) I said, “What do you think: if he had held fast and not eaten from the tree?” He said, “He had no choice but to eat from it, because he was created for the earth.” He said: I asked al-Ḥasan, “Abū Saʿīd, ‘You cannot lead astray anyone concerning it, except one who is to enter the blazing Fire’ (37:162–163).” He replied, “Yes. The devils mislead by their error only those whom God has decreed must enter the blazing Fire.”

Al-Ḥajjāj related to us: Ḥammād related to us, from Khālid al-Ḥadhdhāʾ, who said: I said to al-Ḥasan, “Abū Saʿīd, was Adam created for the earth or for heaven?” He said, “For the earth.” I said to him, “Could he have held fast?” He said, “No.”

Al-Ḥajjāj related to us: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, from Khālid, who said: I said to al-Ḥasan: “Abū Saʿīd, was Adam created for the earth or for heaven?” He said: “What is this, Abū Manāzil?” Then he said: “He was created for the earth.” I said: “What do you think—if he had held fast and not eaten from the tree?” He said: “There was no avoiding his eating from it, because he was created for the earth.”

Abū al-Nuʿmān related to us; Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, from Muḥammad ibn al-Zubayr, who said:

Al-Ḥasan was asked, “Would you pray, given that the market people have already prayed?” He said: “There is no good in the market people. I have heard that one of them turns his brother away over a dirham.”

ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān related to us; ʿAbd Allāh informed us; Sufyān informed us. He said: They mentioned in al-Ḥasan’s presence an increase or decrease of a dāniq. Al-Ḥasan said: “There is no religion without magnanimity.”

ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān related to us; al-Mubārak ibn Saʿīd informed us, from Ṣāliḥ ibn Ḥayy ibn Muslim, from ʿAbd al-Aʿlā, who was a broker, who said: Al-Ḥasan said to me: “Would any of you give his brother a garment on which there was a discount of two or three dirhams?” I said: “No, by God—not even a dāniq.” Al-Ḥasan said: “Fie, fie! What magnanimity is left, then?”

Muḥammad ibn Abī Usāma al-Ḥalabī related to us; Ḍamrah related to us, from al-Sarī ibn Yaḥyā, who said: I never saw al-Ḥasan smile except once. He had complained to us about some food he had eaten. A man in the gathering said: “Food has never troubled me.” Another man said to him: “If there were stones in your stomach, you would grind them.” Al-Ḥasan smiled.

Saʿīd ibn Asad related to us; Ḍamrah related to us, from Rajāʾ, from ʿUthmān al-Battī, who said:

I said to al-Ḥasan: “I have a request of you.” He said: “What is it?” He said: “No.”48

Through the same chain, from Rajāʾ, from Ibn ʿAwn, who said: I never saw a man who was not an Arab more like the Arabs than al-Ḥasan.

Saʿīd ibn Asad related to me; Ḍamrah related to us, from Ibn Shawdhab, from Maṭar, who said:

Al-Ḥasan was a man of night worship.

Saʿīd related to us; Ḍamrah related to us, from Rajāʾ, from Ibn ʿAwn, who said: I was sitting with al-Ḥasan (11a) when a man came to him and said: “Abū Saʿīd, from whom do you transmit?” He said: “From you, and from this one, and from this one.”

ʿAmr ibn ʿĀṣim related to us; Sulaymān ibn al-Mughīrah related to us; Thābit related to us, who said:

I went with al-Ḥasan ibn Abī al-Ḥasan on an errand, and we came to the market. He said: “There is no place more hateful to God than this.” Then we went on until we came to the palace of Aws.

Al-Ḥasan said: “The palace of Aws! The palace of Aws! The palace of Aws! Whoever gives a poor man a handful of dates—it is better for him than leaving something like this.”

[Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us; Ḥammād related to us, from Ibn ʿAwn, from Muḥammad, who said:

“There were three men here who believed everyone who told them anything.” Sulaymān said: “It seems he disapproved of that in them.”]

Muḥammad ibn Manṣūr al-Ṭūsī related to us; Yaḥyā ibn Abī Bukayr related to us; he related:

Ḥammād ibn Salamah, from ʿAlī ibn Zayd, who said: Three of our companions, whenever they heard a report, would attribute it to the Prophet: al-Ḥasan, Abū al-ʿĀliyah, and another.

Muḥammad related to us; ʿAlī informed us, from Khālid ibn al-Ḥārith, from ʿImrān ibn Ḥudayr, from Ṣāliḥ ibn Artabīl, who said: Sulaymān al-Taymī related to us that Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn disliked being instructed in predestination. We were in the house of Abū Makhlad when Muḥammad came in among us. They asked him, and he said: “I did not say that; whoever said it has lied.” I went to Sulaymān al-Taymī and told him. He said: “This muezzin of ours related it to me, and I did not think he would lie.”

Saʿīd ibn Asad related to me; Ḍamrah—a man devoted to night worship—related to us, from Ibn Shawdhab, who said: Thābit al-Bunānī said something. Muḥammad ibn Wāsiʿ became angry and said: “You, squint-eyed one! We knew people whose company you would consider no more than this. How I wish we could wait for al-Ḥasan to come out to us; then he would come out as though he had seen the Hereafter with his own eyes, and would tell us about it.”

Through the same chain, from Ibn Shawdhab, who said: Muṭarrif ibn al-Shikhkhīr said: “I would not entrust myself to a supplication I do not know, except for al-Ḥasan’s supplication, for I trust him.”

Saʿīd related to us; Ḍamrah related to us, from Rajāʾ, from Ibn ʿAwn, from al-Ḥasan, who said:

“Whoever denies predestination has disbelieved.”

Saʿīd related to me; Ḍamrah related to us, from Ibn Shawdhab, who said: A man from among the people of Basra saw Ibn Sīrīn in Paradise in a dream and asked him: “What became of al-Ḥasan?” (11b)

He said: “He is there.” The man asked: “By what means?” He replied: “By his generosity.”

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us; Sufyān related to us; al-Aʿmash said: Al-Ḥasan continued to cultivate wisdom until he spoke with it.

Abū Nuʿaym related to us; Sufyān related to us, who said: I heard a shaykh say: I mentioned al-Ḥasan to Ṭāwūs—or he mentioned him—and he said: “That is a bold man.”

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us; Ḥammād related to us, from Ibn ʿAwn, who said: When al-Ḥasan was appointed judge, a man asked me to speak to him about an orphan’s property, to be handed over to the man with his guarantee. I spoke to him, and he said: “Do you know him?” I said: “Yes.” So he handed it over to him. I told Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn about this, and he said: “You, too, are bold in your judgment.”

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to me; Sufyān related to us; Musāwir—meaning al-Warrāq—related to us, from his brother Sayyār, who said: Al-Ḥasan was asked: “Abū Saʿīd, from whom are these reports that you transmit to us?” He said: “A scroll we found.”

Abū Bakr related to us; Sufyān related to us, from Ibn Shubrumah, from al-Ḥasan, who said:

“I entered upon him and was distressed; I left, and my distress only increased. O God, to You I turn with this young man about whom we used to speak. Why do I hear no voice and see no companion? Young lads, bewildered—what has become of them? If we inform them, they do not understand; if we keep silent, we leave them to grievous error. By God, were it not for what God has charged the people of knowledge with regarding their knowledge, we would not have informed them of anything.”

Ibn Numayr related to us; Abū Bakr related to us, from Mughīrah ibn Ḥafṣ, who said: Ibn Sīrīn was asked and said: “I saw it as though al-Jawzāʾ had moved ahead of the Pleiades.” He said: “This means al-Ḥasan will die before me; then I will follow him, and he is of higher rank than I.”

Salamah related to us; ʿAbd al-Razzāq related to us; Maʿmar informed us, who said: ʿAmr ibn Dīnār said:

“Is Abū al-Shaʿthāʾ more learned among you, or al-Ḥasan?” I said: “What do you say? Some of our people claim that al-Ḥasan is more learned than Ibn ʿAbbās!” He said to me: “Was al-Ḥasan anything but one of Ibn ʿAbbās’s pupils?” I said to him: “And was Abū al-Shaʿthāʾ anything but one of al-Ḥasan’s pupils?” He said: “In our view, he is not more learned than him.” I said to Maʿmar: “Abū ʿUrwah, you have gone too far.”

He said: “He went too far.”

Abū Bishr related to us; Saʿīd ibn ʿĀmir (12a) related to us, who said: I heard my grandfather Asmāʾ relate: Al-Ḥasan said: “The believer dies every kind of death.” He put on his clothes, took up his whip, put his foot in the stirrup, and placed his hand on the pommel of his saddle, then died.49

Abū Bishr related to us; Saʿīd ibn ʿĀmir related to us, who said: I heard Yūnus ibn ʿUbayd. Al-Ḥasan ibn Abī Jaʿfar said to him—al-Ḥasan and Muḥammad had been mentioned in his presence: “What happened between him and Abū al-ʿĀliyah was that he came to the market looking for a garment. He came to me, and I brought out a good garment for him and took the dirhams. He went away and showed it to them. They said: ‘This is better than your dirhams.’ He came back and said: ‘Return our dirhams to us, may God bless you.’ So I returned the dirhams to him and took back the garment.”

Abū Bishr related to me; Saʿīd ibn ʿĀmir related to us, from Asmāʾ ibn ʿUbaydah, who said: I sat with al-Ḥasan in his gathering, sat with him alone, and sat with him in a group. I never saw him desire worldly things, and I never saw him laugh—he would only smile—except on one day. A man came and said: “Abū Saʿīd, my wife asked me to buy her a silk veil, and I dislike buying her silk, so I gave her its price.” Al-Ḥasan said: “You dislike buying it for her, yet you give her its price!” And he laughed.

Saʿīd ibn Asad related to us; Ḍamrah related to us, from a man, from Ibn ʿAwn, from Ibn Sīrīn, who said: He was asked about al-Ḥasan and what the Qadarites were ascribing to him. He said: “They would bring the shaykh ambiguous words; had they explained them to him, they would have regretted it.”

Abū Bishr related to me; Saʿīd ibn ʿĀmir related to us; al-Khazzāz Abū ʿĀmir related to us, from al-Ḥasan, who said: “Whoever disbelieves in predestination has disbelieved in Islam. God has ordained a decree. God created creation according to a decree, apportioned lifespans according to a decree, apportioned provisions according to a decree, apportioned well-being according to a decree, and commanded and forbade.”

Abū Bishr related to us; Saʿīd related to us, from ʿAwf, from al-Ḥasan, with exactly the same wording, except that he said: “And God commanded and forbade.”

Abū Bishr related to me; Wahb ibn Jarīr related to us; my father related to us, who said: I heard Ḥumayd ibn— Hilāl (12b) said: Abū Qatādah said to us: “Stay close to this shaykh”—meaning al-Ḥasan ibn Abī al-Ḥasan—“for, by God, I have never seen a man whose judgment so resembled that of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb as his.”

Abū Bishr related to us; Saʿīd ibn ʿĀmir related to us; Saʿīd related to us, who said: I spoke with Maṭar al-Warrāq about selling muṣḥafs. He said: “Do you forbid me to sell muṣḥafs, when the two leading scholars of this community”—or he said, “its jurists”—“al-Ḥasan and al-Shaʿbī, saw no harm in it?”

Abū Bishr related to me; Saʿīd related to us, who said: I heard Hammām narrating from Maṭar al-Warrāq, who said: “The leading man of the people of Basra was Jābir ibn Zayd. When al-Ḥasan appeared, a man came, as though he had been in the Hereafter and were reporting what he had seen or witnessed.”50

Saʿīd ibn Asad related to me; Ḍamrah related to us, from Ibn Shawdhab, from Maṭar, who said: We visited al-Ḥasan when he was ill. There was nothing in the house—not a bed, rug, cushion, or mat—except a rope-woven couch on which he lay.

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us; Ḥammād related to us, from Ayyūb, who said: Al-Ḥasan said to me:

“Are you not amazed at Saʿīd ibn Jubayr’s opinion? He entered my tent with so-and-so, and he is consulting me about fighting these people!”

Sulaymān related to us; Ḥammād related to us, from Ibn ʿAwn, who said: I asked Muḥammad about something about food on military campaigns. He said: “Ask al-Ḥasan, for he used to go on campaigns.”

Salamah said: Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal said: I think it is from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us; I heard Yaḥyā ibn ʿAtīq say to Ayyūb, when al-Ḥasan was mentioned: “Abū Bakr, do you find anything of what we used to find? If the scholars of the people looked down on us, we looked down on them by means of al-Ḥasan.”

Abū Bakr ibn ʿAbd al-Malik related to me; ʿAbd al-Razzāq related to us, who said: I said to Maʿmar:

“My father told me that Wahb held the judgeship in the time of ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, but his understanding was not praised.” He smiled, then said to me in a voice that seemed scarcely raised: “Al-Ḥasan held the judgeship in the time of ʿUmar, and his understanding was not praised.”

Abū Bakr related to us; ʿAbd al-Razzāq related to us, from Jaʿfar ibn Sulaymān, who said: When people were present, al-Ḥasan was among the most resolute of men; he was the most handsome, the most eloquent, the most generous, and the most articulate of men. (13a) He said: When al-Muhallab fought the polytheists, al-Ḥasan was among the cavalrymen sent forward.

Abū Bakr related to us; ʿAbd al-Razzāq related to us, from Maʿmar, who said: A man said to al-Ḥasan:

“Abū Saʿīd, do you make grammatical errors?” He said: “I outstripped grammatical error.”

Muḥammad ibn Manṣūr al-Ṭūsī related to us; Yaḥyā ibn Abī Bukayr related to us; Ḥammād ibn Salamah informed us, from Ḥumayd, who said: I asked al-Ḥasan about something, and he would nod his head as though saying yes, but he would not say it.

Abū Hāshim Ziyād ibn Ayyūb related to us; Saʿīd ibn ʿĀmir related to us, from Jaʿfar ibn Sulaymān, from ʿAwf, who said: “Muḥammad had sound knowledge, sound judgment, sound knowledge of inheritance law, and sound knowledge of commerce. Yet, by God, I have never seen a man more thoroughly acquainted with the road to Paradise than al-Ḥasan.”

Abū Hāshim Ziyād ibn Ayyūb related to us; Saʿīd related to us; Ḥumayd ibn al-Aswad related to us, who said: I heard Ibn ʿAwn say: “Al-Ḥasan surpassed people only through his renunciation of worldly things. As for knowledge, people shared it with him.”

Abū Hāshim related to us; Saʿīd ibn ʿĀmir related to us, from Muʿtamir ibn Sulaymān, from Yūnus, who said: Al-Ḥasan asked me to buy him a waist-wrapper. I went into the market and saw a waist-wrapper with a man. I asked: “How much?” He said: “Eight dirhams.” I said: “No, seven dirhams.” He said: “Eight.” I said: “No, seven.” [He said: “Seven”] “and a half.” I said:

“No, seven.” He refused to sell it to me. I went into the market, but I saw nothing I thought better than it, so I went back to him and said: “Bring out your scales.” He said: “So I laid out eight [dirhams] for him.”

He said: “Seven and a half.” I said: “The man who sent us to buy this waist-wrapper said: ‘If you buy me anything from the market and there is a shortfall in it, make it up to the seller.’”

The man said: “Then it must be al-Ḥasan.”

Abū Hāshim related to us; Saʿīd ibn ʿĀmir related to us, from one of his companions, who said: Al-Ḥasan’s stipend was withheld. A man came to him with four hundred dirhams, but he returned them to him and said: “I cannot repay you in kind.” Then he said: “Whoever sits in this seat of mine and then takes from people what they know [him to take] has no hope of reverence from God.”

Ibn Abī ʿUmar related to us; Sufyān related to us, from Ayyūb, who said: “No one who heard al-Ḥasan speak could bear the speech of men after him.”

Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥīm related to us; ʿAlī related to us; al-Aṣmaʿī related to us, from Sulaym ibn Akhḍar, from Ibn ʿAwn, who said: “I used to compare the idiom of al-Ḥasan—or al-Ḥasan’s speech—to that of Ruʾbah ibn al-ʿAjjāj”—meaning in eloquence.

Aḥmad ibn al-Khalīl related to us; Shurayḥ ibn al-Nuʿmān related to us; Mahdī ibn Maymūn related to us, from Muḥammad ibn Abī Yaʿqūb, from Muwarriq al-ʿIjlī, who said: Abū Qatādah said to me: “Stay close to this shaykh and learn from him. By God, I have never seen a man whose judgment so resembled that of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb as his”—meaning al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bukayr al-Sahmī related to us; Muḥammad ibn Dhakwān related to me, from Khālid ibn Ṣafwān, who said: I met Maslamah ibn ʿAbd al-Malik at al-Ḥīrah after the death of Ibn al-Muhallab. He said: “Khālid, tell me about the Ḥasan of the people of Basra.” I said: “I am his neighbor, living beside him; I sit with him in his circle and listen to his teaching, and I know him better than anyone on my side.” He was more like of the people, his inner state most closely resembling his outward state, and his words most closely resembling his deeds. If he committed himself to a matter, he carried it through; and if he undertook a matter, he remained committed to it. If he commanded something, he was the person who acted upon it most; and if he forbade something, he was the person who most abstained from it. I found him independent of people, while people were in need of him. He said, “Enough, enough! How could a people go astray when such a man was among them?”—meaning their following Ibn al-Muhallab.

Abū Nuʿaym related to us: Abū Khālid related to us: Abū al-ʿĀliyah was told of al-Ḥasan, and he said, “A Muslim man who commands what is right and forbids what is wrong. We experienced goodness and learned before al-Ḥasan was born.”

Abū Nuʿaym related to us: Abū Khuldah related to us: Anas gave Abū al-ʿĀliyah a mustaḥtaj, and he would cut it with a knife and eat it with bread.

Ibn al-Madīnī said: “Al-Ḥasan did not hear from Mujāshiʿ ibn Masʿūd al-Sulamī, and no sound report from al-Ḥasan is transmitted from ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn through a sound chain. As for the reports of Samurah, they are sound. He heard from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mugh affal, but he did not hear from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās.”

ʿAlī said: “Nor from anyone in Medina, except ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān;” and he did not hear from Jābir.

ʿAlī said: “He would relate to me from the shaykh, saying, ‘He said, he related to me, he informed me,’ and I would be pleased by that. Then he would say, ‘You are pleased by this? Qurrah was not one of those relied upon in this matter.’”

I heard al-Ḥasan say: “I heard Ṣaʿṣaʿah say: ‘This is how it is.’”

ʿAlī said: “Among al-Ḥasan’s companions were Ḥafṣ al-Manqarī, then Qatādah. Ḥafṣ was above him, and Qatādah came after him; also Yūnus and Ziyād al-Aʿlam.

“Ḥafṣ, in relation to al-Ḥasan, was like Ibn Jurayj in relation to ʿAṭāʾ; and Qays ibn Saʿd, in relation to ʿAṭāʾ, was like Ziyād al-Aʿlam in relation to al-Ḥasan. After these came Ashʿath ibn ʿAbd al-Malik, Yazīd ibn Ibrāhīm, and Qurrah—they were a generation, very close to one another. Abū al-Ashhab and Jarīr ibn Ḥāzim were a generation. Abū Ḥurrah and Hishām ibn Ḥassān were a generation in relation to al-Ḥasan. Sallām ibn Miskīn and al-Sarī ibn Yaḥyā were a generation. Abū Hilāl was above Mubārak, and Mubārak is dearer to me than al-Rabīʿ.”

ʿAlī said: “ʿAbd al-Raḥmān struck out the report of Mubārak ibn Faḍālah.”

ʿAlī said: “Some of them said: ‘Hishām ibn Ḥassān got his books from Ḥawshab, and the reports of ʿAṭāʾ on the rites of pilgrimage are from Qays ibn Saʿd.’”

ʿAlī said: “In my view, he is reliable regarding Ibn Sīrīn. Our companions did not disagree about him regarding Ibn Sīrīn. Ismāʿīl ibn ʿUlayyah transmits from him”—meaning from Hishām two reports from al-Ḥasan. ʿAwf heard from al-Ḥasan before the revolt of Ibn al-Ashʿath.

He said: “It reached me that al-Ḥasan was in it.”

ʿAlī said: “Al-Aswad ibn Sarīʿ was [there] before the days of the Battle of the Camel, whereas al-Ḥasan only came to Baṣra after that. Jābir ibn Zayd died about twenty years before al-Ḥasan.”

Al-ʿAbbās ibn Muḥammad related to me: Saʿīd ibn ʿĀmir al-Ḍubaʿī related to us, from Yūnus ibn ʿUbayd, who said: Al-Ḥasan and Ibn Sīrīn were mentioned in his presence, and a man there said of Yūnus:

“Ibn Sīrīn—what a man Ibn Sīrīn was!” Yūnus said, “By God, al-Ḥasan was superior to them both in every respect.”

[Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn]

“It was a book on old parchment, and it was in the possession of Yaḥyā ibn Sīrīn. Muḥammad did not think that a book should be in his possession. At the bottom of the Prophet’s report ﷺ” when he had finished it, was written: “This is the report of Abū Hurayrah”; between them was a divider. “Abū Hurayrah said such-and-such.” He said: “At the divider of every report there was a circle, with dots around it, as though going all around it. Muḥammad did not practice concealment in transmission.”

Sufyān related from ʿĀṣim, who said: “I brought Ibn Sīrīn a book and said, ‘Look through it.’ I asked, ‘May it stay overnight with you?’ but he refused. It was as though he disliked having a book in his possession.”

ʿAlī said: “Umayyah ibn Khālid related to us, from Shuʿbah, who said: Khālid al-Ḥadhdhāʾ said:

“‘These reports that Muḥammad transmits from Ibn ʿAbbās—he only met ʿIkrimah in Kūfah, in the days of al-Mukhtār.’”

Abū Bishr related to me: Saʿīd ibn ʿĀmir related to us, from Asmāʾ, from Anas ibn Sīrīn, who said: “When I was born, I was taken to Anas ibn Mālik. He named me after himself and gave me his teknonym.”

Through the same chain, from Saʿīd ibn ʿĀmir: Mahdī ibn Maymūn related to us, saying: Ḥafṣah spent thirty years without leaving her place of prayer except for the midday rest or to relieve herself.

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to me: Ḥammād related to us, from Shuʿayb, who said to me:

“Keep to that deaf man.”

Salmā related to us, from Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal: ʿAffān ibn Muslim related to us: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, from Yūnus, who said: “Al-Ḥasan spoke in hope of reward, and Muḥammad kept silent in hope of reward.”

Through the same chain, from ʿAffān: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us: ʿĀṣim al-Aḥwal related to us, who said: “I heard Muwarriq al-ʿIjlī say: ‘I have never seen a man more discerning in his scrupulousness, or more scrupulous in his discernment, than Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn.’”

He said: Abū Qilābah said, “Send him wherever you wish; you will find him the most scrupulous of you and the one most in control of himself.”

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us: Sulaym ibn Akhḍar related to us, from Ibn ʿAwn, who said:

ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd said to me—and he was marveling at Ibn Sīrīn’s legal understanding—“Today, the right of pre-emption is not inherited.”

Salmā related to us, from Aḥmad: ʿAffān related to us: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, from Hishām, who said: I heard Muḥammad say, “I have never envied anyone for anything, whether virtuous or wicked.”

“Abū al-Nuʿmān related to us: Ḥammād related to us, from Ayyūb, who said: Abū Qilābah said:

“‘And which of us can endure what Muḥammad endures, as he walks along something sharp as a spearhead?’”

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us: Ḥammād related to us, from Ibn ʿAwn, who related to me from my father, from my grandfather Arṭabān, who said: “I was manumitted and acquired wealth, so I brought its alms-tax to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb. He said, ‘What is this?’ I said, ‘The alms-tax on my wealth.’ He said, ‘Do you have wealth?’ I said, ‘Yes.’

“He said, ‘May God bless your wealth.’ I said, ‘Commander of the Faithful, and my child.’ He said, ‘You have a child?’ I said, ‘I will have one.’ He said, ‘May God bless your wealth and your child.’”

“Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Abī Bakr ibn Anas ibn Mālik, who said: ‘This is the manumission contract of Sīrīn that we have: “This is the agreement Anas ibn Mālik made with his young servant Sīrīn: for such-and-such a sum of thousands, and for two enslaved men who would work as he did.”’”

Sulaymān related to us: Sulaym ibn Akhḍar, the devout and upright, related to us. Sulaymān said:

“Ibn ʿAwn, in relation to [Sulaym], was like Ḥammād in relation to Ayyūb.” He said: “I heard Ibn ʿAwn say, ‘In Baṣra, none of the clients had any standing except Arṭāh and Sīrīn.’” Sulaymān said:

“So I went to ask him what he meant. He said, ‘Sulaymān, are you taking sides with the clients?’”

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us: ʿUmārah ibn Mihrān related to us, who said: Ismāʿīl al-Miʿwalī said to Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn, while I was present, “You command us to pray in congregation, yet you do not pray in congregation.” He replied, “I do not approve of every man.”

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us: ʿUmārah ibn Mihrān related to us, who said: “We were at the funeral of Ḥafṣah daughter of Sīrīn. The bier was set down, and Muḥammad entered the cistern of Ibn Burthum to perform ablution. Al-Ḥasan said, ‘Where is he?’ They said, ‘He is performing ablution.’ He said, ‘Pouring and pouring, rubbing and rubbing—he is tormenting himself and his family.’”

“Sulaymān related to us: Ḥammād related to us, from Hishām ibn Ḥassān, from Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn, who said: ‘Abū al-Walīd took us on pilgrimage; we were seven, the children of Sīrīn. He passed through Medina with us and brought us to Zayd ibn Thābit. He said to him, “These are the sons of Sīrīn.”

“‘Zayd said, “These two are from one mother, these two are from one mother, these two are from one mother, and these two are from one mother.”

“‘He said, “He did not get it wrong.”’ Yaḥyā ibn Sīrīn was Muḥammad’s maternal brother.”

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, from Ayyūb and Ibn ʿAwn, who said: “Yaʿlā ibn Khālid ibn Sīrīn appointed Muḥammad as executor and left behind an enslaved woman who had borne him a child, pregnant. Muḥammad sent to ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Yaʿlā to ask him about her maintenance. He said, ‘It is to come from the child’s share.’ Muḥammad’s view was that it should come from the entire estate.”

“Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmar related to us: Sufyān related to us, who said: I heard ʿĀṣim say:

“‘I wanted to leave with Ibn Sīrīn a book from among the books of knowledge, but he refused to accept it and said, “No book spends the night in my possession.”’”

Ibn Abī ʿUmar related to us: Sufyān related to us, who said: Ayyūb said: “When Ibn Sīrīn was told of the death of one of his brothers, it was as though one of his limbs and one of his supports had fallen away, or something like that.”

Sufyān said: Zuhayr said: “When death was mentioned in Ibn Sīrīn’s presence, each of his limbs would die separately, or one by one.”

Ibn Abī ʿUmar related to us: Sufyān related to us, from ʿĀṣim, who said: “When a man followed Ibn Sīrīn, he would stop until the man had taken care of his need, then continue walking.”

Al-ʿAbbās ibn Muḥammad related to me: ʿAwn ibn ʿUmārah related to us: Hishām ibn Ḥassān related to us, saying: “The most truthful person I encountered among humankind was Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn.”

Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān related to me, saying: I asked ʿAlī, “Who are the most reliable transmitters regarding Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn?” He replied: “Ayyūb, then Ibn ʿAwn, then Salamah ibn ʿAlqamah, then”

Ḥabīb ibn al-Shahīd, then Yaḥyā ibn ʿAtīq, then Hishām ibn Ḥassān. What Yazīd ibn Ibrāhīm al-Tustarī said—“I heard Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn”—is more reliable to me than Khālid al-Ḥadhdhāʾ’s [account]. The wordings of ʿĀṣim al-Aḥwal and Khālid al-Ḥadhdhāʾ regarding Muḥammad are alike; their wordings do not resemble those of their companions.

He said: “I heard Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb lend support to Yazīd ibn Ibrāhīm, affirm his report, and rank him close to Ayyūb.”

ʿAlī said: “Ibn Sīrīn heard from Abū Hurayrah, Ibn ʿUmar, Jundub, and Anas.” I asked him, “And Rāfiʿ?” He replied, “No; nor is there any report heard from Zayd ibn Thābit—except that he saw him when they entered to visit him, and Zayd said, ‘These are from one mother’—ever; he did not memorize anything from him.”

“Al-Faḍl ibn Ziyād related to me: Aḥmad related to us: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Anṣārī related to us: Abū Sufyān related to us, from Muḥammad, who said: ‘Whenever he was asked about a matter of lawful and unlawful jurisprudence, his complexion changed and he became unsettled, as though he were no longer the person he had been.’”

Aḥmad said: Mūsā ibn Hilāl related to us: Hishām ibn Ḥassān related to us, from al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Ziyād, who said: “He used to say: ‘If I were to wish for something, I would wish for al-Ḥasan’s legal understanding, Ibn Sīrīn’s scrupulousness, and the sound judgment of Muṭarrif, and the prayer of Muslim ibn Yasār.’”

Ibn Sīrīn’s sound judgment, and the prayer of Muslim ibn Yasār.

Aḥmad ibn al-Khalīl related to me: Rawḥ ibn ʿUbādah related to us: al-Ḥajjāj al-Aswad related to us, who said: “A man made a wish and said, ‘If only I had al-Ḥasan’s renunciation, Ibn Sīrīn’s scrupulousness, ʿĀmir ibn ʿAbd Qays’s worship, and Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab’s legal understanding,’ and he mentioned something about Muṭarrif—Rawḥ said, ‘I do not know what it was.’ They considered the matter and found all of it complete in al-Ḥasan.”

Aḥmad related to us: Abū al-Ḥasan al-Fusāyiqī said: I heard Ismāʿīl ibn ʿUlayyah say: “We used to think that Yūnus heard it from Ashʿath, and Ashʿath from Ḥafṣ.”

Aḥmad related to me: al-Ḥasan ibn Mūsā al-Ashyab related to us: Ḥammād ibn Salamah related to us, from Thābit, who said: Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn said to me: “Nothing kept me from sitting with you except fear of becoming famous. The affliction kept pursuing me until I was seized by my beard and made to stand on the platform, and it was said, ‘This is Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn; he has consumed people’s property,’ while he had a great deal of debt.”

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us: Ṭawq ibn Wahb said: I went in to Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn when I was ill. He said, “It seems to me that you are ill.” I said, “Yes.” He said, “Go to so-and-so, the physician, and ask him for a prescription.” (16b)

Then he said to me, “Go to so-and-so, for he is more skilled than him.” Then he said, “I ask God’s forgiveness! I see that I have burdened you.”

Saʿīd ibn Asad related to me: Ḍamrah related to us, from Rajāʾ, from Ibn ʿAwn, who said:

I saw Ibn Sīrīn looking for a garment. I travelled, then returned, and he had not bought it. He would inspect its knot and the material. Al-Ḥasan was not like that: he would place his hands on the garment, then say, “How fine this is!”

Saʿīd related to me: Ḍamrah related to us, from Rajāʾ, from Ibn ʿAwn, who said: Ibn Hubayrah sent for Ibn Sīrīn, and he went to him. He asked him, “How did you leave the people of your town?”

He replied, “I left them with injustice widespread among them.” Ibn ʿAwn said: It seemed that Muḥammad considered this testimony for which he would be questioned, and so he disliked concealing it.

Saʿīd related to me: Ḍamrah related to us, from Ibn Shawdhab, from Ayyūb, who said: A man came to Ibn Sīrīn and said, “Abū Bakr, I have spoken ill of you. Will you absolve me?” He replied, “I dislike making lawful what is forbidden.”

“Al-Muʿallā ibn Asad related to us: Abū ʿAwānah related to us, saying: I saw Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn pass through the market by the sugar sellers, and whenever he passed a group, they would glorify God and remember God.”

Muslim ibn Ibrāhīm related to us: Abū ʿAwānah related to us, saying: I saw al-Ḥasan come out of the maqṣūrah on the Day of ʿArafah, after the afternoon prayer. He sat down, and was recognized.

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us: Ḥammād related to us, from Ayyūb, who said: Muḥammad said, “I see people daring to give legal opinions on the basis of their own judgment. I think that, if the Qurʾān were being revealed, it would have been revealed contrary to what they give as legal opinions.”

Muḥammad ibn Abī Usāmah al-Ḥalabī related to us: Ḍamrah related to us, from al-Sarī ibn Yaḥyā, who said: Ibn Sīrīn would laugh until he fell back.

Saʿīd ibn Asad related to us: Ḍamrah related to us, from Ibn Shawdhab, who said: Ibn Sīrīn married an Arab woman and disliked marrying the mawālī, because they were liable to be taken captive. Ibn ʿAwn went and tried to imitate him, but the Arabs would not let him get away with it. They brought him before Bilāl ibn Abī Burdah ibn Abī Mūsā al-Ashʿarī, who beat him and separated the two of them. He said to him, “Divorce her.”

He said, “She is divorced.” The man said, “Three times.” He replied, “One, which makes her irrevocably divorced.”

He said, “I say ‘three times’ to him, and he makes her irrevocably divorced.” He said to him, “Divorce her.” He replied, “She is divorced three times.” The man said, “One.”

He said, “I say ‘three times’ to him, and he gives me a legal opinion that she is divorced.”

Saʿīd related to us: Ḍamrah related to us, from Ibn Shawdhab, who said: Ibn Sīrīn would laugh until he fell back.

Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥīm al-Daylī related to us: Ḍamrah related to us: al-Sarī related to us, saying: Ibn Sīrīn gave up forty thousand dirhams of profit because he had doubts about it, and so he left it.

He said: I heard Sulaymān al-Taymī say, “I have not heard of anyone among the people of knowledge having doubts about it.”

Salamah related to us, from Aḥmad: ʿAbd al-Razzāq related to us, from Maʿmar, from Ayyūb, from Muḥammad, who said: “I used to hear a ḥadīth from ten people: the meaning was one, but the wording differed.”

Abū Bishr related to me: Muʿādh related to us: Ibn ʿAwn informed us, saying: Muḥammad had one fixed price.

Abū Bishr related to us: Saʿīd ibn ʿĀmir related to us, saying: I heard Hishām ibn Ḥassān say: Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn left forty thousand dirhams tied up in something that people today see no harm in.

Saʿīd ibn Asad related to us: Ḍamrah related to us, from Rajāʾ, who said: Al-Ḥasan would go to the authorities and criticize them, whereas Ibn Sīrīn would neither go to the authorities nor criticize them.

[Abū Qilābah al-Jarmī]

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us: Ḥammād related to us, from Ayyūb, from Muslim ibn Yasār, who said: “If Abū Qilābah had been a non-Arab, he would have been a mōbedh mōbedhān.”

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us: Ḥammād related to us, from Ayyūb, from Abū Rajāʾ, the client of Abū Qilābah, who said: Abū Qilābah was with ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, who asked them about qasāmah. Abū Qilābah recited a lengthy ḥadīth. ʿAnbasah ibn Saʿīd said, “Glory be to God!” Abū Qilābah said, “Do you suspect me, ʿAnbasah?” He replied, “No, but this army will continue to prosper so long as God keeps you among them.”

Saʿīd ibn Asad related to me: Ḍamrah related to us, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamlah, who said: Muslim ibn Yasār came to Damascus, and they said to him, “Abū ʿAbd Allāh, had God known that there was anyone in Iraq better than you, He would have brought him to us.” He kept saying, “If only you had seen ʿAbd Allāh ibn Zayd al-Jarmī, Abū Qilābah!” Days and nights passed, and then God brought Abū Qilābah to us.

Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad related to us: al-Ḥārith ibn ʿUmayr related to us, from Ayyūb, from Abū Qilābah, who said: “The judge is like a man swimming in the sea: how long can he swim before drown?” He said: Abū Qilābah was sought out for the judgeship, so he fled.

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, from Ayyūb, from Abū Qilābah, who said: “I stayed in Medina for three days, and I had no reason to be there except for a man who was away at an estate of his. I had heard a ḥadīth from him, and waited for him to arrive so that I could ask him about it.”

Sulaymān related to us: Ḥammād related to us, from Ayyūb, from Abū Qilābah, who said: “Some young men went away from us before the plague. Their families said to me, ‘If only you would speak to them.’ I said, ‘Leave them; perhaps they will die with their friends.’” Then the plague came, and they all died.

He said: ʿAlī ibn al-Madīnī said: “The name of Abū al-Muhallab was ʿAmr ibn Muʿāwiyah.”

“Abū Bishr related to me: Saʿīd ibn ʿĀmir related to us: Ṣāliḥ ibn Rustum related to us, saying: Abū Qilābah said to Ayyūb, ‘When God gives you new knowledge, respond with a new act of worship for God. Do not let your only concern be to tell people about it.’”

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us: Ḥammād related to us, from Ayyūb, from Abū Qilābah, who said: Umm al-Dardāʾ related to me that Abū al-Dardāʾ would come after morning had broken and ask, “Do you have breakfast?” If he found none, he would say, “Then I am fasting.”

By the same chain, from Ayyūb, who said: Abū Qilābah would observe retreat in the mosque of his people. He would not have a mat or anything else laid out for him there; he would sit to one side. On the night of the Feast of Breaking the Fast, he would stay there until he went in the morning to his prayer ground from the place where he had observed retreat.

No mat or anything else would be laid out for him there; he would sit to one side. On the night of the Feast of Breaking the Fast, he would stay there until he set out in the morning for his prayer ground from the place where he had observed retreat.

Ayyūb said: I went to him in the morning on the day he broke his fast. In his lap was an adorned young girl, whom I thought was his daughter. He embraced her, then went on to the prayer ground.

Abū ʿUmar al-Namirī related to us: Ḥammād related to us. Ayyūb said: “I found that the people most knowledgeable about judging were the people most averse to it and most fearful of it.” Then he said, “I never met anyone more knowledgeable about judging than Abū Qilābah—I do not know what Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn was like.” He would be pressed to take up the judgeship, so he would flee to Syria one time and to al-Yamāmah another. When he came to Basra, he would stay as though in hiding until he left.

Abū al-Nuʿmān related to us: Ḥammād related to us, saying: Ayyūb claimed that Abū Qilābah fell ill in Syria, and ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz came to visit him. He said, “Abū Qilābah, be strong; do not give the hypocrites cause to rejoice over us.”

[Ḥumayd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Ḥimyarī]

“...a streamlet.” He said: Al-Ḥasan replied, “A nobleman, a prophet.” Ḥumayd said, “Abū Saʿīd, it means a streamlet.” Al-Ḥasan said, “The rulers have got the better of you.”

Saʿīd related to us (18a): Abū ʿAwānah related to us, from Qatādah, from al-Ḥasan, that he recited, “Your Lord has placed beneath you a streamlet.” He said, “It was a streamlet, and it was, and it was.” Ḥumayd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Ḥimyarī said to him, “Abū Saʿīd, it means a streamlet.” He said, “The rulers have got the better of you.”

ʿĪsā ibn Muḥammad related to us: Azhar informed us, from Ibn ʿAwn, from Muḥammad, who said: Ḥumayd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said, “I would rather return it, unable to answer, than pretend to know what I do not know.”

Salamah related to us, from Aḥmad: Ḥajjāj related to us: Shuʿbah related to us, from Manṣūr ibn Zādhān, from Ibn Sīrīn, who said: “For ten years before his death, Ḥumayd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Ḥimyarī was the most learned in jurisprudence among the people of Basra.”

[Ḥassān ibn Abī Sinān]

Saʿīd ibn Asad related to me: Ḍamrah related to us, from Rajāʾ ibn Abī Salamah, who said:

I said to Ḥassān ibn Abī Sinān, “Do you ever imagine yourself in poverty?” He said, “Yes.” I said:

“Then I tell it: ‘My soul, if that happens, you will take the spade and sit with the laborers, and earn…”

“...a dāniq or two dāniqs, and live on that, and then you will be content.”

Ibn Shawdhab said: Ḥassān ibn Abī Sinān was a merchant from among the people of Basra. He had a business partner in Basra, while he himself resided in al-Ahwāz, sending goods to his partner in Basra. At the end of every year they would meet, settle their accounts, and divide the profit. He would take his living expenses from his share of the profit and give the rest in charity, while his partner built a house and acquired lands. He said: Ḥassān came to Basra once and distributed what he intended to distribute. Someone mentioned to him a household whose need had not become apparent. He said, “Why didn’t you tell us?”

He borrowed three hundred dirhams for them and sent it to them.

[ʿĀmir ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Qays al-ʿAnbarī]

“Saʿīd related to us: Ḍamrah, from Rajāʾ ibn Abī Salamah, from Ibn ʿAwn and Ibn Sīrīn, said: Ḥumrān, the client of ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān, brought ʿĀmir ibn ʿAbd Allāh, who was known as Ibn ʿAbd Qays, before Ziyād. He said, ‘He does not eat meat and does not marry women. He was called, “O likeness of Abraham,” and he fell silent.’ Ḥumrān disputed with him in Ziyād’s presence. Ḥumrān said to him, ‘May God not increase the beatings you give us!’ ʿĀmir said to him, ‘Rather, may God increase the beatings you give us, until you become tailors, tanners, and cobblers.’ Ibn Sīrīn said: ‘That is the sort of beating: when they speak, this comes from them’—meaning, when they get angry.”

ʿAmr ibn ʿĀṣim related to us: Hammām related to us, from Qatādah, who said: ʿĀmir ibn ʿAbd Allāh asked his Lord to make ritual purification easier for him in winter. Water would then be brought to him with steam rising from it. He asked his Lord to remove desire for women from his heart, and he became indifferent to whether he met a man or a woman. He asked his Lord to place a barrier between Satan and his heart during prayer, but He could not do that. When he went on a military campaign, people would say to him, “This thicket is dangerous for you; there may be a lion in it.” He would reply, “I would be ashamed before my Lord to fear anyone besides Him.”

ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān related to us: ʿAbd Allāh informed us: Jaʿfar ibn Ḥayyān informed us, from Ṭarīf ibn Shihāb, who said: I mentioned to al-Ḥasan ʿĀmir’s saying, “For spears to cross in me is dearer to me than to experience what you describe”—that is, during prayer. Al-Ḥasan said:

“God has not subjected us to that.”

ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān related to us: ʿAbd Allāh informed us: Ibn ʿAwn informed us, from Muḥammad, from Maʿqil ibn Yasār, who said: “The first time I came to know ʿĀmir ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-ʿAnbarī was when I…”

“I saw him”—he described a place near Raḥbat Sulaym—“and he was riding an animal while a man from among the protected non-Muslims was being wronged. He forbade them, but when they refused, he said, ‘By God, you are lying! God’s protected status shall not be violated today while I am a witness.’ He dismounted (19a) and rescued him.

“After that, I went to him at his home. People used to say that ʿĀmir did not eat meat, did not marry women, did not touch anyone’s skin, and used to say, ‘I am like Abraham.’ When I went in to him, he took his hand out from beneath his burnus and took my hand. I said, ‘That is one [of the claims disproved].’ When we had talked for a while, I said, ‘People say that you do not eat meat or ghee, do not marry women, and say, “I am like Abraham.”’ He said, ‘As for their claim that I do not eat meat, these people have done something with the slaughtered animals, and I do not know what it is. So, when I crave meat, we get a sheep bought for us, slaughter it, and eat its meat. As for their claim that I do not eat ghee, I do not eat what comes from this direction, but I eat what comes from that direction. As for their claim that I do not marry women, it is only one soul, and it has almost overcome me. As for their claim that I said, “I am like Abraham,” I did say, “I hope that God will place me among the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs, and the righteous.”’

ʿĪsā ibn Muḥammad related to me: Azhar related to us, from Ibn ʿAwn, from Muḥammad, from Maʿqil ibn Yasār, who said:

“The first time I became acquainted with ʿĀmir ibn ʿAbd Allāh, I met him among the protected Christians. A man from Kūfa had sat down to speak with them, asking them to release him. ʿĀmir turned aside with his mount and dismounted. He said, ‘By God, you have lied. Today God’s protected covenant shall not be violated while I am a witness.’”

He said: “He kept at them until he got him away.
