People accused him of those traits, saying, ‘He does not eat clarified butter or meat; he does not let anyone touch his skin; he does not pray in mosques; he does not marry women; and he says, “I am like Abraham.”’ I went to him while he was sitting in the mosque, and he took my hand and shook hands with me.” He mentioned something similar, and added:

“As for their claim that I do not pray in mosques, when Friday comes I go and pray the Friday prayer with the people. Then I prefer to pray afterward here.”

ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān related to us: ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mubārak informed us: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd informed us: Bilāl ibn Saʿd related to me that ʿĀmir ibn ʿAbd Qays had been reported to Ziyād—another says: Ibn ʿĀmir—and they said, “There is a man here who is called: ‘Abraham is no better than you,’” yet he remained silent. He had also given up women. They wrote about him to ʿUthmān, who wrote back to him, “Exile him to Syria on a packsaddle.”

When the letter reached him, he sent for ʿĀmir and said, “Are you the one who was told, ‘Abraham is no better than you,’ and kept silent?” He replied, “By God, I was silent only out of astonishment. I would have wished to be dust beneath his feet, so that he might carry me into Paradise.”

He said, “Why have you given up women?” He replied, “By God, I have given them up only because I know that—”

“Whenever there is a wife, there may be a child; and whenever there is a child, worldly affairs will divide my heart. So I preferred to withdraw from that.”

He exiled him to Syria on a packsaddle. When he arrived, Muʿāwiya lodged him in the Green Palace and sent him a slave girl, instructing her to find out what he was like. He would go out at dawn and she would not see him again until after nightfall. Muʿāwiya would send him his food, but he would not touch any of it. He would bring some pieces of bread with him, put them in water, eat some, and drink the water. Then he would stand and remain there until he heard the call to prayer. He would go out, and she would not see him until the same time the next day.

Muʿāwiya wrote to ʿUthmān, telling him about ʿĀmir’s condition. ʿUthmān wrote back, “Have him be the first to enter and the last to leave, and assign him ten slaves and ten mounts.” When Muʿāwiya received the letter, he sent for ʿĀmir and said, “The Commander of the Faithful has written to me, ordering that I give you ten slaves.”

ʿĀmir said, “I have one devil who has overcome me; how could I take ten more upon myself?”

Muʿāwiya said, “He has also ordered that I give you ten mounts.”

ʿĀmir said, “I have only one mule with me, and I fear that God, mighty and majestic, will ask me on the Day of Resurrection to account for its excess capacity.”

[Muʿāwiya] said, “He has ordered me to have you be the first to enter and the last to leave.”

ʿĀmir said, “I have no need of that.”

Bilāl ibn Saʿd related to us, from someone who had seen ʿĀmir in Roman territory, riding that same mule in relays and carrying the emigrants in relays.

Bilāl ibn Saʿd also related to us that when ʿĀmir set out on a campaign, he would look over the traveling parties. If he saw a party that suited him, he would say, “O people, I wish to join you on the condition that you grant me three things from among yourselves.”

They would ask, “What are they?”

He would say, “I will serve you, and none of you will dispute the service with me; I will be the caller to prayer, and none of you will dispute the call to prayer with me; and I will spend on you according to my means.”

If they agreed, he would join them. If any one of them disputed with him over any of that, he would depart from them and go to another party.

Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr related to us: Khalaf ibn Khalīfa related to us: a man from Baṣra called Isḥāq related to me, from ʿAnbasa al-Khawwāṣ, who said:

“When ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĀmir arrived in Baṣra as its governor, he said, ‘People of Baṣra, name for me one man of the Qurʾān reciters for every five of you, so that I may consult them about my affairs, seek their help in what God has entrusted to me, and let them in on my confidential matters.’

They named for him Abān ibn Maṭar al-ʿAdawī, who had wept until he lost his sight; Ghazwān, a man of Banū Ruqāsh, who had sworn never to laugh until he knew where God would place him; Jābir ibn Usayd of Ghaṭafān; ʿĀmir ibn ʿAbd Qays al-ʿAnbarī; and al-Nuʿmān ibn Shawwāl al-ʿAbdī.

When they entered his presence, he said to them, ‘You are the Qurʾān reciters. I have assigned each of you two thousand and such-and-such an amount of land measured in jarībs.’

Al-Nuʿmān ibn Shawwāl answered him—leave him to answer, for he was the oldest of the group. He said, ‘O Commander, is this for us alone or for the people of Baṣra generally?’

He said, ‘For you alone. This wealth cannot suffice for the people of Baṣra.’

Al-Nuʿmān said, ‘Then you call it charity? If it is charity, it will not enter our bellies or cover our skins. The official receives only the wages for his work, and we have no need of it.’

He said, ‘It seems I am an abusive man, driving out those who are with me.’

Al-Nuʿmān said to him, ‘You have not known me to be one who visits rulers.’

Then he turned to ʿĀmir and said, ‘I have assigned you two thousand and such-and-such an amount of land measured in jarībs.’

ʿĀmir said, ‘Look at the scribes at the mosque gate. They are poorer than I am.’

He said, ‘I have undertaken that no door will be closed to me.’

ʿĀmir said, ‘You should go to Saʿd ibn Qarḥāʾ; he frequents rulers’ courts more than I do.’

He said, ‘Look—any woman you might wish for, I will marry you to her.’

ʿĀmir said, ‘O Commander, when a man has a wife and a child, that occupies his heart.’

He said, ‘Yes.’

ʿĀmir said, ‘Then I have no need of it. I will make my concern one concern until I meet my Lord.’

He said, “Any woman you might wish for, I will marry you to her.”

ʿĀmir said, “O Commander, when a man has a wife and a child, that occupies his heart.”

He said, “Yes.”

ʿĀmir said, “Then I have no need of it. I will make my concern one concern until I meet my Lord.”

“I found that the affairs of this world come down to four things: wealth, women—and I have no need of wealth or women—sleep, and food. By God, if I were able, I would make both of them difficult for myself.”

ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān related to us: ʿAbd Allāh informed us: al-Sarī ibn Yaḥyā informed us, from al-Ḥasan, who said:

“ʿĀmir said to some people who were talking about this world, ‘And yet you are so concerned with it! By God, if I am able, I will make it one single concern.’”

He said: “By God, he did so, until he joined God.”

He said: “ʿAbd Allāh also informed us: Maʿmar informed us: Muḥammad ibn Wāsiʿ related to me, from Abū al-ʿAlāʾ Yazīd ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Shikhkhīr. Ibn ʿĀmir ibn ʿAbd Qays informed me that ʿĀmir—”

“Would take his stipend and place it in the edge of his garment. Whenever one of the poor met him, he would give it to him. When he entered his house, he would throw it to them, and they would count it and find that it was exactly as he had received it.”

ʿĪsā ibn Muḥammad related to us: Azhar informed us, from Ibn ʿAwn, from Muḥammad, who said:

“Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī wrote to ʿĀmir ibn ʿAbd Qays:

‘In the name of God, Most Gracious, Most Merciful. From the servant of God to ʿĀmir ibn ʿAbd Allāh, who is called ʿAbd Qays.

‘To proceed: I knew you to be committed to a certain course. If you remain as I knew you, then fear God and persevere. If you have changed, then fear God and return.’”

ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān related to us: ʿAbd Allāh informed us: Jaʿfar ibn Sulaymān related to us, from al-Jurayrī, who said:

“A man came to ʿĀmir ibn ʿAbd Qays and said, ‘Pray to God for me.’

“He replied, ‘You have come to a man who is incapable of helping himself. But obey God, my nephew, and God will forgive you.’”

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us: Ḥammād related to us, from Hishām, from al-Ḥasan, who said:

“ʿĀmir ibn ʿAbd Allāh said, ‘I found that this world consists of four traits: women, clothing, food, and sleep. As for women, by God, I care no more about whether I see a woman or a wall. As for clothing, by God, I care no more about what covers my nakedness. As for food and sleep, they have overcome me; but if I can manage it, by God, I will make them difficult for myself as much as I can.’”

Al-Ḥasan said: “By God, he did so.”

[By God, he did so.]

[Abū Dāwūd al-Aʿmā]

ʿAmr ibn ʿĀṣim related to us: Hammām related to us, saying:

“We were with Qatāda when Nufayʿ, Abū Dāwūd al-Aʿmā, came in. When he left, one of those present said to Qatāda, ‘This man claims that he met eighty men who had pledged allegiance beneath the tree, and such-and-such a number of men who fought at Badr.’”

Qatāda said, “I encountered him as a boy asking ʿAbd ibn ʿĀmir. He used to sit with him. He cast himself into destruction, and he told him so.” Abū Hurayra said, “No! Rather, he was seeking this verse: ‘And among the people is one who sells himself, seeking God’s good pleasure; and God is kind to His servants’ (2:207).”

[Ṣila ibn Ashyam]

ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān related to us: ʿAbd Allāh informed us: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd ibn Jābir informed us, saying:

“It reached us that the Messenger of God ﷺ used to say, ‘There will be in my community a man called Ṣila ibn Ashyam, through whose intercession such-and-such a number will enter Paradise.’”

ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān related to us: ʿAbd Allāh informed us: Jarīr ibn Ḥāzim related to us: Ḥumayd ibn Hilāl related to us, from Ṣila ibn Ashyam al-ʿAdawī, who said:

“I went out to some of the villages along the Nahr Tīrī, riding my mount in a time of flooding. I was traveling along the water embankment, and I traveled for a day without finding anything to eat, until my hunger became severe.”

He said: “Then I met—”

“a foreigner carrying something on his neck. I said, ‘Put it down.’ He put it down, and there was bread. I said, ‘Give me some of it to eat.’ He said, ‘Yes, if you wish, but it is pig fat.’”

He said: “When he said that, I left it and went on. Then I met another man carrying food on his neck, and I said, ‘Give me some to eat.’

“He said, ‘I have provisioned myself with this for such-and-such a day. If you take any of it, you will harm me and leave me hungry.’

“I left it and went on. By God, I was traveling when I heard behind me a thud like the fluttering of birds—that is, the sound of their flying. I turned around, and there was something wrapped in a white sibb—that is, a head covering. I dismounted and found a small basket of dates, at a time when there was not a single fresh date on earth. I ate some of them; I had never eaten dates more delicious. I drank some water, then wrapped up what remained, mounted the horse, and carried their pits with me.”

He said: “Awfā ibn Dulham related to me, saying, ‘I saw that sibb with his wife; her codex was wrapped in it. Then it went missing, and after that no one knew whether it had been stolen, gone away, or what had become of it.’”

Saʿīd ibn Asad related to me: Ḍamra related to us, from Ibn Shawdhab, who said:

“Ṣila ibn Ashyam used to go by day to the cemetery and pray there. He would pass a group sitting together, moving from one patch of shade to another. When this had gone on for some time, for him and for them, he stopped by them, greeted them, and then said, ‘What do you think, may God have mercy on you, of a people traveling on a journey who have covered ground by day and slept at night? When will these people arrive?’”

They said, “No—when indeed!”

Then he went on. One of them said, “Woe to you! By this he meant no one but us. May God never see us in this gathering again!”

He said: “Saʿīd ibn Asad related to me: Ḍamra related to us, from Ibn Shawdhab, who said: Muʿādha al-ʿAdawiyya said, ‘Ṣila would come from the mosque in his house to his bed only crawling. He would stand [in prayer] until he could no longer remain steady.’”

“We went on a campaign to Kabul, and Ṣila ibn Ashyam was in the army. At nightfall, the people went to rest. I said, ‘I shall watch what he does, to see what people say about his worship.’

“He prayed the night prayer, then lay down, waiting for the people to become inattentive. When their eyes had grown quiet [that is, when they had settled down], he sprang up and entered a nearby thicket. I followed him. He performed ablution, then stood to pray and began [the prayer].

“He said: A lion came and drew near him, so I climbed a tree. He said: He saw it, turned toward it, or turned a jerboa away from him, then prostrated. I said, ‘Now it will devour him.’ But nothing happened. He sat up, then gave the salutation and said, ‘O beast, seek your provision somewhere else.’”

“He turned away, and his roar was such that I thought the mountains would split from it. Ṣila continued praying in this way until dawn. Then he sat and praised God with praises such as I had never heard, except as God wills. He then said, ‘O God, I ask You to protect me from the Fire. Would a man like me dare ask You for Paradise?’ Then he returned. In the morning, he looked as though he had spent the night on soft cushions, while I was left with a weakness that God alone knows.”

He said: “When we drew near enemy territory, the commander said, ‘Let no one stray from the army.’ His mule went off with his baggage, and he began to pray. They said to him, ‘The people have gone.’ He went on, then said, ‘Let me pray two rakʿas.’

“They said, ‘The people have gone.’ He went on, then said, ‘Let me pray two rakʿas.’

“They said, ‘The people have gone.’

“He said, ‘They are only two short ones.’

“He made a supplication, then said, ‘O God, I adjure You to return my mule and its baggage to me.’

“He said: It came and stopped before him. When we met the enemy, he and Hishām ibn ʿĀmir charged them with thrusts, blows, and slaughter. The enemy was routed, and they said, ‘Two Arabs have done this to us; what would it have been like if they had fought us!’ Then they gave the Muslims what they wanted. Abū Hurayra was asked, ‘Hishām—’”

Muṭarrif ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Shikhkhīr

“I heard Muṭarrif say, ‘It is as though hearts are not with us, and as though this report—’”

“—is meant for anyone but us.”

Abū al-Nuʿmān related to us: Mahdī ibn Maymūn related to us: Ghaylān related to us, saying:

“Muṭarrif used to wear cloaks with hoods and maṭārif, ride horses, and frequent the ruler’s court. Yet when you got close to him, you came upon a delight to the eye.”

Al-Ḥajjāj ibn al-Minhāl related to us: Mahdī related to us: Ghaylān related to us, saying:

“Muṭarrif said, ‘The fear of the Fire nearly kept me from asking God for Paradise.’”

Abū al-Nuʿmān and Saʿīd related to us, saying: Mahdī related to us: Ghaylān related to us, saying:

“Muṭarrif used to say, ‘A sound heart, sound deeds, and sound intention.’”

Abū al-Nuʿmān related to us: Mahdī related to us: Ghaylān related to us, saying:

“I heard Muṭarrif say, ‘I have found the son of Adam to be like something cast between God and Satan. If God wills to revive him, He will draw him to Himself; but if He wills otherwise for him, He leaves him between himself and his enemy.’”

Through the same chain, from Muṭarrif, who said: “If someone came to me from my Lord and gave me the choice between being told whether I am in Paradise or in the Fire, and becoming dust, I would choose to become dust”.

Al-Ḥajjāj related to us; Mahdī related to us; Ghaylān related to us, from Muṭarrif, who said: “I heard him say:

“If I am granted well-being and give thanks, that is dearer to me than being tested and showing patience”. He said: “I considered well-being and found in it the good of this world and the Hereafter.”

ʿAmr ibn ʿĀṣim related to us; Sulaymān ibn al-Mughīrah related to us; Ḥumayd ibn Hilāl related to us, who said: Muṭarrif said: “What good is there that has no evil and no affliction? Everything has an affliction. So it is that a servant is granted well-being and gives thanks.”

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us, who said: Muṭarrif said: “There was a time when the best people were those who hastened; the best people of your time, however, are those who proceed deliberately”.

Sulaymān related to me, and a companion of mine related to me, who said: Muṭarrif said: “All people are foolish in their dealings with God, but some foolishness is less grievous than other kinds.”

He said: Sulaymān said: A companion of ours related to us, who said: Muṭarrif said: “If only I had two souls, so that I could learn from one of them—but I have only one soul”.

Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr related to us; Abū ʿAwānah related to us, from Qatādah, from Muṭarrif ibn— ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Shikhkhīr, who said: “The merit of knowledge is dearer to me than the merit of worship, and the best of your religion is scrupulous piety”.

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us; Abū Hilāl related to us; Abū Ṣāliḥ al-ʿUqaylī related to us, who said:

Abū al-ʿAlāʾ used to read from the codex until he would faint.

Sulaymān related to us; Ḥammād related to us, from Saʿīd al-Jarīrī, who said: Abū al-ʿAlāʾ used to read from the codex. He said: Muṭarrif would sometimes say: “Let this codex of yours suffice you for the rest of the day”.

He said: I heard Abū al-Nuʿmān say: Muṭarrif used to say: “If I am granted well-being and give thanks, that is dearer to me than being tested and showing patience”.

He said: Abū al-ʿAlāʾ used to say: “O God, if something is to happen, then hasten it.”

Abū al-Nuʿmān said: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us; Ayyūb related to us, from Abū al-ʿAlāʾ, who said: “I set out to perform the lesser pilgrimage. When I was at al-Dathnūmah, I fell from my riding camel and broke [a bone]. So I sent for Ibn ʿUmar and Ibn ʿAbbās. They asked about it and said: ‘It has no fixed period like the period of the pilgrimage; he is to remain in his state of consecration until he reaches the House.’ I remained in that condition for six or seven months, until I reached the House.”

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us; Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, from Saʿīd al-Jarīrī, from Abū al-ʿAlāʾ, who said: “When I broke [a bone], I sent Muṭarrif to Ibn ʿUmar to ask him. He said: ‘What do you say about my brother?’ He replied: ‘What can I say? If he dies in this state of his, he will enter Paradise.’”

[Ṣafwān ibn Muḥriz]

Al-Muʿallā ibn Asad related to us; Jaʿfar related to us; Hishām ibn Ḥassān related to us, from al-Ḥasan, from Ṣafwān, who said: “When I eat a loaf that strengthens my back and drink a jug of water, then upon this world—”

—and its people, ruin.”

Al-Muʿallā and Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Raqāshī related to us; they said: Jaʿfar related to us; al-Muʿallā ibn Ziyād al-Firdawsī related to us, who said: Ṣafwān had a secluded place where he would weep. Ṣafwān used to say: “I can see the place of martyrdom, if only my soul would accompany me”.

[Muslim ibn Yasār]

ʿĪsā ibn Muḥammad related to us; Azhar informed us, from Ibn ʿAwn, who said: No one was considered superior to Muslim ibn Yasār in that time, until he did that deed. Abū Qilābah met him and said: “By God, I will never do it again.” Abū Qilābah replied: “God willing.”

Abū Qilābah recited: “It is only Your trial: by it You lead astray whom You will” (Qurʾān 7:155). Muslim’s eyes began to flow with tears.

ʿĪsā ibn Muḥammad related to us; Azhar informed us, from Ibn ʿAwn, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muslim ibn Yasār, that his father, when he prayed, seemed as though he wished not to say this or that.

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us; Sulaymān ibn al-Mughīrah related to us, from Ḥumayd ibn Hilāl, who said: When Muslim ibn Yasār stood to pray, he was like a garment cast down.

Saʿīd ibn Asad, Abū ʿUmayr, and Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz al-Ramlī related to us; they said: Ḍamrah related to us, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamlah, who said: “I heard Muslim ibn Yasār, and he heard a man praying against someone who had wronged him. Muslim said to him: ‘Leave the wrongdoer to his wrongdoing, for it will reach him more swiftly than your prayer against him—unless he is overtaken by a deed and [the following wording is corrupt]’”51

Abū Bishr related to me; Saʿīd ibn ʿĀmir related to us, who said: Ḥumayd Abū al-Aswad related to us, from Ibn ʿAwn, who said: “I found this mosque in a state where there was no study circle in it in which jurisprudence was discussed except the circle of Muslim ibn Yasār.” He said: “There were people in the circle older than him, but it was attributed to him.”

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us; Ḥammād related to us, from Ayyūb, who said: Ibn al-Ashʿath was told: “If you would like people to be killed around you as they were killed around ʿĀʾishah’s camel, take Muslim ibn Yasār with you.” So he took him along against his will.

Ḥammād ibn Zayd said: Ayyūb mentioned the poor men who went out with Ibn al-Ashʿath and said: “I know of none of them who was killed but that he would have preferred to be spared his place of death; and none of them who escaped but that he regretted what he had done.” He said: Abū Qilābah accompanied Muslim ibn Yasār. He said: “Abū Qilābah, I give thanks to God in your presence that I did not thrust a spear in it nor struck with a sword in it, nor shot an arrow at them.” He said to him: “Abū ʿAbd Allāh, what of the one who saw you standing and said, ‘This is Abū ʿAbd Allāh; by God, he would not have taken this stand unless he were in the right,’ then went forward and fought until he was killed?” He said: “He wept until I wished I had not said anything”.

Abū ʿUmayr related to us; Ḍamrah related to us, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamlah, who said: “When Muslim ibn Yasār came to us, we said to him: ‘Abū ʿAbd Allāh, had God known that there was anyone in Iraq better than you, He would have sent him to us.’ He said: ‘What if you had seen ʿAbd Allāh ibn Zayd, Abū Qilābah al-Jarmī?’

“Days and nights passed, and then Abū Qilābah came to us.

“ʿAlī said: Ibn [Abī] Idrīs said to his father: ‘Father, aren’t you impressed by how long Abū ʿAbd Allāh Muslim ibn Yasār remains silent?’ He said: ‘My son, speaking the truth is better than keeping silent about it.’ He went to Muslim and told him. Muslim said: ‘My son, keeping silent about falsehood is better than speaking it’”.

Abū Bishr Muʿādh ibn Hishām related to us; my father related to me, from Qatādah, who said: Muslim ibn Yasār, Abū ʿAbd Allāh, was counted as one of the five leading jurists of the people of Basra.

Salamah related to us, from Aḥmad; Ismāʿīl related to us; Khālid al-Ḥadhdhāʾ informed us, who said:

Abū Qilābah mentioned ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shaqīq and said: “What a man he is—except that he became a Bedouin.”

“Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us; Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, from Ayyūb, from Muḥammad, who said: I said to ʿUbaydah: ‘May I write down from you what I hear?’ He said: ‘No.’ I said: ‘May I consult a book I have found?’ He said: ‘No’”.

He said: Ḥammād related to us, from Ayyūb, who said: “I found in Abū Qilābah’s book, from Anas: ‘If one of you becomes drowsy while praying, let him sleep until he understands what he is saying.’”

Sulaymān said: In another place, from Ayyūb, from Abū Qilābah, he said: Ḥammād said:

“Jarīr ibn Ḥāzim read a book of Abū Qilābah’s to Ayyūb. He said: ‘I heard all of this from Abū Qilābah. Some of it I have memorized, and some I have not.’” He said: Sometimes Ḥammād would relate something to us and say: “This is what was in the book.”

“Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us; Ḥammād related to us, who said: Abū Qilābah died in Syria and bequeathed his books to Ayyūb. Ayyūb sent for them, and they were brought, a camel-load. Ayyūb said:

“When they came to me, I said to Muḥammad: ‘Abū Qilābah’s book has come to me. Shall I relate from it?’ He said: ‘Yes.’ Then he said: ‘I neither command you nor forbid you’”.

Salamah related to us, from Aḥmad; Ismāʿīl related to us; Ayyūb related to us, who said: “Abū Qilābah bequeathed his books to me. I brought them from Syria and was given a little over ten dirhams for their transport”.

“Abū al-Nuʿmān Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, who said: Abū Qilābah bequeathed [his books] and said: ‘Give my books to Ayyūb if he is alive; otherwise, burn them’”.

Muḥammad ibn Manṣūr related to us; Yaḥyā ibn Abī Bukayr related to us; Ḥammād ibn Salamah related to us, from Ḥumayd, who said: He took al-Ḥasan’s books, copied them, then returned them to him.

ʿAlī ibn al-Madīnī said: Wahb ibn Jarīr related to us, from his father, who said: “Yaʿlā ibn Ḥakīm wrote to me: ‘Ask Qatādah about a hadith, then write to me.’ I went to him, and he said: ‘Go to Saʿīd ibn Abī ʿArūbah, for he has taken down my hadiths and will dictate them to you. Then bring them to me.’ I went to Saʿīd, and he dictated them to me. Then I brought them to Qatādah, and he changed only two words.”

ʿAlī said: Each of them would have his own messengers who came to Qatādah. Saʿīd’s messengers were Maṭar, and Hishām al-Dastawāʾī’s messenger was Abū ʿAmr ibn ʿĀmir.

ʿAlī said: Yaḥyā said: “The first to come to me in this matter was Abū ʿUbaydah al-Ḥaddād; before him, it was Ḥasan al-Juʿfarī, during the lifetime of Ibn Abī Jurayj.”

He said: I heard Bakr ibn Khalaf mention, from one of the shaykhs of the people of Basra—and I think it was about this—that Ḥammād ibn Salamah said: “I used to hear that the storytellers did not retain their hadiths. So I went to Thābit al-Bunānī and mixed up his hadiths for him. I would ask him: ‘How does the hadith of Anas about such-and-such compare with the hadith of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā?’

“He would say: ‘No, this is the hadith of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān.’ Then I would ask: ‘How does the hadith of Ibn Abī Laylā about such-and-such compare with the hadith of Anas?’ He would say: ‘This is the hadith of Anas.’”

He said: I heard Abū Mūsā say: “They call Ḥumayd ibn Tirawayh by that name, and they are angered by it.”

[Madhʿūr and Muṭarrif]

ʿAmr ibn ʿĀṣim related to us; Sulaymān ibn al-Mughīrah related to us; Ghaylān ibn Jarīr related to us, who said: Muṭarrif said: “Whenever two people love one another for God’s sake, the one who loves his companion more is the better of the two.” He said: I mentioned this to al-Ḥasan, who said: “Muṭarrif speaks truly.”

He said: Ghaylān said: Muṭarrif said: “I love Madhʿūr more, and he is better than I am—so what is this?” When the group was ordered to go to Syria, Madhʿūr was ordered to go with them. He said: “He met me and took hold of my riding animal’s bridle. Whenever I wanted to leave, he would hold me back.” He said: “I told him: ‘The place is far away.’” He kept holding me back.

He said: “I said: ‘I adjure you by God, will you not let me go and stop holding me back?’ When I adjured him, he said a phrase, concealing it from me as best he could: ‘O God, for Your sake.’ When morning came, he was asked: ‘Did you feel as though your brother had been taken away?’ He said: ‘Then I realized that he loved me more than I loved him.’”

ʿAmr ibn ʿĀṣim related to us; Sulaymān related to us, from his father, who said: Madhʿūr used to come to us and say: “Come to the remembrance of God.” A man from the tribe said: “Do we have a Friday sermon from Madhʿūr every single day?” He said: I mentioned that to Thābit, and he was pleased by it.

ʿAmr related to us; Sulaymān related to us, from his father, who said: Madhʿūr had two sisters, Umm Ṣafiyyah and Hunaydah. Umm Ṣafiyyah would care for orphans and the poor, while Hunaydah was a devout woman. He said: When he was about to be taken away, she said to him: “Give us your advice.” He said: “Act as though you have already—”

ʿAmr related to us; Sulaymān related to us; Qatādah related to us, who said: Muṭarrif ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Shikhkhīr said: “Madhʿūr used to visit us, and our family would rejoice at his coming.”

ʿAmrū narrated to us; Sulaymān narrated to us (25a); Thābit narrated to us. He said: Muṭarrif ibn ʿAbd Allāh said, “If anyone in this community has a heart tested and proven, then Madhʿūr has a heart tested and proven.”

ʿAmrū narrated to us; Sulaymān narrated to us; Ayyūb al-Sakhtiyānī narrated to us. He said: When that group of men was sent to Syria, Madhʿūr, ʿĀmir ibn ʿAbd Qays, and Ṣaʿṣaʿah ibn Ṣūḥān were among them. When their innocence became clear, they were ordered to return. Some of them returned, while Madhʿūr and ʿĀmir were among those who stayed. Ṣaʿṣaʿah ibn Ṣūḥān was among those who went down.

ʿAmrū narrated to us; Sulaymān narrated to us. He said: Thābit said to me, “I love you because of my love for Madhʿūr,” or, “I used to visit you because of Madhʿūr.”

ʿAmrū narrated to us; Sulaymān narrated to us; Thābit narrated to us. He said: Muṭarrif said, “One day, while I was with Madhʿūr, a man suddenly said, ‘These two are among the people of Paradise.’” He said: Madhʿūr looked at him, and I saw displeasure on his face. Then he raised his gaze to the sky and said, “O God, let us know, but do not make us known. O God, let us know, but do not make us known”—three times.

Saʿīd ibn Asad narrated to me; Ḍamrah narrated to us, from Rajāʾ ibn Abī Salamah, from Muṭarrif ibn al-Shikhkhīr. He said: When ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir entered Baṣrah on the day of the Camel, I sat with him, and he began denouncing ʿUthmān. I said to him, “You are the Companions of Muḥammad; you preceded us in companionship, then we caught up with you. You taught us that no sin in Islam is greater than denouncing another, yet today you make it lawful.” He said: Then a messenger from ʿAlī came to him and said, “Answer the Commander of the Faithful, Abū al-Yaqẓān. He says that he [ʿUthmān] changed [the religion].”

[Al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Ziyād and Bushayr ibn Kaʿb]

Saʿīd narrated to us; Ḍamrah narrated to us, from [Ibn] Abī Ḥamlah. He said: “I have not seen an Iraqi better than al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Ziyād ibn Maṭar al-ʿAdawī.”

[Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī narrated to us; Sufyān narrated to us; ʿAmrū narrated to us. He said: Ṭāwūs said to me, “Come, let us sit with people.” He said: We sat with a man from Baṣrah called Bushayr ibn Kaʿb al-ʿAdawī. Ṭāwūs said, “I saw this man come to Ibn ʿAbbās and begin telling him reports. Ibn ʿAbbās said, ‘It is as though I hear the report of Abū Hurayrah.’”]

Abū Bishr Bakr ibn Khalaf narrated to us; Wahb narrated to us; my father narrated to us. He said: I heard Ḥumayd ibn Hilāl [relating] from al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Ziyād (25b). He said: “In a dream I saw people following something, so I followed it. There was an old woman, one-eyed and toothless, adorned with every kind of finery and jewelry. I said, ‘Who are you?’ She said, ‘I am this world.’ I said, ‘I ask God to make you hateful to me.’”

She said, “Yes—if you hate the dirhams.”

[Iyās ibn Muʿāwiyah]

“Every hundred years a man of complete intelligence is born.” They considered Iyās ibn Muʿāwiyah to be one of them.”

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī and Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā narrated to us; they said: Sufyān narrated to us. He said:

I heard Ibn Shubrumah say: They said to Iyās ibn Muʿāwiyah, “You are impressed with your own judgment.”

He said, “If I were not impressed with my judgment, I would not rule by it.”

Saʿīd ibn Asad narrated to me; Ḍamrah narrated to us, from Rajāʾ ibn Abī Salamah. He said: Ibn al-Ahtam said to Iyās ibn Muʿāwiyah, “Were it not for certain traits in you, you would be the man.” He said, “And what are they?” He said, “You give judgment before you understand; you do not care whom you sit with; and you do not care what you wear.”

He said, “As for your saying that I judge before I understand: which is greater in number, three or two?” He said, “Three, of course.” He said, “How quickly you understood!” He said, “Who would not understand that?” He said, “Just so: I do not give judgment until I understand. As for your saying that I do not care whom I sit with, I would rather sit with someone who regards me as good than with someone whom I regard as good. As for your saying that I do not care what I wear, I would rather wear a garment that protects me than wear a garment that I must protect with my own person.”

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb narrated to us; Ḥammād ibn Zayd narrated to us. He said: Iyās ibn Muʿāwiyah and al-Ṣalt ibn Dīnār were in Ayyūb’s gathering. Whenever Ayyūb related something, Iyās would not let him continue without interrupting him. When he had finished, al-Ṣalt would start to relate something, and Iyās would say to him, “Be quiet.”

And he continued speaking. He said: Al-Ṣalt said, “You do not even let me swallow my saliva and take a breath.” Iyās said, “This man has a wife who treats him badly.” He said: The man replied, “You are right.” Iyās said:

“Your bad temper comes from that: you left home annoyed and distressed, and your bad temper comes from that.”

Sulaymān narrated to us again (26a), in Baṣrah. Ḥammād ibn Zayd narrated to us. He said:

“We were at Ayyūb’s place, and Iyās ibn Muʿāwiyah and al-Ṣalt ibn Dīnār were there. Iyās began speaking, and al-Ṣalt kept making excuses to him so that he could speak when Iyās had finished. Iyās struck his thigh with his hand and said, ‘Be quiet!’ Al-Ṣalt said to him, ‘Swallow your saliva; let me take a breath.’ Iyās said, ‘Do you see this man? His wife has a bad temper.’”

He said: Al-Ṣalt replied, “By God, you are right: she has a bad temper. How did you know?” He said:

“You left her while she was treating you badly; that is the source of your bad temper now.”

Sulaymān narrated to us; ʿUmar ibn ʿAlī ibn Muqaddam narrated to us, from Sufyān ibn Ḥusayn. He said: I was with Iyās ibn Muʿāwiyah, and there was a man with him whom I feared would speak ill of me if I left. So I stayed until he got up. When he had left, I mentioned him to Iyās. Iyās kept looking at my face and said nothing until I had finished. Then he said to me, “Have you campaigned against Daylam?” I said, “No.” He said, “Have you campaigned against Sind?” I said, “No.” He said, “Have you campaigned against the Romans?” I said, “No.” He said, “Daylam, Sind, India, and the Romans are safe from you, but your brother here is not?” Sufyān did not do that again.

Sulaymān narrated to us; ʿUmar ibn ʿAlī ibn Muqaddam narrated to us, from Sufyān ibn Ḥusayn. He said:

Iyās ibn Muʿāwiyah was asked, “Is the scholar better, or the devout worshipper?” They said, “Tell us, so that we may know.”

He said: He replied, “Do you not see this?” Sulaymān mentioned something that I did not understand: “This one comes to learn plastering, this one carries bricks, and this one is a laborer. At midday, a drink made from parched grain is brought and drunk. At night, each man is given a dirham, while this one is given four or five dirhams.”

Saʿīd ibn Asad narrated to me; Ḍamrah narrated to us, from Ibn Shawdhab. He said: I heard Iyās ibn Muʿāwiyah say, “People do not know their own faults. I know my own fault: I am a man who talks too much.” And so he was: when he sat in a gathering, he was usually the one who spoke most.

Ḍamrah said: I heard someone say, “Abū Iyās used to say: ‘People were born as sons, but I was born a father.’”

(29a) Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb narrated to us; Ḥammād narrated to us, from Ibn ʿAwn. He said: Muḥammad mentioned Iyās ibn Muʿāwiyah and said, “He is indeed intelligent, he is indeed intelligent.”

[ʿUqbah ibn ʿAbd al-Ghāfir]

[Mālik ibn Dīnār]

Fahd ibn Ḥayyān narrated to us; Muḥammad ibn Yazīd narrated to us. He said: I heard al-Taymī say: “I never knew anyone who was more ascetic toward this world than Mālik ibn Dīnār.”

Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Raqāshī narrated to us; Jaʿfar narrated to us, from Mālik. He said:

“I was ill until I became delirious.” He said: “I remained lucid during that. Al-Ḥasan came in to visit me, along with so-and-so and so-and-so. I said, ‘Abū Saʿīd, if I were not afraid it would be an innovation, I would instruct my family, when I die, to bury me with a rope, as is done with a runaway slave.’ Al-Ḥasan said, ‘Your companion is raving.’” He said: Mālik said, “Then God restored me to health.”

He said: “I was sitting with al-Ḥasan among his family when he said to me, ‘O man with the rope, in a shelter beneath the earth.’ He turned to me and began admonishing me, and he was a teacher.”

[Shahr ibn Ḥawshab]

“Ibn ʿAwn would mention no one except Shahr ibn Ḥawshab, for he used to say, ‘Shahr …’”

“They have abandoned him, abandoned him.”

Al-ʿAbbās ibn Muḥammad narrated to me; Yaḥyā ibn Abī Bukayr narrated to us, from his father. He said: Shahr was in charge of the public treasury, and I took a pouch containing dirhams. The poet said:

“Shahr has sold his religion for a pouch—

Who, after you, will trust the Qurʾān reciters, O Shahr?”

Muḥammad narrated to me. He said: I heard ʿAlī say: Ibn ʿAwn related the report of Hilāl ibn Abī Zaynab, from Shahr, from Abū Hurayrah: The martyrs were mentioned in the presence of the Prophet ﷺ and Shuʿbah whispered it to him, but Ibn ʿAwn did not mention him.

Aḥmad ibn al-Khalīl narrated to me; Abū al-Naḍr narrated to us; ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn Bahram narrated to us. He said: I heard reports from Shahr ibn Ḥawshab at Khawlān in the year one hundred.

[Thābit al-Bunānī]

They said to him, “What did you see of the gardens?” He said, “I saw nothing that impressed me except that I saw a woman praying.”

Saʿīd ibn Asad narrated to us; Ḍamrah narrated to us, from Ibn Shawdhab. He said: I heard Thābit al-Bunānī say, “O God, if You have granted anyone of Your creation that he should pray to You in his grave, grant it to me.”

Muḥammad ibn Manṣūr narrated to us; ʿAffān narrated to us; Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us. He said: “I used to reverse the isnād for Thābit, and he would say, ‘No, this one is from so-and-so; this one is from so-and-so.’”

Salamah narrated to us; Aḥmad narrated to us, from someone he mentioned, from Ḥammād ibn Zayd. He said:

I heard ʿAlī ibn Zayd mention Yūsuf ibn Mihrān and say, “His memorization was likened to that of ʿAmr ibn Dīnār.”

(29b) Al-Faḍl ibn Ziyād narrated to us; Aḥmad narrated to us; Ḥasan ibn Mūsā narrated to us; Abū Hilāl narrated to us; Qatādah narrated to us. He said: “Among the people of Baṣrah, they did not consider anyone more learned than Ḥumayd ibn Hilāl.”

Aḥmad ibn al-Khalīl narrated to me; Yaḥyā ibn Ayyūb narrated to us; ʿAbbād ibn ʿAbbād al-Muhallabī narrated to me. He said: We heard that Shuʿbah had spoken critically of Ayyūb and Khālid. He said: Ḥammād ibn Zayd and I went to him and said, “We have heard something from you. Beware of saying anything about those two, lest you ruin yourself.” He said: “So he stopped.”

Yaḥyā ibn Ayyūb said: A man among the senior scholars of ḥadīth heard these words from ʿAbbād—I dislike naming him—and spoke with me about them in this way. Then later I heard that he had added to the report. He said: Then Shuʿbah resumed criticizing the two of them, so we went to him and spoke with him about it. He said, “I have no choice but to do so.” Yaḥyā ibn Ayyūb said: “This criticism was not about them; it was about the case of Abān ibn Abī ʿAyyāsh. He forgot and attached it to the case of these two. He is a man whose word is accepted, so I disliked contradicting him. I thought Yaḥyā ibn Ayyūb was alluding to Ibn Maʿīn.”

[Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī]

Through the same chain, from Shuʿbah, from Hushaym, from Mughīrah, from Ibrāhīm—as far as I know—concerning a man who said to his wife, “You are not my wife”: He said, “That does not count.” He said: Al-Shaʿbī said:

“Even less than this is counted as divorce.”

ʿUqbah ibn Mukram narrated to us; Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿAdī narrated to us; Shuʿbah related to us, from Hushaym, from Mughīrah, from Ibrāhīm. He said: If a man says to his wife, “Go and marry…”

“...,” he said, “that does not count.” Al-Shaʿbī said, “Even less than this is counted as divorce.”

Through the same chain, from Ibrāhīm, who said: They used to say, “When the heat becomes severe, prostrate on a man’s back”—meaning during Friday prayer (30a).

Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Ḥammād; Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿUqbah—who is Ibn Abī Thābit al-Rāsibī, a reliable transmitter—from Abū al-Jawzāʾ: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb forbade women to spend the night without performing the ʿishāʾ prayer, for fear they might menstruate. He meant the ʿishāʾ prayer.

Bundār narrated to us. He said: Abū Dāwūd said: “Al-Ḥasan ibn ʿImrān is Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-ʿAsqalānī.”

Bundār narrated to us; Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, from Abū al-Fayḍ. He said:

“I met Abū Qirṣāfah, a man among the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ and asked him”—meaning about fasting while traveling. Maslamah ibn ʿAbd al-Malik used to say, “Whoever fasts Ramaḍān while traveling must make it up while resident.” Abū Qirṣāfah said, “I fasted while traveling; then I continued fasting, and I did not make it up.”

Bundār narrated to us; Abū Dāwūd narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, from Yazīd ibn Ḥumayd. He said: I heard— Sālim ibn Abī al-Jaʿd narrates from Ibn ʿAbbās concerning the Black Stone.

Bundār related to us: Muḥammad ibn Shuʿayb related to us, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh, the client of Juhaynah—namely Mūsā al-Juhanī.

Bundār related to us: Muḥammad related to us, from Shuʿbah, from Ghaylān ibn Jarīr, who said: I heard Abū al-Ḥalāl al-ʿAtakī say: “Ibn ʿĀmir sent me to ʿUthmān on an errand. When I had finished, he said: ‘Do you have a request?’”

Bundār related to us: Ibn Abī ʿAdī related to us, from Shuʿbah, from Sulaymān ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Rāshid ibn Yasār, who had been a slave of ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Marwān. Al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib bought him and freed him.

Bundār related to me: Yaḥyā and Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿAdī related to us, from Shuʿbah, who said:

I heard Ṭalḥah [say]: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwsajah said: “I had forgotten…”

“Adorn the Qurʾān with your voices”—until al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Muzāḥim reminded me of it.

[Bundār related to us, from Abū Dāwūd, from Shuʿbah, from Abū Balj, from ʿAmr ibn Maymūn, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr, who said: “A time will surely come upon Hell when its gates will rattle and no one will be inside it.”

Abū Dāwūd said: “ʿAlī ibn Salamah related to us, from Thābit, who said: ‘I asked al-Ḥasan (30b) about this report, and he rejected it.’”]

And from Muḥammad, from Shuʿbah, from ʿĀmir ibn Shaqīq ibn Jamrah. Shuʿbah said:

Sufyān informed me, from him, that he said: “This is what you should do with a foundling.”

Al-Ushnānī, al-Rabīʿ al-Marʾī, related to us: Shuʿbah related to us, from Abū Jaʿfar, from Muslim Abū al-Ḥasan, from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: “In the time of the Messenger of God ﷺ, the call to prayer was said twice and the commencement of prayer once each, except that he would say, ‘The prayer has begun’ twice.”

Bundār related to us. Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar said: Shuʿbah said: “I heard only this one report from Abū Jaʿfar.”

Abū Mūsā related to us: Yaḥyā ibn Abī Bukayr related to us, from Shuʿbah, who said: “We were at the funeral of Ṭalḥah ibn Muṣarrif. Abū Miʿshar praised him and said: ‘He left no one like himself.’”

[Bundār related to us, from Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar, Ghundar, and Ibn Muʿādh, from his father, from Shuʿbah, who said: “I heard al-Ashʿath al-Athram before he became confused.”]

Bundār related to us, from Muḥammad, from Shuʿbah, who said: “I heard ʿUthmān, the client of Ibn ʿUqayl al-Thaqafī—he is ʿUthmān ibn al-Mughīrah, and he is ʿUthmān al-Aʿmash.”

Bundār related to us, from Muḥammad, from Shuʿbah, from Ibrāhīm ibn Maymūn, who said: “I heard Abū al-Aḥwaṣ relate from ʿUrwah ibn al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah, from ʿĀʾishah, that a man came in to the Prophet ﷺ and mentioned another man in his presence. He said: ‘What a wretched servant of God, a brother of the clan!’ Then that man came in to him, and he turned toward him with his face, until I thought that the man held a standing with him.” Shuʿbah said: “Or, until it seemed as though the man held a standing with him.”

Abū Mūsā related to us, from ʿAbd al-Wahhāb and ʿAbd al-Aʿlā, from Dāwūd. ʿAbd al-Wahhāb said: “from Qushayr ibn ʿUmar”; ʿAbd al-Aʿlā said: “from Qushayr ibn ʿĀmir.” ʿAbd al-Wahhāb and ʿAbd al-Aʿlā, from Dāwūd, from al-Qāsim ibn ʿUmar, said—; and Ḥammād ibn Salamah said, from…

Dāwūd, from al-Qāsim ibn So-and-so, said—; and ʿAbd al-Aʿlā said: “From Dāwūd, from Suwayd ibn Ḥujayr,” who said—; and Abū Muʿāwiyah said: “From Dāwūd, from Abū Qazʿah Ḥujayr ibn Bayān.” Dāwūd said:

“From Abū Hunaydah Ḥurayth ibn Mālik.”

Al-Ḥajjāj related to us: Ḥammād related to us, from Dāwūd, from ʿAmmār, a man from Syria (31a), who said: “We trained, and there was an old man among us.” Abū Mūsā said: “He is ʿAmmār ibn ʿUbayd.”

Abū Mūsā related to us: Ibn Abī ʿAdī related to us, from Ḥumayd, from Abū ʿUthmān al-Nahdī, who said: “I was in Madīnah with Abū Hurayrah. The city was in an uproar, so I said: ‘What is the matter with them?’ They said: ‘Are you not one of the people of this town?’ I said: ‘No.’ They said: ‘You are right. If you were one of the people of this town, you would have known: Abū Saʿīd has died.’”

Abū Mūsā related to us: Ghundar related to us, from Shuʿbah, who said: Ḥamzah al-Aʿwar, Abū ʿUmārah ibn Ḥamzah, related to me. He said: Muḥammad also related to us: Shuʿbah related to us, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from Abū al-Bukhtarī, from ʿAlī, who said concerning the “forbidden”, the “irrevocable”, the “separated”, and the “released”…

and the “free” three times each. Shuʿbah said: “Waraqāʾ told me that he relates it from Zādhān. I met ʿAṭāʾ and asked him: ‘Who related it to you from ʿAlī?’ He said: ‘Abū al-Bukhtarī.’”

Abū Mūsā and Bundār related to us. He said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān related to us, from Shuʿbah, from al-Haytham: “Murrah used to pray two hundred cycles every day.”

Abū Mūsā related to us: Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿAdī related to us, from Shuʿbah, from Ḥabīb, who said: “I was informed about ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Miswar, so I met him in the year ninety and asked him.”

He said: “We stayed with Saʿd in a village of the villages of Syria called Nuʿmān. I would pray four…” and pray two cycles. I asked him about that, and he said: “We know better.”

Abū al-Walīd related to us: Shuʿbah related to us, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, who said: “When the Day of al-Jamājim came, they wanted to appoint Abū al-Bukhtarī as their commander. Abū al-Bukhtarī said: ‘I am a client, so appoint a man from the Arabs.’ They did so.”

Bundār related to me: Abū Dāwūd related to us: Shuʿbah related to us, who said: “I asked ʿAmr ibn Murrah: ‘Tell me, do you know Uways al-Qaranī among your people?’ He said: ‘No.’”

Bundār related to us: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar related to us, from Shuʿbah, from Furāt, from a client of Umm Salamah, who said: Umm Salamah said: “When Saʿd died and his bier was brought in to her, she began to weep and say: ‘A target for the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ!’”

(31b) And from Shuʿbah, from Furāt, who said: “I heard Abū Ḥāzim say: ‘I kept company with Abū Hurayrah for five years.’”

And from Shuʿbah, from Zayd ibn al-Ḥuwārī al-Aʿmā.

Bundār related to us: Muḥammad related to us, from Shuʿbah, who said: “I heard ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿImrān, a shaykh among the finest shaykhs, from Abū al-ʿAshīr, the client of Umm Salamah, who said: ‘I came as a courier from Sijistān to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, wearing a fur cloak with long sleeves. He either struck it or forbade him.’”52

Bundār related to us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and Muḥammad, from Shuʿbah, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Asʿad ibn Zurārah, who said: “I heard ʿUmar, and I have not seen a man among us who resembled him.”

Bundār related to us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Shuʿbah, from Muḥammad ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, who said: “ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz said to me: ‘Write down for me ʿAmrah’s hadith.’ ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz used to ask her.”

Bundār related to us, from Muḥammad, from Shuʿbah, from Ḥudhayfah—who is Abū al-Yamān—who said: “I saw al-Shaʿbī raise the whip over his boy and say: ‘This is the hardest blow I have ever struck one of my boys.’”

And from Muḥammad, from Shuʿbah, from the son of the brother of Muṭarrif ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Shikhkhīr, whose name is ʿAbd Allāh ibn Hāniʾ, from Muṭarrif.

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Bundār related to us, from Abū Dāwūd, from Shuʿbah, from Mishāsh, who said: “Al-Ḍaḥḥāk heard nothing from Ibn ʿAbbās.”

And from Abū Dāwūd, from Shuʿbah, from ʿAbd al-Malik (32a) ibn Maysarah, who said: “Al-Ḍaḥḥāk met Saʿīd ibn Jubayr only in al-Rayy, and heard tafsīr from him.”

Bundār related to us: Muslim ibn Qutaybah related to us: Shuʿbah related to us, from Yūnus ibn ʿUbayd, who said:

“Al-Ḥasan heard nothing from Abū Hurayrah.”

Bundār related to us: Umayyah ibn Khālid related to us: Shuʿbah related to us, who said: “I was with Abū Isḥāq al-Hamdānī when someone said to him: ‘Shuʿbah says that you heard nothing from ʿAlqamah.’ He said:

‘He speaks the truth.’”

Bundār related to us: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd related to us: Shuʿbah related to us, from Ismāʿīl ibn Rajāʾ, from al-Maʿrūr ibn Suwayd, who said: “I heard ʿUmar say: ‘People, hasten along, for we have found that the proper pace is haste.’”

Bundār said: “I heard ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, and he was asked about this report. He said: ‘I heard it from Shuʿbah, but it is an objectionable report.’”

Bundār related to us: Muḥammad related to us, from Shuʿbah, from Ayyūb, from Ibn Sīrīn, from his father, who prepared food and invited some of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, among them Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, who came while fasting.

Bundār related to us: Abū al-Walīd related to us: Shuʿbah related to us: “Ayyūb is the master of the jurists.”

Bundār related to us: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān related to us, from Shuʿbah, who said: “I heard ʿAlī ibn Zayd, who used to fabricate reports.”

Bundār related to us: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān related to us: Shuʿbah related to us, who said: “I heard al-Ḥasan ibn Abī al-Ḥasan say: ‘Whenever a caller cries out, they follow him.’”

Bundār related to us: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar related to us, from Shuʿbah, who said: “I saw al-Ḥasan wearing a black turban.”

And from Muḥammad, from Shuʿbah, from Ziyād ibn Mikh­rāq, who said: “I heard Qays ibn ʿUbāyah, Abū Naʿāmah al-Qaysī, relate from a client of Saʿd, from a son of Saʿd, a report about supplication.”

Bundār related to us: Yaḥyā—and I asked him about this report. Shuʿbah related to us: Ziyād ibn Mikh­rāq related to me, from Abū Naʿāmah Qays ibn ʿUbāyah, from a son of Saʿd, from Saʿd. I said to Yaḥyā: “Abū Saʿīd, they have contradicted you in the chain of transmission of this report.” Yaḥyā said: “I do not have this report in a book.”

Bundār related to us: Abū Dāwūd and Sālim related to us. They said: Shuʿbah related to us (32b), from Abū Isḥāq, who said: Ḥudhayfah said: “A heart of gold.”

Bundār related to us: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar related to us: Shuʿbah related to us, from Hushaym, from Abū Bishr, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and ʿIkrimah, concerning His words: “You will be called to fight a people of great might”. He said: “Hawāzin and Banū Ḥanīfah.”

Bundār related to us: Ibn Abī ʿAdī related to us, from Shuʿbah, from Qays ibn al-Rabīʿ, from Abū Ḥuṣayn, from Khālid ibn Saʿd, from Abū Masʿūd, that he disapproved of the pilfering of sugar.

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Muʿādh related to us: My father related to me: Qurrah related to us, who said: “The spirit of a woman from our family was taken up for some days. Nothing prevented them from burying her except that a vein was still moving. Then she spoke and said:

‘What happened to Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr?’ Jaʿfar had died during those days when she was unconscious. We said: ‘He died.’ She said: ‘By God, I saw him. I was in the seventh heaven, and suddenly they were saying: “The one called al-Mujashshar has come! The one called al-Mujashshar has come!” Then there was Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr in his shrouds.’”

[Bundār related to us: Muḥammad and Abū ʿĀmir related to us, from Shuʿbah, from Abū Ṣadaqah, who is Sulaymān ibn Kindīr.]

Bundār said: “I asked ʿAbd al-Raḥmān: ‘Is Sulaymān ibn Kindīr Abū Ṣadaqah al-ʿIjlī?’”

He said: “Yes.”

Bunḍār related to us: Muḥammad related to us, from Shuʿba, from ʿAbd al-Malik al-Zarrād, from Kurdūs, who used to preach.

Bunḍār related to us: Azhar related to us, from Ibn ʿAwn, who said: “I saw Kurdūs, who was the preacher of the people of Kūfa.”

Bunḍār related to us, from Muḥammad, from Shuʿba, from Abū al-Azhar Ṣāliḥ ibn Dirham.

Bunḍār related to us: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān related to us, from Shuʿba, from Abū Ḥuṣayn, who said: “ʿUbayda al-Salmānī instructed that al-Aswad ibn Yazīd perform the funeral prayer over him. It was near sunset, and he feared that al-Mukhtār would perform the prayer over him, so he hastened and performed it over him.”

Muḥammad ibn Bashshār related to us: Muḥammad related to us, from Shuʿba, who said: “I heard Abū Miʿshar, who narrates from Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī, say: ‘There is no town without someone through whom its people are protected, and I hope that Abū Wāʾil is one of them.’”

Bunḍār related to us: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān related to us: Shuʿba related to us, from Mughīra: It was said to Ibrāhīm:

“Abū Wāʾil performs the prayer on a carpet.” He said: “Abū Wāʾil is better than that.”

Bunḍār related to us: Wahb related to me: Shuʿba related to us, from Ziyād ibn ʿAlāqa, from Usāma ibn Sharīk, the brother of Banū Thaʿlaba ibn Saʿd.

Abū Mūsā related to us: Abū ʿĀmir ʿAlī ibn al-Mubārak related to us, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, who said: Qayluwayh, whose kunya was Abū Ṣāliḥ, related to me: “A man from among the hunters owed me twenty dirhams, and he began giving me gifts. Whenever he gave me [a gift …]—until, when his gifts amounted to thirteen dirhams, I went to Ibn ʿAbbās and asked him. He said:

‘Count thirteen for him and take seven.’”

Ḥumayd al-Ṭawīl is Ibn Tayrawayh; his kunya is Abū ʿUbayda. Abū ʿUbayda al-Nājī, the preacher, is Bakr ibn Abī al-Aswad.

Sawwār ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sawwār related to me, from Muʿāwiya ibn ʿAbd al-Karīm, a trustworthy Basran.

Ibn Rajāʾ related to us: Abū Rajāʾ al-Kalbī related to us; he is a trustworthy shaykh.

Ashʿath ibn ʿAbd al-Malik al-Baṣrī is trustworthy.

Ashʿath ibn Sawwār is weak.

Al-Ḥumaydī related to us, from Sufyān, that he criticized him, deemed him weak, and preferred not to narrate from him.

Ādam related to us, from Ashʿath ibn Saʿīd Abū al-Rabīʿ al-Sammān; his hadith is worthless.

[His hadith] is worthless.

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us: Ḥawshab ibn ʿAqīl related to us—his kunya was Abū Daḥya, and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī narrated from him. I heard Ṣadaqa ibn al-Faḍl, to whom the hadith of Ḥawshab ibn ʿAqīl was mentioned: that the Prophet ﷺ forbade fasting on the Day of ʿArafa at ʿArafa. He praised Ḥawshab and said: “Who related this hadith to you?”

They said: “Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb.” He said: “From whom did he relate it to you—from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān?”

They said: “No. Sulaymān heard it from Ḥawshab.” He said: “He is an old shaykh.”

Ibn Qaʿnab related to us: Juhayr ibn Zayd related to us. He and Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb praised him highly. He is trustworthy and preponderantly reliable.

Ādam and Sulaymān related to us, from Shuʿba, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Maymūna. His kunya is Abū Muʿādh; he is trustworthy.

Ziyād ibn Ayyūb related to us, from Abū ʿUbayda al-Ḥaddād, ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn Wāṣil, who is trustworthy.

(33b) ʿAbd al-Muʾmin Abū ʿUbayda ibn ʿUbayd Allāh al-Sadūsī is trustworthy.

Al-Ḥajjāj ibn Nuṣayr related to us: Ismāʿīl ibn Muslim al-ʿAbdī related to us the hadith concerning currency exchange. Ismāʿīl is trustworthy, while al-Ḥajjāj ibn Nuṣayr has some weakness. He was an old, absent-minded, harmless shaykh. The son of al-Azhar’s daughter had inserted hadiths into his material.

Ismāʿīl ibn Muslim al-Makkī is weak. Ismāʿīl was originally a Basran, but he used to live in Mecca, and he used to travel to Basra and arrive there at the time of the pilgrimage.

Ādam related to us: Shuʿba related to us, from al-Jarīrī, who is trustworthy and from whom they narrated. Whoever heard from him while he was sound [heard reliably], for age had affected him and he changed. The people of knowledge used to hear from him; the hearing of those who heard from him later is affected by this.

Saʿīd ibn Abī ʿArūba related to me through Yaḥyā ibn Ḥammād. Yaḥyā said:

“People used to say that he had changed, and you know best. Whoever heard from him before the change, his hadith is authoritative.”

Abū Nuʿaym related to us: Ṣāliḥ ibn Rustum Abū ʿĀmir al-Khazzāz, who was Muzanī, related to us: Abū Ḥamza related to me: “I asked Ibn ʿAbbās”—and, on the authority of Ibn Abī Mulayka: “I accompanied Ibn ʿAbbās.”

Abū Nuʿaym related to us: Ṣāliḥ related to us: Ḥumayd ibn Hilāl related to me: al-Aḥnaf ibn Qays said: “I arrived in Medina and entered its mosque. While I was praying, a man entered: dark-complexioned, tall, white-haired and white-bearded, and shaven; his hair and beard resembled one another. He went out, so I followed him and asked, ‘Who is that?’ He said, ‘Abū Dharr.’”

Abū Nuʿaym related to us: Qurra ibn Khālid al-Sadūsī related to us; he is one of the trustworthy Basrans.

Abū Nuʿaym related to us: Ḥurayth ibn al-Sāʾib, the caller to prayer of Banū Asad, related to us: “We were at the funeral of Ḥafṣa daughter of Sīrīn. Al-Ḥasan said: ‘Where is their companion’—meaning Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn?’ They said: ‘He is performing ablution.’ He said: ‘The heat [comes] from water.”

He said: Ḥurayth also said: “Muḥammad ibn al-Munkadir informed me, from his father, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: ‘Whoever circumambulates this House seven times without idle talk during it will be equivalent to one who frees a slave.’ Ḥurayth is a firmly established shaykh; there is nothing wrong with him.”

(34a) Abū Nuʿaym related to us: ʿUmar ibn al-Walīd al-Shannī related to us; there is nothing wrong with him.

Shihāb ibn ʿAbbād al-ʿAṣrī related to me that his father told him: “ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb stopped by them at ʿArafāt and said: ‘Whose tents are these?’ They said: ‘They belong to ʿAbd al-Qays.’ He called them and prayed for forgiveness for them. Then he said: ‘This is the day of the greater pilgrimage, so let none of you fast on it.’ I performed the pilgrimage after my father, then came to Medina and asked about the most excellent person among the people of Medina. They said: ‘Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab.’”

He said: “I saw a venerable old man from Kūfa enter to see Abū Nuʿaym on the day of his session. The hadith scholars had gathered around him so that he might relate hadith to them, and he was on a raised platform. The man greeted him and asked him: ‘I have heard that you related that a qaṭīfa was placed in the Prophet’s grave.’ Abū Nuʿaym said: ‘Yes. Shuʿba related to us—and he was a shaykh from whom we wrote—on the authority of Abū Ḥamza, who said: “I heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: A red qaṭīfa was placed in the Prophet’s grave ﷺ.”’”

Abū Nuʿaym related to us: Hishām al-Dastawāʾī—who is Ibn Sanbar—related to us.

Abū Nuʿaym related to us: Hishām related to us, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, from Abū Salama, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān: “He entered upon ʿUmar and found him praying the noon prayer. He said: ‘What prayer is this?’—or, ‘What is this?’ He replied: ‘It is part of the night prayer.’”

He said: “I have heard that Abū Nuʿaym used to say ‘ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf.’ He was told: ‘It is actually ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd al-Qārī.’ So he limited himself to saying ‘ʿAbd al-Raḥmān’ and did not give his lineage.”

Abū Nuʿaym related to us: Hishām related to us, from Yaḥyā, from Abū Salama, from Zayd ibn Thābit, who used to say: “For the expiation of an oath, feeding the poor is satisfied by giving each poor person one mudd of wheat.” Maʿmar disagrees with Hishām over the chain of transmission of this hadith and erred in it; the preserved version is Hishām’s hadith.

Abū Nuʿaym related to us: Hishām related to us, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, from al-Muhājir ibn ʿIkrima, that ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Bakr related to him that the Prophet ﷺ said: “It is not lawful for a man who believes in God and the Last Day to administer more than ten lashes, except in a prescribed legal punishment.” Some whose narrations are not trusted related it as: “ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Bakr al-Ṣiddīq related to him.” It is actually ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Bakr ibn ʿAmr ibn Ḥazm.

Abū Nuʿaym related to us: Hishām related to us, from Ayyūb, from Nāfiʿ: Ibn ʿUmar used to have an orphan’s property in his keeping, pay its alms-tax, invest it on the orphan’s behalf, and borrow from it.

Ibrāhīm, Sulaymān, Abū al-Nuʿmān, Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr, and Ibn ʿUthmān related to us. They said: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us: Abū Ismāʿīl al-Azraq related to us, from Ghaylān ibn Jarīr, from Abū al-Ḥallāl Rabīʿa ibn Zurāra al-ʿAtakī, who said: “I entered upon ʿUthmān with a delegation from Basra. We presented our requests to him, and he said: ‘Whenever you wish.’ Then he said: ‘May God prolong your life; may God prolong your life.’ I said: ‘A man among us has placed the matter of his wife in her hands.’

“He said: ‘Her matter is in her hands.’” This is a good chain of transmission. Ghaylān ibn Jarīr is Maʿwalī; Ayyūb al-Sakhtiyānī, Qatāda, Jarīr ibn Ḥāzim, and Mahdī ibn Maymūn narrated from him.

Abū al-Ḥallāl was a distinguished man among the distinguished Azd, combining nobility, modesty, and righteousness.

Ibn ʿUthmān added: Ḥammād said: “Hishām used to say in this hadith:

“‘And the judgment is whatever I decide.’” Ḥammād said: “I mentioned this hadith to Ayyūb, and he said: ‘Ghaylān related it just as you remember it.’”

Abū Nuʿaym related to us: ʿUmāra ibn Zādhān al-Ṣaydalānī related to us, from Makḥūl al-Azdī.

“ʿUmāra is trustworthy.” Makḥūl is a Basran, not the Syrian Makḥūl, and his hadith is sound; he heard from Ibn ʿUmar.

Abū Nuʿaym related to us: Abū Qudāma al-Ḥārith ibn ʿUbayd al-Iyādī related to us.

Abū Nuʿaym related to us: Naṣr ibn ʿAlī al-Jahḍamī related to us; he is trustworthy. He narrated from al-Naḍr ibn Shaybān, from Abū Salama ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, who said: “ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf related to me.” This is an error: Abū Salama did not hear anything from his father.

Abū Nuʿaym related to us: Rāshid ibn Maʿbad al-Wāsiṭī, the client of al-Ḥajjāj, related to us. He said:

“I saw Anas ibn Mālik.” Rāshid is a shaykh of little-known standing.

Mūsā ibn Ismāʿīl related to us, from Mubārak ibn Ḥassān, who is trustworthy.

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ḥammād al-Shaʿīthī related to us: Kahmas ibn al-Ḥasan related to us; he is trustworthy.

Abū al-Nuʿmān related to us: Mulāzim ibn ʿAmr related to us; he is trustworthy.

Abū Bishr Bakr ibn Khalaf and Ibn al-Muthannā related to us. They said: ʿAbd al-Aʿlā ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā al-Sāmī, Abū Hammām, related to us; he is trustworthy.

Muslim ibn Ibrāhīm related to us: Abū ʿAqīl al-Darūqī related to us; he is trustworthy.

Abū ʿAqīl, from whom Shuʿba and Hushaym narrate, is trustworthy. His name is Hāshim ibn Bilāl.

Khālid ibn Yazīd related to us: Abū ʿAqīl Yaḥyā ibn al-Mutawakkil related to us, from his father and he is weak.

Abū ʿUmar al-Nimrī related to us: Muḥammad ibn Muhazzam al-Rammām al-Shaʿʿāb related to us; he is trustworthy.

Al-Muʿallā ibn Asad related to us: Ḥātim ibn Wardān related to us; he is trustworthy.

Muslim ibn Ibrāhīm related to us: al-Barāʾ al-Ghanawī related to us; he is trustworthy.

Abū ʿUmar related to us: Murjiʾ ibn Rajāʾ related to us; there is nothing wrong with him.

Abū ʿUmar al-Nimrī related to us: al-Ḥārith ibn Wajīh related to us; he is weak.

ʿUqba ibn Mukram related to me, and Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar related to us, from Shuʿba, from Khālid al-Ḥadhdhāʾ, from Abū Bishr, from al-Thaʿlab—but it is actually al-Talab, with a tāʾ. Shuʿba said:

“With a thāʾ.”

Mūsā ibn Ismāʿīl al-Tabūdhakī related to us: Bakkār ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Abī Bakra related to us; he is weak.

Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr related to us: Yūsuf ibn ʿAṭiyya al-Ṣaffār related to us; he is weak.

Abū al-Walīd related to us: Muḥammad ibn Jābir related to us: Ayyūb ibn ʿUtba related to us. Both are weak, and their hadiths are not to be welcomed.

Ayyūb ibn Jābir is likewise [weak], though Ayyūb is better than Muḥammad ibn Jābir.

Abū al-Walīd said: “Ibn al-Mubārak supplied me with four hadiths from Muḥammad ibn Jābir. I went to him and asked him about them, and he related them to me on the authority of someone other than the person from whom Ibn al-Mubārak had supplied them to me. I went back to Ibn al-Mubārak and informed him. He said: ‘He is nothing; he made a mistake in them.’ He said:

‘So I erased it.’”

Ādam related to us: al-Rabīʿ ibn Badr related to us; he is weak, and his hadith is worthless.

Muslim related to us: al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Nibrās related to us; he is weak, and his hadith is worthless.

(35b) Muslim informed us: ʿAbbād ibn Manṣūr related to us; he is weak.

Muslim related to us: Abū Bakr al-Hudhalī related to us; he is weak, and his hadith is worthless.

ʿAmr ibn al-Rabīʿ ibn Ṭāriq related to us; ʿIkrima ibn Ibrāhīm related to us. He is weak.

Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Raqāshī related to us; ʿAdī ibn al-Faḍl related to us. He is weak and abandoned.

Muslim related to us; al-Ḥārith ibn Nabhān related to us. He is weak; his ḥadīth is nothing.

ʿUqba al-Aṣamm is weak.

ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn Zayd—Ibn Ḥassāb related to us from him—is weak. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī refrained from transmitting his ḥadīth.

Muslim ibn Ibrāhīm related to us; Saʿīd ibn Nadā related to us. His ḥadīth is nothing.

Ḥajjāj ibn Nuṣayr related to us from Abū Umayya ibn Yaʿlā. His ḥadīth is nothing.

Ādam related to us from ʿĪsā ibn Maymūn, from al-Qāsim. His ḥadīth is nothing.

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā and Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Anṣārī related to us from Saʿīd al-Sammāk, that the Prophet ﷺ—said: “Whoever gives the call to prayer should lead the prayer.” He is weak; his ḥadīth is nothing.

Abū ʿUmar al-Ḍarīr related to me: Naṣr ibn Ṭarīf informed us.

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā related to us: Abū Juzayy informed us—and he is Naṣr ibn Ṭarīf. He is weak, weak, and abandoned.

ʿUthmān al-Burrī is weak and abandoned. Ibn al-Mubārak, Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd, and the others abandoned him. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī used to say something different about him from what the others said, claiming that there was no harm in him.

Muslim related to us from “al-Ṣalt ibn Dīnār. He is weak; his ḥadīth is nothing”.

Abū al-Nuʿmān related to us from Ḥammād, from Muḥammad ibn Faḍāʾ. He is weak.

Saʿīd ibn Abī ʿArūba transmitted from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUmar, from Hishām ibn ʿUrwa, and from Abū Bishr, but he did not hear from them. He only practiced tadlīs in transmitting from them. By my life, he transmitted only objectionable reports from them.

Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān al-Dimashqī related to me; Saʿīd ibn Bashīr related to us from Qatāda from al-Ḥasan, from Samura: “The Prophet ﷺ—commanded us to come to the imām, to love one another, and to greet one another.” He said: “I asked Abū Mushir (36a) about Saʿīd ibn Bashīr. He said: ‘There was no one in our district with a better memory than he, yet he is weak and his ḥadīths are objectionable’”.

Ṣafwān ibn Ṣāliḥ related to us; al-Walīd ibn Muslim related to us; Saʿīd ibn Bashīr related to us from Qatāda, from Mujāhid, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, from the Messenger of God ﷺ—that on the night he was taken on the Night Journey, he found a pleasant fragrance. He said: “What is this pleasant fragrance?” He replied: “This is the fragrance from the grave of the woman who combed hair, her son, and her husband.” Qatāda did not hear anything from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, al-Shaʿbī, al-Nakhaʿī, or Mujāhid, and he did not hear anything from Abū Qilāba. He only transmitted from them by means of mursal reports.

Muslim ibn Ibrāhīm related to us; Mubashshir ibn Mukassir related to us. There is no harm in him.

Muslim related to us; ʿUmāra ibn Zādhān related to us; Ziyād al-Numayrī related to us. There is no harm in him. As for Ziyād Abū ʿAmmār, his ḥadīth is nothing.

Saʿīd Abū Masʿūd al-Jarīrī: Ibn al-Mubārak and Yazīd ibn Hārūn transmitted from him.

ʿAbbās al-Jarīrī: Ḥammād ibn Salama and Saʿīd transmitted from him. Age had affected Saʿīd, and he had changed. Both are reliable.

Abū Nuʿaym al-Nakhaʿī related to us; he related to us: “Abū Sahl Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr al-Anṣārī is weak”.

Shuʿba transmitted from ʿAmr ibn Abī Ḥakīm, Abū Saʿīd al-Wāsiṭī. He is reliable.

Mūsā ibn Ismāʿīl related to us; Muḥammad ibn Rāshid related to us. He was a Syrian who settled in Baṣra.

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Muʿādh related to us; my father related to us; Ibn ʿAwn related to us from Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq, from Miskīn al-Kūfī, and from Abū Muḥammad ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿUbayd. As far as we know, no one related from any of them except Ibn ʿAwn.

Muslim related to us; Sallām ibn Miskīn related to us; Abū al-ʿAlāʾ al-Qasmalī related to us. His ḥadīths are soft.

Abū Nuʿaym related to us; Muʿādh ibn al-ʿAlāʾ, brother of Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ, related to us. He said:

“I saw al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad on a riding camel, with a brocade coverlet on it. I saw him wearing a green robe of silk and a cloak dyed with safflower. The two of them had a brother— (36b) whose teknonym was Abū Sufyān.

Al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAẓīm related to us; Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd and Akhḍar ibn ʿAjlān related to us. He is reliable.

As for ʿAṭāʾ ibn ʿAjlān, he is weak; his ḥadīth is nothing.

Ibn ʿAwn transmitted from ʿUbayd ibn Bāb. He is not Abū ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd the Qadarī; he is another man.

ʿUbayd, Abū ʿAmr, was a weaver, then he changed his occupation and became a policeman for al-Ḥajjāj”. He was among the captives taken from Sīstān.

Al-Ḥajjāj related to us; Ḥammād ibn Salama related to us from Hishām ibn ʿAmr al-Fazārī. We know of no one other than Ḥammād who transmitted from him, and he is reliable.

ʿAyyāḍ ibn Maysara is an Egyptian.

ʿAbbād ibn Rāshid, ʿAbbād ibn Manṣūr, and ʿAbbād ibn Kathīr: their ḥadīths are weak.

Sulaymān related to us from Ḥammād, from Ḥanẓala al-Sadūsī. Age had affected him, and he had changed.

Ismāʿīl ibn Sālim al-Ṣāʾigh related to us; Hushaym related to us from Ḥuṣayn ibn Zayd al-Tamīmī. He is a Basran.

He said: They related to us from Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd and ʿImrān ibn Muslim al-Qaṣīr. He is reliable.

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Muʿādh related to us. He said: “I saw in my father’s book, in his own handwriting: Ḥātim ibn Abī Ṣaghīra, Abū Ṣaghīra, Abū Ummihi—and he is Ḥātim ibn Muslim.”

Abū ʿĀṣim related to us from Ḥajjāj ibn Abī ʿUthmān al-Ṣawwāf. He is reliable.

Aḥmad ibn Ḥafṣ related to me from his father, from Ibrāhīm ibn Ṭahmān, from Ḥajjāj al-Aswad al-Bāhilī. He is reliable and good in ḥadīth.

Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Anṣārī related to us from Ḥumayd, from Maymūn ibn Siyāh. His ḥadīths are soft, as are those of Yazīd al-Raqāshī and Ziyād al-Numayrī.

Ṣāliḥ al-Murrī is reliable; I have mentioned him before this.

Abū al-Nuʿmān related to us from Yazīd ibn Zurayʿ, from Abū Rajāʾ, whose name is Muḥammad ibn Sayf. Shuʿba transmitted from him.

Thābit al-Bunānī ibn Aslam.

Zayd ibn al-Ḥawwārī—he is al-Aʿmā. Al-Aʿmash transmitted from him.

“Muḥammad ibn (37a) ʿAbd Allāh al-Anṣārī related to us: al-Ḥasan ibn Dīnār related to me. Al-Ḥasan is Ibn Wāṣil, and Dīnār was his mother’s husband. He is weak”.

Abū al-Walīd related to us from Muḥammad ibn Thābit al-ʿAbdī. Yaʿqūb said: “I saw that Abū al-Walīd seemed to consider him weak.”

Muḥammad ibn Aslam al-Bunānī is weak.

Muḥammad ibn Thābit is the brother of ʿAzra ibn Thābit, and he is ʿAzra.

Al-Ḥajjāj related to us; Hammām ibn Yaḥyā related to us. Ibn ʿUlayya transmitted [from him].

Al-Ḥajjāj related to us; Ḥammād related to us from Saʿīd ibn Jumhān. He is reliable. Ḥashraj ibn Nubāta is likewise reliable.

ʿUqba ibn Aws, ʿUqba ibn ʿAbd al-Ghāfir, and ʿUqba ibn Wassāj are considered reliable.

ʿAmr ibn ʿĀṣim related to us from al-Mughīra, from Ḥumayd ibn Hilāl, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughaffal. Ḥumayd heard from Anas ibn Mālik. Ḥumayd ibn Hilāl is one of the reliable transmitters; he is ʿAdawī. Among Banū ʿAdī are reliable men, including Yazīd ibn Muslim, from whom Ibn ʿAwn transmitted.

ʿAbd Allāh related to us; my father related to us; ʿImrān ibn Ḥudayr, Abū ʿUbayda, related to us from Abū Mijlaz. ʿImrān is one of the reliable transmitters.

Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd said: “When I first sought ḥadīth, I looked in ʿImrān’s book and saw nothing in it but the opinions of men, so I did not write anything down.” Or words to this effect.

Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥīm related to me. He said: “I asked ʿAlī about ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shaqīq— “Did he see Ibn ʿUmar?” He said: “No, but he did see Abū Dharr and Abū Hurayra.”

Muḥammad said: “I heard ʿAlī, and he was asked, ‘Did Yūnus transmit from Nāfiʿ?’ He said:

“‘He did transmit from him. I do not know whether he heard from him or not, but I do not think he heard from him.’”

Muḥammad said: “I heard ʿAlī say: ‘Abū Mikh lad did not meet Samura or ʿImrān.’”

ʿAlī was asked: “Wuhayb transmitted from Ibn Ṭāwūs, from his father, that he met Abū Mūsā and mentioned the civil strife to him.” He said: “None of that is true. He did not meet Abū Mūsā, nor did he hear from ʿĀʾisha.”

ʿAlī said: “Abū Yazīd al-Madanī did not hear from Jābir, but he saw Ibn ʿUmar; he did not hear from Abū Hurayra.”

ʿAlī said: ʿUthmān ibn ʿUmar said (37b): “I came to Baṣra and found that if a man applied kohl during the daytime and shaved the back of his head, people would criticize him.”

He said: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd said: “I have not applied kohl for such and such a time.”

ʿAlī said: “The name of Abū al-Muhallab was ʿAmr ibn Muʿāwiya; Abū Qilāba was ʿAbd Allāh ibn Zayd ibn Muʿāwiya. Al-Awzāʿī was mistaken about the name of Abū al-Muhallab.”

ʿAlī said: “Sulaymān al-Taymī was Murri, not Taymī; he was staying among Taym.”

Abū al-Nuʿmān related to us; ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Muslim al-Qasmalī, Abū Zayd, related to us. He said: “What a shaykh he was, and what humility!” “Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥīm related to me. He said: ‘I heard ʿAlī say: I heard Ḥātim ibn Wardān say: “Yaḥyā, Ismāʿīl, Wuhayb, and ʿAbd al-Wahhāb would sit with Ayyūb. When they got up, they would all sit around Ismāʿīl, asking him, “How did he say it?”

“He said: Ibn [ʿUlayya] would supply the answer”’”.

ʿAlī said: “No one among them knew Ayyūb better than Ḥammād ibn Zayd, and none among them was more precise in what he transmitted than Ismāʿīl, Wuhayb, and ʿAbd al-Wārith.”

ʿAlī said: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad said: “I did not write down Ayyūb’s words in ink—I mean, with ink—until he died. He used to utter expressions, and when he died, I wrote them down in ink—I mean, with ink.”

Muslim ibn Ibrāhīm related to me. He said: “As far as I know, I heard Ḥammād ibn Zayd say: ‘Whenever we came to Ayyūb, Ḥammād ibn Salama had already finished.’”

“He said: ‘I heard Abū al-Walīd Hishām ibn ʿAbd al-Malik say: Ḥammād ibn Zayd said: “When we disagree with Shuʿba”—as if he meant, ‘What he says is correct’—“we would hear and leave, whereas Shuʿba would return, listen, and transmit.

“‘Abū al-Walīd said: I mentioned to him something about which Shuʿba had disagreed with him while Shuʿba was alive.

“‘He said: I asked him about something after Shuʿba’s death, but he paid no attention to it’”.

Abū al-Walīd said: “Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb rejects this.”

“I heard Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb say: ‘Ḥammād ibn Zayd knew more about Ayyūb than anyone who transmitted from Ayyūb. He said: “As for ʿAbd al-Wārith, he said, ‘I wrote down Ayyūb’s ḥadīths after his death from memory.’ Something like this is liable to include (38a) the same kinds of errors.

“‘He used to praise Wuhayb ibn Khālid, except that he would hint against him that he was a merchant, kept busy by his market.

“‘As for Ismāʿīl, he would hint against him concerning what he had become involved in. One day I was present, and a middle-aged man from Baghdad was speaking to him, exalting Ismāʿīl’s standing and magnifying him. Sulaymān would not concede to him, until he said: “He came to you and made drinking intoxicants permissible for you—and from whom did he take this? It is as though he meant to curry favor”. The Baghdadi said: “Abū Ayyūb, whenever I looked at his face, I saw that dignity; whenever I looked at the back of his head, I saw that humility.” Sulaymān said:’”

“He ought to have withdrawn from keeping the company of Ayyūb, Yūnus, and Ibn ʿAwn.”

“Al-Faḍl ibn Ziyād related to me. He said: I asked Abū ʿAbd Allāh Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal about Wuhayb and Ismāʿīl ibn Ibrāhīm ibn ʿUlayya. I asked: ‘Which of the two do you prefer when they differ?’ He replied: ‘Wuhayb. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī used to prefer Wuhayb to Ismāʿīl.’ I asked: ‘In his retention?’ He replied: ‘In everything. Ismāʿīl remained diminished in esteem because of what he said until he died.’ I asked: ‘Did he not recant and repent publicly?’ He replied: ‘Indeed, but after those words he continued to provoke the people of ḥadīth until he died. I have been told that he was brought before Muḥammad ibn Hārūn’—then he said to me, ‘Ibn Hārūn?’ I said, ‘Yes, I know him’—‘and when Muḥammad saw him, he moved toward him. Muḥammad kept saying to him, “O son of …! O son of …! You speak about the Qurʾān!” Ismāʿīl kept saying, “May God make him my ransom: it was a scholar’s slip. May God make him my ransom: it was a scholar’s slip.”’

“Abū ʿAbd Allāh repeated this more than once, and gave emphasis to his words—as though he were recounting Ismāʿīl’s words. Then Abū ʿAbd Allāh said to me: ‘Perhaps he will be forgiven for denouncing Ismāʿīl.’ Later he said: ‘He is reliable’—meaning Ismāʿīl. I asked: ‘Abū ʿAbd Allāh, ʿAbd al-Wahhāb said: “My heart will never take to Ismāʿīl. I saw him in a dream, as though his face were black.”’ (38b) Abū…”

“ʿAbd Allāh said: ‘May God grant ʿAbd al-Wahhāb well-being.’ Then he said: ‘There was a man from the Anṣār with us who used to visit regularly. He brought me in to see Ismāʿīl. When Ismāʿīl saw me, he became angry and said, “Who brought this man in to me?” After those words, he remained hostile to the people of ḥadīth. I stayed close to him for ten years, except when I was away.’ Then he began shaking his head as though lamenting, and said: ‘He was not fair-minded in ḥadīth.’ I asked: ‘How was he not fair-minded?’ He replied: ‘He used to transmit reports about intercession. How fair-minded he was in everything!’”

I heard Abū ʿAbd Allāh being asked: “When Ḥammād ibn Salama and Ḥammād ibn Zayd both transmit a ḥadīth, which do you prefer?” He replied: “Neither of them is anything but trustworthy. However, Ḥammād ibn Salama heard earlier; he wrote from Ayyūb on his first visit. Ḥammād ibn Zayd knew Ayyūb better, because he kept his company frequently. Ayyūb died in the year thirty-four, and Ḥammād ibn Zayd [died in that year]. Ḥammād often kept company with Ayyūb; he was the one most devoted to him and the one who spent the longest time in his company.”

Muḥammad related to me. He said: I heard ʿAlī being asked: “Did Yaḥyā criticize Ḥammād ibn Salama?” He replied: “No. Yaḥyā said: ‘I had taken down excerpts for him from so-and-so’”—ʿAlī named the man—“‘then I would go to Ḥammād and he would dictate them to me.’”

ʿAlī said: I asked Ḥātim ibn Wardān: “Did you used to see Ḥammād ibn Zayd?” He replied:

“He had had enough”—that is, in his dealings with Ayyūb.

“I heard ʿAlī—and he was speaking about those who pursued ḥadīth—say: ‘Among our companions, only three pursued it, devoted themselves to it, memorized it, and persevered in it until they transmitted it: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd, Sufyān ibn Ḥabīb, and Yazīd ibn Zurayʿ. From the time they began pursuing it, these men never abandoned it; they did not occupy themselves with anything else, and they continued in it until they transmitted.’” Ismāʿīl ibn Ibrāhīm had memorized it, but then forgot it. ʿAlī said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: “Ismāʿīl gave me excerpts from Ibn Abī Najīḥ’s material. I met Ibn Abī Najīḥ as he was returning from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn al-Ḥasan, and asked him about them. He had retained only one or two ḥadīths from them; later he memorized them.”

(39a) “ʿAlī said: ‘I would not say that anyone had stronger retention of ḥadīth than Ismāʿīl.’

“ʿAlī said: Yaḥyā said: ‘I never saw Ismāʿīl pursuing ḥadīth. We knew that he had heard it and then left it.’ ʿAlī said: ‘ʿAbd al-Raḥmān never saw a book belonging to Ismāʿīl.’”
