He said: I heard Abū ʿAbd Allāh say: “I was born at the beginning of the year 164, in Rabīʿ.” He died on Friday, in the forenoon, on the twelfth night having passed of Rabīʿ al-Ākhir, in the year 241. He had reached the age of sixty-seven.

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Aḥmad ibn al-Khalīl related to us: Yaḥyā ibn Ayyūb related to me: ʿAbbād ibn ʿAbbād al-Muhallabī related to me, saying: “It reached us that Shuʿbah had criticized Ayyūb and Khālid, so I went to him— “—along with Ḥammād ibn Zayd, and we said to him, ‘What is this we have heard? Take care not to say anything about the two of them that would ruin you.’ He said: So he stopped.” Yaḥyā ibn Ayyūb said: “A man among the senior hadith scholars heard these words from ʿAbbād. I would rather not name him. He discussed them with me in this form. Later, I heard that he had added something to them. He said: Then Shuʿbah went back to criticizing the two of them. We went to him and spoke to him about it, and he said, ‘I have no choice but to do that.’”

Yaḥyā ibn Ayyūb said: “This criticism was not about him. It was about the case of Abān ibn Abī ʿAyyāsh, but he forgot and attributed it to the case of these two. He is a man whose word is accepted, so I disliked contradicting him. I saw that Yaḥyā ibn Ayyūb seemed to be alluding to Ibn Maʿīn.”

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Abū Saʿīd al-Ashajj related to us: Abū Usāmah related to us from al-Muʿallā, from Shuʿbah, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Maysarah, who said: I said to al-Ḍaḥḥāk, “Did you hear anything from Ibn ʿAbbās?” He said, “No.” I said, “Then from whom did you hear this that you relate?” He said:

“From you, and from this one, and from that one.”

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Samurah related to me: Ismāʿīl— Ibn Muḥammad ibn Juḥādah related to us: Ibn [Abī] al-Ḥurr related to us from Yūnus al-Azdī, Abū al-Jahm, from Ibn ʿImrān: “The lowest-ranking of the people of Paradise.” [Qur’anic quotation]

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Naṣr ibn Sulaymān related to me, saying: “He is Umayy ibn Rabīʿah al-Ṣayrafī.” He also said: Hushaym related to us: Abū Sāsān, from Sudayr ibn Ḥakīm ibn Ṣuhayb.

Abū Yūsuf related to us: al-Faḍl related to me, saying: I heard Abū ʿAbd Allāh being asked:

“Did ʿAbd Allāh hear from Maʿmar?” He replied: “He heard from him in Mecca.” He was asked, “So did he hear nothing from him in Basra?” He replied: “No. In Basra, only outsiders such as Ismāʿīl ibn ʿUlayyah and Yazīd ibn Zurayʿ wrote from Maʿmar.”

I heard [Abū] ʿAbd Allāh say: ʿAbd al-Razzāq said: “I heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mubārak say, ‘I have not seen anyone transmit more from al-Zuhrī than ʿUqayl, except for Yūnus ibn Yazīd, who wrote down everything.’”

He said: I heard ʿUthmān say: I heard Yūnus ibn Yazīd say, “No one— “—transmits more from al-Zuhrī than ʿUqayl.”

Abū Yūsuf related to us: al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAẓīm related to me: ʿAlī informed me from Sufyān, who said: I said to Ziyād ibn Saʿd, “Tell me about ʿUqayl, for I am seeking him.”

He replied: “He was a ḥāfiẓ.”

I heard ʿAbd al-Raḥmān say: “Yūnus ibn Yazīd is among those who wrote from their own books.”

Abū Yūsuf related to us: al-Faḍl related to me, saying: I heard Abū ʿAbd Allāh being asked:

“Which do you prefer in al-Zuhrī’s hadith, Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq or al-Zuhrī’s nephew?” He replied: “I don’t know.”

Abū Jaʿfar asked him, “Then which do you prefer in al-Zuhrī’s hadith?” He replied:

“Mālik, because of how little he transmitted; then Maʿmar. ‘If you compare anyone with Maʿmar, you will find him surpassed by Maʿmar. He traveled to Yemen in pursuit of hadith, and he was the first to travel.’” Abū Jaʿfar asked him, “And Syria?” He replied, “No, the Jazīrah.”

He said: “And Yūnus and these men bring the exact wording of reports; they are men of books— “—while Maʿmar related from memory and made errors. He was the most devoted of them to seeking knowledge.” He was asked, “So what did he transmit from Thābit?” He replied, “How excellent his hadith is!” Then he said: “Ḥammād ibn Salamah is dearer to me. No one is more precise in [transmitting] from Thābit than Ḥammād ibn Salamah. I would go to him and say, ‘This is a storyteller,’ and turn the hadith around on him, asking, ‘How does this one go?’ He would say:

‘No, it is from so-and-so.’”

Abū Ṭālib said: Abū ʿAbd Allāh said: “Mālik is more precise in the hadith of al-Zuhrī than all those who transmitted from him, despite transmitting little. Sufyān made errors in fifteen hadiths from al-Zuhrī, and Maʿmar is more precise than Sufyān.” He also said: “What is sound of Hushaym’s hearing from al-Zuhrī consists of four hadiths in which he says, ‘Al-Zuhrī related to us’: the long hadith about kinship, the hadith about Ṣafiyyah, the hadith of the disputant, and the hadith of Ibn ʿUmar, ‘Whatever offering is readily available.’ For anything else, he says, ‘I don’t know whether I heard it from Sufyān ibn Ḥusayn or from al-Zuhrī.’” I said, “They say that Shuʿbah accepted his book?” He replied:

“No. That is nothing. He only heard [him] at the pilgrimage season, then forgot.”

Abū Yūsuf related to us: al-Faḍl related to me, saying: I heard Abū ʿAbd Allāh say:

“I heard Ghundar say: ‘I kept company with Shuʿbah for twenty years and, during that time, wrote from no one else.’”

He said: “I heard him say: ‘I would hear the ḥadīth from him and write it down, then bring it to him and read it back to him.’”

Abū ʿAbd Allāh said: “I think he did this only because of his dullness.”

He said: “I asked Abū ʿAbd Allāh, ‘Whom do you rank highest among Shuʿbah’s companions?’ He replied: ‘In number and abundance, Ghundar. He said, “I kept company with him for twenty years.” But Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd was more reliable. Ghundar’s notebook was accurate, though those reports were not in his books. Bahz, Yaḥyā, and ʿAffān, however, used to write down the precise wording and reports.’ ʿAffān said, ‘I used to consult the ḥadīth of Abū Isḥāq in a book I had with me.’ He was asked, ‘Would Shuʿbah let them write things down in his presence?’ He replied, ‘They would write things down.’ Then he said, ‘Yaḥyā, Khālid ibn al-Ḥārith, and Muʿādh would all gather with him. When Shuʿbah got up, Khālid would withdraw to one side and Muʿādh to another, and they would write down what they had heard; Yaḥyā would leave and go away.’ I said, ‘Abū al-Walīd said, “I asked Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd, ‘How many years did you attend Shuʿbah?’ He replied, ‘Twenty years. I never took more than ten ḥadīths from Shuʿbah in a single session.’” Abū ʿAbd Allāh said, “Yes, he had memorized them.”’”

I heard Abū ʿAbd Allāh, when Abū Jaʿfar mentioned to him the ḥadīth of ʿImrān ibn Abī Anas, say: “The ḥadīth belongs to al-Layth ibn Saʿd. Anas ibn Abī Anas—who is this? ʿImrān ibn Abī Anas is well known.”

He said: “I heard Abū ʿAbd Allāh mention Shuʿbah’s error. He said: ‘Shuʿbah only erred in the names: he made the ḥadīth of Sulaymān ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān [into that of] ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Yazīd.’” Abū Jaʿfar asked him, “The ḥadīth about the sandal?” He replied, “Yes.”

He confused the names, making the ḥadīth of Sulaymān ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān that of ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Yazīd. Abū Jaʿfar asked him, “The ḥadīth about the sandal?” He replied, “Yes.”

I asked Abū ʿAbd Allāh, “Who, in your view, is the most reliable transmitter from Abū Isḥāq?” He replied:

“Sufyān and Shuʿbah.” I asked, “Do you prefer al-Aʿmash, or Sufyān’s transmission from Abū Isḥāq?”

He replied: “Sufyān has more. Sufyān and Shuʿbah are more reliable to us than al-Aʿmash, with respect to everyone from whom al-Aʿmash transmitted.”

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥīm related to me, saying: “I heard ʿAlī say to me, ‘Yaḥyā was asked Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar: “You have disgraced Shuʿbah with these bad ḥadīths.”’”

ʿAlī said: “Yaḥyā told me: ‘Abū Usāmah asked me to go with a companion of his to Shuʿbah, so that Shuʿbah would narrate to him. I went with him, and Shuʿbah narrated to him about sixty ḥadīths—bad ḥadīths.’”

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Abū Nuʿaym related to us: Hishām ibn ʿĀʾidh al-Asadī related to us from his father, that he heard Ibn ʿUmar. A man asked him about various drinks, and he replied:

“Do not drink wine, do not serve it to drink, do not buy it, and do not sell it.” Shuʿbah also transmitted from Abū Hishām ʿĀʾidh ibn Naṣīb.

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Bakr ibn Khalaf related to us: Azhar related to me: al-Muthannā ibn Saʿīd, from Qatādah, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yas al-Makkī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr: The Prophet ﷺ used to say: “God boasts of the people at ʿArafah to His angels in the evening, saying, ‘Look at My servants: disheveled and dusty.’”

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Qabīṣah related to us: Sufyān related to us, from Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bābāh, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, who said: “Mix with people and keep apart from them; greet them in the way they like, but do not compromise your religion.”

Ḥabīb Abū Yaḥyā is one of the reliable transmitters. He heard from Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn ʿUmar. Ibn Jurayj transmitted: “Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit informed me, from ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī ʿAmr and al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Hishām. The two informed him that they heard Abū Bakr ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Hishām relate that Umm Salamah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ said: ‘When I arrived in Medina, I told them that I was the daughter of Abū Umayyah ibn al-Mughīrah, but they did not believe me. They used to say, “How false are the reports about strangers!” Then some of them came to us on pilgrimage, and they said, “Will you write to your family?” I wrote with them. They returned believing me, and so I gained greater esteem among them.’”

Abū Yūsuf mentioned the story. ʿUtbah ibn Mukram related it to me, from Abū ʿĀṣim, from Ibn Jurayj. Ibn Jurayj also transmitted: “ʿAṭāʾ related to me, from Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit, from Ibn ʿUmar, from the Prophet ﷺ concerning the slave.” Ibn Jurayj said: “I met Ḥabīb, and he related it to me. Ḥabīb denied that it was traced back to the Prophet.”

[THE ḤADĪTH OF ʿABD ALLĀH IBN BĀBĀH]

Abū Yūsuf related to us: [Abū] ʿĀṣim related to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Sulaymān ibn ʿAtīq, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bābāh, from one of Yaʿlā’s descendants, from Yaʿlā, who said: “I performed ṭawāf with ʿUmar. When we reached the two western corners, I said, ‘Shall we greet them?’ He struck between himself and the wall.55 He said, ‘Did you not perform ṭawāf with the Messenger of God ﷺ?’ I said:

‘Indeed.’ He said, ‘Did you see the Messenger of God ﷺ do it?’ I said, ‘No.’

He said, ‘The Messenger of God ﷺ was a good example.’”

“Abū Yūsuf related to us: Abū ʿĀṣim related to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿAmmār, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bābāh, from Yaʿlā ibn Umayyah, who said: ‘I said to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, “God, Mighty and Exalted, says: ‘When you travel through the land, there is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer, if you fear that those who disbelieve may harm you’ (4:101). The people are now safe, so why shorten the prayer?” He replied, “I wondered about it just as you did, so I asked the Messenger of God ﷺ. He said, ‘It is a charity from God to you, so accept it.’”

“Abū Yūsuf related to us: al-Ḥumaydī and Ibn Qaʿnab related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us: Abū al-Zubayr related to us, that he heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bābāh relate from Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: ‘O sons of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib—or O sons of ʿAbd Manāf! If you are ever entrusted with any part of this authority, do not prevent anyone who has performed ṭawāf around this House and prayed at any hour he wishes, by night or by day.’”

“Abū Yūsuf related to us: Aḥmad ibn Yūnus related to us: Zuhayr related to us, from Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bābāh, from Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim, that the Messenger ﷺ said: ‘O sons of ʿAbd Manāf, let me never find you preventing anyone who performs ṭawāf around this House at any hour, by night or by day.’”

Abū Yūsuf related to us: al-Ḥumaydī and Saʿīd related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, saying:

“I heard ʿAmr ibn Dīnār relate from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bābāh, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said, ‘It is as though I see you kneeling before Hell.’”

“ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bābayh, Ibn Bābāh, and Ibn Bābī are one and the same person, and he is a Meccan.”

Abū Yūsuf said: “ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Najīḥ, Sayf ibn Sulaymān, and Zakariyyā ibn Isḥāq were accused of Qadarism.”

[THE ḤADĪTHS OF ʿAMR IBN DĪNĀR]

Abū Yūsuf related to us: al-Ḥumaydī related to us: Sufyān related to us: “They informed me, from Ibn Jurayj, from ʿAmr, that Ibn al-Zubayr prayed the noon prayer in Mecca on the Day of Tarwiyah, then departed.”

Sufyān said: “Perhaps that was due to an illness.”

Abū Yūsuf related to us: al-Ḥumaydī related to us: Sufyān related to us: “My nephew ʿAmr related to me, from ʿAmr, who said: ‘I saw Ibn al-Zubayr sacrifice a camel, standing and tethered, while he was mounted on a piebald mule.’ Sufyān used to relate this ḥadīth. When he mentioned a piebald mule in it, he attributed it to ʿAmr’s nephew; when he did not mention riding a piebald mule, he attributed it to ʿAmr. Perhaps he heard that from ʿAmr but did not hear the words “on a piebald mule.””

Abū Yūsuf related to us: al-Ḥumaydī related to us: Sufyān related to us: ʿAmr related to us: al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad informed us that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb saw some people from Bahrain at ʿArafah, wearing shirts and turbans, and ordered that the poll tax be levied upon them. Sufyān was asked:

“Ibn Jurayj transmitted it, saying: ‘ʿAmr was asked, “Who were they, and where were they?” He said, “I do not know.”’” Sufyān replied: “But ʿAmr informed us that they were from Bahrain and that ʿUmar saw them at ʿArafah. But I think ʿUmar …”

Abū Yūsuf related to us: al-Ḥumaydī related to us: Sufyān related to us: ʿAmr related to us, on another occasion—or from the outset—saying: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī informed me that ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib said: “The one who deprives the sons of the imam of their share of the blood money has wronged them.” Sufyān was asked: “Muḥammad ibn Muslim transmits it from al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad.” He replied: “He did not retain it.”

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr, who said: “Whoever kills a sparrow without just cause, God will question him about it on the Day of Resurrection.” He was asked, “What is its just cause?” He replied: “That he slaughter it, and not cut off its head.”

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb said: “Ḥammād ibn Salamah related to me, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from Ṣuhayb al-Ḥadhdhāʾ, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: ‘Whoever kills a sparrow without just cause, God will question him about it on the Day of Resurrection.’ He was asked:

‘What is its just cause?’ He replied: ‘That he slaughter it, and not take it by the neck and cut off its head.’”

Abū Yūsuf related to us: al-Ḥumaydī related to us: Sufyān related to us: ʿAmr ibn Dīnār related to us: “Ṣuhayb, the client of ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĀmir ibn Kurayz, informed me.” Sufyān was asked: “Ḥammād says in this report, ‘Ṣuhayb al-Ḥadhdhāʾ informed me.’” Sufyān replied: “I never heard ʿAmr call him anything but Ṣuhayb, the client of ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĀmir.”

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Sulaymān related to us: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, who said: “I saw Ibn al-Zubayr sacrifice a camel while it was standing, as he rode a white mule, with a spear in his hand.”

And from ʿAmr: Ibn al-Zubayr prayed the noon prayer in Mecca on the Day of Tarwiyah, then said:

“O people, enter into the state of consecration and proclaim the takbīr.”

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Sulaymān related to us: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from ʿAṭāʾ, who said: “The waiting period of a slave woman who menstruates is two months.” He was told: “Ibn Jurayj says, from ʿAṭāʾ, ‘forty-five days.’” He replied: “Bear witness about ʿAṭāʾ that he said ‘two months.’”

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Sulaymān related to us: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from Yazīd al-Faqīr, who said: “Ibn ʿUmar said: ‘If you are in a village where the call to prayer is made and the prayer is established, that suffices you.’”

Abū Yūsuf related to us: al-Ḥumaydī related to us: Sufyān related to us, saying: “I heard ʿAmr relate from ʿIkrimah ibn Khālid, that he heard [someone] relate from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Wāqid that Ibn ʿUmar would not perform the prayer in a land where the prayer was performed. He would not pray the two rakʿahs before dawn while travelling, but he would never omit them when at home.”

Sufyān was asked: “Ḥammād ibn Zayd says that in this ḥadīth, or in part of it, he transmits from Yazīd al-Faqīr.” Sufyān replied: “I never heard ʿAmr mention Yazīd al-Faqīr. He only told us that he heard ʿIkrimah relate from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Wāqid.”

Abū Yūsuf related to us: al-Ḥumaydī related to us: Sufyān related to us: ʿAmr ibn Dīnār related to us: “Yaḥyā ibn Jaʿdah informed me that a man sought the Prophet’s permission on a rainy day.”

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā transmitted this ḥadīth from Ibn ʿUyaynah with a remarkable chain. What we have cited from al-Ḥumaydī is correct. Among our companions, ʿUbayd Allāh is considered to have erred in what he transmitted.

Abū Yūsuf related to us: al-Ḥumaydī related to us: Sufyān related to us: “I heard ʿAmr relate—more times than I can count—that he heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṣafwān ibn Umayyah. Yazīd ibn Shaybān al-Azdī, a man from his maternal kin, informed me: ‘We were standing at ʿArafah behind the main standing place. ʿAmr would keep him far from the imam’s place of standing. Ibn Murbiʿ al-Anṣārī came to us and said:

“The Messenger of God ﷺ has instructed you: ‘Remain at these sacred sites, following the ancient inheritance from Abraham.’” Sometimes Sufyān said “Stay firm” instead of “Remain”; sometimes he said, “Abraham ﵇.”

Ibn al-Mubārak transmitted from Sufyān, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from ʿAmr ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṣafwān, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yazīd, who said: “We were standing.”

Abū Yūsuf said: “I mentioned this to Ṣadaqah ibn al-Faḍl, and he said, ‘Ibn al-Mubārak made an error in this.’ I said to him, ‘But ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Shaqīq said:

“I heard it from Sufyān in the same form.” Ṣadaqah said, “Rely on someone else’s hearing.”

“Abū Yūsuf related to us: al-Ḥumaydī related to us: Sufyān related to us: ʿAmr related to us, saying: ‘Abū Jaʿfar and I were walking past Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ. He said to me:

“Wait for me while I ask him about a ḥadīth he relates.” ʿAmr said: “He went to him, then came back and told me that Ibrāhīm had related to him that ʿAlī came to the Prophet ﷺ while some people were with him, and entered. When ʿAlī entered, they went out. Then they said, ‘By God, why did we leave when the Messenger of God ﷺ did not send us out?’ So they returned and went in to the Prophet ﷺ. The Prophet ﷺ said, ‘By God, I did not send you out and let him in; rather, God Himself let him in and sent you out.’”

Abū Yūsuf related to us: al-Ḥumaydī related to us: Sufyān related to us: ʿAmr related to us: “A shaykh from Banū Jumah, whose kunyah was Abū al-Thawrayn, related to me: ‘I asked Ibn ʿUmar about fasting on the Day of ʿArafah, and he forbade me.’”

“Abū Yūsuf related to us: al-Ḥajjāj related to us: Shuʿbah related to us: ʿAmr ibn Dīnār related to us, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Qurashī, that Ibn ʿUmar said to him: ‘Do not fast on the Day of ʿArafah.’ He is Abū al-Thawrayn.” If that is not a nickname, then Shuʿbah erred, except that— “He was known by two teknonyms.”

Abū Yūsuf related to us; al-Ḥumaydī related to us; Sufyān related to us; ʿAmr related to us, saying: Abū al-Shaʿthāʾ said to me: “Ziyād was more prone than al-Ḥajjāj to kill among the people of his own town those whose inclinations opposed his. He was more indiscriminate in killing, here and there.”

(62a) “Abū Yūsuf related to us; al-Ḥumaydī related to us; Sufyān related to us; ʿAmr related to us, from Abū al-Shaʿthāʾ, who said: ‘A man has a greater right to wash a woman than her brother does.’

“Sufyān said: ‘I had forgotten this until I found it written in my own hand.’”

Abū Yūsuf related to us; Abū Bakr related to us; Sufyān related to us; ʿAmr ibn Dīnār related to us, saying: “I heard Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh—indicating his ears—say: ‘I swear, I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ with these two ears of mine say: “Some people will come out of the Fire and enter Paradise.”’” Abū Yūsuf related to us; Abū al-Nuʿmān related to us; Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “A people will come out of the Fire through intercession and grow like the shaʿārīr.” He was asked, “What are the shaʿārīr?” He said: “The ṣaghābīs.” He said: “His mouth had collapsed.” I said:

“Yes. I heard Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh say: ‘I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: “Indeed, God will bring a people out through intercession.”’” He said: “Yes.”

Abū Yūsuf related to us; Ibn Qaʿnab and Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us; they said: Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd related to us, from his father, from Ḥafṣ ibn ʿĀṣim, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Mālik ibn Buḥaynah, from his father: “The Prophet ﷺ passed by a man just after the dawn prayer had been called to begin and said something to him, though we did not know what it was. When we had finished, we gathered around him and asked, ‘What did the Messenger of God ﷺ say to you?’ He replied, ‘He said: “One of you is about to pray four units for the dawn prayer.”’”

Abū Yūsuf related to us; ʿAmr ibn Marzūq related to us; Shuʿbah informed us, from Saʿd ibn Ibrāhīm, from Ḥafṣ ibn ʿĀṣim, from Ibn Buḥaynah, who said: “The Messenger of God ﷺ saw—”

ﷺ saw a man praying two units after the prayer had been called to begin. The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “The dawn prayer is four! The dawn prayer is four!” Abū Yūsuf said: “This is the correct version, and Ibrāhīm made a mistake. Ḥammād ibn Salamah (62b) related it from Saʿd as Shuʿbah related it. Al-Awzāʿī and Shaybān related it from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Thawbān, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Mālik ibn Buḥaynah: ‘The Prophet ﷺ passed by him.’”

Abū Yūsuf related to us; Ibn Qaʿnab and [the rest of the name is erased] Naṣr related to us, from Mālik, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Bakr ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr ibn Ḥazm, from his father, from Abū al-Baddāḥ ibn ʿĀṣim, who informed him from his father: “The Messenger of God ﷺ granted the camel herders a concession to spend the night away and to stone on the Day of Sacrifice, then to stone the following day and, after that, on the next two days, then to stone on the Day of Sacrifice.”

Abū Yūsuf related to us; al-Ḥumaydī related to us; Sufyān related to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Bakr, from his father, from al-Baddāḥ, from his father: “The Messenger of God ﷺ granted the herders a concession to stone and leave one day.”

Abū Yūsuf related to us; Ismāʿīl ibn al-Khalīl related to us; Ibn Abī Zāʾidah informed us; Ibn Jurayj informed us; Muḥammad ibn Abī Bakr related to us, from his father, from Abū al-Baddāḥ, from ʿĀṣim ibn ʿAdī: “The Prophet ﷺ granted the herders a concession to take turns stoning: they were to stone on the Day of Sacrifice, then leave a day and a night, then stone the following day. No one who transmitted this report is said to have stated that he granted the herders a concession to stone the pillars at night.”

Abū Yūsuf related to us; ʿAbd Allāh ibn Saʿīd related to me; my paternal uncle related to us; Ibn Akhī al-Zuhrī informed us, from his paternal uncle, who informed me: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Hurmuz informed me, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Buḥaynah—who was one of the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ—that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Did any of you recite during the prayer just now?” He said: “Yes.” He said:

“I say: Why am I being contended with over the Qurʾān?” The people stopped reciting when he said that. This is undoubtedly and unquestionably an error. Mālik, Maʿmar, Ibn ʿUyaynah, al-Layth ibn Saʿd, Yūnus ibn Yazīd, and Zubayr all related it from al-Zuhrī, from Ibn— (63a) Ukaymah, then he retracted it.

“I know of no book among all the books more authentic than the Book of ʿAmr ibn Ḥazm. He said: ‘The Companions of the Prophet ﷺ and the Successors used to refer back to it,’” and set aside their own opinions.

Abū Yūsuf related to us; Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us; al-Layth related to me; Khālid ibn Yazīd related to me, from Saʿīd ibn Abī Hilāl, from Abū Umayyah al-Anṣārī, from ʿUbayd ibn Rifāʿah ibn Rāfiʿ, from his father, who said: “One day I entered upon the Prophet ﷺ, and there was a pot boiling meat beside him. A piece of meat appealed to me, so I swallowed it. I suffered from it for a year. Then I mentioned this to the Messenger of God ﷺ, and he said: ‘It contained the choicest portions of seven people.’ Then he rubbed my belly, and I brought it up, still green. By Him who sent him with the truth, my belly has not hurt me from that moment to this.”

I attended Ibn Bukayr while he was reading this report, and Jaʿfar ibn ʿAbd al-Wāḥid was present. was present. I do not know whether he was reading to him from al-Layth’s book, transmitted from Khālid or someone else. He reached this report, and there it read: “From ʿUbayd ibn Rifāʿah, who said: ‘I entered upon the Prophet ﷺ.’”

Abū Yūsuf said: “Abū Ṣāliḥ also related it as ‘from his father.’ That is false.”

He said so, and lied; I offended him, and he offended me. He said to Jaʿfar: “Meet me tomorrow morning so I can bring out al-Layth’s original, for al-Layth’s original book has it only as I say: ‘from ʿUbayd ibn Rifāʿah.’” He again offended me, and I offended him, until someone present said to him: “Abū Zakariyyā, these people have written reports from Abū Ṣāliḥ. If you confront Abū Ṣāliḥ, they will offend you.” He said: “The meeting is tomorrow.” I left and met Ḥarmalah, who had heard what had happened. He said to me: “This dispute goes back to the days of Abū Ṣāliḥ, because it appears in al-Layth’s book on parchment, but not in the original. The original is on sheets of paper. Al-Layth had transferred his books to parchment, made them an endowment or a bequest to his children, and left the original record of his auditions on paper to his eldest son. The eldest used to be with Abū Ṣāliḥ, so the original remained with Abū Ṣāliḥ. The parchment copy alone is a transcription.” The next morning I went to Ibn Bukayr. I think Jaʿfar was present. He had sent for the parchment book and brought it; he opened it to the place of the report and said: “This is al-Layth’s original, and it does not say ‘from his father.’” I said to him:

“Send for the original book on paper, which is at Abū Ṣāliḥ’s house. I do not think they will send it, nor will they acknowledge your claim.”

“They will not send it, nor will they acknowledge your claim.” He said: “Did Ḥarmalah tell you this?” I said: “Yes, he told me. The original book is with Abū Ṣāliḥ, on paper, and it says ‘from his father.’ ʿUbayd was neither a Companion nor a transmitter, and there is no point on which a person could be mistaken. I think al-Madāʾinī had made it ‘from Rāfiʿ ibn Khadīj.’ It was as God willed.”

Abū Yūsuf related to us; Abū Kurayb related to me; Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān related to us, from ʿUbaydah ibn al-Aswad, from Mujālid, from Qays ibn Abī Ḥāzim, from al-Mustawrid, who said: “I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: ‘I was sent at the breath of the Hour; I preceded it as this one preceded this one’”—and he pointed with his two fingers—“and, God knows best, I consider this to be an error.”

Abū Yūsuf related to us; Ibn ʿUthmān related to us; ʿAbd Allāh informed us.

Ibn Numayr related to us; my father related to us, saying: Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid informed us, from Shubayl ibn ʿAwf, who informed me, from Abū Jubayrah, from some [of the] Anṣār— They said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “I and the Hour were sent like this”—and he joined his index and middle fingers together—“at the breath of the Hour, or at the [unclear] of the Hour.”

Ibn Numayr said: From Abū Jubayrah ibn al-Ḍaḥḥāk, from some Anṣārī elders, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: (64a) “I and the Hour were sent like this”—and he indicated with his two fingers—“I preceded it as this one preceded this one …” “at the breath of the Hour, or at a breath of the Hour.”

Abū Yūsuf related to us; Ibn ʿUthmān related to us; ʿAbd Allāh related to us; Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid informed us, from Qays ibn Abī Ḥāzim, from al-Ṣunābiḥī, who said: “I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: ‘I shall precede you at the Pool, and I shall take pride in your great numbers among the nations, so do not fall into temptation after me.’” Thus al-Ṣunābiḥī transmitted it from Ibn al-Mubārak.

Abū Yūsuf related to us; Salamah related to us, from Marwān.

Abū Yūsuf related to us; al-Ḥumaydī related to us, from Sufyān.

Abū Yūsuf related to us; Ibn Numayr related to us, from his father; and Muḥammad ibn Bishr, from Ismāʿīl, from Qays, from al-Ṣunābiḥī. Ibn Numayr said: “He is Ibn al-Aʿsar al-Aḥmasī. Aḥmas belongs to Bajīlah.”

Abū Yūsuf related to us; Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm ibn al-ʿAlāʾ al-Zubaydī related to me; ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith ibn al-ʿAlāʾ al-Zubaydī related to me; ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sālim related to me, from al-Zubaydī—namely, Muḥammad ibn al-Walīd—who said: Abū ʿAwn ibn Abī ʿAbd Allāh related to us that Qays ibn al-Ḥārith al-Ghāmidī related to us, from Ibn al-Ṣunābiḥī, who said: “A man—” came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: “Messenger of God, curse Ḥimyar.” He said:

“May God have mercy on Ḥimyar.” The man said: “Messenger of God, curse Ḥimyar.” He said: “May God have mercy on Ḥimyar.” The man said: “Messenger of God, I meant to say, ‘Curse Ḥimyar.’” He said: “Ḥimyar are an excellent people: greetings are on their lips, and food is in their hands.”

Abū Yūsuf related to us; Ibn Qaʿnab and Ibn Bukayr related to us, from Mālik, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Dīnār, from ʿAbd Allāh al-Ṣunābiḥī, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “The sun rises with Satan’s horn accompanying it. When it rises higher, he departs from it; then, when it reaches its zenith, he accompanies it; then, when it declines, he departs from it; when it draws near setting, he accompanies it; and when it sets, he departs from it.” The Messenger of God ﷺ forbade prayer during those times.

Abū Yūsuf related to us; Ibn Qaʿnab and Ibn Bukayr related to us, from Mālik, from Abū ʿUbayd, the client of Sulaymān ibn ʿAbd al-Malik, that ʿUbādah ibn Nasī informed him that he had heard— Qays ibn al-Ḥārith used to say: “Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Ṣunābiḥī told me that he had come to Medina during the caliphate of Abū Bakr and had prayed the sunset prayer behind Abū Bakr.”

Abū Yūsuf narrated to us; ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yūsuf narrated to us; Ibn Lahīʿa narrated to us, from Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb, from Abū al-Khayr, from al-Ṣunābiḥī, from Bilāl, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said, “The Night of Decree is the night of the twenty-fourth.”

Abū Yūsuf narrated to us; Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr narrated to us; Ismāʿīl ibn Ibrāhīm narrated to us; Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq narrated to us; Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb told me, from Marthad ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Yazanī, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Ṣunābiḥī, who said: “I saw Abū Bakr wiping over the head covering.”

He said: “Ibn ʿUthayla”—Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr said it this way. Abū Yūsuf said:

“Others say ‘Ibn ʿUsayla’, and that is correct. ‘When Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr saw an error in his book, he would not retract it.’”

Abū Yūsuf narrated to us; al-Rabīʿ ibn Yaḥyā narrated to us; Saʿīd narrated to us; Muḥammad ibn al-Munkadir narrated to us. He said: “I heard Masʿūd ibn al-Ḥakam relate from ʿAlī, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ stood for the funeral, and we stood with him.”

“Abū Yūsuf narrated to us; Ibn ʿUthmān narrated to us; ʿAbd Allāh informed us; Mūsā ibn ʿUqba narrated to us; Ismāʿīl ibn Masʿūd ibn al-Ḥakam told me, from his father, that he had attended a funeral in Kūfa with ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib. He saw the people standing, waiting for the bier to be set down so that they could sit. He said: I saw ʿAlī, who was gesturing to the people with a whip he had with him—or with a lash—[saying], ‘Sit down, people! The Messenger of God ﷺ used to sit after he had stood.’”

Abū Yūsuf narrated to us; Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr narrated to us; Ismāʿīl ibn Ibrāhīm narrated to us; Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAlqama al-Zuraqī narrated to us. The person from whom Wahb ibn Munabbih narrated was in fact al-Ḥakam ibn Masʿūd al-Thaqafī.

Abū Yūsuf narrated to us; Abū al-Nuʿmān Muḥammad ibn al-Faḍl narrated to us; ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mubārak narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Simāk ibn al-Faḍl—a Khawlānī—from Wahb ibn Munabbih, from al-Ḥakam ibn Masʿūd al-Thaqafī, who said: “I witnessed ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb include the full brothers with the maternal siblings in the one-third share. A man said to him, ‘You ruled differently in this matter last year.’ He asked, ‘How did I rule?’ The man said, ‘You gave it to the maternal siblings and gave nothing to the full brothers.’ He said, ‘That ruling was according to what we decided then, and this ruling is according to what we decide now.’”

Abū Yūsuf narrated to us; Zayd ibn al-Mubārak narrated to us, from Ibn Thawr, from— Maʿmar, from Simāk, from Wahb, from al-Ḥakam ibn Masʿūd al-Thaqafī, from ʿUmar, with a report to the same effect.

Abū Yūsuf said: Yaḥyā ibn ʿĪsā told me, from Ibn al-Mubārak, from Maʿmar, from Simāk ibn al-Faḍl al-Khawlānī, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, from al-Ḥakam ibn Masʿūd al-Thaqafī, with a report to the same effect.

Abū Yūsuf narrated to us; Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr narrated to us; Sufyān narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Simāk ibn al-Faḍl, from Masʿūd ibn al-Ḥakam: “He came to him regarding an inheritance obligation.”

Abū Yūsuf said: “This is an error. It was al-Ḥakam ibn Masʿūd.”

Abū Yūsuf narrated to us; al-Makkī ibn Ibrāhīm told me, from Fāʾid Abū al-Warqāʾ, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn [Abī] Awfā, who said: “We performed the lesser pilgrimage with the Messenger of God ﷺ.”

Abū Yūsuf said: “Fāʾid is weak. Fāʾid, the client of ʿAbādal, is a trustworthy Medinan.”

Abū Yūsuf narrated to us; Ibn Numayr told me; Yazīd ibn Hārūn narrated to us; Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid informed us. He said: “I saw a wound on the hand of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Awfā. He said, ‘I was struck by it on the day of Ḥunayn with the Prophet ﷺ.’ I asked, ‘Were you at Ḥunayn?’ He replied:

‘And before that.’”

Abū Yūsuf narrated to us; Ibn Numayr narrated to us; ʿUqba ibn Khālid narrated to us; Ismāʿīl narrated to us— He said: “I saw Ibn Abī Awfā; he had two braids.”

Abū Yūsuf narrated to us; ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā narrated to us; Ibn Abī Laylā informed us. A man with two braids came to him and said, “Abū ʿĪsā, tell me what you heard from your mother about furs.” He told me: “My father was sitting with the Prophet ﷺ when a man came to him and said, ‘Messenger of God, may I pray wearing furs?’ The Messenger of God ﷺ replied, ‘Then where are the sacrificial animals?’”

Thābit said: “When he turned away, I asked, ‘Who is that?’ He said, ‘Suwayd ibn Ghafala.’”

Abū Yūsuf narrated to us; Ibn Numayr narrated to us; Abū Muʿāwiya narrated to us, from Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid, who said: “I saw Anas dyeing his hair with henna.”

Abū Yūsuf narrated to us; Ibn Numayr narrated to us; Yaḥyā ibn al-Yamān narrated to us; Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid narrated to us. He said: “I heard ʿAmr ibn Ḥurayth say: ‘My brother and I went to the Prophet ﷺ, and he wiped my head and prayed that I be provided for.’”

Abū Yūsuf narrated to us; Ibn Numayr narrated to us; Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid, who said: “I saw Abū Kāhil—who had been a Companion.” He said: “My brother related to me from him that he said: ‘I saw the Prophet ﷺ preaching from atop a she-camel, while an Abyssinian held its halter.’”

Abū Yūsuf narrated to us; Ibn Numayr narrated to us; Muḥammad ibn ʿUbayd narrated to us; Ismāʿīl narrated to us, from Qays ibn ʿĀʾidh, who said: “I saw the Prophet ﷺ on a she-camel, while an Abyssinian held its halter.”

Abū Yūsuf said: “Qays ibn ʿĀʾidh is Abū Kāhil, and he is Bajalī.”

Abū Yūsuf narrated to us; Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī narrated to us; Sufyān narrated to us; my father told me: “Hishām ibn ʿAbd al-Malik performed the pilgrimage and circumambulated the House. Sālim ibn ʿAbd Allāh was with him. He wanted to enter the Ḥijr, but Sālim pushed him aside like this”—and Sufyān gestured with his shoulder—“so he circumambulated outside the Ḥijr.”

Sufyān said: “My father witnessed it.”

Abū Yūsuf narrated to us; al-Ḥumaydī narrated to us; Sufyān narrated to us; my father narrated to us. He said: “I saw al-Ḥasan ibn Abī al-Ḥasan wearing a black turban.”

Ibn Yūnus narrated to us; al-Ḥumaydī narrated to us; Sufyān narrated to us; my father narrated to us. He said:

“I heard Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, the client of the family of Ṭalḥa, say: ‘The letter of ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz forbids such-and-such—or forbids vessels sealed with pitch.’”

Abū Yūsuf narrated to us; al-Ḥumaydī narrated to us; Sufyān narrated to us; my father narrated to us. He said:

“I heard Maslama ibn ʿAbd al-Malik say: ‘I remember that ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz and I would reach the crops. ʿUmar would make his horse plunge in, while I held my horse back.’”

He said: “I heard Maslama ibn ʿAbd al-Malik say: ‘The least troubled by cares in this world are the least troubled by cares in the Hereafter.’”

He said: Sufyān narrated to us; Muzāḥim informed me. He said: “ʿUmar ibn Hubayra said to me, ‘I have withheld from no one as much of my opinion as I have from you.’”

Abū Yūsuf narrated to us; al-Ḥumaydī narrated to us; Sufyān narrated to us; my father told me: “I heard a shaykh from Banū ʿĀmir say: ‘ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said about a certain matter: “So-and-so: they are only from Muḥammad …”’”

Abū Yūsuf narrated to us; al-Ḥumaydī narrated to us; Sufyān narrated to us. He said: “I heard my father say:

‘The first to hear and see were the followers of al-Ḥārith ibn Abī Rabīʿa.’”

Abū Yūsuf narrated to us; al-Ḥumaydī narrated to us; Sufyān narrated to us. He said: “I heard my father say: ‘I accompanied my mother as far as al-Qādisiyya, and I loaded the camel onto every litter-bearer.’”

Sufyān said: “They would perform the pilgrimage only on riding camels.”

Abū Yūsuf said: “We know of no one who narrated from ʿUyayna except Sufyān. ʿUyayna was a money-changer in Kūfa. I was informed that he had fled from Ṭāriq and gone to Mecca.”

Abū Yūsuf narrated to us; Ibn Numayr narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn ʿUbayd, from Ismāʿīl, from Maḥmūd ibn ʿAmāra.

Abū Yūsuf said: “This is an error, because ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā narrated to us from Ismāʿīl, from Maḥmūd ibn ʿAmāra.” Abū Yūsuf said: “Muḥammad ibn ʿUbayd also erred when he said ‘from Ismāʿīl, from Ḥabkhār’; rather, it is from Ḥajjāj. He also erred when he said ‘Ismāʿīl, from al-Shaʿbī, from Shamir’; rather, it is from Samura ibn Jundub.”

Abū Yūsuf said: “Abū Ismāʿīl’s name is Haram, and he was a client of Bajīla.”

Abū Yūsuf narrated to us; Ibn Numayr narrated to us; Yaʿlā and my father narrated to us, from Ismāʿīl, from Abū Ḥāzim, whose name was Nabtal and who was a client of Ibn ʿAbbās.

Abū Yūsuf narrated to us; Ibn Numayr narrated to us, from Yaʿlā and my father, from Ismāʿīl, from ʿImrān ibn Abī al-Jaʿd, from ʿAbd Allāh, who said: “People have spoken well of the one whose deeds agree with his words; that is the one who has attained his due share. But the one whose deeds contradict his words—that is the one who reproaches himself.”

Abū Yūsuf narrated to us; Ibn ʿUthmān narrated to us, from Ibn al-Mubārak, from Ismāʿīl, from ʿImrān ibn Abī al-Jaʿd. The correct version is the one narrated by Ibn Numayr.

As for Ismāʿīl’s report from Abū Ḍamra, from ʿAlī, concerning the dawn prayer, he is Saʿd ibn ʿUbayda.

Abū Yūsuf narrated to us; Ibn Numayr narrated to us; Yaʿlā and Yazīd ibn Hārūn narrated to us, from Ismāʿīl, from his sister Sukayna, who said: “I visited ʿĀʾisha on the Day of Tarwiya. She was wearing a black head covering and a flower-patterned tunic.”

Abū Yūsuf narrated to us; al-Ḥumaydī narrated to us; Sufyān narrated to us; Ibn Abī Khālid narrated to us. He said:

“I heard Umm Khunays say: ‘I went with my mistress, ʿAmra bint Rawāḥa—the sister of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rawāḥa and the mother of al-Nuʿmān ibn Bashīr—to ʿUmar to greet him when he had been stabbed. I heard him say, “I have set the roads in order for you; do not make them crooked after me.”’”

Al-Ḥumaydī said: “Al-Fazārī said: She said, ‘I went at night.’”

Abū Yūsuf said: “Umm Khunays was the paternal aunt of Yaʿqūb the judge. Yaʿqūb’s clientage was among the Anṣār, but when he rode the mule, he disavowed his patrons and claimed that his clientage was among Quraysh.”

Abū Yūsuf narrated to us; Ibn Numayr narrated to us; Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid narrated to us, from Shibl ibn ʿAwf. Ibn Idrīs said it this way: “Shibl.” He said: “My foot has never gathered dust “in pursuit of worldly gain, ever. I have never sat in an assembly except while waiting for a funeral or some need, and I have never opened a saddlebag except [for something] like the earnings of a householder.”

Abū Yūsuf said: “Mujāhid ibn Jabr al-Makkī, and Mujāhid ibn Rūmī—whom I think was a Meccan, and from whom Sufyān narrated—and Mujāhid, from whom Ibn al-Aṣbahānī narrated, is a third.”

Abū Yūsuf narrated to us; Ibn ʿUthmān narrated to us; ʿAbd Allāh informed us; Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid informed us, from Qays ibn Abī Ḥāzim, from Ḥuṣayn ibn ʿAwf, who said:

“When ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb was informed of the death of al-Nuʿmān ibn Muqarrin, and was told, ‘So-and-so and so-and-so have been struck down, along with others whom we do not know,’ he said, ‘But God knows them.’ He was also told, ‘A man sold himself.’ A man from Aḥmas named Mālik ibn ʿAwf said, ‘That was my maternal uncle, Commander of the Faithful. Some people claim that he cast himself into destruction.’ ʿUmar said, ‘Those people have lied. Rather, he is among those who purchased the Hereafter with this world.’”

Qays said: “The one who was carried away was ʿAwf ibn Abī Ḥayya, who was Abū Shibl.”

Abū Yūsuf narrated to us; Ibn Numayr narrated to us, from his father, from Ismāʿīl, from Qays, who said:

“Mudrik ibn ʿAwf al-Aḥmasī—and Mālik was more like him.”

“Abū Yūsuf said: Yūsuf ibn Māhak and Yūsuf ibn Mihrān are one and the same.

“Shuʿba says ‘ibn Māhak’, while Ḥammād ibn Salama says ‘ibn Mihrān.’ They both narrate from ʿAlī ibn Zayd, from him, and he is Meccan.”

[Ayyūb al-Sakhtiyānī]

Abū Yūsuf narrated to us; Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī narrated to us; Sulaymān narrated to us; Hārūn ibn Riʾāb narrated to us. As far as I know, he used to conceal his asceticism.

Abū Yūsuf narrated to us; Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb narrated to us; Ḥammād ibn Zayd narrated to us; Maymūn Abū ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us. He said: “I was present with al-Ḥasan when Ayyūb came to him and spoke with him about something concerning— Between him and him. When Ayyūb got up and left, al-Ḥasan said, “This is the master of the young men.”

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Abū al-Nuʿmān related to us: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, from Abū Khushayna, who said: “One day Muḥammad related something to us about such-and-such.” They asked, “From whom did you get that, Abū Bakr?” He said:

“Ayyūb al-Sakhtiyānī related it to me.”

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us: Ḥammād related to us, from Ayyūb, who said:

“I wrote nothing down from Muḥammad except the report of the piebald horse. When I had memorized it, I erased it.”

(67b) Abū Yūsuf related to us: Sulaymān related to us: Ḥammād related to us, who said: They disagreed over a report in Ayyūb’s session, so they turned to Ayyūb’s memory. Ayyūb said:

“The people in the session will remember it.”

He said: Ḥammād also said: “A man ought not to be impressed by another’s words.”

Sulaymān said: Ḥammād said: Ayyūb was asked, “Is there more knowledge today, or has it diminished today?” He replied, “There is more talk today, but there was more knowledge before today.”

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, who said:

“Ayyūb was among the people most skilled at finding his way around the city. He would seek out routes without gatherings, fearing that people would speak of him.”

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Sulaymān related to us: ʿAmr ibn Marzūq related to us, who said: I once asked Ayyūb, “May I drink the nabīdh of the watering place?” He replied, “When I have no choice.”

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Sulaymān related to us: Ḥammād related to us, who said: Ayyūb said, “If you do not get what you want, then want what comes to be.” Sulaymān said, “This applies to everything.”

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Sulaymān related to us: Ḥammād related to us, from Ayyūb, who said: “If I knew that my family needed a dastaja of greens, I would not sit as a teacher.”

He also said: Ḥammād related to us, from Ayyūb, who said: Abū Qilāba said, “Wealth is part of well-being.”

He also said: Ḥammād related to us, who said: I went out to the market and met Ayyūb. I said:

“Abū Bakr, where are you going?” He replied, “To a funeral.” I was about to follow him, but he said, “Go to your market, go to your market.”

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā related to us: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said:

I heard Mālik ibn Anas mention Ayyūb al-Sakhtiyānī, speak of his merit, and say, “He was the most scrupulous of people.”

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Yūnus related to us: Ibn Wahb related to us: he told me—I mean Ibn ʿUyayna—from Hishām ibn ʿUrwa, who said: “I have seen no one like Ayyūb in Baṣra.”

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Abū al-Nuʿmān related to us: (68a) Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, who said:

Ayyūb was asked about something and said, “Nothing has reached me concerning it.” He was told, “Give your opinion about it.”

He replied, “My opinion does not reach it.”

Abū al-Nuʿmān said: These people buy books at al-Qanṭara and say, “Whoever says anything contrary to this is wrong.”

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Sulaymān related to us: Ḥammād related to us, who said: Whenever someone asked Ayyūb about something, he would say to him, “Repeat it.” If the man answered as he had asked, Ayyūb would answer him; otherwise, he would not answer him.

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Saʿīd ibn Asad related to us: Ḍamra related to us, from Ibn Shawdhab, who said: Whenever Ayyūb was asked about something concerning which he had no information, he would say, “Ask the people of knowledge.”

He said: Ḍamra also related to us, from Ibn Shawdhab, who said: Ayyūb used to perform the lesser pilgrimage in Rajab, then return to perform the pilgrimage that same year. He would perform the lesser pilgrimage from al-Jiʿirrāna.

He did not fast any of the first ten days while travelling. He would fast on the Day of ʿĀshūrāʾ and would prepare his pre-dawn meal in advance. He did not approve of those reports about the pre-dawn meal.

He also said: Ḍamra related to us, from Ibn Shawdhab, who said: Ayyūb would not leave al-Ṣafā and al-Marwa for his lodging until the stars tilted, after standing in prayer and supplication for a long time.

He said: Whenever I saw him on the pilgrimage, I knew that he had come for that alone. He would neither buy nor sell during the pilgrimage, and sometimes he would dismount and lead one of us along. He said:

Whenever he arrived, many skinned sheep would be given to him.

He also said: Ḍamra related to us, from Ibn Shawdhab, who said: Ayyūb used to wear a ṭaylasān, with its sleeve in his hand.56 When you saw him, recitation would not [unclear] until he spoke or was asked.

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Saʿīd related to us: Ḍamra related to us, from Ibn Shawdhab, who said: Ayyūb would lead the people of his mosque in prayer during Ramaḍān. He would pray with them about thirty verses in each rakʿa. Between the two breaks, he would pray on his own about thirty verses. He would say to the people himself, “The prayer!” He would give them precedence, supplicating with the supplication of the Qurʾān while those behind him said “Amen.” The last thing he would say was a blessing upon the Prophet ﷺ—then he would say, “O God, employ us in following his Sunna and inspire us to follow his guidance. O God, make us leaders for the God-fearing.” Then he would say the takbīr and prostrate. He would supplicate after bowing.

He said: When he finished the prayers, he would offer supplications.

He said: He, Yūnus ibn ʿUbayd, and Ḥumayd al-Ṭawīl once met. Ḥumayd said to Yūnus, “I have learned that Ayyūb has begun to shorten [his prayers].”

Ibn Shawdhab said: Of those men of Baṣra between whom al-Ḥasan was [the link], I encountered only Ayyūb and Yūnus.

Ayyūb said, “Were it not that the storytellers would revile me in their stories, I would relate something about them that would displease them.”

He said: We were in Ayyūb’s session when he mentioned the people of heterodox views and spoke against them. A man got up from the session. Someone said to him, “Abū Bakr, this man follows his own inclination.” He replied, “We belong to God! He thinks we were speaking about him.” He said: This distressed him.

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us: Sufyān related to us, who said: Ayyūb said, “If I knew that my family needed a bundle or a dastaja of greens, I would not sit with you.”

He said: Abū Qilāba said, “Stay at your market, for wealth is part of well-being.”

He said: Ayyūb said, “You will not recognize your teacher’s mistake until you sit with someone else.”

He said: Ayyūb was asked, “May an enslaved person give charity?” He replied, “I do not know.” Then he said, “What is the matter with you? A man asks about fear, and he does not know what to say.”

“Abū Yūsuf related to us: Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us: Ḥammād related to us, who said: Ayyūb was asked a question and fell silent. The man said, ‘Abū Bakr, did you not understand? Shall I repeat it to you?’ Ayyūb replied, ‘I understood, but I am thinking about how to answer you.’”

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Sulaymān related to us: Ḥammād related to us, who said: One of the governors summoned Ayyūb (69a) and consulted him about something. Ayyūb said, “I have heard nothing about it that I can tell you.” He said:

“What is your opinion?” He replied, “I have no opinion about it.” The man said, “Then go.”

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Salama related to me: Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal related to us: ʿAbd al-Razzāq related to us, from Maʿmar, who said: Ayyūb used to say, “It pains me to hear a report from Muḥammad that I have not heard from him.”

Maʿmar said: “And it pains me to hear a report from Ayyūb that I have not heard from Ayyūb.”

Salama related to us, from Aḥmad: Ḥajjāj related to us, who said: Shuʿba said: Yūnus ibn ʿUbayd said, “I have never written anything down.”

Shuʿba said: Khālid al-Ḥadhdhāʾ said, “I never wrote anything down except one long report; whenever I memorized it, I erased it.”

Shuʿba said: Ayyūb said, “I remembered, though I would rather not remember.”

Ḥajjāj said: I heard Shuʿba say: Sometimes Ayyūb would go out on an errand, and I would want to walk with him, but he would not let me. He would go out and take one route and then another, so that he would not be noticed.

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb said: Ḥammād ibn Zayd said:

“I fear nothing for Ayyūb and Ibn ʿAwn in the Hereafter except the reports.” Then Sulaymān mentioned the report of ʿAṭiyya al-Sarrāj, and I have no doubt that he related the report.

Abū Yūsuf related to us—and Abū al-Nuʿmān had related to us: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, from Ayyūb from ʿAṭiyya al-Sarrāj, who said: I passed with al-Shaʿbī by one of the mosques of Juhayna. He said, “I testify that such-and-such a number of the people of this mosque, from among the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ” I think he said, “three hundred of them”—“drink nabīdh from large jars in the courtyards.”

Sulaymān said: Given Ayyūb’s merit and his position on intoxicants, what would he have done with this report, had his desire to relate reports not moved him to mention it? (69b)

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Salama related to us, from Aḥmad: Abū Quṭn related to us, who said: I heard Ibn ʿAwn say, “I wish I had come away from it—meaning from knowledge—with neither gain nor loss.”

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Salama related to us, from Aḥmad: ʿAffān related to us: Bishr ibn al-Mufaḍḍal related to us: Ibn ʿAwn related to us, who said: When Muḥammad died, we said, “Who?” He said: We said, “Ayyūb.”

“Abū Yūsuf related to us: Abū Bishr related to us: Muʿādh related to us: Hishām ibn Ḥassān told me: I saw Ayyūb correcting their books with his own hand.”

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us: Ḥammād related to us, from Hishām, who said:

Then I wrote nothing down from Muḥammad except the report of the necks; when I had memorized it, I erased it.

He also said: Ḥammād related to us, who said: Mūsā al-Aswārī used to come during Ramaḍān and pray behind Ayyūb.

He also said: Ḥammād related to us, who said: Ayyūb was present when Hishām ibn ʿUrwa related this report—I mean ʿĀʾisha’s report concerning Fāṭima bt. Abī Ḥubaysh—and he said to me:

“He is relating this report to me from memory.”

He also said: Ḥammād related to us, who said: Ayyūb said, “When you see a man doing something, do not speak about him until you ask him why he did it.”

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Salama related to us, from Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal: ʿAffān related to us: ʿAbd al-Wahhāb related to us, who said: When Ayyūb came to us from Mecca, he would say to us:

“Memorize the chain of transmission, for I forget it.”

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, who said: When Ayyūb arrived—I mean, from Mecca—he would say, “I have brought you four or five reports.”

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Abū Hāshim Ziyād ibn Ayyūb related to us: Saʿīd ibn ʿĀmir related to us: One of our companions related to us, who said: Ayyūb passed by the mosque of Banū Ḍubayʿa, and they returned his greeting. He realized they had added something to it, and began saying to himself, “God knows that I dislike this.”

(70a) Abū Yūsuf related to us: Abū Hāshim related to us: Saʿīd related to us, from Wuhaib ibn Khālid, Abū Bakr, the associate of the cloth merchants, who said: I heard Ayyūb say, “When the righteous are mentioned, I am far removed from them.”

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmar said: Sufyān said: I said to Ayyūb, “Ismāʿīl related to us a report from Muḥammad that he had memorized.” He replied, “It pains me to hear a report from Muḥammad that I have not memorized.”

Sufyān said: “Ayyūb related to us—and he was the most reliable person I had seen in his time—from Abū Bishr.”

Abū Yūsuf said: Sulaymān used to reject these reports and say, “These are barakat [unclear]; Ayyūb would not do anything like this.”

ʿAlī ibn al-Madīnī said: ʿAbd al-Aʿlā informed me: He said, “I saw Ayyūb escort Maʿmar as far as Iraq.” I said to ʿAbd al-Aʿlā, “What kept you from [learning] from Ayyūb?” He replied, “We used to hear from Ḥawshab, who practiced Sufism. They used to say, ‘Ayyūb has a hyena in his house,’ so we left him; then we regretted it afterward.”

ʿAlī said: It reached us from Ḥammād ibn Zayd that he said: “Ayyūb came back from Mecca, and I saw on his bed a saffron-colored covering. I went to look and lifted the covering; beneath it was coarse cloth.”

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Abū al-Nuʿmān related to us: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, from Ayyūb, who said: “I do not know predestination to be part of religion.”

He also said: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, who said: “I have never seen anyone smile more warmly in people’s faces than Ayyūb when he met them. Hārūn ibn Riʾāb was something remarkable.”57

ʿAlī said: I heard Sufyān say: Ayyūb was approached about giving someone a gift. He put his hand into the purse and gave him a handful, without counting or weighing it.

ʿAlī said: It reached me that Ayyūb used to pray at night. When morning came, he would clear his throat and speak, giving the impression that he had only just gotten up at that hour.

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Abū Saʿīd al-Ashajj related to us: Abū Khālid related to us, who said: I heard Shuʿba say, “Yes, a thousand and a thousand.”

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us: Sulaymān ibn Akhḍar related to us, who was to Ibn ʿAwn as Ḥammād ibn Zayd was to Ayyūb.

ʿAlī ibn al-Madīnī said: Yaḥyā used to rank Azhar above Sulaymān, and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān used to say the same about them. I would say this to Yaḥyā, and he would reply, “Be quiet! No one among them was more devoted to him or more sound.”

“ʿAlī said: I heard ʿAbd al-Raḥmān—and he mentioned those who pursued the study of reports—”

[He said: “There was no one among our companions who sought it] and devoted himself to it, memorized it, and persisted in it, until only three remained in it: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd, Sufyān ibn Ḥabīb, and Yazīd ibn Zurayʿ. They did not leave it from the time they began seeking it, nor did they occupy themselves with anything else; they remained devoted to it [until] they had transmitted it.”) Ismāʿīl ibn Ibrāhīm had memorized, then forgot. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: “Ibn Ismāʿīl gave me some excerpts from Ibn Abī Najīḥ. I met him as he was returning from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn al-Ḥasan, and asked him about them. He had memorized only one or two reports from them, but memorized them later.”

ʿAlī said: “ʿAbd al-Raḥmān never saw a book belonging to Ismāʿīl.”

[ʿAlī said:] “I cannot say that anyone is more firmly grounded in ḥadīth than Ismāʿīl.”

ʿAlī said: Yaḥyā said: “I never saw Ismāʿīl seeking ḥadīth, though we knew that he had heard it and then left it.”

Abū Yūsuf related to us: ʿAlī said: “Ismāʿīl was appointed over the alms collected from us in the year seventy-eight, and was given one-eighth. He was appointed because of his trustworthiness, and so he would not inspect anyone. He came to greet ʿAbd al-Wārith, who said to him: ‘Abū Bishr, what is this that Ayyūb—’”

“and Yūnus do?” We said: “Abū ʿUbayda, it is debt and dependents.” He replied: “Do you think the One who provides for the tiny creatures in the hard rock would overlook you?” Then ʿAbd al-Wārith said: “A morsel and some salt—and die with dignity.”

ʿAlī said: “It seems ʿAbd al-Wārith feared for him, for he was a young man.”

ʿAlī said: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad told me: “He came in to my mother and said, ‘I am dying.’ She said, ‘Glory be to God! May God protect you.’ He said, ‘I am dying; my sustenance has been cut off. I heard that sustenance has been cut off.’”

ʿAlī said: “He had seven servants, and they kept dying until the last one remained, the only one who worked. When that servant died, seven days before him, he went in to his wife and said these words to her:

‘This servant has died, and I will accept nothing from anyone. My sustenance has been cut off.’

He fell ill and died seven days later.”

ʿAlī said: “I never heard him say anything of what they accuse him of, nor did I hear him mention anyone who said any such thing. ʿAbd al-Wārith was a client of Balʿanbar ibn Tamīm, and Ibn ʿUlayya was a client of Banū Asad.”

Abū Yūsuf said: “I asked his son, and he said that their clientage was to Banū Asad.”

[Knowledge of the Judges]

The first judge to exercise jurisdiction over Baṣra was Abū Maryam al-Ḥanafī. Abū Mūsā appointed him to judge.

I heard Ibn al-Rahaṭī say: “He was the one who testified before Muʿāwiya on behalf of Ziyād ibn Sumayya, then Kaʿb ibn Saʿd, then Zurāra ibn Awfā, then ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn.”

After him, Zurāra exercised jurisdiction over Baṣra before ʿImrān, and twice after ʿImrān.

Then, after him, came ʿUmayra ibn Yathribī; Sayyid al-Jamal ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Yaʿlā; ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Faḍāla; and Hishām ibn Hubayra, a client of the Laythīs.

Among the Anṣār

Then came Thumāma ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Anas, Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Anṣārī, and al-Ḥasan, a client of the Anṣār. No client ever judged over them except al-Ḥasan; the Arabs used to judge over them.

Abū Yūsuf related to us: “I heard Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb say: ‘Al-Ḥajjāj ibn Arṭāh used to say to a man when he wanted to rule against him: “Do you have evidence? Do you have anything to say? Do you ... do you ...?” It was as though he were a judge over Baṣra.’”

And Sawwār ibn ʿAbd Allāh; ʿUbayd Allāh ibn al-Ḥasan al-ʿAnbarī; Khālid ibn Ṭulayq al-Anṣārī; Ibn Abī Ḥanīfa (71b); and Ibn Aktham.

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Sawwār ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sawwār told me: “Sawwār died in Dhū al-Ḥijja. He died in the year fifty-six, while serving as judge over Baṣra.”

“Bishr ibn Marwān ibn al-Ḥakam died as governor in Baṣra.” The third was Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān.

After Sawwār, ʿUbayd Allāh ibn al-Ḥasan was appointed judge. Al-Mahdī dismissed him and appointed Ḥammād ibn Ṭulayq, who was dismissed and faced hardship. After him, ʿUmar ibn ʿUthmān al-Taymī was appointed judge, but asked to be relieved. Then Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān appointed Muʿādh ibn Muʿādh ibn Naḍr ibn Ḥassān ibn Mālik ibn al-Khashkhāsh. He said: “I think al-Makhzūmī came before Muʿādh.” Then Hārūn dismissed them and appointed ʿUmar ibn Ḥabīb. After ʿUmar came Muʿādh, and after Muʿādh came al-Anṣārī.

Abū Yūsuf said: “I asked ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Muʿādh privately: ‘Abū ʿAmr, what happened between your father and al-Anṣārī?’”

“ʿAmr, what happened between your father and al-Anṣārī?” He was alarmed and said: “What business is it of yours?” He became angry, then looked at my face and said: “The Persian?” I said: “Yes.” He said: “Leave this alone.” I said: “Abū ʿAmr, people are spreading rumors, and perhaps they are false.”

He said: “I’ll put it plainly for you. By God, I fear for my father, my mother, my brothers, your little children and the older ones after us.” And whenever I said, “Abū ʿAmr, what was the reason for what you say?” he replied:

“It was that cloak of yours that stood here as an endowment and dedicated it to a group of people. If they died out, the endowment would revert to al-Anṣārī and others from his father’s Banū. During the days my father was judge, the endowment needed that fact to be established before my father. So he summoned al-Anṣārī and another man, and the two testified before my father. But my father did not accept al-Anṣārī’s testimony because the endowment would revert to him. Then it was said in the mosque that Muʿādh ibn Muʿādh had rejected al-Anṣārī’s testimony. He turned against us with every kind of harm and hurt us most severely, until my father, my mother, the youngest of us and the oldest all feared for ourselves in our homes.”

Sawwār ibn ʿAbd Allāh said: “After al-Anṣārī, my father ﵀—held office. Al-Anṣārī had been appointed to the second term by Ismāʿīl ibn Jaʿfar during the days of the civil strife, after your order.”

Sawwār said: “Sulaymān ibn al-Khalīl related to us: ‘I was present with Sawwār and ʿUmar ibn ʿĀmir. [Someone said:] “What can be hoped for from that? That is more courteous and better; I do not consider this a fault.” He said: “Anything that goes against the practice of the people at large, I consider a fault, and I reject it.”’”

So he returned to Sawwār’s position.

Sawwār said: “Muʿādh ibn Muʿādh told me: ‘Sawwār judged among us on the basis of his knowledge.’”

Muʿādh said: “Sulaymān ibn ʿAlī ordered a man to undergo retaliation on the basis of a document from Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Anṣārī concerning a sworn collective testimony that had been established before him. The man came forward with the sworn testimony, carrying a judge’s letter to another judge.”

I heard Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Anṣārī in the year two hundred and eleven say: “I am nearing ninety-four years of age, and my wish is that I might have authority in Baṣra for just one hour, so that I could drive this blind in sight, blind in heart, out of the mosque and send him back to al-Ubulla, where he could relate reports to his cousins”—meaning Abū ʿUmar the Blind.

Abū al-Rabīʿ al-Zahrānī said to him: “What is the matter with him, Abū ʿAbd Allāh?” He said: “He relates and dictates ḥadīths, then says, ‘Abū ʿUmar said such-and-such,’ contrary to what he relates from the early authorities. I have heard that he related that the Prophet ﷺ freed Ṣafiyya, married her, and made her emancipation her marriage gift.”

Abū ʿAmr said: “Abū ʿUmar would have preferred it if he had specified a marriage gift for her.” Abū al-Rabīʿ said: “They distort his words; he did not say that. He only said: ‘If someone did this today, I would prefer him to specify a marriage gift for her.’” He replied: “That is worse, and an even greater disinclination for what the Messenger of God ﷺ did and for his practice. Has he seen anyone among our companions do what he did and say what he said?” (72b) “He relates a ḥadīth, then says, ‘Abū ʿUmar said otherwise!’”

Abū Yūsuf said: “I heard al-Anṣārī say: ‘I heard many ḥadīths from Dāwūd ibn Abī Hind—I have mentioned a great number. A man heard them with me and set about copying them. He was away from me for a long time, so I left him and did not transmit them.’”

I heard him say: “I fell ill with an illness that took away my understanding and reason. When I regained my senses, my father said to me: ‘My son, Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd came to visit you while you were ill.’”

Al-Anṣārī said: “I did not understand him, because the illness had overwhelmed me.”

[ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAwn]

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us: Ḥammād [from] Ibn ʿAwn said: “I said [during a midday rest] at al-Ḥasan’s and Muḥammad’s, and the two of them remained standing until they spread out [a bed for me].”

He said: “I saw al-Ḥasan shake out the bedding for me with his own hand.”

I heard Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb say: Ḥammād ibn Zayd said: “When Ismāʿīl was born to me and began to move about, I took him to Ibn ʿAwn’s study circle, thinking that perhaps Ibn ʿAwn would pray for him. When we got up, the child said to us: ‘My father, who is that man’—meaning Ibn ʿAwn—‘that one looks as if he were one of the angels,’ or words to that effect.”

Abū Yūsuf said: Sulaymān related to us: ʿAbbād ibn ʿAbbād al-Muhallabī related to us: “A man asked Ibn ʿAwn about the witr prayer: ‘When should one pray witr?’ He told him what they used to do.”

The man said: “Tell me how you yourself do it.” When he said that, we said: “Abū ʿAwn, tell him.” He replied: “A man’s own mistakes are enough for him.”

Abū Bishr related to me: Khālid ibn al-Ḥārith related to us, from Ibn ʿAwn, who said: “I went to ʿIkrima with two men. We met him and asked him about it: ‘O you who believe, do not ask about things ...’ (Qurʾān 5:101). He said: ‘That was a day when the Prophet ﷺ stood up and said: “You will not ask me about anything without my telling you.”’

“A man stood up, and the Muslims disliked his standing that day. He said: ‘Messenger of God, who is my father?’ He replied: ‘Your father is Ḥudhāfa.’” Ibn ʿAwn said: “I never asked ʿIkrima about anything before this verse or after it. I asked Nāfiʿ about this verse—I had kept it in reserve to ask more than one person: ‘O you who believe, do not ask about things which, if disclosed to you, would distress you’ (Qurʾān 5:101). Nāfiʿ said: ‘As long as anyone can remember, asking too many questions has always been disliked.’” He said that when Nāfiʿ was asked, he would say, “I do not know.”

Abū Bishr related to me: Muʿādh related to us: Ibn ʿAwn related to us, saying: “Ḥumayd ibn Hilāl and Ghaylān ibn Jarīr used to visit Abū Burda. So I set out to visit Abū Burda, and met them coming from him. They said that Abū Burda had related to them from Ribʿī ibn Ḥirāsh.”

Abū Bishr related to me: Muʿādh said to me—and Bishr ibn al-Mufaḍḍal related to me—“One day I came home and found my father saying: ‘Ibn—’”

“ʿAwn came asking about you; go to him.’ So I went to him and said: ‘I heard that you came to ask me something.’

“He said: ‘Yes. That ḥadīth you related to me on such-and-such a day—what was its wording?’ I said: ‘Such-and-such.’ He said: ‘Yes, I was afraid I might not have related it to you as I have it.’”

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmmār related to us: Yaʿqūb al-Ḥaḍramī related to us: “Shuʿba says: ‘I heard him wanting to go to our master ʿAlī ibn ʿAlī.’”

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥīm related to us: ʿAlī said: “I heard ʿAbd al-Raḥmān say: ‘I know of no Successor who abandoned what Ibn ʿAwn abandoned of the Successors, leaving them for the sake of personal opinion.’”

ʿAlī said: “ʿAṭāʾ and Ṭāwūs held the view concerning currency exchange; Mujāhid related that he disliked currency exchange. He took this from Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn: ‘This knowledge is religion.’ In Medina, Mālik was among those who considered this matter. He took it from Ibn Shihāb, who took it from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab.”

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb said: Ḥammād said: “I have never seen anyone with a deeper understanding of jurisprudence than Dāwūd ibn Abī Hind.”

Abū Yūsuf related to us: ʿAmr ibn ʿĀṣim related to us: Sulaymān ibn al-Mughīra said: “We were with Ḥumayd ibn Hilāl, and Ayyūb and Yūnus ibn ʿUbayd were with him. When [Ḥumayd] got up—”

(73b) “as he was heading home, Ayyūb and Yūnus ibn ʿUbayd followed him. He said:

“I could see the distress on Ḥumayd ibn Hilāl’s face. He turned to me and said: ‘I used to think that if something happened to these two elders, these two would succeed them’—meaning al-Ḥasan and Ibn Sīrīn, and meaning Ayyūb and Yūnus. I said: ‘We do hope that of them.’ He said: ‘Did you not see them following me?’ He strongly disapproved of it.”

Abū Yūsuf related to me: Saʿīd ibn Ibrāhīm related to us, from Ḍamra, from Ibn Shawdhab, who said: “Yūnus ibn ʿUbayd and ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAwn met and discussed what was lawful. Each of them said: ‘I do not think there is a single lawful dirham in my house.’”

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Rabīʿ al-Khazzāz said: “Shawdhab’s wife brought a fine garment and laid it over Yūnus, saying: ‘Buy this, you there.’ He said: ‘For how much?’

“She said: ‘One hundred.’ He said: ‘Your garment is worth more than that.’ She said: ‘Two hundred.’ He said: ‘Your garment is worth more than that.’ She said: ‘Three hundred.’ He said: ‘Your garment is worth more than that.’ She said: ‘Four hundred.’ Abū Bishr said: ‘So I kept asking until it reached four or five hundred.’

“He said: ‘Is this how it is with us: if a man buys it and puts it away until a customer comes along who would make a profit of one hundred on it, should I take it?’ She said: ‘Take it.’ When she left, his companions turned to him and said: ‘Abū ʿAbd Allāh, what would it have cost you to buy it for one hundred?’ He said: ‘Nothing, except that I thought she was a woman who had been deceived, and I wanted to give her sincere advice.’”

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us: ʿUmāra al-Ṣaydalānī ...

Abū Yūsuf said: “Abū al-Nuʿmān also told me about him: ‘We were with Ayyūb—’”

Then Yaḥyā ibn ʿAytuq came. When he got up, Ayyūb said, “Whoever would be pleased to see my way of life in its entirety, let him look at Yaḥyā.”

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, from Yazīd al-Shannī, from Muwarriq al-ʿIjlī, who said: “I am rarely angry; perhaps I do not become angry even once in a year. [folio 74a] And perhaps, when angry, I say something that I regret once I am calm.”

[Muḥammad ibn Wāsiʿ]

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Saʿīd ibn Asad related to me: Ḍamrah related to us, from Ibn Shawdhab, who said: When it was asked in Basra, “Who is the finest of the people of Basra?” they would say, “Muḥammad ibn Wāsiʿ.” He was not seen to perform much worship, and he used to wear a shirt a Basran one, and a sājj cloak.

Through the same chain, from Ibn Shawdhab, who said: Muḥammad ibn Wāsiʿ attended a gathering where religious exhortation was given. When they finished, they ordered food, and Muḥammad ibn Wāsiʿ moved off to one side. They said, “Abū Bakr, will you not come closer to this food?” He replied, “Only those who have wept eat.”

Through the same chain, he said: Muḥammad ibn Wāsiʿ and Mālik ibn Dīnār met and spoke about livelihood. Mālik said, “There is nothing better than for a man to have an income from which he can live.” Muḥammad ibn Wāsiʿ said, “Blessed is the one who finds breakfast but not supper, and finds supper but not breakfast, while God is pleased with him.” Muḥammad ibn Wāsiʿ also said, “A little supplication suffices when accompanied by scrupulous piety, just as a little salt suffices for a pot.” Muḥammad ibn Wāsiʿ had an upper room; when night came, he would enter it and shut himself inside.

Through the same chain, from Ibn Shawdhab, who said: I said to Muḥammad ibn Wāsiʿ, “Abū Bakr…”

[Manṣūr ibn Zādhān]

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Salamah related to us, from Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, who said: Yazīd—meaning Ibn Hārūn—said: They claimed that Manṣūr—meaning Ibn Zādhān—used to complete a recitation by midmorning. This was known of him only from his prostrations during recitation of the Qurʾān. He recited quickly, and when he wanted to recite slowly, he could not. So he would send the codex to so-and-so, and he would cut it off [there]…

to so-and-so, and he would cut it off. Yazīd al-ʿAwwām mentioned that he was devoted to enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong. Al-Faḍl ibn Dalham was a butcher among us. I saw Layna Abū al-Mushrifī; [folio 74b] he was of fine appearance. Abū ʿAqīl was our judge. I saw Abū Balj, who was our neighbor; he had no interest in women, so he kept pigeons. Abū Balj said—while we were with him and he was remembering God—“If the Resurrection were to come and we entered Paradise,” he means, “we would still remember God.”

[Al-Aswad ibn Shaybān]

Salamah related to us, from Aḥmad; and ʿAffān related to us, who said: I once followed him—I mean al-Aswad ibn Shaybān—and said to him, “I want to go to the market, but you have kept me from my work.” He said, “And do I have an errand or a job?” I said to him, “What errand do you have?” He replied, “I pray.” Then I came to him another time, and he said, “Did you see me yesterday evening? They surrounded me as though I were an emir.” I was told that his family wanted to marry him off, but he kept refusing. He said to them, “And will she sleep with me on the bed?” They said, “Yes.” He said, “Then I have no need of her.”

ʿAffān related to us: Yazīd related to us, saying: Al-Aswad ibn Shaybān performed the pilgrimage without provisions for himself or fodder for his camel. His camel began grazing on the ground, while he drank its milk, until he completed the pilgrimage and returned. He would go every day to the cemetery and pray over the dead.

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Muḥammad ibn Manṣūr related to us: ʿAffān related to us: Yazīd ibn Zurayʿ related to us, who said: Whenever al-Aswad ibn Shaybān performed the pilgrimage, he would buy a milch camel, make the pilgrimage on it without taking provisions, and drink its milk until he returned.

[Abū Yūsuf related to us: Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us: Sufyān related to us, from Mujālid, from al-Shaʿbī, who said: I contended with the people of Basra and overcame them by citing the people of Kufa. Al-Aḥnaf sat silent and did not speak. When he saw that I had overcome them, he sent one of his servants, who came back with a letter.

He said to me, “Here, read this.” I read it, and it said: “From al-Mukhtār to him,” stating that he was a prophet.

He said: Al-Aḥnaf means, “How could there be anyone like this among us?”]

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Abū Bakr related to us: Sufyān related to us, saying: I heard ʿAmmār ibn Ruzayq say: We were told that there was a man in Kufa who claimed to be a prophet. He said: I went to him [folio 75a], and there we found a weaver weaving. We spoke to him, and he said, “I am a prophet.” We said to him, “A prophet who is a weaver?” He said, “What would you have me be, a money changer?”

He also said: Sufyān related to us: Shuʿbah ibn al-Ḥajjāj related to us, who said: Al-Ḥasan was asked:

“Which are better, the people of Kufa or the people of Basra?” Al-Ḥasan replied, “He would begin with the people of…”

Kufa.

[Abū Yūsuf related to us: Abū Bakr related to us, from al-Ḥuwayṭī and another man, one of whom related from Ḥammād ibn Zayd and the other from Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh. One of them said, “Ḥamzah al-Zayyāt’s recitation is an innovation.” The other said, “If a man led me in prayer and recited according to Ḥamzah’s recitation, I would repeat my prayer.”]

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Salamah related to us, from Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal: ʿAffān ibn Muslim related to us: Muʿādh related to us, who said: Al-Ashʿath said, “I never saw Hishām with al-Ḥasan at all.” He was asked, “ʿAmr says this. If you say it, you will strengthen his case against him—or confirm it, or something to that effect.” He said, “I will not say this, and I will not return to this.”

He also said: ʿAffān related to us: Wahb related to us, who said: I saw Mubārak ibn Faḍālah narrating from Yūnus in Yūnus’s study circle, while Yūnus [the wording here is unclear]. Ḥammād said:

Mubārak used to sit with us with al-Aʿlam. When a connected Prophetic report came, Mubārak would speak; when a legal opinion came, it was referred to al-Aʿlam.

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Aḥmad ibn al-Khalīl related to us, saying: I heard Yazīd ibn Hārūn say: I heard ʿĀṣim al-Aḥwal in Kufa, then I came to Wāsiṭ, and Shuʿbah related to me from ʿĀṣim—while he was still alive.

I heard Yazīd say: ʿAlī ibn Zayd lived for some time after Qatādah, and he transmitted from Qatādah the story of the robe: “The Prophet ﷺ bought a robe.”

Aḥmad ibn al-Khalīl related to us: Hārūn ibn Maʿrūf related to us: Ḍamrah related to us, from Ibn Shawdhab, who said: Qatādah entrusted [his affairs] to Maṭar, and Maṭar entrusted [his affairs] to Farqad. I sometimes heard Maṭar say to Saʿīd ibn Abī ʿArūbah, “What will you face from the people after me?”—meaning, legal questions. [folio 75b]

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Muḥammad ibn al-Minhal related to us: Yazīd ibn Zurayʿ related to us: Saʿīd ibn Abī ʿArūbah and Hishām al-Dastawāʾī related to us, from Qatādah, from Anas ibn Mālik, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “One who says ‘There is no god but God’ and has in his heart goodness weighing as much as a barley grain will come out of the Fire. One who says ‘There is no god but God’ and has in his heart goodness weighing as much as a wheat grain will come out of the Fire. Then one who says ‘There is no god but God’ and has in his heart goodness weighing as much as an atom will come out of the Fire.” Yazīd said: I met Shuʿbah and related the hadith to him. Shuʿbah said, “Qatādah related to us…” from Anas ibn Mālik, from the Prophet ﷺ with a report like it, except that Shuʿbah put “a small pearl” in place of “an atom.” Yazīd said: Abū Bisṭām [Shuʿbah] made a transcription error in it.

Yazīd said: I met ʿImrān, Abū al-ʿAwwām al-Qaṭṭān, and related the hadith to him. He said, “Qatādah related it to us, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yazīd al-Laythī, from Abū Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ” with the hadith.

Yazīd said: ʿImrān was mistaken; he erred about it. He said: ʿImrān was a Ḥarūrī, and held that the sword should be used against the people of the qiblah. He said: Ibrāhīm appointed him when the raiding force set out from Basra.

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Muḥammad ibn al-Minhal, Abū Dāwūd, related to us, saying: Shuʿbah said, “Where were you all when I was free, during the time Yazīd ibn Zurayʿ used to visit me?”

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Muḥammad related to me: Yazīd related to us, saying: I used to visit Shuʿbah before Ibrāhīm set out. I would arrive while he was asleep, with flies on his face, and wake him. He would relate to me without my having any notes with me for him to dictate from. Later, there were two of us, Ibn ʿUlayyah and me; then there were three of us, Ibn ʿUlayyah, Abū ʿAwānah, and me; then after that we became four, with ʿUbayd Allāh ibn al-Ḥasan.
