We remained four until we had learned what he had.

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Muḥammad related to us: Yazīd related to us, saying: Shuʿbah [folio 76a] never said anything to me that displeased me, except once. He related a hadith to me from Muḥammad ibn Ziyād, from Abū Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said in a hadith, “Does one of you not fear, when he raises his head…” I said to him, “Who is below Muḥammad?” He said, “I am, I am.” He struck his chest and shouted in my face. I left him for a while without speaking to him. He said to me, “What is the matter? Why do you not ask?” I said, “I have absolutely no desire to ask you about this evening’s hadith.” Before dawn, he came to the house and knocked at the door. He said, “Do not be upset; forgive me for…” I said, “I will, Abū Bisṭām. May God not let you be distressed; you did nothing but good.”

[ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd]

Sufyān said: Abū Mūsā related to us: ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd related to us before he began transmitting.

[Sufyān said: Al-Ḥasan saw Ayyūb and said, “This is the foremost of the young men of Basra.” He once saw ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd and said, “This is one of my foremost young men of Basra, if he does not begin transmitting.”]

[Abū Yūsuf related to us: Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, who said: Ayyūb was told, “ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd related from al-Ḥasan that he said that a person intoxicated by date wine is not flogged.” Ayyūb said, “ʿAmr lied. I heard al-Ḥasan say, ‘A person intoxicated by date wine is flogged.’”]

[Abū Yūsuf related to us: Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us, from Sallām ibn Abī Muṭīʿ, who said: Ayyūb said to me, “How can you trust the hadith of a man whose religious integrity you do not trust?”—meaning ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd.

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, from Ayyūb, who said: “How astonishing—a boy among boys, who deludes himself58 in plain view, right before him and between his legs, calling people to himself.”

He also said: Ḥammād related to us, saying: ʿAmr sent word to Ayyūb, “I would like to meet you, for people are telling lies about me.” We met in such-and-such mosque—Sulaymān named it. When Ayyūb had finished the prayer, he turned to ʿAmr to question him. He said: Then a man came… [folio 76b] to speak to Ayyūb, so Ayyūb turned toward him and left ʿAmr. ʿAmr got up and left.

[Abū Yūsuf related to us: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Makhramī related to us: Zakariyyā ibn ʿAdī related to us: Ibn al-Mubārak related to us, from Maʿmar, who said: “I never considered ʿAmr a rational man.”]

[Abū Yūsuf related to us: Sulaymān related to us: Bakr related to us, who said: I sat with ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd among the Basran scholars, and he said, “A thief is not exempted from punishment.” I said, “What about the hadith of Ṣafwān?” He said to me, “Would you swear that the Prophet ﷺ said this?” I said, “Would you swear by God that the Prophet ﷺ did not say this?”

[He swore by God that the Prophet ﷺ did not say it.] He said: I related that to Ibn ʿAwn. After that, he would say, “My son, relate it to the people.”]

[Sulaymān said: Ḥammād ibn Zayd said: ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd and Shabīb ibn Shaybah sat arguing one night until dawn. He said: They did not pray even two rakʿahs that night.

He said: ʿAmr kept saying, “Go on, Abū Maʿmar! Go on, Abū Maʿmar!”]

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Salamah related to us, from Aḥmad: ʿAbd al-Razzāq related to us, who said: I said to Maʿmar:

“People claim that all these hadiths from al-Ḥasan come through ʿAmr?”

He said: “No. I only sought knowledge when al-Ḥasan died”. He said: “Then I was …” and he related something transmitted from him.

ʿAbd al-Razzāq said: “I kept pressing him for the chain of transmission, but he would say, ‘Somebody said.’”

[Abū Yūsuf narrated to us; Abū Bishr related to me; Muʿādh ibn Muʿādh narrated to us. He said:

“I was sitting with ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd when a man called ʿUthmān, the brother of al-Samarī, came to him and said, ‘Abū ʿUthmān, by God, today I heard disbelief.’

“He said, ‘Do not be hasty. What did you hear?’

“He said, ‘I heard Hāshim al-Awqaṣ say: “Perish the hands of Abū Lahab” (111:1), and His words, “Leave Me with him whom I created alone” (74:11), and “I shall cast him into Saqar” (74:26)—that this is not in the Mother of the Book. (77a) Yet God says: “Ḥā Mīm. By the clear Book, We have made it an Arabic Qurʾān, so that you may understand. And indeed it is, in the Mother of the Book with Us, exalted, wise” (43:1–4). So what is disbelief, if not this, Abū ʿUthmān?’

“ʿAmr was silent for a while, then turned to me and said, ‘By God, if the matter were as he says, neither Abū Lahab nor al-Walīd would deserve blame.’

“He said, ‘Does ʿUthmān say that?’ This, by God, is the religion, Abū ʿUthmān.” Muʿādh said:]

“He entered into Islam and came out in disbelief [or so he said]”.

Abū Yūsuf narrated to us; Salamah narrated to us; Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal narrated to us; ʿAffān narrated to us; Hammām related to me; Maṭar narrated to us. He said: “ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd met me and said, ‘By God, you and I are certainly upon one and the same matter.’” He said: “By God, he lied. He meant that we were both upon the earth.”

Maṭar said: “By God, I do not believe him about anything.”

I heard al-Ḥasan ibn al-Rabīʿ say: “We used to hear hadith from ʿAbd al-Wārith. When the prayer was called, we would leave and not pray behind him.”

He said: Ibn al-Mubārak was asked, “How could you transmit from ʿAbd al-Wārith but leave ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd?” He replied, “ʿAmr was a propagandist.”

[Abū Yūsuf narrated to us; Salamah narrated to us; Aḥmad narrated to us; ʿAffān narrated to us; Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us. He said: “Ḥumayd was among those most careful to avoid him. One day he came to Ḥumayd, and Ḥumayd related a hadith to us. ʿAmr said, ‘Al-Ḥasan used to say it.’ Ḥumayd said to me, ‘Do not take anything from this man: he lies about al-Ḥasan. He would come to al-Ḥasan after he had grown old and say, “Abū Saʿīd, do you not say such-and-such about the matter …”’]

“—something that was not his own words.” He said: “The shaykh would nod his head like this”.

[Abū Yūsuf narrated to us: I heard Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb say: Hārūn al-Aʿwar narrated to us—he was severe in his statements about predestination.]

Saʿīd ibn ʿĀmir al-Ḍabʿī

Abū Yūsuf narrated to us; ʿUqbah related to me; Saʿīd ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us, from Jaʿfar ibn Sulaymān. He said: (77b) “We were with Mālik ibn Dīnār when the time for the afternoon prayer came, and he got up to perform ablution.

“Ibn Wāsiʿ said, ‘Mālik is an excellent man, Mālik is an excellent man. Take from Mālik, take from Mālik and Thābit. And Abū ʿImrān al-Jawnī has excellent hadith.’”

Abū Yūsuf narrated to us; ʿUqbah ibn Mukram narrated to us; Saʿīd ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us, from Asmāʾ ibn ʿUbayd. He said: “I said to Yūnus, ‘Abū ʿAbd Allāh!’ He replied, ‘Abū al-Mufaḍḍal!’”

And from Saʿīd ibn ʿĀmir, from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, who said: “I intended to set out for India. I said to al-Ḥasan, ‘Give me counsel.’ He said, ‘Go on a campaign; may God grant victory wherever you are, through the work of God.’”

And from Saʿīd, from Asmāʾ, who said: “I went to Yūnus ibn ʿUbayd. He came out to me and sat at the door of the house. He looked distressed and sorrowful. I said, ‘Abū ʿAbd Allāh, what is troubling you?’ He was silent for a long while, then raised his head and said, ‘By God, this is what I see among the common people.’”

And from Saʿīd: al-Rabīʿ ibn Ṣubayḥ narrated to us. He said: “When Yazīd ibn al-Muhallab was defeated and driven from Baṣrah, and Friday came, Abū Naḍrah said, ‘A city in such a state should not hold a congregational Friday prayer.’

“They sent for al-Ḥasan, but he did not come. Abū Naḍrah went to him and brought him back. There were two screened prayer enclosures, and the pulpit was in the outer one. He ascended the pulpit, preached to us, and led us in the Friday prayer. He pronounced the full takbīr, whereas the Marwānids did not pronounce the full takbīr.

“When the following Friday came, the people of Syria arrived, but their governor, Ibn Sulaym, did not arrive.

“They said, ‘Let the one who led you in prayer last Friday lead you today.’ They sent for al-Ḥasan, and he came and did as he had done the previous Friday.”

And from Saʿīd, from Bishr, from Ibn Mālik, from Ibn ʿAwn, who said: “I went to Sālim al-ʿAdawī and said, ‘I was told that you saw the new moon last night.’ He said, ‘Yes.’

“I said, ‘Then I shall go straight to Ibn Sīrīn.’ I said, ‘This is Sālim; he claims that he saw the new moon last night.’ He said, ‘I do not know who Sālim is.’”

And from Saʿīd, from Ḥumayd ibn al-Aswad, who said: “Mālik ibn Anas said: ‘The leading authority among the people in our view after ʿUmar was Zayd ibn Thābit, and the leading authority among the people in our view after Zayd ibn Thābit was Ibn ʿUmar.’”

(178a) And from Saʿīd, from Ḥumayd ibn al-Aswad, from Ibn ʿAwn, who said:

“I encountered hadiths that were not known; they are the ones known today.”

And through the same chain, from Ibn ʿAwn, who said: “I found this mosque such that no circle in it discussed jurisprudence except the circle of Muslim ibn Yasār; the other circles told stories.”

And from Saʿīd, from Ṣāliḥ ibn Rustum, who said: “I have never seen anyone more in control of himself when listening than Ayyūb.”

And from Saʿīd, from Ḥumayd ibn al-Aswad, from Thawr ibn Yazīd, from Khālid ibn Maʿdān, who said: “I heard ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Marwān preaching”—then he mentioned him.

And from Saʿīd, who said: “Whenever one of Ayyūb’s brothers died, he would go to his family the next morning and sit with them.” Yaʿlā ibn Ḥakīm mentioned that Ayyūb had no family here except his mother, so he came the next day and sat at the door. He said: “When one of his brothers was gravely ill, Ayyūb would see to his family’s needs, then come and spend the night with the sick man, keeping him company. Ayyūb’s tongue was bound before he died. Abū Ḥamzah came in, and Ayyūb began pointing with his finger to his back. Abū Ḥamzah used to relate this account.”

He said: “Ibrāhīm said:

‘If I heard that one of them did no more than wash a man’s back, I would not even wash my palms; I seek the greater reward.’”

And from Saʿīd, from Saʿīd ibn Sulaymān, who said: “My brother and I went in to visit Ayyūb when he had been stabbed. My brother was older than I was, and Ayyūb’s tongue had become bound. My brother said to him:

“‘May my father and mother be your ransom! Rejoice, may my father and mother be your ransom, in one of the two best outcomes: either a life spent in obedience or death. What is with God is better for the righteous.’”

He said: “It was as though that pleased him.” He said: “Then my brother repeated it to him, and it was as though that pleased him.”

He said: “I heard Saʿīd ibn ʿĀmir say: ‘I saw Yazīd al-Rishk.’” He said: “His mother was a client of Banū Ḍubayʿah, and his father was among those whom God had blessed with Islam.”

And from Saʿīd, who said: “ʿAwf ibn Abī Jamīlah al-Aʿrābī was born in the year fifty-seven or fifty-eight, during the time of Muʿāwiyah.”

And from Saʿīd, from Hishām, who said: “Yaḥyā ibn Sīrīn would take precedence over Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn.”

And from Saʿīd ibn ʿĀmir, who said: “Muḥammad ibn ʿUmar came to us in the year 137 or 138, with Sulaymān ibn ʿAlī.”

And from Saʿīd ibn ʿĀmir, who said: “Anas ibn Mālik died in the year 93, and Sulaymān al-Taymī died in the year 143.”

And from Saʿīd: “Al-Ḥajjāj ordered Yazīd al-Rishk to survey Baṣrah. He found it to be two farsakhs long and five dāniqs wide. In its middle he found the cemetery of Banū Yashkur or Banū Ḍubayʿah”—Saʿīd was uncertain.

And from Saʿīd, who said: “Sulaymān al-Taymī would glorify God seventy times in every prostration and bowing.”

He said: “I heard Saʿīd ibn ʿĀmir say: ‘You have never seen a Kūfan or a Baṣran like Ibn ʿAwn.’”

And from Saʿīd, from Sallām, from Ayyūb, who said: “As for my taking sūdah, that is easy enough”—meaning a short measure—“but I find it difficult to give a measure that is full.”

And from Saʿīd, who said: “A companion of ours said: ‘Some people went in to see Abū Rajāʾ.’ He said:

“They looked around and saw nothing, so his wife said to them, ‘He is beneath the cloak and the quilt.’

“They lifted its edge, and there were his eyes, darting about. They spoke to him in words that made him long for death. They said:

“‘You poor man, what is this love of life that makes you breathe?59 That I should pray and remember my Lord—even if I died, that would cease for me.’”

And from Saʿīd: Sallām ibn Abī Muṭīʿ related to me. He said: “Ayyūb would pray at night in secret. Then, just before dawn, he would raise his voice as though he had only just begun praying at that hour.”

And from Saʿīd, who said: “Al-Ḥasan died at the age of eighty-seven, and he was born …”

…for two years of the caliphate of ʿUmar remained.

ʿUqbah ibn Mukram narrated to us; ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĪsā narrated to us. He said: “I asked Yūnus, ‘How old was al-Ḥasan on the day ʿUthmān was killed?’ He said, ‘Fourteen. He was born in a year remaining of ʿUmar’s caliphate.’”

Abū Yūsuf narrated to us; Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad al-Shāfiʿī narrated to us; Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ narrated to us. He said: “Ibn Abī Rawwād claimed that he saw al-Ḥasan praying before it”—that is, before the Eid prayer.

(79a) Abū Yūsuf narrated to us; Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm narrated to me in Mecca; ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Abū Laylā [ibn] ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Maḥmūd ibn Asad. He said: “Men from my people, the Anṣār, informed me: ‘We were sitting with the Messenger of God ﷺ. So-and-so was among us’”—he named him. “The Messenger of God pointed to so-and-so and said, ‘This man will one day seek authority. When he does, do such-and-such to him.’”

Abū Yūsuf narrated to us; Isḥāq related to me; Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh narrated to us; Abū Ḥuṣayn narrated to us. He said: “My uncle and I went in to see Ibn ʿAbbās and asked him.”

Abū Yūsuf narrated to us; Isḥāq related to me; Marwān informed us; Yaḥyā ibn Maysarah, a shaykh known by the kunya Abū Yazīd, narrated to us; ʿAmr ibn Murrah narrated to us. He said: “I was with Abū ʿUbaydah ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, who at that time was the judge appointed by Maṭar ibn Nāḥiyah.”

Abū Yūsuf narrated to us; Isḥāq related to me; Marwān informed us; Abū Mālik al-Ashjaʿī narrated to us; Nubayṭ ibn Sharīṭ ibn Anas al-Ashjaʿī, Abū Salamah, narrated to us.

[Isḥāq] informed us; Marwān narrated to us; Ismāʿīl ibn Sumayʿ related to us, from Mālik ibn ʿUmayr al-Ḥanafī, who said: “I had an uncle called ʿAbbār ibn Salamah—ʿAbbār, the trustworthy elder—and he was among those who testified against Qudāmah ibn Maẓʿūn.”

[Isḥāq] informed us; Marwān narrated to us; Abū Sufyān Ṭarīf al-ʿAṭāridī narrated to us.

Abū Yūsuf narrated to us; Isḥāq related to me; Marwān informed us; ʿImrān ibn Ḥurayth informed us …

He said: “I saw ʿAzzah, the mother of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yazīd ibn al-Shikhkhīr.”

Abū Yūsuf narrated to us; Isḥāq related to me; Marwān informed us; Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid informed us, from his brother al-Nuʿmān.

Abū Yūsuf narrated to us; Isḥāq related to me; ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, from al-ʿAlāʾ ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, who said: “I heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar relating a hadith to my father.”

Abū Yūsuf narrated to us; Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm related to me; Hushaym informed me; Yaʿlā ibn ʿAṭāʾ informed us, from al-Walīd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Jurashī, from Ibn ʿUmar, who said to Abū Hurayrah: “Abū Hirr—(79b)—you were the most constant among us in keeping company with the Messenger of God ﷺ and the most knowledgeable among us about his hadith.”

Abū Yūsuf narrated to us; Isḥāq related to me; Hushaym informed us; Abū Balj informed us; Thuwair, the client of Banū Hāshim, narrated to us.

Abū Yūsuf narrated to us; Isḥāq related to me; ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar ibn Najīḥ informed us, from Rabīʿah ibn Abī ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from a shaykh of the people of Medina, from Zayd ibn Khālid al-Juhanī—the hadith concerning found property.

Rabīʿah said: “Ziyād ibn Abī Ziyād informed me that the shaykh who narrated to me was Yazīd ibn al-Munbaʿith.”

Abū Yūsuf narrated to us; Isḥāq related to me; ʿAbbād informed me; Saʿīd informed us, from Abū …

Maʿshar—from Ibrāhīm—that he used to travel with ʿAlqama and al-Aswad. He would visit the Mothers of the Believers and see them in red blankets.

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Isḥāq related to me: Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh related to us. He said:

“I heard al-Mughīra say: ‘Among the companions of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, only they could be trusted regarding reports from ʿAlī.’”

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Abū Bishr Bakr ibn Khalaf related to me: Khālid ibn al-Ḥārith related to us: Saʿīd related to us. He said: “I saw Ibn Sīrīn in the congregational mosque. I was beside him during the afternoon prayer, and he sat cross-legged at the end of his prayer.”

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Bakr related to us: ʿAbd al-Wahhāb related to us, from Ayyūb, who said: ʿAlī ibn Nāfiʿ came and said, “Your friend ʿIkrima has arrived.” I went to him and asked him, but he said, “By God, I will not relate anything to you.” I said, “Then I will walk with you.” He said, “Yes.” He related to me reports that seemed more precious in my eyes than pearls. Then a Bedouin came to him and said, “A man who marries his daughter for the mahr of the mahr—60” He replied, “The one who has intercourse with her, though he had not …”61

Abū Yūsuf related to us: ʿUqba ibn Mukram related to us: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar related to us: Shuʿba, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from Ṭāwūs, from Ibn al-ʿAdalī—or he said, al-ʿAndalī—from Zayd ibn Thābit from the Prophet ﷺ. He said: “The ʿumrā?” He replied: “It belongs to the heir.”

Abū Yūsuf related to us: ʿUqba ibn Mukram related to me: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar related to us (80a): Shuʿba, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār. I heard Ṭāwūs relate from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said concerning a man who has intercourse before making the circumambulation of the House on the Day of Sacrifice: “He owes a sacrificial camel.”

Shuʿba said: “I related this to Ayyūb, and he said to ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, ‘From whom is it?’ He replied, ‘I heard Ṭāwūs relate from Ibn ʿAbbās.’ Ayyūb said, ‘From Ibn ʿAbbās?’ ʿAmr replied, ‘I heard Ṭāwūs,’ and left out Ibn ʿAbbās.”

Abū Yūsuf related to me: ʿUqba related to us: al-Walīd ibn Khālid said: Shuʿba said to me, “Ayyūb said to me, ‘Do not transmit from Khilās, for he is a ṣuḥufī.’” He said: “Later he said, ‘I consider him a ṣuḥufī.’”

Abū Yūsuf related to us: ʿUqba related to us: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar related to us, from Furāt, from a client of Umm Salama, who said: “When Saʿd died, he was brought on a bier and taken in to Umm—”

Salama. She began to weep and said, “The last of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ.”

Abū Yūsuf related to us: ʿUqba related to me: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar related to us: Shuʿba, from Furāt. He said: “I heard Abū Ḥāzim say, ‘I kept company with Abū Hurayra for five years.’”

Abū Yūsuf related to us: ʿUqba related to us: Saʿīd ibn ʿĀmir related to us, from Shuʿba, from Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid, from Qays ibn Abī Ḥāzim, that ʿAmmār said: “Bury me in my clothes, for I am a litigant.”

Abū Yūsuf related to us: ʿUqba related to me: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī related to us, from Shuʿba, from Yazīd ibn Abī Ziyād, who said: “I asked Abū Wāʾil, ‘Are you older, or Masrūq?’”

He replied, “I am older than Masrūq.”

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Muḥammad ibn Bashshār said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said:

“Sufyān heard no report from Abū ʿAwn other than this one: Marwān said, ‘How can we ask anyone when the wives of the Prophet ﷺ are among us?’”

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Ibn Bashshār related to us: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar related to us, from Shuʿba, from Ghaylān ibn Jarīr, who said: “I heard Abū al-Ḥallāl al-ʿAtakī say, ‘I was sent by Ibn ʿĀmir to ʿUthmān on an errand. When I had finished, he said, “Do you have a request?” I said, “No, except—”’”

“—that a man asked me to ask you about a man (80b) who has put the matter of his wife in her hands.”

He replied, “Then the matter is in her hands.”

He also said: Shuʿba related to us. He said: “I heard Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Shaqirī, Salama ibn Nammām.”

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Bundār related to us: Abū Dāwūd related to us: Shuʿba related to us: ʿUbayda ibn Muʿtab related to me. One of his earliest reports was the report of Abū Ayyūb.

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Abū Bishr and Muḥammad ibn Bashshār related to me; they said: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar related to us: Shuʿba said: “I heard Mubashshir ibn ʿImrān ibn ʿUmayr relate from Umayya, from his grandfather, that he went out with ʿAbd Allāh, riding behind him on his mule, for a journey of four parasangs. He prayed the noon prayer as two rakʿas and the afternoon prayer as two rakʿas.” Shuʿba said: “Mubashshir ibn ʿImrān ibn ʿUmayr related this to me from his father, and his father was present.”

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Muḥammad ibn Bashshār related to us. He said: “I heard Ibn Abī ʿAdī say, ‘I recited the Qurʾān to Abū Rajāʾ, but I heard nothing from him.’”

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Bundār related to us: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar informed us—God willing—: Shuʿba, from ʿĀṣim, who said: “I presented al-Shaʿbī with a book containing a report from Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ: ‘A woman is not to be married together with her paternal aunt or her maternal aunt.’”

And from Shuʿba, from ʿĀṣim, from Abū Qilāba, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib, concerning a man who broke his fast on a day in Ramaḍān. He said: “He must fast for a month.”

And from Shuʿba, from ʿĀṣim, from Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn, who said: “ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb would give a slave recourse against his master when the slave sought redress against him. My father sought redress against Anas ibn Mālik before ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb.”

“Abū Yūsuf related to us: Ibn Bashshār related to us: Abū Dāwūd related to us: Shuʿba, from ʿĀṣim, from Abū Ḥājib, from al-Ḥakam ibn ʿAmr—al-Aqraʿ—: The Prophet ﷺ forbade a man to perform ablution with the water left over from a woman’s ablution.”

Abū Yūsuf related to us: ʿUqba ibn Mukram related to me, from Abū ʿĀṣim, from Ibn Jurayj. Sulaymān ibn Bābayh, a client of the Banū Nawfal, informed me; and Ibn Jurayj said:

“I heard Muḥammad ibn ʿAbbād ibn Jaʿfar say: ‘Muslim ibn Yasār, the client of Nāfiʿ ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥārith, instructed me to ask Ibn ʿUmar—and I was sitting between the two of them—:

“Did you hear the Prophet ﷺ regarding one who drags his garment out of pride?”’”

He said: “I heard him say, ‘God will not look upon him on the Day of Resurrection.’”

Abū Yūsuf related to us. He said: “I heard Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Numayr mention, on the authority of ʿAmmār ibn Rizayq, who was one of the learned men of Kūfa, that he said: ‘When you are asked about something and its answer is not clear to you, consider what Abū Ḥanīfa said and oppose him; you will be right.’”

Abū Yūsuf related to me: ʿUqba related to us: Muḥammad ibn Bakr related to us: Ibn Jurayj, from Sulaymān al-Aḥwal, informed me that Thābit, the client of ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, had informed him. He was Thābit al-Aḥnaf.

[Qatāda]

Abū Yūsuf related to me: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥīm related to us: ʿAlī related to us: Abū al-Khayr, from Ibn Idrīs, from Shuʿba, who said: “I agreed with Qatāda on the reports, except for four.”

Abū Yūsuf related to me: ʿUthmān ibn Abī Shayba related to us: Jarīr, from Mughīra, who said: “Al-Shaʿbī was asked, ‘Did you see Qatāda?’ He replied, ‘Yes. I saw him gathering wood in the night.’”

Abū Yūsuf said: “Qatāda went to Wāsiṭ, harming people and informing against them—”

So they said, “Deport him.”

Abū Yūsuf related to me: Abū Bishr related to us: Muʿādh ibn Muʿādh, from Ashʿath, said:

“When Qatāda was deported, al-Ḥasan said, ‘Indeed, those who fulfill [their obligations] are tested.’”62

Salama related to us: Aḥmad said: ʿAbd al-Razzāq related to us: Maʿmar informed us: “Al-Zuhrī was asked, ‘Is Qatāda more learned among you, or Makḥūl?’ He said, ‘No, rather Qatāda. Makḥūl had only a little.’” He said: “It was not known whether Makḥūl was more learned than him or his equal.”

Salama related to us: Aḥmad informed us: ʿAbd al-Razzāq related to us: Maʿmar informed us. He said: “We used to sit with Qatāda when we were young and ask him about the chain of transmission. The elders around him would say, ‘Enough! Abū al-Khaṭṭāb has a chain of transmission,’ and they would discourage us from doing that.”

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Abū Bishr related to us: ʿAbd al-Razzāq, from Maʿmar, said:

“Al-Zuhrī was asked, ‘Which of the two is more learned, Makḥūl or Qatāda?’ He said, ‘Qatāda.’ He said, ‘What did Makḥūl have? Only a little.’” (81b)

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Salama related to us: Aḥmad informed us: ʿAbd al-Razzāq related to us, from Maʿmar, who said: Qatāda said to Saʿīd, “Abū al-Naḍr, take the muṣḥaf.” He said: “I recited it to him—”

Surat al-Baqara, and he did not make a single mistake in it. He said, “Abū al-Naḍr, have you mastered it?” He replied, “Yes.” He said, “I know the written collection of Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh better than I know Surat al-Baqara.” It had been read to him.

I heard Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb say: “Sulaymān al-Yashkurī spent a year residing in Mecca. Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh also resided there, and Sulaymān wrote down a written collection from him. He died early, and the collection remained with his mother. The people of Baṣra asked her to lend it to them, but she refused. They said, ‘Then let us have access to it so that we can read it.’ She said, ‘That, yes.’ Qatāda and others came and read it. This is the collection that our colleagues refer to when they say, ‘Sulaymān al-Yashkurī related’—or something similar.”

Salama related to us: Aḥmad related to us: ʿAbd al-Razzāq, from Maʿmar, said: Qatāda said, “I sat with al-Ḥasan for twelve years, praying the dawn prayer with him for three years.” He said, “A man like me learned from a man like him.”

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us: Sufyān related to us: ʿUmayr— He said: “I heard Ṭāwūs say, ‘Send Maʿbad al-Juhanī away.’” He was a Qadarite.

Salama related to us: Aḥmad related to us: Wakīʿ related to us. He said: Shuʿba said: “Qatāda would become angry when I pressed him for the chain of transmission. One day I related a report to him and he liked it. He said, ‘Who related it to you?’ I said, ‘So-and-so, from so-and-so.’ After that, he began giving the chain of transmission.”

Salama related to us: Aḥmad related to us: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad related to us: Abū Hilāl related to us. He said: “I asked Qatāda about a question, and he said, ‘I do not know.’ I said, ‘Give me your opinion.’ He said, ‘I have not given my opinion for forty years.’” He said: “How old was he then?” He replied: “About fifty.”

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Saʿīd ibn Asad related to us: Ḍamra related to us, from Ibn Shūdhub, who said: “Qatāda would not be satisfied until he shouted about predestination”—meaning, he shouted about the doctrine of predestination.

I heard Abū ʿUmar Ḥafṣ ibn ʿUmar al-Ḍarīr mention, on the authority of Abū— ʿAwāna, who said: “I went in to visit Hammām ibn Yaḥyā while he was ill. He said to me, ‘Abū ʿAwāna, pray to God that He does not let me die before my young children grow up.’ I replied, ‘The appointed term has already been decreed.’ He said to me, ‘You are still in your error.’”

Abū Yūsuf related to me: Saʿīd ibn Asad related to us: Ḍamra related to us, from Ṣadaqa ibn Yazīd, who said: “Al-Ḥajjāj used to torture Maʿbad al-Juhanī with different kinds of torment, but he would neither panic nor cry out for help. When the torment was stopped, he would see flies approaching and settling on him. Then he would shout and cry out.”

He said that Maʿbad said to him: “This torment is from human beings, and I can bear it. But flies are a torment from God, and I cannot bear it.” So he killed him.

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us: Sufyān related to us: ʿAmr ibn Dīnār related to us. He said: “I entered the house of Wahb ibn Munabbih in Ṣanʿāʾ, and he gave me a walnut from a walnut tree in his courtyard. I said to him, ‘I wish you had not written a book about predestination.’”

He replied, “By God, I wish that too.”

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Abū ʿUmayr said: “I heard Ḍamra relate from Ibn Shūdhub, who said: ‘I heard Qatāda shouting about predestination in the mosque of Baṣra.’”

[We were told:] Abū Yūsuf related to me: Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Abī al-Sarī related to us: ʿAbd al-Razzāq said: “I heard Mālik say”—and I asked him about Maʿmar, and he said—“Indeed, if it were not for—” I said, “If it were not for what?” He replied, “If it were not for his transmission from Qatāda.”

Abū Yūsuf related to us: Salama related to us: Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal related to us: ʿAffān related to us— Ismāʿīl ibn Ibrāhīm [transmitted] from Rūḥ ibn al-Qāsim, from Maṭar, who said: “Whenever Qatāda heard a ḥadīth, he would snatch it up instantly. If he heard a ḥadīth and had not memorized it, anxiety and agitation would seize him until he had memorized it.”

Aḥmad said: ʿAffān related to us; Ḥammād ibn Salama related to us. He said: “Qatāda would relate to us, saying, ‘It has reached us that the Messenger of God ﷺ—used to say such-and-such, and it has reached us that ʿUmar …’—without giving a chain of transmission.” Then Ḥammād ibn Abī Sulaymān came to us.63 We went to him and said, “We were told such-and-such from Ibrāhīm.” He said:

“Al-Ḥasan related to us, and Anas related to us, and Zurāra related to us; and I asked Saʿīd.”

He then poured out the chains of transmission upon us. He said: “We could not manage to memorize them. I would memorize seven from eighteen.” He said: “I would come and write down the ḥadīth at the chapter heading, and when I came back, I had memorized it from the heading. Once I had memorized it, I would erase it.”

Volume Two

Shuʿba ibn al-Ḥajjāj

“I heard Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb say: ‘If you had looked at Shuʿba’s clothes, you would have found that they were worth no more than ten dirhams: his waist-wrapper, shirt, and cloak. He was an elderly man who gave much in charity.’”

Sulaymān said: “I was present when Shuʿba was asked about ten bowls into which a mouse had fallen and died. He did not answer him, and was unable to give him an answer.”

Sulaymān said: “I heard that questions of al-Ḥakam and Ḥammād had been written down for him. He asked them both about those questions, and they were written down with him.”

Sulaymān said: “One day he related to us the ḥadīth of al-Aʿmash, from Zayd ibn Wahb, from ʿAbd Allāh: ‘The Messenger of God ﷺ—related to us, and he is the truthful one, the one whose truth was affirmed,’ along with similar ḥadīths. A man from the Qadariyya said to him, ‘Abū Bisṭām, do not relate these to us; we too forget.’ He then mentioned the ḥadīth of al-Aʿmash, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Abū Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ—said: ‘Every newborn is born in a state of natural purity.’”

Abū Yūsuf related to us; Salama related to us; Aḥmad related to us; Ḥajjāj related to us. Shuʿba said:

“I asked ʿĀṣim al-Aḥwal about a woman observing a mourning period. Ḥafṣa bint Sīrīn said:

‘Ḥumayd ibn Nāfiʿ, known as Ḥumayd the Younger, wrote to Ḥumayd al-Ḥimyarī and mentioned the ḥadīth of Zaynab bint Umm Salama.’ Shuʿba said: ‘I told ʿĀṣim, “I heard it myself from Ḥumayd ibn Nāfiʿ.” He said, “You?” I said, “Yes, and he is still alive.”’ Shuʿba said:

“ʿĀṣim had thought that he had been dead for a hundred years.”

I heard Abū al-Walīd Hishām ibn ʿAbd al-Malik say: “I heard Shuʿba say: ‘This ḥadīth keeps you from remembering God and from prayer. Will you not desist?’”

Salama related to us; Aḥmad related to us; Abū Qaṭan related to us. Shuʿba said: “There is nothing I persist in that I fear might cause me to enter the Fire, except this.”

Abū Yūsuf related to us; Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us. He said: “I heard Ḥammād say:

‘I fear nothing for Ayyūb and Ibn ʿAwn in the Hereafter except the ḥadīth.’”

Salama related to us; Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal related to us. I heard Yazīd ibn Hārūn say: “Shuʿba was generally a client of the Azd.”

“Abū Yūsuf related to us; Mujāhid ibn Mūsā related to me; Abū Kāmil Muẓaffar ibn Mudrik related to us. He said: ‘They mentioned to Shuʿba a ḥadīth he had not heard, and he kept saying, “Alas, how sad!”’”

Salama related to us; Aḥmad related to us; ʿAffān related to us. He said: “We were with Shuʿba, and they kept saying, ‘Abū Bisṭām, Abū Bisṭām!’ He said: ‘By God, I will not relate to anyone who says, “Abū Bisṭām, Abū Bisṭām,”’”

“Abū Bisṭām, Abū Bisṭām!” Then he mentioned the ḥadīth of ʿAwf, from Wahb ibn Munabbih: “The hypocrite loves praise and dislikes blame.”

Abū Yūsuf related to us; Salama related to us, from Aḥmad; Quraysh ibn Anas related to us. He said:

“Saʿīd ibn Abī ʿArūba swore to me that he had never written anything from Qatāda, except that Abū Maʿshar wrote to me asking me to write down Qatāda’s commentary for him. He meant to have me write down the commentary, and I kept …”

Salama related to us; Aḥmad related to us; Quraysh related to us. He said: “Ibn ʿAwn said: ‘What is being transmitted from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr in the book?’ Wuhayb ibn Khālid said: ‘The ḥadīth of ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb.’ He said: ‘I saw ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb.’ Ibn ʿAwn said: ‘Neither Abū Bakr nor ʿUmar wrote.’”

Ibrāhīm said: “The people have not been mentioned as having …” Someone else said:

“It is better for you.”

Salama related to us; Aḥmad related to us; ʿUthmān ibn ʿUmar related to us. Ibn ʿAwn said:

“I saw ʿAṭāʾ and Ṭāwūs.”

Aḥmad related to us; Quraysh related to us, from Ibn ʿAwn. He said: “Ḥammād kept asking Ibrāhīm, and he said, ‘What is this?’ He replied, ‘May God set you right; they are only fragments.’”

Aḥmad said: ʿAffān related to us. Ḥammād ibn Zayd said: “When strangers arrived, we would go to them, and Hishām al-Dastawāʾī would say, ‘Bring it while it is still fresh.’” He said:

“Of us, Jarīr ibn Ḥāzim had the best memory.”

He said: ʿAffān related to us, from Hammām. Qatāda said: “The one who transmits the most from me is Maṭar, and the one who transmits a ḥadīth most accurately is Saʿīd ibn Abī ʿArūba.”

Abū Yūsuf related to us; Muḥammad ibn Muṣaffā related to us; Baqiyya related to us. He said: “I have seen no one in Iraq like Ḥammād ibn Zayd.”

I heard from Ibn al-Madīnī, who said: I heard ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī say:

“I have never seen a man more knowledgeable about the Sunna than Ḥammād ibn Zayd, nor anyone more knowledgeable about a ḥadīth that pertains to it.”

Abū Yūsuf related to us; Abū Saʿīd ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm related to us. He said:

Al-Walīd related to us, from al-Awzāʿī, who said: “Naṣr ibn Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr used to give knowledge freely.”

Abū Yūsuf related to us; Abū Bakr ibn ʿAbd al-Malik related to us; ʿAbd al-Razzāq related to us, from Maʿmar, who said: “I was with Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, and I said, ‘Abū Naṣr …’”

Salama related to us. He said: Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal related to us; ʿAbd al-Razzāq related to us. Maʿmar said: “Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr was summoned to give the oath of allegiance to one of the Umayyads, but he refused, until …”

“he was beaten and treated as Ibn al-Musayyib had been.”

Abū Yūsuf related to me; Abū Bishr related to us; Yazīd ibn Zurayʿ related to us; Ḥabīb al-Muʿallim related to us, from ʿAṭāʾ, who said: “A father may eat from his child’s property, clothe himself, and spend in a reasonable manner, but he must not be extravagant with the child’s property or emancipate a slave. The child may do likewise.”

Yazīd said: “ʿUbayd Allāh ibn al-Ḥasan and Ibn ʿUlayya came to me. Ibn ʿUlayya said, ‘Abū Muʿāwiya, we have come to greet you.’ ʿUbayd Allāh said, ‘That is not why we came; we came to ask you about this ḥadīth.’”

Abū Yūsuf related to us; Salama related to me, from Aḥmad; ʿAbd al-Razzāq related to us. He said:

Ibn Jurayj asked Rabāḥ about something in commentary. Rabāḥ said: “Maʿmar told me such-and-such.” Ibn Jurayj said: “Maʿmar drank deeply of knowledge, and it benefited him.”

Abū Yūsuf related to us; Abū Bakr ibn ʿAbd al-Malik related to me; ʿAbd al-Razzāq related to us.

Rabāḥ informed us: “Ibn Jurayj asked me about something in commentary, and I said, ‘Maʿmar said such-and-such.’ He said, ‘Maʿmar drank deeply of knowledge, and it benefited him.’”

Volume Two

[Syria]

“Abū Yūsuf Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān al-Fasawī related to us. He said:

Abū ʿĀṣim related to us, from Bahz ibn Ḥakīm, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: “I said, ‘Messenger of God, choose what is best for me.’ He gestured with his hand toward Syria.”

“ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṣāliḥ related to us. He said: Muʿāwiya ibn Ṣāliḥ related to me, from Abū Yaḥyā, that Jubayr ibn Nufayr related to him, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥawāla, from the Messenger of God ﷺ—who said: ‘You will become several organized armies: an army in Syria, an army in Yemen, and an army in Iraq. You must go to Syria, for it is the choice of God, mighty and majestic, among His lands, and in it are the chosen among His servants. In it is the tethering place of God, mighty and majestic—His light.’64 ‘Whoever refuses, let him join his Yemen and drink from its pools, for God, mighty and majestic, has taken responsibility for Syria and its people.’”

“ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yūsuf related to us. He said: Yaḥyā ibn Ḥamza related to us. He said: Abū ʿAlqama Naṣr ibn ʿAlqama related to me, tracing the ḥadīth back to Jubayr ibn Nufayr, who said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥawāla said: ‘We were with the Messenger of God ﷺ—and complained to him of nakedness, poverty, and having little. The Messenger of God ﷺ—said: “Rejoice! By God, I fear that abundance will be more troubling for you than scarcity. By God, this affair will continue …”’”

“among you until God, mighty and majestic, opens the lands of Persia, the Romans, and Ḥimyar for you, and until you become three armies: an army in Syria, an army in Iraq, and an army in Yemen; and until a man is given a hundred and is displeased with it.”

Ibn Ḥawāla said: “I said, ‘Messenger of God, who could manage Syria, when it is inhabited by the Romans, men with horns?’ He said: ‘By God, God, mighty and majestic, will surely open it for you and appoint you as its successors, until a band of their fair-skinned men, wearing quilted tunics, with their necks exposed, stand around a small, dark man among you, shaven-headed; whatever he commands them to do, they do. Yet today there are men there before whose eyes you are more contemptible than ticks on the rumps of camels.’”

Ibn Ḥawāla said: “I said, ‘Messenger of God, choose for me, if I live to see that.’ He said: ‘I choose Syria for you, for it is the choice of God, mighty and majestic, among His lands, and to it the choice of His servants will be gathered. People of Yemen, you must go to Syria, for Syria is the choice of God’s land. Whoever refuses, let him drink from the pools of Yemen, for God, mighty and majestic, has guaranteed Syria and its people.’”

Abū ʿAlqama said: “I heard ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Jubayr say: ‘The Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ—recognized the description in this ḥadīth in Juzʾ ibn Suhayl al-Sulamī, who was in command of the non-Arabs at that time. Whenever they went to a mosque, they would look at him and at them standing around him, and they marveled at how the Messenger of God ﷺ—had described him and them.’”

Abū ʿAlqama said: “In this ḥadīth, the Messenger of God ﷺ—swore three times; we do not know of his swearing so in any similar ḥadīth.”

“three times.”

“Yaḥyā ibn Ḥamza related to us, from Zayd ibn Wāqid, who said: Bus r ibn ʿUbayd Allāh related to me. He said: Abū Idrīs ʿĀʾidh Allāh al-Khawlānī related to me, from Abū al-Dardāʾ, that the Messenger of God ﷺ—said: ‘While I was asleep, I saw the pillar of the Book being lifted from beneath my head. I thought it was being taken away, so I followed it with my eyes; it was directed toward Syria. When tribulation comes, faith will be in Syria.’”

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yūsuf related to us. He said: Yaḥyā ibn Ḥamza related to us. He said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd ibn Jābir related to me. He said: Zayd ibn Arṭāʾa related to me. He said: I heard Jubayr ibn Nufayr al-Ḥaḍramī relate, from Abū al-Dardāʾ, that the Messenger of God ﷺ—said: “The Muslims’ encampment on the day of the great battle will be in al-Ghūṭa, beside a city called Damascus, one of the finest cities of Syria.”

“ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yūsuf related to us. He said: Muḥammad ibn Muhājir …”

…from al-ʿAbbās ibn Sālim, from Mudrik ibn ʿAbd Allāh—or Ibn Mudrik—who said: “We went on a campaign to Egypt with Muʿāwiya, and we stopped at a place. ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ said to Muʿāwiya:

‘Commander of the Faithful, will you permit me to address the people?’ He gave him permission. He stood leaning on his bow, praised God, mighty and majestic, and lauded Him, then said: ‘I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ—say: “In a dream I saw the pillar of the Book lifted from beneath my pillow. I followed it with my eyes, and there it was, like a pillar of light, being directed toward Syria. Indeed, when tribulation occurs, faith will be in Syria”—he said this three times.’”

“ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yūsuf related to us. He said: al-Walīd ibn Muslim related to us. He said: Abū Ḥafṣ ʿUthmān ibn Abī al-ʿĀtika related to us. He said: Sulaymān ibn Ḥabīb al-Muḥāribī related to us, from Abū Hurayra, who said: I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ—say: ‘When the great battles occur, a force will emerge from Damascus under the governor. They are the noblest of the Arabs in horsemanship and the finest of them in weaponry. God, mighty and majestic, will support the religion through them.’”

“Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us. He said: Muʿāwiya ibn Ṣāliḥ related to us, from Rabīʿa ibn Yazīd, from Ibn al-Daylamī, who said: ‘A report about ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn …’” al-ʿĀṣ, so I rode to him to ask him about it. I entered his garden and said:

“What is this report I have heard from you, that you cite from the Messenger of God ﷺ?”

He said, “And what is that?” I said, “I have heard that you say that a prayer in Bayt al-Maqdis is like a thousand prayers.” He said, “O God, I do not permit them to say anything about me except what they have heard from me”—he repeated this three times. “I did not put it that way. Rather, I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ—say: ‘Solomon son of David asked God, mighty and exalted, for three things. He asked Him for a kingdom such as none after him should have, and He granted it to him; he asked Him for a judgment that would accord with wisdom, and He granted it to him; and he asked Him that whoever came to this House, desiring nothing but to pray in it, be forgiven.’”

“ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yūsuf related to us: Muḥammad ibn Muhājir related to us, from ʿUrwa ibn Ruwaym, from Ibn al-Daylamī—who lived in Bayt al-Maqdis—that he rode in search of ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ to Medina and asked about him. They said, ‘He has set out for Mecca.’ So he followed him and found him in his field, which was called al-Wahṭ.” Ibn al-Daylamī said: “I entered…”

I said to him, “Abū ʿAbd Allāh, what is this report that has reached us from you?” He said, “What is it?”

I said, “You say that a prayer in Bayt al-Maqdis is better than a thousand prayers elsewhere, except in the Kaʿba.” He said, “O God, I do not permit them to attribute to me what I have not said. When Solomon ﵇ had finished building Bayt al-Maqdis, he offered a sacrifice, and it was accepted from him. He then supplicated to God, mighty and exalted, with several prayers, among them: ‘O God, whichever believing servant visits You in this House, repentant and having come only to disavow his errors and sins, accept him and remove him from his errors as on the day his mother gave birth to him.’”

Al-ʿAbbās ibn al-Walīd ibn Mazīd al-ʿUdhri related to me. He said: My father informed me. He said:

Al-Awzāʿī related to us: Rabīʿa ibn Yazīd and Yaḥyā ibn [Abī] ʿAmr al-Saybānī related to me, saying: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Fayrūz al-Daylamī related to us: “I went in to ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ while he was in a walled garden of his at al-Ṭāʾif, called al-Wahṭ. He said:

‘I heard him’”—meaning the Messenger of God—“say: ‘Solomon son of David asked his Lord, mighty and exalted, for three things, and He granted him two; we hope that He granted him the third as well. He asked Him for a judgment that would accord with wisdom, and He granted it to him. He asked Him for a kingdom such as none after him should have, and He granted it to him. And he asked Him that whichever man left his house desiring nothing but prayer in this mosque should emerge from his sin as on the day his mother gave birth to him.’ We hope that God, mighty and exalted, granted it to him.” Abū ʿAmr said: Rabīʿa ibn Yazīd related this report to me between…

al-Miqsalāṭ—meaning Bāb al-Ṣaghīr.

Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us: al-Layth related to me: Ibn al-Hād related to me.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Maslama related to us, from Mālik, from Ibn al-Hād.

Abū al-Aswad related to me: Nāfiʿ ibn Yazīd informed us, from Ibn al-Hād and ʿUmāra ibn Ghaziyya.

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us: Ibn Abī Ḥāzim related to us, from Ibn al-Hādḥ65 All of them said, from Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm ibn al-Ḥārith al-Taymī, from Abū Salama ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Abū Hurayra, from Basra ibn Abī Basra al-Ghifārī, who said: “I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ—say: ‘No riding beasts are to be saddled for a journey except to three mosques: the Sacred Mosque, this mosque of mine, and the Mosque of Īliyāʾ—or Bayt al-Maqdis; he was uncertain which of the two he said.’” This is the wording of Mālik’s report; the others are not uncertain and say “Bayt al-Maqdis.”

Abū al-Walīd Hishām ibn ʿAbd al-Malik, Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb, and al-Ḥajjāj ibn al-Minhāl related to me. They said: Shuʿba related to us, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr, from Qazʿa, from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ—said: “Travel is to be undertaken only to three mosques: the Sacred Mosque, this mosque of mine, and the Mosque of Īliyāʾ.”

Saʿīd ibn Abī Maryam related to us: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn Abī Kathīr informed me: Zayd ibn Aslam informed me, from Saʿīd ibn Abī Saʿīd al-Maqburī, from Abū Hurayra, who said: “I came to al-Ṭūr, and Ḥumayl ibn Basra al-Ghifārī, a Companion of the Prophet ﷺ—met me…”

ﷺ—saying: “No camels are to be ridden except to three mosques: the Sacred Mosque, this mosque of mine, and the Mosque of Īliyāʾ.”

Hishām ibn ʿAmmār related to us: Ṣadaqa ibn Khālid related to us: Yazīd ibn Abī Maryam related to us, from Qazʿa, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr, from the Messenger of God ﷺ—who said: “Travel is to be undertaken only to three mosques: to the Sacred Mosque, to the Farthest Mosque, and to this mosque of mine.”

“Abū Nuʿaym al-Faḍl ibn Dukayn related to us: al-Aʿmash related to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḍirār al-Asadī, from his father, from ʿAbd Allāh, who said: ‘God, mighty and exalted, divided goodness into ten parts. He placed nine-tenths of it in Syria, and the remainder throughout the other lands. And He divided evil into ten parts: He placed one part of it in Syria, and the remainder throughout the other lands.’”

Sulaymān ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Dimashqī related to us: ʿĪsā ibn Yūnus related to us: Shuʿba related to us, from Muʿāwiya ibn Qurra, from his father—who was a Companion—who said:

The Messenger of God ﷺ—said: “When the people of Syria become corrupt, there is no good in people.”

“Al-Rabīʿ ibn Yaḥyā related to us: Shuʿba related to us: I heard Muʿāwiya ibn Qurra relate from his father—who had seen the Prophet ﷺ—and the Prophet ﷺ—had wiped his head. He said: ‘When the people of Syria become corrupt, there is no good in you.’”

Abū Bishr related to us: Ghundar related to us: Shuʿba related to us, from Abū Iyās, from his father, from the Prophet ﷺ—who said: “When the people of Syria become corrupt, there is no good in you.”

Abū ʿUmayr related to us: Ḍamra related to us, from Abū Shuʿba, from Muʿāwiya ibn Qurra, from his father, from the Prophet ﷺ—who said: “When the people of Syria become corrupt, there is no good in you.”

“Makkī ibn Ibrāhīm related to us: Bahz related to us, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: ‘I said, “Messenger of God, where do you direct me? Choose for me.” He said, “Here”—and he gestured with his hand toward Syria—“You will be gathered on foot and mounted, and dragged upon your faces.”’”

“ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yūsuf related to us: Yaḥyā ibn Ḥamza related to us: Abū ʿAlqama Naṣr ibn ʿAlqama al-Ḥaḍramī, from the people of Ḥimṣ, related to me that ʿUmayr ibn…” al-Aswad and Kathīr ibn Murra al-Ḥaḍramī both said: “Abū Hurayra and Ibn al-Simṭ used to say: ‘The Muslims will remain in the land until the Hour is established.’ That is because the Messenger of God ﷺ—said: ‘A band of my community will continue to stand firm in God’s command, mighty and exalted. Those who oppose them will not harm them; they will fight their enemies. Whenever one war ends, the war of another people breaks out. God turns the hearts of some people aside so that He may provide them from His bounty, until the Hour comes upon them like pieces of a dark night. They are seized with fear at that, until they put on coats of mail for it.’ The Messenger of God ﷺ—said: ‘They are the people of Syria’”—and the Messenger of God ﷺ—tapped with his finger, pointing toward Syria, until it hurt.

“ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yūsuf related to us: Yaḥyā ibn Ḥamza related to us: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd ibn Jābir related to me that ʿUmayr ibn Hāniʾ related to him, saying: I heard Muʿāwiya ibn Abī Sufyān say: ‘I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ—say: “A group of my community will continue to uphold the command of God, mighty and exalted. Those who abandon them or oppose them will not harm them, until God’s command, mighty and exalted, comes, while they remain dominant over people.”’”

Mālik ibn Yukhāmir stood and said: “Commander of the Faithful, I heard Muʿādh ibn Jabal say: ‘They are the people of Syria.’” Muʿāwiya raised his voice and said: “This is Mālik ibn Yukhāmir, and by him is the oath; he claims that he heard Ibn Jabal say: ‘They are the people of Syria.’”

Abū Saʿīd ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm related to us: al-Walīd ibn Muslim related to us: ʿUfayr ibn Maʿdān related to us, from Sulaym ibn ʿĀmir, from Abū Umāma, that the Messenger of God ﷺ—said: “Prophethood was sent down to me in three places: Mecca, Medina, and Syria.”

“Ṣafwān ibn Ṣāliḥ related to us: al-Walīd ibn Muslim related to us: Muḥammad ibn Muhājir al-Anṣārī related to me that al-Walīd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Jurashī related to him, from Jubayr ibn Nufayr, from Salama ibn Nufayl al-Ḥaḍramī, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ—said: ‘The central stronghold of Islam is in Syria.’”

“Abū Yaḥyā Zakariyyā ibn Nāfiʿ al-Arṣūfī and Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz al-Ramlī related to us. They said: ʿAbbād ibn ʿAbbād Abū ʿUtba related to us, from Abū Zurʿa, from Ibn Waʿla—a shaykh from ʿAkk—who said: ‘Kurayb came to us from Egypt, intending to visit Muʿāwiya, and we visited him. He said: “I cannot count the number of times Murra al-Bahzī related to me, in private and in company, that he heard the Messenger of God ﷺ—say: ‘A group of my community will continue to uphold the truth, dominant over those who oppose them. They will be like a vessel among eaters until God’s command, mighty and exalted, comes, while they remain as they are.’” We said, “Messenger of God, who are they?”

‘And where are they?’ He said: ‘On the slopes around Bayt al-Maqdis.’”

He said: “He also told me that al-Ramla is the high ground, because it slopes toward the west and the east.”

Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz related to us: Ḍamra related to us, from ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAwf al-Qārī, from Muṭāʿ ibn al-Ajtham al-ʿAnazī, from Kaʿb, who said: “On the Day of Resurrection, al-Ramla will plead on behalf of its people, saying: ‘My Lord, would You punish them when You buried them in me?’”

“Ādam ibn Abī Iyās related to us: Abū ʿUmar al-Ṣanʿānī related to us, from Abū Sulaymān, from Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq al-Madanī, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: A man said to the Messenger of God ﷺ: ‘I want to go on a military expedition.’ The Messenger of God ﷺ—said to him: ‘Stay close to Syria and its people; then, of Syria, remain in ʿAsqalān, for when the millstone turns among my community, the people of ʿAsqalān will be in ease and well-being.’”

Saʿīd ibn Asad related to me: Ḍamra related to us, from ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd al-ʿAnazī Abū al-Akhtam, from al-Muṭāʿ ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-ʿAnazī, who said: “I heard Kaʿb say: ‘On the Day of Resurrection, al-Ramla will plead on behalf of its people, saying: “My Lord, You buried them in me, yet You punish them.”’”

“Ādam related to us: ʿAṭṭāf ibn Khālid al-Makhzūmī related to us, from his brother al-Miswar ibn Khālid, from Makkī ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Mālik ibn Buḥayna, from his father, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ—prayed for the people of that cemetery”—three times. One of his Companions went to one of the wives of the Prophet ﷺ—and said to her: “Mother of the Believers, the Messenger of God ﷺ—mentioned the people of a cemetery and prayed for them three times, but did not tell us which cemetery it was. Ask him about it when he comes in to you.” When he came in to her, she said: “Messenger of God, which cemetery was the one for which you prayed?” The Messenger of God ﷺ—said to her:

“It is a cemetery at ʿAsqalān.”

“Abū Saʿīd ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm and Ṣafwān ibn Ṣāliḥ related to me. They both said:

Al-Walīd ibn Muslim related to us: Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz related to us, from Yūnus ibn Maysara, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ—said: ‘I saw the pillar of the Book pulled from beneath my pillow. I followed it with my gaze, and there it was, a bright light, directed toward Syria. Know that when tribulations arise in Syria, faith…’”

“Ṣafwān related to us: al-Walīd related to us: Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz related to us, from Yūnus ibn Maysara ibn Ḥalbas, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ—said: ‘I saw the pillar of the Book pulled from beneath…’” my pillow. I followed it with my gaze, and there it was, a bright light, until I thought it had been taken away; then it was directed toward Syria. I interpreted this to mean that, when tribulations arise, faith will be in Syria.

“He said: Al-Walīd related to us: ʿUfayr ibn Maʿdān related to me that he heard Sulaym ibn ʿĀmir relate, from [Abū] Umāma, from the Messenger of God ﷺ—a report like that.”

Abū al-Ṭāhir Aḥmad ibn ʿAmr and Muḥammad ibn [Abī] Zukayr related to me, from Ibn Wahb, from Ibn Lahīʿa and ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith, from Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb, from Ibn Shimāsa, who related to him that he heard Zayd ibn Thābit say: “One day the Messenger of God ﷺ—was with us, and we were in his presence. He said: ‘Blessed is Syria!’ We said:

‘What is the reason for that, Messenger of God?’ He said: ‘The angels of the All-Merciful are spreading their wings over it.’” However, Ibn Lahīʿa said: “He heard Zayd, or someone who had heard him related it to him.”

“Ṣafwān ibn Ṣāliḥ related to me: al-Walīd related to us: Abū ʿAmr related to us, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, from Abū Hurayra, transmitting it from the Prophet, who said: ‘A band of my community will continue to uphold the truth, dominant over people. They will not care who opposes them, until Jesus descends…’”

Ibn Maryam.

Abū ʿAmr said: “I related this report to Qatāda, and he said: ‘I know those people to be none other than the people of Syria.’”

“Hišām ibn ʿAmmār related to me: Muḥammad ibn Ayyūb—who is Ibn Maysara ibn Ḥalbas—related to us, from his father, who related to him, from Ḫuraym ibn Fātik al-Asadī, who said: ‘The people of Syria are the scourge of God, Mighty and Majestic, upon His earth; through them He takes vengeance on the rest of His servants. It is forbidden for their hypocrites to prevail over their believers. God, Mighty and Majestic, will cause them to die only in sorrow and grief.’

Ṣafwān related to me: al-Walīd related to us: Muḥammad ibn Ayyūb related to us, from his father Ayyūb ibn Maysara ibn Ḥalbas, from Ḫuraym ibn Fātik al-Asadī, Companion of the Messenger of God ﷺ who heard him say that.”

He said: al-Walīd related to us: Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz related to us, from Makḥūl and Rabīʿa ibn Yazīd, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥawāla al-Ḥawālī, who was of the Azd, who said: “I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: ‘You will be organized into armies: an army in Syria, an army in Iraq, and an army in Yemen.’ ʿAbd Allāh said: ‘I said: “Choose for me, Messenger of God.” He said: “Stay with Syria; and whoever refuses, let him join his Yemen and drink from its pools, for God, Mighty and Majestic, has guaranteed me Syria and its people.”’ Saʿīd said: Rabīʿa said: ‘ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥawāla was among those who settled in the Jordan region.’”

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yūsuf related to us: Yaḥyā ibn Ḥamza related to us, from al-Awzāʿī. from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kaṯīr, from Abū Qilāba al-Jarmī, from Sālim ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from his father, who heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: “A fire will emerge at Ḥaḍramawt, or from the sea of Ḥaḍramawt.” We said: “Messenger of God, what do you command us to do?” He said: “Stay with Syria.” Ṣafwān ibn Ṣāliḥ related to me: al-Walīd related to us: al-Awzāʿī related to us. He said:

Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kaṯīr related to us: Abū Qilāba al-Jarmī related to me: Sālim ibn ʿAbd Allāh related to us: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar related to us: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “At the end of time, a fire will emerge from Ḥaḍramawt or from the sea of Ḥaḍramawt, driving the people together.” It was said: “Messenger of God, what do you command us to do?” He said: “Stay with Syria.”

Ḥarīz ibn ʿUṯmān al-Raḥabī related to us, from Jubayr ibn Nufayr, who said: “I was with ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar, asking him for a legal opinion about something. He said: ‘Who are you?’ I said: ‘I am from the people of Ḥimṣ.’ He said: ‘You have left the foremost army, its forelock! The Companions of Muḥammad ﷺ marched, following the Messenger of God ﷺ until they settled there. I am not one to give you a legal opinion.’”

Ibn Bukayr related to me, from al-Layṯ ibn Saʿd, who said: “In Syria were Abū ʿUbayda ibn al-Jarrāḥ, Muʿāḏ ibn Jabal, and Yazīd ibn Abī Sufyān. We have been told that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: ‘The most knowledgeable of them concerning the lawful and the unlawful is Muʿāḏ ibn Jabal.’ It is also said that Muʿāḏ ibn Jabal will come on the Day of Resurrection ahead of the scholars by a bow’s length. Also there were Šuraḥbīl ibn Ḥasana, Abū al-Dardāʾ, and Bilāl ibn Rabāḥ. In Ḥimṣ were seventy men from the people of Badr.” Ibn— Bukayr mentioned: “This is in al-Layṯ’s letter to Mālik ibn Anas.”

“Abū ʿUtba ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Muslim al-Sakūnī related to me: Baqiyya ibn al-Walīd related to me, from Yazīd ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Ḫawlānī (92b), from Kaʿb al-Aḥbār, who said: ‘Five cities are among the cities of Paradise: Jerusalem, Ḥimṣ, Damascus, Bayt Jibrīn, and Ẓafār of Yemen. And five cities are among the cities of Hell: Constantinople, Ṭuwāna, Antioch, Palmyra, and Ṣanʿāʾ—Ṣanʿāʾ of Yemen.’”

“Abū al-Naḍr Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Yazīd and Hišām ibn ʿAmmār, both of Damascus, related to us: Yaḥyā ibn Ḥamza related to us: al-Awzāʿī related to us, from Nāfiʿ—Abū al-Naḍr said: ‘from someone who related it to him, from Nāfiʿ’—from Ibn ʿUmar, that the Prophet ﷺ said: ‘The people of the earth will migrate, one migration after another, to the place of Abraham’s migration, until none of its wicked people remain. The lands will cast them out, and the Breath of the Merciful will find them loathsome. The Fire will herd them together with the apes and swine; it will spend the night with them wherever they spend the night, and take its midday rest wherever they take theirs. It will have whatever falls from them.’”

“Qabīṣa and Mūsā ibn Masʿūd related to us: they said: Sufyān related to us, from al-Aʿmaš, from Ḫayṯama, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr, who said: ‘A time will come upon you when no believer remains who has not joined Syria.’”

“Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd related to me: Šarīk related to us, from ʿUṯmān ibn Abī Zurʿa, from Abū Ṣādiq, who said: ‘ʿAlī ﵁ heard a man cursing the people of Syria, so ʿAlī said: “Do not condemn them all, for among them are the Substitutes.”’”

“Qabīṣa related to us: Sufyān related to us, from al-Aʿmaš, from al-Qāsim ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from his father, from ʿAbd Allāh, who said: ‘They complained to him about the Euphrates and the scarcity of water, so he said: “A time will come upon you when you will not find even a basinful of water from it. Every water will return to its source, while the water and the believers will remain in Syria.”’”

Saʿīd related to me: Sufyān related to us, from Ziyād, from al-Zuhrī, from Abū ʿUṯmān ibn Sunna, who said: “A man reviled the people of Syria in ʿAlī’s presence ﵁ and ʿAlī ﵁ said: ‘Do not revile the people of Syria as a whole, for among them—or from among them—are Substitutes.’”

“Ibrāhīm ibn al-Munḏir related to us: ʿAbbās ibn Abī Šamla related to me, from Mūsā ibn Yaʿqūb, from Zayd ibn Abī ʿAttāb, from Usayd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb, from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: ‘Satan descended in the East and carried out his decree there. Then he set out, intending the Holy Land, Syria, but was prevented. So he went out on foot until he reached the West, where he laid his eggs and spread his carpet.’”

These are the uppermost generation among the Successors of the people of Syria.

Among them: al-Ṣunābiḥī

“Farwa ibn Abī al-Miġrāʾ related to me: ʿAbd al-Raḥīm ibn Sulaymān related to us, from Muḥammad ibn Ḥassān, from al-Muhājir ibn Ġānim al-Rabaḍī—who belonged to a clan of Maḏḥij—who said: ‘I heard Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Ṣunābiḥī say: “I heard Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq say: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: ‘Whoever wishes God, Mighty and Majestic, to hear his supplication and relieve his distress in this world and the next, let him look to one in hardship and pray for him. Whoever is pleased that God, Mighty and Majestic, should shelter him from the blaze of Hell on the Day of Resurrection and place him in His shade, let him not be harsh toward the believers, but let him be compassionate toward them.’””

Among them: Sulaym Abū ʿĀmir

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm related to us: Suwayd ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz related to us: Ṯābit ibn ʿAjlān informed us, from Sulaym Abū ʿĀmir, who said: “I heard Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq say: ‘The Messenger of God ﷺ said to me: “Go out and proclaim among the people (93b): Whoever testifies that there is no god but God, Paradise is assured to him.”’ ʿUmar said: ‘Go back to the Messenger of God ﷺ for I fear they will rely on that alone.’ I went to the Messenger of God ﷺ and he said: ‘What brought you back?’ I told him what ʿUmar had said. ʿUmar said: ‘Yes, Messenger of God, leave the people to act.’ The Messenger of God ﷺ said: ‘ʿUmar is right.’”

Among them: Jubayr ibn Nufayr “stood in my place here a year ago and said: ‘People, ask God, Mighty and Majestic, for well-being three times, for no one has been given anything like well-being after certainty.’”

Among them: Ḥābis al-Ṭāʾī al-Yamānī

ʿAmr ibn ʿUṯmān related to us: Aḥmad ibn Ḫālid al-Wahbī related to us, from ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn Abī ʿAwn, from Saʿd ibn Ibrāhīm, from Ḥābis al-Yamānī, from Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Whoever performs the dawn prayer is under God’s protection, Mighty and Majestic. So do not violate God’s protection, Mighty and Majestic, in His covenant. Whoever kills such a person, God, Mighty and Majestic, will pursue him until He casts him into the Fire upon his face.”

Among them: Abū Muslim al-Ḫawlānī

(94a) Kaṯīr ibn ʿUbayd ibn Numayr al-Ḥaḏḏāʾ related to me: Muḥammad ibn Ḥimyar related to us, from Maslama ibn ʿAlī, from ʿUmar ibn Ḏarr, from Abū Qilāba, from Abū Muslim al-Ḫawlānī, from Abū ʿUbayda ibn al-Jarrāḥ, from ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb, who said: “The Messenger of God ﷺ took hold of my beard—and I could see grief on his face—and said: ‘We belong to God, and to Him we return. Gabriel has just come to me and said: “We belong to God, and to Him we return.”’

“I said: ‘Indeed, we belong to God, and to Him we return. What is the reason for that, Gabriel?’ He said: ‘Your community will be put to trial a short time after you, not a long time.’ I said: ‘A trial of unbelief or a trial of error?’”

He said: “Both will occur.” I said: “How can that be, when I am leaving among them the Book of God, Mighty and Majestic?”

He said: “They will be led astray by the Book of God, Mighty and Majestic. This will begin with their commanders and their reciters: the commanders will withhold people’s due rights, and the people will demand their rights but not receive them, so they will become angry and fight one another. The reciters will follow the commanders’ desires and encourage them in error, then will not desist.” I said: “Gabriel, what should those among them who remain safe do?” He said: “Restraint and patience: if they are given what is theirs, they should take it; if they are denied it, they should leave it.”

This Muḥammad ibn Ḥimyar is from Ḥimṣ, “not strong.” “Maslama ibn ʿAlī is from Damascus, weak in ḥadīṯ.” As for ʿUmar ibn Ḏarr, I think he is not the al-Hamaḏānī; in my view, he is an unknown šayḫ. This report is not sound.

Among them: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ġanm Abū al-Aswad al-Naḍr ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār related to me: Ibn Lahīʿa related to us, from Ibn Hubayra, from Abū Qays ibn Mālik ibn al-Ḥakam, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ġanm al-Ašʿarī, who said: “He came to them in Egypt with Marwān and used to relate that ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb had written to the commanders of the military districts, instructing them to send him their Qurʾān reciters, and had ordered them, when they reached al-Marwa, to hold back those at the front for those behind them until they all entered together. He said: ‘When we reached Ḏū al-Marwa, we waited until we had assembled. When we entered, ʿUmar ﵁ was informed of our arrival, and he came out to meet us and said: “Dismount.” We dismounted. He said: “Uncover your faces and heads.” We uncovered them, and he found among us men with two braids, two locks, long hair hanging down, full hair, and shaved heads. He said:

“‘By Him in whose hand is my soul, had I found you all with shaved heads, I would have done to you something that would be heard about far and wide. I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: “People will emerge from my community who recite the Qurʾān with their tongues, but it will not pass beyond their collarbones. They will leave the religion as an arrow passes through its quarry. Their distinguishing mark is that they shave their heads.”’ Then he ordered us to disperse, and we went down to Medina.’”

Among them: ʿUrwa ibn Muʿtib al-Anṣārī

Abū al-Yamān related to us: Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAyyāš related to us, from Abū Sabāʾ ʿUtba ibn Tamīm—Abū al-Yamān said: “How excellent this man was,” meaning ʿUtba—from al-Walīd ibn ʿĀmir al-Yazanī, “from ʿUrwa ibn Muʿtib al-Anṣārī, from ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb ﵁ who said: ‘The Messenger of God ﷺ ruled that the owner of a riding animal has the greater right to its front.’”

Among them: al-Sāʾib ibn Mihjān

(95a) Aḥmad ibn Ṣāliḥ related to me: Ibn Wahb related to us: Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī al-ʿAmayyāʾ informed me, from al-Sāʾib ibn Mihjān—one of the people of Syria, who had encountered the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ—that ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb delivered a sermon in Syria, which he transmitted from the Messenger of God ﷺ. He said:

“Be moderate in seeking the world, for God, Mighty and Majestic, has guaranteed your provisions, and everyone is made ready for the deed he was destined to do. Seek God’s help, Mighty and Majestic, for your deeds: He effaces whatever He wills and confirms whatever He wills, and with Him is the Mother of the Book.”

Among them: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Qays

“Naṣr ibn Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān al-Ḥimṣī related to me: [My father,] Abū Ḍamra Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān al-Sulamī, related to us: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Qays related to me, who said: ‘I heard ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb ﵁ say: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “I saw a pillar of light emerge from beneath my head, shining until it came to rest in Syria.”’”

Among them: Ibn al-Simṭ

Abū Bišr related to me: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān related to us: Šuʿba related to us.

From Yazīd ibn Khumayr, from Ḥabīb ibn ʿUbayd, from Jubayr ibn Nufayr, from Ibn al-Simṭ, who said: “I saw ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb praying two cycles at Dhū al-Ḥulayfa. I asked him about it, and he said: ‘I do only as I saw the Messenger of God ﷺ do.’”

And Mālik ibn Yukhāmir

Among them was Kathīr ibn Murra

Among them was Jubayr ibn Nufayr al-Ḥaḍramī The people of Paradise will regret nothing except an hour that passed them by in which they did not remember God, Mighty and Glorious.

Maḥmūd ibn Khālid related this to me, from Sulaymān ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, who said:

Yazīd ibn Yaḥyā Abū Khālid related to us, from Thawr ibn Yazīd, from Khālid ibn Maʿdān, from Jubayr ibn Nufayr.

Among them was ʿĀṣim ibn ʿUbayd al-Sakūnī

Abū al-Yamān related to us, saying: Ḥurayz ibn ʿUthmān al-Raḥabī related to us, from Rāshid ibn Saʿd, from ʿĀṣim ibn ʿUbayd al-Sakūnī, a companion of Muʿādh ibn Jabal, from Muʿādh, who said: “One night we waited for the Messenger of God ﷺ for the evening prayer. He delayed it until someone thought that he had already prayed or would not come out. Then he came out (96a), and someone said to him: ‘Prophet of God, we thought that you had already prayed, or that you would not come out.’”

He ﷺ said to us: “Delay this prayer, for by it you have been favored over all other communities; no community before you prayed it.”

Among them was Abū Baḥriyya ʿAbd Allāh ibn Qays al-Sakūnī

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yūsuf, Sulaymān ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm related to us. They said: Al-Walīd related to us, saying: Abū Bakr ibn Abī Maryam related to us, from al-Walīd ibn Sufyān ibn Abī Maryam al-Ghassānī, from Yazīd ibn Quṭb al-Sakūnī, from Abū— Baḥriyya, a companion of Muʿādh ibn Jabal, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “The Great Battle, the conquest of Constantinople, and the emergence of the Antichrist will take place within seven months.”

Among them was ʿAmr ibn al-Aswad al-ʿAnsī

ʿAbd al-Wahhāb ibn al-Ḍaḥḥāk related to us, saying: Ibn ʿAyyāsh related to us, saying:

Ibn Abī Maryam related to me, from Ḍamra ibn Ḥabīb, from ʿAmr ibn al-Aswad al-ʿAnsī, who said: “I passed by ʿUmar while traveling to Syria and entered to see him. When he [ʿUmar] left ʿUmar’s presence, he said: ‘Whoever wishes to see the conduct of the Messenger of God ﷺ should look at the conduct of ʿAmr ibn al-Aswad.’”

Among them was ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿUsayla al-Ṣanābiḥī

He said: “By God, the news is long—or grave—. We buried the Messenger of God (96b) …” may ﷺ only the day before yesterday.”

Among them was al-Ḥārith ibn Muʿāwiya al-Kindī

Abū al-Yamān related to us; Ḥurayz related to us, from “Sulaym”, from al-Ḥārith ibn Muʿāwiya, who came to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb ﵁. He asked him: “How did you leave the people of Syria?” He informed him of their condition, and ʿUmar praised God, Mighty and Glorious, then said: “Perhaps you sit in the company of the people of polytheism?” He said: “No, Commander of the Faithful.” ʿUmar said: “If you sit with them, you will eat and drink with them. You will remain in a good state so long as you do not do that.”

Among them was Abū ʿUthmān Shurāḥīl ibn Murthid al-Ṣanʿānī

Hishām ibn ʿAmmār related to me, saying: ʿAbd al-Malik related to us, saying: Rāshid ibn Dāwūd al-Ṣanʿānī related to us, saying: Abū ʿUthmān al-Ṣanʿānī, Shurāḥīl ibn Murthid, related to me, saying: “Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq ﵁ sent Khālid ibn al-Walīd to al-Yamāma and sent Yazīd ibn Abī Sufyān to Syria. I was among those who traveled with Khālid ibn al-Walīd to al-Yamāma. When we arrived there, they fought us fiercely, but we prevailed over them. Abū Bakr died, and ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb was appointed his successor. ʿUmar wrote to Khālid: ‘Proceed to Abū ʿUbayda—’” in Syria.” Khālid then summoned [him], and I have mentioned his report in the second part of this book.

Among them were Junāda ibn Abī Umayya al-Azdī, Yazīd ibn al-Aswad al-Jurashī, and Sulaym Abū ʿĀmir

Abū Saʿīd ʿAbd al-Raḥmān related to me, saying: Suwayd related to us, saying: Thābit ibn al-ʿAjlān related to us (97a), from Sulaym Abū ʿĀmir, who said: “I saw Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq and prayed behind him for seven months. I saw those to his right and left, and they had nothing on but a single wrap.”

And Abū Saʿd al-Ḥabrānī

Al-Rabīʿ ibn Rūḥ related to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Ḥarb related to us, from Ṣafwān ibn ʿAmr, from Abū al-Yamān al-Hawzanī, from Abū Saʿīd al-Khayr al-Ḥabrānī, who said:

Ḥajar said: “The correct view is to distinguish between them. Al-Bukhārī, Abū Ḥātim, Ibn Ḥibbān, al-Baghawī, Ibn Qāniʿ, and a group of others explicitly stated that Abū Saʿd al-Khayr was a Companion. As for Abū Saʿīd al-Ḥabrānī, he was certainly a Successor. Some transmitters erred in his report, saying ‘from Abū Saʿīd al-Khayr’; perhaps this is a scribal error. God knows best.” (Tahdhīb al-Tahdhīb, 12/109).

I was among the group in whose presence Kaʿb stood when the people suffered drought during ʿUthmān’s time. He said: “People of Yemen, leave the people alone so long as they leave you alone. There is congestion in your hearts, inarticulateness in your tongues, and weakness in your striking power. People of Yemen, do not help in the campaign against ʿUthmān. ʿUthmān only wanted to keep your mounts from being cut off, lest you pass by without reaching anything.

“You claim that ʿUthmān wants to prevent emigration. By Him in whose hand is my soul, if ʿUthmān were to build a palace on the face of the earth until it reached the constellations of the sky, the people of Yemen would scale it to emigrate. That is because God, Mighty and Glorious, stood upon Mount Sinai and called out: ‘O Yemen, come to Me!’ So I sought them before they sought Me, and I gave to them before they asked Me. A yellow [light]—a yellow [light]—entered the heart of every Yemeni. That is what God, Mighty and Glorious, says in His Book: ‘You were not on the side of the Mount when We called, but [this is] a mercy from your Lord, so that you may warn a people to whom no warner had come before you, that they might take heed.’”

And Kurayb ibn Abraha

Abū al-Yamān and ʿAlī ibn ʿAyyāsh al-Ḥimṣī related to us. They said: Ḥurayz ibn ʿUthmān related to us, from Saʿīd ibn Murthid, who said: I heard ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ḥawshab relate— (97b) from Thawbān ibn Shahr, who said: “I heard Kurayb ibn Abraha, as he sat with ʿAbd al-Malik on a rooftop at Dayr al-Murrān, and they were discussing arrogance. Kurayb said: ‘I heard Abū Rayḥāna say: “I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: ‘Nothing of arrogance will enter Paradise.’” Someone said: “Messenger of God, I like to adorn myself with the strap of my whip and the sandal thong of my sandal.” The Prophet ﷺ said: “That is not arrogance. God, Mighty and Glorious, is beautiful and loves beauty. Arrogance is only to scorn the truth and to look down on people.’” The wording is Abū al-Yamān’s.’”

Among them was Abū Rāshid al-Ḥabrānī

Abū al-Yamān related to us, saying: Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAyyāsh related to us, from Shurayḥ ibn ʿUbayd, from Abū Rāshid al-Ḥabrānī, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Shibl: “The Prophet ﷺ forbade eating monitor lizards.”

Among them were ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿĀʾidh al-Azdī, Rabīʿa ibn ʿAmr al-Jurashī, and Muslim ibn Qurra al-Ashjaʿī He relates from ʿAwf ibn Mālik: “The best of you are the best of your leaders.” Muʿāwiya related it from Rabīʿa.

Among them was Abū Idrīs al-Khawlānī

Al-Ḥumaydī related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, saying: al-Zuhrī related to us—and I heard it from him—from Abū Idrīs al-Khawlānī, from Abū Thaʿlaba al-Khushanī: “The Messenger of God ﷺ forbade every beast of prey with fangs.” Al-Zuhrī said: “I did not hear this report until I came to Syria.”

Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us, saying: al-Layth ibn Saʿd related to me, saying: Yūnus related to me, from Ibn Shihāb, who said: “I did not hear that from any of our scholars in Medina.”

Ibn ʿUthmān related to us, saying: ʿAbd Allāh informed us, saying: Yūnus informed us (98a), from al-Zuhrī, who said: “Abū Idrīs al-Khawlānī—who was ʿĀʾidh Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh—related to me that he heard Abū Thaʿlaba al-Khushanī say: ‘The Messenger of God ﷺ forbade eating every beast of prey with fangs.’” Muḥammad said: “I had not heard this from any of our scholars in the Ḥijāz until Abū Idrīs al-Khawlānī related it to me. He was a man among the jurists of the people of Syria.”

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm related to us, saying: al-Walīd related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Namir related to us, saying: “I asked Ibn Shihāb about sniffing water into the nose, and he said: ‘Abū Idrīs informed me—’”

Abū Idrīs al-Khawlānī, ʿĀʾidh Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh—who was the preacher and judge of the people of Syria during ʿAbd al-Malik’s caliphate—that he heard Abū Hurayra say: “I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: ‘Whoever performs ablution should snort water out of his nose, and whoever uses stones for cleansing should use an odd number.’”

Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr—a man from Nīshāpūr who lived in Mecca—related to us, saying: Ḥassān ibn Ibrāhīm al-Kirmānī related to us, saying: Yūnus related to us, from al-Zuhrī, who said: “Abū Idrīs al-Khawlānī informed me that he heard Abū Hurayra and Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī say:

‘The Messenger of God ﷺ said that; he spoke those words.’” Abū Ṣāliḥ and Muḥammad ibn Rumḥ related to us, saying: al-Layth related to us, saying: ʿUqayl related to me, from Ibn Shihāb, who said: “I sat with Abū Idrīs al-Khawlānī while he was preaching. He said: ‘Shall I tell you who had the most wholesome food?’ When he saw that the people were looking at him, he said: ‘John son of Zechariah had the most wholesome food. He ate only with the wild beasts, because he disliked sharing people’s livelihoods.’”

Al-Ḥumaydī related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, saying: “This is what we memorized from al-Zuhrī, from Abū Idrīs al-Khawlānī, who informed him: ‘I met Abū al-Dardāʾ and retained knowledge from him; ʿUbāda ibn al-Ṣāmit and retained knowledge from him; and Shaddād ibn Aws and retained knowledge from him. I missed Muʿādh ibn Jabal, but so-and-so informed me from him’”—Sufyān said: “Al-Zuhrī named him, but I forgot his name”—“that Muʿādh ibn Jabal would not sit in any gathering without saying: ‘God, Mighty and Glorious, is a just judge; blessed is His name; the doubters have perished.’”

Sufyān said: “The report was long, and I memorized only this much.”

Abū Idrīs also heard from Ḥudhayfa.

Abū al-Yamān related to us, saying: Shuʿayb informed me, from al-Zuhrī. Ḥ.

And Ḥajjāj related to us, saying: My grandfather [related] from al-Zuhrī, who said: “Abū Idrīs ʿĀʾidh Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Khawlānī related to me that Yazīd ibn ʿUmayra, a companion of Muʿādh, informed him that Muʿādh used to say whenever he sat down: ‘God, Mighty and Glorious, is a just arbiter.’”

Abū al-Yamān said: “He would say: ‘He is just; blessed is His name; the doubters have perished.’” One day, Muʿādh ibn Jabal said in a gathering he attended: “There lie ahead of you trials in which wealth will abound and the Qurʾān will be made widely available, until believer and hypocrite, free man and slave, man and woman, old and young will all take it up. A man will soon say: ‘What is wrong with the people that they do not follow me, when I have recited the Qurʾān?’ By God, they will not follow me until I devise something else for them. So beware of what is devised, for what is devised is error. Beware of four things: the sage—for Satan may speak a word of error through the sage’s mouth—and the hypocrite—for he may speak a word of truth.” He said: “I asked him: ‘How can I know, may God have mercy on you, that the sage is speaking a word of error and the hypocrite a word of truth?’”
