He said: “Avoid the doubtful things in the sage’s speech, those that make you say, ‘What is this?’ Do not let that make you doubt him,, for perhaps he will reconsider and encounter the truth. When you hear the truth, there is light in it.”

Muḥammad ibn Manṣūr told me: Yaʿqūb told us: my father told us, from Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn Shihāb, who said: Abū Idrīs al-Khawlānī told me, and he mentioned a report like it.

Abū Ṣāliḥ and Ibn Bukayr told us, both saying: al-Layth told us: ʿUqayl told us, from Ibn Shihāb, that Abū Idrīs al-Khawlānī (99a) informed him that Yazīd ibn ʿUmayra—who was one of Muʿādh’s companions—said that Muʿādh ibn Jabal would never sit in a gathering for remembrance without saying, when he sat down, something like the foregoing. He added:

Yazīd said: I stayed for as long as God willed, then came to Kūfa. Some Qurʾān reciters from among the people of Kūfa began saying, “O man from Syria, do you testify that you are a believer?” I would reply, “Yes.”

They would say, “Do you testify that you are among the people of Paradise?” I would reply, “I fear my sins.”

They would say, “Then we testify that the believers are in Paradise.” The matter reached ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd. I passed by him in the mosque, and they said, “This is the Syrian we told you about.”

Ibn Masʿūd sent for me and said, “Do you testify that you are a believer?” I said, “Yes.” He said, “Then do you testify that you are among the people of Paradise?” I said, “I fear my sins.” ʿAbd Allāh smiled and then said:

“If I testified that I was a believer, I would not mind testifying that I was in Paradise.” He said: I said, “May God, Mighty and Majestic, forgive you! This is what Muʿādh ibn Jabal used to warn us against: people like you.” He said, “And what did he warn you against?” I said, “He warned us against the sage’s deviation, for Satan may speak a word of error on the tongue of a sage, while the hypocrite may speak a word of truth.” Then he said to him, “Reproach yourself, for by God you are only one of three: a believer, an unbeliever, or a hypocrite.” He said:

“May God have mercy on Muʿādh ibn Jabal! He was always counted as gentle and held in esteem in the gathering.”

Mālik related, from Ibn Abī al-Zinād, from Abū Idrīs al-Khawlānī, who said:

I entered the mosque of Damascus and saw a young man with gleaming front teeth, who was long in his silence. The people were with him; whenever they disagreed about something, they referred it to him and followed his opinion. I asked about him, and was told, “This is Muʿādh ibn Jabal.”

Shahr related: ʿĀʾidh Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh told me that one day he entered the mosque, when the Companions of the Prophet of God ﷺ—were at their fullest number, at the beginning of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb’s rule. He said: I sat in a gathering of some thirty-odd men. In the circle was a young man, brown-skinned and very dark-complexioned, handsome in appearance and radiant; he was the youngest of the people there. He mentioned the ḥadīth. He said: I asked him, “Who are you, Abū ʿAbd Allāh?” He said, “I am Muʿādh ibn Jabal.”

The ḥadīth in which he said that the Messenger of God ﷺ—said: “My love is assured for those who love one another for My sake, visit one another for My sake, and give generously to one another for My sake.” Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz al-Wāsiṭī told me: Yazīd ibn Abī al-Zarqāʾ told us: Jaʿfar ibn Burqān told us, from Ḥabīb ibn Abī Marzūq, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ, from Abū Salama al-Khawlānī, from ʿUbāda ibn al-Ṣāmit, from the Messenger of God ﷺ—relating from his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, who said: “My love is assured for those who give generously to one another for My sake; My love is assured for those who visit one another for My sake; and My love is assured for those who love one another for My sake.”

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Muʿādh told us: my father told us: Shuʿba told us, from Yaʿlā ibn ʿAṭāʾ, from al-Walīd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Abū Idrīs al-ʿĀʾidhī or al-Khawlānī.

Ibn Shamir told us: he informed me, from Shuʿba, from Yaʿlā ibn ʿAṭāʾ, from al-Walīd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Abū Idrīs al-ʿĀʾidhī, who said: I sat in a gathering of twenty men from among the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ. Among them was a handsome young man, with dark, wide-set eyes and bright front teeth. Whenever they disputed about something and he gave his opinion, they accepted it. It was Muʿādh ibn Jabal. The next day I came and found him praying. When he saw me, he shortened his prayer, then sat down and remained silent. I said, “By God, I love you for the majesty of God, Mighty and Majestic.” He said, “Did you say, ‘By God’?” I said, “By God, those who love one another for God, Mighty and Majestic—I think he said—in the shade of God, Mighty and Majestic, on the day when there is no shade but His shade—and I have no doubt about this—will have chairs of light set out for them. The prophets, the steadfastly truthful, and the martyrs will envy them for their place with God, Mighty and Majestic.”

Abū Idrīs said: I related this to ʿUbāda ibn al-Ṣāmit, and he said: I heard Muḥammad ﷺ—say: “My love is assured for those who love one another for My sake; My love is assured for those who give generously to one another for My sake; and My love is assured for those who maintain ties with one another for My sake, or those who are devoted to one another for My sake.” (100a)

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṣāliḥ told us: ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd told me, from Shahr ibn Ḥawshab, who said: ʿĀʾidh Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh told me that Muʿādh ibn Jabal had come to them in Yemen.

Hishām ibn ʿAmmār told us: Ṣadaqa told us: Ibn Jābir told us: ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī told us: I heard Abū Idrīs al-Khawlānī say: I entered the mosque of Damascus and sat in a circle, all of whose members were relating reports from the Messenger of God ﷺ. Among them was a young man: when he spoke, the people listened attentively to him, and when one of them related a report, he listened attentively. They dispersed, and I did not know who that young man was. I returned to my lodging, but could not rest until I went back to the mosque. There he was again, so I stood and walked with him until he came to a pillar. He performed several excellent units of prayer, then sat down and faced me. He remained silent for a long time, not speaking.

I said, “Tell me, may God have mercy on you. By God, I love you and love your words.” He said, “For God’s sake?”

I said, “For God’s sake.” He pulled me close by my66 until his knee was pressed against mine. Then he said, “I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ—say: ‘Those who love one another for the majesty of God, Mighty and Majestic, will be in the shade of God, Mighty and Majestic, on the day when there is no shade but His.’” ʿUbāda said to me, “Come, I shall relate to you what I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ—relate from his Lord, Mighty and Majestic.” He said:

So I went to him. He said: I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ—say: God, Mighty and Majestic, said, “My love is assured for those who love one another for My sake; My love is assured for those who sit together for My sake; and My love is assured for those who give generously to one another for My sake.”

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm told me: Abū Mushir told us: Saʿīd told us, from Rabīʿa, from Abū Idrīs al-Khawlānī, from Abū Dharr, from the Prophet ﷺ—relating from God, Mighty and Majestic, that He said: “My servants, I have forbidden injustice to Myself and made it forbidden among you, so do not wrong one another. My servants, you sin by night and by day, and I am the one who forgives sins, and I do not mind; so ask Me for forgiveness, and I shall forgive you.

“My servants, all of you are hungry except those whom I feed; so ask Me for food (100b), and I shall feed you.

“My servants, all of you are unclothed except those whom I clothe; so ask Me for clothing, and I shall clothe you. My servants, if the first and the last of you, the humans and the jinn, were as pious in heart as the most pious man among you, that would add nothing to My dominion. My servants, if the first and the last of you, the humans and the jinn, were as wicked in heart as the most wicked man among you, that would diminish nothing from My dominion. My servants, if the first and the last of you, the humans and the jinn, gathered on a single plain and asked Me, and I gave every one of them what he asked for, that would diminish nothing from My dominion, except as the sea is diminished when a needle is dipped into it just once. My servants, these are only your deeds— “I record them for you. Whoever finds good, let him praise God, Mighty and Majestic; and whoever finds otherwise, let him blame no one but himself.” He said: Whenever Abū Idrīs related this ḥadīth, he knelt down.

Among them: Umm al-Dardāʾ

Al-ʿAbbās ibn al-Walīd ibn Ṣubḥ told me: I heard Abū Mushir say:

I heard Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz say: Umm al-Dardāʾ’s name was Juhayma, daughter of Luḥayy al-Waṣṣābiyya.

Abū al-Walīd, Ḥajjāj, and Abū ʿUmar told us, all saying: Shuʿba told us, who said:

Al-Qāsim ibn Abī Bazza informed me: I heard ʿAṭāʾ al-Kaykhārānī, from Umm al-Dardāʾ, from Abū al-Dardāʾ, from the Prophet ﷺ—who said: “Nothing weighs more heavily on the Balance than good character.”

Among them: Bilāl ibn Abī al-Dardāʾ

ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān told us: ʿAbd Allāh informed us: Abū Bakr ibn Abī Maryam informed us, from Khālid ibn Muḥammad al-Thaqafī, from Bilāl ibn Abī al-Dardāʾ, from the Prophet ﷺ—who said: “Your love of a thing makes you blind and deaf.” Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb told us: Ḥammād ibn Salama told us, from ʿAlī ibn Zayd, from Bilāl ibn Abī al-Dardāʾ (101a), from Abū al-Dardāʾ, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ—said: “Neither the green sky above nor the dusty earth below has borne anyone more truthful in speech than Abū Dharr.”

Among them: Maʿdān ibn Abī Ṭalḥa

Aḥmad ibn Yūnus told us: Zāʾida told us: al-Sāʾib ibn Ḥubaysh told us, from Maʿdān ibn Abī Ṭalḥa, who said: Abū al-Dardāʾ said to me, “Where do you live?”

I said, “In a village below Ḥimṣ.” Abū al-Dardāʾ said: I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ—say: “There are no three people in a village or in the countryside, where the call to prayer is not made, but that Satan has gained mastery over them. So keep to the congregation, for the wolf eats the sheep that strays apart.” Zāʾida said: al-Sāʾib said, “By ‘the congregation’ he meant prayer in congregation.”

Among them: Abū ʿUbayd Allāh Muslim ibn Mishkam

Hishām ibn ʿAmmār told us: Yaḥyā ibn Ḥamza told us: Yazīd ibn Abī Maryam told me that Abū ʿUbayd Allāh related to us, from Abū al-Dardāʾ, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ—said: “I shall be ahead of you at the Pool, and I shall surely find one of you being pulled away from me, so I will say, ‘This one is [from] my community.’ It will be said, ‘You do not know what they introduced after you.’”

I said, “O Messenger of God, pray to God, Mighty and Majestic, that He not make me one of them.” He said, “You are not one of them.”

Among them: Rajāʾ ibn Ḥaywa al-Kindī,

the leading man of the people of Palestine;

ʿAdī ibn ʿAdī al-Kindī, the leading man of the people of al-Jazīra;

ʿUbāda ibn Nasī al-Kindī, the leading man of the people of Jordan;

Yaḥyā ibn Yaḥyā al-Ghassānī, one of the leading men of the people of Damascus;

and ʿAmr ibn Qays, one of the leading men of the people of al-Jazīra.

“Bilāl ibn Saʿd ibn Tamīm al-Sakūnī was the imam of the people during Hishām’s caliphate (101b).”

And Kathīr ibn Qays, Sulaymān ibn Marthad, ʿAbd Allāh ibn [Abī] Zakariyyā al-Khuzāʿī, al-Qāsim Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, client of the family of Muʿāwiya, and Yazīd ibn Khumayr al-Raḥabī.

Abū al-Yamān told us: Ṣafwān ibn ʿAmr told us, from Yazīd ibn Khumayr al-Raḥabī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Busr al-Māzinī, from the Prophet ﷺ—who said: “There is no one from my community whom I will not recognize on the Day of Resurrection.” They said, “How will you recognize them, O Messenger of God, among the great multitude of creatures?” He said, “Tell me: if you entered a herd of entirely black horses, among which was a horse with a white blaze and white stockings, would you recognize it among them?” They said, “Yes.” He said, “Then my community on that day will have radiant marks from prostration and white marks from ablution.”

Among them: Shurayḥ ibn ʿUbayd

Abū al-Yamān told us: Ṣafwān told us, from Shurayḥ ibn ʿUbayd al-Ḥaḍramī, from Abū al-Dardāʾ, that the Prophet ﷺ—said: “God, Mighty and Majestic, says: ‘Son of Adam, do not neglect four units of prayer at the beginning of the day; I shall suffice you for its end.’” And from Shurayḥ ibn ʿUbayd al-Ḥaḍramī, from Abū Dharr, from the Prophet ﷺ may ﷺ—who said: “O Abū Dharr, if you pray with your imam and then depart, the night’s devout vigil will be recorded for you.”

Among them: Sulaym ibn ʿĀmir al-Kalāʿī

Among them: Abū ʿĀmir ʿAbd Allāh ibn Luḥayy

(102a) Abū al-Yamān told us: Ṣafwān told us, from al-Azhar ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Abū ʿĀmir ʿAbd Allāh ibn Luḥayy, who said: We made the pilgrimage with Muʿāwiya. When we arrived, he was informed of a preacher, a client of Banū Makhzūm, who was preaching to the people of Mecca. Muʿāwiya sent for him and said, “If I had warned you before this time of mine, I would have cut a piece off you.” Then he stood and prayed the noon prayer in Mecca, and said: The Messenger of God ﷺ—said:

“The People of the Book split over their religion into seventy-two sects, and this community will split into seventy-three sects”—meaning, factions of desire—“all of them in the Fire except one, and that is the community.” He also said: “There will arise among my community peoples who will be swept along by those desires as a rabid dog is swept along by its madness, so that no vein or joint remains “…except that it will enter it.” By God, people of the Arabs, if you do not uphold what Muḥammad brought, others among the people are even less likely to uphold it.

Among them: ʿUthmān ibn Jābir

Abū al-Yamān related to us: Ṣafwān related to us, from ʿUthmān ibn Jābir, from Anas ibn Mālik, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “War is stratagem.”

Abū al-Yamān related to us: Ṣafwān related to us, from Māʿiz al-Tamīmī, from Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ who said: “Satan has despaired of being worshipped by those who pray, but he has not despaired of stirring discord among them.”

Among them: ʿAṭiyya ibn Qays al-Kilāʿī, Makhūl, Khālid ibn Maʿdān, Rāshid ibn Saʿd al-Maqraʾī al-Ḥimyarī, ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yazīd al-Laythī al-Jundaʿī, Yaḥyā ibn Jābir al-Ṭāʾī, and ʿAmr ibn Ruʾbah.

He transmits from Wāthilah, from the Prophet ﷺ: “A woman has a claim to three inheritances: those of her foundling, her emancipated slave, and the child concerning whom she has entered into a mutual imprecation.”

Among them: Yaʿlā ibn Shaddād ibn Aws

He transmits from his father that he used to recite aloud “In the name of God, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful.”

And ʿUbaydah ibn Abī al-Muhājir

He relates from Muʿāwiyah ibn Abī Sufyān, from the Prophet ﷺ: “A man from among those who came before you killed ninety-nine people.”

And Abū ʿAbd Rabb

And Muslim ibn Qarẓah

I heard ʿAwf ibn Mālik say: I heard the Prophet ﷺ say: “The best of your leaders are those whom you love.”

Ibn Jābir relates from Zurayq, from Muslim; and Busayr ibn ʿUbayd Allāh said: I heard Wāthilah.

And Abū Sallām al-Aswad

He heard ʿUbādah ibn al-Ṣāmit: The Prophet ﷺ saw a man wearing a safflower-dyed garment.

And Muḥammad ibn Ziyād al-Alhānī

He heard Abū Umāmah, who heard the Prophet ﷺ say: “Gabriel continued to urge me to treat the neighbor well until I thought he would give him a share of the inheritance.”

And al-Walīd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Jurashī

He relates from Abū Dharr concerning the Prophet’s prayer ﷺ in Ramaḍān.

And Yazīd ibn [Abī] Mālik al-Hamadhānī And Numayr ibn Aws al-Ashʿarī, the judge

And ʿAbd Allāh ibn Busr al-Yaḥṣubī

He relates from Abū Umāmah: “Make God, mighty and majestic, beloved to the people.”

And ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥayrīz

(103a) Maḥmūd ibn Khālid al-Azraq related to us: Marwān al-Ṭāṭarī related to us: Rabāḥ ibn al-Walīd al-Dhimārī related to us: Ibrāhīm ibn Abī ʿAblah related to me: Rajāʾ ibn Ḥaywah said: “If the people of Medina boast to us of their worshipper ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar, then we boast to them of our worshipper ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥayrīz.”

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAmr related to me: Abū Mushir related to us: Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz related to us, from Ismāʿīl ibn ʿUbayd Allāh, who said: Umm al-Dardāʾ went out to propose on behalf of the daughter of Abū Maḥjaz al-Laythī. She met ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yazīd, who said, “I am ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yazīd”—seeking a favorable omen.

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm related to us: Abū Mushir related to us: Saʿīd related to us, who said: We used to sit in the mornings with Yazīd ibn Abī Mālik and Sulaymān ibn Mūsā; after noon, with Ismāʿīl ibn ʿUbayd Allāh and Rabīʿah ibn Yazīd; and after the afternoon prayer, with Makhūl.

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAmr related to me: Abū Mushir related to us: Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz related to us, from al-Qāsim ibn Mukhaymirah, who said: I went in to see ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz. He paid off seventy dinars of my debt, gave me a mule to ride, and assigned me a stipend of fifty. I said, “You have freed me from the need to trade.”

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm related to us: Abū Mushir related to us: Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz related to us, from Rabīʿah ibn Yazīd, who said: We returned from a military expedition and came upon a road leading to ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz. We were with Ibn Abī Zakariyyā, who said, “If I do not come to ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz by this road, I will not come to him at all.” He was a stubborn man. We came to ʿUmar and asked permission to enter. He gave it, and seated Ibn Abī Zakariyyā beside him. Rabīʿah said: I began to look from one to the other, wondering which of them I should address. He said: With us was [Ibn] the son of Ibn Abī Zakariyyā, wearing a turban that he had wound in folds. ʿUmar said, “Who is this?”

Ibn Abī Zakariyyā said to him, “This is ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd Allāh; he is my son.” ʿUmar said, “How do you find him?” He replied, “I would begrudge him being any better than he is.” He said:

ʿUmar said, “He is young; God, mighty and majestic, will set him right.” (103b) He granted us twenty dinars, less a dinar by which Ibn Abī Zakariyyā had surpassed us.

“ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm related to us: al-Walīd related to us: Saʿīd related to us: Bashīr ibn ʿUqbah met ʿAbd al-Wāḥid al-Naṣrī during the caliphate of al-Walīd, Bashīr was in charge of al-Walīd’s police force, and he brought a complaint against him before Zurʿah ibn Thawb al-Muqriʾ, who was a judge, so Bashīr was given the prescribed punishment.” Zurʿah ibn Thawb did not take payment for judging. On Zurʿah ibn Thawb’s signet ring was inscribed: “Every deed has its reward.”

These are the transmitters from ʿAwf ibn Mālik

Al-Wuḥāẓī related to us: Jābir ibn Ghānim related to us, from Sulaym ibn ʿĀmir, from Maʿdīkarib ibn ʿAbd Kulāl, from ʿAwf ibn Mālik, from the Prophet ﷺ who said: “Gabriel ﵇ came to me, and my Lord gave me the choice between two things: that He admit half my community to Paradise, or intercession for my community. I chose intercession.”

And Mālik ibn Hadm

Ibn ʿUthmān related to us: ʿAbd Allāh informed us: Saʿīd ibn Abī Ayyūb related to us:

“ʿAmr ibn al-Rabīʿ related to me: Ibn Lahīʿah informed us, from Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb, from Rabīʿah ibn Laqīṭ, who informed him, from Mālik ibn Hadm, who said: We went on a military expedition under the command of ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ. Among us were ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb and Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ. We were struck by severe famine, so I went off in search of a livelihood and came upon some people who wanted to slaughter a camel of theirs.” I said, “If you like, I will take care of slaughtering and preparing it for you, and you can give me some of it.” I returned, and they gave me some. (104a) I cooked it, then went to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb. He asked me where it came from. I told him, and he said, “I see that you took your payment in advance.” He refused to eat it. Then I went to Abū ʿUbaydah and told him. He said the same thing and refused to eat it. When I saw that, I left it. He said: Then they sent me ahead as a courier during a conquest of ours, and I arrived before the Messenger of God…”

…of God ﷺ and he said, “The man with the camel.” He said nothing more to me. In Saʿīd’s report: “He said no more to me than that.”

Among them: Qays ibn Marthad al-Judāmī

Burd ibn Sinān related to me: Sulaymān ibn Mūsā related to me, from Makhūl, from Kathīr ibn Murrah, from Qays—namely, Ibn Marthad al-Judāmī—from Nuʿaym ibn Habbār al-Ghaṭafānī, from the Prophet ﷺ reporting from his Lord, mighty and majestic, who said: “Son of Adam, pray four rakʿahs at the beginning of the day, and I will suffice you for its end.”

Among them: Yaḥyā ibn Jābir al-Ṭāʾī, judge of Ḥimṣ

Abū al-Yamān related to us: Ṣafwān ibn ʿAmr related to us, from Yaḥyā ibn Jābir, from Nawwās ibn Samʿān, who asked the Messenger of God ﷺ “What is righteousness?”

He said, “Good character.” He asked, “And what is sin, Messenger of God?” He said, “That which troubles your conscience and which you would dislike people knowing.”

Among them: Ḥabīb ibn ʿUbayd

Abū al-Yamān related to us: Abū Bakr ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Maryam al-Ghassānī related to us, from Ḥabīb ibn ʿUbayd, from ʿAmr ibn ʿAbsah, from the Prophet ﷺ who said: “The night prayer is two by two, and the latter part of the night is the most responsive to supplication.”

I said, “The most obligatory.” He replied, “No, rather, the most responsive”—meaning, in answering the prayer. (104b)

Among them: ʿUbādah ibn Awfā al-Numayrī

Sulaymān ibn Salamah al-Khabāʾirī al-Ḥimṣī related to us: Muḥammad ibn Shuʿayb ibn Shābūr al-Qurashī related to us: Yazīd ibn Abī Maryam informed me, from al-Walīd ibn Hishām al-Muʿayṭī, from ʿUbādah ibn Awfā al-Numayrī, from ʿAmr ibn ʿAbsah, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Delay the noon prayer on a hot day, for the severity of the heat comes from the breath of Hell.”

Among them: ʿUbādah ibn Awfā

From ʿAmr ibn ʿAbsah: I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: “Any Muslim man or Muslim woman who emancipates a Muslim slave will be shielded from the Fire, limb for limb, by the one he or she has emancipated. And whoever shoots an arrow in the path of God, mighty and majestic, will have a light on the Day of Resurrection.” Abū Tawbah mentioned this, from Muʿāwiyah ibn Sallām, who said: Zayd ibn Sallām informed me that he heard Abū Sallām say that ʿUbādah ibn Awfā had related it to him.

Among them: ʿĀmir ibn Zayd al-Bakkāʾī

Abū Tawbah related to me: Muʿāwiyah ibn Sallām related to us, from Zayd ibn Sallām, who heard Abū Sallām say: ʿĀmir ibn Zayd al-Bakkālī related to me that he heard ʿUtbah ʿAbd al-Sulamī say: A Bedouin came to the Messenger of God ﷺ and asked him, “What is this Pool of yours that you speak of?” He replied, “It is as far across as the distance between al-Bayḍāʾ and Buṣrā. Then God, mighty and majestic, will extend it for me by a stretch of ground, so that no human being among His creation will know where its two ends are.”

ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb exclaimed, “God is greatest!” He said, “As for the Pool, the poor among the Emigrants who are killed in the path of God, mighty and majestic, or die in His path, will crowd around it. I hope that God, mighty and majestic, will bring me to the stretch of ground, so that I may drink from it.” The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “My Lord, mighty and majestic, has promised me that He will admit seventy thousand of my community to Paradise without reckoning. Then each thousand will intercede for seventy thousand, and then He will scoop for me three handfuls with both His hands.” ʿUmar exclaimed, “God is greatest!” and said: “God, mighty and majestic, will allow the first seventy thousand to intercede for their fathers, their sons, and their clans. I hope that God, mighty and majestic, will include me in one of the later handfuls.” The Bedouin said, “Messenger of God, will there be fruit there?” He replied, “Yes. There is a tree there called Ṭūbā, which extends over Paradise.”

He asked, “Which tree in our land is like it?” He replied, “It is not like any tree in your land. Have you been to Syria?” He said, “No, Messenger of God.” He replied, “It is like a tree in Syria called a walnut tree; it grows from a single trunk, and its crown spreads out.” He asked, “How large is its base?” He replied, “If you traveled around it on the largest camel of your people, you would not encircle its base before…” until her collarbones break from old age. He said: “Are there grapes in it?” He said: “Yes.” He said: “How large is a cluster there?” He said: “A raven would travel for a month without landing, tiring, or resting.” He said: “How large is its bunch?” He said: “Has your father ever slaughtered a large he-goat from his flock?” He said: “Yes.” He said: “Then he skinned it, gave its hide to your mother, and said, ‘Tan this for us, then cut off a piece of it for us.’ Even if a part of it were folded over, would it be enough?” He said: “Yes.” He said: “Then would that be enough for me and my household?” He said:

“Yes, and for most of your clan.”

And among them: Abū al-Muthannā al-Mulaykī

Hishām ibn ʿAmmār, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm, and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yūsuf related to us. They said: al-Walīd ibn Muslim related to us. He said: Ṣafwān ibn ʿAmr related to me.

And Ibn ʿUthmān related to us. He said: ʿAbd Allāh informed us. He said: Ṣafwān ibn ʿAmr related to us, that Abū al-Muthannā al-Mulaykī had related to him that he heard ʿUtba ibn ʿAbd al-Sulamī—who was one of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ—relate that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Those slain are three kinds of men: a believing man who strives with his life and wealth in the path of God, Mighty and Majestic, until he encounters the enemy and fights them until he is killed. That is the tested martyr in God’s tent beneath His Throne; the prophets surpass him only by the degree of prophethood. And a believing man burdened with sins and transgressions who strives with his life and wealth in the path of God, until he encounters the enemy and fights until he is killed. That is the tested one in God’s tent beneath His Throne; the prophets surpass him only by the degree of prophethood. And a man [with] a remnant beneath his sins and transgressions67—for the sword effaces sins—and he is admitted through whichever of the gates of Paradise he wishes, for it has eight gates. Hell has seven gates, some more hateful than others. And a hypocritical man who strives in the path of God, Mighty and Majestic, with his life and wealth, until he encounters the enemy and fights until he is killed: the sword does not eradicate hypocrisy.”

And among them: Shuraḥbīl ibn Shufʿa

Hishām ibn ʿAmmār, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm, and Ṣafwān ibn Ṣāliḥ related to us. They said: al-Walīd related to us. He said: Ḥurayz ibn ʿUthmān related to us, from Shuraḥbīl ibn Shufʿa, who said: I heard ʿUtba ibn ʿAbd al-Sulamī say: I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: “No servant whose three children die before reaching puberty will fail to be met at one of the eight gates of Paradise; through whichever gate he wishes, he may enter.”

And among them: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿAwf al-Jurashī and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Busr

Ḥaywa ibn Shurayḥ related to us. He said: Baqiyya ibn al-Walīd related to us, from Ṣafwān ibn ʿAmr, who said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿAwf al-Jurashī and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Busr related to me, from ʿUtba ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Thumālī, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Were I to swear an oath, I would be true to it: none shall enter Paradise before the foremost of my community except a dozen or so men, among them Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, the twelve Tribes, Moses, and Jesus son of Mary daughter of ʿImrān.” (106a)

And among them: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAmr al-Sulamī

Abū ʿĀṣim related to us, from Thawr ibn Yazīd, from Khālid ibn Maʿdān, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAmr al-Sulamī, from al-ʿIrbāḍ ibn Sāriya, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ prayed with us, then turned to us and admonished us with a powerful admonition that brought tears to our eyes and made our hearts tremble—or words to that effect. Someone said: “Messenger of God, it is as though this were the admonition of one taking leave. So give us your counsel.” He said: “I counsel you to be mindful of God, Mighty and Majestic, and to listen and obey, even if [your leader] is an Abyssinian slave. Whoever among you lives on will see much disagreement. So adhere to my Sunna and the Sunna of the rightly guided, rightly guiding caliphs, and hold fast to them with your molars. Beware of newly introduced matters, for every innovation is error.”

And Ḥujr ibn Ḥujr al-Kalāʿī

Al-Walīd ibn Muslim transmitted from Thawr, from Khālid ibn Maʿdān, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAmr al-Sulamī and Ḥujr ibn Ḥujr al-Kalāʿī, who said: Al-ʿIrbāḍ related to us, and he mentioned the report.

And among them: Yaḥyā ibn Abī al-Muṭāʿ

He heard al-ʿIrbāḍ mention this report.

And among them: Abū Ruhm al-Samaʿī

Abū Ṣāliḥ said to us: Muʿāwiya ibn Ṣāliḥ related to me, from al-Ḥārith ibn Ziyād, from Abū Ruhm, who heard al-ʿIrbāḍ ibn Sāriya, the Companion of the Prophet ﷺ say: The Messenger of God ﷺ invited us to the pre-dawn meal in Ramaḍān and said: “Come to the blessed breakfast.” I heard him say: “O God, teach Muʿāwiya the Book and arithmetic, and protect him from the punishment.”

And among them: ʿAbd al-Aʿlā ibn Hilāl al-Sulamī

(106b) Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us. He said: Muʿāwiya ibn Ṣāliḥ related to me, from Saʿīd ibn Suwayd, from ʿAbd al-Aʿlā ibn Hilāl al-Sulamī, from al-ʿIrbāḍ ibn Sāriya, the Companion of the Prophet ﷺ who said: I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: “I am God’s servant and the Seal of the Prophets, while Adam was still cast in clay. I shall tell you about that: my father Abraham’s supplication, Jesus’s glad tidings of me, and the vision my mother saw; likewise, the mothers of the prophets see visions. When the Messenger of God ﷺ was born, his mother saw a light by which the palaces of Syria were illuminated.”

And among them: Saʿīd ibn Hāniʾ

Muʿāwiya ibn Ṣāliḥ related to me, from Saʿīd ibn Hāniʾ, from al-ʿIrbāḍ ibn Sāriya al-Sulamī: I sold the Messenger of God ﷺ a young camel. I came to collect its price and said: “Messenger of God, pay me the price of my young camel.” He paid me, and paid me handsomely. Then a Bedouin came to him and said: “Messenger of God, pay me the price of my young camel.” He paid him with a fine camel. The man said: “Messenger of God, this is better than my young camel.” He said: “It is yours. The best of people are those best in repayment.” ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz and Abū al-Ṭāhir related to me, from Ibn Wahb, from Muʿāwiya, who said: I said: “Pay me the price of my young camel.” He said: “Yes. I will repay you both only with something good.” He paid me, and paid me handsomely.

And among them: Ibn Abī Bilāl

Ḥaywa ibn Shurayḥ, Abū ʿUtba al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī al-Sakūnī, and al-Walīd ibn ʿUtba related to me. They said: Baqiyya related to us, from Buḥayr ibn Saʿīd, from Khālid ibn Maʿdān, from Ibn Abī Bilāl, from al-ʿIrbāḍ ibn Sāriya, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “The martyrs and those who die in their beds, as well as those who die of the plague, will contend before our Lord, Mighty and Majestic. The martyrs will say: ‘Our brothers were killed just as we were killed.’ Those who died in their beds will say: ‘They died just as we died.’ Then our Lord will say: ‘Look at their wounds. If their wounds resemble the wounds of those who were killed, then they are among them and with them.’ And their wounds were found to resemble theirs.” Al-Ḥasan added: “Then they will be joined to them.”

Al-Walīd ibn ʿUtba, Ibrāhīm ibn al-ʿAlāʾ, ʿAmr ibn ʿUthmān, and Ibn al-Muṣaffā related to us. They said: Baqiyya ibn al-Walīd related to us. He said: Buḥayr ibn Saʿīd related to me, from Khālid ibn Maʿdān, from Ibn Abī Bilāl, from al-ʿIrbāḍ ibn Sāriya, that the Messenger of God ﷺ used to recite “the Glorifiers” before lying down and say: “In it is a verse better than a thousand verses.”

And among them: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Maysara

Al-ʿArabāḍ related that he heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: “Those who love one another for the majesty of God, Mighty and Majestic, will be in My shade on the Day when there is no shade but Mine.”

And among them: Kathīr ibn Murra and ʿAmr ibn al-Aswad

Abū ʿUtba ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ḥimṣī related to us in the cloth market—he was among the finest of men. He said: Abū Muṭīʿ Muʿāwiya ibn Yaḥyā al-Aṭrābulusī related to me, from Buḥayr ibn Saʿīd, from Khālid ibn Maʿdān, from Jubayr ibn Nufayr, Kathīr ibn Murra, and ʿAmr ibn al-Aswad, from al-ʿIrbāḍ ibn Sāriya, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Every deed of a person ceases when he dies, except for the one stationed on the frontier in the path of God, Mighty and Majestic. His deed continues to grow, and his provision continues to reach him until the Day of Reckoning.”

And among them: Ḥabīb ibn ʿUbayd

Muḥammad ibn Khālid ibn al-ʿAbbās ibn Zaml al-Saksakī related to us. He said: Baqiyya ibn al-Walīd related to me. He said: Abū Bakr ibn Abī Maryam related to us, from Ḥabīb ibn ʿUbayd, from al-ʿIrbāḍ ibn Sāriya al-Sulamī, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: God, Mighty and Majestic, said: “If I take from My servant the most precious of his two eyes, while he is deeply attached to it, and he praises Me for it, I shall not be satisfied with a reward for him less than Paradise.”

And among them: Suwayd ibn Jabala

Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm ibn al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Razīq related to us. He said: ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith ibn al-Ḍaḥḥāk related to me. He said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sālim related to me, from al-Zubaydī, who said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿAwf related to me, that Suwayd ibn Jabala had related to them, that al-ʿIrbāḍ ibn Sāriya had related to them, tracing it back to the Messenger of God ﷺ who said: “When you ask, ask God, Mighty and Majestic, for al-Firdaws, for it is the very heart of Paradise. A man among you says to his shepherd: ‘Stay by the heart of the valley, for that is where its grass is thickest and most abundant.’”

And among them: Yaḥyā ibn ʿUtba ibn ʿAbd

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm and Sulaymān said: Muḥammad ibn Shuʿayb related to us. He said: Muḥammad ibn al-Qāsim al-Ṭāʾī related to us. He said: I heard Yaḥyā ibn ʿUtba ibn ʿAbd al-Sulamī relate from his father, who said: I was among a group of people intending to make a raid. He said:

When the Messenger of God ﷺ saw me, he called me over. I was a young boy. He said: “What is your name?” I said: “ʿAtala ibn ʿAbd.” He said: “Rather, it is ʿUtba ibn ʿAbd.” He said: “Show me your sword.” He drew it and looked at it. When he saw that it was thin and weak, he said: “Do not strike with this; thrust with it.”

And among them: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Nāsiḥ al-Ḥaḍramī

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm and Sulaymān related to us. They said: Ibn Shuʿayb related to us. He said:

Al-Ḥasan ibn Ayyūb al-Ḥaḍramī related to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Nāsiḥ, from ʿUtba ibn ʿAbd al-Sulamī, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said to his Companions: “Stand up and fight!”

A man shot an arrow, and the Prophet ﷺ said: “This one has secured his reward.”

(108a) He said: “Yes. We do not say, as the Children of Israel said to Moses ﵇ ‘Go, you and your Lord, and fight; we will sit here.’ Rather, ‘Go, you and your Lord, and fight; we are fighting alongside you.’”

And among them: Luqmān ibn ʿĀmir

Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr, Ādam, and Ibrāhīm ibn al-ʿAlāʾ related to us. They said: Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAyyāsh related to us, from ʿAqīl ibn Mudrik, from Luqmān ibn ʿĀmir, from ʿUtba ibn ʿAbd al-Sulamī, who said: I asked the Messenger of God ﷺ for clothes, and he gave me two coarse linen garments. I remember wearing them while being the best-dressed of my Companions.

And among them: ʿAmr ibn Qays al-Kindī

Abū Ṣāliḥ said to us: Muʿāwiya ibn Ṣāliḥ related to us, from ʿAmr ibn Qays al-Kindī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Busr, who said: Two Bedouins came to the Messenger of God ﷺ and asked him questions. One of them said: “Messenger of God, the laws of Islam have become too numerous for me. Tell me something to which I can hold fast.” He said: “Let your tongue remain moist with remembrance of God, Mighty and Majestic.”

And among them: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿIrq al-Yaḥṣubī

Ādam related to us. He said: Baqiyya ibn al-Walīd related to us. He said: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Yaḥṣubī related to us. He said: I heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn Busr say: Whenever the Messenger of God ﷺ came to the door of a people, he would walk alongside the wall and not face the door. Rather, he would stand to the right or left and ask permission. If permission was granted, he entered; otherwise, he went back. That was because the people had no curtains over their doorways.

I heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn Busr say: (108b) The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Be steadfast and rejoice, for God, Mighty and Majestic, is not quick to punish you. And there will come a people for whom there is no proof.” I heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn Busr say: I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: “Blessed is whoever saw me; blessed is whoever believed in me without seeing me. Blessed is he, and excellent is his return.” ʿAmr ibn ʿUthmān ibn Kathīr ibn Dīnār related to us. He said: My father related to me. He said: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān related to us. He said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Busr related to us, who said: I gave the Prophet ﷺ a sheep as a gift. He said to his family: “Cook this sheep and look at…”

“Make this flour into bread, cook it, and crumble it over it.” The Prophet ﷺ—had a bowl called al-Farrāʾ. Four men could carry al-Farrāʾ. When morning came and he had performed the midmorning prayer, that bowl was brought, and they gathered around it. When the people became numerous, the Messenger of God ﷺ—knelt. A Bedouin said, “What is this way of sitting?” The Prophet ﷺ—replied, “God, Mighty and Majestic, has made me a noble servant, and has not made me an arrogant tyrant.” Then the Messenger of God ﷺ—said, “Eat from its sides, and leave its highest part; it will be blessed.” Then he said, “Eat, for by Him in whose hand is my soul, the lands of Persia and the Romans will surely be opened to you, until food becomes plentiful and God’s name, Mighty and Majestic, is no longer invoked over it.”

Among them was al-Azhar ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Ḥarāzī.

ʿAmr ibn ʿUthmān related to us: Baqiyyah related to us, from Ṣafwān, who said:

Al-Azhar ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Ḥarāzī related to me, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Busr al-Māzinī, who said: My mother said to my father, “If we made food for the Messenger of God ﷺ—and you invited him?” He said:

So we made a dish of tharīd with ghee. Then the Messenger of God ﷺ—came and entered the house. My mother placed one of our rugs for him and folded it together for him so that it would be thicker. The Messenger of God ﷺ—sat upon it (109a). He said: We set it before him, and he said, “Eat, in the name of God,” and gestured toward its highest part with his three fingers. When he had finished, we said, “Pray to God, Mighty and Majestic, for us, Messenger of God.” He said, “O God, have mercy on them, forgive them, and bless their provision.”

Among them was Muḥammad ibn Ziyād al-Alhānī.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yūsuf related to us: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sālim related to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Ziyād related to us, from Abū Umāmah al-Bāhilī—whose name was Ṣudayy ibn ʿAjlān—who said:

He saw a plowshare and some farming equipment. I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ—say, “This will not enter the house of a people without God, Mighty and Majestic, bringing humiliation into it.”

Muḥammad ibn Muṣaffā ibn Bahlūl related to us: Baqiyyah related to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Ziyād related to us that he had met men among the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ—and men among the Companions of Muʿādh ibn Jabal, who had accepted Islam while the Messenger of God ﷺ—was still alive. He had eaten blood during the pre-Islamic era. Among the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ—whom he met were al-Miqdām ibn Maʿdīkarib, Abū Umāmah al-Bāhilī, and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Busr al-Māzinī. As for the Companions of Muʿādh, they were Abū ʿInabah al-Khawlānī and Abū Ṣāliḥ al-Anṣārī.

Baqiyyah related to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Ziyād related to us: I met the early generations, when people would live together with their families in a single dwelling. He said: Sometimes a guest would arrive at one of their homes while another man’s pot was on the fire. The host would take that man’s pot for his guest. When the pot was missed, its owner would ask, “Who took the pot?” The host would say, “We took it for our guest.” The owner of the pot would say, “May God bless you in it,” or words to that effect. He said: They did the same with bread when they baked it, and they thought well of one another. There was nothing between them but a reed wall.

Baqiyyah said: I myself experienced this with Muḥammad ibn Ziyād and his companions.

Baqiyyah also related to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Ziyād related to us: Waqqāṣ ibn Rabīʿah and one of the Prophet’s Companions—he named him (109b)—sat together. Baqiyyah said: “I refrained from naming him because that would be backbiting.” He said: We spoke of women. Waqqāṣ ibn Rabīʿah said, “My wife is among the most beautiful of women, yet I may go a month, two months, or three without approaching her. If I were in a house with someone who disliked me and whom I disliked, that would be dearer to me than having a young woman in his place, when there is no degree of kinship between me and her that would make her unmarriageable.” The Prophet’s Companion said, “But I do not say that.” He said: Then he was tested with an orphan girl who was in his care, and later he married her.

Among them was Abū Ḥayy the muezzin.

Muḥammad ibn Muṣaffā related to us: Baqiyyah related to us, saying: Ḥabīb ibn Ṣāliḥ—who was good in his transmission—related to us, from Yazīd ibn Shurayḥ—who was one of the righteous people of Syria—the Ḥaḍramī, from Abū Ḥayy al-Muʾadhdhin, from Thawbān, from the Messenger of God ﷺ—who said: “It is not lawful for a Muslim to look inside another man’s house until he has asked his permission. If he looks, he has entered. Nor may a man lead a people in prayer and reserve a supplication for himself, excluding them; if he does so, he has betrayed them. And no one should stand for prayer while holding in his urine or stool, until he relieves himself.”

Among them was ʿAyyāsh ibn Muʾnis.

Ḥaywah ibn Shurayḥ and Muḥammad ibn al-Muṣaffā related to us, saying: Baqiyyah related to us. He said: Ḥabīb ibn Ṣāliḥ related to us: ʿAyyāsh ibn Muʾnis related to me, from Shaddād ibn Shuraḥbīl al-Anṣārī, who said: “Whatever I may have forgotten, I have not forgotten that I saw the Messenger of God ﷺ—standing in prayer, with his right hand over his left, clasping it.”

Among them was Waqqāṣ ibn Rabīʿah.

Muḥammad ibn Muṣaffā related to us: Baqiyyah related to us, saying: Ibn Thawbān related to us, from his father68 from (110a) Makḥūl, from Waqqāṣ ibn Rabīʿah, that al-Mustawrid related to him that the Messenger of God ﷺ—said: “Whoever eats a meal at the expense of a Muslim man, God, Mighty and Majestic, will feed him a like meal from Hell. Whoever is clothed at the expense of a Muslim man, God, Mighty and Majestic, will clothe him with a like garment from Hell. And whoever assumes a position through a Muslim man for the sake of being seen or showing off, God, Mighty and Majestic, will place him in a position of being seen and showing off on the Day of Resurrection.”

Among them was ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Qatādah al-Naṣrī.

Ḥaywah ibn Shurayḥ and Ibn al-Muṣaffā related to us, saying: Baqiyyah related to us: al-Zubaydī related to me: Rāshid ibn Saʿd related to me, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Qatādah al-Naṣrī, from Hishām ibn Ḥakīm, that a man came to the Prophet ﷺ—and said, “Messenger of God, shall we undertake deeds, now that the decree has already been decided?” The Messenger of God ﷺ—said:

“God, Mighty and Majestic, took the progeny of Adam from their loins, then made them bear witness against themselves. Then He scattered them from His palm, saying, ‘These are for Paradise, and these are for the Fire.’ The people of Paradise are made ready for the deeds of the people of Paradise, and the people of the Fire are made ready for the deeds of the people of the Fire.”

Among them was Yaḥyā ibn al-Miqdām.

Muḥammad ibn al-Muṣaffā related to us: Baqiyyah related to us, saying: Thawr ibn Yazīd related to me, from Ṣāliḥ ibn Yaḥyā ibn al-Miqdām, from his father, from his grandfather, from Khālid ibn al-Walīd, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ—forbade the meat of horses, mules, and donkeys, and that of every beast of prey with fangs.

Among them was Ḥabīb ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Kabshah al-Anmārī.

Ḥaywah ibn Shurayḥ, Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, and Muḥammad ibn al-Muṣaffā related to us, saying: Baqiyyah related to us: Abū Sufyān al-Anmārī related to me, from Ḥabīb ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Kabshah, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: The Prophet ﷺ—liked looking at citron, and liked looking at red doves.

Among them was Yazīd ibn Marthad.

(110b) Sulaymān ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān related to me, saying: Yaḥyā ibn Ḥamzah related to us: al-Waḍīn ibn ʿAṭāʾ related to me, from Yazīd ibn Marthad, from Abū Dharr, who said:

I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ—say: “Whoever acts well in what remains will be forgiven for what has passed; whoever acts badly in what remains will be taken to account for what remains and what has passed.”

Among them was Usāmah ibn Salmān al-ʿAnsī.

ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn Bakkār al-Sulamī al-Bayrūtī and Ṣafwān ibn Ṣāliḥ related to us, saying: al-Walīd related to us: Ibn Thawbān informed us, from his father, from Makḥūl, from Usāmah ibn Salmān al-ʿAnsī, who said: Abū Dharr related to us, from the Messenger of God ﷺ—that he said: “God, Mighty and Majestic, forgives a servant so long as the barrier has not fallen.” They asked, “Messenger of God, what is the falling of the barrier?” He said, “That you die while associating partners with God.”

Among them was Maʿdīkarib.

Mahdī ibn Jaʿfar, Muḥammad ibn Abī Usāmah al-Ḥalabī, and Abū ʿUmayr ibn al-Naḥḥās related to us, saying: Ḍamrah related to us, from Ibn Shawdhab, from Maṭar, from Shahr ibn Ḥawshab, from Maʿdīkarib, from Muʿādh ibn Jabal, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ—said: “Three things are what I fear most for you. [First,] a man who recites the Qurʾān until its splendor is seen upon him and he becomes a support for faith; God lends it to him, Mighty and Majestic, for as long as He wills, then he draws his sword and accuses his neighbor of associating partners with God, and strikes him.” They asked, “Messenger of God, which of the two is more deserving of the charge of associating partners with God, the accuser or the accused?” He said, “The accuser. [Second,] a ruler like yourselves, to whom God, Mighty and Majestic, grants authority, who says, ‘Whoever obeys me has obeyed God, Mighty and Majestic, and whoever disobeys me has disobeyed God, Mighty and Majestic.’ He lies: no created being may have his due [except] from the Creator. [Third,] a man whom reports have made light-headed: whenever he finishes relating one report, he connects it to one longer than it, hoping to encounter the Antichrist and follow him.”

Among them was Qays ibn al-Ḥārith al-Madhḥijī.

(111a) Ṣafwān related to us, saying: al-Walīd related to me: ʿĪsā ibn Mūsā and another related to me, saying: Ismāʿīl ibn ʿUbayd Allāh related to us that Qays ibn al-Ḥārith al-Madhḥijī related to him that he and al-Ṣunābiḥī entered. When he saw al-Ṣunābiḥī, he said, “Whoever would be pleased to look upon a man as though he had ascended to heaven, and to see him doing what he sees, let him look at this man.”

Among them was al-Ḥārith ibn Muʿāwiyah al-Kindī.

Manṣūr related to me, from Abū Yazīd Ghaylān, the client of Kinānah, from Abū Sallām al-Ḥabashī, from al-Miqdām ibn Maʿdīkarib, from al-Ḥārith ibn Muʿāwiyah, who said: ʿUbādah ibn al-Ṣāmit related to us, with Abū al-Dardāʾ present, that the Prophet of God ﷺ—prayed toward a camel from the spoils. When he had finished his prayer, he took a tuft of wool from it between his fingers and said: “Behold, this is from your spoils, and I have no share of it except one-fifth”—“and the one-fifth” “is returned to you. So render up the thread and the needle, and anything smaller or larger than that. For embezzlement from the spoils is a disgrace to the one responsible for it in this world and the next. Fight people for the sake of God, Mighty and Majestic, those near to you and those far away; let no blame from any blamer deter you concerning God, Mighty and Majestic. Uphold God’s prescribed limits, Mighty and Majestic, whether traveling or at home. Take up the struggle, for it is a great gate among the gates of Paradise; through it God, Mighty and Majestic, saves one from anxiety and grief.”

Ṣafwān related to me, saying: al-Walīd related to us: Abū Muḥammad ʿĪsā ibn Mūsā related to me, from Ismāʿīl ibn ʿUbayd Allāh, from Qays ibn al-Ḥārith al-Madhḥijī, who heard ʿUbādah ibn al-Ṣāmit say: The Messenger of God ﷺ—used to say, “I am telling you a report, so let those of you who are present convey it to those who are absent.”

Among them was Yaʿlā ibn Shaddād ibn Aws.

Yūsuf ibn Mukhlad al-Ṣaffār al-Kūfī related to me, saying: Abū Usāmah related to us, from Abū Sinān (111b), ʿĪsā ibn Sinān, from Yaʿlā ibn Shaddād, from ʿUbādah ibn al-Ṣāmit, who said: The Prophet ﷺ—led us in prayer at Ḥunayn beside a camel from the spoils. Then he reached for the camel’s hump and took a tuft of wool from it, holding it between his fingers. He said:

“O people, this is from your spoils. Render up the thread and the needle, anything less than that, and anything more. For embezzlement from the spoils is disgrace, fire, and shame on the Day of Resurrection.”

Among them was Abū Umayyah al-Shaʿbānī.

He had been a pagan.

Sulaymān ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Dimashqī related to us, saying: Maṭar ibn al-ʿAlāʾ al-Fazārī related to us: ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Yasār al-Thaqafī related to us: Abū Umayyah al-Shaʿbānī—who had been a pagan—related to me, saying: Muʿādh ibn Jabal related to me, saying: The Messenger of God ﷺ—said: “Thirty [years] of caliphate under prophethood; thirty [years of] prophethood and kingship; thirty [years of] kingship and tyranny; and whatever comes after that has no good in it.”

[Al-Ṣunābiḥī]

ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān related to us, saying: ʿAbd Allāh related to us: Ibn ʿAwn informed us, from Rajāʾ ibn Ḥaywah, from Maḥmūd ibn al-Rabīʿ, who said: We were with ʿUbādah ibn ʿUbāda ibn al-Ṣāmit fell ill, and al-Ṣunābiḥī came to him. ʿUbāda said, “Whoever would be pleased to look upon a man as though he had been raised above the seven heavens and had acted according to what he saw, let him look at this man.” When al-Ṣunābiḥī had reached him, ʿUbāda said, “If I am called to testify, I shall testify for you; if I am asked to intercede, I shall intercede for you; and if I am able, I shall benefit you.”

Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us: al-Layth related to us: Muḥammad ibn ʿAjlān related to me, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā ibn Ḥibbān, from Abū Muḥayrīz, from al-Ṣunābiḥī, who said:

“I visited ʿUbāda ibn al-Ṣāmit while he was at the point of death, and I wept. He said, ‘Wait—why are you weeping? By God, if I am called to testify, I shall testify for you; if I am asked to intercede, I shall intercede for you; and if I am able, I shall benefit you.’”

“Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Zabr related to me: my father, ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Zabr, related to us, from al-Zuhrī, who said: ‘There are four scholars: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib in Medina, ʿĀmir al-Shaʿbī in Kūfa, al-Ḥasan ibn Abī al-Ḥasan in Baṣra, and Makḥūl in Syria.’”

Saʿīd ibn Asad related to us: Ḍamra related to us, from Barā, who said— Makḥūl said: “After I was questioned, I knew no more than I had known before I was questioned.”

Ibn Numayr related to us: my father related to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, from Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb, from Murthid ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Yazanī, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿUsayla al-Ṣunābiḥī, who said: “I missed the Prophet ﷺ—by only five nights. The Prophet ﷺ—died while I was at al-Juḥfa. I came to his Companions while they were still numerous, and asked Bilāl about the Night of Decree. He said: ‘The night of the twenty-third; he did not pray.’”

Saʿīd ibn Asad related to me: Ḍamra related to us, from Rajāʾ, from ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd al-Dimashqī, who said: “Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Ṣunābiḥī would relate traditions to one or two people. If he saw a third, he would say, ‘There can be no more hadith today.’”

Hishām ibn ʿAmmār related to us: ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Muḥammad related to us, who said: “I heard al-Awzāʿī say: ‘The caliphs were in Syria. When a calamity arose, they would ask the scholars of Syria and the people of Medina about it. The traditions of the people of Iraq did not get beyond the walls of their houses. Yet the scholars of Syria would transmit from the Khārijites of Iraq!’”

“ʿAbd Allāh ibn Maslama related to us: Ibn Lahīʿa related to us, from Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb, from Abū al-Khayr, from al-Ṣunābiḥī, who was asked, ‘When did you migrate?’ He said:

‘When the Prophet ﷺ—had died, a man met me at al-Juḥfa, and I said, “What is the news, ʿAbd Allāh?” He said, “Yes, by God—a long or momentous piece of news: we buried the Messenger of God ﷺ—only the day before yesterday.”’”

“‘What news, ʿAbd Allāh?’ He said, ‘Yes, by God—a long or momentous piece of news: we buried the Messenger of God ﷺ—only the day before yesterday.’”

[ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥayrīz]

Muḥammad ibn Abī Usāma al-Ḥalabī related to us: Ḍamra related to us, from Bashīr ibn Ṣāliḥ, who said: Ibn Muḥayrīz entered a shop in Dābiq, intending to buy a garment. A man said to the shopkeeper, “This is Ibn Muḥayrīz; give him a good price.”

Ibn Muḥayrīz became angry, left, and said, “We buy with our money; we do not buy with our religion.”

Muḥammad ibn Abī Usāma related to us: Mubashshir related to us, from Salm ibn al-ʿAlāʾ, who said: “I saw Ibn Muḥayrīz standing in Dābiq. He heard a man bargaining with another man, saying, ‘No, by God,’ and ‘Yes, by God.’ He said, ‘Man, do not let God be the least valuable part of your merchandise.’”

Saʿīd ibn Asad related to me: Ḍamra related to us, from Rajāʾ ibn Abī Salama, from Muqbil ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Kinānī, who said: “I have never seen anyone more likely than Ibn Muḥayrīz to bring discredit upon his own good qualities, nor anyone more truthful when he saw—”

[Ibn] Muḥayrīz. He once saw Khālid ibn Yazīd ibn Muʿāwiya wearing a robe of brocade in Bayt al-Maqdis and said to him, “You wear brocade?” He replied, “I wore it only for these people,” and pointed to ʿAbd al-Malik. Ibn Muḥayrīz became angry and said, “Your fear of God ought not to be equal to your fear of any person.”

Saʿīd related to me: Ḍamra related to me, from Rajāʾ, from al-Walīd ibn Hishām, who said:

“Al-Walīd ibn ʿAbd al-Malik appointed me to command the summer expedition. I said to Ibn Muḥayrīz, ‘You see what I have been put to; I cannot do without your counsel. If there is no avoiding it, then [make it] a little.’”

Saʿīd related to me: Ḍamra related to us, from Rajāʾ and al-Saybānī, who said: “Ibn Muḥayrīz wore two garments woven by his family. Khālid ibn Durayk met him at the place for ablutions. Khālid said to him, ‘I dislike the thought that people might make you seem ascetic or call you miserly.’ He replied, ‘I seek refuge in God from praising myself or praising anyone else. Go to the market and buy me two white garments.’

“He said: ‘I went out and bought him two white Egyptian garments.’ He said: ‘He made one into a shirt and the other into a cloak.’”

“Saʿīd related to me: Ḍamra related to us, from Rajāʾ ibn Abī Salama, from Rajāʾ ibn Ḥaywa: ‘News of Ibn ʿUmar’s death reached us while we were in Ibn Muḥayrīz’s gathering. Ibn Muḥayrīz said, “By God, I used to count Ibn ʿUmar’s remaining alive as a safeguard for the people of the earth.”’” “Rajāʾ ibn Ḥaywa said after Ibn Muḥayrīz’s death, ‘By God, I too used to count Ibn Muḥayrīz’s remaining alive as a safeguard for the people of the earth.’”

Saʿīd related to us: Ḍamra related to us, from Rajāʾ, who said: “Ibn Muḥayrīz would bring ʿAbd al-Malik a letter containing advice. He would bring it close to him, then not leave it in his hand.”

Saʿīd related to me: Ḍamra related to us, from Rajāʾ, who said: “ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Marwān said to Ibn Muḥayrīz, ‘Why has al-Ḥajjāj written to complain about you?’ He replied, ‘I did say something about him that I wish I had not said.’

“Rajāʾ said: One day ʿAbd al-Malik spoke while Ibn Muḥayrīz was sitting there, and the people of Iraq were asking him to dismiss al-Ḥajjāj. Ibn Muḥayrīz said, ‘They have asked him for very little.’”

Saʿīd related to me: Ḍamra related to us, from Rajāʾ, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAwf al-Qāriʾ, who said: “I saw us at Rhodes: there was no one in the army who prayed more openly than Ibn Muḥayrīz—and a man from Mecca who had been cut off.”

He said: “Then I saw that Ibn Muḥayrīz did less of that once he had become known and recognized.”

Saʿīd related to us: Ḍamra related to us, from Rajāʾ, who said: “Ibn Muḥayrīz had a need that concerned Yazīd ibn Abī Yazīd al-Anṣārī. He was told, ‘You will meet him in the mosque after the night prayer.’ He said, ‘I dislike being seen as one of those who attend the night prayer in the mosque.’”

Saʿīd related to me: Ḍamra related to us, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamla, who said: “No one in Syria could criticize al-Ḥajjāj with a reproach except Ibn Muḥayrīz and Abū al-Abyaḍ al-ʿAnsī. Al-Walīd ibn ʿAbd al-Malik said to Abū al-Abyaḍ, ‘Why has al-Ḥajjāj written to complain about you? You must stop, or I shall send you to him.’”

Saʿīd related to me, from Ḍamra, from al-Saybānī, who said: “Ibn al-Daylamī was the strongest defender of his brothers. Ibn Muḥayrīz was mentioned in his gathering, and a man said, ‘He was miserly.’ Ibn al-Daylamī became angry and said, ‘He was generous in what God loves, and miserly in what you love.’”

Muḥammad ibn Yazīd al-Kūfī related to us: Ḍamra related to us: ʿAbbād ibn ʿAbbād related to us, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī ʿAmr al-Saybānī, who said: Ibn Muḥayrīz said:

“I am relating traditions to you, so do not say, ‘Ibn Muḥayrīz related to us.’ I fear that this will cast me down, to my sorrow, on the Day of Resurrection.”

[Rajāʾ ibn Ḥaywa]

Saʿīd ibn Asad related to me: Ḍamra related to us, from Rajāʾ, from Ibn ʿAwn, who said:

“I have never met anyone more restrained than three men: Rajāʾ ibn Ḥaywa in Syria, al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad in the Ḥijāz, and Ibn Sīrīn in Iraq.” He meant that they did not go beyond what they knew, or that they did not take it upon themselves to speak from their own opinion.

“Abū Saʿīd al-Aṣmaʿī related to us: I heard Ibn ʿAwn say, ‘I met six men: three of them were strict about the wording, and three allowed latitude in matters of meaning. Among those strict about the wording were al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad, Rajāʾ ibn Ḥaywa, and Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn; among those concerned with meanings were al-Ḥasan, al-Shaʿbī, and al-Nakhaʿī.’”

Saʿīd ibn Asad related to us: Ḍamra related to us, from Rajāʾ, who said: Makḥūl said:

“I had long been occupied with meanings until Rajāʾ ibn Ḥaywa helped them against me. That was because he entered Syria among them. Rajāʾ had come to Kūfa with Bishr ibn Marwān, and Abū Isḥāq al-Hamdānī and Qatāda heard from him on that visit…”

“Abū Isḥāq al-Hamdānī and Qatāda heard from him on that visit.”

Saʿīd related to me: Ḍamra related to us, from Rajāʾ; and ʿĀṣim ibn Rajāʾ ibn Ḥaywa related to me, who said: “Makḥūl came to my father to complain and said, ‘Abū al-Miqdām, they want my blood.’

“He said, ‘I warned you about the Qurashīs and keeping their company. Yet they have harmed and betrayed you, though you related traditions to them. When they spread them about you, you came to dislike them.’ ʿAlī added: When he left, those who used to criticize Makḥūl came to him and mentioned him. My father said, ‘Leave Makḥūl alone. You used to be unknown, and he spoke well of you.’ So they desisted.”

Saʿīd related to me: Ḍamra related to us, from Rajāʾ, who said: Al-Muʿallā ibn Ruʾba al-Tamīmī related to me, who said: “I had a need that concerned Rajāʾ ibn Ḥaywa, who was with Sulaymān. I met him on the road, and he said, ‘Today the Commander of the Faithful appointed ʿAbd Allāh ibn Mawhab as judge. If I had to choose between being carried to my grave and what Ibn Mawhab has been appointed to, I would choose to be carried to my grave.’ I said to him, ‘People claim that you were the one who recommended him.’ He said, ‘They are right. I only had the public’s interests in view—’”

“‘and I did not have his interests in view.’”

Saʿīd related to me: Ḍamra related to us, from Rajāʾ, from Ibrāhīm ibn Yazīd al-Naṣrī, who said: “I came to ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz with robes sent by the ruler of Yemen, ʿUrwa ibn Muḥammad. He set aside one robe and said, ‘This is for my dear friend, Rajāʾ ibn Ḥaywa.’”

Through him, from Rajāʾ, who said: “Yazīd ibn ʿAbd al-Malik came to Bayt al-Maqdis and wanted Rajāʾ ibn Ḥaywa to accompany him, but Rajāʾ refused and asked to be excused. ʿUqba ibn Wassāj said to him:

‘God will benefit people through your presence.’ He replied, ‘Those people you have in mind are gone.’ ʿUqba said to him, ‘These are people who, if a man keeps his distance from them after having been close, will almost certainly turn against him.’ He replied:

‘I hope that the One to whom I summon them will suffice me against them.’

Saʿīd ibn Asad related to me: Ḍamra related to us, from Rajāʾ ibn Abī Salama, who said: “Yazīd ibn ʿAbd al-Malik used to grant Rajāʾ ibn Ḥaywa thirty dinars each month. When Hishām took power, he said, ‘This was not a sound decision,’ and stopped the payments. Hishām then saw his father in a dream reproaching him for that, so he resumed the payments he had stopped.

“Through him, from Rajāʾ, who said: ʿUqba ibn Wassāj said to Rajāʾ ibn Ḥaywa, ‘Were it not for certain qualities in you, you would be the man—’”

“‘in you, you would be the man.’ He asked, ‘What are they?’ He said, ‘Your brothers come to you, while you do not go to them; and you have branded the thighs of your riding animals with your name, when the clan’s brand would have sufficed for you.’ He replied, ‘As for your saying that my brothers come to me while I do not go to them, sometimes they distract me from my prayer. As for your saying that I branded my name on the hindquarters of my riding animals, and that the clan’s brand would suffice for me, I did not think there was any harm in a man writing his name on his riding animal’s thigh.’”

Through him, from Rajāʾ, who said: Rajāʾ ibn Ḥaywa saw a man nodding off after dawn and said, “Wake up, lest someone think that this is because you stayed up late.”

Saʿīd ibn Asad related to me: Ḍamra related to us, from Ibn Shūdhub, from Maṭar, who said: “I have never met a Syrian more learned in jurisprudence than Rajāʾ ibn Ḥaywa, except that if you stirred him, you would find him a Syrian; and sometimes, when something came up, he would say, ‘ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Marwān did this.’”

Maṭar said: “We know of no one whose testimony was accepted on his own except Rajāʾ ibn Ḥaywa”—meaning that his testimony alone was accepted in the time of ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz.

Saʿīd related to us: Ḍamra related to us, from Rajāʾ ibn Abī Salama, from Nuʿaym ibn Salāma— He said: “There is no man among the people of Syria whom I would rather take as a model than Rajāʾ ibn Ḥaywah.”

Through the same chain, from Rajāʾ ibn Abī Salamah, from Ismāʿīl ibn ʿUbayd Allāh al-Makhzūmī, who said:

“I spoke with Rajāʾ ibn Ḥaywah and ʿAdī ibn ʿAdī about something, and it seemed that they took offense.

“So I said to them: ‘It is not sound judgment on your part to place your opinion in the position of someone whose word should not be challenged in any matter.’ Rajāʾ ibn Ḥaywah said: ‘Abū ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, if we have been deprived of that in someone else, let us at least not be deprived of it in you, Abū ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd.’”

Abū ʿUmayr related to us: “I heard Kathīr ibn al-Walīd say: ‘Whenever I saw Ibn Shūdhub, I remembered the angels.’”

Zayd ibn Bishr related to us: “I informed Ibn Wahb, who said: ‘I heard al-Layth ibn Saʿd say: “Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd told me that Sulaymān ibn Yasār said to him: ‘If two brothers were brought down from a fortress, and one settled in Syria while the other settled in Iraq, then if you met the Syrian, you would find him speaking of obedience, the duty of obedience, and jihād. But if you met the other, you would find him asking about doubts, saying: “What about such and such? What is the ruling concerning such and such?”’”’”

Saʿīd ibn Asad related to me: “Ḍamrah related to us, from Rajāʾ ibn Abī Salamah:”

“I was told that Juzʾ ibn Jābir was judge over Palestine and left behind only half a dirham. He was one of those who wept profusely. Ibn Muḥayrīz used to say: ‘You should turn to Juzʾ ibn Jābir’—meaning, because of his righteousness and excellence.

“I heard that ʿAbd Allāh ibn Razām used to walk through the cemeteries and say: ‘People of the graves, raise your heads and see who has taken up the judgeship after you.’

“Through the same chain, from Rajāʾ, who said: ‘ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAwf al-Qāriʾ passed by me, and I said to him: “Abū al-Qāsim, where have you come from?” He said: “I have come from Ibn Mawhab. Something about me reached him, so I came to apologize to him. I like there to be reconciliation between me and my righteous brothers.”

“Through the same chain, from Jābir, from Rashdīn ibn Khabbāb, who said: ‘Khārijah ibn al-Walīd ibn Bujayr al-Azdī fell ill, so I called a physician for him. The physician examined him, and when he left him, he said:

“‘There is nothing wrong with your companion but grief.’ When I returned, I told him that the physician had said, ‘There is nothing wrong with your companion but grief.’ He said: ‘He spoke truly. I recalled the scenes of the Day of Resurrection, and my heart was seized with fear.’

“Saʿīd related to me: Ḍamrah related to us, from Rajāʾ, who said: ‘Makhūl used to say:

“‘Sometimes I intended to pray against Rabīʿah ibn Yazīd—one of those who testified against him—but then I would remember how early he went to the mosque, and I would refrain from doing so.’

“Saʿīd related to me: Ḍamrah related to us, from Rajāʾ, who said: ‘I heard ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī say: “I never encountered in Palestine a man more complete than Nuʿaym ibn Salāmah.”’”

Through the same chain, from Rajāʾ, who said: “I said to ʿUthmān ibn Abī Sawdah: ‘Do you think you will go on campaign this year?’ He said: ‘I would not like to miss campaigning this year, even if I had one hundred thousand dinars.’”

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAmr related to me: Abū Mushir related to us; Saʿīd told me: “Among us, no one had a better manner in worship than Makhūl and Rabīʿah ibn Yazīd.”

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAmr related to me: Abū Mushir said: “I heard Rabīʿah ibn Yazīd say: ‘For forty years, whenever the caller to prayer gave the call for the noon prayer, I was in the mosque—unless I was ill or traveling.’”

Muḥammad ibn al-Muṣaffā related to us: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-ʿAṭṭār al-Anṣārī related to us: ʿUthmān ibn ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Muslim related to me, from Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, who said: “I went in to ʿĀʾishah and said: ‘Mother, Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh says: “Water is required only because of water.”’ She said: ‘Jābir is mistaken. Is Jābir more knowledgeable about the Messenger of God than I am? I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ—say: “When the two circumcised parts pass one another, ritual bathing becomes obligatory.”’ Does it make stoning obligatory but not ritual bathing?”

Saʿīd related to me: Ḍamrah related to us, from Rajāʾ, who said: “I heard Maʿn al-Tanūkhī say: ‘I have seen only two ascetics in this community: ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz and Ismāʿīl—’” ibn ʿUbayd Allāh al-Makhzūmī, who was an uncle of Hishām ibn ʿAbd al-Malik. Rajāʾ said: “When Ismāʿīl ibn ʿUbayd Allāh returned from the summer campaign, he would spread out his saddle blankets. He, the mother of his child, and his riding animals were in one house in one area, while he and the mother of his child were in another area. He used to say: ‘If only these jars could not manage a day’s supply, I would prefer it’—meaning, the cooked provisions in the waterskin.”

Ḍamrah said: “I heard someone relate that Ismāʿīl ibn ʿUbayd Allāh once served a man raisins. The man began eating and spitting out the seeds. He said to him: ‘If you are full, leave them.’”

Saʿīd related to me: Ḍamrah related to us, from Rajāʾ, who said: “Muḥammad ibn Hishām ibn Ismāʿīl, the uncle of Hishām ibn ʿAbd al-Malik, fell ill at Dābiq, and ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī visited him. He said: ‘There is no one among my brothers who has not visited me, except for what happened with ʿUthmān ibn Abī Sawdah.’ ʿUthmān was a companion of ʿAṭāʾ. When ʿAṭāʾ returned to the man, he said to ʿUthmān:

“‘Muḥammad said: “There is no one among my brothers who has not visited me, except for what happened with ʿUthmān ibn Abī Sawdah.”’ ʿUthmān said: ‘That is a walk I will never let God see me fail to make.’”

Saʿīd related to me: Ḍamrah related to us, from Rajāʾ ibn Ḥaywah, who said: “There was a dispute between a man and ʿUbādah ibn Nasīʾ, and the man hurried toward him. Rajāʾ ibn—”

Ḥaywah met ʿUbādah ibn Nasīʾ and said: “I have heard that so-and-so did something to you. Tell me about it.” He said:

“If I were not afraid that I would be backbiting him, I would tell you what he did.”

Saʿīd related to me: Ḍamrah related to us, from Rajāʾ, from Muqbil ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Kinānī, who said: “I do not fear that I might deliberately lie; rather, I fear for myself when I repeat a report.”

[ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī]

Ḍamrah related to us, from Ibrāhīm ibn Abī ʿAblah, who said: “We used to sit with ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī. He would supplicate with certain prayers after dawn. One day he was absent, and a man among the callers to prayer began speaking. Rajāʾ ibn Ḥaywah disapproved of his voice and said to him:

“‘Who is that?’ He said: ‘It is I, Abū al-Miqdām.’ Rajāʾ said: ‘Be quiet. We dislike hearing what is good except from those who are its people.’”

Abū ʿUmayr ʿĪsā ibn al-Naḥḥās al-Ramlī related to us: Ḍamrah related to us, from Ibn Abī ʿAblah, who said: “I used to sit with ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī after dawn, and he would supplicate with certain prayers. One day he was absent, and a man among the callers to prayer began speaking. Rajāʾ ibn Ḥaywah disapproved of his voice and said to him:

“‘Who is that?’ He said: ‘It is I, Abū al-Miqdām.’ He said: ‘Be quiet. We dislike hearing what is good except from those who are its people.’”

Abū Saʿīd ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm related to me: al-Walīd related to us; he said— Ibn Jābir said: “We used to campaign with ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī. He would spend the night in worship from its beginning until a short sleep at daybreak. Often, when most of the night had passed—or, he said, half of it—he would turn toward us and call out to us while we were in our tent: ‘ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd, Yazīd ibn Yazīd, Hishām ibn al-Ghāz, and so-and-so and so-and-so: get up, perform ablution, and pray! Get up, fast, and pray! Standing in prayer this night and fasting this day are easier than drinking pus and wearing pieces of iron.’ Then he would turn back to his prayer.”

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Saʿīd, Abū Qudāmah, related to me: al-Walīd ibn Muslim related to us, saying:

“ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd ibn Jābir related to us: ‘We used to campaign with ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī, and he would spend the night in worship. When half or a third of the night had passed, he would turn toward us while we were in our tent and call to us: “Yazīd, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd, and Hishām ibn al-Ghāz, get up, perform ablution, and pray! Praying this night and fasting this day are easier than wearing pieces of iron and drinking pus. Make haste, make haste; then escape, escape!” Then he would turn back to his prayer.’”

[Yazīd ibn Marthad]

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Saʿīd related to me: al-Walīd ibn Muslim related to us: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd ibn Jābir said to Yazīd ibn Marthad: “Why do I see that your eyes do not grow dry?” He said: “Why do you ask about this?” I said: “Perhaps God will make it beneficial.” He said: “Brother, even if God had threatened me, should I disobey Him, only with making me sit in a bathhouse, it would be fitting that my eyes never grow dry. How much more so when He has threatened me with the Fire of Hell!” I said: “Are you like this all the time?” He said: “Why do you ask about this?” I said:

“Perhaps God will make it beneficial.” He said: “Sometimes I draw near to my family as a man approaches his wife, but something comes to mind and comes between me and what I want. Sometimes food is set out, and something comes to mind, so I weep. My family weeps because I weep, and the children weep because we are weeping, though they do not know what made me weep. Sometimes I even distress my wife, and she says: ‘Woe to her! What has she been singled out for, among all the women of the world, that she must endure such long grief with you in this life?’”

[ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Zakariyyā]

He said: Saʿīd related to me: Ḍamrah related to us, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamlah, who said:

“I was at a gathering of Ibn Abī Zakariyyā al-Dimashqī. Mishkān al-Dimashqī was mentioned; he had been a companion of Abū al-Dardāʾ. They said: ‘He is certainly a righteous man, despite being the son of a man who loves authority.’

“He said: ‘God, grant me an excuse! We were with him aboard the ships at sea, and things grew severe for us, so we would hang his Qur’an around our necks. Then he came to me, struck my thigh, and said: “Ibn Abī Zakariyyā, what is it that you fear? I wish it would carry you and me rumbling along until the Day of Resurrection!”’”

He said: Saʿīd ibn Asad and Abū ʿUmayr related to me. They said: Ḍamrah related to us, from Ibn Abī Ḥamlah, who said: “I struggled to master silence for twenty years before I could attain from it what I wanted.” He said: “No one was ever backbitten in his gathering. He used to say: ‘If you speak of God, I will help you; if you speak of people, I will leave you alone.’”

ʿAlī ibn ʿUthmān ibn Nufayl and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAmr related to me. They said: Abū Mushir related to us: Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz related to us, from Rabīʿah ibn Yazīd, who said: “I went in with Ibn Abī Zakariyyā to ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, who seated Ibn Abī Zakariyyā beside him on the couch.” He said: “I began weighing the two of them against one another—which of them was better?” He said:

“He gave each of us twenty dinars. Ibn Abī Zakariyyā was not given more than us.”

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm related to us—Yaʿqūb said: “I have no doubt”—from Abū Mushir: Saʿīd related to us, from Rabīʿah, who said: “When we returned from the campaign, we came to a road that led to ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, and we were with Ibn Abī Zakariyyā. Ibn Abī Zakariyyā said: ‘If I do not visit ʿUmar on this road, I will never visit him.’ He was a persistent man.”

“We went to ʿUmar and asked permission to enter. He gave us permission and seated Ibn Abī Zakariyyā beside him. Rabīʿah said: ‘I began weighing the two of them against one another—which of them was better?’ He said: ‘Ibn Abī Zakariyyā’s son was with us, wearing a turban that he had neatly wrapped.’ He said: ‘ʿUmar asked: “Who is this?” Ibn Abī Zakariyyā said to him: “This is my son, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd Allāh.” ʿUmar said to him: “How do you find him?”’

“He said: ‘I would begrudge him being better than he is.’ ʿUmar said: ‘He is young; God alone brings things to right.’ He gave each of us twenty dinars. Ibn Abī Zakariyyā was not given more than us.”

[Mālik ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Khathʿamī]

Saʿīd ibn Asad related to me: Ḍamrah related to us, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamlah, who said: “The bell was never struck in a town—and they used to strike it at midnight—without Mālik [that is, Mālik ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Khathʿamī] having gathered his clothes around himself and entered the mosque in his house to pray.”

[Yazīd ibn al-Aswad al-Jurashī]

Abū al-Yamān related to us: Ṣafwān related to us, from Sulaym ibn ʿĀmir al-Khabāʾirī, that the sky withheld rain. Muʿāwiyah ibn Abī Sufyān and the people of Damascus went out to pray for rain. When Muʿāwiyah sat on the pulpit, he said: “Where is Yazīd ibn al-Aswad—” al-Jurashī?” The people called out to him, and he came forward, making his way through them. Muʿāwiyah ordered him to ascend the pulpit, and he sat at Muʿāwiyah’s feet. Muʿāwiyah said: “O God, today we seek the intercession with You of the best and most excellent among us. O God, we seek the intercession with You of Yazīd ibn al-Aswad al-Jurashī. Yazīd, raise your hands to God.” Yazīd raised his hands, and the people raised their hands. It was scarcely any time before a cloud swelled up in the west, like a shield, and a wind drove it along. We were given rain until the people could scarcely reach their homes.

Saʿīd ibn Asad related to us: Ḍamrah related to us, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamlah, who said:

“A drought struck the people of Damascus, and al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Qays al-Fihrī was in charge of them. He went out with the people to pray for rain and said: ‘Where is Yazīd ibn al-Aswad al-Jurashī?’ No one answered him.

“Then he said: ‘Where is Yazīd ibn al-Aswad al-Jurashī? I insist that, if he can hear me, he must stand up.’ A man stood up wearing a burnous. He faced the people and raised the two sides of his burnous onto his shoulders. Then he raised his hands and said: ‘My Lord, Your servants have drawn near to You through me, so give them rain.’

“He said: ‘The people departed, wading through the water.’ Yazīd said: ‘O God, he has made me famous; relieve me of him.’ No more than a week passed before al-Ḍaḥḥāk killed him.”

[ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās]

Saʿīd related to me: Ḍamrah related to us, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamlah and al-Awzāʿī, who said:

“ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās used to perform one thousand prostrations every day.”

[Abū Muslim al-Khawlānī]

ʿAmr ibn ʿĀṣim related to us: Sulaymān related to us: Ḥumayd related to us, saying: When Abū Muslim al-Khawlānī grew old, he was told, “You have grown old and frail; perhaps you should take it easy.”

He said, “When the racing horses are brought out, their riders are told, ‘Raise them up and urge them on.’ When you draw near the finish, do not hold anything back. I have seen the finish, so let me be.”

Ḥumayd related to us, saying: Abū Muslim al-Khawlānī said, “I have never done a deed without caring who saw it, except when a man is alone with his family or relieving himself.”

Al-Walīd ibn ʿUtba al-Dimashqī related to us, saying: Abū Mushir related to us, saying: I heard Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz say, “The name of Abū Muslim al-Khawlānī was ʿAbd Allāh ibn Thawb.”

I said to Hishām ibn ʿAmmār, “Was the name of Abū Muslim ʿAbd Allāh ibn Thawb?” He said, “Indeed: Ibn Thawb.” I said, “He used to say, ‘Dāriyā.’” He said, “Yes.”

Hishām said: Abū Muslim said, “He heard people saying, ‘So-and-so has gone ahead! So-and-so has gone ahead!’ He said, ‘Rather, Abū Muslim has gone ahead.’” (118a) I set out from Dāriyā with the books of those for whom the mosque’s gate had been opened. He said, “There are four nights’ journey between Dāriyā and the mosque.”

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm related to us, from Abū Mushir, whom I heard, from Saʿīd, who said:

His name was ʿAbd Allāh ibn Thawb, but his people say “Ibn Ayyūb.”

[ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿĀʾidh al-Azdī]
