Ibn Bukayr said: Abū al-Haytham was a Medinan, and his name was Sulaymān ibn ʿAmr. He was trustworthy. He came to Egypt and settled there, seeking a livelihood and means of subsistence.

ʿAlī ibn Qādim al-Kūfī related to us. I was sparing in writing from him because of his Shiʿism, for he leaned toward Shiʿism. Then I found that most of our elders had written from him and said: “He is trustworthy.”

Ghālib ibn ʿUbayd Allāh al-Jazarī al-ʿUqaylī related to us. He is weak, his hadith is abandoned, his hadith is not to be written down (137b), and the people of learning do not transmit from him. Only the heedless transmit from him; as for the discerning people of learning, they pay no regard to his hadith. “A heedless Kūfan shaykh from Anbār, named Waḍḍāḥ ibn Ḥassān, did transmit: He said, ‘Wazīr ibn ʿAbd Allāh related to us, from Ghālib ibn ʿUbayd Allāh al-Jazarī, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ, from Abū Hurayra: The Prophet ﷺ gave Muʿāwiya an arrow and said, “Here, take this, Muʿāwiya, until you meet me with it in Paradise.”’”

Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz al-Ramlī—“who was a traditionist of great retention”—related to me: ʿAbbād ibn ʿAbbād Abū ʿUtba al-Khawwāṣ al-Filasṭīnī—“who was among the ascetics and devout worshippers, trustworthy”—related to us, from “al-Saybānī, Yaḥyā ibn Abī ʿAmr, a trustworthy Syrian”. Yaḥyā transmitted from ʿAmr ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Ḥaḍramī—a trustworthy Syrian—from Abū Umāma. And he transmits— Al-Saybānī transmitted from Abū al-ʿAjfāʾ, who said: Someone said to ʿUmar, “If only you would appoint [a successor]!” He said: “If I were to encounter Khālid ibn al-Walīd, I would then appoint him.”

This is false, and Abū al-ʿAjfāʾ is unknown; it is not known who he is.

Hishām ibn ʿAmmār related to us: Ṣadaqa ibn Khālid al-Qurashī related to us; he is a trustworthy Damascene.

Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz al-Ramlī related to me: al-Walīd related to us, from “Ṣadaqa ibn Yazīd, a Damascene with good hadith.”

Some of our companions related to us: Ṣadaqa ibn ʿAbd Allāh—al-Samīn—related to us. I heard ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm deem him sound and incline toward regarding him as upright. For this reason, he told me about Marwān al-Ṭāṭarī—whose hadith I consider weak: “There was a shaykh named ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yazīd who used to sit with Hishām. He had Ṣadaqa ibn ʿAbd Allāh’s books and hadith. It was not hidden from me when he looked through them, and I do not write from him.”

“ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm related to us: al-Walīd related to us: al-Awzāʿī related to us: Nahīk ibn Yarīm al-Awzāʿī—who is acceptable—from Mughīth ibn Sumayy al-Awzāʿī—these are Syrian transmitters, and every one of them is trustworthy—who said: ‘ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr led us in the morning prayer in the late darkness.’” I turned to Ibn ʿUmar and said: “What is this prayer?” prayer?” He said: “This is how we prayed with the Messenger of God ﷺ and with Abū Bakr and ʿUmar. When ʿUmar was killed, ʿUthmān made it lighter (138a).”

“Abū Nuʿaym related to us: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz—who is trustworthy—related to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Mawhib—who is a trustworthy Hamadhānī—who said: ‘I heard Tamīm al-Dārī.’ This is an error: Ibn Mawhib did not hear from Tamīm, nor did he meet him.”

His grandson Yazīd ibn Khālid ibn Yazīd ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Mawhib, a trustworthy man, related to us.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yūsuf al-Dimashqī and Yazīd ibn Khālid ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Mawhib related to us, both saying: Yaḥyā ibn Ḥamza related to us, from ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Mawhib, from Qabīṣa ibn Dhuʾayb, from Tamīm al-Dārī: He asked the Prophet ﷺ “What is the rule concerning a man from among the unbelievers who accepts Islam at the hands of a Muslim?” The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “He has the strongest claim over him in his life and after his death.”

Ibn al-Muthannā related to us: Abū Bakr al-Ḥanafī said: Yūnus ibn Abī Isḥāq related to us, from his father, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Mawhib, from Tamīm al-Dārī, who said: “I asked—” the Messenger of God ﷺ. The hadith is the one transmitted by Yaḥyā ibn Ḥamza.

Abū ʿUmayr ʿĪsā ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Naḥḥās related to us: Aḥmad ibn Yazīd ibn Rūḥ al-Dārī—a man from the family of Tamīm—related to us, from Muḥammad ibn ʿUqba al-Qāḍī, from his father, from his grandfather: “We came upon Tamīm al-Dārī while he was preparing barley for his horse. We said to him:

‘Abū Ruqayya, have you no one to take care of this for you?’ He said: ‘Yes, but I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: “Whoever keeps a horse in the path of God and prepares its fodder with his own hand will receive a good deed for every grain.”’”

Abū ʿUmayr said: “Tamīm had no son; he had only a daughter called Ruqayya, and he took his teknonym from her.”

Abū al-Aswad al-Naḍr ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Murādī, the righteous man, related to us: Ibn Lahīʿa informed us, from Abū Ṣakhr, from Makḥūl, who said: I heard Abū Hind al-Dārī say: I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: “Whoever takes a stand to be seen and heard, God will make him be seen and heard.” They say that Tamīm and Abū Hind were brothers, but God knows best.

Sulaymān ibn Salama Abū Ayyūb al-Ḥimṣī related to me: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-ʿAlāʾ al-Ghassānī, of the family of Abū Bakr ibn Abī Maryam, related to us, from Abū Bakr ibn Abī Maryam, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: “I came to the Prophet ﷺ and said to him: ‘A girl was born to me tonight.’ He said: ‘Tonight a sūra called Maryam was sent down to me, so name her Maryam.’” He was therefore given the teknonym Abū Maryam.

Ibn Bukayr related to us: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Lahīʿa related to me: Bukayr related to me, from— Busr ibn Saʿīd, from ʿUbayd Allāh al-Khawlānī—who was an orphan in Maymūna’s care—who said: “I saw Maymūna praying in a long-sleeved garment, a full-length garment, and a head covering; she had no waist-wrapper on.” Bukayr and Busr are trustworthy, and their transmission is sufficient to serve as proof.

Ibn Bukayr said: He is ʿUbayd Allāh ibn al-Asad, but he had been registered in Medina when he was young, and they left him with Maymūna, who raised him.

[Al-Layth ibn Saʿd]

Ibn Bukayr said: Shuʿayb ibn al-Layth was born in the year thirty-five. I said to Ibn Bukayr: “Did he hear alongside you?” He said: “No.”

Ibn Bukayr said: Shuʿayb ibn al-Layth related to me: My father said: “I took leave of Abū Jaʿfar, Commander of the Faithful, at Bayt al-Maqdis. He said: ‘What I have seen of your good judgment pleases me, and I was delighted that God left someone like you among the people.’” Shuʿayb said: My father told me: “Do not relate this from me as long as I am alive.” He said: Abū Jaʿfar said to me: “Will you find me a man whom I can appoint over Egypt?”

I said to him: “So-and-so, your governor, has served over it.” He said: “No, he is weak.” I said: “Commander of the Faithful, he is strong.” He said: “No, he is weak.” I said: “The Commander of the Faithful knows better what is best for his subjects.” He said to me: “Find me a man whom I can appoint over it.” I said: “I will.” He said: “So—”

“Would you prevent me?” He said: I replied, “I am not strong enough; I am weak.” He said: He then said to me, “You are strong, unless your intention toward us grows weak.”

Al-Layth was kunya’d Abū al-Ḥārith.

Ibn Bukayr said: He used to say, “Our origin is from Isfahan.” Ibn Bukayr said: “They are from al-Ṭabna.”75

Ibn Bukayr related to me, saying: Ibrāhīm ibn Ṣāliḥ related to us. He said: I asked Ibn Lahīʿa:

“How did you hear from al-Aʿraj when al-Layth did not hear from him?” He said: “Al-Aʿraj arrived and stayed with Jaʿfar ibn Rabīʿa. I used to attend to him, even buying barley for his horse with dirhams.” He said: “He used to slight al-Layth and ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith.”76 He then said to me:

“I want to hear something.” He said, “You may hear it, but do not tell anyone about it.” He said: “So we heard from al-Aʿraj (139a), and he went to Alexandria. People talked about it, saying, ‘Al-Aʿraj ibn Hurmuz is in Alexandria.’” Ibn Bukayr said: “I heard al-Layth say, ‘I saw him in Egypt by the pulpit. He was asked about the letters of the Qur’an, but I did not recognize him and did not know who he was.’”

Ibn Bukayr said: I heard al-Layth say: “I saw ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb in Mecca, but I did not ask him about anything.”

Ibn Bukayr said: Someone I trust informed me, on the authority of al-Layth ibn Saʿd, that he said: “I saw Abū al-Khayr Marthad ibn ʿAbd Allāh [was] judging cases for the people of Alexandria.”

Ibn Bukayr said: Al-Layth ibn Saʿd made the pilgrimage in the year thirteen. He heard from Ibn Shihāb in Mecca, and from Ibn Abī Mulayka, ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ, Abū al-Zubayr, Nāfiʿ, ʿImrān ibn Abī Anas, and a number of shaykhs.

Ibn Bukayr said: Mubashshir ibn Saʿīd informed me, on the authority of al-Layth, who said: “I went to Abū al-Zubayr, and he brought out books for me. I asked, ‘Is this what you heard from Jābir?’ He said, ‘And from others as well.’”

I asked, “Is this what you heard from Jābir?” He then brought out this sheet for me. I asked Ibn Bukayr, “Was al-Layth then twenty years old?” He replied, “Twenty years old.” Al-Layth said: “I went in to see Nāfiʿ, and he questioned me. I said, ‘I am a man from Egypt.’ He said, ‘From whom?’ I said, ‘From Qays.’ He said, ‘The son of Rifāʿa?’ I said, ‘I am the son of a man from his people.’ He asked me, ‘How old are you?’ I said, ‘Twenty.’ He said, ‘As for your beard, it is the beard of a forty-year-old.’” Al-Layth said: “A man recited to Nāfiʿ, ‘Like the one whom you have spread—’”

“His father has a story about it”—meaning, “the one who drinks from silver vessels.”

Ibn Bukayr said: Someone who heard al-Layth say informed me: “I wrote down a great deal of Ibn Shihāb’s knowledge, and I considered riding the postal service to him at al-Ruṣāfa. I feared that this might not be for God’s sake, so I left it.”

Ibn Bukayr said: Shuʿayb ibn al-Layth informed me, on the authority of his father al-Layth, who said: “Some of my family told me that I was born in the year ninety-two, but the year I am certain of is ninety-four.”

Ibn Bukayr said: Al-Layth ibn Saʿd was born in the year ninety-four and died on the middle day of Shaʿbān, a Friday, in the year one hundred and seventy-five (139b). Mūsā ibn ʿĪsā al-Hāshimī led the funeral prayer for him, and he was buried after the Friday prayer. He was kunya’d Abū al-Ḥārith.

Ibn Bukayr related to me, saying: Al-Layth related to us. He said: “I made the pilgrimage, and when I was in Medina, pilgrims from the various regions had arrived. The roads were full of dung. When I went to the mosque in the morning, I wore a pair of leather socks. When I entered the mosque, I took one off and prayed in the other. Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Anṣārī said to me, ‘You are someone people look to.’ I think he may have said, ‘You are a leader whom people look to, so do not do this. Wipe over your leather sock and pray in it.’”

“Abū Ṣāliḥ ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṣāliḥ, the righteous man” said: Abū Shurayḥ ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Shurayḥ, one of the residents of Alexandria, related to us; “he was among the best of men.”

Mālik ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Khathʿamī, commander of the summer campaigns.

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yaḥyā ibn Ismāʿīl ibn ʿUbayd Allāh al-Makhzūmī related to me: al-Jarrāḥ ibn Malīḥ al-Ḥimṣī, Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, related to us. He said: Bakr ibn Zurʿa al-Khawlānī related to us, from his father, from Abū ʿAnaba al-Khawlānī—who was among those who ate blood in the pre-Islamic period and prayed toward both qiblas with the Messenger of God ﷺ. He said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “God will continue to plant people in this religion and employ them in His obedience—or employ them through His obedience.”

Saʿīd ibn al-Ḥakam ibn Abī Maryam, Abū Muḥammad al-Qurashī, a client of Banū Umayya, related to us. Yaḥyā ibn Ayyūb—who is trustworthy—Abū al-ʿAbbās, informed us, from Khālid ibn Yazīd—who was one of the Egyptians and trustworthy—from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masrūḥ, from Rabīʿa ibn Nūrā, from Faḍāla ibn ʿUbayd, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Whoever wants to store up hadith should say, ‘There is no might nor power except through God.’”

Someone from the family of Abū Maryam related to me, from Yaḥyā, who said: “I was in Mecca, and I went out with Ibn Jurayj to a funeral on a scorching day. He said to me, ‘Abū al-ʿAbbās, hadith has enslaved you.’ He had a study circle in the mosque of Egypt. One day al-Layth ibn Saʿd passed by him—” and stopped by him. Yaḥyā rose to meet him and went with him to al-Layth’s study circle. Al-Layth would ask him about new cases, and he was a hadith memorizer (140a), so he would tell him what he knew. He said: Al-Layth sent him dinars, and he kept close to al-Layth until he died.

Ibn Bukayr related to us, saying: Al-Mufaḍḍal ibn Faḍāla ibn ʿUbayd, Abū Muʿāwiya al-Ḥimyarī, then al-Qatabānī, related to us; he is trustworthy.

Abū al-Aswad related to us, from Bakr ibn Muḍar ibn Muḥammad ibn Ḥakīm ibn Salmān, Abū ʿAbd al-Malik; he is trustworthy.

Ibn Rumḥ said: I saw al-Layth ibn Saʿd sitting by a grave while someone was being buried, with tears streaming down his beard.

Ibn Abī Maryam related to us: Nāfiʿ ibn Yazīd al-Qaysī, the client of Umm al-Maḍāʾ, related to us. Abū al-Walīd related to me: ʿAwf ibn Sulaymān ibn Ziyād, an Egyptian—I think he heard from him in Mecca—is acceptable.

Abū al-Yamān related to us: Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAyyāsh related to us, from Abū Rawāḥa Yazīd ibn Ayham, from al-Haytham ibn Mālik al-Ṭāʾī, who said: I heard al-Nuʿmān ibn Bashīr, while he was on the pulpit, say: I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: “Satan has strainers and traps. Among his strainers and traps are exulting over God’s blessings, boasting of God’s gifts, acting arrogantly toward God’s servants, and following one’s desires in matters that are not for God.”

Abū al-Yamān related to us: Ismāʿīl related to us, from Abū Sabāʾ ʿUtba ibn Tamīm, who said: “How excellent this is, from al-Walīd ibn ʿĀmir al-Yazanī, from ʿUrwa ibn Mughīth al-Anṣārī, from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb: The Messenger of God ﷺ ruled that the owner of a mount has the greater right to its front.”

Abū al-Yamān related to us: Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAyyāsh related to us, from Ḍamḍam ibn Zurʿa, from Shurayḥ, from Abū Rāshid al-Ḥabranī, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Shibl: The Prophet ﷺ forbade eating the dhabb lizard.

Abū Nuʿaym related to us: ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Ḥumayd ibn Abī Ghanīya—who is trustworthy—related to us, from Muḥammad ibn Muhājir al-Anṣārī, from his father, from Asmāʾ bt. Yazīd al-Anṣāriyya, who said: I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: “Do not kill your children secretly, for coitus with a nursing woman can overtake a horseman and throw him from his horse.”

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yūsuf related to us: Muḥammad ibn Muhājir related to us, from his father, who said: Asmāʾ bt. Yazīd (140b) related to me. She said: The Messenger of God ﷺ was invited to the funeral of a man from the Anṣār. When the bier was set down, the Prophet of God ﷺ stepped forward to pray. He said, “Does your companion owe a debt?” They replied, “Yes, O Prophet of God: two dinars.” He said:

He said, “Pray over your companion.” Abū Qatāda al-Anṣārī said, “They are my responsibility, O Prophet of God.”

He said: Then he prayed over him. Abū Yūsuf said: “This man is the brother of ʿAmr ibn Muhājir, the commander of ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz’s guard. They are both trustworthy men among the Syrians, and they have sound, significant hadiths.”

Abū al-Yamān related to us: Ṣafwān related to us, from Abū al-Zāhiriyya Ḥudayr ibn Kurayb, who is trustworthy and from whom the Egyptians narrated.

Aḥmad ibn Yūnus related to us: Abū Shihāb related to us, from Ḥamza ibn Abī Ḥamza al-Jazarī, from Naṣībīn. He is weak; his hadith is not to be welcomed.

ʿAnbasa ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrates from Muḥammad ibn Zādhān the hadith of ʿUthmān, from the Prophet ﷺ

and al-Furāt ibn al-Sāʾib.

And Abū al-ʿAṭūf al-Jazarī, from whom Yazīd ibn Hārūn narrates; his name is al-Jarrāḥ ibn al-Minhāl. and Muḥammad ibn Saʿīd.

And Rashdīn ibn Saʿd.

And al-Muwaqqarī.

And Wazīr ibn ʿAbd Allāh.

And Ghālib ibn ʿUbayd Allāh al-Jazarī al-ʿUqaylī.

And Yaḥyā ibn Abī Unaysa.

And Maslama ibn ʿAlī, from whom Ibn Rumḥ related to us.

And Rukn al-Shāmī.

Scholars should not occupy themselves with the hadiths of these men.

I heard Abū Bishr Bakr ibn Khalaf say: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī said:

“A man should not occupy himself with writing down the hadiths of weak transmitters. The least that will happen is that, to the extent he writes down hadiths from weak transmitters, he will miss out on hadiths from trustworthy transmitters.”

Saʿīd ibn Sinān, Abū al-Mahdī, related to us. His hadith is weak.

And Ghuḍayr ibn Maʿlān—his hadith is weak. Abū al-Yamān used to read out his hadith, but I would not listen, even when I was sitting there with nothing to do; I only wrote down the chains of transmission for his hadith.

And Abū Mūsā al-Wajīhī, from whom Baqiyya narrates: he is nothing.

And Khālid ibn Yazīd ibn Abī Mālik, from whom Sulaymān ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān related to us (141a); his hadith is weak.

Abū ʿIṣām al-ʿAsqalānī: his hadith is weak.

Kathīr ibn Marwān is a Syrian; “his hadith is worthless.”

Al-Ḥakam ibn ʿAmr al-Ruʿaynī is a Syrian and weak.

Al-Walīd ibn ʿAmr ibn Sāj is weak; his hadith is not to be written down.

ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥamza ibn Ṣuhayb and Ḥumayd ibn Mālik al-Lakhmī: Ādam related to us, from Ismāʿīl, from both of them; they are both weak.

ʿAṭāʾ ibn ʿAjlān, from whom Mubārak and others narrate: his hadith is not to be written down.

ʿĪsā ibn Sinān: his hadith is soft.

Muʿān ibn Rifāʿa has soft hadith.

And ʿImrān ibn Abī al-Faḍl, from whom Ismāʿīl narrates: his hadith is worthless.

Isḥāq ibn Najīḥ al-Malṭī: his hadith is not to be written down.

Yazīd ibn Bazīʿ al-Ramlī is weak.

Suwayd ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz was judge over Damascus; his hadith is weak.

Abū Farwa Yazīd ibn Sinān al-Jazarī is weak.

Abū al-Muʿāfā Muḥammad ibn Wahb ibn ʿUmar ibn Abī Kurayma, a client of Banū Umayya in Kafr Jadā, related to us: Muḥammad ibn Salama al-Qaysī related to us, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥīm Khālid ibn Abī Yazīd. Abū al-Muʿāfā related to us—he was the son of my grandfather ʿUmar ibn Abī Kurayma’s paternal uncle, and he was the maternal aunt’s son of Muḥammad ibn Salama—: Zayd ibn Abī Unaysa al-Jazarī related to me.

Khālid ibn Abī Yazīd is acceptable. “Zayd ibn Abī Unaysa is trustworthy,” and his hadith is good. “Yaḥyā ibn Abī Unaysa, Zayd’s brother, is weak; his hadith should be written down only for purposes of identification.”

“Marwān ibn Shujāʿ is from al-Jazīra. Aḥmad ibn al-Khalīl al-Baghdādī related from him to me, and he is trustworthy.”

“ʿAfīf ibn Sālim al-Mawṣilī is trustworthy,” and Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmmār al-Mawṣilī related from him to me.

“Muḥammad ibn ʿAmmār is trustworthy,” and Ayyūb related from him to me, from Muḥammad ibn Ziyād al-Wazzān al-Barqī, who is a shaykh and is acceptable.

“Al-Mughīra ibn Ziyād al-Mawṣilī is trustworthy.” Abū ʿĀṣim al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Makhlad related from him to me.

“ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Zabr, Abū Zabr, is trustworthy and a Damascene. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm praised him and said that he was trustworthy.”

Al-Naḍr ibn ʿAdī is trustworthy. Abū Ṣāliḥ al-Ḥarrānī and Yaḥyā ibn Ṣāliḥ related from him to me.

ʿImrān ibn Abī Qays is trustworthy.

Al-Nuʿmān ibn Rāshid is acceptable.

“Sūwayd ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz is of concealed standing, and there is some weakness in his hadith.” Sulaymān ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Dimashqī related from him to us, and Sulaymān is trustworthy.

Aḥmad ibn Yūnus related from ʿUmar ibn Rāshid to us, and there is some weakness in his hadith.

“Yaḥyā ibn Yaḥyā al-Ghassānī is trustworthy.” Ibrāhīm related from him to us; he is firmly reliable. As for Yaḥyā and Hishām, Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna heard from both of them. Sufyān also heard from Yazīd ibn Jābir. “Yazīd and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd ibn Jābir are two trustworthy men of Azd. They had settled in Baṣra, then moved to Damascus.” ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd ibn Jābir related from Yazīd ibn Yazīd ibn Jābir, from Makḥūl, from Abū Hurayra, concerning the screen of the person praying. Hishām ibn ʿAmmār related this to me, from Ṣadaqa ibn Khālid.

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd ibn Jābir was older than Yazīd, and Yazīd ibn Jābir outlived him and was the older of the two.

“Muḥammad ibn Muslim ibn Abī al-Waḍḍāḥ was Mūsā’s tutor before he became caliph, and he is trustworthy.”

Al-Walīd ibn Abī Mālik related from Abū ʿUbayd Allāh, from Abū Hurayra:

“The screen of the person praying is like the rear pommel of a saddle, in a size like the leather of a whip.” Abū Nuʿaym related this to us, from Misʿar, from al-Walīd. Al-Walīd is a trustworthy Syrian.

“Yazīd ibn Abī Mālik was a Syrian and served as a judge; there is some weakness in the hadith of him and his son Khālid ibn Yazīd ibn Abī Mālik.”

“Abū ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mishkam, a companion of Muʿādh, is trustworthy.”

Khālid ibn Yazīd ibn Ṣāliḥ ibn Ṣubayḥ was a Medinan Damascene; al-Walīd ibn Muslim relates from him.

Ibrāhīm ibn Adham was an Arab. He used to reside in Khurāsān, then moved to al-Layth.

Abū Yūsuf said: Abū ʿAdī al-ʿAsqalānī told me that he had campaigned with Ibrāhīm, “who is among the best and most virtuous.”

“Al-Muqriʾ related to us: Ḥaywa ibn Shurayḥ related to us. He was a noble, trustworthy, upright and esteemed man of Kinda. He was known by the kunya Abū Zurʿa, and died in the year 158.”

He said: Abū Hānīʾ Ḥumayd ibn Hānīʾ, a man of Khawlān, informed me that he had heard ʿAmr ibn Ḥurayth. This man was an Egyptian who had no hearing [from the Prophet], no transmissions, and no association [with him]. He is not ʿAmr ibn Ḥurayth al-Makhzūmī, a Kūfan who has transmitted reports.

“Abū Nuʿaym related to us. He said: Jaʿfar ibn Burqān related to us. He was from al-Jazīra, trustworthy. It reached me that he was illiterate, unable to read or write, and that he was among the best.”

Abū Marḥūm ʿAbd al-Raḥīm ibn Maymūn was an Egyptian. He relates from Sahl ibn Muʿādh ibn Anas al-Juhanī, from his father, that the Prophet ﷺ—said: “Whoever gives up fine clothing, despite being able to afford it, out of humility toward God, God will summon him on the Day of Resurrection before all creation and let him choose from among the garments of faith whatever clothes he wishes to wear.” Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, who is Ibn Nawfal ibn Furāt, related this to us. Abū Salama Sulaymān ibn Sulaym was a Ḥimṣī, “trustworthy,” and his hadith is good.

Abū Maʿbad Ḥafṣ ibn Ghaylān al-Ruʿaynī relates from Makḥūl.

Al-Qāsim, Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, the client of the family of Muʿāwiya, is trustworthy.

Ādam related to us. He said: Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAyyāsh related to us. He said: Sharḥabīl ibn Muslim related to me. He is one of the trustworthy people of Syria, and his hadith is good.

Saʿīd ibn Asad related to me. He said: Ḍamra related to us, from Ibrāhīm ibn Abī ʿAbla, who is trustworthy.

Hishām related to us: Ṣadaqa ibn Khālid related to us, from ʿUtba ibn Abī Ḥakīm, who is trustworthy.

Ādam related to us. He said: Baqiyya related to us, from Muḥammad ibn Ziyād al-Alhānī, who is trustworthy.

Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Muqriʾ related to us. He said: Mūsā ibn Ayyūb al-Ghāfiqī related to us; he is trustworthy.

Abū Sulaymān Ayyūb ibn Muḥammad ibn Ziyād said: Maʿmar ibn Sulaymān al-Barqī related to us. He is trustworthy, and he related from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bishr, a Kūfan who moved to al-Jazīra.

Abū ʿAbd Allāh Marzūq was a Syrian who settled in Baṣra. The shaykhs of Baṣra related from him, and he is trustworthy.

Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAyyāsh related from Muḥammad ibn Dirham, a Syrian who is acceptable.

“Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us. He said: Muʿāwiya ibn Ṣāliḥ related to me, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa, a Syrian. Shuʿba and Ḥammād ibn Zayd related from Budayl ibn Maysara, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa, a Syrian. He was known by the kunya Abū Ṭalḥa. He is weak in hadith, his reports are objectionable, and his doctrine is not praiseworthy.”

“Khulayʿ ibn Daʿlaj was originally from Baṣra, then moved to Syria. He is more estimable than Saʿīd ibn Bashīr.”

Ibn ʿUthmān related to us, from ʿAbd Allāh, from al-Awzāʿī, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Malik, who is Ibn Marwān and was killed at the River of Abū Fuṭrus.

“[He] said: Abū al-ʿAbbās Hishām ibn al-Ghāz, ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-ʿAlāʾ Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥīm, Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Shuʿaythī, and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Thābit ibn Thawbān.

Some of them transmitted [reports], and some came to Baghdad; our companions wrote from him in Baghdad.”

Ibn Abī Maryam related to us, from Yaḥyā ibn Ayyūb, from al-Walīd ibn Ubayy. Al-Walīd is an Egyptian and trustworthy.

“Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us, from Muʿāwiya ibn Ṣāliḥ, from al-ʿAlāʾ ibn al-Ḥārith, who is trustworthy.”

Ādam related to us. He said: Hushaym related to us, from Zakariyyā ibn Ḥakīm, who is a Syrian.

Abū ʿĀṣim related to us, from ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn Jaʿfar, a Medinan Anṣārī, trustworthy. Though Sufyān criticized him, he is trustworthy and his hadith is good. [He related] from Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb, Abū Rajāʾ, from Abū al-Khayr Marthad ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Yazanī, a virtuous and good man, who had standing among his troops, an ascetic, a worshipper, trustworthy.

Mūsā ibn Wardān. “Abū al-Aswad—an Egyptian—related to us, from Ibn Lahīʿa, from Mūsā ibn Wardān. He was virtuous and acceptable.”

Abū al-Aswad related to us, from Ibn Lahīʿa, from Abū ʿUqayl Zahra ibn Maʿbad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Hishām al-Qurashī, then al-Taymī, from his grandfather, who said: “We were with the Messenger of God ﷺ.” He is trustworthy.

Abū Umayya ʿAmr ibn Hishām al-Ḥarrānī, trustworthy, related to us from “Makhlad ibn Yazīd al-Ḥarrānī, who is trustworthy.”

Abū al-Walīd related to us. He said: Al-Layth ibn Saʿd related to me, from Abū Shujāʿ Saʿīd ibn Yazīd, who is trustworthy.

“Hishām related to us. He said: Ṣadaqa ibn Khālid related to us. He said: Abū al-ʿAbbās Hishām ibn al-Ghāz al-Jurashī related to us; he is trustworthy.”

Hishām related to us. He said: Yaḥyā ibn Ḥamza related to me. He served as a judge over Damascus.

He is trustworthy.

Khuṣayf related from Abū Hishām Saʿd al-Sanjārī.

“Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us. He said: Al-Hiql ibn Ziyād al-Bayrūtī related to me. He is trustworthy, one of the trustworthy men, and the foremost of al-Awzāʿī’s companions.”

Ibn ʿUthmān related to us. ʿAbd Allāh related to us. He said: Ibn ʿUlātha informed us. They were three brothers. Maʿmar related from the eldest of them, and Ḥafṣ ibn Ghiyāth related from the judge among them in Baghdad.

Ādam related to us. He said: Baqiyya related to us, from Bashīr ibn Ṭalḥa.

He said: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz related to me. Bashīr ibn Ṭalḥa related to us; he used to live in al-Ḥalba, in the district of ʿAsqalān.

ʿAbd al-Wahhāb ibn Bukht was a Syrian who settled in Medina, “trustworthy.”

Qurra ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ḥaywil is counted among the Egyptians. He was a Maʿāfirī and trustworthy.

“I heard the shaykhs of Egypt say: When Hishām ibn ʿAbd al-Malik had his ṣāʿ and mudd made, he sent them to Egypt. The ṣāʿ was brought into the mosque, and they carried it around to the circles in the mosque. When they brought it to Ḥaywil’s circle, he took it, struck it against the ground, and broke it. The report was conveyed to Hishām. He said: ‘Be quiet, and do not speak of it.’ They said:

When it was the caliphate of the Banū Hāshim, a delegation came from Egypt, and Qurra was among them. They said:

‘This is so-and-so, and this is Ibn Ḥaywil, the breaker of the ṣāʿ.’ They said: Abū Jaʿfar asked him, ‘Would you break a mudd for us?’ He replied, ‘Commander of the Faithful, if our dead are brought back to life, I will break the sealed measure and the ṣāʿ.’”

Abū al-Muʾammil, from whom Shuʿba related, was a Syrian.

Ṣafwān ibn Ṣāliḥ related to me. He said: Zayd ibn Abī al-Zarqāʾ al-Mawṣilī related to us; he is trustworthy.

Al-Aḥwaṣ ibn Ḥakīm was related from by Ibn ʿUyayna and others. They claimed he was “a devout and assiduous man, but his hadith is not strong.”

Yaḥyā ibn al-Ḥārith al-Dhimārī was related from by the people of Syria. He was a Syrian, “and is acceptable.”

“Ḥakīm ibn Nāfiʿ was from al-Raqqah; there is no objection to him.”

Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr related to us: Miskīn ibn Maymūn, the muezzin of the mosque of al-Ramlah, related to us. There is no objection to him. We ourselves heard from his son, and there was no objection to him.

“Saʿīd ibn Abī Maryam and ʿAmr ibn Ṭāriq related to me, from Ibn Lahīʿah, from Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb, from Yaḥnas ibn Ẓabyān, who reported that he heard ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ḥassān say: ‘A man from Judhām told me that he heard Ibn ʿAtāhiyah, whose name was Mālik, say: “I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: [When you see a tax collector, kill him.]”’”

Ibn Bukayr related to us, saying: Mālik ibn ʿAtāhiyah said: “The Messenger of God ﷺ said”—they say, “I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ”—then he made a circle with his forefinger and thumb and blew. Ibn Ramḥ said: “He heard nothing from the Prophet ﷺ.”

Abū Nuʿaym related to us: Sufyān related to us, from Sālim al-Afṭas, who is Ibn ʿAjlān, and he is displeasing.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yūsuf related to us, saying: al-Ḥakam ibn Hishām related to us. He was a Thaqafī from the family of Abū ʿUqayl, a Syrian.

Abū ʿUthmān Muslim ibn Bashshār related to us. This man was Egyptian; [there was also] Muslim ibn Bashshār al-Baṣrī.

Jābir ibn Yazīd ibn Rifāʿah was from Mosul. Our companions related to us from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from him.

ʿAlī ibn Maʿbad ibn Shaddād related to us. He used to live in Egypt and was one of the early abnāʾ.

Abū Ẓabyah was a Kalāʿī, a Syrian; he related traditions from Muʿādh ibn Jabal.

Abū Sālim al-Jayshānī was Egyptian.

Saʿīd ibn Abī Ayyūb related to us, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Abī Jaʿfar, from Sālim ibn Abī Sālim al-Jayshānī, from his father, from Abū Dharr, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Abū Dharr, I see that you are weak, and I wish for you what I wish for myself. Do not take authority over two people, and do not administer an orphan’s property.”

Abū Sālim was Sufyān ibn Hāniʾ.

I heard Ibn Wahb say: “Ḥaywah held among us the position that Ibn ʿAwn holds among you. He was dutiful to his parents. He said: He kept company with ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ and his generation, but did not speak freely about knowledge until his parents died; then he spoke freely.”

“I heard ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm Duḥaym relate to us: al-Walīd related to us, saying: ‘When al-Awzāʿī related traditions to us, he would say: “Yaḥyā related to us,” then he would say, “So-and-so related to us,” and continue until he reached the end of the chain.’ Al-Walīd said: ‘Sometimes I related it as he had related it to me, and sometimes I said “from, from, from,” to lighten the chains of reports.’”

“Duḥaym ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm—their judge in Damascus—related to us (144a): al-Walīd related to us; al-Awzāʿī related to us; al-Walīd ibn Hishām al-Muʿayṭī related to me—and he is trustworthy and upright.”

Maʿdān ibn Ṭalḥah al-Yaʿmurī related to me, saying: “I met Thawbān”—the people of Baṣrah disagree about him: some say Maʿdān ibn Ṭalḥah, and some say Ibn Abī Ṭalḥah.

“This is a good chain of transmission.” Maʿdān said: “Then I met Abū al-Dardāʾ and asked him, and he told me the same”—meaning the report of Thawbān.

He said: Al-Awzāʿī related to us, saying: Ḥassān ibn ʿAṭiyyah related to me, saying: Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿĀʾishah related to me, saying: “I heard Abū Hurayrah.” This is a good chain of transmission, and its transmitters are trustworthy.

He said: Al-Walīd related to us, saying: Al-Awzāʿī related to us; “ʿUmayr ibn Hāniʾ, Abū al-Walīd, related to me, and there is no objection to ʿUmayr.”

Junādah ibn Abī Umayyah related to me from ʿUbādah ibn al-Ṣāmit. The route of Maʿdān’s report is stronger than this route, though this one too is unobjectionable.

He said: Al-Walīd related to us; al-Awzāʿī related to us, saying: Ḥassān ibn ʿAṭiyyah related to us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Sābiṭ, a trustworthy Jumahī, from ʿAmr ibn Maymūn al-Awdī, who said:

“Muʿādh ibn Jabal came to us in Yemen as the Messenger of the Messenger of God ﷺ to us.

“I heard a man with a hoarse voice proclaim the takbīr at dawn. I offered him my greeting and never parted from him until I buried him, dead, in Syria. Then I looked for the most learned person among the people, and went to Ibn Masʿūd and stayed with him until he died.”

Abū Yūsuf said: “This is the finest and clearest chain of transmission there could be.”

Al-Awzāʿī said: Abū al-Najāshī related to me; he was a client of Nāfiʿ ibn Khadīj, trustworthy.

Al-Awzāʿī [transmitted] from Isḥāq ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Ṭalḥah, who was trustworthy. Al-Awzāʿī heard from him in al-Yamāmah; he was in charge of the ṣawāfī and estates.

Al-Awzāʿī [transmitted] from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, who was trustworthy and had collected his traditions. He was originally from Baṣrah, but moved away from there because of Qatādah, who used to harass him. He was a perfumer in Hajar, in al-Yamāmah: a man of fine character, trustworthy. He transmitted from Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿĀʾishah (144b), and from Abū Hurayrah. Yaḥyā transmitted from Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm ibn al-Ḥārith al-Taymī, a trustworthy Medinan, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Thawbān, who was trustworthy; his traditions are sound, and the traditions of Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm are accepted as proof. Abū Salamah heard from Rabīʿah ibn Kaʿb al-Aslamī, a Companion of the Prophet ﷺ. Yaḥyā heard from ʿAmr ibn Umayyah al-Ḍamrī, a Companion of the Prophet ﷺ. Abū Salamah heard from Hilāl ibn Abī Maymūnah. Mālik ibn Anas transmitted from Hilāl, as did Fulayḥ ibn Sulaymān. Hilāl was trustworthy, with good traditions; he transmitted fine traditions from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār, and his traditions are accepted as proof. Yaḥyā transmitted from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Qatādah fine, foundational traditions, and his traditions are accepted as proof. Yaḥyā also transmitted from Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm, who said: “Shaqīq ibn Salamah related to me, saying: …”

Ḥumrān. This is how al-Walīd ibn Muslim transmitted it. Al-Hiql and Ibn Abī al-ʿIshrīn, the scribe of al-Awzāʿī and al-Walīd ibn Mazīd, said: “Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm related to me, saying: ʿĪsā ibn Ṭalḥah related to me, saying: ‘Ḥumrān, the client of ʿUthmān, related to me.’”

Abū Yūsuf said: “I asked ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm: ‘Does al-Walīd differ regarding Shaqīq?’ He said: ‘Yes.’ I asked: ‘Which do you think is more correct?’ He said: ‘Those who said it was from ʿĪsā ibn Ṭalḥah.’”

Ibn Salamah transmits: “Muʿayqīb related to me”—he was a Companion. Yaḥyā said: “Qurrah ibn Abī Qurrah related to me that Abū Usayd told him he heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: ‘There is no prayer after the afternoon prayer until the sun sets.’” Qurrah was a trustworthy Medinan.

He said: Abū Qilābah said: “Abū al-Muhājir, who was his paternal uncle, related to me.” This is an error. It is related that the report came from al-Awzāʿī; rather, it is from Abū al-Muhallab. This is how the people of Iraq transmitted it, and this is the correct version.

Yaḥyā transmits, saying: Abū Qilābah related to me, saying: Abū Umayyah related to me—or a man related it from Abū Umayyah. The transmission of this report is inconsistent. He said: “I came to the Messenger of God ﷺ (145a) from a journey. He said: ‘Will you not wait for lunch, Abū Umayyah?’ I said: ‘I am fasting.’ He said: ‘Come, let me tell you about the traveller: God has exempted him from fasting and half the prayer.’”

Mūsā ibn Ismāʿīl related to me, saying: Abān related to us, saying: Yaḥyā related to us, from Abū Qilābah, from Abū Umayyah.

Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us, saying: Muʿāwiyah ibn Ṣāliḥ related to us, saying that ʿIṣām ibn Yaḥyā had related to him, from Abū Qilābah, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Ziyādah, from Abū Umayyah, the brother of Banū Jaʿdah, who said: “The Messenger of God ﷺ was having lunch on a journey, and I was sitting nearby. He said: ‘Come to lunch.’ I said: ‘I am fasting.’ He said: ‘Come, let me tell you what applies to the traveller: God has exempted my community from half the prayer and from fasting while travelling.’”

Ādam related to us: Shuʿbah related to us: Ayyūb al-Sakhtiyānī related to us, from a man of Banū ʿĀmir, from a man of his people, who said: “I came to the Prophet ﷺ while he was eating— “—or, he said, having lunch—so he said: ‘Come near, or get down, and eat.’ I said: ‘I am fasting.’ The Messenger of God ﷺ said: ‘And half the prayer is waived for a pregnant woman.’”

Qabīṣah related to us: Sufyān related to us, from Ayyūb, from Abū Qilābah, from Anas, who said: “I came to the Prophet ﷺ while he was having lunch. He said: ‘Come, let me tell you: God has exempted the traveller, the pregnant woman, and the nursing woman from fasting and half the prayer.’”

Al-Muʿallā ibn Asad related to us, saying: Wuhayb related to us, from Ayyūb, from Abū Qilābah, from a man of Banū ʿĀmir. Ayyūb said: “I met him and asked him, and he related to me from a man of his people that he had come to Medina in search of camels belonging to him. He entered to see the Prophet ﷺ and found him having lunch. He said to him: ‘Come to lunch.’ The man said: ‘I am fasting.’ The Prophet ﷺ said to him: ‘Fasting has been waived for the traveller, along with half the prayer; and for the pregnant woman or nursing woman.’”

Al-Ḥajjāj related to us: Ḥammād related to us, from al-Jarīrī, from Abū al-ʿAlāʾ, from a man of his people, that he came to the Prophet ﷺ while he was eating. He said to him: “Come and eat.” The man said: “I am fasting.” (145b) He said: “Come near, so I can tell you about fasting: God has waived half the prayer for the traveller, and fasting for the pregnant woman and nursing woman.”

Al-Ḥajjāj related to us: Ḥammād related to us, from Ayyūb, from Abū Qilābah, from that man from Banū ʿĀmir, from the Prophet ﷺ with a report like it.

Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr related to us, saying: Hushaym related to us, saying: Khālid informed us, from Abū Qilābah and Yazīd ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Shikhkhīr, from a man of Banū ʿĀmir, that a man of theirs came to the Prophet ﷺ riding a young camel. He entered to see the Messenger of God ﷺ and found him having lunch. He said: “Come.” The man said: “I am fasting.”

He said: “Come, let me tell you about fasting.” In Abū Qilābah’s report, he said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “God has waived fasting and half the prayer for the traveller, and [fasting] for the pregnant woman and nursing woman.” Yazīd ibn ʿAbd Allāh’s report says: “Fasting and half the prayer have been waived for the traveller, and [fasting] for the pregnant woman and nursing woman.”

Al-ʿAbbās ibn al-Walīd ibn Mazīd related to me, saying: My father informed me, saying: al-Awzāʿī related to us], saying: Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr related to me, saying: Abū Qilābah al-Jarmī related to me, saying: Abū Umayyah or Abū al-Muhājir related to me, from Abū Umayyah, who said: “I came to the Messenger of God ﷺ and he said: ‘Will you not wait for lunch?’ I said: ‘I am fasting.’ He said: ‘Come, let me tell you about the traveller: God has waived fasting and half the prayer for him …’” half the prayer.

Abū Nuʿaym and Abū ʿUmar al-Namarī related to us: Abū Hilāl related to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sawādah, from Anas ibn Mālik—a man of Banū ʿAbd Allāh ibn Kaʿb—who said: “The cavalry of the Messenger of God ﷺ raided us. I set out for the Prophet ﷺ and came to the Messenger of God ﷺ while he was eating. He said: ‘Come near and have some of this food.’ He said: ‘Sit down, and I will tell you about prayer or fasting: God has waived half the prayer for the traveller (146a), and has waived fasting—or the fast—for the traveller, and for the pregnant woman and nursing woman.’ He said: ‘By God, he said both of them, or one of them. Alas, I wish I had eaten some of the food of the Messenger of God ﷺ.’”

Muslim ibn Ibrāhīm and al-Muʿallā ibn Asad related to us, both saying: Wuhayb related to us: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sawādah al-Qushayrī related to us, from his father, from Anas ibn Mālik—[who said of] a man of their people—that he came to the Prophet ﷺ in Medina while the Prophet ﷺ was having lunch. The Prophet ﷺ said: “Come to lunch.” He said: “I replied: ‘Prophet of God, I am fasting.’” The Prophet ﷺ said: “God has waived fasting and half the prayer for the traveller, and [fasting] for the pregnant woman or nursing woman.”

This is Muslim’s wording. Al-Muʿallā’s wording, from Anas ibn Mālik—a man of their people—says: “His camels were stolen, so he came to Medina in search of them. He entered to see the Prophet ﷺ and found him having lunch. He said to him: …”

“Come to the midday meal.” He said, “I am fasting.” He said, “Fasting has been waived for the traveller, as has half of the prayer, and for the pregnant woman or nursing mother.” Al-Awzāʿī, from Yaḥyā, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Miqsam, a Medinan, reliable.

Al-Awzāʿī relates from Hind, from Barīm, a Syrian.

Al-Awzāʿī, from Mughīth ibn Sumayy, an al-Awzāʿī and Syrian, reliable.

Al-Awzāʿī relates from al-Muṭṭalib ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥanṭab al-Makhzūmī, reliable.

And Yaḥyā relates from ʿIyāḍ ibn Abī Zuhayr, a Medinan, reliable.

Al-Awzāʿī related from Abū ʿUbayd al-Ḥājib—Mālik related from him, and he is reliable—from ʿUqbah ibn Wassāj, who is reliable.

Al-Awzāʿī related from ʿUthmān ibn Abī Sawdah, reliable.

He related from Shaddād Abū ʿAmmār, reliable, from whom al-Nahhās ibn Fahm.

Yaḥyā related from Rabīʿah ibn Yazīd, a Syrian, reliable.

Al-Awzāʿī related from Ismāʿīl ibn ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Abī al-Muhājir (146b), a Makhzūmī, Syrian, reliable.

Al-Awzāʿī related from a shaykh of his called Ḥiṣn: “I know of no one who related from him except al-Awzāʿī.”

Al-Awzāʿī related, saying: “Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Fāṭimah related to me: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib related to me, saying: Ibn ʿAbbās related to me.”

Al-Awzāʿī related from Hārūn ibn Riyāb al-Asadī al-Baṣrī, reliable.

He related from a shaykh called Usayd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, a Syrian, reliable.

He said: “ʿAmr ibn al-Walīd, reliable, related to me.”

He related from Ibrāhīm ibn Qāriẓ, from al-Sāʾib ibn Yazīd, reliable.

Al-Awzāʿī said: “Qatādah said: Yazīd al-Raqāshī, whose reports are weak, related to me.”

Al-Awzāʿī, from Ibn Surāqah, a Syrian, reliable.

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm related to us, saying: al-Walīd related to us, saying: al-Awzāʿī related to us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Arqam, who said: “I entered upon ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb while he was standing in prayer at midday. I stood to his left, so he took my hand and placed me at his right. Then Yarfaʾ, ʿUmar’s chamberlain, came, and ʿUmar stepped forward; we formed rows behind him.”

Such is the transmission from al-Awzāʿī.

Hiql, al-Walīd ibn Mazīd, and Ibn al-Mubārak said: “From ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Arqam.”

Ibn Qanʿab and Ibn Bukayr related to us, from Mālik, from Ibn Shihāb, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtbah, from his father, who said: “I entered upon ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb at midday and found him performing voluntary prayer. I stood behind him, and he drew me close until he placed me at his right. When Yarfaʾ came, I stepped back, and we formed rows behind him.” Ibn ʿUyaynah, Shuʿayb, Maʿmar, Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥafṣah, Yūnus, and ʿUqayl concurred with Mālik. They said: “From ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from his father.” This is the established version, God willing.

Al-ʿAbbās ibn al-Walīd related to me, saying: “My father related to me, saying: al-Awzāʿī related to us: Muḥammad ibn Abī Kathīr related to me: Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān related to me: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd al-Qārī related to us…”

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd al-Qārī said: (147a) “I entered upon ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb while he was praying at midday. He prayed four rakʿahs, then turned away and said: ‘I hope this is counted as part of the night prayer, or as its equivalent.’”

Abū Nuʿaym related to us, saying: Hishām related to us, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, from Abū Salamah, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, that he entered upon ʿUmar. They said that Abū Nuʿaym used to say: “From ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, that he entered upon ʿUmar.” It was said to him: “It is ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd al-Qārī.” He then said: “From ʿAbd al-Raḥmān,” and thereafter did not give his lineage.

Ibn Qanʿab and Ibn Bukayr related to us, from Mālik, from Dāwūd ibn al-Ḥuṣayn, from al-Aʿraj, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd al-Qārī, that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said: “If someone misses his portion of the night prayer, then recites it from the sun’s decline until the noon prayer, it is as though he did not miss it—or as though he caught up with it.”

Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us, saying: al-Layth related to me, saying: Yūnus related to us, from Ibn Shihāb, who said: “Al-Sāʾib ibn Yazīd and ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtbah informed me that ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd said: ‘I heard ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb say: The Messenger of God ﷺ—used to say: “Whoever sleeps through his portion of prayer, or some of it, and recites it between the dawn prayer and the noon prayer, it will be recorded for him as though he had recited it during the night.”’”

Ādam ibn Abī Iyās and ʿĀṣim ibn ʿAlī related to us, saying: Ibn Abī Dhiʾb related to us, saying: al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān related to us, saying: “I was with Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān…”

…when a son of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṭahfah al-Ghifārī came to us. Abū Salamah said to him: “Did your father relate this to you?” He said: “Yes. My father related to me, saying: ‘When guests gathered with the Messenger of God ﷺ—he would say: “Let each man go back with his companion.” I was among those who went back with the Messenger of God ﷺ. When he entered, he said: “ʿĀʾishah, is there anything?” She said: “Yes, a little dish I had prepared for you to break your fast with.” The Prophet ﷺ—said: “Bring it to me.” She brought it, and the Messenger of God ﷺ—said (147b): “Eat, in the name of God.” By God, we ate from it until it could no longer be seen. Then he said: “Do you have a drink?” She said: “Yes, a little milk I had prepared for you to break your fast with.” He said: “Bring it to me.” She brought it, and he said: “Drink, in the name of God.” By God, we drank until it could no longer be seen.

“Then I went out and lay face down in the mosque. The Messenger of God ﷺ—went out for the dawn prayer and woke his family for the dawn prayer. Whenever he went out to wake his family, he would say: ‘The prayer!’ He saw me lying face down and said: ‘Who is this?’ I said:

“‘I am ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṭahfah.’ He said: ‘This is a way of lying that God dislikes.’” This is Ādam’s wording.

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm and Ṣafwān related to us, saying: al-Walīd related to us, saying:

“Al-Awzāʿī related to us: Yaḥyā related to me, from Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm, from Ibn Qays ibn Ṭahfah…”

…Ṭahfah al-Ghifārī, from his father.

He said: “Al-ʿAbbās ibn al-Walīd ibn Mazīd related to me, saying: My father informed me: al-Awzāʿī related to us, saying: Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr related to us, from Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm al-Taymī, who said:

“‘A son of Qays ibn Ṭakhfah al-Ghifārī related to me, from his father—who was among the people of the Ṣuffah—who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ—would come to us after sunset prayer and say: “So-and-so, go with so-and-so.”’”

[Ibn] ʿUthmān related to us, saying: ʿAbd Allāh related to us, saying: Hishām al-Dastawāʾī informed us, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, from Abū Salamah, from Yaʿīsh ibn Ṭaghfah al-Ghifārī, who said: “My father was among the people of the Ṣuffah. The Prophet ﷺ—gave them instructions, and each man would go off with two men.”

Saʿīd ibn Yaḥyā al-Umawī related to me, saying: my father related to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq related to us, from Muḥammad [ibn] ʿAmr ibn ʿAṭāʾ, from Ṭahfah al-Ghifārī and Nuʿaym al-Mujmir, who both said that Ṭaghfah related to them: “I was a guest of the Messenger of God ﷺ—among the poor whom he hosted. When it was the middle of the night…”

He said: “ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Ziyād related to me, saying: Khālid ibn Makhlad related to us, from ʿAbd al-Salām ibn Ḥafṣ (148a), from Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr ibn Ḥalḥalah al-Duʾalī, from Nuʿaym ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Mujmir, from Abū Ṭakhfah al-Duʾalī, from his father, who said: ‘The Messenger of God ﷺ—came out while I was lying on my stomach. He said: “This is the way the people of Hell lie.”’”

Al-Awzāʿī related from Ghaylān ibn Anas, a Syrian of Kalb, who had seen ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz.

Al-ʿAbbās ibn al-Walīd ibn Mazīd related to us, saying: “My father informed me, saying: Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz related to us: Abū Muslim al-Khawlānī died in the land of the Byzantines, during Busr’s campaign, in the caliphate of Muʿāwiyah. He said to Busr ibn Arṭāʾah—who was an evil man, though many people of Syria claim that he was a Companion, which is false: ‘Put me in command of the Muslims with you, and make my grave the farthest of the graves, for I hope to come on the Day of Resurrection bearing their banner.’”

Al-ʿAbbās related to me, saying: “My father related to me, saying: al-Awzāʿī related to us: Sālim…”

…ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Muḥāribī, a Syrian, reliable.

Al-Awzāʿī said: “Abū ʿUrwah al-Qāsim ibn Mukhaymirah used to say: ‘When I shut my door, my concerns do not go beyond it.’”

He said: “I heard him when I was still a boy, not yet mature. A funeral procession passed, followed by women, and he said:

“‘I would not wish to have their rewards in exchange for my sandal.’”

Al-ʿAbbās related to me, saying: “My father informed me, saying: al-Awzāʿī related to us: Dāwūd ibn ʿAlī related to me that he heard al-Ḥasan ibn Abī al-Ḥasan say: ‘While the Messenger of God ﷺ—was addressing the people on Friday, a shawsh of clarified butter arrived. The people began rising and going toward it until only a few remained. The Messenger of God ﷺ—said: “Had you continued, the valley would have been set ablaze over you.”’”

Al-ʿAbbās related to me, saying: “My father informed me, saying: I heard al-Awzāʿī say: ‘Muʿāwiyah ibn Abī Sufyān was the first to explain to the people why he sat during the first sermon on Friday. He did so only because of his advanced age and weakness.’”

He said: “ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Marwān was the first to raise his hands on Friday and perform the qunūt in it.”

He said: “Al-Muṣʿab ibn al-Zubayr was the first to introduce the three takbīrs after sunset and dawn prayers, and Hishām ibn (148b) Ismāʿīl was the first to gather the people at…”

…at al-Dirāsimah.

He said: “ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz used to sit during the first sermon.”

Al-Walīd ibn ʿUtbah al-Dimashqī and Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm related to us, saying: Baqiyyah ibn al-Walīd related to us, saying: Ḥiṣn ibn Mālik al-Fazārī related to me, saying: “I heard a shaykh, known by the kunya Abū Muḥammad—he was an old man—relate from Ḥudhayfah ibn al-Yamān, from the Messenger of God ﷺ—that he said: ‘Recite the Qurʾān in the modes and voices of the Arabs. Beware the mode of the openly sinful and the people of the markets, for after me a people will come who will modulate the Qurʾān with the modulation of singing, monastic chanting, and lamentation. It will not pass beyond their throats; their hearts will be ensnared, as will the hearts of those who admire their conduct.’” Baqiyyah said: “He has only one hadith, and he is from Ifrīqiyah.”

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm related to me, saying: al-Walīd related to us, saying: Ḥuṣayn ibn al-Walīd, client of Banū Yazīd, related to us, saying: al-Azhar ibn al-Walīd al-Ḥimṣī related to me, saying: “I heard Umm al-Dardāʾ in Bayt al-Maqdis relating: ‘Some people of this community will surely disbelieve after their faith.’”

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm related to me, saying: al-Walīd related to us, saying: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yazīd ibn Abī Muslim al-Thaqafī related to us, from his father, who said: “Al-Ḥajjāj was ʿAbd al-Malik’s governor over Mecca when he wrote to him appointing him governor over Iraq. He set out, and I set out with him among a party of eight or nine, riding alongside him. When we were near al-Kūfah…”

…he dismounted, dyed his hair with henna, and made ready. That was on a Friday. Then he set out, wearing a turban with its tail hanging between his shoulders and a sword at his side, until he dismounted by the governor’s residence beside the mosque of al-Kūfah. The caller had already given the first call to prayer for Friday prayer. Al-Ḥajjāj came out to them while they did not know who he was, and he led them in prayer. Then he ascended the pulpit and sat upon it. He fell silent while they craned their necks toward him, knelt down, and picked up pebbles to throw at him and drive him out. They had previously stoned a governor until he left them. He said:

“He fell silent for a moment, stunning them with it, and they wished to hear what he would say. The first words of his speech were: ‘People of Iraq, people of discord, and people of (149a) hypocrisy! By God, your affairs concerned me before I came to you. But I used to pray to God to test you through me and to test me through you, and He answered my prayer. Know that last night I rode out, and my whip fell from me, so I took this”—and he pointed his sword at them—“in its place. By God, I shall drag it through you as a woman drags her train, and I shall do this and that.’”

Yazīd said: “Then I saw the pebbles fall from their hands.” He said: “Stand up and give your pledge of allegiance.” The tribes rose, one tribe at a time, to pledge allegiance. He would ask, “Who are you?” They would answer, “The Banū So-and-so.” This continued until a tribe came to him. He said, “And who are you?” They said, “The Nakhaʿ.” He said, “Is Kumayl ibn Ziyād among you?” They said, “Yes.” He said, “What has happened to him?” They said, “Commander, he is an old man.” He said: “You will have no pledge of allegiance from me, nor77 until you bring him to me.” He said:

“They brought him to him, carried on a bier, and placed him beside the pulpit. He said: ‘Know that of those who entered the house against ʿUthmān, none remains but this man.’ Then he called for a hide and struck off his head.”

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān related to me, saying: al-Walīd related to us, saying: ʿUbayd Allāh related to me, saying: “I entered upon al-Ḥajjāj. He gestured with his hand, and I said: ‘ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Yazīd ibn Abī Muslim al-Thaqafī.’ He said:

“‘We have assigned you a stipend of such-and-such.’ ʿUbayd Allāh said: ‘When al-Ḥajjāj died, during the remainder…’”

During al-Walīd’s caliphate, Yazīd ibn Abī Muslim took charge of Iraq for four months. When al-Walīd died and Sulaymān became caliph, he dismissed him and appointed Yazīd ibn al-Muhallab over Iraq. He had him brought to Sulaymān, who was at al-Balqāʾ. Sulaymān presented him before the people, but no one came forward to say anything against him—except that a man from Medina reported that Yazīd had once slapped him in Iraq. The man demanded legal retaliation, and Yazīd submitted to it. The man slapped him once, making his eye turn green. When Sulaymān saw that no one else was pursuing a claim of injustice against him, he brought Yazīd in and began asking him about the people’s affairs and about al-Ḥajjāj’s conduct and actions. Whenever Yazīd told him something he disliked, Sulaymān would say, “Woe to you, Yazīd! What do you think God will do with al-Ḥajjāj on the Day of Resurrection?” He said:

Yazīd was silent. When Sulaymān pressed him repeatedly, he said, “Shall I speak, Commander of the Faithful? God will make him the third of your father and your brother, between the two of them. If they enter Paradise, he will be their servant and carry out their orders; and if they enter the Fire, why do you ask about him?” Sulaymān said, “Woe to you, so-and-so!” (folio 149b) “Write to al-Yamāmah that they are to stop cursing al-Ḥajjāj and are not to mention him either with a curse or with a prayer.”

He had previously written to al-Yamāmah ordering them to mention him only with a curse, and they had been doing so.

He gave Yazīd permission to return to his family. Yazīd arrived in Damascus and prepared to go to the mosque. Those around him spoke to one another and said, “This is Ibn Abī Muslim. He has prayed, and now he is coming to you, seeking the companionship and friendship that used to be between you and him. Go to him and drive him away before he comes to you; if he comes and you drive him away, it will become a scandal and a notorious story against you.” They went to him. When Yazīd saw them, he thought they had come to greet him, and he welcomed them. They said, “You there, keep away from us. You used to sit with us, but you did what you did in Iraq. So do not sit with us or come near us.” He gestured with his hand and said, “I did what I did? By God, the only thing I regret is that I left many people in the prisons of Iraq without having dealt with them.”

Abū Saʿīd ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm related to me: Abū Ḥafṣ told us, from Saʿīd, from Ismāʿīl, who said: I fell ill, and Abū Ṣāliḥ al-Ashʿarī came to visit me. He related to me, from Kaʿb, who said: “Fever is a bellows from the Fire, which God sends upon His believing servant in this world, so that it may be an expiation from the Fire of Hell.”

[Egypt]

Abū Yūsuf told us: Abū Ṣāliḥ ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṣāliḥ told us: Ibn Shurayḥ told us that he heard ʿUmayrah ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Maʿāfirī say: My father told me that he heard Ibn al-Ḥamiq say: The Messenger of God ﷺ said, “There will be a tribulation in which the Arab army will be the safest of people”—or he said, “the best of people.”

Ibn al-Ḥamiq said, “That is why I came to Egypt.”

Abū Yūsuf told us: Abū Ṣāliḥ told us: al-Layth told us, from Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd, who said: “Today, I know of piety only among the people of Medina and the people of Egypt.”

Abū Yūsuf told us: Abū Nuʿaym and Qabīṣah told us, saying: Sufyān told us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Waʿlah, who said: I said to Ibn ʿAbbās, “We raid in the East and are brought waterskins, but we do not know what they are made of.” He replied, “I do not know what to say to you, except that I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say, ‘Any hide that has been tanned is purified.’”

Abū Yūsuf told us: Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd told us: Abū Muʿāwiyah told us, from Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd, from al-Ḥārith ibn Yazīd al-Ṣanʿānī, from Abū Dharr, who said: I asked the Prophet ﷺ for a governorship. He said, “Abū Dharr, you are weak, and it is a trust. On the Day of Resurrection it will be disgrace and regret, except for one who takes it with its due and fulfills what is incumbent upon him in it.”

Abū Yūsuf told us: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Maslamah told us, from Mālik ibn Anas, from ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith, from ʿUbayd ibn Fayrūz, from al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib: The Messenger of God ﷺ was asked, “What defects should be avoided in sacrificial animals?” He gestured with his hand and said, “Four.” Al-Barāʾ would gesture with his hand and say, “My hand is shorter than the hand of the Messenger of God ﷺ: the lame animal whose lameness is evident, the one-eyed animal whose defect is evident, the sick animal whose sickness is evident, and the emaciated animal with no marrow.”

—the Messenger of God ﷺ. The lame animal whose lameness is evident, the one-eyed animal whose defect is evident, the sick animal whose sickness is evident, and the emaciated animal with no marrow.

Abū Yūsuf (folio 84b) told us: Zayd ibn Bishr said: Rabīʿah used to say:

“While that short man is there, learning will continue to flourish in the Maghrib”—meaning ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith.

“I heard Ibn Bukayr say: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Muḥammad said, ‘I saw al-Layth ibn Saʿd debating legal questions with them in Rabīʿah’s circle, and he had surpassed the people of the circle.’”

Ibn Bukayr said: Al-Layth said, “Abū Dharr was in Egypt, as were al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwām and Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ. ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar also came to Egypt and laid out the plot for Dār al-Barakah. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Marwān asked him for it, and he gave it to him, but did not compensate him for any of it.”

He said: Yaḥyā ibn Sulaymān al-Juʿfī told me: Ibn Wahb told me: Ḥarmalah ibn ʿImrān told me, from ʿUmayr ibn Abī Mudrik, from Sufyān ibn Wahb al-Khawlānī, who said: I heard him say, “While we were travelling with ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ along the slope of this mountain”—he said, “and al-Muqawqis was with us”—“ʿAmr said to him, ‘Muqawqis, why is this mountain of yours so bare, with no plants or trees on it, unlike the mountains of Syria?’ He replied, ‘I do not know, but God has made the people here independent of that through this Nile. Yet beneath it, we find something better than that.’ ʿAmr asked, ‘And what is it?’ He replied, ‘A people will surely be buried beneath it—or laid in a grave—whom God will raise on the Day of Resurrection, with no reckoning upon them.’ ʿAmr said, ‘O God, make me one of them.’”

Ḥarmalah said, “I saw the tomb of ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ there, and in it are also the tombs of Abū Baṣrah al-Ghifārī and ʿUqbah ibn ʿĀmir.”

I heard Ibn Bukayr say: “Al-Layth ibn Saʿd held three governorships for Ṣāliḥ ibn ʿAlī.” He said: Ṣāliḥ told ʿAmr, “I will not let him go until he accepts an office for me.” ʿAmr said, “Do not do that.” Ṣāliḥ replied, “I will have his head struck off.” ʿAmr went and warned him. Al-Layth then took charge of the stipend bureau; he governed al-Jazīrah in the days of Abū Jaʿfar, and in the days of al-Mahdī he governed the bureau.

He said: “Ibn Lahīʿah held the office of the treasury for them, governed al-Qulzum, and served as judge for ten years in the days of Abū Jaʿfar. Al-Qulzum and the treasury were in the days of al-Mahdī.”

He said: Al-Layth said, “I used to see ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith wearing three garments for a dinar: his shirt, his cloak, and his waist-wrapper. Then nights and days had scarcely passed before I saw him trailing brocade and silk. ‘We belong to God, and to Him we return.’”

(folio 153a) Abū Yūsuf Yaʿqūb al-Fasawī informed us. He said:

These are the trustworthy Successors from among the people of Egypt.

Among them: Sufyān ibn Wahb al-Khawlānī.

He heard from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb and related sound hadiths.

And Abū Tamīm al-Jayshānī and Abū Thawr al-Fahmī.

Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān told us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ziyād ibn Anʿam al-Ifrīqī, who told me, from Muslim ibn Yasār, from Sufyān ibn Wahb al-Khawlānī, who said: “I was with ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb in Syria when he said, ‘I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say—’”

“Every intoxicant is forbidden.”

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān told us, from Ḥaywah ibn Shurayḥ, who told me: Bakr ibn ʿAmr told me that he heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn Hubayrah say that he heard Abū Tamīm al-Jayshānī say that he heard ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb say that he heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: “If you were to rely upon God as He deserves to be relied upon, you would be provided for as the birds are provided for: they go out in the morning with empty stomachs and return in the evening full.”

Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bukayr told us, from Ibn Lahīʿah, who told me: Yazīd ibn ʿAmr said, “I heard Abū Thawr al-Fahmī say: I came to ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān. While I was with him, he said, ‘I have kept myself in reserve with my Lord for ten years; I am the fourth—’”

“of four in Islam. I have neither been overcome by anxiety nor entertained a wish, nor have I placed my right hand upon my private parts since I pledged allegiance to my beloved. No Friday has passed since I became Muslim without my freeing a slave on that day—unless I could not, in which case I freed one afterward. I have never lied, either in the pre-Islamic period or in Islam.”

Among them: Abū Qays, the client of ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ.

(folio 153b) Abū Ṣāliḥ told us: al-Layth told me, from Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb, from Abū Qays, the client of ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān, who said:

“I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: ‘Wickedness is seventy parts: one part is among humankind, and sixty-nine parts are on land.’”

Among them: ʿAlī ibn Rabāḥ ibn Quṣayr al-Lakhmī, “born in the Maghrib.”

Abū al-Aswad al-Naḍr ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār and Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bukayr told us, saying: Ibn Lahīʿah informed us, from al-Ḥārith ibn Yazīd al-Ḥaḍramī, from ʿAlī ibn Rabāḥ, from ʿUtbah ibn al-Nudr al-Sulamī—who was one of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ—who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ was asked, “Which of the two terms did Moses fulfill more completely?” He said, “The more honorable and more complete of them.” He also said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said, “When Moses wanted to part from Shuʿayb, he told his wife to ask her father for some of his sheep, by which they could make a living. He gave her [some]—”

“which bore offspring of a single color. When she came to the watering place, Moses stood beside it. Every ewe that came away from it, he struck on the flank with his staff, and it bore offspring in a variety of colors. They bore two or three at a time, none of them feeble, narrow-teated, short-rumped, or with an extra teat. When you conquer Syria, you will find remnants of them there; they are the Samaritan sheep.”

Among them: Abū al-Khayr Marthad ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Yazanī.

Abū ʿĀṣim told us, from ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn Jaʿfar, from Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb, from Abū al-Khayr Marthad ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Yazanī, from Abū Baṣrah al-Ghifārī, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said, “When you pass by Jews and Christians, do not greet them. If they greet you, say, ‘And upon you.’”

Among them: Muḥammad ibn ʿUbayd ibn Jabr

(154a) Abū Ṣāliḥ and Yaḥyā ibn Bukayr related to us; they said: al-Layth related to us; Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb related to me, from Kulayb ibn Dhuʾl al-Ḥaḍramī, from ʿUbayd ibn Jabr, that he traveled with Abū Baṣrah al-Ghifārī during Ramaḍān to Alexandria. When they set out from al-Fusṭāṭ, [he called for food]. I said to him, “Will you eat when we have only just looked back at al-Fusṭāṭ?” He said, “Would you turn away from the practice of the Messenger of God ﷺ and his Companions? So break your fast.”

And Abū Tamīm al-Jayshānī

Abū Ṣāliḥ and Ibn Bukayr related to us; they said: al-Layth related to us, from Khayr ibn Nuʿaym al-Ḥaḍramī, from Ibn Hubayrah al-Sabaʾī, from Abū Tamīm al-Jayshānī, that Abū Baṣrah al-Ghifārī said: “The Messenger of God ﷺ led us in the afternoon prayer at al-Mukhammis. He said: ‘This prayer was prescribed for those before you, but they neglected and abandoned it. Whoever among you observes it will receive its reward twice. There is no prayer after it until the witness appears.” Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us, from al-Layth, from Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb, from Khayr ibn Nuʿaym.

And Ibn Bukayr, Abū al-Aswad, and Qutaybah ibn Saʿīd related to us, from Ibn Lahīʿah, from Ibn Hubayrah, that Abū Tamīm informed him that he had heard Abū Baṣrah al-Ghifārī say: “The Messenger of God ﷺ led us in the afternoon prayer at Mukhammis—a valley from some of their mantles.78 He said: ‘This prayer was presented to those before you, but they were lax about it and abandoned it. So, whoever among you performs it will have its reward doubled. There is no prayer after it until the witness sets—and that is the star.’”

Among them: Abū al-Haytham Sulaymān ibn ʿAmr

Originally from Medina.

Saʿīd ibn ʿUfayr related to me. He said: Ibn Lahīʿah related to me, from Mūsā ibn Wardān, from Abū al-Haytham, that he heard Abū Baṣrah al-Ghifārī speak about the conversion of Ghifār—and he mentioned an account—and say: “O Abū Baṣrah (154b), the unbeliever eats from seven intestines, while the believer eats from one intestine.”

Among them: Abū ʿImrān Aslam al-Tujībī

Sulaymān ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān related to us. Ibn Wahb related to us, from Qurrah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb, that Aslam, Abū ʿImrān al-Tujībī, informed him, saying: “Maslamah ibn Mukhallad sent me to the ruler of Abyssinia. When I arrived, I waited at the door and found Hubayb ibn Mughfil al-Ghifārī, a Companion of the Prophet ﷺ and Muḥammad ibn ʿUlbah al-Qurashī. He admitted Muḥammad ibn ʿUlbah, who rose, dragging his lower garment. Hubayb ibn Mughfil looked at him and said, ‘I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: “Whoever treads with an arrogant gait, treads a gait in the Fire.”’”

Among them: Mūsā ibn Wardān

Muḥammad ibn al-Muṣaffā related to us. Al-Walīd related to us. Ibn Lahīʿah related to us, from Mūsā ibn Wardān, who said: “I heard ʿUqbah ibn ʿĀmir say: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: ‘My community has been absolved of error, forgetfulness, and what they are compelled to do.’”

And Ziyād ibn Nuʿaym al-Ḥaḍramī

Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān related to us. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ziyād ibn Anʿam related to us. Ziyād ibn Nuʿaym al-Ḥaḍramī—one of the people of Egypt—related to us. He said: “I heard Ziyād ibn al-Ḥārith al-Ṣudāʾī, a Companion of the Messenger of God ﷺ narrate: I came to the Messenger of God ﷺ and pledged allegiance to him upon Islam. A man came to him and said, ‘Give me some of the alms.’ The Messenger of God ﷺ said: ‘God, Mighty and Majestic, did not leave the judgment concerning them—that is, the alms—to a prophet or anyone else. He Himself decreed them and divided them into eight portions. If you are among those portions, I will give you—or give you your due.’”

Then the Messenger of God ﷺ took an early supper, during one of his journeys. I stayed close to him, and I was strong, while his Companions would fall behind and lag, until no one remained with him but me. When it was time for the dawn prayer, he ordered me to call the adhān. I kept asking, “Shall I call the commencement, Messenger of God?” The Messenger of God ﷺ would look toward the east, toward the dawn, and say, “No.” When dawn had broken, the Messenger of God ﷺ dismounted and went to relieve himself, then returned to me. His Companions had caught up by then. He said, “Is there any water, Ṣudāʾī brother?” I said, “Only a little, not enough for you.” The Prophet ﷺ said, “Put it in a vessel, then bring it to me.”

I did so, and he placed his palm in the vessel. The Ṣudāʾī said: “I saw a spring gush forth between each pair of his fingers.” The Messenger of God ﷺ said to me, “Ṣudāʾī brother, were I not too modest before my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, we would have drunk and given others to drink. Call out to my Companions; whoever needs water may come.” I called out among them, and whoever wished took some. Then the Prophet of God may ﷺ went to the prayer. Bilāl wanted to call the commencement of prayer, but the Prophet of God ﷺ said to him, “The Ṣudāʾī brother called the adhān, and whoever calls the adhān is the one who calls the commencement.” The Ṣudāʾī said: “So I called the commencement of prayer.”

Among them: Sulaymān ibn Ziyād al-Ḥaḍramī

Abū al-Walīd Hishām ibn ʿAbd al-Malik related to me. He said: Ghawth ibn Sulaymān ibn Ziyād related to me. He said: Sulaymān ibn Ziyād related to me. He said: “We visited ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Jazʾ al-Zubaydī on a Friday. He called for a basin and said, ‘Screen me from the people.’ He urinated in it and performed ablution. Then he said: ‘I found no place to relieve myself except a place facing the qiblah, and I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: “Let none of you urinate while facing the qiblah.”’”

Among them: ʿUqbah ibn Muslim

Abū Ṣāliḥ and Ibn Bukayr related to us; they said: al-Layth ibn Saʿd related to us, from Ḥaywah ibn Shurayḥ, from ʿUqbah ibn Muslim, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Jazʾ al-Zubaydī, who said (155b): “I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: ‘Woe to the heels and the soles of the feet, from the Fire!’”

Among them: ʿUbayd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah

Abū al-Aswad and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yūsuf related to me; they said: Ibn Lahīʿah related to us, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from Ibn Jazʾ, who said: “I have never seen anyone smile more often than the Messenger of God ﷺ.”

Among them: Abū Zurʿah ʿAmr ibn Jābir al-Ḥaḍramī

Abū Ṣāliḥ al-Ḥarrānī related to us. Ibn Lahīʿah related to us, from Abū Zurʿah ʿAmr ibn Jābir al-Ḥaḍramī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Jazʾ al-Zubaydī, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “People will emerge from the East and prepare the way for the Mahdī’s rule.”

Among them: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Malīl al-Sulayḥī

Saʿīd ibn Abī Maryam, ʿAmr ibn al-Rabīʿ ibn Ṭāriq, and Ibn Bukayr related to us; they said: Ibn Lahīʿah related to us, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Malīl, that his father informed him that he heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Jazʾ al-Zubaydī mention that the Jews brought a Jewish man and woman who had committed adultery after having been married. The Messenger of God ﷺ ordered that they be stoned. “I was among those who stoned them.” Abū Yūsuf said: “In my view, these men are more trustworthy than the people of Kūfah; and if they are not trustworthy, they are no less so than them.”

Among them: Muslim ibn Yazīd al-Ṣadafī

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yūsuf related to us. Ibn Lahīʿah informed us. ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yazīd al-Ḥaḍramī related to us, from Muslim ibn Yazīd al-Ṣadafī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Jazʾ al-Zubaydī, that the Messenger of God (156a) ﷺ entered the mosque and ascended the pulpit. When he climbed the first step, he said, “Amen”; then, when he climbed the second, he said, “Amen”; then, when he climbed the third, he said, “Amen.” When he came down, he was asked, “You did something you do not usually do.” He said: “Gabriel ﵇ appeared to me on the first step and said:

‘Muḥammad ﷺ whoever lives to see either one of his parents but is not admitted by them to Paradise—may God cast him far away, then cast him farther away.’ I said, ‘Amen.’ Then, on the second step, he said: ‘Whoever lives to see the month of Ramaḍān but is not forgiven—may God cast him far away, then cast him farther away.’ I said, ‘Amen.’ Then, on the third step, he said: ‘May God cast far away, then cast farther away, whoever is mentioned in someone’s presence and does not invoke blessings upon you.’ I said, ‘Amen.’”

Among them: ʿAbbās ibn Julayd al-Ḥajrī

Abū al-Aswad related to us. Ibn Lahīʿah related to us, from al-Miqdām ibn Salāmah al-Ḥajrī, from ʿAbbās ibn Julayd al-Ḥajrī, who said: “I asked ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Jazʾ al-Zubaydī, ‘What do you think about ṭilāʾ?’79 He said, ‘Is anyone in the house?’ ‘No,’ I said, ‘only you and me.’ He did not believe me until he called his wife and his servant girl and asked them, ‘Is anyone in the house?’ They said, ‘No, except ʿAbbās, by God.’ He said: ‘It is forbidden. We neither condemned nor openly discussed this drink until Muʿāwiyah ibn Abī Sufyān. He neither makes it lawful nor declares it forbidden. If you declare it lawful, you will make the forbidden lawful; and if you declare it forbidden, they will hear you and strike off your head. If you are among some of those people and they offer it to you, say, “I cannot drink it; I have a cramp in my belly.”’”

Among them: Abū al-Khayr Marthad ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Yazanī

Abū ʿĀṣim al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Makhlad and ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā related to us; they said: ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn Jaʿfar informed us, from Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb, from Marthad ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Yazanī, from ʿUqbah ibn ʿĀmir al-Juhanī, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “The most deserving conditions to be fulfilled are those by which you have made the women’s private parts lawful to you.”

Among them: Mishraḥ ibn Hāʿān al-Maʿāfirī

(156b) Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yazīd related to us. Ḥaywah ibn Shurayḥ related to us, from Bakr ibn ʿAmr, from Mishraḥ ibn Hāʿān al-Maʿāfirī, from ʿUqbah ibn ʿĀmir al-Juhanī, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “If there were to be a prophet after me, it would be ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb.”

Among them: Abū ʿUshānah al-Maʿāfirī

Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us. Ḥarmalah ibn ʿImrān al-Tujībī related to us, from Abū ʿUshānah al-Maʿāfirī, from ʿUqbah ibn ʿĀmir al-Juhanī, from the Prophet ﷺ who said: “Whoever has three daughters, is patient with them, and feeds, gives drink, and clothes them from his means—they will be a shield for him from the Fire.”

Among them: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Shimāsah al-Mahrī

Abū Ṣāliḥ and Ibn Bukayr related to us; they said: al-Layth related to us. Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb related to me, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Shimāsah, that he heard ʿUqbah ibn ʿĀmir say: The Messenger of God may ﷺ said: “The believer is the brother of the believer. It is not lawful for a believer to outbid his brother in a sale until he withdraws, nor to propose marriage over his brother’s proposal until he withdraws.”

Among them: Abū ʿAlī al-Hamdānī, Thumāmah ibn Shafiyy al-Iskandarānī

Saʿīd ibn Abī Maryam related to me. Yaḥyā ibn Ayyūb informed us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ḥarmalah, who said: Abū ʿAlī al-Hamdānī informed me—he lived in Alexandria—and said: “I went on a journey with ʿUqbah ibn ʿĀmir. We said to him, ‘Lead us in prayer.’ He said, ‘I will not do that. I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: “Whoever leads people in prayer, performs it at the proper time, and completes it, will have its reward, and so will they. Whoever falls short in any of that bears the responsibility; they do not.”’”

And Khālid ibn Zayd

[ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān and Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr related to us; they said: ʿAbd Allāh (157a) ibn al-Mubārak related to us. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd ibn Jābir related to us. Abū Sallām related to me. Khālid ibn Zayd related to me.

And Abū Saʿīd ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm related to me. Al-Walīd related to us. Ibn Jābir related to us, that he heard Abū Sallām al-Aswad ibn Karb, from Khālid ibn Zayd, who said: “I was a skilled archer, and ʿUqbah ibn ʿĀmir would pass by me and say, ‘Khālid, come out with us to shoot.’ One day I was late getting to him. He said, ‘Khālid, come here; I will tell you what the Messenger [of God] told me—’

…of God ﷺ. I went to him, and he said: “I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: ‘By means of a single arrow, God admits three people into Paradise: the one who makes it, seeking reward for the good in his craft; the one who shoots it; and the one who hands it to him. So shoot and ride; shooting is dearer to me than riding. There is no amusement except three things: a man training his horse, his playing with his wife, and his shooting with his bow and arrows. Whoever abandons shooting after learning it, out of disinterest in it, has rejected—or abandoned—a blessing.”

Abū Bishr related to us: Abū ʿĀmir related to us: Hishām related to us, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, from Abū Sallām, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yazīd al-Azraq, from ʿUqba ibn ʿĀmir, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “By means of a single arrow, God, Mighty and Majestic, admits [three people into Paradise]”—and he mentioned something like the foregoing.

Among them was: Iyās ibn ʿĀmir al-Ghāfiqī

Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Muqriʾ related to us: Mūsā ibn Ayyūb al-Ghāfiqī related to us, from his paternal uncle Iyās ibn ʿĀmir al-Ghāfiqī, from ʿUqba ibn ʿĀmir al-Juhanī: When “So glorify the name of your Lord, the Most Great” was revealed, the Messenger of God ﷺ said to us: “Make it part of your bowing.” When “Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High” was revealed, he said to us: “Make it part of your…

prostration.

Among them was: Dukhayn Abū al-Haytham al-Ḥijrī

ʿUqba’s secretary.

(157b) [Abū] al-Walīd related to us: al-Layth ibn Saʿd related to me; he said:

Ibrāhīm ibn Nashīṭ al-Waʿlānī informed me, from Kaʿb ibn ʿAlqama, from Dukhayn Abū al-Haytham, ʿUqba’s secretary, who said: I said to ʿUqba ibn ʿĀmir, “We have neighbors who drink wine, and I am going to summon the police so they can seize them.” He said, “Do not do that. Rather, admonish them and threaten them.” He said: I did so, but they did not stop. Dukhayn then came to ʿUqba and said, “I have forbidden them, but they have not stopped, and I am going to summon the police for them.”

“Woe to you! Do not do that, for I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: ‘Whoever conceals a person’s nakedness is as one who rescues a buried girl from her grave.’”

Among them was: Mālik ibn Qays

Ibn Qaʿnab related to us: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ghānim related to us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ziyād, from Mālik ibn Qays, who said: ʿUqba ibn ʿĀmir came to Muʿāwiya ibn Abī Sufyān while he was at Īliyāʾ and said: “We were with the Messenger of God ﷺ on one of his journeys, and he said:
