‘Whoever performs ablution, performing it well, then prays two units seeking God’s favor, God will forgive him the sins he committed before them.’”

And Abū Salmā al-Qitbānī

Saʿīd ibn Abī Maryam related to us; he said: Ibn Lahīʿa informed us: Yazīd ibn ʿAmr al-Maʿāfirī related to me that Abū Salmā al-Qitbānī informed him, from ʿUqba ibn ʿĀmir, who said: I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: “Three men from the Children of Israel set out seeking a place to stay. Rain overtook them, so they took shelter beneath a rock. The rock slid and sealed them in. One looked at the others and said, ‘Nothing will save you from this except truthfulness. Let each of you call upon God by virtue of the best deed he has done.’ One of them said: ‘O God, I had a beautiful, lovely female cousin. I sought to seduce her, but she refused me. Then a year of hardship came upon us, and I offered her one hundred dinars in return for yielding herself to me. She did so. When I was between her legs, she began to tremble. I said, “What is the matter with you?” She said, “I fear God.”’”

“So I left her and let her keep the hundred. O God, if You know that I did this only seeking Your approval and fearing Your displeasure, then relieve us.” The rock shifted until they could see light through it.

Then the second said: “I had two elderly parents, and I had sheep that I pastured for them. Whenever I returned to them, I would attend to them before my family. One day the trees led me far away, and I came back when they had fallen asleep. I sat waiting for them. Then I brought the vessel to them and stood over them while they slept. I disliked waking them, and I disliked tending to my children before them. I kept standing over them until dawn broke. O God, if You know that I did this only seeking Your good pleasure and fearing Your displeasure, then relieve us.” The rock split open once more.

Then the third said: “I was tending sheep when the time for prayer came, so I stood to pray. A wolf came and entered the flock. I disliked interrupting my prayer, so I persisted until I had finished it. O God, if You know that I did this only seeking Your good pleasure and fearing Your displeasure, then relieve us.” He said: The rock shifted.

ʿUqba said: I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ relate this account. When the rock shifted, he said: “Ṭāqin, and they came out of it.”80

Among them was: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Mālik

Al-Ḥajjāj related to us: Ḥammād related to us, from Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Zukayr, from Abū Saʿīd al-Yaḥṣubī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Mālik, from ʿUqba ibn ʿĀmir…

al-Juhanī: A woman vowed to perform the pilgrimage for a year without wearing a veil. The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Let her ride, wear a veil, and fast for three days.”

Among them was: Hishām ibn Abī Ruqayya al-Lakhmī

(158b) Saʿīd ibn Abī Maryam related to us: Yaḥyā ibn Ayyūb informed us: al-Ḥasan ibn Thawbān and ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith related to me, from Hishām ibn Abī Ruqayya, who said:

I heard Maslama ibn Mukhallad say to ʿUqba ibn ʿĀmir, “Stand and tell the people what you heard from the Messenger of God ﷺ.” He said: I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: “Whoever deliberately lies about me, let him take his seat in Hell.” And I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: “Silk and gold are forbidden to the males of my community and permitted to its females.”

ʿAmr ibn al-Rabīʿ ibn Ṭāriq related to me: Yaḥyā ibn Ayyūb informed us, from ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith, from Hishām ibn Abī Ruqayya. Zayd ibn Bishr and ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn ʿImrān related to me; they said: Ibn Wahb informed us: ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith informed me that Hishām ibn Abī Ruqayya al-Lakhmī related to him, saying: I heard Maslama ibn Mukhallad, while he was on the pulpit—and ʿUqba ibn ʿĀmir was seated there—say: “O people of Islam, what makes you wear silk when linen and ʿaṣb cloth are available to you and suffice you? This man is among you; he will tell you what he heard from the Prophet ﷺ. Stand, ʿUqba, and inform them.” He stood and said:

“I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: ‘Whoever wears silk in this world…’”

“…God will forbid him to wear it in the hereafter.” And I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: “Whoever deliberately tells a lie about me, let him take his seat in the Fire.” —The word “a lie” occurs only in the version of ʿAmr ibn al-Rabīʿ.—

Among them was: Abū Qabīl al-Maʿāfirī

Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us: al-Layth related to me, from Abū Qabīl al-Maʿāfirī, from ʿUqba. Ḥ.

Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Muqriʾ related to us: Ibn Lahīʿa related to us, from Abū Qabīl, who said:

I heard ʿUqba ibn ʿĀmir al-Juhanī say: I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: “The ruin of my community lies in the Book and milk.” It was said, “O Messenger of God, what are the Book (159a) and milk?” He said: “They learn the Qurʾān and interpret it in a way other than that in which God revealed it; they love milk and abandon the congregational prayers and the Friday prayers, and they make a show of themselves.” Abū Qabīl said: I heard only this report from ʿUqba ibn ʿĀmir.

Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: Ibn Lahīʿa related to us, from Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb, from Abū al-Khayr Marthad, from ʿUqba, from the Prophet ﷺ something like it. The wording of the report is that of al-Muqriʾ.

Among them was: ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Malīl al-Sulayḥī

ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān related to us: “ʿAbd Allāh informed us: Ḥarmala ibn ʿImrān informed us: [he said,] ‘…’”

ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Malīl al-Sulayḥī related to me: My father said: I was sitting with ʿUqba ibn ʿĀmir near the pulpit on Friday when Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥudhayfa came out and mounted the pulpit. He preached to the people, then recited a sūra of the Qurʾān to them—he was among the finest reciters. ʿUqba ibn ʿĀmir said: “God and His Messenger have spoken truly, for I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: ‘Men will recite the Qurʾān, but it will not pass beyond their collarbones; they will pass out of the religion as an arrow passes through its quarry.’” Ibn Abī Ḥudhayfa heard us and said: “By God, if you are telling the truth—and I think you are, as far as I know, a liar—you are one of them.”

ʿAbd Allāh said: The interpretation of this report is that they assemble with them and say this statement to them.

Among them was: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ḥujayra

Ibn ʿUthmān related to us: ʿAbd Allāh related to us: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Shurayḥ related to us; he said:

I heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn Thaʿlaba al-Ḥaḍramī mention that he heard Ibn Ḥujayra the Elder, standing on a Friday, mention that he heard ʿUqba ibn ʿĀmir relate from the Prophet ﷺ who said: “Five kinds of people: whoever dies in any one of these circumstances is a martyr. One killed in the path of God (159b) is a martyr; one drowned in the path of God is a martyr; the one afflicted by the plague in the path…” of God is a martyr”; one who dies of an abdominal illness in the path of God is a martyr; and a woman who dies in childbirth in the path of God is a martyr.

Among them was: Shuʿayb ibn Zurʿa.

Saʿīd ibn Abī Maryam related to me: Nāfiʿ ibn Yazīd informed us: Bakr ibn ʿAmr related to me: Shuʿayb ibn Zurʿa related to me that he heard ʿUqba ibn ʿĀmir say: The Messenger of God ﷺ says: “Will you not frighten people with one of its lashes?” They said:

“O Messenger of God, what is that?” He said: “Debt.” Saʿīd ibn Abī Maryam related to me: Bakr ibn ʿAmr informed me, from Jaʿfar ibn Rabīʿa, that Muʿāwiya ibn Abī Sufyān said: “Debt makes a free man submissive.”

Among them was: al-Mughīra ibn Nuhayk

He transmitted from ʿUqba ibn ʿĀmir, from the Prophet ﷺ: “Whoever learns shooting, then abandons it, has disobeyed me.”

Among them was: Abū ʿAmr al-Saybānī

“Among the people of Palestine.”

Ḥarmala ibn Muḥammad related to me, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī ʿAmr al-Saybānī, from his father, from ʿUqba ibn ʿĀmir: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Pray in sheepfolds, but do not pray in camel enclosures.”

Among them was: Wāhib ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Maʿāfirī

Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us: Yaḥyā ibn Ayyūb related to us, from ʿAyyāsh ibn ʿAbbās, from Wāhib ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Maʿāfirī, who said: A man from among the Anṣār, one of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ came to Maslama ibn Mukhallad and found him asleep. He said, “Wake him.” They said, “Rather, let us leave him until he wakes.” He said, “I will not do that.” So they woke Maslama. He welcomed the man and said:

“Come in.” The man said, “No, not until you send for ʿUqba ibn ʿĀmir, for I have a matter to discuss with him.” Maslama sent for ʿUqba, who came to him. The man said, “Have you heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say…”

“Whoever finds a Muslim in a compromising situation and conceals it, is as one who rescues a buried girl from her grave?”

(160a) ʿUqba said: “I am Abū Ḥammād. I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say that.”

Among them was: Muʿādh ibn Anas al-Juhanī

Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Muqriʾ related to us: Saʿīd ibn Abī Ayyūb related to us, from Abū Marḥūm ʿAbd al-Raḥīm ibn Maymūn, from Sahl ibn Muʿādh ibn Anas, from his father, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Whoever gives up clothing, though able to afford it, out of humility before God, God will summon him on the Day of Resurrection before all creatures and let him choose from among the garments of faith, to wear whichever he wishes.”

Among them was: Saʿīd ibn Abī Shamir al-Sibāʾī

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā ibn Ismāʿīl related to me: Ibn Wahb informed us: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Shurayḥ informed me; he said: I heard Saʿīd ibn Abī Shamir al-Sibāʾī say:

I heard Sufyān ibn Wahb al-Khawlānī say: I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: “The hundredth year will not come with anyone still alive upon the earth.” He said: I related this to Ibn Ḥujayra. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ḥujayra went in to see ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Marwān. He said: Sufyān, an old man, was brought in haste, carried. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz asked him about the report, and he related it to him. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz said: “Perhaps he meant that no one who was alive with him would remain until the end of the hundredth year.” Sufyān said: “That is how I heard the Messenger of God, God bless him and grant him peace…” in a statement.

Among them: Zuhayr ibn Qays al-Balawī

Abū Ṣāliḥ and Ibn Bukayr related to us [saying: al-Layth ibn Saʿd related to us; he said], “Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb related to me, from Suwayd ibn Qays al-Tujībī, from Zuhayr ibn Qays al-Balawī, from ʿAlqamah ibn Ramthah al-Balawī, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ—sent ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ to Bahrain. Then the Messenger of God ﷺ—set out on an expedition, and we went out with him. The Messenger of God ﷺ—dozed, then awoke and said, ‘May God have mercy on ʿAmr.’ They said: We began recalling every man named ʿAmr. Then he dozed a second time, [awoke], and said, ‘May God have mercy on ʿAmr.’ Then he dozed a third time, awoke, and said, ‘May God have mercy on ʿAmr.’ We asked, ‘Who is ʿAmr, Messenger of God?’ He said:

‘ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ.’ They asked, ‘What about him?’ He said, ‘I remembered him: whenever I called on people to give charity, he would bring a generous amount of charity. I would ask him, “Where did you get this, ʿAmr?” and he would say, “From God.” ʿAmr spoke truly: ʿAmr has much good with God’. Zuhayr said: When the civil strife came, I said, ‘I shall follow this man of whom the Messenger of God ﷺ—said what he said,’ and I never left his side.

And Shufayy al-Aṣbaḥī

Abū Ṣāliḥ and Muḥammad ibn Rumḥ related to us; they said: al-Layth related to us, from Ḥaywah ibn Shurayḥ al-Tujībī, from Ibn Shufayy, from his father, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ:

The Messenger of God ﷺ—said: “The one who goes on a military expedition has his reward, and the one who provides the payment has his reward and the reward of the one who goes on the expedition.” The Messenger of God ﷺ—also said: “Returning from an expedition is like going on one”.

Among them: Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yazīd al-Ḥublī

Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Muqriʾ related to us; Ḥaywah ibn Shurayḥ and Ibn Lahīʿah related to me, from Abū Hāniʾ Ḥumayd ibn Hāniʾ al-Khawlānī, who said: I heard Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Ḥublī say, “I heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr say: I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ—say…”

He said: al-Aṣbagh ibn Faraj, Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bukayr, and al-Ḥajjāj al-Azraq—[all] Medinese—related to me. They said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Wahb—an Egyptian—reported to us, from Abū Hāniʾ al-Khawlānī, who informed him, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Ḥublī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ, who said: I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ—say: “God decreed all things fifty thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth.” In Ibn Wahb’s version of the report, it says: “And His Throne was upon the water.” He said: “God wrote the destinies of all creatures”.

And Yazīd ibn Rabāḥ

Ibn Bukayr related to me; ʿAbd Allāh ibn Lahīʿah related to me; Bakr ibn Sawādah related to me that Yazīd ibn Rabāḥ had related to him, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ, from the Prophet ﷺ.

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā ibn Ismāʿīl and Abū Saʿīd related to me; they said: Ibn Wahb related to us; ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith informed me that Bakr ibn Sawādah (161a) had related to him that Yazīd ibn Rabāḥ had related to him, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ, from the Messenger of God ﷺ—who said: “When the treasuries of Persia and Byzantium are opened to you, what sort of people will you be?”

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf said: “We will say as the Messenger of God ﷺ—instructed us.”

[The Messenger of God ﷺ—said: “Or will you do otherwise? You will vie with one another, then envy one another…”

“then turn their backs on one another or hate one another—or something to that effect—then go to the poor among the Emigrants and make some of them ride on the backs of others”.

Among them: Abū Firās and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Jubayr,

the client of Nāfiʿ ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar al-Qurashī.

Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Muqriʾ related to us; Ḥaywah ibn Shurayḥ related to us, from Kaʿb ibn ʿAlqamah, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Jubayr, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ: The Messenger of God ﷺ—said: “When you hear the caller to prayer, say what he says. Then invoke blessings upon me: whoever invokes a blessing upon me once, God will bless him ten times for it. Then ask God to grant me the means of approach, for it is a station in Paradise that befits none of God’s servants. I hope that I shall be that one. Whoever asks God to grant me the means of approach will be entitled to my intercession.”

Among them: ʿĪsā ibn Hilāl al-Ṣadafī

Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us; al-Layth related to me; Khālid ibn Yazīd related to me, from Saʿīd ibn Abī Hilāl, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from ʿĪsā ibn Hilāl al-Ṣadafī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr, from the Messenger of God ﷺ—who said: “A servant may remain a believer for ages and then for ages more, yet die while God is displeased with him. And a servant may remain an unbeliever for ages and then for ages more, yet die while God is pleased with him. Whoever dies as a slanderer and backbiter, one who disparages people, will be marked publicly on the Day of Resurrection by God on the snout, from one lip to the other.” (161b)

Among them: Abū al-Ḥuṣayn al-Haytham ibn Shufayy and Abū ʿĀmir al-Maʿāfirī, later al-Ḥajrī

Saʿīd ibn Abī Maryam, Abū al-Aswad, Abū Zayd, and Yazīd ibn Khālid ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Mawhab related to us. They said: al-Mufaḍḍal ibn Faḍālah reported to us; ʿAyyāsh ibn ʿAbbās related to me, from Abū al-Ḥuṣayn al-Haytham ibn Shufayy. I heard him say: “Abū ʿĀmir al-Maʿāfirī and I went out to pray in Īliyāʾ. Their preacher was a man of the Azd, called Abū Rayḥānah, one of the Companions. Abū al-Ḥuṣayn said: My companion reached the mosque ahead of me. Then I caught up with him and sat beside him. He asked me, ‘Did you attend Abū Rayḥānah’s sermons?’

“I said, ‘No.’ He said, ‘I heard him say: The Messenger of God ﷺ—prohibited…’”

“ten things: tooth filing, tattooing, plucking [hair], a man lying closely with another man without a covering between them, a woman lying closely with another woman without a covering between them, a man adorning the hem of his garment with silk, as the non-Arabs do, plunder, riding on a tiger-skin, and wearing a signet ring—except for one in authority”.

Among them: Sufyān ibn ʿAwf al-Qārī

Abū al-Aswad and Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bukayr related to us. They said: Ibn Lahīʿah related to us; al-Ḥārith ibn Yazīd related to me, from Jundub ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-ʿAdawī, who heard Sufyān ibn ʿAwf al-Qārī say: I heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ say: The Prophet ﷺ—said to me, “Blessed are the strangers.” They asked, “Who are the strangers, Messenger of God?”

He said: “Righteous people, few among many wicked people; those who disobey them are more numerous than those who obey them.” He also said: “One day we were with the Messenger of God ﷺ—and the sun rose. The Messenger of God ﷺ—said, ‘On the Day of Resurrection, God, Mighty and Majestic, will bring people whose light is like the sun.’ Abū Bakr said, ‘Are we they, Messenger of God?’ (162a)

“He said, ‘No, but you have much good. They are the poor among the Emigrants.’ Ibn Bukayr added: ‘They are afflicted by hardships…’”

“they are tested by hardships; one of them dies with his need still in his heart.” Both of them said: “They will be gathered from the farthest reaches of the earth”.

Among them: Suwayd ibn Qays

Abū al-Aswad related to us; Ibn Lahīʿah reported to us, from Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb, that Suwayd ibn Qays had informed him, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ: The Messenger of God ﷺ—said: “A day of guarding in the path of God is better than a month of fasting and night prayer.”

Among them: al-Walīd ibn ʿAbdah

Al-Ḥajjāj ibn al-Minhāl related to us; Ḥammād related to us, from Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq, from Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb, from al-Walīd ibn ʿAbdah, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ: The Messenger of God ﷺ—forbade wine, gambling, the kubah, the ghubayrāʾ, and every intoxicant is forbidden.

Sulaymān ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān related to us; Saʿdān related to us, from ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn Jaʿfar, from Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb, from ʿAmr ibn al-Walīd ibn ʿAbdah, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr, that the Messenger of God ﷺ—used to say: “Whoever [says] of me what I did not say, let him take his seat in Hell”. And I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ—say: “God has forbidden wine, gambling, the kubah, the ghubayrāʾ, and every intoxicant”.

And ʿAmr ibn al-Walīd al-Sahmī

Hāniʾ ibn al-Mutawakkil al-Iskandarānī and Ibn Bukayr related to us. They said: Ibn Lahīʿah related to us, from Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb, from ʿAmr ibn al-Walīd al-Sahmī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ, who asked the Messenger of God ﷺ “Do you sense the revelation coming over you?” The Messenger of God ﷺ—said: “Yes. I hear a ringing sound, then I become still from that. Whenever revelation comes to me, I think my soul is about to be taken then.” (162b)

And ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Qaḥdham

Abū Ṣāliḥ and Ibn Bukayr related to us; they said: al-Layth related to us; Yazīd ibn Abī…

Ḥabīb, from Saʿīd ibn Abī Hilāl, from Rabīʿah ibn Sayf: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Qaḥdham—Abū Ṣāliḥ said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Muḥarram—informed him that a son of al-ʿĀṣ ibn ʿUqbah died on Friday, and his grief for him was intense. A man from Ṣadaf said to him, “Abū Yaḥyā, shall I give you some good news that I heard from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ? I heard him say: The Messenger of God ﷺ—said: ‘No Muslim dies on the night of Friday or on Friday except that he is spared the trial of the grave’”.

Among them: Nāʿim, the client of Umm Salamah

Aṣbagh ibn al-Faraj related to us; Ibn Wahb related to me, from ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith, from Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb, that Nāʿim, the client of Umm Salamah, related to him that ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ said: A man came to the Messenger of God ﷺ—and said, “I pledge allegiance to you to emigrate and strive in God’s cause, seeking reward from God.” He asked, “Do you have either of your parents?” He said, “Yes, both of them.” He said, “And you seek reward from God, Mighty and Majestic?” He said:

“Yes.” He said, “Then return to your parents and treat them well.”

And Mālik ibn ʿAbd Allāh

Abū Ṣāliḥ ʿAbd al-Ghaffār ibn Dāwūd al-Ḥarrānī related to us; Ibn Lahīʿah related to us, from Abū Qabīl, from Mālik ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ, from the Prophet ﷺ—that he sought refuge from seven kinds of death: sudden death, being bitten by a snake, being killed by a beast of prey, [burning, and drowning,] having something fall on him, and being killed while fleeing from battle.

And ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Daylamī

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṣāliḥ related to us; Muʿāwiyah ibn Ṣāliḥ related to me, from Rabīʿah ibn Yazīd, from Ibn al-Daylamī, who said: I heard a report from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ, so I rode to him to ask him about it. I entered his garden while he was holding a man by the hand81 We used to report that this man was one of those who drank wine. He said, “Abū Muḥammad, have you heard the Messenger of God ﷺ—say anything about a wine drinker?”

The man drew his hand away from the hand of ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr. He said, “I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ—say: ‘Whoever drinks wine, God will not accept his prayer for forty days’”. I said to him, “What is this report that has reached us from you, that you mention from the Messenger of God ﷺ?” He said, “What is that?” I said, “It has reached me that you say: ‘A prayer in Bayt al-Maqdis is like a thousand prayers,’ and that ‘knowledge has dried up.’” He said, “O God, I do not permit…”

“They may say of me what they have not heard from me”—he repeated this three times. He said: “That is not what I said. Rather, I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: ‘Solomon son of David asked God for three things. He asked Him for a dominion such as no one after him would have; God granted it to him. He asked Him for a judgment that would not coincide with sound judgment; God granted it to him. And he asked that whoever comes to this House, seeking nothing but prayer there, be forgiven.’”

Among them was Abū Kabshah al-Salūlī

[Abū ʿĀṣim related to us, from al-Awzāʿī, from Ḥassān ibn ʿAṭiyyah, from Abū Kabshah al-Salūlī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Convey from me, even if only one verse of the Qurʾān. Relate reports from the Children of Israel; there is no harm in that. And whoever deliberately tells a lie about me, let him take his seat in Hell.”]

And Ḥibbān ibn Zayd al-Sharʿabī

Abū al-Yamān related to us; Ḥurayz ibn ʿUthmān related to us, from Ḥibbān ibn Zayd al-Sharʿabī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ, from the Prophet ﷺ who said: “Show mercy, and you will be shown mercy; forgive, and God will forgive you. Woe to those who are like funnels for speech; woe to those who persist in what they have done, while knowing.”

And ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Salamah al-Jumaḥī

Yaḥyā ibn Ṣāliḥ al-Wuḥāẓī related to us; Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz al-Tanūkhī related to us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Salamah al-Jumaḥī, who said: I heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ relate a report from the Messenger of God ﷺ. I wrote it down, and when I had memorized it, I erased it: “Successful is the one who submits to God, whose provision is sufficient, and who bears that patiently.”

And Yūnus ibn Maysarah ibn Ḥalbas

[Yaḥyā ibn Ṣāliḥ al-Wuḥāẓī related to us; Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz related to us, from Ibn Ḥalbas, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “I saw that the pillar of the Book had been pulled from beneath my pillow. I followed it with my gaze, and there it was, a brilliant light, being carried toward Syria. Behold, faith is in Syria when tribulation occurs.”]

Among them was Mudrik ibn ʿAbd Allāh

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yūsuf related to us; Muḥammad ibn Muhājir related to us, from al-ʿAbbās ibn Sālim, from Mudrik ibn ʿAbd Allāh—or from Abū Mudrik—who said: We went on campaign with Muʿāwiyah and ʿAmr in Egypt. We dismounted at a stopping place, and ʿAmr said to Muʿāwiyah: “Commander of the Faithful, may I address the people?” He gave him permission, and ʿAmr stood upon his horse, praised God and lauded Him, then said:

“I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: ‘In a dream I saw the pillar of the Book being carried from beneath my pillow. I followed it with my gaze, and there it was, like a pillar of light, being carried toward Syria. Behold, faith is in Syria when tribulation occurs’”—repeating this several times.

And Mughīth ibn Sumayy al-Awzāʿī

Hishām ibn ʿAmmār related to us: Ṣadaqah ibn Khālid related to us; Zayd ibn Wāqid related to us; he said: Mughīth ibn Sumayy al-Awzāʿī related to me— (164a) from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ, who said: I asked, “Messenger of God, who are the best of people?” He replied: “The one whose heart is cleansed and whose tongue is truthful.” We said: “We know what a truthful tongue is. But what is a cleansed heart?” He replied: “It is the God-fearing, pure heart, in which there is neither sin nor envy.” We asked: “And who comes after him?” He replied: “The one who disdains the world and loves the Hereafter.” They said: “We know of no one among us who fits this description except [Abū] Rāfiʿ, the client of the Messenger of God ﷺ. And who comes after him?” He replied: “A believer of good character.” They said: “As for that, there are such people among us.”

Among them was Abū Saʿd al-Mahrī

Abū Saʿīd Yaḥyā ibn Sulaymān al-Juʿfī related to us; Ibn Wahb related to me; Ḥarmalah related to me that Abū al-Sumayṭ Saʿīd ibn Abī Saʿīd al-Mahrī had related to him, from his father, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ: Muʿādh ibn Jabal intended to travel and said:

“Prophet of God, give me counsel.” He replied: “Worship God and associate nothing with Him.” He said: “Prophet of God, give me more.” He replied: “When you do wrong, do good in return.” He said: “Prophet of God, give me more.” He replied: “Be upright, and make your character good toward people.”

Among them was Abū Ghuṭayf al-Ḥaḍramī

Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān related to us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ziyād ibn Anʿum; ʿUmārah ibn Ghurāb al-Yaḥṣubī related to me, from Abū Ghuṭayf al-Ḥaḍramī, who said: I came to the mosque, and there was ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr. He saw me and called to me, then said: “Come, I shall relate to you what I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say about your people. He came out to us while we were sitting, and when we saw him, we made room for him. He sat among us, then said: ‘Where are my companions, those who are of me and I am of them, and who will enter with me?’ We fell silent. Then he stood and went inside. He remained for a little while, then came out to us and sat as he had before. Then he stood and went inside. We said:

‘Why did we not ask the Messenger of God ﷺ who they are?’ Then he came out to us and said the same thing.

“We said: ‘Tell us, Prophet of God.’ He replied: ‘Yes: the people of Yemen, the forthright ones at the ends of the earth, kept away from the doors of rulers; one of them dies with his need still within him, unfulfilled.’”

Among them was ʿImrān ibn ʿAbd al-Muʿāfirī

Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān related to us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ziyād ibn Anʿum; ʿImrān ibn ʿAbd al-Muʿāfirī related to me, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “There are three who incur debts for certain purposes and then die without paying them; God will pay on their behalf: a man who is in the path of God, whose strength weakens, so he takes on a debt to regain his strength, then dies without paying it; [and a man who fears temptation for himself while abroad, so he is helped to marry a woman by taking on a debt, then dies before consummating the marriage. He said: God will pay on his behalf”]; and a man who has a Muslim die in his care and can find nothing with which to shroud him or bury him except by taking on a debt, then dies without paying it: God, Mighty and Glorious, will pay it on his behalf on the Day of Resurrection. And there are three whose prayer God does not accept: a man who leads a people while they dislike him; a man who comes to prayer dibāran—he said: dibār is when one comes after the appointed time has passed—and a man who enslaves an emancipated person.

Among them was Zayd ibn Qāṣid al-Saksakī

Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān related to us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ziyād ibn Anʿum; Zayd ibn Qāṣid al-Saksakī—one of the people of Egypt who took part in the conquest of al-Andalus—related to us. He said: I asked ʿAbd Allāh about fasting while traveling. He said: “Yes. The Messenger of God ﷺ would fast and would break his fast; so I fast and break my fast.”

Among them was Ḥudayj ibn Ṣawmī al-Ḥimyarī

Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān related to us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ziyād ibn Anʿum, who said:

Ḥudayj ibn Ṣawmī al-Ḥimyarī—one of the people of Egypt—related to me, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Heedlessness is in three things: heedlessness of the remembrance of God; [heedlessness] between the dawn prayer and sunrise; and a man’s being heedless, within himself, of debt until it overtakes him.”

Among them was ʿAbd Allāh ibn Munayn

From Banū ʿAbd Kalāl.

Saʿīd ibn Abī Maryam related to me; Nāfiʿ ibn Yazīd informed us; al-Ḥārith ibn Saʿīd al-ʿAtqī informed me (165a), from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Munayn, of Banū ʿAbd Kalāl, from ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ: The Messenger of God ﷺ taught him fifteen prostrations in the Qurʾān, three of them in the Mufaṣṣal, and two prostrations in Sūrat al-Ḥajj.

Among them was Wāhib ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Muʿāfirī

ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn ʿImrān related to us; Idrīs ibn Yaḥyā, Abū ʿUmar—the resident of Khawlān—related to us; Rajāʾ ibn Abī ʿAṭāʾ al-Muʿāfirī related to us, from Wāhib ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Kaʿbī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Whoever feeds his brother bread until he is full, and gives him water until his thirst is quenched, God will place between him and the Fire seven trenches, each trench a journey of five hundred years.”

Among them was ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Rāfiʿ

Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān related to us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ziyād ibn Anʿum, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Rāfiʿ, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Knowledge is of three kinds; anything beyond that is additional: a clear verse, an established practice, and a justly apportioned obligation.”

Among them were Muḥammad ibn Hadiyyah and Muʿāwiyah ibn Khudayj al-Tujībī

They say that he has a report attributed to him.

Ibn ʿUthmān related to us; ʿAbd Allāh related to us. And:

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā related to me; Ibn Wahb informed us. Both of them, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Shurayḥ, who said: Shurāḥīl ibn Yazīd al-Muʿāfirī related to me, from Muḥammad ibn Hadiyyah, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Most of the hypocrites in my community are its reciters.” Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr related to us; ʿAbd Allāh ibn Wahb related to us; Abū Hānīʾ related to me al-Khawlānī, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mālik, from Muʿāwiyah ibn Khudayj, who said: We were all in the mosque, with Maslamah ibn Mukhallad, and they were discussing who had precedence. While they were thus engaged, ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr entered before the dawn prayer, in the darkness before dawn. Muʿāwiyah said to Maslamah: “Settle the matter between us and you, Abū Muḥammad. Tell us what you heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say about the Emigrants.” He said: “Yes. They preceded the people by forty autumns, enjoying themselves while the people were held back for the reckoning; then the second group will come one hundred autumns later.”

Among them was Abū ʿAdhabah

A Ḥimṣī.

[Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us; Muʿāwiyah ibn Ṣāliḥ related to me, from Shurayḥ ibn ʿUbayd, from Abū ʿAdhabah, who said: A man came to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb ﵁—and told him that the people of Iraq had pelted their governor with stones. ʿUmar went out in anger and led us in a prayer, during which he made a mistake, until the people began saying, “Glory be to God! Glory be to God!” When he had concluded the prayer, he turned to the people and said: “Who here is from Syria?” A man stood up, then another, then I stood up as the third or fourth. He said: “People of Syria, prepare yourselves for the people of Iraq, for Satan has laid eggs and hatched young among them. O God, they have confused matters for me, so confuse matters for them, and hasten against them the Thaqafī lad, who will judge among them by the judgment of the Age of Ignorance: he will accept nothing from those who do good among them, nor overlook anything from those who do wrong.”]

Among them was Ḥanash ibn ʿAbd Allāh

Abū Ṣadaqah Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā al-Miṣrī related to me, from Nāfiʿ ibn Yazīd, who said: Qays ibn al-Ḥajjāj informed me, from Ḥanash al-Ṣanʿānī, who related to him that he heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās say: I was riding behind the Messenger of God ﷺ when he turned toward me and said: “Young man, I shall teach you some words: Be mindful of God, and He will protect you. Be mindful of God, and you will find Him before you. When you seek help, seek help from God; when you ask, ask God. The pens have been lifted and the pages have dried. By Him in whose hand is Muḥammad’s soul, if the community were to gather to benefit you, it could benefit you only with something God had written for you; and if the community wanted to harm you, it could harm you only with something God had written against you.”

Among them was ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Waʿlah

Abū Nuʿaym related to us; Sufyān related to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Waʿlah, who said: I said to Ibn ʿAbbās: “We campaign in the East and are brought waterskins, but we do not know what they are made of.” (166a) He said: “I do not know what to tell you, except that I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: ‘Any hide that has been tanned is purified.’”

And Mālik ibn Saʿīd al-Tujībī

Zayd ibn Bishr and ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz related to me. They said: Ibn Wahb informed us; he related to me— Mālik ibn al-Khayr al-Zubādī related that Mālik ibn Saʿīd al-Tujībī had told him that he heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-ʿAbbās say: The Messenger of God ﷺ cursed wine, the one who presses it, the one who has it pressed, the one who carries it, the one to whom it is carried, the one who drinks it, the one who sells it, the one who buys it, the one who serves it, and the one to whom it is served.

Among them was ʿAbd Allāh ibn Hubayrah al-Sibāʾī

Abū al-Aswad related to us; Ibn Lahīʿah informed us, from Ibn Hubayrah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: The Messenger of God ﷺ went on one of his campaigns, and they acquired sheep. [The account then says, obscurely, that] he “made the poor Emigrants yaʿṣī.” One of his Companions said to him: “What could these people do among us? We are our own people and have made our gains.” He said, “This, and some of it.”82 The Messenger of God ﷺ said to them: “Are you granted victory by any means other than through your weak?”

Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Muthannā ibn Anas ibn Mālik al-Anṣārī related to us; Ḥumayd related to us, from Anas ibn Mālik, who said: When this verse was revealed, “You will never attain righteousness until you spend from that which you love” (3:92), or he said, “Who is it that will lend God a goodly loan?” (2:245), Abū Ṭalḥah said: “Messenger of God, will my walled garden at such-and-such a place suffice? Had I been able to keep it secret, I would not have made it public.” He said: “Put it toward the poor among the people of—”

…your house. Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Muthannā related to us: Ḥumayd al-Ṭawīl related to us, from Anas ibn Mālik, who said: al-Rubayyiʿ bt. al-Naḍr, Anas ibn Mālik’s aunt, slapped a girl and broke one of her front teeth. They asked the girl’s family to forgive her, but they refused. They offered them compensation for the injury, but they refused. So they came to the Prophet ﷺ—and he ordered retaliation. Then her brother, Anas ibn al-Naḍr, Anas ibn Mālik’s uncle, came and said: “Messenger of God, is al-Rubayyiʿ’s front tooth to be broken? No, by Him who sent you with the truth, her front tooth shall not be broken!” (166 b) The Messenger of God ﷺ—said:

“The Book of God prescribes retaliation.” Then he said: “The people forgave her and were satisfied.” The Messenger of God ﷺ—said: “Among God’s servants are those who, if they swore an oath by God, He would make it come true.”

Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Anṣārī related to us: Ḥumayd al-Ṭawīl related to us, from Anas ibn Mālik, from Umm Sulaym, that the Prophet ﷺ—came to her. She said:

“Messenger of God, your little servant, Anas, is here; pray for him.” He said: “He prayed for me concerning matters of my afterlife and this world that had never occurred to me.” He said: “O God, grant him wealth and bless him in it.” I think he said: “And prolong his life.” He said: “Then his daughter Amīnah told me that he had buried … in the years leading up to al-Ḥajjāj, nine…”

…and twenty, and I am the wealthiest of my people.

FIRST REPORTS ABOUT THE PEOPLE OF KUFA

“Qabīṣah related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Shimr ibn ʿAṭiyyah, from a man, from ʿUmar, who said: ‘The people of Iraq are the treasure of faith and the skull of the Arabs. They are God’s spear: they secure their frontier posts and reinforce the Anṣār.’”

He also said: Sufyān related to us, from Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit, from Nāfiʿ ibn Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim, who said: “The people of Kufa were mentioned in ʿUmar’s presence, and he said: ‘The leading men of the Arabs are in Kufa.’”

Qabīṣah related to us: Yūnus ibn Abī Isḥāq related to us, from Abū Isḥāq, who said: ʿUmar said: “The people of Kufa are my treasure.” He was asked: “Commander of the Faithful, why are they your treasure among the people of the garrison towns?” He said: “They secure their frontier posts and reinforce those below them, the people of Baṣra, while those above them, the people of Syria, do not reinforce them.”

REPORTS ABOUT ʿABD ALLĀH IBN MASʿŪD

Abū Nuʿaym and Qabīṣah related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Ḥārithah ibn Muḍarrib, who said: ʿUmar wrote to the people of Kufa—Qabīṣah said: “ʿUmar’s letter came to us”—“I have sent you ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir as your commander, and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd as your teacher and minister. (167 a) They are both among the distinguished Companions of Muḥammad ﷺ—and among the people of Badr. Follow their example and heed what they say. I have preferred ʿAbd Allāh for you over myself.”

“of the people of Badr. Follow their example and heed what they say. I have preferred ʿAbd Allāh for you over myself.”

Abū ʿĀṣim and Qabīṣah related to us, from Sufyān, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr, from a freedman of Ribʿī, from Ribʿī ibn Ḥirāsh, from Ḥudhayfah, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ—said: “Hold fast to the covenant of Ibn Umm ʿAbd.”

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rajāʾ related to us, from Isrāʾīl, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Ḥārith, from ʿAlī, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ—said: “If I were to appoint anyone without consulting the believers, I would appoint Ibn Umm ʿAbd.”

Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd Allāh related to us: Zuhayr related to us: Manṣūr ibn al-Nuʿmān related to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Ḥārith, from ʿAlī, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ—said: “If I were to appoint anyone from my community without consultation, I would appoint Ibn Umm ʿAbd.”

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us: Shuʿbah related to us, from al-Mughīrah, from Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAlqamah, who said: We came to Syria, and I said: “O God, grant me a righteous companion.” I sat with Abū al-Dardāʾ, and he said: “Where are you from?” I said: “From the people of Kufa.” He said: “Was there not among you the man with the tooth-stick and cushion?”—meaning ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd—“And was there not among you the one whom God protected from Satan through the words of His Prophet?”—meaning ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir—“And was there not among you the foremost one, whose distinction no one else knows: Ḥudhayfah?” Then he said: “How did ʿAbd Allāh recite, ‘By the night when it covers, and by the day when it shines forth’ (92:1–2)?”

I said: “‘And by the male and the female’ (92:3)?” He said: “These people nearly confused me, though I heard it from the Messenger of God ﷺ.”

“Was there not among you the man with the tooth-stick and cushion?”—meaning ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd—“And was there not among you the one whom God protected from Satan through the words of His Prophet?”—meaning ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir—“And was there not among you the foremost one, whose distinction no one else knows: Ḥudhayfah?” Then he said: “How did ʿAbd Allāh recite, ‘By the night when it covers, and by the day when it shines forth’ (92:1–2)?”

I said: “‘And by the male and the female’ (92:3)?” He said: “These people nearly confused me, though I heard it from the Messenger of God ﷺ.”

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā related to us: al-Masʿūdī related to us, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr, from Abū al-Malīḥ, from ʿAbd Allāh, who said that he used to wake the Messenger of God ﷺ—when he slept, screen him when he performed the ritual bath, and walk with him in seclusion.

THE NAMES OF THE CLOSE COMPANIONS OF THE MESSENGER OF GOD ﷺ

(167 b) Ḥamzah, Jaʿfar, ʿAlī, Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, Abū ʿUbaydah ibn…

al-Jarrāḥ, ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān, ʿUthmān ibn Maẓʿūn, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, Ṭalḥah ibn ʿUbayd Allāh, al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwām ﵃.

ʿAmr ibn ʿAwn related to us: Khālid informed us, from Ibn ʿAwn, from ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb, from Ḥumayd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Ibn Masʿūd, who said: “I was not kept away from my private chamber, or from this or that.”83

Ibn Numayr and ʿUthmān ibn Abī Shaybah related to me. He said: Ibn Idrīs related to us,

from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿUbayd Allāh, from Ibrāhīm ibn Suwayd, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd, from ʿAbd Allāh, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ—said to me: “Your permission to come to me means that the curtain is to be raised, and that you may hear my private conversation, until I forbid you.”

ʿAmr ibn Ḥafṣ ibn Ghiyāth related to me: my father related to us: al-Aʿmash related to us: Shaqīq ibn Salamah said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd addressed us when ʿUthmān had forbidden him, saying: “Let the one who orders me to recite [to him] read it to me! By God, I learned more than seventy sūrahs from the mouth of the Messenger of God ﷺ. The Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ—know that I am among those most knowledgeable of the Book of God, mighty and majestic is He, though I am not the best of them.”

Shaqīq said: “I sat in the circles, listening to what they said, and I heard no rebuttal to him, nor anyone say otherwise.”

Al-Ḥajjāj related to us: Ḥammād related to us, from ʿĀṣim, from Zirr, from Ibn Masʿūd, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ—and Abū Bakr ﵁—came to me after they had fled from the polytheists, while I was tending sheep belonging to Ibn Abī Muʿayṭ at Jiyād. He said: “Later I came to him and said: ‘Messenger of God, teach me some of these words.’ He said: ‘You are a learned young man.’ I learned seventy sūrahs from his mouth, and no one disputes this with me.”

Abū ʿUmar Ḥafṣ ibn ʿUmar al-Namarī related to us: Shuʿbah related to us, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, from Ibrāhīm, from Masrūq, who said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd was mentioned in the presence of ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr, and he said: “That is a man whom I shall always love, after I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ—say…”

“…Learn the Qurʾān from four: from ʿAbd Allāh, Sālim the freedman of Abū Ḥudhayfah, Muʿādh, and Ubayy ibn Kaʿb.” (168 a)

Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad related to me: Fuḍayl related to us, from Sulaymān, from Khaythamah, who said: I was with ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr when Ibn Masʿūd was mentioned. He said:

“That is a man whom I love. I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ—say: ‘Take the Qurʾān from four: Ibn Umm ʿAbd’—and he began with him—‘Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, Muʿādh ibn Jabal, and Sālim the freedman of Abū Ḥudhayfah.’”

Abū Nuʿaym related to me: al-Aʿmash related to us, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqamah, who said: A man came to ʿUmar and said: “I have come to you from a man who dictates the codices from memory.” ʿUmar was alarmed and said: “Woe to you! Watch what you say.” He became angry and rose up—meaning, away from the man—and said: “Watch what you say.” The man said: “I have come to you with nothing but the truth.” ʿUmar said: “Who is he?” He said:

“ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd.” ʿUmar said: “I know no one more entitled to that than he. And I will tell you something about ʿAbd Allāh. One night we sat up in Abū Bakr’s house, discussing some matter concerning a need of the Prophet ﷺ. We went out, and the Messenger of God ﷺ—walked between Abū Bakr and me. When we reached the mosque, there was a man reciting. The Prophet ﷺ—stood listening. I said: ‘Messenger of God, it is late.’ He nudged me with his hand to be quiet. The man recited, bowed, and prostrated; then he sat and prayed, and asked God’s forgiveness. The Prophet said…”

“The Messenger of God ﷺ—said: ‘Ask, and you will be given.’ Then he said once: ‘Whoever would be pleased to recite the Qurʾān fresh as it was revealed, let him recite it as Ibn Umm ʿAbd recites it.’ I and my companion realized that he meant ʿAbd Allāh. In the morning I went to him to give him the good news, but he said: ‘Abū Bakr got there before you. I have never raced him to a good deed without his getting there before me.’” Yaḥyā al-Qaṭṭān said to al-Aʿmash: “Didn’t Abū Khaythamah say that the man’s name was Qays ibn Marwān?”

He said: “Yes.”

Al-Ḥajjāj ibn al-Minhāl related to us: Ḥammād related to us, from ʿĀṣim, from Zirr, who said:

Abū Bakr asked him: “What did you ask for?” He said: “I said: ‘O God, I ask You for faith that does not turn back, blessing that does not end, and the companionship of the Prophet ﷺ—in the highest part of the Garden of Eternity.’”

Qabīṣah related to us: Sufyān related to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Ḥamzah ibn Mālik, who said:

ʿAbd Allāh said: “I learned seventy sūrahs from the mouth of the Messenger of God ﷺ—while Zayd ibn Thābit still had two pigtails and was playing with the boys.” (168 b)

ʿAmr ibn Ḥafṣ ibn Ghiyāth related to us: my father related to us: al-Aʿmash related to us: ʿAmr ibn Murrah related to me, from Abū al-Bakhtarī, who said: ʿAlī was asked about the Companions of Muḥammad ﷺ—and said: “Which of them are you asking me about?” They said: “About ʿAbd Allāh.” He said:

“He learned the Qurʾān and learned the Sunnah, then stopped—and that is enough knowledge for him.” They said: “Tell us about Abū Mūsā.” He said: “He was steeped in knowledge.” They said: “Tell us about Ḥudhayfah.” He said: “He was the most knowledgeable of the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ—about the hypocrites.” They said: “Tell us about ʿAmmār.”

He said: “A believing man who forgets, but remembers when reminded.” They said: “Tell us about Abū Dharr.” He said: “He retained knowledge that others were unable to bear.” They said: “Tell us about Salmān.” He said: “You ask me about Luqmān the Sage? He knew the knowledge of the first and the knowledge of the last: an ocean whose depths cannot be reached. He is one of us, the People of the House.” They said: “Tell us about yourself.” He said: “When I was asked, I gave; when they were silent, I began.”

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb and Abū ʿUmar related to us a similar report. They said: Shuʿbah related to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd, who said: We asked Ḥudhayfah about a man whose bearing and conduct were close to those of the Messenger of God ﷺ—so that we might learn from him. He said: “I know no one whose bearing, conduct, and manner are more like those of the Messenger of God ﷺ—than Ibn Umm ʿAbd.” This is Sulaymān’s wording.

Abū ʿUmar related to us, saying: Shuʿbah related to us: Abū Isḥāq related to us, saying: I heard ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd say: We asked Ḥudhayfah and said: “Tell us about a man whose bearing is close and whose conduct and manner are close to those of the Messenger of God ﷺ—so that we may learn from him.” He said: “We know no one whose bearing, conduct, and manner are closer to those of the Messenger of God ﷺ—than Ibn Umm ʿAbd, until he disappears behind a house’s wall. Those of Muḥammad’s Companions who were entrusted with preserving knowledge certainly knew that Ibn Umm ʿAbd was the closest of them to God in rank.”

Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shaybah related to us: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam related to us: Quṭbah related to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Mālik ibn al-Ḥārith, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, who said: We were in Abū Mūsā’s house (169 a) with some of ʿAbd Allāh’s Companions, looking at a muṣḥaf. ʿAbd Allāh stood up and said: “I do not know that the Messenger of God ﷺ—left behind anyone more knowledgeable than this man standing here about what God, mighty and majestic is He, revealed.” Abū Mūsā said: “If you say that, then he was present when we were absent, and he was admitted when we were kept outside.”

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā related to us, from Shaybān, from al-Aʿmash, from Abū ʿAmr al-Shaybānī, who said: I came to Abū Mūsā and mentioned to him what Ibn Masʿūd had said. He said:

“Do not ask me about anything while this report remains among you. By God, I saw him, and I can only regard him as a servant of the family of Muḥammad ﷺ.”

“ Ibn Numayr related to us: Yaḥyā ibn ʿĪsā related to us, from Sufyān, from al-Aʿmash, from Muslim, from Masrūq, who said: ʿAbd Allāh said: ‘No verse was revealed without my knowing what it was revealed about. If I knew that anyone knew the Book of God better than I did, and camels and mounts could carry me to him, I would go to him.’”

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā related to us, along with ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rajāʾ. They said: Isrāʾīl informed us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Ḥāritha, who said: “ʿUmar’s letter was read to us: ‘I have sent to you ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir as your governor, and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd as your teacher and adviser. They are both among the distinguished Companions of Muḥammad ﷺ—from the people of Badr.’ Ibn Rajāʾ added: ‘I have appointed Ibn Masʿūd over your treasury, so learn from them and follow their example.’ They both said: ‘I have preferred ʿAbd Allāh for you over myself.’”

Muḥammad ibn Abī al-Sarī related to me: ʿAbd al-Razzāq related to us: al-Thawrī informed us from al-Aʿmash, from Zayd ibn Wahb, who said: “I was sitting with ʿUmar when Ibn Masʿūd came to him. The people sitting there nearly hid him from view because of his short stature. ʿUmar laughed when he saw him. Ibn Masʿūd stood before him, speaking with him and making him laugh; then he turned and left. ʿUmar followed him with his eyes until he disappeared, and said: ‘How full of learning he was!’”

Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd related to me: Sharīk related to us, from al-Rukayn, from Nuʿaym ibn Ḥanẓala, from Jarīr ibn ʿAbd Allāh, who said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said: “O Ibn Umm ʿAbd, you have been given a considerable share of knowledge.”

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā related to us, from Misʿar, from ʿAmr ibn Murra, from Abū ʿUbayda, who said: “ʿAbd Allāh traveled on a journey, and they reported that thirst had killed him and his companions. This was mentioned to ʿUmar, and he said: ‘It is more fitting in my estimation that God cause a spring to gush forth for him, from which he and his companions might drink, than that thirst should kill him.’”

ʿUbayd Allāh related to us, from Isrāʾīl, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd, who said: “We came to Ḥudhayfa and said to him, ‘Tell us about the person closest to the Messenger of God ﷺ—in conduct, bearing, and manner, so that we may follow him and hear from him.’ He said: ‘The person closest to the Messenger of God ﷺ—in conduct, bearing, and manner was ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, until he disappeared from us in his house. Those of the Companions of Muḥammad ﷺ—who were entrusted with preserving knowledge knew that Ibn Umm ʿAbd was among those nearest to God in rank.’”

ʿUbayd Allāh related to us: Maṭar informed us, from Shaqīq, who said: “I was with Ḥudhayfa in the mosque when Ibn Masʿūd passed by. Ḥudhayfa said: ‘Those of the Companions of Muḥammad who were entrusted with preserving knowledge knew that he was the closest of them to God in rank.’”

ʿUbayd Allāh related to us: Shaybān related to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Mālik ibn al-Ḥārith, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, who said: “I came to Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, and Abū Masʿūd al-Anṣārī while they were looking at a codex. We talked for a while, then ʿAbd Allāh went out and left. Abū Masʿūd said: ‘By God, I do not know that the Prophet ﷺ—left anyone more knowledgeable of the Book of God than this man who has just left.’”

Abū ʿUmar Ḥafṣ ibn ʿUmar related to us: Shuʿba related to us: Abū Isḥāq informed us, saying: “I heard Abū al-Aḥwaṣ say: ‘I was sitting with Abū Mūsā and Abū Masʿūd when ʿAbd Allāh was mentioned. One of them said to his companion, “Do you think he left anyone like himself?” He replied, “If you say that, then indeed he used to be present when we were absent, and to enter when we were kept out.”’”

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā related to us, from Misʿar, from ʿAmr ibn Murra, from Abū al-Bukhtarī, who said: “ʿAlī was asked about ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, and he said: ‘He recited the Qurʾān and then remained devoted to it, and that is enough for him.’”84

And that is sufficient for him.

Ibn Numayr related to us: Abū Muʿāwiya related to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Shaqīq, from Ḥudhayfa, who said: “Those of the Companions of Muḥammad ﷺ—who were entrusted with preserving knowledge knew that ʿAbd Allāh was among those closest to God in rank on the Day of Resurrection.”

He also said: Abū Muʿāwiya related to us: al-Aʿmash related to us, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqama, who said: “ʿAbd Allāh resembled the Prophet ﷺ—in his conduct, manner, and bearing.”

And ʿAlqama was likened to ʿAbd Allāh.

He also said: Yaʿlā related to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū ʿUbayda, who said: “A gathering in which I would sit with Ibn Masʿūd was more reassuring to me than a year’s worth of deeds.”

Al-Ḥajjāj related to us: Ḥammād related to us: ʿĀṣim ibn Bahdala informed us, from Zirr ibn Ḥubaysh, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, who said: “I used to gather for the Messenger of God ﷺ—[branches of] arāk for toothpicks, and the wind would expose him—and his shins were slender—so the people laughed. The Prophet ﷺ—said, ‘What are you laughing at?’ They said, ‘At the slenderness of his shins.’ The Prophet ﷺ—said, ‘By Him in whose hand is my soul, they will weigh more heavily in the Balance than Mount Uḥud.’”

ﷺ—a tooth-stick from the arāk tree. The wind would lift his garment, and his shins were slender. The people laughed. The Prophet ﷺ—said, “What are you laughing at?” They said, “At the slenderness of his shins.” The Prophet ﷺ—said, “By Him in whose hand is my soul, they weigh more heavily in the Balance than Mount Uḥud.”

Abū Bakr Bundār, Muḥammad ibn Bashshār, related to us: Sahl ibn Ḥammād related to us: Shuʿba related to us, from Muʿāwiya ibn Qurra, from his father, who said: “Ibn Masʿūd climbed a tree to gather from it. The wind lifted his garment from his shin, and they laughed at the thinness of his shins. The Prophet ﷺ—said, ‘Are you laughing at the thinness of his shins? They weigh more heavily in the Balance than Mount Uḥud.’”

Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shayba related to me: Ibn Fuḍayl related to us, from Mughīra, from Umm Mūsā, who said: “I heard ʿAlī say: ‘The Messenger of God ﷺ—ordered ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd to climb a tree and bring him something from it. His Companions looked at the thinness of his shins and laughed at them.’ The Prophet ﷺ said, ‘Why are you laughing at a man whose feet weigh more heavily in the Balance than Mount Uḥud?’”

Abū al-Nuʿmān Muḥammad ibn al-Faḍl related to us: Abū ʿAwāna related to us, from Mughīra from Umm Mūsā, who said: “Ibn Masʿūd was mentioned in ʿAlī’s presence, and he said: ‘I saw him gathering from a tree, and some of the people laughed at the slenderness of his shins.’ The Prophet ﷺ said, ‘What are you laughing at? They will weigh more heavily in the Balance on the Day of Resurrection than Mount Uḥud.’”

Al-Ḥajjāj related to us: Mahdī ibn Maymūn related to us, from Wāṣil al-Aḥdab, from Abū Wāʾil, from Ḥudhayfa, who said: “Those of the Companions of Muḥammad ﷺ—who were entrusted with preserving knowledge knew that Ibn Masʿūd was among those closest to God in rank.”

Ibn Numayr related to me: Wakīʿ related to us, from al-Aʿmash, from al-ʿAlāʾ, from some elders of theirs, who said: “ʿUmar was supervising a house belonging to ʿAbd Allāh in Medina and inspecting its construction. A man of Quraysh said, ‘Commander of the Faithful, you can spare yourself this.’ He picked up a brick, threw it, and said, ‘Would you have me think less of ʿAbd Allāh?’”

“Ibn Numayr related to me: Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUbayda related to us, from his father, from al-Aʿmash, from al-ʿAlāʾ—meaning Ibn Badr—from Tamīm ibn Ḥadhlam, who said: ‘I kept company with the Prophet’s Companions, Abū Bakr and ʿUmar. I never saw anyone more detached from this world, more desirous of the Hereafter, or more beloved to me to be in his likeness than you, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd.’”

Abū Nuʿaym and Ādam related to us. They said: Al-Masʿūdī related to us: Muslim al-Baṭīn, from ʿAmr ibn Maymūn, who said: “I used to visit ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd—Ādam said: ‘for a year’—but during that time I never heard him relate anything from the Messenger of God ﷺ—except that one day he related a report. The words ‘The Messenger of God ﷺ—said’ slipped from his tongue, and distress overcame him until I saw sweat streaming down him. Then he said: ‘God willing, either more than that, or close to that, or less than that.’”

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Maslama related to us: Sufyān related to me, from ʿAmmār al-Duhnī, from Muslim al-Baṭīn, from ʿAmr ibn Maymūn, who said: “I accompanied ʿAbd Allāh for eighteen months and heard him relate only one report from the Messenger of God ﷺ. I saw him sweat, then become overwhelmed by breathlessness; then he said something like it, or similar to it.”

Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr related to us: Abū Muʿāwiya related to us: al-Aʿmash related to us, from Muslim ibn Ṣubayḥ, from Masrūq, who said: ʿAbd Allāh said: “By Him besides whom there is no god, you will not give up any practice you have been commanded to observe without God replacing it for you with something harder on you.”

Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr related to us: Abū Muʿāwiya related to us: al-Aʿmash related to us, from Ibrāhīm al-Taymī, from al-Ḥārith ibn Suwayd, who said: ʿAbd Allāh said: “I would wish that God, Mighty and Majestic, forgive me one of my sins, even if I were called ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rawtha.”

Saʿīd related to us: Hushaym related to us, from Sayyār, from Abū Wāʾil, who said: “ʿAbd Allāh said—”

“‘I would wish that God forgive my sins and that my lineage not be known.’”

Saʿīd related to us: Khālid ibn ʿAbd Allāh related to us, from Yūnus ibn ʿUbayd, from Ḥumayd ibn Hilāl, who said: Ibn Masʿūd said: “I would wish that I were ascribed to Rawtha and that God accept from me a single good deed of mine.”

Saʿīd related to us: Khālid related to us, from Yūnus ibn ʿUbayd, from Ḥumayd ibn Hilāl, who said:

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd said: “If I knew that God had accepted a deed of mine, it would be dearer to me than possessing the whole earth filled with gold.”

Saʿīd related to us: Abū Muʿāwiya related to us: al-Aʿmash related to us, from Ibrāhīm al-Taymī, from al-Ḥārith ibn Suwayd, who said: “One day they pressed ʿAbd Allāh with questions, and he said: ‘By Him besides whom there is no god, if you knew what I know, you would surely throw dust upon your own heads.’”

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us: Sufyān related to us: Ibn Shubrumah related to us, who said: “ʿAbd Allāh was speaking while Tamīm ibn Ḥadhlam sat silent. ʿAbd Allāh said, ‘Tamīm, if you can be the one who relates, then do so.’”

Qabīṣa related to us: Sufyān related to us, from al-Aʿmash, who said: “I heard Abū Wāʾil say: ‘That is a man whom I would not equate with anyone’”—meaning ʿAbd Allāh.

Sufyān related to us: Abū ʿUmays related to us, from al-Qāsim, who said: The Prophet ﷺ—said to ʿAbd Allāh: “Stand and speak.” He praised God, Mighty and Majestic, and extolled Him, and bore witness to the testimony of truth: that there is no god but God and that Muḥammad is His servant and Messenger God bless him and grant him peace. The Prophet ﷺ said: “O God, I am content for my community with what Ibn Umm ʿAbd is content for it.”

Abū Nuʿaym related to us: al-Masʿūdī related to us, from ʿAyyāsh al-ʿĀmirī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shaddād ibn al-Hād, that ʿAbd Allāh was the companion of the pillow, the tooth-stick, and the two sandals.

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us: Sufyān related to us: Saʿīd ibn al-Ḥajjāj related to us, who said:

Al-Ḥasan was asked, “Which are better, the people of Kūfa or the people of Baṣra?” Al-Ḥasan said, “He used to give precedence to the people of Kūfa.”

[Muʿādh ibn Jabal]

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us: Ḥammād related to us, from Ayyūb, from Abū Qilāba, from a man who used to serve Muʿādh, who said: “When Muʿādh fell ill with the illness from which he died, he would sometimes lose consciousness and sometimes recover. He lost consciousness so completely that we thought it was because of his condition. Then he came to, while I was facing him and weeping. He said to me, ‘What makes you weep?’ I said, ‘By God, I am not weeping for some worldly benefit I used to receive from you, nor for any kinship between us. Rather, I weep because the knowledge and wisdom I used to hear from you are going away.’ He said, ‘Do not weep, for knowledge and faith remain where those who seek them may find them. Seek them where Abraham sought them: he asked God when he did not know. Then he recited, “I am going to my Lord; He will guide me”. And after me, seek them from four men—’”

“If you find it with them; otherwise, the rest of the people are their successors: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām, Salmān al-Fārisī, and ʿUwaymir, Abū al-Dardāʾ. Beware the sage’s deviation and the hypocrite’s wisdom.” I said to him, “How can I recognize the sage’s deviation and the hypocrite’s wisdom?” He said:

“A word of error that Satan puts on the sage’s tongue: he neither embraces it nor … from him. A hypocrite may indeed speak wisdom. Take knowledge when it comes to you, for truth has a light. Beware matters that are obscure.”

Ḥammād ibn Zayd said: “We asked Khalīl ibn Aḥmad about ‘obscure matters,’ and he said: … ‘That which one examines but whose face does not open itself to you, like an eye that is closed.’”

Salama ibn Shabīb related to us: ʿAbd al-Razzāq related to us: Maʿmar informed us, who said: “I heard al-Zuhrī say: ‘ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd is no more learned among us than ʿUtba ibn Masʿūd, but he died young.’”

Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmar related to us, who said: Sufyān said: “I heard al-Zuhrī say: ‘ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd did not precede his brother ʿUtba in migration, but ʿUtba died before him.’”

Muḥammad ibn Fuḍayl related to me: Shuʿba related to us, from ʿAmr ibn Murra, who said: “I asked Abū ʿUbayda, ‘Did you see your father?’ He said, ‘No.’”

Muḥammad ibn Bashshār related to me: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar related to us: Shuʿba related to us, from ʿAmr ibn Murra, who said: “I asked Abū ʿUbayda, ‘Was ʿAbd Allāh with the Prophet ﷺ’”

“On the Night of the Jinn?” He said, “No.” I asked Ibrāhīm, and he said, “If only our companion had been that man.”

Al-Ḥumaydī related to us: Yaḥyā ibn Sulaymān related to us, from Ibn Khuthaym, from al-Qāsim ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from his father ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, who said: “Al-Walīd ibn ʿUqbah delayed the prayer in Kūfah. ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd stood up and called the people to prayer, then led them in prayer. He then returned to his seat, while I was with my father. The messenger of al-Walīd ibn ʿUqbah came (172b) and said:

“‘Al-Walīd asks you: What made you do what you did?’”

Salmān al-Fārisī

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us: Sufyān related to us; he said: I heard ʿAmmār—I mean al-Duhnī—say: “Salmān al-Fārisī’s stipend was four thousand, along with a bundle of clothing. He would give it in charity and work with palm fronds.”

Abū Bishr related to me: Saʿīd ibn ʿĀmir related to us; he said: ʿAwf related to us, from Abū ʿUthmān, who said: “Salmān said to me, ‘Abū ʿUthmān, have you seen Rāmhurmuz?’ He said:

“‘For I am one of its people.’”

What has been related about ʿAlqamah ibn Qays al-Nakhaʿī and his companions

Abū Saʿīd Yaḥyā ibn Sulaymān related to us: Wakīʿ related to us, from Sufyān, from— Manṣūr, from Ibrāhīm, who said: “The knowledge of the people of Kūfah came down to six of the companions of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd. They were the ones who gave legal opinions to the people, taught them, and gave them legal opinions: ʿAlqamah ibn Qays al-Nakhaʿī; al-Aswad ibn Yazīd al-Nakhaʿī; Masrūq ibn al-Ajdaʿ al-Hamdānī; ʿUbaydah al-Salmānī; al-Ḥārith ibn Qays al-Juʿfī; and ʿAmr ibn Shuraḥbīl al-Hamdānī.”

“ Ibn Numayr related to us: Abū Muʿāwiyah related to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrāhīm, who said: ‘ʿAlqamah was likened to ʿAbd Allāh.’”

Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shaybah related to us: Abū Usāmah related to us: al-Aʿmash related to us: ʿUmārah related to us, from Abū Maʿmar, who said: “We were sitting with ʿAmr ibn Shuraḥbīl when he said:

“‘Come with us to the person most like ʿAbd Allāh in manner and bearing.’ He did not reveal where he was going until we set out for—” him, until we went to ʿAlqamah.”

“ ʿAmr ibn Ḥafṣ ibn Ghiyāth related to us: my father related to us: al-Aʿmash related to us: ʿUmārah related to us, from Abū Maʿmar, who said: ‘We were with ʿAmr ibn Shuraḥbīl, and he said, “Let us go to the person most like ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd in manner, bearing, and conduct.” We went with him. He gave no indication of where he meant to go until he brought us to ʿAlqamah.’”

Ismāʿīl ibn al-Khalīl related to us: ʿAlī ibn Mushir related to us: al-Aʿmash informed us, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqamah, who said: “I was sitting with Ḥudhayfah and Abū Masʿūd al-Anṣārī when a man came and sat before them. He asked them about an inheritance allotment. Each of them began looking at the other, and neither answered him. The man said to them:

“‘Will you not answer me about what I asked you?’ They fell silent and gave him no answer. I said to them:

“‘If you wish, I can tell you what ʿAbd Allāh used to say about it.’ They said, ‘Is there someone among you who has memorized what he said?’ I said, ‘Yes.’ (173a) ‘ʿAbd Allāh used to say such-and-such.’ They said, ‘We did indeed relate that it was so, but we feared that we might have forgotten.’”

Abū Nuʿaym related to us: al-Aʿmash related to us, from Ibrāhīm, who said: ʿAlqamah said:

“What I memorized when I was young is as if I can see it before me on a sheet or piece of paper.”

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā related to us, from Isrāʾīl, from Ghālib Abū al-Hudhayl, who said:

“I asked Ibrāhīm, ‘Was ʿAlqamah superior, or al-Aswad?’ He said, ‘ʿAlqamah—and he had been present at Ṣiffīn.’”

Ibn Numayr related to us: ʿĪsā ibn Yūnus related to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Mālik ibn al-Ḥārith, who said: “ʿAlqamah was asked, ‘Will you not go out and teach the people?’ He said, ‘If I go out, they will follow at my heels and say, “This is ʿAlqamah.”’ They said, ‘Then why not visit the ruler and benefit from him?’ He said, ‘I gain nothing from their worldly life without their taking an equal amount from my religion.’”

Ibn Numayr related to us: Wakīʿ related to us: al-Aʿmash related to us, from Ibrāhīm, who said: “ʿAlqamah said to Masrūq, ‘Write down the parallels for me.’ Masrūq said, ‘Did you not know that writing things down is disapproved of?’

“ʿAlqamah said, ‘I will only look at it, then erase it.’ Masrūq said, ‘There is no harm in that.’”

Ibn Numayr related to us: my father related to us: al-Aʿmash related to us, from Ibrāhīm, who said: “When ʿAlqamah proposed marriage, he would choose a family of lower standing than his own.”

Qabīṣah related to us: Sufyān related to us, from Manṣūr, from Ibrāhīm: “Abū Burdah wrote to ʿAlqamah about the delegation, and ʿAlqamah wrote back to him: ‘Erase me, erase me.’”

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us: Sufyān related to us, from Abū Isḥāq, who said: “ʿAlqamah was one of the deeply learned men.”

“ Ibn Numayr related to us: Ibn Idrīs related to us, from his uncle, from al-Shaʿbī, who said:

“‘Shurayḥ was the most knowledgeable of them in judicial matters, and ʿUbaydah was Shurayḥ’s equal in judicial matters.’” ʿAlqamah adhered to the position of ʿAbd Allāh, while Rabīʿ ibn Khuthaym was the most scrupulous of the group and the least learned.

Ibn Numayr related to us: Ḥafṣ related to us, from Ashʿath, from Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn, who said:

“I came to Kūfah, where there were four men counted among its jurists. Whoever began with al-Ḥārith named ʿUbaydah second; whoever began with ʿUbaydah named al-Ḥārith second. ʿAlqamah was third and Shurayḥ fourth.” Then Ibn Sīrīn would say: “If four men, the least of whom is Shurayḥ, are the best, [then—]”

Ibn Numayr related to us: Ḥafṣ related to us, from Ashʿath, from Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn, who said: “I came to Kūfah, where there were four hundred people seeking knowledge.”

Abū Saʿīd ʿAbd Allāh ibn Saʿīd al-Ashajj related to me: Ḥafṣ ibn Ghiyāth related to us, from al-Aʿmash, who said: “Fiṭr and I went to ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī al-Hudhayl to ask him about a report. He said, ‘ʿUthmān is being killed, and you ask about reports!’”

Abū Saʿīd related to us: Abū Muʿāwiyah informed me, from al-Aʿmash, who said: “Abū— Ṣāliḥ, whenever ʿUthmān was mentioned, would weep until he said, ‘Hāh, hāh.’”

Abū Saʿīd related to me: Ibn Idrīs informed me, from al-Aʿmash, from Ṭalḥah ibn Muṣarrif, who said: “My heart would accept nothing but love for ʿUthmān.”

“ Ādam related to us: Shuʿbah related to us, from al-Mughīrah, from Ibrāhīm, who said: ‘ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd gave ʿAlqamah ibn Qays the kunya Abū Shibl. ʿAlqamah was childless; no children were born to him.’”

Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥīm related to me: ʿAlī related to us, who said: “The people most knowledgeable about ʿAbd Allāh were ʿAlqamah, al-Aswad, ʿUbaydah, (174a) al-Ḥārith ibn Qays, ʿAmr ibn Shuraḥbīl, and another man he named. The knowledge and reports of these men came down to Sufyān ibn Saʿīd. After Sufyān, Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd favored this line of transmission and followed it.”

Aḥmad ibn al-Khalīl related to us: Abū Aḥmad al-Zubayrī related to us: Sufyān related to us; he said: I heard Zubayr say: I heard Saʿīd ibn Jubayr say:

“The companions of ʿAbd Allāh were the elders of this community.”

[Al-Aswad ibn Yazīd]

Abū Nuʿaym related to us: Ḥanash ibn al-Ḥārith related to us; he said: “I saw al-Aswad ibn Yazīd after one of his eyes had been lost from fasting.”

He also said: Ḥanash related to us, from Ziyād al-Nakhaʿī, who said: “Al-Aswad used to fast while travelling until his color changed from thirst on a hot day, while one of us would drink repeatedly before even finishing with his riding beast, outside of Ramaḍān.”

Abū Nuʿaym related to us: Ḥanash related to us: ʿAlī ibn Mudrik related to us, that ʿAlqamah used to say to al-Aswad, “Why do you torment this?” He would reply, “I only intend rest by it.”

Abū Nuʿaym related to us: Ḥanash related to us, from Ziyād al-Nakhaʿī, who said: “I travelled with al-Aswad to Mecca. When the time for prayer came, he would dismount whatever the circumstances, and if he was on rough ground, he would dismount and pray. If his camel’s foreleg was going up or down, he would make it kneel and would not wait.

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us: Sufyān related to us, from Misʿar, who said: “Abū Wāʾil would visit al-Aswad ibn Yazīd and say, ‘Every time I have come to you, I have wished that people would announce your death to me.’ Al-Aswad said, ‘I would grieve over losing a month of life in which God might record fifty prayers for me.’ Misʿar said: ‘The people found al-Aswad’s response more remarkable.’”

Ismāʿīl ibn al-Khalīl related to me: Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh related to us, from ʿĀṣim ibn Kulayb, from his father, who said: “I met ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Aswad walking beside a wall. I said to him, ‘What is the matter with you?’ He said, ‘I dislike someone coming up to me and asking me about something.’

“I said to him, ‘But ʿUmar used to tread heavily upon the earth and had a powerful voice.’”

[Masrūq ibn al-Ajdaʿ]

Abū al-Walīd Hishām ibn ʿAbd al-Malik and Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to me; both said: Saʿīd related to us, from Abū Isḥāq, who said: “Masrūq performed the pilgrimage [and] slept only prostrating on his face.”

Abū al-Nuʿmān related to us: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, from Anas ibn Sīrīn (174b) who said: “We heard in Kūfah that Masrūq used to flee from the plague.” Muḥammad rejected this.

He said: “He said, ‘Come with me to his wife; we will ask her.’ We went in to her and asked her about that. She said, ‘No, by God, he did not flee. Rather, he used to say, “These are days of distraction, and I would like to devote myself to worship.”’ He was an old man who would withdraw for worship. She said, ‘Sometimes I would sit behind him and weep at what I saw him doing to himself. He would pray until his feet swelled.’ She said:

“‘I heard him say: “The plague, abdominal illness, childbirth, and drowning: whoever dies in one of these as a Muslim has martyrdom as his reward.”’”

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us: Sufyān related to us: Ayyūb ibn ʿĀʾidh al-Ṭāʾī related to us; he said: “I asked al-Shaʿbī about a man who had vowed to slaughter his son. He said, ‘Perhaps you are one of the dealers in people! I have never seen anyone, in any region, more avid for knowledge than Masrūq.’” He said, “There is no vow in an act of disobedience.”

Ismāʿīl ibn al-Khalīl related to me: ʿAlī ibn Mushir related to us: al-Aʿmash informed us, from Muslim, who said: “Masrūq ibn al-Ajdaʿ was a man afflicted by a head wound. He used to say:

“‘I would not be pleased to have in exchange for it such-and-such of this world. Were it not for it, I would not feel secure from some of these trials overwhelming me.’” He was at al-Silsilah, then came to Kūfah and bought a ram—

for twenty-two dirhams. He had no cash, so he borrowed them from one of his neighbors. He entered the palace, and I was with him. Some people met him and praised him, saying, “May God reward you with good. You have acted justly and done well.” He did no more than recite this verse: “Is one to whom We have made a good promise”—until he reached: “Then on the Day of Resurrection he will be among those brought forth”.

Aḥmad ibn Yūnus related to us: Zuhayr related to us, saying: I heard Abū Isḥāq say:

Abū Maysara ʿAmr ibn Shuraḥbīl used to say, “Would that my mother had never borne me!” His wife said to him, “Why, Abū Maysara?” He replied, “Because I have been promised that I shall arrive, but I have not been promised that I shall depart.”

Abū Bakr ibn Bashshār related to us: Abū Dāwūd and Sālim related to us, saying: Shuʿba related to us, from Abū Isḥāq, who said: Ḥudhayfa said, “Ṣilat ibn Zufar’s heart is made of gold.”

(175a)

Ibn Bashshār related to us: Umayya ibn Khalaf related to us, saying: Shuʿba said: I was with Abū Isḥāq when a man said to him, “Shuʿba says that you heard nothing from ʿAlqama.”

He said, “He is right.”

Qabīṣa related to us: Yūnus ibn Abī Isḥāq related to us, from Abū Isḥāq, who said: ʿAmr ibn Maymūn, whenever he entered the mosque and was seen, would remind people of God.

Volume Two

Reports about al-Rabīʿ ibn Khuthaym

Abū Nuʿaym and Qabīṣa related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, from Manṣūr, from Ibrāhīm, who said:

So-and-so said, “I do not think al-Rabīʿ ibn Khuthaym has spoken a word in twenty years except one that ascends.”

Abū Nuʿaym and Qabīṣa related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, from Nuṣayr ibn Dhuʿlūq, from Ibrāhīm al-Taymī, who said: Someone who had kept al-Rabīʿ ibn Khuthaym’s company for twenty years informed me that he had heard no word from him that could be faulted.

Qabīṣa related to us: Sufyān related to us, from a man of Banū Taymi Allāh, from his father, who said:

I kept company with al-Rabīʿ ibn Khuthaym for two years, and he never asked me about anything concerning people. Once, however, he said to me, “Is your mother alive? How many mosques do you have?”

He also said: Sufyān related to us, saying: I was told that al-Rabīʿ ibn Khuthaym had not been seen sitting in any gathering since he first girded himself with his waist-wrap.

Abū Nuʿaym related to us: Sufyān related to us, from Nuṣayr ibn Dhuʿlūq, from Hubayra ibn Khuzayma, who said: When al-Ḥusayn was killed, al-Rabīʿ ibn Khuthaym said to me, “O God, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the seen…”

“…and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the seen, You will judge between Your servants concerning that over which they differed” (39:46).

[Abū Nuʿaym] related to us: Sufyān related to us, from his father, who said: When al-Rabīʿ ibn Khuthaym was asked, “How have you come to the morning?” he would say, “We have come to the morning weak and sinning, eating our provisions and awaiting our appointed times.”

“Abū Nuʿaym related to us: Sufyān related to us, saying: Al-Rabīʿ ibn Khuthaym said, ‘Some reports have a radiance like the radiance of day, and you recognize them; and some reports have a darkness like the darkness of night, and you reject them.’”

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rajāʾ related to us: Isrāʾīl informed us, from Saʿīd—that is, Saʿīd ibn Masrūq—from Mudir al-Thawrī, from al-Rabīʿ ibn Khuthaym, who said: Whenever a man came to him, he would say, “Servant of God, fear God regarding what you know. Whatever has been kept from you, leave to its Knower. I fear for you more on account of deliberate action than I do on account of error. Those who are best among you today are not truly good; rather, they are better than those who come after them, who are worse than they are. They do not follow the truth as it ought to be followed, nor do they flee from evil as one ought to flee from it. Not everything that was revealed to Muḥammad ﷺ—has reached you; then, do you understand everything you recite? Then he said, ‘The innermost secrets’—three times—‘which are hidden from people but are manifest to God: seek their remedy.’ Then he would say, ‘And what is their remedy?’ You repent, then do not return to it.”

Abū Nuʿaym related to us: al-Rabīʿ ibn al-Mundhir al-Thawrī related to us, from his father, who said: Al-Rabīʿ ibn Khuthaym used to say, “Whoever fears God, He will make a way out for him.” Then he would say, “From everything that has become constricted for people.”

Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr related to us: Khalaf ibn Khalīfa related to us, from Yasār, from Abū Wāʾil, who said: My brother and I set out until we came in to al-Rabīʿ ibn Khuthaym. There he was, seated in his mosque. We greeted him, and he returned our greeting. Then he said to us, “What brings you here?”

We said to him, “You remember God, and we remember Him; you praise God, and we praise Him with you.” He raised his hands and said, “Praise be to God, since you did not say, ‘We have come so you can drink and we can drink with you, or so you can commit adultery and we can commit adultery with you.’”

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rajāʾ related to us: Isrāʾīl informed us, from Saʿīd, from Abū Wāʾil…

who said: We came to al-Rabīʿ ibn Khuthaym at his house. A man said, “You are going to meet a man who, if he tells you something, tells you the truth, and if you entrust him with something, he will not betray you.” We went in to him, and he said, “Praise be to God, who kept you from coming to me so that I might commit adultery and you commit adultery with me, or so that I might steal and you steal, or so that I might drink and you drink with me.”

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rajāʾ related to us: Isrāʾīl informed us, from Saʿīd, from Mundhir, from al-Rabīʿ ibn Khuthaym, who said: He used to say, “Speak good, do good, persist in what is good in that, and do much good. Regard evil as little. Do not let your hearts grow hard, and do not let the passage of time seem long to you. Do not be like those who said, ‘We hear,’ while they do not hear” (8:21).

(176a)
