“‘I had brought with me for the Messenger of God ﷺ a water-skin with a cloth over its mouth. I poured the milk into it until its lower part had cooled. Then I went to the Messenger of God ﷺ and found that he had awakened. I said, “Drink, Messenger of God.” The Messenger of God drank—’”

“—until I was satisfied. Then I said, ‘It is time to depart, Messenger of God.’

“He said: We set out, while the people were pursuing us. None of them caught up with us except Surāqa ibn Juʿshum on his horse. I said, ‘The pursuer has caught up with us, Messenger of God.’ He said:

“‘Do not grieve; God is with us’ (9:40). When he drew near to us, and was within two or three spear-lengths, I said, ‘The pursuer has caught up with us, Messenger of God,’ and I wept. He said:

“‘Why are you weeping?’ I said, ‘By God, I am not weeping for myself; I am only weeping for you.’

“He said: The Messenger of God ﷺ prayed against him, saying, ‘O God, protect us from him however You will.’ His horse sank into the ground up to its belly, and he jumped off it. Then he said:

“‘Muḥammad, I know this is your doing. Pray to God, Mighty and Majestic, to rescue me from what I am in. By God, I shall turn the pursuers behind me away from you. Here is my quiver; take an arrow from it, for you will pass by my camels and sheep at such-and-such a place, so take what you need from them.’ The Messenger of God ﷺ said, ‘We have no need of your camels.’ The Messenger of God ﷺ prayed for him, and he turned back to his companions. The Messenger of God ﷺ and I continued until we reached Medina by night. The people disputed among themselves over which of them would host him. The Messenger of God ﷺ said, ‘We shall stay only with Banū al-Najjār, the maternal uncles of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib; by this I honor them.’ The Messenger of God ﷺ went out, and we reached Medina. The people were in the roads and on the rooftops, and the boys and servants— [were shouting,] “The Messenger of God has come! Muḥammad has come! God is greatest! The Messenger of God ﷺ has come!” When morning came, he set out and alighted where he had been instructed.

Ibn Rajāʾ added: The Messenger of God ﷺ prayed facing the direction of the Holy House for seventeen months, or sixteen months. The Messenger of God ﷺ wished to face the Kaʿba, so God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: “We have seen you turning your face toward heaven, so We shall surely turn you toward a direction that pleases you. Turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque” (2:144). So he turned toward the Kaʿba. The foolish among the people—that is, the Jews—said, “What has turned them away from the direction of prayer they had been facing?” (2:142). Then God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: “Say: To God belong the East and the West; He guides whom He wills to a straight path” (2:142).

He said: A man prayed with the Prophet ﷺ, then left after praying and passed a group of the Anṣār who were bowing in the afternoon prayer, facing the direction of the Holy House. (195a) He testified to them that he had prayed with the Messenger of God ﷺ, and that he had been turned toward the Kaʿba. The people turned around until they faced the Kaʿba.

Al-Barāʾ said: “The first of the Emigrants to arrive among us was Muṣʿab ibn ʿUmayr, the brother of Banū ʿAbd al-Dār ibn Quṣayy. I asked him, ‘What has the Messenger of God ﷺ done?’ He said, ‘He is where he is, and his companions are following behind me.’ Then, after him, ʿAmr ibn Umm Maktūm, the brother of Banū Muḍar, came to us. We asked, ‘What have the Messenger of God ﷺ and his companions done?’ He said, ‘They are following behind me.’ Then ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir, Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, and Bilāl came to us. Then ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb came to us with twenty riders. Then the Messenger of God ﷺ came to us after them.”

Abū Nuʿaym and ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā related to us, both saying: Sufyān ibn Saʿīd ibn Masrūq ibn Ḥamza al-Thawrī—of Thawr of Hamdān—related to us, from Abū Isḥāq, ʿAmr ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Sabīʿī, who said: I was granted an allowance of forty dirhams in the time of Muʿāwiya.

Through the same chain, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Barāʾ: When the Prophet ﷺ returned from a journey, he would say, “Returning, repenting, and praising our Lord.”

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā related to us: Sufyān informed us, from Abū Isḥāq, who said:

“I heard al-Barāʾ when a man came to him and said, ‘Abū ʿUmāra, did you turn your backs on the day of Ḥunayn?’ He said, ‘As for me, I testify that the Messenger of God ﷺ did not turn his back. Rather, the swiftest of the people rushed forward, and Hawāzin showered them with arrows. Abū Sufyān ibn al-Ḥārith was holding the bridle of his white mule, saying:

“‘I am the Prophet; no lie,

“‘I am the son of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib.’”

Muslim ibn Ibrāhīm related to us: Shuʿba related to us, from Abū Isḥāq, who said:

“The people went out to pray for rain. Zayd ibn Arqam was among them, with only one man between him and me. I said, ‘Abū ʿAmr, how many campaigns did the Prophet ﷺ undertake?’ He said, ‘Nineteen.’

“I asked, ‘How many did you undertake with him?’ He said, ‘Seventeen.’ ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yazīd led us in a two-unit prayer.”

Al-Ḥajjāj ibn al-Minhāl and Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr related to us, both saying: Abū ʿAwāna related to us, from Abū (195b) Isḥāq, who said: I saw ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib delivering the Friday sermon. Abū ʿAwāna said: I asked him, “At what time would he pray?”

He said, “At about the time we pray.” That was during the governorship of Yūsuf ibn ʿUmar; he would not pray until the sun had passed its zenith.

Al-Ḥumaydī related to us: Sufyān related to us, from Abū Isḥāq, who said: I saw ʿAlī, whose head and beard were white. I saw ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwa, his waist-wrapper reaching halfway down his shins.

Qabīṣa related to us: Sufyān related to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Ḥāritha ibn Wahb al-Khuzāʿī, who said: “At Minā, during the Farewell Pilgrimage, we prayed two units with the Prophet ﷺ—as numerous and as secure as people could be.”

Through the same chain, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAmr ibn Ḥurayth, who said:

“The Companions of the Prophet ﷺ used to pray on Friday. ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr sent word to ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yazīd al-Khaṭmī, ‘Lead the people in the prayer for rain.’ He went out, and the people went out with him. Zayd ibn Arqam and al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib were among them.”

Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Makhzamī related to me: Isḥāq ibn Sulaymān related to us who said: Abū Sinān related to us, from Abū Isḥāq, who said: I saw some of the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ wearing their waist-wrappers halfway down their shins. Among them were al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib, Usāma ibn Zayd, and Zayd ibn Arqam.

Muḥammad related to me: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam related to us, from Isrāʾīl, from Abū Isḥāq, who said: I saw ʿAdī ibn Ḥātim, a large-bodied, one-eyed man. I saw him prostrating on a wall whose height above the ground was a cubit or nearly a cubit.

Aḥmad ibn Yūnus related to us: Zuhayr related to us: Abū Isḥāq related to us:

“He prayed the Friday prayer behind ʿAlī, who prayed it in the late morning, after the sun had passed its zenith. He saw him standing, white-bearded and bald at the forepart of his head.”

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā related to us, from Isrāʾīl, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū Juḥayfa Wahb al-Suwāʾī: He prayed the afternoon prayer with the Messenger of God ﷺ at al-Abṭaḥ, in two units. Abū Isḥāq said: He was asked, “How old were you then?” He said, “At that time I was sharpening arrows and fitting feathers to them.”

Aḥmad ibn Yūnus related to us: Zuhayr related to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū Juḥayfa: He saw the Messenger of God ﷺ, and this was from him— White—and he placed his hand upon his ʿanfaqah [the hair beneath the lower lip].

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rajāʾ related to us; he said: Isrāʾīl informed us, from Abū Isḥāq, who said:

I saw al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Qays al-Fihrī recite “Ṣād. By the Qur’an” from the pulpit. He then descended, prostrated, and ascended again.

Through the same chain, from Abū Isḥāq, from Ḥabashī ibn Junādah al-Salūlī—who was among those present at the Farewell Pilgrimage—who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Whoever asks for something despite not being in need is as though he were eating embers.”

Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm related to us; he said: Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh related to us; he said: I heard Abū Isḥāq say: “I have never seen a man with a larger mark of prostration between his eyes than ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr.”

Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Makhramī related to us; he said: Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh related to us; he said:

I heard Abū Isḥāq say: “Muʿāwiyah assigned me a stipend of three hundred. Muʿāwiyah asked me, ‘How much was your father’s stipend?’ I said, ‘Three hundred.’ He said, ‘Then Muʿāwiyah assigned me a stipend of three hundred.’”

He said: That was how they would set a man’s stipend at the same amount as his father’s.

Abū Bakr said: I came upon Abū Isḥāq when his stipend was one thousand dirhams, including supplementary allowances.

He said: I heard Abū Isḥāq say: “I went on six or seven campaigns in the time of Ziyād.” Abū Bakr said: Ziyād had died before Muʿāwiyah.

Al-Faḍl ibn Ziyād related to me, from Aḥmad, who said: Mubārak used to report from al-Ḥasan without naming his intermediary. He was asked, “Did he practice tadlīs?” He replied, “Yes.” He said: One day he related a report from al-Ḥasan, but when he was challenged about it, he said, “Some of the scholars of ḥadīth related it to me, from Abū Ḥarb, from Yūnus.” I said to him, “What about Abū al-Ashhab?” He said, “Is there something [to say] about him?” I said, “Didn’t Bahz say, ‘We challenged him, and he clarified it for us’?” He said, “Yes, whenever he was challenged.” Then he said, “Some people practiced tadlīs.” He then mentioned al-Aʿmash. He said: “Hushaym did it frequently”—meaning tadlīs—“and so did Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah. Then Abū Ḥarrah, the associate of [—]”96

He then said:

“Abū Ashhab used to practice tadlīs, except that in Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd’s book he makes clear when a report was heard directly: he says, ‘He related to me.’ When it was not [heard directly, he says], ‘Abū al-Zinād said,’ ‘Abū al-Zinād mentioned,’ or ‘So-and-so said.’”

“Abū Yūsuf said: ‘Our companions unanimously agree that Abū Nuʿaym was unsurpassed in precision and memorization, and that he is a reliable authority.’” Sufyān al-Thawrī was likewise in his time. Abū Isḥāq was a man among the Successors, one on whom people relied for ḥadīth, as they did on al-Aʿmash—though they and Sufyān practiced tadlīs. Tadlīs is an old practice.

Muḥammad ibn Bashshār related to us; he said: ʿAbd al-Kabīr ibn ʿAbd al-Majīd al-Ḥanafī related to us; he said: ʿAbbād ibn Rāshid related to us, from Qatādah, from Anas ibn Mālik. He mentioned an account. A man said to Qatādah, “Did I hear this from Anas?” He replied, “Yes.” A man asked Anas, “Did you hear it from the Messenger of God ﷺ?” He replied, “Yes. And someone who did not lie related it to me.”

“By God, we did not lie, nor did we know what lying was.”

Abū Yūsuf said: I was told that Shuʿbah said: “Sufyān related a ḥadīth to me, from Manṣūr, from Ibrāhīm. Shuʿbah said: ‘I would not be pleased to have [such-and-such] of this world if I were to say of him, “Manṣūr said,” and not mention Sufyān.’” Misʿar ibn Kidām said of tadlīs: “It is sweet and lowly.” ʿAbd al-Wārith ibn Saʿīd said: “It is humiliation.”

[Sulaymān ibn Mihrān al-Aʿmash]

Ibn Numayr related to us; he said: Wakīʿ related to us; he said: Al-Aʿmash related to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Barāʾ, who said: “Not everything we relate to you did we hear from the Messenger of God ﷺ. Rather, we heard things and our companions related them to us; but we do not lie.”

I heard Abū Nuʿaym say: Al-Aʿmash related to us, from Ibrāhīm, from al-Aswad, from ʿĀʾishah: “The Messenger of God ﷺ once sent sacrificial sheep.”

“Abū Nuʿaym related to us; he said: Al-Aʿmash related to us, from Ibrāhīm, who said: ʿAlqamah said:

‘I memorized it when I was young, and it is as though I can see it on a sheet or a piece of paper.’”

Abū Nuʿaym related to us; he said: Al-Aʿmash related to us, from Sufyān, from Salamah who said: ʿAbd Allāh said: “When we prayed behind the Prophet ﷺ we used to say, ‘Peace be upon God, the Mighty and Majestic, and upon His servants; peace be upon Gabriel and Michael; and upon so-and-so and so-and-so.’ The Messenger of God ﷺ turned toward us and said: ‘God, the Mighty and Majestic, is Peace. When one of you prays, let him say: “Greetings belong to God, as do prayers and good things. Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and God’s mercy and blessings. Peace be upon us and upon God’s righteous servants.” For when you say this, it reaches every righteous servant of God, the Mighty and Majestic, in heaven and on earth. I bear witness that there is no deity but God, and I bear witness that Muḥammad is His servant and Messenger.’”

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us; he said: Sufyān related to us; he said: ʿUmar ibn Saʿīd and others, from al-Aʿmash, who said: “I came to al-Shaʿbī with a small matter. He said:

‘Someone like you comes for something like this?’ Then al-Shaʿbī said to me: ‘How do you recite, “By God, our Lord” (Qur’an 6:23)—or “our Lord”?’ He said: ‘And how do you recite, “For God does not guide the one who leads astray” (Qur’an 16:37)—or “does not guide the one who is led astray” (Qur’an 16:37)?’ I said: ‘“That He should not guide the one who leads astray.”’

Al-Shaʿbī said: “I heard ʿAlqamah recite it that way: ‘By God, our Lord’ (Qur’an 6:23), and ‘does not guide the one who leads astray’ (Qur’an 16:37).”

Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shaybah related to us; he said: Wakīʿ related to us; he said: Al-Aʿmash related to us; he said:

“When I was alone with Abū Isḥāq, he would relate to us the report of ʿAbd Allāh fresh and intact.”

Al-Ḥumaydī related to us; he said: Sufyān related to us; he said: Al-Aʿmash said: “Were it not for the Qur’an, I would have been a greengrocer.”

Sufyān said: ʿĀṣim said to al-Aʿmash, “Did you not recite to me?” He replied:

“Yes, but I went elsewhere for knowledge and left you.”

Ādam related to us; he said: Sufyān, from al-Aʿmash, who said: “My father recognized a man by his resemblance, and they said that the man was his brother. They disputed the matter before Masrūq ibn al-Ajdaʿ, who gave a ruling.”

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā related to us, from Shaybān, from al-Aʿmash, who said: “My father recognized a brother of his. His brother died and left property, but my father’s brother’s clients said to him, ‘You have no share in his inheritance.’ Then Iyās ibn ʿAyyāsh al-Kāhilī informed me: ‘Your father and I went to Masrūq, who was serving as judge. Masrūq said, “Do you testify that he had with him the same prohibited degrees of kinship as a brother has with his brother, and that he maintained the same ties as a brother maintains with his brother?” We said, “Yes.” So he gave him all the property.’”

Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr related to us; he said: ʿĪsā ibn Yūnus related to us; he said:

Al-Aʿmash related to us, from his father Mihrān, that Masrūq awarded him inheritance from a brother of his who was a ḥamīl.

The reports of Sufyān, Abū Isḥāq, and al-Aʿmash count as authoritative unless it is known that the narrator practiced tadlīs.

Abū Isḥāq and al-Aʿmash leaned toward Shiʿism. Al-Aʿmash’s walāʾ was to Banū Kāhil; Kāhil was a clan of Banū Asad, and his walāʾ was the walāʾ of emancipation.

[Manṣūr ibn al-Muʿtamir]

Qubayṣah related to us [on fol. 197b]; he said: Sufyān related to us, from Manṣūr, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqamah, who said: “I kept going to ʿAbd Allāh for a month about a woman whose husband had died without having consummated the marriage or stipulated a dowry for her. He said: ‘She is entitled to a dowry equal to that of women like her; she must observe the waiting period, and she is entitled to inheritance.’”

Maʿqil ibn Sinān al-Ashjaʿī said: “The Messenger of God ﷺ issued the same ruling as yours concerning a woman of ours called Barwaʿ bint Wāshiq, of Banū Rawās ibn Kaʿb.” ʿAbd Allāh was delighted by this.

Qubayṣah related to us; he said: Sufyān related to us, from Manṣūr, from Ibrāhīm, from al-Aswad, from ʿĀʾishah, who said: “I and the Messenger of God ﷺ used to bathe from the same vessel, both of us in a state of major ritual impurity. He would put his head out from the mosque while he was in retreat and I was menstruating, and I would wash it. He would tell me to wrap myself in a waistcloth, then he would be intimate with me while I was menstruating.”

Al-Ḥumaydī related to us; he said: Sufyān related to us; he said: “I saw Manṣūr. When he heard the sound of the writing tablets, he stood up.”

He said: Sufyān related to us; he said: “Manṣūr served in the government bureau. When his turn came, he would put on his clothes and stand guard. Manṣūr said to his mother: ‘If you want to marry, and have a need concerning marriage, do not let my presence prevent you.’” Sufyān said: “He meant to show filial devotion to her.”

Al-Ḥumaydī said: “Manṣūr ibn al-Muʿtamir, Abū ʿAttāb al-Sulamī, was one of the Farāqīd, from the family of ʿUtbah ibn Fayrūz.”

ʿUthmān ibn Abī Shaybah related to us; he said: Abū Nuʿaym related to us; he said: Ḥammād ibn Zayd said to me: “I saw Manṣūr in Mecca. He had reverent fear, and I do not think he used to lie.”

ʿAlī said: “Manṣūr was the most reliable of people in reports from Mujāhid.”

He also said: “He is more reliable than Ibn Abī Najīḥ in everything concerning Mujāhid and others.”

Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal said: “Salamah is precise in ḥadīth, and Qays ibn Muslim is precise in ḥadīth too. You need have no misgivings when you take their ḥadīth.” I asked, “Are Simāk’s reports inconsistent?” He replied, “Yes.”

“Aḥmad said: Al-Muʾammal related to us; he said: Sufyān related to us [on fol. 198a]; he said:

ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Abī Bashīr related to us”—Sufyān said, “He was a trustworthy elder”—“and Wāqid—”

—Aḥmad said: “He means the client of Zayd ibn Khulayda”—“and al-Ḥakīm ibn al-Daylam were two trustworthy elders.”

Abū Saʿīd al-Ashajj related to me; he said: Ḥafṣ asked al-Aʿmash about the name of Abū Razīn. He said: “Masʿūd ibn Mālik.”

Abū Nuʿaym and Qubayṣah related to us; they said: Sufyān related to us, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, Abū Yaḥyā, who said: “I heard Jundab say: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: ‘Whoever seeks to be heard by people, God, the Mighty and Majestic, will make him heard; and whoever shows off, God, the Mighty and Majestic, will expose him.’”

Ibrāhīm ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Yaḥyā ibn Salamah ibn Kuhayl related to me; he said:

My father related to me, from his father, from Salamah, from Zayd ibn Arqam, who said: “We were with the Messenger of God ﷺ on a journey. I heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy say: ‘If we return to Medina, the mightier will surely expel the lowlier from it.’ I went to the Messenger of God ﷺ and told him. Then the whole of Sūrat al-Munāfiqūn was revealed, and God, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed my vindication and confirmed my truthfulness.”

Khallād ibn Aslam related to us; he said: Al-Naḍr informed us; he said: Shuʿbah informed us; he said: Salamah related to us; he said: “I heard Abū Juḥayfah relate from the Prophet ﷺ”

Qubayṣah related to us; he said: Sufyān related to us, from Jundab ibn Abī Thābit, Abū Yaḥyā, who said: “I heard Ibn ʿUmar say: ‘O people of Iraq, you bring us difficult questions.’”

I heard Ibn ʿUmar, when he was asked about a found object, say: “Hand it over to the ruler.”

Abū al-Walīd and Ḥajjāj related to us; they said: Shuʿbah related to us, from Ḥabīb, who said: “I heard Ibn ʿAbbās when a man asked him: ‘I am in the Sawād and take a siesta; I do not want to increase [my obligation], I only want to ward it off from myself.’ He recited this verse: ‘Fight those who do not believe in God or the Last Day’ (Qur’an 9:29), and said: ‘Do not take the poll tax off their necks and place it on your own neck.’”

Aḥmad ibn al-Khalīl related to us; he said: I heard ʿAlī ibn ʿĀṣim say: “Yazīd ibn Abī Ziyād was about twenty years older than Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī” [on fol. 198b].

Abū Saʿīd al-Ashajj related to me; he said: Ḥafṣ related to us, from Abū Isḥāq al-Shaybānī, who said: “I went to Khurāsān, and Ibrāhīm was not being mentioned. I returned to find that he had issued legal opinions and died.”

“Ismāʿīl ibn [Abī] Khālid related from Ḥabīb ibn al-Kindī, who is Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit, Abū Yaḥyā.”

Abū Zayd Saʿīd ibn al-Rabīʿ and Ḥajjāj ibn Minhāl related to me; they said: Shuʿbah related to us; he said: Abū Isḥāq informed me; he said: I heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Baṣīr, from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, who said: “The Messenger of God ﷺ prayed the dawn prayer and said:

‘Is so-and-so present?’ They said, ‘No.’ He said, ‘Is so-and-so present?’ He said: ‘These two prayers are among the heaviest prayers for the hypocrites. If they knew what reward they contain, they would come to them even crawling. The front row is like the row of the angels; if you knew its merit, you would hasten to it.

A man’s prayer with another man is purer than his prayer alone, and his prayer with two men is purer than his prayer with one man. The more numerous they are, the dearer it is to God, the Mighty and Majestic.’”

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rajāʾ related to us, from Isrāʾīl, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Baṣīr, from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, who said:

Sulaymān ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān related to us; he said: Shuʿayb related to us; he said: Saʿīd ibn Abī ʿArūbah related to us, from Khālid ibn Maymūn, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Baṣīr, from his father, from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, who said:

Al-Ḥasan ibn al-Rabīʿ related to us; he said: Abū al-Aḥwaṣ related to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-ʿAyzār ibn Ḥurayth, from Abū Baṣīr, who said: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb said:

He said: ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Muʿādh related to us; he said: Ibrāhīm related to us; he said: Shuʿbah related to us— From Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Baṣīr, from his father—Shuʿba said: Abū Isḥāq said, “He heard it both from him and from his father”—who said: I heard Ubayy ibn Kaʿb say: “The Messenger of God ﷺ prayed…” He then mentioned something like the report of Saʿīd ibn al-Rabīʿ.

(199a) Abū Nuʿaym and Qabīṣa related to us. They said: Sufyān related to us, from Abū Nuhayk, from Ziyād ibn Ḥudayr, who said: “I have never seen anyone more consistently use the tooth-stick while fasting than ʿUmar.”

Abū Nuhayk’s name was al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad; someone other than Sufyān gave this name.

Abū Nuʿaym related to us. He said: Sufyān related to us, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Marwān—an Aslamī, Abū Muṣʿab, from whom Misʿar and Ḥajjāj transmitted; he was trustworthy.

Abū Nuʿaym and Qabīṣa related to us. They said: Sufyān related to us, from Abū al-Jahm, who said: I heard Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, when a man under a contract of manumission asked him about paying zakāt. He said, “No.” The man said, “My masters stipulated that I must not leave.” He said, “Leave,” or he instructed him to do so. Ibn al-Mubārak said:

“You have burdened his back, then made the whole earth a maze for him, so that he may leave if he wishes.”

His name was Ṣubayḥ ibn al-Qāsim.

Abū al-Jahm, the companion of Muṭarrif, was Sulaymān ibn al-Jahm al-Jawzajānī.

Abū Nuʿaym related to us. He said: Sufyān related to us, from Abū Farwa Muslim ibn Sālim al-Juhanī, who said: When the mother of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā died, ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUkaim came forward to lead her funeral prayer, and he was…

their imam.

Abū Farwa al-Hamdānī was ʿUrwa ibn al-Ḥārith.

Abū al-Aḥwaṣ was ʿAwf ibn Mālik ibn Naḍla.

Al-Ḥumaydī related to us. He said: Sufyān related to us, saying: Abū al-Zaʿrāʾ ʿAmr ibn ʿAmr related to us, from his uncle Abū al-Aḥwaṣ ʿAwf ibn Mālik ibn Naḍla al-Jashmī, from his father.

Abū ʿAṭiyya al-Wādiʿī was Mālik ibn ʿAwf.

Abū al-Shaʿthāʾ was Sulaym ibn Aswad al-Muḥāribī.

Abū Fākhta was Saʿīd ibn ʿAlāqa.

Abū al-Qaʿqāʿ was ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Khālid.

Abū Nuʿaym and Qabīṣa related to us. They said: Sufyān related to us, from Abū al-Sawdāʾ ʿAmr ibn ʿImrān al-Nahdī and Abū al-Rawwāʿ Mujmaʿ al-Arḥabī; both were trustworthy.

Abū al-Miqdām was Thābit ibn Hurmuz al-Ḥaddād.

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā related to us. He said: al-Aʿmash informed us. [A transmission marker: ḥāʾ.]

He said: Abū Nuʿaym related to us. He said: Sufyān related to us. Both transmitted from Abū al-Miqdām, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab: “The blood-money for a Jew and a Christian is four thousand each, and the blood-money for a Magian is eight hundred.”

Abū Nuʿaym said: “From Saʿīd” (199b). One of our companions said: “From Sufyān, who said: from ʿUmar.” ʿUmar was trustworthy; al-Aʿmash, Sufyān, and Shuʿba transmitted from him.

And Ibn Abī Nuʿm

was trustworthy.

Abū Nuʿaym related to us. He said: Ibn Abī Nuʿm al-Bajalī related to us—he was al-Ḥakam ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Nuʿm, and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān was kunya’d Abū al-Ḥakam—who said: My father related to me, from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn are the masters of the youths of the people of Paradise, except for the two cousins, Jesus son of Mary and Yaḥyā son of Zakariyyā.”

Abū al-Ḥuwayrith was ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Muʿāwiya.

Abū Nuʿaym and Qabīṣa related to us. They said: Sufyān related to us, from Abū al-Ḥuwayrith, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “I hear a child crying behind me, so I shorten the prayer out of compassion, lest his mother be distressed by it.” Shuʿba called him Abū al-Ḥuwayritha.

“Abū Nuʿaym related to us. He said: al-Aʿmash related to us—he was Sulaymān ibn Mihrān al-Aʿmash, a client of Banū Kāhil ibn Asad. Abū Nuʿaym said: ‘He died in the year 148’”—from Ibrāhīm ibn Yazīd ibn al-Aswad ibn ʿAmr ibn Rabīʿa ibn Dhuhl ibn Rabīʿa ibn Ḥāritha ibn Saʿd ibn Mālik ibn al-Nakhaʿ ibn ʿAmr. Ibrāhīm’s mother was Mulayka bt. Qays ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAlqama ibn Sulaymān ibn Kuhayl ibn…

Bakr ibn al-Mubashshir ibn al-Nakhaʿ ibn ʿAmr. She was the sister of ʿAlqama ibn Qays and was the mother of Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī. Abū Nuʿaym said: “Ibrāhīm ibn Yazīd al-Nakhaʿī died in the year 96”—from al-Aswad ibn Qays ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAlqama ibn Sulaymān ibn Kuhayl ibn Bakr ibn al-Mubashshir ibn al-Nakhaʿ ibn ʿAmr.

I heard ʿUmar ibn Ḥafṣ ibn Ghiyāth mention that he had found this lineage in the book of Ṭalq ibn Ghanām.

And Ibrāhīm ibn Yazīd ibn Sharīk al-Taymī.

Al-Shaybānī transmitted from Jawwāb al-Taymī, from Yazīd ibn Sharīk, Abū Ibrāhīm.

ʿAlī said: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd said: “I was present when al-Aʿmash was asked about the report of Abū Wāʾil that Ibn ʿAwn transmits from him. He said: ‘I do not know it.’”

ʿAlī said: Yaḥyā said: “The report of Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid, from Qays ibn ʿAbd Allāh—‘We were with him’—the report about fasting that Abū Isḥāq transmitted from Qays: Ismāʿīl did not hear it from Qays; he heard it only from Abū Isḥāq.”

(200a) Abū ʿUmar al-Namirī related to us. He said: Shuʿba related to us. He said: Abū Isḥāq informed me: “I went to Qays ibn Abī Ḥāzim to give testimony, and a cup of milk was brought to us. He said, ‘Drink.’ I said, ‘I will not eat anything.’ Qays said: I heard ʿAbd Allāh say: ‘If one of you is invited to a meal while fasting, let him say: “I am fasting.”’”

I was invited to a meal while fasting, let him say: “I am fasting.”

Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥīm related to me. He said: I asked ʿAlī about Abū ʿIyāḍ, who transmits from Mujāhid, al-Hajarī, and ʿAbd Rabbih from Abū ʿIyāḍ. He said: “He is one and the same.” I asked, “What is his name?” He said: “I do not know.”

ʿAlī said: Yaḥyā said: “What Sufyān related to me from al-Aʿmash is more firmly established in my view than what I myself heard from al-Aʿmash.”

“ʿAlī said: Yaḥyā used to say: ‘Ḥafṣ is reliable.’ I said to him: ‘But he makes mistakes.’ He replied: ‘His book is sound.’

“Yaḥyā said: ‘In Kūfa, I have seen no one like these three: Ḥarām, Ḥafṣ, and Ibn Abī Zāʾida. These men were scholars of ḥadīth.’

“ʿAlī said: ‘When Ḥafṣ brought out his books, they were as Yaḥyā had said: they contained…’”

“expressions and reports, just as Yaḥyā had said.”

ʿAlī said: In Yaḥyā’s book, from al-Aʿmash, was: “Ibrāhīm related to us.” Ibrāhīm said: “Shaqīq related to us.” Shaqīq said: “ʿAbd Allāh said: ‘This path is close at hand.’” I asked Sufyān about it, and he said: “This is the report of Manṣūr.”

He said: I heard ʿAlī say: Abū al-Ḥusayn informed me, from Ibn Idrīs, who said: “I avoided Qatāda in four reports from Anas.”

ʿAlī said: Ayyūb ibn al-Mutawakkil said to me: “A ruler passed by, and some people stood up for him. Among them was Abān ibn Taghlib, but he did not stand. He was asked, ‘Why did you not stand?’ He said, ‘I disliked humiliating the Qurʾān.’”

He said: Sufyān said: “I heard a remark from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Idrīs that I have always liked. He used to say: ‘I am delighted when a boy in the school recites a verse, but I do not like to certify it for him until I know what it is.’”

[Salama ibn Kuhayl]

Abū Saʿīd al-Ashajj related to me. He said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ajlaḥ related to us. He said:

“I saw Salama ibn Kuhayl: his head and beard were white, and he did not dye them.”

I heard (200b) Ibrāhīm ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Yaḥyā ibn Salama ibn Kuhayl say: My father, Ismāʿīl ibn Yaḥyā, related to me, from Salama ibn Kuhayl, from Jundab ibn Sufyān, who said: I heard the Prophet ﷺ say: “Whoever acts ostentatiously, God—Mighty and Majestic—is made to expose him; and whoever seeks to be heard, God—Mighty and Majestic—makes him heard. Whoever has two tongues and comes with two faces will be in the Fire with two tongues and two faces.” Salama said: “I did not hear anyone say, ‘I heard the Prophet ﷺ’ other than Jundab ibn Sufyān.”

He said: Ibrāhīm ibn Kuhayl ibn Ḥuṣayn ibn Tamāriḥ ibn Hāniʾ ibn ʿUqba ibn Mālik ibn Shihāb ibn Ḥasanayn ibn Namir ibn Kulayb ibn Namir ibn ʿUmar ibn Ḥawlā ibn Yazīd ibn al-Ḥārith ibn al-Ḥaḍramī ibn Qaḥṭān ibn ʿAlam—and he is the Prophet Hūd ﷺ—was descended from Fālij.

He said: Salama had three sons: Yaḥyā, Muḥammad, and Ibrāhīm.

Ibrāhīm said: Abū Nuʿaym informed me, from Yaḥyā ibn Salama, who said: Salama ibn Kuhayl died in the year 121, on the day of ʿĀshūrāʾ. He was brought in a litter; he died on the road to Mecca.

Ibrāhīm said: Yaḥyā ibn Salama died in the year 167.

Muḥammad ibn Salama died in the year 149. My father, Ismāʿīl ibn Yaḥyā, died in the year 195, in Shaʿbān, on the eighteenth night, a Friday, at noon. He said: “I have nearly reached seventy: sixty-eight or sixty-nine.”

He said: Ibrāhīm related to me. He said: My father related to me, from his father, from Salama, from Abū Idrīs al-Murhibī, from al-Musayyab ibn Najaba ibn Rabīʿa ibn Rabāḥ al-Fazārī, whom Khaṣafa ibn Thaqafa ibn Rabīʿa ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Taym Allāh ibn Thaʿlaba killed.

Abū Saʿīd al-Ashajj related to me. He said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ajlaḥ related to us. He said: “I saw Abū Isḥāq dyeing with henna. I saw ʿAmmār ibn Abī Muʿāwiya al-Duhnī dyeing with henna. I saw ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sharīk al-ʿĀmirī dyeing with henna. I saw Manṣūr ibn al-Muʿtamir dyeing with henna; he was the best of people in the way he stood in prayer. I saw Mughīra dyeing with henna. I saw ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥasan and Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad dyeing lightly and sparingly with henna. I saw ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib (201a), whose beard was white. I saw Yazīd ibn Abī Ziyād dyeing with henna. I saw Ibn Abī Laylā and al-Ḥajjāj ibn Arṭāʾa dyeing with wasma. I saw al-Shaybānī dyeing with henna.”

“I saw Khuṣayf, whose head and beard were white. I saw al-Mukhtār ibn Fulful dyeing with wars. I saw ʿUmar ibn Qays al-Māṣir dyeing with henna.”

Abū Saʿīd said: I asked Abū Nuʿaym about al-ʿAyzār ibn Ḥurayth. He said: “He was among us, and he was the imam of the mosque of Abū Isḥāq al-Sabīʿī.”

Abū Yūsuf said: al-Faḍl said: Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal said: “ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Rāzī was transmitted from by al-Ḥakam, al-Aʿmash, Ibn Abī Laylā, Saʿīd ibn Masrūq, al-Ḥajjāj, and Fiṭr. His grandmother had been ʿAlī’s concubine, and he was judge over al-Rayy.”

Qabīṣa related to us. He said: Sufyān related to us, from ʿUbayd al-Laḥḥām ibn [Abī] Umayya—he was Abū Yaʿlā ibn ʿUbayd—from a man, from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: “They reduce much from a great deal, while you reduce little from a small amount.”

Aḥmad ibn Yūnus related to us. He said: Zuhayr related to us, from ʿUthmān ibn Ḥakīm, who was called…

al-Aḥlāfī.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rajāʾ related to us, from ʿAmr ibn Abī al-Miqdām al-Ḥaddād.

Abū Yūsuf said: I heard Abū al-Walīd Hishām ibn ʿAbd al-Malik say: “We wrote down reports from him, and we transmit from him.” Someone said to him: “Ibn al-Mubārak criticized him.” Abū al-Walīd said: “He followed the Zaydī doctrine, but there was nothing wrong with him.”

Abū Nuʿaym and Qabīṣa related to us. They said: Sufyān related to us, from ʿAlī ibn al-Aqmar, who said: Abū Juḥayfa informed me: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “I do not eat while reclining.”

Abū Nuʿaym related to us. He said: Sufyān related to us, from ʿAlī ibn al-Aqmar, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, concerning “Successful indeed is he who purifies himself.” He said: “He gave a small amount.”

I heard Muḥammad ibn Fuḍayl say: “ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and Abū Nuʿaym arrived and met in the Sacred Mosque. Abū Nuʿaym mentioned this report, and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān objected to it. Neither of them knew the other. Abū Nuʿaym got up from him, looking somewhat angry. Then one of the leading Kūfan scholars of ḥadīth met him and said:

“‘Abū Nuʿaym, what do I see in your face?’

“He said: ‘I sat with a man dressed in women’s clothes. I mentioned to him the report of ʿAlī ibn al-Aqmar, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, and he rejected it.’

“(201b) He was told: ‘Abū Nuʿaym, that was ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Mahdī.’”

ʿAlī was trustworthy. Misʿar, Manṣūr, and Mālik ibn Mighwal transmitted from him.

Al-Aʿmash—he is trustworthy. “I know of no kinship between ʿAlī ibn al-Aqmar and Kulthūm ibn al-Aqmar.”

Al-Ḥumaydī related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, from Aswad ibn Qays, from Kulthūm ibn al-Aqmar, from Shurayḥ, who said: “I do not accept the testimony of a man sitting with his knees drawn up and his garment wrapped around him.”

Asbāṭ ibn Muḥammad, Abū ʿAmr

Yaḥyā ibn Khalaf al-Jawbarī related to us, from Muʿtamir, from Abū ʿAmr al-Qāṣṣ, from ʿIkrima—and he is Muḥammad, Abū Asbāṭ.

Abū Nuʿaym related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, from Ḥammād ibn [Abī] Sulaymān, who was a client of the family of Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī.

Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm related to us, from Yaḥyā ibn Ādam, from Sharīk. He said: Sharīk was asked, “Why do you narrate so much from Ḥammād?” He replied, “I used to pass him by and go to someone else. He had a kind of madness, and I used to say, ‘I do not write from madmen.’”

Abū Nuʿaym related to us, from Sufyān, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Sulaymān, a Fazārī and one of their finest, trustworthy men. I heard al-Anṣārī Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh say in the year 211: “I have nearly reached seventy-four years of age, and my wish is that I might have authority for an hour, so that I could drive this blind-eyed, blind-hearted man out of our mosque and send him back to al-Ubulla…”

…so that he could narrate there to his paternal cousins. Abū al-Rabīʿ asked him, “Abū ʿAbd Allāh, what is the matter with him?” He replied:

“He relates that the Prophet ﷺ freed Ṣafiyya and made her emancipation her bridal gift.

“Then he says: ‘Abū ʿAmr said, “Had he given her something as a dower, that would have been dearer to me.”’” Abū al-Rabīʿ said to him, “He is misquoting him. He only said: ‘If a man today were to free his wife, it would be dearer to me that he give her a dower.’” Al-Anṣārī said, “And this is a preference for something over the act of the Messenger of God ﷺ.” Then he said: “Al-Ashʿath related to us, from al-Ḥasan, from a man who freed his slave girl and made her emancipation her bridal gift, then divorced her before touching her. He said: ‘He must return to her half her value.’”

Al-Anṣārī said: “I wrote many reports from Dāwūd ibn Abī Hind. One of our companions heard some of them from me and took my book” (folio 202a). “He was away from me for a long time, and I did not think it right to narrate any of them.

“He said: I fell seriously ill and lost consciousness. When I recovered and came to, my father told me that Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Anṣārī had visited me; I myself had no recollection of that. Dāwūd had gone to Kūfa, and Abū Muʿāwiya and Ḥafṣ ibn Idrīs heard from him there in Kūfa.

“Ibn ʿUyayna mentioned, from his father, who said: Dāwūd was called ‘the reciter.’ He would read to people in some of the villages of al-Sawād. Abū Sinān related from Thābit ibn Jābān…”

—This is how a group of them said it. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī used to say: “Ibn ʿAjlān.”

Abū Sinān is Saʿīd ibn Sinān, and the first view is more correct.

Qabīṣa related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, from al-Aʿmash, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, from Ḍirār ibn al-Azwar, who said: “I milked—or a man milked—in the presence of the Prophet ﷺ and he said, ‘The caller for milk has called.’” My father related to us, saying: al-Aʿmash related to us, saying: Yaʿqūb ibn Yaḥyā related to me, from Ḍirār ibn al-Azwar, who said: “My family sent a she-camel with me to the Messenger of God ﷺ. I brought it to him, and he ordered me to milk it, so I milked it. When I had finished and went to prepare it, the Messenger of God ﷺ said, ‘The caller for milk has called.’” Ibn Numayr related to us, from Wakīʿ and ʿUthmān, from Jarīr; and Ibn ʿUthmān related from Ibn al-Mubārak and Bundār ibn Bashshār, from Dāwūd; and Wakīʿ related from al-Aʿmash, from Yaʿqūb ibn Yaḥyā, from Ḍirār.

Abū Nuʿaym related to us, saying: Hishām al-Dastawāʾī related to us, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, from…

Abū Salama ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān: He entered upon ʿUmar and found him praying before noon. He asked, “What is this prayer?” or, “What is this?” He replied, “It is one of the night prayers.” I was told that he used to say it was from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf. He was told, “It is ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd al-Qārī,” but after he was told this, he did not give the man’s lineage.

Abū Nuʿaym related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, from Abū Ḥayyān, from Abū al-Zanbāʿ Ṣadaqa ibn Ṣāliḥ.

Abū Nuʿaym related to us, saying: Misʿar related to us, from Abū al-ʿAnbas, from al-Qāsim, from ʿĀʾisha, who said: “If I were to give this ring of mine in charity, that would be dearer to me than being given a thousand.”

(Folio 202b) Abū Nuʿaym al-Nakhaʿī, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Hāniʾ, related to us, saying: Abū al-ʿAnbas Saʿīd ibn Kathīr ibn ʿUbayd related to us.

Abū Nuʿaym related to me, saying: Abū ʿUmays related to me—his name is ʿUtba ibn ʿAbd Allāh. He is the brother of al-Masʿūdī, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd Allāh. His hadith is inconsistent, and he changed in his later years.

Abū Nuʿaym al-Faḍl ibn Dukayn related to us, saying: Yūsuf ibn Ṣuhayb related to us, from Mūsā ibn Mukhtār ibn Bilāl, from Ḥudhayfa, who said: “There are no encampments from which as much affliction is warded off as from these encampments”—meaning Kūfa.

Al-Faḍl related to us, saying: Yūsuf related to us, from Mūsā ibn Bilāl, from Ḥudhayfa, who said:

“People dispersed from the Messenger of God, God bless him and grant him peace…”

ʿUbayd Allāh and Abū Nuʿaym related to us, from Zakariyyā ibn Abī Zāʾida, Nārūq.

Ibn Rajāʾ related from ʿUmar ibn Abī Zāʾida. Zakariyyā was older than ʿUmar. “Zakariyyā [is trustworthy], and ʿUmar is acceptable.”

Abū Nuʿaym related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAjlān al-Barjamī related to us; he is trustworthy.

Abū Nuʿaym al-Faḍl ibn ʿAmr—Dukayn was his name, ʿAmr—and Qabīṣa related to us, both saying: Sufyān related to us, from Mūsā ibn Abī Kathīr, who is Abū al-Ṣabbāḥ. Misʿar and Hushaym narrated from him. He was an adherent of irjāʾ, and was one of those who went as a delegation to ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz with Dharr and others.

Aḥmad ibn al-Khalīl related to me, saying: Yaḥyā ibn Ayyūb related to us, saying: Muʿādh ibn Muʿādh related to us, saying: “We were with Ḥumayd al-Ṭawīl when Shuʿba came to him and said, ‘Abū ʿUbayd, do you have doubts about such-and-such a report?’ He replied, ‘Sometimes doubt does occur to me.’ He said, ‘You related such-and-such—did you doubt it?’ He replied in much the same way: ‘Sometimes doubt does occur to me.’ Shuʿba then left. Ḥumayd said, ‘I have no doubts about any of those reports, but he is an impudent young man, and I wanted to spoil them for him.’”

Among those from whom Shuʿba heard, but Sufyān did not hear, are:

Al-Ḥakam ibn ʿUtayba, a client of Kinda, trustworthy and a jurist.

I heard Ibn Numayr mention—God willing—from his father. He said: Sufyān was asked, “If only you had caught up with ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ and al-Ḥakam!” (folio 203a). He replied, “As for al-Ḥakam…”

“Fiṭr informed me about him, and he is truthful. He said, ‘I saw you with al-Ḥakam.’” Sufyān said, “I do not remember him.” He said, “I thought my father had sent me to him on an errand when I was a boy. As for ʿAṭāʾ, Ibn Jurayj has sufficed you.”

ʿAlī ibn Mudrik; Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif al-Yāmī; al-Minhal ibn ʿAmr;

ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Maysara; ʿAdī ibn Thābit al-Anṣārī, a Shiʿi; al-Ḥajjāj ibn ʿAmr al-Muḥāribī; al-Walīd ibn al-ʿAyzār; Sayyār Abū al-Ḥakam; ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī al-Mujālid; Muḥill ibn Khalīfa; Abū Bakr ibn Ḥafṣ; ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jubayr al-Anṣārī; Yaḥyā ibn al-Ḥuṣayn al-Bajalī al-Aḥmasī; Nuʿaym ibn Abī Hind; Khubayb ibn al-Zubayr; ʿAmmār al-ʿAbsī; ʿĀʾidh ibn Nuṣayb;

al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Badr; Abū al-Safar Saʿīd ibn Yaḥmad; ʿUqba ibn Ḥurayth;

Ḥayyān al-Bāriqī; Zāʾida ibn ʿUmayr, a Ṭāʾī; Nājiya; Yaḥyā ibn ʿUbayd al-Bahrānī; Saʿīd ibn Abī Burda; ʿĀrim ibn ʿAmr … al-Bajalī;

Abū Ziyād al-Ṭaḥḥān; Abū al-Mukhtār; Ismāʿīl ibn Rajāʾ al-Zabīdī; al-Ḥurr ibn al-Ṣabbāḥ; ʿUbayd ibn Jabr; Yazīd ibn Abī Yarīm; and Abū Maʿshar.

Simāk Abū Zumayl al-Ḥanafī; Abū Baḥr al-Hilālī; Yazīd ibn Zādhī;

Mālik ibn ʿUrfuṭa—though he is in fact Khālid ibn ʿUrfuṭa—and Ḥayyān al-Azdī;

Shumaysa.

Muḥammad ibn Bashshār related to us, saying: Hishām related to me, saying: “Shuʿba related to us, from ʿAmr ibn Murra, who said: ‘ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salama used to relate to us, and at times he would get it right and at times he would err.’”

[Misʿar ibn Kidām]

Abū Nuʿaym related to us, saying: Misʿar ibn Kidām ibn Ẓuhayr ibn ʿUbayda ibn al-Ḥārith al-Hilālī related to us, saying: “I saw Muslim al-Baṭīn while we were here in the mosque, reviling the Murjiʾa. I said, ‘Glory be to God!’”

Abū Nuʿaym related to us, saying: Misʿar related to us, from ʿUmayr ibn Saʿīd, Abū Yaḥyā al-Nakhaʿī, who said: “I was sitting in a gathering that included ʿAmmār. They mentioned touching the penis, and he said:

‘It is only a part of you, and the palm of the hand has another place.’ I prayed behind ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṣālib at the funeral prayer for the son of al-Mukaffif, and he said four takbīrs over him. Then he went to his grave” (folio 203b) “and said:”

“O God, Your servant and the son of Your servant has come to You, and You are the best to whom one may come. O God, make his place of entry spacious, and forgive his sin, for we know nothing but good of him, and You know him better. I prayed behind Abū Mūsā on Friday, and he recited ‘Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High’, then said:

‘Glory be to my Lord, the Most High,’ and ‘Has the account of the Overwhelming Event come to you?’

And from Abū Bakr ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAbsah; from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn al-Qibṭiyya; and from Wabara ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān.

Misʿar said: I heard ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Aswad—or it reached me from him—and from al-Qāsim, from ʿImrān ibn ʿUmayr, and from al-Walīd ibn Abī Mālik. Ḥ.

Misʿar related to us, saying: Abū Maṭar related to us; he had seen ʿAlī. And from Yazīd al-Faqīr, who heard Ibn ʿUmar and heard Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh; and from Ibrāhīm al-ʿUqaylī, from his uncle, who read the book of ʿAmra to us; and from Abū Maʿshar.

Misʿar said: I heard al-ʿAlāʾ al-Ghanawī; and from al-Qāsim ibn Abī Bizza; from ʿAṭiyya al-ʿAwfī; from Abū Bakr ibn ʿUmāra; from Mūsā ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yazīd al-Anṣārī; from Kathīr ibn ʿAbbās; and from al-Naḍr ibn Qays.

Abū Nuʿaym related to us, saying: Misʿar ibn Kidām ibn Ẓahīr related to us, from Suwayd, the client of ʿAmr ibn Ḥurayth; from Saʿīd ibn Sinān; from ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Wāthila; from al-Walīd ibn Sarīʿ; from Thābit ibn ʿUbayd; from Jawwāb al-Taymī; and from Qatāda.

He said: I heard ʿAṭāʾ being asked about a man who prays facing away from the qibla, or faces away from it during part of his prayer. He said: “It suffices him.”

He said: Al-Qāsim ibn Zakariyyā related to me, saying: Muḥammad ibn Bishr related to us, saying: Misʿar related to me, saying: ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr related to me, from Jundab al-ʿAlaqī, who said: “I heard—I think he said Ibn Sufyān—say: ‘I heard the Prophet ﷺ say: “I will precede you at the Pool.”’” Jundab ibn ʿAbd Allāh and Jundab ibn Sufyān are one person. ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr, al-Aswad ibn Qays, and al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī narrated from him.

Abū Yūsuf said: “All of these are trustworthy.”

Abū Yūsuf said:

“These are the teachers of the Baṣrans”.

Saʿīd ibn Zarbī is weak. (folio 204a)

Al-Anṣārī Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh related to us, from Saʿīd al-Sammāk, who is weak.

Saʿīd ibn Abī ʿArūba is trustworthy. He did not hear from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr, Hishām ibn ʿUrwa, Abū al-Tayyāḥ, or Abū Bishr.

Qatāda did not hear from Mujāhid, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, Abū Qilāba, al-Shaʿbī, Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī, or Sulaymān al-Yashkurī. The hadith of Sulaymān al-Yashkurī is only a written collection: he had written it down from Jābir. He died early, and the collection remained with his mother among the people of Baṣra.

“Abū Sahl Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr: Abū Nuʿaym al-Nakhaʿī related from him, and he is weak.”

“Abū Ẓilāl al-Qasmalī has weak hadith.”

Al-Ḥajjāj related to us, saying: Ḥammād ibn Salama related to us, and he is trustworthy.

Sulaymān related from “al-Ṣaʿiq ibn Ḥazn, who is sound in his reports”.

Sulaymān related from Ḥammād ibn Zayd, from Ḥanẓalah al-Sadūsī.

He said: Ibn ʿUthmān also related to us from Ibn al-Mubārak, from Ḥanẓalah. He changed, and age affected him.

Maymūn ibn Siyāh, Yazīd ibn Abān al-Raqāshī, and Ziyād al-Numayrī are somewhat alike; they all have some weakness.

“I heard Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb say: A man said to Ḥammād ibn Zayd, ‘Do you know the report from Ayyūb, from Abū Qilābah, that whoever is present for the Opening of the Book [al-Fātiḥah] when it is begun is like one present at a campaign in God’s path, and whoever is present for it when it is completed is like one present when the spoils are distributed?’ Ḥammād strongly rejected it. Then afterward he said to the man, ‘Who told you this?’ He replied, ‘Ṣāliḥ al-Murrī.’ Ḥammād said, ‘I seek God’s forgiveness. How likely it is that it is fabricated! Ṣāliḥ used to have this sort of thing, and the like, on his mind, and would pursue this sort of thing. How likely it is that it is authentic!’”

“Some of the shaykhs related to me from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī, who said: Sufyān said:

‘Do you have someone to remind you?’ I said, ‘Yes, we have a preacher.’ He [said]: ‘Then take us to him.’ He said: I went with him between the sunset prayer and the night prayer. When he had finished, he said, ‘ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, you call him a preacher! This man is a warner to his people’—meaning Ṣāliḥ al-Murrī.”

Abū al-Nuʿmān related to us from Ḥammād, from Muḥammad ibn Faḍāʾ (204b); he is mild in his reports.

Ādam related to us from al-Haytham ibn Jammāz; he is weak.

Abū Bishr related to me from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim ibn al-Muthannā. He was from Baṣrah, and Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd related from him, as did Abū al-Walīd. Shuʿbah relates from his father, Muslim ibn al-Muthannā, and Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid relates from Abū al-Muthannā; this is the same man.

Hudbah related to us from Ḥammād ibn al-Jaʿd, from Qatādah. Ḥammād was from Baṣrah, and he is weak.

Muslim related to us. He said: Abān related to us, saying: Qatādah related to us from Sālim ibn Abī al-Jaʿd, from Maʿdān ibn Abī Ṭalḥah.

Muslim said: Bukayr ibn Abī al-Samīṭ also related to us, saying: Qatādah related to us from Sālim ibn Abī al-Jaʿd, from Maʿdān ibn Ṭalḥah.

Muslim said: Bukayr says “ibn Ṭalḥah”, and that is what the Syrians say: Maʿdān ibn Ṭalḥah. Shuʿbah, Saʿd, Hammām, al-Ḥajjāj al-Aswad, Hishām al-Dastawāʾī, Shaybān, and Muḥammad ibn Bashshār say: from Qatādah, from Sālim ibn Abī al-Jaʿd al-Ghaṭafānī, from Maʿdān ibn Abī Ṭalḥah al-Yaʿmurī.

As for Muḥammad ibn Thābit al-ʿAbdī of Baṣrah, I heard Abū al-Walīd declare him weak.

“Muḥammad ibn Thābit al-Bunānī is not strong.”

Muḥammad ibn Thābit and ʿAzrah ibn Thābit are brothers, and there is no fault in either of them. Muḥammad served as judge of Marw.

Al-Barāʾ ibn Yazīd al-Ghanawī is mild [in his reports], a man of Baṣrah.

Al-Barāʾ ibn Yazīd al-Hamdānī was from Kūfah; there is no fault in him.

Al-Ḥajjāj related to us from Ḥammād, from Abū Ghālib.

Al-Ḥumaydī related to us from Sufyān, from Abū Ghālib, the companion of the staff. I have been told that his name was Ḥazūr.

Abū Jazīʾ—ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā related from him—[and] Naṣr ibn Ṭarīf is abandoned.

I heard someone say to Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb: “Is Abū Umayyah ibn Yaʿlā weak?”

[He said: I heard someone say to Aḥmad ibn Yūnus: “Is ʿAbd Allāh al-ʿUmarī weak?”] He replied: “Only a Rāfiḍī who hates his forefathers declares him weak. If you saw his beard, his dye, and his appearance, you would know that he is trustworthy.”

“Yūsuf ibn Khālid al-Samtī: his reports are not to be written down, and the people of religious probity, reason, and knowledge do not relate from him.”

“I heard ʿAbbād ibn Ṣuhayb mention reports from Ayyūb ibn Khawṭ. Neither ʿAbbād nor Ibn Ḥawṭ’s reports are to be written down.”

(205a) I heard Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr—or Ibn Fuḍayl related from him—say:

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī came to Hushaym and asked him about some reports. He took care not to practice tadlīs, listening carefully, and took care, but did not write anything. Then he moved aside and began writing down, selectively, what he had asked him. Among the things he asked him was: “Is there anything from Manṣūr ibn Zādhān, from al-Ḥasan, concerning glass vessels?”

He wrote it down, choosing what to include. I said to him, “Abū Saʿīd, you did not hear this from Manṣūr, so you are not accountable for it.” The squinting al-Madāʾinī said to me, “May God do this and that to you! Why didn’t you leave the little stone to tumble down?”97

I asked Sulaymān: “Where did Jarīr ibn Ḥāzim hear from ʿĪsā ibn ʿĀṣim?”

He said: The people of Armenia were struck by famine. The people of Baṣrah gathered provisions and sent them to them. Jarīr ibn Ḥāzim went with them and heard from ʿĪsā ibn ʿĀṣim on that journey. He went to Egypt, to So-and-so ibn al-Muhallab, and heard from the Egyptians, who wrote reports from him. I said to him, “Was Jarīr an Arab?” He turned away from answering, then said: We were at a gathering of Wahb ibn Jarīr when a Bedouin came to us while we were discussing something about lineage— He said, “I am So-and-so ibn So-and-so ibn So-and-so ibn So-and-so. By God, I am noble.”

Some of those in the gathering disapproved of what he said. He said, “I’ll tell you more: you are not an Arab; this one is an Arab; this one is not an Arab; and this one is not an Arab.” He said: We confronted him and silenced him.

Al-Ḥumaydī related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, saying: Ḥumayd ibn Ḥibbān related to me from Ibn ʿAbbās ibn Urayd al-Jaʿfarī, who said: I saw Sālim ibn ʿAbd Allāh when he greeted the Stone; he did this with his hand—and Sufyān placed his hand on his forehead. Ḥibbān is pronounced with a fatḥah on both the ḥāʾ and the bāʾ.

Al-Ḥumaydī related to us, saying: Marwān related to us, saying: Ismāʿīl related to us from Qays, who said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd said, “When a man says to his companion, ‘You are my enemy,’ he has disbelieved.”

Qays said: Abū Juḥayfah later informed me that ʿAbd Allāh said, “Except one who repents.”

Al-Ḥumaydī related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, saying: Ismāʿīl related to us, saying: I heard a shaykh—they told me, “This is Zirr ibn Ḥubaysh”—say: I heard Ubayy ibn Kaʿb say, “The Night of Decree is the night of the twenty-seventh.”

(205b) Ismāʿīl ibn al-Khalīl related to me, saying: Zakariyyā ibn ʿAdī informed us from Ibn al-Mubārak. I said to Ismāʿīl, “Did you hear anything else from Zirr?” He said, “No.”

Al-Ḥumaydī related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, saying: Ismāʿīl related to us from Ḥakīm ibn Jābir, who said: When al-Ashʿath ibn Qays died, al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī came to them and instructed them to wash him thoroughly with camphor.

Ibn Numayr related to us, saying: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Idrīs related to us, saying: Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid related to us, saying: I saw Abū Juḥayfah holding the handle of Abū Maysarah’s bier and saying, “May God forgive you, Abū Maysarah.”

Abū al-Nuʿmān related to us, saying: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, saying: Yazīd ibn Ḥāzim related to us from Sulaymān ibn Yasār, that a man came to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb and said, “Commander of the Faithful, his wife has committed adultery, so carry out the prescribed punishment against her.” ʿUmar sent ʿAbd Allāh ibn Wāqid al-Laythī and said, “Go to this man’s wife and tell her: ‘This ʿAbd Allāh has accused you of a grave matter, so prove God’s enemy wrong.’” He went to her. She had put on her shroud, applied funeral perfume, and dug her grave; her family were with her. He conveyed to her what ʿUmar had said. She replied, “I will not confess to the indecency and the wrath of God.” She persisted in that answer, and she was stoned. Sulaymān ibn Yasār said to my uncle Ḥirz ibn Zayd, “Abū Salamah, she was a woman from your people, from Banū Salāmān.”

I heard Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb. Some people of Baṣrah said to him in Mecca, “ʿĀrim mentioned that you heard from Ḥammād ibn Salamah with me?” Sulaymān became confused and said, “I listened along with Abū al-Nuʿmān,” then fell silent. Then he said, “Abū al-Nuʿmān is certainly someone with whom I could listen. But the truth is the most deserving thing to be said: Jarīr ibn Ḥāzim had only asked Ḥammād ibn Salamah to relate to Wahb. So we gathered and selected these reports, and we disagreed. The book was in my hand; I would alter and correct it while they watched with me.”

Abū al-Walīd related to us, saying: Abū Hāshim al-Zaʿfarānī related to us. He is ʿAmmār ibn ʿImārah, trustworthy.

Muḥammad ibn al-Muthannā related to us, saying: Isḥāq ibn Idrīs related to us. I was told that Ibn Maʿīn said, “He is nothing; he fabricates reports,” and it seems he was right.

“Dāwūd ibn al-Zibriqān is weak.”

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥārith’s reports are not to be written down. (206a)

“ʿUlaylah al-Rabīʿ ibn Badr’s reports are not to be written down.”

Al-Ḥumaydī related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, saying: I saw the ring of my maternal grandfather, Abū al-Masāyid. It was made of iron, colored, and overlaid with silver. He had been among the earliest companions of ʿAbd Allāh.

Al-Ḥumaydī related to me, saying: My grandmother told me, “I once saw the wars; it had turned to ashes.”98

Sufyān related to us, saying: Abū al-Jaḥḥāf related to us; he was one of the Shīʿah. Abū Bakr said: His name was Dāwūd ibn Abī ʿAwf.

He said: Sufyān related to us, saying: ʿAmmār al-Duhnī related to us, saying: ʿAlī said, “Do not kill the man wearing the black burnous”—meaning Muḥammad ibn Ṭalḥah ibn ʿUbayd Allāh—“for he was brought out against his will.” Sufyān sometimes said of this, “I heard ʿAmmār.”

He said: Sufyān related to us, saying: I kept company with ʿAmmār in the year 123, at the home of ʿAmr ibn Dīnār.

Abū Bakr related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us from Abū Isḥāq, who said: I saw ʿAlī, his head and beard white, and I saw ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah.

Sufyān said: Abū Isḥāq related to me in the year 126. He related while neither I nor anyone else was with him. He said: Ṣilah ibn Zufar related to me seventy years ago.

Yaḥyā ibn Sulaymān al-Juʿfī related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us in the year 172, saying: Abū Isḥāq related to us seventy years ago, saying: Ṣilah ibn Zufar related to us seventy years ago, saying: I was sitting with ʿAbd Allāh.

Ibn Numayr related to us, saying: My father related to us from al-Aʿmash, from Abū Isḥāq, who said:

“Shurayḥ accepted my testimony alone.”

Al-Ḥumaydī related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, saying: I said to Abū Isḥāq, “Did you see ʿAlī?”

“ʿAlī?” He said, “Yes.”

Sufyān said: Abū Isḥāq died in the year 126.

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī said: Abū Isḥāq was ʿAmr ibn ʿAbd Allāh, and Abū Ḥuṣayn was named ʿUthmān ibn ʿĀṣim.

Abū Nuʿaym related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, saying: Al-Shaʿbī was asked, “What do you advise us?” He said:

“I am no scholar, and I do not abandon a scholar. Abū Ḥuṣayn is indeed a righteous man.”

Al-Ḥumaydī related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, saying: When Abū Ḥuṣayn was asked about a question, he would say, “I have no knowledge of it; God knows best.”

Sufyān related to us, saying: Abū Yaʿfūr al-ʿAbdī related to us, saying: I heard a shaykh from Khuzāʿah, who had been dispatched from Mecca by al-Ḥajjāj when Ibn al-Zubayr was killed and al-Ḥajjāj was governor there, say: The Prophet ﷺ said to ʿUmar, “Abū Ḥafṣ, you are a strong man.” Sufyān said: I said to Abū Yaʿfūr, “He is ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Nāfiʿ ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥārith.”

He said: Al-Ḥajjāj had appointed him over Mecca when he departed from there, at the time Ibn al-Zubayr was killed.

Al-Ḥumaydī said: Abū Yaʿfūr’s name was Waqdān.

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī said: Abū Yaʿfūr was ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿUbayd ibn Nasṭās; he relates from Muslim ibn Ṣubayḥ.

Abū Bakr related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, saying: Ibn al-Sammāk said, “I intended to make the pilgrimage…”

Zarārah ibn Aʿyan, the brother of ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Aʿyan, said to me: “When you meet Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, convey my greetings to him and ask him: ‘Tell me, am I in Paradise or in the Fire?’”

He said: I met Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad and said to him: “O son of the Messenger of God, do you know Zarārah ibn Aʿyan?” He said: “Yes—a wicked Rāfiḍī.” I said: “He sends you his greetings and says: ‘Tell me, am I in Paradise or in the Fire?’” He said: “Tell him that he is in the Fire.” Then he said:

“Do you know how you knew that he is a Rāfiḍī? He claims that I know the unseen. Whoever claims that anyone knows the unseen except God, mighty and glorious is He, is an unbeliever, and the unbeliever is in the Fire.”

He said: When I arrived in Kūfah, he came among the people who were greeting me and asked: “What did you do about my request?” I told him what Jaʿfar had said. He replied: “The son of the Messenger of God was cautious.”

Abū Bakr related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, saying: Mūsā ibn Abī ʿĀʾishah related to us; he was “trustworthy.”

He said: Sufyān related to us, saying: I went to Mūsā ibn Abī ʿĀʾishah. Whenever I saw him, I would say—as al-Zuhrī said—“If you had seen Ṭāwūs, you would have known that he did not lie.”

I went to him between noon and mid-afternoon, and stayed with him until he came out to me (207a) (208a) my brother.99 Sufyān said: I asked him, “How old are you?” He said: “I am the son of sixty…”

…and one hundred. Sufyān said: We had entrusted him with some food and belongings of ours. When we returned, we asked him for them. He said: “If it’s food, perhaps the living have eaten it.” We said: “We belong to God; our food is gone!” Then it turned out he was joking with me, and he brought out our belongings and food.

Abū Bakr related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, saying: Libṭah ibn al-Farazdaq related to me from his father, who said: We set out as pilgrims. When we were at al-Ṣifāḥ, there was a whole caravan, with young she-camels and shields. As I drew near, I saw al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī. I said: “Abū ʿAbd Allāh?”

He said: “Abū ʿAbd Allāh. Woe to you, Farazdaq! What news do you bring?” I said: “You are the person most beloved to the people, but the decree is in Heaven, and the swords are with the Umayyads.” Then we went on.

When we had completed our pilgrimage and were at Minā, we said: “What if we went to ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr and asked him about al-Ḥusayn and his setting out?” So we went to his dwelling and found some black boys of his, born to him. We asked: “Where is your father?” They said: “In the tent, performing ablution.” Before long, he came out to us. We asked him about al-Ḥusayn and his setting out. He said: “As for him, weapons will not affect him.” I said to him:

“You say this about him, when only yesterday you were fighting him and his father!” He insulted me, and I insulted him. Then we left his presence and came to a watering place of ours called Tiʿshār. We kept asking everyone who passed us about al-Ḥusayn, until his caravan passed by. We asked them: “What happened to al-Ḥusayn?” They said: “He was killed.” I said: “May God do [as He wills] to ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr!”

Sufyān said: Farazdaq misunderstood the interpretation. What ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr meant by “weapons will not affect him” was that weapons would not harm him, given what had already been decreed for him—that he would not be killed. It is like your saying: “What was said about so-and-so affected him.”

Sufyān said: Al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Abī al-ʿAbbās related to us from Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, who said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr said of al-Ḥusayn: “Weapons will not affect him.”

Abū Bakr related to us, saying: [folio 208b] Sufyān related to us, saying: I saw Ḥammād ibn Abī Sulaymān come to Abū Ṭalḥah the cupping practitioner to ask him for help with something. He was on a horse. I saw that his beard was ash-gray.

[Muḥārib ibn Dithār]

Abū Bakr said: Sufyān related to us, saying: I saw Muḥārib ibn Dithār in a corner of a mosque, judging between people.

Al-ʿAbbās ibn Muḥammad related to me, saying: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Muṣʿab, Abū Yazīd al-Maʿnī, related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us from Muḥārib ibn Dithār, who said: “I was appointed to the judgeship, and I wept, and my family wept. Then I was removed from the judgeship, and I wept, and my family wept.”

Aḥmad ibn al-Khalīl related to us, saying: Aḥmad ibn ʿImrān al-Akhnasī related to us, saying: al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUmar al-Ḍabbī related to us from Abū al-Ṣahbāʾ al-Taymī, who said: I came and found Muḥārib ibn Dithār standing in prayer. When he saw me, he shortened his prayer, then sat in the seat of judgment. Then he sent someone to ask me: “Are you a litigant, a fellow Muslim, or do you have a request?” I said: “No, I am a fellow Muslim.” The messenger went and told him, then came to me and said: “Stand.” He said: I greeted him, and he praised God and extolled Him, then said: “O God, You know that I sat in this seat, with which You have tested me and which You have decreed for me, only though I dislike and detest it. So spare me the evil consequences of it.”

He said: Then he took out a clean cloth, put it over his face, and kept weeping until I stood up.

He said: I wept for as long as God willed.

After him, Ibn Shubruma held the office. He said: I came and found him standing in prayer. When he saw me, he shortened his prayer, then sent someone to ask me: “Are you a litigant, a fellow Muslim, or do you have a request?” He said:

I replied: “No, I am a fellow Muslim.” The messenger went and told him, then came to me and said: “Stand.” I stood, greeted him, and sat beside him. He said: “Tell me [about] my brother Muḥārib ibn Dithār.” I told him the story. He said: “O God, You know that I sat in this seat, with which You have tested me, only because I love and desire it. So spare me the evil consequences of it.” Then he took out a cloth, put it over his face, and kept weeping until I stood up.

Al-Ḥumaydī related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, saying: Abū ʿUrwah the perfumer related to us (209a); he was trustworthy.

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī said: One day Sufyān related the report of Abū ʿUrwah, and [text uncertain] Layl al-Makkī said to him: “Abū ʿUrwah the perfumer related to us; he was one of your fellow Murjiʾites.”

Abū Bakr related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, saying: Quʿnub al-Tamīmī related to us; he was trustworthy, reliable, and among the outstanding men.

Sufyān said: A governor had summoned Quʿnub and appointed him to the judgeship, but he refused him. The governor kept pressing him until he accepted. When Quʿnub left the governor with his letter of appointment, he threw it away and went into hiding.

He said: The governor sent people to look for him. While they were searching for him, the house in which he was hiding collapsed on him. They had no idea what had happened before he was brought out to them on his bier.

(212a) Abū Bakr related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, saying: ʿUmayr ibn ʿAbd Allāh said: “The leading men of Kūfah are Ziyād ibn ʿAlāqah, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sharīk, Abū Isḥāq al-Hamdānī, and Yazīd ibn Mushir.”

He said: Sufyān related to us, saying: Raqabah ibn Maṣqalah came to me about something. When he wanted to visit Muḥammad ibn Sūqah, he would say to us: “Let us go to Muḥammad ibn Sūqah, for I heard Ṭalḥah ibn Muṣarrif say: ‘In Kūfah there are two men worth visiting: Muḥammad ibn Sūqah and ʿAbd al-Jabbār ibn Wāʾil.’”

He said: Sufyān related to us, saying: ʿUmar ibn Saʿīd related to me from his father. His father was alive at the time, I think; I would see him coming toward us and going away. I wanted us to visit him, but I was too shy because of his two sons. I kept putting it off until he died.

He said: Sufyān related to us, saying: ʿUmar ibn Saʿīd and someone else related to me from al-Aʿmash, who said: I went to al-Shaʿbī about a small matter, and he said to me: “Would someone like you come over something like this?”

Then al-Shaʿbī said to me: “How do you recite, ‘By God, our Lord,’ or ‘our Lord’?” I said: “‘By God, our Lord.’” He said: “And how do you recite, ‘For God does not guide whom He leads astray,’ or ‘He guides whom He leads astray’?” He said: “‘For God does not guide whom He leads astray,’” and he mentioned the report.

He said: Sufyān related to us, saying: One day we went to al-Aʿmash. I said: “May God grant Abū Muḥammad well-being. I have rarely come to him with a report without his relating it to me.” Al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAyyāsh, the brother of Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh, said: “Mention what you said to him; let him know that something happened afterward.”

He said: Sufyān related to us, saying: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sharīk related to us that he heard Jundub say:

Salmān looked out over Kūfah and said: “The dome of Islam, twice over: the mosque of Noah and his prayer place. I know of no town whose people are spared what these people are spared, except those who lived in houses, or buildings, or huts with the Messenger of God ﷺ ﷺ. Soon no believer will remain whose heart is set on it, and its people will grow numerous until they fill the land between the two rivers. A man will set out at daybreak on an ash-gray mule and not make it to Friday prayer.”

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, saying: I saw Jarīr ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd visiting Mughīrah. I said to ʿAmr ibn Saʿd: “Who is this young man?” ʿUmar said to me: “This young man is a decent fellow.”

Sufyān said: I heard Ibn Shubruma say: “I was in charge of collecting the sadaqah of al-Sahmān, and I said to Jarīr: ‘Come, and I will put you in charge of one of the four districts and give you a hundred dirhams.’”

I said to him: “Then take from it what you think is permissible for you, and give the rest in charity.” He said:

“I fear that I would not be at ease if I took it.” He refused me.

He said: Sufyān related to us, saying: Abū Farwah related to us: “I washed ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUkaim.”

Abū Nuʿaym related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us from Sālim al-Juhanī, who said: The mother of…

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā died, and ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUkaim came to her; he was their imam.

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us: “Qaylah, who met the Prophet ﷺ was the mother of Farwah.”

Al-Faḍl ibn Ziyād related to me, saying: I heard Abū ʿAbd Allāh say: “Ṭalḥah and Zubayd had the same prayer place. Ṭalḥah was an ʿUthmānī, and Zubayd an ʿAlawī. Ṭalḥah was among the outstanding men, and Zubayd’s argument cannot be dismissed. Ṭalḥah prohibited intoxicating drink, whereas Zubayd did not prohibit it.”

I was told from Jarīr that he mentioned the reports of ʿĀṣim al-Aḥwal and said: “They became confused for me, and I could not distinguish them from the reports of Ashʿath until Bahz of Baṣrah came to us and sorted them out for me, so I related them.”

Bishr ibn al-Azhar related to us, saying: “Whenever Jarīr related a report of al-Aʿmash, he would say: ‘Al-Aʿmash’s brocade, except that it is patched.’” Then we would discuss it among ourselves…

…and correct one another, or something to that effect.”

He said: Jarīr said: “In Kūfah, they offered me two thousand dirhams to give me along with the Qurʾān reciters, but I refused. (213a) Then today I have come asking for what they have—or what is in their hands.”

Jarīr said: “I did not write anything down from Manṣūr.”

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, saying: Mughīrah related to us from Ibrāhīm, who said: A man said in the presence of the Prophet ﷺ: “Whoever obeys God and His Messenger has been rightly guided, and whoever disobeys them has gone astray.” The Prophet ﷺ said: “Do not say that. Rather say: ‘Whoever obeys God and His Messenger has been rightly guided, and whoever disobeys God and His Messenger has gone astray.’” Sufyān said to Mughīrah: “Did you hear this from Ibrāhīm?” He said: “Why do you want to know that?”

He evaded the question and did not tell me, “I heard it from Ibrāhīm,” or, “I did not hear it.” After that, I no longer sat with him.

Ibn Numayr related to me, saying: Ibn Fuḍayl said: Mughīrah said: “I had heard it from Ibrāhīm.”

Ibn Numayr said: Ibn Fuḍayl held that Mughīrah had heard from Ibrāhīm only what Ibn Fuḍayl himself had transmitted from him, which was fewer than two hundred reports. I think he said around one hundred and fifty, or fewer.

Aḥmad ibn al-Khalīl related to me, saying: Yaḥyā ibn Ayyūb related to us, saying: Ḥumayd related to us, saying: al-Ḥasan ibn Ṣāliḥ said: “Mughīrah used to ask me about Ibn Abī Laylā’s opinion, but I would not tell him.”

Aḥmad ibn al-Khalīl and Isḥāq related to us, saying: I was present when Jarīr ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd was reading the book of Manṣūr to us. Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn said to him: “Abū ʿAbd Allāh, ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Abān claims that you only read these reports aloud to Manṣūr.”

Jarīr said: “If he is lying, may God set him right. By God, I had memorized only five reports with him; he related them to me only once. Yet I memorized forty reports in one sitting in which he related them to me.”

[Misʿar ibn Kidām]

Abū Bakr related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, saying: Misʿar said: “No one knows the reports of Ibn Masʿūd better than al-Masʿūdī.”

He said: Sufyān related to us from Misʿar that, when asked about a report, he would not say, “Then I will hear it,” but would say, “I do not have it memorized.” He would say: “Perhaps you heard it but do not have it memorized.”

He said: Sufyān related to us, saying: Misʿar said to his son Kidām:

“I have given you this counsel, Kidām,

so heed a father’s words, from one devoted to you.

As for joking and disputation, leave them both—

two traits I do not approve in a friend.

I have tried them and found them wanting … for a neighbor as neighbor,

and for a companion.”

Ibn Abī ʿUmar related to me, saying: Sufyān related to us from ʿĀṣim, from al-Qāsim ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, who said: “In Kūfah, no one knows the reports of ʿAbd Allāh better than…”

Sulaymān.”

Abū Nuʿaym related to us: Sufyān related to us, from Mujammiʿ ibn Ṣamghān, from a man among them. Murrah al-Yāmī related it from a man of his people, who said: “I saw ʿAlī bring out a sword of his and say, ‘Who will buy this sword of mine? If I had the price of a waist-wrapper, I would not sell it.’” Al-Ḥumaydī related to us: Sufyān said, “I heard Ibn Abjar hear a son of his say to his servant, ‘You weaver!’ He said, ‘My son, you are only insulting your father.’”

Sufyān said: “He means: If that is a fault, it was your father who led him to it.”

I was told that Ibn Idrīs had young men who were weavers—I do not know whether they were hired by the piece or wage-workers—and they wove for him. Ibn Idrīs brought a dispute before Sharīk, who ruled against Ibn Idrīs. He said, “Your judgment is not the right judgment.” Sharīk said to him, “Go, then, and let the weavers of al-Daʿāfira issue a legal opinion for you.”

Abū Bakr related to us: Sufyān said, “We visited Mūsā al-Juhanī to see how he was. I saw that the place where he prayed was like a camel’s resting place.”

Sufyān said: “He was a righteous and excellent man.”

Mūsā said: “I washed Zayd ibn Wahb when he died.”

“He said: Sufyān related to us: Abū Ḥayyān related to us, from Mujammiʿ al-Taymī, who said: ‘ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib went out to the market with his sword and said, “Who will buy this sword of mine? If I had four dirhams with which to buy a waist-wrapper, I would not sell it.”’” He also said: “Sufyān related to us: Abū Ḥayyān swore to me—and I had not asked him—that the deed I most firmly trust is my love for Mujammiʿ—counting the people with whom he sat.”

Sufyān said: Mujammiʿ al-Taymī said, “I have neither performed the pilgrimage nor asked God to let me do so.”

He was asked, “Why?” He replied, “An obligation has been removed from me, and I do not know whether, if it were imposed upon me, I would fulfill it or not.”

Sufyān said: Misʿar said (214a), “Mujammiʿ brought a ewe to the market to sell and said, ‘It seems to me there is a salty taste in her milk.’”

Abū Bakr related to us, from Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna, from Wāʾil ibn Dāwūd, from al-Ḥasan, who said: “The Messenger of God ﷺ put those two ahead; so who is there who would put them behind?”

Sufyān related from Wāʾil, from al-Ḥasan, who said: “There are three whom no one will ever put in fourth place: the Prophet ﷺ, Abū Bakr, and ʿUmar ﵄.”

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī said: “I heard these two reports from Sufyān and found them in my first audition notebook, which we used to call ‘al-Rāshidiyya.’ We would stand, and the dictation assistant would dictate to us when Sufyān stood.”

He said: “Sufyān related to us: Saʿīd ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ al-Ṭāʾī related to us. He was an old scholar and a poet.”

He said: “Sufyān related to us: My grandfather—or my grandmother—sent her with Muḥammad ibn Muzāḥim, al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Muzāḥim, on a pilgrimage.”

Sufyān said: “I said, ‘My grandmother’—my mother was a client of Zirr—‘so I used to see Zurāra.’”

He said: “Sufyān related to us: al-Walīd ibn Ḥarb, the truthful and reliable man, related to me.”

Abū Bakr said, concerning the report of ʿAlī, “Whenever he found the truth in them”: Sufyān said: Qays ibn al-Rabīʿ told me, “Al-Mahdī related this report.”

He said: “Sufyān related to us: Ibn Abī Khālid related to us, from al-Shaʿbī, who said:

‘Al-Rabīʿ ibn Khuthaym related to me.’ I said, ‘Who related it to you—may God have mercy on you?’ He replied, ‘ʿAmr ibn Maymūn al-Awdī.’ I went to ʿAmr and said, ‘Who related it to you?’ He replied, ‘ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn—’”

“Abī Laylā. I went to ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and said, ‘Who related it to you?’ He replied, ‘Abū Ayyūb al-Anṣārī said that the Messenger said: “Whoever says after the dawn prayer ten times, ‘There is no god but God alone, without partner; to Him belongs dominion and to Him belongs praise, and He has power over all things,’ it will be as though he had freed four enslaved people from the descendants of Ismāʿīl.”’”

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us: Sufyān related to us: Ismāʿīl said, “I used to ask al-Shaʿbī and hear reports from him. When he saw how eager I was, he would say, ‘Now, Ibn Abī Khālid, drink deeply of knowledge!’”

He said: Sufyān related to us, from Ibn Abī Khālid, who said: “I saw al-Shaʿbī pass by Abū Ṣāliḥ—or go to Abū Ṣāliḥ—and take hold of his ear and twist it. Then he said, ‘You wicked little man, you explain the Qurʾān when you cannot even read it!’”

Sufyān said: “I heard Ismāʿīl—or Mālik ibn Mighwal; Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī was uncertain—which said, ‘I heard Abū Ṣāliḥ say, “There is no one in Mecca whom I have not taught the Qurʾān, or whose father I have not taught.”’”

Sufyān said: “I asked ʿAmr ibn Dīnār about Abū Ṣāliḥ, and he said, ‘I do not know him.’”

He said: “Sufyān related to us: Ibn Abī Khalaf related to us: I said to ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Aswad, ‘What prevented you from asking questions as Ibrāhīm did?’ He replied, ‘It used to be said—’”

“‘Study the Qurʾān on its own.’”

He said: “Sufyān related to us: I heard Ismāʿīl say, ‘Whenever I asked Abū Ṣāliḥ about anything from the Qurʾān, he would inform me about it.’”

He said: Sufyān related to us: “Yaḥyā ibn Abī Khalaf would relate a report, then say, ‘So-and-so related it to me,’ as though you were sitting there.”

He said: “Sufyān related to us: Muḥammad ibn Qays related to us, from Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit, who said, ‘We used to call Abū Ṣāliḥ nothing but Bādarwazadhā.’”

He said: “Sufyān related to us: al-Rabīʿ ibn Lūṭ, a descendant of al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib, related to us—he was about my age, or a little older.”

Sufyān said: “Musāwir—the copyist—was a righteous man, with nothing wrong with him, except that he had a particular view concerning Abū Ḥanīfa. He composed poetry and said these verses about him. It would have been better had he not said them—or Sufyān said, ‘It would have been better for him had he not said them’:

When people one day confront uswith a difficult, subtle question of law,we answer them with a firm measure,a sound one, in the style of Abū Ḥanīfa.

Sufyān said: “Musāwir practiced asceticism, though there was something about his clothing. He was invited to a gathering, but the people at the door turned him away because they thought little of him. He left and went to his home, put on two clean garments, then came back. He was not stopped and went inside. When they saw him, they made room for him and treated him generously. When the food was set out, he took hold of the edge of his clothes and said, ‘Eat!’ They asked, ‘What is this?’ He told them what had happened.

“He refused to eat and left them with it.”

(215a) Sufyān said: “I think he meant by this to admonish them, so that no one who is looked down upon would be turned away.”

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us: Sufyān related to us: “I went to Mujammiʿ to ask him about these reports. I thought he would refuse, so I recited to him Mujammiʿ’s report about the Dajjāl, which was transmitted from al-Zuhrī. He said, ‘These are my teachers.’ Then he said, ‘Bring out your writing tablets.’ I replied, ‘I have no tablets with me.’ So he related it to me. Then he said, ‘No one in Kūfa has it. Al-Ḥajjāj ibn Arṭāʾa came to me and asked me about it.’”

He said: “Sufyān related to me: Abū ʿĀṣim al-Thaqafī—he was trustworthy—related it to me. He had heard it from Qays ibn Muslim al-Jadalī, who said: ‘I heard Ṭāriq ibn Shihāb say:

“When ʿUthmān was killed…”’—and he mentioned his report.”

Sufyān said: “Umayy also related to us—he was trustworthy. He had heard it from a man of—”

“Bajīla, a nursling of al-Qasrī. He heard it from Ṭāriq ibn Shihāb, with similar wording, and added: ‘ʿAlī said, “By God, I have examined this matter from every side, and found nothing but fighting or disbelief in what was sent down to Muḥammad ﷺ.”’”100

He said: “Sufyān related to us: I heard Umayy say, ‘Ibrāhīm used to urge people to sit with al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Badr.’”

Ibn Numayr related to us: Yaʿlā ibn ʿUbayd related to us, from al-Aʿmash, who said: “I mentioned al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Badr to Ibrāhīm. He said, ‘I have seen no one among the people of his time bolder than he in interpreting the Qurʾān, nor anyone more likely to get right much of what you attribute to him.’”
