Abū Bakr related to us: Sufyān related to us, from Misʿar, from Maʿn, from his father’s book, from ʿAbd Allāh, who said: “Prayer is light.”

Misʿar said: “Maʿn swore to me that it was in his father’s handwriting.”

He said: “Sufyān related to us: Misʿar related to us, from ʿAmr ibn Murra, who said: ‘We sat with al-Zuhrī, and Dharr al-Hamdānī was with us. Al-Zuhrī began relating reports, and Dharr kept saying to us, “Memorize! Memorize!”’”

He said: “Sufyān related to us: One day I went to al-Aʿmash and said, ‘May God grant Abū Muḥammad good health! I have hardly ever come to him with a report without his relating it to me.’”

Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā related to us: Ibn Wahb dictated to us. He said:

Ibn ʿUyayna related to us: Maʿn said, “I have never seen Misʿar on any day but that he was better than he had been the day before.”

(215b) He said: Ibn Wahb also informed us: “He—meaning Ibn ʿUyayna—related to me, from Hishām ibn ʿUrwa, who said, ‘I have seen no one in Basra like Ayyūb, nor anyone in Kūfa like Misʿar.’”

Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmmār related to us: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Dāwūd related to us, saying:

“Al-Ḥasan ibn Ṣāliḥ ibn Ḥayy related to me, from myself, from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrāhīm, who said, ‘Water is washed away with water.’” He said: “I told him, ‘I do not remember this.’ He replied, ‘You related it to me.’”

ʿAlī ibn al-Madīnī said: “Mālik ibn Mighwal is firmly reliable, and Misʿar is more reliable than he. He is trustworthy, sound in his reports, and meticulous.”

Aḥmad ibn al-Khalīl related to me: Aḥmad ibn Sulaymān related to us: Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh related to us, from Abū Isḥāq, who said: “Kharijites came out, and Abū al-Aḥwaṣ went out to them, and they killed him.”

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us: Sufyān related to us: Misʿar related to us, saying: “I heard Abū—”

“Al-Ṣabbāḥ say, ‘The doctrine of predestination is a father who is generous with heresy.’”

Sufyān said: “Abū al-Ṣabbāḥ was one of the group who came as a delegation to ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz.”

He said: Sufyān related to us: “Ibrāhīm ibn Yaḥyā ibn Abī Yaʿqūb related to me—Sufyān said, ‘He was about my age and was a righteous man’—from al-Ḥakam ibn Abān, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: ‘I asked Gabriel, “Which of the two terms did Moses fulfill?” He replied, “The longer and more complete of the two.”’”

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us: Wakīʿ related to us, from Sufyān, from ʿAmr, from ʿIkrima, concerning His words, “their strongholds.” He said: “Their fortresses.” We mentioned this to Sufyān, and he rejected it. He said: “I do not remember it from ʿAmr, from ʿIkrima. I do not remember it except from people: ‘Their strongholds: their fortresses.’ Perhaps he was referring to His words, ‘and a land you have not trodden.’” ʿAmr related to us, from ʿIkrima, concerning “and a land you have not trodden.” He said: “It is whatever the Muslims gain victory over until the Day of Resurrection.”

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us. He was asked, “Ḥumayd al-Ruʾāsī relates from you, from Ḥuṣayn, from Abū Mālik, ‘Go forth, lightly and heavily armed…’”

“Lightly and heavily armed.” As for the interpretation, I suppose Ibn Jurayj reported it from Mujāhid.

“Abū Bakr related to us: Abū Muʿāwiya al-Ḍarīr related to us: Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna related to us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, concerning His mighty and glorious words, ‘On the day the heaven sways violently,’ who said, ‘It turns round and round.’ We asked Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna about it, and he said:

‘I do not remember it.’”

ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Shaqīq related to us: ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mubārak related to us: Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna related to us, from Ibn Ṭāwūs, from his father, who said: “There is no ablution required for regurgitation.”

This is among the reports Sufyān rejected. Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī said: “I think this was a mistake by Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna; he erred in it. I was present when Bishr ibn al-Sarī spoke to Sufyān about reviewing something he had heard long ago—Abū Bakr said, ‘In the old days, Sufyān was not permitted to attend audition sessions.’ As Sufyān reviewed what was presented to him, there passed before him Ibn Ṭāwūs and another man—al-Ḥumaydī had named him, but Abū Yūsuf forgot his name—both transmitting from Ṭāwūs: ‘There is no ablution required for regurgitation.’ Sufyān said, ‘Strike out Ibn Ṭāwūs.’ Abū Bakr said, ‘I therefore thought that Sufyān had narrated from him long ago.’”

Ibn Abī ʿUmar related to us: Sufyān related to us, from Ibn Ṭāwūs—or Hishām ibn Ḥujayr—from Ṭāwūs, who said: “There is no ablution required for qalas.”

Abū Bakr related to us: Sufyān related to us. He said: “I heard Mūsā ibn Abī ʿĀʾishah—who was one of the reliable authorities—say: ‘I heard Sulaymān ibn Qattah, a man from among the people of Baṣra.’”

He also said: “Sufyān related to us: I heard Mālik ibn Anas ask Zayd ibn Aslam. Zayd said: ‘I heard my father say: ʿUmar said, “I was given a horse for the cause of God.”’”

Abū Bakr said: Regarding the ḥadīth, “Continue to perform ḥajj and ʿumrah, for performing them in succession increases one’s lifespan,” Sufyān said: “ʿAbd al-Karīm al-Jazarī first related this ḥadīth to us from ʿAbdah, from ʿĀṣim. When ʿAbdah arrived, we went to him to ask about it. He said: ‘ʿĀṣim was the one who related it to me, and here ʿĀṣim is present.’ So we went to ʿĀṣim and asked him, and he related it to us in this form. Then, after that, he heard it directly from him. Sometimes he attributed it to ʿUmar, without mentioning his father in the chain; but most often he related it from ʿAbd ibn ʿĀmir, from his father, from ʿUmar, from the Prophet ﷺ.”

(216b) Sufyān said: “Sometimes we would omit this phrase: ‘increases one’s lifespan.’”

“So we did not relate it, for fear that these people”—meaning the Qadariyyah—“might use it as an argument, though they have no argument in it.”

Sufyān said: “ʿAbdah related to us—and we memorized it from him more than once. He said: ‘I heard Abū Wāʾil Shaqīq ibn Salamah say: “Very often, Masrūq ibn al-Ajdaʿ and I would go to al-Ṣabī ibn Maʿbad and review this ḥadīth with him.”’”

Sufyān said: “He meant that al-Ṣabī had joined ḥajj and ʿumrah with the Prophet ﷺ and regarded it as permissible—not that he himself had done so.”

Abū Bakr related to us: Sufyān related to us, from Maʿmar and others, from al-Zuhrī, from al-Sāʾib ibn Yazīd, from Ḥuwayṭib ibn ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Saʿdī: He came from Syria to ʿUmar, who said to him, “Have I not been told that you administer its affairs?”

Abū Bakr said: Sufyān said regarding the ḥadīth of Abū al-ʿAjfāʾ from ʿUmar: “‘So-and-so was killed as a martyr, and so-and-so died as a martyr.’ Perhaps—or it may be—he had loaded the rear of his mount and its hindquarters with gold.” Sufyān said: “Ayyūb used to ask about this ḥadīth: ‘Is it so, or something else?’ If Ḥammād ibn Zayd related it in this form, then so be it; otherwise, he did not memorize it.”

I heard Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb express astonishment at Sufyān, saying: “Are you not amazed at Sufyān and his words, when he did not get the ḥadīth right? Consider when he says, ‘He had loaded the rear of his mount and its hindquarters’—what did he include them in? He had loaded the two rear flanks of his mount.”

I heard Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr say: “I heard Sufyān say: ‘Ayyūb heard—’”

“—from Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn, who heard Abū al-ʿAjfāʾ, who heard ʿUmar.” Then he mentioned this ḥadīth.

I heard Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb mention this and say: “Abū al-ʿAjfāʾ has no narrator other than this one ḥadīth. So what is the objection to Muḥammad having heard it from him, and to his having heard it from ʿUmar?”

Saʿīd related to us: Ismāʿīl ibn Ibrāhīm related to us. He said: Salamah ibn ʿAlqamah, Ayyūb, Ibn ʿAwn, and Hishām informed us, from Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn. Salamah said, “I was informed on the authority of Abū al-ʿAjfāʾ”; the others said, “From Abū al-ʿAjfāʾ,” who said: “ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said: ‘Take heed: do not be extravagant.’”

Saʿīd related to us: Hushaym related to us: Manṣūr informed us, from Ibn Sīrīn, who said: “Abū al-ʿAjfāʾ al-Sulamī related to us. He said: ‘I heard ʿUmar addressing the people in a sermon. He praised and extolled God, then said: “Take heed: do not be extravagant.”’”

Abū Bakr said: “In the ḥadīth of ʿAlī, ‘The Messenger of God ﷺ—said to me, “Ask God for guidance,”’ Sufyān used to say: ‘From Abū Bakr ibn—’”

“—Abū Mūsā.” He was asked, “Do they not relate it from Abū Burdah?” He said to me:

“As for what I memorized, it is from Abū Bakr. If you disagree with me, then make it from Abū Mūsā.” After that, Sufyān would sometimes say, “From Ibn Abī Mūsā,” and sometimes he would forget and relate it as he had heard it, from Abū Bakr.

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us: Sufyān related to us, from Misʿar, from Saʿd ibn Ibrāhīm, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shaddād, from ʿAlī, who said: “The Messenger of God ﷺ—called both his parents together for no one but Saʿd. On the day of Uḥud, he said: ‘Shoot! May my father and mother be your ransom.’” Then Sufyān abandoned Misʿar’s ḥadīth thereafter and began relating a ḥadīth from Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, from ʿAlī, who said: “The Messenger of God ﷺ—called both his parents together for no one but Saʿd.” Abū Bakr said: “He abandoned the sound version and related the erroneous one. At first, he had related to us, from Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, who said: ‘I heard Saʿd say: “On the day of Uḥud, the Messenger of God ﷺ—called both his parents together for me and said: ‘Shoot! May my father and mother be your ransom.’”’”

Abū Bakr said, regarding the ḥadīth of Ibn Masʿūd, “On the day of the Conquest, the Prophet entered, and around the House were three hundred and sixty idols,” and the ḥadīth “The moon split”: Sufyān said, “Ibn Abī Najīḥ established these two ḥadīths for us, from Abū Maʿmar.”

Regarding the ḥadīth, “Three men—two Qurashīs and a Thaqafī—met,” he said: “At first, Sufyān used to say of this ḥadīth, ‘Manṣūr related to us,’ or ‘Ibn Abī Najīḥ,’ or ‘Ḥumayd al-Aʿraj’—the last of them—or two of them. Then he settled on Manṣūr for this ḥadīth.” (217b)

Abū Bakr said: “Sufyān related this ḥadīth to us through Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid, in a form different from the one al-Zuhrī related to us. He said: ‘I heard Qays ibn Abī Ḥāzim say: “I heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd say: The Messenger of God ﷺ—said: ‘There is no envy except in two cases: a man to whom God has given wealth and granted authority to spend it up in the cause of truth, and a man to whom God has given wisdom, so that he judges by it and teaches it.’”’”

He also said: “Sufyān related to us: al-Zuhrī related to us, from Sālim ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from his father, that the Messenger of God ﷺ—said: ‘There is no envy except in two cases: a man to whom God has given the Qurʾān, and who devotes himself to it during the hours of night and day; and a man to whom God has given wealth, and who spends from it during the hours of night and the hours of day.’”

Abū Bakr said, regarding the ḥadīth, “Ibn Masʿūd was told that a man in the mosque was saying, ‘When the Day of Resurrection comes, smoke will afflict the people’”: “Sufyān said: ‘Al-Aʿmash related it to us—or I was informed about it.’”

Abū Bakr related to us: Sufyān related to us, from ʿAbd al-Karīm ibn Abī Umayyah, from Ḥassān ibn Bilāl al-Madanī: He saw ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir performing ablution and combing water through his beard. He was asked, “Do you comb water through your beard?” He replied, “What would prevent me, when I saw the Messenger of God ﷺ—comb water through his beard?”

Al-Ḥumaydī said: “Sufyān related to us, from Saʿīd ibn Abī ʿArūbah, from Qatādah, from Ḥassān ibn Bilāl, from ʿAmmār, from the Prophet ﷺ—the like of it.”

Abū Bakr said: “I heard it from Sufyān once”—meaning the ḥadīth of Saʿīd.

Abū Bakr related to us: Sufyān related to us: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Lubayd related to us. He was one of the devout worshippers among the people of Medina, and he held the Qadariyyah doctrine.

He also said: “Sufyān related to us: Sālim Abū al-Naḍr related to us, from Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (218a), from ʿĀʾishah, who said: ‘The Messenger of God ﷺ—would pray the two rakʿahs before dawn. If I was awake, he would talk with me; otherwise, he would lie down until he got up for the prayer.’”

He also said: “Sufyān related to us: Ziyād ibn Saʿd al-Khurāsānī related to us, from Ibn Abī ʿAttāb, from Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿĀʾishah, from the Prophet ﷺ—the like of it.”

He also said: “Sufyān related to us: Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAlqamah related to us, from Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿĀʾishah, who said: ‘The Messenger of God ﷺ—would pray his night prayer while I lay across the space between him and the direction of prayer. When he wished to perform witr, he would nudge me with his foot. He would pray the two rakʿahs; if I was awake, he would talk with me, otherwise he would lie down until he got up for the prayer.’”

Abū Bakr said: “Sufyān would be uncertain about this ḥadīth and confused over it. Sometimes he would be uncertain about Ziyād’s ḥadīth, then say, ‘They get mixed up for me.’ Then, more than once, he said: ‘Abū al-Naḍr’s ḥadīth is thus; Ziyād’s ḥadīth is thus; Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr’s ḥadīth is thus’— “—as I have described all of that.”

Abū Bakr said, regarding the ḥadīth of Ḥafṣah: Sufyān said: “ʿAmr ibn Qays used to relate it from Umayyah, but I did not dare ask him about it. He used to sit with Khālid ibn Muḥammad al-Zuhrī and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shaybah. At that time, they were among the leading men of Quraysh. They used to sit together in the night market at the mosque gate—which at that time was at the mosque gate. Umayyah asked me to look for Khālid ibn Muḥammad for him. I do not know whether I found him or not. When Umayyah asked me, I dared to approach him and ask him, and he related it to me.”

Abū Bakr related to us: Sufyān related to us: ʿAmr ibn Dīnār said: Abū al-Shaʿthāʾ Jābir ibn Zayd informed me that he heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: “Maymūnah informed me that she and the Messenger of God ﷺ—used to bathe from one vessel.”

Sufyān said: “Shuʿbah admired this chain of transmission: ‘He informed me; I heard.’ It was as if he wished to connect it.”

Abū Bakr said: “Sufyān said, regarding the ḥadīth of al-Rabīʿ about ablution: ‘Ibn ʿAjlān first related it to us from ʿUqayl, from al-Rabīʿ, adding a detail about wiping. He said: “Then he wiped from the crown of his head along his temples until he reached the end of his beard.” When we asked who ʿUqayl was, he did not describe the wiping of the temples to us. There was something in his handwriting, and I disliked prompting him.’”

Abū Bakr related to us: Sufyān related to us: Mujālid related to us, from al-Shaʿbī, who said: “Fāṭimah bint Qays came to Kūfah to visit her brother al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Qays, who was its governor. We went to her and asked her.”

Abū Bakr said: “Sufyān would relate the ḥadīth of al-Khiḍr to us. We would write down some of it, while some would escape us. Then he would relate it to us again, and we would write down what we had missed. When we had completed it, I spoke with him about it, and he related it to us while we looked at the written text.”

Abū Bakr related to us: Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd related to us, from Ibn Shihāb, from Abū Bakr ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Marwān, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Aswad. Abū Bakr said: “Others say: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān.” Abū Bakr said: “I think Ibrāhīm’s version is sounder, because he is one of them and knows him better than anyone else.”

Abū Bakr related to us: Sufyān related to us: ʿAmr ibn Dīnār related to us, from ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Rufayʿ, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār, from a man among the people of Egypt, who said: “I asked Abū al-Dardāʾ about the words of God Most High, ‘For them there is good tidings in the life of this world’ (Qurʾān 10:64).” Sufyān said:

“Then I met ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, and he related it to me from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from ʿAṭāʾ, from a man among the people of Egypt, from Abū al-Dardāʾ, from the Prophet ﷺ—the like of it.”

Sufyān said: “ʿAmr and Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd used to relate the ḥadīth about five wasqs from ʿAmr ibn Yaḥyā. Then I met ʿAmr ibn Yaḥyā, and he related it to me. ʿAmr used to relate— “—from ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Rufayʿ the ḥadīth of Mūsā ibn Ṭarīf: ‘ʿAlī summoned a man on account of his standing among the people.’ I heard it myself from ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, with his chain of transmission, from Mūsā ibn Ṭarīf (219a), from his father. ʿAmr used to relate the ḥadīth of Abū Asmāʾ about Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī’s complaint in abbreviated, interrupted form. Then I heard it myself from Yaḥyā, with a complete, connected chain. ʿAmr used to relate the ḥadīth of Ṣāliḥ ibn Kaysān about the Prophet ﷺ—stopping at al-Abṭaḥ. Then Ṣāliḥ arrived, and ʿAmr said to us, ‘Go and ask him about this ḥadīth.’ We went to him and asked him about—”101 “ʿAmr used to relate the ḥadīth of al-Sanad from ʿUthmān ibn Abī Sulaymān, and he said to us, ‘Go to ʿUthmān and hear it from him.’ We went to ʿUthmān and heard it from him.”

Sufyān said: “ʿAmr ibn Ibrāhīm related to us that Ṭāwūs used to say: ‘I did not handle the paper.’” ʿAmr used to say of it, “It reached me from Ṭāwūs.”

Abū Bakr said, regarding Sufyān’s ḥadīth from Ibn Abī Laylā, from Dāwūd ibn ʿAlī:

Sufyān said: “Ibn Abī Laylā heard this ḥadīth from Dāwūd ibn ʿAlī during the time of the Umayyads.”

Abū Bakr related to us: Sufyān related to us: al-Shaybānī said: “I entered the mosque with al-Shaʿbī, and he said, ‘Do you see any of our companions whom we might sit with? Do you see—’”

“—Abū Ḥuṣayn?” I said, “No.” Then he looked and saw Yazīd ibn al-Aṣamm. He said, “Would you like us to sit with him? His maternal aunt is Maymūnah.” So we sat with him.

Abū Bakr said, regarding the ḥadīth of Sulaymān ibn Suḥaym: Sufyān said: “Ziyād ibn Saʿd had given it to me before I heard it. I said, ‘Will you convey my greetings to Sulaymān?’ He said, ‘Yes.’ When we arrived in Medina, I conveyed my greetings to him and asked him about it, and he related it to me.”

Abū Bakr related to us: Sufyān related to us: ʿAmr related to us, from ʿAṭāʾ. He said: “Ibn Jurayj related to us, from ʿAṭāʾ,” from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: “The Messenger of God ﷺ—performed ʿumrah one night.” He said: “Sometimes Sufyān would relate this ḥadīth, attaching it to Ibn ʿAbbās through ʿAmr and Ibn Jurayj, without mentioning the report. But when he said, ‘He related to us,’ or ‘I heard,’ or ‘He informed us,’ he would give this one through this route and that one through that route.”

Abū Bakr said: Sufyān said: “When Munkadir ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Munkadir arrived, I said, ‘I shall test his memory.’ (219b) I went to him and said, ‘How do you memorize your father’s ḥadīth?’ He said, ‘I saw Abū Bakr standing at Quzaḥ?’ He said, ‘My father related to me, from Jābir.’”

I said, “That was easier for him.”

Sufyān said, regarding the ḥadīth of Ibn ʿAbbās, “Is there a ḥajj for this?”: “Ibn—”

Al-Munkadir had related it to us first as a mursal report. He was told, “You heard it only from Ibrāhīm.” So I went to Ibrāhīm and asked him about it, and he related it to me. He said, “I related it to Muḥammad ibn al-Munkadir, and he performed the pilgrimage with all his family.”

Abū Bakr related to us: Sufyān related to us: Sulaymān al-Aḥwal related to us; he was trustworthy.

“Abū Bakr was asked about al-Zuhrī’s report, in which he said, ‘ʿUrwah related to me: I heard Karz ibn ʿAlqamah.’ Was it ‘he informed me’ or ‘he related to me’? He replied, ‘I know of only two reports from al-Zuhrī in which he says “he related to me”: this one and the report about the wasq.’ He said, ‘Sufyān did not do this deliberately. He regarded “he related to me” and “he informed me” as equivalent.’”

Abū Bakr related to us: Sufyān related to us, saying: Kathīr related to us, from one of his relatives, that he heard his grandfather, al-Muṭṭalib ibn Abī Wadāʿah, say: “I saw the Prophet ﷺ—praying near the gate of Banū Sahm, while people passed in front of him. There was no screen between him and the circumambulation.”

Sufyān said: Ibn Jurayj had related it to us at first from Kathīr ibn Kathīr, from his father, from al-Muṭṭalib ibn Abī Wadāʿah. When we asked him about it, he said, “It is not from my father. One of my relatives told us that he heard it from al-Muṭṭalib.”

Abū Bakr said: I asked ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Qāsim ibn Abī al-ʿAbbās, “What was your grandfather’s name?” He replied, “Al-Sāʾib ibn Farūkh. He was Abū al-ʿAbbās, the blind poet.”

Ādam related to us, from Shuʿbah: Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit related to us, saying: I asked Abū al-ʿAbbās al-Makkī, who was a poet and whose reports were not regarded with suspicion.

Abū Bakr related to us: Sufyān related to us: Ibn Abī Najīḥ related to us: ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿĀmir informed us that he heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr say: The Messenger of God ﷺ—said, “He is not one of us who does not show mercy to our young and recognize the right of our elders.” Sufyān said: There were three men of Banū ʿĀmir in Mecca. ʿAmr related to us from ʿUrwah ibn ʿĀmir; Ibn Abī Najīḥ related to us from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿĀmir; and I heard directly from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿĀmir.

Abū Bakr related to us: Sufyān related to us: ʿAmr related to me, saying: Ṣuhayb, the client of ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĀmir ibn Kurayz, informed me: I heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr say: The Prophet ﷺ—said, “Whoever kills a sparrow or anything larger without just cause, God will question him about killing it.” They said, “Messenger of God, what is its just cause?” He said, “He slaughters it and eats it, and does not cut off its head and throw it away.” Sufyān was told, “Ḥammād says in this report, ‘Ṣuhayb al-Ḥadhdhāʾ informed me.’” Sufyān replied, “I never heard ʿAmr say ‘Ṣuhayb al-Ḥadhdhāʾ’ in it. He said only ‘Ṣuhayb, the client of ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĀmir.’”

He said: Sufyān related to us: ʿAmr ibn Dīnār said, “I heard Wahb ibn Munabbih at his home in Ṣanʿāʾ, and he gave me a walnut from his house.”

Sufyān said: Al-Zuhrī would always express uncertainty, saying, “Zayd or Abū Lubābah.”

Abū Bakr said: Sufyān was told, “Shuʿbah made ʿAbd Allāh ibn Dīnār swear an oath—”

—concerning the report, “The sale of the right of clientage and its gift were forbidden.” Sufyān said, “But we did not make him swear; we heard it from him many times.” Then he laughed.

Abū Ṣāliḥ and Ibn Bukayr related to us, saying: al-Layth ibn Saʿd related to us: Rabīʿah ibn Abī ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said, “ʿAbd Allāh ibn Dīnār related to me—and he was among the upright Muslims, truthful and devout—: The sun set while we were with ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar, and we continued on our way. When we realized that evening had come, we said to him, ‘The prayer!’ He fell silent and continued until the twilight had disappeared and the stars had come out. Then he dismounted and performed the two prayers together. Afterward he said, ‘When the Messenger of God ﷺ—was traveling at a brisk pace, I saw him perform these two prayers’”—meaning, “he joined them after nightfall.”

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us: Sufyān related to us: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar related to us, more than seventy years ago, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: ʿUmar came to the Prophet ﷺ—and said, “Messenger of God, I have acquired wealth unlike any I have ever acquired. I have secured the hundred shares that are in Khaybar, and I wish to draw near to God, Mighty and Majestic, through them.” The Prophet ﷺ—said, “ʿUmar, retain the principal and dedicate its yield.”

He said: Sufyān related to us: Ibn Jurayj said, “I went to Nāfiʿ, and he spread his saddlebag for me. I sat on it, and he dictated to me while I wrote on my tablets. He said, ‘I heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn—’”

ʿUmar say: The Messenger of God ﷺ—said, “When two parties enter into a sale, each of them has the option to withdraw from the sale so long as they have not separated, unless their sale was made with an option.” He said: When Ibn ʿUmar made a sale and wished to make it binding, he would walk a short distance and then return.

Abū Bakr said: Regarding the report of Ibn Abī Ṣaʿṣaʿah, “It is likely to become the best of a man’s possessions,” and his other report, “Neither jinn nor human beings will hear it”:

Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd had related it to me from him. I met him and he related it to me.

Abū Bakr related to us: Sufyān related to us, regarding the report of ʿIyāḍ, from Abū Saʿīd, from the Prophet ﷺ: “The thing I fear most for you is what God brings forth from the earth’s vegetation.” Sufyān said: Al-Aʿmash would often ask me to repeat this report whenever I came to him.

Abū Bakr related to us: Sufyān related to us: A shaykh from among the people of Kūfah, called Shuʿbah—and he was trustworthy—said, “I was with Abū Burdah ibn Abī Mūsā.”

He said: Sufyān said, “I heard four reports from Ziyād ibn ʿAlāqah, from four Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ. I heard no others from him.”

“Sufyān said regarding the report of Tamīm al-Dārī, that the Prophet ﷺ—said, ‘Religion is sincere counsel’: ʿAmr ibn Dīnār had related it to us at first from al-Qaʿqāʿ ibn Ḥakīm, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, as a mursal report. I met Suhayl and said, ‘If I were to ask him about it, perhaps he would relate it to me from his father, and then ʿAmr and I would be on equal footing regarding it.’ So I asked him (221), and Suhayl said, ‘I heard it from the one my father heard it from. ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yazīd al-Laythī, a friend of my father’s from Syria, informed me of it.’”

Al-Ḥumaydī said: Sufyān related to us: Ṣafwān ibn Sulaym related to us, from a woman called Unaysah, from Umm Saʿīd bint Murrah al-Fihrīyah, from her father, that the Messenger of God ﷺ—said, “I and the one who cares for an orphan, whether related to him or not, will be in Paradise like these two,” and he pointed with his two fingers. Sufyān was told, “ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī says that Sufyān is more accurate in this report than Mālik.” Sufyān said, “How would he know? Did he meet Ṣafwān?” They said, “No. But he said that Mālik related it from Ṣafwān, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār.” Sufyān said, “But Unaysah related it from Umm Saʿīd bint Murrah, from her father. Where did he get this chain of transmission from?” Sufyān said, “How well he would have done if he had said to us, ‘Ṣafwān’s cloak is ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār’! That would have been easier for us than having to come up with this difficult chain of transmission.”

Abū Bakr said, regarding the report of ʿUrwah ibn Abī al-Jaʿd, “The Prophet ﷺ—gave him a dinar with which to buy a sacrificial animal”: Sufyān said, “We heard al-Ḥasan ibn ʿUmārah relating it to us, and he said in it, ‘I heard Shabīb say, “I heard ʿUrwah.”’”

When Shabīb was asked, he said, “I did not hear it from ʿUrwah. Al-Ḥasan related it to me from ʿUrwah.”

Abū Bakr said: And the report of al-Sāʾib ibn Khallād, from the Prophet ﷺ: “Gabriel came to me and said, ‘Tell your Companions to raise their voices with the declaration of God’s oneness and the talbiyah.’” Sufyān said, “Ibn Jurayj had concealed a report from me. When ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Bakr came to us, I did not tell him. When he set out for Medina, I related it to him. He said, ‘ʿAwd, you conceal reports from us, then tell us about them after their people have gone? I will not transmit it from you. Or do you want me to transmit it from you?’ So he wrote to ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Bakr about it.”

“Sufyān said: Ibn Abī Khālid used to say, ‘I heard al-Mustawrid, the brother of Banū Fihr’—he would pronounce it ungrammatically. I said, ‘Akhā Banī Fihr.’”

“Sufyān said: Abū Bakr related to us: I heard ʿAṭāʾ relate from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr. Sufyān would sometimes say of this report, ‘I do not know whether he mentioned “from his father” in it or not.’ He said: Ibn ʿUmar was asked, ‘Why do we see you touching only these two corners?’

“He replied, ‘The Messenger of God ﷺ—said, “Touching the two corners sheds sins just as the leaves of trees fall away.”’ Sufyān said, ‘ʿAṭāʾ related this to me while he and I were circumambulating.’ He said, ‘It seemed that he did not see me showing admiration for it, so he said, “Do you think little of this, Ibn ʿUyaynah?”’ He replied, ‘I related it to al-Shaʿbī, and he said, “If he had traveled such and such a distance for this report, he would have been worthy of it.”’”

Abū Bakr related to us: Sufyān said, “I heard ʿAṭāʾ often reciting the talbiyah during the circumambulation. He used to enter the state of consecration from Kūfah. I heard from him long ago. Then he came to us on a later visit, and I heard him relate some of what I had heard from him before, but he confused it. So I kept away from him and avoided him.”

Abū Bakr related to us: Sufyān related to us: ʿUmārah ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ ibn Shabramah related to us. He was older than his uncle, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shabramah, and ʿUmārah was also the better of the two.

[SĀLIM IBN ABĪ ḤAFṢAH]

Al-Ḥumaydī related to us: Sufyān related to us: Sālim related to us, saying: “The first time I recognized Saʿīd ibn Jubayr in Mecca was when he prayed one night behind the Station. I was close to Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, though I did not know who he was. I said, ‘O God, bless Muḥammad and the family of Muḥammad as You blessed Abraham and the family of Abraham, and bless Muḥammad and the family of Muḥammad as You blessed—’”

Abraham and the family of Abraham. You are indeed Praiseworthy, Glorious.’ Saʿīd ibn Jubayr tossed a pebble at me, and it seemed he liked that. He said, “Where are you from?” I replied, “From the people of Kūfah,” and that pleased him.

He said: Sufyān related to us, saying: I heard Sālim say: “Whenever al-Shaʿbī saw me, he would say:

‘O God’s constable, stop and fly— like a grain of barley flying away.’

Sālim said: He was mocking me.”

He said: Sufyān related to us: Sālim related to us, saying: “I spoke to Ibrāhīm ibn Yazīd ibn Sharik (222a) al-Taymī as I used to speak to al-Shaʿbī, and he told me a story among his stories.”

Sufyān said: Sālim related to us, saying: “In one of his sermons, Ibrāhīm al-Taymī recited, ‘For those who disbelieve, garments of fire shall be cut out for them’ (Qurʾān 22:19). Ibrāhīm said, ‘Glory be to Him who cut garments from fires!’”

[KARZ AL-ḤĀRITHĪ]

Abū Saʿīd al-Ashajj related to me: Ibn Fuḍayl related to us, from his father, who said: “I saw Karz al-Ḍabbī’s mosque. It had a pit in it, with straw inside, and he had placed a cloak over it to stand on. I saw in Karz’s mosque a peg that he would lean on.”

Ibn Abī ʿUmar related to us: Sufyān related to us, from Ibn Shubrumah, who said: “We accompanied—”

Karz al-Ḥārithī. Whenever we stopped, he would simply look around like this. When he saw a spot that pleased him, he would go and pray there until it was time to depart.”

[MUṬARRIF IBN ṬARĪF]

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us: Sufyān related to us, saying: “Muṭarrif ibn Ṭarīf said—and I was told this from him—‘I would not like to have spoken, even if I possessed the whole world and all that is in it.’”

Sufyān said: He means, “I would not like to have exposed myself to the displeasure of God, Exalted is He.”

[ABŪ SINĀN ḌIRĀR IBN MURRAH]

Abū Bakr related to us: Sufyān related to us, saying: “Abū Sinān would buy something from the market and carry it. A man would come to him and say, ‘Abū Sinān, let me carry it for you,’ but he would refuse. Then he would say, ‘He does not love the arrogant’ (Qurʾān 16:23). Sufyān said: He was an Arab elder, a man of fine bearing.”

Sufyān said: I heard Abū Sinān say, “Today I milked the ewe and drew a waterskin’s worth of water for my family.” It used to be said, “The best of you is the one most beneficial to his family.”

Abū Bakr related to us: Sufyān related to us, saying: Abū Sinān said, “A dining table in Kūfah at which even a single lawful dirham is eaten is a rarity.”

Abū Saʿīd al-Ashajj related to us: ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Aḥlaj related to us, saying: Ḍirār ibn Murrah, Abū Sinān, used to say, “Do not come to me as a group; let each man come alone. When you gather together, you talk; when one of you is alone, he cannot help but study his portion or remember his Lord, Mighty and Majestic.”

Abū Saʿīd related to us: al-Muḥāribī related to us, saying: “On Fridays, Ḍirār (222b) and Muḥammad ibn Sūqah would each seek out the other. When they met, they would sit and weep.”

Abū Bakr related to us: Sufyān related to us: Yazīd ibn Abī Ziyād related to us—in Mecca—that he heard ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā relate from al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib, who said: “I saw the Messenger of God ﷺ—raise his hands when he began the prayer.” Then I came to Kūfah, met him there, and heard him relate it. He added to it, “Then he did not do so again.” I thought they had prompted him. When I met him in Mecca, his memory was better than when I met him in Kūfah, for his memory had deteriorated—or he said, “had changed.”

Abū Bakr related to us, saying: Sufyān said: “Al-Hajarī was one who raised reports to the Prophet, and he would raise most of these reports. When he related the report, ‘That he should worship idols,’ I said, ‘As for this one, yes.’ I told him, ‘Do not raise these reports.’”

Sufyān said: “One day I went looking for him. They said, ‘He is in the house.’ I found him playing chess, and found that they had set him up.”

Abū Bakr related to us: Sufyān related to us: Ṣāliḥ ibn Ṣāliḥ ibn Ḥayy related to us. He was better than his two sons, and ʿAlī was the better of the two.

[ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Saʿīd ibn Abjar]

He said: Sufyān related to us; he said: Ibn Abjar said: “We have no authority over the daytime.”

He said: Sufyān related to us; he said: Ibn Abjar said: “An hour of our lives was lost in the bathhouse.”

Al-Ḥumaydī said: Sufyān related to us; he said: Ibn Abjar heard a son of his say to his servant:

“O weaver!” He said: “My son, you are only insulting your father.” Sufyān said: “He means: ‘He is the one who put him to work at weaving; if that is a fault, it was your father who put him to it.’”

He said: Sufyān related to us; he said: I heard Ibn Abjar say: “What excellent property—or livestock—is the knife: chickens.”

I heard Ibn Abjar, when something was sent to him, say: “Do such-and-such, and seek God’s healing.”

He said: One day I came to Ibn Abjar, and he said: “This is a sickly face.” I disliked what he said, and replied: “I am in good health.” Ibn Abjar said: “I do not know, I do not know.”

He said: Ibn al-Khurāsānī came with a boy of his, and Ibn Abjar felt his neck and sent him a remedy. The man said: “Do you think it is scrofula?” Ibn Abjar said: (223a) “A breath from among the breaths of your Lord.” He refused to call it scrofula.

He said: A boy was brought, and he felt his belly and said: “I find ḥadhar.” The man said to him: “Do you think it is a hernia?”

“I find ḥadhar,” he said. He did not say “hernia.”

Ibn Abjar would begin with those who came to ask him for a legal opinion, taking them in order, one after another.

[Layth ibn Abī Sulaym]

Abū Bakr related to us; Saʿīd al-Qaddāḥ related to us; he said: Ummat Allāh, the client of Ṭāwūs, told me: “I never saw anyone writing in Ṭāwūs’s presence except Layth ibn Abī Sulaym, on tablets.”

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us; Sufyān related to us; he said: I asked Ayyūb: “Abū Bakr, what kept you from hearing from Ṭāwūs—that is, hearing a great deal from Ṭāwūs?” He said:

“I came to him and saw him between two men: Layth ibn Abī Sulaym and ʿAbd al-Karīm Abū Umayyah. So I went back and left him.”

Abū Saʿīd ʿAbd Allāh ibn Saʿīd al-Ashajj related to me; he said: Abū Khālid al-Aḥmar related to us; he said: “The devout worshippers of Kūfah were four. Some were given to worship both night and day; some were given to worship by day, but not by night; and some were given neither to worship by night nor by day. Layth ibn Abī Sulaym was given to worship night and day; Khalaf ibn Ḥawshab was given to worship by night; Mughīrah ibn Ayyūb was given to worship by day; and I have forgotten the other.”

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us; Sufyān related to us, from Ibn Sawqah; he said: “ʿAwn ibn ʿAbd Allāh charged me with a bequest—”

“—to me.”

He said: Sufyān related to us; he said: I heard Muḥammad ibn Sawqah say: Muḥārib ibn Dithār said to me: “Jāmiʿ ibn Abī Rāshid is more pleasing to me than al-Rabīʿ ibn Abī Rāshid because he helps his brothers.”

ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān related to us; ʿAbd Allāh informed us; Mālik—that is, Ibn Miʿwal—informed us; he said: Al-Rabīʿ ibn Abī Rāshid was asked: “Will you not sit and relate traditions?” He said: “Whenever remembrance of death leaves my heart for an hour, my heart is corrupted.”

Mālik said: “I have never seen a man display more grief than he did.”

“Ibn ʿUthmān related to us; ʿAbd Allāh informed us; he said: Sufyān related it to us from Zubayd; he said: ‘I would be glad if there were an intention behind everything, even eating and sleeping.’”

Ibn Abī ʿUmar related to us; Sufyān related to us; he said: I heard ʿAbd al-Karīm Abū Umayyah say: “No knowledge comes to me, nor leaves me, until I become angry.” Then he said to the man: “Ask whatever you wish.” And he became angry and said: “I will not say, ‘I do not know’; nor will I say, ‘I have not heard it’; nor will I say, ‘I have no knowledge of it.’”

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us; he said: Sufyān related to us; ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Saʿīd ibn Abjar related to us, and he was the son of Ḥayyān ibn Abjar.

Abū Bakr ibn ʿAbd al-Malik related it to us; ʿAbd al-Razzāq related to us, from Maʿmar, from Ayyūb; he said: ʿAbd al-Karīm was mentioned, and Ayyūb said: “May ﵀; he was not trustworthy.” I asked: “Why, Abū Bakr?” He replied: “He asked me about a tradition from ʿIkrimah, and I related it to him; then later he said: ‘ʿIkrimah related it to me.’”

Abū Bakr ibn ʿAbd al-Malik related to us; ʿAbd al-Razzāq related to us, from Maʿmar; he said: Ḥammād said to me: “Tell me about the scholars of Baṣrah.” He said: “I mentioned them, but did not mention ʿAbd al-Karīm.” He laughed and said: “You left out the most learned of them.”

Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmar related to us; Sufyān related to us; he said: “ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Abjar was ill in Kūfah. Whenever we went in to see him, the words he would say were: ‘I am content with God.’”

Sufyān said: “If I had looked in Kūfah for a man who was careful in retaining traditions, I would not have found one.”

[Jābir ibn Yazīd al-Juʿfī]

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us; Sufyān related to us; he said: I heard Jābir al-Juʿfī say: “I have thirty thousand traditions that no one has asked me about since.”

He said: Sufyān related to us; he said: I heard a man ask Jābir about God’s words, “I will not leave this land until my father gives me permission, or God decides for me; He is the best of judges.”

Jābir replied: “The interpretation of this verse has not yet come.” Sufyān said: “He lied.” We asked Sufyān: “What did he mean by that?” He said: “The Rāfiḍīs say that ʿAlī is in the clouds, and that he will not come forth with any of his descendants who rise until a caller calls from heaven”—meaning ʿAlī, who calls out, “Go forth with so-and-so.” Sufyān said: “Jābir claimed that he had read the interpretation of the verse, but he lied; it concerned Joseph’s brothers.”

Abū Bakr related to us; Sufyān related to us; he said: I heard Jābir relating about thirty traditions, none of which do I consider it lawful for me to mention.

He said: “I would not like to have mentioned any of it (224a), even if I had such-and-such.”

Abū Bakr said: I heard Ibn Aktham al-Khurāsānī say to Sufyān: “Abū Muḥammad, what do you think of those who criticized Jābir al-Juʿfī for saying, ‘The legatee of the legatees related it to me’?”

Sufyān said: “That is the least of it.”

Abū Bakr said: Sufyān related to us; he said: “People used to criticize Jābir before he openly professed what he professed. When he openly professed it, people began to suspect his traditions, and some people abandoned him.” He was asked: “What did he profess?” He said: “Belief in the return.”

Abū Bakr related to us; Sufyān related to us; he said: I heard Jābir al-Juʿfī concerning a tradition [and] Ibn Ḥayy related it to me from him, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā: “He drank fermented nabīdh from a clay jar among the participants at Badr.” Jābir said to me: “What would he do with it? And what do you think his answer is?” I heard Abū Jaʿfar say: “Our nabīdh has never turned sour.”

Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmmār related to us; ʿAbd Allāh ibn Dāwūd related to us; he said:

Munkhal, a descendant of Bahz ibn Ḥakīm, related to me from Ibn ʿAwn, from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad: “He used to ask me, ‘When will so-and-so come forth? And when will so-and-so come forth?’” He said: “I thought he meant Jābir al-Juʿfī.”

Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh related to us; he said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and Yaḥyā related to us, from Sufyān, from Manṣūr, from Mujāhid, and Ibn al-Aṣbahānī from ʿIkrimah, concerning “Then We made him another creation”: “He breathed the spirit into him.” Muḥammad said: I said to Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd: “Wakīʿ says it is from Layth.” He replied: “Glory be to God! I tell Sufyān, ‘Do not relate to me from—’”

“—Jābir, and you say it is from Layth?” Muḥammad said: I mentioned it to Wakīʿ. Wakīʿ said:

“Manṣūr was more beloved to us.”

Abū Bakr related to us; Sufyān related to us; al-Zuhrī related to us; Sulaymān ibn Yasār and Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān informed me, from Abū Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “The Jews and Christians do not dye their hair, so differ from them.” Sufyān said: “When we left al-Zuhrī, Ayyūb al-Sakhtiyānī, Ismāʿīl ibn Umayyah, Ismāʿīl ibn Muslim (224b), and Ashʿath ibn Suwwār al-Hudhalī sat with other jurists. They said: ‘Come, let us review what we heard from al-Zuhrī.’ They sat down, and I sat with them. Ayyūb said: ‘May I be ransomed for you! Did you not hear him say, “Sālim ibn ʿAbd Allāh informed me; Abū Bakr ibn ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh informed me”?’ He kept going back to the descendants of ʿAbd Allāh, as if that pleased him. Then they reviewed what they had heard and mentioned this tradition, ‘The Jews and Christians do not dye their hair.’ Some said it was from Abū Salamah; others said it was from Sulaymān ibn Yasār. When they had gone on at length, I said—and I was a boy—‘It is from both of them.’ They protested at my grammatical solecism. Then Ismāʿīl said: ‘It is as the boy, the one among you with the best memory, said: it is from both of them.’” “At that gathering Ashʿath ibn Suwwār said: ‘There is nothing that came to al-Zuhrī that we had not already heard from our companions in Kūfah.’ The people loathed him so much that I could see it. From that day on, I loathed him and transmitted nothing from him. After that, I studied Arabic grammar.”

Abū Bakr related to me; Sufyān related to us; he said: I heard al-Zuhrī say: Abū Idrīs al-Khawlānī informed me that he heard ʿUbādah ibn al-Ṣāmit say: “We were with the Prophet ﷺ—in an assembly when he said: ‘Give me your pledge.’” He then mentioned the tradition.

He mentioned the tradition. Sufyān said: “When al-Zuhrī related this tradition, Abū Bakr al-Hudhalī said to me: ‘Memorize this for me.’ When I stood up, I dictated it to him”—or he said: “I informed him of it.”

Abū Bakr related to us; Sufyān related to us; he said: Al-Zuhrī said: “I did not hear this tradition until I came to Syria”—meaning that the Prophet ﷺ forbade eating any beast of prey with fangs. Abū Bakr said: Sufyān related this to us; he said: “This is what we retained from al-Zuhrī, from Abū Idrīs al-Khawlānī, who informed him: ‘I met Abū al-Dardāʾ and retained what I heard from him; ʿUbādah ibn al-Ṣāmit and retained what I heard from him; and Shaddād ibn Aws and retained what I heard from him. But Muʿādh ibn Jabal eluded me.’ So-and-so informed me”—Sufyān said: “Al-Zuhrī named him, but I forgot his name.” “And Maʿmar said in his version of the tradition: ‘Yazīd ibn ʿUmayrah informed me’ ‘that Muʿādh ibn Jabal would never sit in an assembly without saying: “God is a just judge; blessed is His name; the doubters have perished.”’”

Sufyān said: “The tradition went on at length, so I retained only this.”

Abū Bakr said: Sufyān said: “The tradition went on at length, so I retained only this.”

Abū Bakr said: Sufyān said: “I heard al-Zuhrī relating it, but I did not retain it”—meaning the tradition of Wāʾil ibn Dāwūd from his father. Sufyān said: “When al-Zuhrī related a tradition to us from Anas, his wording was ‘I heard.’”

Abū Bakr said: Sufyān related to us; he said: Al-Zuhrī related to us—no further authority is needed for him—he said: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab informed me, from Abū Hurayrah, who said: “A Bedouin entered the mosque while the Prophet ﷺ—was sitting there. He stood up, and when he had finished, he said: ‘O God, have mercy on me and Muḥammad.’”

Abū Bakr said: Sufyān said: “I heard al-Zuhrī, and retained it from him, from Shuʿbah, who informed him, from Abū Hurayrah, who said: The Prophet ﷺ—said: ‘When Friday comes, there is at every door of the mosque—’” Sufyān was asked: “They say ‘al-Aghar’ in this tradition.” He replied: “I never heard al-Zuhrī mention al-Aghar at all. He only says it from Saʿīd, who informed him, from Abū Hurayrah.”

Sufyān said: “I heard al-Zuhrī invite people to sit with him over this tradition: ‘ʿUmar had Abū Bakrah repent.’” He said: “When we left al-Zuhrī, our companions ʿAmr and others told us that he had related it from Saʿīd. I had not retained that. When they informed me that he had related it from Saʿīd, I imagined that I had recalled it, and from then on I always say of it, God willing, ‘from Saʿīd.’”

Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr related to us; Sufyān related to us, from al-Zuhrī, from Saʿīd; he said:

ʿAlī said: “He has the better right to take her back so long as she has not performed the ritual bath after her third menstrual period.”

I heard ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh say: I said to Sufyān: “I found this tradition in my father’s book, from al-Ḥasan ibn Ṣāliḥ, from you, from al-Zuhrī, from Saʿīd, from ʿAlī.”

He replied: “Yes.”

Abū Bakr said: Sufyān was asked: “But Mālik ibn Anas says of it, ‘The child belongs to the bed; the adulterer gets the stone’—”

“—that is, in the tradition of ʿUrwah from ʿĀʾishah.” (225b) Sufyān replied: “But we did not retain from al-Zuhrī that he said it in this tradition.”

Sufyān was asked about the tradition of ʿUrwah from ʿĀʾishah: “It says that she observes mourning for him for four months and ten days.” He replied: “Al-Zuhrī did not tell us this in his version of the tradition. Ayyūb ibn Mūsā told us this in his version.”

Abū Bakr said: Sufyān would sometimes say of this tradition: “And upon you”; when he stopped, he would say: “Upon you”—that is, when the Jew greeted the Prophet ﷺ.

Sufyān said: I heard Ibn Jurayj relate from al-Zuhrī; he said:

“Have you not seen Muḥriz al-Mudlijī?” I said: “Abū al-Walīd, it is Mujazziz.” He fell silent and withdrew.

Abū Bakr said: For a time, Sufyān was uncertain about the tradition, “The Prophet ﷺ—heard Abū Mūsā’s recitation.” He was uncertain about the authority from ʿUrwah and would waver over it, saying “or ʿAmrah” and not mentioning the report. Then he mentioned the report, affirmed ʿUrwah in its chain, and abandoned the uncertainty.

Abū Bakr said: Sufyān was asked: “Maʿmar relates the tradition of the Prophet ﷺ—‘No one’s property benefited us as much as Abū Bakr’s property’ from Saʿīd.” He replied:

“We heard it from al-Zuhrī only from ʿUrwah, from ʿĀʾishah.”

I heard Abū al-Walīd Hishām ibn ʿAbd al-Malik say: Sufyān related to us from al-Zuhrī. He was asked, “From ʿUrwa?” He said, “I think so.” He was asked, “From ʿĀʾisha?” He said, “I suppose so.”

Then he said: I heard him say, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUrwa, from ʿĀʾisha, that the Prophet ﷺ—said: “No one’s wealth benefited us as much as Abū Bakr’s wealth.”

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us: Sufyān related to us from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUrwa, from ʿĀʾisha, who said: “With these two hands of mine, I perfumed the Messenger of God ﷺ—for his consecration when he entered the state of ritual consecration, and for his release from it before he circumambulated the House.” Sufyān was asked, “Did you hear it from al-Zuhrī?” He said:

“Yes.”

He also said: Al-Zuhrī related to us—and no one else is needed in this report—saying: ʿUrwa informed me, from Zaynab bt. Abī Salama, from Ḥabība bt. Umm Ḥabība, from her mother; or Ḥabība, from Zaynab bt. Jaḥsh, who said: “The Messenger of God ﷺ—awoke with his face flushed, saying, ‘There is no god but God. Woe to the Arabs, from an evil that has drawn near. Today, an opening this size has been made in the barrier of Gog and Magog.’” Sufyān made a circle of ten with his fingers. I said, “Messenger of God, shall we perish while the righteous are among us?” He said, “Yes, when wickedness becomes widespread.”

Sufyān said: “In this report, I remember four women from al-Zuhrī who had seen the Prophet ﷺ: two of his wives, Umm Ḥabība and Zaynab bt. Jaḥsh, and two of his stepdaughters, Zaynab bt. Umm Salama and Ḥabība bt. Umm Ḥabība. Their father was ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaḥsh; he died in Abyssinia.”

Abū Bakr related to us: Sufyān related to us: al-Zuhrī related to us, saying: ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr informed me, from al-Miswar ibn Makhrama and Marwān ibn al-Ḥakam, who both said: “The Messenger of God ﷺ—set out from Medina in the year of al-Ḥudaybiya with a little over a thousand people. When he reached Dhū al-Ḥulayfa, he garlanded the sacrificial animals, marked them, and entered the state of consecration there for the lesser pilgrimage.” Sufyān said: “This is what I retained from him and mastered; Maʿmar confirmed it for me here.”

Sufyān was asked, “Maʿmar relates it from ʿUrwa, from al-Miswar and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd al-Qārī, in the report about the bees, from ʿUmar.” Sufyān said: “I did not hear al-Zuhrī mention al-Miswar in it.”

Abū Bakr related to us: al-Zuhrī and Hishām ibn ʿUrwa related to us, from ʿUrwa, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd al-Qārī, who said: “I heard ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb teaching the people the testimony of faith from the pulpit.” Sufyān said: “The two of them mentioned ʿUmar’s testimony in their report, but I did not retain it.” Sufyān said: “That was because I used to recite the testimony of Ibn Masʿūd.”

He also said: Sufyān related to us: “We retained it from al-Zuhrī, and al-Zuhrī related it to us from ʿUrwa, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd al-Qārī, who said: ‘After the dawn prayer, ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb circumambulated the House seven times, then set out for Medina. When he reached Dhū Ṭuwā and the sun had risen, he prayed two cycles.’” Sufyān was asked, “Mālik, Maʿmar, and al-Awzāʿī relate it from Ḥumayd, not from ʿUrwa.” Sufyān said: “As for me, I retain it from ʿUrwa.”

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us (226b), saying: Sufyān related to us; al-Zuhrī related to us and one of them was Hishām ibn ʿUrwa—from Marwān ibn al-Ḥakam, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Some poetry contains wisdom.” Sufyān once said: “Al-Zuhrī, from ʿUrwa, from Marwān; and Hishām, from his father”—Marwān is not in that chain. Sufyān was asked, “Mālik says that the Prophet ﷺ—was asked about bitʿ.” Sufyān said: “I did not hear him mention bitʿ in it.”

He also said: Sufyān related to us: “I heard Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, the client of the family of Ṭalḥa, ʿAbd Rabbih and Yaḥyā, the sons of Saʿīd, and Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAlqama relate that they heard it from Abū Salama, who heard it from Abū Qatāda, from the Messenger of God ﷺ—with wording like al-Zuhrī’s report, except that they did not mention its beginning: ‘I used to see dreams.’ Their report begins only at this point: ‘A dream is from God,’ and continues to the end.” Sufyān said: “Al-Zuhrī was the one among them with the best retention and the most reliable narration of the report. We heard it from al-Zuhrī in its entirety.”

Sufyān related to us: “Al-Zuhrī related to us—I have mastered it for you—saying: Abū Salama ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān informed me, from Abū Hurayra, that the Messenger of God ﷺ—said: ‘Whoever fasts Ramaḍān in faith and seeking reward will be forgiven his past sins.’” Sufyān was asked:

“Mālik does not give this report from Abū Salama, from Abū Hurayra; he gives it only in the report of Ḥumayd.” Sufyān said: “But I do give it; I have mastered it for you from Abū Salama—”

—from Abū Hurayra. I did not hear Ḥumayd’s report from him.

He also said: Sufyān related to us: al-Zuhrī related to us: Abū Salama related to me, from Abū Hurayra, that he said: “When the Negus died, the Prophet ﷺ—said, ‘Ask forgiveness for him.’” Sufyān said: “This is from Abū Hurayra, and I retained it from al-Zuhrī. As for Saʿīd’s report, that the Prophet performed the funeral prayer over him, I did not hear him mention Abū Hurayra in it.”

He also said: Sufyān related to us: “Al-Zuhrī related to us exactly this; he added nothing beyond these three. He said:

‘Ḥumayd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh, and Sulaymān ibn Yasār informed me that they heard Abū Hurayra say: “I asked ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb (227a) about a man from Bahrain who had divorced his wife once or twice, after which her waiting period ended; another man married her, then divorced her or died leaving her a widow, and then her first husband married her again.”

“He said: ‘She is with him according to what remains of her divorces.’”

Sufyān was asked, “Was Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab among them?” He said: “Al-Zuhrī related it to us exactly this way; he added nothing beyond these three. When he had finished, he said: ‘I do not retain Saʿīd from al-Zuhrī in this report. But Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd related it to us from Saʿīd, from Abū Hurayra, with the same wording.’ He said, ‘That is enough for you.’”

Sufyān was asked, “Mālik and Maʿmar do not say….” He said: “But I do say it; I have mastered it from al-Zuhrī in both reports.”

Sufyān was asked, “Maʿmar relates the report about avoiding vessels from ʿAṭāʾ—”

—ibn Yazīd al-Laythī.” He said: “He did not retain it.” He said, “He did not retain it; he said, ‘ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh informed me.’” Then he said: “Maʿmar was mistaken.”

He said: “Al-ʿAbbās ibn al-Walīd related to me: My father informed me, from al-Awzāʿī, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh and ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yazīd, from Abū Saʿīd.” Sufyān said: “Al-Zuhrī related it to us, and I retained it from him. It was a long report, so I retained this part. He said:

‘ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh informed me. He said: I asked ʿĀʾisha, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ—and said, “Mother of the Believers, tell me about the illness in which the Messenger of God ﷺ—died.” She said: “During the illness in which he died, the Messenger of God would become distressed and blow as a raisin eater blows.”’ Sufyān would sometimes say, ‘Then we began comparing his blowing to that.’ ‘He used to go around among his wives. When he grew weaker and his pain became severe, he asked their permission to stay with me; they gave him permission. He came to me leaning on two men, one of whom was al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib.’ ʿUbayd Allāh said: ‘I related it to Ibn ʿAbbās, and he said, “Did she not tell you who the other was?” I said, “No.” He said, “The other was ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib.”’”

Sufyān said: “People say, ‘And the Prophet ﷺ—was leading the prayer at Minā’; what I retained is what we know.”

(227b) Abū Yūsuf said: “He was mistaken in the report of al-Zuhrī, from ʿUbayd Allāh, from Ibn ʿAbbās.”

Sufyān said: “ʿAmr ibn Dīnār had related it to us at first, from al-Zuhrī, before he met him, and said in it, ‘They are [to be attributed] to their fathers.’ When al-Zuhrī related it to us, I checked the wording, and he did not say ‘They are [to be attributed] to their fathers’; he said, ‘They are among them.’”

Regarding the report of al-Ṣaʿb ibn Jaththāma, Sufyān used to say in the report:

“I gave the Messenger of God ﷺ—the meat of a wild ass”. Sufyān would sometimes add, “dripping with blood,” and sometimes not. At times, Sufyān would say, “an ass”; then he came to say “meat” until he died.

Abū Bakr said regarding the report, “The Prophet ﷺ—passed by a sheep”:

Sufyān said: “Sometimes he attributed it to Ibn ʿAbbās without mentioning Maymūna; when he was pressed, he said it was from Maymūna.” He was told, “Maʿmar does not say in it, ‘So they tanned it,’ and says that al-Zuhrī used to reject tanning.” Sufyān said: “But I retain it in this report, and in the other report—that of ʿAmr, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās. We wanted from this report only this phrase: ‘Only eating it was forbidden.’”

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us: Sufyān related to us, saying: I heard al-Zuhrī say:

“ʿUbayd Allāh informed me, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he heard ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb ﵁—say: ‘We used to recite: “Do not disavow your fathers, for it is disbelief on your part to disavow your fathers.”’”

Sufyān said: “I heard al-Zuhrī, and he related it to us from ʿUbayd Allāh, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said: ‘Know that stoning is due for anyone who commits adultery, if that person is muḥṣan and the proof is established against them, or if there is pregnancy or confession.’”

I heard al-Zuhrī say: “ʿUbayd Allāh informed me, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: ‘When the sun had passed its zenith, ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb went out and sat on the pulpit. The muezzin began his call to prayer, and when he fell silent, ʿUmar stood and spoke, praising and extolling God.’”

Sufyān would sometimes say in this report: “Maʿmar confirmed it for me.” When pressed on it, he would say: “As for these words, I retain them from al-Zuhrī, from what was written on my tablets.” Sometimes he would say, “He confirmed it for me,” when the report extended beyond these words to the account of the portico (228a).

Sufyān said: “Maʿmar related to us from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUbayd Allāh, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: ‘I heard ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb on the pulpit say: “God sent Muḥammad with the truth and sent down the Book to him. Among what was sent down to him was the verse of stoning. The Messenger of God ﷺ—stoned, and we stoned after him.”’”

Sufyān said: “I heard the whole report from al-Zuhrī and retained some parts of it that day.”

Abū Bakr said: Sufyān related to us: “We came to al-Zuhrī at the house of Ibn al-Kharrār. He said, ‘If you wish, I will relate twenty reports to you; or, if you wish, I will relate the report of the portico.’ I was the youngest of the group, and, because of its length, I wished that he would not relate it.” He said the group: “Relate the report of the portico to us.” Al-Zuhrī related it to us from ʿUbayd Allāh, from Ibn ʿAbbās: “I heard ʿUmar ﵁.” I retained some parts of it that day; afterward, Maʿmar related the remainder to me.

Abū Bakr said: I heard Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Qaṭṭān ask Sufyān about this report: “We performed dry ablution with the Messenger of God ﷺ—up to the shoulders.” Sufyān said: “I was present when Ismāʿīl ibn Umayya came to al-Zuhrī and said, ‘Abū Bakr, people are criticizing you over two reports.’ He said, ‘What are they?’ He replied, ‘We performed dry ablution with the Prophet ﷺ—up to the shoulders.’ Ismāʿīl also mentioned the report of ʿUbayd Allāh about touching the armpit.”

Al-Zuhrī seemed to reject it and did reject it. I went to ʿAmr ibn Dīnār and told him, for I had heard him relate from al-Zuhrī. ʿAmr said: “Al-Zuhrī related to me from ʿUbayd Allāh that ʿUmar ordered a man to perform ablution because he had touched his armpit.”

Abū Bakr said: “After that, I heard one of our companions say that he had visited Sufyān to ask a favor and asked him about the report of dry ablution. Sufyān related it to him from ʿAmr. I said to the man who told me: ‘I think he was referring only to the report about touching the armpit.’ I told him some of this story, or something like it. The matter continued to trouble me until I asked Sufyān about it. He said: ‘It is from al-Zuhrī, not from ʿAmr. The report that ʿAmr related to us is the report about the armpit.’”

I told him about the man who had recounted it to me. Sufyān said: “Either he did not retain what I said to him, or I was mistaken.”

Abū Bakr related to us: Sufyān related to us (228b), saying: “I heard al-Zuhrī more than once say: ‘I heard Sulaymān ibn Yasār say: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: A woman—’”

“—from Khathʿam asked the Messenger of God ﷺ—on the morning of the Sacrifice, while al-Faḍl was riding behind him. She said: ‘God’s obligation of pilgrimage upon His servants has come due for my father, who is an old man and cannot keep himself steady on a mount. Do you think I may perform the pilgrimage on his behalf?’ He said, ‘Yes.’”

Sufyān said: “At first, ʿAmr had related it to us from al-Zuhrī, from Sulaymān ibn Yasār, from Ibn ʿAbbās. This is how I remember it: ‘Do you think I may perform the pilgrimage on his behalf?’ Others give this report with the wording: ‘Do you think I may perform the pilgrimage on his behalf?’ He said, ‘Yes.’ She then said:

‘Will that benefit him, Messenger of God?’ He said, ‘Yes, just as if one of you had a debt and paid it.’ When al-Zuhrī came to us and related it, I checked the wording and found that he did not say these words that ʿAmr had related.”

Abū Bakr related to us: Sufyān related to us: “At first, before we met al-Zuhrī, ʿAmr ibn Dīnār related to us from Ibn Shihāb, from Mālik ibn Aws ibn al-Ḥadathān, who said: ‘I came with one hundred dinars, seeking to exchange them. Ṭalḥa ibn ʿUbayd Allāh said to me, “We have exchange money. Wait for us until our treasurer comes from al-Ghāba.” He took the hundred dinars from me. I asked ʿUmar, and he said to me, “Do not part from him, for I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ—say: ‘Gold for silver is usury, except hand to hand; wheat for wheat, except hand to hand; barley for barley is usury, except hand to hand; and al-namir for dates is usury, except hand to hand.’”’”102

Sufyān said: “When al-Zuhrī came to us, I checked his version and found that he did not mention these words. Al-Zuhrī said: ‘I heard Mālik ibn Aws ibn al-Ḥadathān al-Naṣrī say: I heard ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb say: I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ—say: “Gold for silver is usury, except hand to hand.”’ He then mentioned the rest in exactly the same way.”

Sufyān said: “This is the soundest report transmitted from the Prophet ﷺ—on this matter—meaning exchange.” Sufyān explained his words “hand to hand” explicitly: “except like for like.” Sufyān said regarding this report: “Al-Zuhrī related to us, saying: Mālik informed me.”

Sufyān said regarding it: “Al-Zuhrī related to us.” He said: “Mālik informed me.”

Abū Bakr related to us: Sufyān related to us: al-Zuhrī related to us more than once—I attest to it for you—saying: “Sālim ibn ʿAbd Allāh informed me, from his father, who said: ‘I saw the Messenger of God ﷺ—Abū Bakr, and ʿUmar walking in front of the funeral procession.’” Sufyān was asked, “Is ʿUthmān included?” He said: “I do not retain that.” He was asked, “Some people relate it only from Sālim.” At that point he said: “Al-Zuhrī related it to us more than once; I attest to it for you.” He was asked:

“Ibn Jurayj relates it as you do, but adds ʿUthmān.” Sufyān said: “I did not hear him mention ʿUthmān.”

Sufyān said concerning the report about ill fortune: “I never heard al-Zuhrī mention Ḥamza in this report. He mentioned Ḥamza only in another report, the report about standing.”

Abū Bakr said, concerning the report, “God forbids you to swear by your fathers”:

He said: Sufyān said: “Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, the client of the family of Ṭalḥa, was well versed in Arabic, and there was no report—I have traced it from no one else—that he informed me he had sworn by them.”103

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us: Sufyān related to us, saying: “The first time I saw al-Zuhrī, I came upon him while he was relating traditions to people. I heard him say: ‘Sālim ibn ʿAbd Allāh informed me, from his father, who said: ʿUmar was asked about a snake that a pilgrim in the state of consecration kills. He said: “It is an enemy, so kill it wherever you find it.”’”

Abū Bakr said: This was in a tradition about which Sufyān was asked, “People relate it on the authority of ʿUrwa.”

He replied: “As for me, my recollection is that it is from Sālim. How likely it is, though, that it is from ʿUrwa, because the tradition says that it concerned a slave woman belonging to Banū ʿAdī ibn Kaʿb. If it had been from Sālim, he would have said, ‘a slave woman of ours,’ since he belonged to Banū ʿAdī.”

Abū Bakr related to us: Sufyān related to us, saying: “I heard al-Zuhrī say: ‘Kathīr ibn ʿAbbās informed me, from his father, who said: I was with the Prophet ﷺ on the day of Ḥunayn. The Messenger of God ﷺ was riding his mule, which had been given to him by Farwa al-Judhāmī. When the Muslims turned and fled, the Messenger of God ﷺ said to me:

“ʿAbbās, call out: ‘People of the Tree! People of Sūrat al-Baqara!’” I had a loud voice, so I called out: “People of the Tree! People of Sūrat al-Baqara!” They turned back, rushing like cows turning to their calves. The voices of the Anṣār rose as they called:

“Company of the Anṣār!”—twice. Then the call was narrowed to the Banū al-Ḥārith ibn al-Khazraj. He said: The Messenger of God ﷺ sat upright on his mule and said: ‘This is when the battle furnace is blazing!’ He was saying: ‘Forward, forward, O ʿAbs!’ while I held his bridle. Then the Messenger of God ﷺ took some pebbles and threw them at them, then said: ‘They have been routed, by the Lord of the Kaʿba!’ Sufyān sometimes said: ‘By the Lord of Muḥammad.’

Sufyān said: “Al-Zuhrī related this tradition to us in full. This is what I remember of it.”

Sufyān said: “I heard al-Zuhrī say: ‘ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh informed me, from his father; and Jaʿfar ibn ʿAmr ibn Umayya al-Ḍamirī informed me, from his father, that the Messenger of God, God bless him and grant him peace…’ One of them said: ‘The Messenger of God ﷺ ate bread and meat, then prayed without performing ablution.’ The other said: ‘The Messenger of God ﷺ cut meat from a sheep’s shoulder, ate some of it, then prayed without performing ablution.’ Sufyān said: ‘I have no doubt that al-Zuhrī related this to us from both of them with this chain of transmission. I only doubt which of them said this—that is, “he cut meat”—and which of them said this—that is, “he ate.”’”

Abū Bakr said, concerning the tradition of Qabīṣa ibn Dhuʾayb, “Whoever drinks wine…” He said:

Sufyān said: “When al-Zuhrī related this tradition to Manṣūr ibn al-Muʿtamir and Makhūl—a Kūfan—he said to them: ‘Do you two suppose that you are the delegates of the people of Iraq for this tradition?’”

“…and he struck their shoulders; they were beside him.” Sufyān said: “Al-Zuhrī did not say this to them while I was listening. I heard him say it to them at a gathering I did not attend.”

Abū Bakr related to us: Sufyān related to us, saying: “I heard al-Zuhrī relate, from Muḥammad ibn Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim, from his father—if God wills—that the Prophet ﷺ said: ‘If al-Muṭʿim ibn ʿAdī were alive, and then spoke to me about these captives—these prisoners—I would release them for him’”—meaning the prisoners of Badr. When Sufyān related this tradition and mentioned the report in it, he would say in it, “from his father, if God wills.” Sometimes he would not say “if God wills.” When he did not mention the report in it, sometimes he would not say “if God wills,” and sometimes he would say it.

Abū Bakr said: Sufyān was asked about the tradition of Abū Ayyūb, “Do not face the qibla when defecating.” They said that Nāfiʿ al-Jumaḥī did not transmit it with a chain of transmission. He replied: “But I do transmit it with a chain, and I remember it.”

Sufyān said: “The Meccans had found a book that had been with Ḥumayd al-Aʿraj in Syria, from al-Zuhrī. It came into the hands of Ibn Karīma, and they showed it to Ibn Shihāb. We used to hear it from his mouth.”

Sufyān said: “Al-Zuhrī related to us: ‘I heard ʿĪsā ibn Ṭalḥa ibn ʿUbayd Allāh…’”

“…relating from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ that a man asked the Prophet ﷺ: ‘Messenger of God, I slaughtered before I stoned [the pillar].’ He said: ‘Stone it; there is no blame on you.’ Another man said: ‘I shaved my head before I slaughtered.’ He said: ‘Slaughter; there is no blame on you.’”

Abū Bakr said: “I heard Sufyān being asked about this tradition. Budayl said to him:

‘This is what I remember from al-Zuhrī, Abū Muḥammad.’ He replied: ‘Yes, as though you had not heard it, except that he used to apply it. This is what I remember of it.’”104

I heard Budayl say to Sufyān: “ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī said that you had said, ‘I do not remember it.’” Sufyān replied: “Ibn Mahdī spoke truly: I do not remember it in full, but I have mastered this much of it.”

Sufyān said: “Al-Zuhrī related to us—or I was told it from him—from ʿĪsā ibn Ṭalḥa. Sometimes Sufyān said, ‘I think it is from ʿĪsā ibn Ṭalḥa,’ and sometimes Sufyān did not mention ʿĪsā ibn Ṭalḥa at all—from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: ‘The prayer of one sitting is half the prayer of one standing.’”

Abū Bakr said, concerning al-Zuhrī’s tradition: “He said: ‘Abū Bakr ibn ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar informed me, from his father.’”

He said: Sufyān said: “I heard Maʿmar relate it from al-Zuhrī, from Sālim, from his father. I said to him: ‘Abū ʿUrwa, it is only from Abū Bakr ibn ʿUbayd Allāh.’ Maʿmar said:

‘This is one of the traditions we read back.’ Later, Sufyān sometimes said, when relating this tradition:

‘Maʿmar said to me, “We read it back.”’”

Abū Bakr said, concerning the tradition, “The hand of a thief is cut off for a quarter-dīnār or more”:

Sufyān was asked: “Al-Zuhrī traced it back to the Prophet, but no one else did.” Sufyān said: “Yaḥyā and ʿAbd Rabbih, the two sons of Saʿīd, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Bakr, and Ruziq ibn Ḥakīm al-Aylī related it to us from ʿAmra, from ʿAmra, from ʿĀʾisha, who said: ‘The hand is cut off for a quarter-dīnār or more.’ Except that Yaḥyā used a word indicating the quarter—I have forgotten it, and it has been a long time—‘The hand is cut off for a quarter-dīnār or more.’ Al-Zuhrī was the most accurate of them all.”

“Sufyān said: ‘Al-Zuhrī related to us, from ʿAmra, from ʿĀʾisha, that Ḥabība bint Jaḥsh suffered prolonged bleeding.’ He then mentioned the tradition.

Sufyān said: ‘What I remember is that it was Ḥabība bint Jaḥsh, while people say Umm Ḥabība.’”

Sufyān said: “Al-Zuhrī related to us, from ʿAmra, from ʿĀʾisha, who said: ‘The aqrāʾ are the periods of purity.’”

Sufyān sometimes said of this: “I think it is from ʿAmra or ʿUrwa”; sometimes he said, “I think it is from ʿAmra,” without mentioning ʿUrwa. Then, more than once, he affirmed ʿAmra and left aside the doubt.

Al-Zuhrī said: “I think it is from ʿAmra, that ʿĀʾisha separated her sister in her waiting period.”

Al-Zuhrī related to us: “ʿĀʾisha separated her sister when she entered the bleeding of the third menstrual period.” Sufyān sometimes said of this, “I think it is from ʿAmra”; most often…

“…he does not mention ʿAmra in it.”

He said: “Al-Zuhrī related to us from four people: ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUtba; ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Thaʿlaba, in the tradition of the Dajjāl; ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar, in the tradition of Zayr al-Nisāʾ; and ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith, in the tradition ‘We entered this house.’” If Ibn Abī Dhiʾb said that the transmitter of the tradition of the Dajjāl was ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh, he was mistaken. Rather, it is ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Thaʿlaba. Al-Zuhrī related to us from no one named ʿUbayd Allāh except ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtba.

Sufyān said: “Al-Zuhrī related to us: ‘Ḥasan and ʿAbd Allāh, the sons of Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, related to us—and Ḥasan was more reliable than ʿAbd Allāh, while ʿAbd Allāh had collected the traditions of the Sabāʾiyya from their father—that ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib said to Ibn ʿAbbās: “You are a man who has lost his way. The Prophet ﷺ forbade temporary marriage and the meat of domesticated donkeys.”’”—Ḥasan’s wording.

Sufyān said: “I said to al-Zuhrī: ‘Abū Bakr, what is the wording of your tradition, “The worst food is the food of the rich”?’ He laughed and said: ‘It is only, “The worst food is the food of a wedding feast.”’”

Sufyān said: “My father was wealthy, and this tradition alarmed me when I heard it. I asked al-Zuhrī, and he said: ‘Al-Aʿraj related to me: I heard Abū Hurayra say: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “The worst food is the food…”

“…of a wedding feast, to which the rich are invited while the poor are excluded. Whoever does not accept the invitation has disobeyed God and His Messenger.”’ Sufyān sometimes traced this tradition back to the Prophet, and sometimes did not trace it back except in its final part.

Sufyān said: “Al-Zuhrī related to us: ‘ʿAnbasa ibn Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ informed me, from Abū Hurayra, who said: I came to the Messenger of God ﷺ and his Companions at Khaybar after they had conquered it. I asked the Messenger of God ﷺ to allot me a share of the spoils. Some of the Banū Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ said: “Do not allot him a share, Messenger of God. This is the man who killed Ibn Qawqal.” Ibn Saʿd said: “How astonishing! A wabar has descended upon us from the tip of a ḍāl tree, reproaching me for killing a Muslim man whom God honored through my hand, while He did not humiliate me through his.”’

Sufyān said: “I do not remember whether he said that a share was allotted to him or that one was not allotted to him.”

Sufyān said: “I heard Ismāʿīl ibn Umayya ask al-Zuhrī about it; I was there.”

Al-Ḥajjāj ibn Minhāl related to us: Ḥammād related to us, from ʿAlī ibn Zayd, from ʿAmmār ibn Abī ʿAmmār, from Abū Hurayra, who said: “Whenever I attended a campaign with the Messenger of God ﷺ he allotted me a share, except at Khaybar, for it belonged to the people of al-Ḥudaybiya. So I came to him”—Abū Mūsā and Abū Hurayra had arrived between al-Ḥudaybiya and Khaybar.

Saʿīd ibn Abī Maryam related to us: al-Darāwardī related to us, saying: Khaytham ibn ʿIrāk ibn Mālik related to me, from his father, from Abū Hurayra, who said: “The Messenger of God ﷺ went out and left Sibāʿ ibn ʿUrfuṭa in charge of Medina.” Abū Hurayra said:

“I came to Medina as an emigrant and prayed the dawn prayer behind Sibāʿ. In the first unit he recited Sūrat Maryam, and in the last, ‘Woe to the defrauders’ (83:1).” Abū Hurayra said:

“I said: ‘Woe to Abū Fīl!’ He was a man of the Azd who had died. He had two measures: one by which he measured for himself, and another by which he short-measured for people.”

Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yūnus related to us: Zuhayr related to us; Dāwūd ibn ʿAbd Allāh related to us that Ḥumayd al-Ḥimyarī told him: “I met a man among the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ. He had accompanied him for four years, just as Abū Hurayra had accompanied him for four years.”

Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr related to us: Abū ʿAwāna related to us, from Dāwūd al-Awdī, from Ḥumayd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Ḥimyarī, who said: “I met a man who had accompanied the Messenger of God ﷺ just as Abū Hurayra had accompanied him for four years.”

Al-Ḥumaydī related to us: Sufyān related to us: Ismāʿīl related to us, saying: “I heard Qays say: ‘I heard Abū Hurayra say: I accompanied the Messenger of God ﷺ for three years. I was more eager than anyone to remember anything I heard from him during those years.’”

“Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us: al-Fazārī related to us: Ismāʿīl related to us, from Qays, from Abū Hurayra, who said: ‘We came to him when he arrived in Kūfa, and he said to us: “Welcome; you are among your own people.”’”

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us: Sufyān related to us: ʿUthmān ibn Abī Sulaymān related to us, saying: “I heard Abū Hurayra say: ‘I arrived in Medina while the Prophet ﷺ was at Khaybar, and a man from Banū Ghifār was leading the people in prayer.’”

He said: “I heard Sufyān say: I heard al-Zuhrī say: ‘I heard Hudhayl al-Aʿmā, a companion of Ibn Masʿūd, say: Ibn Masʿūd was asked about such-and-such’”—Sufyān said: “I have forgotten it.” It was said: “They say that a man asked Ibn Masʿūd, ‘Should I ask permission before entering upon my mother?’ He said, ‘Yes.’” Sufyān said: “Perhaps we did not master it, because we heard this from Mukhāriq relating it from Ṭāriq from ʿAbd Allāh.”

Abū Bakr related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, saying: “I heard al-Zuhrī relate from ʿĀʾisha, who said: ‘Ḥafṣa and I began the day fasting, then food was sent to us, and we ate some of it.’

“ʿĀʾisha said: ‘The Messenger of God ﷺ came in to us, and Ḥafṣa—who was her father’s daughter—quickly spoke before me and said: “Messenger of God, ʿĀʾisha and I began the day fasting…”

“…then food was sent to us, and we ate some of it.’” She said: “The Messenger of God ﷺ smiled and said: ‘Fast a day in its place.’” Sufyān said: “Al-Zuhrī was asked, ‘Is it from ʿUrwa?’ He said: ‘No.’”

That was when he was rising from the gathering, and the prayer was being established.

Sufyān said: “I had heard Ṣāliḥ ibn Abī al-Akhḍar relate to us from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUrwa. [When] al-Zuhrī said, ‘It is not from ʿUrwa,’ I thought Ṣāliḥ had been misled in the course of reading the report back to his teacher.”

Abū Bakr related to us, saying: “More than one person informed me from Maʿmar that he said concerning this tradition: ‘It was from the traditions of ʿUrwa; I have forgotten it.’”

He said: “More than one person informed me from Ibn Jurayj that he said: ‘I asked al-Zuhrī about this tradition—whose tradition it was—and he said: “It is from a man of Syria, who related it to me at the gate of ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Marwān.”’”

He said: Sufyān related to us, saying: “I saw Ibn Judʿān sitting with al-Zuhrī. Ibn Judʿān admired perfume, so he said to him: ‘Abū Bakr, why did you not have these two garments of yours fumigated with incense?’ Ibn Shihāb had washed them, and Ibn Judʿān detected the smell of the wash water.”

ʿAlī ibn al-Madīnī said: Sufyān said: “I saw Saʿd ibn Ibrāhīm with al-Zuhrī on the bedding, and I saw ʿAlī ibn Zayd on the bedding. ʿAlī ibn Zayd said to him: ‘Abū Bakr, I went to Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib and he honored me; I went to ʿAlī ibn Ḥusayn and he honored me.’

“ʿAlī ibn Zayd ibn Judʿān suffered confusion in his old age.”

Abū Bakr related to us: Sufyān related to us, saying: “I saw al-Zuhrī visit ʿAmr ibn Dīnār and greet him. ʿAmr apologized to him on account of the illness he had, and said: ‘If I were able, I would come to you.’”

Abū Yūsuf said: “I can only suppose that I heard Abū Bakr relate from Sufyān, who said: ‘I heard al-Zuhrī. Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq came to him, and al-Zuhrī said: “Muḥammad, where have you been? I have not seen you.” He replied: “I cannot get to you with this doorkeeper of yours.” Al-Zuhrī called his doorkeeper and said: “When he comes, do not keep him out.”’”

Sufyān said: “I was told that Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq came to al-Zuhrī, though I was not present. When he had left, al-Zuhrī said: ‘Knowledge will continue to exist in Medina as long as this man remains.’”

“He said: Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq ibn Yasār was a Persian client and the author of the Sīra.”

Abū Bakr related to us: Sufyān related to us; Abū al-Zaʿrāʾ ʿAmr ibn ʿAmr related to us, from his uncle, Abū al-Aḥwaṣ ʿAwf ibn Mālik al-Jushamī, from his father: “I came to the Messenger of God”—(232b).

He also said: Sufyān related to us; al-Zuhrī related to us, saying: “Ḥasan and ʿAbd Allāh, the two sons of Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, related to us. Ḥasan was more reliable than ʿAbd Allāh, and ʿAbd Allāh used to collect the reports about the sabīʾa—from their father, that ʿAlī said to Ibn ʿAbbās: ‘You are a confused man. The Messenger of God ﷺ forbade temporary marriage and the meat of domestic donkeys at the time of Khaybar. Do not give legal opinions permitting temporary marriage.’”

Abū Mūsā related to us, from ʿAbd al-Wahhāb, from Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd, from Mālik, from al-Zuhrī, who said, “on the day of Ḥunayn.” All of al-Zuhrī’s companions say “Khaybar”; Mālik likewise says this in the Muwaṭṭaʾ, and “the day of Khaybar” is correct.

I heard ʿAlī ibn al-Madīnī mention the report, “Their incense burners were al-uluwwa”. He said:
