“I said to Sufyān: ‘So-and-so said, “Their incense burners were al-uluwwa.”’ He replied: ‘This is just a man who read it in a book. It is as though he is saying that he did not hear it from my brother, but only read it and did not know what it was.’”

He said: “I said: ‘Abū Muḥammad, he does lead the prayer, and he …’”105

I heard someone other than ʿAlī say: “It was Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Qaṭṭān.”

ʿAlī said: “Ibn ʿUyayna said: ‘Woe to you! Ask the perfumers; they will tell you.’”

Abū Bakr said: “Sufyān said: ‘When al-Zuhrī related to us from Anas and Sahl ibn Saʿd, he would say, “I heard, I heard.”’”

Abū Bakr said: “Sufyān transmitted seven or eight reports from Mālik.”

Abū Bakr said: “Sufyān said: ‘Everything I heard from ʿAmr, he said to us concerning it, “I heard Jābir”, except for these two reports—the meat of horses and mukhābara. I do not know whether there was anyone between him and Jābir in these two reports or not. As for the report about shares, I was the one who said, “If I had heard Jābir,” according to what you related to us.’”

Abū Bakr related to us: Sufyān related to us, saying: “They related to me, from Warqāʾ, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, that Ibn al-Zubayr would give one salutation.”

He also said: Sufyān related to us, saying: “My nephew related to me, from ʿAmr, that Ibn al-Zubayr exacted retaliation from the Muslim.”

He also said: Sufyān related to us, saying: “They informed me, from Ibn Jurayj, from ʿAmr, that the Prophet ﷺ prayed the noon prayer in Mecca on the Day of Tarwiya (233a), then departed.”

Sufyān said: “Perhaps this was due to an illness.”

He also said: Sufyān related to us, saying: “My nephew related to me, from ʿAmr, who said:

‘I saw Ibn al-Zubayr slaughter a sacrificial camel while it was standing, suspended, as he rode a piebald birḏawn.’”

Sufyān would relate this report. When he mentioned in it “a piebald birḏawn,” he attributed it to ʿAmr’s nephew; when he did not mention “riding a birḏawn,” he attributed it to ʿAmr. Perhaps he heard it from ʿAmr but did not hear “a piebald birḏawn.”

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us: Sufyān related to us; ʿAmr related to us, repeatedly and from the beginning, saying:

“ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī informed me that ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib said: ‘He has done wrong who deprives the sons of the same mother of their share of the blood-money.’”

Sufyān was asked: “But Muḥammad ibn Muslim says it on the authority of al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad.”

He said: “He did not retain it. ʿAmr related to us, repeatedly and from the beginning, saying: ‘ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad informed me.’”

Abū Bakr related to us: Sufyān related to us; ʿAmr related to us, from Yaḥyā ibn Jaʿda, who said:

“I heard Zādhān Farūkh say: ‘The Sacred Mosque measures seven and a half ajriba, and the Mosque of Kūfa measures nine and a half ajriba.’” Sufyān said: “I think he meant the foundations laid by Ibn al-Zubayr.”

He also said: Sufyān related to us; Jaʿfar related to us, from his father, from Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh, who said: “ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib entered upon ʿUmar while he was shrouded, and said: ‘May God bless you! Among all people, there is no one I would rather meet God with what is in his record than this man who is shrouded.’”

Sufyān said: “Bishr the money-changer, who was with us, said: ‘By God, what is in his record’—meaning Jaʿfar’s—‘is greater than what is in his record’—meaning ʿUmar’s.”

Sufyān said: “I wanted to raise my hand and strike his nose, but al-Ḥasan ibn ʿUmāra said to me:

‘I know that this man is misguided.’”106

He said: “Sufyān related to us; ʿAmr related to us, saying: ‘On one occasion I heard ʿAṭāʾ, and on another I heard Ṭāwūs say: “I heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: ‘The Messenger of God ﷺ was cupped while in consecration.’”’”

Sufyān said: “I do not know whether ʿAmr transmitted it from both of them, or whether it was one of the two occasions”—[the phrase here is unclear].107

Sufyān said: “It was mentioned to me that he heard it from both of them.”

Abū Bakr said: “I saw this report from both of them in the book of ʿAmr ibn Dīnār’s nephew (233b).”

Volume Two

Reports concerning Kūfa

Volume Two

Abū Ḥanīfa al-Nuʿmān ibn Thābit, his companions, al-Aʿmash, and others

“Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz al-Ramlī related to us: Ḍamra ibn Rabīʿa related to us, from Ibn Shawdhab, from Tawba al-ʿAnbarī, from Sālim, from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: The Messenger of God said—”

God bless him and grant him peace: “O God, bless our city, our ṣāʿ, our mudd, our Yemen, and our Syria.” A man said: “Messenger of God, and our Iraq?” The Messenger of God ﷺ replied: “There will be earthquakes and tribulations there, and from it the horn of Satan will emerge.”

Saʿīd ibn Asad related to me, saying: Ḍamra related to us; Ibn Shawdhab related to us, from Tawba al-ʿAnbarī, from Sālim, from his father, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “O God, bless our city, our mudd, our ṣāʿ, our Yemen, and our Syria.” A man said: “Messenger of God, and our Iraq?” The Prophet ﷺ said: “O God, bless our city, our mudd, our ṣāʿ, our Yemen, and our Syria.” A man said: “Messenger of God, and our Iraq?” The Prophet ﷺ said: “O God, bless our city, our mudd, our ṣāʿ, our Yemen, and our Syria.” A man said: “Messenger of God, and our Iraq?” The Prophet ﷺ said: “There will be earthquakes and tribulations there, and from it the horn of Satan will emerge.”

Ibn Shawdhab said: “Do you think Mecca is counted as part of Yemen in this report?”

Al-ʿAbbās ibn al-Walīd ibn Mazīd related to us; my father informed me, saying:

ʿĪsā ibn Muḥammad related to us; al-Walīd ibn Mazīd informed me, saying: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shawdhab related to us (234a); ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Qāsim, Maṭar, and Kathīr related to me— Abū Sahl, from Tawba al-ʿAnbarī, from Sālim ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from his father, that the Prophet of God ﷺ supplicated, saying: “O God, bless our Mecca; bless our Medina; bless our Syria; bless our Yemen. O God, bless our ṣāʿ and bless our mudd.”

The man said: “And our Iraq?” He turned away from him. The man repeated this three times, each time saying, “And our Iraq?” while the Prophet turned away from him. Then he said: “There will be earthquakes and tribulations there, and from it the horn of Satan will emerge.”

Abū al-Yamān al-Ḥakam ibn Nāfiʿ related to us, saying: Shuʿayb informed me. [The transmission continues with ḥāʾ of transition.]

Ḥajjāj ibn Abī Manīʿ reported: My grandfather and I were both informed by al-Zuhrī, who said:

“Sālim ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar informed me that ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar said: ‘I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say—while he was on the pulpit: “Take heed: the tribulation is here”—pointing toward the east—“where the horn of Satan rises.”’”

Abū Bishr related to us; Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd related to us, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUmar, who said:

“Nāfiʿ informed me, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar, that the Prophet ﷺ stood beside the door of Ḥafṣa and said: ‘The tribulation is here—or from here—where the horn of Satan rises,’” twice or three times.

“Abū Ḥafṣ Ḥarmala ibn ʿImrān related to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed me—”

He said: Yaḥyā ibn Ayyūb and Ibn Lahīʿa informed me, from ʿUqayl, from Ibn Shihāb, from Yaʿqūb ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīra ibn al-Akhnas, from Ibn ʿUmar, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Iblīs entered Iraq and relieved himself there. Then he entered Syria, and they drove him away until he reached Bīsiq. Then he entered Egypt, where he laid eggs, hatched them, and spread out a ʿabqariyya.”

Qabīṣa ibn ʿUqba related to us: Sufyān ibn Saʿīd al-Thawrī related to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Dīnār, from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ (234b)—and he pointed toward the east—said: “The tribulation is from here; the tribulation is from here, where the horn of Satan rises.”

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Maslama ibn Qaʿnab related to us, from Mālik, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Dīnār, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar, who said: “I saw the Messenger of God ﷺ pointing toward the east and saying: ‘Take heed: the tribulation is here; the tribulation is here, from where the horn of Satan rises.’”

Through the same chain, from Mālik, from Abū al-Zinād, from al-Aʿraj, from Abū Hurayra, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “The head of unbelief lies toward the east.”

“Qabīṣa related to us: Sufyān related to us, from Muḥammad ibn Juḥāda, who said: ‘I heard al-Ḥasan say: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “O God, bless our city. O God, bless our Syria.” A man said to the Messenger of God: “And Iraq? For our provisions come from there, and our needs are there.” He fell silent, then repeated it and said: “Here the horn of Satan rises, and there you will have earthquakes and tribulations.”’”

“Qabīṣa ibn ʿUqba related to us: Sufyān related to us, from Ziyād ibn ʿIlāqa, from Thābit ibn Quṭba, who said: ‘I heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd say: “You are in the place where tongues were confused, between Babylon and al-Ḥīra. Nine-tenths of good are in Syria, and one-tenth elsewhere; nine-tenths of evil are elsewhere, and one-tenth of evil is there. A time will come upon you when a man’s most cherished possession will be donkeys on which he can travel to Syria.”’”

Qabīṣa related to us: Sufyān related to us, from Sālim ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Nakhaʿī. I heard Ibn— Mīnāʾ al-Yamāmī said: “I heard ʿAlī, who was displeased with them for something, say: ‘I had indeed warned you and made you afraid. I was told: “You are going to a place of nine-tenths of evil, inhabited by human devils and rebellious jinn.”’”

He also said: Sufyān related to us, from Furāt al-Qazzāz, from Kaʿb, who said: “ʿUmar intended to go to Iraq, and Kaʿb said to him: ‘There are rebels against the truth there, and every grievous malady.’”

(235a) He was asked: “What is the grievous malady?” He replied: “Conflicting desires for which there is no cure.”

“ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Uwaysī related to us: Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd related to us, from Shuʿba, from Abū ʿAwn Muḥammad ibn ʿUbayd Allāh al-Thaqafī, from Abū Ṣāliḥ al-Ḥanafī, who said: ‘I saw ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib take the codex and [place it] on his head, until I could see its pages rustling. Then he said: “O God, they prevented me [from upholding what is in it among the community], so grant me [the reward] for what is in it.” Then he said: “O God, I have grown weary of them, and they have grown weary of me; I hate them, and they hate me. They have driven me to act contrary to my nature and character, and to ways not known of me. Replace them for me with better people, and replace me for them with someone worse than me. O God, make their hearts die the death of salt in water.”’ Ibrāhīm said: “He meant the people of Kūfa.”’”

(Folio 239a) “Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yūnus related to us; Zāʾida related to us, from al-Aʿmash, that [Abū] Saʿīd al-Taymī said: ‘I heard ʿAlī addressing the people while he was at Maskin. He said, “March out against a great enemy.” They began to hang back, saying, “It is winter.” He called down a prayer against them, saying, “O God, bring humiliation into their homes, fill their breasts with terror, and cause their hearts to die as You cause salt to dissolve in water.”’”

Shihāb ibn ʿAbbād al-Qaysī related to us; Sufyān related to us, from Mujālid, from al-Shaʿbī, who said:

ʿAlī said: “Whoever makes a charge with these people”—meaning the people of Kūfa—“has charged with the most ill-fated arrow.” Shihāb said: “He related this to us in the year al-Ḥusayn was killed at Fakhkh”—and that was the year fifty-one.

He said: “Shihāb related this to us in the year two hundred and twenty-one.”

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā related to us; Talīd ibn al-Khashshāb informed us; Sharīk, the client of ʿAmr ibn Ḥurayth, related to me— ʿAmr ibn Ḥurayth said: “I went out with ʿAmr ibn Ḥurayth from his house. He saw ʿAlī coming out of the palace, holding a whip. ʿAmr greeted him, and he said: ‘O ʿAmr, I used to think that the governor wronged the people, but it turns out that the people wrong the governor. O God, separate me from them and set over them someone worse than me.’

“Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr related to us; ʿAwn ibn Mūsā related to us, saying: I heard Hilāl ibn Khabbāb say: So-and-so said: ‘Al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī gathered the leaders of the people of Iraq in this palace’—and he gestured with his hand toward the palace of al-Madāʾin—‘and said: “People of Iraq, were it not for only three things that make my soul turn away from you, I would turn away: your killing my father, your stabbing my belly, and your stripping the sandals from my feet and the cloak from my shoulder”’—ʿAwn was uncertain.”

“Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us; Sufyān related to us; ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shurayk related to us, from Bishr ibn Ghālib, who said that he heard him say: ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr said to Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī: ‘Where are you going—to a people who killed your father and stabbed your brother?’ Ḥusayn said to him: ‘It is dearer to me to be killed in such-and-such a place than for you to violate me’—meaning Mecca.”

He also said: “Sufyān related to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shurayk, who said: Bishr ibn Ghālib had been with Ḥusayn and was among those who abandoned him. He would go to his grave, roll on it, and weep.”

Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us; Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd related to me, from his father, from Ibrāhīm ibn Qāriẓ, who said: “I heard ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb say: ‘The people of Kūfa have wearied and confounded me. They satisfy no one, nor is anyone satisfied with them; they set nothing right, nor can anything be set right among them.’”

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā related to me, from Sufyān, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr, from Jābir ibn Samura, who said: “I was sitting with ʿUmar when some people from Kūfa came to him and spoke ill of Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ. They persisted in their accusations until they said, ‘He does not know how to lead us in prayer.’ ʿUmar said: ‘My last knowledge of him is that he prayed well.’ He sent for him, and he came. ʿUmar said: ‘Abū Isḥāq, what are these people saying?’ He said: ‘What are they saying?’ ʿUmar said: ‘They say you do not know how to pray.’ He said: ‘As for me, by God, I lead them in prayer as the Messenger of God ﷺ—prayed, leaving nothing out. I lead them in the evening prayer: I make the first two rakʿahs long and shorten the last two.’ ʿUmar said: ‘That is what I think of you, Abū Isḥāq.’”

“Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us; Muʿāwiya ibn Ṣāliḥ informed me, from Shurayḥ ibn ʿUbayd, from Abū ʿAdhaba, who said: A man came to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb ﵁—and told him— “—that the people of Iraq had pelted [their governor] with stones——so he went out in anger and led them in prayer, making mistakes in it until the people began to say, ‘Glory be to God!’ When he had finished the prayer, he turned to the people and said: ‘Who here is from Syria?’ A man stood up, then another, and I stood up as the third or fourth. He said: ‘People of Syria, prepare yourselves for the people of Iraq, for Satan has laid eggs and hatched them among them. O God, they have confused matters for me, so confuse matters for them, and hasten against them the Thaqafī youth, who will judge them by the judgment of the Age of Ignorance, accepting nothing from their virtuous and overlooking nothing from their wrongdoers.’”

“Abū al-Yamān related to us; Ḥurayz ibn ʿUthmān related to us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Maysara, from Abū ʿAdhaba al-Ḥimṣī, who said: I arrived to visit ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb as the fourth of four men from Syria, and we were pilgrims. While we were with him, someone came from Iraq and reported that they had pelted their prayer leader with stones. ʿUmar had appointed this man to replace a prayer leader who had been there before him, and they had pelted him with stones. ʿUmar went out to prayer in anger and made a mistake in his prayer. Then he turned to the people and said: ‘Who here is from Syria?’ I and my companions stood up. He said: ‘People of Syria, equip yourselves to face the people of Iraq, for Satan has laid eggs and hatched them among them.’ Then he said: ‘O God, they have confused matters for me, so confuse matters for them, and hasten against them the Thaqafī youth, who will judge them by the judgment of the Age of Ignorance, accepting nothing from their virtuous and overlooking nothing from their wrongdoers.’”

“Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us; Sufyān related to us, from ʿAmmār al-Duhnī, who said: Al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī dismounted at al-Madāʾin, and Qays ibn Saʿd was at the head of his vanguard. He dismounted at al-Anbār, where they stabbed Ḥasan and plundered his tent.”

“Abū Bakr related to us; Sufyān related to us; ʿAbd Allāh, the son of Yazīd’s brother, related to me, from Yazīd al-Aṣamm, who said: I came to al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī while he was being brought a bundle of books. I was with him. He did not break a single seal or look at a single address before saying, ‘Girl, bring the basin.’ The basin was brought, with water in it, and he took those books and washed them in the water. I said, ‘Abū Muḥammad, whose books are these?’ He said, ‘These are the books of people who do not return to what is right and do not desist from what is wrong—the books of the people of Iraq.’ He sometimes said, ‘who do not withdraw from what is wrong.’”

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us; Ḥammād related to us, from Ayyūb, from Nāfiʿ, from Nubayh ibn Wahb, who said: “A Qurashī man proposed marriage to a woman while Abān ibn ʿUthmān was the commander of the pilgrimage season. He said, ‘I see he is a crude Iraqi. A person in a state of consecration may neither marry nor be given in marriage. ʿUthmān informed us of this from the Messenger of God ﷺ.’”

“Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us; Yaḥyā ibn Sulaym related to us (folio 240b), saying: I heard Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿUthmān relate, from al-Zuhrī, who said:

“ʿĀʾisha said: ‘People of Iraq, the people of Syria are better than you. Many men from among the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ—went out to them and related to us things we know. Few men from among the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ—went out to you, yet you related to us things we know and things we do not know.’”

He said: “Al-Zuhrī also said: ‘When you hear an Iraqi report, reject it, then reject it again.’”

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us; Yaḥyā ibn Sulaymān related to us; Ibrāhīm ibn Nāfiʿ related to me, saying: I heard Ṭāwūs say: “If an Iraqi relates a hundred reports to you, discard ninety-nine of them.” He said: “I saw Ṭāwūs count them off on his fingers.”

Hishām ibn ʿAmmār related to us; ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Muḥammad related to us; Zuhayr related to us, saying:

He said: “Hishām ibn ʿUrwa said to me: ‘Zuhayr, if an Iraqi relates a thousand reports to you, discard nine hundred and ninety-nine of them, and remain doubtful about what is left.’”

“He also said: ʿAbd al-Malik related to us, saying: I heard al-Awzāʿī say: ‘The caliphs were in Syria. Whenever a calamity arose, they asked the scholars of Syria and the people of Medina about it. The reports of the people of Iraq did not get beyond the walls of their houses. When, then, did the scholars of Syria transmit from the Khārijites among the people of Iraq?’”

“I heard al-Ḥasan ibn al-Rabīʿ say: I heard Ibn al-Mubārak say: ‘I travelled to Syria only to free myself of the reports of the people of Kūfa.’”

Makkī ibn Ibrāhīm related to us, from ʿAbd Rabbihi ibn Abī Rāshid, who said: “I was in Mecca, in the Sacred Mosque, when I saw a circle of people. I approached them and found Ibn ʿUmar among them. He said to me:

“‘Where are you from?’ I said, ‘From the people of Baṣra.’ He said, ‘The people of Baṣra are better than the people of Kūfa.’”

Al-Faḍl ibn Sahl related to me; Muḥammad ibn Sābiq, Abū Jaʿfar, related to us; Mālik ibn Mighwal related to us, from Abū al-Walīd, from Sālim ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar (folio 241a), who said: “He asked me:

“‘Where are you from?’ I said, ‘From the people of Kūfa.’ He said, ‘Wretched people, between a Sabaʾī and a Ḥarūrī.’”

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us; Yaḥyā ibn Sulaymān related to us, saying: I heard ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAlī ibn Nāfiʿ ibn Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim say: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar said:

“ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Marwān wrote to me, and he wrote to ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr. The only thing that prevented me from writing to Muṣʿab ibn al-Zubayr was my fear of the people of Iraq adding to the report.”

Abū Bakr related to us; Sufyān related to us, saying: I heard ʿAmmār ibn Ruzayq say: “We were told that there was a man in Kūfa who claimed to be a prophet. We went to him and found a weaver at his loom. We spoke to him, and he said, ‘I am a prophet.’ We said, ‘A prophet who is a weaver?’ He said, ‘What do you want—a money changer?’”

ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn ʿImrān related to me; Muḥammad ibn Yūsuf al-Firyābī related to us— Fuḍayl ibn Marzūq related to us; Jabalat ibn al-Muṣaffiḥ related to me, from his father, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, who said: “People of Kūfa, ask us about what God and His Messenger said, for we, the People of the House, know best what God and His Messenger said. As for you, people of Kūfa, you know best how to lie about them.”

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā related to us, from Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid, from Qurra al-ʿIjlī, from ʿAbd al-Malik, the nephew of al-Qaʿqāʿ, Abū Thawr, who said: “I performed the pilgrimage and met ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar. I asked him about some matters, and he rebuked and scolded me. When I had completed the rites of my pilgrimage, I said, ‘I shall go to him and greet him.’ I went to him and said, ‘Peace be upon you, Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān. I have come from a distant place and want to ask you about some matters, but you rebuked and scolded me. It seems to me you have been spreading reports about me.’ He said, ‘You people of Iraq relate things about us that we never say.’”

ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Uwaysī related to us; Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd related to us, from his maternal aunt, the daughter of Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, who said: “I asked Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ about something, and he was surprised. He was asked about this, and he said, ‘I dislike relating a single report to you, only for you to turn it into a hundred reports.’”

Qabīṣa related to us (folio 241b), from Sufyān; Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit related to us, saying: “I heard Ibn ʿUmar say, ‘People of Iraq, you bring us difficult questions.’”

Aḥmad ibn Abī al-ʿAbbās related to me; Muḥammad ibn Yūsuf related to us, from Sufyān, from Rabīʿa ibn Abī ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, who said: “I asked Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib about a difficult question, and he said, ‘Are you an Iraqi?’”

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā related to me; Sufyān related to us, from al-Zuhrī, who said: “When a report goes deep in that direction”—meaning Iraq—“reject it.”

Saʿīd ibn Asad related to me; Ḍamra related to us, from Rajāʾ ibn Abī Salama, from al-Zuhrī, who said: “A report continues to be recognized as such so long as it has not been said ‘here’”—and he gestured with his hand toward Iraq.

Abū al-Nuʿmān Muḥammad ibn al-Faḍl related to us; Ḥammād ibn Zayd and al-Nuʿmān ibn Rāshid related to us, who said: I heard al-Zuhrī relate the report about the leper. I said, “Abū Bakr, who told you?” He said, “Did you not tell it to me, from the person you heard it from?” I said, “From a man of Kūfa.” He said, “You have corrupted it. There is much interpolation in the reports of the people of Kūfa.”

Abū Nuʿaym al-Faḍl ibn Dukayn related to us; al-Aʿmash related to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān al-Asadī, who said: “When the pledge of allegiance to ʿUthmān came, ʿAbd Allāh said: ‘We did not fail to choose the best among those who remained.’”

Abū Nuʿaym and ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā related to us, saying: Misʿar related to us, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Maysara, from al-Nazzāl ibn Sabra, who said: “I heard Ibn Masʿūd say, at the time of the pledge of allegiance to ʿUthmān: ‘Our choice is the best of those who remain, and we did not fail in our duty.’”

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā related to us, from Isrāʾīl, from Abū Isḥāq, from Jāriya, who said: “I heard Ibn Masʿūd say, when the pledge of allegiance to ʿUthmān reached us: He praised God and extolled Him, then said, ‘We did not fail to choose the best among those who remained, when we pledged allegiance to him.’”

Al-Ḥajjāj related to us; Ḥammād ibn Salama related to us, from ʿĀṣim ibn Bahdala, from Abū Wāʾil, that Ibn Masʿūd travelled from Medina to Kūfa in eight nights when ʿUmar was killed. He praised God and extolled Him, then said: “To proceed: The Commander of the Faithful, ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, has died.” No day was seen on which there was more sobbing than that day. “We, the Companions of Muḥammad, assembled, and we did not fail to choose the best among us, Dhū Fawq—ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān—and they pledged allegiance to him.”

Volume Two

Chapter

Abū Saʿīd Yaḥyā ibn Sulaymān related to me; Aḥmad ibn Ashkīb related to me; Abū Yaḥyā al-Taymī related to me; al-Aʿmash related to us, from ʿAmr ibn Murra, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salama al-Murādī, from ʿUbayda al-Salmānī, who said: “One day I came upon ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd while he was in the passageway of his house. He said: ‘I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ—say: “The one who succeeds me will be in Paradise; the one who succeeds him will be in Paradise; and the third and the fourth will be in Paradise.”’”

Ibn Abī ʿUbayda also related it from al-Aʿmash. ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAẓīm related to us; ʿAbd al-Razzāq related to us, from Maʿmar, who said: “I heard al-Zuhrī say: ‘A report leaves us a span’s length, then returns an arm’s length’”—meaning from Iraq.

He said—and gestured with his hand—“When a report goes deep there, it begins and begins with it.”108

Al-ʿAbbās related to us: Sulaymān ibn Ayyūb al-Hāshimī related to us, from Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd, who said: “Were it not for reports reaching us from the direction of the East that we disapprove of, I would neither have written a hadith nor permitted it to be written.”

Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yūnus related to us: Abū Muʿāwiyah related to us, from Ḥajjāj al-Ṣawwāf, from Ḥumayd ibn Hilāl, from Yaʿlā ibn al-Walīd, from Jundab, that he entered upon Ḥudhayfah and said: “They have set out against this man”—meaning ʿUthmān. He said: “By God, they will kill him.” I asked: “And where will he be?” He said: “In Paradise.” I asked: “And where will they be?”

He said: “In the Fire.”

Al-Ḥajjāj related to us: Mahdī ibn Maymūn related to me: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Yaʿqūb109 related to us, from al-Walīd ibn Muslim, Abū Bishr, from Jundab ibn ʿAbd Allāh, who said:

“I heard that Ḥudhayfah had spoken ill of the Commander of the Faithful, so I met him and asked him about it. He said: ‘Indeed, they will kill him.’ I asked: ‘And where will he be?’ He said: ‘In Paradise.’ I asked: ‘And where will his killer be?’”

He said: “In the Fire.”

Abū Nuʿaym related to us: al-Aʿmash related to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Yazīd ibn Yathīʿ, who said: “Some people of Banū ʿAbs prepared to go against ʿUthmān to fight him. Ḥudhayfah said: ‘No people have striven to abase God’s authority on earth without God abasing them in this world before they die.’”

Ibn Numayr related to me: my father related to us: al-Aʿmash related to us, from Ismāʿīl ibn Rajāʾ al-Zubaydī, from al-Walīd ibn Ṣakhr al-Fazārī, from Jazīʾ ibn Bukayr al-ʿAbsī, who said:

“When ʿUthmān was killed, we went to Ḥudhayfah and entered a shaded portico of his. He said: ‘By God, I do not know what became of ʿUthmān. By God, I do not know the state of the one who killed ʿUthmān. He was either an unbeliever who killed the other, or a believer who plunged into the turmoil until he killed him—and he would then be the most complete in faith of all people.’”

Maḥfūẓ ibn Abī Tawbah related to me: Abū Nuʿaym related to me: al-Aʿmash related to us, from Ismāʿīl ibn Rajāʾ, from Ṣakhr ibn al-Walīd, from Jazīʾ ibn Bukayr, who said: “When ʿUthmān was killed, we fled in alarm to Ḥudhayfah, in a shaded portico of his. He said: ‘By God, I do not know whether it was an unbeliever or a believer who plunged into the turmoil to kill an unbeliever.’”

Abū Saʿīd ʿAbd Allāh ibn Saʿīd al-Ashajj related to me, saying: I heard Ibn Idrīs say: “Al-Aʿmash had a tremor from fear.”110

Abū Saʿīd related to me: Mūsā ibn Maʿmar Abū Ṣāliḥ al-ʿAnzī related to me, saying:

“I prayed the dawn prayer, then slept on the bank of the Euphrates. In a dream, I saw a small boat going up the Euphrates. People were saying, ‘This is Jesus son of Mary, passing by, arriving to visit me.’ I took a woolen robe and threw it over myself, then said: ‘Now asceticism has become pleasant. Are you al-Yasaʿ ibn Nūn, Moses’ successor over his people?’ He said: ‘No, I am Jonah son of Mattā.’

“I said: ‘Tell me: Are the things related about the Children of Israel true?’ He said: ‘He lies about them just as al-Aʿmash lied about ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān.’”

“Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd related to us: ʿAlī ibn Mushir related to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Mūsā ibn Ṭarīf, from ʿAbāyah, from ʿAlī, who said: ‘I am the divider of the Fire. On the Day of Resurrection, I will say: “This is yours, and this is mine.”’” I also saw in the book of ʿUmar ibn Ḥafṣ ibn Ghiyāth: “My father related to me, from al-Aʿmash, the hadith of ʿAlī: ‘I am the divider of the Fire.’” I asked Mūsā: “What was ʿAbāyah like among you?” He spoke of his virtue, his prayers, his fasting, and his truthfulness.

I heard al-Ḥasan ibn al-Rabīʿ say: Abū Muʿāwiyah said: “We said to al-Aʿmash:

“‘Do not relate these reports.’ He said: ‘People ask me, so what can I do? Perhaps I forget. If they ask me about something of this sort and I forget, remind me.’ One day we were with him when a man came and asked him about the hadith, ‘I am the divider of the Fire.’ I cleared my throat. Al-Aʿmash said:

“‘These Murjiʾites won’t let me relate reports about the merits of ʿAlī. Get them out of the mosque so that I can relate to you.’”

Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmmār related to us: ʿAmr ibn ʿUthmān related to us: Abū Shihāb related to us, saying: al-Aʿmash said: “I never thought I would live in a time when I would hear them prefer ʿAlī to Abū Bakr and ʿUmar.”

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Numayr related to us, saying: I heard al-Aʿmash say: “We related to them the anger of the Companions of Muḥammad ﷺ—and they made it their religion.”

ʿUmar ibn Ḥafṣ ibn Ghiyāth related to us: my father related to us: al-Aʿmash related to us: Zayd ibn Wahb related to us, who said: “We were with ʿUmar in the mosque of Medina, and the people were fasting. Clouds covered the sky. A large bowl of milk was brought from Ḥafṣah’s house. The people drank, and soon those clouds cleared, and there was the sun. He said: ‘It is simply a day of fasting in place of a day.’ ʿUmar said: ‘It is simply one day in place of another. We will not make it up, nor will we fast it, so long as we have not inclined toward sin or acted out of sin. By God, we will not make it up.’”

Ibn Numayr related to us: Abū Muʿāwiyah related to us: al-Aʿmash related to us, from Zayd ibn Wahb, who said: “As evening approached in Ramaḍān, bowls of milk were brought out to us from Ḥafṣah’s house. Clouds had covered the sky, and they thought the sun had set, so they broke their fast. Then the clouds soon cleared, and there was the sun, still shining. ʿUmar said: ‘We will not make it up, so long as we did not incline toward sin.’”

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā related to us, from Shaybān, from al-Aʿmash, from al-Musayyib ibn Rāfiʿ, from Zayd ibn Wahb, who said: “While we were sitting in the mosque of Medina, with the sky overcast, we thought that the sun had set and that evening had come. Bowls of milk were brought out to us from Ḥafṣah’s house. ʿUmar drank, and we drank. Before long, the clouds disappeared and the sun appeared. Some of us began saying to one another, ‘We should make up this day of ours.’ ʿUmar heard that and said: ‘By God, we will not make it up, since we did not incline toward sin.’”

A Chapter

Abū Nuʿaym related to us: Sufyān related to us, from Jabalā ibn Suḥaym, from ʿAlī ibn Ḥanẓalah, from his father, who said: “We were with ʿUmar when a large bowl of food was brought in the month of Ramaḍān. The caller to prayer said: ‘The sun is still shining!’ He said: ‘May you spare us your evil! We did not send you as a herald of the sun; we sent you as a caller to prayer. People, whoever among you has broken the fast may make up a day—it is easy. Otherwise, let him complete his fast.’”

Ādam ibn Abī Iyās related to us: Shuʿbah related to us: Jabalā ibn Suḥaym related to us, saying:

“I heard ʿAlī ibn Ḥanẓalah relate from his father—and his father was a friend of ʿUmar—who said:

“‘I was with ʿUmar in Ramaḍān. He broke his fast, and the people broke theirs. The caller to prayer went up to give the call and said:

“‘People, the sun has not set.’ ʿUmar said: ‘May God spare us your evil! We did not send you as a caller.’ ʿUmar said: ‘Whoever has broken the fast should fast a day in its place.’”

Ādam related to us: Shuʿbah related to us: Ziyād ibn ʿIlāqah related to us, from a man of his people, who said: “I witnessed ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb break his fast one day in Ramaḍān before the sun had set. Then the sun appeared, and ʿUmar ordered whoever had broken the fast to make up a day in its place.”

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rajāʾ related to us: Isrāʾīl informed us, from Ziyād, from Bishr ibn Qays, from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, who said: “One evening I was with him. He thought the sun had set, so ʿUmar drank and gave me a drink. Then they looked toward it on the mountain slope, and ʿUmar said:

“By God, we do not mind making up a day in its place.”

Saʿīd related to us: al-Walīd ibn Abī Thawr al-Hamdānī related to us, from Ziyād ibn ʿIlāqah, from Bishr ibn Qays, who said: “One evening in Ramaḍān we were with ʿUmar. It was a cloudy day. He brought us some parched barley flour mixed with water, drank, and said to me, ‘Drink.’ I drank. After that, we saw the sun, and he said: ‘By God, we do not mind making up a day in its place.’”

He also said: Hushaym related to us: Abū Isḥāq al-Shaybānī informed us, from ʿAlī ibn Ḥanẓalah, from his father, who said: “We were with ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb in Ramaḍān. When the sun had set, as they thought, some of the people broke their fast. A man said: ‘Commander of the Faithful, the sun is still visible.’ He said: ‘May God protect us from your associating partners with Him! We did not send you as a caller to the sun.’ Then he said: ‘Whoever has broken the fast should fast a day in its place.’”

Al-Ḥajjāj related to us: Ḥammād related to us, from al-Ḥajjāj, from Ziyād ibn ʿIlāqah, from Quṭbah ibn Mālik, who said: “They were with ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb and broke their fast on a cloudy day. The clouds parted, and there was the sun over the mountains. ʿUmar said: ‘We do not mind making up another day.’”

Abū Yūsuf said: “This is an error on al-Ḥajjāj’s part. This and similar reports are among the things that show al-Ḥajjāj’s weakness as a narrator, because the hadith masters attributed the report to Bishr ibn Qays. Ziyād also transmitted something different from this from Quṭbah. Al-Ḥajjāj made the two into one report, finding this easier for himself.”

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Maslamah and Ibn Bukayr related to us, from Mālik, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from— “His father”—Ibn Bukayr said: “from Zayd, from his brother”—that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb broke his fast one day in Ramaḍān on a cloudy day, thinking evening had come and the sun had set. A man came to him and said: “Commander of the Faithful, the sun has appeared.” ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said: “A slight matter; we did our utmost.” Mālik said: “By this ʿUmar means making up the fast. By ‘its ease’ he means its cost and lightness, as he saw it—and God knows best.”

Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr related to us: Sufyān related to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his brother, from his father: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb broke his fast. They said to him, “The sun has appeared,” and he said: “A slight matter. We had been unaware.”

A Chapter

Ibn Numayr related to us: Muḥammad ibn al-Ṣalt related to us: Manṣūr ibn Abī al-Aswad related to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Zayd ibn Wahb, from Ḥudhayfah, who said: “Whoever loved [the name ‘ʿUthmān’ appears to have fallen out here; see footnote 2] the advent of the Antichrist would follow him; if he died before he appeared, he would believe in him in his grave.”

Abū Yūsuf said: “Among the things that demonstrate this hadith’s falsity is the sound report from Ḥudhayfah that, when asked about ʿUthmān, ‘If he is killed, where will he be?’ he said: ‘In Paradise.’ And his statement, ‘No one has marched against a ruler to abase him without God abasing them,’ when he was told, ‘They have set out against ʿUthmān.’ Among the things that demonstrate the weakness of this report of Zayd ibn Wahb, and of what he related from ʿUmar about breaking the fast before sunset, when ʿUmar said, ‘We will not make it up,’ is that the Kūfans and Ḥijāzīs contradicted him. Then there is his report from ʿUmar that he said to Ḥudhayfah: ‘I am one of the hypocrites.’”

Ibn Numayr related to me: Abū Muʿāwiyah related to us: al-Aʿmash related to us, from Zayd ibn Wahb, who said: “A man from among the hypocrites died, but Ḥudhayfah did not pray over him. ʿUmar said to him:

“‘Was he one of the people?’ He said: ‘Yes.’ ʿUmar said: ‘By God, am I one of them?’ He said: ‘No, and I will not tell anyone after you.’ This is impossible, and I fear it was fabricated. How could this be, when he was one of those with whom God was pleased, one of the people of Badr, and one to whom the Prophet ﷺ—said: ‘If there were a prophet after me, it would be ʿUmar’; and, ‘There have been inspired people among the nations, and if there is one in my community, it is ʿUmar’? This is in addition to countless reports of this kind. How can it be permissible for him to say to Ḥudhayfah, ‘Am I one of the hypocrites?’ Yet Zayd’s report has many flaws.”

Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shaybah related to us: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam related to us: ʿAmmār ibn Zurayq related to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Zayd ibn Wahb, from Ḥudhayfah, who said: “Do you recall the Day of the House? There was turmoil on the day of ʿUthmān, and its end will be the Antichrist.” This is among the things used to demonstrate the weakness of Zayd’s report. How can he say in the first report, “If the Antichrist appears, whoever loved ʿUthmān will follow him; and if he has died, he will believe in him in his grave,” and then make ʿUthmān’s killing the beginning of the turmoil?

Abū Yūsuf said: “Among the flaws in Zayd’s reports is what ʿUmar ibn Ḥafṣ ibn Ghiyāth related to us: my father related to us: al-Aʿmash related to us: Zayd ibn Wahb related to us: ‘By God, Abū Dharr related to us at al-Rabadhah. He said: I was with the Prophet ﷺ—as we walked in the lava plain of Medina one evening. When Uḥud came into view before us, he said: “Abū Dharr, I would not like that anyone’s worth in gold should come upon him for a night while I have a dinar of it with me, except a dinar I reserve to pay a debt—unless I were to spend it among God’s servants in this way, and this way, and this way”—and he gestured with his hand. Then he said: “Abū Dharr.”’

“I said: ‘At your service, and ready to obey you, Messenger of God.’ He said: ‘The ones with the most are the ones with the least, except whoever spends wealth in this way and this way.’ Then he said: ‘Stay where you are; do not leave until I return to you.’

“He went off until he was out of my sight. Then I heard a sound and feared that something had happened to the Messenger of God ﷺ. I wanted to go, but then I remembered the Messenger of God’s words, ‘Do not leave,’ so I stayed. He came back, and I said: ‘Messenger of God, I heard a sound and feared that something had happened to you. I wanted to come to you, but I remembered your words, “Do not leave,” so I stayed.’ The Messenger of God ﷺ—said: ‘That was Gabriel. He came to me and told me that whoever from my community dies without associating anything with God will enter Paradise.’

“I said: ‘Messenger of God, even if he commits adultery and steals?’ He said: ‘Even if he commits adultery and steals.’ Al-Aʿmash said: ‘I said to Zayd ibn Wahb: “I heard that it was Abū al-Dardāʾ.” He said:’”111

“‘I testify that Abū Dharr related it to me at al-Rabadhah.’”

“Abū Bakr related to us: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam related to us: Zuhayr related to us, saying:

“‘I heard al-Aʿmash [say]: “If you hear your hadith from Zayd ibn Wahb, it will do you no harm not to hear it from its original source.”’”

Abū Yūsuf said: “I also heard from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Dāwūd al-Ḥazībī, from ʿAbbād ibn Mūsā al-Ḥimṣī, from his father, who said: ‘I used to go back and forth on errands for Zayd ibn Wahb, and al-Aʿmash would keep close to him.’”

A Chapter

Ibn Numayr related to me: my father related to me, from al-Aʿmash, from Shaqīq, who said:

“We were sitting with Ḥudhayfah when ʿAbd Allāh and Abū Mūsā entered the mosque. He said:

“‘One of the two is a hypocrite.’ Then he said: ‘Of all people, the one most like the Messenger of God ﷺ—in guidance, bearing, and demeanor is ʿAbd Allāh.’”

He also said: Ḥafṣ related to us: al-Aʿmash related to us, saying: “Abū Wāʾil mentioned Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, and spoke of their virtue and precedence. I said: ‘What about ʿAbd Allāh—will you leave him unmentioned?’ He said:

“‘That is a man alongside whom I count no one.’”

Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd related to us: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Dāwūd related to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit, who said: “I saw the gifts of al-Mukhtār being brought to Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn ʿUmar”

So they accepted it from him.

Sulaymān said: “How does he know? Perhaps it was his description, which Ibn ʿUmar accepted without knowing [who he was], or words to that effect.”

Then Sulaymān said: “Ḥammād related to us, from Ayyūb, from Nāfiʿ, who said: ‘Ibn ʿUmar never [challenged?] anyone over a bequest or a gift except al-Mukhtār ibn Abī ʿUbayd.’”

A Chapter

ʿAlī ibn ʿUthmān ibn Nufayl related to us: [Abū] Mushir related to us: Saʿīd related to us, saying:

Abū al-Dardāʾ said: “I have never seen a people more given to asking about knowledge, nor have I seen any people from whom I withhold it more, than you, people of Iraq.”

Abū Muslim al-Khawlānī said: “I have never seen a people more given to asking about minor matters, nor have I seen any people more willing to take on major matters, than you, people of Iraq.”

Aḥmad ibn al-Khalīl related to me: Saʿīd ibn Sulaymān related to us: ʿUqba ibn Abī al-Ṣahbāʾ, Abū Khuzaym, related to us, saying: “I was present with Sālim ibn ʿAbd Allāh on the evening of the Day of Sacrifice. He said:

‘I suppose you are Iraqis.’ They were asking him about various things. He said: ‘I have never seen any people more apt to abandon the Book of God, Exalted is He, than the people of Iraq; nor any more insistent in asking about a Sunna or an obligatory duty; nor any more neglectful of all of that.’”

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, from Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd, from Bashīr ibn Yasār, client of the Anṣār, from Rāfiʿ ibn Khadīj and Sahl ibn Abī Ḥathma, who related to him—or related—that ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sahl and Muḥayyiṣa ibn (246a) Masʿūd went to Khaybar, then separated among the palm groves. ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sahl was killed, and they suspected the Jews in connection with his death. He said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Sahl, Ḥuwayyiṣa, and Muḥayyiṣa came to the Prophet ﷺ. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān began to speak, being the youngest of them, so the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Let the eldest speak.” (Yaḥyā said: “That is, let the eldest take the lead in speaking.”) He said: They spoke about their companion’s case, and the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “You may establish your claim concerning your companion—or your slain man—by taking fifty oaths.” They said:

“Messenger of God, we did not see it.” He said: “Then the Jews may clear themselves of responsibility by taking fifty oaths.” They said:

“They are an unbelieving people.” So the Messenger of God ﷺ paid the blood money on their behalf. Sahl said: “I once came upon a she-camel from among those camels, which had entered their enclosure, and it kicked me with its leg.”

Ibn Abī Uways related to us: My father related to me, from Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd, that Bashīr ibn Yasār, client of Banū Ḥāritha of the Anṣār, informed him. He was an elderly, learned man who had encountered men among the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ from the people of his own household among Banū Ḥāritha, including Rāfiʿ ibn Khadīj, Sahl ibn Abī Ḥathma, and Suwayd ibn al-Nuʿmān. They related to him that the procedure of qasāma had taken place among them, among Banū Ḥāritha ibn al-Ḥārith, concerning a man of the Anṣār named ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sahl, who was killed at Khaybar. The Messenger of God ﷺ said to them: “Will you take fifty oaths and thereby establish your claim concerning your slain man?”—or he said, “your companion.” They said: “Messenger of God, we were neither witnesses nor present.” Bashīr claimed that the Messenger of God ﷺ said to them: “Then the Jews may clear you by taking fifty [oaths],” or words to that effect.

Ibn Qanʿab and Ibn Bukayr related to us, from Mālik, from Abū Laylā ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Sahl, from Sahl ibn Abī Ḥathma, who informed him, from men among the elders of his people, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Will you take oaths and establish your claim to your companion’s blood?” They said: “No.” He said: “Then the Jews will take oaths for you.” They said: “They are not Muslims.”

So the Messenger of God ﷺ paid the blood money himself.

ʿAmmār al-Nasāʾī related to us: Salama related to us, from Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq, who related to me, from al-Zuhrī ibn Shihāb, from Sahl ibn Abī Ḥathma.

Ibn Isḥāq said: Bashīr, client of Banū Ḥāritha, also related this to me, from Sahl ibn Abī Ḥathma: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Name your companion, then take fifty oaths concerning him, and we will hand him over to you.” They said: “Messenger of God, we would take an oath only on what we know.” He said: “Then they [the Jews] will swear by God fifty times that they did not kill him and do not know who killed him, and then they will be free of responsibility for his blood.” They said: “Messenger of God, we would not accept the oaths of the Jews. There is no disbelief among them greater than their swearing to a sin.” So the Messenger of God ﷺ paid the blood money himself.

Abū Nuʿaym related to us: Saʿīd ibn ʿUbayd related to us, from Bashīr ibn Yasār, who claimed that a man of the Anṣār named Sahl ibn Abī Ḥathma informed him that a group of his people set out for Khaybar and dispersed there. They found one of their party slain, and said to those among whom they found him: “You killed our companion.” They replied: “We did not kill him, nor do we know who killed him.” He said:

They went to the Prophet of God ﷺ and said: “Prophet of God, we set out for Khaybar and found one of our party slain.” The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Let the eldest, the eldest [speak].” He said to them: “Bring proof against the person who killed him.” They said: “We have no proof.” He said:

“Then they will swear oaths for you.” They said: “We are not satisfied with the Jews’ oaths.” The Messenger of God ﷺ disliked letting his blood go unavenged, so he paid one hundred camels as blood money.

A Chapter

Ādam related to us: Shuʿba related to us: al-Ḥakam related to us, saying: “I heard Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Jadalī, whom al-Mukhtār used to appoint as his deputy.” Abū ʿAbd Allāh’s name was ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd—.

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us: ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib related to us, saying: “When we were adolescent boys, we used to visit Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān. He would say:

‘Do not sit with the storytellers, except Abū al-Aḥwaṣ. Beware of Shaqīq and Saʿd ibn ʿUbayda.’”

Ḥammād said: “He did not mean Shaqīq Abū Wāʾil.”

Ibn Numayr related to us: Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh related to us, from Mughīra, who said: “Only the companions of ʿAbd Allāh used to affirm things about ʿAlī…”

…against ʿAlī.”

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā related to me: Sufyān related to us, from Sulaymān, who said: “Shurayḥ said:

‘We heard [traditions] before the ḥadīths were sullied.’”

ʿAmr ibn ʿĀṣim related to us: Hammām related to us, saying: “We were with Qatāda when Nufayʿ, Abū Dāwūd al-Aʿmā, came in. When he left, one of those present said to him:

‘This man claims that he met eighty men who had pledged allegiance beneath the tree, and so-and-so many men of Badr.’ Qatāda said: ‘I knew this man when he was a boy, begging at the sick during the plague.’ Then Qatāda said: ‘Al-Ḥasan never told us that he had met any of the men of Badr face-to-face to receive ḥadīth from them. Nor did Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib, except [that he met] Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ.’”

Ibn Numayr related to me: Ṭalq ibn Ghannām related to us, saying: “Sharīk said: ‘If you wanted to, you could make Abū Dāwūd say: “ʿAlī and ʿAbd Allāh.”’”

Saʿīd ibn Asad related to me: Ḍamra related to us, from Rajāʾ ibn Abī Salama, from Ibn ʿAwn, who said: “Al-Shaʿbī said to me: ‘Beware of these liars’”—meaning Mughīra ibn Saʿīd and Bayān.

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, from Ayyūb, from Abū Maʿshar, who said: “ʿAlqama used to keep company with ʿAbd Allāh, and al-Aswad used to keep company with ʿUmar. Then the two would meet, and they would not disagree.”

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, from ʿĀṣim, who said:

“I knew people who made this night their mount: they wore safflower-dyed garments and drank fermented beverage from earthenware jars, seeing no harm in it. Among them were Zirr and Abū Wāʾil.” ʿĀṣim said: “Abū Wāʾil used to give us fermented beverage from earthenware jars in our meal of parched grain.”

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, from Abū Muṣʿab ibn Zuhayr, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn al-Aswad, who said: “My father used to send me to ask ʿĀʾisha (247b), then I would come back and tell him. When I reached puberty, I went to her and called to her from behind the curtain. She recognized my voice and said: ‘You rascal, have you done it?’ I said: ‘What makes the ritual bath obligatory?’ She said: ‘When the two circumcised parts meet.’”

Abū Yūsuf said: “I have no doubt that I heard Sulaymān say: ‘How does this hearing compare—a child’s hearing, or hearing from behind a curtain—with the hearing of ʿUrwa and al-Qāsim?’”

Salama related to us: Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal related to us: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam related to us, saying: “Ḥammād ibn Yūnus said to me: ‘Had I wished, ʿĪsā al-Ḥannāṭ could have told me everything that the people of Medina do.’”

Aḥmad said: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam related to us: Maʿlā ibn Khālid related to us, saying: “Shuʿba said:

‘Had I wished, Abū Hārūn al-ʿAbdī could have told me, from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, everything I see the people of Wāsiṭ doing. I would have done it’”—or, “I would have done so.”

ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān related to us, from his father, who said: “Shuʿba said: ‘If I were told, “You may enter Paradise, or meet Abū Hārūn and then enter Paradise,” I would say, “Rather, I will meet Abū Hārūn.”’ He said: ‘Then I met him, and he turned out to be nothing.’”

Salama related to me, from Aḥmad: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam related to us, saying: Zuhayr said:

“I saw Ashʿath ibn Suwār standing by Abū al-Zubayr while people stood between them. Abū al-Zubayr was relating ḥadīths, and Ashʿath kept asking, ‘How did he say it? What exactly did he say?’”

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us: Sufyān related to us, saying: “I heard Ibn Shubrumah say:

‘Abū Wāʾil used to say to Shaqīq al-Ḍabbī: “Shaqīq, have you found your religion since you lost it?”’ Shaqīq held the Khārijite doctrine.

He also said: Sufyān related to us: Ibn Shubrumah said: “I was with al-Shaʿbī when he saw an old woman. He said: ‘If I gave this woman four dirhams, it would be dearer to me than offering a sacrifice. I heard Ḥudhayfa ibn al-Yamān.’” I said to Sufyān: “It was only Ibn Usayd.” He said:

“Ḥudhayfa—and I will not attribute it further. I had thought he meant only Ḥudhayfa ibn al-Yamān.”

Mujāhid ibn Mūsā related to us: ʿAffān related to us, saying: “I heard Shuʿba say:

‘If you asked ʿĀṣim ibn ʿUbayd Allāh who built the mosque of Baṣra, he would say: “So-and-so, from so-and-so, from the Prophet ﷺ.”’ He said something about Simāk that I do not remember.”

A Chapter

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us: Sufyān related to us, saying: “We were with Ruʾba when he saw people hurrying away. He asked: ‘Where are they coming from?’ He was told: ‘From Abū Ḥanīfa.’ He said: ‘Well! He lets them have their fill of an opinion they have chewed over, and they return to their families without conviction.’”

Salama related to us, from Aḥmad: Abū Nuʿaym related to us, saying: “I heard Sufyān say:

‘I passed by Jawāb without putting a question to him.’”

Yūsuf ibn Muḥammad al-Ṣaffār related to me: Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh related to us, from Abū Ḥuṣayn, who said: “I was with Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān when we encountered Shaqīq al-Ḍabbī. He said:

‘Uncle, you forbid people to sit with me.’ He asked: ‘Who is this?’ We said: ‘Shaqīq.’ He said:

‘I have seen you only as one who has lost his religion and is seeking it, saying, “I saw you, I saw you.”’

He also said: Abū Bakr related to us, from ʿĀṣim, who said: “When Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān began his session, he would say: ‘No man who sits with Shaqīq al-Ḍabbī may sit with us; no Ḥarūrī may sit with us.’”

Zayd ibn Akhzam related to us, saying: “I heard Wahb ibn Jarīr say: I heard…”

…Shuʿba. He was asked about Abū Maryam and said: “He has a good memory.” He said: “I went to al-Minhal ibn ʿAmr and heard something in his house. I also went to al-Ḥārith al-ʿUklī and asked him: ‘What do you make of the Prophet’s statement ﷺ: “When one of you follows a funeral procession, let him not sit until the bier is lowered from the men’s shoulders or placed in the niche or grave”?’ He said: ‘What if we arrive and no grave has been dug for him? Should we stand upright?’” He said: “So I left him.”

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm related to us, saying: Abū Mushir said, from Muzāḥim ibn Zayd, who said: “I asked Shuʿba about Abū Bakr al-Hudhalī, and he said: ‘Leave me alone; I’m going to vomit.’”

Suwayd said: “I came to Mecca while Abū al-Zubayr was still alive and wanted to visit him. Shuʿba said to me: ‘Do you not see how he prays?’”

Abū Taqī Hishām ibn ʿAbd al-Malik related to us: Suwayd ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz related to us. One of his companions asked him: “Why [do you] not transmit from Abū al-Zubayr?” He said: “Shuʿba deceived me. He said to me (248b): ‘Do not transmit from him, for I saw him praying badly.’ I wish I had never met Shuʿba.”

Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmmār related to us, saying: “I heard al-Muʿāfā say: ‘I heard Shuʿba say: “It would be dearer to me to commit fornication than to practice tadlīs.”’” I said to him: “Abū Masʿūd, what do you say about tadlīs?” He said: “I consider it a form of embellishment.”

Abū ʿAlī Mujāhid ibn Mūsā related to us: Qirād, Abū Nūḥ, related to us: Shuʿba related to us, saying: “I asked ʿAmr ibn Murra and Abū Isḥāq about Uways, but they did not recognize him.”

He said: Mujāhid related to us: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam related to us: Abū Shihāb related to us, saying: “Shuʿba said to me: ‘You should seek out al-Ḥajjāj ibn Arṭāʾa and Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq; but keep what I say about Khālid and Hishām secret from the people of Baṣra.’”

Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmmār related to us: Ibn Idrīs related to us, from Shuʿba, who said:

“I asked Abū al-Yaqẓān about a ḥadīth, and he related it to me. Later, I asked him about his birth, and he told me. It turned out that he had heard the ḥadīth when he was less than two years old.”

[ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm related to us; Abū Mushir related to us, from Muzāḥim ibn Zufar, who said: I said to Abū Ḥanīfa, “Abū Ḥanīfa, is this which you give legal opinions on and which you have set down in your books the truth, about which there is no doubt?” He replied, “By God, I do not know. Perhaps it is falsehood, about which there is no doubt.”]

Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmmār related to us; Yaʿqūb ibn Isḥāq al-Ḥaḍramī related to us, who said: Shuʿba said, “I used to visit Abū Sufyān about poetry.”

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Muʿādh related to us; Muḥammad ibn Muʿādh related to me, who said: I heard Saʿīd ibn Muslim say: I asked Abū Yūsuf, “Was Abū Ḥanīfa a Jahmī?” He replied, “Yes.” I asked, “Was he a Murjiʾ?” He replied, “Yes.” I said, “I once said to him: ‘What do you think of a woman who married a Sindī and bore him children with tightly curled hair, then married a Turk after him and bore him children with small eyes and broad faces?’ He said, ‘They belong to the first husband.’ I said to him, ‘Then why did you sit with him?’ He replied, ‘To study knowledge together.’”

Salama related to us; Aḥmad related to us; Yaḥyā ibn Ādam related to us; Mufaḍḍal related to us from Mughīra, who used to say: “Abū Ṣāliḥ, the companion of al-Kalbī, only teaches children and weakens his exegesis.” He said, “Someone wrote it for her!!” He said, “He wonders at those who relate from him.”

His Exegesis. He said, “Someone wrote it for her!!” He said, “He wonders at those who relate from him.”

[Aḥmad ibn al-Khalīl related to us; ʿAbda related to us, who said: I heard Ibn al-Mubārak mention Abū Ḥanīfa. A man asked, “Was there any doctrinal inclination in him?” He replied, “Yes: irjāʾ.”]

[Abū Juzʾ related to us, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd ibn Muslim, who said: I heard my grandfather say: I asked Abū Yūsuf, “Was Abū Ḥanīfa a Murjiʾ?” He replied, “Yes.” I asked, “Was he a Jahmī?” He replied, “Yes.” I said, “Then where do you stand in relation to him?” He replied, “Abū Ḥanīfa was only a teacher. Whatever he said that was good, we accepted; whatever was objectionable, we left to him.”]

[Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmar related to me, who said: Sufyān said, “No child was born in Islam more harmful to the people of Islam than Abū Ḥanīfa.”]

[Aḥmad ibn Yūnus related to us, who said: I heard Nuʿaym say: Sufyān said:

“No evil was introduced into Islam by anyone as much as by Abū Ḥanīfa—except so-and-so,” he said: “A hard-headed man.”]

[Muḥammad ibn Bashshār related to us, who said: I heard ʿAbd al-Raḥmān say, “Between Abū Ḥanīfa and the truth there is a veil.”]

[ʿAlī ibn ʿUthmān ibn Nufayl related to me; Abū Mushir related to us; Yaḥyā ibn Ḥamza related to us—while Saʿīd was listening—that Abū Ḥanīfa said, “If a man were to worship this sandal, seeking nearness to God through it, I would see no harm in that.” Saʿīd said, “This is outright unbelief.”]

[ʿAbd al-Raḥmān related to me, who said: I heard ʿAlī ibn al-Madīnī say: Bishr ibn Abī al-Azhar al-Naysābūrī said to me, “I saw in a dream a funeral bier covered with a black cloth, with priests around it. I asked, ‘Whose bier is this?’ They said, ‘Abū Ḥanīfa’s bier.’ I told Abū Yūsuf about it, and he said, ‘Do not tell anyone about it.’”]

[Abū Bakr ibn Khallād related to us, who said: I heard ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī say: I heard Ḥammād ibn Zayd say: I heard Ayyūb mention Abū Ḥanīfa and say, “They wish to extinguish God’s light with their mouths, but God refuses to do otherwise than perfect His light” [Qurʾān 9:32].]

Ibn Numayr related to me; ʿAbd Allāh ibn Idrīs related to us, from Zakariyyā, who said: I saw al-Shaʿbī (249b) pass by Abū Ṣāliḥ. He took him by the ear and said, “You interpret the Qurʾān, but you do not read it.”

[Ibn Numayr related to us; one of our companions related to us, from ʿAmmār ibn Razīq, who said: “If you are asked about something and have no answer, look at what Abū Ḥanīfa said and oppose him; you will get it right.”]

[Nuʿaym ibn Ḥammād related to us; Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad al-Fazārī related to us, who said: We were with Sufyān al-Thawrī when news came to him of Abū Ḥanīfa’s death. He said, “Praise be to God, who has relieved the Muslims of him. He was undoing the bonds of Islam one bond at a time. No child was born in Islam more ill-omened for Islam than he.”]

[Nuʿaym said: I heard Muʿādh ibn Muʿādh and Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd say, “We heard Sufyān al-Thawrī say, ‘Abū Ḥanīfa was asked to repent of unbelief twice.’”]

[Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us; Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, who said: Ibn ʿAwn said, “I have been told that there are among you people who turn others away from the path of God.” Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb said, “Abū Ḥanīfa and his companions are among those who turn people away from the path of God.”]

[Al-Walīd ibn ʿUtba al-Dimashqī related to me—and he was one who had subdued his own self—Abū Mushir related to us; Yaḥyā ibn Ḥamza related to us, while Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz was sitting there. Sharīk ibn ʿAbd Allāh, the judge of Kūfa, related to me that Abū Ḥanīfa was asked to repent of heresy twice.]

[Al-Walīd related to me; Abū Mushir related to me; Muḥammad ibn Fulayḥ al-Madanī related to me, from his brother Sulaymān—who was highly knowledgeable about people—[who said]: “The one who asked Abū Ḥanīfa to repent was Khālid al-Qasrī. He said: When he saw that, he turned to rational opinion so as to disobey by means of it.”]

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us; Muʿādh ibn Muʿādh related to us, from Bishr ibn al-Mufaḍḍal, who said: I heard Abū Ḥanīfa being asked about a woman of the tribe who had a boy. He had intercourse with her without penetrating the vagina, but his semen was lost inside her vagina, and she became pregnant. “What is the solution?” he was asked. He said, “Does she have a paternal aunt?” They said, “Yes.” He said, “Let her give the child to her paternal aunt, then marry her to him; then he will be spared from associating with him.”112

Ḥammād said: I sat with Abū Ḥanīfa in the Sacred Mosque. He said, “Abū [Ḥanīfa] has arrived at the gates of Medina.” So I sat with him and said to ʿAlī, “Shall I seize on a slip of his?” He said: Then he came (250a) and stood between the pulpit and the tomb. He said, “Whenever I recall where he stood, my skin shivers.” Sulaymān said, “I think he was lying.” Then Sulaymān said, “Do you think there was faith in his heart when he intended to seize on a slip of Ayyūb’s? Have you ever seen anyone worse in manners than him, when he knows that Ḥammād is Ayyūb’s companion, and then says this to him?!”

Ibn ʿUthmān related to us; ʿAbd Allāh related to us; Zuhayr informed us, from Abū Ḥanīfa, who said: Ayyūb came, approached the Prophet’s tomb ﷺ—turned his back to the direction of prayer, faced the tomb, and wept, not pretending to weep.

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us; Ḥamza ibn al-Ḥārith, the client of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, related to us, from his father, who said: I heard a man ask Abū Ḥanīfa in the Sacred Mosque about a man who said, “I testify that the Kaʿba is true, but I do not know whether this is it or not.” He replied, “A true believer.” He asked him about a man who said, “I testify that Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh is a prophet, but I do not know whether he is the one whose tomb is in Medina or not.” He replied, “A true believer.” Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī said, “Whoever says this has disbelieved.”

Abū Bakr said: Sufyān used to relate from Ḥamza ibn al-Ḥārith. Muʾammal ibn Ismāʿīl related to us, from al-Thawrī, a report with the same meaning as Ḥamza’s report.

Ṣafwān ibn Ṣāliḥ al-Dimashqī related to me; ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-Wāḥid al-Sulamī related to us, who said: I heard Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad al-Fazārī relate to al-Awzāʿī: “My brother was killed with Ibrāhīm al-Fāṭimī at Baṣra, so I set out to inventory his estate. I met Abū Ḥanīfa. He asked me, ‘Where have you come from, and where are you headed?’ I told him that I had come from al-Maṣṣīṣa and was going to see a brother of mine who had been killed with Ibrāhīm. He said, ‘If you had been killed with your brother, it would have been better for you than the place you came from.’ I said, ‘What kept you from doing that yourself?’ He said, ‘Had I not had deposits entrusted to me and people’s belongings, I would not have become involved in that.’”

[Ṣafwān ibn Ṣāliḥ related to me; ʿUmar related to us, who said: I heard al-Awzāʿī say:

Shuʿayb ibn Isḥāq, Ibn Abī Mālik, Ibn ʿAllāq, and Ibn Nāṣiḥ came to me and said, “We have taken some things from Abū Ḥanīfa; examine them.” He and they stayed with me until I showed them, in what they had brought me from him, that they had been permitted to revolt against the rulers.]

Abū Bakr related to me, from Abū Ṣāliḥ al-Farrāʾ, from al-Fazārī, who said: Abū Ḥanīfa said, “The faith of Adam and the faith of Iblīs are one. Iblīs said, ‘My Lord, because You led me astray…’”

“And he said, ‘My Lord, grant me respite until the day they are raised up,’ while Adam said, ‘Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves.’”

[Al-Faḍl ibn Sahl related to me; al-Aswad ibn ʿĀmir related to us, from Sharīk, who said: “Abū Ḥanīfa was nothing but a scab.”]

Aḥmad ibn ʿUthmān ibn Ḥakīm related to us, who said: I heard Abū Nuʿaym say: I heard Sharīk say, “It is better for a tribe to have a wine-seller among them than a man who holds the views of Abū Ḥanīfa.”

Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā ibn ʿUthmān related to me, who said: ʿUmar ibn Ḥafṣ ibn Ghiyāth said: I heard him relate from his father, who said: I used to sit with Abū Ḥanīfa, and I heard him change his position on a single question five times in one day. So I got up, left him, and pursued hadith.

[Aḥmad related to me, who said: I heard ʿAbd al-Razzāq ibn ʿUmar al-Buzayʿī say:

I was with ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mubārak when a man came and asked him about a question. He gave him a legal opinion on it. The man said, “I asked Abū Yūsuf, and he disagreed with you.” He replied, “If you have prayed behind Abū Yūsuf any prayers that you remember, repeat them.”]

ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān related to us, who said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mubārak said, “I dislike sitting in a gathering where Yaʿqūb is mentioned.”

[Al-Ḥasan ibn al-Ṣabbāḥ related to me; Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm al-Ḥunaynī related to us, who said:

Mālik said, ‘No child was born in Islam more harmful to the people of Islam than Abū Ḥanīfa, and he used to criticize rational opinion and say, “The Messenger of God ﷺ passed away when this matter had been completed and perfected. We ought only to follow the reports of the Messenger of God ﷺ and his Companions, and not to follow rational opinion. [For whoever follows rational opinion,] a man comes along with stronger reasoning than yours, and you follow him; then, whenever a man comes along and overcomes you, you follow him. I see that this matter will never be finished.”]

[I heard Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr say: A man asked Abū Yūsuf, “A man prayed with the imam in the Mosque of ʿArafa, then stood there until (251a) he moved on with the imam’s departure. What do you say of him?” He replied, “There is no harm in it.” The man said, “Glory be to God! Ibn ʿAbbās said, ‘Whoever departs from ʿArafāt has no pilgrimage.’ The Mosque of ʿArafa is in the valley of ʿUranah.” He replied, “You know more about the transmitted reports, and we know more about jurisprudence.” The man said, “If you do not know the basis, how can you be a jurist?”]

Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmar related to us, who said: Sufyān said: Raqaba said to al-Qāsim ibn Maʿn, “Where are you going?” He replied, “To Abū Ḥanīfa.” He said, “He will let you chew over his opinions, and you will return to your family without any jurisprudence.”

Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh related to me; Saʿīd ibn ʿĀmir related to us, from Sallām ibn Abī Muṭīʿ, who said: I was with Ayyūb in the Sacred Mosque. Abū Ḥanīfa saw him and came toward him. When Ayyūb saw him coming toward him, he said to his companions, “Get up, lest he infect us with the scab. Get up, lest he infect us with the scab.”113

I heard Nuʿaym ibn Ḥammād say: A boy in Medina said to Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, “What do you say about one date in exchange for two fresh dates?” He replied, “There is no harm in it.” The boy said, “Uncle, you are ignorant of the Sunna and speak about difficult matters.”

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā related to me, who said: Abū Yūsuf and Abū Ḥanīfa were mentioned in the presence of Sufyān al-Thawrī, and he said, “Who are these people? And what are these people, anyway?” Sufyān said, “We used to visit Ḥammād secretly, away from our companions. They would say to us, ‘You visit him? You sit with him?’ So we only went to him in secret.”

I heard Abū Ḥudhayfa Mūsā ibn Masʿūd say: Sufyān said, “I used to meet Ḥammād after I had related hadith, but I would not greet him.”

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us, who said: Ḥammād ibn Abī Sulaymān arrived, but Ayyūb did not visit him, though Ayyūb hardly ever failed to visit a scholar who arrived. He said: We did not visit him because Ayyūb had not visited him. Al-Ṣalt ibn Dīnār came to him and said, “Who are you?” He replied, “Ṣalt.”

He asked him about nabīdh. Ayyūb said to him, “Have you seen your she-ass bringing Ḥammād and his talk?”114

And [he said], “Or something like that.”

Ibn Numayr related to us: I heard Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh say: I said to al-Aʿmash:

“Did you hear Ibrāhīm say to us that he disapproved of mixing unripe dates with dried dates on account of extravagance, just as he disapproved of mixing clarified butter with meat?” He said: “No.” I said: “Then from whom did you hear it?” He said:

“From Ḥammād—and we did not believe him.”

Ismāʿīl ibn al-Khalīl related to us (251b): Ibn Abī Zāʾida and al-Aʿmash related to us. He said: “I asked Ibrāhīm about the fuller. He said: ‘He is liable for damages.’ Then I heard that Ḥammād related on the authority of their father that he had said: ‘He is not liable.’ So we met him, and I said: ‘By God, I do not know whether I have ever seen you with Ibrāhīm or not.’ He said: ‘Do not do that, Abū Muḥammad, for this is hard on me.’”

Abū Nuʿaym related to us: Sufyān related to us, from Manṣūr, from Ibrāhīm, who said: “Whether it has grown hair or not, [the fetus is lawful] if you have not struck it down”—meaning the fetus.

He also said: Sufyān related to us, from al-Zubayr ibn ʿAdī, from Ibrāhīm, who said: “Its slaughter is the slaughter of its mother.”

Ādam related to us: Shuʿba related to us, from al-Mughīra, from Ibrāhīm, who said: “The fetus’s slaughter is the slaughter of its mother.”

Abū Yūsuf said: It has also been transmitted from Ḥammād, from Ibrāhīm, who said: “The slaughter of one life cannot serve as the slaughter of two lives.”

He said: Some of our companions related to us: ʿUthmān ibn ʿUthmān related to us: al-Battī informed us, saying: “When Ḥammād gave his own opinion, he was right; when he said, ‘Ibrāhīm said,’ he was wrong.”

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, saying: “I was present when Abū Ḥanīfa was asked about the witr prayer. He said: ‘It is obligatory.’ I said: ‘How many prayers are there?’ He said: ‘Five.’

“I said: ‘And the witr?’ He said: ‘It is obligatory.’”

[He also said: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, saying: “I sat with Abū Ḥanīfa in the Sacred Mosque. He mentioned Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and attributed Irjāʾ to him. I said: ‘Abū Ḥanīfa, who is your source?’ He said: ‘Sālim al-Afṭas.’ I said: ‘Sālim was a Murjiʾite, but Ayyūb related to us, saying: “Saʿīd saw me sitting with Ṭalq and said: ‘Did I not see you sitting with Ṭalq? Do not sit with him.’”’ A man said: ‘Abū Ḥanīfa, what was Ṭalq’s opinion?’ He said:

“He fell silent. Then the man asked him, and he fell silent; then he asked him again, and he fell silent. He said: ‘Woe to you! He held that justice [should be upheld].’” Then he turned to me and said: “May God have mercy on Ayyūb. He came to Medina while I was there.”]

“I said: ‘I shall sit with him, hoping to catch him in a slip.’ He came and stood by the grave, in a place—I do not recall that place without my skin crawling.”

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb said: “I spoke with Yaḥyā ibn Aktham, and he said (252a): ‘I am not a man of personal opinion.’ He mentioned Abū Ḥanīfa, so I said to him: ‘Let us leave aside the dispute. In his time there were leading scholars in Kūfa and elsewhere. Tell me of even one man who praised his conduct and his opinion.’ Sulaymān said: He was silent for a while, then said: ‘Jarīr related, from Mughīra, about a man who gave a garment to a tailor and said: “If you finish it today, I will give you two dirhams; if you put it off until tomorrow, then one dirham.” So-and-so said this, so-and-so said that, and so-and-so said this, while these men said that he was entitled to the going rate.’ He said: I replied: ‘This is enough to show his abasement: he could not rely on anyone else and had to resort to Mughīra.’”

Saʿīd ibn Asad related to me: Ḍamra related to us, from al-Awzāʿī, who said: “I made the pilgrimage and met ʿAbda ibn Abī Lubāba at Minā. He said to me: ‘Have you met al-Ḥakam?’ I said: ‘No.’ He said: ‘Go and meet him. There is no one between its two lava fields more learned in jurisprudence than he.’ I met him, and there was a man of fine bearing, with his head covered.”

Saʿīd related to me: Ḍamra related to us, from al-Awzāʿī, who said: “We used to visit Ibn Sīrīn while standing; he suffered from an intestinal ailment.”

Abū Yūsuf said: “Al-Awzāʿī was from al-Yamāma.”

He said: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmmār related to us: Ibn Idrīs related to us, from Abū Isḥāq al-Shaybānī, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Iyās, who said: “I asked Ibrāhīm: ‘Whom should we ask after you?’ He said: ‘Ḥammād.’” Ibn Idrīs said: “I heard my father and my uncle say that ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Iyās was one of those who heard and then remained silent.”

Abū Bakr ibn ʿAbd al-Malik related to me: ʿAbd al-Razzāq related to us, from Maʿmar, who said: “I said to Ḥammād ibn Abī Bukayr: ‘You were a leader among your companions, then you became a follower in a matter over which people disagreed with you.’ He said: ‘To be a follower in what is good is better than to be a leader in what is evil.’”

ʿUthmān ibn Abī Shayba related to us: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Idrīs related to us, from Shuʿba, who said:

“I asked al-Ḥakam about Zādhān. He said: ‘He talks too much.’

“I asked Salama ibn Kuhayl, and he said: ‘Abū al-Bakhtarī al-Ṭāʾī is more pleasing to me.’”

Abū Saʿīd al-Ashajj related to me: Abū Usāma related to us, from Sufyān, from— Al-Aʿmash, who said: Dharr ibn ʿAbd Allāh (252b) said to me: “You have gone rather quickly in something that I fear may become fixed among us”—Abū Usāma said: “meaning the opinion of the traditionist.”

ʿUthmān ibn Abī Shayba related to me: Jarīr related to us, from Mughīra, from Simāk ibn Salama, who said: “I went in to visit Kudayr al-Ḍabbī while he was ill. I said to his wife:

“‘Where is he?’ She said: ‘Standing, praying.’ I went up to him, and he leaned on me. I heard him say: ‘Peace be upon the Prophet and the legatee.’ I said: ‘I hope I never have to visit you again after today.’”

He said: Jarīr related to us, from Mughīra, who said: “Salama ibn Kuhayl was among the strongest in his opposition to ʿAlī—he would forbid him from going out.”

Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Numayr related to me, saying: “Abū al-Shaʿthāʾ al-Muḥāribī is Sulaym ibn Aswad, and Abū al-Shaʿthāʾ al-Kindī is Yazīd ibn al-Muhāṣir. ʿAmr ibn Murra is older than Qays ibn Muslim, and Salama is older than ʿAmr ibn Murra. Abū Qays Wāʾil is less accomplished in retention than these men. Zubayd and the others are close in standing. Ashʿath ibn Abī al-Shaʿthāʾ is good in his transmission. Al-Ḥakam is comparable to Salama. Al-Aʿmash has a better memory than Manṣūr, while Manṣūr’s transmissions are more sound and less divergent. Al-Ḥakam was a client of Kinda. ʿAmr ibn Murra was from Murād, one of their most distinguished men. Muḥammad ibn— Sālim is reported to have taken al-Shaʿbī’s book from the register.

He was asked about Ibrāhīm al-Hajarī and said: “Keep your distance from him.”

He said: “Abū Yaḥyā al-Qattāt is good in his transmission. Muslim is weak; I did not hear his reports from my father, because he disliked him.”

He said: “ʿAmr ibn Murra was a Murjiʾite, and Qays was a Murjiʾite and would argue about it. Hubayra ibn Yarīm took part in the sedition—that is, he went out [in rebellion]. ʿAbd Khayr was Khaywānī. When he was asked about him, he said: ‘Excellent!’”

Ibn Numayr said: Zuhayr ibn [Muʿāwiya] said: “ʿAbbād ibn Kathīr met me and said: ‘I found a sheet containing good reports. Take it and relate them to people when they come to you.’”

Ibn Numayr said: “The name of Abū Sufyān, the companion of al-Aʿmash, was Ṭalḥa ibn Rāfiʿ, a man of Wāsiṭ. The other Abū Sufyān was Ṭarīf al-Saʿdī, a weak transmitter.” (253a) Ibn Numayr said: “Abū al-Zubayr used to crack his knuckles in the Sacred Mosque, and Abū— The companion of al-Aʿmash, Abū Razīn, was named Masʿūd.

Ibn Numayr said: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam related to us, from Mufaḍḍal ibn Muhalhil, from al-Aʿmash, who said: “Abū Razīn was one of the reciters from whom people received recitation and to whom they recited.”

Ibn Numayr said: “The ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith from whom Khalaf ibn Khalīfa transmits, from Ḥumayd al-Aʿraj, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith, from Ibn Masʿūd, did not hear anything from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd. He is ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith al-Muktab.”

I said to him: “Do you reject anything in ʿAbd Allāh’s reports?” He said: “No.”

Ibn Numayr said: “This Ḥumayd al-Aʿraj is weak. He said: ‘My father had reports on a sheet, but he did not relate them to me.’ He said: ‘What would you do with him? He was weak.’ He is Ḥumayd ibn ʿAṭāʾ.”

[Ibn Numayr said: “Fiṭr is a retentive and intelligent transmitter.”] I heard Ḥammād ibn Ḥafṣ say: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Dāwūd said: “Fiṭr is the most reliable of the people of Kūfa.”

ʿUthmān ibn Abī Shayba related to me: Abū Nuʿaym related to us, saying: Ḥammād ibn Zayd said:

“I saw Manṣūr in Mecca. He had reverent fear, and I do not think he used to lie.”

He said: Ibn Numayr related to me, saying: “Abū Ḥizām, the client of Ibn ʿAbbās, was Nabtal; Abū Ḥāzim al-Madanī was Salama ibn Dīnār; and Abū Ḥāzim, the client of Ashjaʿ, was Kaysān. I heard from ʿAlī that his name was Salmān, the client of ʿAzza al-Ashjaʿiyya.”

Abū Ṣāliḥ Dhakwān, the client of Ghaṭafān, was al-Sammān, also known as al-Zayyāt. Abū Ṣāliḥ al-Ḥanafī was Māhān. Some said his name was ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Qays, the brother of Ṭalq ibn Qays.

Saʿīd ibn Yaḥyā related to us: Ibn Idrīs related to us, saying: “I asked Shuʿba about Manṣūr and ʿAmr ibn Murra. He said: ‘ʿAmr ibn Murra was the more reticent of the two men.’”

Bakr ibn Khalaf related to us: al-ʿAqadī related to us, from ʿAlī ibn al-Mubārak, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, who said: “Abū Ṣāliḥ was Qaylawa. Abū Ṣāliḥ al-Madanī, from whom the Egyptians transmit, was Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Ghifārī. The one from whom the people of Palestine transmit, and from whom al-Taymī transmits, was named Durayḥ” (253b). “As for the Abū Ṣāliḥ from whom Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr transmits, Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal said his name was Qaylawa.”

Abū Ṣāliḥ al-Baṣrī, from whom al-Taymī, Khālid al-Ḥadhdhāʾ, and Abū Ḥalda transmit, was named Mīzār.

Abū Ṣāliḥ, who transmits from Ibn ʿAbbās, was named Samīʿ.

Abū Ṣāliḥ, the client of Ḍubāʿa.

Abū Ṣāliḥ, the client of the Saʿdīs.

Abū Ṣāliḥ al-Ghifārī.

And Abū Ṣāliḥ Maysara.

Abū Ṣāliḥ ʿUbayd, the client of al-Saffāḥ, was one from whom Busr ibn Saʿīd transmitted.

Abū Ṣāliḥ, the client of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, used to order us to stay up with him for three [nights].

Abū Ṣāliḥ al-Ashʿarī was one from whom Ḥassān ibn ʿAṭiyya transmitted.

Abū Ṣāliḥ, the companion of al-Aʿmash, was Abū Suhayl.

Abū Ṣāliḥ, the companion of al-Kalbī, was Bādhān, also said to be Bādhām, the client of Umm Hāniʾ.

Abū Ṣāliḥ, the client of ʿUthmān, was one from whom Kāmil transmitted; no one else transmitted from him.

Abū ʿUbayda Aḥmad ibn Abī al-Safar related to me, saying: “Hubayra ibn Yarīm, Saʿīd ibn Dhī Ḥaddān, Saʿīd ibn Dhī Laʿwa, Yazīd ibn Yarīm, and ʿAmr al-Aṣamm were from Hamadhān.

“As for Maṭar ibn ʿAkāmis, I heard al-Qāsim al-ʿAqrī say: ‘He was Salmī.’

“ʿAmr Dhū Marra and Saʿīd ibn Nimrān were from Hamadhān.

“Masrūq ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, Shaddād ibn al-Azmaʿ, and ʿAmr ibn Shuraḥbīl were from Wadāʿa of Hamdān.”

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us, saying: “Thuwair ibn Abī Fākhita was mentioned to Sufyān— “—and he made a disparaging gesture.”
