[ʿUmar ibn Ḥafṣ ibn Ghiyāth related to us, saying: I heard my father say: I heard Sufyān, when asked about Abū Khālid al-Aḥmar, say: “What an excellent man Abū Hishām ʿAbd Allāh ibn Numayr is.”]

ʿUmar related to us, saying: I heard my father say: “Abān ibn Abī ʿAyyāsh came to us, and Abū Khālid al-Aḥmar came to us with his long hair. He sat with us there, and the scholars of ḥadīth exchanged glances over him. He got up and cut off his long hair, then kept coming back to seek ḥadīth with us. When Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd Allāh rose up in Baṣra, the troops were sent against him (254a), and Abū Khālid was among them. Then he joined Ibrāhīm. When they arrived, he came and went into his house, then sent his packhorse to be sold in al-Kunāsa. The next day he shaved his head. When al-Ḥajjāj arrived, he went out with them as though he had been in Mecca.”

ʿUmar said: “I heard my father say: ‘When Abū Usāma saw ʿĀʾisha in a book, he would erase her. I hope there is no excess in the opposite direction.’”

I heard Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Numayr disparage Abū Usāma. Then he said: “It is astonishing that Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shayba knows Abū Usāma so well, yet still transmits from him.”

[Ibn Numayr said: “He is the one who transmits from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd ibn Jābir. We think he is not the well-known Ibn Jābir. I was told that there is a man called Ibn Jābir, and he became mixed up with him; he is simply a person called Ibn Jābir.”]

[Yaʿqūb said: “He was right; he is Ibn Tamīm.”]

Abū Yūsuf said: “It seemed to me that I saw Ibn Numayr suspecting Abū Usāmah of having known and recognized that, but of having deliberately overlooked it. Ibn Numayr said to me: ‘Do you not see that his narration resembles none of the sound reports of his that the Syrians and his trustworthy companions transmitted?’”

Al-Ḥasan ibn al-Rabīʿ mentioned something about Abū Usāmah. He said: “Sufyān was a leading authority among people, and his narrations were examined so they could be authenticated; his hadith was known by that means.”

Salamah related to me: Aḥmad said that Wakīʿ said: “Abū al-ʿAlāʾ—he is Ibn Hubayrah—keeps at it.” Wakīʿ said: “Ibn Hubayrah was fierce on the day of al-Mukhtār.”

Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Makharrimī related to me: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam related to us, from Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh, who said: “I heard Abū Isḥāq say: ‘You should seek out Sammāk ibn Ḥarb and ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr.’” Abū Bakr said: “I mentioned that to Mughīrah, and he said: ‘I do not think either of those two sought out any of this knowledge in order to gain understanding through it.’”

Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Makharrimī related to us: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam related to us: Misʿar related to us, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr, who said: ʿAlī said: “We used to go to great lengths, while today you overdo it; so follow the stones with water.”

Misʿar said: “This is not among the early hadith reports of ʿAbd al-Malik; ʿAbd al-Malik narrates from young men.” (254b)

Volume Two

Chapter

[Ḥajjāj ibn Arṭāʾah]

“Ibn Abī ʿUmar related to us: Sufyān related to us, saying: ‘I heard Ibn Abī Najīḥ say: “No one like him has come to us from among you”—meaning Ḥajjāj ibn Abī Arṭāʾah.”’”

Mujāhid ibn Mūsā related to us: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam related to us: Abū Shihāb related to us, saying:

“Shuʿbah said to me: ‘You should seek out Ḥajjāj ibn Arṭāʾah.’”

He also said: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam related to us: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, saying: “Ḥajjāj’s hadith is sounder than that of Sufyān al-Thawrī.”

Mujāhid said: “I heard Abū Muʿāwiyah saying: ‘Ḥajjāj said to us: “Do not say, ‘Who related it to you?’” He would then recite it to us straight through.’”

“Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmmār related to us: Ḥafṣ ibn Ghiyāth related to us, saying:

“‘I heard Sufyān al-Thawrī say: “You will not find anyone you visit with a better memory than Ḥajjāj ibn Arṭāʾah.”

“Ḥafṣ said: ‘I heard Ḥajjāj say: “I have never disputed with anyone, nor have I sat with people who were disputing.”’”

Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmmār related to us: Ibn Idrīs related to us, saying: “Ḥajjāj ibn Arṭāʾah was in charge of the night watch. He struck a weaver who was our neighbor, and the man cried out for help. I said to him: ‘Abū Arṭāʾah, after all your knowledge and your recitation of the Qurʾān!’ He said: ‘Be quiet, boy. What do you know?’ I said:

“‘I swear I will never speak to you again or transmit from you.’ So he did not transmit from him.”

ʿAlī ibn al-Madīnī said: Ibn Abī Najīḥ said: “Ḥajjāj said to me: ‘My father related to us, and my grandfather related to us, until I had related it to you.’”

Aḥmad ibn al-Khalīl related to us: Yaḥyā ibn Ayyūb related to us, saying: “I heard Abū ʿAlī al-Ḥawwārī say: ‘One day Ḥajjāj ibn Arṭāʾah was relating a report and said, “I asked an uncle about the sacrificial animal.” He was fond of eloquence and made his speech grandiose. Dāwūd al-Ṭāʾī called out to him”—he said, “Dāwūd wanted to humble himself before him”—“and said: ‘Abū Arṭāʾah, it is not al-ḍaḥiyyah; it is al-uḍḥiyah.’ Ḥajjāj stretched himself up toward him until he could see his face. Then he said: ‘The tongue is Arabic, but the face is Nabataean.’”

By this chain, Abū ʿĪs related to me, saying: “Al-Thawrī”—meaning Sufyān—“came to Ḥajjāj and asked him about one or two reports. Ḥajjāj said: ‘We suppose Abū Thawr has bestowed a gift upon us.’”

Aḥmad ibn al-Khalīl related to us—he said: Yaḥyā ibn Ayyūb related to us: I heard Abū ʿĪs (255a) say: “One day Ḥajjāj came and sat at the edge of the circle. He was told: ‘Abū Arṭāʾah, why don’t you move up?’ He said: ‘Wherever I am, I am at the head.’”

By this chain, I heard Abū ʿĪs say: “Ḥajjāj often used to say: ‘The love of distinction has destroyed us. Although we have entered into what we have entered into, we do not lie.’”

He said: “He used to tell the hadith scholars: ‘Do not say, “Who related it to you?” Rather—’”

“‘Say, “Who mentioned it,” for fear that he might forget.’”

[Al-Ḥasan ibn Ṣāliḥ]

ʿUmar ibn Ḥafṣ ibn Ghiyāth related to us: Ṭalq related to me, saying: “I was with Zāʾidah when he mentioned al-Ḥasan ibn Ṣāliḥ and said: ‘He is eager to be crucified, if only he could find someone to crucify him.’”

He said: “Then afterward he related a report to them. He asked me: ‘Who related it to you?’ I said: ‘I would rather not tell you; I will present it to you.’” He said: “I had heard it from Ḥasan.”

Al-Ḥasan ibn al-Rabīʿ related to me, saying: “I heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn Dāwūd say:

“‘Al-Ḥasan ibn Ṣāliḥ stopped attending Friday prayer and stayed away from it. A certain man came to him”—al-Ḥasan named him, but I have forgotten his name—“and argued with him through the night until morning. Al-Ḥasan urged him to stop attending Friday prayer with them and to take up the sword against them, while the other man argued back. But al-Ḥasan would accept nothing but that.’

“I heard al-Ḥasan—or someone else among the trustworthy people of Kūfah—say: ‘Al-Ḥasan ibn Ṣāliḥ and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Dāwūd used the same mosque for prayer. Ibn Dāwūd was away when part of the mosque’s minaret collapsed. Al-Ḥasan ibn Ṣāliḥ demolished it and rebuilt it. When Ibn Dāwūd returned, he said to al-Ḥasan: “What made you demolish and rebuild the minaret when I would have sat as a builder for the mosque alongside you?” Al-Ḥasan said: “You were there to speak to me about this. Either I move away from you, or you move away from me.” Ibn Dāwūd’s house was on the qiblah side of the mosque. Ibn Dāwūd said: “I will move away from you.” Al-Ḥasan said: “No, I will move away from you.” He said: “Do you want to make me a spectacle among the people, so they will say, ‘Al-Ḥasan moved because of Ibn Dāwūd’? But I—’”

“‘will move away from you.’ So he moved to Baṣrah, settled in al-Ḥarbayn and left his house, which has remained in ruins to this day.”

I heard al-Ḥasan ibn al-Rabīʿ say: “Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Idrīs—who, in our view, was better than his father and was a truthful man—said: ‘I went in to see Wakīʿ so that he could read some of his books to me. Al-Ḥasan ibn Ṣāliḥ came up in the conversation, and I said to him: “Will you not leave off transmitting his hadith?” He said: “Why should I leave off transmitting his hadith? He is an imam in my view.” I said: “He did not invoke God’s mercy upon ʿUthmān.” Wakīʿ said to me:

“‘“Do you invoke God’s mercy upon al-Ḥajjāj? Do you invoke it upon Abū Jaʿfar?”’”

Muḥammad ibn Abī al-Sarī related to me, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzāq related to us, from Maʿmar, who said: “I asked al-Zuhrī about ʿUthmān and ʿAlī—which of them was superior. He said: ‘Bloodshed, bloodshed: ʿUthmān was the better of the two.’” He said: “He would say ‘Abū Bakr and ʿUmar,’ then fall silent.”

Ibn Abī al-Sarī said: “I asked ʿAbd al-Razzāq: ‘What is your opinion?’ He refused to tell me.”

He said: “Sufyān al-Thawrī would say ‘Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, and ʿUthmān,’ then fall silent.”

ʿAbd al-Razzāq said: “Sufyān said to us: ‘I would like to be alone with Abū ʿUrwah tonight.’”

He said: “We told Maʿmar: ‘Abū ʿAbd Allāh wants to spend a night alone with you.’ He said: ‘Yes.’

“He spent the night alone with him. In the morning I said: ‘Abū ʿUrwah, what did you think of him?’ He said: ‘He is a man, but you scarcely sound out a Kufan without finding this in him’”—as if he meant pro-ʿAlid sentiment.

ʿAbd al-Razzāq said: “Mālik ibn Anas would say ‘Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, and ʿUthmān,’ then fall silent.”

He said: “Hishām ibn Ḥassān would say ‘Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, and ʿUthmān,’ then fall silent.”

Ibn Abī al-Sarī said: “Ḥafṣ ibn Ghiyāth and a man among Ibn Idrīs’s companions used to discuss the matter with him. He said: ‘ʿUthmān was [in power] for six years.’ Then a man said to him: ‘Was ʿUthmān superior before he was killed, or after he was killed?’ He fell silent.”

Saʿīd ibn Yaḥyā related to us, saying: Ibn Idrīs related to us, saying: “I asked Shuʿbah about Manṣūr and ʿAmr ibn Murrah. He said: ‘ʿAmr was the quieter of the two men.’”

He also said: Ibn Idrīs related to us, from ʿUtbah ibn Isḥāq, who said: “Manṣūr ibn al-Mughīrah used to visit Zubayd and mention that the People of the House were being killed. He wanted to persuade him to go out with Zayd ibn ʿAlī. Zubayd said: ‘I will go out only with a prophet, and I do not think I will find one.’”

He also said: Ibn Idrīs related to us, from al-Qāsim ibn Maʿn (256a), who said: “Abū Ḥuṣayn went out, saying: ‘Praise be to God, who made me travel beneath the banners of guidance.’”

Al-Faḍl ibn Ziyād related to me, saying: “I heard Abū ʿAbd Allāh say: ‘Ṭalḥah and Zubayd used the same place for prayer. Ṭalḥah was an ʿUthmānī, while Zubayd was an ʿAlawī. Ṭalḥah was among the excellent men, and Zubayd did not refute his argument. Ṭalḥah used to forbid intoxicating drink, while Zubayd did not forbid it.’”

“Zubayd did not forbid it.”

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us: I heard Ismāʿīl al-Shaybānī say: “I stayed with the wife of Rāfiʿ ibn Khadīj. She told me that Rāfiʿ ibn Khadīj practiced withdrawal with her because she had sores, so that she would not have to bathe.”

Sufyān was asked: “Ḥammād ibn Zayd says that he did not practice withdrawal with her.” Sufyān said: “I only retained it as ‘he practiced withdrawal.’ I heard it from another source.” Then he said:

“ʿUthmān ibn Abī Sulaymān informed me that he heard Nāfiʿ ibn Jubayr relate from Ismāʿīl al-Shaybānī”—and he would say: “‘You know better.’”

Sufyān said: “Ḥammād only kept company with ʿUmar after his people had gone.”

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us: ʿAmr related to me, saying: ʿAbd Allāh, the client of Asmāʾ, informed me: “We would pray the dawn prayer with Asmāʾ bint Abī Bakr at her house in Minā on the Day of Sacrifice.”

Abū Bakr said: “I asked Ibn Abīh and he said: ‘ʿAbd Allāh ibn Kaysān.’”

He said: “Sufyān related to us: ‘He is called Ibn Sakrah’—meaning Muslim ibn Yasār.”

He also said: Sufyān related to us: ʿAmr related to us, saying: “I heard al-Qāsim ibn Abī Bazzah say:

“‘The daughter of Ṭāriq relates from ʿĀʾishah that she said, concerning children born of fornication: “Emancipate them and treat them well.”’

“Sufyān was told: ‘Ibn Jurayj relates it from a certain woman”—a woman whose name they gave to Sufyān, other than Umm Ḥakīm bint Ṭāriq—”

“(256b) Sufyān said: ‘The person who transmitted it did not retain it, having carried it on in a way other than what I related to you. It is as I told you.’

“Sufyān said: ‘Al-Zubayr ibn Mūsā was of the same generation as ʿAmr, except that he died early.’

“Sufyān was asked about the report, ‘When the prayer has been called, there is no prayer except the prescribed one,’ since they transmit it as a Prophetic report. He said: ‘Be quiet; I know that.’

“Abū Bakr said: ‘Sometimes Sufyān would say that ʿAmr considered it a Prophetic report, and sometimes he would not say that.’

Abū Bakr related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us: “I heard ʿAmr say to ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUmar and Mālik ibn Anas: ‘What became of your client, Thābit al-Aʿraj?’ He began describing him, while ʿUbayd Allāh and Mālik did not know him at the time, and Thābit was alive.”

Sufyān said: “I heard ʿAmr say: ‘Thābit al-Aʿraj related to me, saying:

“‘I married the mother of a child belonging to ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd ibn al-Khaṭṭāb. He summoned me and two of his young men. They tied me up and beat me with whips, saying: “You will divorce her, or we will do this to you.” So I divorced her. Then I asked Ibn ʿUmar and Ibn al-Zubayr, and they saw nothing wrong with it.’”

Abū Bakr said: “Sufyān thought that ʿUbayd Allāh and Mālik had heard from him what they later recanted.”

Abū Bakr related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us: ʿAmr related to us, saying: “We were in a circle, with Naṣr ibn ʿĀṣim among us. Al-Zuhrī heard him speak and said: ‘This man is surely uprooting Arabic—’”

“—uprooting it completely.”115

He also said: Sufyān related to us: ʿAmr related to us, from Ṭalq, who said: “I said to Ibn ʿUmar:

“‘What do you think about silk, when it is forbidden? Is that something you heard from the Messenger of God ﷺ?’ He said: ‘No, but I saw the people of Islam disapprove of it.’”

Al-Ḥumaydī related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us: ʿAmr related to us, saying: “I heard Abū Fākhtah, Saʿīd ibn ʿAlāqah, say: ‘I heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: “The person staying in the mosque in retreat fasts.”’”

Sufyān recounted that Hushaym would say it this way, from ʿAmr, from Abū Fākhtah: “Ibn ʿAbbās said: ‘There is no retreat without fasting.’” Sufyān said: “Hushaym was mistaken. It is as I told you.”

Abū Nuʿaym related to us, saying: Sufyān (257a) related to us, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from Abū Fākhtah, who said: “I heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: ‘The person staying in the mosque fasts.’”

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us, saying: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us: “A man said to ʿAmr ibn Dīnār: ‘Abū Muḥammad, what did Ibn ʿAbbās say about the person staying in the mosque?’ ʿAmr said: ‘Ibn ʿAbbās did not say that. He only said: “The person staying in the mosque fasts.”’ Abū Fākhtah was the client of Jaʿdah ibn Hubayrah al-Makhzūmī.”

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us: “A man who had seen ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ informed me that he was on a pulpit made of ʿajal, which he had dragged up so that he could look down over the people. He was looking at them and saying to his son, ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr: ‘ʿAbd Allāh, straighten the row, your moustache clipped close, for these people have brought down a sin that reached the sky.’ Then he said: ‘Bring me the weapon.’ A weapon like a black snake was brought before him. Then he said: ‘Take it, so-and-so; take it—’”116

“‘so-and-so. You must deal with the Antichrist, Hāshim ibn ʿUtbah.’”

Sufyān said: “A man from Kūfah informed me that ʿAmr ibn Dīnār had told him that the person who saw ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ on a pulpit made of ʿajal had tied him up.”

He also said: Sufyān related to us: My uncle related to us, saying: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Intercede with me, and you will be rewarded; and let God decree through the tongue of His Prophet what He wills. A man among you asks me for something, and I refuse him so that you may intercede with me and be rewarded.” Sufyān was asked:

“ʿAbd al-Razzāq relates from you, from ʿAmr and from Wahb ibn Munabbih, from his brother, from Muʿāwiyah.” He said: “That is only the wording, ‘Do not press in asking.’ As for this wording, ‘A man among you asks me for something, and I refuse him,’ it is only a mursal report. That is how we retained it from ʿAmr.”

He also said: Sufyān related to us: “ʿAmr related to us—I retained this from him—that ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib left a bequest to al-Ḥasan, and there were only two witnesses to it: Abū al-Hayyāj ibn Abī Sufyān ibn al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib and ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Abī Rāfiʿ; and he wrote it down.”

Sufyān said: “He was Ibn Abī al-Hayyāj; ʿAmr simply made a mistake.”

He also said: Sufyān related to us: ʿAmr related to us, saying: “Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ and Ibn ʿUmar witnessed the two arbitrators at Dūmat al-Jandal.”

He also said: Sufyān related to us, from ʿAmr, who said: “Qays ibn Saʿd was a man—”

He was large and corpulent, with a small head and a beard—and Sufyān gestured toward his neck. He said:

When he rode a donkey, his feet dragged along the ground.

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us: Sufyān related to us, saying: We went to Khālid ibn Salamah al-Makhzūmī, and he said, “Boy, bring us some of that counted variety.” He brought us large dates called al-maʿdūd.

ʿAmr said: We went to ʿAbd Rabbih at Minā, and he served us fālūdhaj.

Sufyān said: I heard from ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr that he said: “The awwāh is the vigilant one who never rises from a gathering without asking God’s forgiveness.”

He also said: Sufyān was asked about the report of ʿUthmān, “I do not care whether I wake to what I love or to what I dislike”: “Did you hear it from Abū al-Sawdāʾ?” He replied: No. Ḥafṣ ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, Ibn Sūqah’s nephew, related it to me. He said: Abū al-Sawdāʾ informed me, from Abū Mijlaz, who said: ʿUmar said. ʿUthmān said: Misʿar added to me, from ʿĀmir ibn Shaqīq, from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿAbd Allāh: “This is how we deal with a lost-and-found item.”

Sufyān said: I do not know whether ʿĀmir related it to me and I overlooked it, or whether he said nothing about it.

Sufyān said: Khālid ibn Salamah al-Makhzūmī related to me—I heard him relating it to Ibn Shubruma during the circumambulation. He said: I heard al-Shaʿbī relate, from Masrūq, who said: “Love of Abū Bakr and ʿUmar,[and] knowing their merit, is part of the Sunnah.”

Sufyān said: Abū al-Wasmī related to me that he heard a man from Banū Fazārah relate, from Abū Hurayrah, who said: “The mosque recoils from sputum just as a piece of flesh or a patch of skin recoils from fire—or in fire.”

Sufyān said: Misʿar also related it to me, from Abū al-Wasmī, who said: “The Fazārī’s name was Zibād ibn Mulqiṭ.” As for me, I only retained his name from Misʿar.

Sufyān said: Misʿar related to us, from Saʿīd. Then Saʿīd ibn Sinān related to us, saying:

Someone who had seen ʿAdī ibn Ḥātim crumble bread for the ants informed me.

Sufyān said: Saʿīd was learned in Arabic. He heard me say, “We hang from the fruits of Paradise,” and said, “Say, ‘You hang from them.’” I said, “You hang from them.”

Sufyān related, from ʿAmmār al-Duhnī: The first head carried in Islam was the head of ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥumq al-Khuzāʿī. He had been bitten and died; the messengers feared that they would be suspected, so they cut off his head and carried it away.

Sufyān said: As for the report of Muḥammad ibn Qays from Ibn al-Aṣbahānī, from ʿIkrimah: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, “Messenger of God, I passed by the southern outskirts of Badr and saw a white, smooth-skinned man, pursued by a black man carrying an iron mallet in his hand. He struck him with it, and he disappeared into the earth; then his exposed hair appeared…”

…then he struck him with it, and he disappeared into the earth; then his exposed hair appeared. The Prophet ﷺ said to the man, “And you saw him?” He replied, “Yes.” He said, “That is Abū Jahl ibn Hishām; this will be done to him until the Day of Resurrection.” Sufyān said: I asked Ibn al-Aṣbahānī about it, but he did not confirm it. Rather, he confirmed for us the report of Sahl ibn Ḥunayf, that ʿAlī performed the funeral prayer over him.

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, saying: Ibrāhīm related to us, from his father, who said: Masrūq had two shirts, one cotton shirt and one linen shirt, and he would wear one beneath the other.

Sufyān said: Misʿar added to me, from Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Masrūq: The one against his skin was the linen shirt.

Sufyān said: Raqabah related it to me, from Bayān, from al-Shaʿbī, that he did not accept the testimony of a man sitting with his knees drawn up and arms wrapped around them. Then I heard it from Bayān.

He also said: Sufyān related to us, saying: ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd related to me, from Abū Ṭuʿmah:

I saw Ibn ʿUmar call the adhān while atop a camel.

(261a) Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us, saying: Sufyān said: ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd related to me, from Abū al-Juwayriyyah al-Jarmī: I asked Ibn ʿAbbās about a lost-and-found item, and he said: “Announce it, mention it often, and make it known.”

Sufyān said: I asked Abū al-Juwayriyyah about it, and he did not deny it.

Sufyān was asked: “Ibn Mahdī related it from you, from Raqabah, from Bayān, from al-Shaʿbī.” He said: Ibn Mahdī spoke truly. Raqabah related it to me, from Bayān, from al-Shaʿbī; then I heard it from Bayān. So sometimes I was told it this way, and sometimes I was told it that way—that is, the report about the testimony of a man sitting with his knees drawn up and arms wrapped around them.

He said: Sufyān related to us—ʿAbd al-Karīm related it to me, from ʿĀṣim; then I heard it from ʿĀṣim, meaning Ibn Kulayb—ʿĀṣim related to us, from a man of Balḥārith, who said:

I heard Abū Dharr say: “A boy serves us for a year, then he is free.”

Sufyān said: I went to Yaḥyā al-Jābir—who used to set bones in Kūfah—and he said to me:

“Bring out your tablets.” I said, “I have no tablets with me.” Then he related this report to me, the report of Ibn Masʿūd, about a man with a moustache who came to him. I had not retained it, so I went to him another time. He related it to me, and I retained it. I said to Yaḥyā, “Who is Abū Mājid?” He replied, “A newcomer who came among us.”

ʿAlī said: Yaḥyā al-Jābir is reliable in what he relates from anyone other than Abū Mājid, because Abū Mājid is unknown and unrecognized. As for his reports from others, there is no problem with them.

Sufyān said: Kulayb ibn Wāʾil related to us, saying: Sufyān said: When I came to him, he said to me, “Bring out your tablets.” I said, “I have no tablets with me.”

Abū Bakr related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, saying: Khālid ibn Abī Khuldah al-Ḥanafī related to us, saying: Dharr and I disagreed over which was better: performing the ḥajj on foot or riding in a litter. I asked Ibrāhīm, and he said: “On foot.”

Sufyān said: His report was from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd; then I asked about it.

Al-Ḥumaydī related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, saying: Misʿar related to us, saying: Sunbulah, the client of the Waḥīdiyyah women, informed me. (261b) Sufyān said: I had seen Sunbulah. She used to come to us from our client, the Waḥīdiyyah woman whom ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib had married. She said:

Ibn Jurmūz, the killer of al-Zubayr, sought permission to enter upon ʿAlī ﵁. ʿAlī said:

“Admit him, and give him the glad tidings of the Fire.”

Abū Nuʿaym related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Aʿlā al-ʿAnazī related to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī al-Hudhayl, Abū al-Mughīrah, who said: I intended to set out, and the people of Kūfah learned of it. They gathered questions and then brought them to me on a sheet. When I arrived before Ibn ʿAbbās, he came out and sat for the people. They kept asking him until not a single thing remained on my sheet that they had not asked him about.

Abū Nuʿaym said: I asked, “Who related it to you?” He replied, “ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī al-Hudhayl; his teknonym is Abū al-Mughīrah.”

“Abū Nuʿaym related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, who said: I heard ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā say: ‘I encountered, in this mosque, one hundred and twenty men from among the Anṣār, Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ. Whenever one of them related a report, he wished his brother had spared him from relating it; and whenever he was asked for a legal opinion, he wished his brother had spared him from giving it.’”

“Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, saying: ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib related to us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā, who said: ‘I encountered one hundred and twenty men from among the Anṣār, Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ. One of them would be asked a question and pass it on to another, and that one to another, until it returned to the first.’”

“Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, saying: ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib related to us, saying: ‘I encountered people such that when one of them was asked about something and began to speak, he would tremble.’”

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us, saying: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā, who said: I encountered one hundred and twenty men from among the Anṣār—

…from among the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ—all of them from among the Anṣār. When one of them was asked about something, he wished that his companion would spare him from answering.

Salamah related to us, saying: Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal related to us, saying: Yaḥyā ibn Abī Bukayr related to us, from Nuʿaym ibn Maysarah—who used to live in Rayy—who said: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said:

“If I were given the choice of a servant to meet God, mighty and majestic, in his very guise, I would choose Zubayd al-Yāmī.”

He also said: Aḥmad related to us, saying: (262a) Yaḥyā ibn [Abī] Bukayr related to us, saying: I heard Shuʿbah say: “I was at Ṭalḥah’s funeral.” He said: Abū Miʿshar—who praised him—said: “He left no one like himself behind.”

He also said: Aḥmad related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī related to us, saying: Sufyān related the report of ʿAbd al-Aʿlā, saying: “We used to think it came from a book.” Aḥmad said:

I mean the report of Ibn al-Ḥanafiyyah from ʿAlī.

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā related to us, from Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid, from Abū Isḥāq, who said: Abū al-Safar and I went in to see Abū Jaʿfar, and he said: “I see you are both old men, but there is no problem with you.” I said: What do you say about a man who gives his wife the choice, and she chooses her husband?

He said: “That has no effect. If she chooses herself, it is one [divorce], and her husband has the greater right to her.”

We said: “People relate something different from this on the authority of ʿAlī.” He said: “That is something they find in written sheets.”

Mujāhid ibn Mūsā related to me, saying: Qirād Abū Nūḥ related to us, saying: Shuʿbah related to us, saying:

I saw no elder in Kūfah better than Zubayd, and whenever I saw ʿAmr ibn Murrah praying, I would think, “He will not finish until his supplication is answered.”

Salamah related to us, saying: Aḥmad related to us, saying: Yaḥyā ibn Abī Bukayr related to us, from Shuʿbah, who said: Hishām—that is, Ibn ʿUrwah—did not hear his father’s report about touching the penis.

Yaḥyā said: I asked Hishām, and he said: “My father informed me.”

Through the same chain, he said: Yaḥyā related to us, from Ibn Jubayr, who said: I asked ʿAṭāʾ, and Yaʿqūb ibn ʿAṭāʾ related to me, from him, from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning īlāʾ—meaning that she is irrevocably separated—and [he said] not [so] if he swore for less than four months.

Salamah related to us, saying: Aḥmad related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzāq related to us, saying: Rabāḥ asked Ibn Jurayj about something concerning Qurʾānic commentary. He said, “Maʿmar informed me of such-and-such.” He replied: “Maʿmar has drunk deeply of knowledge that has benefited him.”

ʿAbd al-Razzāq said: Maʿmar used to [perform ablution] because of what fire had cooked. Ibn Jurayj said to him: “You are a shooting star, Abū ʿUrwah.”

Aḥmad said: He said: ʿAbd al-Razzāq related to us, saying: Maʿmar ibn Abī ʿAmr—that is, Ibn Rāshid—informed me, saying: It used to be said: “A man may learn knowledge for other than God, mighty and majestic, but God, mighty and majestic, refuses to let him be so, until it is for God, mighty and majestic.”

Salamah related to me, saying: Aḥmad related to us, saying: (262b) ʿAbd al-Razzāq related to us, saying: Mālik said: “Maʿmar would have been an excellent man, were it not for his narrating Qurʾānic commentary from Qatādah.”

Abū Saʿīd al-Ashajj related to me, saying: Ashʿath ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zubayd related to me, from his father, who said: Zubayd divided the night into three parts between me and my brother. He would get up, and if he found me asleep, he would strike me with his foot. When he saw me being sluggish, he would say, “My son, I will get up in your place.” Then he would stand and pray until morning. When he saw my brother being sluggish, he would say to him, “I will get up in your place,” and then stand and pray until morning.

ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn ʿImrān, Abū al-Ṭāhir and Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: I heard Mālik relate, from Ibn Saʿīd, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Qāsim, that Ibn al-Ḍaḥḥāk, the governor of Medina, sent them at the mosque a document to attest to its contents: a judgment he had issued. Al-Qāsim went over to him, and I entered the screened area with him…

…He prayed the sunset prayer with him. Then he said to him: “Did you write this document that you sent to us?” He said to al-Qāsim: “Did you not see how well I wrote it?” The other said: “So, was it you who wrote this?” He said:

He turned to ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and said: “Did you not see how well I wrote it?” He said: “Yes.” He said:

“I wrote it, then. So attest to its contents.”

ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, Abū al-Ṭāhir, and Yūnus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb related to us, saying:

ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar ibn Ḥafṣ related to me, from Saʿīd ibn Zayd, from Ḥafṣ ibn ʿĀṣim ibn ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb: Whenever he intended to travel, he would write his testament, seal it, then give it to Sālim ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar and say: “Attest to its contents if something should happen to me.” When he returned, he would take it back from him.

He said: Ibn Wahb said: I heard Mālik ibn Anas say, concerning a man who wrote his testament, sealed it, then gave it to a group of people and had them attest that its contents were his, and instructed them not to break his seal until he died: “That is valid, if he had them attest that its contents were his.”

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us, saying: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, from Ayyūb: Abū Qilābah disliked testifying to the contents of a sealed document. He said: “Perhaps it contains an injustice.”

Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr related to us, saying: (263a) Khālid related to us, from Yūnus, from al-Ḥasan, that he disliked a man testifying to a testament written on a sealed document until he knows what is in it.

ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan related to us. He said: Ibn al-Mubārak related to us, from Hishām, from al-Ḥasan, who said: “Do not testify concerning a document until you know what is in it. If it is just, testify; if it is unjust, do not testify.”

Saʿīd related to us. He said: Jarīr related to us, from Mughīra, from Ḥammād, from Ibrāhīm, concerning a man who seals his testament and says, “Bear witness to what is in it.” He said:

“It is not valid until he reads it, or it is read to him and he acknowledges what is in it.”

ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn ʿImrān related to me. He said: Muḥammad ibn Yūsuf related to us, from a man who wrote his testament, sealed it, and said, “Bear witness to what is in it.” Ibn Abī Laylā would invalidate it.

Sufyān said: “The judges do not validate it.”

A CHAPTER

“Abū Yūsuf related to us. He said: Ibrāhīm ibn al-Mundhir related to us. He said: Yaḥyā ibn al-Zubayr related to us, from ʿAbbād ibn Ḥamza ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr, who said: ‘I asked Hishām ibn ʿUrwa for his father’s traditions. He brought them out to me and said: “Here are my father’s traditions. I have verified them and know what is in them, so take them [from me], and do not say what those people say until—’”

“—I have reviewed them.’”

“Abū Saʿīd ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm related to us. He said: Muḥammad ibn Shuʿayb related to us. He said: ʿUtba—meaning Ibn Abī Ḥakīm al-Hamdānī—told me: Hubayra ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān told me: ‘When people pressed Anas ibn Mālik with many questions, he would bring out notebooks for them and say: “I wrote these down, then read them to the Messenger of God ﷺ.”’”

“Ibrāhīm ibn al-Mundhir related to us. He said: [Abū] Ḍamra related to us, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUmar ibn Ḥafṣ, who said: ‘I can attest that Ibn Shihāb used to be brought a book from among his books. He would leaf through it and look it over, then say: “This is my tradition; I recognize it. Take it from me.”’”

“ ʿAbd Allāh ibn Wahb and Muṭarrif related to us. They said: Mālik ibn Anas related to us: ‘Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd said to me, “Write down for me the traditions on judicial rulings from Ibn Shihāb’s traditions.” So I wrote them for him. I can almost see him now, with them on a yellow sheet.’ Mālik was asked, ‘Abū ʿAbd Allāh, did he review them with you?’ He said: ‘He is more knowledgeable than to need that.’” (263b)

Muḥammad ibn Abī Zukayr related to me. He said: Ibn Wahb related to me. He said: Mālik related to me: “Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd said to me, ‘Select one hundred traditions for me from Ibn Shihāb’s traditions.’ He gave me an old piece of parchment that had turned yellow. I think he had had it since he was young. I wrote those traditions for him until I had filled it, and I checked them carefully for him.”

Mālik said: “Few of the men from whom I used to learn died before they came to me to ask me for a legal opinion.”

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm related to us. He said: Shuʿayb ibn Isḥāq related to us, from Hishām ibn ʿUrwa, who said: “Ibn Jurayj came with a written document and said to me, ‘Abū al-Mundhir, are these traditions that I may transmit from you?’ I said, ‘Yes.’ He left and did not ask me about anything else.”

“Zayd ibn Bishr related to us. He said: Ibn Wahb informed me: al-Layth informed me: ‘I took books from Khālid ibn Yazīd without reviewing them with him, and I transmit them from him.’

Ibn Wahb said: ‘Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd used to write to al-Layth ibn Saʿd, saying, “Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd related to me.” Hishām ibn ʿUrwa used to write to him, saying—’”

“‘Hishām related to me.’”

“Ibrāhīm ibn al-Mundhir related to us. He said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith al-Makhzūmī related to us: ‘Ibn Jurayj wrote to [Ibn] Abī Sabra, and he wrote back to him with some of his traditions and sealed them.’”

“Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us. He said: Someone who had seen Ibn Jurayj bring a book to Abān ibn Abī ʿAyyāsh told me: ‘He said, “These are your traditions; authorize them for me.” He said, “Yes.”

“He took the book and left.’”

ʿAlī ibn ʿUthmān ibn Nufayl related to me. He said: Abū Mishar related to us. He said: Saʿīd related to us: “I saw Yazīd ibn Yazīd ibn Jābir reviewing material with al-Zuhrī.”

“Muḥammad ibn Wahb al-Ḥarrānī related to me. He said: Sukayn ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz al-ʿAbdī related to us. He said: Shuʿba related to us: ‘Manṣūr wrote a tradition to me. I met him—’”

I said: “May I transmit it from you?” He said: “When I wrote to you, had I not thereby related it to you?”

[He] said: “I asked Ayyūb al-Sakhtiyānī about that, and he said the same.”

Muḥammad ibn al-Muṣaffā related to us (264a). He said: Baqiyya related to us, from Shuʿba, from Ayyūb and others, who said: “When a scholar writes to you, he has related [the material] to you.”

Yaḥyā ibn Yaḥyā related to us. Abū Miʿshar al-ʿAṭṭār related to us, from ʿImrān ibn Ḥudayr. Abū Mujliz informed me: “Bashīr ibn Nuhayk used to write down Abū Hurayra’s traditions from what he heard from him. When Bashīr was about to depart from him, he brought him what he had written from him and read it back to him. He said, ‘Yes.’”

“Ibrāhīm ibn al-Mundhir related to us. He said: Dāwūd ibn ʿAṭāʾ, the client of al-Zubayr, related to us. He said: Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad related to us, from his father, who said: ‘Reviewing a book and [reviewing] a tradition are the same.’”

“Ibrāhīm related to us. He said: Marwān ibn Muʿāwiya related to us, from ʿĀṣim al-Aḥwal, who said: ‘We reviewed legal traditions with al-Shaʿbī, and he approved them.’”

Sulaymān ibn Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā ibn ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr related to us. He said: Hishām ibn ʿUrwa said: “My father used to review traditions with us just as he reviewed a book.”

“Abū al-Walīd Hishām ibn ʿAbd al-Malik related to us. He said: Shuʿba related to us: ‘I read to Manṣūr and asked him, “May I say, ‘Manṣūr related to me’?” He said, “Yes.”’”

“Zayd ibn Bishr related to us. He said: Ibn Wahb informed me: Mālik informed me: ‘I saw Ibn Shihāb having knowledge read to him.’”

“ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā related to me: Sufyān al-Thawrī said: ‘Your reading to a scholar and his reading to you are the same.’ ʿUbayd Allāh said: ‘I mentioned that to Sharīk—or I asked Sharīk about it—and he said, “Are they anything but the same?”’”

“ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Shaqīq related to us. He said: ʿAbd Allāh related to us: Maʿmar said: ‘I read the material to al-Zuhrī. When I had finished, I said, “May I transmit this from you?” He said, “Who else related it to you besides me?”’”

Salama related to me. He said: Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal related to us: ʿAbd al-Razzāq related to us: Maʿmar said: “I saw Ayyūb having material read to him, and he would approve it. Manṣūr ibn al-Muʿtamir saw no harm in review by reading aloud.”

Maʿmar also informed us: “I heard Ibrāhīm ibn al-Walīd—a man from Banū Umayya—ask al-Zuhrī, and he presented him with a book of material. He said, ‘May I transmit this from you, Abū Bakr?’ He said, ‘Yes. Who else related it to you?’” (264b)

“Ibn Bukayr related to us: ‘When we reviewed the Muwaṭṭaʾ with Mālik, a man from the people of the Maghrib said to him, “Abū ʿAbd Allāh, may I transmit this from you?” He said, “Yes.” He asked, “And may I say, ‘Mālik related to me’?” He said, “Yes. Did you not see that I devoted myself to you, listened to your presentation, and corrected its omissions and mistakes? Who else related it to you? Yes, transmit it from me, and say, ‘Mālik related to me.’”’”

Salama related to me. He said: Aḥmad related to us: Yaḥyā related to us, from Shuʿba, who said: “I asked Manṣūr and Ayyūb about reading aloud. They said, ‘Good’”—meaning, reading the traditions.

Aḥmad said: Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Wāsiṭī related to us. He said: ʿAwf informed us:

“A man asked al-Ḥasan, saying, ‘Abū Saʿīd, my home is far away, and the journey is difficult for me. I have traditions with me. If they have not been reviewed by reading them aloud, they have at least been read to you.’

“He said, ‘I do not mind whether they were read to me, so long as I have told you that he related them to me, or I have related them to you.’ The man said, ‘Abū Saʿīd, may I say, “Al-Ḥasan related to me”?’ He said, ‘Yes. Say, “Al-Ḥasan related to me.”’”

Abū Bakr ibn ʿAbd al-Malik related to us. He said: ʿAbd al-Razzāq related to us: Maʿmar informed us, from Manṣūr, Ayyūb, and al-Zuhrī, that they considered review by presentation acceptable.

ʿAlī ibn ʿUthmān ibn Nufayl related to me. He said: Abū Mishar related to us, from Saʿīd ibn— ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, who said: “I saw ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Abī al-Sāʾib reviewing material with Makhūl.”

Zayd ibn Bishr related to me. He said: Ibn Wahb informed me: Mālik ibn Anas informed me: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Bakr related to me: “My father said: ‘My son, you are young, and you sit with people. Listen to what people ask about, and do not ask questions yourself. If you miss something at the beginning of a tradition, you can infer its beginning from its end.’”

Ibn Numayr related to me: Muḥammad ibn Fuḍayl said: “We used to go to al-Aʿmash, and he would relate traditions to us. When al-Aʿmash got up, we would gather around so-and-so”—he said, “a blind man; I think Ibn Numayr named him”—“and he would dictate to us what al-Aʿmash had related to us.

“I heard Bishr ibn al-Azhar al-Nīsābūrī say: ‘Whenever Jarīr ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd mentioned hearing traditions from al-Aʿmash, he would say, “Al-Aʿmash’s brocade—if only it weren’t patched!” When we left al-Aʿmash, we would patch it together, one from another, to correct it.’”

“I heard Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb (265a) say: ‘Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd came to us and related traditions to them. Our companions did not write anything down. Later, they wrote them down.

“He said: Ḥammād said: ‘Jarīr ibn Ḥāzim and others said to me, “We are eager to write down Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd’s traditions. If only you would join us.”’ Ḥammād said: ‘I joined them, and we reviewed his traditions together—’”

“—afterward, and then they wrote them down.’”

Muḥammad ibn al-Minhāl related to me. He said: Yazīd ibn Zurayʿ Abū Muʿāwiya al-ʿĀʾishī related to us: “Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Anṣārī did not dictate. When he came to us in Baṣra, we went to him. He did not dictate to us; he would relate traditions. When we left him, we would sit at the door of the house and review among ourselves, one reporting from another, and another from another. I said, ‘I find myself taking my religion from you,’ so I left them and took nothing from them. All our companions transmitted them.”

Yazīd said: “Ḥammād ibn Zayd said to me: ‘I heard ʿAmr ibn Dīnār’s tradition through our back-and-forth review.’”

Salama related to me. He said: Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal related to us: Shuʿayb ibn Ḥarb related to us: Mālik said: “We used to sit with al-Zuhrī and Muḥammad ibn al-Munkadir. Al-Zuhrī would say, ‘Ibn ʿUmar said such-and-such.’ Later, we would sit with him and ask, ‘Who told you what you related from Ibn ʿUmar?’ He would say, ‘His son Sālim.’”

A CHAPTER

Abū Yūsuf related to us. He said: Salama related to me, from Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, who said: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd related to us: “I asked Ismāʿīl about a tradition of Ibn Abī ʿArūba concerning a person who does not become sexually impure. He did not recognize it. Yaḥyā said: ‘We intended it to be [the report of] Ibn Abī Khālid, from his father, but he declined.’”117 He said: “He means in his report from Muḥammad ibn Saʿīd, from the Prophet ﷺ: ‘The month is twenty-nine [days].’” Yaḥyā said: Shuʿba said: “Al-Ḥakam did not hear the tradition of Miqsim about cupping and fasting from Miqsim.”

[Al-Ḥakam did not hear] the report about cupping and fasting from Miqsim.

Yaḥyā said: “Shuʿba related to us, from al-Ḥakam, who said: ‘Yaḥyā ibn al-Jazzār was extreme’”—meaning, in his Shiʿite views.

Yaḥyā said: “Shuʿba omitted al-Ḥakam’s report, ‘When a person in a state of major ritual impurity wishes to eat, he performs ablution’; he omitted the words ‘wishes to eat.’”

Yaḥyā said: “Sufyān related to me in Kūfa, during al-Aʿmash’s lifetime, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿUmar, concerning ostrich eggs.”

Anas said (265b): “This is from his old material”—he considered it weak.

Ibn Numayr related to us. He said: I heard Abū Bakr say: “I said to al-Aʿmash:

“‘Did you hear Ibrāhīm say that ʿUmar ruled concerning ostrich eggs: “tumnihi”?’ He said, ‘No.’ I asked, ‘From whom did you hear it?’ He said, ‘I do not know.’”

Salama related to me, from Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, who said: Ḥajjāj related to us: “I heard Abū Isrāʾīl say: ‘The first day I knew al-Ḥakam was the day al-Shaʿbī died.’ He said: ‘A man came asking about a question, and they said, “Go to al-Ḥakam ibn ʿUtayba.”’”

And he said: Aḥmad related to us; Ḥajjāj related to us; Shuʿbah said: “Rafīʿ”—meaning Abū al-ʿĀliyah—“did meet ʿAlī, but he heard nothing from him.”

Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr related to me: Hushaym related to us, saying: Mughīrah informed us, from Ibrāhīm, who said: Among the things that ʿUrwah al-Bāriqī brought to Shurayḥ from ʿUmar were these: the fingers are equal, the little finger and the thumb; the injuries inflicted on men and women are equal in the cases of a tooth and a wound exposing bone; in other cases, the amount is half; for an animal’s eye, one quarter of its price is due; and a man’s most valid declaration is accepted concerning his child at the time of his death, if he acknowledges the child. Mughīrah said: “I had forgotten the fifth matter until he reminded me in his presence: if a man divorces his wife three times, she inherits from him as long as she is in her waiting period.”

Abū Nuʿaym and Qabīṣah related to us. They said: Sufyān related to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from ʿAṭāʾ, from the Prophet ﷺ—that he disliked taking more than he had given her.

Salamah related to me from Aḥmad, who said: Wakīʿ said: “I asked Ibn Jurayj about it, but he did not recognize it and denied it.”

Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from ʿAṭāʾ, who traced it back to the Prophet ﷺ—who said: “He must not take from a woman who has obtained a divorce in return for compensation more than he gave her…”

…he gave her. ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān related to us, saying: ʿAbd Allāh related to us; Ibn Jurayj informed us, from ʿAṭāʾ, who said: A woman came to the Prophet ﷺ—and said: “Messenger of God, I detest my husband and wish to part from him.” He said: “Will you return to him the garden he gave you as your bridal gift?”—he had given her a garden—She said: “Yes, and something more.” The Prophet ﷺ—said: “As for anything more from your property, no; but the garden.” She said: “Yes.” The Prophet ﷺ—then ruled accordingly against the man. When he was informed of the Messenger of God’s ruling, he said: “I accept the Messenger of God’s ruling.”

Bakr ibn Khalaf related to me, saying: Abū ʿĀṣim informed us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said:

“I said to ʿAṭāʾ: ‘I bought a garment from a man for a dinar less one dirham. I said, “Give me a dirham, and I will owe you a dinar.”’ He said: ‘That is not permissible.’”

Bakr said: Abū ʿĀṣim related to us, saying: “As for Sufyān, he related to us from Ibn Jurayj, from ʿAṭāʾ, that he disliked buying a garment for a dinar less one dirham.”

Mahdī ibn Mahdī related to me, saying: Hishām ibn Yūsuf related to us, from…

…from Ibn Jurayj, who said: ʿAṭāʾ was asked: “A man bought a garment for a dinar less one dirham, then said, ‘I will give you a dirham so that I will owe you a dinar, which I will take from you later.’” He said: “No.”

Abū Nuʿaym related to us, saying: Hishām ibn Yūsuf related to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said:

“I said to ʿAṭāʾ: ‘I bought from one of the rulers the alms due from a clan of the Arabs, after the alms collector had collected that clan’s due and taken possession of it. A man came to me, although I had not yet taken possession of it myself, and said, “Transfer it to me at its price, and do not charge me anything extra.”’ He said: ‘No; not until you take possession of it. That is a sale.’ He said: ‘Then there can be no sale until you take possession.’ I said: ‘I made no profit on it.’ He said: ‘You may not transfer it to him until you take possession of it, for that is a sale.’ I said to him: ‘May I make him a partner in one third of it before I take possession?’ He said: ‘Yes, there is no harm in that.’ I said: ‘Why are the two cases different?’ He said: ‘Because if he transfers it to him at its price, he has sold it, and it has passed out of his hands. But if he brings him in as a partner, he is then only a partner whom he has made a partner and brought in with him; he has not given it to him. He has called it a partnership, and so it is.’”

Volume Three

[Volume Three]

[Continuation of the Biographical Entries]

Chapter

Abū Yūsuf related to us, saying: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān related to us; ʿAbd Allāh informed us; Yūnus informed us, from al-Zuhrī, from Abū Salamah, from ʿĀʾishah: The Messenger of God ﷺ—said: “There is no vow in disobedience to God, Mighty and Majestic, and its expiation is the expiation for an oath.”

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṣāliḥ and Ibn Bukayr related to us. They said: al-Layth related to us; Yūnus related to me, from Ibn Shihāb, from Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, that ʿĀʾishah said: The Messenger of God ﷺ—said: “There is no vow in disobedience to God, Mighty and Majestic, and its expiation is the expiation for an oath.”

Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us at the end of Yūnus’s book, saying: al-Layth ibn Saʿd related to me; Yūnus related to me, from Ibn Shihāb, from Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, who was told by ʿĀʾishah: The Messenger of God ﷺ—said: “There is no vow in disobedience to God, Mighty and Majestic, and its expiation is the expiation for an oath.”

ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān related to us from Yūnus’s book in the original: ʿAbd Allāh related to us, saying: Yūnus informed us, from al-Zuhrī. I was told, from Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿĀʾishah, who said: “There is no vow in disobedience to God, Mighty and Majestic, and its expiation is the expiation for an oath.”

Abū Muḥammad al-Umawī related to me, from ʿAnbasah ibn Khālid, who said: Yūnus related to us, from Ibn Shihāb, who said: Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān informed me that ʿĀʾishah, the Prophet’s wife, said: “There is no vow in disobedience, and its expiation is the expiation for an oath.”

Abū Yūsuf said: Ibn Abī Uways gave me a book, from which I copied:

“My brother related to me, from Sulaymān ibn Bilāl, from Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿAtīq and Mūsā ibn ʿUqbah, from Sulaymān ibn Arqam, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr—who lived in al-Yamāmah—who told him that he had heard Abū Salamah relate from ʿĀʾishah bt. Abī Bakr that she said: The Messenger of God ﷺ—said: ‘There is no vow in disobedience to God, Mighty and Majestic, and its expiation is the expiation for an oath.’”

I was not able to hear it directly from Ibn Abī Uways, so he said to me: “This is what I heard from my brother Abū Bakr; transmit it on my authority.”

I mentioned this report to Aḥmad ibn Ṣāliḥ and said to him: “I have been told that Ibn Sulaymān ibn Bilāl transmitted it from Abū Bakr ibn Abī Uways, from Sulaymān, from Ibn Abī ʿAtīq and Mūsā ibn ʿUqbah, from al-Zuhrī, from Sulaymān ibn Arqam.” Aḥmad said: “It was only suggested to him that it ought to be from al-Zuhrī, so he made it from al-Zuhrī. Otherwise, al-Zuhrī is not in the original copy of Abū Bakr’s book. We think that Abū Bakr omitted al-Zuhrī.”

Muslim ibn Ibrāhīm related to me, saying: Abān related to us; Yaḥyā related to us, from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad, from ʿĀʾishah: The Messenger of God ﷺ—used to say: “Whoever vows to disobey God, Mighty and Majestic, must not disobey Him.”

Al-Rabīʿ ibn Rūḥ related to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Ḥarb related to us, saying:

… related to us, from al-Zuhrī, that it had reached him that al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad used to relate from ʿĀʾishah that she said: The Messenger of God ﷺ—said: “There is no vow in disobedience to God, Mighty and Majestic.”

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Maslamah and Ibn Bukayr related to us, from Mālik, from Ṭalḥah ibn ʿAbd al-Malik al-Aylī, from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad, from ʿĀʾishah, the Prophet’s wife, who said: “Whoever vows to obey God, Mighty and Majestic, let him obey Him; and whoever vows to disobey God, Mighty and Majestic, must not disobey Him.”

Abū Saʿīd ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm related to me: ʿUmar related to us, from al-Awzāʿī, who said: Muḥammad ibn Abān related to us; al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Bakr al-Ṣiddīq related to me, saying: Umm al-Muʾminīn ʿĀʾishah related to me that the Messenger of God ﷺ—said: “Whoever vows to disobey God, Mighty and Majestic, must not disobey Him.”

Chapter

Abū Yūsuf related to us, saying: Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us; Sufyān related to us; Ibn ʿAjlān related to us, from a man of the family of Abū Rabīʿah, from al-Aʿraj, from Abū Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ—said: “The strong believer is better and more beloved to God, Mighty and Majestic, than the weak believer, though there is good in each. Be keen for what benefits you, and do not give up. If something overcomes you, then God, Mighty and Majestic, has decreed it, and whatever He wills, He does. Beware of saying ‘if only,’ for ‘if only’ opens the work of Satan.”

Abū al-Nuʿmān related to us, saying: ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mubārak related to us; Muḥammad ibn ʿAjlān related to me, from Rabīʿah, from al-Aʿraj, from Abū Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ. He said—and I heard it from Rabīʿah, but did not retain it accurately—: “The strong believer is better, more excellent, and more beloved to God, Mighty and Majestic, than the weak believer, though each is good. Be keen for what benefits you, and do not give up. If something overcomes you, say: ‘God, Mighty and Majestic, has decreed it, and whatever He wills, He does.’ Beware of saying ‘if only,’ for ‘if only’ opens the work of Satan.”

ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan related to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubārak related to us; Muḥammad ibn ʿAjlān informed us, from Rabīʿah, from al-Aʿraj, from Abū Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ—said: “The strong believer is better and more beloved to God, Mighty and Majestic, than the weak believer, though each is good. Be keen for what benefits you, and do not give up. If something overcomes you, say: ‘God, Mighty and Majestic, has decreed it, and whatever He wills, He does.’ Beware of saying ‘if only,’ for ‘if only’ opens the work of Satan.”

Then he said: “I heard it from Rabīʿah and retained it from Muḥammad.”

Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Numayr related to me, saying: Ibn Idrīs related to us and said:

Rabīʿah ibn ʿUthmān al-Taymī informed us, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā ibn Ḥibbān, from al-Aʿraj, from Abū Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ—said: “The strong believer is better and more beloved to God, Mighty and Majestic, than the weak believer, though there is good in each. Be keen for what benefits you, seek the help of God, Mighty and Majestic, and do not give up. If something befalls you, do not say, ‘If only I had done such-and-such’; rather, say, ‘God, Mighty and Majestic, has decreed it, and whatever He wills, He does.’ Beware of saying ‘if only,’ for ‘if only’ opens the work of Satan.”

Chapter

Abū Yūsuf related to us, saying: Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us; Ḥammād related to us, from Ayyūb, from Nāfiʿ, that Ibn ʿUmar used to make the enslaved women observe a waiting period of one menstrual cycle.

Ḥammād said: Before that, Ayyūb had said, from Nāfiʿ: “Ibn ʿUmar used to say: ‘The waiting period of an umm walad is one menstrual cycle.’” Ḥammād said: “I asked ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sarrāj about it, and they both related to me from Nāfiʿ that Ibn ʿUmar used to say: ‘The waiting period of an umm walad is one menstrual cycle.’”

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us, saying: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, from Ayyūb, from Sulaymān ibn Yaʿqūb al-Riyāḥī, who said: I met Sulaymān, and he related to me from his father, who said:

“A man appointed me as his executor and bequeathed his sacrificial animal to me. I went to Ibn ʿAbbās and said to him: ‘A man appointed me as his executor and bequeathed his sacrificial animal to me. Will a cow suffice for me?’ He said: ‘Yes.’ Then he said: ‘Where is your companion from?’ I said: ‘From Banū Riyāḥ.’ He said: ‘Since when have Banū Riyāḥ preferred cattle over camels? They are your people, and cattle belong only to al-Azd and ʿAbd al-Qays.’”

Ḥammād said: “Ayyūb and our companions were pleased with this report.”

“ʿAlī ibn al-Madīnī was asked about the report of al-Anṣārī, from Ḥabīb ibn al-Shahīd, from Maymūn ibn Mihrān, from Ibn ʿAbbās: ‘The Prophet ﷺ—was cupped while fasting.’ He said: ‘There is nothing to that report. He meant the report of Ḥabīb, from Maymūn…’”

“…from Yazīd ibn al-Aṣamm: ‘The Prophet ﷺ—married Maymūnah while in a state of consecration.’”

Chapter

“Al-ʿAbbās related to us, saying: ʿAlī related to us; Yaḥyā said to me: ‘Of my teachers from whom I learned, none remain except Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah.’ I said: ‘Abū Saʿīd, Sufyān is an authority in ḥadīth.’ He said: ‘Sufyān has been the people’s authority for forty years.’

ʿAlī said: I heard Bishr ibn al-Mufaḍḍal say—and he gestured toward the ground with his hand—: ‘There is no one left on the face of the earth who resembles Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah.’

ʿAlī said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī said: ‘I would hear a report from Ibn ʿUyaynah, then get up and hear Shuʿbah relate it, but I would not write it down.’”

A man related to us, saying: Shuʿbah related to us, from Ghaylān ibn Jāmiʿ, from Abū Ḥuṣayn, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, concerning the singing women. I was told that Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah had heard it from Abū Ḥuṣayn. I went to Mecca and said: “Abū Muḥammad, there is something Shuʿbah related to us from Ghaylān, from Abū Ḥuṣayn.” I told him about it, and he said: “Shall I relate it to you?” I left him alone that day, out of humility.

Al-ʿAbbās related to me, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzāq related to us; the trustworthy authority said, from Manṣūr, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqamah, from ʿAbd Allāh: “This is an Arab chain of transmission.”

Al-ʿAbbās said: I heard ʿAlī say: Yaḥyā said: “I said to Ḥafṣ ibn Ghiyāth: ‘Is this what you say about Ibrāhīm’s lineage?’ He denied it and said: ‘He is one of us.’ I heard Ibn Dāwūd deny it vehemently as well.”

Al-ʿAbbās said: I heard Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd say: “One day I went to Ibn Dāwūd, and they were discussing Sufyān al-Thawrī. Ibn Dāwūd then said: ‘He is one of us.’”

He said: “Maḥlūt”—and he was present for that. He said: “I said to him: ‘We have knowledge of this.’ He said: ‘Be quiet.’ I said: ‘Abū Saʿīd said: I asked Sufyān, “What people are you from?” He replied: “People disagree about us: some say we are from Banū Tamīm, and some say we are the brothers of Tamīm.”’”

Al-ʿAbbās related to me, saying: Shihāb related to us, from Muḥammad ibn Bishr, from ʿAlī ibn Ṣāliḥ, who said: “I went to Abū Sinān al-Shaybānī, and he said to me: ‘Where have you come from?’ I said: ‘From Banū Thawr.’ He said: ‘From Banū Thawr Aṭḥal or Thawr of Hamdān?’ I said: ‘Rather, Thawr…’”

Hamdān. He said: “Your road is indeed long, so shorten your journey by remembering God, Mighty and Majestic.”

Al-ʿAbbās related to me: Muḥammad ibn Maḥbūb related to me: I heard Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd say: “I asked Sufyān about the Arabs and the clients.” He replied: “Have I ever discussed any such thing with you?”

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm related to me: Yaḥyā ibn Ḥassān related to us, from Muʿāwiya ibn Sallām, who said: “Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr took from me the books of my brother, Zayd ibn Sallām.”

Salama related to me from Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, who said: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad ibn Ḥarb ibn Shaddād related to us: “Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr said to me: ‘Everything transmitted from Abū Sallām is from a book.’”

Abū Sallām’s name was Mamṭūr al-Ḥabashī; it is said that he was from Yemen.

Aḥmad said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī related to us, from Ḥammād ibn Zayd, who said:

Ayyūb said to Maṭar: “From whom did Abū al-Khaṭṭāb transmit from ʿAlī?” He replied: “From Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab.” Ayyūb said: “Bring it.” But he brought only one or two chapters. Ayyūb said:

“From Julās. I saw Julās, and I saw that he had scrolls with him.”

Salama related to us from Aḥmad, who said: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd (269a) said: Shuʿba said: “Abū Bishr did not hear from Ḥabīb ibn Sālim.” Shuʿba used to regard the reports of Abū Bishr from Mujāhid as weak.

Yaḥyā said: Muṭarrif was older than al-Ḥasan.

Aḥmad said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī related to us: Sufyān said: “Al-Aʿmash did not hear Ibrāhīm’s report about laughter.”

He said: Sufyān said: “I asked al-Aʿmash: ‘Is the report about the pellet not one of your reports?’”

He replied: “What can I do? They would not leave me alone. They said that Shuʿba had related it from you.”

Yaḥyā said: “We heard that the reports of Samura narrated by al-Ḥasan were from a book. They also thought that Mujāhid was transmitting from Jābir’s scroll.”

Yaḥyā said: “I heard al-Taymī say: ‘So-and-so and so-and-so took it. They told me, “Take it,” but I said, “No.”’”

Yaḥyā said: “I asked Mālik: ‘What do you think of Shuʿba’—meaning the client of Ibn ʿAbbās? He replied: ‘He was not like the Qurʾān reciters.’”

Yaḥyā said: “Shuʿba said: ‘Sulaymān al-Taymī and Ibn ʿAwn came to visit me and my mother. Al-Taymī said, “Abū Naḍra related to us,” and Ibn ʿAwn said, “I have seen—”’”

Abū Naḍra. Al-Taymī said: “I did not see him.”

“Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmmār related to us: I heard Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd say: ‘Sufyān knew al-Aʿmash’s reports better than al-Aʿmash himself.’”

Muḥammad said: “I heard ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī say, concerning the report of Ibn Masʿūd, ‘There is no harm in a pilgrim in consecration marrying’: ‘No one relates it from Jarīr except someone who wants to discredit Jarīr. It is only Ibrāhīm’s own statement.’”

Abū Bakr ibn ʿAbd al-Malik related to us: ʿAbd al-Razzāq related to us, from Maʿmar, who said:

“I was with Yaḥyā ibn [Abī] Kathīr, writing ḥadīth from him, and I dictated to him. He said to me:

‘Write down for me the report about such-and-such and the report about such-and-such.’ I said: ‘Abū Naṣr, what will you do with the written record?’

He said: ‘Write, man! If you do not write, you have failed’—or he said, ‘you have wasted [the opportunity].’”

ʿAlī said: “The most reliable transmitters from Ibrāhīm are Manṣūr and al-Ḥakam. Yaḥyā al-Qaṭṭān used to say: ‘They are equal; we do not prefer one over the other.’ Then comes Fuḍayl ibn ʿAmr, from Sulaymān al-Aʿmash.”

Al-Faḍl related to me: I heard Abū ʿAbd Allāh being asked: “When Manṣūr and al-Aʿmash differ in their reports from Ibrāhīm (269b), whose account do you follow?” He replied: “Manṣūr’s, for he makes fewer omissions.”

Aḥmad and ʿAlī said: Yaḥyā said: Sufyān said: “Whenever I related to al-Aʿmash from one of Ibrāhīm’s pupils, if I said ‘Manṣūr,’ he fell silent.”

Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd said: “Kahmas said to me: ‘We rejected him’—meaning al-Jarīrī—‘during the plague.’”

He said: Hishām ibn ʿUrwa said: “He used to visit my wife”—meaning Ibn Isḥāq, that is, Fāṭima bint al-Mundhir ibn al-Zubayr, the wife of Hishām ibn ʿUrwa.

Aḥmad said: Ḥajjāj related to us: Shuʿba informed us: “Ghaylān and al-Haytham were writing with Jābir. Jābir said: ‘Are you two writing?!’ Then he got up and went inside.

“Al-Haytham said: ‘We are not writing.’ Ghaylān said: ‘He did not say, “I did not write”; he said, “Who writes? Who writes?”’”

Salama related to me from Aḥmad, who said: Ḥajjāj related to us: Shuʿba related to us, from al-Haytham, who said: “A grocer among us married a woman for a dirham, so they bought two heads for two daniqs—”

—and they bought vegetables and something else.

Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmmār related to us: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān related to us:

“I asked Sufyān about Abū Isḥāq’s report concerning green produce, that there is no alms tax on it. He replied:

‘This is not one of Abū Isḥāq’s reports.’”

I heard Abū ʿĀṣim al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Makhlad mention, from Sufyān, from ʿĀṣim, from Abū Razīn, from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning an apostate woman. He said: “She is to be kept alive.”

Abū ʿĀṣim said: “Abū Ḥanīfa informed us, from ʿĀṣim, from Abū Razīn, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: ‘She is to be killed.’”

Abū ʿĀṣim said: “It reached me that Sufyān heard it from Abū Ḥanīfa, or that it reached him on Abū Ḥanīfa’s authority.”

Salama related to us from Aḥmad, who said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān related to us: “I asked Sufyān about ʿĀṣim’s report concerning the apostate woman. He said: ‘As for a reliable authority, no.’ The report was related by Abū Ḥanīfa, from ʿĀṣim, from Abū Razīn, from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning a woman who apostatizes. He said:

‘She is imprisoned and not killed.’”

ʿAlī said: “I know of no one who relates from Ibrāhīm in the musnad tradition what al-Aʿmash related. Mughīra knew better than anyone what he had heard from Ibrāhīm and what he had not heard; no one knew more about him than Mughīra. He transmitted from Ibrāhīm and from his pupils. Then there was Abū—”

Maʿshar and Ḥammād; Ḥammād was superior to Abū Maʿshar. I did not see that Yaḥyā had an opinion about Abū Maʿshar in this matter.

Yaḥyā said: “Manṣūr is the most reliable transmitter from Mujāhid. He is more reliable than Ibn Abī Najīḥ in everything, whether from Mujāhid or anyone else.”

ʿAlī said: “ʿAbd al-Raḥmān asked Sufyān about the report of ʿĀṣim from Abū Razīn. He replied: ‘I did not hear it from a reliable authority.’”

Muḥammad ibn Manṣūr related to us: Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr related to us: I heard Shuʿba say: “Whenever Sufyān related a report to me from someone, and I met that person and asked him about it, it was just as Sufyān had related it to me.”

Saʿīd ibn Asad related to me: Ḍamra related to us, from Ibn Shawdhab, who said: “I heard a son-in-law of Ayyūb say: ‘Ayyūb said: I have never met a Kūfan whom I would rank above Sufyān.’”

Saʿīd related to me: Ḍamra related to us: I heard Sufyān say: “I wish I could escape from this matter with nothing to my credit or against me. I am seeking knowledge today—what is this for?”

I heard Zayd ibn al-Mubārak al-Ṣanʿānī say: “Sufyān came to Ṣanʿāʾ on a trading trip.

“He bought silver and stayed there for forty-three nights.”

Zayd said: “It was said to Ibn Thawr: ‘ʿAbd al-Razzāq says, “I sealed up my record of what I heard from Sufyān. I heard him with Hishām [ibn] Yūsuf, and I kept watch over him until I had copied it.”’ Ibn Thawr replied: ‘I did not see him with Sufyān. I missed him for several days. When Sufyān came to us, his head was shaved and he was weak.’ He asked someone, ‘What is the matter with him?’ The man replied, ‘He was ill.’”

“Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmmār related to us: I heard Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd say: ‘I have seen no one better than Sufyān and Khālid ibn al-Ḥārith.’”

ʿAlī ibn al-Madīnī said: “Among al-Shaʿbī’s pupils were Abū Ḥuṣayn, then Ismāʿīl, then Dāwūd ibn Abī Hind, then al-Shaybānī, Muṭarrif, and Bayān. Those of al-Shaybānī’s generation were the foremost. Mughīra was among al-Shaʿbī’s pupils; he transmitted from him and did it well.

—and Zakariyyā ibn Abī Zāʾida (270b) and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī al-Safar were of one generation. Mālik ibn Mighwal, Abū Ḥayyān al-Taymī, and Ibn Abjar were of another. Ashʿath ibn Suwār ranked above Jābir and Ibn Sālim. Mujālid ranked above Ashʿath ibn Suwār and above Ajlaḥ al-Kindī.

Al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAẓīm related to us: I heard ʿAlī ibn al-Madīnī say: “Al-Shaʿbī, ʿUrwa, ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh, and al-Zuhrī were alike in their standing; their standing was close, one to another. They engaged with people’s knowledge in much the same way. Qatāda engaged with some of this, but did not reach their level. As for al-Aʿmash, if you like, you could say his standing was closer to al-Zuhrī’s than Qatāda’s.”

I heard ʿAlī say: “ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Khaṭṭābī informed me: ‘Our client Isḥāq ibn Rāshid informed me: Ibn Shihāb said to me, “Does anyone remain who possesses knowledge?” I replied, “Yes, a man from Kūfa called Sulaymān al-Aʿmash.”’

“He said: ‘Bring me a report from him.’ I replied: ‘I do not have one memorized, but if you like, I can bring you a book I have.’

“He said: ‘Bring it.’ So I brought him a book. He read it and said: ‘Woe to you! I did not think anyone remained who could do this well.’”

Saʿīd ibn Asad related to me: Ḍamra related to us, from Rajāʾ ibn Abī Salama, who said:

“I heard ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb repeatedly say: ‘We do not perish after the Prophet ﷺ.’ Sulaymān ibn Mūsā said to him: ‘Eating raisins in al-Ṭāʾif has kept you busy.’”

Abū ʿUmar related to us: Shuʿba related to us: Wāṣil al-Aḥdab informed me: “I heard al-Maʿrūr ibn Suwayd—who used to say to his brother’s sons, ‘Learn from me: I was present when ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb was brought a slave girl’—”

Abū Bakr ibn ʿAbd al-Malik related to me: ʿAbd al-Razzāq related to us, from Maʿmar, who said:

“I heard Ayyūb say to al-Layth ibn Abī Sulaym: ‘Consider what you heard from these two men and hold fast to it’—meaning Ṭāwūs and Mujāhid—‘and beware of your two saddle bags’ (271a)—meaning ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb.”

Abū Bakr related to me: ʿAbd al-Razzāq related to us, from Maʿmar, who said: “Whenever Ayyūb sat with ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb, he covered his head.”

“ʿAbd al-Razzāq said: ‘We were with Muqātil ibn Sulaymān when Sufyān al-Thawrī passed by. The people moved away from him, but I felt embarrassed, so I stayed and sat with him.

“He said: ‘Ibn ʿUyayna said, “You transmit from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, though they say you did not hear from him?” He replied: “He used to shut a door between himself and me.” I said to myself, “Indeed—the city gate!”’”

“ Ibn Abī ʿUmar related to us: Sufyān related to us: I heard Misʿar say to Ḥammād ibn ʿAmr: ‘What did you think of the man?’—meaning Muqātil. He replied: ‘If what he brings is knowledge, then he certainly knows it.’”

“Abū Yūsuf said: ‘The people of Medina say that Ḥabīb ibn Maslama and Bus r ibn Arṭāʾa heard nothing from the Prophet ﷺ and had no companionship with him. The people of Syria say that they did hear from him and were his Companions.’” They doubt whether al-Nuʿmān ibn Bashīr heard from him.

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us: Ḥammād related to us, from Ayyūb, from ʿĀʾisha bint Saʿd, who said: “I met six of the Prophet’s wives ﷺ.”

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us: Ḥammād related to us, from Ayyūb, from Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd ibn Ḥayyān, from his father, who said: “Al-Mukhtār summoned the quarters of Kūfa to a sealed document, so that they might affirm what it contained and pledge allegiance to him. When he summoned the Taym, I said, ‘I shall watch what al-Ḥārith ibn Suwayd does.’ I said to him, ‘Will you affirm a sealed document when you do not know what is in it?’ He replied, ‘Leave me alone. I heard ʿAbd Allāh say: “If a word that would spare me two lashes were enough to make me speak, I would say it.”’”

Ḥammād said: Then I heard from Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd ibn Ḥayyān.

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us, saying: Ḥammād related to us, from Yūnus, from Muḥammad, that he used to disapprove of selling fruits before they had been harvested.

Sulaymān said: This is an error. The report is from Ayyūb. Ḥammād said, from Ayyūb, from Muḥammad, that he saw no harm in buying a date while it was still on the palm tree—[but] harm [in selling fruit before harvest].118 He said: I do not know what [the rule is for] selling them before they are harvested. (271b) Sulaymān said: Ayyūb had reservations about these three: Rabīʿa, al-Battī, and Abū Ḥanīfa.

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us, saying: Ḥammād related to us, from Ayyūb, who said: I was with Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd in Medina. A man asked him about something, but he did not answer. He said, “Ask this man”—meaning Rabīʿa. I objected to him and said, “You direct him to this man to give him a legal opinion based on his own judgment?”

He said: One day Yaḥyā said, “If only you would sit with him.” So I sat with him and heard what he said. Then I got up and said, “This is a teacher among us”—meaning al-Battī.

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, from Hishām ibn ʿUrwa—he had mentioned a chain of transmission, but I did not retain it—who said: The Prophet ﷺ said: “The affairs of the Children of Israel remained sound and upright until there arose among them the sons of captives from other nations, and they spoke on the basis of personal opinion, so they went astray and led others astray.”

Sufyān said: We investigated and found that the first to speak on the basis of personal opinion in Medina was Rabīʿa, in Kūfa Abū Ḥanīfa, and in Baṣra al-Battī. We found them to be sons of captives from other nations.

I said to Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb: “Al-Muʿallā ibn Asad related to us, from Wuhayb, from Ayyūb, that ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz gave a ṣāʿ of food for the zakāt al-fiṭr.” He said:

“This is an error. Among the evidence for the error in this report is what Abū al-Nuʿmān al-Sadūsī, ʿĀrim, related to us, from Abū Zayd, from ʿĀṣim”—Sulaymān said, “I think it was from Ḥafṣa”—who said: “Ibn Sīrīn used to give a ṣāʿ of food for the zakāt al-fiṭr. When the letter of ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz arrived, specifying half a ṣāʿ of wheat, he stopped doing so and used to give dates.”

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us, saying: Ḥammād related to us, saying: Ayyūb would not permit us to distribute the zakāt without the authority of the ruler.

Ḥammād said: I mentioned this to al-Ḥajjāj al-Ṣawwāf, and he said: Ayyūb said, “If he puts it where it belongs, that suffices him.”

Sulaymān said regarding the report of Thawbān: “The garden path of Paradise.” He said: Ismāʿīl ibn ʿUlayya said, “The fruit-picking of Paradise.” He said: That is an error. Al-makhrafa means “the road.”

Sulaymān related to us, saying: Sulaymān ibn Akhḍar related to us, from Ibn ʿAwn, who said: Muḥammad would attribute only three reports to Abū Hurayra as going back to the Prophet: that the Prophet ﷺ prayed one of the two evening prayers, and a man stood up and said:

“Messenger of God, may one of us pray in a single garment?” He replied, “Does every one of you have two garments?” And: “The men and women boasted about which of them would be more numerous in Paradise.” Sulaymān said of this: “It can only be transmitted as going back to the Prophet.”

Yaḥyā ibn Khalaf related to us, saying: Bishr ibn al-Mufaḍḍal related to us, from Khālid, who said: Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn said: “Everything I have related from Abū Hurayra goes back to the Prophet.”

Sulaymān related to us, saying: Ḥammād related to us, from Ayyūb, who said: I found in the book of Abū Qilāba, from Anas: “If one of you becomes drowsy while praying, let him sleep until he understands what he is saying.”

Sulaymān said: In one place it reads: “From Ayyūb, from Abū Qilāba, from Anas.”

Sulaymān said: Jarīr ibn Ḥāzim read a book of Abū Qilāba’s to Ayyūb and he said: “I heard all of this from Abū Qilāba. Some of it I remember, and some of it I do not remember.”

He said: Ḥammād would sometimes relate something to us and say, “This is something that was in the book.”

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us, saying: Ḥammād related to us, from Ayyūb, from Abū Qilāba, from Anas, from the Prophet ﷺ that he prayed the noon prayer in Medina as four units and the afternoon prayer at Dhū al-Ḥulayfa as two units. Anas said: “I heard them clearly state both.”

Sulaymān said: Abū Qilāba heard this from Anas, and he was a jurist. Ḥumayd and Yaḥyā ibn Abī Isḥāq related from Anas, who said: “I heard the Prophet ﷺ chanting the talbiya for ʿumra.” He said: He did not retain which of the two accounts was correct: what Abū Qilāba said, that the Prophet ﷺ performed the ḥajj alone; or that some of the Prophet’s Companions combined the ḥajj and ʿumra. These were his words, or words to that effect.

I heard Sulaymān mention the report of Abū al-ʿĀliya: A man laughed during the prayer, so the Prophet ﷺ ordered him to repeat the ablution and the prayer. He declared it weak. (272b)

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us, saying: Sulaymān ibn Akhḍar related to us—and in the case of Ibn ʿAwn, he was like Ḥammād ibn Zayd in the case of Ayyūb.

Sulaymān related to us, saying: Ḥammād related to us, from Shuʿayb ibn al-Ḥabḥāb, who said: The first thing that happened between Abū al-ʿĀliya and me was that he came to the market looking for a garment—a piece of merchandise he had with him. He came to me, and I brought out a good garment for him and took the dirhams. He said:

“He left and showed it to them. They said, ‘It is worth more than your dirhams.’ So he came back and said, ‘Give us back our dirhams, may God bless you.’ I returned the dirhams to him and took the garment.”

He said: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, from Shuʿayb, who said: Abū al-ʿĀliya would come to our house and say, “Do not go to any trouble for us; feed us from the household’s food.”

He said: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, from ʿAlī ibn Zayd, from ʿUqba ibn Ṣahbān, from Abū Bakra, regarding His words, “A multitude from the earlier generations, and a multitude from the later ones” (Qurʾān 56:39–40). He said: “Each group is from this community.” I said, “From whom did you hear that?” He said, “I do not know.” I said, “Could you not have asked him?” He said, “Abū al-Ḥasan, if I had known he would not be angry, I would have asked him.”

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us, saying: Ḥammād related to us, from Saʿīd ibn Abī Ṣadaqa, from Muḥammad, from Abū Hurayra, who said: “When one of you gets up during the night, let him pray two units, reciting in them; then let him recite in two units before or after the obligatory prayer.” Ḥammād said: I mentioned to Ayyūb that Hishām says, “two short units,” and he rejected it.

He said: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, from Thābit, who said: Ibn ʿAbbās said: “What do you object to about—when God, Mighty and Majestic, has made it a concession? If God, Mighty and Majestic, were to put wheat in a drink of water, it would be an act of piety.” I said, “Abū Muḥammad, did you hear this from Ibn ʿAbbās?” He said, “Rather, Abū Ḥamza informed me of it.”

He said: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, from Thābit, who said: I heard Ibn al-Zubayr preach, and he said: Muḥammad ﷺ said: “Whoever wears silk in this world will not—”

—touch it in the Hereafter.” And through the same chain, from Thābit, who said: I said to Ibn ʿUmar, “Did the Messenger of God ﷺ forbid nabīdh prepared in a jar?” He said, “They claim that.”

He said: Ḥammād related to us, from Yazīd ibn Ḥāzim, from Sulaymān ibn Yasār, who said:

He said to my uncle Jarīr ibn Zayd, “Abū Salama, [there is] a woman from your people, from Banū Sulaymān.”

And through the same chain, from Yazīd ibn Ḥāzim, from Sulaymān ibn Yasār, who said: I saw Ḥassān ibn Thābit let his forelock hang between his eyes.

And through the same chain, from Yazīd ibn Ḥāzim, from Sulaymān ibn Yasār, who said: Abū Usayd said:

“I came when ʿUthmān was killed; his sight had gone.”

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us, saying: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, from Hishām, from al-Ḥasan, who said: Al-Ḥakam ibn ʿAmr captured spoils in Khurāsān, among which were gold and silver. Ziyād or Ibn Ziyād wrote to him that the Commander of the Faithful had written, ordering him to take all the gold and silver for himself. Al-Ḥakam said: “If the heavens and earth were closed up over a man, and he feared God, Mighty and Majestic, God, Mighty and Majestic, would surely make a way out for him from that.”

He said: He then summoned the people and divided their spoils among them. Al-Ḥasan said: Al-Ḥakam died on the road before he met him.

Sulaymān related to us, saying: Abū al-Nuʿmān related to me, saying: Ḥammād said: “When I have not heard a report from Ayyūb, I dislike saying, ‘Ayyūb said such-and-such,’ lest people think that I heard it from him.”

Sulaymān related to us, saying: al-Sarī ibn Yaḥyā related to us, from Muḥammad, who said:

“May God have mercy on Shurayḥ. He used to bring my seat close.” Sulaymān said: He was deaf—meaning Muḥammad.

Sulaymān related to us, saying: Salama ibn ʿAbāya related to us, who said: Shuʿba said, “Have you met al-Sarī ibn Yaḥyā?” I said, “No.” He said, “Go to him, for he is the most truthful of people.” Salama said:

I went to al-Sarī, and he brought us a tray of fālūdhaj.

Sulaymān related to us, saying: Ḥammād related to us, from ʿĀṣim, who said: Abū al-ʿĀliya said: “We recited the Qurʾān for twelve years before they killed their leader and did what they did”—meaning before they killed ʿUthmān.

He said: Ḥammād related to us, from Ayyūb, from Nāfiʿ, who said: Ibn ʿUmar used to say:

“The waiting period of an umm walad is one menstrual period.” (273b)

Ḥammād said: Then Ayyūb later said: “Ibn ʿUmar used to have a slave woman observed for one menstrual period.”

Ḥammād said: I asked ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUmar and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sarrāj, and they related to me from Nāfiʿ that Ibn ʿUmar used to say: “The waiting period of an umm walad is one menstrual period.”
