I heard an elder from among our companions, from the people of Marw, say: ʿAbbād ibn ʿAbbād said: “I heard Yūnus ibn Khabbāb say: ‘ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān killed the two daughters of the Messenger of God ﷺ.’” It is widely and abundantly reported of him that he used to attack ʿUthmān. He was an evil man.

Abū Nuʿaym related to us: Sufyān related to us, from Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Muntashir—a distinguished, reliable Kūfan.

Abū Nuʿaym related to us: Sufyān related to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sharīk al-ʿĀmirī, a reliable man, one of the senior people of Kūfa, inclined toward Shīʿism.

Qabīṣah related to us: Sufyān related to us, from ʿImrān ibn Ẓabyān, a reliable man, one of the senior people of Kūfa (293b), inclined toward Shīʿism.

Abū ʿĀṣim and Qabīṣah related to us, from Sufyān, from Ḥakīm ibn Jubayr, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd, [from his father], from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, who said:

The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Whoever begs from people despite having enough to sustain him will come on the Day of Resurrection with scratches, or gouges, or wounds on his face.” They said: “Messenger of God, what counts as enough for him?” He said: “Fifty dirhams, or their weight in gold,” or something similar—this is Abū ʿĀṣim’s wording. Shuʿbah related from him on some occasions and criticized him. He was extreme in his Shīʿism. I know of no one who related from Shuʿbah, from him, except Ibrāhīm ibn Ṭahmān.

Abū Nuʿaym related to us: Sufyān related to us, from ʿUthmān ibn al-Mughīrah al-Thaqafī, a reliable man, from whom Shuʿbah and Misʿar related.

Qabīṣah related to us: Sufyān related to us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿĀbis ibn Rabīʿah. ʿĀbis ibn Rabīʿah had heard from ʿUthmān: “When you have put the saddles down.”

Abū Nuʿaym related to us: Sufyān related to us, from Ibn ʿUmar, from Muslim al-Baṭīn. Misʿar said: “I saw Muslim al-Baṭīn satirizing the Murjiʾah in the mosque.”

Qabīṣah related to us: Sufyān related to us, from al-Aghar, one of his elders, from Wahb ibn— Munabbih; Sufyān narrated from him.

Abū Nuʿaym related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, from Zuhayr ibn Abī Thābit, a Kūfan; there is no objection to him.

He said: Sufyān related to us, from Abū Bakr al-Zubaydī, reliable.

He said: Sufyān related to us, from Abū Jaʿfar al-Farrāʾ, reliable.

He said: Sufyān related to us, from Sulaymān—namely, Ibn al-Mughīrah—from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥanash, reliable. Abū Bakr related to us from Sufyān, from him; he praised and commended him, saying: “He was a tutor; what an excellent shaykh!”

Abū Nuʿaym related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, from ʿUthmān ibn Ḥakīm, a reliable Kūfan.

He said: Sufyān related to us, from Mujālid ibn Saʿīd: “People have criticized him, especially Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd, yet he is reliable.”

Abū Nuʿaym related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, from al-Jaʿd ibn Dhakār, a Kūfan.

ʿAlī al-Shaqīqī related to us, from Ibn al-Mubārak, from Sufyān, from Abū ʿAwn al-Thaqafī, Muḥammad ibn ʿUbayd Allāh. Shuʿbah narrated from him. He was a reliable Kūfan.

He said: Sufyān related to us, from Hārūn ibn ʿAntarah, Abū Wakīʿ, who was a Kūfan by origin; there is no objection to him.” His son ʿAbd al-Malik is weak and discredited.

He said (214a): Abū Nuʿaym related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, from “Wāʾil ibn Dāwūd, from Saʿīd ibn ʿUmayr, who was al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib’s nephew,” a man of whom there is no objection, a Kūfan.

He said: Sufyān related to us, from al-Qaʿqāʿ ibn Yazīd ibn Sabrah. Sufyān narrated from both al-Qaʿqāʿ ibn Yazīd and al-Qaʿqāʿ ibn Shubrumah.

He said: Sufyān related to us, from al-Rabīʿ ibn Abī Rāshid, a reliable, reliable Kūfan.

He said: Sufyān related to us, from ʿAbdah ibn Abī Lubābah, reliable. He moved to Syria. Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit, al-Aʿmash, al-Awzāʿī, and others narrated from him. “He is one of the reliable men of Kūfa.”

He said: Sufyān related to us, from “Kulayb ibn Wāʾil, a Kūfan of whom there is no objection.”

He said: Sufyān related to us, from Marzūq, Abū Bukayr.

He said: Sufyān related to us, from Muzāḥim ibn Zufar.

He said: Sufyān related to us, from al-Mughīrah ibn al-Nuʿmān, from whom Shuʿbah narrated, a Kūfan, “reliable.”

He said: Sufyān related to us, from Zufar al-ʿAjalī, from Qays ibn Ḥabtar. He said:

Those who swoon were mentioned to him, and he said: “I have heard that they are from Satan.”

He said: Sufyān related to us, from Jamīl ibn Yazīd, a man of whom there is no objection.

He said: Sufyān related to us, from “Mūsā ibn Abī Kathīr, a reliable Kūfan, an Irjāʾ adherent.”

Qabīṣah related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, from “Mūsā ibn al-Musayyab, a man of whom there is no objection.”

He said: Abū Nuʿaym related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, from Jaḥsh, a shaykh.

He said: Sufyān related to us, from “Ismāʿīl ibn Sumayʿ, a man of whom there is no objection.”

He said: Sufyān related to us, from Ibn Shubrumah—whose name was ʿAbd Allāh—a man of whom there is no objection.

Al-Ḥumaydī said: From Sufyān, from ʿUmārah ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ ibn Shubrumah. He was older than his uncle ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shubrumah, and ʿUmārah was also the better of the two.

He said: Abū Nuʿaym related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, from Abū Yaḥyā al-Qattāt, a man of whom there is no objection.

He said: Sufyān related to us, from Iyād ibn Laqīṭ, from whom Misʿar narrated; “he is reliable.” His son ʿAbd Allāh ibn Iyād was related to us by Abū Nuʿaym; he was reliable and served as the representative of his people.

He said: Sufyān related to us, from Maʿn ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, from whom Misʿar narrated. Maʿn’s son al-Qāsim “served as judge over Kūfa.”

“He said: Sufyān related to us, from Yazīd ibn Ḥayyān, who was among the early people of Kūfa.” (294b)

He said: Sufyān related to us, from Saʿīd ibn Ashwaʿ, who heard from Shurayḥ ibn al-Nuʿmān al-Ṣāʾidī.

He said: Sufyān related to us, from Yaḥyā ibn Ghassān, Abū Ghassān. He said: I heard ʿAmr ibn Maymūn say: “I prayed the dawn prayer behind ʿUmar, and he did not recite the qunūt.” Misʿar narrated from him.

Abū Nuʿaym related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, from al-Zibriqān, a shaykh of whom there is no objection.

“He said: Sufyān related to us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān [ibn] al-Aṣamm, reliable.”

Qabīṣah related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, from ʿAmr ibn ʿĀmir.

Abū Nuʿaym related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, from ʿImrān ibn Muslim, a man of whom there is no objection.

Sufyān related to us, from al-ʿArab ibn Kaʿb al-Azdī. He said: “I saw al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī standing on a white large riding horse. He had dyed his beard and head with wasmah.” There is no objection to him.

He said: Sufyān related to us, from Abū al-Juwayriyyah al-Jarmī, “reliable, a man of whom there is no objection.”

He said: Sufyān related to us, from Yaḥyā ibn ʿAmr ibn Salamah, a man of whom there is no objection.

He said: Sufyān related to us, from Ziyād ibn Ismāʿīl al-Makhzūmī—though someone else said: al-Sahmī. Ziyād’s hadith is worthless, and he was a Meccan.

He said: Sufyān related to us, from Ḥuraysh the scribe, a Kūfan, a shaykh.

He said: Sufyān related to us, from Ajlaḥ, a Kūfan, “reliable, though there is some weakness in his hadith.”

Qabīṣah ibn ʿUqbah, Abū ʿĀmir al-Suwwāʾī, related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Khālid al-ʿAnsī, a reliable man, well known in Kūfa, a Kūfan. Al-Aʿmash narrated from him, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Maʿqil: ʿAlī recited the qunūt, invoking a curse upon so-and-so and so-and-so.

He said: Sufyān related to us, from Dithār ibn Shabīb al-Qaṭṭān, a Kūfan of whom there is no objection.

He said: Sufyān related to us, from Ibn Yasīr ibn ʿAmr, from his father: He came to Uways al-Qaranī and found him not concealing himself from exposure, so he clothed him.

Wakīʿ said: From Qays ibn Bashīr.

Qabīṣah related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, from Qulāmah ibn Ḥamāṭah, a shaykh of whom there is no objection.

He said: Sufyān related to us, from ʿĪsā ibn Wahb, a reliable Kūfan.

He said: Sufyān related to us, from Khālid ibn Abī Karīmah, a man of whom there is no objection.”

He said: Sufyān related to us, from Yaʿlā ibn Nuʿmān al-Asadī, from Abū Muḥammad, who was Ibn Shafī. Al-ʿAlāʾ ibn al-Musayyib also narrated from him.

He said: Sufyān related to us, from Abū Balj, a Kūfan of whom there is no objection.

He said: Sufyān related to us, from Ibrāhīm al-Ḥaḍramī, a Kūfan of whom there is no objection.

He said: Sufyān related to us, from “al-Ḥakam ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Baṣrī, a man of whom there is no objection.”

He said: Sufyān related to us, from Ḥabīb ibn Abī ʿAmrah, a man of whom there is no objection.

He said: Sufyān related to us, from Abū Rawq, a man of whom there is no objection.

He said: Sufyān related to us, from Abū al-Miḥjal al-Rudaynī, whose name was Murrah, a reliable Kūfan, a man of whom there is no objection.

He said: Sufyān related to us, from ʿUbayd the butcher, who was Abū Yaʿlā ibn ʿUbayd al-Ṭanāfisī.

Qabīṣah ibn ʿUqbah, Abū ʿĀmir al-Suwwāʾī, related to us, saying: Sufyān al-Thawrī related to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muslim, a shaykh of whom there is no objection.

He said: Sufyān related to us, from “Nūḥ ibn Abī Bilāl, a Medinan of whom there is no objection.”

He said: Sufyān related to us, from Abū Shihāb, a man of whom there is no objection.

He said: Sufyān related to us, from ʿImrān ibn al-Ḥasan, a man of whom there is no objection.

He said: Sufyān related to us, from Ṭalḥah ibn Yaḥyā, a distinguished man of whom there is no objection, though there is some weakness in his hadith.

He said: Sufyān related to us, from Ghaylān.

He said: Sufyān related to us, from ʿAmr, the brother of [Abū] al-Aḥwaṣ:

Abū al-Aḥwaṣ performed a retreat in a mosque above him.

Aḥmad ibn al-Khalīl related to me, saying: Abū Aḥmad related to us, saying: Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh related to us, from Abū Isḥāq, who said: “Khawārij emerged, and Abū al-Aḥwaṣ went out among those who went out; they killed him.”

Aḥmad said: I heard Yazīd ibn Hārūn, when he was asked about the name of Rabʿī ibn Ḥirāsh’s brother, say: “Al-Rabīʿ ibn Ḥirāsh.”

Qabīṣah related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, from Abū Mālik, from Rabʿī, from Ḥudhayfah, who said: “Your Prophet ﷺ—said: ‘Every good deed is charity.’”

Abū Nuʿaym related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, saying: Abū Mālik al-Ashjaʿī related to us, from some shaykhs of theirs: “A slave from Ṭayyiʾ (295b) confessed—or acknowledged against himself—that he had committed fornication four times, and ʿAlī carried out the prescribed punishment against him.”

Qabīṣah related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, from Abū Junāb, Yaḥyā ibn Abī Ḥayyah al-Kalbī, who was “weak and used to practice tadlīs,” a Kūfan.

He said: Sufyān related to us, from Yūnus ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Jarmī, a Kūfan of whom there is no objection.

He said: Sufyān related to us, from Abū Hammām, from Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbbād; Abū Hammām is a man of whom there is no objection.

He said: Sufyān related to us, from Saʿīd ibn ʿUbayd al-Ṭāʾī, a reliable Kūfan.

He said: Sufyān related to us, from Waqqāʾ, Abū Yazīd ibn Iyās, a Kūfan of whom there is no objection. He said: He and his father together narrated from Ibrāhīm al-Hajarī, Abū Isḥāq. He used to attribute reports to higher authorities; he is a Kūfan of whom there is no objection.

Qabīṣah related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, from ʿUmārah, a shaykh of whom there is no objection.

Sufyān related to us, from Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAbd al-Malik, said to be Ibn Abī al-Ṣafīrāʾ.

Abū Nuʿaym and ʿUbayd Allāh related to us, from Raqabah, whose transmission is soft.

Qabīṣah related to us, from “Zakariyyā ibn Abī Zāʾidah, reliable. Abū Nuʿaym, ʿUbayd Allāh, and his brother ʿUmar—all reliable—related to us from him.”

Qabīṣah related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, from al-ʿAlāʾ ibn ʿAbd al-Karīm al-Yāmī, who is reliable. Abū Nuʿaym heard from al-ʿAlāʾ.

Abū Nuʿaym related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, saying: I heard al-Aʿmash, while Muḥāḍir was asking him. He said: “Al-ʿAlāʾ ibn ʿAbd al-Karīm sends you greetings and asks: ‘I came yesterday wearing my sock; may I wipe over it?’” He replied: “Yes.”

Qabīṣah related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, from Nājiya al-Muḥāribī, who was a shaykh.

He said: Sufyān related to us, from ʿUmar ibn Ḥarb, from Simāk ibn ʿUbayd al-ʿAbsī.

He said: Qabīṣah related to us, saying: Salamah ibn Nubayṭ ibn Sharīṭ al-Ashjaʿī related to us. Abū Nuʿaym and ʿUbayd Allāh related reports to us from him; he was a reliable Kūfan.

He said: Sufyān related to us, from Ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Fuḍayl, from Ibrāhīm:

Ibn ʿAbbās differed from all the people of prayer concerning a husband and two parents.

He said: Sufyān related to us, from Abū al-Rabīʿ, a shaykh of the clan. Qabīṣah said: His name was Ṣalawāt.

And he said: Sufyān related to us from Yaḥyā ibn al-Naḍr, a shaykh of no concern.

And he said: Sufyān related to us from Abū ʿUmar al-Hilālī, a shaykh, trustworthy, from an earlier generation.

And he said: Sufyān related to us from ʿAlwān al-Kūfī.

And he said: Sufyān related to us from al-Rabīʿ, Abū Ṣāliḥ al-Aslamī. Abū Nuʿaym and ʿUbayd Allāh related to us from him by direct hearing (296a). He is of no concern, a Kūfan.

Qabīṣah related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us from Hishām ibn ʿĀʾidh ibn Nuṣayb al-Asadī. Abū Nuʿaym heard from him, and Shuʿbah related from ʿĀʾidh.

And he said: Sufyān related to us from Wahb ibn ʿUqbah al-Khārifī.

And he said: Sufyān related to us from Sudayr, a money-changer. Ibn ʿUyaynah related from him.

And he said: [Sufyān] related to us from Razīn, the pomegranate seller. Abū Nuʿaym and ʿUbayd Allāh related to us from him. “He is of no concern, a Kūfan”.

He said: Sufyān related to us from Ibrāhīm ibn Abī Ḥafṣah, a Kūfan.

And he said: [Sufyān related to us] from ʿAmr ibn ʿUthmān, “a Kūfan, trustworthy”.

And he said: Abū Nuʿaym related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us from the nephew of Yazīd al-Aḥmar; he is of no concern.

And he said: Sufyān related to us from ʿUqbah. ʿAbd Allāh said: “Speak the Qur’an according to its grammar.” Qabīṣah said: ʿUqbah is al-Asadī.

Abū Nuʿaym related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us from Abū al-Zaʿrāʾ, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtbah, a Kūfan, trustworthy.

And he said: Sufyān related to us from Mughīth al-Bajalī, a Kūfan.

And Sufyān said: from ʿUmar ibn Yaʿlā ibn Murrah; his hadith is somewhat weak.

And he said: Sufyān related to us from Sinān: “ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz used to take the jizyah.”

And he said: Sufyān related to us from Abū Farwah: “Al-Ḍaḥḥāk instructed: Do not turn me face down.”

Qabīṣah said: From Abū Farwah, from Yazīd: “Al-Ḍaḥḥāk instructed.”

He said: Sufyān related to us from Zayd—a shaykh who belonged to Muḥārib—: “I heard Ibrāhīm reviling al-Ḥajjāj.”

And he said: Sufyān related to us from “Fuḍayl ibn Ghazwān, a Sunnī, trustworthy”. He is Abū Muḥammad ibn Fuḍayl ibn Ghazwān, and “Muḥammad is trustworthy, a Shīʿī”.

Abū Nuʿaym said: Sufyān related to us from Ḥabīb ibn Abī ʿAmrah, who was a Kūfan silk merchant, a client of Banū Jumān; “he is of no concern”.

Aḥmad ibn Ḥumayd related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us from Abū Jaḥḍam; he is of no concern.

And he said: Muḥammad ibn Bashshār related to us from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Sufyān, from Nuwayr al-Hamdānī, a Kūfan; “and Thuwayr ibn Abī Fākhitah is a Shīʿī whose hadith is somewhat weak”.

“And Aḥmad ibn al-Khalīl related to me, saying: Isḥāq related to us, saying:

Shabābah ibn Sawwār informed me: I said to Yūnus ibn Abī Isḥāq, ‘Why did you abandon Thuwayr?’ He said, ‘Because he is a Rāfiḍī.’ I said, ‘Your father related from him.’ He said:

‘He knows better’”.

[Abū] Yūsuf said: Muḥammad ibn Bashshār related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān Ibn Mahdī, from Sufyān, from Ḥakīm ibn (296b) al-Daylam: a Kūfan, of no concern.

Through the same chain, from Sufyān, from Bukayr ibn ʿAtīq: he is of no concern.

Through the same chain, from Sufyān, from ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn Rāfiʿ: a Kūfan, of no concern.

Through the same chain, from Sufyān, from ʿUmar ibn Shaybah: a Kūfan, of no concern.

Through the same chain, from Sufyān, from al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Abī al-ʿAbbās: he is of no concern; he inclines toward Shīʿism.

Through the same chain, from Sufyān, from ʿUrwah ibn al-Ḥārith, who is Abū Farwah al-Hamdānī.

Abū Farwah al-Juhanī is Muslim ibn Sālim, from Sufyān ibn Khālid al-Nakhaʿī, a Kūfan.

Abū ʿĀṣim related to us from Sufyān, from a man whose name Bundār gave me, from Abū Muḥammad—a man from Banū Naṣr—from Ibn ʿUmar: “Whoever has a delicate face has delicate knowledge.”

Muḥammad ibn Bashshār related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī related to us from Sufyān, from Sadūs—a man from the tribe—from al-Rabīʿ ibn Khuthaym, who used to say to his muezzin: “Do you give the call to prayer for the dawn prayer?”

From Sufyān, from Rukayn, trustworthy, but he is not Ibn al-Rabīʿ. Tamīm ibn Ḥadhlam—who was one of ʿAbd Allāh’s companions—said to his muezzin: “You give the call to prayer.”

Through the same chain, from Sufyān, from Yazīd ibn Abī Khālid al-Dālānī: his hadith is rejected.

Through the same chain, from Sufyān, from Ibn Abī Nubātah.

Through the same chain, from Sufyān, from al-Rabīʿ ibn al-Mundhir.

Through the same chain, from Sufyān, from Muḥammad ibn Khālid, from a man called al-Ḥakam, from Ibn ʿAbbās: “There is no marriage except with four: a guardian, two witnesses, and a suitor.”

Muḥammad ibn Kathīr related to me, saying: Sufyān related to us from al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Khālid al-Asadī, a Kūfan, trustworthy.

Abū Nuʿaym related to us, saying: ʿUbādah ibn Muslim al-Fazārī related to us, a Kūfan; Sufyān al-Thawrī also related from him.

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb, Abū ʿUmar al-Namirī, and Ādam related to us. They said: Shuʿbah related to us, saying: al-Ḥakam related to us, saying: I heard Yaḥyā al-Jazzār relate from Ibn Udhaynah, from his father, that a man said to ʿUmar …

Al-Ḥumaydī related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Aʿyan related to us, saying:

I heard ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Udhaynah at Wāsiṭ al-Qaṣab, when al-Ḥajjāj came to Wāsiṭ and built al-Khaḍrāʾ, relating from his father.

Salamah ibn Kuhayl said, from al-Ḥasan al-Madanī, from Ibn Udhaynah al-ʿAbdī:

“I came to ʿUmar.”

Abū Yūsuf said: I do not think ʿAbd al-Raḥmān met ʿUmar. Rather, this report is from his father, Udhaynah, who is counted among the Kūfans. ʿAbd Allāh ibn Udhaynah was a Baṣran and was its judge.

Al-Ḥumaydī, Ibn Quʿnab, and Saʿīd related to us (297a). They said: Sufyān related to us from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from Udhaynah: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās say, “Amber is not a fragrant plant; it is something the sea casts up”.

Ibn ʿUthmān related to us from Ibn al-Mubārak, and Ṣafwān related to us from al-Walīd, from Ibn Jurayj, from ʿAmr, from Udhaynah, who heard Ibn ʿAbbās.

Ibn Quʿnab and Ibn Bukayr related to us from Mālik, from ʿUrwah ibn Udhaynah al-Laythī, who said: “I set out with a grandmother of mine, who had an obligation upon her, toward the House of God, Mighty and Exalted. When we were on part of the road, she became unable to continue. She sent a client of hers to ask ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar.” He said:

“I went out with him, and he asked him. He replied: ‘Tell her to ride, then to walk from the point where she became unable to continue.’”

Abū al-Walīd related to us, saying: Abū ʿAwānah related to us from ʿĀṣim, from Shaqīq, from ʿUrwah ibn Qays, from Khālid ibn al-Walīd, who said: “The Commander of the Faithful wrote to me …”

…when Syria cast its gateway121 at Thaniyyah and ʿAsal, saying: “Go to the land of India”—and India at that time, in our view, meant al-Baṣrah. I was reluctant to do so. A man said: “Fear God, Abū Sulaymān, for tribulations have appeared.” He replied: “No, by God, while Ibn al-Khaṭṭāb is alive. They will occur only after him, while people are at Dhū Bulayān—or in Dhū Bulayān, a place or suchlike. Let a man see whether he can find a place in which he will remain undisturbed, if he leaves the place where he is, given the tribulation and evil. He will not find, in those days, the days the Messenger of God ﷺ described as preceding the Hour—the days of killing. We seek refuge in God from those days overtaking me or you.”

Ibn Numayr related to us, saying: Abū Muʿāwiyah related to us from al-Aʿmash, from Shaqīq, from ʿUrwah ibn Qays, who said: Khālid ibn al-Walīd addressed us in Syria and said: “ʿUmar sent me to Syria when it was in a state of turmoil. When he encountered Syria, its gateway was at Thaniyyah and ʿAsal.”

Aḥmad ibn Yūnus related to us, saying: Zuhayr related to us, saying: Abū Isḥāq related to us, saying: Abū Jabr related to us from his father—he was Abū Jabr ibn Tamīm ibn Ḥadhlam—who said: I heard ʿAbd Allāh recite: “They thought that they had been denied” (12:110).

Zuhayr said: Zuhayr would pronounce it lightly. And I heard him recite: “And all of them will come to Him, humbled” (27:87)—in the jussive mood.

“And Aḥmad ibn al-Khalīl related to me, saying: Hārūn ibn Maʿrūf related to us, saying:

Jarīr related to us from Mughīrah, from al-Shaʿbī, who said: “Al-Ḥārith related to me”—and he was a liar”. (297b)

Aḥmad related to me, saying: al-Ḥasan ibn Qutaybah al-Khuzāʿī related to me, saying:

ʿĪsā ibn al-Musayyib related to us, saying: I heard Ibrāhīm—he was asked, and it was said to him: “You met the companions of ʿAbd Allāh and the companions of ʿAlī. How is it that you took reports from the companions of ʿAbd Allāh but left the companions of ʿAlī?” He said: “I consider the companions of ʿAlī suspect.”

Abū ʿAṭiyyah al-Wādiʿī: Mālik ibn ʿĀmir, a Kūfan, a Hamdānī.

Abū al-Kunūd: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAwf, a Kūfan.

Abū Iyās al-Bajalī: ʿĀmir ibn ʿAbdah. Al-Aʿmash related from a man, from him.

Abū Thābit: Ayman ibn Thābit: “Whoever122”

Abū al-Shaʿthāʾ: Sulaym ibn Aswad al-Muḥāribī.

Abū Nuʿāmah al-Kūfī: Shaybah ibn Nuʿāmah. Sufyān related from him.

Abū Yaʿfūr al-ʿAbdī: Waqdān.

Abū Yaʿfūr the Younger: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿUbayd ibn Qusṭās.

Abū Sulaymān: Zayd ibn Wahb al-Juhanī.

Al-Ḥumaydī related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, saying: Yazīd ibn Abī Ziyād related to us from al-Qāsim ibn Mukhaymirah, a Kūfan who moved to Damascus.

Abū al-Muthannā: Mūthir ibn Ghaffārah, an ʿAbdī Kūfan.

Abū Nuʿaym related to us, saying: Bashīr ibn Salmān al-Nahdī related to us, saying: I heard Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbbād, Abū Hubayrah al-Anṣārī, a Kūfan.

“Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us, saying: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us from Mujālid, from ʿUmayr ibn Rawdhī, Abū Kabīr, who said: ʿAlī was preaching when they interrupted his sermon. He came down and went inside. He said: ‘My case and ʿUthmān’s case are like that of three bulls living in a thicket: a white one, a red one, and a black one. A lion lived with them there. Whenever it went after one of them, the others gathered against it, and it could not overcome them. So it said to the black and the red one: “This white one exposes us in our thicket; its whiteness can be seen. Leave it to me so I can eat it. Then it will be just you and me; my color will match your colors, and your colors will match mine.”’ He said: ‘So they left him alone, and the lion soon ate him.

“‘Then whenever it went after either of the other two, they both gathered against it, and it could not overcome them. So it said to the red one: “This black one exposes us in our thicket; its blackness can be seen. Leave it to me so I can eat it. Then it will be just you and me; my color will match yours, and yours will match mine.”

“‘So he left him alone, and the lion soon ate him. After a while, it said: “Red one, I am going to eat you.” He said: “You’re going to eat me?” It said: “Yes.” He said: “Then let me go, so I can cry out three times.” He said: Then he cried, “Indeed, I was eaten on the day the white one was eaten”—three times.’ (298a)

“He said: ʿAlī said: ‘I was weakened only on the day ʿUthmān was killed’—he said it three times—‘indeed …’”

“‘…I was weakened on the day ʿUthmān was killed. Indeed, I was weakened on the day ʿUthmān was killed’”.

Al-Ḥumaydī related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, saying: Abū Zuhayr Muʿāwiyah ibn Ḥudayj related to us. He said: I saw Ṭāwūs sitting with his buttocks resting on his heels. I said to him: “I saw you sitting that way.” He said:

“You did not see me; it was during prayer. I saw the three ʿAbādilah doing that: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās, ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar, and ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr. They used to do it.”

Abū Zuhayr said: I did see him sitting that way.

Al-Ḥumaydī related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, saying: I heard ʿAlī Abū Ḥusayn al-Juʿfī say: I heard Mujāhid say: “When a person mounts a riding animal without pronouncing God’s name, Satan rides behind him and says to him, ‘Sing!’ If he cannot sing well, Satan says to him, ‘Wish for something.’”

Sufyān said: Ibn Abī Najīḥ related to us from Mujāhid, from ʿAbd Allāh. As for Manṣūr, he related to us from Mujāhid, from Abū Maʿmar, from ʿAbd Allāh. Abū Maʿmar’s name was ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sakhbarah.

Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr related to us, saying: Khalaf ibn Khalīfah related to us from Ḥafṣ, Anas’s nephew. Khalaf ibn Khalīfah alone related from this shaykh.

Al-Ḥumaydī related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, saying: Yazīd ibn Kaysān al-Yashkurī, Abū Munayn, a trustworthy Kūfan, related to us.

ʿUbayd Allāh related to us, from Shaybān; and Aḥmad ibn Yūnus, from Zuhayr; and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rajāʾ, from Zāʾidah, from al-Aʿmash, from Abū Ḥāzim, from Abū Hurayrah, who said: “The Messenger of God ﷺ never found fault with food. If he desired it, he ate it; if he disliked it, he left it.”

Qabīṣah related to us, from Sufyān, from al-Aʿmash, from Abū Ḥāzim, from Abū Hurayrah.

ʿUthmān related to us, saying: Jarīr related to us with the same report.

Abū Ḥāzim was the client of Jaʿdah ibn Hubayrah al-Makhzūmī. Abū Muʿāwiyah related from Abū Yaḥyā, the client of Jaʿdah, from Abū Hurayrah.

Abū Nuʿaym related to us, saying: Bashīr ibn Salmān al-Nahdī related to us, from Abū Ḥāzim al-Nahdī, who said: “A companion of mine and I bought straw from Ibn ʿUmar, who reserved some of it. We came to take possession of it, and he came and sat down. One of us went to him and said, ‘Get up from this dust, Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān’ (298b). He said, ‘I don’t mind.’ When we had moved it around a great deal, one of us said to another, ‘He has sat down only to make sure that we don’t take any of what belongs to him.’ One of us then went to him and said, ‘Get up from this dust, for we hope for what you hope for.’

“He said, ‘I did not sit down to keep watch over you; I sat down only to keep watch over myself.’ This man was an Ashjaʿī. ʿUmar ibn Ḥafṣ related this to us, saying: My father related to us, saying: al-Aʿmash related to us, saying—”

Abū Ḥāzim al-Ashjaʿī related to me, saying: “I bought straw from Ibn ʿUmar.”

Abū Nuʿaym related to us, saying: Bashīr ibn Salmān related to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Mujālid, the husband of Mujāhid’s daughter.

Abū Nuʿaym related to us, saying: Bashīr related to us, saying: “I was with Abū al-Jald, Jaylān ibn Farwah.”

Ibn Sīrīn said: “I was informed about Abū al-Jald.”

Abū Nuʿaym related to us, saying: Bashīr related to us, saying: “I was in al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Muzāḥim’s school.”

Abū Nuʿaym related to us, saying: A shaykh in the mosque related to us. I mentioned him to some of our companions, and one said: “He is Abū Līnah.” From al-Ḍaḥḥāk, who said: “Do not take your mount’s saddle out of one village to another.”

Regarding the words, “They repent soon” (Qurʾān 4:17), he said: “Everything short of death is soon.”

Wakīʿ related from Abū Līnah, whose name was al-Naḍr ibn Abī Maryam; Abū Maryam’s name was Ṭahmān.

Abū Nuʿaym related to us, saying: Misʿar related to us, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Maysarah al-Zarrād, whose kunya was Abū Zayd.

Al-Ḥumaydī said: I asked Sufyān, “What does al-Zarrād mean?” He replied: “He makes coats of mail.”

Abū Nuʿaym related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Jabbār ibn ʿAbbās al-Hamdānī related to us. He was trustworthy, a Kūfan.

Abū Nuʿaym related to us, saying: Mūsā ibn ʿUmayr al-ʿAnbarī related to us, saying: ʿAlqamah ibn Wāʾil related to me, from his father, that the Prophet ﷺ, when he stood for prayer, would grasp his left hand with his right. I saw ʿAlqamah do this. Mūsā ibn ʿUmayr was a trustworthy Kūfan. Isḥāq ibn Kaʿb related from a Mūsā ibn ʿUmayr who is not this al-ʿAnbarī; (and he is weak).

Al-Muʿallā ibn Asad—a blind man from Baṣrah—related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn Ziyād al-ʿAbdī, a trustworthy man, related to us, from Maymūn Abū Manṣūr, from Ibrāhīm, who said: “Their khisab123 was in their houses and in their clothes; it was permitted.” (299a) This Abū Manṣūr was a Kūfan from Juhaynah.

Abū Saʿīd Sahl ibn Muḥammad al-ʿAskarī related to me, saying: ʿAbthar, Abū Zubayd—a trustworthy Shīʿī—related to us, from Burd ibn Abī Ziyād, from al-Musayyab ibn Rāfiʿ, who said: I heard al-Barāʾ say: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Whoever prays over a Muslim’s funeral and remains until the burial will have two qīrāṭs; each qīrāṭ is like Mount Uḥud.” It is said that al-Musayyab heard from none of the Prophet’s Companions ﷺ except al-Barāʾ.

Al-Ḥumaydī related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, from Saʿīr ibn al-Khims, who is a trustworthy Kūfan. He had a son called Qaṭan, whose reports are worth nothing.

Ibn ʿUyaynah related from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, a trustworthy Kūfan.

Abū Nuʿaym related to us, saying: Bashīr ibn al-Muhājir al-Ghanawī related to us, saying: “I saw Anas ibn Mālik.” He had also seen Jarīr ibn ʿAbd Allāh, and he related reports from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Buraydah, from his father.

Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Muqriʾ related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ziyād ibn Anʿum related to us. His kunya was Abū Ayyūb; ʿAbd al-Raḥīm ibn Sulaymān and other Kūfans gave him that kunya.

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us, saying: Ḥawshab ibn ʿUqayl related to us. His kunya was [Abū Ḍaḥiyyah]. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī also related from him, and he was trustworthy.

Ibn Quʿnub related to us, saying: Juhayr ibn Yazīd, a trustworthy man from Baṣrah, related to us.

Ādam related to us, saying: Shuʿbah related to us, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Maymūnah, whose kunya was Abū Muʿādh, a trustworthy man from Baṣrah.

“ʿAbd al-Muʾmin Abū ʿUbaydah ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Sadūsī is trustworthy”.

“Abū ʿUbaydah al-Ḥaddād, ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn Wāṣil, is trustworthy”.

Abū al-Walīd related to us, saying: Shuʿbah related to us, from Jullās, who said: I heard ʿUthmān ibn Shammās say: “Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ sent me to Medina, and I was with Marwān. Abū Hurayrah passed by, and Marwān said, ‘Tell us some of your reports, Abū Hurayrah.’ He went on, then came back, and we said:

“‘Now he’ll confront him.’ He asked him, ‘How did you hear the Messenger of God ﷺ pray over the funeral?’ He replied: ‘You created him or her, guided him or her to Islam, and took his or her soul. You know what is hidden and what is manifest. We have come as intercessors, so forgive him or her.’”

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Mubārak related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Wārith related to us (299b), saying: Abū al-Jullās, ʿUqbah ibn Sayyār, related to us, saying: ʿAlī ibn Shammākh related to me, saying:

“I heard Marwān ask Abū Hurayrah.”

Ibn Rajāʾ related to us, saying: Zāʾidah related to us, saying: Yaḥyā ibn Abī Sulaym related to me, saying: I heard Jullās relate: “Marwān asked Abū Hurayrah, ‘How did you hear the Prophet ﷺ?’”

Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr related to us, saying: Hushaym related to us, saying: Abū Balj al-Fazārī informed us, saying: Jullās al-Shāmī related to me: “Marwān passed by Abū Hurayrah while he was relating a report from the Messenger of God ﷺ. He said, ‘The Messenger of God ﷺ said—’ Marwān said, ‘Tell us some of your reports, Abū Hurayrah.’ He had gone only a short distance when he turned back the way he had come and asked, ‘How did you hear the Messenger of God ﷺ pray over the deceased?’ Abū Hurayrah replied, ‘That, after what you said just now?!’”

Then Abū Hurayrah said: “O God, You created him or her.”

Saʿīd related to us, saying: Ismāʿīl ibn Ibrāhīm—namely, Ibn ʿUlayyah—related to us, saying:

Ziyād ibn Mikhraq informed us, from ʿUqbah ibn Sayyār, from a man, who said: “We were sitting with Abū Hurayrah when Marwān stood over him and said, ‘Abū Hurayrah, you keep relating reports that we do not know.’ Then he went away. Afterward he returned to them and said, ‘Abū Hurayrah, how is the prayer over the deceased?’ He replied, ‘After what you just said?’ He said, ‘Yes.’ He replied, ‘We used to say: You are its Lord.’”

[Saʿīd] related from ʿAbd al-Ṣamad ibn ʿAbd al-Wārith, from his father, who said: “I took Shuʿbah to Abū al-Jullās. There was a small vessel with nabīdh in front of him, and he had long hair. He had been a Syrian soldier, and Shuʿbah turned Abū al-Jullās into Jullās.”

ʿAbd al-Ṣamad said: My father said: “I was the one who took him to him, and he reversed its chain of transmission.”

Al-Ḥajjāj related to us, saying: Ḥammād related to us, from ʿAlī ibn Zayd, from al-Rabīʿah ibn al-Nābighah, from his father, from ʿAlī, who said: “The Messenger of God ﷺ forbade visiting graves.” Then he said: “I had forbidden you to visit graves, but visit them, for they remind you of the Hereafter”.

Abū Maʿmar related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Wārith related to us, saying: ʿAlī ibn Zayd said: al-Nābighah ibn al-Mukhāriq ibn Sulaymān related to me, from his father, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said (300a): “I had forbidden you…”—a report to that effect. This is the sound version.

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us, saying: Ḥammād related to us, from Khālid al-Ḥadhdhāʾ, from al-Qāsim ibn Rabīʿah, from ʿUqbah ibn Aws, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr: The Messenger of God ﷺ delivered a sermon and said: “The blood-money for an accidental killing that resembles an intentional one—what is done with a whip or a stick—is one hundred camels.”

Abū al-Nuʿmān related to us, saying: Ḥammād related to us, saying: al-Qāsim ibn Rabīʿah ibn Jawshan, from ʿUqbah—or Yaʿqūb al-Sadūsī—from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr.

Al-Namirī related to us, saying: Shuʿbah related to us, saying: Ayyūb related to us, from al-Qāsim ibn Rabīʿah, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr.

Yaḥyā ibn Yaḥyā related to us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from Khālid al-Ḥadhdhāʾ, from al-Qāsim ibn Rabīʿah ibn Jawshan, from ʿUqbah ibn Aws al-Sadūsī, from Ibn ʿAmr.

Ibn ʿUyaynah said: ʿAlī heard al-Qāsim ibn Rabīʿah relate from Ibn ʿAmr.

The well-preserved report is that of Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr.

Ḥajjāj related to us, saying: Abū ʿAwānah related to us, from Firās, from al-Shaʿbī, from Samurah ibn Jundab: “One day the Messenger of God ﷺ prayed, then said:

“Is anyone from Banū al-Najjār here?”

Al-Ḥajjāj related to us, saying: Abū al-Aḥwaṣ related to us, from Saʿīd ibn Masrūq, from al-Shaʿbī, from Samʿān, from Samurah.

Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shaybah related to us, saying: Wakīʿ ibn al-Jarrāḥ related to us, from his father, from Saʿīd ibn Masrūq, from al-Shaʿbī, from al-Mushannij ibn Samʿān, from Samurah.

Ibn Abī al-Sarī related to me, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzāq related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, from his father, from al-Shaʿbī, from Samʿān ibn Mushannij, from Samurah ibn Jundab.

Abū Nuʿaym related to us, saying: Isrāʾīl related to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿĀmir ibn Masʿūd al-Qurashī, who said: He—meaning the Prophet ﷺ—said: “Fasting in winter is a cool gain: its days are short and its nights are long.” “ʿĀmir had no Companionship”.

Aḥmad ibn Yūnus related to us, saying: Zāʾidah related to us, from ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Rufayʿ, from ʿĀmir ibn Masʿūd al-Qurashī, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “If people knew what there is in the front row, they would draw lots for a place in it.” Ibn Muʿāwiyah used to relate it (300b) from Jarīr, from ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Rufayʿ, from ʿĀmir ibn Masʿūd, from the Prophet ﷺ, but he was mistaken about it. Some of them related from ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, who said: “A man called ʿĀmir ibn Masʿūd jostled me in Mecca. I spoke to him, and he said to me…” Sufyān al-Thawrī and Jarīr also related this from Ibrāhīm ibn ʿĀmir.

Abū Nuʿaym and Qabīṣah related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, from Qābūs ibn Abī Ẓabyān, Ḥuṣayn ibn Jundab.

ʿUmar ibn Ḥafṣ ibn Ghiyāth related to us, saying: My father related to us, saying: al-Aʿmash related to us, saying: I heard Hilāl ibn Yasāf relate from al-Rabīʿ ibn Khuthaym, who said: ʿAbd Allāh said: “Whoever says ten times, ‘There is no god but God alone, without partner. To Him belongs sovereignty and praise, and He has power over all things,’ they are equivalent to four emancipated persons from the descendants of Ishmael.”

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā related to us, from Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid, from al-Shaʿbī, from al-Rabīʿ ibn Khuthaym, who said: “Whoever says, ‘There is no god but God’”—and he mentioned a report to that effect.

Ādam related to us, saying: Shuʿbah related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Maysarah related to us, saying:

I heard Hilāl ibn Yasāf relate from al-Rabīʿ ibn Khuthaym, from ʿAmr ibn Maymūn, from Ibn Masʿūd, who said: “To say, ‘There is no god but God alone, without partner. To Him belongs sovereignty and praise, and He has power over all things,’ is dearer to me than freeing four slaves.”

Al-Ḥajjāj related to us, saying: Ḥammād related to us, from Dāwūd, from al-Shaʿbī, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā, from Abū Ayyūb al-Anṣārī, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Whoever says, ‘There is no god but God alone, without partner. To Him belongs sovereignty and praise, and He has power over all things,’ will have the equivalent of one or two emancipated persons”—Dāwūd was uncertain.

Al-Ḥumaydī related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, saying: Ibn Abī Khālid related to us, from al-Shaʿbī, who said: “Al-Rabīʿ ibn Khuthaym related to me.” I asked, “Who related it to you, may God have mercy on you?”

He said: “ʿAmr ibn Maymūn al-Awdī.” I went to ʿAmr and asked, “Who related it to you?” He said:

“ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā.” I asked, “Who related it to you?” He said: “Abū Ayyūb al-Anṣārī,” who said: “Whoever says, ‘There is no god but God alone, without partner. To Him belongs sovereignty and praise’ (301a), ‘and He has power over all things,’ ten times after dawn will have the equivalent of freeing four slaves from the descendants of Ishmael ﵇.”

ʿĪsā ibn Muḥammad related to me, saying: Muḥammad ibn ʿUbayd informed us, from Sufyān al-ʿUṣfurī, from his father, from Ḥabīb ibn al-Nuʿmān al-Asadī, from Khuraym ibn Fātik, who said: The Prophet ﷺ prayed, and when he had finished, he said: “You have equated false testimony…”

…by associating partners with God, Mighty and Majestic, three times. Then he recited: “So shun the abomination of idols, and shun false speech” (Qurʾān 22:30). Marwān contradicted Muḥammad, and the correct account is the report of Muḥammad.

Abū Muʿāwiyah also transmitted it from Misʿar, from Mūsā ibn Abī Kathīr, from a man whom he did not name, from his father, who said: ʿAbd Allāh said, “I have no doubt that I am a believer.”

I heard al-Ḥumaydī say: An argument broke out between al-Ḥuwayṭī and Marwān al-Fazārī, and they began boasting. Marwān said, “Were glory in the clouds, I would attain it through my grandfather, ʿUyaynah”. He denounced al-Ḥuwayṭī, harmed him, and people shunned him.

I heard Zuhdam ibn al-Ḥārith say: I went to him and said, “Tell me a tradition.” He said:

“I will not tell you a tradition until you gather a group who will assemble before me, and I will tell it to all of you.” I think he may have told him to bring a specified number of people to assemble before him.

“I heard Mahdī ibn Abī Mahdī say: Marwān al-Fazārī had a harsh temperament. He had memorisers [of traditions], and he was burdened with dependants and in great need. People used to be generous to him. When a person showed him generosity, so long as that gift remained in his house, the generosity and warm welcome he showed that person could be seen. He said: I looked and found nothing that would keep better in a man’s house than vinegar, nor anything cheaper in Mecca. So I would buy a jar of vinegar and give it to him as a gift, and I would see the effect it had on him. When it ran out, I would observe him and ask his servant girl, “Has your vinegar run out?” She would say, “Yes.” Then I would buy another jar, and he would return to how he had been”.

“He said: [ʿAlī ibn al-Madīnī was with him.] A man took some books, tore them up, and threw them at Marwān al-Fazārī, saying, ‘This is your tradition.’ He replied, ‘Never! If you are telling the truth, tear up my tradition. This is not my tradition; my backbone is stronger than that.’”124

ʿAlī said: Bilāl and I spoke to him about Wakīʿ. He used to criticise him, so I said to him, “He says that you used to seek out the shaykhs, and that people spoke well of you.” He replied:

“You know me; I know my cousin better. He is a man of the sword.”

It reached me that Ibn Maʿīn said: I saw with Marwān ibn Muʿāwiyah a tablet bearing written traditions and the names of the shaykhs, with notations such as “So-and-so is a Rāfiḍī,” and “So-and-so is such-and-such.” When he came to Wakīʿ’s name, there it was written: “Wakīʿ is a Rāfiḍī.” I said to Marwān, “Wakīʿ is better than you.”

Marwān said to me, “Better than me?” I said, “Yes.” I was asked, “Then did he say nothing to you?”

He said, “Had he said anything to me, the hadith scholars would have jumped up and beaten him.”

“Abū al-Walīd Hishām related to us: Abū Wakīʿ al-Jarrāḥ ibn Mulayḥ related to us; he is trustworthy.”

Abū al-Walīd related to us: ʿUmar ibn Abī Zāʾidah, the brother of Zakariyyā ibn Abī Zāʾidah, who is trustworthy.

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā related to us from Shaqīq ibn Abī ʿAbd Allāh, a trustworthy Kūfan.

Abū ʿĀṣim al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Makhlad related to us from Muḥammad ibn Bishr, a trustworthy Kūfan, from Ziyād ibn ʿAlāqah. This is not Muḥammad ibn Bishr al-ʿAbdī; al-ʿAbdī is also a trustworthy Kūfan.

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā related to us from al-Ḥasan and ʿAlī, the sons of Ṣāliḥ; both are trustworthy.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rajāʾ related to us from Kāmil Abū al-ʿAlāʾ, who is trustworthy.

Sahl ibn ʿĀmir al-Bajalī and Abū Nuʿaym related to us from “Abū Kudaynah Yaḥyā ibn al-Muhallab, who is trustworthy.”

Al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan related to me from Ubayy al-Jawwāb, a trustworthy Kūfan who inclined toward Shīʿism.

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā related to us, saying: al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Ṣāliḥ, a trustworthy Kūfan, informed us from ʿAdī ibn Thābit, an Anṣārī, a Kūfan, and a Shīʿī. He said: Abū Rāshid related to us, saying: When ʿAlī’s pledge of allegiance reached Ḥudhayfah, he said: He placed one of his hands over the other in the pledge, then said:

“I will pledge allegiance after him to no one from Quraysh. After him, there will be only someone younger or one cut off.”125

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā related to us from Abū Isrāʾīl al-Malāʾī, who is trustworthy; his name is Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Isḥāq.

“Saʿīd ibn Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Umawī related to me, saying: My father, Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd, related to us. Both father and son are trustworthy; their home is in Baghdad.”

“ʿUbayd Allāh related to us from Jaʿfar al-Aḥmar, a trustworthy Kūfan.”

(302a) “Ibn ʿUthmān related to us, saying: ʿAbd Allāh related to us, saying: ʿAnbasah ibn Saʿīd, a trustworthy Kūfan and a judge in a locality, informed us.”

“Abū ʿĀṣim related to us from ʿUmar ibn Dharr, a trustworthy Kūfan Murjiʾ.”

ʿUbayd Allāh related to us from Fuḍayl ibn Marzūq, a trustworthy Kūfan.

Yaḥyā ibn Yaḥyā related to us, saying: Hushaym related to us from Ḥuṣayn, from Saʿd ibn ʿUbaydah, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī and Ḥibbān ibn ʿAṭiyyah al-Sulamī: They used to dispute about ʿAlī and ʿUthmān. Ḥibbān loved ʿAlī, while Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān loved ʿUthmān.

Saʿīd ibn Sulaymān related to us, saying: Mubārak ibn Saʿīd related to us, saying: Mūsā al-Juhanī related to us from Abū al-Jahm, who said: I kept company with ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā and ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUkaim for twenty years. This one was an ʿAlid and that one an ʿUthmānī. Each would visit the other’s house on such-and-such a day, and the other would visit on such-and-such a day, once.

The mother of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā died, and ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUkaim led the prayer over her. He had prayed behind Abū Bakr.

Abū Nuʿaym related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us from Abū Farwah Muslim al-Juhanī, who said:

The mother of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā died, and ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUkaim led the prayer over her; he was their imam.

ʿAlī ibn al-Mundhir related to us, saying: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam related to us. Ibn Abī al-ʿAbbās al-Ramlī also related to us, saying: al-Faryābī related to us. Both reported from Sufyān, from Manṣūr, from Ibrāhīm, who said: They used to visit one another, though they differed.

Saʿīd ibn Sulaymān related to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Muṣarrif related to us, saying: al-Aʿmash related to us, saying: I met elders, among them Zirr and Abū Wāʾil; some of them preferred ʿUthmān over ʿAlī, while for others ʿAlī was dearer than ʿUthmān. Yet they were as affectionate toward one another and as deeply devoted to one another as could be.

Ibn Abī ʿUmar related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us. I said to ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Abjar:

“Who is the finest person you have seen in Kūfah?” He did not tell me, but said, “May God have mercy on Ṭalḥah.”

Ṭalḥah is the son of Muṣarrif ibn ʿAmr ibn Kaʿb.

Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥīm Ṣāʿiqah related to me, saying: I heard ʿAlī say—Yaḥyā said:

ʿAwf went to visit al-Ṣalt ibn Dīnār and hired him a donkey from Banū Jammān. ʿAwf was a Shīʿī and al-Ṣalt an ʿUthmānī (302b). They mentioned something, and ʿAwf said to him, “May your side never be raised, Abū Shuʿayb.”126

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and ʿAbd Allāh are the sons of Maʿqil. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān heard from ʿAlī.

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Muʿādh related to us, saying: My father related to me, saying: Shuʿbah related to us from ʿUbayd Abū al-Ḥasan, who heard ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Maʿqil say: I witnessed ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib perform the qunūt in the late-evening prayer, after bowing, and in his qunūt supplicate against five men, including Muʿāwiyah and Abū al-Aʿwar.

He also heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd.

Abū Nuʿaym related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us from ʿAbd al-Karīm, from Ziyād ibn Abī Maryam, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Maʿqil, who said: My father asked ʿAbd Allāh, “Did you hear the Prophet ﷺ—say, ‘Remorse is repentance’?” He replied, “Yes.” Abū ʿĀṣim related to us from Ibn Jurayj, from ʿAbd al-Karīm, from Ziyād, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Maʿqil, who said: I entered with my father to see ʿAbd Allāh, and my father said to him.

Abū ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā related to us from Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid, from Qurrah al-ʿAjalī. No one is known to have transmitted from him or mentioned him in the field of learning except Ismāʿīl.

Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shaybah related to us, saying: Abū Nuʿaym related to us from Ibn Abī Ghanīyah, from Abū al-Khaṭṭāb al-Hajarī. “We know of no one who transmitted from Abū al-Khaṭṭāb or mentioned him in the field of learning except [Ibn] Abī Ghanīyah.” I heard Kurayb ibn Abī Ghanīyah from Abū Nuʿaym, but he was not among the material we had written down or that had been related to us.

Abū ʿĀṣim related to us from Sufyān, from Manṣūr, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿUbaydah, from ʿAbd Allāh, who said: A man from among the Jews, or from the People of the Book, came to the Prophet ﷺ.

Abū Bishr related to me, saying: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd related to us from Sufyān, who said:

Manṣūr and Sulaymān related to me from Ibrāhīm, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh: A Jew came to the Prophet ﷺ. The tradition is ʿUbaydah’s, not al-Aʿmash’s report from ʿAlqamah; that is the version preserved in my view.

Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm al-Makkī related to us from [Ibn] al-Mubārak, from “Yaḥyā ibn Ayyūb al-Bajalī, who is unobjectionable.”

Ibn Rajāʾ related to us from Jarīr, from Ayyūb (303a), who is not strong.

Abū Nuʿaym related to us from Abū ʿĀṣim Muḥammad ibn Abī Ayyūb al-Thaqafī—who is trustworthy—who said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Maʿqil ibn Muqarrin related to me. Abū ʿĀṣim said: So-and-so said to ʿAbd Allāh ibn Maʿqil, “Abū al-Walīd—you can hear me—is turning in prayer disliked?” He replied, “Yes.” The man said, “But you turn around.” He replied, “Indeed, by God, I do.”

I heard al-Ḥasan ibn al-Rabīʿ say: Ibn al-Mubārak said, “Al-Muʿallā ibn Hilāl is unobjectionable until he begins transmitting traditions; when he does, he lies in hadith. ʿAbbād ibn Kathīr was likewise unobjectionable as long as he did not transmit. When he transmitted, he was…”127

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us from “Marḥūm ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz al-ʿAṭṭār, who is trustworthy.”

Our companions related to us from ʿAbd al-Razzāq, from Bishr ibn Rāfiʿ, whose hadith is soft.

Ibn Ẓahīrah related to us from Yaḥyā ibn Ayyūb, from Zayd ibn Abī Jubayrah, a Madinan Anṣārī, weak and objectionable in hadith.

“Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān was a judge in Baghdad, and his hadith is soft.”

“Ibrāhīm ibn al-Faḍl was a Madinan; his hadith is recognised and rejected.”

“Our companions related to us from al-Darāwardī, from Ḥarām ibn ʿUthmān, a Madinan Anṣārī, abandoned [as a transmitter]. I heard Ḥarملah say: al-Shāfiʿī said, ‘Transmitting from Ḥarām is forbidden.’”

Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us from al-Layth ibn Saʿd, from Khālid ibn Yazīd, from Saʿīd ibn Abī Hilāl, from ʿAmr ibn Ṣahbān, who is the maternal uncle of Ibrāhīm ibn [Abī] Yaḥyā. He is objectionable in hadith and weak; as for Ibrāhīm, he is abandoned and shunned.

ʿĪsā ibn Maymūn is a Madinan, objectionable in hadith.

Ibn Abī Uways related to us from Qays ibn ʿAmārah, the client of Sawdah, a Madinan whose hadith is soft.

“Al-Qāsim ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-ʿUmarī is abandoned and shunned.”

Al-Faḍl ibn ʿĪsā al-Raqāshī is a Baṣran, the maternal uncle of al-Muʿtamir; he is “a Muʿtazilī, weak in hadith.”

ʿĪsā ibn [Abī] ʿĪsā: ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā related to us from him. He was a Kūfan who settled in Medina. Sufyān transmitted from him. He is weak. Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Qaṭṭān had seen him, but did not transmit from him and declared him weak. He is ʿĪsā ibn Maysarah al-Ḥannāṭ, who was called al-Khabbāṭ; he used to work with grain and fodder.

Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr was a Sulamī who settled in Baṣrah. His place of prayer was in the mosque of ʿImrān ibn Ḥudayr. He is weak, abandoned, and shunned.

“Bishr ibn Numayr is a Qushayrī from Baṣrah, and weak.” ʿAlī ibn al-Madīnī stopped transmitting from him.

Muḥammad ibn Ghunaym was transmitted from by Muʿtamir. He is weak, abandoned in hadith, and transmitted from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Baylamānī.

Ziyād ibn Maymūn, Abū ʿUmārah, reports from Anas. He is weak, and his hadith is abandoned.

Maṭar ibn Maymūn: ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā reports from him. He is weak. Jald al-Awdī: “ʿUbayd Allāh reported to us from him. He is a Shīʿī; if someone called him a Rāfiḍī, I would not object. He is objectionable in hadith.”

Ḥabīb ibn Ḥassān, a Kūfan, is objectionable in hadith and weak; his hadith is not to be welcomed.

Suhayl ibn Dhakwān is weak, and his hadith is abandoned. Yazīd ibn Hārūn reports from him, and Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd criticized Yazīd for reporting from him.

ʿAbbād ibn Kathīr was originally from Baṣrah and settled in Mecca. “He is remembered for asceticism, austerity, and worship, but his hadith is worthless.” ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rajāʾ al-Makkī al-Muzanī—who is reliable—reported from him, from Azwar ibn Rajāʾ, from al-Taymī, who is weak.

Muḥammad ibn Mūsā al-Aḥmūsī, a Syrian, is weak, weak.

ʿUmar ibn Mūsā ibn Wajīh is sometimes accepted and sometimes rejected.

“Yaḥyā ibn al-ʿAlāʾ al-Rāzī is sometimes accepted and sometimes rejected.”

Furāt ibn al-Sāʾib, a Jazīran, is abandoned and shunned.

Fāʾid, Abū al-Warqāʾ, reports from Ibn Abī Awfā. He is objectionable in hadith and shunned.

Kurayz ibn Ḥakīm: Abū Naṣr al-Tammār reported to us from him, and Hushaym reported from him. He is objectionable in hadith.

“Wāṣil ibn al-Sāʾib is objectionable in hadith and weak.”

Wāziʿ ibn Nāfiʿ is objectionable in hadith.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥarrir al-ʿĀmirī, a Jazīran, is abandoned and weak.

Al-Ḥārith ibn Shibl is shunned and unknown.

Al-Ḥārith ibn Nabḥān, a Baṣran, is objectionable in hadith.

Al-Ḥasan ibn Dīnār is in fact al-Ḥasan ibn Wāṣil; Dīnār was his mother’s husband. He is abandoned.

Saʿīd reported to us: Hushaym reported to us from Abū Sahl—who is Muḥammad ibn Sālim—whose hadith is worth nothing.

“Ismāʿīl ibn Sālim is reliable, unobjectionable, and a Kūfan.”

[Khaythamah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān]

Ismāʿīl ibn al-Khalīl told me: Yūnus ibn Bukayr reported to us from al-Aʿmash from Khaythamah, who said: “A man or two would sit with al-Ḥārith ibn Qays, and he would tell them hadith. When they became numerous, he would get up and leave them. He was one of the best people of Kūfah.”

Ādam reported to us: Shuʿbah reported to us from al-Aʿmash, who said: “I heard Khaythamah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn [Abī] Sabrah.”

Qabīṣah reported to us: Sufyān informed us from al-Aʿmash, who said: “Khaythamah sent for me and for Ibrāhīm. I went, though I do not know what kept Ibrāhīm. When I reached the house, I heard voices and thought they were the sons of Abī Sabrah, so I turned back. He said to me:

“‘What is the matter with you?’ I said, ‘I came, but heard voices and thought they were the sons of Abī Sabrah, so I turned back.’ He said, ‘I am calling them; I am less to them than a piebald dog.’ I said:

“‘Why is that?’ He said, ‘A believer does not love a hypocrite.’”

Abū Nuʿaym reported to us: Sufyān reported to us from al-Aʿmash, from Khaythamah, who said: “Jesus son of Mary said: ‘When food was prepared, he would invite the Qurʾān reciters and provide for them.’” Then he said:

“Do likewise with the Qurʾān reciters.”

Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shaybah reported to us: Abū Khālid reported to us from al-Aʿmash, from Khaythamah, who said: “He invited me. When I arrived, there were men in turbans and cloaks mounted on horses, so I felt insignificant and went back.” He said: “He met me afterward and said to me, ‘Why didn’t you come?’”

I said: “I did come, but I saw men in turbans and cloaks mounted on horses, so I felt insignificant.” He said: “By God, you are dearer to me than they are.” When we entered to see him, he would bring out the basket from under the bed and say, “Eat. By God, I crave it, and I make it only for you.”

Mūsā ibn Masʿūd reported to us: Sufyān reported to us from al-Aʿmash, who said:

“I visited Khaythamah, and he brought us a sweet dish. He said, ‘Know that I did not make it for myself; I made it only for you.’”

Abū Muʿāwiyah reported to us from al-Aʿmash, from Khaythamah, who said: “When death came upon him, he said to his wife, ‘I adjure you by God: do not let anyone who drinks wine enter my house, after the Qurʾān used to be recited in it three times [a day].’” He said: “Before long, she married after his death.”

Ibn Numayr told me: Sulaymān ibn Ḥayyān reported to us from al-Aʿmash, from Khaythamah: “He gave Ibrāhīm a servant. Ibrāhīm did not say, ‘She came to me,’ nor did Khaythamah say, ‘I sent her.’”

Ibn Numayr reported to us: Ḥafṣ reported to us from al-Aʿmash, from Khaythamah: “He used to wrap up dirhams. If he saw that one of his companions’ waist-wraps had worn through, he would slip the money to him and say, ‘Buy such-and-such with it.’”

He also said: Ḥafṣ reported to us from al-Aʿmash, from Khaythamah, who said: “When his family sent a bucket to the leatherworker, he would ask, ‘How much will you charge for it?’ They would say, ‘A dāniq, or a dāniq and a half.’ He would say, ‘I’ll do it. Send this one to so-and-so and that one to so-and-so.’”

Mūsā ibn Masʿūd reported to us: Sufyān reported to us from al-Aʿmash, from Khaythamah, from al-Ḥārith ibn Qays, who said: “ʿAbd Allāh said to me, ‘Ḥārith, why do you see them asking about what they ask about?’ I said, ‘So that they may learn it and then abandon it.’ He said, ‘He spoke truly, by Him besides whom there is no god.’”

Aḥmad ibn Yūnus reported to us: Zuhayr reported to us from ʿUthmān ibn Ḥakīm, who is reliable.

Qabīṣah reported to us: Sufyān reported to us from Muḥammad ibn Juḥādah, who said: “I heard al-Ḥasan say: ‘The Messenger of God ﷺ would accept neither an accusation of illicit sex nor anyone’s testimony against another.’” Muḥammad is a Kūfan, one of the reliable people of Kūfah, and he is al-Awdī.

“Muḥammad ibn Sābiq al-Baghdādī reported to us from Abū Zubayd ʿAbthar, a reliable Kūfan.”

Abū Nuʿaym reported to us: ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Iyād ibn Laqīṭ reported to us. He is a reliable Kūfan, and Iyād is reliable; Sufyān and others reported from him.

Al-Ḥimmānī reported to us: Abū al-Muḥayyā reported to us. He is reliable; Ibn ʿUyaynah and others reported from him.

Abū Nuʿaym reported to us: Sufyān reported to us from “Qābūs ibn Abī Ẓabyān (folio 305a), who is reliable.”

Abū ʿĀṣim reported to us from al-Ḥasan ibn Abī Yazīd, who is Abū Yūnus al-Qawī. He is unobjectionable.

Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shaybah and Ibn Numayr reported to us; they said: Wakīʿ reported to us. He said:

Al-Aʿmash reported to us from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from Abū Ẓabyān—Ibn Numayr said, “He is not Abū Mikhnaf, and he is Qurashī”—that he was with ʿUmar, who asked him, “How much is your stipend?”

He replied, “Four thousand.” ʿUmar said, “Acquire something that I do not regard as expendable, lest you soon be denied your stipend.”

I was told from Sufyān, from “ʿUbaydah ibn Muʿattib al-Ḍabbī, whose hadith is worth—”

“—worth nothing. When al-Thawrī reported from him, he would use his kunya.

Abū ʿAbd al-Karīm said: ‘Sufyān hardly ever used a man’s kunya unless there was some weakness in him.’” He disliked making the man’s name known, lest people shun him.

Muḥammad ibn Bashshār reported to us from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Sufyān, from Mustaghfir al-Bajalī, a Kūfan who is unobjectionable.

Through the same chain, from Sufyān, from Hārūn ibn Abī Wakīʿ. Abū Wakīʿ is ʿAntarah, and Hārūn’s kunya is Abū ʿAmr. He is a reliable Kūfan. Ibn Hārūn’s hadith is worthless.

ʿUbayd Allāh reported to us from Shaybān, from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrāhīm ibn Yazīd al-Taymī. Ibrāhīm ibn Yazīd al-Taymī’s kunya is Abū Asmāʾ.

Abū Nuʿaym and Qabīṣah reported to us; they said: Sufyān reported to us from Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid. Abū Nuʿaym said: from Abū al-Ḥakam, who said: “ʿAbd Allāh said—”

Qabīṣah reported to us: Sufyān reported to us from Ismāʿīl, from Sayyār Abū Ḥamzah, from Ibn Masʿūd, who said: “Give the Qurʾān its proper grammatical inflection, for it is Arabic; and a people will come who will imitate its recitation, but they are not the best among you.”

Ibn Abī Khālid reported from Abū Ḍamrah, from ʿAlī. Abū Ḍamrah is— Saʿd ibn ʿUbaydah is Ṭuhawī, and the daughter of Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī was his wife.

Abū al-Walīd and Sulaymān told me; they said: Shuʿbah reported to us: ʿAmr ibn Murrah informed me: “I heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith relate from Abū Kathīr al-Zubaydī, whose name is ʿAbd Allāh ibn Mālik.” Ibn Numayr reported this to us from Abū Ghassān.

Ibn Numayr reported to us: Ibn Fuḍayl reported to us from al-Aʿmash, who said: “I heard Mujāhid recite: ‘Be mindful of God, in whose name you make requests of one another, and of the ties of kinship’ (Qurʾān 4:1).” Ibrāhīm used to recite it with the yāʾ.

ʿUmar ibn Ḥafṣ told me: My father told me: Al-Aʿmash reported to us:

“Mujāhid told me, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr, who said: ‘Perform the ritual bath after intercourse, on Friday, after a major impurity, after cupping, and after using the razor.’”

Through the same chain, he said: “A man says, ‘O God, I seek refuge in You from the hardship of affliction,’ then falls silent. After saying that, let him add, ‘except for an affliction that brings well-being.’”

Through the same chain, he said: “I heard Mujāhid relate from ʿAbd ibn ʿUmayr, who said: ‘Every day He is engaged in some matter’ (Qurʾān 55:29). He said: ‘Among His matters is freeing a captive, answering a servant, and healing—’” a sick person, or giving to a petitioner.”

Ibn Numayr told me: Wakīʿ reported to us: al-Aʿmash reported to us, saying: “I heard Mujāhid relate from ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr al-Laythī: When the people of Noah were struck by the flood, there was among them a woman with a small child. She lifted him to her waist. When the water reached him, she lifted him to her chest; when the water reached him, she lifted him to her head; when the water reached him, she raised her hands. God—Mighty and Majestic—said: ‘If I were to show mercy to any one of them, I would have shown mercy to her.’”

Al-Ḥajjāj reported to us: Abū ʿAwānah reported to us from al-Aʿmash, who said: “Mujāhid reported to us from ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr that the Bridge is like the edge of a sword: slippery, treacherous. The angels and prophets stand there, saying, ‘Lord, deliver us, deliver us!’ And the angels snatch people with hooks.”

ʿUmar ibn Ḥafṣ told me: My father reported to us: al-Aʿmash reported to us:

“Mujāhid told me: A man brought the Prophet ﷺ a camel he had bought and said, ‘Ask God—Mighty and Majestic—to bless it for me.’ He said, ‘O God, bless it for him.’ It was not long before it died. Then the man bought another and came to him with the same request. It was not long before that camel died too. Then he came to him with a third and said, ‘Messenger of God, you asked God—Mighty and Majestic—to bless the two camels I bought for me. God—Mighty and Majestic—blessed them for me, but it was not long before they died. Ask God—Mighty and Majestic—to make me endure.’ He prayed to God—Mighty and Majestic—and said, ‘O God, make him endure.’ He lived with him for twenty years.”

Ibn Numayr reported to us: my father reported to us: al-Aʿmash reported to us: “I heard Mujāhid say (folio 306a): The Messenger of God ﷺ said: ‘The most insolent of people toward God is one who kills someone other than the killer.’”

Ibn Numayr reported to us: Wakīʿ reported to us: al-Aʿmash reported to us, saying:

“I heard Mujāhid relate from Ṭāwūs, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Prophet ﷺ passed by two graves and said: ‘They are being punished, though they are not being punished for something difficult to avoid. One of them used to spread malicious gossip; the other did not clean himself thoroughly of his urine.’ He called for a fresh palm stalk, split it in two, then planted one piece on this grave and one on the other, and said: ‘Perhaps their punishment will be lightened as long as these have not dried out.’” Through the same chain, al-Aʿmash said: “I heard them relate from Mujāhid: ‘On the day He gathers them’ (Qurʾān 6:128)—he said: ‘The gathering is death.’”

Ibn Numayr reported to us: my father reported to us: al-Aʿmash reported to us, saying: “I used to visit Mujāhid, and he would say, ‘If I were able to walk, I would come to you.’”

Al-Ḥumaydī reported to us: Sufyān reported to us: ʿUmar ibn Saʿīd al-Thawrī told me from al-Aʿmash, who said: “I heard Saʿīd ibn Jubayr.” Ibn Ṭayr told me:

Wakīʿ reported to us: al-Aʿmash reported to us: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr reported to us from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān— From Abū Mūsā, who said: The Prophet ﷺ said: “No one is more patient in the face of harm than God, Mighty and Majestic. They associate partners with Him, yet He provides for them and grants them well-being!” Through the same chain, he said: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr told us: Ibn ʿAyyāsh led us in prayer on a carpet that covered the whole house.

Al-Ḥumaydī told us: Sufyān related to us: al-Aʿmash told us: I heard Saʿīd ibn Jubayr say: Ibn ʿAbbās said: “The witr prayer is seven or five, and I dislike [praying] three as a severed thing.”

Ibn Numayr told us: Abū Muʿāwiyah related to us, from al-Aʿmash, who said: I mentioned to Saʿīd ibn Jubayr ʿAlqamah’s statement concerning the muḥṣan. He said: “That is what Ibn ʿAbbās said.”

Abū ʿUmar al-Numarī informed us: Shuʿbah related to us, from al-Aʿmash, who said: I asked Saʿīd ibn Jubayr about praying on a carpet. He said: “We were with Ibn ʿAbbās, and he led us in prayer on a carpet that covered the whole house.”

ʿUmar ibn Ḥafṣ ibn Ghiyāth told us: My father related to us: al-Aʿmash related to us.

Ibn Numayr told us: Wakīʿ related to us: al-Aʿmash related to us: I heard Saʿīd ibn Jubayr say: “We have indeed written in the Psalms” (21:105)—he said: “The Qurʾān, the Torah, and the Gospel”—“after the Reminder” (21:105)—he said: “The Reminder that is in heaven”—“that the earth shall be inherited by My righteous servants” (21:105). He said: “The earth of Paradise.”

ʿUmar told us: My father related to us: al-Aʿmash related to us: I heard Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, and I asked him about his father: “Did he mention the vision in it?” He said: “A green garden from Paradise.”

Abū Nuʿaym told us: Sufyān related to us, from “Muhājir Abū al-Ḥasan, a trustworthy Kūfan.”

And he said: Sufyān related to us, from Abū Muʿādh al-Tayyās, who is trustworthy.

And he said: Sufyān related to us, from ʿAṭiyyah ibn ʿUthmān al-Thaqafī, from whom Sharīk also narrated; he is trustworthy.

And he said: Sufyān related to us, from Abū Ḥāzim—who is not the Medinan—from Rābiṭah, who is trustworthy.

“He said: Sufyān related to us, from al-Mukhtār ibn Fulful, a trustworthy Kūfan.”

Abū Nuʿaym told us: Sufyān related to us, from Abū al-Jahm, who is trustworthy.

Sufyān’s transmission from Thuwair ibn Abī Fākhitah is weak.

And he said: Sufyān related to us, from al-Qāsim ibn Kathīr, Abū Hāshim, a trustworthy Kūfan: “There is no harm in him.”

He said: Sufyān related to us, from Abū Hilāl, a trustworthy Kūfan; there is no harm in him.

And he said: Sufyān related to us, from ʿAlī, Abū al-Ḥasan, from his grandmother Surayyah, [the wife of] al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī. He is a Kūfan in whom there is no harm.

And he said: Sufyān related to us, from Masʿūd ibn Mālik, who is a trustworthy Kūfan.

And he said: Sufyān related to us, from Salamah ibn al-Minhal, a Kūfan in whom there is no harm.

And he said: Sufyān related to us, from Abū ʿĀṣim al-Ghaṭafānī, whose name is ʿAlī ibn ʿUbayd Allāh. Ibn Idrīs also narrated from him; he is a Kūfan.

Abū ʿĀṣim al-Ghanawī is one from whom Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrates.

And [there is] Abū ʿĀṣim Muḥammad ibn Ayyūb al-Thaqafī.

Abū Nuʿaym told us: Sufyān related to us, from Muṣʿab ibn al-Muthannā, a Kūfan in whom there is no harm.

And he said: Sufyān related to us, from “Yaḥyā ibn ʿUbayd Allāh al-Taymī. There is no harm in him when he narrates from a trustworthy person.”

And he said: Sufyān related to us, from Abū Naṣr, from Sālim ibn Abī al-Jaʿd. Abū Naṣr was in my book as being from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, but I struck that out.

And he said: Sufyān related to us (307a), from Ibrāhīm ibn ʿĀmir, who is Qurashī.

And ʿĀmir ibn Masʿūd: Abū Isḥāq narrated from Numayr ibn ʿArīb, from “this ʿĀmir ibn Masʿūd, who was not a Companion.”

And he said: Sufyān related to us, from ʿUrwah Abū Mahal, a Kūfan.

And he said: Sufyān related to us, from Abū al-Muʿtamir, a Kūfan in whom there is no harm.

And he said: Sufyān related to us, from Abū Rabāḥ, from Abū ʿAmr al-Shaybānī, in whom there is no harm.

And he said: Sufyān related to us, from Ṣāʿid, a Kūfan in whom there is no harm.

And he said: Sufyān related to us, from “Nahshal al-Ḍabbī, in whom there is no harm, a Kūfan.”

He said: Sufyān related to us, from Layth al-Mashrafī, a Kūfan.

And he said: Sufyān related to us, from Abū Mūsā, who said: I heard al-Shaʿbī say: “The Emigrants used to dislike it, but we do it”—meaning the sale of Bedouins.

And he said: Sufyān related to us, from Abū Manṣūr, a Juhanī.

And he said: Sufyān related to us, from Abū Suʿād, a Kūfan in whom there is no harm.

Abū Nuʿaym said: Sufyān related to us, from ʿUmar ibn Rāshid al-Sulamī, a Kūfan.

“Qabīṣah said: ‘ʿAmr ibn Rāshid,’ and he was mistaken.” It is as Abū Nuʿaym said; he narrated from his brother Ismāʿīl ibn Rāshid.

Abū Nuʿaym told us: Hārūn ibn Ibrāhīm al-Thaqafī, a trustworthy Kūfan, related to us.

Ibn Idrīs said: Hārūn ibn Ibrāhīm is Hārūn ibn Abī Ibrāhīm al-Barbarī. I heard some of his descendants reject what Ibn Idrīs said, and say: “We were not Berbers; we are among the clients of Thaqīf.”

Abū Nuʿaym told us: Qubays—who was a shaykh in whom there is no harm—related to us. He said:

“I saw Anas ibn Mālik praying the ḍuḥā prayer in the howdah.”

Abū Nuʿaym told us: Sufyān related to us, from Abū Naṣr al-Tammār, who is ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Sālim ibn Abī al-Jaʿd, from Salmān: “Prayer is a measure.”

Abū Nuʿaym and Qabīṣah told us: They said: Sufyān related to us, from al-ʿAlāʾ ibn ʿAbd al-Karīm, from Abū Karbah—or Karamah.

Abū Nuʿaym said: Sufyān said, from Zādhān, concerning “Indeed, those who do wrong shall have a punishment short of that” (52:47): “The punishment of the grave.”

Abū Nuʿaym told us traditions from al-ʿAlāʾ ibn ʿAbd al-Karīm. Abū Nuʿaym heard from [al-ʿAlāʾ ibn] ʿAbd al-Karīm, and likewise [heard] from Sufyān, from al-ʿAlāʾ.

Abū Nuʿaym told us: He said: Sufyān related to us (307b), from Khuṣayf al-Jazarī, whose teknonym was Abū ʿAwn; there is no harm in him.

Qabīṣah told us: Sufyān related to us, from Ayyūb al-Sakhtiyānī, from Ḥumayd ibn Hilāl, from Hishām ibn ʿĀmir, who said: The Prophet ﷺ said concerning those killed at Uḥud: “Dig deep, do it well, and bury two or three in one grave.”

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb told us: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, from Ayyūb, from Ḥumayd ibn Hilāl, from Saʿd ibn Hishām ibn ʿĀmir, from his father, who said: “The wounds became severe on the day of Uḥud, and this was brought to the Messenger of God ﷺ. He said: ‘Dig, make it wide, do it well, and bury two or three in the grave.’”

ʿAbdān told us: I heard ʿAbd Allāh say: They reported from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: “Dig, make it wide, and dig deep.” ʿAbd Allāh said: “I approve of that.”

Ibn ʿUthmān said: ʿAbd Allāh informed us: Sulaymān ibn al-Mughīrah related to us, from Ḥumayd ibn Hilāl, from Hishām ibn ʿĀmir, who said: “The Anṣār suffered wounds and hardship on the day of Uḥud. So how do you command us?” He said: “Dig, and make it wide.”

ʿAbd Allāh said: “I think it is ‘and dig deep.’” Then ʿAbd Allāh said: “Rather, it is this way.”

I was present with Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb, and when he came to mention this report, he said to me:

“How did Sulaymān ibn al-Mughīrah narrate it? Did you write it down from Sulaymān’s report?” I said: “Yes.” He said:

Ḥumayd ibn Hilāl related to us, from Hishām ibn ʿĀmir al-Anṣārī, who said: “The Anṣār suffered wounds and hardship at Uḥud. The Anṣār came to the Messenger of God ﷺ and said: ‘Messenger of God, we have suffered wounds and hardship. How do you command us?’ He said: ‘Dig, make it wide, and place two or three in one grave.’” I mentioned Qabīṣah’s transmission to him, and he gave particular weight to Sulaymān ibn al-Mughīrah’s report.

Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad al-Shāfiʿī told us: al-Ḥārith ibn ʿUmayr related to us, from Sulaymān, from Ḥumayd ibn Hilāl, from Hishām ibn ʿĀmir, who said: The Prophet ﷺ said (308a): “Dig, make it wide, do it well, and bury two or three in a grave.”

Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān told me: I heard ʿAlī say: Bahz said: I asked Ḥammād ibn Salamah about the report of Thābit, from Anas: “A Bedouin asked the Prophet ﷺ about prayer and almsgiving.” He said: “This is only a disconnected report from Thābit.” I said: “It is Sulaymān ibn al-Mughīrah.” He said: “He used to ask me about the reports of Thābit.”

Al-Faḍl ibn Ziyād told me, from Abū Ṭālib, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh, who said:

He was asked about Sulaymān ibn al-Mughīrah. He said: “Was Sulaymān not reliable?” He was asked:

“When did he write this from Ḥumayd ibn Hilāl?” He said: “Because of how often he went to him during the al-rawghāt.”128

Abū Ṭālib said, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh: He said: I asked him about Ḥammād ibn Salamah.

He said: “Ḥammād ibn Salamah is among the best of God’s righteous servants. Who has gathered as much of the Sunnah as he has? Ayyūb said: ‘Bring us someone like our young man Ḥammād!’”

Abū ʿAbd Allāh said: “One day a man said, ‘Knowledge is with Shuʿbah, Sufyān, and Ḥammād.’ I objected to his placing Ḥammād on a par with Shuʿbah and Sufyān, for I was not familiar with Ḥammād’s ḥadīth. But when I wrote down his ḥadīth, I realized that the man had spoken truly: Ḥammād is indeed a scholar.”

Hadīyah ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb told me, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Shaqīq, who said:

ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mubārak said: “The ḥadīth of Ḥammād ibn Salamah has baffled me.”

Al-Faḍl told me: I heard Abū ʿAbd Allāh being asked, “What do you think of Ḥammād ibn Salamah?” He said: “How excellent!”

ʿAlī said: I heard ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī say: “There are two men whose ḥadīth, when I write it all down as it is, I find [to contain things I would omit]; but when I select from it, it is good: Maʿmar and Ḥammād ibn Salamah.”

ʿAlī said: Sufyān said: “We met ʿAmr ibn Dīnār when his teeth had fallen out and only his canine tooth remained. Had we not spent a long time sitting with him, we would not have understood his speech.”

Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥīm told me: I heard ʿAlī ibn al-Madīnī say:

Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd said: ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUmar said: “When Ibn Shihāb arrived, I went to him, but he did not answer me. I said: ‘My fathers did not use to treat you this way.’ He said: ‘Who are you?’ I traced my lineage for him.”

He said: “Yes.” I went to Mālik and took his book (308b). He said: “It must be heard.” So we heard part of it, and part remained.

Al-Ḥumaydī told us: Sufyān related to us: I saw ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUmar and Mālik ibn Anas come to al-Zuhrī in Mecca and speak with him. He said: “I intend to go to Medina, and my route takes me past you two. Come to me in Medina, God willing.”

Sufyān said: “ʿUbayd Allāh was the one who spoke, and Mālik was with him. Neither of them heard anything from him in Mecca.”

Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥīm told me: ʿAlī informed us: al-Aṣmaʿī related to us, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUmar al-ʿUmarī, who said: “I saw Mālik reciting to al-Zuhrī. He said: ‘This man is dull; bring someone else.’”

Al-ʿAbbās told us: ʿAbd al-Razzāq related to us: ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUmar said to me:

“What we, Yaḥyā, and Mālik took from Ibn Shihāb was only by reading aloud to him. Mālik used to read to us, and he read well.”

Al-ʿAbbās said: ʿAlī told me: I heard ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī say: I asked Mālik—meaning about his hearing from al-Zuhrī. He said: “The least of it was by presentation [to the teacher].”

Al-ʿAbbās said: ʿAlī informed me, from Yaḥyā, who said: I said to Ibn al-Mubārak:

“Write down for me the report of the Slander, from Maʿmar.” He said: “If you wish, I will write it down for you from Maʿmar, by reading aloud; or, if you wish, I will write it down for you from Yūnus, from dictation.” I said: “I do not want it.”

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad ibn Dhakwān al-Dimashqī told me: ʿIrāk ibn Khālid ibn Yazīd ibn Ṣāliḥ ibn Ṣubayḥ al-Murrī related to us, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿAṭāʾ, from his father, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: When the Messenger of God ﷺ was offered condolences for his daughter Ruqayyah, the wife of ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān, he said: “Praise be to God. The burial of daughters is among the acts of honor.”

Al-Ḥajjāj ibn Abī Manīʿ told us: My grandfather related to me, from al-Zuhrī, who said:

“Ruqayyah died at the time of Badr, and ʿUthmān stayed behind to bury her. That is what kept him from witnessing Badr. Ruqayyah, the daughter of the Messenger of God ﷺ died on the day Zayd ibn Ḥārithah, the client of the Messenger of God ﷺ arrived bringing the good news of the victory at Badr.”

As for Umm Kulthūm, the daughter of the Messenger of God ﷺ she too married ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān, after her sister Ruqayyah, the daughter of the Messenger of God ﷺ. She then died while with him, and bore no children.

Hānī ibn al-Mutawakkil al-Iskandarānī told me: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Lahīʿah al-Ḥaḍramī related to me (309a), from ʿUqayl ibn Khālid, from Ibn Shihāb, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “ʿUthmān, here is Gabriel, commanding me by the command of my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, to marry you to Umm Kulthūm for a dower like hers—that is, Ruqayyah’s dower—and with a marriage like hers.” The Messenger of God ﷺ married her to him.

“ʿĪsā ibn Marḥūm al-ʿAṭṭār told us: My father related to us, from Dāwūd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥurr, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: ‘Is there no father of an unmarried woman? Is there no brother of an unmarried woman to marry ʿUthmān? For I married my two daughters to him, and they both died—’”

“Were I to have a third daughter, I would marry her to him. I married him only by revelation from heaven.”

Al-Ḥajjāj related to us: Abū ʿAwānah related to us, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Mawhib, who said: A man from Egypt came to Ibn ʿUmar and said, “Do you know that ʿUthmān stayed behind from Badr and did not witness it?” He replied, “Yes. He was married to a daughter of the Messenger of God ﷺ—and she fell ill. The Messenger of God ﷺ—said to him, ‘You have the reward and share of a man who witnessed Badr.’”

Al-Ḥasan ibn al-Rabīʿ related to us: Ibn Idrīs related to us, from Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq, who said: At the time of the conquest, the Messenger of God ﷺ—sent ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rawāḥah to the people of al-ʿĀliyah with news of the victory, and Zayd ibn Ḥārithah to the people of al-Sāfilah. Usāmah said: “The news reached us as we were leveling the grave over Ruqayyah, the daughter of the Messenger of God ﷺ—who had been married to ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān. The Messenger of God ﷺ—had left me behind with ʿUthmān to care for her.”

Al-Ḥumaydī related to us: Sufyān related to us: al-Zuhrī related to us, saying:

ʿAnbasah ibn Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ informed me, from Abū Hurayrah, who said: “I came to the Messenger of God ﷺ—and his Companions at Khaybar after they had conquered it.”

Saʿīd ibn Abī Maryam related to us: al-Darāwardī informed us: Khushaym ibn ʿIrāk ibn Mālik related to me, from his father, from Abū Hurayrah, who said: “The Messenger of God ﷺ—set out after appointing Sibāʿ ibn ʿUrfuṭah over Medina.” Abū Hurayrah said: “I came to Medina as an emigrant and prayed the dawn prayer behind Sibāʿ.”

Al-Ḥajjāj related to us: Ḥammād related to us, from ʿAlī ibn Zayd (309b), from ʿAmmār ibn Abī ʿAmmār, from Abū Hurayrah, who said: “I never witnessed a battle with the Messenger of God ﷺ—in which he did not allot me a share, except Khaybar, for it was exclusively for the people of al-Ḥudaybiyah. Abū Mūsā and Abū Hurayrah had arrived between al-Ḥudaybiyah and Khaybar.”

Aḥmad ibn Yūnus related to us: Zuhayr related to us. Ḥāʾ.

And Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr related to us: Abū ʿAwānah related to us—both from Dāwūd ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Awdī, from Ḥumayd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Ḥimyarī, who related to them, saying:

“I met a man among the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ—who had accompanied him for four years, just as Abū Hurayrah had accompanied him.”

Al-Ḥumaydī related to us: Sufyān related to us: Ismāʿīl related to us, saying: I heard Qays say: “I heard Abū Hurayrah say, ‘I accompanied the Messenger of God ﷺ—for three years.’”

Ibn Numayr related to me: My father related to us: Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid related to us, from Qays ibn Abī Ḥāzim, who said: We entered upon Abū Hurayrah, and he said: “I accompanied the Messenger of God ﷺ—for three years. Never in any years was I more attentive, nor did I ever have a greater desire to retain what the Messenger of God ﷺ—said than I did during them. I saw the Messenger of God ﷺ—gesturing with his hand and saying: ‘Shortly before the Hour, you will fight a people whose sandals are made of hair. You will fight a people with red faces and small eyes, as though their faces were hammered shields. By God, if one of you were to go out in the morning, gather firewood on his back, sell it, and use the proceeds for his needs or give them in charity, that would be better for him than going to a man and asking him, and being refused or given something. That is because the upper hand is better than the lower hand. Begin with those for whom you are responsible.
