And the changed breath of the fasting person’s mouth is more pleasing to God than the scent of musk.”

Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr related to us: Abū al-Aḥwaṣ related to us, from Bayān, from Qays ibn Abī Ḥāzim, who said: Abū Hurayrah said: “I accompanied the Messenger of God ﷺ—for three years, during which I was more attentive than ever.” He then related something similar. He said, “more pleasing.” Jarīr related it this way as well.

Likewise, al-Khalīl ibn ʿAmr al-Karkhī related to me: Muḥammad ibn Salamah al-Ḥarrānī related to us, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥīm, from Zayd ibn Abī Unaysah, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from al-Muṭṭalib, from Abū Hurayrah, who said: “I entered upon Ruqayyah, the daughter of the Messenger of God ﷺ—and wife of ʿUthmān, while she had a comb in her hand. She said: ‘The Messenger of God ﷺ—has just left me; I combed his hair.’ He said to me, ‘What do you think of Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān?’ I replied, ‘He is good.’ He said, ‘Treat him generously, for among my Companions he most resembles me in character.’”

Maḥfūẓ ibn Abī Tawbah related to me: ʿAffān related to us: Ḥammād related to us, from Thābit, from Anas, who said: “When Ruqayyah, the daughter of the Messenger of God ﷺ—died, the Messenger of God ﷺ—said, ‘Let no one who was intimate with his wife last night enter the grave.’” He said: “So ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān stepped aside.”

ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān related to us: ʿAbd Allāh informed us: Fulayḥ ibn Sulaymān related to us, from Hilāl ibn ʿAlī, from Anas ibn Mālik, who said: “We attended the funeral of a daughter of the Messenger of God ﷺ. The Messenger of God ﷺ—was sitting beside the grave, and I saw his eyes shedding tears. He said, ‘Is there among you a man who did not have intercourse last night?’ Abū Dharr and Abū Ṭalḥah said”—ʿAbd Allāh said, “My recollection is that it was Abū Ṭalḥah”—“‘I am, Messenger of God ﷺ.’ He said, ‘Then descend into her grave.’” Fulayḥ said: “I thought he meant sin.”

ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān related to us: ʿAbd Allāh related to us: Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī. Ḥāʾ. And Mahdī ibn Abī Mahdī related to me: Hishām ibn Yūsuf related to us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī. Ḥāʾ.

And Muḥammad ibn al-Faḍl related to us: Saʿīd ibn Zayd related to us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from Anas ibn Mālik, who said: “I saw Zaynab, the daughter of the Messenger of God—may God bless him and grant him peace—wearing a striped silk garment.”

Abū al-Yamān related to us: Shuʿayb informed me. Ḥāʾ.

And Ḥajjāj related to us: my grandfather related to us—both from al-Zuhrī. Ḥāʾ.

And ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yūsuf related to us: Yaḥyā ibn Ḥamzah related to us: Muḥammad ibn al-Walīd related to me, from al-Zuhrī, from Anas ibn Mālik, who said: “He saw Umm Kulthūm, the daughter of the Messenger of God ﷺ—wearing a striped silk garment.”

Abū Bakr ﵁

Al-Ḥajjāj ibn Abī Manīʿ related to us: my grandfather related to us, from al-Zuhrī, who said: “Abū Bakr ibn Abī Quḥāfah ibn ʿĀmir ibn ʿAmr ibn Kaʿb ibn Saʿd ibn Taym ibn Murrah ibn Kaʿb ibn Luʾayy ibn Ghālib ibn Fihr. Abū Bakr’s name was ʿAtīq, and Abū Quḥāfah’s name was ʿUthmān.”

Abū Ḥafṣ ﵁

“ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb ibn Nufayl ibn ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā ibn Riyāḥ ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Qurṭ ibn Razāḥ ibn ʿAdī ibn Kaʿb ibn Luʾayy ibn Ghālib ibn Fihr.”

“ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān ﵁

He was at first given the teknonym Abū ʿAbd Allāh, and afterward the teknonym Abū ʿAmr; he was known by both. ʿAffān ibn Abī al-ʿĀṣ ibn Umayyah ibn ʿAbd Shams ibn ʿAbd Manāf ibn Quṣayy ibn Kilāb ibn Murrah ibn Kaʿb ibn Luʾayy ibn Ghālib ibn Fihr” “ibn Mālik ibn al-Naḍr ibn Kinānah ibn Khuzaymah ibn Mudrikah—and Mudrikah’s name was ʿĀmir—ibn Ilyās ibn Muḍar ibn Nizār ibn Saʿd ibn ʿAdnān ibn Add ibn Muqawwim ibn Nāḥūr ibn Yafraḥ ibn Yaʿrub ibn Yashjub ibn Thābit ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Ibrāhīm, the Intimate Friend.”

“ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, Abū al-Ḥasan ﵁

Abū Ṭālib’s name was ʿAbd Manāf ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib; ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib’s name was Shaybah ibn Hāshim; Hāshim’s name was ʿAmr ibn ʿAbd Manāf; ʿAbd Manāf’s name was al-Mughīrah ibn Quṣayy ibn Kilāb ibn Murrah ibn Kaʿb ibn Luʾayy ibn Ghālib ibn Fihr ibn Mālik ibn al-Naḍr.

Ṭalḥah ibn ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān ibn ʿAmr ibn Kaʿb ibn Saʿd ibn Taym ibn Murrah ibn Kaʿb ibn Luʾayy ibn Ghālib ibn Fihr ibn Mālik. He was given the teknonym Abū Muḥammad.”

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Ḥafṣ related this to me, saying: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ḥammād related to us, from ʿImrān ibn Mūsā ibn Ṭalḥah, who said: Ṭalḥah ibn Yaḥyā ibn Ṭalḥah related to us, from his father, from his father, from Ṭalḥah ibn ʿUbayd Allāh, who said: “I entered upon the Prophet ﷺ—while he had a quince in his hand. He tossed it to me—or said: he handed it to me—and said, ‘Here, Abū Muḥammad; it invigorates the heart.’”

“Al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwām ibn Khuwaylid ibn Asad (311a) ibn ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā ibn Quṣayy ibn Kilāb ibn Murrah ibn Kaʿb ibn Luʾayy ibn Ghālib ibn Fihr ibn Mālik ibn al-Naḍr ibn Kinānah.

Saʿd ibn Mālik:

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us: Sufyān related to us: Ibn Judʿān related to us, from Saʿīd, who said: Saʿd came to the Prophet ﷺ—and said, ‘Messenger of God, who am I?’ He replied, ‘You are Saʿd ibn Mālik ibn Wuhayb ibn ʿAbd Manāf ibn Zuhrah. Whoever says otherwise, upon him be the curse of God.’ Sufyān said: ‘Once, in this report, I think it was Ibn Saʿd.’ Zuhrah was ibn Kilāb ibn Murrah ibn Kaʿb ibn Luʾayy ibn Ghālib ibn Fihr ibn Mālik ibn al-Naḍr.

Abū Muḥammad ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf ibn ʿAbd ʿAwf ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Zuhrah ibn Kilāb ibn Murrah ibn Kaʿb ibn Luʾayy ibn Ghālib ibn Fihr ibn Mālik.

Abū al-Aʿwar Saʿīd ibn Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Nufayl ibn ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā ibn Riyāḥ ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Qurṭ ibn Razāḥ ibn ʿAdī ibn Kaʿb ibn Luʾayy ibn Ghālib ibn Fihr ibn Mālik.

‘Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ—his name was ʿĀmir ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Jarrāḥ ibn Hilāl ibn Uhayb ibn Ḍabbah ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Fihr’ had no descendants.

Al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī was given the teknonym Abū Muḥammad.

Al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī was given the teknonym Abū ʿAbd Allāh.

Al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib was given the teknonym Abū al-Faḍl.”

“ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās was given the teknonym Abū al-ʿAbbās.

Jaʿfar ibn Abī Ṭālib was given the teknonym Abū [ʿAbd Allāh].”

ʿAqīl ibn Abī Ṭālib was given the teknonym Abū Yazīd.

Abū Marthad Kannāz ibn Ḥiṣn al-Ghanawī, confederate of Ḥamzah ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib; a veteran of Badr.

Wāthilah ibn al-Asqaʿ, who was given the teknonym Abū al-Asqaʿ.

Abū Sufyān Ṣakhr ibn Ḥarb ibn Umayyah ibn ʿAbd Shams.

Ḥajjāj related to us: my grandfather related to us, from al-Zuhrī, who said: “Abū Sufyān Ṣakhr ibn Ḥarb ibn Umayyah ibn ʿAbd Shams ibn ʿAbd Manāf ibn Quṣayy ibn Kilāb ibn Murrah ibn Kaʿb ibn Luʾayy ibn Ghālib ibn Fihr.

Umm Ḥabībah’s name was Ramlah.

Ḥakīm ibn Ḥizām ibn Khuwaylid ibn Asad was given the teknonym Abū Khālid.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd was given the teknonym Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān. He was of Hudhayl, a confederate of Banū Zuhrah and their sister’s son.

Khabbāb ibn al-Aratt ibn Jandal ibn Saʿd ibn Khuzaymah ibn Kaʿb ibn Sufyān: an emigrant and veteran of Badr, a client of Banū Zuhrah. (311b) Al-Miqdād ibn ʿAmr al-Bahrānī, confederate of Banū Zuhrah.

Dhū al-Shimālayn ibn ʿAmr ibn Naḍlah ibn ʿAbshān ibn Sulaym ibn Mālik ibn Afṣā al-Khuzāʿī, confederate of Banū Zuhrah and veteran of Badr.

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and Sharḥabīl, the sons of Ḥasanah, confederates of Banū Zuhrah.”

Ibn Bukayr said: “They are from Ghawth.”

Ṣuhayb ibn Sinān was given the teknonym Abū Yaḥyā and was a client of Ibn Judʿān. It is said that he belonged to al-Namir ibn Qāsiṭ; he came to him through capture.

Abū Salamah—whose name was ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Asad ibn Hilāl ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn Makhzūm—was a veteran of Badr and among those who emigrated to Abyssinia.

Khālid ibn al-Walīd al-Makhzūmī was given the teknonym Abū Sulaymān.

ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir was given the teknonym Abū al-Yaqẓān. He was a client of Abū Ḥudhayfah ibn al-Mughīrah al-Makhzūmī. It is said that he was ʿAbsī and had been captured.

Safīnah, Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān—whose name was Aḥmar—was a client of Umm Salamah.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar, Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān.

Ṣafwān ibn Umayyah ibn Khalaf ibn ʿAmr ibn Ḥudhāfah ibn Jumāḥ was given the teknonym Abū Wahb.

Abū Maḥdhūrah, Samurah ibn Mughīrah al-Ḥabshamī.

ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil ibn Hāshim ibn Saʿd ibn Sahm was given the teknonym Abū ʿAbd Allāh.

ʿAmr ibn Umm Maktūm, the blind man, was one of Banū ʿĀmir ibn Luʾayy.

Abū Dharr, Jundab ibn Junādah al-Ghifārī, then al-Kinānī.

Ḥudhayfah ibn Usayd was given the teknonym Abū Sarīḥah; he was Ghifārī.

Abū Qurṣāfah—whose name was Jandarah ibn Khayshanah ibn Naqīr ibn Murrah ibn ʿAriyah ibn Dāyah ibn al-Fākih ibn ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Mālik ibn al-Naḍr ibn Kinānah—was a Companion who settled in Palestine.”

Nuqādah ibn Zayd ibn Mālik al-Asadī.

Muʿāwiyah ibn Qurrah ibn al-Aghar al-Muzanī.

Abū Juḥayfah Wahb al-Suwāʾī, then al-ʿĀmirī.

Abū Ḥājiz Yazīd ibn ʿĀmir al-Suwāʾī.

Abū Zirr Laqīṭ ibn ʿĀmir ibn al-Muntafiq al-ʿĀmirī, then one of Banū ʿAqīl.

Bahz ibn Ḥakīm ibn Muʿāwiyah ibn Ḥaydah al-Qushayrī.

Abū Hurayrah: [his name was] ʿAbd Shams; it is also said, rather, ʿAbd Fahm ibn ʿĀmir; and it is also said:

ʿAbd Ghanam; and it is also said: Sukayn.

Abū ʿAyyāsh al-Zuraqī—his name was Zayd ibn al-Nuʿmān; it is also said, Ibn al-Ṣāmit.

Abū al-Ṭufayl ʿĀmir ibn Wāthilah al-Bakrī.

Abū Bakrah, Nufayʿ ibn al-Ḥārith.

Abū Barzah (312a), Naḍlah ibn ʿUbayd.

Abū al-Dardāʾ, ʿUwaymir ibn ʿĀmir.

Abū Umāmah al-Ṣudayy ibn ʿAjlān al-Bāhilī, from the line of Sahm of Bāhilah.

Abū Ḥumayd, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Saʿīd ibn al-Mundhir.

Abū Ruhm al-Ghifārī, Kulthūm ibn al-Ḥuṣayn. Ḥāmid related this to me, from Ṣadaqah, from Ibn Isḥāq, from Ibn Shihāb ibn Ibn Ukaymah, from the nephew of Abū And they [transmitted] from Abū Ruhm Kulthūm ibn al-Ḥuṣayn.

Abū Ṣirma Mālik ibn Qays al-Māzinī.

Yazīd ibn Abī Maryam; Abū Maryam’s name was Mālik ibn Rabīʿa.

Abū Thaʿlaba al-Khushanī, Jurhum ibn Nāshij. Abū Mushir said: “I heard Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz say: ‘Abū Thaʿlaba’s name was Jurthūm.’”

Ibn Mirbaʿ was named Zayd ibn Mirbaʿ.

Abū al-Yamān related to me—or it was read aloud to him—from Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, who said: “ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām’s name was al-Ḥuṣayn, and the Messenger of God ﷺ named him ʿAbd Allāh. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf’s name was ʿAbd ʿAmr, and the Messenger of God ﷺ named him ʿAbd al-Raḥmān. ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī ibn Salūl’s name was al-Ḥubāb, and the Messenger of God ﷺ named him ʿAbd Allāh.”

Our companions related to us, from Aḥmad, who said: Abū Dāwūd related to us; he said: Shuʿba related to us, from ʿAmr ibn Murra, who said: “At the time of the Battle of al-Jamājim, on the day of al-Jamājim, the Qurʾān-reciting scholars wanted to appoint Abū al-Bakhtarī as their leader. Abū al-Bakhtarī said: ‘I am a man from the clients, so appoint as your leader a man from the Arabs.’ They appointed as their leader a man from the Arabs.

Abū Wahb al-Jayshānī was al-Daylam ibn al-Huwayshiʿ.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Maslama related to me; he said: Yaʿqūb and Ḥammād related to us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd, from his father: “ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar said to my father, ‘O Abū Khālid.’”

Ibn Bukayr and Abū al-Ṭāhir related to us. They said: Ibn Wahb related to us; he said:

Hishām ibn Saʿd informed me, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, who said: “ʿUmar said to me, ‘O Abū Khālid.’”

Aḥmad said: “Abū Maryam al-Ḥanafī’s name was Iyās ibn Ṣubayḥ.”

Aḥmad said: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd related to us; he said: “I asked Shuʿba, ‘How much did you hear from Abū Maʿshar?’ He replied, ‘Four incomplete [reports].’”

Aḥmad said: Sufyān related to us; he said: “Yūsuf ibn ʿUmar came to us in Kūfa when I was thirteen years old. (312b) Yūsuf appointed Ibn Abī Laylā to the judgeship. He had first appointed Ibn Shubrumah, then removed him and sent him to Sijistān to oversee the treasury.”

Salama related to me; he said: Aḥmad related to us; he said: Sufyān related to us; he said:

“I kept company with Ibn Jurayj when he was forty-three. He would say to me, ‘Read to me so that I may explain it to you.’”

I was told, from ʿAffān, who said: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd related to me; he said: “I asked Shuʿba, Sufyān ibn Saʿīd, Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna, and Mālik ibn Anas about a man who does not retain reports or is suspected regarding ḥadīth. They all said, ‘His condition is clear.’”

Salama related to us; he said: Aḥmad related to us; he said: Abū ʿĀmir ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿAmr related to us; he said: “I heard Shuʿba say: ‘I saw Ḥabīb ibn Sālim, and I saw Muḥammad ibn al-Muntashir.’”

Aḥmad said: Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad related to us; he said: Shuʿba related to us, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā, from his brother. “I had seen his brother”—meaning ʿĪsā ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān.

Abū al-Waddāk Jabr ibn Nawf. Abū Ṣāliḥ related this to us; he said: Muʿāwiya ibn Ṣāliḥ related to me, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa, that Abū al-Waddāk Jabr ibn Nawf informed him.

Wāthila ibn al-Asqaʿ, Abū al-Asqaʿ. Abū Ṣāliḥ related this to us; he said: Muʿāwiya ibn Ṣāliḥ related to me, from al-ʿAlāʾ ibn al-Ḥārith, from Makhūl, who said: “Abū al-Azhar and I entered upon Wāthila ibn al-Asqaʿ, and I said, ‘O Abū al-Asqaʿ!’”

Abū Ṭalḥa al-Anmārī, Nuʿaym ibn Ziyād. Abū Ṣāliḥ related this to us; he said:

Muʿāwiya ibn Ṣāliḥ related to me; he said: Abū Ṭalḥa Nuʿaym ibn Ziyād related to me. He transmitted the report of al-Nuʿmān ibn Bashīr about the Prophet’s ﷺ night prayer in Ramaḍān.

Sulaymān ibn ʿĀmir, whose teknonym was Abū Laylā, was Kalāʿī.

Abū ʿĀmir al-Hawzanī: al-Azhar ibn ʿAbd Allāh transmitted from Abū ʿĀmir ʿAbd Allāh ibn Laḥy.

ʿUfayr ibn Maʿdān, Abū ʿĀʾidh, the muezzin, was Yaḥṣabī; Abū al-Yamān gave us his lineage.

Abū al-Yamān related to us; he said: Ṣafwān related to us that ʿUtba ibn ʿAbd al-Sulamī was named Nashba (313a), but the Prophet ﷺ changed his name and named him ʿUtba.

[Abū] al-Yamān related to us; he said: Ṣafwān related to us, from Abū al-Yamān ʿĀmir ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Laḥy al-Hawzanī.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Busr had the teknonym Abū Ṣafwān. Abū al-Yamān related this to us; he said:

Ṣafwān related to us, from Sawāda and ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥajjāj, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Jundī, who said:

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Busr said to me, “O son of al-Jundī!” I replied, “At your service, Abū Ṣafwān. (316a)

And Abū Ḥabīb al-Ḥārith ibn Muḥammad, the judge. Abū al-Yamān related this to us, from Ṣafwān.

And Abū Idrīs ʿĀʾidh Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Khawlānī. Al-Rabīʿ ibn Rawḥ related this to us, from Muḥammad ibn Ḥarb, who said: Al-Zubaydī related to us, from Yūnus ibn Sayf al-Kalāʿī, from Abū Idrīs ʿĀʾidh Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Khawlānī.

Abū al-Yamān related to us; he said: Abū Bakr ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Maryam al-Ghassānī related to us, from ʿAṭiyya ibn Qays al-Kilābī.

And Abū Baḥriyya ʿAbd Allāh ibn Qays, the companion of Muʿādh ibn Jabal, from whom he transmitted excellent reports.

Al-Haytham ibn Mālik, a Ṭāʾī.

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Faḍāla, Abū Dharr, related to us; Abū al-Yamān related to us; he said: Ḥurayz related to us.

Ḥibbān ibn Zayd, whose teknonym was Abū Khirāsh.

And ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Maysara, a Ḥaḍramī.

And Saʿīd ibn Marthad al-Raḥbī.

Sulaymān ibn Bashīr, an Alhānī.

And Ḥabīb ibn ʿUbayd, a Raḥbī.

Abū al-Yamān related to us; he said: Ḥurayz related to us; he said: “I saw Marthad ibn Busr, who was among those who lived into the time of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib.”

Abū Nuʿaym related to us; he said: Misʿar related to us. He was Misʿar ibn Kidām ibn Ẓuhayr ibn ʿUbayd ibn al-Ḥārith.

Abū Nuʿaym said: Misʿar related to us; he said: “I saw Muslim al-Baṭīn satirizing the Murjiʾa, and I said to him, ‘Glory be to God!’”

Abū Nuʿaym related to us; he said: Mushir related to us; he said: “Khaythama ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān had a basket of khabīṣ. Whenever the Qurʾān-reciting scholars—or, he said, his companions—came, he would bring it out for them.”

Abū Nuʿaym related to us; he said: ʿĪsā ibn Muḥammad, Abū Hammām, related to us. Abū Nuʿaym said:

“Sufyān held this shaykh in great esteem.”

Abū Nuʿaym related to us; he said: Abū Ḥurayz the baker related to us—and he praised him highly.

Abū Nuʿaym said: “This Abū Ḥurayz is not that one”—meaning the shaykh of ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā.

Abū Nuʿaym related to us; he said: Bishr ibn al-Hazhāz ibn Yazan al-Rawāsī related to us.

Abū Nuʿaym related to us; he said: al-ʿAlāʾ ibn ʿAbd al-Karīm al-Yāmī related to us.

And Saʿīd ibn Ṣāliḥ al-Asadī.

And Qays ibn Sulaym al-ʿAnbarī.

And Abū Rifāʿa al-ʿĀmirī.

And ʿAmr ibn Ḥassān al-Muslī.

And ʿImrān ibn Abī Muslim (316b), a shaykh who was among the Juhayna.

And Muḥammad ibn Abī al-Jaʿd, a shaykh who was among Banū al-Waṣṣāf.

And Abū Salām al-Ḥanafī.

And Ḥammād ibn Abī al-Dardāʾ al-Anṣārī.

And Saʿd ibn Sinān, Abū Sinān al-Shaybānī.

And Mujammiʿ ibn Yaḥyā al-Anṣārī.

And ʿĪsā ibn al-Musayyab said: “Qays ibn Abī Ḥāzim asked for the milk of a milch camel.” I said to ʿĪsā, “Did you hear this from Qays?” He replied, “Do you think I would lie about him?”

And Suwayd ibn Najīḥ, Abū Quṭba.

And Yūsuf ibn Muhājir al-Ḥaddād.

Ḥusayn related to me; he said: Sufyān related to me, from Yūsuf ibn Muhājir al-Ḥaddād. Sufyān said: “He was trustworthy.”

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā related to us, from Ḥashraj ibn Nubāta— a trustworthy Kūfan— from “Saʿīd ibn Jumhān—a trustworthy Baṣran—”.

Abū Nuʿaym related to us; he said: Razīn, the pomegranate seller, related to us, from al-Shaʿbī: “Zayd ibn Thābit pronounced four takbīrs over his mother.” He said: “Then a riding beast was brought, and Ibn ʿAbbās took hold of the stirrup for him.”

Zayd said, “Leave him”—or, “Let him be.” Ibn ʿAbbās said, “No, this is how we treat the great scholars.” Razīn was the patterned-cloth seller, and he was trustworthy; al-Thawrī transmitted from him.

Abū Nuʿaym and Qabīṣa related to us; they said: Sufyān related to us, from Zubayd, from Ibrāhīm, from Masrūq, from ʿAbd Allāh, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “He is not one of us who slaps his cheeks, tears his garments, and calls out with the call of the Jāhiliyya.” Zubayd was trustworthy and inclined toward Shīʿism, and Sufyān did not hear from Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif.

Qabīṣa related to us; he said: Sufyān related to us, from al-Aʿmash and Manṣūr, from Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwsaja, from al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: “God—mighty and majestic—and His angels bless the front rows.”

“Adorn the Qurʾān with your voices.” Muslim ibn Ibrāhīm related to us; he said: Shuʿba related to us, from Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwsaja, from al-Barāʾ, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: “Whoever gives the use of silver as a loan, guides someone along a road, or gives milk to drink, it is equivalent for him to freeing a slave. And whoever says, ‘There is no god but God alone, without partner,’ it is equivalent for him to freeing a slave.”

“When we stood for prayer, we would straighten our ankles129 and say, ‘Straighten your rows; do not let your hearts differ. God—mighty and majestic—and His angels bless the front row.’” Abū al-Nuʿmān related to us; he said: Jarīr ibn Ḥāzim related to us, from Zubayd (317a), from Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwsaja, from al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib, who said: “The Prophet ﷺ said: ‘Whoever gives silver as a loan …’”—then he mentioned a report similar to Shuʿba’s. Al-Ḥajjāj related to us; he said: Muḥammad ibn Ṭalḥa related to us, from Ṭalḥa, and he mentioned the like of it, adding: “And adorn the Qurʾān with your voices.” Muʿādh ibn Muʿādh and Ghundar said, on Shuʿba’s authority, that ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwsaja said:

“I had forgotten ‘Adorn the Qurʾān with your voices’ until al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Muzāḥim reminded me of it.”

Ṭalḥa and Zubayd used to pray in one mosque. Zubayd leaned toward Shīʿism, while Ṭalḥa was a staunch ʿUthmānī. Zubayd permitted drinking nabīdh, while Ṭalḥa prohibited strong nabīdh, saying, “It is wine.” They remained this way until they died, and there was no estrangement or separation between them. Ṭalḥa died ten years before Zubayd. Muḥammad ibn Ṭalḥa’s father died when he was very young; people have criticized his transmission from his father, though, on the whole, he was a virtuous and judicious man.

Sufyān transmitted from al-Rukayn al-Ḍabbī, who was trustworthy and of an earlier generation.

Abū Nuʿaym related to us; he said: Sufyān related to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḍamra, from ʿAlī ﵁: “For twenty-five camels, [the due is] one fifth”—meaning one sheep. Ibn ʿUthmān related to us; he said: ʿAbd Allāh informed us; he said: Sufyān informed us, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḍamra, from ʿAlī ﵁—with the like of it, adding: “When they exceed one hundred and twenty, he said: ‘Return the prescribed dues to their starting point; and when the camels become numerous, for every fifty there is a ḥiqqa.’ This is preferable to Sufyān over the view of the people of the Ḥijāz.”

Muḥammad ibn Bashshār related to us; he said: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd related to me, from Sufyān, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḍamra, from ʿAlī ﵁—regarding camels: “When they exceed one hundred and twenty, the prescribed dues are calculated afresh according to that amount.”

And from Sufyān, from Manṣūr, from Ibrāhīm, the like of that. I was told from Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn, who said: “Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd used to transmit a report in which he erred, from Sufyān al-Thawrī, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿĀṣim, from ʿAlī ﵁—who said: ‘When the camels exceed one hundred and twenty, the prescribed due begins anew.’” Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd did not err in this; Ibn al-Mubārak corroborated him. This is well known as a transmission of Sufyān from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿĀṣim, from ʿAlī. The scholars criticized ʿĀṣim ibn Ḍamra for this, because ʿĀṣim’s transmission from ʿAlī contradicts ʿAlī’s letter to ʿAmr ibn Ḥazm and the letter of Abū Bakr and ʿUmar ﵄.

Abū Nuʿaym and Qabīṣa related to us; they said: Sufyān related to us, from Wāʾil ibn Dāwūd, from Saʿīd ibn ʿUmayr al-Anṣārī, who said: “The Messenger of God ﷺ was asked: ‘Which …’”

“Which form of earning is finest?” He replied: “A man’s work with his own hands, and every honest sale.” Saʿīd ibn ʿUmayr was the son of al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib’s brother.

He said: Al-Masʿūdī disagrees in this report and makes an error in it.

Abū Nuʿaym related to us: Umayy al-Ṣayrafī related to us—he is trustworthy, and Sharīk and Ibn ʿUyayna narrated from him.

Abū Nuʿaym related to us: ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Iyād ibn Laqīṭ, of Sadūs, related to us. He is trustworthy and was the appointed representative of his people.

Abū Nuʿaym related to us from Misʿar; and Sufyān, from Iyād ibn Laqīṭ, who is trustworthy.

Abū Nuʿaym related to us: al-Muṭṭalib ibn Ziyād—who is trustworthy—related to us: Ḥamza al-Zayyāt, a righteous and trustworthy man, related to us.

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā and Abū al-Walīd related to us from Abū Bakr al-Nahshalī, who is trustworthy.

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā related to us: Usāma ibn Zayd related to us from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥunayn, who said: I heard ʿAlī ﵁—say: “The Messenger of God ﷺ forbade me to wear a gold ring and to wear clothing dyed with safflower. I do not say, ‘He forbade you.’” He also said: Usāma related to us from ʿAṭāʾ, from Jābir: The Messenger of God ﷺ stoned [the pillars], then sat. A man came to him and said: “Messenger of God—”

“I shaved my head before sacrificing?” He replied: “There is no harm.” Then another man came to him and said:

“I shaved my head before stoning?” He replied: “There is no harm.” “He was asked about nothing except that he said, ‘There is no harm.’” Then the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “All of ʿArafa is a place of standing; all of Muzdalifa is a place of standing; all of Minā is a place of sacrifice; and every mountain pass of Mecca is a road and a place of sacrifice.”

Yaḥyā al-Qaṭṭān used to reject this report and criticized Usāma on account of it. Among the people of his own city, Medina, Usāma was trustworthy and reliable. Yaḥyā should have done otherwise than what he said, for Qays ibn Saʿd narrated some of this from ʿAṭāʾ, from Jābir, from the Prophet ﷺ.

Abū al-Ṭāhir ibn al-Sarḥ related to me: Ibn Wahb related to us from Usāma ibn Zayd, who heard Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib say: “There is no usury except in what is measured or weighed, among things eaten or drunk.”

Ibn Wahb said: Usāma heard only this one report from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib.

ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn ʿImrān related to me: Ibn Wahb related to us: Usāma ibn Zayd related to me that Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥunayn had related to him, from his father, from ʿAlī ﵁—that he heard him say: “The Messenger of God ﷺ forbade me to wear clothing dyed with safflower.” Usāma said: “I entered the house of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥunayn. He was then a very old man, wearing a cloak dyed heavily with safflower. I asked him about this report. ʿAbd Allāh said—”

“I heard ʿAlī say: ‘The Messenger of God ﷺ forbade me—I do not say, “He forbade you”—to wear clothing dyed with safflower.’”

Ismāʿīl ibn al-Khalīl related to us: Zakariyyā ibn ʿAdī related to me: Ibn al-Mubārak said: “I asked Ismāʿīl ibn [Abī] Khālid: ‘Did you hear anything from Zirr ibn Ḥubaysh besides this report, the report about the Night of Decree?’ He said: ‘No.’”

Muḥammad ibn Rumḥ al-Tujībī related to me: al-Layth ibn Saʿd related to us: Mālik ibn Anas related to me from Ibn Shihāb, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Hurmuz al-Aʿraj, from Abū Hurayra, from the Messenger of God ﷺ who said: “If your neighbor asks you to fix a piece of wood in your wall, do not refuse him.” Ibn Rumḥ said: I heard al-Layth, while relating this report, say:

“This is the first report of Mālik’s that we have, and his last.”

Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmmār related to us: Yaʿqūb related to us: Shuʿba said:

“I heard only two reports from ʿAlī ibn Badīma.”

Abū Bakr ibn ʿAbd al-Malik related to me: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Ḥanbal related to us: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Qaṭṭān related to us: “I asked Shuʿba: ‘Did you hear from Abū Maʿshar?’ He said: ‘Four, cut off.’”

Abū Bakr related to us: Ḥammād ibn Khālid related to us: I asked Makhrama about his father’s books. He said to me: “I heard nothing from him.”

Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmmār related to us: I heard Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Qaṭṭān mention ʿAlī ibn al-Mubārak (318b). He said: “He had two books. He had heard one of them, but had not heard the other. As for what we narrated from him, it was from what he had heard. As for what the Kūfans narrated from him, it was from the book he had not heard.”

ʿAbd al-Aʿlā ibn Wāṣil ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā related to me: Abū Nuʿaym al-Faḍl ibn Dukayn related to us from ʿAmr ibn Abī al-Miqdām, from Abū Isḥāq, who said: “There were three who would not invoke blessings upon ʿAlī ﵁: Shurayḥ, Murra, and Masrūq. This Murra was called Murra al-Ṭayyib; he was Murra ibn Sharāḥīl.”

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Muʿādh related to us: My father related to us: Shuʿba related to us from ʿAmr ibn Murra, who said: “I heard Murra disparaging ʿAlī ﵁—and I said to him: ‘You say this about a man among the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ for whom good had already been secured?’ He replied:

“What fault is mine, if his good preceded me, while his evil caught up with me?”

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā related to us: Sufyān related to us from al-Shaʿbī, concerning a child of fornication: “May he lead people in prayer?” He said: “Our imam is said to be such.”

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us from Abū Isḥāq al-Kūfī, who said: “I asked al-Shaʿbī about praying behind a child of fornication.” He said: “That is our muezzin and our imam.” He said: “He called the prayer, and we prayed behind him.”

“ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr ibn ʿĪsā al-Ḥumaydī, Abū Bakr—among those I have met, I have found none more sincere toward Islam and the Muslims than he was”—related to us: Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna ibn Abī ʿImrān al-Hilālī related to us: Ṣāliḥ ibn Ṣāliḥ al-Hamdānī related to us. He was better than his two sons, and ʿAlī was the better of the two—meaning, of al-Ḥasan. He said: “A man came to al-Shaʿbī while I was with him and said: ‘Abū ʿAmr—’”

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā related to us from ʿAlī and al-Ḥasan, the two sons of Ṣāliḥ. They were both trustworthy and inclined toward Shiʿism.

He said: I heard ʿĪsā ibn Muḥammad—who was strongly inclined toward Sufyān al-Thawrī, and Sufyān deserved that—say: “I was talking with Abū Nuʿaym, and he mentioned Sufyān and al-Ḥasan ibn Ṣāliḥ. He began to favor al-Ḥasan, and I argued against him. He said: ‘Woe to you! Be quiet, boy. I kept company with the two of them and knew them. I cannot say that I ever saw al-Ḥasan smile. Yet sometimes I saw Sufyān laugh until he fell back and stretched his legs against the wall from laughing.’”

He said: I heard Aḥmad, Abū Nuʿaym’s copyist, come to Abū Nuʿaym and say: “Abū Nuʿaym, Muḥammad ibn ʿUbayd Allāh has died, and we have lost ʿUbayd Allāh. ʿUbayd Allāh used to relate to him.”

He replied: “Abū Nuʿaym, if you had seen him, you would have said it was no calamity.” He said: “We have lost al-Ḥasan’s company.”

One of the elders of Kūfa told me: They had a female servant who served them, and they needed to sell her, so they sold her. At the beginning of the night, she went and kept urging her former masters to get him up, saying, “The night has passed,” again and again, until she vexed him and he shouted at her.

When morning came, she went to al-Ḥasan and said: “Glory be to God! Was it not your duty, after I served you, to sell me to a Muslim?” Al-Ḥasan said to her:

“Glory be to God! What is the matter with him?” She said: “I waited for him to get up for night prayer, but he did not. I kept urging him, so he rebuked and cursed me.” He called out to ʿAlī and said: “Are you not amazed by this? Go borrow her price from one of our brothers and set her free.”

Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmmār related to us: Yaḥyā ibn al-Yamān related to me from Sufyān, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAlī ﵁—who said: “There is nothing due on green produce.”

Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmmār al-Mawṣilī related to us: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī related to us: I said to Sufyān about the report of ʿAlī. Sufyān said to me: “This is not a report from Abū Isḥāq.”

Muḥammad said: I heard Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd say: “Sufyān knew the reports of al-Aʿmash better than al-Aʿmash did.”

Muḥammad ibn Wahb related to us: Miskīn related to us from Shuʿba, from ʿAmr ibn Murra, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salama. He used to relate a long report from Ibn Masʿūd that he— “was with the Messenger of God ﷺ on the night the jinn came to him.” It was as though he had been with the Prophet ﷺ but I did not hear this from ʿAbd Allāh.

ʿAmr said: I mentioned this (319b) to Abū ʿUbayda: “Was Ibn Masʿūd with the Messenger of God ﷺ on the Night of the Jinn?” He said: “No.”

Abū Nuʿaym and Qabīṣa related to us: Sufyān related to us from ʿUrwa, Abū Mahil. Qabīṣa said: “Abū Muhayl al-Juʿfī; he was a Kūfan.” Aḥmad ibn Yūnus traced his lineage as ʿUrwa ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Qushayr, through Zuhayr.

Qabīṣa related to us: Sufyān related to us from al-Suddī, from Abū Hubayra, from Anas:

“The Prophet ﷺ was asked about wine being turned into vinegar, and he disapproved of it.”

Abū Nuʿaym related to us: Isrāʾīl related to us from al-Suddī, from Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbbād, who was Abū Hubayra. Al-Suddī’s name was Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Kurayma, a client of the Banū Hāshim. “Muḥammad ibn Marwān al-Suddī was a client of the Khaṭṭābīs; he is called al-Suddī al-Ṣaghīr, and he is weak and unreliable.” As for the elder al-Suddī, Sufyān al-Thawrī said: “He was a jurist.”

Abū Nuʿaym also related to us: Isrāʾīl related to us from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿUrayb ibn Ḥumayd, who said: “On the Day of the Camel, a man spoke ill of ʿĀʾisha. ʿAmmār came to him and said: ‘Be quiet, you disgraced man! Do you speak ill of the beloved of the Messenger of God ﷺ? She is his wife in Paradise.’”

ʿUrayb ibn Ḥumayd is Abū ʿAmmār, from whom al-Aʿmash narrated. I heard Ibn— ʿAbbās, and a man asked him: “Did you go out with the Messenger of God ﷺ for the two ʿĪd prayers?” He said: “Yes.”

Abū Nuʿaym related to us: Sufyān related to us from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿĀbis ibn Rabīʿa, from ʿAlī ﵁—who said: “Every divorce is valid except the divorce of one bereft of reason.” He said: Sufyān also narrated this from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, who was Ibn ʿĀbis.

Qabīṣa said: From Sufyān, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿĀbis ibn Rabīʿa.

Qabīṣa related to us: Sufyān related to us from al-Agharr, who was Ibn al-Ṣabāḥ, a client of the Banū Minqar, from Khalīfa ibn Ḥuṣayn, from his father: His grandfather, Qays ibn ʿĀṣim, came to the Prophet ﷺ embraced Islam, and the Prophet ordered him to wash with water and lotus leaves.

Abū Nuʿaym related to us: ʿUbāda ibn Muslim al-Fazārī related to us. He is sound in his reports, and Sufyān al-Thawrī and others narrated from him (320a).

Abū Nuʿaym and Qabīṣa related to us: Sufyān related to us from Nahshal al-Ḍabbī, who is trustworthy.

Abū Nuʿaym related to us: Sufyān related to us from Kulayb ibn Wāʾil, who said: “I asked Ibn ʿUmar.” He was a Kūfan.

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā related to us: As for Zāʾida, from ʿĀṣim, from Zirr, from ʿAbd Allāh, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “If only one day remained of this world, God would send a man from my family whose name would match mine and whose father’s name would match my father’s.”

Zāʾida is trustworthy and a Kūfan. His teknonym was Abū al-Ṣalt, and he was a Thaqafī. The Rāfiḍīs claim that Zāʾida was illegitimate, but it is not as they say.

“Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yūnus related to us. He mentioned Zāʾida and said: ‘He would not relate to the Rāfiḍīs.’

“He said: ‘This one, ʿUbayd Allāh, the one-eyed Kindī, contrived and came and went until he heard two reports from him. I went with the shaykhs to him, and I think he mentioned Abū Usāma and someone else. I greeted him and rose to leave, but he caught the hem of my shirt and said:

“‘Sit down so you can hear this that I want to read aloud to them.’”

Shuʿba also said: “ʿAmr ibn Murra related to us from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salama, except ʿAmr ibn Murra.” Ibn Numayr related to us from his father, from Nahshal, and Ibn Numayr deemed him weak.

Qabīṣa related to us: Sufyān related to us from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jābir, who, in my view, was a trustworthy Kūfan.

Abū Nuʿaym related to us: Sufyān related to us from ʿAṭiyya ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Thaqafī who is trustworthy—said: al-Qāsim ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān informed me: A thief who had stolen a garment was brought to ʿUmar ﵁. He said to ʿUthmān: “Appraise it.” He appraised it at eight dirhams, so ʿUmar did not cut off his hand.

Abū Nuʿaym related to us: Sufyān related to us from Manṣūr ibn Ḥayyān, who is trustworthy; Marwān and Yazīd ibn Hārūn narrated from him.

He said: Sufyān related to us from Yazīd ibn Ḥayyān, from ʿAnbasa ibn ʿUqba, who said: “I heard Ibn Masʿūd say: ‘Nothing is more deserving of imprisonment than a long tongue.’”

Yazīd is a trustworthy Kūfan, and there is no kinship between him and Manṣūr ibn Ḥayyān.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rajāʾ and Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yūnus related to us from Maʿrūf ibn Wāṣil, a trustworthy Kūfan.

Abū Nuʿaym related to us: Sufyān related to us from ʿAmmār al-Duhnī—he was a branch of Bajīla.

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā related to us: Badr ibn al-Khalīl informed us: I entered upon Shaqīq ibn Salama on a Friday while he was heating a kettle. I said to him: “You are an old man; you do not come to the Friday prayer.” He said: “I heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd say this about the one who does not bathe:

“I am more incapable and foolish than the one who does not bathe on Friday.”

ʿUbayd Allāh said: Badr ibn ʿUthmān reported to us; he is reliable. Badr ibn al-Khalīl is likewise sound in ḥadīth.

Ādam reported to us; Shuʿbah reported to us; al-Ḥakam reported to us, from Sayf, the seller of al-sābirī, from Rashīd al-Hajarī, from his father, that a man said to ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr:

“Relate to us something you heard from the Messenger of God ﷺ and leave aside what you found in your two sacks on the day of Yarmūk.” He said: “I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: ‘A Muslim is one from whose tongue and hand the Muslims are safe.’” Al-Shaʿbī had seen Rushayd, Ḥabbah al-ʿUranī, and al-Aṣbagh ibn Nubātah, but their ḥadīths are worthless.

Likewise, Abū Saʿīd ʿUqaysā—these men nearly became Rāfiḍīs.

Abū Nuʿaym reported to us: Muḥammad ibn Qays al-Asadī reported to us, from Sālim ibn ʿAṭiyyah—who is reliable—from his maternal grandfather, who said: “I prayed behind Shurayḥ.”

Abū Nuʿaym also reported to us from ʿĪsā ibn al-Musayyib.

Ibn Mūsā reported to us from ʿĪsā ibn Qirṭās. Both of them have weakness.

Abū Nuʿaym and Qabīṣah reported to us, saying: Sufyān reported to us, from ʿImrān ibn Muslim ibn Riyāḥ, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Maʿqil, who said: ʿAlī said: “Clientage is a branch of enslavement; secure the clientage and secure the inheritance.” Misʿar also reported from ʿImrān—he was a Kufan—ibn Ẓabyān; there is no harm in him.

The companion of Suwayd ibn Ghaflah is in fact Ḥayyān, not ʿImrān.

Al-Ḥajjāj reported to us: Abū ʿAwānah reported to us, from Manṣūr, from Ḥayyān, the seller of patterned cloth, who said: “I was sitting with Suwayd ibn Ghaflah.”

Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbs reported to me, from Ibn al-Mubārak, from Sufyān, from Ḥayyān al-Juʿfī, who said: “I was with Suwayd ibn Ghaflah when a case was brought before him concerning a daughter, a wife, and a client. He said: ‘ʿAlī ﵁—used to give the daughter half and the wife an eighth (321 a), then return what remained to the daughter.’” Qabīṣah reported to us: Sufyān reported to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Abū al-Ḍuḥā Muslim ibn Ṣubayḥ al-ʿAṭṭār, client of Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ.

“Qabīṣah reported to us: Sufyān reported to us, from Abū al-Wāziʿ, who said: ‘I said to Ibn ʿUmar: “People will continue to be in a good state as long as God keeps you among them.”’ He became angry and said: ‘I suppose you are an Iraqi. What do you know about what your mother’s son shuts his door upon?’”

Abū al-Wāziʿ’s name was Zuhayr ibn Mālik al-Nahdī.

Abū Nuʿaym reported to us: ʿUbādah ibn Muslim al-Fazārī reported to us: Yūnus ibn Khabbāb—who was a Rāfiḍī, although the people of Kūfah reported from him; he made no secret of his views, reviled ʿUthmān, and disparaged him ﵁—reported to us, from Abū al-Bakhtarī Saʿīd al-Ṭāʾī, who said: “Abū Kabshah al-Anmārī reported to me that he heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: ‘There are three things I swear by…’”

“He said: Al-Ḥumānī reported to me: ʿAlī ibn Mushir reported to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Mūsā ibn Ṭarīf, from ʿAbāyah ibn Rabʿī al-Asadī, from ʿAlī, who said: ‘I am the divider of the Fire.’” He said: “I read in the book of ʿUmar ibn Ḥafṣ ibn Ghiyāth, from his father, from al-Aʿmash: I said to Mūsā, ‘What standing did ʿAbāyah have among you?’ He spoke of his virtue, prayer, fasting, and truthfulness.” “Mūsā is weak and requires someone to authenticate him; he is not reliable. ʿAbāyah is of lesser standing than he, and his ḥadīth is worthless.”

Ādam reported to us: Shuʿbah reported to us: Idrīs al-Awdī—who is Abū ʿAbd Allāh ibn Idrīs, a reliable man—reported to me, from his father, from Abū Hurayrah, who said: “Let none of you pray while he finds filth present.”

Others besides Ādam traced it back to the Prophet, on Shuʿbah’s authority. I think Muslim ibn Ibrāhīm reported it to us from Shuʿbah and traced it back to the Prophet. Idrīs used to serve as the muezzin for Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq al-Hāshimī.

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā reported to us: Dāwūd ibn Yazīd al-Awdī reported to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Idrīs; he is not strong.

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā reported to us: ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar al-Asadī reported to us, from al-Suddī, from Rifāʿah al-Fityānī, who said: “One day I entered upon al-Mukhtār, and he said:”

“Girl!” (321 b) “Bring Rifāʿah a cushion.” I said, “Are these not cushions?”

He said: “Gabriel ﵇ stood up from this one, and Michael from that one.”

He said: “Then I entered upon him the next day while he was making a lute. He said: ‘Will you not help us make it, then burn it, then scatter it thoroughly into the sea?’” He said: “I wanted to kill him, but I recalled the ḥadīth of my brother ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥamq: ‘My brother ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥamq told me, from the Prophet ﷺ who said: “Whoever gives a man a guarantee of safety for his life, then kills him, I disavow him, even if the man killed is an unbeliever.”’”

ʿUbayd Allāh said: Zāʾidah reported to us, from al-Suddī, from Rifāʿah al-Fityānī, from ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥamq, from the Prophet ﷺ who said: “Whoever gives or grants a man a guarantee of safety for his life, then kills him, I disavow him, even if the man killed is an unbeliever.”

This is the Kufan one. ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar the grammarian was a Basran.

ʿUbayd Allāh reported to us from Hāshim ibn al-Burayd, a Kufan Shiʿi.

Shādh ibn Fayyāḍ al-Baṣrī reported to us from Hāshim, who is also called Hāshim al-Burayd; he is weak.

Abū Farwah al-Hamdānī is ʿAwf ibn al-Ḥārith.

Abū Farwah al-Juhanī is Muslim ibn Sālim.

Abū Farwah al-Rahāwī is Yazīd ibn Sinān. He is weak, and his son is weak, weaker than his father.

Abū Nuʿaym and Qabīṣah reported to us, saying: Sufyān reported to us, from Zayd ibn Jubayr ibn— Ḥarmalah is reliable, a Kufan.

Abū Nuʿaym reported to us: Sufyān reported to us, from Ḥakīm ibn Jubayr, a Kufan. Shuʿbah reported from him, then stopped reporting his ḥadīths. There is no kinship between him and Zayd.

“Abū Nuʿaym and Qabīṣah reported to us, saying: Sufyān reported to us, from Ḥakīm ibn al-Daylam, a reliable Kufan.”

Abū Nuʿaym reported to us: Sufyān reported to us, from Zufar al-ʿAjalī, from Qays ibn Ḥabtar, who is a reliable Kufan.

Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr reported to us: ʿĪsā ibn Yūnus reported to us, from Muḥammad ibn Abī Ismāʿīl, from ʿĀmir ibn Shaqīq, from Abū Wāʾil, who said: “My mother died a Christian.” (322 a)

ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān reported to us: ʿAbd Allāh reported to us: Ḥammād ibn Salamah reported to us, from ʿAlī ibn Zayd, from Yūsuf ibn Mihrān, who said: “The mother of Ibn Abī Rabīʿah died a Christian.”

Abū Nuʿaym reported to us: He informed us of “Ḥanash ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Laqīṭ al-Nakhaʿī—a reliable Kufan.”

He said: “I saw Suwayd ibn Ghaflah pass by one of his wives from Banū Asad when he was one hundred and twenty years old. He said: ‘I saw al-Aswad ibn Yazīd after one of his eyes had gone from fasting.’” He said: “ʿAmr ibn Maymūn used to greet us when we were boys, and he would stand up and greet us.”

Al-Aswad ibn Yazīd was Abū ʿAmr.

ʿUbaydah al-Salmānī was Abū Muslim.

Abū al-Nuʿmān reported to us: ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn Ziyād reported to us, from Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Zubaydī, who was a Kufan.

Abū Nuʿaym reported to us: Sufyān reported to us, from Abū Ṣakhrā—who was Jāmiʿ ibn Shaddād, a reliable Kufan—from Ṣafwān ibn Muḥriz al-Māzinī, from ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn, who said: “A group of Banū Tamīm came to the Prophet ﷺ and he said: ‘Accept the glad tidings, Banū Tamīm.’ They said: ‘You have given us glad tidings, so give us something.’ That showed on his face.” He said:

“A man from the people of Yemen came and said: ‘Accept the glad tidings, since Banū Tamīm did not accept them.’

“They said: ‘We accept them, Messenger of God.’” ʿUmar ibn Ḥafṣ ibn Ghiyāth reported to me: My father reported to us: al-Aʿmash reported to us: Jāmiʿ ibn Shaddād reported to us, from Ṣafwān ibn Muḥriz, who related to him, from ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn, who said: “I entered upon the Messenger of God ﷺ …” He then related the ḥadīth, adding: “They said: ‘We have come to ask you about this matter.’ He said: ‘God, mighty and glorious, existed when there was nothing besides Him, and His Throne was upon the water. He wrote everything in the Remembrance and created the heavens and the earth.’”

Some of the shaykhs of the people of Kūfah transmitted it but made an error in it, saying: “And He created the Remembrance.”

All the companions of al-Aʿmash contradicted him.

Ibn Numayr reported to us: My father reported to us: al-Aʿmash reported to us, from Abū Yaḥyā, the client of Jaʿdah ibn Hubayrah. Ibn Numayr said: “Abū Yaḥyā was Thuwair ibn Abī Fākhitah” (322 b), “and Jaʿdah ibn Hubayrah al-Makhzūmī was the son of Umm Hāniʾ, daughter of Abū Ṭālib.”

Abū Isḥāq al-Shaybānī was Sulaymān ibn Khāqān. He did not hear from Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī. Ibrāhīm died while Sulaymān was in Khurāsān.

Abū Nuʿaym reported to us: Sufyān reported to us, from “ʿImārah ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ ibn Yazīd, who is reliable”—and he is Yazīd ibn Shubrumah.

Abū Nuʿaym reported to us: Sufyān reported to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from ʿAṭāʾ, concerning one who performs mutual imprecation and then denies his own accusation. He said: “There are cases more serious than that for which no one is flogged.”

Abū Nuʿaym reported to us: Sufyān reported to us, from Ibn Shubrumah, whose name was ʿAbd Allāh, from al-Ḥārith al-ʿAklī, who said: “No fixed penalty applies to him.”

He said: Sufyān reported to us, from Salamah ibn al-Majnūn al-Ḥanafī, who said: “I said to a man, ‘You who fornicate with your mother!’ He brought me before Abū Hurayrah, who flogged me with the fixed penalty.” Salamah’s teknonym was Abū ʿUthaymah, and he was from Banū Shaybān.

Shuʿbah said, reporting from Abū Maymūnah, who said: “I came to Madīnah.”

Ibn Rajāʾ said: Sharīk reported from Salamah ibn al-Majnūn, who said: “They took me to Abū Hurayrah, who was the judge of Madīnah, and he imposed a fixed penalty upon me.”

Al-Firyābī said, reporting from Sufyān, from a shaykh of Banū Shaybān called Abū ʿUthaymah:

“He took me before Abū Hurayrah in al-Baḥrayn.”

Abū Saʿīd al-Juʿfī reported to me: Aḥmad ibn Ashkīb al-Kūfī reported to us:

Abū Yaḥyā al-Taymī reported to us: al-Aʿmash reported to us, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salamah al-Hamdānī, from ʿUbaydah al-Salmānī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, who said: “I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: ‘The one who succeeds me is in Paradise, and the one who succeeds him is in Paradise, and the third and fourth are in Paradise.’” Abū Yaḥyā’s name was Ismāʿīl ibn Ibrāhīm, and it reached me that Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal said: “He is reliable.”

Abū Nuʿaym reported to us: Sufyān reported to us, from Ādam ibn ʿAlī, who is reliable.

He said: Sufyān reported to us, from Muḥārib ibn Dithār, who is reliable.

He said: Sufyān reported to us, from “ʿĀṣim ibn Abī al-Najūd Bahdalah: there is inconsistency in his ḥadīth, but he is reliable.”

Abū Nuʿaym reported to us: Sufyān reported to us, from Abū Ḥuṣayn, and Ḥuṣayn ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, and from Abū Sinān Ḍirār ibn Murrah al-Shaybānī, from (323 a)

ʿAlqamah ibn Marthad, and from Ziyād ibn ʿAlāqah, and from Thābit Abū al-Miqdām, and from ʿAyyāsh al-ʿĀmirī, and from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Abī Bashīr, and “from al-Rukayn ibn al-Rabīʿ al-Fazārī”, and from Hilāl ibn Khabbāb. All of these men are reliable.

He said: “I heard ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm say: ‘Abū Thaʿlabah’s name was Jurthūm, and Abū Ghādiyah al-Muzanī’s name was Yasār ibn Sabʿ.’”

Mujāhid ibn Mūsā reported to us: Yazīd reported to us: Shuʿbah reported to us, from Sulaymān ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿUbayd ibn Fayrūz, Abū al-Ḍaḥḥāk al-Shaybānī.

Al-ʿAbbās ibn al-Walīd ibn Ṣubḥ reported to us: Abū Mushir reported to us: I heard Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz say: “Abū Thaʿlabah al-Khushanī’s name was Jurthūm.”

He said: “I heard Abū Mushir say: I heard Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz say:

“Umm al-Dardāʾ’s name was Hujaymah, daughter of Ḥuyayy al-Awṣābīyah.”

Al-ʿAbbās ibn al-Walīd ibn Ṣubḥ reported to us: I heard Abū Mushir say: “Abū Umayyah al-Shaʿbānī’s name was Yaḥmad”.

ʿUbayd Allāh said: “I heard a man descended from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Abī al-Muhājir, whose name was…”

Arqam.

“He said: I said to Hishām ibn ʿAmmār: ‘What was the name of Abū Thaʿlabah al-Khushanī?’ He said:

“‘Jurthūm ibn ʿAmr.’” He was then asked: “Some people here say that they are his descendants, and that they are so-and-so.” He said: “They have lied; these people are not his descendants.” I said: “Then Abū Muslim al-Khawlānī’s name was ʿAbd Allāh ibn Thawb?” He said: “Indeed—ibn Thawb.”

Abū al-Walīd was ʿUmayr ibn Hāniʾ.

Hishām ibn ʿAmmār reported to us: Ṣadaqah ibn Khālid al-Qurashī, client of Umm al-Banīn, Abū al-ʿAbbās, reported to us: Ibn Jābir reported to us, from ʿUmayr ibn Hāniʾ, that he would laugh, and I would say to him: “Abū al-Walīd, what is this?” He would say: “I have heard that Abū al-Dardāʾ used to say: ‘I refresh myself with a little falsehood so that I may be more energetic in pursuing the truth.’”

The ḥadīth of Saʿīd ibn Zayd: ʿAmr ibn Mālik reported to us: Abū al-Jawzāʾ Yūnus ibn Jābir al-Rabaʿī reported to us.

Al-Muʿallā ibn Asad and Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd reported to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Wāḥid reported to us, from Abū Rawq ʿAṭiyyah ibn al-Ḥārith—who is reliable—who said: Abū al-Gharīf reported to us…

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Khalīfah, who is trustworthy.

Al-Walīd ibn ʿUtbah narrated to us. He said: Abū Mushir narrated to us. He said: I heard Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz say: “The name of Abū Muslim al-Khawlānī is ʿAbd Allāh ibn Thawb.”

Abū Rifāʿah al-ʿAdawī: Tamīm ibn Asad.

Abū al-Zaʿrāʾ, the companion of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Hāniʾ.

And Abū al-Zaʿrāʾ, the nephew of Abū al-Aḥwaṣ. Al-Ḥumaydī narrated to us. He said: Sufyān narrated to us. He said: Abū al-Zaʿrāʾ narrated to us—he is ʿAmr ibn ʿAmr.

Abū Lubābah, the companion of ʿĀʾishah: Marwān.

Abū Qatādah al-ʿAdawī: Tamīm ibn Nudhayr.

Abū Ḥājib: Sawādah ibn ʿĀṣim.

Abū al-ʿAsharāʾ: Usāmah ibn Mālik ibn Quhṭum al-Dārimī. Some of them said:

ʿUṭārid ibn Buzr.

Abū Tamīmah al-Hujaymī: Ṭarīf ibn Mujālid.

Abū al-Minhal: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Muṭʿim.

Abū al-Aswad al-Duʾalī: Ẓālim ibn ʿAmr ibn Sufyān.

Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb narrated to us. He said: Ghassān ibn Muḍarr narrated to us, from Abū Salamah ibn Yazīd, who said: ʿUthmān ibn Abī al-ʿĀṣ was in charge of ʿAmmān, and al-Ḥakam ibn Abī al-ʿĀṣ was in charge of Bahrain. ʿUmar wrote to ʿUthmān, ordering him to march with the people of Bahrain to Shahrek.

He said: ʿUthmān ibn Abī al-ʿĀṣ said to the people of ʿAmmān: “Find me a man whom I can appoint in my place.” He said: They brought him Abū Ṣufrah. He asked: “What is your name?” He replied: “Ẓālim ibn Surāq.” He said: “I sent for you because I want to appoint you in my place, but since this is your name, I cannot.” He said: “Then do not prevent me from going on the expedition.” He said: “As for that, yes.” He said:

So he set out with them.

Abū ʿUbaydah Aḥmad ibn ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī al-Safar, and Abū al-Safar Saʿīd ibn Aḥmad al-Thawrī—of Thawr of Hamdān—narrated to me. He said: I heard Ṣāliḥ ibn Suhayl, the client of Fāṭimah, the wife of Ibn Abī Zāʾidah, say: Yaḥyā ibn Abī Zāʾidah used to recite these two verses:

Why has Salmā now begunto cast at you a downcast glance?

She says, “I was ill, yet you did not visit me.”How can an ill person visit another ill person?

Abū ʿUbaydah said: Ibn Bishr claimed that he heard Sufyān say:

I no longer call a physician for his healing arts;instead, I call upon You, O Sender of rain.

“Shihāb ibn ʿAbbād claimed that it had reached him that Sufyān used to recite verses by al-Aʿshā:

If you do not set out with piety as provision,and meet, after death, one who has so provided,

you will regret that you were not like him,and that you did not prepare as he had prepared.”

It has reached me from Isḥāq ibn al-Ṣabbāḥ al-Kindī that he used to recite verses by al-Samawʾal:

My poverty does not diminish my trustworthiness,though betrayal may weigh heavily on the heart, as long as I live.

Many an insult I heard, and feigned not to hear;many a wrong I left alone, and so was spared its harm.

The avaricious are not granted an excess of … provision,nor is the frail, feeble one deprived of it.

For each person has of his provision what God has decreed,

even if the one who would die of thirst scratches his nose.

A little wholesome provision is of benefit,but abundant ill-gotten provision is of no benefit.

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī said: Abū al-Aswad al-Nahdī is ʿAmr ibn ʿImrān.

Abū al-Ṣiddīq al-Nājī: Bakr ibn ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith.

Abū al-Zāhiriyyah: Ḥudayr ibn Kurayb.

Abū Idrīs al-Azdī al-Madanī, from whom Ismāʿīl ibn Sālim narrated: his name is Ibrāhīm ibn Abī Ḥadyah.

Ibn Bukayr narrated to us. He said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Lahīʿah narrated to us. He said: Darrāj, Abū al-Samḥ—a man from Egypt named ʿAbd al-Raḥmān—narrated to us, from Abū al-Haytham, whose name is Sulaymān ibn ʿAmr, a Medinan.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Lahīʿah narrated to us, from Abū Qubayl, Ḥuyayy ibn Hāniʾ al-Muʿāfirī, from Shufayy ibn Mātiʿ.

Ibn Bukayr said: Whoever says “Shufayy ibn ʿUbayd” is mistaken; he has confused him with his kunya.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Lahīʿah also narrated to me. He said: Abū Qubayl narrated to me that ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Ashʿarī arrived in Egypt. Ibn Bukayr said: He arrived with Marwān in the year 65.

He said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Lahīʿah narrated to me. He said: Abū Qubayl narrated to me that he heard Abū ʿUshānah Ḥayy ibn Yuʾmin, who was one of the best men of Yemen.

Ibn Bukayr said: I heard al-Layth say: Abū ʿUshānah narrated to me: “I saw ʿUqbah ibn ʿĀmir dyeing his hair black. He said, ‘We blacken its upper part, but its roots refuse.’” He said: He was a poet.

Abū Wajzah: Yazīd ibn ʿUbayd al-Saʿdī.

Abū Kabīr al-ʿAnbarī: Yazīd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān.

Abū Farwah: Muslim ibn Sālim al-Juhanī.

Abū Farwah al-Hamdānī: ʿUrwah ibn al-Ḥārith.

Abū Ḥadrad: his name is ʿAbd.

Abū Hunaydah: al-Barāʾ ibn Nawfal. Al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿĪsā, Abū Nuʿāmah al-ʿAdawī, narrated this to us, from Abū Hunaydah al-Barāʾ ibn Nawfal, from Wālān ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-ʿAdawī, from Ḥudhayfah, from Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq.

Abū al-Dahmāʾ: Qirfah ibn Buhays.

Abū Nuʿāmah al-Saʿdī: ʿAbd Rabbih.

Abū Naʿāmah al-Ḥanafī: Qays ibn ʿAbāyah.

Abū al-Zinbāʿ: Ṣadaqah ibn Ṣāliḥ.

Abū al-Ḥuwayrith: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Muʿāwiyah.

Abū Nuʿāmah al-Kūfī: Shaybah ibn Nuʿāmah, from whom Sufyān, Jarīr, and Hushaym narrated.

Abū al-Yamān narrated to us. He said: Abū Bakr ibn (Abī) Maryam said: Abū Baḥriyyah is ʿAbd Allāh ibn Qays al-Tarāghamī.

Abū al-Yamān narrated to us. He said: Ḥurayz ibn ʿUthmān al-Raḥabī narrated to us, from Ḥibbān ibn Zayd, whose kunya is Abū Khidāsh.

Abū al-Yamān narrated to us. He said: Ḥurayz narrated to us, from Abū al-Ḥasan Nimrān ibn ʿUtbah.

Abū al-Yamān narrated to us. He said: Ḥurayz narrated to us, from Ghaylān ibn Maʿshar al-Fazārī, who used to narrate from Abū Qutaylah Marthad ibn Widāʿah.

Abū al-Yamān narrated to us. He said: Ḥurayz narrated to us, from Abū Ḥabīb al-Ḥārith ibn Muḥammad, the judge.

Abū al-Yamān narrated to us. He said: Ḥurayz ibn ʿUthmān narrated to us: I saw Marthad ibn Sumar, who was among those who lived to the time of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib ﵁.

Ḥurayz narrated to us that he heard Abū Maryam, the attendant of the mosque of Ḥimṣ, who had lived to the time of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib and was among those whom Khālid ibn Yazīd appointed at the mosque of Ḥimṣ, say that he heard Abū Hurayrah say: “On Friday, the angels are at the doors of the mosques.”

Abū al-Aḥwaṣ: ʿAwf ibn Mālik, whose father was Mālik ibn Naḍlah.

Abū ʿAqīl: Zuhrah ibn Maʿbad al-Qurashī. Abū al-Aḥwaṣ narrated this to us, from Ibn Lahīʿah.

Abū ʿUqayl al-Dawraqī: Bashīr ibn ʿUqbah. Muslim ibn Ibrāhīm narrated this to us. (325a)

He said: Abū ʿAqīl, the companion of Buhayyah, is Yaḥyā ibn al-Mutawakkil. Khālid ibn Yazīd al-Kāhilī narrated this to us.

Abū ʿAqīl al-Shāmī: Hāshim ibn Bilāl. Saʿīd ibn al-Rabīʿ narrated this to us, from Shuʿbah. Hāshim was in charge of the judgeship of Wāsiṭ.

Abū ʿAqīl al-Kūfī: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAqīl al-Thaqafī.

Abū Maʿshar, the companion of Ibrāhīm: Ziyād ibn Kulayb.

Abū Maʿshar, the author of the military campaigns: Najīḥ al-Sindī al-ʿAjamī. ʿAbd Allāh ibn Maslamah narrated this to us.

Abū al-ʿAbbās, from whom Misʿar narrated: his name is al-Ḥārith.

“Aḥmad said: Ḥajjāj said: Shuʿbah narrated to us: ‘Jundab ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-ʿAlqī had come to the Prophet ﷺ; and if you wish, you may say that he was his Companion.’”

Aḥmad said: Ḥajjāj narrated to us. He said: I heard Shuʿbah say: I heard Abū Isḥāq say: “I asked: ‘Are you older, or al-Shaʿbī?’ He replied: ‘Al-Shaʿbī is older than me by a year or two.’ Abū Isḥāq had seen ʿAlī ﵁ and would describe him to us as having a large belly and being bald.”

Shuʿbah said: “Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān did not hear from ʿUthmān or from ʿAbd Allāh, but he did hear from ʿAlī ﵁.”

Wakīʿ said: “Abū Baḥr al-Hilālī’s name is Aḥnaf.”

“And Abū Baḥr, from whom Ḥasan narrated, is a nephew of ours who was with us. I saw him being called Yazīd ibn ʿAbd Allāh.”

Yaʿqūb narrated to us. He said: Abū Jaʿfar narrated to me, from Muʾammal, from Sufyān, from Abū Sinān Ḍirār ibn Murrah al-Shaybānī.

Abū ʿAmr al-Shaybānī: Saʿd ibn Iyās.

Abū Maʿmar: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sakhbarah al-Azdī.

Abū ʿAṭiyyah: Mālik ibn ʿĀmir.

Abū Nuʿaym narrated to us. He said: Abū Sinān Saʿd ibn Sinān al-Shaybānī narrated to us.

Abū ʿUmar narrated to us. He said: Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us. He said: Abū Sinān narrated to us whose name is ʿĪsā ibn al-Mutawakkil.

Saʿīd ibn Yasār, Abū Mahdī, a Syrian; Rūḥ ibn al-Rabīʿ narrated to us from him.

Abū Bishr narrated to me. He said: ʿAbd al-Salām ibn Hāshim al-ʿAdawī, Abū ʿUthmān al-Aʿwar, narrated to us. He said: Juwayriyah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, the brother of Abū Ḥarrah, informed us. He said: Abū Ḥurayz, the judge of Sijistān, informed me.

Aḥmad said: Ḥajjāj narrated to us. He said: I heard Shuʿbah relate, saying: Sulaymān said: “ʿUmārah ibn ʿUmayr returned from a journey and said to Jāmiʿ ibn Shaddād, ‘Do not tell Sulaymān that I have returned.’” (325b)

Ḥajjāj narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, who said: “Abū Isḥāq was older than Abū al-Bukhtarī, and Abū al-Bukhtarī did not live to see ʿAlī ﵁ nor did he see him.”

He said: I heard Shuʿbah say: “Maṭar al-Warrāq said: ‘These people are good; they narrate.’”

Abū al-Tayyāḥ narrated to us, from Abū al-Waddāk.

Aḥmad said: Ḥajjāj narrated to us. He said: Shuʿbah narrated to us: “Ayyūb said to me, ‘You are under—’” the chain of transmission, and this is a chain of transmission.” He said: I asked, “Did Abū al-Muhallab not hear from Ubayy?” He said:

“He heard him.” ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abzā did not live to see ʿAlī ﵁.

Shuʿbah said: “Sammāk related to me more times than I can count”—meaning the report of ʿIkrimah: “When one of you builds, let him lean against his neighbour’s wall; and when there is disagreement about the road…” People would sometimes prompt him, saying, “From Ibn ʿAbbās?” and he would say, “Yes.”

“As for me, I did not prompt him.”

Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd narrated to us. He said: Shuʿbah informed us. He said: I asked Abū Isḥāq:

“How did Abū al-Aḥwaṣ narrate?” He replied: “He would pour them out to us in the mosque, saying, ‘ʿAbd Allāh said…’”

Shuʿbah said: “I could tell which reports Qatādah had heard and which he had not heard. When he came to what he had heard, he would say, ‘Anas ibn Mālik narrated to us,’ ‘al-Ḥasan narrated to us,’ ‘Saʿīd narrated to us’, and ‘Muṭarrif narrated to us’. When he came to what he had not heard, he would say, ‘Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said,’ or ‘Abū Qilābah said.’”

Abū Dāwūd narrated to us. He said: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Maysarah, who said:

“Al-Ḍaḥḥāk did not meet Ibn ʿAbbās. He met Saʿīd ibn Jubayr in al-Rayy and took [knowledge] from him.”

Exegesis.

Shuʿbah said: I asked al-Ḥakam, “What part of ʿAlī’s war ﵁ did Abū Ayyūb witness?” He said: “He witnessed Ḥarūrāʾ with him.”

Khālid al-Ḥadhdhāʾ, ibn Mihrān.

Abū al-Manāzil, Ghālib al-Tammār, ibn Mihrān.

Sulaymān ibn Ṭarkhān al-Taymī.

Al-Aʿmash, Sulaymān ibn Mihrān.

Ghālib al-Qaṭṭān, ibn Khaṭṭāf.

Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit: Ḥabīb ibn Qays; he is Abū Thābit ibn Dīnār.

Ḥarām—it seems that he is the one from whom Shuʿbah narrated.

Abū al-Juwayriyyah al-Jarmī: Ḥaṭṭān ibn Khifāf al-Jarmī.

ʿUthmān ibn al-Haytham related to us; he said: ʿImrān ibn Ḥudayr related to us, from Abū ʿUthmān, namely ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mall.

Abū Naḍrah, al-Mundhir ibn Qaṭʿah.

Abū al-Mutawakkil al-Nājī, ʿAlī ibn Dāwūd.

Abū Hārūn, ʿUmārah ibn Juwayn.

Abū al-Tayyāḥ, Yazīd ibn Ḥumayd.

Abū Ḥabrah, Shīḥah ibn ʿAbd Allāh.

Ādam related to us. Shuʿbah said, from Abū ʿImrān al-Jawnī, ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Ḥabīb al-Azdī.

ʿAlī said: “Ibn Ḥabīb ibn Ḥubaysh.” ʿAlī was asked: “Is ʿAbd al-Raḥmān related to Abū ʿImrān?” He said: “No, this man is Tamīmī.”

Ādam related to us. He said: Shuʿbah related to us. He said: Ibrāhīm ibn al-Muntashir, the son of Masrūq’s brother, related to us.

Abū al-Malīḥ, Zayd ibn Usāmah.

Abū Mujliz, Lāḥiq ibn Ḥumayd.

Abū Qilābah, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Zayd.

Abū al-Salīl, Ḍurayb ibn Nuqayr.

Ḥajjāj and ʿAmr ibn ʿĀṣim related to us. They said: Hammām related to us. He said: Qatādah related to us. He said: Abū Ghullāb, Yūnus ibn Jubayr, related to us.

Bakr ibn Khalaf related to me. He said: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad related to us, from Hammām, from Qatādah, from Yaḥyā ibn Mālik al-Marāghī, who was Abū Ayyūb al-Azdī.

Abū Nuʿaym and [Abū] al-Nuʿmān related to us. They said: Ghaylān ibn Jarīr related to us, from Abū al-Ḥalāl Zurārah ibn Rabīʿah al-ʿAtakī. He said: “We came to ʿUthmān in a delegation from Baṣrah and presented our needs to him. He said, ‘Whenever you wish.’ Then he said, ‘God, Mighty and Majestic, is more entitled; God, Mighty and Majestic, is more entitled.’”

Abū al-Muhazzam, Yazīd ibn Sufyān.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān related to us. He said: My father informed me. He said: ʿAbbād ibn Manṣūr related to us. He said: I heard al-Ḥārith ibn So-and-so say: “I accompanied Abū Hurayrah and heard him say: ‘Whoever follows a funeral procession and then carries the bier three times has fulfilled what was due from him on its account.’”

He said: Abū Rajāʾ, ʿImrān ibn Khaytham.

Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us. He said: al-Layth ibn Saʿd related to me. He said: Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb related to me, from Bilāl, the client of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥasan ibn Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, that Dhakwān, Abū Ṣāliḥ al-Sammān, the client of Ghaṭafān, had informed him.

Al-ʿAbbās ibn al-Walīd ibn Mazyad related to me. He said: Ibn Abī informed me. He said: I heard al-Awzāʿī say: “Abū ʿUrwah al-Qāsim ibn Mukhaymirah used to say, ‘When I close my door, my concerns do not go beyond it.’”

He said: “I heard him say this when I was a boy, not yet grown up. A funeral procession passed, followed by women, and he said:

‘I would not like their faces to be in front of my sandals.’”

The name of Abū Ṣāliḥ, from whom Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr narrated, is Qaylūwiyyah.

Abū Ḥurayz, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥusayn, judge of Sijistān.

Abū Ḥāzim al-Ashjaʿī, Sulaymān, the client of ʿAzzah al-Ashjaʿiyyah.

Abū Khuldah, Mīzān.

Aḥmad said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān related to us, from ʿAbd al-Wāḥid, from Waqāʾ.

He said: “I saw ʿAzrah regularly visiting Saʿīd ibn Jubayr. He had the exegesis in a book with him, along with his inkwell, which he would alter.”

He said: Aḥmad also said: ʿAffān related to us. He said: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, from ʿAlī ibn Zayd, who mentioned Yūsuf ibn Mihrān. He said: “His memorization used to be likened to the memorization of ʿAmr ibn Dīnār.”

Abū Saʿīd al-Raqāshī’s name is Qays, the client of Ḥuḍayn ibn al-Mundhir.

Abū al-ʿAjfāʾ al-Sulamī, Haram.

Abū Nawfal ibn Abī ʿAqirab’s name is Muʿāwiyah ibn Muslim ibn ʿAmr ibn Abī ʿAqirab.

Abū al-Bakhtarī al-Ṭāʾī’s name is Saʿīd.

Abū Jaʿfar, the client of Ibn ʿAyyāsh: Yazīd ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ.

Abū Dālān, Ḥibbān ibn Yazīd.

Aḥmad said: Abū Qaṭan related to us. He said: Abū Khuldah related to us. He said: “I saw Anas dyeing with saffron, as well as al-Ḥasan, Saʿīd ibn Abī al-Ḥasan, Jābir ibn Zayd, Muṭarrif, Zurārah ibn Awfā, Abū al-Sawwār, and Abū Rajāʾ, and Abū al-ʿAlāʾ Yazīd ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Shikhkhīr.”

Salamah related to me, from Aḥmad: ʿAbd al-Razzāq related to us. He said: My father informed me:

“My mother used to send me with food to Ḥajar al-Madārī while he was in prison. He would pass his hand over my head and pray for me.”

I heard Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bukayr say: “Abū al-Haytham, Sulaymān ibn ʿAmr, was Medinan. Darrāj was a storyteller; I think he lived in the time of Hishām. He died, and he was from an earlier generation.”

Ibn Bukayr said: “Abū Salamah and al-Shaʿbī came to ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Marwān.”

Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥīm, Ṣāʿiqah, related to me. He said: I heard ʿAlī say: Nimrān ibn Mūsā, from whom Ibn Jurayj narrated, is the brother of Ayyūb ibn Mūsā. (326a)

ʿAlī also said: “Ṭāwūs was a client of Khawlān; he was not Persian.”

ʿAlī said: “Abū Yaḥyā al-Aslamī’s name is Samʿān.”

ʿAlī said: “ʿAbd al-Raḥīm used to say: ‘Muḥammad ibn Muslim wrote ...’” al-Ṭāʾifī, soundly.

Abū Ṣāliḥ al-Ḥanafī’s name is ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Qays.

Shuʿayb ibn al-Ḥabḥāb is Abū Ṣāliḥ.

The name of Abū al-Khayr ibn Tamīm ibn Ḥudhlam is ʿAbd al-Raḥmān.

ʿAlī said: “Ḥayyān ibn Mukhāriq was narrated from by ʿAwf; Ḥayyān al-Aʿraj was narrated from by Manṣūr ibn Zādhān. As for Abū Hilāl, I have been unable to find someone who identifies his lineage.”

Muḥammad said: I asked ʿAlī about ʿAlī ibn Ḥuṣayn, from whom Ibn Jurayj narrated. He said: “ʿAlī ibn Ḥuṣayn ibn Mālik ibn al-Khashkhāsh al-ʿAnbarī; and our judge is ʿUbayd Allāh ibn al-Ḥasan ibn al-Ḥuṣayn.”

He said: ʿAlī said, and Sufyān said: “I saw ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥuṣayn crucified. He held the Khārijite position.”

ʿAlī said: “I have heard that he rebelled in Mecca with the sword of Ḥakam. Ḥuṣayn ibn Abī al-Ḥurr is Mālik ibn al-Khashkhāsh.”

“And Tawbah al-ʿAnbarī ibn Kaysān is Abū al-Muwarriʿ, and he is the son of Abī Asad.”

ʿAlī said: “ʿAwf ibn Abī Ḥumaylah is Abū Sahl, and Jarīr ibn Ḥāzim is Abū al-Naḍr.”

ʿAlī said: “Shuʿbah used to say: ‘Dāwūd ibn Farāhīj related to us,’ though he was weak.”

Ibn Numayr related to me. He said: Abū Muʿāwiyah related to us. He said: Al-Aʿmash related to us, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqamah, who said: “ʿAbd Allāh gave me the kunya Abū Shubayl.”

I heard ʿUmar ibn Ḥafṣ ibn Ghiyāth say: “I found the following genealogies in Ṭalq ibn Ghannām’s book:

“ʿAlqamah ibn Qays ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAlqamah ibn Sulaymān ibn Kuhayl ibn Bakr ibn al-Bashar ibn al-Nakhaʿ ibn ʿAmr.

“Al-Aswad ibn Yazīd ibn Qays ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAlqamah ibn Sulaymān ibn Kuhayl ibn Bakr ibn al-Mubashshir ibn al-Nakhaʿ ibn ʿAmr.”

Ibn Numayr related to us. He said: Ḥafṣ related to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqamah, who said that he said to al-Aswad: “O Abū ʿAmr.”

I heard ʿUmar ibn Ḥafṣ ibn Ghiyāth say: “I found these genealogies in Ṭalq ibn Ghannām’s book.” He said:

“ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd ibn Qays ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAlqamah ibn Sulaymān ibn Kuhayl ibn Bakr ibn al-Mubashshir (327b) ibn al-Nakhaʿ ibn ʿAmr.

“Ubayy ibn Qays ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Qays ibn Sulaymān ibn Kuhayl ibn Bakr ibn Mubashshir ibn al-Nakhaʿ ibn ʿAmr.

“Ibrāhīm ibn Yazīd ibn al-Aswad ibn ʿAmr ibn Rabīʿah ibn Dhuhl ibn Rabīʿah ibn Jāriyah ibn Saʿd ibn Mālik ibn al-Nakhaʿ ibn ʿAmr.

“Mulaykah, the mother of Ibrāhīm, is the daughter of Qays ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAlqamah ibn Sulaymān ibn Kuhayl ibn Bakr ibn al-Mubashshir ibn al-Nakhaʿ ibn ʿAmr. She is the sister of ʿAlqamah ibn Qays. She is the mother of Ibrāhīm ibn Yazīd ibn al-Aswad. The mother of al-Aswad and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, the two sons of Yazīd, is Asmāʾ daughter of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Mālik, the paternal aunt of Ibrāhīm ibn Suwayd.

“Qays ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd ibn al-Mukaffif ibn Qays ibn Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Shayṭān.

“ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Hāniʾ said: Hammām ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Qays ibn ʿAmr ibn Rabīʿah ibn Dhuhl ibn Rabīʿah ibn Khaldathah ibn Miswar.

“He said: Mughallis ibn Bujaylah ibn Qays ibn Shammās, and Thābit ibn Qays ibn Shammās.

“He said: Qays suffered thirty blows on the day of al-Qādisiyyah, between thrusts and strikes. Then he witnessed Ṣiffīn with ʿAlī ﵁.

“Yaḥyā ibn Zakariyyā ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Suwayd ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAwf ibn Sulaymān ibn Kuhayl ibn Bakr ibn al-Mubashshir ibn al-Nakhaʿ ibn ʿAmr; he belonged to the clan of ʿAlqamah. Al-Aswad was from Banū Bakr.

“Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī, Abū ʿImrān.”

Qabīṣah related to us. He said: Sufyān related to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAmr ibn Shuraḥbīl, who was Abū Maysarah.

Al-Ḥumaydī related to us. He said: Sufyān related to us. He said: Ṣāliḥ ibn Ṣāliḥ related to us. He said: “I was with al-Shaʿbī when a man came to him and said, ‘O Abū ʿAmr.’ His name is ʿĀmir ibn Shurāḥīl al-Hamdānī.”

Shurayḥ ibn al-Ḥārith, the judge, is Abū Umayyah.

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā related to us. He said: Shaybān informed us, from al-Aʿmash, from Saʿd ibn Iyās, who was Abū ʿAmr al-Shaybānī.

Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us. He said: Sufyān related to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Muslim ibn ʿImrān al-Baṭīn, the associate of al-Sābirī.

ʿUmar ibn Ḥafṣ ibn Ghiyāth related to us. He said: My father related to us. He said: Al-Aʿmash related to us, from Sulaymān ibn Mushir, from Kharashah ibn al-Ḥurr, who had been an orphan in ʿUmar’s care.

He said: And al-Aʿmash related to us: Ṣāliḥ ibn Ḥayyān al-Kaysamī related to me. He said: Ḥuṣayn ibn ʿAqabah al-Fazārī related to us, ḥ.130

And with the same chain, he said: Al-Aʿmash related to us. He said: Abū Ḥāzim, the client of Jaʿdah—he said:

“Abū Jaʿdah”—Abū Hurayrah said: The Prophet ﷺ said: “There are three to whom God, Mighty and Majestic, will not speak.” With the same chain, he said: Al-Aʿmash related to us. He said: Abū Ḥāzim al-Ashjaʿī related to me. He said:

“I bought straw from Ibn ʿUmar.”

With the same chain, he said: Al-Aʿmash related to us. He said: Ḥuṣayn ibn Jundab al-Khansī related to me, who was Abū Ẓabyān.

ʿUbayd Allāh related to us, from Shaybān, from al-Aʿmash, from Tamīm ibn Salamah al-Sulamī, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Hilāl al-ʿAbsī, from Jarīr, from the Prophet ﷺ said: “Whoever is deprived of gentleness is deprived of good.”

Ādam related to us. He said: Shuʿbah related to us, from al-Aʿmash, who said: I heard Khaythamah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn [Abī] Sabrah.

Abū Nuʿaym related to us. He said: Sufyān related to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Abū al-Ḍuḥā, who was Muslim ibn Ṣubayḥ.

ʿUbayd Allāh related to us, from Shaybān, from al-Aʿmash, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Murrah al-Hamdhānī.

Ibn Numayr related to us. He said: Abū Khālid al-Aḥmar related to us. He said: I heard al-Aʿmash say: “I heard a thousand hadiths from Abū Ṣāliḥ.”

Ibn Numayr related to us. He said: Mūsā ibn ʿĪsā related to us, from Zāʾidah, from al-Aʿmash, from Mundhir, from ʿĀṣim, from ʿAlī ﵁ who said: “There will be five tribulations in this community.”

Ibn Numayr related to us. He said: Abū Nuʿaym related to us, from ʿAbd al-Salām, from al-Aʿmash, from Mundhir, from Ibn al-Ḥanafiyyah, from ʿAlī ﵁ who said: “There will be five tribulations in this community.”

Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shaybah narrated to me: Abū Usāmah narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Mundhir, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḍamrah, from ʿAlī ﵁—who said: ʿAlī ﵁—said, “Mighty and Majestic God placed five tribulations in this community: a general tribulation, then a particular tribulation, then a general tribulation, then a particular tribulation, then a black, dark tribulation, in which people will become like beasts.” Ibn Numayr narrated to me: Ibn Abī ʿUbaydah narrated to us, from his father, from al-Aʿmash, from Mundhir al-Thawrī, from Saʿd ibn Ḥudhayfah, who said: Ḥudhayfah said, “Five tribulations were appointed for this community (328b): a particular tribulation, a general tribulation, a particular tribulation, a general tribulation, and the black, dark tribulation in which people will be like beasts.”

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā narrated to us, from Shaybān, from al-Aʿmash, from Ismāʿīl ibn Rajāʾ al-Zubaydī.

[And from Shaybān, from al-Aʿmash, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Rāzī, who was trustworthy [and unobjectionable], the judge of Rayy].

Al-Ḥumaydī narrated to us: Sufyān narrated to us: al-Aʿmash narrated to us, saying, “I heard Namāmah ibn ʿUqbah al-Muḥallimī.” Al-Aʿmash mentioned that he was a Bedouin, not a hadith scholar.

Ibn Numayr narrated to us: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrāhīm, who said:

ʿAbd Allāh said, “You, people of Yemen, are the people most likely to die without leaving behind your agnatic kin.” I mentioned this to al-Shaʿbī, and he said, “When did Ibrāhīm hear that?” So I went to Ibrāhīm and said to him. He replied, “Hammām narrated to me, from ʿAmr ibn Shuraḥbīl, from ʿAbd Allāh.”

Ibn Numayr narrated to me: Ibn Ḥafṣ ibn Ghiyāth narrated to me, from al-Aʿmash, who said, “We encountered the companions of ʿAbd Allāh campaigning during the rule of al-Ḥajjāj.”

Abū Juḥayfah, Wahb al-Suwāʾī.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bashshār, an Asadī.

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd, a Nakhaʿī.

ʿUmar ibn Ḥafṣ ibn Ghiyāth narrated to me: my father narrated to us: al-Aʿmash narrated to us, saying, “Ziyād ibn al-Ḥuṣayn, Abū Jahmah, narrated to me, from Abū al-ʿĀliyah, Rafīʿ.”

[Ḥafṣ] narrated to us: al-Aʿmash said, “Abū ʿUmārah al-Hamdānī narrated to us, saying, ‘I heard Ḥudhayfah.’”

Abū Nuʿaym narrated to us: Sufyān narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḍirār al-Asadī.

He said: Al-Aʿmash also narrated to us, from Rajāʾ al-Anṣārī.

Ibn Numayr narrated to us: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Thābit ibn Hurmuz, who was Abū al-Miqdām. Abū ʿAmr ibn Abī al-Miqdām.

ʿUbayd Allāh narrated to us, from Shaybān, from al-Aʿmash, from Sahl—whose teknonym was Abū al-Asad—from Bukayr al-Jazarī, from Anas ibn Mālik, from the Prophet ﷺ—who said, “The leaders are from Quraysh.” [Ibn Numayr narrated to me: Ibn Idrīs narrated to us, saying, “I heard al-Aʿmash say, ‘I discussed a hadith with Iyās ibn Muʿāwiyah, and I asked, “From whom do you cite [this]?” He gave me an example from the Khārijites. I said, “Why give this example? Do you want me to sweep the road with my garment, so that I leave behind no dung or beetle without carrying it away?”’”].

ʿUmar ibn Ḥafṣ narrated to us: my father narrated to me: al-Aʿmash narrated to us, saying:

“Zubayd ibn al-Ḥārith narrated to me.”

Ibn Numayr narrated to me—and Ibn Abī Shaybah, from Ibn Numayr, related to them—saying: al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Abū al-Yaqẓān, whose name was ʿUthmān, from Abū Ḥarb ibn Abī al-Aswad, who said:

“I heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar say, ‘I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ—say, “Neither the green canopy nor the dusty earth has shaded or borne anyone more truthful than Abū Dharr.”’” Ibn Numayr narrated to us [saying: my father narrated to us: al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Abū Yaḥyā, the client of Jaʿdah ibn Hubayrah. Ibn Hubayrah said].

Abū Yaḥyā was Thuwair ibn Abī Fākhitah, and Jaʿdah ibn [Hubayrah] was the son of Umm Hānīʾ, daughter of Abū Ṭālib.

ʿUmar ibn Ḥafṣ narrated to me: my father narrated to us: al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Abū al-Ḥasan, whose name was ʿUbayd ibn al-Ḥasan, from Ibn Abī Awfā.

Ibn Numayr narrated to us [saying: my father narrated to us: al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Abū Dāwūd, whose name was Nufayʿ.

Ibn Numayr said]: Ṭalq narrated to us: Sharīk said, “If I had wanted it to be made [to appear] that Abū Dāwūd had heard from ʿAlī and ʿAbd Allāh, I would have said so.”131

Ibn Numayr narrated to me: my father narrated to us: al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim, namely Ibn Bahdalah, Abū al-Najūd.

Abū Nuʿaym narrated to us: al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Jāmiʿ ibn Shaddād, whose teknonym was Abū Ṣakhrah.

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā narrated to us, from Shaybān, from al-Aʿmash, from al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Badr al-Ghanawī.

Ibn Numayr narrated to me: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from his father, who said, “I was a dependent, and Masrūq made me heir to my brother’s estate.”

ʿUbayd Allāh narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yasār al-Juhanī; and al-Aʿmash, from ʿĀmir al-Bāriqī, from al-Ḥasan.

ʿUmar ibn Ḥafṣ narrated to us: my father narrated to us: al-Aʿmash narrated to us, saying, “Abū Surrah al-Nakhaʿī.”

Yaḥyā al-Ḥummānī narrated to me, from Qays, from al-Aʿmash, from ʿAbāyah ibn Ribiʿī al-Asadī.

ʿUmar ibn Ḥafṣ narrated to us, from his father, from al-Aʿmash, who said, “Muʿallā al-Kindī narrated to me,” and he praised him.

Ibn Numayr narrated to me, from Yaʿlā, from al-Aʿmash, from Abū Saʿīd, from Abū al-Kunūd, who said, “ʿAbd Allāh passed by a preacher.”

Ibn Numayr said, “Abū Saʿd.” Ibn Abī Shaybah narrated to me:

and he is the one from whom Yazīd ibn Abī Ziyād narrated.

Ibn Numayr narrated to me, from his father, from al-Aʿmash, from Muʿāwiyah ibn Isḥāq, from Abū Ṣāliḥ al-Ḥanafī (329b).

Ibn Numayr and Ibn Abī Shaybah narrated to me, from Wakīʿ, from al-Aʿmash, from Zuhayr al-ʿAnsī.

And the two of them said: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd ibn Ḥayyān al-Taymī.

Ibn Numayr narrated to me, from his father, from al-Aʿmash, from ʿImrān ibn Muslim, who was a Jaʿfī.

ʿUmar ibn Ḥafṣ narrated to me, from his father, from al-Aʿmash, who said, “Abū ʿAwn Muḥammad ibn ʿUbayd Allāh al-Thaqafī narrated to me.”

Abū ʿĀṣim and Abū Nuʿaym narrated to us, from Sufyān, from al-Aʿmash, from al-Ḥakam al-Asadī, from Nawf.

Abū Nuʿaym said, “It is not Ibn ʿUtaybah, from Nawf, who said, ‘The ants among the Children of Israel were like flies.’”

Ibn Numayr narrated to us: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥakam ibn Nawf.

Ibn al-Ḥummānī narrated to me, from his father, from al-Aʿmash, from Manṣūr, namely Ibn al-Muʿtamir al-Sulamī.

Abū Nuʿaym said: It is not al-Ḥakam ibn ʿUtaybah, from Nawf: “The ants among the Children of Israel were like flies.”

Ibn Numayr narrated to me, from Ibn Abī ʿUbaydah, from his father, from al-Aʿmash, from Ḥuṣayn, namely Ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī.

Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Mandal, from al-Aʿmash, from Saʿīd al-Ṭāʾī.

ʿUmar narrated to me, from his father, from al-Aʿmash, who said, “Ḥamzah, Abū ʿUmārah, narrated to me, from Shahr.”

And from al-Aʿmash: Muḥammad ibn al-Zubayr, the Ḥanẓalī, informed me.

Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shaybah narrated to me: Ibn Idrīs narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, who said, “Maʿbad ibn Khālid and ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Rufayʿ informed me about a variant in the readings: ‘Gardens of Eden, their gates opened for them’ (Qurʾān 38:50)—with the accusative. They asked me, and I said, ‘mufattaḥatan lahum’—in the accusative. Maʿbad then turned to ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz and said, ‘You are a porter.’”

[Ibn Numayr narrated to me, from Abū Khālid, from al-Aʿmash, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk al-Mashriqī, namely Ibn Muzāḥim al-Hilālī].

ʿUmar narrated to me, from his father, from al-Aʿmash, who said, “Abū Mālik narrated to me —and they called him Ḥabīb ibn Ṣahbān al-Kāhilī—.

From al-Aʿmash: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Saʿīd ibn Wahb narrated to me.

And from al-Aʿmash, from Ḥabbah ibn Juwayn.

Qabīṣah ibn ʿUqbah narrated to us, from Sufyān, from al-Aʿmash, from Yaḥyā—namely Ibn ʿUmārah—from Saʿīd, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said, “Abū Ṭālib fell ill.”

Ibn Numayr narrated to me, saying: Ḥafṣ narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash (330a), who said, “A narrator narrated to me from Ghaylān ibn Bishr, who told me: Yaʿlā ibn al-Walīd—one of the reciters of the people of Syria—narrated to me, saying, ‘I walked beside Abū al-Dardāʾ and asked, “Abū al-Dardāʾ, what do you wish for someone you love?” He said, “Death.” I said, “And if he does not die?” He said:

“His wealth and children diminish.”’”

[Abū Bakr narrated to us, saying: Jarīr narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from al-Ḥasan, who said, “We have books that we regularly review.”].

Ibn Numayr narrated to me, saying: Abū al-Jawwāb narrated to us, from ʿAmmār ibn Rizq, from al-Aʿmash, from Shuʿbah, from Thābit, from Anas, who said, “I prayed with the Messenger of God ﷺ—and with Abū Bakr and ʿUmar ﵄—and they did not recite the basmalah aloud.” the Merciful.

Ibn Numayr narrated to me, saying: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, who said, “I saw Anas ibn Mālik, but I did not approach him, being content with my companions.”

Ibn Numayr narrated to me, saying: Yaḥyā ibn ʿĪsā narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from ʿAdī ibn Thābit, who said, “I am one of the generation for whom the Messenger of God ﷺ—prayed.”

Isḥāq ibn Manṣūr narrated to me, from al-Aʿmash, from Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit, who said:

“We were with Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, and in our conversation we mentioned Dharr. He spoke ill of him, so I said, ‘Abū ʿAbd Allāh, he surely loves you and praises you well.’ He said, ‘He will remain astray, seeking his religion every day.’”
