Bashīr entered Egypt on Monday in Rajab and marched until they reached Darnah. Then the wind was not favorable to them, so they returned to Alexandria. Their authorization reached them while they were there, and they returned.

The year ninety-five

Abū al-Qāsim ibn al-Samarqandī informed us; Abū Bakr ibn al-Ṭabarī informed me; Muḥammad Abū al-Ḥusayn informed me; ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar informed me; Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to us, saying: Ibn Bukayr said: Al-Layth ibn Saʿd said: In that year—that is, the year ninety-five—Bashīr ibn al-Walīd, the Commander of the Faithful’s son, led the people on the pilgrimage.

… Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān said: Al-Faḍl—who was Ibn Ziyād—related to me, saying: I heard Abū ʿAbd Allāh say: “Sharīk was born in the year ninety-five”.

The year ninety-eight

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān said: He—that is, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Kaʿb al-Anṣārī—died during the caliphate of Sulaymān ibn ʿAbd al-Malik.

The year ninety-nine

Al-Khaṭīb al-Baghdādī related, by way of Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān al-Ḥāfiẓ, from Saʿīd ibn Abī Maryam, from Rashdīn ibn Saʿd, who said: ʿUqayl related to me, from [Ibn] Shihāb, from ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, who said:

“The Messenger of God and the caliphs after him established practices. Following them is affirmation of the Book of God and observance of obedience to God. No one may alter or change them, nor consider the opinion of anyone who opposes them. Whoever follows what came before is guided; whoever seeks insight through them sees clearly; and whoever opposes them and follows a path other than that of the believers, God will turn him toward that to which he has turned and consign him to Hell—an evil destination.”

One day ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ordered his caller to announce to the people, “The prayer is about to begin!” The people gathered, and he delivered a sermon to them. In it he said:

“I have gathered you only because one of you who affirms what lies before him—meeting with God and the Abode of the Hereafter—but does not act for it or prepare for it is a fool; and whoever denies it is an unbeliever.”

Then he recited the words of the Exalted: “Indeed, they are in doubt about meeting their Lord” (41:54), and His words: “Most of them do not believe in God without also associating others with Him” (12:106).

The year one hundred

In Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān’s chronicle, from Yaḥyā ibn Bukayr, from al-Layth, it says: In the year one hundred, al-Mughīra ibn Abī Burda set out with the army for Ifrīqiya.

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān mentioned in the chronicle, saying:

“In that year—that is, the year one hundred—ʿAbbās ibn Ajīl [spelled with a dotted sīn and a bāʾ] came from al-Andalus to Ifrīqiya. That is how I saw it vocalized; God knows best”.

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān said: Abū Nuʿaym said: Ribʿī ibn Ḥirāsh died during the time of ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz.

(The letter of al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī to ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz):

Abū Ḥāmid ibn Jabala related to us; Abū al-ʿAbbās al-Sarrāj related to us; ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Ḥarb ibn Jabala related to us; Ḥamza ibn Rashīd Abū ʿAlī related to us; ʿAmr ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Qurashī related to me, from Abū Ḥumayd al-Shāmī, who said: Al-Ḥasan wrote to ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz.

Muḥammad ibn Badr related to me; Ḥammād ibn Mudrik related to us; Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to us; Muḥammad ibn Yazīd al-Laythī related to us; Maʿn ibn ʿĪsā related to us; Ibrāhīm related to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī al-Aswad, from al-Ḥasan, that he wrote to ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz—the version given here follows Abū Ḥumayd al-Shāmī:

“Know that reflection calls one to goodness and acting upon it, and regret for evil calls one to abandon it. What perishes, however plentiful, is not equal to what endures, even if it is hard to attain. Bearing a temporary hardship that is followed by rest that lasts is better than hastening to a temporary rest followed by an enduring hardship. Beware this ruinous, deceptive, beguiling abode, adorned by its deceptions and deluding through its vanity. It has slain its people with its hopes and has made itself alluring to its suitors. It is like a bride displayed in her finery: eyes gaze upon her, souls fall in love with her, hearts are enamored of her, and minds are captivated by her. Yet she kills all her husbands. The one who remains is not admonished by the one who has passed; the later one is not deterred by what he has seen of the earlier one; the intelligent person does not benefit from many experiences; and the one who knows God and believes what He has told him about it does not take heed. Hearts insist on loving it, and souls insist on clinging to it. This is nothing but infatuation with it; whoever loves something sees nothing else clearly, and dies in pursuit of it or attains it. They are two lovers pursuing it: one lover has attained it, become deluded and transgressed, and forgotten through it the beginning and the return. It occupied his mind and bewildered his reason until his foot slipped away from it. Then, when he was most secure in it, his appointed time came, and his regret grew great, his sorrow multiplied, and his anguish intensified, along with what he suffered in his death throes.

The agonies of death gathered upon him with their pain, and death’s sorrows with their constriction; what came upon him cannot be described. The other died before attaining what he wanted from it: he departed with his anguish and grief, gained none of what he sought from it, and found no relief from toil and hardship. Both set out without provisions and arrived without a resting place.

Beware of it with all your caution, for it is like a snake: its touch is gentle, but its poison kills. Turn away from whatever delights you in it, for little of it will accompany you. Lay aside its burdens, having witnessed its calamities and become certain of its departure. Bear firmly whatever hardship comes from it, in hope of the ease that will reach you— And when you are at your most135 secure in it, be most wary of it. For whoever feels at ease in it on account of some joy, it soon drives him away from it with something displeasing; and whenever he gains something from it and sets his foot upon it, it turns against him. What brings joy in it is deceptive, and what benefits in it today brings harm tomorrow. It joins ease in it to affliction, and makes life in it lead to extinction. Its joy is mingled with sorrow, and the end of life in it is weakness and frailty. Look upon it, then, with the gaze of one who renounces and departs; do not look upon it with the gaze of a passionate lover. Know that it removes the settled and dwelling, and brings grief upon the deceived and secure. What has passed from it does not return; what is coming in it is unknown, and so one waits.

Beware of it, for its promises are false and its hopes vain. Its life is misery; its clarity, clouded; and you are in danger from it. Either a blessing that passes away, a calamity that descends, a painful misfortune, or a death that brings matters to an end. Life has nearly become constricted for the one who understands: he is in danger from its blessings, wary of its trials, and certain of death. If the Creator, exalted is He, had not told us anything about it, set forth no parable concerning it, and commanded no renunciation of it, this abode itself would have awakened the sleeper and roused the heedless. How much more so, when there has come from God, exalted is He, a deterrent concerning it and an admonition within it! It has no worth with God, mighty and glorious is He, nor any weight with God, exalted is He, even the least. It does not weigh with God, exalted is He, as much as a pebble among pebbles, nor as much as a speck of dust among all the dust. As far as I have learned, He created nothing more hateful to Him than this world, nor has He looked upon it since He created it except with loathing. The keys and treasures of this world were offered to our Prophet ﷺ yet they did not diminish his standing with God by so much as a gnat’s wing. He refused to accept them. Nothing kept him from accepting them—nor would accepting them have diminished anything with God, exalted is He—except that he knew God, exalted is He, hated something, and so he hated it; deemed something insignificant, and so he deemed it insignificant; and set something low, and so he set it low. Had he accepted them, that would have been proof of his love for it, since he would have accepted it. But he disliked loving what its Creator hated, and raising up what its Sovereign had lowered.

Even if nothing else showed him the smallness of this abode, it would be enough that God, exalted is He, deemed it too low to make its best things the reward of the obedient or its punishment the torment of the disobedient. He removed the reward for obedience from it and the punishment for disobedience from it. The evil of this abode is also shown by the fact that God, exalted is He, withheld it from His prophets and beloved ones as a test, while extending it to others as a lesson and a snare. The one deceived by it and captivated by it thinks that God has honored him with it, and forgets what He did for Muḥammad the Chosen ﷺ and Moses the Chosen ﵇: speaking to him and conversing with him. As for Muḥammad ﷺ he tied a stone around his belly from hunger. As for Moses ﵇ the green of the plants was visible through the thinness of his belly from emaciation. When he took shelter in the shade, he asked God, exalted is He, for nothing but food to eat, because of his hunger. Traditions have come down concerning him that God, exalted is He, revealed to him: “Moses, when you see poverty approaching, say, ‘Welcome, badge of the righteous’; and when you see wealth approaching, say, ‘A sin whose punishment has been hastened.’”

If you wish, add to them a third: the one who is Spirit and Word. There is something wondrous in his way of life. He used to say: “My food is hunger, my emblem is fear, my clothing is wool, my mount is my own feet, my lamp by night is the moon, my warming place in winter is the sun, and my fruit and fragrance are what the earth grows for beasts and livestock. I pass the night with nothing, yet no one is richer than I am.” If you wish, add a fourth: Solomon son of David ﵉. He is no less wondrous than they. In private he ate barley bread, while he fed his family coarse flour and the people fine white flour. When night came, he wore sackcloth, bound his hand to his neck, and spent the night weeping until morning. He ate coarse food and wore garments of hair. All of them hated what God, mighty and glorious is He, hated; considered insignificant what God, exalted is He, considered insignificant; and renounced what He renounced. Then the righteous followed their path and followed in their footsteps. They committed themselves to toil and136 They refined their thought and endured throughout the short allotted term, turning away from the delusion’s enjoyment that ends in extinction. They considered the end of this world, not its beginning; they considered the outcome of its bitterness, not the immediate sweetness of it. Then they made themselves endure patiently, regarding this world as carrion, of which it is not lawful to eat one’s fill except when necessity requires it. They ate of it only as much as would sustain the self and preserve the spirit. They made it serve their needs for the day, and regarded it as a carcass whose stench had grown strong, so that everyone who passed by held his nose against it. They took from it only what necessity required and did not eat their fill of its stench. So it was kept away from them, and this was its place in their estimation. They marvel at the one who eats his fill of it and takes pleasure in it with insolence. They say to themselves, “Do these people not fear eating? Do they not smell the stench?” By God, my brother, in its final outcome and the Hereafter it stinks more than a carcass piled up in a heap. Yet some people have hastened their endurance, and so they do not smell the stench. One who has grown up amid the stench of a foul hide does not notice its stink, nor does he detect in its smell anything that troubles passersby or those sitting beside him. It may suffice the intelligent person that, if he died leaving much wealth, he would be glad he had been poor in this world; if he had been eminent, he would be glad he had been lowly in it; if he had been healthy in it, he would be glad he had been afflicted in it; or if he had held power in it, he would be glad he had been an ordinary subject. And when you leave it, you will be glad if you were the least protected of its people and the most needy among them. Is that not proof, for whoever understands its nature, of its disgrace?

By God, if this world were such that whoever wanted something from it found it at his side without seeking or toil, yet if he took anything from it, God’s claims upon it would bind him, He would question him about it, and hold him to account then the intelligent person ought to take from it only what sustains him and suffices him, out of fear of being questioned and dislike of the severity of the reckoning. This world, if you reflect upon it, consists of three days: a day [that has passed], which you do not hope to regain; a day in which you are now, which you ought to seize; and a day [to come], though you do not know whether you will be among those who see it—or whether you may die before it. As for yesterday, it is a wise teacher; as for today, it is a friend bidding farewell. Though yesterday has grieved you by departing, it has left its wisdom in your hands. Even if you wasted it, a replacement has come to you. It had been away from you for a long time, but now it is on a swift journey away from you; tomorrow, too, holds a hope for you. So take assurance from deeds, and abandon delusion through hope before the appointed term arrives. Beware of bringing into today the worry of tomorrow or the day after it: you will add to your grief and toil, and seek to gather into your day what would suffice you for all your days. How far-fetched! Work has multiplied, grief increased, toil grown great, and the servant has wasted his deeds through hope. If hope for tomorrow were to leave your heart, you would do well today in your work and limit yourself to today’s concerns. Yet hope for tomorrow in you has called you to neglect, and called you to seek more.

If you wish, and are content with this, I will describe the world for you as an hour between two hours: an hour that has passed, an hour to come, and the hour in which you are now. As for the past and the future, you will find no pleasure in their ease and no pain in their affliction. The world is only the hour in which you are now. That hour has deceived you away from Paradise and brought you to the Fire. Today, if you understand, is a guest who has come to you and will soon depart. If you treat it well and honor it, it will bear witness for you, praise you for that, and speak truthfully about you. But if you treat it as a poor guest and do not honor it, it will stand before your eyes137

They are two days, like two brothers. One of them came to you, and you wronged him and did not honor him while he was with you. Then the other came after him and said, “I have come to you after my brother. Your kindness to me will erase your wrong toward him and forgive you for what you did. So take advantage: I have come to you after my brother, who has departed from you. If you understand, you have found a replacement for him. Make amends for what you wasted.

If you make the second follow the first in this way, how likely you are to perish through the testimony of both against you! What remains of a lifetime has no price and no equivalent. Were you to gather the entire world, it would not equal one remaining day of its possessor’s life. So do not sell today, and do not exchange it for any part of this world unless you receive its price. Let not the one buried in his grave value what is in your hands more than you do, when it belongs to you. By my life, if someone buried in his grave were told, “This world, from beginning to end, will be yours to give to your children after you, so that they may enjoy it when you are gone; or you may have a day in which you leave them and work for yourself”—he would choose that day. And he would choose nothing to accompany that day; rather, he would choose the day itself over it, desiring it and honoring it. Indeed, were he offered an hour of its goodness, and all that I have described to you multiplied many times over, and multiplied again, for someone else, he would still choose that hour for himself over all of that for someone else. Rather, were he offered just one word to say, to be recorded for him, and all that I have described to you multiplied many times over for someone else, he would choose that one word over it. So take stock of today for yourself, pay heed to the hour, magnify the word, and beware of regret when the death throes descend. Do not be sure that this discourse will not stand as an argument against you. May God benefit us and you through admonition, and grant us and you the best of outcomes. Peace be upon you, and God’s mercy and blessings.

Ismāʿīl ibn Aḥmad al-Samarqandī informed us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Hibat Allāh al-Ṭabarī informed us, saying: Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Faḍl reported to us, saying: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar ibn Durustawayh reported to us, saying: Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān reported to us, saying: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān reported to us, saying: ʿAwn ibn Maʿmar reported to us, saying: “Al-Ḥasan wrote to ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz: ‘To proceed: it is as though the last person upon whom death was decreed has died.’” ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz wrote to him: “To proceed: it is as though you had never been in this world, and as though you had always been in the Hereafter.

Peace be upon you”.

Year 101 AH

Ibn al-Faḍl informed us; Ibn Durustawayh reported to us; Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related: Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb said: ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz died in the year 101.

Abū al-Qāsim ibn al-Samarqandī informed us; Abū Bakr ibn al-Ṭabarī reported to us; Abū al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Faḍl related to us; ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar related to us; Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān said: In that year—that is, the year 101—Ayyūb ibn Sharāḥīl was removed from office, and Bishr ibn Ṣafwān was appointed—that is, over Egypt.

Year 102 AH

In that year Bishr ibn Ṣafwān was appointed governor of Ifrīqiya, and he appointed his brother Ḥanẓala as his deputy in Egypt.

In that year al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Muzāḥim al-Hilālī died.

Year 103 AH

In that year ʿUrwa was dismissed from authority over the people of Yemen, and Masʿūd ibn Ghawth was appointed.

Year 105 AH

In that year Bishr—that is, ibn Ṣafwān—was dismissed from Ifrīqiya.

Year 106 AH

In that year Bishr ibn Ṣafwān returned as governor of Ifrīqiya.

Year 109 AH

Abū al-Qāsim ibn al-Samarqandī informed us, saying: Abū Bakr ibn al-Ṭabarī reported to us; Abū al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Faḍl related to us; ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar related to us; Yaʿqūb said: In that year—that is, the year 109—Bishr ibn Ṣafwān died.

Year 110 AH

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān said: Saʿīd ibn Asad related to me; Ḥamza related to us, from Ibn Shawdhab, who said: Ibn Sīrīn died one hundred nights after al-Ḥasan.

Year 113 AH

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān said: al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Makhlad al-Shaybānī died in the year 113.

Year 114 AH

In that year Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn—the Bāqir—died.

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān said, from Ḥaywa ibn Shurayḥ, from ʿAbbās ibn al-Faḍl, from Ḥammād ibn Salama: “I came to Mecca in the year ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ died, 114 AH”.

Year 117 AH

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn al-Qaṭṭān informed us; ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar ibn Durustawayh reported to us; Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to us, saying: Abū Nuʿaym said: Qatāda died in the year 117.

Year 119 AH

Abū al-Qāsim ibn Abī al-Ashʿath reported to us; Muḥammad ibn Hibat Allāh reported to us; Muḥammad Abū al-Ḥusayn related to us; ʿAbd Allāh related to us; Yaʿqūb said: In that year—that is, the year 119—al-Zuhrī went out with Abū Shākir ibn Hishām. Hishām remitted for him seventeen thousand dinars, which al-Zuhrī had been using to buy off a debt owed to the sultan. Al-Zuhrī stayed at the home of the Banū al-Dayl, among his maternal uncles, because his mother was of the Bagāthiyya. Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd, Rabīʿa, and the people used to visit him. Some of the people of Medina claim that on this visit al-Zuhrī provided servants in a single night for fifteen women of the Banū Zuhra, one servant for each woman.

Through the preceding chain of transmission, Yaʿqūb related to us; Zayd ibn Bishr related to us; Ibn Wahb reported to me: al-Layth told me, from Akīma, who said: “Were it not for Ibn Shihāb, many of the Prophetic practices would have been lost”.

He said: Yaʿqūb related to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥīm related to me, saying: ʿAlī said: “Those who gave legal opinions were al-Ḥakam, Ḥammād, Qatāda, and al-Zuhrī; and in my view al-Zuhrī was the most learned of them”.

Year 120 AH

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān said: al-ʿAbbās ibn al-Walīd ibn Ṣubḥ related to us; ʿArfa ibn Ismāʿīl related to us, from Ibn Idrīs, who said: I heard Shuʿba say: Ḥammād ibn Abī Sulaymān died in the year 120. Ibn Idrīs said: “I was born in that year”.

Year 122 AH

Yaʿqūb al-Fasawī said: Zayd ibn ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn had come to Kūfa and rebelled there because he had disputed with Hishām ibn ʿAbd al-Malik over the matter of Muʿāwiya, and Hishām rejected his argument and spoke harshly to him.

Year 124 AH

Abū al-Qāsim al-Samarqandī informed us; Abū Bakr Muḥammad ibn Hibat Allāh reported to us; Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn related to us; ʿAbd Allāh related to us; Yaʿqūb said: Abū Nuʿaym said: al-Zuhrī died in the year 124.

Through the preceding chain of transmission, Yaʿqūb related to us; Ḥāmid ibn Yaḥyā and Yūsuf ibn Muḥammad related to us, saying: Maʿn ibn ʿĪsā said: My nephew Ibn Shihāb told me: “Ibn Shihāb died in the year 124.”

Yaʿqūb said: Al-Zuhrī died at his properties in Shiʿb. I passed by his grave there; he was buried on open ground. It is said that he died on the night of Tuesday, when seventeen nights of Ramaḍān had passed.

Through the preceding chain of transmission, Yaʿqūb related to us; al-ʿAbbās ibn al-Walīd told me; my father informed me— Saʿīd ibn Bashīr informed me, from Qatāda, who said: “The last of the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ to die in Mecca was ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar.”

Ibn Bukayr said: “Al-Zuhrī was then sixteen years old”.

Through the preceding chain of transmission, Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to us; Ibrāhīm ibn al-Mundhir related to us, from Maʿn—that is, ibn ʿĪsā—from the nephew of Ibn Shihāb, who said: “Ibn Shihāb compiled the Qurʾān in eighty days”.

Year 125 AH

Abū al-Qāsim ibn al-Samarqandī informed us; Abū Bakr ibn al-Ṭabarī reported to us; Abū al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Faḍl related to us; ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar related to us; Yaʿqūb said: Ibn Bukayr said: al-Layth said:

In that year—that is, the year 125—Balj ibn Bishr was killed, after Ibn Qaṭan had crossed over to the people of al-Andalus as their governor. Balj died two months later.

Year 126 AH

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān said: Muḥammad ibn Khālid ibn al-ʿAbbās al-Saksakī related to me; al-Walīd ibn Muslim related to me; Abū ʿAmr al-Awzāʿī related to me, from Ibn Shihāb, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, who said: “A boy was born to the brother of Umm Salama, and they named him al-Walīd. The Messenger of God ﷺ said: ‘You have begun giving your children the names of your tyrants. In this community there will be a man called al-Walīd who will be more harmful to my community than Pharaoh was to his people.’” Abū ʿAmr al-Awzāʿī said: “People used to think that he meant al-Walīd ibn ʿAbd al-Malik. Then we came to think that he meant al-Walīd ibn Yazīd, because of the turmoil people faced on his account, until they rose up against him— So they killed him, and tribulation and bloodshed broke out among the community.

The Year 128

Ibn al-Faḍl informed us; ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar informed us; Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to us: I heard one of the scholars of Egypt say: Yazīd—that is, Ibn Abī Ḥabīb al-Miṣrī—was born in the year 53 and died in the year 128.

The Year 131

Al-Qaṭṭān informed us; Ibn Durustawayh informed us; Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to us: I heard Abū ʿUmar al-Ḍarīr say: Ibrāhīm al-Ṣāʾigh, Ibrāhīm ibn Maymūn, was killed by Abū Muslim in the year 131.

Someone other than Abū ʿUmar said: He was killed in the year 130.

The Year 132

In it, Ḍirār ibn Murra, Abū Sinān al-Shaybānī, died.

The ʿAbbāsid Era

The Year 133

In it, Dāwūd ibn ʿAlī died while governor over Medina.

The Year 134

(The Battle of Ṭalkh)

In it, Yaʿqūb al-Fasawī said: The ruler of China made a military move. Ziyād ibn Ṣāliḥ was at Samarqand, and news of this reached him: the ruler of China had advanced with one hundred thousand, besides the Turks who followed him. Ziyād ibn Ṣāliḥ mustered his troops and wrote to Abū Muslim about the matter. Abū Muslim mustered at Marw, gathered his armies, and Khalid ibn Ibrāhīm came to him from Ṭukhāristān. The army of Khurāsān marched to Samarqand in Shawwāl of the year 134, and [Abū Muslim] reinforced Ziyād ibn Ṣāliḥ with ten thousand. Ziyād marched with his armies until he crossed the river of al-Shāsh. The Chinese army advanced, and they besieged Saʿīd ibn Ḥumayd. When they learned that Ziyād was approaching, they withdrew. Then the ruler of the Chinese mountains encamped at the city of Ṭalkh, and Ziyād marched against him. They met the following day. Ziyād placed the archers in a line before the army; behind them were the spear-bearers, then the cavalry, then the infantry. He also prepared a force of cavalry in ambush. The two armies met, and both sides stood firm through the day until nightfall. When the sun set, God cast terror into the hearts of the Chinese, and victory descended, so the unbelievers were routed.

The Year 150

… Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān said: I heard Makkī ibn Ibrāhīm say: Ibn Jurayj died in the year 150.

The Year 187

In it, Zakariyyā ibn Yaḥyā al-Dhāriʿ died.

The Year 207

In it, Rūḥ ibn ʿUbāda al-Qaysī died.

Texts on the Knowledge of Men, Quoted from the Book al-Maʿrifa wa-l-tārīkh Abū al-Qāsim ibn al-Samarqandī informed us; Abū Bakr ibn al-Ṭabarī informed us; Abū al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Faḍl informed us; ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar informed us; Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to us: Muḥammad ibn Muqātil al-Marwazī related to me; Aws—he is Ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Burayda—related to us, from his brother, who, I think, reported it from his father. He said: My father died at Marw, and his grave is at Ḥuṣayn. My father told me: I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: “Whoever among my Companions dies in a land will be their leader on the Day of Resurrection.” He transmitted it with uncertainty, while others transmitted it from Aws without uncertainty.

From Yaʿqūb al-Fasawī, with a fine chain of transmission, raised to the Prophet: “On the Day of Resurrection, an old man will be brought whose limbs are trembling and whose knees are knocking together”. In the biographical entry for ʿImrān ibn Khālid ibn Ṭalīq al-Khuzāʿī, it is stated that he transmitted from his forefathers the report, “Looking at ʿAlī is an act of worship”; Yaʿqūb al-Fasawī transmitted it from him. Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān said: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad al-Azraqī informed us; al-Zinjī related to us, from al-ʿAlāʾ ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from his father, from Abū Hurayra, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “In a dream I saw the sons of Abū al-Ḥakam ibn Abī al-ʿĀṣ leaping about on my pulpit as monkeys leap.” He said: Thereafter, the Messenger of God ﷺ was never seen laughing wholeheartedly again until he died. Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān said: Ṣafwān related to us; al-Walīd ibn Muslim related to us; ʿAbd Allāh—or ʿAbd al-Ghaffār—ibn Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAbd Allāh related to us, from his father, who told him, from an early Muslim scholar…

He said: I heard Abū al-Dardāʾ say: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “I shall precede you at the Basin, waiting for those of you who come to me. Let me not find myself disputing with one of you, saying, ‘He is one of my community,’ only to be told, ‘Do you know what they introduced after you?’”

Abū al-Dardāʾ said: I feared that I might be among them, so I went to the Messenger of God ﷺ and told him about it. He said: “You are not among them.” Abū al-Dardāʾ died before ʿUthmān was killed and before the tribulations occurred.

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān transmitted from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā, from Isrāʾīl, from Manṣūr, from Ribʿī, from al-Barāʾ ibn Nājiya al-Kāhilī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “The millstone of Islam will turn at thirty-five, or thirty-seven. If it is destroyed, that is the way of those who have been destroyed; but if their religion remains established, it will remain established for them for seventy years.”

He said: ʿUmar asked, “O Messenger of God, by what has passed, or by what remains?” He replied, “Rather, by what remains”. Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān said: Muḥammad ibn Fuḍayl related to me; Muʾammal related to us; Ḥammād ibn Salama related to us, from ʿAlī ibn Zayd, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakra, who said:

I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: “Prophetic succession lasts thirty years; then God grants His dominion to whomever He wills.” Muʿāwiya said, “We are content with dominion”. Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAmr al-Ḥizāmī informed us; Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān related to us, from Abū Tamīm al-Baʿlabakkī, from Hishām ibn al-Ghāz, from Makhūl from Abū Thaʿlaba al-Khushanī, from Abū ʿUbayda ibn al-Jarrāḥ, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “This affair will continue to be balanced and upheld with justice until a man from the Umayyads makes a breach in it”. Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān said: ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Muʿādh related to us; my father related to us; Shuʿba related to us, from Abū Salama, from Abū Naḍra, from Abū Hurayra, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said to ten of his Companions: “The last of you to die will be in the Fire.” Among them was Samura ibn Jundub. Abū Naḍra said: Samura was the last of them to die.

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān said: Ḥajjāj ibn Minhāl related to us; Ḥammād ibn Salama related to us, from ʿAlī ibn Zayd, from Aws ibn Khālid, who said: When I came to Abū Maḥdhūra, he would ask me about Samura; and when I came to Samura, he would ask me about Abū Maḥdhūra. I said to Abū Maḥdhūra, “Why is it that when I come to you, you ask me about Samura, and when I come to Samura, he asks me about you?” He said: “Samura, Abū Hurayra, and I were in a house when the Prophet ﷺ came and said, ‘The last of you to die will be in the Fire.’” He said: Abū Hurayra died, then Abū Maḥdhūra died, then Samura died.

The ḥāfiẓ al-Bayhaqī transmitted by way of Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān: Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us; Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, from Muḥammad ibn Zayd, from Muḥammad ibn al-Zubayr al-Ḥanẓalī, who said: Al-Zibriqān ibn Badr, Qays ibn ʿĀṣim, and ʿAmr ibn al-Ahtam came to the Messenger of God ﷺ. He said to ʿAmr ibn al-Ahtam, “Tell me about al-Zibriqān. As for this one, I will not ask you about him”—and I think he already knew Qays. He said:

“He is obeyed among his close associates, forceful in argument, and protective of what lies behind his back.” Al-Zibriqān then said, “He has said what he has said, though he knows that I am better than what he said. He said…”

…“what he said, while knowing that I am better than what he said.” ʿAmr said, “By God, I know you only as a man who obstructs honorable conduct, narrow-minded, foolish in his paternal lineage, and ignoble in his maternal uncle.” Then he said, “Messenger of God, I have spoken truthfully about them both: I pleased him, so I said the best I knew of him; and I angered him, so I said the worst I knew.” The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Indeed, some eloquence is magic”. Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān said: Abū al-Nuʿmān Muḥammad ibn al-Faḍl related to us; Abū ʿAwāna related to us, from Qatāda, from Safīna, from Umm Salama, who said: At the time of his death, the Messenger of God ﷺ made prayer and those whom your right hands possess the main subject of his bequest. He continued to repeat it in his chest, scarcely able to articulate it with his tongue.

Al-Bayhaqī said: Abū al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Faḍl al-Qaṭṭān informed us; ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar informed us; Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān informed us; Muslim ibn Ibrāhīm related to us; Shuʿba related to us, from Sulaymān al-Aʿmash, from Ibrāhīm, from al-Aswad, from ʿĀʾisha, that the Messenger of God ﷺ prayed behind Abū Bakr.

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān said: Hishām ibn ʿAmmār related to us; ʿAmr ibn Wāqid related to us; Yūnus ibn Maysara related to us, from Abū Idrīs, from Muʿādh ibn Jabal, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “I saw that I was placed on one pan of a scale and my community on the other, and I outweighed them. Then Abū Bakr was placed on one pan and my community on the other, and he outweighed them. Then ʿUmar was placed on one pan and my community on the other, and he outweighed them. Then ʿUthmān was placed on one pan and my community on the other…”

…and he outweighed them. Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān transmitted by way of al-Naḍr ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār, from Ibn Lahīʿa, from Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb, who related to him from Ibn Shamāsa, from a man who told him that he had heard ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAdīs say: I heard the Prophet ﷺ say: “People will emerge, passing out of the religion as an arrow passes through its quarry. They will be killed at Mount Lebanon and Hebron”. In his History, Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān transmitted by way of Ṣāliḥ ibn Kaysān, from Ibn Shihāb, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Kaʿb ibn Mālik, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Who is your chief, Banū Naḍla?” They said, “Jadd ibn Qays.”

He said, “What makes you call him your chief?” They replied, “He has more wealth than any of us, though we would indeed consider him a miser.”

He said, “What ailment is more grievous than miserliness? This man is not your chief.” They said, “Then who is our chief, Messenger of God?” He replied, “Bishr ibn al-Barāʾ ibn Maʿrūr”. Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān transmitted by way of Yaḥyā ibn Rāshid, from Dahtham ibn Dalham, from ʿĀbid ibn Rabīʿa al-Qurayʿī, from Qurra ibn Damʿūṣ, that al-Ḥārith ibn Shurayḥ set out for the Prophet ﷺ.

Imām Aḥmad said: Abū Saʿīd, the client of Banū Hāshim, related to us; al-Dhayyāl ibn ʿUbayd related to us: I heard my grandfather Ḥanẓala ibn Ḥudhaym. My father related to me that my grandfather Ḥanīfa said to Khudaym, “Gather my sons for me.” He then gave them his instructions, saying: “My orphan, who is in my care, is owed one hundred camels…”

Ḥudhaym said: “Father, I heard your sons saying, ‘We are only agreeing to this so that our father’s eyes may be comforted; when he dies, we will take it back.’” So they went up to the Messenger of God ﷺ. Ḥanīfa and Ḥudhaym came, along with those who were with them, including Ḥanẓala, who was a boy riding behind his father, Ḥudhaym. Ḥanīfa recounted his story to the Prophet ﷺ. He said: The Prophet became angry, knelt, and said, “No, no. The charitable gift is five; otherwise, ten; otherwise, twenty; otherwise, thirty; and if it is more, then forty.” He said: They took their leave, and the orphan had a staff with him. The Prophet ﷺ said, “How great is this orphan’s staff!” Ḥudhaym said, “I have sons with beards, and this one is the youngest of them”—meaning Ḥanẓala—“so pray to God for him.” He stroked his head and said, “May God bless you”—or he said, “May you be blessed.”

Al-Dhayyāl said: I saw Ḥanẓala brought a person whose face was swollen. He would spit on his hands, say, “In the name of God,” and place his hand on the person’s head, at the spot where the Messenger of God ﷺ had placed his palm. He would stroke it, then stroke the place of the swelling, and the swelling would disappear. Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān transmitted it likewise. Abū Mūsā transmitted from Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān’s History, by way of Ṣafwān ibn ʿAmr, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿAwf, from ʿUtba ibn ʿUbayd al-Thumālī, who attributed to the Prophet: “None of my community will enter Paradise before the rest except Ibrāhīm and Ismāʿīl”—the report continues.

In his History, Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān transmitted from Sahl ibn Waqāṣ ibn Sarīʿ, who related to me: My uncle Sarīʿ ibn Sarīʿ related to us; my uncle Kurayz ibn Abī Waqāṣ related to us, that his father Waqāṣ ibn Sarīʿ told him, that his father Sarīʿ ibn al-Ḥakam told him: I went out with a delegation from Banū Tamīm until we came to the Messenger of God ﷺ and we presented to him…

the alms due on our wealth,” and he related the report in full.

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān transmitted, through Sulaymān ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Maṭar ibn ʿAlāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Yasār al-Thaqafī, who told me: Abū Umayya al-Shaʿbānī—who had been a pagan—told me: Muʿādh ibn Jabal related from the Prophet: “Thirty years of caliphate and prophethood, then thirty years of caliphate and kingship, then thirty years of kingship and tyranny; whatever comes after that contains no good”. In his entry on Ghiyāth in al-Muʾtalif, al-Khaṭīb cited a report transmitted by Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān, from Ṣāliḥ ibn Sulaymān, from Ghiyāth ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, from Maṭar, from al-Ḥasan, from Abū Waqqāṣ, a Companion of the Prophet, who said: “The shares of the callers to prayer in God’s sight on the Day of Resurrection are like the shares of those who strive in God’s cause. During the time between the call to prayer and the commencement of prayer, they are like one drenched in his blood in the cause of God, the Mighty and Glorious”. In the Book of Heart-Softening Reports of Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, following the report of ʿUthmān ibn al-Aswad, from Ibn Abī Mulayka, from ʿĀʾisha, comes the ḥadīth: “Whoever is scrutinized in the reckoning will be punished.”

Ibn Jurayj and Muḥammad ibn Sulaym corroborated it, as did others—that is, from Ibn Abī Mulayka. Ibn Ḥajar said: “The reports of Ibn Jurayj and those mentioned with him were transmitted by Abū ʿAwāna in his Ṣaḥīḥ, from Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān and others, from Abū ʿĀṣim, from them”.

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān transmitted, from the ḥadīth of Ḥafṣ ibn Ghiyāth, from Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: “I saw the Prophet wipe his head once”.

Ibn Sufyān said: Al-Ḥasan ibn Bishr narrated it to us; ʿAbd Allāh ibn Numayr narrated to us [my father narrated to us], from ʿUbayd Allāh, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, the ḥadīth “Each of you is a shepherd,” and the rest of the ḥadīth.

Al-Qaṭṭān informed us; ʿAbd Allāh informed us; Yaʿqūb told us: Ibrāhīm ibn al-Mundhir told us; ʿAbbās ibn Abī Shamlah told us, from Mūsā ibn Yaʿqūb, from Asīd ibn ʿAlī ibn ʿUbayd, from his father, from Abū Asīd al-Sāʿidī, who said: “I was the youngest of the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ and the one who heard the most from him. The Messenger of God ﷺ said: ‘A child’s filial duty to a parent after the parent’s death consists of four things: praying for the parent, supplicating for the parent, carrying out the parent’s bequest after death, maintaining ties with the parent’s kin, and honoring the parent’s friend’”.

I am al-Qaṭṭān; ʿAbd Allāh told us; Yaʿqūb told us: Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb told us; Sulaymān ibn al-Mughīra and Ḥammād ibn Zayd told us, from Thābit, from Anas ibn Mālik, who said: “I served the Prophet ﷺ for ten years. He never once said ‘Uff!’ to me, nor did he ever say of anything I had done, ‘Why did you do such-and-such?’ or of anything I had not done, ‘Would that you had done such-and-such!’”

Al-Ḥasan ibn Abī Bakr informed us; ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar told us; Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān told us; Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmmār ibn Sawāda al-Ghāmidī of Mosul told us Yaʿqūb ibn Isḥāq al-Ḥaḍramī told us, from Sulaymān ibn Muʿādh, from Muḥammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Nothing is to be asked of God by His countenance except Paradise”.

Al-Ḥasan ibn Abī Bakr informed us; ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar ibn Darastawayh informed us; Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān told us; Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Anṣārī told us; Ismāʿīl ibn Sulaymān al-Yashkurī told us; ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aws al-Khuzāʿī told me that Burayda al-Aslamī told them that the Prophet of God ﷺ said: “Give glad tidings of perfect light on the Day of Resurrection to those who walk to the mosques through the darkness”.

Al-Ḥasan ibn Abī Bakr informed us; Ibn Darastawayh informed us; Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān told us; Abū Bakr Fahd ibn Ḥayyān told us; Ḥafṣ ibn Ghiyāth told us, from Bard ibn Sinān al-Shāmī, from Makḥūl, from Wāthila ibn al-Asqaʿ ﵁ who traced it back to the Prophet ﷺ saying: “Do not gloat over your brother’s misfortune, lest ﵀ and afflict you”.

Al-Qaṭṭān informed us; Ibn Darastawayh informed us; Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān told us; Abū Nuʿaym told us; Sufyān told us, from ʿAbd al-Karīm, from Ziyād ibn Abī Maryam, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Maʿqil, who said: My father asked ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, “Did you hear the Prophet ﷺ say, ‘Regret is repentance’?” He replied, “Yes”.

Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Aḥmad ibn Ibrāhīm al-Bazzāz—in Baṣra—informed us; al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān al-Fasawī told us; Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān told us;

Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd al-Ḥimmānī told us; ʿAbd al-Wārith ibn Saʿīd told us, from Ḥusayn al-Muʿallim, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, from Abū Salama, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār, from Zayd ibn Khālid al-Juhanī, who said: “I asked ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān ﵁ about a man who has intercourse with his wife and then becomes limp without ejaculating. He said, ‘He need not perform the ritual bath.’ I went to Ṭalḥa, al-Zubayr, and Ubayy ibn Kaʿb ﵃ and asked them. They gave the same answer, reporting it from the Messenger of God ﷺ”.

Al-Ḥasan ibn Abī Bakr informed us; Ibn Darastawayh informed us; Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān told us; Abū Bishr Sahl ibn Bakkār told us; Yazīd ibn Ibrāhīm told us, from Ayyūb, from Ḥumayd ibn Hilāl, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from ʿAbd Allāh ﵁ from the Prophet ﷺ who said: “Whoever deliberately swears a binding oath, thereby sinning, in order to seize property unjustly, will meet God on the Day of Resurrection while He is angry with him”.

Al-Ḥasan ibn Abī Bakr informed us; Ibn Darastawayh informed us; Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān told us; Jaʿfar ibn Jisr told us: My father, Jisr, told us, from al-Ḥasan, from Abū Barza al-Aslamī ﵁ who said: I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: “The people of Paradise will go out in the morning wearing one garment and return in the evening wearing another, just as one of you goes out in the morning and returns in the evening to visit a king among the kings of this world. So too will they go out in the morning and return in the evening to visit their Lord, exalted is He. This will be apportioned to them according to appointed times and signs; they will know the hour at which they are to come to their Lord, mighty and glorious is He”.

Al-Ḥasan ibn Abī Bakr informed us; Ibn Darastawayh informed us; Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān told us; Abū al-Qāsim ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār told us; ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥumayd al-Muzanī told us, from his father, from Muʿāwiya ibn Ḥayda ﵁ who said: “I came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, ‘Messenger of God, what is enough for me in this world?’ He replied, ‘What covers your nakedness and satisfies your hunger. If you have a house, then that is excellent; if you have a donkey, then excellent indeed. A piece of bread and a jug of water, and you are accountable for anything beyond the waist-wrapper’”.

Al-Ḥasan ibn Abī Bakr informed us; Ibn Darastawayh informed us; Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān told us; Abū ʿAlī Qurra ibn Ḥabīb al-Qushayrī, companion of al-Fanā, told us; Iyās ibn Abī Tamīma, Abū Makhlad, told us; ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ informed us, from Abū Hurayra, who said: “The fever came to the Messenger of God ﷺ and said, ‘Messenger of God, send me to the dearest of your family to you.’ The Messenger of God ﷺ sent it to the Anṣār. It stayed with them for seven days and nights, until they were severely afflicted and complained to him about it. He went to their homes and went from house to house and from room to room, praying for their well-being. As he was returning, one of their women followed him and said, ‘Messenger of God, by Him who sent you with the truth, my father is one of the Anṣār and my mother is one of the Anṣār. Pray to God for me as you prayed for my companions.’ He said, ‘As you wish: if you wish, I will pray to God for you and He will restore you to health; or if you wish, you may endure it for three days and have Paradise.’

“She said, ‘Messenger of God, I would rather endure it for three days, and then three more, and then three more; I will not put Paradise at stake.’ Abū Hurayra said: ‘There is no illness that afflicts me that I love more than fever. It enters every part of my body, and God gives each part its share of reward’”.

Yaʿqūb said: I heard Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb mention, from one of his shaykhs, that he had seen Qays ibn Saʿd stop keeping the company of ʿAṭāʾ. He said: I asked him about that. He replied, “He had grown forgetful or changed, and I nearly spoiled what I had heard from him”.

Yaʿqūb said: Ibn Numayr told us; Ḥafṣ told us, from Ashʿath, from Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn, who said: “I came to Kūfa when there were four men there counted among its jurists. Whoever began with al-Ḥārith put ʿAlqama second, and whoever began with ʿAlqama put al-Ḥārith second; then came ʿAlqama third and Shurayḥ fourth.” He said: Then Ibn Sīrīn would say, “Even the least of the four, Shurayḥ, was among the best”.

Yaʿqūb said: ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Abī Sulaymān was a Fazārī, one of their own, and trustworthy.

Yaʿqūb said: I heard al-Ḥasan ibn al-Rabīʿ say: “We used to hear ḥadīth from ʿAbd al-Wārith. When the prayer was announced, we would leave and not pray behind him.”

He said: Ibn al-Mubārak was asked, “How did you transmit from ʿAbd al-Wārith while leaving ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd?” He replied, “ʿAmr was a propagandist”.

Yaʿqūb said: ʿUbayd, Abū ʿAmr’s father, was a weaver, then became a policeman for al-Ḥajjāj. He was among the captives from Sīstān.

Abū al-Qāsim ibn al-Samarqandī informed us; Abū Bakr ibn al-Ṭabarī informed us; Abū al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Faḍl informed us; ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar told us; Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān told us; Abū Tawba al-Rabīʿ ibn Nāfiʿ told us; Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAyyāsh told us, from Tammām ibn Najīḥ, who is trustworthy.

Abū al-Qāsim Ismāʿīl ibn Aḥmad ibn al-Samarqandī informed us; Abū Bakr ibn al-Ṭabarī informed us; Abū al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Faḍl informed us; ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar told us; Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān told us; Ṣafwān ibn Ṣāliḥ told us; al-Walīd told us; Khulayl told us:

From Qatāda, who said: God, mighty and glorious is He, said: “Indeed, Our hosts—they shall be victorious” (37:173).

Qatāda said: “I know those to be none other than the people of Syria”.

Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Numayr said: “Abū Usāma transmits from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd ibn Jābir, and we consider that he is not that man.”

Al-Fasawī said: “He was right: it is ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Bilāl ibn Tamīm”.

Al-Fasawī said: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad al-Azraq al-Makkī told us; al-Ḥubāb ibn Faḍāla al-Yamāmī al-Ḥanafī told us: “I came to Baṣra and met Anas ibn Mālik. I said to him:

“‘I intend to travel, and I wanted to ask your advice.’ He said, ‘Where do you intend to go?’ I said, ‘India.’

“He said, ‘Are your parents—or at least one of them—alive?’ I said, ‘Both are alive.’ He said, ‘Are they pleased with your departure?’ I said, ‘No, they are angry. My father brought a complaint against me, and the authorities imprisoned me.’

“He said, ‘Do you seek this world or the next?’ I said, ‘Both.’ He said, ‘I think you will lose them both. Return to your parents, treat them dutifully, and keep them company. You will never find a better means of earning’”.

Al-Fasawī said: Makkī ibn Ibrāhīm told us: “I sat with Ibn Isḥāq—who dyed his hair black—and he mentioned ḥadīths concerning the divine attributes. I recoiled from them and did not return to him”.

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān said, quoting Yaḥyā ibn Bukayr: “The only one who transmits from ʿAnbasa is a madman, a fool, who used to come to me. He was not fit for anything to be written down, nor for anyone to write from him”.

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān said: Aḥmad ibn Abī Bakr ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Zarrāra ibn Muṣʿab ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿAwf, told me: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Muḥammad told us, from ʿUbayd Allāh, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: “We came to Mecca and stayed at al-ʿAṣaba: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, Abū ʿUbayda ibn al-Jarrāḥ, and Sālim, the client of Abū Ḥudhayfa. Sālim, the client of Abū Ḥudhayfa, led them in prayer because he had memorized more of the Qurʾān than they had”.

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān said: “Al-Aḥnaf was generous and forbearing, and he was a righteous man. He lived into the pre-Islamic period, then became Muslim. He was mentioned to the Prophet ﷺ who prayed for forgiveness for him. He was trustworthy and reliable, and related few ḥadīths. He prayed frequently at night; he would light a lamp and pray and weep until morning. He would put his finger in the lamp and say, ‘Feel that, Aḥnaf! What made you do such-and-such? What made you do such-and-such?’ He would say to himself, ‘If you cannot endure the lamp, how will you endure the greater Fire?’ He was asked, ‘How did your people make you their chief when you are the ugliest of them in form?’ He replied, ‘If my people were to find fault with water, I would not drink it’”.

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān said: Abū Ghassān told us that Isḥāq ibn Saʿīd told him: Saʿīd ibn ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd and my two brothers informed me, from Umm Khālid bint Khālid whose father had been among those who migrated to Abyssinia, and she was born there.

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān transmitted, by his route and chain of transmission, from Karīma, the wife of al-Miqdād:

“Al-Miqdād had a large belly and a Roman slave. The slave said to him, ‘I will cut open your belly and remove some of the fat, so you become slimmer.’ He cut open his belly and then stitched it up. Al-Miqdād died, and the slave fled”.

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān said: I asked Duḥaym, “What about ʿUmayr ibn Hānī?” He said, “He died long ago.” I asked, “Was he killed?” He said, “No, it was his son who was killed”.

Al-Fasawī said: Ibn Muṣaffā told us; Baqiyya told us: Shuʿba said to me, “Baḥḥir lanā, baḥḥir lanā”.138

Abū Salama Mūsā told us; Ḥammād ibn Zayd told us: “Jarīr ibn Ḥāzim came to us from Medina. We went to him and greeted him, and we stayed until we began discussing ḥadīth. In the course of what he was saying, he said, ‘Qays ibn Saʿd told us, from al-Ḥajjāj ibn Arṭāh.’ Some time later, al-Ḥajjāj came to us, aged thirty—or thirty-one. I saw such a throng around him as I had never seen around Ḥammād ibn Abī Sulaymān. I saw Maṭar al-Warrāq, Dāwūd ibn Abī Hind, and Yūnus ibn ʿUbayd squatting on their heels before him, saying, ‘Abū Arṭāh, what do you say about such-and-such? Abū Arṭāh, what do you say about such-and-such?’” Al-Fasawī said: “I wrote down reports from more than a thousand shaykhs. Of them, I take no one as proof before God except Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal and Aḥmad ibn Ṣāliḥ”.

Ibn al-Faḍl informed us; ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar informed us; Yaʿqūb told us: Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal said: ʿAffān told us; Ḥammād ibn Salama told us: “I came to Mecca while ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ was still alive. I said, ‘When I break my fast, I will visit him.’ He died during Ramadan. Ibn Abī Laylā used to visit him, and ʿUmāra ibn Maymūn said to me, ‘Keep to Qays ibn Saʿd, for he is more learned in jurisprudence than ʿAṭāʾ’”.

Ibn Maʿīn said—as Yaʿqūb al-Fasawī heard from him: “The masters of ḥadīth are five: Mālik, Ibn Jurayj, Sufyān, Shuʿba, and ʿAffān”.

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān said: “The pinnacle of authority in knowledge, jurisprudence, and precision is reached with Mālik, al-Thawrī, and Ibn ʿUyayna”.

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān said: “He—that is, ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib ibn Mālik—is trustworthy and an authoritative proof. The reports transmitted from him by Sufyān, Shuʿba, and Ḥammād ibn Salama are based on their early hearing. ʿAṭāʾ changed in his later years, and the reports of Jarīr, Ibn Fuḍayl, and their contemporaries are weak”.

I am Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn al-Qaṭṭān; ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar ibn Darastawayh informed me; Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān told us; Abū Bakr ibn ʿAbd al-Malik told us; ʿAbd al-Razzāq told us, from Maʿmar: “Ayyūb used to relate to us from Nāfiʿ while Nāfiʿ was still alive, so we were content with him”.

I am al-Qaṭṭān; ʿAbd Allāh told us; Yaʿqūb said: I heard al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan say: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī said: “If someone saw Sufyān transmitting, he would say, ‘This is not …’”

[He was] among the people of knowledge; he would put things forward and back and garble them, but if you tried hard to turn him away from the meaning, he would not do so.139

I, al-Qaṭṭān—[I was told by] ʿAbd Allāh—[I was told by] Yaʿqūb, who said: I heard al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan say: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī said: “I would ask Sufyān, and he would say, ‘Put this off; put this off.’ I have not looked through my books for four years”.

Ibn al-Faḍl informed us, saying: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar informed me, saying: Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to us, saying: Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Aʿyan—who was a Shīʿī, and, in our view, a Rāfiḍī with his own opinions—related to us.

Ibn al-Faḍl informed us; ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar informed us; Yaʿqūb related to us, saying: Abū Bakr ibn ʿAbd al-Malik related to me; ʿAbd al-Razzāq related to us; Maʿmar related to us, saying: Ayyūb said to me: “If you are going to travel to anyone, travel to Ṭāwūs; otherwise, attend to your trade”.

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān said: He—meaning ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṣāliḥ, Abū Ṣāliḥ al-Miṣrī—was born in the year 173 and died in the year 222.

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān said: I heard Abū al-Aswad—meaning al-Naḍr ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār—and a man said to him, “Ibn Bukayr speaks against Abū Ṣāliḥ; what do you say about him?” He replied, “If Abū Ṣāliḥ tells you to write from someone, then write from him and leave everyone else”.

… Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to us: Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us, saying: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, from ʿUbayd Allāh, from Nāfiʿ, that Ibn ʿUmar was presented to the Prophet ﷺ—on the day of [Uḥud], but he did not accept him; he was presented to him on the day of the Trench, and he accepted him, when he was fifteen years old.

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUmar related from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: “I was presented to the Messenger of God ﷺ—on the day of Uḥud, when I was fourteen, but he did not accept me; he accepted me on the day of the Trench”.

Al-Qaṭṭān informed us; ʿAbd Allāh informed us; Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to us; Muḥammad ibn Muṣaffā related to us; Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd related to us, from Abū Muʿtamir, from Muḥammad ibn Qays, from the son of ʿUmāra ibn Khuzayma ibn Thābit, who said: “My grandfather kept his weapon sheathed until ʿAmmār was killed at Ṣiffīn. Then he drew his sword and fought until he was killed”.

Al-Qaṭṭān informed us; ʿAbd Allāh informed us; Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to us; Ibrāhīm ibn al-Mundhir related to us, saying: Muṭarrif, Maʿn, and Muḥammad ibn al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: Whenever Mālik was asked about the military campaigns, he would say, “You should consult the campaigns of the righteous man Mūsā ibn ʿUqba, for his accounts of the campaigns are the soundest”.

I, al-Qaṭṭān—I, ʿAbd Allāh—Yaʿqūb related to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Abī Dhakīr related to me; Ibn Wahb informed me; Mālik related to me that a man came to Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib while he was ill and asked him about a report. Saʿīd was reclining, but sat up and related it to him. The man said, “I wish you had not troubled yourself.” He replied, “I disliked relating to you a report from the Messenger of God ﷺ—while reclining”.

Ibn al-Faḍl informed us; ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar informed us; Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to us, saying: Zayd ibn Bishr and ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn ʿImrān related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us; Mālik said: I heard Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd say: “I would rather have written down what I hear than possess wealth equal to all that I own”.

… Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān said: I was told from Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn, who said: I heard Wakīʿ say: “I never wrote down a report from Sufyān al-Thawrī. I would memorize it, and when I returned home, I would write it down”.

… Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān: Abū Saʿīd Aḥmad ibn Dāwūd al-Ḥaddād related to us; Muḥammad ibn Fuḍayl related to us, from Ibn Shubrumah, who said: I heard al-Shaʿbī say: “I have not written a single mark in black upon white to this day. Whenever a man related a report to me, I memorized it, and I did not like him to repeat it to me”.

… Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān: al-Ḥumaydī related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, saying: Ibn Shubrumah related to us, saying: I heard al-Shaʿbī say: “For twenty years, whenever I heard a man relating a report, I knew it better than he did. I have indeed forgotten so much knowledge that, had a man retained it, he would have been learned”.

… Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān said: Muḥammad ibn Abī Dhakīr related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us; Mālik related to me, saying: “ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar reached the age of eighty-seven”.

… Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān said: Mujāhid ibn Mūsā related to us; Yaḥyā ibn Ādam related to us; Abū Shihāb related to us, saying: Shuʿba said to me: “You should consult al-Ḥajjāj ibn Arṭāh and Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq”.

… Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to us: Muḥammad ibn Yasār related to us; Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd related to us, from Sufyān, from al-Aʿmash, from ʿAmmār ibn ʿUmayr, from Ḥurayth ibn Ẓahīr, who said: When news of ʿAbd Allāh’s death reached Abū al-Dardāʾ, he said, “He left no one like himself behind”.

… Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān said: Khallād ibn Aslam related to me; al-Naḍr ibn Shumayl related to us; al-Rabīʿ ibn Muslim related to us; ʿAmr ibn Dīnār related to us, saying: ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith came on pilgrimage and went to Ibn ʿUmar. He greeted him while the people were seated, but Ibn ʿUmar did not show him the warmth he used to show him. He said, “Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, do you not recognize me?” He replied, “Indeed. Are you not Babbah?”

That distressed him, and the people laughed. ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar realized what had happened and said, “What I said is nothing bad; it is no disgrace to a man. He was just an unusual boy, and his mother used to call him—or nickname him—saying:

‘I shall marry Babbahto a buxom girl,honored and beloved,who loves the people of the Kaʿba.’”

Yaʿqūb said: This was ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Nawfal ibn al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib al-Hāshimī. After Yazīd ibn Muʿāwiya died, the people of Baṣra were left without a governor, so they agreed upon him. He appeared righteous and enjoyed the people’s approval. The people of Baṣra wanted him to act harshly for the good of the city, but he removed himself from office and stayed at home.

A woman came to Baqī ibn Makhlad and said, “The Byzantines have taken my son captive, and I have no property beyond a little house, which I cannot sell.” Al-Ḥumaydī related this in Tārīkh al-Andalus, by authorization from al-Qushayrī; al-Khaṭīb related it from al-Fasawī.

I mentioned in Taʿlīq al-Taʿlīq that Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṣāliḥ, the scribe of al-Layth, from al-Layth, from Khālid ibn Yazīd, from Saʿīd ibn Abī Hilāl, from Hilāl, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn Salām. Through this chain, from ʿAṭāʾ, he said: “Abū Wāqid al-Laythī informed me that he heard Kaʿb say the same.” Ibn al-Zubayr said: “There was nothing in my domain that he had not told me about. He told me that a people would gain control of the House.” Al-Fākihī recorded it.

ʿAmr ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Kaʿb al-Anṣārī:

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān deemed him trustworthy, but called him ʿUmar.

Muʿāwiya ibn ʿAmmār al-Duhnī:

Yaʿqūb said: “He is acceptable”.

Miqsam ibn Bajra, also said to be Ibn Najda:

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān said: “Trustworthy”.

Mūsā ibn Ayyūb al-Mihrī:

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān said: “He has sound reports”.

Ismāʿīl ibn Kathīr al-Ḥijāzī:

Al-Fasawī said: “A Meccan, trustworthy”.

Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿUbayd al-Qurashī:

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān said: “Trustworthy”.

al-Qāsim ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Shāmī al-Dimashqī:

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān said: “Trustworthy”.

Qays ibn Wahb al-Hamdānī:

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān said: “Trustworthy”.

ʿAnbasa ibn Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ al-Umawī:

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān deemed him trustworthy.

Muḥārib ibn Dithār ibn Kurdūs:

Yaʿqūb said: “Trustworthy”.

Maḥmūd ibn Labīd al-Ashhalī:

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān said: “Trustworthy”.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rajāʾ al-Ghudānī:

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān said: “Trustworthy”.

Khālid ibn Yazīd al-Jumaḥī:

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān said: “An Egyptian, trustworthy”.

Khālid ibn Yazīd al-Kāhilī, the Kūfan physician:

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān said: “He was trustworthy”.

Ziyād ibn Rabīʿa ibn Nuʿaym al-Ḥaḍramī:

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān deemed him trustworthy.

Ḥafṣ ibn Maysara al-ʿUqaylī al-Ṣanʿānī:

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān said: “Trustworthy, acceptable”.

Ḥaṭṭān ibn Khuffāf al-Jarmī:

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān said: “Trustworthy, acceptable”.

Jabala ibn Suḥaym al-Taymī al-Shaybānī al-Kūfī:

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān said: “A Kūfan Successor, trustworthy”.

Jāmiʿ ibn Abī Rāshid al-Kāhilī:

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān said: “A Kūfan, trustworthy, trustworthy”.

Abū ʿUbayd al-Madhḥijī:

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān said: “Trustworthy”.

Ayyūb ibn Muḥammad ibn Ziyād ibn Farrūkh al-Wazzān:

Yaʿqūb related from him and said: “A shaykh, acceptable”.

Jaʿfar ibn Rabīʿa ibn Sharāḥīl al-Kindī:

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān said: “Weak, abandoned, shunned”.

Ḥuṣayn ibn ʿUmar al-Aḥmasī al-Kūfī:

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān said: “Extremely weak”.

Ziyād ibn Ismāʿīl al-Makhzūmī:

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān said: “His reports are worth nothing”.

Rawwād ibn al-Jarrāḥ al-ʿAsqalānī:

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān said: “Weak in reports”.

Khuṣayf ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Jazarī:

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān said: “Acceptable”.

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Isḥāq ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Madanī:

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān said: “There is no fault in him”.

ʿAbd al-Jabbār ibn Wāʾil al-Ḥaḍramī al-Kūfī:

Ibn Saʿd said: “He was trustworthy, God willing, and had few reports. They criticize his narrations from his father, saying that he did not meet him.”

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān expressed the same meaning.

Khālid ibn Yazīd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Hamdānī al-Dimashqī:

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān said: “Sulaymān related from him to us, and he is weak”.

Hishām ibn Saʿd al-Madanī:

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān listed him among the weak narrators.

Abū Zurʿa ʿAmr ibn Jābir al-Ḥaḍramī al-Miṣrī:

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān included him among the weak narrators.

Faraj ibn Faḍāla ibn al-Nuʿmān al-Tanūkhī al-Ḥimṣī, also said to be al-Dimashqī:

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān listed him under “Those whose reports one should avoid”.

Kathīr ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr al-Muzanī:

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān declared him weak.

Abū ʿAbd Allāh Muḥammad ibn ʿAwn al-Khurāsānī:

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān said: “His reports are objectionable”.

ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn Sulaym al-Mālikī al-Baṣrī:

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān said: “Weak”.

ʿUmar ibn Nabḥān al-ʿAbdī al-Ghubrī al-Baṣrī:

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān said: “Weak”.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar ibn Ḥafṣ al-ʿUmarī:

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān reported from Aḥmad ibn Yūnus: “If you had seen his appearance, you would have known that he was trustworthy”.

Shahr ibn Ḥawshab al-Ashʿarī:

Yaʿqūb said: “Shahrūwān”.140

Hilāl ibn Abī Hilāl al-Qasmalī al-Baṣrī:

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān said: “His reports are soft”.

ʿUmāra ibn Ukayma al-Laythī al-Madanī:

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān said: “He was one of the well-known Successors in Medina”.

ʿUthmān ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā ibn Surāqa al-Azdī:

Yaʿqūb al-Fasawī deemed him trustworthy.

Ayyūb ibn Muḥammad al-ʿAjlī al-Yamāmī:

Al-Fasawī deemed him trustworthy.

al-Zubayr ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Kilābī:

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān listed him among those who met the Prophet ﷺ.

ʿĀmir ibn Abī ʿĀmir al-Ashʿarī:

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān included him among the Companions.

Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā al-Anṣārī al-Kūfī, the jurist:

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān said: “Trustworthy and upright; there is some criticism of his hadith, and they regard his hadith as weak”.

Muṣʿab ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-ʿAbdarī al-Makkī:

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān said: “Saʿīd related to us, from Sufyān, from Muṣʿab ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān”—the report.

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Kaʿb ibn Mālik al-Anṣārī al-Madanī:

He died during the caliphate of Sulaymān; Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān mentioned the same.

ʿAbbās ibn Sahl ibn Saʿd al-Sāʿidī:

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān placed his death later, in the time of al-Walīd ibn ʿAbd al-Malik.

ʿĀmir ibn Rabīʿah ibn Kaʿb al-ʿAnazī al-ʿAdawī:

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān said: “He died during the caliphate of ʿUthmān”.

Abū Ḥāzim Salamah ibn Dīnār al-Aʿraj al-Tammār al-Madanī:

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān said: “He died sometime between the thirtieth and fortieth years”.

Ṣāliḥ ibn Rustum, the client of the Hāshimids:

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān mentioned him.

Al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Sharāḥbīl al-Ghāfiqī al-Miṣrī:

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān did not mention a report of his from a Companion.

Ṣuhayb ibn Sinān al-Rūmī:

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān said: “He died at the age of eighty-four, and Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ led the funeral prayer for him”.

Yazīd ibn ʿAbd Rabbih al-Zubaydī al-Ḥimṣī al-Jarjasī:

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān said: “I heard him say: ‘I am an Arab man, but I have been afflicted by this church, to which I am ascribed’”.

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Qays ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Ashʿath:

In Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān’s text it appears as: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Muḥammad ibn Qays ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Ashʿath.

Yazīd ibn Ṣāliḥ:

It is also said: Ibn Ṣulayḥ; Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān decisively adopted this latter form.

Al-Walīd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Jurashī al-Ḥimṣī:

Al-Bukhārī said: “A client of Abū Sufyān al-Anṣārī.” Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān agreed with him.

Al-Walīd ibn ʿUbādah ibn al-Ṣāmit al-Anṣārī:

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān said: “We asked Muḥammad ibn al-Ṣabbāḥ about him. He said: ‘He came to Hushaym, who honored him, so we wrote down reports from him’”.

Maʿmar, the father of Abū Khuzaymah:

Some included him because of a report he transmitted without naming his source. Abū Mūsā cited him in al-Dhayl, quoting Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān’s History; however, the name is in fact Yaʿmar.

ʿĪsā ibn Ḥaṭṭān al-Raqāshī, also said to be al-ʿĀʾidhī:

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān distinguished between the Raqāshī and the ʿĀʾidhī.

Al-Ṣalt ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Nawfal ibn al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib ibn Hāshim:

Ibn Ḥajar said: “The reason al-Bukhārī thought that he was Ibn Babbah is that he entered him under this heading: ‘Al-Ṣalt ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith.’ Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān did the same. Apparently, his grandfather Nawfal was omitted from their accounts”.

Bashīr ibn Maʿbad al-Aslamī:

Thus Yaʿqūb distinguished Ibn al-Khaṣāṣiyyah al-Sadūsī from Bashīr ibn Maʿbad al-Aslamī.

Zayd ibn Khārijah ibn Abī Zuhayr al-Anṣārī al-Khazrajī:

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān listed him among those who fought at Badr, and stated that he was the one who spoke after death.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḍārib:

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān listed him among those named ʿAbd Allāh, and mentioned no shaykh for him other than Ḥuṣayn.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Maʿiyah al-Suwāʾī al-ʿĀmirī:

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān listed him under the diminutive form ʿUbayd Allāh.

Ṭaysalah ibn Maysās al-Sulamī and Ṭaysalah ibn ʿAlī al-Nahdī al-Yamāmī:

The correct view is that they are one person; Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān treated them as one.

Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbd al-Ṣamad:

He transmitted from Mālik a reprehensible report, which al-Fasawī related from Aḥmad ibn Saʿīd, from him.

Texts quoted that I believe are from al-Fasawī’s Book of the Sunna Texts that I believe are from Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān’s Book of the Sunna

(Exhortation to adhere firmly to the Sunna and condemnation of innovations)

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Bakrān informed us: al-Ḥasan ibn ʿUthmān informed us: Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān informed us: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān related to us: ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mubārak informed us: al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas informed us, from Abū Dāwūd, from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, who said: “Adhere to the path and the Sunna, and remember the All-Merciful. His eyes overflowed with tears out of fear of God, Mighty and Majestic. God will punish him. No servant on earth who follows the path and the Sunna, and remembers the All-Merciful within himself, will have his skin shiver from fear of God without being like a tree whose leaves have dried up: when a fierce wind strikes it and strips away its leaves, his sins will fall away just as the leaves fall from that tree. Moderation on the path and the Sunna is better than striving in opposition to the path and the Sunna. So see that your action—whether it is striving or moderation—accords with the way and the practice of the prophets”.

Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn ʿAlī ibn Ḥāmid informed us: Aḥmad ibn al-Sarī ibn Ṣāliḥ related to us: Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to us: Saʿīd ibn Abī Maryam related to us: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar related to us: Mūsā ibn ʿUqbah related to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “There are only two things: speech and guidance. The finest speech is the speech of God, and the finest guidance is the guidance of Muḥammad. Beware of newly introduced matters; the worst matters are those newly introduced, and every newly introduced matter is an innovation. Do not let the passage of time grow long for you, lest your hearts grow hard”.

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Bakrān informed us: al-Ḥasan ibn ʿUthmān related to us: Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to us: Muḥammad ibn ʿUqbah al-Shaybānī related to us: Abū Isḥāq related to us, from al-Awzāʿī, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī ʿAmr, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Daylamī, who said: “The beginning of the loss of religion is the abandonment of the Sunna: religion goes away one Sunna at a time, and the rope loses its strength fiber by fiber.” Ibn al-Daylamī said: “I heard Ibn ʿAmr say: ‘Whenever an innovation was introduced, it gained further momentum; and whenever a Sunna was abandoned, it sank further’”.

And ʿAlī—that is, ibn Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Bakrān—informed us: al-Ḥasan—that is, ibn ʿUthmān—related to us: Yaʿqūb related to us: Ṣafwān ibn Ṣāliḥ related to us: ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-Wāḥid related to us, from al-Awzāʿī, from Ḥassān ibn ʿAṭiyyah, who said: “Whenever a people introduced an innovation into their religion, God removed from their practice a Sunna of equal measure, and then never restored it to them until the Day of Resurrection”.

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Bakrān informed us: al-Ḥasan ibn ʿUthmān informed us: Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to us: Saʿīd ibn Abī Maryam related to us: Rushdayn ibn Saʿd related to me: ʿUqayl related to me, from Ibn Shihāb, from ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, who said: “The Messenger of God ﷺ and the leaders of affairs after him established practices. Acting upon them is affirmation of the Book of God, Mighty and Majestic, completion of obedience to Him, and strength in the religion of God. No one may alter them, change them, or consider the opinion of one who opposes them. Whoever follows the example of what they established is rightly guided; whoever seeks insight through them sees clearly; and whoever opposes them and follows a path other than that of the believers, God, Mighty and Majestic, will turn him over to what he has chosen, and consign him to Hell—an evil destination”.

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad informed us: al-Ḥasan ibn ʿUthmān informed us: Yaʿqūb related to us: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṣāliḥ related to us: al-Layth related to me: Yūnus related to me, from Ibn Shihāb: “It has reached us from men of learning that they used to say: ‘Adhering firmly to the Sunnas is salvation. Knowledge is taken away swiftly, and the revival of knowledge is the stability of religion and worldly life; the loss of all of that lies in the loss of knowledge’”.

And ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Bakrān al-Baṣrī informed us: al-Ḥasan ibn ʿUthmān informed us: Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to us: Qabīṣah related to us: Sufyān related to us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ziyād, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yazīd, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “What befell the Children of Israel will surely befall my community, exactly as one sandal matches another. Even if there was among them one who publicly had intercourse with his mother, there will be someone in my community who does that”.

And ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Bakrān informed us: al-Ḥasan ibn ʿUthmān informed us: Yaʿqūb related to us: Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us, that al-Awzāʿī told him, that Yazīd al-Raqāshī told him he had heard Anas ibn Mālik say: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “The Children of Israel divided into seventy-one sects, all of them in the Fire except one.” It was said: “O Messenger of God, which is that one?” He clenched his hand and said:

“The community. So hold fast together to the rope of God and do not divide”.

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Bakrān informed us: al-Ḥasan ibn ʿUthmān informed us: Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to us: ʿAmr ibn ʿUthmān ibn Dīnār al-Ḥimṣī related to us.

Yaʿqūb said: “I read to Yazīd ibn ʿAbd Rabbih.” Both of them said: ʿAmmār ibn Yūsuf related to us: Ṣafwān ibn ʿAmr related to me, from Rāshid ibn Saʿd, from ʿAwf ibn Mālik, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “The Jews divided into seventy-one sects: one is in Paradise and seventy in the Fire. The Christians divided into seventy-two sects: one is in Paradise and seventy-one in the Fire. By Him in whose hand is my soul, my community will surely divide into seventy-three sects: one is in Paradise and seventy-two in the Fire.” It was said: “O Messenger of God, who are they?” He said: “They are the community”. sect: one is in Paradise and seventy are in the Fire. The Christians divided into seventy-two sects: one is in Paradise and seventy-one are in the Fire. By Him in whose hand is my soul, my community will surely divide into seventy-three sects: one is in Paradise and seventy-two are in the Fire.” It was said: “O Messenger of God, who are they?” He said: “They are the community”.

And ʿAlī related to us: al-Ḥasan ibn ʿUthmān said: Yaʿqūb related to us: Abū al-Yamān al-Ḥakam ibn Nāfiʿ related to us: Ṣafwān ibn ʿAmr related to us, from al-Azhar ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Abū ʿĀmir ʿAbd Allāh ibn Luḥayy, who said: “We made the pilgrimage with Muʿāwiyah. When we arrived in Mecca, we prayed the noon prayer there; then he stood and said: ‘The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “The People of the Book divided into seventy-two communities”—meaning sects—all of them in the Fire except one, which is the community.’”

And he said: “There will emerge among my community people who will be tossed about as a dog is tossed about by its owner; no vein or joint of theirs will remain without it entering it”.141

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Bakrān informed us: al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān related to us: Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to us: al-Ḥumaydī related to us: Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ related to us, from Manṣūr, from Ibrāhīm, who said: “When a person shuts Satan out, he says: ‘From where can I approach him?’ Then he says: ‘Indeed, I shall approach him through sectarian passions.’”

ʿAlī informed us: al-Ḥasan said: Yaʿqūb related to us: Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us: Sallām ibn Miskīn related to us, from Yaḥyā al-Bakkāʾ, from al-Ḥasan, who said: “The people of sectarian passions are like the Jews and Christians”.

ʿAlī informed us: al-Ḥasan said: Yaʿqūb related to us: Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb said: Ḥammād related to us, from Ayyūb, from Yaḥyā ibn ʿAqīl, from Muḥammad, who said: “They used to regard the people of apostasy and those who plunged into unbelief as people of sectarian passions”.

ʿAlī informed us: al-Ḥasan said: Yaʿqūb related to us: Ṣafwān related to us: al-Walīd related to us: I heard al-Awzāʿī relate: “Iblīs met his troops and said: ‘From where do you approach the children of Adam?’ They said: ‘From every direction.’ He said: ‘Can you approach them through seeking forgiveness?’ They said: ‘We find it joined with professing God’s oneness.’ He said: ‘I shall approach them through a sin for which they do not seek forgiveness.’ Then he sent the sectarian passions out among them.”

ʿAlī informed us: al-Ḥasan said: Yaʿqūb related to us: ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan related to us, from Ibn al-Mubārak, from al-Awzāʿī: the same report.

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Bakrān informed us: al-Ḥasan ibn ʿUthmān related to us: Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān informed us: Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us: Ḥammād ibn Zayd related to us, from Ayyūb, from Abū Qilābah, who said: “Do not sit with them or mix with them, for I do not feel safe that they may immerse you in their misguidance and confuse you about much of what you know”.

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Bakrān informed us: al-Ḥasan ibn ʿUthmān related to us: Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to us: ʿAmr ibn ʿUthmān related to us: Baqiyyah related to us: Thābit ibn al-ʿAjlān related to us, who said: “I met Anas ibn Mālik, Ibn al-Musayyib, al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, al-Shaʿbī, Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī, ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ, Ṭāwūs, Mujāhid, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Mulaykah, al-Zuhrī, Makḥūl, al-Qāsim Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī, Thābit al-Bunānī, and al-Ḥakam ibn ʿUtaybah— Ayyūb al-Sakhtiyānī, Ḥammād, Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn, Abū ʿĀmir—who had met Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq—Yazīd al-Raqāshī, and Sulaymān ibn Mūsā: all of them used to command me to adhere to the community and forbid me from associating with the people of caprice.

Baqiyya said: Then he wept and said, “Nephew, no deed is more hopeful or more reliable than walking to this mosque”—meaning the Mosque of the Gate—.

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad informed us: al-Ḥasan ibn ʿUthmān informed us: Yaʿqūb related to us: Abū ʿĀṣim related to us, from Hishām, from al-Ḥasan. They said: “God accepts nothing from an adherent of innovation”.

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn Bakrān informed us: al-Ḥasan ibn ʿUthmān related to us: Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to us: al-Rabīʿ ibn Nāfiʿ related to us: Mukhlad ibn Ḥusayn related to us, from Hishām ibn Ḥassān, from al-Ḥasan, who said: “God accepts from an adherent of innovation neither prayer, fasting, pilgrimage, minor pilgrimage, jihād, alms, nor just conduct”.

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Bakrān informed us: al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān informed us: Yaʿqūb related to us: Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us: Muʿāwiya ibn Ṣāliḥ told me that al-Ḥasan ibn Abī al-Ḥasan said: “God ﵎ has refused to grant repentance to an adherent of caprice”.

ʿAlī informed us: al-Ḥasan informed us: Yaʿqūb related to us: Muḥammad ibn Rāfiʿ al-Nīsābūrī related to us: Saʿīd ibn ʿĀmir related to us: Salām ibn Abī Muṭīʿ said: A man said to Ayyūb, “Abū Bakr, ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd has abandoned his former opinion.”

He said, “He has not abandoned it.” The man said, “Indeed, Abū Bakr, he has abandoned it.” Ayyūb said, “He has not abandoned it.” The man said, “Indeed, Abū Bakr, he has abandoned it.” Ayyūb said, “He has not abandoned it.”

Three times he said, “He has not abandoned it.” Then he said, “Have you not heard what he said: ‘They pass out of the religion as an arrow passes through its prey, and then they do not return until the arrow returns to its nock’?”142

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Bakrān informed us: al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad informed us: Yaʿqūb related to us: Muḥammad ibn Bashshār related to us: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar related to us, from ʿAwf ibn Abī Jamīla, from Khālid ibn Thābit al-Rabaʿī, who said: I was told that among the Children of Israel there was a young man who had read the Scripture and acquired knowledge, but was obscure. He sought status and wealth through his reading and knowledge, and introduced an innovation. Thus he attained status and wealth in this world, and remained as he was until he reached a certain age. While he was sleeping in his bed one night, he reflected and said to himself, “Suppose these people do not know—but did not God, Mighty and Exalted, know what I introduced? The end is near; what if I repent?” He strove so earnestly in repentance that he deliberately pierced his collarbone, passed a chain through it, and fastened it to one of the mosque’s pillars. He said, “I shall not leave this place until God sends down a revelation concerning my repentance, or I die a natural death.” He was accustomed to revelation coming to the Children of Israel.
