So God, Mighty and Exalted, revealed concerning him—or to one of the prophets—“Had you committed a sin between Me and you, I would have accepted your repentance, whatever its extent. But what of those of My servants whom you led astray, who died and whom you caused to enter Hell? I shall not accept your repentance”.

Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Aḥmad ibn Ibrāhīm al-Bazzāz informed us—at Baṣra: al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān al-Fasawī related to us: Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to us: Aṣbagh ibn al-Faraj related to us: Ibn Wahb told me: ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith informed me, from Bukayr ibn al-Ashajj, from Busr ibn Saʿīd, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Abī Rāfiʿ, the client of the Messenger of God ﷺ: When the Ḥarūriyya revolted, while they were with ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, they said, “Judgment belongs to God alone.” ʿAlī said, “A word of truth by which falsehood is intended. The Messenger of God ﷺ described to me some people whose description I recognize among these men: they speak the truth with their tongues, but it does not pass beyond this”—and he pointed to his throat. “They are the most hateful of God’s creation to Him. Among them is a black man, one of whose hands is like a goat’s teat or a breast’s nipple.” When ʿAlī had killed them, he said, “Look.” They looked but found nothing. He said, “Go back. By God, I neither lied nor was lied to”—he said this two or three times. Then they found him in a ruin and brought him until they placed him before ʿAlī. ʿUbayd Allāh said: I was present for that affair and heard ʿAlī’s words concerning them.

(Condemnation of Opinion)

Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Bakrān al-Fawī informed us at Baṣra. He said: Abū ʿAlī al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān al-Fasawī related to us. He said: Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to us. He said: al-Faḍl ibn Ziyād related to us. He said: I asked Abū ʿAbd Allāh—meaning Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal—about al-Karābīsī and what he had put forward. His face darkened, then he said:

“Their affliction came only from these books they composed. They abandoned the reports of the Messenger of God ﷺ and his Companions, and turned to these books”.

Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Bakrān al-Fawī informed us at Baṣra: Abū ʿAlī al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān al-Fasawī related to us: Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to us: Ibrāhīm ibn al-Mundhir related to us: ʿUmar ibn ʿIṣām related to us: Mālik ibn Anas related to us, from Nāfiʿ, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar, who said: “Knowledge is three things: a speaking Book, an established Sunna, and ‘I do not know’”.

ʿAlī ibn Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Bakrān al-Fawī informed us: al-Ḥasan ibn ʿUthmān al-Fasawī informed us: Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān informed us: Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī informed us: Sufyān informed us: Mujālid related to us, from al-Shaʿbī, from Masrūq, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, who said: “One year is not rainier than another, nor is one ruler better than another. Rather, it is the loss of your jurists and scholars. Then people arise who measure matters by their own opinions, and thereby demolish Islam and make breaches in it”.

Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Aḥmad ibn Ibrāhīm al-Bazzāz informed us: Abū ʿAlī al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān al-Fasawī related to us: Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to us: Muḥammad ibn ʿAwf related to us: Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAyyāsh al-Ḥimṣī related to us: Hishām ibn ʿUrwa related to us, from his father, who said: “The affairs of the Children of Israel remained upright until the sons of captive women from the nations arose among them. They spoke according to opinion, and so perished and brought others to perish”.

(The Qurʾān Is the Speech of God, Not Created)

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Bakrān informed us: al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān informed us: Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to us: al-Ḥasan ibn al-Ṣabbāḥ al-Bazzāz related to us: Maʿbad Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Kūfī related to us, from Muʿāwiya ibn ʿAmmār, who said: I asked Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad about the Qurʾān. He said: “It is neither Creator nor created; rather, it is the speech of God”.

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Bakrān informed us: al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān informed us: Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to us: I heard Abū al-Walīd Hishām ibn ʿAbd al-Malik say: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd said, “Are you not amazed by this man who says, ‘Say: He is God, One’ (112:1) is created?” Abū al-Walīd said: “The Qurʾān is the speech of God, and speech concerning the Qurʾān is speech concerning God”.

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Bakrān informed us: al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān informed us: Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to us: I heard al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAẓīm say: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd told me: I heard Muʿādh ibn Muʿādh say: “Whoever says, ‘The Qurʾān is created,’ is, by God—there is no god but He—a heretic,” or he said, “a heretic”.

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Bakrān informed us: al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān informed us: Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to us: I heard Abū Hāshim Ziyād ibn Ayyūb say: I said to Abū ʿAbd Allāh Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, “Abū ʿAbd Allāh, a man said, ‘The Qurʾān is created,’ and I said to him, ‘You infidel.’ Do you think I have sinned in doing so?” He replied, “ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī used to say: ‘If one of them were a relative of mine and then died, I would not inherit from him.’” A man from Khurāsān then said to him—in Persian—“Should I say that the one who says, ‘The Qurʾān is created,’ is an infidel?” He replied:

“Yes”.

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Bakrān informed us: al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān informed us: Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to us: Ibrāhīm ibn al-Mundhir related to us: Ibrāhīm ibn al-Muhājir ibn Mismār related to us, from ʿUmar ibn Ḥafṣ ibn Dhakwān, the client of al-Ḥurqa, from Abū Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “God recited ‘Ṭā Hā’ and ‘Yā Sīn’ a thousand years before He created Adam”. ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Bakrān informed us: al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān informed us: Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to us: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥīm related to us: I heard ʿAlī—meaning Ibn al-Madīnī—say: “Bishr ibn al-Mufaḍḍal used to pray four hundred cycles every day and fast every other day. When a man from among the Jahmiyya was mentioned in his presence, he said, ‘Do not mention that infidel’”.

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Bakrān informed us: al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān related to us: Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to us: I asked Aḥmad ibn Ibrāhīm al-Dawraqī, who said: Zuhayr Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sijistānī related to us that he asked Salām ibn Abī Muṭīʿ about the Jahmiyya. He replied: “They are infidels, and one should not pray behind them”.

(The Vision of God, Mighty and Exalted, on the Day of Resurrection)

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Bakrān informed us: al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān related to us: Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to us: Ṣafwān ibn Ṣāliḥ related to us: al-Walīd ibn Muslim related to us: Zuhayr ibn Muḥammad related to us: someone who heard Abū al-ʿĀliya al-Riyāḥī relate, from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, who said: I asked the Messenger of God ﷺ about the “increase” in God’s Book, Mighty and Exalted: “For those who do good is the best reward, and more” (10:26). He said:

“The best reward is Paradise, and the increase is looking upon God, Mighty and Exalted”. ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Bakrān informed us: al-Ḥasan ibn ʿUthmān informed us: Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to us: Muḥammad ibn al-Muṣaffā related to us: Suwayd ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz related to us: ʿAmr ibn Khālid related to us, from Zayd ibn ʿAlī, from his father, from his grandfather, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “The people of Paradise see” their Lord ﵎ every Friday”—and he mentioned what you will be given. “Then God ﵎ says, ‘Uncover a veil.’ A veil is uncovered, then another veil, and then He ﵎ reveals Himself to them. It will be as though they had never before seen a blessing. This is His saying, Exalted is He: ‘And with Us is yet more’” (50:35).

(Faith Is Word and Deed)

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Makkī informed us: al-Ḥasan ibn ʿUthmān informed us: Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to us: Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us: Yaḥyā ibn Sulaym related to us: I asked ten jurists about faith. They said: “Word and deed.”

I asked Sufyān al-Thawrī, and he said: “Word and deed.” I asked Ibn Jurayj, and he said: “Word and deed.” I asked Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿUthmān, and he said: “Word and deed.” I asked Nāfiʿ ibn ʿUmar ibn Jamīl, and he said: “Word and deed.” I asked Muḥammad ibn Muslim al-Ṭāʾifī, and he said: “Word and deed.” I asked Mālik ibn Anas, and he said: “Word and deed.” I asked Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna, and he said: “Word and deed”.

(The Excellence of Knowledge)

Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Aḥmad ibn Ibrāhīm al-Bazzāz informed us—at Baṣra: Abū ʿAlī al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān al-Fasawī related to us: Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to us: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ḥammād al-Shuʿaythī related to us: Kahmas related to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Burayda, who said: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib said, “Visit one another and review the ḥadīth, for if you do not, it will fade away”. Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Aḥmad ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Ismāʿīl al-Bazzāz related to us at Baṣra—he said: Abū ʿAlī al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān al-Fasawī related to us: Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to us: Khalaf ibn al-Walīd Abū al-Walīd related to us: Khālid ibn ʿAbd Allāh related to us, from Ziyād ibn Abī Ziyād, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqama, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd: “Learn, learn; and when you have learned, act”.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad related to us: al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān related to us: Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to us: al-Ḥajjāj related to us: Jarīr ibn Ḥāzim said: I heard Ḥumayd ibn Hilāl say: I heard Muṭarrif say: “The excellence of knowledge is better than the excellence of action, and the best of your religion is scrupulous piety.”

Qatāda and Ghaylān ibn Jarīr narrated it from Muṭarrif with the same meaning.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad informed us: al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān related to us: al-Ḥajjāj ibn Nuṣayr related to us: Hilāl ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Ḥanafī related to us, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Maymūna, the client of Anas ibn Mālik ﵁ from Abū Salama, from Abū Hurayra and Abū Dharr, who said: “A chapter of knowledge that one learns is dearer to us than a thousand supererogatory cycles of prayer; and a chapter of knowledge that one teaches, whether one acts on it or not, is dearer to us than a hundred supererogatory cycles of prayer.”

They said: We heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: “When death comes to the seeker of knowledge while he is in that state, he dies a martyr”. ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad related to us: al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān related to us: Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to us: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān related to us: ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mubārak related to us, from Thawr ibn Yazīd, from Khālid ibn Maʿdān, who said: Abū al-Dardāʾ said: “The world is accursed, and all that is in it is accursed, except for the remembrance of God and what leads to it, and the scholar and the learner who share in goodness. The rest of the people are rabble, with no good in them”.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Muʾmin ibn Yaḥyā and Abū ʿAlī al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān al-Fasawī related to me—in Baghdad: Abū Yūsuf Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān al-Fasawī related to us and said: Ḥajjāj ibn al-Minhāl and Ḥammād ibn Salama related to us, from Ḥumayd, from al-Ḥasan, that Abū al-Dardāʾ said: “Be a scholar, a learner, a lover, or a follower; do not be the fifth, lest you perish.” I said to al-Ḥasan, “What is the fifth?” He said, “The innovator”.

ʿAbd Allāh related to us: al-Ḥasan related to us: Yaʿqūb related to us: Zayd ibn Bishr al-Ḥaḍramī and ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn ʿImrān related to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us: Ḥanẓala informed us that ʿAwn ibn ʿAbd Allāh told him: I told ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz that he used to say, “If you can, be a scholar; if you cannot, be a learner; if you cannot, love them; and if you cannot, do not hate them.” ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz said, “God, Mighty and Exalted, has indeed made him a way out, if he accepts”.

God, Mighty and Exalted, has indeed made him a way out, if he accepts.

ʿAbd Allāh related to us: al-Ḥasan related to us: Yaʿqūb related to us: Abū al-Walīd Khālid ibn al-Walīd related to us: Khālid ibn ʿAbd Allāh related to us, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from al-Ḥasan, who said: “Go out in the morning as a scholar, a learner, or a listener; do not be a fourth, lest you perish”.

ʿAbd Allāh related to us: al-Ḥasan related to us: Yaʿqūb related to us: al-Ḥumaydī related to us: Sufyān related to us: ʿĀṣim related to us, from Zayd, who said: ʿAbd Allāh said: “Go out in the morning as a scholar or a learner; do not go out as an imitator in between.”

Abū Yūsuf said: The people of knowledge said: “The imitators are the people of opinion”.

ʿAbd Allāh informed us: al-Ḥasan related to us: Yaʿqūb related to us: Ṣafwān ibn Ṣāliḥ related to us: ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-Wāḥid related to us, from al-Awzāʿī, who said: Hārūn ibn Riʾāb told me:

Ibn Masʿūd used to say: “Go out in the morning as a scholar or a learner; do not go out as anything in between, for what lies in between is only ignorance or an ignorant person. The angels spread their wings for the man who goes out in the morning seeking knowledge, in approval of what he does”.

ʿAbd Allāh related to us: al-Ḥasan related to us: Yaʿqūb related to us: Ibn Numayr related to us: Wakīʿ related to us: al-Aʿmash related to us, from Tamīm ibn Salama, from Abū ʿUbayda, who said: ʿAbd Allāh said: “Go out in the morning as a scholar or a learner; do not go out as anything in between”.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad related to us, al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān related to us, Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to us, Ādam related to us, Sharīk related to us, from Layth ibn Abī Sulaym, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, from al-Azdī, who said: I asked Ibn ʿAbbās about fighting in God’s cause. He said: “Shall I direct you to something better than fighting in God’s cause?” I said: “Yes.” He said: “Build a mosque, and teach there the prescribed religious duties, the Sunna, and understanding of religion.”

Through the same chain, Yaʿqūb related to us: Abū al-Yamān and Ādam said: Ḥurayz ibn ʿUthmān al-Raḥabī related to us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿAwf, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Masʿūd al-Fazārī, that Abū al-Dardāʾ said: “Anyone who sets out early for the mosque to learn or teach something good is credited with the reward of a fighter in God’s cause, who returns with spoils and no loss”.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā related to us, al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān al-Fasawī related to us, Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to us, Ādam ibn Abī Iyās said: Abū Jaʿfar al-Rāzī informed us; ʿĀṣim ibn Bahdalah, from Zirr ibn Ḥubaysh, said: I went to Ṣafwān ibn ʿAssāl al-Murādī, and he said: “What brings you here?” I said: “Seeking knowledge.” He said: “I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ—say:

‘Whoever leaves his home seeking knowledge, the angels spread their wings in approval of what he is doing.’” ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad related to us, al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān related to us, Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to us, Ḥajjāj ibn Minhāl related to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah, from ʿĀṣim ibn Bahdalah, from Zirr ibn Ḥubaysh, said: I set out early to see Ṣafwān ibn ʿAssāl al-Murādī. He asked: “What brings you here?” I said: “Seeking knowledge.” He said: “Shall I give you good news?”—and he traced the report back to the Prophet.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Muʾmin related to us; al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān al-Fasawī related to us—in Baghdad—; Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān al-Fasawī related to us; ʿAbd al-Wahhāb ibn al-Ḍaḥḥāk related to us; Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAyyāsh, from ʿĀṣim ibn Rajāʾ ibn Ḥaywah, from Dāwūd ibn Jamīl, from Kathīr ibn Qays, said: A man came from Medina to Abū al-Dardāʾ in Damascus to ask him about a report he had heard that Abū al-Dardāʾ transmitted from the Messenger of God ﷺ. Abū al-Dardāʾ said to him: “Did you come for trade?”

He said: “No.” He asked: “And did you come seeking some need?” He said: “No.” He asked: “Did you come seeking only this report?” He said: “Yes.” He said: “I bear witness that, if you are truthful, I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ—say: ‘There is no man who leaves his home seeking knowledge but that the angels spread their wings [for him].’” He then related the report in a form similar to what precedes.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Muʾmin related to us; Abū ʿAlī al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān al-Fasawī related to us in Baghdad; Abū Yūsuf Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān al-Fasawī related to us; Abū Nuʿaym al-Faḍl ibn Dukayn related to us; ʿĀṣim ibn Rajāʾ ibn Ḥaywah, from someone who related it to him, from Kathīr ibn Qays, said: I was with Abū al-Dardāʾ in Damascus, and he said: I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ—say: “Whoever follows a path seeking knowledge, God guides him by it to one of the paths of Paradise. The angels spread their wings in approval of the seeker of knowledge. Those in the heavens and on earth seek forgiveness for the scholar, even the fish in the sea. The superiority of the scholar over the worshipper is like the superiority of the moon on the night of the full moon over the rest of the stars. The scholars are the heirs of the prophets. The prophets did not bequeath a dirham or a dinar; rather, they bequeathed knowledge. Whoever takes hold of it has taken hold of an abundant share”. ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad related to us, al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad related to us, Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to us, al-Ḥimānī related to us, from Ibn al-Mubārak, from al-Awzāʿī, from Kathīr ibn Qays, from Yazīd ibn Sumayrah, from Abū al-Dardāʾ, from the Prophet ﷺ—with a report similar to what precedes.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Muʾmin informed us; Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān informed us; Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān informed us; Abū Kulthūm Salāmah ibn Bishr ibn Budayl al-ʿAdawī al-Dimashqī informed us; Ṣadaqah ibn ʿAbd Allāh informed us; Ṭalḥah ibn Zayd, from Mūsā ibn ʿUbaydah, from Saʿīd ibn Abī Hind, from Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī, said: The Messenger of God ﷺ—said: “On the Day of Resurrection, God will raise the servants and then distinguish the scholars. He will say: ‘O company of scholars, I placed My knowledge among you only because I knew you; I did not place My knowledge among you in order to punish you. Go forth, for I have forgiven you’”. ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā said: Al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān related to us; Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to us and said: Abū al-Nuʿmān Muḥammad ibn al-Faḍl al-Sadūsī—and he had no peer—and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Mubārak al-ʿĀʾishī related to us. They said: Al-Ṣaʿq ibn Ḥazn related to us, from ʿAqīl al-Jaʿdī, from Abū Isḥāq al-Hamadhānī, from Suwayd ibn Ghaflah, from Ibn Masʿūd, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ—said to me: “O ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd.” I said: “At your service, Messenger of God.” He said: “Do you know which people are best?” I said: “God and His Messenger know best.” He said: “The best of people are those whose deeds are best, when they have understanding of their religion.” He said: “O ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd.” I said: “At your service, Messenger of God.” He said: “Do you know which people have the most knowledge?” I said: “God and His Messenger know best.”

He said: “The most knowledgeable of people are those with the clearest insight into the truth when people disagree, even if they fall short in action, even if they crawl on their buttocks.”

ʿAbd Allāh informed us; al-Ḥasan related to us; Yaʿqūb related to us; Ṣafwān ibn Ṣāliḥ related to us; al-Walīd related to us; Bukayr ibn Maʿrūf, from Muqātil ibn Ḥayyān, from al-Qāsim ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from his father, from his grandfather ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, said: The Messenger of God ﷺ—said to me: “O ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd.” I said: “At your service, Messenger of God.”

143 Something like it, or similar to it. Abū Yūsuf said: “This is the description of the jurists”.

I, Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Aḥmad ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Ismāʿīl al-Bazzāz, in Basra, [said:] Abū ʿAlī al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān al-Fasawī related to me; Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to me; Ibn ʿUthmān—that is, ʿAbdān al-Marwazī—related to me; ʿAbd Allāh—that is, Ibn al-Mubārak—related to me; Ḥabīb ibn Ḥajar al-Qaysī related to me, saying: It used to be said: “How excellent faith is, and knowledge adorns it; how excellent knowledge is, and action adorns it; how excellent action is, and gentleness adorns it. Nothing has been added to anything like forbearance added to knowledge”.

Other texts transmitted by Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān through al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān al-Fasawī

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Bakrān informed us; al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān informed us, saying: Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to us; Abū Bakr al-Ḥumaydī related to us; Sufyān related to us; ʿAmr ibn Dīnār related to us; ʿIkrimah informed me, saying: I heard Abū Hurayrah say that the Prophet of God ﷺ—said: “When God decrees a matter in heaven, the angels beat their wings in submission to His word, as though it were a chain dragged over a smooth stone.”

He said: “When fear is removed from their hearts, they say: ‘What has your Lord said?’ They say: ‘The truth; He is the Most High, the Great’”. Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Aḥmad ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Ismāʿīl informed us in Basra; Abū ʿAlī al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān al-Fasawī related to us; Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to us; Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd related to us; Ḥuṣayn ibn ʿUmar al-Aḥmasī, from Mukhāriq, from Ṭāriq, from ʿUthmān, said: I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ—say: “Whoever loves the Arabs loves them because of his love for me, and whoever hates the Arabs hates them because of his hatred for me”. ʿAlī ibn Aḥmad ibn Ibrāhīm al-Baṣrī informed us; al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān al-Fasawī related to us; Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to us; al-Ḥumaydī related to us; Sufyān related to us.

ʿĀṣim al-Aḥwal related to us, from Ḥafṣah bint Sīrīn, from al-Rabāb, from her uncle Salmān ibn ʿĀmir al-Ḍabbī ﵁ who said: I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ—say: “Charity given to a poor person is charity; given to a poor relative, it is two things: charity and maintaining kinship.” Al-Khaṭīb said: Al-Rabāb was a woman from Banū Ḍabbah. The only person who transmitted from her was Ḥafṣah bint Sīrīn, and she was the mother of Umm al-Rāʾiḥ bint Ḍulayʿ.

ʿAlī ibn Aḥmad ibn Ibrāhīm informed us; al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad al-Fasawī related to us; Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to us; Ibn ʿUthmān—that is, ʿAbdān al-Marwazī—related to us; ʿAbd Allāh—that is, Ibn al-Mubārak—informed us; ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAwn informed us, from Ḥafṣah bint Sīrīn, from Umm al-Rāʾiḥ bint Ḍulayʿ, from Salmān ibn ʿĀmir ﵁ who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ—said: “Your charity to a poor person is charity, and to a relative it is two things, because it is charity and maintaining kinship.” This is the wording of Ibn al-Mubārak’s report. Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Aḥmad ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Ismāʿīl al-Bazzāz informed us in Basra; Abū ʿAlī al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān al-Fasawī related to us; Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to us; ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān related to us; ʿAbd Allāh—that is, Ibn al-Mubārak—related to us; ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUmar related to us, from Saʿīd al-Maqburī, from Abū al-Ḥubāb, from Abū Hurayrah, from the Messenger of God ﷺ—who said: “There is no believing servant who gives charity from lawful earnings—and God, exalted is He, accepts only what is good—but that God takes it in His right hand and nurtures it for him, just as one of you nurtures his young colt, or his she-camel, or his foal, until a single date becomes as large as Mount Uḥud”.

ʿAlī ibn Aḥmad ibn Ibrāhīm al-Bazzāz informed us; al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān al-Fasawī related to us; Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to us; Abū Muḥammad Miḥraz related to me, saying:

I was with Abū al-ʿAbbās al-Baghdādī in Mecca. He saw a date stone lying on the ground and picked it up. When we entered the mosque, there was a beggar asking for alms. He handed him the date stone and said: “This is the utmost effort of one with little”.

ʿAlī ibn Aḥmad ibn Ibrāhīm al-Baṣrī informed us; al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān al-Fasawī related to us; Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to us; Rūḥ ibn Siyābah al-Ḥārithī related to us, saying: I heard Saʿīd ibn Abī Ayyūb relate, from Dāwūd ibn al-Ḥuṣayn, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās ﵄ from the Messenger of God ﷺ—who said: “There is to be no harm or reciprocating harm; and your neighbor may place a beam in your wall”. Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Aḥmad ibn Ibrāhīm al-Baṣrī informed us; al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān al-Fasawī related to us; Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to us; Zayd ibn Bishr and Aṣbagh ibn al-Faraj related to us. They said: Ibn Wahb related to us; Yaḥyā ibn Ayyūb related to me, from al-Walīd ibn Abī al-Walīd, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Dīnār, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar ﵄ that a Bedouin met him on the road to Mecca. ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar ﵄ greeted him, gave him the donkey he was riding, and gave him the turban that was on his head. Ibn Dīnār said: We said, “May God set you right, they are Bedouins and are content with little.” ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar ﵄ said: “This man’s father was a friend of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb ﵁ and I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ—say: ‘The finest act of filial piety is for a man to maintain his father’s friendships’”.

ʿAlī ibn Aḥmad ibn Ibrāhīm al-Baṣrī informed us; al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān al-Fasawī related to us; Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to us; Hilāl ibn Fayyaḍ related to us; al-Ḥārith ibn Shibl said: Umm al-Nuʿmān al-Kindiyyah related to us, from ʿĀʾishah ﵂ that when the Messenger of God ﷺ—lay down to sleep, he would say: “O God, Lord of the seven heavens and Lord of the Mighty Throne, our Lord and Lord of all things, Revealer of the Torah, the Gospel, and the Mighty Qurʾān: We seek refuge in God from the evil of every creature whose forelock is in Your hand. You are the First, and there is nothing before You; You are the Last, and there is nothing after You; You are the Manifest, and there is nothing above You; You are the Hidden, and there is nothing beneath You. Settle my debt and free me from poverty”.

Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Aḥmad ibn Ibrāhīm al-Bazzāz informed us in Basra; al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān al-Fasawī related to us; Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to us; Muḥammad ibn Manṣūr and Abū Bakr ibn Abī al-Naḍr related to us. They said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ghazwān, Qirād Abū Nūḥ, related to us; Layth ibn Saʿd related to us, from Mālik ibn Anas, with a chain of transmission similar to it. [That is, similar to a report al-Khaṭīb mentioned by way of al-Zuhrī, from ʿUrwah, from ʿĀʾishah: that a man among the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ—said: “Messenger of God, I have two servants who lie to me and betray me”—and he related the report—]. I, ʿAlī ibn Aḥmad ibn Ibrāhīm al-Baṣrī, said: Al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān al-Fasawī related to me; Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to me; Yaḥyā ibn Ṣāliḥ al-Wuḥāẓī related to me; Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz related to me, from Makḥūl, from Umm Ayman, that the Messenger of God ﷺ—said to one of his family: “Obey your parents if they order you to leave your religion; do not do so”. I, ʿAlī ibn Aḥmad ibn Ibrāhīm al-Baṣrī, said: Al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān al-Fasawī related to me; Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to me, saying: A transmitter related to me, from al-Mughīrah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Khālid ibn Ilyās, from Muhājir ibn Mismār, from ʿĀmir ibn Saʿd, from his father, from the Prophet ﷺ—who said: “God is good and loves what is good; clean and loves cleanliness; generous and loves generosity; munificent and loves munificence”. I, ʿAlī ibn Aḥmad ibn Ibrāhīm al-Baṣrī, said: Al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān al-Fasawī related to me; Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to me; Yūsuf ibn Muḥammad al-Ṣaffār related to me; Ibn Abī Fudayk related to me, from Hishām ibn Saʿd, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Kaʿb al-Aḥbār, who said: “We find three [types of people] in the Book, and it is incumbent on us to honor them, show them respect, and make room for them in gatherings:

“the elderly person, the person of authority on account of his authority, and the bearer of the Book”.

I, al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Aḥmad ibn Ibrāhīm al-Bazzāz, in Basra, said: Abū ʿAlī al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān al-Fasawī related to me; Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to me; Nūḥ ibn al-Haytham al-ʿAsqalānī and Ayyūb ibn Muḥammad al-Raqqī related to us. They said: Marwān ibn Muʿāwiyah related to us, from Mālik ibn Abī al-Ḥasan, from ʿUtbah—a shaykh from Fazārah—from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: ʿUyaynah ibn Ḥiṣn ibn Ḥudhayfah ibn Badr came to the Prophet ﷺ—while Abū Bakr and ʿUmar were with him, seated on the ground. He had a cushion brought for him and seated him upon it. He said: “When a noble person from a people comes to you, honor him”.

I, ʿAlī ibn Aḥmad ibn Ibrāhīm al-Bazzāz, said: al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad al-Fasawī related to me; Yaʿqūb related to me; Abū ʿUmar al-Numayrī related to me; Shuʿbah said: Abū Isḥāq informed me, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Jadalī, from ʿĀʾishah, who said: “The Messenger of God ﷺ—was neither foul-mouthed nor given to foul speech, nor did he shout in the marketplaces. He did not repay an evil deed with another like it; rather, he pardoned and overlooked”.

Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Aḥmad ibn Ibrāhīm al-Bazzāz informed us in Basra. He said: Abū ʿAlī al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān al-Fasawī related to us; Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to us; al-Ḥakam ibn Mūsā related to us; Yaḥyā ibn Ḥamzah related to us, from Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd, who said: al-Zuhrī related to me, from Abū Bakr ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr ibn Ḥazm, from his father, from his grandfather, that the Messenger of God ﷺ—wrote to the people of Yemen in a letter that said: “The greatest of the grave sins before God on the Day of Resurrection are associating others with God, killing a believing soul without right, fleeing on the day of battle from the cause of God, and disobeying one’s parents”. ʿAlī ibn Aḥmad ibn Ibrāhīm informed us; al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad al-Fasawī related to us; Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān al-Fārisī related to us, saying: Yūsuf ibn ʿĪsā related to me; Sharīk related to us, from Mughīrah, from al-Shaʿbī, from ʿIyāḍ, who said: I attended a festival in al-Anbār and said: “Why do I not see you performing taqlīs?” They used to perform taqlīs in the time of the Messenger of God ﷺ; they practiced it.

ʿAlī ibn Aḥmad ibn Ibrāhīm informed us; al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad al-Fasawī related to us.

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to us: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Hāniʾ related to us: Fiṭr and al-ʿArzamī related to us, from Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit, who said: When someone sat with the Messenger of God, he did not extend his knee ahead of him, nor did he get up until he had asked their permission.

Yaʿqūb said: Abū Nuʿaym related to us: ... Ibn Shihāb said: I entered the Sacred Mosque with Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, and we all sat together. The circle grew large, and he wanted to get up, so he asked their permission. He said, “You sat with us; had I been the one sitting with you, I would not have asked your permission.”

ʿAlī ibn Aḥmad ibn Ibrāhīm related to us: al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān al-Fasawī related to us: Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to us: al-Ḥumaydī related to us: Sufyān related to us: Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid said, “I heard Qays say, ‘I heard Jarīr ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Bajalī ﵁ say: The Messenger of God ﷺ never saw me without smiling at me.’”

ʿAlī ibn Aḥmad ibn Ibrāhīm al-Bazzāz al-Baṣrī related to us: al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān al-Fasawī related to us: Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to us: Abū Ḥudhayfa Mūsā ibn Masʿūd related to us: Zuhayr related to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAqīl, from Muḥammad ibn Jubayr, from his father, that a man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, “Messenger of God, which lands are worst?” He said, “I do not know.” When Gabriel came to him, he asked, “Which lands are worst?” He said:

“I do not know; I must ask my Lord ﵎ is He.” Gabriel departed and remained away as long as God willed. Then he came and said, “Muḥammad, you asked me, ‘Which lands are worst?’ and I said, ‘I do not know.’ I asked my Lord, exalted is He, ‘Which lands are worst?’ and He said, ‘Their markets.’”

Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Aḥmad ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Ismāʿīl al-Bazzāz—at Baṣra—reported to us: Abū ʿAlī al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān al-Fasawī reported to us: Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to us: Abū Khālid Yazīd ibn Bayān al-ʿUqaylī reported to us: Abū al-Raḥḥāl al-Anṣārī reported to me, from Anas ibn Mālik, who said that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Whenever a young man honors an old man on account of his age, God appoints someone to honor him when he reaches old age.”

ʿAlī ibn Aḥmad ibn Ibrāhīm al-Baṣrī related to us: al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān al-Fasawī related to us: Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to us: Ibn ʿUthmān—meaning ʿAbdān al-Marwazī—related to us: ʿAbd Allāh—meaning Ibn al-Mubārak—related to us: Usāma ibn Zayd related to us, from Nāfiʿ, that Ibn ʿUmar said: “I saw the Messenger of God ﷺ using a toothstick. He gave it to the eldest of the people, then said:

‘Gabriel commanded me to give precedence to the eldest.’”

ʿAlī ibn Aḥmad ibn Ibrāhīm related to us: al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān al-Fasawī related to us: Abū Ṣāliḥ and Ibn Bukayr related to us, both saying: al-Layth ibn Saʿd related to us: Yazīd ibn Ḥabīb related to me, from Saʿd ibn Sinān, from Anas ibn Mālik, from the Messenger of God ﷺ who said: “Deliberation is from God, and haste is from Satan.” Yaʿqūb said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad al-Miṣrī related to us: Sulaymān ibn Bilāl related to us, from Saʿd ibn Saʿīd, from al-Zuhrī, from a man of Balī, who said: My mother and I came to the Messenger of God ﷺ. Then my father came and spoke privately with him. Among the things he said to him was:

“When you resolve to do something, proceed with deliberation until God shows you the way out of it.”

Other texts of Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān, transmitted by Aḥmad ibn al-Sarī ibn Ṣāliḥ from him

(Dalāʾil al-Nubuwwa):

Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Ḥāmid al-Ṭabarī reported to us: Aḥmad ibn al-Sarī ibn Ṣāliḥ related to us: Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to us: Muḥammad ibn Kathīr related to us: Sulaymān ibn Kathīr related to us: I heard Ibn Shihāb, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, from Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh, who said:

The Messenger of God ﷺ used to stand by a palm trunk and preach before the pulpit was made. When the pulpit was set in place, he climbed onto it, and the trunk groaned until we heard its groaning. The Messenger of God ﷺ came to it and laid his hand on it, and it fell silent.

(Tafsīr):

Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn ʿAlī ibn Ḥāmid al-Ṭabarī reported to us: Aḥmad ibn al-Sarī ibn Ṣāliḥ related to us: Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to us: Aḥmad ibn ʿUthmān ibn Nūḥ al-Ṭayālisī related to us: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Saʿd related to us: Abū Jaʿfar al-Rāzī related to us, from al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas, from Abū al-ʿĀliya Rafīʿ, from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, concerning His words, “And when your Lord took from the children of Adam—from their loins—their descendants, and made them testify concerning themselves: ‘Am I not your Lord?’ They said, ‘Indeed, we testify,’ lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection, ‘We were unaware of this,’ or lest you should say, ‘Our fathers associated others with God before us, and we were descendants after them. Will You then destroy us for what those who dealt in falsehood did?’” (7:172–173). He said: He gathered them all for Him that day—all that would come to be until the Day of Resurrection. He made them into pairs, then formed them, then brought them forward and took from them the covenant and pledge. He made them testify concerning themselves: “Am I not your Lord?” They said, “Indeed, we testify”—“lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection” (7:172) through “for what those who dealt in falsehood did” (7:173). He said: “I call the seven heavens and the seven earths to witness against you, and I call your father Adam to witness against you, lest you say on the Day of Resurrection, ‘We knew nothing of this.’ Know that there is no god other than Me and no lord other than Me; do not associate anything with Me. I shall send messengers to you to remind you of My covenant and pledge, and I shall send down to you such-and-such.” They said, “We testify that You are our Lord and our God; we have no lord or god other than You.” That day, they acknowledged their obedience to Him. Their father Adam was raised up before them, and he looked at them and saw among them the poor. He also saw the prophets, like lamps with light upon them; they were singled out by another covenant, that of messengership and prophethood. This is what He says: “And when We took from the prophets their covenant” (33:7), through “and from you and from Noah” (33:7), through “and We took from them a solemn covenant” (4:154). This is what He says: “So set your face toward the religion, inclining to truth—the natural disposition of God upon which He fashioned mankind. There is no altering God’s creation” (30:30). Concerning this: “This is a warning from the former warnings” (53:56), whose covenant He took from the primordial light. Concerning this He says: “We found no covenant with most of them; indeed, We found most of them defiantly disobedient” (7:102). Concerning this also: “Then We sent messengers after him to their peoples, and they came to them with clear proofs. But they would not believe what they had previously denied” (10:74). In His knowledge, on the day they acknowledged it, were those who would deny it and those who would affirm it. Jesus ﵇ was one of those spirits from whom the covenant and pledge were taken among the children of Adam. God, Mighty and Exalted, sent that to Mary when “she withdrew from her family to a place in the east. She screened herself from them, and We sent Our spirit to her, and he appeared before her as a well-proportioned man. She said, ‘I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you, if you are God-fearing.’ He said, ‘I am only [I am] a messenger from your Lord, to grant you a pure son.’ She said, ‘How can I have a son when no man has touched me—’” (19:16–20).

“—and I have not been unchaste” (19:20), through “and she conceived him” (19:22). He said: She conceived the one who had spoken to her, and he was the spirit of Jesus son of Mary.

A text transmitted by ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Khallād al-Rāmahurmuzī from Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān

My father related to us: Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān al-Fasawī related to us: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṣāliḥ related to us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Jubayr ibn Nufayr, from al-Nawwās ibn Samʿān, who said that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “God has set forth a parable: a straight path, and on either side of the path a wall with open doors in it. Over those doors hang lowered curtains. At the entrance to the path is a caller saying, ‘People, enter the path and do not turn aside.’ Above the path is another caller. Whenever someone wants to open one of those doors, he says, ‘Woe to you! Do not open it, for if you open it, you will enter.’ The path is Islam; the curtains are God’s limits; the open doors are the things God has forbidden; the caller is the Qurʾān; and the caller above is God’s admonisher.”

Other texts

Al-Fasawī said: Just as they called it—the sky—“the leprous one,” so too they called it “the lofty one.”

Yaʿqūb said: Jidhʿ Ẓafār is a city in Yemen; the form “Jidhʿ Ẓafārī” is also attested, and it too is correct.

Texts from Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān cited by al-Anṣārī in (Dhamm al-Kalām wa-Ahlih)

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī al-Ḥusayn informed us: Abū Bakr ibn al-Qāsim informed us, at Bukhārā: Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Yaḥyā informed us: Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to us: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṣāliḥ related to us: Muʿāwiya ibn Ṣāliḥ related to me, from Ṣāliḥ ibn Jubayr, who said: Abū Jumʿa al-Anṣārī, a Companion of the Messenger of God ﷺ came to us in Jerusalem to pray there. Rajāʾ ibn Ḥaywa was with us that day. When he finished, we went out with him to see him off. As we were about to part, he said, “I owe you a gift and a due: I will relate to you a report that I heard from the Messenger of God ﷺ.” We said, “Tell us, may God have mercy on you.” He said: We were with the Messenger of God ﷺ and Muʿādh ibn Jabal ﵁ was with us; we were ten in all. We said, “Messenger of God, is there any people whose reward is greater than ours? We believed in you and followed you.”

He said, “What prevents you from that, when the Messenger of God ﷺ is among you and brings you revelation from heaven? Rather, there will be people who come after you, to whom a book between two covers will come. They will believe in it and act according to what is in it. Their reward will be greater than yours; their reward will be greater than yours.”

Al-Qāsim informed us: Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī al-Abī informed us: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUmar related to us: Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān said: Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb related to us: I heard Ḥammād ibn Zayd say, concerning God’s words, “Do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet” (49:2): “I consider raising one’s voice over him after his death to be like raising one’s voice over him during his life. When a report of the Messenger of God is recited, you must listen to it just as you listen to the Qurʾān.”

The wording of Abū Zurʿa.

Yaʿqūb said: Sulaymān said: When Ḥammād was relating a report and saw us talking, he would not relate it to us. He would say, “I fear this may fall under God’s words, ‘Do not raise your voices’” (49:2), and the verse that follows.

ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Balkhī informed us: Muḥammad ibn ʿUmar ibn Shabawayh al-Zāhid related to us—at Marw: al-Munkadirī informed us: Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to us—from the original, with selections by al-Sakkarī Abū ʿAbd Allāh, and it was not in the Musnad: ʿAmr ibn ʿĀṣim al-Kilābī related to us: Hammām related to us, from Maṭar, who reported: al-Zuhrī related to us, from Sālim, from his father, who said: I traveled with the Messenger of God ﷺ and with ʿUmar, and I never saw them pray more than two rakʿahs. We had been astray, and God guided us; by this we follow their example.

Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān informed us: ʿAlī ibn Aḥmad ibn Bakrān informed us—at Baṣra: al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān al-Fasawī related to us: Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related to us: ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Shaqīq related to us: ʿAbd Allāh related to us: Sulaymān al-Taymī reported to me, from Abū ʿUthmān al-Nahdī, who said: ʿUmar wrote to us, “Do not sit with Ḍubayʿ. If he came while we were a hundred, we would disperse and leave him.”

He would sometimes say: “When we sat with him.”
